dandi:000005.question: At what resolution is dVm/dt of the touch-aligned average Vm taken for the latency rule, the recording's own sampling rate (10 or 20 kHz) or the average in 1 ms bins as for the spike PSTH? The same question applies to the laser-onset latencies of exc-thalamus-photoinhibition and to exc-vm-touch-whisking.
dandi:000005.passage: Touch latency was identified as the latency from touch onset to the time when dVm/dt crossed baseline (3x s.d. of the dVm/dt between 0 and 25 ms before touch). All touch-spike PSTHs were constructed with a bin size of 1 ms. (Online Methods, Data analysis)
dandi:000005.why: At the full sampling rate two of the five whole-cell FS cells cross the threshold at 0.0 and 0.3 ms and the mean latency is 1.88 ms (not reproduced); in 1 ms bins the mean over three cells is 3.67 to 4.17 ms (within 4.0 +- 0.4). For the thalamic and cortical light the full rate gives 0.1 ms for both, the 1 ms bins 5.0 and 2.0 ms.
dandi:000005.answer: The recording's sampling rate, not 1 ms bins. The Methods give 1 ms bins for spike PSTHs only ("All touch-spike PSTHs were constructed with a bin size of 1 ms"), and the paper's Vm latencies are not on a 1 ms grid. The FS onset has "median, 4.2 ms, n = 7 neurons" and the E latency "median, 4.7 ms" over 37; with an odd n each median is one cell's value. The laser latencies are 4.2 and 2.8 ms. The paper gives no smoothing and does not say whether a crossing was interpolated. Criteria of fs-vm-touch-whisking, exc-vm-touch-whisking and exc-thalamus-photoinhibition, and header O8, now say dVm/dt is taken at the sampling rate. Claims and expected values unchanged.

dandi:000005.question: The dPSTH/dt latency is found in 1 ms bins. Is the latency the bin's left edge or its centre? It applies also to vpm-touch and pv-enphr-suppression.
dandi:000005.passage: Latency for touch-evoked spikes was defined as the latency from touch onset to the time when dPSTH/dt crossed a threshold (Online Methods, Data analysis); the medians the paper reports (2.5 ms for VPM, 4.5 ms for FS) fall on half milliseconds.
dandi:000005.why: The two differ by 0.5 ms, more than the 0.32 ms tolerance of vpm-touch. No outcome of this attempt changes with it, but a later attempt could.
dandi:000005.answer: The paper does not say. The Methods define the latency as "the latency from touch onset to the time when dPSTH/dt crossed a threshold" with no bin time. The half-millisecond medians do not settle it: 4.5 ms is the median of 24 cells, an even n, so it can be the mean of two whole-millisecond values; the VPM latency n is not printed. Header O9 names (a) the left edge and (b) the centre of the crossing bin, and vpm-touch, fs-touch-response and pv-enphr-suppression now run both.

dandi:000005.question: The claims file defines FS cells as cells "driven by 5 ms light pulses within 5 ms of onset" and inside the waveform boundary of Supplementary Fig. 6. What test, against what baseline and at what threshold, decides that a cell is driven, and how are the peak, the trough and the spike duration of the boundary measured (the polarity of the cell-attached spike, the baseline, and whether duration is the time from peak to trough)? This decides the FS group of every FS claim and the excitatory group of every excitatory claim.
dandi:000005.passage: We recorded from neurons that were directly driven by light within 5 ms after photostimulus onset (Online Methods, Barrel cortex recordings); Supplementary Fig. 6, "Definition of peak and trough is given in inset".
dandi:000005.why: Here a cell is driven when a one-sided binomial test of a spike 0 to 5 ms after isolated pulses against the same 5 ms 50 ms earlier gives p < 0.001 (24 VGAT-ChR2 cells; 27 at p < 0.01), and duration is peak-to-trough time on the 300 Hz high-passed mean spike. With these, 8 of 20 driven cell-attached cells fall outside the boundary, leaving 12 where Supplementary Table 2 has 24, and the outcome of thalamus-drives-fs turns on it (5 cells inside, 9 without the boundary).
dandi:000005.answer: The paper does not give the test, the baseline or the threshold. It says only "We recorded from neurons that were directly driven by light within 5 ms after photostimulus onset", with "Light pulses (5 ms) were delivered at either 5 or 10 Hz" (Online Methods). Peak and trough are defined only graphically in the Supplementary Fig. 6 inset, which this run could not render; the text calls the duration "spike peak to trough duration" (Online Methods), so duration is peak-to-trough time. Polarity and baseline are not stated. The fs-touch-response criterion now names readings: driven at p < 0.001 and at p < 0.01, each with and without the approximate boundary. The check is the paper's counts: 19 ChR2-tagged control FS cells (5 whole-cell, 14 cell-attached), and 14 control plus 10 ION-cut cell-attached FS cells in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice (Supplementary Table 2). The 24 of Supplementary Table 2 includes the 10 ION-cut cells.

dandi:000005.question: Is the chi-squared test of no-lick performance with and without light corrected for continuity (Yates)?
dandi:000005.passage: In 8 mice tested, 6 showed a significant decrease of performance during Nolick trials with PV interneuron inactivation (p < 0.05, Chi-squared test, solid lines) (Supplementary Fig. 14c)
dandi:000005.why: With the correction, 4 mice (trials pooled) or 5 (any session) show a significant decrease; without it, 5 or 6, which moves the outcome between not reproduced, partially reproduced and reproduced.
dandi:000005.answer: The paper does not say. It gives only "(p < 0.05, Chi-squared test, solid lines)" (Supplementary Fig. 14c legend) and "All statistical analyses were performed in Matlab" (Online Methods). Matlab's crosstab returns the uncorrected Pearson chi-squared, but the paper does not name the function and no code was available. The behavior-false-alarms criterion now names (i) no correction and (ii) Yates's correction, each run.

dandi:000005.question: Are the paired tests of light against control one-sided (light lower) or two-sided?
dandi:000005.passage: Photoinhibition reduced spike rates in FS interneurons during nonwhisking (to 4% of control ... (Results, Inhibition is driven by thalamus, paragraph 2)
dandi:000005.why: Only 5 FS cells by the claims file's rule have thalamic light; a two-sided signed-rank test with 5 cells cannot go below p = 0.0625, a one-sided one can reach 0.031.
dandi:000005.answer: Two-sided. The text does not state the sides, but the printed values fit exact two-sided signed-rank tests at the printed n: "to 4% of control, P = 5 × 10−4, n = 13 neurons" is the two-sided exact P when the cell with the smallest change goes up (4.9 x 10^-4), and no one-sided exact P at n = 13 rounds to 5 x 10^-4 (2.4, 3.7 and 6.1 x 10^-4). The P values for n = 15 and 14 (6 x 10^-5 and 1 x 10^-4) are the two-sided minima. The analyses were run in Matlab, whose signrank is two-sided by default. The thalamus-drives-fs criterion now says two-sided; the one-sided P is a reported variant. With 5 cells the claim cannot pass at 0.05, which is a matter of sample size, not of the test.

dandi:000005.question: Do the touch counts and the performance include the trials with light?
dandi:000005.passage: Mice touched the pole at a proximal location multiple times (number of touches: 5.7 +- 5.3, mean +- s.d., 4,147 trials) (Online Methods, Behavior)
dandi:000005.why: With every trial (all sessions, principal whisker) the counts are 6.04 and 0.85, both within tolerance; without the light trials they are 5.74 and 0.80, and the no-lick count falls outside, which moves the outcome from partially reproduced to not reproduced.
dandi:000005.answer: The paper does not say. The Behavior paragraph gives "5.7 ± 5.3, mean ± s.d., 4,147 trials" and performance "during the recordings of 111 cells" with no mention of light trials. The behavior-touches criterion now names light readings (x) every trial and (y) trials without light only, each run with its recording and whisker readings. The trial counts under each are reported against 4,147 and 4,173.

dandi:000005.question: For whisking onsets, over which windows is "the average whisking amplitude increased by at least 2 degrees" judged, and which touches (onset or offset, which whiskers) bound the -10 to 100 ms exclusion around touches in the whisking epochs?
dandi:000005.passage: Transitions from nonwhisking to whisking ... were defined as the end of a nonwhisking epoch followed by a period in which the average whisking amplitude increased by least 2 degrees and no touch occurred within 250 ms (Online Methods, Data analysis)
dandi:000005.why: Here the amplitude 100 to 300 ms after the end of the nonwhisking period is compared with 0 to 200 ms before it, and touches of every tracked whisker are excluded from 10 ms before onset to 100 ms after offset. These set the onsets and epochs behind every whisking measure; the attempt did not run other readings of them.
dandi:000005.answer: The paper gives neither. The rule names no windows ("the average whisking amplitude increased by least 2°"), and the epoch rule says only "excluding ... −10 to 100 ms surrounding touches". The Behavior paragraph says "Touches by the principal and surround whiskers were treated independently", which does not say which touches bound whisking epochs. The only whisking-onset windows the paper gives are those of the Supplementary Fig. 4 legend (0 to 200 ms before, 100 to 300 ms after). Header O10 and O11 name the readings, now cited in exc-vm-touch-whisking: windows (a) the Supplementary Fig. 4 windows (this attempt's) and (b) 0 to 250 ms after against the whole nonwhisking period; touches of (a) every tracked whisker or (b) the principal whisker, spanning (i) 10 ms before onset to 100 ms after offset or (ii) 10 ms before to 100 ms after onset.

dandi:000005.question: Should the dVm/dt crossing that sets the Vm latency be smoothed, or count only when it is sustained, since a 3 s.d. threshold on an unsmoothed dVm/dt at 10 to 20 kHz is crossed by noise? The same applies to exc-vm-touch-whisking and the laser latencies of exc-thalamus-photoinhibition.
dandi:000005.passage: Touch latency was identified as the latency from touch onset to the time when dVm/dt crossed baseline (3x s.d. of the dVm/dt between 0 and 25 ms before touch). (Online Methods, Data analysis)
dandi:000005.why: Raised by the round-2 verifier. Single samples of dVm/dt cross the threshold at 0.0 and 0.3 ms in two of the five FS cells (mean 1.88 ms against 4.0 +- 0.4), and 1 and 3 of the 250 baseline samples of the laser averages already cross it, giving 0.1 ms for both laser latencies. A rule that ignores one-sample crossings could move fs-vm-touch-whisking and the latency part of exc-thalamus-photoinhibition.

dandi:000005.question: The criterion says reproduced when 6 of 8 mice show a significant decrease under a reading, but the header says the outcome is the one all readings give, or the claim is methods_underspecified. Which rule applies?
dandi:000005.why: Raised by the round-2 verifier. Only reading (b)(i) gives 6 mice; the others give 5, 4 and 5. Under the header rule the claim would be partially reproduced or blocked. Reading (b) also counts anm266945 on one of its 11 sessions (p = 0.003), although its pooled test gives p = 0.305.

dandi:000005.question: Should the share of cells with r2 > 0.25 be compared with a null, since the rule is close to chance here? The same applies to fs-whisking-phase.
dandi:000005.passage: Distribution of the goodness-of-fit (r2) of the spike-phase relationship. Dashed line, r2=0.25 (Supplementary Figure legends)
dandi:000005.why: Raised by the verifier in both rounds. Spikes moved to the next trial still pass for 16 of 29 VPM units and 9 of 17 FS cells, so the more than half rule passes on a null. A null comparison could change both outcomes.

dandi:000006.question: The criterion says the reading of the unit selection that reproduces the 61 and 69 units is the one the other electrophysiology claims use. On the dandiset neither does (the code's rule keeps 44 PTupper and 56 PTlower units, the Methods' session rule 42 and 63), because 11 of the paper's sessions are not in it. Which selection should the other claims use when neither reading matches?
dandi:000006.passage: Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis ("Units recorded during behavioural sessions in which performance was not greater than 65% ... 13 units were rejected; 130 were kept"); the claims file's opening comment, Unit inclusion.
dandi:000006.why: pt-spike-rates-similar, pt-variance-explained and pt-single-neuron-early-selectivity give different outcomes under the two selections, and are blocked until it is fixed. On the paper's processed data the code's rule gives 61 and 69.
dandi:000006.answer: Use the code's per-unit rule. The Methods report the selection's outcome ("13 units were rejected; 130 were kept"), and on the paper's processed data the code's rule (loadAndProcessData.m) is the one that gives it, with 61 and 69, as the attempt reports. The Methods' session rule is a variant. Missing sessions on the dandiset do not change which rule is the paper's. Recorded in the opening comment (Unit inclusion) and the pt-tagged-units criterion.

dandi:000006.question: The go-cue aligned rates come precomputed in the paper's data files, so the claims file leaves their trial range open (the unit's range, or all trials). Can the code settle it? In the processed file data_structure_anm372906_WR40_psth.mat, every unit of a session has rates for the same trials, the eleventh to the tenth before the session's last correct trial.
dandi:000006.passage: The claims file's opening comment, Trial range per unit; loadAndProcessData.m (getData reads the precomputed psth; ObjToLickPSTH builds the lick-aligned rates over the unit's range).
dandi:000006.why: With the code's selection, reading (a) of the measure is reproduced with the unit's range and not reproduced with all trials (Mann-Whitney p 0.0041 against 0.026), so the claim is blocked.
dandi:000006.answer: Yes. The premise holds for that session but not for the files as a whole. In the processed files (Ephys.zip, Code/ProcessedData, variable psth, which getData reads), the go-cue rates of units in one session often start and end on different trials (WR29.5 session 2 starts at trial 12 for one unit and 41 for another; WR33 session 2 ends at 110, 159 and 188 for different units). Every range starts at trial 11 or later and ends 10 or more trials before the session's last correct trial. That fits the unit's range of ObjToLickPSTH, reading (a); all trials is a variant. The claim's criterion and the opening comment (Trial range per unit) now say so.

dandi:000006.question: The criterion gives two rules for "larger" ((i) medians; (ii) the PTupper 5th percentile above the PTlower median) and outcomes for each, and "more consistent" as a smaller s.d. over median of the bootstrap. Under (i) the claim is partially reproduced in 31 of 32 combinations of the other readings and under (ii) not reproduced in 27. Which rule decides?
dandi:000006.passage: Results, Preparatory activity, paragraph 2 ("selectivity was larger and more consistent across trials in the PTupper population"); Fig. 5b.
dandi:000006.why: The two rules give different outcomes, so the claim is blocked, and with it pt-upper-persistent, pt-cohort-control and pt-types-differ-in-timing, which depend on it.
dandi:000006.answer: The paper does not give it. The Results say "selectivity was larger and more consistent across trials in the PTupper population" with no number or test. Fig. 5b and its legend give only the bootstrap median and 5-95% band, and Projections.m makes no comparison between the populations. Both rules stay, and the claim is methods_underspecified while they differ. Noted in the criterion.

dandi:000006.question: The levels 0.5 and 0.75 give different outcomes. At 0.5 PTupper's correlation falls below the level 0.37 to 0.40 s after the go cue (reproduced); at 0.75 it falls at 0.17 to 0.19 s, under the 0.2 s bound (partially reproduced). Can the paper or its code fix the level, or the measure of how fast the coding direction changes?
dandi:000006.passage: Results, Movement commands, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 7c, e legends; CDCorrelation.m.
dandi:000006.why: The claim is blocked until one reading decides.
dandi:000006.answer: The paper does not give it. The Extended Data Fig. 7c legend says the change is abrupt "immediately after the go cue onset" in PTlower and, in PTupper, "more slowly (over several hundred milliseconds), largely after initiation of movement". The 7e legend gives no level, and CDCorrelation.m only plots the normalised correlation, with a dotted line at 0.05 s, and computes no crossing time. Both levels stay, and the claim is methods_underspecified while they differ. Noted in the criterion.

dandi:000006.question: The two window readings give different outcomes for CDgo (window (a) holds with the code's selection and the 4 and 8 mice; window (b) does not under any reading). Can the paper fix the windows? Also, the files do not assign licks to trials; the attempt rebuilds each trial's last lick from the stored order (98.1% agreement with the processed data). Is that acceptable for this claim?
dandi:000006.passage: Results, Movement commands, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 10a, b legends.
dandi:000006.why: The claim is blocked until one reading decides.
dandi:000006.answer: The paper gives no windows. The Extended Data Fig. 10a, b legends give only the 5-95% band, and Projections.m plots the lick-aligned selectivity with no window or test, so both readings stay. The last lick is the code's (getLickInfo), the latest left or right lick after the go cue in the trial. The paper says nothing about rebuilding it when licks are not assigned to trials. A rebuilt last lick is a deviation, acceptable if the outcome is the same when the trials where it disagrees with the processed data are left out; show that. Noted in the criterion.

dandi:000006.question: The criterion runs both the unit depth field and the session's manipulator depth. The files hold only the unit depth. May the claim be judged on the unit depth alone? (On the processed data both readings agree.)
dandi:000006.passage: Fig. 4e legend; Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis; simplePlots.m, plotDepth.
dandi:000006.why: The attempt judged it on the unit depth (reproduced) and showed the manipulator depth from the processed data as a variant.
dandi:000006.answer: Yes. Fig. 4e is the plot of the unit depth field (simplePlots.m, plotDepth, meta.depth), and the Methods say "Unit depths (Fig. 4e) were inferred from manipulator readings only". The unit depth decides, and the session manipulator depth is a variant. The criterion now says so.

dandi:000006.question: The claim depends on pt-spike-rates-similar for its rates only, and its own test gives the same result under every reading. Because pt-spike-rates-similar is blocked, the protocol blocks this claim too. Should the dependency be on pt-tagged-units instead?
dandi:000006.passage: The claims file, depends_on of pt-lower-heterogeneous-rates.
dandi:000006.why: With the dependency it is blocked; without it, it would be reproduced under every reading.
dandi:000006.answer: Yes. The claim uses only the rate definitions of pt-spike-rates-similar, not its outcome, so depends_on is now pt-tagged-units. The criterion notes the change. This changes no statement or expected value.

dandi:000006.question: The claim is tested on the single-cell annotation in Seq.zip (SingleCellAnnotation.txt). The claims file gives no rule for counting the ALM glutamatergic clusters. The attempt counts 27 with the clusters not named for VISp (the Cajal-Retzius cluster included), 26 without it, 25 with most of their cells in ALM and 45 with any ALM cell. Which rule does the paper's 27 follow?
dandi:000006.passage: Results, Two types of PT neuron in layer 5, paragraph 1; Fig. 1 legend ("The transcriptomic cluster corresponding to Cajal-Retzius cells was excluded here"); Methods, scRNA-seq analysis.
dandi:000006.why: The attempt took the count as a reading of a reported number (reproduced under the matching reading); a rule from a reader would decide it.
dandi:000006.answer: The paper settles it. Fig. 1a names 26 glutamatergic clusters, and its legend says "The transcriptomic cluster corresponding to Cajal–Retzius cells was excluded here". The Methods give "27 glutamatergic" ALM types. So the 27 are the clusters of Fig. 1a plus the Cajal-Retzius cluster, which is the attempt's count of clusters not named for VISp with Cajal-Retzius included. The other counts are variants. Recorded in the criterion.

dandi:000006.question: The annotation has two injection-site fields, inj_primary_label and inj_roi_label, and a cell must be grouped into medulla, thalamus, superior colliculus or pons. With inj_primary_label and the Allen ontology (medulla IRN, GRN, PARN; thalamus VAL, PF, MD; pons PG, PRNc) the medulla, thalamus and pons counts match the paper; with inj_roi_label the medulla count is 58 and the superior colliculus count matches. Which grouping did the paper use?
dandi:000006.passage: Results, Two types of PT neuron in layer 5, paragraph 4; Methods, scRNA-seq (n = 62 medulla injection; n = 94 thalamus; n = 100 pons; n = 97 superior colliculus).
dandi:000006.why: Under both fields all medulla-labelled cells are Slco2a1 and 91 of 94 thalamus-labelled cells are Npsr1 or Hpgd; the medulla count of 62 holds under one.
dandi:000006.answer: The paper does not say which field defines the Fig. 2f groups. Its notebook for the same cells (Seq/SC_correlations_across_clusters.ipynb, Extended Data Fig. 4a-c) groups by inj_roi_label, matching "IRN" (medulla), "VAL" (thalamus), "PG" (pons) and "SC|SCm" (superior colliculus). The criterion now names that grouping and inj_primary_label with the Allen ontology as readings. The counts are reported numbers, so the claim holds when both match under one reading.

dandi:000006.question: The claim has no criterion or method. The attempt follows the code (Seq/bulkVsSC.m on Seq.zip), which takes the bulk values as stored, and also the legend's log2(CPM + 1). Is the code's method the one to use?
dandi:000006.why: Both give r within tolerance (0.867 and 0.874), so the outcome does not depend on it.
dandi:000006.answer: Partly. The legend fixes the measure, fold change "measured as log2(CPM + 1)". The code (bulkVsSC.m) applies log2(x + 1) to bulk_data.txt as stored, which holds counts, not CPM (columns sum to about 1e7). Where they differ the legend is followed. The genes, cells and replicates are taken from the code, and the code's bulk values are a variant. Recorded in the criterion.

dandi:000006.question: What counts as innervating the thalamus in the reconstructions? With any axon terminus, 11 of the code's 12 neurons do; with axon length, 11; with more termini in the thalamus than in the medulla, 8, the code's thalamus group. The same question holds for pt-lower-medulla-projection ("bypassed the thalamus"). The paper's code groups the neurons by hand (AxonReconstructions.m) and reports termini and lengths per structure.
dandi:000006.passage: Results, Two types of PT neuron in layer 5, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 2a-d legends; Axons/AxonReconstructions.m.
dandi:000006.why: The readings give different counts, so both claims are blocked.
dandi:000006.answer: The paper gives no rule. Supplementary data table 1 (read in the publisher's Supplementary Information PDF) assigns the 12 complete neurons to the two types, the same as the hand grouping in AxonReconstructions.m. Extended Data Fig. 2a, c plot thalamic lengths and termini for both groups. The criteria of both claims now name three readings (any terminus, any length, more termini in the thalamus than in the medulla, and the converse for "bypassed"). The 8 and the 4 are reported counts, so each holds if it matches under one reading.

dandi:000006.question: Which 18 neurons are meant? Axons.zip holds 22; the attempt reads the 18 with somata in motor cortex (MOp or MOs), which gives the paper's count. Supplementary Table 1, which lists them, is not in the text read.
dandi:000006.passage: Results, Two types of PT neuron in layer 5, paragraph 5.
dandi:000006.why: Under both readings one neuron (AA0134) does not reach the superior colliculus, so the outcome is partially reproduced either way.
dandi:000006.answer: The 18 are listed in Supplementary data table 1 (Supplementary Information PDF from the publisher). They are the 12 complete neurons and 6 partial ones, thalamus-projecting AA0132, AA0135 and AA0250 and medulla-projecting AA0131, AA0134 and AA0169. AA0134 is one of the 18. Recorded in the source and criterion.

dandi:000006.question: The claim is marked data elsewhere, but no smFISH images or counts are in any file of the Figshare record (Anatomy.zip holds image stacks of six brains for retrograde and anterograde labelling only), and the paper names no other archive for them. Should it be data dataset, blocked as data missing?
dandi:000006.passage: Methods, In situ hybridization; Data availability.
dandi:000006.why: The checker forbids data_missing for an elsewhere claim, so the attempt blocked it as other.
dandi:000006.answer: Yes, data dataset. The Data availability statement names archives for the bulk RNA-seq (GEO) and the electrophysiology (CRCNS.org, Figshare) only, and Anatomy.zip holds no smFISH images. The where entry naming Anatomy.zip was wrong about the paper. data is now dataset and where is removed, so the claim can be blocked as data missing.

dandi:000006.question: Anatomy.zip holds the image stacks (for example BL648_Thal_Med_H2b, two channels) but no cell counts. Does the paper or its code say how labelled and co-labelled cells were counted?
dandi:000006.passage: Results, Two types of PT neuron in layer 5, paragraph 3; Methods, Histology and imaging.
dandi:000006.why: Without a counting method the claim is blocked as methods underspecified.
dandi:000006.answer: No. The Methods (Histology and imaging) describe sectioning, immunolabelling and imaging only, and the Figshare record holds no anatomy code. The counting method is open, and the claim stays methods_underspecified. Also, the folder names in Anatomy.zip name no superior colliculus labelling, which the 77.1% needs. Recorded in the criterion.

dandi:000006.question: The second part of the statement (both types send collaterals to the subthalamic nucleus, zona incerta and midbrain reticular nucleus) is quoted from the bulk labelling of Extended Data Fig. 2e. The attempt tested it on the reconstructions. Is that the intended test?
dandi:000006.why: The reconstructions support it (both groups reach all three structures); the images were not analysed.
dandi:000006.answer: No. The second part is stated in the Extended Data Fig. 2e legend, from the bulk labelling ("Bulk projections of PTupper and PTlower populations"), with no measure or count. Its intended test is those images, for which the paper gives no method of analysis. The test on the reconstructions is a variant. The first part, on the superior colliculus, is stated of the reconstructions and is tested on them. Recorded in the criterion.

dandi:000006.question: The verifier of round 1 reported that several criteria judge counts out of the paper's 61 PTupper and 69 PTlower units, which the dandiset cannot reach as it holds 44 and 56 of them under the code's rule (11 sessions are missing). They are pt-selective-any-epoch (122 of 130), pt-preparatory-activity part (a) (40 and 44), the 70% counts and the top 10 and top 21 of pt-upper-decoding and pt-upper-decoding-rectified, and the PTupper share of pt-lower-bursting (3.3%, where one of 44 units is 2.3%). Should these be judged as counts, as now, or as fractions of the units the dandiset holds?
dandi:000006.passage: Results, Cell-type-specific recordings and Preparatory activity; Extended Data Fig. 9c, d legend. The paper reports the counts with their fractions (122 of 130, 94%; 15 of 61, 24.6%).
dandi:000006.why: As fractions some would hold. 29 of 44 and 38 of 56 late delay selective units are 65.9% and 67.9%, against the paper's 65.6% and 63.8%; 99 of 100 selective units is 99%, against 94%. On the processed data for the same 100 units the counts are the dandiset's, so the shortfall comes from the missing units.

dandi:000006.question: The verifier of round 1 reported that the criterion's CDearly test asks whether the PTlower-cohort median lies inside the PTupper cohort's 5-95% interval, in either direction. Here it lies above it (9.82 against 4.0 to 8.9), that is the PTlower cohort is the more selective, the opposite of the PT difference (PTupper 3.97 against PTlower 2.09). Is a difference in the opposite direction a failure of "not explained by the animal cohorts", or should the test ask only whether the cohorts reproduce the PT difference?
dandi:000006.passage: Results, Preparatory activity, paragraph 2 ("Differences in coding between PTupper and PTlower neurons could not be explained by variation across animal cohorts"); Extended Data Fig. 8 legend.
dandi:000006.why: Read as the claim's words, the CDearly part would hold (the cohorts do not reproduce the PT difference), and the claim's own test would give reproduced, not partially reproduced. The claim is blocked through pt-upper-early-preparatory either way.

dandi:000008.question: Reading (b) compares the mean pairwise embedding distance of the high-firing Sst Pvalb Calb2 cells with random halves of the t-type over 1,000 permutations, with one-sided p < 0.05. On this data the p-value is 0.0505 when estimated with 100,000 random subsets, and 1,000 permutations give 0.045 to 0.057 depending on the random seed, so the seed decides the outcome. Should reading (b) be judged with a fixed larger number of permutations (or exactly, over all subsets of that size), and with which threshold?
dandi:000008.passage: None found. The paper shows Fig. 5d as a colour overlay only (Results, Variability in individual t-types, paragraph 3, "high-firing cells were mostly grouped in one part of the transcriptomic landscape"); the permutation test is the claims file's reading.
dandi:000008.why: Reading (a) holds (Spearman rho = 0.363, one-sided p = 0.034). If reading (b) holds the claim is reproduced; if not, the readings disagree and the claim stays blocked as methods_underspecified. With the seed used here (1,000 permutations) p = 0.052.
dandi:000008.answer: The paper does not give it. Fig. 5d is a colour overlay with no measure or test, and the code draws only the overlay (phenotype-tsne.ipynb, the cell with ttype = 'Sst Pvalb Calb2', "plt.scatter(pos[:,0], pos[:,1], c=col, ...)" with col the 'Max number of APs'). The 1,000 permutations were the claims file's choice, not the paper's, so the criterion now fixes them so that no seed decides. Exact over all subsets of that size when there are at most 1,000,000, otherwise 100,000 random subsets with p = (k + 1) / (N + 1). The threshold stays one-sided p < 0.05, and (b) holds only when the upper bound of the 95% Clopper-Pearson interval of the estimate is also below 0.05. The claim's statement and readings are unchanged.

dandi:000008.question: Under the answered criterion, reading (b) uses 100,000 random subsets with a Clopper-Pearson bound because there are 10,400,600 subsets, more than 1,000,000. With the section's seed (55) p = 0.0485 with interval 0.0472 to 0.0499, and (b) holds; with seeds 56 to 60 the estimate is 0.0496 to 0.0514 and each interval reaches 0.05 or above, so (b) does not hold. The exact p-value over all 10,400,600 subsets can be computed here and is 0.0497. Should (b) be judged on the exact p-value when it can be computed in reasonable time, whatever the number of subsets?
dandi:000008.passage: None found. Fig. 5d is a colour overlay with no test (Results, Variability in individual t-types, paragraph 3); the permutation test is the claims file's reading.
dandi:000008.why: The exact p-value (0.0497) gives the same outcome as the section's seed (reproduced), but five of six seeds of the 100,000-subset estimate would leave the readings in disagreement, and the claim would be blocked as methods_underspecified, so the seed still decides under the current criterion.

dandi:000008.question: The criterion accepts one fewer cell in one class under reading (b) of cohort-cells-mice when the dandiset lacks a cell with a t-type. The cell the dandiset lacks (20190211_sample_10) is the only L6 CT Gpr139 cell, so the dandiset covers 76 t-types where the paper gives 77. Does the allowance also accept one fewer t-type when the missing cell is the only cell of its t-type?
dandi:000008.passage: None found. The paper gives 77 of the 90 t-types (Results, Patch-seq of mouse primary motor cortex, paragraph 3) for its 1,227 cells, which include the missing cell.
dandi:000008.why: The three cell counts match under the allowance (1,226, 817, 409) and the t-type count is 76. If the allowance covers the t-type, the claim is reproduced; if not, it stays partially reproduced.

dandi:000009.question: The deposited mean waveforms are 29 to 38 samples at 25 kHz with the trough at sample 15 to 19, so trough-to-peak widths above about 0.5 ms cannot be measured (the peak is the last sample in 78% of ALM units labelled wide). The files carry a `cell_type` label ('Wide width spiking', 'Narrow width spiking', 'Cannot be determined') whose rule is not stated. Should the unit classes (ALM pyramidal > 0.6 ms, thalamic > 0.5 ms, SNr GABAergic < 0.45 ms) be taken from widths computed on the deposited waveforms (P1), or from the files' labels (P2)?
dandi:000009.passage: Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis, "Spike widths were computed as the trough-to-peak interval in the mean spike waveform."
dandi:000009.why: P1 gives 577 ALM pyramidal and 148 thalamic units, P2 gives 810 and 682 (paper 1006 of 1214 and 672 of 790). Selections downstream change size, for example 20 against 222 VM/VAL units, and the ALM populations of Fig. 6e are empty under P1. The attempt runs both.
dandi:000009.answer: The paper gives the rule, not the label. Widths are "computed as the trough-to-peak interval in the mean spike waveform" and the classes "separated based on the histogram of spike widths" (Extended Data Fig. 4b); the paper never mentions a deposited cell_type label or how long the stored waveforms are. P1 is the Methods' rule; P2 is a reading only because the paper does not say how the label was made. For thalamus the Methods add "our conclusions ( Fig. 2 , 6 ) are valid if all the units were pooled", a further reading (P3) for the thalamic claims of Fig. 2 and 6. Written as convention C in the opening comment and into alm-unit-classes, thalamus-unit-classes and snr-photoinhibition.

dandi:000009.question: Besides the 18 VGAT-ChR2-EYFP ALM sessions (thalamus photostimulation at 10 mW), the dandiset holds 21 ALM sessions of four PV-Cre x Ai32 mice with thalamic photostimulation at 10, 22.5 and 45 mW. Do these belong to the ALM recordings during thalamus photoinhibition of Fig. 3 (n = 314), and at which power?
dandi:000009.passage: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 1, "using VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice"; Methods, Photoinhibition, "photoinihibition in the PV-IRES-Cre x Ai32 mice was indistinguishable from the VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice" (said of cortical photoinhibition).
dandi:000009.why: VGAT units alone number 234 to 261 (below 314 +/- 31) and fall to 2.1 to 2.5% of control; adding the PV-Cre x Ai32 units at 10 mW gives 360 to 522 units at 5.5 to 11.1% (Q1) with up to 7 significantly activated. The attempt follows the claims file (VGAT) and shows the others as a variant.
dandi:000009.answer: No, by the text. The Results say "using VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice" for Fig. 3, and the Methods list PV-IRES-Cre x Ai32 mice only for ALM photoinhibition ("Fig. 1 and 6 , Extended Data Fig. 8 , 10"); the "indistinguishable" sentence is about cortical photoinhibition. The power is 10 mW ("Laser power at the tip of optical fiber 10mW, n = 314 cells", Extended Data Fig. 2e). Supplementary Table 1, which lists animals and powers per experiment, is not in the text read. The PV-IRES-Cre x Ai32 sessions stay a variant, not a reading. Written into the criterion of fig3-alm-collapse.

dandi:000009.question: ALM photoinhibition trials are at 1.5 mW in most sessions, but some sessions interleave 0.75 or 0.79 mW. Do the lower-power trials enter the photoinhibition condition?
dandi:000009.passage: Methods, Photoinhibition, "We used 40 Hz photostimulation with a sinusoidal temporal profile (1.5mW average power)".
dandi:000009.why: VM/VAL activity falls to 47.5% of control at 1.5 mW and to 57.7% with all powers pooled (P2, T1). The attempt uses 1.5 mW and shows all powers as a variant.
dandi:000009.answer: No. The Methods give one power for ALM photoinhibition, "1.5mW average power", for Fig. 1, 6 and Extended Data Figs 8 and 10, and name no other; trials at 0.75 or 0.79 mW are outside the condition, and pooling all powers is a variant. Supplementary Table 1 gives powers per experiment and is not in the text read. Written into convention P in the opening comment, which these claims use.

dandi:000009.question: The whole-cell files record no photostimulus time (their photostimulus columns are empty; `stim_present` marks the trials). Convention E puts the onset 1.3 s after `pole_in_time`, but there the 20 to 120 ms window precedes the effect; thalamus photoinhibition hyperpolarizes ALM neurons from about 1.49 s after `pole_in_time` (15 of 16 cells between 1.47 and 1.51 s), just before 0.1 s after `pole_out_time` (1.5 s), the sample-epoch end of the Methods. Where should the photostimulus onset be placed in these files?
dandi:000009.passage: Methods, Behavior, "The sample epoch (1.3 s total) was the time from onset of pole movement to 0.1 s after the pole started to retract"; Methods, Photoinhibition, the photostimulus starts "at the beginning of the delay epoch".
dandi:000009.why: With onset E thalamus photoinhibition changes Vm by +0.31 mV in the window; with onset M by -16.83 mV (paper -18.7 +/- 1.1). Onsets in milliseconds need the true laser time, which no reading of the paper gives. The attempt blocks these claims (metadata insufficient) and shows both readings.
dandi:000009.answer: The paper gives the onset relative to the task, not to the files' fields. The photostimulus starts "at the beginning of the delay epoch", 1.3 s after the onset of pole movement and 0.1 s after the pole started to retract; the pole travels 0.2 s, stays 1 s and retracts 0.2 s (Methods, Behavior), so the delay begins 0.1 s before retraction is complete. The paper does not say which events pole_in_time and pole_out_time mark and gives no laser time for these recordings. Both E (pole_in_time as the onset of pole movement) and M (pole_out_time as the start of retraction) are readings it allows; placing the onset from the Vm change is not. The onset in milliseconds cannot be fixed from the paper. Written into the criterion of wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization.

dandi:000009.question: The files do not name a vM1 site. In mouse anm00264943, photostimulation at galvo position (0.5, 0.5) mm at 0.79 mW is interleaved with ALM photoinhibition at 0.79 and 1.5 mW. Is this the vM1 condition of Extended Data Fig. 8f, g, and is vM1 compared with ALM photoinhibition at the same power or at 1.5 mW?
dandi:000009.passage: Extended Data Fig. 8f, g legends, "Photoinhibition conditions were interleaved"; the vM1 coordinates are in Supplementary Table 1, not in the text read.
dandi:000009.why: Against ALM at 1.5 mW the vM1 reduction is smaller (p < 0.0001) and the claim would hold; against ALM at 0.79 mW it is not (p = 0.73). The attempt blocks the claim (metadata insufficient).
dandi:000009.answer: The paper does not say which condition is vM1. It gives no vM1 photoinhibition coordinate or power in the text (Supplementary Table 1 is not in the text read); the only vM1 coordinate, "AP1, ML 0.75", is an Allen tracer injection (Extended Data Fig. 8e), and the frame of the galvo positions is not given. On power, the Methods give only 1.5 mW for cortical photoinhibition in Extended Data Fig. 8, so vM1 is compared with ALM at 1.5 mW; ALM at matched power is a variant. The site stays open. Written into the criterion of vm1-photoinhibition-no-effect.

dandi:000009.question: The criterion says correct trials. In sessions with photoinhibition, do the photoinhibition trials enter the population selectivity time course, or only control trials?
dandi:000009.passage: Extended Data Fig. 4c legend gives the method without naming the trials.
dandi:000009.why: In ALM the delay increase holds in 4 of 4 unit and neuron readings with all correct trials and in 2 of 4 with control trials only; the VM/VAL result does not change. The attempt runs both.
dandi:000009.answer: The paper does not say. The Extended Data Fig. 4c legend names no trials, and the Methods say only "Only trials in which mice correctly reported pole locations were included to compute selectivity". Readings (t1) correct control trials only and (t2) all correct trials both stand, as for fig2e-alm-selectivity. Written into the criterion of selectivity-time-course.

dandi:000009.question: The answer of 2026-10-20 took the whole-cell files to hold no laser time. They do. Each holds an OptogeneticSeries (stimulus/presentation/photostim_on_*, 20 kHz, unit 'watts' with conversion 0.001) that is a 10 mW step in the thalamus photoinhibition cells and a 3 mW peak sinusoid in the cortical ones, present in every stim_present trial. It starts 1.4725 s after pole_in_time in the thalamus cells (between reading E, 1.3 s, and reading M, 1.5 s). Should the photostimulus onset be taken from this trace (first sample above a small fraction of its maximum, here 5%), as a reading beside E and M or in their place? If so, may the onset latency of 7.9 ms be judged under it?
dandi:000009.passage: Results, "measured for 100 ms, starting 20 ms after photostimulus onset"; the criterion says "The onset latency of 7.9 ms needs the true laser time, which no reading gives".
dandi:000009.why: Under the laser onset (L) thalamus photoinhibition changes Vm by -13.68 +/- 1.14 mV (M -16.83, E +0.31; paper -18.7 +/- 1.1), with onset 9.60 +/- 1.98 ms by V2 (within 7.9 +/- 1.7) and 0.40 ms by V1. M1 gives -3.26 mV and -0.01 spikes/s, contralateral ALM -1.38 mV, and thalamus is more negative than both (p < 1e-5). No outcome changes between M and L; the attempt shows L as a further reading.

dandi:000010.question: Every extracellular file holds `lick_trace`, a 10 kHz signal described as the tongue movement when licking (arbitrary units), in 5 s segments that start at each trial start. It rises some tens of ms after the go cue in correct trials, so it looks like the photodiode and laser diode signal of the Methods. The claims file does not say how a reaction time is read from it. Which rule gives the reaction time of a trial (a threshold on the raw signal, a number of standard deviations above a pre-cue baseline, and over which baseline window)?
dandi:000010.passage: Methods, Behaviour, "Mouth movements were monitored using a photodiode and an infrared laser diode to obtain reaction time measurements(Thorlabs)." No other passage gives the rule.
dandi:000010.why: The latency of the first crossing moves with the threshold by tens of ms, the size of the tolerance (61.1 +/- 10.5 ms). The claim is blocked as methods_underspecified until answered.
dandi:000010.answer: The paper does not give the rule. The only passage is the one quoted, "Mouth movements were monitored using a photodiode and an infrared laser diode to obtain reaction time measurements"; no threshold, baseline or onset rule appears in the Methods, legends or Extended Data, and the paper links no code. Written into the criterion of reaction-time as readings (k) a fixed threshold on the raw signal and (z) the baseline mean plus a number of s.d. before the go cue, with the threshold, the number and the baseline window open.

dandi:000010.question: The trial tables mark trials without a lick in the response window as outcome "ignore" (416 of 24,580 non-early ephys trials). Are these left out of the per cent correct, or counted as errors?
dandi:000010.passage: Methods, Behavioural data analyses, "Performance was computed as the fraction of correct reports, excluding the 'lick early' trials." Methods, Behaviour, "Trials in which mice did not lick within a 1.5 s window after the go cue were rare and typically occurred at the end of a session."
dandi:000010.why: Counting them as errors lowers performance by about 1.3 points (76.6% to 75.3% pooled). Both are within the tolerance here, so the outcome does not depend on it; the attempt runs both.
dandi:000010.answer: The paper does not say. The Methods exclude only one kind of trial, "Performance was computed as the fraction of correct reports, excluding the 'lick early' trials", so the literal reading keeps no-lick trials in the denominator as not correct; "fraction of correct reports" can also be read as among trials with a report. Written into the criterion of behaviour-performance as readings (x) counted as not correct and (y) left out, both run.

dandi:000010.question: Three details are not in the criterion. (1) "Normalized to its variance" read literally divides by the variance; dividing by the standard deviation is the usual z-score. Which is meant? (2) Are the 10 trials that set the preferred trial type 10 trials in all, or 10 of each trial type? (3) Which 200 ms bin is the population vector "at go cue onset", the bin that starts at the go cue or the one that ends at it?
dandi:000010.passage: Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, "each neuron's response was mean-subtracted and normalized to the variance of its response across the entire trial epoch (computed in time bins of 200ms)" and "we first determined each neuron's preferred trial type using spike counts from a subset of the trials (10 trials)".
dandi:000010.why: The correlation values move with each choice (the delay-epoch mean runs from 0.04 to 0.78 across them). The attempt runs every combination. One fails when the trials with tagging light are left out (division by the variance, difference vector, all neurons, bin starting at the go cue), so the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified until this and the question on light trials are answered.
dandi:000010.answer: None of the three is given. (1) The Methods say "normalized to the variance of its response across the entire trial epoch"; the text as written divides by the variance, and the z-score (standard deviation) is a reading the paper does not exclude. (2) "a subset of the trials (10 trials)" in the Methods and "using spike counts from 10 trials" in Extended Data Fig. 1b do not say whether per trial type. (3) The Fig. 2c legend gives "t 5 0" and "Averaging window, 200ms" but not how the bin sits on the go cue. Written into the criterion of fig2c-population-dynamics as readings (v)/(s), (n10)/(n20) and bin starting at, centred on or ending at the go cue, all combinations run.

dandi:000010.question: Reading (a) of the Kruskal-Wallis span runs from sample onset to the end of the response epoch, and the rank sum test compares responses over the trial epochs, but the criterion does not say how long the response epoch is for imaging. Is it 1.3 s after the go cue, like the other epochs, or the 1.5 s lick window?
dandi:000010.passage: Methods, Behaviour, "Trials in which mice did not lick within a 1.5 s window after the go cue"; Methods, Calcium imaging data analyses, "across multiple 0.33 s time bins (five image samples) during the task".
dandi:000010.why: The task-related count is 2,551 with 1.3 s and 2,730 with 1.5 s (correct trials, reading a), against 2,740 +/- 274. The attempt runs both lengths as readings.
dandi:000010.answer: The paper does not give the length of the response epoch, for imaging or for electrophysiology. It says only that the go cue "signalled the beginning of the response epoch", Fig. 1b marks the 1.3 s sample and delay epochs only, and the 1.5 s figure is the window for a lick ("did not lick within a 1.5 s window after the go cue"). Written into the criterion of imaging-selectivity-counts as readings (r1) 1.3 s and (r2) 1.5 s, both run.

dandi:000010.question: The imaging files give no depth for any plane, so the layer 5 selection (450 to 700 um) cannot be made. The files label 530 included cells PT and 843 IT. Does the paper say anything that identifies the layer 5 planes otherwise, or should the claim be tested on all labelled cells?
dandi:000010.passage: Results, A movement command emerges in the pyramidal tract neurons, paragraph 4 (534 PT and 542 IT neurons in layer 5); Methods, Two-photon calcium imaging (no depth per plane).
dandi:000010.why: The IT count (843 against 542) and the IT selective count differ from the paper's while the PT counts match, which suggests that IT cells outside layer 5 are included; the IT side of the tests depends on which cells are counted. The attempt tests all labelled cells.
dandi:000010.answer: The paper gives nothing else that marks the layer 5 planes; it selects them only by "imaging depth 450-700 mm" (Results; the extraction prints um as mm), and the Methods give no depth per plane. It also says "intratelencephalic neurons were also found in superficial layers", which fits the excess of IT cells seen here, so all labelled cells is not the paper's population. Written into the criterion of fig4h-pt-contra-imaging. Testing all labelled cells is a substitute recorded as a deviation; the IT counts are not expected to match on it, while the PT side, which the paper places in layer 5B, is less affected.

dandi:000010.question: In 75 of the 99 extracellular sessions the antidromic tagging light (1 ms pulse pairs every 0.5 s, at the pons or the other ALM) was delivered during behavioural trials, in 4,332 of 18,385 correct trials. The trial tables do not flag these trials; the laser traces show them. Should the task analyses of Figures 2 and 3 use all correct trials, or only those without the tagging light?
dandi:000010.passage: Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, "Only trials in which mice correctly reported pole locations were included." Methods, Electrophysiology, "Pairs of laser pulses (1 ms duration, 47-82 mW peak power, separated by 10 ms) were deployed every 500ms to elicit antidromic responses". No passage says whether tagging was done during the task or whether those trials were analysed.
dandi:000010.why: The PT neurons are driven antidromically by the light, and their contra-preference changes with the choice (30 of 45 contra-preferring, bootstrap P = 0.010, with the light trials; 26 of 45, P = 0.14, without), so fig3f-pt-contra-preferring is blocked until the answer. The attempt runs every electrophysiology claim both ways.
dandi:000010.answer: The paper does not say. The Results say only that tagged neurons were recorded "during behaviour" ("We next recorded selectively from ChR2-expressing intratelencephalic or pyramidal tract neurons during behaviour"), and the only trial filter of the Methods is "Only trials in which mice correctly reported pole locations were included". Nothing says whether tagging overlapped task trials or whether such trials were dropped. Written into the criterion of fig2-selective-fraction, for every electrophysiology claim of Figs 2 and 3, as readings (t1) all correct trials, the literal reading of the Methods, and (t2) correct trials without the tagging light.

dandi:000010.question: The dandiset holds the tagging light as laser power traces, so latencies can be measured from pulse onset. The criterion does not say how the antidromic spike is told apart from spontaneous spikes. Which spikes count (a window after the pulse, only the first pulse of each pair, only neurons or pulses with a reliable response), and is the jitter the s.d. over all pulses with a spike in that window?
dandi:000010.passage: Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, "mean antidromic spike latencies" and "temporal jitter (mean s.d. of the antidromic spike latency"; Extended Data Fig. 5 legend. No passage gives the rule.
dandi:000010.why: With the first spike within 10 ms of the first pulse of a pair, PT units give a mean latency of 2.68 ms and IT units 5.11 ms, but the s.d. (0.64 and 0.96 ms) includes spontaneous spikes and is far from 0.1 and 0.2 ms; a narrower rule would change both. The claim is blocked as methods_underspecified until answered.
dandi:000010.answer: The paper gives no rule for telling antidromic from spontaneous spikes. What bears on it is the pulse pairs 10 ms apart, the smaller IT jitter to the second pulse "following a conditioning stimulus" (Extended Data Fig. 5g), which suggests the reported jitter is to the first pulse, and the Results' "sub-millisecond temporal jitter (mean, 0.15 ms)". Written into the criterion of antidromic-latencies as readings (w) the first spike in a window after the first pulse of each pair, window open (about 10 ms for the activated neurons' 8.3 and 9.8 ms latencies); (c) as (w) without pulses preceded shortly by a spontaneous spike; (r) as (w) with only spikes in the evoked peak of the latency histogram. Jitter is the s.d. over the pulses kept, per neuron, averaged over neurons.

dandi:000011.claim: selective-fraction, ed4-return-to-trajectory, fig1f-spike-rate-recovery, fig1g-selectivity-recovery, ed2b-silencing-strength, ed2e-no-rebound, fig2-recordings-recovery, fig2e-selectivity-recovery-times, ed7-larger-photoinhibition, ed7e-roc-larger-photoinhibition and the claims on convention A
dandi:000011.question: Do lick-early trials enter the neural analyses (selectivity tests, rate-change tests, selectivity time courses, activity space)? In the files they are 18% of behaving trials; in them the delay restarts after the early lick, so the go cue comes later than in other trials, and the photostimulus event is logged at the restarted delay, up to 1.6 s after the light in the laser trace.
dandi:000011.passage: Methods, Behavioral data analysis, "Performance was computed as the fraction of correct reports, excluding 'lick early' trials" (for behaviour only); Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis, "We therefore used all trials (correct and incorrect) to compute selectivity when quantifying selectivity changes caused by photoinhibition". No passage says whether lick-early trials enter the neural analyses.
dandi:000011.why: Counts and times move with it; for example the early-delay recovery time of fig1g is 250 to 550 ms with lick-early trials dropped and 650 to 1400 ms with them kept, and with the units of the unlabelled sessions added the selective-fraction counts are all within tolerance only when they are dropped. Both readings are run.
dandi:000011.answer: The paper does not give it, and links no code. The Methods exclude lick early trials from performance only ("Performance was computed as the fraction of correct reports, excluding “lick early” trials"); the electrophysiology Methods and the legends say nothing on them. The claims file now names readings K1 (dropped) and K2 (kept) as convention K, and the criteria of the claims named require their outcome under both, else methods_underspecified.

dandi:000011.question: Convention D determines each neuron's preferred trial type from 10 trials. From the spike counts of which window, the whole trial (sample onset to the end of the response epoch), the delay epoch, or each time bin separately?
dandi:000011.passage: Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis, "we first determined each neuron's preferred trial type using spike counts from a subset of the trials (10 trials), selectivity is calculated as the spike rate difference between the trial types on the remaining data."
dandi:000011.why: The sign of a weakly selective neuron's selectivity, and so the population selectivity and the recovery times, depend on the window. The whole trial and the delay epoch are run; with lick-early trials kept, fig1g holds with one and not with the other.
dandi:000011.answer: The paper does not give it. The Methods say only "we first determined each neuron's preferred trial type using spike counts from a subset of the trials (10 trials)", with no window, and no legend adds one. Convention D now names readings D1 (whole trial), D2 (delay epoch) and D3 (each bin); the outcome is the one all give.

dandi:000011.question: "Selective neurons tested for >3 trials in all conditions": more than 3 trials in each condition, or in each condition and trial type (lick left, lick right)? Either way, 138 to 173 neurons pass in experiment 1 (paper 55), 221 to 293 in experiment 2 (paper 143) and 58 to 62 in experiment 3 (paper 40). Is there a further selection behind the legend counts?
dandi:000011.passage: Figure 1g legend, "selective neurons tested for >3 trials in all conditions, n=55"; Figure 2e legend, "n=143"; Extended Data Fig. 7d, "n=40".
dandi:000011.why: The included population sets the recovery times. The claims file's words (per condition) decide the outcomes here; per condition and trial type is shown as a variant.
dandi:000011.answer: The paper does not give it. The legends say "selective neurons tested for >3 trials in all conditions" (Fig. 1g, Extended Data Figs 5f, 7d) and Fig. 2e says only "Same as Fig. 1g"; no further selection behind 55, 143 or 40 is stated. Per condition, the legend's words, decides (N1); per condition and trial type is a variant (N2), as convention D now says.

dandi:000011.question: Which time is a selectivity bin given when the recovery time is read, its centre or its end? And how far after the offset does the search for the first bin above 80% of control run (to the go cue, or into the response epoch)?
dandi:000011.passage: Methods, "we looked for the first time bin when selectivity on photoinhibition trials reached 80 % of the control selectivity"; the late-delay recovery of Fig. 1g (327 ms after an offset 0.3 s before the go cue) falls after the go cue, so the search here runs to the end of the windows (1.6 s after the go cue).
dandi:000011.why: The two labels differ by half the bin (100 or 200 ms). For ed7 the ipsilateral four-spot time is within tolerance with centre labels and outside it with end labels.
dandi:000011.answer: The paper does not give either. The Methods say "we looked for the first time bin when selectivity on photoinhibition trials reached 80 % of the control selectivity", with no bin label and no end of the search; Extended Data Fig. 7d says "no recovery at end of delay period" for the bilateral case. Convention D now names L1 (centre) and L2 (end), E1 (to the end of the delay) and E2 (into the response epoch); the outcome is the one all give.

dandi:000011.claim: cd-stable-over-epochs, cd-captures-selectivity, fig3c-cd-recovery-roc, ed8-roc-during-photoinhibition, fig3c-cd-predicts-movement, fig3d-persistent-mode, fig3e-ramping-mode, fig4-bilateral-cd-predicts-movement, ed6b-session-bias-predicted, ed9c-cd-window-robust
dandi:000011.question: Convention A's rule (more than 5 neurons recorded simultaneously for more than 5 trials per condition) selects 24 of the 26 experiment-2 sessions here, with 6 to 37 putative pyramidal neurons (19 to 23 sessions when trials are counted per trial type), against the paper's 16 sessions with 6 to 20 neurons (mean 11). Which neurons and sessions did the paper use (only selective neurons, only neurons recorded over the whole session, a cap on the number of neurons)?
dandi:000011.passage: Results, "6-20 neurons recorded simultaneously; average, 11 neurons; 16 sessions"; Methods, "with > 5 neurons recorded simultaneously for > 5 trials per condition (16/38 sessions)".
dandi:000011.why: The ROC values depend on the neurons projected; the control ROC here is 0.65 to 0.68 against the paper's 0.76. The claims file's rule is followed.
dandi:000011.answer: The paper gives no selection beyond the Methods' rule, "with > 5 neurons recorded simultaneously for > 5 trials per condition (16/38 sessions)", and its outcome in the Results, "6-20 neurons recorded simultaneously; average, 11 neurons; 16 sessions" (the Extended Data Fig. 6b sessions have 20, 16, 18, 10, 12 neurons). No restriction to selective neurons, to neurons held over the session, or cap is stated. Convention A now says the rule is followed as written (T1, per condition), T2 is a variant, and the counts are reported against the paper's.

dandi:000011.question: Is the selection test (end against beginning of the delay, 400 ms windows) paired over trials or unpaired? What bin is the normalised rate time course, whose RMS is taken, computed in?
dandi:000011.passage: Extended Data Fig. 4b, "significant spike rate decrease at the end of the delay epoch compared to the beginning of the delay epoch (p < 0.05, two-tailed t-test; 400 ms windows; pooled across trial types)"; Fig. 1e, "PSTH, averaged over 200 ms".
dandi:000011.why: The selection gives 47 to 67 neurons here (paper 27). Both tests and 200 ms and 400 ms bins are run; none of them makes the time-matched RMS smaller.
dandi:000011.answer: The paper does not give either. Extended Data Fig. 4b says "p < 0.05, two-tailed t-test; 400 ms windows; pooled across trial types" without saying paired, and gives no bin for the normalised rate ("The spike rate for each neuron was normalized to the mean spike rate"). The criterion now names s1 (paired) and s2 (unpaired), t1 (200 ms) and t2 (400 ms), and requires the outcome under all.

dandi:000011.question: The criterion counts sessions whose bias is significant by Fisher's exact test, without saying which 2 x 2 table. Is it, on bilateral trials, trial type by correct, or licked side by condition (control against bilateral)?
dandi:000011.passage: Extended Data Fig. 6a, "Behavioral performance on control and bilateral photoinhibition trials"; no test is given.
dandi:000011.why: The number of significant sessions differs (12 or 13). Both are run and both reproduce.
dandi:000011.answer: The paper does not give it. Extended Data Fig. 6a shows "Behavioral performance on control and bilateral photoinhibition trials" with no test; the Fisher's exact test is itself a reading of the claims file. The criterion now names f1 (trial type by correct, bilateral trials) and f2 (licked side by condition) and requires the outcome under both.

dandi:000011.question: (1) Are the ipsilateral trials that build modes 2 and 3 split like the control trials, so that projections use other ipsilateral trials? (2) Which trials give the trial-averaged activity whose captured selectivity and variance are reported (the training trials, or all correct control trials)? (3) The sign of the ramping mode (an SVD eigenvector) is arbitrary; how is it oriented before judging that it rises over the delay?
dandi:000011.passage: Methods, "The modes were computed using a subset of control trials (correct trials only) and ipsilateral perturbation trials. The projections in the figures are for independent control trials and perturbation trials."
dandi:000011.why: Without a rule for the sign, "rises" cannot be judged; here the mode is oriented to a positive weight sum, and the change over the delay is small with either sign.
dandi:000011.answer: (1) Yes, as far as the text goes. The Methods say "The modes were computed using a subset of control trials (correct trials only) and ipsilateral perturbation trials. The projections in the figures are for independent control trials and perturbation trials", so projected ipsilateral trials are ones not used to build the modes; fig3d and fig3e now say so. (2) Not given; cd-captures-selectivity now names v1 (training trials) and v2 (all correct control trials). (3) Not given; the paper has no rule for the sign of the SVD eigenvector. fig3e now names g1 (positive weight sum) and g2 (oriented so the control projection rises, ramping judged by the size of the delay change against 2 bootstrap s.e.m.), outcome under both.

dandi:000011.question: The files hold no lick times, only `lick_trace` (an analogue signal in 5 s chunks per trial, described as the tongue movement when licking). What rule gives the first lick after the go cue from it (a threshold on the raw signal, or a number of standard deviations above a baseline, and over which window)?
dandi:000011.passage: No passage of the paper gives it.
dandi:000011.why: The reaction time moves with the threshold. The claim is blocked as methods_underspecified until answered.
dandi:000011.answer: The paper does not give it. The Methods say only "A two-spout lickport (4.5 mm between spouts) was used to record answer licks" and define no detection from an analogue signal; no code is linked. The criterion now says the outcome stands only if it is the same over the thresholds tried (fixed thresholds on the raw signal and k standard deviations above a pre-go-cue baseline, over a range), else methods_underspecified.

dandi:000011.question: The modular attractor's noise has variance 0.01. Is it white noise of that intensity (Euler-Maruyama increments of sd sqrt(0.01 dt)/tau), or a sample of variance 0.01 drawn every integration step and integrated like an input? And what is the integration step?
dandi:000011.passage: Methods, Modular attractor, "All neurons received a non-selective tonic input T i (t) with amplitude 0.5 and noise ξ i ( t ) with variance 0.01."
dandi:000011.why: With 1 ms steps, Euler-Maruyama noise overwhelms the 50 ms input, and the network ends at the instructed fixed point in about half of unperturbed trials; with per-step samples it ends there in all of them and the claim's attractor part holds.
dandi:000011.answer: The paper does not give either. The Methods say "ξ i ( t ) is Gaussian random noise" and "noise ξ i ( t ) with variance 0.01", with no integration step and no scaling with step. The criterion now names n1 (Euler-Maruyama white noise) and n2 (a variance 0.01 sample each step, integrated as an input), with steps h1 (1 ms) and h2 (0.1 ms), and requires the outcome under all, else methods_underspecified.

dandi:000011.question: Convention A says that w_t is the lick right minus lick left mean response vector of correct control trials, and that cd (the average of w_t) uses a subset of control trials. Which trials give the w_t whose correlation between late sample and late delay is reported, all correct control trials or the training subset that builds cd (H1, a half, or H2, a third)?
dandi:000011.passage: Methods, Analysis of population dynamics in the activity space, "was stable (correlation of w t 's between late sample epoch vs. late delay epoch, 0.61 ± 0.05; Extended Data Fig. 9b)"; the same paragraph defines w_t on correct trials and builds cd from a subset of the trials.
dandi:000011.why: Raised by the verifier of round 1. With all correct control trials the mean correlation is 0.563 and 0.588 (lick-early trials dropped or kept), inside 0.56 to 0.66; with the training subset it is 0.534 to 0.554, outside. Both are run, and the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified until the answer.

dandi:000011.claim: selective-fraction, ed4-return-to-trajectory, fig1f-spike-rate-recovery, fig1g-selectivity-recovery, ed2b-silencing-strength, ed2e-no-rebound, fig2-recordings-recovery, fig2e-selectivity-recovery-times, ed7-larger-photoinhibition, ed7e-roc-larger-photoinhibition and the claims on convention A
dandi:000011.question: Convention K defines K2 as lick-early trials kept "with events at their logged times". In some lick-early trials the light in the laser trace came before one or more restarts of the delay, so the logged photostimulus event and go cue lie up to 10 s after the light (3% to 16% of the trials of each photoinhibition condition of experiment 1, 6.5% to 7.5% in experiment 2, 1% to 4% in experiment 3). Is K2 meant with the logged events, or with those trials aligned to the light in the trace (or left out)?
dandi:000011.passage: None in the paper; the reading K2 is the claims file's (convention K, answered 2026-10-21).
dandi:000011.why: Raised by the verifier of round 1. Under K2 these trials enter the photoinhibition averages without light in the analysis windows, which raises the silenced rate (ed2b-silencing-strength, PV x ReaChR ipsilateral 0.035 to 0.052 with lick-early trials dropped and 0.139 to 0.140 kept) and may change the outcome of the claims whose readings must agree over K1 and K2.

dandi:000011.question: Convention D names the search end E1, to the end of the delay epoch (the go cue). For the late-delay condition of experiment 1, whose light ends 0.3 s before the go cue, the paper's recovery time of 327 ms falls after the go cue. Is E1 meant for this condition, or should the search for it run past the go cue?
dandi:000011.passage: Figure 1g legend, "late delay, 327±112 ms"; Methods, "we looked for the first time bin when selectivity on photoinhibition trials reached 80 % of the control selectivity".
dandi:000011.why: Raised by the verifier of round 1. Under E1 a recovery time can be at most 300 ms for this condition (inside the tolerance of 215 to 439 ms); with bins labelled by their end no bin up to the go cue reaches 80% of control in any of 96 readings, which makes some combinations with E1 fail. The claim is blocked as methods_underspecified under either answer as the readings stand.

dandi:000011.question: The criteria of these claims test several parts and define no partial outcome. The attempt calls a claim partially reproduced when at least half of the parts of its criterion hold under every reading that must agree, and not reproduced otherwise. Does the claims file adopt this rule, give another, or mean that any failed part makes the claim not reproduced?
dandi:000011.passage: None in the paper; the outcome scale is the protocol's, and these criteria name only the condition for reproduced.
dandi:000011.why: Raised by the verifier of round 2, who accepts the partial outcomes for consistency but notes that the rule was written after round 1 and is not in the claims file. Read strictly, the five claims would be not reproduced (four of five parts hold for unit-classification, three of five for fig2-recordings-recovery, three of four under K1 and two under K2 for ed7e and ed8, two or three of four for fig6).

dandi:000013.question: Where does the search for the touch response cutoff t_on start? Read literally, t_on is the first t_i, counted from t = 1 ms, at which the increment of the smoothed curve falls below the 95th percentile of the surrogates. The degree-11 polynomial dips at the start of a steep curve, so this stops at 1 ms in many cells before the response has risen. The Results describe a transition where the curve levels off, which reads as the first t_i at which the increment, having been above chance, falls below it. Which is meant? The same rule decides t_w for the phase windows (fig3d-touch-phase-l4c2), and the touch window feeds spikes per touch (Table 1, fig5c-modulation-index, l4-outside-weaker-touch).
dandi:000013.passage: Results, paragraph on Figure 3, "At some window size, the curve levels off as the proportion of touch spikes increases no faster than expected for a random spike train at the neuron's mean spike rate. This transition point defines the proportion of touch-coupled spikes." Methods, Spikes accounted by active sensation, "the first time point t_i = t_on in which the rate of increase ... is below chance level of the overall firing rate".
dandi:000013.why: Over the 31 L4 C2 cells the touch-coupled fraction is 66.9 to 75.8% in 14.6 to 17.6% of exploration time under the transition reading and 38.6 to 64.5% in 8.5 to 13.4% under the literal one (paper 70.6 +- 20.9% in 14.9%). The two readings give different outcomes for fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2, fig3c-touch-spikes-l5, the fig3d claims and Table 1.
dandi:000013.answer: The paper means the transition. The Results describe "an initially steep curve" that "levels off" and call "This transition point" the cutoff, the Methods say the curves "rise steeply and then plateau", and the example cell's window is 8 to 40 ms. The literal search from 1 ms, which stops in a dip of the polynomial before the rise, does not fit that description. Written into the criteria of fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2 and fig3d-touch-phase-l4c2 (for t_w) as the first t_i at which the increment, having been above chance, falls below it; the literal reading is a variant only. The statement and expected values are unchanged.

dandi:000013.question: Over what range of window sizes t_i is the curve y_ton(t_i) built and fitted with the degree-11 polynomial (the longest window searched)? The fit, and so the cutoff, depend on it. The attempt runs 0 to 100 ms (the limit for prolonged touches) and 0 to 200 ms.
dandi:000013.passage: Methods, Spikes accounted by active sensation, "The derivative was calculated from these curves smoothed with a polynomial fit (degree 11)." No passage gives the range.
dandi:000013.why: For L4 C2 under the transition reading, the fraction of exploration time in touch windows is 14.6 to 16.3% with 100 ms and 16.0 to 17.6% with 200 ms; the tolerance is 13.4 to 16.4%.
dandi:000013.answer: The paper does not give it. The Methods say only "The derivative was calculated from these curves smoothed with a polynomial fit (degree 11)", and Figure 3C, whose axis might show it, was not supplied as an image. Written into the criterion of fig3c-touch-spikes-l4c2 as open detail (4), readings (r100) 0 to 100 ms and (r200) 0 to 200 ms, both run.

dandi:000013.question: Under reading (1a), non-touch epochs taken from the 30 ms before touch in the same responses, which 10 ms integration window is the non-touch sample, the one ending at onset (-10 to 0 ms), the earliest (-30 to -20 ms), or all pre-touch windows? And is the fraction of touches detected (reading 2a) taken with the threshold that maximises percent correct?
dandi:000013.passage: Methods, Population decoding, "At each time point t_j we built a different decoder that was trained to discriminate between the pooled population response at t_j and the population response at epochs without touch".
dandi:000013.why: The population size that first detects 95% of touches is 1 or 2 neurons under (2a) with either pre-touch window, 18 or 30 under (2b), and 11 with exploration windows; the paper gives 15.
dandi:000013.answer: Neither is given. The Methods say only "the population response at epochs without touch" and "We used half of the data to find the optimal threshold", without defining "optimal". Written into the criterion of fig4a-touch-detection-c2 as readings (a1) the window ending at onset, (a2) -30 to -20 ms and (a3) all pre-touch windows under (1a); the threshold stays the one maximising percent correct, the only reading of "optimal" the paper supports.

dandi:000013.question: Which times does the naive Bayes decoder choose among, every 1 ms over the whole -30 to +50 ms response, or only after touch onset? And what smoothing of zero counts was used?
dandi:000013.passage: Methods, Population decoding, "We trained a multinomial naive Bayes classifier ... to report for every time point what was the most likely time elapsed from touch onset".
dandi:000013.why: The minimum RMS error near 10 ms is 1.31 to 1.40 ms with classes from -21 ms and 1.09 to 1.12 ms with classes from 0 ms; the paper gives 0.55 ms. No reading tried reaches it, but the class set moves the value by 0.3 ms.
dandi:000013.answer: Neither is given. The Methods say "for every time point what was the most likely time elapsed from touch onset" and the Results "integrating in 10 ms windows after touch"; no smoothing is named. Written into the criterion of fig4b-touch-time-precision as readings (c-all) every 1 ms over the sampled response and (c-post) from onset on, both run, with add-one smoothing and a smaller pseudocount as a variant.

dandi:000013.question: For the phase decoder, which whisk cycles are used (all complete cycles with peak amplitude above 2.5 deg, or only those of exploration without touch, as for the phase tuning), what is the response to a phase (the count in one 3 deg bin of one cycle, or a rate), and how are bins with no spikes handled in the naive Bayes likelihood?
dandi:000013.passage: Methods, Population decoding, "For each neuron we aligned the spikes to the whisking phase of each whisking cycle (minimum peak whisking amplitude >2.5 deg) and binned the response in 120 bins between pi and -pi."
dandi:000013.why: With counts of single cycles the decoder does not reach 76% correct in most runs; with Poisson rates it reaches it at 58.6 to 60.0 deg in C2; the paper gives 24 deg.
dandi:000013.answer: The cycles are given, the rest is not. The Methods' Whisker analysis defines whisking cycles for the whole paper outside touch epochs, with "Whisking cycles during licking or within 70 ms after touch were excluded" and "Whisking epochs used for phase analysis had monotonic phase for a complete whisking cycle", so the decoder uses the same cycles as phase tuning. Whether the response is a single-cycle count or a rate, and how empty bins are handled, is not said. Written into the criterion of fig4c-phase-decoding, with readings (1a) and (1b) kept and add-one smoothing or a floor rate for empty bins.

dandi:000013.question: Was the rate of the refractory Poisson model raised to make up for the spikes the refractory period removes, so that the model's mean count matches the data, or was the cell's PSTH used as the rate directly?
dandi:000013.passage: Methods, Analysis of spike count variance, "We also computed FFs using a Poisson process with absolute refractory period, with average touch response matched to the data".
dandi:000013.why: Without compensation the model's mean count is lower than the data's, which raises its FF towards 1 less than the data; the comparison of data and model FF is within the sum of their s.e.m. under reading (2a) and significant under (2b), so a matched mean could move it.
dandi:000013.answer: The rate was compensated. The Methods say "a Poisson process with absolute refractory period, with average touch response matched to the data (Berry II and Meister, 1998)", so the model's output PSTH, not its input rate, matches the cell's. The criterion of fig6d-not-refractory said the rate equals the PSTH, which misreads the Methods; it now raises the rate (the free rate of Berry and Meister, or adjusted until the simulated PSTH matches), with the uncompensated model a variant only. The statement is unchanged.

dandi:000013.question: Does "with the median whisking rate higher" in the criterion mean the median of the per-cell differences (whisking minus non-whisking) is positive, or that the median of the whisking rates is above the median of the non-whisking rates?
dandi:000013.passage: Results, paragraph 6, "whereas L5 showed a modest, but significant increase with whisking (p = 0.019, Wilcoxon signed rank)".
dandi:000013.why: The signed-rank test gives p = 0.024 and 0.014, 9 and 10 of 11 cells fire more when whisking and the median difference is +1.8 spikes/s, but the median whisking rate (11.0 spikes/s) is below the median non-whisking rate (12.9).
dandi:000013.answer: The median of the per-cell differences. The paper's test is paired, "a modest, but significant increase with whisking (p = 0.019, Wilcoxon signed rank)", so the increase is the sign of the paired differences. Table 1 also gives group medians for L5 of 12.8 (non-whisking) and 13.5 spikes/s (whisking), but they are not the measure. Written into the criterion of whisking-rate-l5-increase.
