dandi:000015.question: The tagged units of Li et al. (2015) are on DANDI (dandiset 000010, 45 PT and 27 IT, see li2015-tagged-units-link). How is the onset test of fig8d-pt-earlier-than-it to be applied to them? (1) The spike counts for the 3-way ANOVA, the paper's own 400 ms windows in 100 ms steps or another bin. (2) Which trials, given that the sessions of dandiset 000010 contain photostimulation trials and that its early-lick column is separate from its outcome column; and which event is trial start, as the task timing of Li et al. (2015) differs from this paper's. (3) The window and the baseline of convention O for those trials. (4) Whether the units of all sessions are pooled, and whether the bootstrap is over units only, as the criterion says, or hierarchical.
dandi:000015.passage: Spiking data were subjected to the same analyses as imaging data to obtain a(t), b(t), and g(t) using spike counts within 400 ms windows (in 100 ms steps). (STAR Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis). The Discussion gives the cell counts (PT/IT cells; electrophysiology, 45/27) but no method for the Li et al. data.
dandi:000015.why: The onset is the first bin over 6 baseline SD of mean |beta|; with 45 and 27 units it depends on the bin width, on the baseline period and on which trials enter the ANOVA, and including photostimulation trials would change the selectivity itself. The claim is blocked as methods_underspecified until this is answered.
dandi:000015.answer: The paper does not say. It gives no method for the Li et al. (2015) units; the Discussion gives only the counts "(PT/IT cells; electrophysiology, 45/27; imaging, 719/2,631)", and for its own probe units the Methods say "Spiking data were subjected to the same analyses as imaging data to obtain a(t), b(t), and g(t) using spike counts within 400 ms windows (in 100 ms steps)". Trial start is "the pole movement onset" ("At the beginning of each trial, the vertical pole moved into the plane"). The criterion of ephys-pt-it-onset-not-detected now names the readings: (1) 400 ms windows in 100 ms steps; (2) the four trial types without photostimulation, early-lick trials excluded by the early-lick record, time from pole movement onset; (3) onset from trial start to the go cue with baselines O1 (windows wholly before trial start) and O2 (windows within 0.5 s before it), rules S1 and S2; (4) units of all sessions pooled, bootstrap over units (H2) and hierarchical (H1). The outcome rule is now reproduced when no combination finds PT earlier at p < 0.01, partially reproduced when some do. Statement unchanged.

dandi:000015.question: After neuropil subtraction (F = F_roi - 0.7 F_neuropil) the baseline F0 of a trial is zero or negative for 0.26% of ROI-trials, in 1,262 of 15,431 ROIs, and dF/F = (F - F0)/F0 then reaches thousands. Does the paper say how such trials or ROIs are handled (left out, F0 floored, ROIs excluded), or is dF/F used as computed? The same applies to every claim built on dF/F, notably figs4-peak-shift and the mean coefficients of fig8d-pt-contra-bias, fig8d-mm-posterior-preferring and fig8d-error-outnumber-correct.
dandi:000015.passage: DF/F was computed for each trial as (F-F0)/F0, where F0 is the baseline fluorescence averaged over a 0.5 s period immediately before the start of each trial. (STAR Methods, Image analysis)
dandi:000015.why: dF/F is used as computed here. Without the ROIs that have F0 <= 0 on any trial, MM under rule R2, window W1, bins T1 goes from 1,755 (26.6%) to 1,675 of 5,854 (28.6%) selective, and the MM mean dF/F of figs4-peak-shift changes shape (its peak moves from 6.09 to 4.80 s); neither change alters an outcome here, but the means of the bootstrap claims are near their 2 SD bounds.
dandi:000015.answer: The paper does not say. The Methods give only "DF/F was computed for each trial as (F-F0)/F0, where F0 is the baseline fluorescence averaged over a 0.5 s period immediately before the start of each trial", with no exception for F0 <= 0 and no exclusion of ROIs or trials on that ground. Convention T now names (V1) dF/F as computed, the Methods' formula, which decides, and (V2) ROIs with F0 <= 0 on any trial left out, reported as a check; fraction-selective-alm-mm, figs4-peak-shift, fig8d-pt-contra-bias, fig8d-mm-posterior-preferring and fig8d-error-outnumber-correct cite it. Claims and expected values unchanged.

dandi:000015.question: Is the onset the first single bin in which mean |beta| exceeds the baseline by more than 6 SD, or must it stay above that level (for how long)? And is "above baseline" measured from the baseline mean?
dandi:000015.passage: delta onset time; time when selectivity rose to >6 SD above baseline = 1.4 ± 0.6 s; p < 0.01, bootstrap (Results, Projection-Specific Coding)
dandi:000015.why: With the first single bin the IT minus PT difference is 0.2 s (baseline O1) and in one combination negative, with bootstrap SDs of 1.3 to 1.9 s, so single crossings driven by noise may decide the onset; a sustained rule could give a different difference.
dandi:000015.answer: The paper does not say. It gives only "time when selectivity rose to >6 SD above baseline" (Results, Projection-Specific Coding), and the Methods and the Figure 8D legend add nothing on the onset. "Above baseline" is read as above the baseline mean, the plain reading, as the paper defines no other. Convention O now names (S1) the first bin above the baseline mean plus 6 SD and (S2) the first bin from which the measure stays above it up to the go cue, with the onset found again in each bootstrap resample; fig8d-pt-earlier-than-it cites both. Expected values unchanged.

dandi:000015.question: The criterion requires the ALM mean "above its sample-epoch level at the end of the delay". Is the sample-epoch level the mean over the sample epoch or its maximum, and is the end of the delay the last bin before the go cue or a window before it?
dandi:000015.passage: the peak of activity shifted from MM to ALM over the course of the delay epoch (Figure S4) (Results, Mapping Activity Using Two-Photon Calcium Imaging, paragraph 3)
dandi:000015.why: Both readings (mean and maximum, last bin) are run here and agree; the outcome is decided by the peak times, so the answer cannot change it in this attempt but fixes the measure for later ones.
dandi:000015.answer: The paper does not say. The main text has only "the peak of activity shifted from MM to ALM over the course of the delay epoch (Figure S4)", and Figure S4 is not in the text read. The criterion now names (L1) the mean and (L2) the maximum over the sample-epoch bins, and (E1) the last bin before the go cue and (E2) the mean over the last 0.5 s before it; reproduced under one combination, all reported.

dandi:000015.question: In part (c), is the MM fraction's "value in the delay epoch" its mean over the delay bins or its maximum there?
dandi:000015.passage: Lickdirection selectivity, including number of neurons and the strength of coding, continued to increase and spread across ALM layers and to a minor extent into MM (Figure S7), reaching a maximum after the go cue (Results, Spatial Map of Behavior-Related Activity, paragraph 1)
dandi:000015.why: Both readings are run here and agree; the answer fixes the measure for later attempts.
dandi:000015.answer: The paper does not say. The text has only "continued to increase and spread across ALM layers and to a minor extent into MM (Figure S7), reaching a maximum after the go cue", and Figure S7 is not in the text read. Part (c) now reads both the mean over the delay bins and the maximum there, and holds when it holds under one.

dandi:000015.question: The criterion takes the "peak time" of the mean dF/F of ALM and of MM per bin. Over what window is the peak taken, the whole extracted window of convention T (5 s before to 5 s after the go cue), the bins before the go cue, or the delay epoch only?
dandi:000015.passage: the peak of activity shifted from MM to ALM over the course of the delay epoch (Figure S4) (Results, Mapping Activity Using Two-Photon Calcium Imaging, paragraph 3)
dandi:000015.why: Over the whole window the MM mean peaks in the response epoch, after ALM (6.09 against 4.52 s, T1, V1), and the claim is not reproduced. Before the go cue MM peaks first under every bin and dF/F reading (V1 2.08 against 4.16 s with T1 bins, 0.80 against 4.14 s with T2), and the claim would be reproduced. The first verifier noted that the criterion does not set the window. The whole window is used until the answer.

dandi:000019.question: Before the PCA, is each electrode's high gamma z-scored over its whole concatenated (CV x time) series (`row`), or across syllables separately at each time point (`time`)? The second removes the mean time course shared by all syllables. Is the same z-scored input projected onto the PCs to give the state K(s, t)?
dandi:000019.passage: Methods, PCA and Cortical-State Space, "Each electrode's time series was z-scored across syllables to normalize response variability across electrodes."
dandi:000019.why: With `row` the nine PCs explain 0.60 to 0.64 of the variance (within 0.6 +- 0.06), with `time` 0.49 to 0.55 (mostly outside). Consonant-vowel distances exceed consonant-consonant distances under `row` and not under `time` (suppfig13), and the hierarchy and late feature-correlation results also change. The attempt runs both, and these claims are blocked as methods_underspecified where they differ.
dandi:000019.answer: The paper does not say. The Methods have only "Each electrode's time series was z-scored across syllables to normalize response variability across electrodes"; "time series" in the singular fits the row reading and "across syllables" fits the time reading, and no other passage or code settles it (the paper links no code). Nor does it say that the z-scored input is projected; Eq. 5 writes "K ( s k , t ) = M · H γ k ( t )", with Hγ the baseline z-scored measure. The header's state-space definition now names (row) and (time) for the z-scoring and (i) the PCA input or (ii) Hγ as Eq. 5 writes it for the projection; all are run. Claims and expected values unchanged.

dandi:000019.question: The dandiset has CVs with fewer than 15 renditions (EC2 /thi/ 10, GP31 /thi/ 2) and GP31 lacks /tha/ and /thu/. Should CVs with fewer than 15 renditions be left out of the per-syllable averages, as the paper's range of 15 to 100 renditions suggests, or kept?

dandi:000023.question: The criterion says the bins that make up deep L3 are not stated. dandi:000023.question: The `where` of the claim names the NeuN section measurements and Code6 and Code7. dandi:000023.question: The criteria of fig5b-frem3-morph-depth and fig6-deep-morph-anova say only "Not tested on the dandiset". dandi:000045.passage: Appendix 1, table 1d, "For each of the last three sessions ... >80%/90% correct on 100% contrast and all contrasts introduced". The Methods and the claims file do not say more.
dandi:000045.why: P1 is reached by 75 mice when each session must present all contrasts and by 84 when the three together must (1a criteria; 52 and 58 with 1a/1b). The Kaplan-Meier proportion at day 40 is 0.67 under the first reading and 0.76 under the second, so fig2h-proportion-learned-40-days is blocked until this is answered; the other claims listed have the same outcome under both.
dandi:000045.answer: Each of the three sessions, as the main reading. Appendix 1, table 1d, puts the criterion under "For each of the last three sessions: >200/400 trials completed, and >80%/90% correct on 100% contrast and all contrasts introduced". The code that set the paper's status (SessionTrainingStatus in IBL-pipeline, which the paper's code imports) checks only the current session, for 0% and a contrast between 0.1 and 6.5% ("training in progress if the current session does not have low contrasts"); that is a variant. Pooling the three sessions is given by neither. Header P1 and the criterion of fig2h-proportion-learned-40-days now say so; claims and expected values unchanged.

dandi:000045.question: The claims file's second P1 reading applies "the 1b criteria from their introduction (Methods, September 2019, no day given)". From which day are the 1b criteria applied, and do they replace the 1a criteria for a mouse still in training on that day (as run here), or is a mouse proficient when it meets either?
dandi:000045.passage: Methods, "The second set, called '1b', was introduced shortly afterwards (September 2019) and was applied to 60 of the 140 mice."
dandi:000045.why: With 1b from 2019-09-01, 52 and 58 mice reach P1 under the two contrast readings; with 2019-09-30, 60 and 66. Under the 1a/1b readings with pooled contrasts, easy-trial performance differs across labs (corrected p = 0.047), so the outcome of fig3cde-no-lab-difference-medians depends on this reading.
dandi:000045.answer: The code settles it: a mouse is proficient at the first session that meets either set, at any date. The paper's P1 is the first status trained_1a or trained_1b, and SessionTrainingStatus tests the 1b criteria and then the 1a criteria at every session, with no date. The 1b criteria were implemented on 2019-09-12 (text_trained1a_to_1b_sessions.py, "Date at which trained_1b was implemented in DJ pipeline"); the Methods say only "September 2019" and do not say 1b replaced 1a, so replacement from 2019-09-12 is a variant. Header P1 and the criterion of cohort-counts now say so; claims unchanged.

dandi:000045.question: The 1a/1b criteria require more than 200/400 "trials completed" in each session. Are these all trials, or only trials with a response (no-response trials, choice 0, left out)? The attempt counts all trials.
dandi:000045.passage: Appendix 1, table 1d, ">200/400 trials completed"; Methods, "200/400 completed trials".
dandi:000045.why: Counting only trials with a response changes P1 for 1 to 3 mice under the four readings; no outcome is expected to change, but the counts move.
dandi:000045.answer: All trials, no-response trials included. The paper does not define "completed"; the status code compares the session's n_trials with 200/400, and the pipeline sets n_trials = len(trials['choice']), every trial of the session. Header P1 and the criterion of cohort-counts now say so.

dandi:000045.question: The claims file defines P1b as "the code's 'biased' criterion, the first biased-protocol session with status trained_1b". The dataset has no status. Is P1b, without it, the first full-task (biased protocol) session on or after P1 (as run here), or the first full-task session at which the recomputed status is 1b, which under the 1a reading may never come?
dandi:000045.passage: Figure 3, figure supplement 5 legend, "the first three sessions of the full task"; Methods, "Once an animal was proficient in the basic task, it proceeded to the full task."
dandi:000045.why: The window of every claim listed is counted from P1b. Under the reading run here, 51 to 71 mice have a P1b; under the 1b-status reading, fewer would, and the first-session windows would move.
dandi:000045.answer: The legend's reading, the first full-task session on or after P1, is the main one; the legend says "the first three sessions of the full task" and the Methods "Once an animal was proficient in the basic task, it proceeded to the full task". The code's "biased" criterion ('task_protocol LIKE "%biased%" AND training_status="trained_1b"') is a variant; in the pipeline a 1a-only mouse keeps trained_1a on biased sessions until its last three sessions meet the 1b criteria, and has no P1b if they never do. Header P1b and the criterion of fig3s5-first-full-sessions now say so; claims unchanged.

dandi:000045.question: The criteria use "50:50 sessions". In this dataset, every basic-task session has trials whose probabilityLeft is not 0.5 (0 to 1 in steps of 0.1, 24% of basic-task trials, with the stimulus side following it), apparently from the bias-correcting repeat trials. Are 50:50 sessions the basic-task sessions (as run here), or only sessions in which every trial has probabilityLeft 0.5 (none here)?
dandi:000045.passage: Results, Training progression, "a basic task ... where the probability of a stimulus appearing on the left or the right was equal (50:50)"; Methods, "If the response was incorrect and the contrast was 'easy' (>=50%), a 'repeat' trial followed".
dandi:000045.why: Under the second reading no session qualifies and the claims cannot be tested.
dandi:000045.answer: The basic-task sessions, with all their trials, as run. The Results define the basic task as the one where left and right were "equal (50:50)"; the pipeline's per-day summary gives prob_left 0.5 to all trials of a training-protocol day ("0.5 for trainingChoiceWorld") and never reads the trial's probability, and the code's prob_left == 0.5 selects those days. Header and the criterion of fig2bc-threshold-bias-iqr now say so.

dandi:000045.question: The classifier draws 8 mice from each laboratory. In this dataset some laboratories hold fewer than 8 proficient mice under every reading (Lab 7 has only 7 mice with their whole training in the dataset). The Methods say 8 was "the lowest number of mice over all different datasets". May the subsample be the smallest laboratory's count here (6 or 7), or is the claim blocked?
dandi:000045.passage: Methods, Classification of laboratory membership, "The size of the subsample was chosen because eight mice was the lowest number of mice over all different datasets for which classification was performed."
dandi:000045.why: The four classifier claims are blocked (other); with 6 mice per lab the Naive Bayes classifier on the basic task is not above chance (2.5th percentile 0.071 against a null mean of 0.113), shown as a variant that decides nothing. fig3s4 and fig3s5 are decided by their lab tests without the classifier.
dandi:000045.answer: The subsample may be the smallest count. The Methods give the size as a rule, "eight mice was the lowest number of mice over all different datasets for which classification was performed", and the code hard-codes N_MICE = 8, the rule's value on the paper's data. Here the rule gives the lowest lab count over all the datasets classified, one size for every classifier claim; that is the main reading, and 8 (blocked) the code's. Header, Lab classifier, and the criterion of fig3f-classifier-chance-basic now say so.

dandi:000045.question: Under the Methods' reading with 50% contrast in the model, most mice were not shown 50% contrast in the sessions used (it is dropped late in basic training and absent from the full task), so their 50% indicator is all zero and the model cannot be fitted. Is that weight left out for those mice (as run here), or is the Methods' reading the code's (50% trials dropped)?
dandi:000045.passage: Methods, Probabilistic choice model, "W c is the coefficient associated with the contrast c in {6.25, 12.5, 25, 50, 100}".
dandi:000045.why: Leaving the weight out changes the other weights by at most 0.002 in the means shown, and the outcomes are the same with and without 50% trials.
dandi:000045.answer: The paper does not say. Equation 3 has W c for "c in {6.25, 12.5, 25, 50, 100}" and does not say what is done for a mouse shown no 50% trials. The code drops 50% trials for every mouse ("drop trials with contrast-level 50, only rarely present (should not be its own regressor)", figure5_GLM_modelfit.py). Readings named in the criterion of fig5cf-glm-weights, (a) W50 left out for those mice, as run, and (b) the code's; claims unchanged.

dandi:000061.question: O1 lists three lap readings, and the criteria say the notebook runs every one. The dandiset holds no lap intervals (its `trials` table, in the Rat08 and Rat09 files only, holds intervals of 3 to 5 s, partly outside the run) and no position, so readings a and b cannot be run and only reading c (laps between consecutive rewards at opposite ends) can. Is a claim judged on reading c alone, or is it blocked when the other readings cannot be run?
dandi:000061.passage: Online Methods, "a habituation index was calculated for each training session and animal as the total number of back-and-forth laps divided by the total time spent on the maze x 100"; ClassifyLaps.m defines laps from position in a hand-picked 150-cm window.
dandi:000061.why: Under reading c the habituation index rises with training day under every lap count and both readings of "gradually diminished" (pooled p = 0.011 to 0.046), so the attempt records habituation-over-days as reproduced on reading c alone. If readings a and b are required, the claim is blocked as data_missing. The other claims listed are blocked for missing cell types and are not affected.
dandi:000061.answer: Judged on reading c alone. The paper counts "back-and-forth laps" on a track where rats "run back and forth on a linear track for water rewards" (Online Methods, habituation index; Recordings and behavior), so a lap is a run between the two reward ends, which reading c counts from the reward times. Reading a exists only where the dataset holds lap intervals and reading b only where it holds position; neither is a separate measure the paper reports. The hand-picked 150-cm window of ClassifyLaps.m is not given anywhere, so no reading reproduces it exactly. O1 and the habituation-over-days criterion now say that a claim is judged on the O1 readings the dataset allows, reading c alone when a and b cannot be formed, recorded as a deviation.

dandi:000061.question: O4 gives reading a (the monosynaptically identified cells where the dataset marks them) and reading b (all putative cells of each type). Five of the 33 files with units have a `cell_type` column (excitatory, inhibitory, unclassified), read as the identified cells, and no file has the putative types. Is the claim judged on reading a alone, with 152 excitatory and 36 inhibitory BLA units of one rat, or blocked because reading b cannot be run?
dandi:000061.passage: Fig. 2c legend, "monosynaptically identified pyramidal cells; n = 675" and "monosynaptically identified interneurons, n = 175".
dandi:000061.why: The legend's cells are the identified ones, which favours reading a. On it bla-pyr-sleep-firing-increase is reproduced and bla-int-sleep-firing is not reproduced (REM/wake p = 0.020); if reading b is required both are blocked as metadata_insufficient.
dandi:000061.answer: Judged on reading a alone. The Fig. 2c legend gives the cells as "monosynaptically identified pyramidal cells; n = 675" and "monosynaptically identified interneurons, n = 175", and the Online Methods separate these from "the remaining, unidentified cells" typed by k-means, which matches a marking of excitatory, inhibitory and unclassified. Reading b is not the legend's set, so it is shown as a variant where it can be formed and is not needed. O4 now says so. The paper's cells come from all rats; one rat's 152 and 36 cells is a smaller sample, which the notes should state, but the claims carry no expected cell counts.

dandi:000061.question: Each of these claims has a test with all cells as well as one with pyramidal cells, and each lists in depends_on a claim that needs putative pyramidal cells (hpc-bla-reactivation-post-sleep, aversive-direction-stronger, bla-ripple-up-subgroup), which the dandiset cannot give. Under the protocol a claim that depends on a blocked claim is blocked. Do these claims need the dependency for their all-cell tests (for example, for the sessions or the ripple-modulated cells), or could their all-cell parts be judged on their own, at most as a partial outcome?
dandi:000061.passage: M7, "A session enters with at least 6 hippocampal and 6 BLA cells of the type used"; M6 is defined for every BLA unit.
dandi:000061.why: The attempt blocks all three and shows the all-cell tests as descriptions. With all cells, reactivation-peaks-at-ripples gives post above pre in 11 of 15 sessions (one-tailed p = 0.0042), direction-all-cell-pairs matches its statement (air puff p = 0.01, safe p = 0.0043, between p = 0.48), and ripple-modulated-cells-larger-reactivation does not hold (rank sum p = 0.27). If the dependencies are only on method, the first two could be partially reproduced or reproduced.
dandi:000061.answer: The dependencies are on method only, and the all-cell tests can be judged on their own. The paper selects sessions by cell count per type ("a minimum of 1 shank and 6 cells in each structure", Online Methods; M7), which needs no other claim's result, and ripple modulation ("a Poisson test with P < 0.001" on spikes in and outside SPW-Rs, M6) is a per-unit test that uses no cell type. The all-cell n of Supplementary Fig. 11 (27 sessions) and Supplementary Fig. 5b (19 sessions) come from these rules with all cells. The depends_on entries are removed from the three claims. direction-all-cell-pairs has only all-cell tests and is judged in full (laps per O1, as answered above). For reactivation-peaks-at-ripples and ripple-modulated-cells-larger-reactivation the criterion now says that, when the pyramidal test cannot be run, the all-cell test is judged alone; partially reproduced when it holds, not reproduced when it does not.

dandi:000115.question: Which two run sessions of subject 1 (jaq) are "sessions 1 and 3"? The files do not mark them. Numbered in order of recording, they are day 6 epochs 2 and 5, and all eight arms are visited in both; the only jaq session with fewer than eight arms visited is day 6 epoch 4 (session 2 in that order), which fits the Methods' description of the second excluded session. Does the paper number sessions in order of recording, or some other way? The same choice sets the sessions of fig1ef-reward-rate and of every later claim.
dandi:000115.passage: We excluded two sessions (sessions 1 and 3 of subject 1) due to decoding issues; for the first, a much lower fraction of samples was on the same segment (<75%), and for the second, not all arms were visited during the session, so not all positions were decodable. (STAR Methods, Spatial decoding)
dandi:000115.why: The files hold 27 jaq run sessions, so excluding a different pair changes the jaq block count (88 with day 6 epochs 2 and 5 left out, 91 with day 6 epochs 2 and 4, against 89). Both readings were run and give the same outcome here (reproduced), but a later claim that uses jaq's sessions could differ.
dandi:000115.answer: The paper does not say. The Methods name the sessions only as "sessions 1 and 3 of subject 1" and describe them ("a much lower fraction of samples was on the same segment (<75%)", "not all arms were visited during the session"). The code (dfs_ripcontent.m at 1be6a6a) selects sessions with "$gooddecode==1" and has a per-animal "$session" field (for example "$session==27"), both from task records not in the repository, so it does not fix the numbering either. The criterion of fig1d-sessions-blocks now names two readings, (a) the first and third run sessions in order of recording and (b) the two sessions that match the Methods' description; both are run, and (b) decides when they differ.

dandi:000115.question: When the goal changes and the rat's next valid trial is not a visit to the old goal, which trial closes the old block? The claims file gives n + 0.9 for "the final unrewarded visit to the old goal", but not what happens when the first trial after the switch goes to another arm. Two readings were run, (a) only a visit to the old goal closes the block (otherwise the trial is the first search trial of the new block), and (b) the first trial after the switch always closes the old block, as dfa_ripcontent.m shifts `contingency` by one trial. This also applies to fig1ef-reward-rate and every claim that uses task phase.
dandi:000115.passage: "trips.contingency(nonlocktrials) = [1 ctemp(1:end-1)];  % shifted by 1 since the goal change happens on the last trial of the cont" (dfa_ripcontent.m, LorenFrankLab/ Gillespie_Neuron_2021 at 1be6a6a); label_trial_interval.m assigns .9 when "you visit the goal arm but didnt get reward, must be end".
dandi:000115.why: The two readings move one trial between blocks at some switches (montague has 167 or 166 full blocks, against 166). No outcome of this attempt changes, but block lengths, search lengths and the trial sets of the replay claims would.
dandi:000115.answer: The code settles it as reading (b). In label_trial_interval.m the block bounds are "goalbounds = [0; 1+find(diff(valoutersgoals(:,2))~=0); sum(valtrials)]", so each block keeps the first trial whose goal field holds the new goal, and dfa_ripcontent.m does the same with "[1 ctemp(1:end-1)]". That trial is n + 0.9 when it visits the old goal and an error (n + 0.3, 0.5 or 0.8) when it visits another arm; the next trial starts the search. The Methods only say the unrewarded visit to the old goal "are considered correct trials". Written into the opening comment and the criterion of fig1d-sessions-blocks; statement and expected values unchanged.

dandi:000115.question: Which form of the Wilcoxon rank-sum test does the criterion mean for the per-trial comparison of goal and never-goal visits, which are 0 or 1 and so almost all ties? With the normal approximation corrected for ties (as scipy's mannwhitneyu, and Matlab's ranksum for large samples, compute it), roquefort's trial +29 is significant (9 of 39 goal traces against 8 of 170, p = 1.6e-4, below 0.05/80); without the tie correction (scipy's ranksums) it is not (p = 0.074).
dandi:000115.passage: For all panels, red dots indicate which comparisons exceed a 0.05 significance threshold after Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons (80 comparisons each for (A) and (B); 6 comparisons for (C)). (Figure 6 legend)
dandi:000115.why: The criterion takes the last significant trial after 0. With the tie correction it is +29 for roquefort, beyond both bounds (+3 and +5), and the behavioural half of the claim fails; without it every subject ends at +2. The claim stays blocked here because its replay half needs the decoder, but a later attempt that can run the replay half would need the answer.

dandi:000128.question: Header M1 gives two readings of the proto-trial selection, T1 (each velocity component must correlate with the condition mean at r > 0.9) and T2 (the two components concatenated). On the dataset T1 keeps 1452 of 1967 trials with delay > 400 ms (73.8%), leaves two conditions (the straight leftward reaches, whose vertical velocity is flat) with no trial and several with one or two, while T2 keeps 1786 (90.8%) and at least 10 per condition. The paper says the selection kept typically about 90% of trials. Does that sentence allow T1 to be set aside, or are both readings to stand?
dandi:000128.passage: Supplemental Experimental Procedures, Task design and behavioral control ("Subsequent analysis was thus restricted to the subset of trials (typically ~90% of all trials) where the horizontal and vertical velocity profiles correlated with those of a reference 'proto-trial' with r > 0.9.").
dandi:000128.why: Five claims change outcome between the readings and are blocked as methods_underspecified. Under T2 the peri-movement space is best (0.518 against 0.424 kinematic), the shuffled control holds, and one maze neuron keeps its tuning; under T1 the peri-movement space falls below the kinematic and kitchen-sink spaces and below zero at k of 10 or more, the shuffled control fails and no neuron reaches r = 0.72. Performance against dimensionality goes the other way (holds under T1, not under T2).
dandi:000128.answer: T1 can be set aside; T2 alone stands. The paper does not say how the two components combine ("the horizontal and vertical velocity profiles correlated with those of a reference 'proto-trial' with r > 0.9"), but it fixes two properties of its selection. It kept "typically ~90% of all trials", and every one of the 108 maze conditions stayed in the analyses. A third of the maze conditions are straight reaches without barriers, and for a straight horizontal reach the vertical velocity is flat, so a per-component threshold cannot keep those conditions. A reading that empties conditions is not the paper's selection. Header M1, and the criteria of fig4d-mean-correlation-jarray and fig6-peri-movement-space-best, now run T2 only. Claims and expected values unchanged.

dandi:000128.question: Header M6 reads "tuning" as the range over conditions (S1) or the SD over conditions (S2). With the J-array threshold of more than 5 spikes/s, S2 selects 6 of 182 units, and none that also has peri-movement tuning at least 1.5 times as strong, so the correlation claims have no neuron under S2. Does the paper allow S2 with these thresholds, or is it to be dropped?
dandi:000128.passage: Methods, Neural recordings and datasets ("restricted to neurons with at least 10 spikes/s of preparatory tuning" and ">5 spikes/s of preparatory tuning" for the arrays); Methods, Correlations ("at least 1.5 times as strong as preparatory tuning").
dandi:000128.why: S2 gives no result for fig3, fig4d, fig4-no-separate-populations, fig4e and suppfig1, which are decided on S1 alone; in fig6-each-dimensionality, S2 under T2 makes L1 fail where S1 makes it hold.
dandi:000128.answer: S2 is to be dropped. The paper never defines the measure of tuning; it gives only the thresholds ("at least 10 spikes/s of preparatory tuning", ">5 spikes/s of preparatory tuning" for the arrays, and peri-movement tuning "at least 1.5 times as strong as preparatory tuning"). With those thresholds the paper had J-array neurons tuned in both epochs, since Figure 4D gives their distribution with mean r = 0.13 and p = 0.03. A measure that leaves no such neuron is not the paper's. The Methods use one measure for both thresholds, so S2 is set aside throughout. Header M6 and the criteria of fig3-maze-most-not-maintained, fig4d-mean-correlation-jarray, fig6-peri-movement-space-best and prep-dimensionality now use S1 only. Claims and expected values unchanged.

dandi:000128.question: The criterion divides each neuron's rates by "its maximum rate" without saying over what. Is it the maximum over all conditions and times (the attempt's reading a) or over the four plotted conditions (reading b)?
dandi:000128.passage: Supplemental Figure 1 legend, as cited in the criterion.
dandi:000128.why: R2 (below a quarter) holds under (a) and not under (b); R1 holds under both, so the outcome does not change at present, but would if R1 were dropped.
dandi:000128.answer: The paper does not say. The Supplemental Figure 1 legend has only "normalizing each neuron's activity by its maximum rate (results were similar without normalization)". The criterion of suppfig1-population-averages now names both readings, (a) the maximum over all conditions and plotted times and (b) over the four plotted conditions, and both are run. The claim and its rule are unchanged.

dandi:000128.question: The claim's statement and its range of 7 to 11 read the paper's 7-10 as a two-sided range. The supplement says "7-10 dimensions were required", but the main text says "at least 7-10 dimensions". Is the claim a range or a lower bound?
dandi:000128.passage: Results, PD performance in a variety of spaces, paragraph 2 ("because the dimensionality of preparatory activity itself is moderately high (at least 7-10 dimensions, methods)"); Supplemental Experimental Procedures, Estimating the upper limit of PD performance ("This T-matrix also allows us to estimate the dimensionality of preparatory activity" and "7-10 dimensions were required to capture 90% of the data variance").
dandi:000128.why: Raised by the round-1 verifier. On the c x n matrix of preparatory epoch means, which the supplement defines ("T was c×n with each row containing the mean preparatory activity for every neuron"), the attempt finds 15 (N1) and 18 (N2) components, outside 7 to 11 but at least 7, so the outcome is not reproduced as a range and would be reproduced as a lower bound. The round-2 verifier judges the two-sided reading defensible. An earlier version of this question also asked which matrix "This T-matrix" means; the supplement's preceding sentence settles that, and that part is withdrawn.

dandi:000582.question: Reading O3 sets the gridness circle by "the distance from the centre to the outermost peak's centre plus that peak's radius", and removes the central peak "as a disc of the radius of that peak". Is a peak's centre the pixel of its maximum correlation or the centroid of its pixels, and is its radius that of a disc of the same area, or the largest distance from its centre to one of its pixels? The same choice sets the spacing (median distance to the six inner peaks) and the orientation.
dandi:000582.passage: SOM, Autocorrelation of rate maps, "peaks defined as 100 or more contiguous pixels of 1.5 x 1.5 cm2 above a fixed threshold"; "the circle was fitted around the outermost peak". The SOM gives no rule for a peak's position or size.
dandi:000582.why: The attempt runs both centres (maximum and centroid) and takes the radius as that of a disc of the same area. Between the two centres the fraction of grid cells changes by up to 0.06 in a layer (layer II 0.620 to 0.718 over all readings), and the readings decide whether layer II is within tolerance (13 of 32 readings) and whether layers V and VI hold the orientation part of grid-phase-orientation.
dandi:000582.answer: The paper does not give it. The SOM defines spacing as "the distance from the central peak to the vertices of the inner hexagon" and the circle as fitted "around the outermost peak", with peaks "100 or more contiguous pixels", and says nothing of a peak's centre or radius. Both centres (the pixel of highest correlation, the centroid) and both radii (the disc of the same area, the largest distance to a pixel of the peak) are now named as readings under O3 in the claims file, and the same centre serves spacing and orientation.

dandi:000582.question: The claims file says breadth is "the angular standard deviation of the mean vector". Batschelet (1981, the SOM's reference S8) defines two such quantities from the mean vector length r, the angular deviation s = sqrt(2(1 - r)) and the circular standard deviation s0 = sqrt(-2 ln r). Which one do the paper's means (55.9, 52.2 and 58.2 degrees) use?
dandi:000582.passage: SOM, Analysis of head-direction cells, "The breadth of directional tuning was expressed by the angular standard deviation of the mean vector"; fig. S2 and S4 legends, "Angular deviation refers to the circular standard deviation as defined in the Supplementary Materials and Methods".
dandi:000582.why: The circular standard deviation is larger than the angular deviation for the same cells (layer III means 62.5 to 76.2 against 49.1 to 56.5), so only the angular deviation can come near the paper's means, and the two give different numbers of significant layer differences (ANOVA 28 against 45 of 68 rows). The attempt runs both.
dandi:000582.answer: The paper does not settle it. The SOM says "the angular standard deviation of the mean vector" and cites Batschelet (S8); the fig. S2 and S4 legends say "Angular deviation refers to the circular standard deviation", which names one of Batschelet's quantities in the label and the other in the gloss, and the histogram axes (0 to 100 degrees) fit both. The criterion now names both, sqrt(2(1 - r)) and sqrt(-2 ln r), as readings; the claim's rule for readings applies.

dandi:000582.question: The criterion says the claim is reproduced "when, under a combination of readings, all three fractions are within tolerance", and methods_underspecified "when readings disagree between these outcomes". Under counting reading (b), positive slope, all three fractions are within tolerance under 54 combinations of the other readings (speed measure, positions, trials, cell classes) and only the order holds under 200. Is the claim then reproduced (some combination matches) or methods_underspecified (the combinations disagree)? Which of the readings are readings of the reported number (where any one matching suffices) and which are method details (where all must agree)?
dandi:000582.passage: Main text, paragraph 6, "141/150 cells, P < 0.001"; Fig. 4B legend, "Nearly all grid cells, head-direction cells, and grid x head-direction cells had positive slope values".
dandi:000582.why: The attempt follows the last sentence and blocks speed as methods_underspecified, which by the protocol also blocks speed-slope-steeper and speed-intercept, whose analyses ran (partially reproduced and not reproduced under every reading). Under the first sentence speed would be reproduced.
dandi:000582.answer: This is a question of the criterion, which was unclear, and it is now rewritten. The counting readings (a) and (b) and the three significance measures are readings of the reported number (what "141/150 cells, P < 0.001" counts), so for given method details the best of them is taken. The speed measure, the positions, the trials and the cell classes are method details, and the outcome must agree across all their combinations, or the claim is methods_underspecified. The statement and expected values are unchanged.

dandi:000582.question: Are the "head-direction cells" whose units are counted the pure head-direction cells of table S1B, or every cell passing the head-direction criteria including conjunctive cells; and must the grid or conjunctive cell in the same unit be another cell?
dandi:000582.passage: Main text, paragraph 4, "Head-direction cells were usually encountered together with grid cells (fig. S6)"; fig. S6 counts grid cells, head-direction cells and grid x head-direction cells as three classes.
dandi:000582.why: With conjunctive cells counted as head-direction cells and allowed to stand for the grid cell themselves, every unit holding a conjunctive cell passes, which raises the tetrode fraction (0.39 to 0.48 for pure head-direction cells, below the criterion's one half). The attempt uses pure head-direction cells and another cell.
dandi:000582.answer: The paper gives the first part. Fig. S6 counts "grid cells, head-direction cells and grid x head-direction cells" as three classes, and table S1B and the speed paragraph ("headdirection cells (153/220 cells") use head-direction cells for the 220 pure ones, so the cells are the pure head-direction cells, and the cell with them is another cell. Whether that cell must be a pure grid cell (fig. S6's class) or may be a conjunctive cell (which meets the grid criterion) is not given; the criterion now names both readings.

dandi:000582.question: Orientation within files is compared with "the differences between sessions of different rats". Are those pairs taken within the same layer as the simultaneous pairs, or from all layers? And does "Reproduced when both parts hold under every reading" cover readings O1 to O3 as well as the two phase readings?
dandi:000582.passage: Fig. S2 legend, "The broad range of orientations could be due to differences in preferred grid-cell orientation between rats".
dandi:000582.why: Orientation holds in layer VI under 59% of the O1 to O3 readings with the layer's own rats and 44% with all layers; both parts hold in every layer under 14 or 12 of 32 readings. The attempt runs both pools and blocks the claim as methods_underspecified.
dandi:000582.answer: The paper does not name the pool. The fig. S2 legend ("The broad range of orientations could be due to differences in preferred grid-cell orientation between rats") explains the per-layer histograms of fig. S2 but fixes no comparison, and the test is a standard choice; the criterion now names both pools, the same layer and all layers, as readings. "Every reading" covers O1 to O3 as well as the phase readings, and the criterion now says so.

dandi:001754.question: Reading M-b recomputes rate maps from spikes and position. The dandiset gives position only at the spike times of each file's units, so no occupancy time can be computed from it, and the preflight files hold no position at all. Should M-b divide spike counts by the deposited occupancy map of the epoch (the attempt does this for the flight epochs), and when M-b cannot be computed for the preflight cells, is a comparison with preflight judged on M-a alone?
dandi:001754.passage: The Fig. 1 legend says all statistical analyses kept off-track positions; the paper gives no bin size, smoothing or occupancy rule.
dandi:001754.why: Unsmoothed 64 x 64 maps give a spatial information about twice that of the deposited maps (2.9 to 4.0 bits per spike in flight against 0.7 to 1.6 for M-a), so a test of M-b flight values against M-a preflight values finds a difference in every rat, and judging on M-a alone does not. The attempt judges these claims on M-a and shows the M-b flight values and the mixed test as variants.
dandi:001754.answer: The paper does not say. It is a two-page brief communication with no Methods, no supplement and no code; it gives the measure only by citation to Skaggs et al. (ref. 13), whose formula needs occupancy, and says only that "all statistical analyses included these off-track data" (Fig. 1 legend). Dividing spike counts by the epoch's deposited occupancy map is a reading it allows for M-b. It compares one index computed alike for both groups ("An index of spatial tuning specificity ... did not significantly differ between cells recorded preflight and those recorded on FD9"), so a comparison uses the same map reading on both sides; where M-b cannot be computed for preflight, the comparison is judged on M-a and the mixed test is a variant. Written into the criteria of si-comparable-to-preflight (which the rat 1 and rat 3 claims follow) and fd4-abnormal-selectivity, and into the opening comment.

dandi:001754.question: Each preflight file holds one recording day with one epoch labelled ES and one labelled MC. Is each epoch a candidate session under S-a (as the attempt reads it), and under S-b, is the session closest before launch the later epoch of that day (MC in every rat) or the whole day?
dandi:001754.passage: The paper says rat 2 ran a flat rectangular track 4 days before launch (Fig. 2b) and names no track for rats 1 and 3.
dandi:001754.why: For rat 1 the flight day 9 cells do not differ from the preflight ES epoch (p = 0.50) and do differ from the preflight MC epoch (p = 0.0055), so the claim is blocked until the session is fixed.
dandi:001754.answer: The paper does not say. It never mentions ES or MC epochs; for rat 2 it says only that the preflight cells were "recorded 4 days before launch as the rat ran clockwise on a flat, rectangular track", and for rats 1 and 3 it says "that rat's preflight data" and "this rat's place cells before the flight". Each epoch is a candidate under S-a. Under S-b each epoch of the day closest before launch is run on its own, as the paper describes one track for rat 2 and prefers neither epoch; the later epoch is not given. When the epochs disagree the claim stays blocked as the criterion says. Written into the criterion of si-comparable-to-preflight.

dandi:001754.question: The criterion reads "most" as at least 4 of the 7 active cells of session 2. On the dandiset session 2 has 11 active cells under M-a and 16 under M-b, not 7. Is "most" then a count of at least 4, or a fraction of at least 4/7 (or a majority) of the active cells?
dandi:001754.passage: Fig. 3 legend, "Most place cells maintained the same firing locations, although the fourth cell lost its field".
dandi:001754.why: Under M-b, 6 of 16 cells keep their field by reading (a) and 1 of 16 by reading (b); as a count reading (a) passes and (b) fails, as a fraction both fail.
dandi:001754.answer: The paper gives it as a fraction of the cells shown. "Most" refers to "the same seven cells" of Fig. 3, the active cells of session 2, and the legend says "Most place cells maintained the same firing locations, although the fourth cell lost its field", so 6 of 7. "Most" is more than half of the active cells of session 2; the count of 4 in the criterion was that majority for the paper's 7 cells, not a fixed count. Cells that gained a field in session 3 are "not shown" and are not in the denominator. The criterion now reads more than half; the statement and the expected count of 7 are unchanged.

dandi:001754.question: In the pinned version every Rat3 flight day 4 ES rate map has cell_number -1, and the table's link from cell_number to cluster_id fails elsewhere, so the deposited maps of session 2 and session 3 cannot be paired by cell from the dandiset's identifiers. May reading M-a pair them through the unit whose spike-count map each deposited map matches best (shown as a variant), or is M-a not run?
dandi:001754.why: Paired this way, 6 and 5 of 11 cells keep their field under readings (a) and (b), which passes a count reading of "most" and fails a fraction reading.
dandi:001754.answer: The paper does not address it. It only requires that the maps of both sessions are of the same unit ("the same seven cells", Fig. 3 legend); how the dandiset's maps are tied to units is a question about the data. The criterion now allows M-a with the best-match pairing when each deposited map is tied to one unit and no unit to two maps, reported with the match; otherwise M-a is not run for this claim.

dandi:001754.question: The criterion computes, per bin, a counterclockwise rate and a clockwise expected count, which need the time spent in each bin in each direction. The dandiset has position only at spike times and one occupancy map per epoch, not split by direction, and nothing gives the track's layout in the image from which the circuit's direction could be read. Is there a reading the paper allows with these data, or does the claim stay blocked?
dandi:001754.why: Without a time base per direction no rate can be formed, so the attempt blocks the claim.
dandi:001754.answer: The paper gives no method, only "Some cells demonstrated place fields when the rat was moving only counterclockwise through a single location", and no track layout or time base by direction. It allows no reading that does without time spent per bin in each direction, so the claim stays blocked as methods_underspecified; the criterion now says so.

dandi:001828.question: The photometry sessions of the water drop task are stored as reaching sessions whose annotated events (all made with the mouth) are labelled correct (drop retrieved), drop, semidrop, miss and empty (reach to an empty spout). Which of these is the "water drop touch" the signals are aligned to, (a) correct only, or (b) every contact with a drop (correct, drop and semidrop)? The same question applies to fig3e-dlight-dcp-ccp-reward and fig3fg-auc-change-from-baseline.
dandi:001828.passage: Results, Anxa1+ DANs do not encode motivational value, paragraph 1, "The recorded signals were synchronized with licking behavior, tracked via a high-speed camera"; legend of Figure 3D, "Z-scores of FP signals aligned to the water drop touch". No passage names the event types.
dandi:001828.why: Drop and semidrop events are few in most sessions but make up most events in some (for example 29 drops against 6 correct in one Anxa1 session), so the mean AUC per recording can change. The attempt runs both readings.
dandi:001828.answer: The paper does not say. The legend has "aligned to the water drop touch" and the Results "peaked upon contact with the water droplet"; no passage names event types, Supplementary Video 1 and the figures are not in the text, and the code record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.14138011) still answers 404. Both readings fit the text. The criterion of fig3d-anxa1-ramp-to-touch now names (i) correct only and (ii) every contact with a drop (correct, drop, semidrop), empty-spout events excluded in both, and fig3e and fig3fg take the same readings. Claims unchanged.

dandi:001828.question: The dataset holds more recordings of this task than the legend of Figure 3D and 3E counts (Anxa1 GCaMP-dCP 15 sessions of 6 mice against 10 of 7; DAT GCaMP-dCP 8 of 5 against 4 of 3; dLight-dCP 21 of 7 against 13 of 6; dLight-cCP 15 of 6 against 11 of 6). Does the paper say which sessions were kept (for example one session per day, the first sessions, or a minimum number of events), and does "Artifacts and instances of signal intensity loss were excluded" remove whole recordings or only stretches of signal?
dandi:001828.passage: Methods, Fiber photometry recordings, "Artifacts and instances of signal intensity loss were excluded from the final data set."
dandi:001828.why: The RM ANOVA and the Sidak tests depend on which recordings enter. The attempt uses every session of the right group and site with at least one event, and reports the result per mouse.
dandi:001828.answer: The paper does not say. It gives only the legend counts ("mice = 7, n = 10 recordings" and so on) and the Methods sentence "Artifacts and instances of signal intensity loss were excluded from the final data set", which allows both whole recordings and stretches of signal. No rule by day, order or event count is given. The criterion of fig3d-anxa1-ramp-to-touch now uses every recording of the group and site with at least one event, reports the n used against the legend's, and reports a per-mouse summary without judging it. Claims unchanged.

dandi:001828.question: The dataset holds 20 sessions of evoked dLight release, two Anxa1-Flp mice with the fiber in dCP and two in cCP, each at five laser powers (0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1 and 2 mW), with 144 to 175 trains per session. Which powers enter the dCP against cCP comparison (all, pooled per session, or one power), is the unit the session or the mouse, and over which window before the train is the pre-stimulus baseline taken?
dandi:001828.passage: Results, Specialized organization of Anxa1+ DANs, paragraph 2, "Optogenetic activation of Anxa1+ DANs at varying intensities elicited DA release in the dCP (Figure S2)." Figure S2 is not in the text read.
dandi:001828.why: With two mice per site, a test over mice has no power and a test over sessions pools powers; the outcome can differ between them. The attempt runs sessions pooled over powers (10 against 10), each power alone, and a per-mouse summary, with a 1 s baseline before each train.
dandi:001828.answer: The paper does not say. The main text has only "Optogenetic activation of Anxa1+ DANs at varying intensities elicited DA release in the dCP (Figure S2)"; Figure S2 is not in the text and the code record does not resolve. The criterion of figs2-evoked-da-dcp-ccp now names (a) all powers pooled per session and (b) each power alone, the session as unit in both, a per-mouse summary reported and not judged, and baselines of 1 s and 2 s before train onset. Claim unchanged.

dandi:001828.question: The reaching sessions carry manually annotated events labelled correct, drop, semidrop, miss, empty (a reach to an empty spout) and unknown, each with the paw used and its distance from the spout in cm. Which of these are the "grasp attempts" of the target accuracy fraction (all labelled reaches, or all but empty and unknown), and is the preferred forelimb chosen per mouse over all its sessions or per session?
dandi:001828.passage: Methods, Forelimb reaching task, "Behavioral events and distances from the waterspout were manually analyzed and measured using Kinovea"; legend of Figure 6J. No passage defines a grasp attempt or the preferred forelimb.
dandi:001828.why: Empty-spout reaches are a large share in some sessions (up to 191 of 400), and their distances may differ from reaches to a drop. The attempt runs both event sets with the preferred limb per mouse, and per session as a variant.
dandi:001828.answer: The paper does not say. Accuracy is "the percentage of grasping attempts made within the target (< 0.2 cm) with the preferred forelimb" (Results), and an attempt is described as start, "grasping upon contact with the water droplet", and retraction; Figure 6F shows on- and off-target efforts. No passage lists event types or how the preferred forelimb is chosen. The criterion of fig6j-reaching-accuracy now names (a) every labelled reach with a distance and (b) all but empty and unknown, each with the preferred limb (i) per mouse and (ii) per session. Claim unchanged.

dandi:001828.question: The sessions are labelled by test phase (test1, test2, test4, test8), and the dataset holds more mice than the legend (TeTx cohort 10 TeTx and 10 controls; Arch cohort 10 Arch and 7 controls, recorded from 2023 to 2025). In the Arch cohort the session metadata say the laser was switched on after the first reach in test1, on in test2 and test4, and off in test8, while the Methods say it was off on the first day and on for the last three. Which test phases are the first and the fourth session of Figure 6J, and are the controls of Figure 6J the TeTx littermates, the Arch littermates, or both?
dandi:001828.passage: Methods, Forelimb reaching task, "For Arch experiments, the laser remained off during the initial 4 days (habituation and the first day of reaching) and was activated during the final 3 days of the experiment."
dandi:001828.why: The group sizes and the day-1 and day-4 values depend on it. With test1 and test4, mice with annotated reaches on both days, and the controls of both cohorts pooled, the mice recorded before the preprint was posted number 8 controls and 4 TeTx, as in the legend, and 5 Arch against 6. The attempt runs all mice with both days and, as a variant, those recorded before the preprint.
dandi:001828.answer: In part. Day 1 and day 4 are the first and fourth of the training sessions, which ran "for 4 consecutive days in 15-minute sessions" after habituation, with "the laser remained off during the initial 4 days (habituation and the first day of reaching) and was activated during the final 3 days" (Methods); the paper does not use the labels test1 to test8, so the first and fourth training sessions of each mouse are used and laser labels that differ are reported. The legend has one control group, "Ctrl mice (n = 8)", in one RM two-way ANOVA with both silenced groups, so the controls are one pooled group; the cohort they come from is not given. Data recorded after the preprint cannot be in the figure, so the criterion now takes the mice recorded before it as the main run and all mice as a variant. Of note, 8 + 4 + 5 = 17 mice fits the printed F(2,14), where 8 + 4 + 6 does not. Claim and expected values unchanged.

dandi:001828.question: GEO GSE282753 is public (since 2026-10-20) but holds only MitoPark and control counts (7 control and 6 MitoPark mice at 10 weeks, each with 3 to 12 technical libraries), not the cMfn2KO-early data the claim also needs. Does the paper name where the cMfn2KO counts are deposited, and how are the technical libraries of a mouse combined before the differential expression test?
dandi:001828.passage: Code and data availability, "The RNA-seq dataset generated and analyzed during the current study will be available upon publication (NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, accession number GSE282753)"; legend of Figure 1A, "MP-early (n = 5) and cMfn2KO-early (n = 5)".
dandi:001828.why: The claim holds only if Anxa1 is down in both models. Without the cMfn2KO counts it cannot be tested, and the MitoPark result can depend on whether libraries are summed per mouse or treated as samples. The claim is blocked until answered.
dandi:001828.answer: The paper does not name a place for the cMfn2KO counts. Its only deposit is "NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus, accession number GSE282753" (Code and data availability); reference 41 is cited for the cMfn2KO model, not as a data source, and the code record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.14138011) still answers 404 on 2026-10-21. How technical libraries are combined is not given either. The legend counts mice ("MP-early (n = 5)"), so the criterion now sums libraries per mouse, with libraries as samples only as a variant, and says the cMfn2KO half stays blocked while the MitoPark half is run and reported. Claim unchanged.

crcns:ret-1.question: Which flickering-bar recording of a retina gives a cell's spike-triggered average, its firing rate and its LN fit? The data set holds, per retina, one or two recordings of vertical bars (full height) at 8.3 or 16.6 um, and for six retinas also one of horizontal bars (full width) at the same width; retina 20080624_R2 has two vertical-bar recordings at 16.6 um and 20080624_R3 one more at 41.5 um. The claims file names bars of 8.3 or 16.6 um but not their orientation, nor what is done when a retina has more than one such recording. The same question applies to fig9e-slower-time-course, fig9f-lower-firing-rate, fig9g-threshold-unaltered, fig9h-gain-reduced and s3-receptive-field-surrounds. Tested here under three readings, (A) the first vertical-bar recording at 8.3 or 16.6 um, (B) all vertical-bar recordings at 8.3 or 16.6 um pooled (spikes and frames together), (C) the horizontal-bar recording where the retina has one, otherwise as A.
crcns:ret-1.passage: Methods, Electrophysiology, "To map spatio-temporal receptive fields, we projected gratings of adjacent thin bars (8.3 or 16.6 μm width). Each bar flickered black or white according to a pseudo-random binary sequence (16.6 ms frame duration)." Figure 9F legend, "Average firing rate observed during stimulation with flickering gratings."
crcns:ret-1.why: The measures differ between recordings of the same cells (the receptive field profile along a different axis, a different number of spikes and so a different noise level, a different firing rate), and the readings change the six mutant and one control retina with horizontal bars and the mutant retina with two vertical recordings, so a band comparison near its limit could change.
crcns:ret-1.answer: The paper does not give it. The Methods (Electrophysiology) say only "we projected gratings of adjacent thin bars (8.3 or 16.6 μm width)", with no orientation and nothing on retinas with more than one such recording; the Results ("randomly flickering bars") and the Figure 9 legends add nothing, the supplement is not in the text, and the paper links no code. The claims file now names readings A, B and C in the fig9d-rf-size-similar criterion, and fig9e, fig9f, fig9g, fig9h and s3 require their outcome under all three.

dryad:4j0zpc8hz.question: How is the square root taken for starch, sugar and Asat when some values are negative? The claims file names readings S1 (untransformed) and S2 (square root after adding the constant that brings the minimum to zero) only for negative increments, but the dataset also has negative starch (77 tree-campaign rows), sugar (3) and Asat (5) values, and Table S1 marks starch, sugar and Asat as square-root transformed. Tested here with S1 and S2 applied to these three traits as well. The same question applies to every claim that uses the treatment or interaction test on starch, sugar or Asat (disc-oak-warming-no-carbon-change, fig4-beech-mr, fig4-oak-mr, fig4-beech-wmr, fig4-oak-wmr, fig4-wmr-same-as-mr, disc-nsc-unchanged-drier-soil, tables6-no-seasonal-variation and the claims on Supplemental Table S3).
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.passage: Supplemental Tables S1 and S3, the footnote to the starred traits, "square root transformation has been used."
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.why: In beech, the W against C contrast of starch in 2020 has adjusted p = 0.041 under S2 and 0.099 under S1 (T1, yearly tree means), which alone decides whether fig4-beech-warming-none holds under every reading.
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.answer: The paper does not say. Its only words on the transform are the footnote "square root transformation has been used" (Supplemental Tables S1, S3 and S6); it mentions no negative values and no constant. The treatment test header now applies S1 and S2 to negative starch, sugar and Asat values as to negative increments, and adds (S3) negative values dropped, as R's sqrt gives NaN for them. fig4-beech-warming-none, disc-oak-warming-no-carbon-change, disc-nsc-unchanged-drier-soil, the fig4 claims and tables6-no-seasonal-variation now name S1, S2 and S3; the interaction test uses the same readings. Claims and expected values unchanged.

dryad:4j0zpc8hz.question: Which years enter the interaction model (lme(trait ~ (warming + moisture reduction + year + interaction)^3, random = ~1|Chamber))? The claims file gives readings T1 (2019 to 2021) and T2 (2020 and 2021) for the treatment test but none for the interaction test. Tested here under both. The same question applies to every claim on Supplemental Tables S2 and S3 and to oak-mr-no-interaction.
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.passage: Methods, Statistical analysis, paragraph 3, "a second linear mixed-effects model was conducted for both species using an additional species interaction effect (monocultures vs. mixtures) as a fixed effect"; the first model (paragraph 2) uses year 2019, 2020 and 2021.
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.why: The number of significant mixture against monoculture phenology contrasts changes with the years (8 under T1 and 3 under T2 with contrasts per year), and so can any claim that counts them.
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.answer: The text does not say; paragraph 3 adds the interaction factor to the first model, which lists "year (2019, 2020, and 2021)", while the set-up says "The first year of measurements (2019) was not included in this study". The F and p pairs of Table S2 settle it per trait. Year terms have 1 numerator df for bud swelling and development duration (oak Y x I "9.37 (0.003)") and 2 df for onset of senescence, senescence duration and growing season length (beech onset Y x I "0.18 (0.837)"); all Table S3 traits have 2 df (beech diameter Y x I "3.08 (0.047)"). The interaction test header now names (Y1) bud swelling and development duration on 2020 and 2021 and the other traits on 2019 to 2021, used by the criteria, and (Y2) 2020 and 2021 for all, as a variant. Table S1 likewise fits three years (beech Asat W x Y "5.22 (0.006)"), which supports T1. Claims and expected values unchanged.

dryad:4j0zpc8hz.question: Which years and which F tests? The criterion leaves the years open (all of 2019 to 2021, or 2020 and 2021), and the claims file reads the F tests of the supplement as nlme's sequential anova, with marginal tests as a variant. Fitted on the deposited data, the marginal tests reproduce Supplemental Table S1 (oak AGWB increment exactly on yearly tree means, beech Asat within 0.25 of every F on campaign values), while the sequential tests differ by up to 68 in F. Should Table S6 (and the Table S1 terms the criteria report) be read as marginal tests?
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.passage: Supplemental Table S6 footnote, the full model "lme(Measured traits ~ (warming + moisture reduction + Season)3, random = ~1|Chamber)"; Supplemental Table S1, F values per term.
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.why: With sequential tests the season term has p <= 0.05 for at least one of the three traits under all 24 readings tested (not reproduced); with marginal tests on 2020 and 2021 monocultures, pooled or oak, all three have p > 0.05 (the claim would hold under those readings).
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.answer: The paper does not say. Table S6 gives only "Full model: lme(Measured traits ~ (warming + moisture reduction + Season)3, random = ~1|Chamber)" and calls the tests "ANOVA tests"; it links no code, so sequential or marginal is not settled, and Table S6 has no year or species column. The Methods tie Table S6 to the treatment test ("we averaged them per year before the analyses (Supplemental Table S6)"), which is on monocultures with years 2019 to 2021. The tables6-no-seasonal-variation criterion now names the years (y1 2019 to 2021, y2 2020 and 2021) and the F tests (F1 sequential, F2 marginal) as readings, with the outcome the one all readings give. That the marginal tests match Table S1 on the data is a finding of the attempt, which a reader cannot confirm from the paper. Claims and expected values unchanged.

dryad:4j0zpc8hz.question: Over which family are the Tukey-type mixture against monoculture contrasts of the interaction test adjusted? The claims file names readings I1 (within each treatment and year) and I2 (over 2020 and 2021) but no family. Tested here as (A1) each contrast alone, unadjusted, and (A2) single-step over the model's eight treatment and year contrasts (I1) or four treatment contrasts (I2), as the treatment test adjusts over the six pairs of a year. A second detail for this claim. Under S3 (negative increments dropped), is the mixture minus monoculture difference compared with 1.4 taken over the rows the model keeps, or over all trees? The same adjustment question applies to every claim on Supplemental Tables S2 and S3 and to oak-mr-no-interaction.
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.passage: Methods, Statistical analysis, paragraph 3, "Tukey-type post-hoc tests were used to reveal significant differences between mixtures (multcomp function)."
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.why: tables3-oak-wmr-diameter holds only under Y1, S3 and A1 with the difference over the rows S3 keeps (+1.38, p 0.023). Under A2 the same contrast has p 0.16, and over all trees the difference is +1.69, outside 1.4 +- 0.14. The verifier of round 1 raised both points.

dryad:4j0zpc8hz.question: The claims file reads Eq. 3 of Supplemental Methods S4 as [N x (FO x WO / FE - WO) x FE] x 100 with N = 2, applied to one species. With one species this is exactly twice the NBE of Eq. 2, so the complementarity effect cannot be tested apart from the NBE. Its reading of Eq. 4 makes the selection effect exactly 0 under B1 with L1, as the reference FE is the same for every tree of a group. Is that the paper's computation, or should CE and SE be computed over both species of the mixture, as Loreau and Hector (2001) define them? The same question applies to fig5-oak-agwb-nbe-warming-2020, fig5-oak-asat-nbe-wmr-2021 and figs2-beech-asat-selection-warming.
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.passage: Supplemental Methods S4, Eqs. 2 to 4 (garbled in the extracted text, as the claims file notes), and the Results' "explained by complementarity" and "positive selection effect".
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.why: The "explained by complementarity" parts of three claims are not independent tests under the current reading, and figs2-beech-asat-selection-warming can be tested only under B2 or B1 with L2. The verifier of round 1 reported this as a misreading of the paper by the claims file. Under this reading NBE is also not CE + SE. For oak Asat under WMR in 2021, B2 with L2 gives NBE +194, CE +388 and SE -275 (p 0.0039), as the verifier of round 2 pointed out.

dryad:4j0zpc8hz.question: The criterion defines growing season length as bud swelling to onset of senescence, as the Methods do. The dataset's Growth_length ("Growing season length", no definition given) never equals that difference (median 55 days longer), and it gives slopes of 4.46 and 5.65 days per degree, within 0.04 of the paper's 4.5 and 5.7. The criterion's definition gives 1.09 (beech, p 0.085) and 2.16. Which is to be tested, the deposited Growth_length or the difference of the two dates? The same applies to reading (b) of fig1-oak-steeper-advance.
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.passage: Methods, Phenology, "For each tree, the growing season length was calculated as the number of days between the bud swelling stage and the onset of senescence"; Figure 1I and 1J.
dryad:4j0zpc8hz.why: The outcome of fig1ij-growing-season is reproduced with the deposited column and not reproduced with the criterion's definition. The verifier of round 1 raised it.

dryad:tdz08kq5d.question: The OD600 sheet holds seven time points per population, day 0 (the inoculation, OD near 0.06) and days 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12, while the criterion's repeated-measures ANOVA has time as a factor with df 5, so six time points. Which six enter the ANOVA? The same applies to fig1b-phage-reduces-density and fig1b-phage-effect-diminishes, and to which days 'all time points' and 'after inoculation' mean for the readings of auc-phage-reduction-by-temperature. Tested here under (A) days 2 to 12, (B) days 0 to 10, and all seven days as a variant.
dryad:tdz08kq5d.passage: Methods, Ralstonia solanacearum-phage selection experiment, "All cultures were propagated for five serial transfers (total of 12 days...). Before every serial transfer, bacterial optical densities (OD600) were measured"; Table S1 legend, "Three-way repeated measures ANOVA explaining variation in R. solanacearum densities by temperature and phage treatments for 5 transfers."
dryad:tdz08kq5d.why: Days 2 to 12 reproduce every sum of squares of Table S1a and give the temperature x phage x time interaction F(5, 180) = 3.870, p = 0.0024; days 0 to 10 give F = 1.464, p = 0.204, which would make fig1b-phage-effect-diminishes partially reproduced. The temperature and phage effects hold under both. For the area under the curve, the trapezoid over days 0 to 10 gives a 43.0% reduction at 35 C, outside 37.18 +- 3.72, while the claims file's readings mapped to days 0 to 12 and 2 to 12 all match.
dryad:tdz08kq5d.answer: Days 2 to 12, reading (A). The Methods say OD600 was measured "Before every serial transfer", that is at the end of each 48 h growth period, and the last sampled time point is "48-h growth after the fifth transfer", day 12; Figure 1 legend, "Bacterial and phage densities were recorded at every transfer (2 days)". Day 0 is the inoculation, set at 10^7 CFU/ml, not a measurement before a transfer. Days 0 to 10 would leave out the day 12 sample the paper uses for the end of the experiment, so it is not a reading the paper allows. The criterion of fig1b-temperature-density now names days 2 to 12, and fig1b-phage-reduces-density and fig1b-phage-effect-diminishes use its ANOVA. For the area under the curve the paper says only "for the whole duration of the experiment"; the criterion of auc-phage-reduction-by-temperature now names its readings by day, (a) trapezoid over days 2 to 12, (b) trapezoid over days 0 to 12, (c) sum over days 2 to 12. Statements and expected values unchanged.

dryad:tdz08kq5d.question: Under reading (a), is the 0.24% the mean of the four replicate frequencies of the 25 C +P treatment or the share of the treatment's pooled colony counts? fig1d-phage-raises-scv-frequency lists both ways of taking a treatment frequency; this claim does not.
dryad:tdz08kq5d.passage: Results, paragraph 2, "(Figure 1D; hardly visible in the mean plot due to low frequency of SCVs: 0.24% of all colonies within this treatment)".
dryad:tdz08kq5d.why: The mean of replicate frequencies gives 0.244% (within 0.24 +- 0.024) and pooled counts 0.561% (outside), so the outcome is reproduced under the first and not under the second.
dryad:tdz08kq5d.answer: The paper does not say. "0.24% of all colonies within this treatment" reads as the share of the treatment's pooled colonies, while "hardly visible in the mean plot" ties the number to a plotted mean of replicate frequencies; the Figure 1D legend shows each replicate's frequencies and gives no pooling. The criterion now names both under reading (a), (a1) the mean of replicate frequencies and (a2) pooled counts, and keeps its rule that the 0.24% match under one reading, as in fig1d-phage-raises-scv-frequency. Statement and expected value unchanged.

dryad:tdz08kq5d.question: Does the paper fix the unit of the Table S3a to S3c ANOVAs, reading (a) the mean of the clones of each colony type within each replicate population, or (b) each clone? The same question applies to fig2c-scv-lower-carrying-capacity, and to the other Figure 2A to 2C claims, where the readings agree. In the data, (a) gives 22 units, and with sequential sums of squares it reproduces every F, p and residual sum of squares of Tables S3a, S3b and S3c.
dryad:tdz08kq5d.passage: Figure 2 legend, "N = 4 for all treatments and boxplots show the interquartile range (25%-75% of the data), the median as lines and replicate means as dots (based on eight clones isolated per replicate for A-C...)"; Tables S3a to S3c, residual df 15.
dryad:tdz08kq5d.why: For fig2a-temperature-resistance the temperature effect has p < 0.05 under three readings but p = 0.071 with clones and sequential sums of squares; for fig2c-scv-lower-carrying-capacity the colony type interactions are not significant with unit means but are with clones (phage x colony type p = 0.020, temperature x colony type p = 0.0027). Both claims are blocked as methods_underspecified until this is settled; under reading (a) both would be reproduced.
dryad:tdz08kq5d.answer: Reading (a), from the reported degrees of freedom. The models of Tables S3a to S3c have three main effects and three two-way interactions, seven df with the intercept, and "Residuals 15", so 22 values; 128 clones would leave 121 residual df. The Figure 2 legend plots "replicate means as dots (based on eight clones isolated per replicate for A–C", and the Methods isolate "four mucoid and four SCVs" from replicates with both types (Figure S1), so means by colony type within replicate are the paper's unit. The paper does not name the unit in words. The criterion of fig2a-phage-exposed-more-resistant now fixes (a) and shows each clone as a variant; the other Figure 2A to 2C claims, fig2c-scv-lower-carrying-capacity among them, take their unit from it. The sums of squares readings stay open. The claims file's header said 22 units fit neither reading; that was wrong and is corrected. Statements and expected values unchanged.

dryad:tdz08kq5d.question: The claims file marks the sequencing and RNA-seq claims `data: elsewhere` (NCBI SRA). The dataset itself holds the processed results these claims rest on: the Snippy variant calls aggregated by group with gene names (snp_indel, gene_blast in uniprot), the DESeq2 table and the Figure 4B and 4C lists (transcriptome), and the KOBAS output (kegg enrichment). PRJNA1028400 holds no reads (28 BioSamples, 14 assemblies) and PRJNA1032726 holds the ten RNA-seq runs. Should these claims be `data: dataset`, tested on the deposited tables? Applies to sequencing-mutation-count, the three table1 claims and the five rnaseq claims.
dryad:tdz08kq5d.why: This attempt tested them on the deposited tables. It changes how the claims are counted (with the dataset or apart from it), not their outcomes.
dryad:tdz08kq5d.answer: Yes, data dataset. The Data availability statement says "The datasets and code generated during the current study are available in the dryad digital repository" and that the "sequences of evolved R. solanacearum strains and transcriptomics raw data" went to SRA. The variant calls, the DESeq2 results and the KOBAS output are data generated in the study, and the paper's counts rest on them, so the paper places what these claims test in the Dryad dataset; SRA holds the reads they were made from. The nine claims, sequencing-mutation-count, the three table1 claims and the five rnaseq claims, are now data dataset with no where field, and the header says why. Statements, expected values and criteria unchanged.

dryad:tdz08kq5d.question: The criterion leaves open whether the p < .05 of the KEGG enrichment is corrected, and blocks the claim when the two readings differ. Does the paper say which it is? In the dataset's KOBAS table the five named pathways are exactly the five with uncorrected p < 0.05, and no pathway has FDR < 0.05.
dryad:tdz08kq5d.passage: Results, "a total of five metabolic pathways were significantly enriched in phage compared to control treatment (p < .05, Supplementary Figure S5)"; Figure S5 legend, "The significances are shown with dot colors."
dryad:tdz08kq5d.why: Under uncorrected p the claim is reproduced (the five named pathways, p 0.0024 to 0.0464); under FDR none is enriched. The verifier of round 1 read the match as pointing to uncorrected p. The claim is blocked as methods_underspecified until this is answered.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: How are unvisited bins handled when a rate map is smoothed?
