The opening comment gives "spikes over time per bin, Gaussian smoothing with SD 2 bins" for single-cell maps (blanked) and "smoothing 2 bins, unvisited bins not blanked" for the template and decoder maps, without saying how bins the rat never visited enter the smoothing. The attempt runs two readings everywhere - (rm a) spike-count and time maps smoothed separately, then divided; (rm b) the rate per bin, then smoothed, with unvisited bins left out of the kernel (blanked maps) or set to zero (maps not blanked).
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Methods, Firing rate maps and identification of firing fields ("the firing rate in each position bin was calculated as the number of spikes recorded in the bin, divided by the time the rat spent in the bin. The 2D rate map was smoothed with a Gaussian kernel with standard deviation of 2 bins"); the claims file cites rateMapData.m, distanceDecoder.m and calculateRateMap.m for the other maps.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: In fig1c the chance level is 5.02% (11 of 219 controls) under rm a with the Methods' variances, the paper's own count, and 3.65% or 8.22% under rm b, outside 0.0503 +/- 0.00503. In figs2e r is 0.46 under rm b and 0.35 to 0.38 otherwise. The near-object footprint of the Object trial is unvisited, so zero-filling it (rm b) can change decoder likelihoods near the object.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.answer: The paper's code gives it, and agrees with the Methods' order ("the firing rate in each position bin was calculated as the number of spikes recorded in the bin, divided by the time the rat spent in the bin. The 2D rate map was smoothed"). In calculateRateMap.m the raw rate is countRaw ./ (timeRaw + eps), so an unvisited bin enters the Gaussian smoothing (smoothData.m, mirrored edges) as 0; with 'blanks' 'on', the default, bins with zero time are set to NaN after smoothing, and with 'off' (template and decoder maps) they keep the smoothed value. This is rm b with zeros in the kernel for blanked and unblanked maps alike; rm a and rm b with unvisited bins left out of the kernel are not the paper's method. The code for the single-cell maps is not given, so the same function is the reading. Time per position sample is clipped at 0.1 s (maxGap). Written into the opening comment ("Smoothing and unvisited bins") and the criterion of fig1c-object-tuned-fraction.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: Does the rule that a firing field has "a minimum firing rate of at least 1 Hz" apply to the field's peak (field reading a) or to every bin of the field (b, threshold max(3 x MAD, 1 Hz))? The attempt runs both.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Methods, Firing rate maps and identification of firing fields ("Firing fields were defined as contiguous areas within a contour with a size of at least 225 cm2 and with a minimum firing rate of at least 1 Hz").
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: The number of tuned cells without a field is 13 to 26 under reading a and 20 to 62 under b (expected 30 +/- 3), and the number of trace fields changes by up to 50 cells.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.answer: The paper does not say. The Methods give only "with a minimum firing rate of at least 1 Hz", and the code holds no field detection. Both field readings, (a) peak and (b) every bin at least max(3 x MAD, 1 Hz), are allowed. Written into the opening comment and the criterion of fig1d-field-distances.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: The criterion says the vector map's distance and direction bins and its smoothing are those of references 11 and 12 (Hoydal et al. 2019; Andersson et al. 2021), but it does not give them. What are the bins and the smoothing, and over what range of distances is the vector map built?
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Methods, Object-vector score and object-vector cell criteria ("we applied the methods used in previous publications to identify object-vector cells.11,12"); the paper itself gives no bins.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: The vector map's bins and smoothing set the object-vector score and its shuffled distribution, and so the count of cells the method finds. The claim is blocked until they are given.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.answer: The paper does not give them; it cites references 11 and 12. Reference 12 (Andersson et al. 2021, Methods, OV score) gives "distance bins of 2 cm and orientation bins of 10°" and "circularly smoothed with a 2D Gaussian kernel with s.d. of 1.5 bins (3 cm, 15°)"; these are now in the criterion. Neither the paper nor reference 12 gives the range of distances, so the criterion names two readings, the largest distance sampled in either trial or in both trials. The claim stays blocked if the two range readings disagree.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: Is a spatial bin's sampling time that of the whole trial or of the training half, and are testing samples whose position falls in a left-out bin kept or dropped? The attempt runs the four combinations.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Methods, Sampling analysis ("we identified spatial bins in which the animal had spent less time than a threshold value ... in either trial and excluded those spatial bins from both trials").
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: Under all four combinations the criterion is met, so the answer does not change this outcome; it is asked so that a later attempt can use one reading.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.answer: The paper does not say, and the code holds no sampling analysis. The Methods say only that the animal "had spent less time than a threshold value ... in either trial", which allows whole- trial or training-half time, and that the bins were excluded "from both trials", which does not say what happens to testing samples in them. The four combinations are readings, written into the criterion of figs6l-sampling-thresholds.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: Under reading (b), position samples permuted, how are the testing samples formed? The decoder's testing samples are 1 s spike-count vectors, and a random half of position samples does not give 1 s windows.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Methods, Random partitioning into training and testing data ("we generated a random permutation of the set of integers {1, 2, 3...T} and used the first T/2 integers as timepoints for training data and the last T/2 integers for testing data").
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: Reading (a), 1 s bins, meets the criterion under every speed and rate-map reading, so the outcome does not depend on the answer; reading (b) was not run.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.answer: The Methods answer it. The timepoints are 1 s spike-count vectors, so reading (b) does not apply. Random partitioning "was analogous to the shuffling procedure above", and in that procedure the permuted timepoints are the "N×1 spike count vectors" (Methods, Shuffling trial labels). Training rate maps come from the position and spike samples within the training windows (the Methods do not say this; it follows from the windows). Written into the criterion of figs5f-random-partition.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: The rank-sum test of NO against O is over "n = 16 sessions". Is each session's value its number of distinct words over the whole trial (16 against 16), or are the 80 session and distance bin values compared? The attempt runs both.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Supplementary Figure 7 legend (image on PDF page 46), "z = 0.221, p = 0.8252", n = 16 sessions.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: Both readings give p >= 0.05 here (0.85 and 0.94), so the outcome does not depend on the answer.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.answer: The paper does not say. The legend (PDF page 46) gives "n = 16 experiments" and "z = 0.221; p = 0.8252, Wilcoxon rank-sum test", and panels C and D (PDF page 45) plot only values per session and distance bin, so both readings are allowed. Written into the criterion of figs7cd-number-of-words as readings w-a and w-b.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: Are the NO and O rate maps of the population vector correlation speed-filtered, and are unvisited bins blanked (left out of the correlation) or filled by smoothing? The attempt uses maps not blanked, like the decoder's, under both speed readings and both rate-map readings.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Methods, Population vector correlation ("we stacked the rate maps from the No Object trial and Object trial separately"); Methods, Firing rate maps ("Only time epochs in which the animal was moving at a speed above 2.5 cm/s were used for constructing the rate maps and for spatial analyses").
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: Bins at the object's footprint are unvisited in the Object trial and lie in distance bin 1, where the correlation is lowest; blanking them could change bin 1. Under the readings run, the criterion is met.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.answer: The paper does not say. The Population vector correlation section gives only "we stacked the rate maps from the No Object trial and Object trial separately" with m = n = 50 bins, and the code holds no such analysis. The Methods' general speed rule and the decoder code's unfiltered, unblanked maps each give a reading. The criterion of fig4h-population-vector- correlation now names speed-filtered or not, and blanked or not, as readings.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: In the spatial information, is the mean rate (lambda) the trial's spikes over time (speed-filtered, as the attempt uses) or the occupancy-weighted mean of the smoothed map?
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Methods, Spatial information content ("l is the mean firing rate in the trial").
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: Spatial information is the one property whose correlation with distance tuning misses here (r about 0 against -0.13); the definition of lambda changes the values for sparse cells.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.answer: The paper does not say. It gives "l is the mean firing rate in the trial" and Pi as "the occupancy in the i-th bin (time spent in the bin) divided by the total duration of the trial", which allow both the speed-filtered spikes over time and the occupancy-weighted mean of the smoothed map. Both are named as readings in the criterion of fig7-single-cell-properties.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: Which cells are excluded before the object-vector criteria as having "firing fields that would fall outside of the arena in the Object Moved trial"? The attempt runs (x-a) a cell is excluded when any of its Object-trial fields, moved with the object to its Object Moved position, would have its centroid outside the arena, and (x-b) when all of them would. The criterion also does not say which fields count for criteria 3 and 4 (the field rule of fig1d-field-distances, and which field must lie 15 cm from the object) or which lambda the spatial information uses (the fig7 readings si-a and si-b); these are run as the fig1d and fig7 readings.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Methods, Object-vector score and object-vector cell criteria ("Before applying the criteria, we excluded cells with firing fields that would fall outside of the arena in the Object Moved trial (for example, when the object was moved to the south-east corner, when the cell fired at a south-east angle from the object) (28.8% of CA1 cells were excluded)").
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: Under x-a 59 to 70% of CA1 cells are excluded and the count is 9 to 15, never within 40 +/- 4; under x-b 19 to 21% are excluded and the count is 34 to 53, within tolerance under 27 of 48 readings. The claim is blocked until the exclusion rule is given. Neither reading excludes the paper's 28.8%.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: Are the c most frequent words chosen once per session and distance bin, from both trials together (as the criterion says, "Per session and distance bin, keep the c most frequent words"), or separately in each trial, as the Methods' "In a given trial" can be read? Raised by the first verifier. When each trial keeps its own words, a word kept in one trial only marks the trial, and the mutual information of downsampled words (0.30 bits) exceeds that of all words.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Methods, Downsampling words ("In a given trial, we identified how many unique counts were present, c, and then kept the c words with the largest frequencies. The frequency distribution was then normalized, creating a downsampled probability distribution for words").
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: Both selections give p below 1e-14 here, words higher in all 80 pairs, so the outcome does not depend on the answer; but only the selection over both trials gives a measure that does not carry the label by construction. The attempt uses the criterion's selection and shows the other as a variant.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: The criterion says the claim "needs the implant sites". The Supplementary Figure 2C legend orders the implants by proximodistal site and gives their cell counts in that order (39, 129, 43, 13, 242, 151, 26, 135, 378, 33); eight rats of the CA1 file match one count each. May that order stand for the implant sites, and if so, how is rat 27207 (620 cells, the two probes of 242 and 378 cells, not told apart in its file) treated? Raised by the first verifier.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Supplementary Figure 2C legend ("Animals are ordered according to the proximodistal implantation site ... from left to right, n = 39, 129, 43, 13, 242, 151, 26, 135, 378, 33").
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: The claim is blocked as data missing. As a variant, with the Methods' template variances (w b) every treatment of rat 27207 gives p = 0.18 to 0.37, as the paper; with the code's SDs (w a) p = 0.022 to 0.065, so the outcome would depend on the width reading and on rat 27207.

ebrains:q0fg-1x8.question: The opening comment gives firing fields as "contours from the peak down to 3 x MAD of all bins". The attempt takes each field as a connected region of bins above 3 x MAD, the region the contour at that level encloses. The Methods say the contour function was applied "iteratively", starting from the peak. Does the iteration only lower the level until it reaches 3 x MAD, so that the field is the region at that level, or does it split a region into separate fields where two peaks are apart at a higher level, or stop at a level above 3 x MAD? If it splits or stops, at which level and by which rule? Raised by the second verifier.
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.passage: Methods, Firing rate maps and identification of firing fields ("Firing fields in the rate map were detected by iteratively applying the Matlab "contour" function (Mathworks), starting from the cell's peak firing rate until it reached 3 x median absolute deviation (MAD) of the firing rates of all bins in the rate map").
ebrains:q0fg-1x8.why: The field count, each field's centroid and area, and so the field distances and ROIs depend on it. fig1d fails only on its range (2 to 19 tuned cells beyond 88.8 cm), fig1e on the two fractions together and figs4 on the trace fraction; a rule that splits merged fields could move each of these. Joining bins only along edges changes the field count by less than 1%, so it does not test this.

figshare:24639285.question: Reading (b) says the 590.4 TRM (40 uT) should be "no more than about twice" the 590.1 TRM (20 uT), but its cutoff fails a crystal only when the ratio of the 590.4 TRM to twice the 590.1 TRM is above 2, that is when the 40 uT TRM exceeds four times the 20 uT TRM. Is the cutoff meant to be on TRM40/TRM20 (fail above 2, matching "about twice") or on TRM40/(2 TRM20) as written? The verifier of round 1 raised this.
figshare:24639285.passage: If alteration had resulted in the formation of new magnetic minerals, apparent recording efficiencies ≫ 100% should have be observed (but these were not), and alteration checks should fail (Background & Summary, paragraph 5).
figshare:24639285.why: TRM40/TRM20 is 1.54 to 2.35 over the twelve crystals, and three (12053g1 2.35, 14053g3 2.08, 12053g2 2.06) are above 2. With a cutoff of 2 on TRM40/TRM20 reading (b) would fail three crystals and reading (a) fails one or two, so the claim would not pass under either reading. As written, TRM40/(2 TRM20) is 0.77 to 1.17 and every crystal passes, so the claim is reproduced.

figshare:26877211.question: Does "the unknowns" mean the rows unknown on both functional class and evaluation year, or each set of unknowns in Table 2 separately? The criterion applies the 90% threshold to the rows with an unknown class and to the rows with an unknown year, each on its own. The verifier of round 1 reports that the paper's sentence fits the rows unknown on both.
figshare:26877211.passage: The unknowns have only the JECFA name without associated compound names or additional information. (Data Records, paragraph 3, after the Table 2 counts of 118 unknown years and 110 unknown classes)
figshare:26877211.why: The 95 rows with neither class nor year all carry only a URL and a JECFA name (100%). Taken separately, they are 95 of 110 unknown-class rows (86.4%) and 95 of 118 unknown-year rows (80.5%), below the 90% threshold, so the claim is not reproduced as the file has it and would be reproduced under the other reading.

claims.statement: The second-stage classification divided dentate excitatory neurons into 586 putative granule cells (GC) and 500 putative mossy cells (MC).
claims.source: Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 2; Figure 1F
claims.quote: K-means clustering on the three sets of features reliably segregated excitatory neurons as putative granule cells (n = 586) and putative mossy cells (n = 500)
claims.criterion: Counted from the units' cell_type labels over all files, once per recording day. Reproduced when both counts are within tolerance; partially reproduced when one is.

claims.statement: Narrow-waveform interneurons have a trough-to-peak latency below 0.425 ms, and among wide-waveform units the excitatory cells have a burst index above the threshold separating them from wide-waveform interneurons.
claims.source: Figure 1A; STAR Methods, Unit classification
claims.quote: Units with trough-to-peak latency < 0.425 ms were classified as narrow-waveform putative interneurons ... Wide-waveform units were grouped into putative excitatory cells (E cells, red; burst index>1.8) and wide-waveform putative interneurons
claims.criterion: Trough-to-peak latency from the mean of each unit's first 200 stored waveforms, on the channel of largest amplitude, upsampled to 100 kHz; burst index from the spike times as the Methods define it. The threshold reads 1.2 in the Methods and 1.8 in the Figure 1A legend; both readings are tested. Reproduced when, under one reading, at least 90% of labelled narrow-waveform units are below 0.425 ms, at least 90% of GC and MC are at or above 0.425 ms with a burst index above the threshold, and at least 90% of wide-waveform interneurons are at or above 0.425 ms with a burst index at or below it. Partially reproduced when two of the three groups meet it.

claims.statement: Narrow-waveform interneurons fire faster than wide-waveform interneurons (medians 7.97 and 2.11 Hz; Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.00001).
claims.source: Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The mean firing rates of narrow (median = 7.97 Hz) and wide-waveform (median = 2.11 Hz) interneurons were significantly different
claims.criterion: The rate is not defined in the paper; readings are (a) spikes over the span of the recording and (b) the rate in `awake` periods. The dandiset's interneuron labels include CA3 interneurons, which the paper counts apart. Reproduced when, under one reading, both medians are within tolerance and the Kruskal-Wallis test gives P < 0.00001; partially reproduced when only the test holds.

claims.statement: The waveform of granule cells is narrower than that of mossy cells.
claims.source: Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 3; Figure 1E
claims.quote: Overall, the waveform of granule cells was narrower
claims.criterion: Trough-to-peak latency as in first-stage-labels. Reproduced when the GC median is below the MC median with a two-sided Mann-Whitney P < 0.05. The share of units whose peak falls at the end of the stored 1.6 ms is reported, as their latency is a lower bound.

claims.statement: In DRD2-Cre::Ai35 mice, 29 of 107 putative mossy cells were suppressed by green light, against none of 202 putative granule cells, 8 of 68 wide-waveform and none of 69 narrow-waveform interneurons.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic validation of the physiology-based separation of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 1H; STAR Methods, Optogenetic tagging
claims.quote: 29 out of 107 putative mossy cells were light responsive ... whereas only eight of 68 w-I interneurons and none of the putative granule cells (n = 202) or n-I interneurons (n = 69) were suppressed significantly by green light
claims.criterion: Units of DRD2-Cre::Ai35 sessions that hold the 20 ms light pulses; suppressed when the rate in +2 to +15 ms after pulse onset is at least 20% below the baseline (Methods). The baseline is read two ways (the 20 ms before the pulse; 50 to 200 ms after onset). Reproduced when, under one reading, the MC fraction is within tolerance and the GC fraction is below 0.05; partially reproduced when, under one reading, the MC fraction exceeds four times the GC fraction but the values are outside these bounds.

claims.statement: Mossy cells are more active than granule cells during both waking and NREM sleep (Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001 for each).
claims.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 2A
claims.quote: Mossy cells were more active than granule cells during both waking and NREM sleep
claims.criterion: Per-unit rates in each state from the `states` table. Reproduced when, under one reading of wake, the MC median exceeds the GC median in wake and in NREM with Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001 for each; partially reproduced when it holds in one state.

claims.statement: Granule cells fire most during NREM sleep and at similar rates during wake and REM.
claims.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 2A
claims.quote: Granule cells had their highest firing rates during NREM sleep and similar rates during wake and REM
claims.criterion: The paper's test, a Kruskal-Wallis test across the three states followed by pairwise Mann-Whitney tests with Bonferroni correction (three comparisons). Reproduced when, under one reading of wake, NREM exceeds wake and REM (adjusted P < 0.05 for both) and wake against REM is not significant (adjusted P >= 0.05). Partially reproduced when the NREM part holds and wake and REM differ.

claims.statement: CA3 pyramidal neurons are most active during wake and least active during REM.
claims.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 2A
claims.quote: CA3 pyramidal neurons were most active during wake and least active during REM
claims.criterion: As in gc-nrem-highest. Reproduced when, under one reading of wake, the wake median is the highest and the REM median the lowest, with each pairwise test at adjusted P < 0.05; partially reproduced when the ordering holds but not every test is significant.

claims.statement: Granule cells increase their firing in NREM sleep compared with waking, while mossy cells fire at equivalent rates in the two states.
claims.source: Figure 1D; Discussion, first paragraph
claims.quote: Granule cells had cell bodies located near the depth of DS2 reversal, had increased firing in NREM compared to waking ... In contrast, mossy cells ... had equivalent firing rates in NREM and waking
claims.criterion: Per-unit ratio of the NREM rate to the wake rate (units with a wake rate above 0). Reproduced when, under one reading of wake, the GC median ratio is above 1 and above the MC median ratio (two-sided Mann-Whitney P < 0.05). The MC median ratio and a Wilcoxon test of MC NREM against wake are reported.

claims.statement: Granule cells are more strongly phase-modulated by theta oscillations than mossy cells and fire at later theta phases (Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001 for both).
claims.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 2C
claims.quote: Granule cells fired on earlier phases of gamma waves ... and later phases of theta oscillations ... Granule cells were more strongly phase-modulated by both gamma ... and theta
claims.criterion: Theta (4 to 10 Hz) phase from the file's theta-reference LFP channel during `awake` periods (up to an hour per file) where the amplitude exceeds median + 0.5 SD; units with Rayleigh P < 0.05 and kappa > 0.1. MRL compared by Kruskal-Wallis. Phases are compared on (a) (-pi, pi] with 0 at the peak of the filtered LFP, (b) [0, 2 pi). Reproduced when the GC MRL median is higher with P < 0.0001 and, under one phase reading, the GC circular mean phase is later than the MC one with Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001; partially reproduced when one part holds.

claims.statement: Granule cells are more strongly phase-modulated by gamma oscillations than mossy cells and fire at earlier gamma phases (Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001 for both).
claims.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 2B
claims.quote: Granule cells fired on earlier phases of gamma waves ... Granule cells were more strongly phase-modulated by both gamma
claims.criterion: As theta-modulation, for gamma (30 to 80 Hz, amplitude above median + 1 SD), with earlier in place of later.

claims.statement: Slow-firing neurons are more strongly coupled to gamma than fast-firing ones (GC r = -0.176, MC r = -0.184, P < 0.0001 for each).
claims.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Interestingly, slow firing neurons had stronger phase coupling to gamma waves than fast firing cells
claims.criterion: Rate is spikes over the recording span. Readings are (a) all GC or MC with a gamma MRL, (b) only the units passing Rayleigh P < 0.05 and kappa > 0.1. Reproduced when, under one reading, both r are within tolerance with P < 0.0001; partially reproduced when both r are negative with P < 0.0001.

claims.statement: Granule cells are more effectively recruited by type 2 dentate spikes than mossy cells and fire earlier (Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001 for both).
claims.source: Results, Physiological properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 2D and 2E
claims.quote: Granule cells were also more effectively recruited to LFP DS2 than mossy cells ... and fired earlier
claims.criterion: Histograms of spikes around the DS2 peaks stored in the file (2 ms bins, +-100 ms). Reproduced when the GC median peak ratio exceeds the MC median and the GC median peak time is earlier, each with Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.0001; partially reproduced when one holds.

claims.statement: 5.5% of granule cells monosynaptically excite mossy cells (32 pairs), whereas no mossy cell significantly excites a granule cell.
claims.source: Results, Granule cell-mossy cell spike transmission, paragraph 1; Figure 3B and 3C
claims.quote: The spike transmission probability between excitatory neuron pairs determined that 5.5% of the granule cells monosynaptically excited mossy cells (n = 32 pairs), whereas no mossy cell significantly excited putative granule cells
claims.criterion: The automatic test of the Methods on all GC-MC pairs recorded together; the paper's manual inspection is not repeated. The fraction is read three ways (a) significant GC to MC pairs over all GC, (b) GC with at least one MC target over all GC, (c) significant pairs over tested pairs. Reproduced when, under one reading, the fraction is within tolerance and no MC to GC pair is found; partially reproduced when GC to MC pairs outnumber MC to GC pairs at least four to one; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Spike transmission probability from granule cells to mossy cells increases from the first to the second spike of a granule cell burst (P < 0.001).
claims.source: Results, Granule cell-mossy cell spike transmission, paragraph 2; Figure 3E to 3G
claims.quote: Spike transmission probability increased from first to second spike
claims.criterion: For the detected GC to MC pairs, transmission probability (excess MC spikes at +1.5 to +5 ms over the CCG baseline, per GC spike) for first and second spikes of bursts (spikes at most 6 ms apart). Reproduced when the second spike's probability exceeds the first's by a paired Wilcoxon test at P < 0.001; partially reproduced at P < 0.05.

claims.statement: GC to MC spike transmission is lower during NREM sleep than during waking (n = 31, P < 0.005).
claims.source: Results, State-dependent changes in spike transmission probabilities, paragraph 1; Figure 4B
claims.quote: Granule cell to mossy cell and granule cell to interneuron comparisons showed reduced probability of spike transmission during NREM compared to wake
claims.criterion: Transmission probability as in burst-facilitation, from GC spikes in `awake` periods against GC spikes in `nrem` periods, per detected pair. Reproduced when NREM is lower by a paired Wilcoxon test at P < 0.005; partially reproduced at P < 0.05.

claims.statement: Synchronous co-activation within 1 ms is found in 23% of mossy cells and 9% of CA3 pyramidal cells, but in fewer than 0.2% of granule cell pairs.
claims.source: Results, Granule cell-mossy cell spike transmission, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Only <0.2% of granule cell pairs showed significant peaks at < 1 ms while 23% of mossy cells and 9% of CA3 pyramidal cells showed synchronous (< 1 ms) co-activation
claims.criterion: The Methods' test at -1 to +1 ms on all same-type pairs recorded together. The MC and CA3 fractions are read as (a) fractions of pairs and (b) fractions of cells with at least one synchronous partner; the GC value as a fraction of pairs, where the claim holds for any value up to 0.0022. Reproduced when, under one reading, all three are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the MC and CA3 fractions exceed the GC pair fraction by at least ten times. Units on one shank cannot be told apart from units on different shanks, as the files do not say which shank a unit is on.

claims.statement: On the circular T-maze, the fraction of active neurons (above 1 Hz) is higher in the central arm than in the side arms, for granule cells, mossy cells and CA3 pyramidal cells (Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.00001 for each).
claims.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 5B
claims.quote: The fraction of active neurons (> 1 Hz) was significantly higher in the central arm compared to the side arms
claims.criterion: Fraction of each type's units above 1 Hz in each spatial bin of the linearised maze; central-arm bins against side-arm bins. Reproduced when the central median exceeds the side-arm median with Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.00001 for all three types; partially reproduced when it holds at P < 0.05 for all three or at P < 0.00001 for one or two.

claims.statement: Few granule cells have two or more place fields on the T-maze (6.6%), against 57.8% of mossy cells and 36.1% of CA3 pyramidal cells (Kolmogorov-Smirnov P < 0.0001).
claims.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 5C and 5D
claims.quote: only a small fraction (6.6% of recorded cells) had two or more. In contrast, 57.8% of mossy cells and 36.1% of CA3 pyramidal neurons had two or more place fields
claims.criterion: Fields from linearised rate maps of every GC, MC and CA3 unit in sessions with T-maze runs. The fractions are read as (a) of all units, (b) of units with at least one field. Reproduced when, under one reading, all three fractions are within tolerance and the GC against MC Kolmogorov-Smirnov test on field counts gives P < 0.0001; partially reproduced when the GC fraction is the lowest and the test holds.

claims.statement: Granule cells have the lowest within-field peak firing rates (GC against MC, Kolmogorov-Smirnov P < 0.003) and the lowest spatial information of the three types (P < 0.0005).
claims.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 5E and 5F
claims.quote: Of the three neuron types, granule cells had the lowest within-place field peak firing rates ... and lowest spatial information
claims.criterion: Within-field peak rate of units with a field; spatial information (bits/s) of all units. Reproduced when the GC median peak rate is below the MC median with KS P < 0.003, and the GC median information is below the MC and CA3 medians with KS P < 0.0005 for both; partially reproduced when the medians are ordered so but a test fails.

claims.statement: The fraction of splitter cells, whose central-arm firing predicts the coming turn, is comparable in granule cells, mossy cells and CA3 pyramidal cells.
claims.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The fraction of splitter cells was comparable in the three principal cell groups
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. A splitter is a unit with a central-arm field whose per-run rates in the field's bins differ between left and right runs by a two-way ANOVA (position x choice, choice P < 0.001, Methods). The paper names no test for the comparison across types; a chi-square test of splitter counts across the three types is fixed here. Reproduced when P >= 0.05, not reproduced when P < 0.05; the fractions are reported either way.

claims.statement: For neurons with stable place fields, the remapping index between open fields A and B is above zero in each group (Wilcoxon signed-rank; GC P < 0.05, MC and CA3 P < 0.00001).
claims.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 6C and 6D
claims.quote: For neurons with significant place fields ... the remapping index was significantly higher than zero in each group
claims.criterion: Remapping index r(AA') - mean(r(AB), r(BA')) from smoothed rate maps; place cells are units with, in at least one of A, B, A', first-half against second-half map correlation of at least 0.5 and a place field of at least 100 pixels with a peak of at least 1 Hz. Reproduced when the three Wilcoxon tests reach the paper's levels; partially reproduced when all three are positive at P < 0.05.

claims.statement: Granule cells with stable place fields remap less than mossy cells (Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.034; post hoc GC against MC P = 0.028).
claims.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 6D
claims.quote: but granule cells showed less remapping compared to mossy cells
claims.criterion: Place cells as in remap-positive. Reproduced when the GC median is below the MC median with Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.05 across the three types and a Bonferroni-corrected Mann-Whitney GC against MC P < 0.05; partially reproduced when the GC median is lower and only one test holds.

claims.statement: Only 36.7% of granule cells with place fields (11 of 30) remap, against 61.3% of mossy cells (68 of 111) and 55.6% of CA3 pyramidal cells (80 of 144).
claims.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 6C
claims.quote: only a minority of granule cells (36.7%, n = 11 out of n = 30 place cells) showed remapping, whereas the majority of both mossy cells (61.3%, n=68 out of n = 111 place cells) and CA3 pyramidal neurons (55.6%, n = 80 out of n = 144) did
claims.criterion: Remapping when the index is at least 0.2, among place cells as in remap-positive. Reproduced when all three fractions are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the GC fraction is the lowest. The place-cell counts (30, 111, 144) and the units per type (247, 181, 317 in 5 mice) are reported.

claims.statement: Population-vector remapping is smaller for granule cells than for mossy cells and CA3 pyramidal cells, for populations of 5, 10, 15 and 20 place cells.
claims.source: Results, Spatial and memory properties of granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 3; Figure 6E to 6G
claims.quote: The magnitude of population remapping was significantly smaller for granule cells compared to mossy cells and CA3 pyramidal cells ... These results remained robust within a range of threshold values with different numbers of neurons comprising the population vector
claims.criterion: Place cells pooled across sessions per type; for each population size, 1000 random draws (fixed seed); population-vector correlation as the mean over pixels visited in both maps of the Pearson correlation of the stacked rates; index PV(AA') - mean(PV(AB), PV(BA')). Reproduced when, for every size, the GC median index is below the MC and CA3 medians with Kruskal-Wallis P < 0.00001; partially reproduced when it holds for some sizes.

claims.statement: Mossy cells rarely inherit place fields from single presynaptic granule cells; of 10 place fields of connected granule cells, only 2 overlapped a field of the postsynaptic mossy cell.
claims.source: Results, Transmission of place information between granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 1; Figure 7A and 7B
claims.quote: Across 10 place fields from granule cells and 48 place fields from mossy cells, only two place fields showed overlap between monosynaptically connected pairs
claims.criterion: Detected GC to MC pairs in sessions with T-maze runs; a GC field overlaps when it shares a bin with a field of the partner MC on the same arm. "Rarely" is taken as at most a third of the GC fields (the paper's 2 of 10 is inside it). Reproduced when at most a third of GC fields overlap; not reproduced otherwise. Fewer than 5 GC fields leaves it blocked.

claims.statement: In the open fields, the rate maps of connected granule cells and mossy cells are not correlated within the granule cell's place field (median near 0, n = 19, Wilcoxon P = 0.60).
claims.source: Results, Transmission of place information between granule cells and mossy cells, paragraph 2; Figure 7J
claims.quote: GC-MC map correlations of all comparisons in which the presynaptic GC had significant place fields. Note median correlation around 0
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a Wilcoxon signed-rank test of the correlations against 0. For detected GC to MC pairs, in each open-field session (A, B, A' and the curtain sessions) where the GC has a place field, the correlation of the GC and MC maps over the field's pixels. Reproduced when P >= 0.05; not reproduced when P < 0.05. Fewer than 5 comparisons leaves it blocked.

claims.statement: Mossy cells are located deeper than granule cells relative to the reversal of the type 2 dentate spike (DS2) (Mann-Whitney P < 0.001).
claims.source: Figure 1G; Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 3
claims.quote: MC were located significantly deeper than GC
claims.criterion: The files give no coordinates for the recording sites, so depth is read from the DS2 amplitude at each unit's site, the feature the paper uses to place units (positive below the reversal, in the hilus, and negative above it). Only the 17 files whose units carry their shank (`electrode_group`) and waveforms can be used; the site is the channel where the unit's spike is largest in the wide-band signal (revised after verification round 1; the first version took the shank channel with the largest stored waveform through the electrodes table, now a variant). Reproduced when the MC median DS2 amplitude exceeds the GC median with a two-sided Mann-Whitney P < 0.001; partially reproduced at P < 0.05.

claims.statement: K-means clustering on the DS2 amplitude at the unit's site, the NREM to wake rate ratio and two principal components of the waveform's second derivative separates excitatory dentate units into granule cells and mossy cells.
claims.source: Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 2; Figure 1D to 1F; STAR Methods, Unit classification
claims.quote: Based on the bimodality of the distribution, K-means clustering over the four parameters was performed to classify E units into putative GC (yellow) and MC (magenta)
claims.criterion: On the GC and MC of the 17 files where the site is known (see mc-deeper). Features as in the Methods, with the NREM to wake rate ratio itself and the unfiltered wide-band waveform at the unit's site (normalised to its trough, upsampled to 100 kHz, second derivative from the trough to 0.8 ms after it), wake read as `awake`; the four features standardised, then k-means with two clusters (fixed seed, 50 starts). Reproduced when the clusters agree with the labels for at least 90% of units (under the better of the two ways of naming the clusters); partially reproduced at 75% to 90%.

claims.statement: Granule cells reside 59 +- 35 um above the mossy cells they drive.
claims.source: Results, Granule cell-mossy cell spike transmission, paragraph 1; Figure 3D
claims.quote: Granule cells resided 59±35 μm above their driven mossy cell partners

claims.statement: Granule cell spikes show a delay from the soma to the proximal dendrites, absent in mossy cells.
claims.source: Results, Identification of granule cells and mossy cells in extracellular recordings, paragraph 3; Figure S3D to S3F
claims.quote: Indeed, the spikes of granule cells showed a delay from the soma to the proximal dendrites ... whereas no such delays were observed in putative mossy cells

claims.statement: The dataset holds 1863 single neurons recorded from the medial temporal lobes of 59 subjects.
claims.source: Abstract; Technical Validation, proportion of selective cells, paragraph 3
claims.quote: we present a NWB-formatted dataset of 1863 single neurons recorded from the medial temporal lobes of 59 human subjects
claims.criterion: Neurons are the rows of the units tables over all files, subjects the distinct subject_id values. The readings are (a) every unit row of every file, as the paper counts neurons per session, and (b) units whose spike trains are deposited in two files counted once. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading. The exact differences are reported.

claims.statement: The patients performed 87 sessions, listed by subject and session id in Online-only Table 1 (the Methods give 89).
claims.source: Methods, Subjects, paragraph 1; Online-only Table 1
claims.quote: In total, we recorded from patients across 89 sessions (see Online-only Table 1) ... Total Sessions: 87
claims.criterion: Each file's identifier gives a subject label and a session id. Reproduced when the set of (subject, session id) pairs in the files equals the set in Online-only Table 1; partially reproduced when the count is within tolerance but the sets differ; not reproduced otherwise. The Methods' 89 is the other reading of the count and is reported.

claims.statement: Online-only Table 1 gives the age and sex of every subject; there are 25 female and 34 male subjects.
claims.source: Online-only Table 1
claims.quote: Total Female: 25 ... Total Male: 34
claims.criterion: The subject age and sex in the files are compared with the table, subject by subject. Reproduced when every subject matches; partially reproduced when some do not; not reproduced when fewer than half match. The diagnosis is reported side by side, as the files use a coarser coding (the paper's session list defines it).

claims.statement: Each session has 100 encoding trials showing 100 novel images and 100 recognition trials, of which 50 show new and 50 old images, and the images come from 5 visual categories.
claims.source: Methods, Task, paragraph 1; Data Records, stimuli group, paragraph 1; Technical Validation, proportion of selective cells, paragraph 2
claims.quote: In the encoding phase, subjects were presented with 100 novel images ... in the recognition phase, subjects were presented with 50 “novel” images and 50 “old” images ... (there are 5 different categories in each experiment)
claims.criterion: Per session, counted from the trials table and the stimulus images. Reproduced when every session has 100 encoding trials with 100 distinct image files, 100 recognition trials with 50 of each label, and 5 categories; partially reproduced when each part holds in more than half of the sessions; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: In the trials table, new_old_labels_recog is 0 for old stimuli (seen during encoding) and 1 for new stimuli.
claims.source: Data Records, interval group, paragraph 1
claims.quote: New_old_labels_recog provides the ground truth label of whether the trial showed a new or old stimulus during the recognition phase (0 is old, 1 is new).
claims.criterion: Two tests per session. (1) Under the stated coding, old trials (label 0) should show image files from the session's encoding block and new trials (label 1) should not. (2) Old trials should receive "old" responses (4 to 6) more often than new trials. Reproduced when both hold in every session; not reproduced when, in most sessions, both hold with the labels reversed.

claims.statement: The events stream holds the TTL markers 55, 1, 2, 3, 20 or 21, 31 to 36, 6 and 66 with the meanings of Table 1, and the events and experiment_ids streams have one entry each, in the same order.
claims.source: Data Records, acquisition group, paragraphs 1 and 2; Table 1
claims.quote: Both streams include the same number of entries in the same order. ... The following TTL values are used: Start of Experiment (55), Stimulus Onset (1), Stimulus Offset (2), Question Screen Onset (3), New/Old Response (20 or 21), Confidence of Response (31–36), End of Trial (6), End of Experiment (66).
claims.criterion: Reproduced when, in every file, events and experiment_ids have the same length and timestamps, the events hold only the listed codes, and every trial shows stimulus onset (1), offset (2), question (3), a response of the phase's kind and end of trial (6) in this order; partially reproduced when this holds in most files.

claims.statement: The learning block is labelled with one of 80, 83 or 88 and the recognition block with one of 81, 84 or 89.
claims.source: Data Records, acquisition group, paragraph 3; Table 2
claims.quote: The learning block is labeled with only one of the following: 80, 83, or 88, while the recognition block is labeled with only one of the following: 81, 84, or 89
claims.criterion: Reproduced when the two experiment ids of every file fall in these sets; partially reproduced when they do in most files.

claims.statement: To protect patient information, session_start_time keeps only the year and month of the experiment, with the day set to the first of the month for all sessions.
claims.source: Data Records, structure of the NWB file, paragraph 2
claims.quote: in the field session_start_time, we set only the year and month of the experiment but defaulted the actual day of the experiment to the first of the month for all sessions.
claims.criterion: Reproduced when every file's session_start_time falls on the first of a month; partially reproduced when some do not. Years outside the span of the recordings are reported.

claims.statement: The units table holds spike_times, waveform_mean_encoding, waveform_mean_recognition (sampled at 100 kHz), origClusterID, SNR, IsolDist and electrodes, with one electrode per neuron.
claims.source: Data Records, units group, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We use the following columns: spike_times_index, spike_times, waveform_mean_encoding, waveform_mean_recognition, origClusterID, SNR, IsolDist, and electrodes. ... (sampled at 100 kHz) ... here this link is 1:1 since each neuron is only visible on one channel.
claims.criterion: Reproduced when every file holds each column, each unit links to exactly one electrode, the stated sampling rate of the waveforms is within tolerance, and the quality metrics are finite for every unit; partially reproduced when the columns are there but some values are missing or not finite.

claims.statement: The electrodes table gives each electrode's brain area, MNI coordinates, impedance, the filter applied before spike sorting (300 to 3000 Hz) and the original hardware channel.
claims.source: Data Records, general group, paragraph 1; Methods, data acquisition, paragraph 1
claims.quote: General/extracellular_ephys contains information about the electrodes recorded from, including their location (brain area and coordinates), impedance, and filters used ... The origChannel (a custom column) refers to the hardware channel that was used to record from this electrode.
claims.criterion: Reproduced when every file has these columns and every electrode has a value for each; partially reproduced when the columns are there but some are empty for some electrodes; not reproduced when a column is empty for every electrode.

claims.statement: Clusters were accepted as units only when fewer than 3% of their interspike intervals were shorter than 3 ms.
claims.source: Methods, data acquisition, paragraph 2
claims.quote: To classify the detected clusters as putative units, we assessed the following criteria: ... (3) violation of the refractory period (<3% of the spikes have an ISI of less than 3 ms)
claims.criterion: For each unit, the fraction of interspike intervals below 3 ms, from its spike times sorted in time. Reproduced when every unit is below 3%; partially reproduced when at least 95% of units are; not reproduced otherwise. The count with the spike times as stored is a variant.

claims.statement: All neurons were recorded from the medial temporal lobe, in the amygdala and the hippocampus.
claims.source: Abstract; Figure 5a
claims.quote: 1863 single neurons recorded from the medial temporal lobes of 59 human subjects ... Summary of recording locations. ... (Pink: Amygdala, Yellow: Hippocampus).
claims.criterion: Reproduced when the electrode location of every unit names the amygdala or the hippocampus.

claims.statement: Subjects distinguished new from old images; the behavioural AUC averaged over all sessions is 0.74 ± 0.10.
claims.source: Technical Validation, behaviour, paragraph 1; Figure 5b and 5c
claims.quote: We used the area under the curve (AUC) of the ROC to quantify the ability of subjects to successfully differentiate between new and old stimuli (Fig. 5b). The average AUC across all sessions was 0.74 ± 0.10
claims.criterion: The tolerance of the mean is the stated spread, as the protocol prescribes; the spread itself is held to 10%. AUC per session as in the paper's code (see the opening comment), over all 87 sessions. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Performance was similar at the two study sites, with an average AUC of 0.74 ± 0.09 for CS sessions and 0.69 ± 0.13 for TWH sessions.
claims.source: Technical Validation, behaviour, paragraph 1; Figure 5c
claims.quote: performance was similar across the two study sites, with an average AUC for CS and TWH sessions of 0.74 ± 0.09 and 0.69 ± 0.13, respectively
claims.criterion: Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when both means are but a spread is not. The difference between sites (Welch's t-test) is reported.

claims.statement: The ROC curve is asymmetric (p < 0.05), as expected for declarative memory.
claims.source: Technical Validation, behaviour, paragraph 1; Figure 5b
claims.quote: Also, the shape of the ROC curve was asymmetric (Fig. 5b, p < 0.05), as expected for declarative memories
claims.criterion: The paper does not name the measure or the test. Asymmetry is measured, as in the paper's code (calcZROCSlope), by the slope of the z-ROC, the regression of z(hit rate) on z(false alarm rate) over the five interior points of each session. Reproduced when the mean slope over sessions is below 1 with a two-sided one-sample t-test against 1 at p < 0.05. The Wilcoxon signed-rank test and the slope of the pooled ROC are variants.

claims.statement: Accuracy is significantly higher in high than in low confidence trials (P < 0.001, paired t test) across all sessions.
claims.source: Technical Validation, behaviour, paragraph 1; Figure 5d
claims.quote: Accuracy was significantly larger in high compared to low confidence trials (P < 0.001) (Fig. 5d) across all sessions.
claims.criterion: Per session, the percentage of correct responses among high and among low confidence responses. The readings of the split are (a) the fixed split of the paper's MATLAB code (high is 1 or 6, low is 2 to 5) and (b) the dynamic split of its Python code. Sessions without responses in one group are left out and counted. Reproduced when, under one reading, high exceeds low with a paired t-test p < 0.001. The unpaired test the code runs is a variant.

claims.statement: 343 of the 1863 cells (18.4%) are visually selective, by a one-way ANOVA (P < 0.05) of the firing rate in recognition trials, in a 1 s window starting 200 ms after stimulus onset, across the 5 visual categories.
claims.source: Technical Validation, proportion of selective cells, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 5f
claims.quote: To select for VS cells, we performed a 1 × 5 ANOVA (one way, P < 0.05) ... Out of these 1863 cells (Fig. 5e), 343 cells qualified as VS cells (18.4%)
claims.criterion: Every unit, Methods' window. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance. The code's window, units of duplicated spike trains counted once, and the proportion with the category labels shuffled within each session (a null) are variants.

claims.statement: 146 of the 1863 cells (7.8%) are memory selective, by a two-tailed bootstrap comparison of mean firing rates (1,000 runs, P < 0.05) between the 50 novel and 50 familiar recognition trials in a 1 s window starting 200 ms after stimulus onset.
claims.source: Technical Validation, proportion of selective cells, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 5f
claims.quote: To select for an MS cell, we compared the firing rate between the 50 novel and 50 familiar trials during the retrieval period ... 146 cells qualified as MS cells (7.8%)
claims.criterion: Every unit, Methods' window and all 50 and 50 trials, with the bootstrap of the paper's code (bootstrapMeanEqualTest, Efron and Tibshirani algorithm 16.2), at a fixed seed. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance. The code's choices (correct trials only, its window), units of duplicated spike trains counted once, and a null with labels shuffled within each session are variants.

claims.statement: 26 cells (1.4%) are both visually and memory selective.
claims.source: Technical Validation, proportion of selective cells, paragraph 3; Figure 5f
claims.quote: 26 cells qualified as both VS and MS cells (1.4%) (Fig. 5f).
claims.criterion: Units selected by both main tests. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: The percentages of VS, MS and dual cells are comparable between CS sessions (18.4%, 7.7% and 1.4%) and the new TWH sessions (19.4%, 10.4% and 1.3%).
claims.source: Technical Validation, proportion of selective cells, paragraph 3; Figure 5f (the values as written into plotFigure5.ipynb at commit 1d95162)
claims.quote: We found that the percentages of VS, MS, and dual VS/MS cells were comparable to previously reported percentages in our locally recorded dataset (Fig. 5f)
claims.criterion: The paper names no test for "comparable". Two-sided Fisher's exact test between sites for each of VS, MS and dual cells, at 0.05. Reproduced when no test finds a difference and at least four of the six values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when only one of these holds.

claims.statement: The dataset includes 9 sessions from a new institution, Toronto Western Hospital.
claims.source: Technical Validation, proportion of selective cells, paragraph 3; Online-only Table 1
claims.quote: this dataset includes recordings from 23 new sessions, including 9 sessions from a new institution (Toronto Western Hospital, TWH)
claims.criterion: Sessions whose subject label starts with T. Reproduced when the count is within tolerance.

claims.statement: The sessions of the earlier release (Faraut et al. 2018) are found in this dandiset under the same subject, session id and task variant.
claims.source: Faraut et al. 2018, Scientific Data 5, 180010 (doi:10.1038/sdata.2018.10), Table 1
claims.criterion: Sessions are matched by session id. A matched session agrees when its subject label and task variant are those of the earlier table. Reproduced when every session of the earlier table is found and agrees; partially reproduced when at least 90% are found and agree, with the others listed; not reproduced otherwise. Age and sex of the matched subjects are compared and reported. Added in revision after the first verification round (see the opening comment).

claims.statement: Relative to the earlier release of this task's data (Faraut et al. 2018), this release adds 23 sessions, 17 subjects and 288 neurons.
claims.source: Background & Summary, paragraph 3; Technical Validation, proportion of selective cells, paragraph 3
claims.quote: we added 17 subjects and 288 neurons, including from a new study site, relative to our previously released dataset ... this dataset includes recordings from 23 new sessions
claims.criterion: The earlier release's session list is Table 1 of Faraut et al. 2018, the paper describing it (the Dryad archive, doi:10.5061/dryad.46st5, could not be fetched by a script). New sessions are those of the dandiset not in that list, new subjects those with no session in it, and new neurons the unit rows of the new sessions. Reproduced when all three values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when one or two are; not reproduced otherwise. The differences of the totals the two papers state (sessions, subjects, neurons) are a variant.

claims.statement: Neuron 132-177-4-RA (session 132, channel 177, cell 4, right amygdala) is visually selective, responding most to images of animals.
claims.source: Figure 4
claims.quote: An example VS neuron selective for the visual category of animals is shown at the bottom (The ID of this neuron 132-177-4-RA corresponds to: session ID – channel number – cell number – brain area).
claims.criterion: The unit on channel 177 of session 132 with electrode row 4, in the right amygdala. Reproduced when the one-way ANOVA across the 5 categories of recognition trials, Methods' window, has p < 0.05 and the animal category has the highest mean rate. The code's window is a variant.

claims.statement: Neuron 144-140-3-RH (session 144, channel 140, cell 3, right hippocampus) is visually selective for phones.
claims.source: Figure 3
claims.quote: An example VS neuron selective for the visual category of phones is shown at the bottom (The ID of this neuron 144-140-3-RH corresponds to: session ID – channel number – cell number – brain area).
claims.criterion: As for fig4-example-vs-neuron, with phones as the preferred category.

claims.statement: Mice touched the pole often when it was within reach (lick trials, 5.7 +- 5.3 touches per trial over 4,147 trials) and rarely when it was distal (0.9 +- 3.4 over 4,173 trials); performance was 0.72 +- 0.11 in cortical and 0.71 +- 0.07 in VPM recordings.
claims.source: Online Methods, Behavior, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Mice touched the pole at a proximal location multiple times (number of touches ... Mice touched the pole at a distal location less often (number of touches, 0.9 ± 3.4, mean ± s.d., 4,173 trials) and withheld licking. Average performance (proportion of correct trials) was 0.72 ± 0.11 (mean ± s.d., during the recordings of 111 cells) for cortical recordings and 0.71 ± 0.07 for VPM recordings (during the recordings of 29 cells).
claims.criterion: Touches counted per trial and split by pole position (Online Methods, Behavior). Performance is the proportion of correct trials per recording, averaged over the 111 control cortical cells (85 E and 26 FS, Fig. 5) and separately over the 29 VPM units. The paper does not say which recordings the touch counts and their trial counts (4,147 and 4,173) come from, nor whether they count touches of the principal whisker only (the Methods restrict touch responses to it, not touch counts). Readings, each run: recordings (a) the trials of the 111 control cortical cells, (b) all behavioral sessions of the dandiset (cortical, VPM, ION-cut and eNpHR control trials); whiskers (i) principal whisker only, (ii) any tracked whisker. Nor does it say whether trials with light (thalamic or eNpHR) enter the touch counts or the performance (answer of 2026-10-20); light readings, each run with the others: (x) every trial, (y) trials without light only. The trial counts under each reading are reported against 4,147 and 4,173. Reproduced when every expected value is within tolerance under a reading; partially reproduced when the touch counts are and a performance value is not, or the reverse.

claims.statement: VPM neurons respond to active touch with a sharp, short-latency increase in spike rate (0.6 +- 0.5 spikes per touch, median 0.4; latency 3.2 +- 1.0 ms, median 2.5 ms).
claims.source: Results, Chronic extracellular recordings from somatosensory thalamus, paragraph 1; Figure 1b,d; Figure 5b,c
claims.quote: Neurons responded to active touch during behavior with an increase in spike rate (Fig. 1b). The peristimulus time ... histogram aligned to touch onset showed a sharp peak in spike rate (mean ± s.d., 0.6 ± 0.5 spikes per touch; median, 0.4 spikes per touch), with short latency after touch onset (mean ± s.d., 3.2 ± 1.0 ms; median, 2.5 ms)
claims.criterion: Over the 29 VPM units, spikes per touch by the VPM definition (0 to 25 ms after minus 0 to 25 ms before onset) and spike latency by the dPSTH/dt rule, on principal-whisker touches with intertouch interval at least 25 ms (Online Methods, Data analysis; header, Measures). The latency n is the units that pass the Methods' exclusion; the paper does not print it. Filter readings O1 do not enter (no whisking measure); latency readings O8 and O9 (a) left edge and (b) centre of the crossing bin, which the paper does not fix. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the spikes-per-touch values are and a latency value is not.

claims.statement: VPM neurons fire at 5.1 +- 5.5 spikes/s without whisker movement or touch; most (25 of 29) increase their rate during whisking without touch, and the mean rate rises from 5.1 to 13.5 spikes/s. Three of 29 do not increase with whisking but still respond to touch.
claims.source: Results, Chronic extracellular recordings from somatosensory thalamus, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 1c,e; Figure 5d,e; Supplementary Figure 2b,c
claims.quote: Typical VPM neurons showed significant spike rates (mean ± s.d., 5.1 ± 5.5 spikes per s; median, 3.3 spikes per s; n = 29 neurons), even in the absence of whisker movement and touch. ... Most VPM neurons increased their spike rate during whisking in the absence of touch (25 out of 29 neurons ... The average spike rate increased severalfold after onset of whisker movement (from 5.1 ± 5.5 spikes per s to 13.5 ± 12.7 spikes per s; P = 4 × 10−6; n = 29 neurons, Wilcoxon signed-rank test
claims.criterion: Over the 29 VPM units, the rate in nonwhisking periods and in whisking epochs (Online Methods; header, Measures). A unit increases when a Wilcoxon rank-sum test of whisking against nonwhisking rate gives p < 0.05 with the whisking rate higher (Results, the test named for the 25 of 29), under samples O2 (a) and (b) and filters O1 (a) and (b). The population test is a Wilcoxon signed-rank test of per-unit nonwhisking against whisking rate. The text gives the 13.5 spikes/s as the rate "after onset of whisker movement"; it is read as the whisking-epoch rate, the quantity Fig. 5d plots for these units, since the paper defines no spike-rate window after whisking onset. Reproduced when the signed-rank test gives p < 0.05 with whisking higher and the expected values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the test holds and a value is not within tolerance; not reproduced when the test fails.

claims.statement: The spike rate of VPM neurons is modulated by the phase of whisker movement.
claims.source: Results, Chronic extracellular recordings from somatosensory thalamus, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 2d-f
claims.quote: The spike rate was modulated by the phase of the movement (Supplementary Fig. 2d).
claims.criterion: For each VPM unit, spike rate in 12 phase bins during whisking epochs (Supplementary Fig. 2d, bins read from the figure), fitted with a sinusoid; a unit is phase modulated when r2 > 0.25 (Supplementary Fig. 2e,f). The paper gives no count; its histogram (Supplementary Fig. 2e) has most of the 29 units above 0.25 (about 23 to 26, read from the bars). Reproduced when more than half of the 29 units have r2 > 0.25 under both filter readings O1; not reproduced otherwise. The number above 0.25 and the coupling strengths are reported.

claims.statement: In L4 excitatory neurons (37 whole-cell), resting Vm spans -76 to -45 mV (-63 +- 8 mV); every neuron depolarizes after touch (latency 4.8 +- 0.8 ms, amplitude 6.0 +- 2.9 mV), while whisking causes only a small depolarization or hyperpolarization (1.2 +- 2.1 mV).
claims.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 2f
claims.quote: Across the excitatory population, the resting membrane potential (Vm) spanned a large range (−76 to −45 mV, mean ± s.d., −63 ± 8 mV; median, −64 mV, n = 37 neurons ... Touches evoked short-latency depolarizations (latency: mean ± s.d., 4.8 ± 0.8 ms; median, 4.7 ms; amplitude: mean ± s.d., 6.0 ± 2.9 mV; median, 5.7 mV; n = 37 neurons) for all neurons (Fig. 2f) ... Whisking induced small depolarization or hyperpolarization (mean ± s.d., 1.2 ± 2.1 mV; median, 1.2 mV; Fig. 2f)
claims.criterion: The 37 whole-cell L4 E neurons of control mice. Touch-aligned average Vm (spikes removed) over principal-whisker touches with intertouch interval at least 25 ms; latency by the dVm/dt rule, with dVm/dt at the recording's sampling rate (10 or 20 kHz), not in 1 ms bins (reading O8; the paper's median latency, 4.7 ms over 37 cells, is one cell's value and not a whole millisecond; answer of 2026-10-20); amplitude is the peak of the average minus the mean 0 to 5 ms before onset (Supplementary Fig. 4 legend). The paper does not say how the whisking change (1.2 +- 2.1 mV) is measured. Readings, each run: (a) the mean Vm 100 to 300 ms after whisking onset minus the mean 0 to 200 ms before, averaged over onsets (Supplementary Fig. 4 legend windows; Fig. 2f shows whisking-onset-aligned averages); (b) the mean Vm in whisking epochs minus the mean Vm in nonwhisking periods (Online Methods epochs), spikes removed. Resting Vm by O4 (a) and (b). Whisking onsets and epochs by readings O10 and O11, which the paper leaves open (answer of 2026-10-20). Reproduced when a touch latency is found in every neuron with a positive amplitude and the four values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when every neuron depolarizes and a value is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: Touch moves the membrane potential of L4 excitatory neurons much closer to spike threshold than whisking does (shift 6.1 +- 3.2 mV against 1.1 +- 2.0 mV).
claims.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 2g,h
claims.quote: Compared to whisking, touch caused a larger shift of membrane potential toward spike threshold (whisking, 1.1 ± 2.0 mV; touch, 6.1 ± 3.2 mV; P = 1 × 10−7, Wilcoxon signed-rank test; Fig. 2g,h)
claims.criterion: For each of the 37 whole-cell L4 E neurons, the 10th percentile of distance to threshold in nonwhisking, whisking and touch epochs (Online Methods; header, Measures), with threshold readings O3 (a) and (b) and filters O1. The shift is the nonwhisking value minus the whisking (or touch) value (Fig. 2h compares these percentiles across periods; the baseline period is the paper's nonwhisking period). Reproduced when the touch shift exceeds the whisking shift by a Wilcoxon signed-rank test at p < 0.05 and both means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when only the test holds.

claims.statement: The effective reversal potential of the touch response of L4 excitatory neurons is more depolarized than resting Vm, while that of whisking is close to rest and more hyperpolarized than that of touch.
claims.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 4
claims.quote: of the touch response was more depolarized than the resting Vm and sometimes crossed the spike threshold ... In contrast, the effective reversal potential for whisker movement was close to the resting Vm, below the spike threshold and more hyperpolarized than that for touch
claims.criterion: Per Supplementary Fig. 4 legend. For each touch, pre-Vm is the mean 0 to 5 ms before onset and post-Vm the Vm at the peak time of the neuron's average PSP; for each whisking onset, pre-Vm the mean 0 to 200 ms before and post-Vm the mean 100 to 300 ms after. dVm = post minus pre, fitted linearly against pre-Vm; the reversal is where the line crosses zero. The legend leaves open whether one line is fitted per neuron or over all neurons (panel b shows all neurons, panel c compares reversals). Readings (a) per neuron, compared across the 37 neurons; (b) one pooled fit per event type. The paper reports no test. Reproduced when, under the reading, the touch reversal lies above the whisking reversal (in more than half of the neurons and in the medians for a) and above the median resting Vm; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: With L4 excitatory neurons depolarized near 0 mV to reveal inhibition, touch evokes strong, transient inhibition that follows excitation by 0.4 +- 0.8 ms at half maximum.
claims.source: Results, Membrane-potential dynamics of L4 excitatory neurons, paragraph 3; Figure 3b-d
claims.quote: Touch elicited strong and transient inhibitory input (Fig. 3b,c), which followed excitation with a short delay (mean ± s.d., 0.4 ± 0.8 ms at half max; n = 6 neurons; Fig. 3d).
claims.criterion: The 6 L4 E neurons recorded both at rest and with steady depolarizing current (about 1 nA, baseline near 0 mV; Online Methods, Barrel cortex recordings). For each, the touch-aligned average Vm at rest (excitation) and with current (inhibition, sign inverted), each normalized to its peak (Fig. 3d); the time at which each first reaches half its peak after onset; the delay is inhibition minus excitation. Trials at depolarized potential are those with injected current (or a Vm baseline near 0 mV, as the dandiset marks them). Reproduced when the mean delay is within tolerance; not reproduced otherwise. The range over neurons is reported against the paper's -0.8 to 1.6 ms (Discussion, paragraph 3).

claims.statement: L4 FS interneurons fire at 9.3 +- 8.5 spikes/s without whisker movement and fire 1.9 +- 1.0 spikes per touch, with a spike latency of 5.3 +- 2.1 ms.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 1; Figure 5b,c
claims.quote: FS interneurons were active during baseline conditions, even in the absence of whisker movements (mean ± s.d., 9.3 ± 8.5 spikes per s; median, 6.4 spikes per s; n = 26 neurons ... and spike rates increased after touch (mean ± s.d., 1.9 ± 1.0 spikes per touch; median, 1.9 spikes per touch; n = 26 neurons ... and spiking (mean ± s.d., 5.3 ± 2.1 ms; median, 4.5 ms, n = 24 neurons; Fig. 5c)
claims.criterion: Over the control L4 FS cells (26 in the text, 25 in Supplementary Fig. 7; both sets reported), the nonwhisking rate, spikes per touch by the cortical Fig. 5 definition and spike latency by the dPSTH/dt rule with its exclusion (header, Measures; readings O8 and O9). FS identification (answer of 2026-10-20). The paper names no test, baseline or threshold for "directly driven by light within 5 ms after photostimulus onset" (5 ms pulses at 5 or 10 Hz; Online Methods), and defines peak and trough of Supplementary Fig. 6 only in the figure's inset; the text gives duration as "spike peak to trough duration" (Online Methods, Barrel cortex recordings) and nothing on polarity or baseline. The author states its test and its waveform measures; readings, each run: driven at (a) p < 0.001 and (b) p < 0.01, each (i) with and (ii) without the approximate boundary of the header. The paper's counts are the check: 19 ChR2-tagged control FS cells (5 whole-cell, 14 cell-attached), and 14 control plus 10 ION-cut cell-attached FS cells in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice (Supplementary Table 2); the count of each reading is reported against them, and dandiset cell-type labels, where present, take precedence (header, Cell types). Reproduced when the three values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when two are.

claims.statement: In whole-cell L4 FS interneurons (n = 7), touch depolarizes the membrane by 7.0 +- 5.2 mV with onset 4.0 +- 0.6 ms, and whisking depolarizes it by 2.7 +- 2.1 mV toward threshold.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 4d-h
claims.quote: Membrane potential depolarized (mean ± s.d., 7.0 ± 5.2 mV; median, 6.7 mV; n = 7 neurons, Fig. 4d,f) ... Response latencies were short for membrane potential depolarization (onset ... 4.0 ± 0.6 ms; median, 4.2 ms, n = 7 neurons; Fig. 4d,f) ... after onset of whisking, the membrane potential of FS neurons depolarized closer to spike threshold (mean ± s.d., 2.7 ± 2.1 mV; median, 2.4 mV, n = 7 neurons; Fig. 4e–h)
claims.criterion: The 7 whole-cell L4 FS cells. Touch amplitude and latency as in exc-vm-touch-whisking, with dVm/dt at the sampling rate, not in 1 ms bins (the paper's median, 4.2 ms over 7 cells, is one cell's value; answer of 2026-10-20); whisking depolarization as the post-onset (100 to 300 ms) minus pre-onset (0 to 200 ms) mean Vm (Supplementary Fig. 4 legend, the paper's whisking-onset measure), with the nonwhisking minus whisking 10th percentile of distance to threshold (Fig. 4h) as reading (b). Reproduced when all three values are within tolerance under a reading; partially reproduced when the touch values are and the whisking value is not.

claims.statement: Most L4 FS interneurons (23 of 26) increase their spike rate during whisking without touch and 3 of 26 decrease it; over the population the rate roughly doubles (to 21.1 +- 15.8 spikes/s).
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 2; Figure 5d,e
claims.quote: most L4 FS neurons significantly increased their spike rate during whisker movement without touch (23 of 26 neurons ... and a small subset (3 of 26 neurons ... decreased spike rate. Overall, after onset of whisking ... and the spike rate doubled (mean ± s.d., 21.1 ± 15.8 spikes per s; median, 14.6 spikes per s, n = 26 neurons, P = 2.7 × 10−5; Fig. 5d)
claims.criterion: Over the control L4 FS cells, per-cell Wilcoxon rank-sum tests of whisking against nonwhisking rate at p < 0.05 (Results), samples O2 (a) and (b), filters O1 (a) and (b). The population test is not named; it is paired, so a Wilcoxon signed-rank test (Online Methods, Statistical analysis). Reproduced when the signed-rank test gives p < 0.05 with whisking higher and the counts and mean are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the test holds and a value is not within tolerance; not reproduced when the test fails.

claims.statement: Spikes of L4 FS interneurons are coupled to whisking phase.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 7d,g
claims.quote: Spikes of L4 FS neurons were also coupled to whisking phase (Supplementary Fig. 7).
claims.criterion: For each control L4 FS cell, spike rate in 12 phase bins during whisking epochs, fitted with a sinusoid, or a sinusoid plus one of twice the frequency when that raises r2 by 50% (Supplementary Fig. 7g); coupled when r2 > 0.25 (the threshold of Supplementary Figs. 2e and 12a). Supplementary Fig. 7g shows fits for all 25 cells (18 single, 7 double). Reproduced when more than half of the cells are coupled under both filter readings O1; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Touch- and whisking-evoked spikes are typically multiplexed in individual L4 FS neurons, as in VPM neurons.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 3; Figure 5b,d; Supplementary Figure 7
claims.quote: Touch- and whisking-evoked spikes were typically multiplexed in individual L4 FS neurons (Fig. 5b,d and Supplementary Fig. 7), as in VPM neurons.
claims.criterion: A control L4 FS cell multiplexes when its spikes per touch (Fig. 5 definition) has a 95% bootstrap interval above zero (Fig. 5b legend) and its whisking rate is significantly different from its nonwhisking rate by the per-cell rank-sum test of fs-whisking-rate (Fig. 5d; the 23 increases and 3 decreases), readings O1 and O2. "Typically" is read as more than half of the cells. Reproduced when more than half multiplex under every reading; not reproduced otherwise. The same count for the 29 VPM units is reported.

claims.statement: L4 excitatory neurons respond mostly to touch (0.3 +- 0.4 spikes per touch, n = 85) and only weakly to whisker movement; their rate does not change significantly between nonwhisking and whisking (0.4 to 0.6 spikes/s, P = 0.20).
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of L4 fast-spiking interneurons, paragraph 3; Figure 5b,d,e
claims.quote: Excitatory neurons responded mostly to touch (mean ± s.d., 0.3 ± 0.4 spikes per touch; median, 0.1 spikes per touch; n = 85 neurons; Fig. 5b,d) and showed weak response to whisker movement ... (nonwhisking ... 0.4 ± 0.6 spikes per s; median, 0.1 spikes per s; whisking ... 0.6 ± 0.9 spikes per s; median, 0.2 spikes per s; n = 85, P = 0.20; Fig. 5d,e). In contrast to VPM and L4 FS neurons, L4 excitatory neurons responded selectively to touch
claims.criterion: The 85 control L4 E neurons (37 whole-cell, 48 cell-attached; control trials only for cells in eNpHR mice). Spikes per touch by the cortical Fig. 5 definition; rates in nonwhisking and whisking periods (header, Measures). The absence part is judged on the paper's test, a paired test of per-neuron nonwhisking against whisking rate; the test is not named, and the Methods' paired test is the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, at 0.05. Reproduced when that test gives p >= 0.05 and the three values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the test gives p >= 0.05 and a value is not within tolerance; not reproduced when the test finds a difference. The size of the whisking change is reported either way, with filter readings O1 shown (the absence test is judged on each; a split is reported as a deviation).

claims.statement: Photoactivating TRN axons in VPM of VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice reduces thalamic activity to 17% of control.
claims.source: Results, Inhibition is driven by thalamus, paragraph 1; Figure 6b,c
claims.quote: Photoactivation of TRN axons reduced activity in the thalamus (to 17% of control, P = 3 × 10−4, n = 17 multiunit recordings; Fig. 6b,c).
claims.criterion: The 17 VPM multiunit recordings made by pipette during behavior. Rate over all time inside the light (Supplementary Fig. 9i, no behavioral epochs for multiunits) against control, windows O5 (a) and (b), fractions O6 (a) and (b), laser powers O7 (a) and (b). Reproduced when a Wilcoxon signed-rank test of per-recording rates (paired; the paper does not name the test, the Methods give this one for paired data) gives p < 0.05 with light lower and the fraction is within tolerance under a reading; partially reproduced when only the test holds.

claims.statement: Thalamic photoinhibition hyperpolarizes L4 excitatory neurons and reduces their Vm fluctuations, with an onset latency of 4.2 ms, longer than the 2.8 ms latency of direct cortical GABAergic activation.
