Reading (a) is the code's, reading (b) keeps them; the 50 t-types and 200 pairs show which the paper used. Reproduced when, under one reading, r is within tolerance; the counts are reported. Needs the reference 10x v2 data (Yao et al. 2021) as the code reads them.

claims.statement: The correlation between transcriptomic and electrophysiological distances is also seen within several individual families and for many individual features.
claims.source: Results, Continuous phenotypic variation, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 7c-n
claims.quote: The correlation was also observed within multiple individual families and for many individual electrophysiological features (Extended Data Fig. 7 ).
claims.criterion: As the code does it (families.ipynb, the loop over families) and the Extended Data Fig. 7 legend says. For each of the families Pvalb, Sst, Vip, Lamp5, IT and CT, t-types with at least 5 cells, Sst Chodl and Pvalb Vipr2_2 left out; transcriptomic distance over the 500 most variable genes of that family's transcriptomic group in the reference 10x v2 data (MGE for Pvalb and Sst, CGE for Vip and Lamp5, excitatory for IT and CT); distances as in fig4c-distance-correlation; Pearson r over the family's pairs, and, as the code does, for each feature alone within each family. The paper gives no p or threshold. "Multiple families" is read as (a) at least two or (b) a majority (at least four) of the six families with r > 0. "Many features" is read as at least half of the 17 features having r > 0 in at least half of the counted families; the code computes per-family feature correlations and no pooled one, so this count is the reader's reading, not the paper's. Reproduced when the feature part holds and the family part holds under reading (b); partially reproduced when it holds only under reading (a). Families with fewer than three t-types are reported and not counted.

claims.statement: Among IT t-types (eight with at least five cells), transcriptomic distances are strongly correlated with differences in average soma depth, r = 0.70.
claims.source: Results, Continuous phenotypic variation, paragraph 4; Figure 4d legend
claims.quote: Transcriptomic distances between t-types were strongly correlated with the average soma depth differences ( r = 0.70; Fig. 4d ).
claims.criterion: As the code does it (families.ipynb). IT cells (family from the t-type), not excluded, with a soma depth; t-types with at least 5 such cells; mean normalized soma depth per t-type; depth distance the absolute difference of means; transcriptomic distance the correlation distance between mean log(x + 1) counts of the reference 10x v2 data over the 500 most variable genes of the excitatory group (Methods, Within-family analysis); Pearson r over all pairs. Reproduced when r is within tolerance.

claims.statement: Within the Vip subclass the membrane time constant varies continuously across the transcriptomic landscape, largest near the Sncg subclass and decreasing towards Vip Gpc3.
claims.source: Results, Continuous phenotypic variation, paragraph 1; Figure 4a
claims.quote: For example, electrophysiological properties of the t-types within the Vip subclass varied continuously across the transcriptomic landscape; the membrane time constant, for instance, had its largest values close to the Sncg subclass and gradually decreased towards Vip Gpc3 (Fig. 4a ).
claims.criterion: The paper shows this as a colour overlay on the reference t-SNE and gives no measure. Vip cells (family Vip, not excluded, all 17 features), positioned on the CGE reference t-SNE of Fig. 1c as the Methods and code (rnaseqTools.map_to_tsne, median of the 10 nearest reference cells by correlation over the t-type assignment genes) do it. Two readings of "close to Sncg and decreasing towards Vip Gpc3", both run, (a) over cells, the Spearman correlation between tau and the cell's position along the line from the centroid of the Sncg reference cells to the centroid of the Vip Gpc3 reference cells in the embedding (projection onto that line), and (b) over Vip t-types with at least 5 cells, the Spearman correlation between the t-type's median tau and its transcriptomic correlation distance to the Sncg subclass mean in the 10x v2 data (500 CGE genes). Reproduced when both correlations show tau falling away from Sncg (negative in (a), negative in (b) with distance) with one-sided p < 0.05; when the readings disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: In layer 5 Sst neurons (Sst Chodl excluded), morpho-electric properties vary continuously across the transcriptomic landscape, neighbouring t-types having similar rebound values.
claims.source: Results, Continuous phenotypic variation, paragraph 2; Figure 4b; Extended Data Figure 6i
claims.quote: Here we also found that morpho-electric properties varied continuously across the transcriptomic landscape, with neighbouring t-types consistently showing similar morphologies and similar rebound values (Fig. 4b ).
claims.criterion: The electrophysiological part only. As the code's room-temperature version of the Extended Data Fig. 6i inset (physiological-temperature.ipynb, cell 18), whose legend describes it as the correlation between transcriptomic and electrophysiological distances between Sst t-types with at least 5 cells, Sst Chodl left out. Layer 5 Sst cells, not excluded, all 17 features; per-t-type mean of the standardized 17 features; Euclidean distance; transcriptomic correlation distance over the 500 MGE genes of the 10x v2 data; Pearson r and its p over all pairs. The legend reports a p-value without giving it in the text. As a second reading named by the Results sentence, the same with the rebound alone (absolute difference of t-type mean rebound). Reproduced when r > 0 with p < 0.05 under the full-feature reading, the code's; the rebound-only reading is reported. The morphological part is not tested (morphology is not in the dandiset).

claims.statement: In layer 5 Pvalb neurons the shape of the axonal arbor changes continuously across the transcriptomic landscape, from shrub-like to horizontally and vertically elongated basket cells, with intermediate forms in between.
claims.source: Results, Continuous phenotypic variation, paragraph 5; Figure 4e
claims.quote: The shape of the axonal arbor showed continuous changes across the transcriptomic landscape (Fig. 4e ): small shrub-like basket cells, horizontally elongated basket cells, and vertically elongated classical basket cells were located in different corners of the t-SNE embedding, with intermediate morphologies in between.
claims.criterion: Shown only as a colour overlay; the paper gives no measure, so a test would be chosen by an agent. Recorded for coverage; the dandiset holds no morphology.

claims.statement: Between inhibitory families, separability is weaker with morphological features than with electrophysiological ones, and it is strongest with the two combined.
claims.source: Results, Distinct phenotypes of major families, paragraph 4; Figure 3b-d
claims.quote: The separability between inhibitory families was weaker than with electrophysiological features (Fig. 3d ). The between-family separability was strongest when we had combined electrophysiological and morphological features into a joint representation (Fig. 3c, d ), showing that these sets of properties are not redundant.
claims.criterion: The three representations of the Methods (t-SNE visualization) and the code (phenotype-tsne.ipynb), the kNN classifier as in fig3d-families-ephys. Morphology is the paper's published morphometric features and z-profiles (mini-atlas), combined with the dandiset's electrophysiology for the 628 cells with both. Separability is the mean of the diagonal of the confusion matrix, over the four inhibitory families for the first part and over all seven for the second (the paper names no summary; the mean diagonal is read from "mostly diagonal"). The Methods call the electrophysiological block of the combined representation "16-dimensional", while they build 17 PCs and the code stacks all 17; both are run, (a) the first 16 PCs and (b) all 17, and if they give different outcomes the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified. Excluded cells are left out (Methods); the code's handling, as in fig3d-families-ephys, is shown as a variant. Reproduced when the inhibitory mean is lower for morphology than for electrophysiology and the seven-family mean is highest for the combined representation.

claims.statement: Most t-types are classified into their own family from electrophysiology, but some lie between two families; many Sst Pvalb Calb2 neurons are classified as Pvalb, Lamp5 Egln3_1 neurons have Vip- and Sst-like firing, and Vip Mybpc1 neurons often have Sst-like firing.
claims.source: Results, Variability in individual t-types, paragraph 1; Figure 5a and legend
claims.quote: Most t-types could be unambiguously placed into the correct family (Fig. 5a ), but some t-types were in between two families. For example, many Sst Pvalb Calb2 neurons were classified as belonging to the Pvalb subclass on the basis of electrophysiology. ... Vip Mybpc1 neurons often had Sst -like firing.
claims.criterion: As the code does it (get_type_confusion in phenotype-tsne.ipynb), the classifier of fig3d-families-ephys applied to the cells of each t-type with at least 10 cells (Fig. 5a legend); the legend marks a t-type misclassified when more than 25% of its cells go to wrong families. Parts, (i) more than half of these t-types have at most 25% wrong; (ii) Sst Pvalb Calb2 has more than 25% classified as Pvalb; (iii) Lamp5 Egln3_1 has more than 25% classified as Vip and Sst together; (iv) for Vip Mybpc1 more than 25% classified as Sst, the t-type read as (a) any of the Vip Mybpc1 t-types with at least 10 cells or (b) all Vip Mybpc1 t-types pooled. Reproduced when all four hold (iv under one reading); partially reproduced when (i) and at least two others hold. A t-type below 10 cells is reported and its part not judged. Excluded cells are left out (Methods); the code's get_type_confusion keeps the 5 excluded cells in their t-types and as labelled neighbours, shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Many t-types have a normalized total variance of electrophysiological features well above that of k-means clusters; some, such as Pvalb Vipr2_2 (chandelier cells), appear homogeneous, while Vip Mybpc1_2 is highly variable.
claims.source: Results, Variability in individual t-types, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 5b
claims.quote: We found that many t-types had total variance substantially above the variances of the k -means clusters (Fig. 5b ) ... some of them, such as Pvalb Vipr2_2 (chandelier cells), appeared morpho-electrically homogeneous. By contrast, Vip Mybpc1_2 was marked as having high electrophysiological variability
claims.criterion: As the Methods (T-type variability analysis) and the code (get_type_variability and get_cluster_variability in phenotype-tsne.ipynb) do it, in the ephys representation. For each t-type with at least 10 cells, the sum of its per-dimension variances over that of all 1,320 cells; k-means (scikit-learn defaults, random_state 42, as the code) with K the number of such t-types on their cells pooled; the band from the smallest to the largest variance of clusters with at least 10 cells. "Substantially above" is read as above the band's top. "Many" is read as (a) at least a quarter or (b) at least a third of the t-types. Reproduced when "many" holds under one reading, Pvalb Vipr2_2 is not above the band (if it has at least 10 cells), and Vip Mybpc1_2 is above it; partially reproduced when two of the three hold. T-type members are cells with a t-type and no exclusion (Methods); the code's get_type_variability keeps the 5 excluded cells in their t-types, shown as a variant.

claims.statement: An alternative analysis using the entropy of Leiden cluster assignments within each t-type often highlights the same t-types as variable.
claims.source: Results, Variability in individual t-types, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 8g-l
claims.quote: an alternative analysis using entropies of Leiden clustering 35 often highlighted the same t-types as variable (Extended Data Fig. 8 ).
claims.criterion: As the Methods and the code (phenotype-tsne.ipynb, Leiden section) do it. kNN graph with k = 10 on the ephys representation (directed, scikit-learn kneighbors_graph), Leiden (leidenalg, RBConfigurationVertexPartition) at resolution 2, the code's "fine" setting for electrophysiology, 100 repetitions, repetition i with Leiden seed i and numpy seed i for the subsampling, each t-type with at least 10 cells subsampled to 10 cells, natural-log entropy of its cluster labels (scipy.stats.entropy); median entropy per t-type. The paper gives no measure of agreement with Fig. 5b; the reader's reading is a Spearman correlation across t-types between median entropy and the normalized variance of fig5b-ttype-variability, positive with one-sided p < 0.05. Reproduced when it holds.

claims.statement: Vip Mybpc1_2 neurons vary in input resistance, membrane time constant and rebound, and this variability is not random; cells with low rebound lie close to the boundary with the low-rebound Vip Sncg type.
claims.source: Results, Variability in individual t-types, paragraph 3; Figure 5c
claims.quote: This variability was not random: overlaying the rebound values on the t-SNE embedding (Fig. 5c ) showed that cells with low rebound were located close to the boundary with the low-rebound Vip Sncg type.
claims.criterion: Shown as a colour overlay, without a measure. Vip Mybpc1_2 cells (not excluded, all 17 features), positioned on the CGE reference t-SNE as in fig4a-vip-tau. Two readings of "close to the boundary with Vip Sncg", (a) the cell's distance in the embedding to the nearest reference cell of Vip Sncg, (b) the cell's Pearson correlation with the Vip Sncg mean expression of the 10x v2 data over the CGE assignment genes (higher is closer). Reproduced when, under both readings, rebound rises with distance from Vip Sncg (Spearman, one-sided p < 0.05), and the Vip Sncg median rebound is below the Vip Mybpc1_2 median; when the readings disagree, methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Sst Pvalb Calb2 cells vary widely in maximum firing rate, but high-firing cells are mostly grouped in one part of the transcriptomic landscape.
claims.source: Results, Variability in individual t-types, paragraph 3; Figure 5d
claims.quote: Similarly, Sst Pvalb Calb2 cells had high variability in terms of the maximum firing rate, but high-firing cells were mostly grouped in one part of the transcriptomic landscape (Fig. 5d ).
claims.criterion: Shown as a colour overlay, without a measure. Sst Pvalb Calb2 cells (not excluded, all 17 features), positioned on the MGE reference t-SNE of Fig. 1d as in fig4a-vip-tau; firing rate the maximum number of APs. Two readings of "grouped in one part", (a) the Spearman correlation between maximum AP count and the cell's position along the line from the Sst reference centroid to the Pvalb reference centroid, positive, and (b) cells above the t-type's median firing having a smaller mean pairwise embedding distance among themselves than random halves of the t-type (one-sided p < 0.05). Reproduced when both hold; when the readings disagree, methods_underspecified. Neither the paper nor the code (phenotype-tsne.ipynb, the Fig. 5d cell, which only colours the mapped cells by maximum number of APs on 10x-tsne-pvsst) gives a test, so the number of permutations in (b) is not the paper's; it is fixed here so that no random seed decides the outcome (answer of 2026-10-21). The p-value of (b) is exact, over all subsets of the same size, when there are at most 1,000,000 of them; otherwise it is estimated from 100,000 random subsets as (k + 1) / (N + 1). Reading (b) holds when p < 0.05 and the upper bound of the 95% binomial (Clopper-Pearson) interval of the estimate is also below 0.05; a p-value whose interval contains 0.05 does not show the grouping at p < 0.05, and (b) does not hold.

claims.statement: The 1,329 sequenced cells had median 1.3 million exonic and 0.7 million intronic reads (log10 mean 6.0 and 5.6) and 9,100 detected genes on average (s.d. 3,500).
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq of mouse primary motor cortex, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 2
claims.quote: The mRNA of these 1,329 cells was sequenced, yielding on average 1.3 million exonic and 0.7 million intronic reads (medians ... 6.0 ± 0.6 and 5.6 ± 0.8, respectively) and 9,100 ± 3,500 (mean ± s.d.) detected genes per cell
claims.criterion: Over the 1,329 sequenced cells; medians of exonic and intronic read counts per cell, and the mean number of detected genes, a detected gene being one with a non-zero exonic or intronic count (Methods, RNA sequencing of patched cells). Default 10% tolerances. Reproduced when all three values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: In the first round of mapping, 78 cells had a highest correlation below 0.4, 14 mapped to non-neural types and 5 were ambiguous between large groups, leaving 1,232 cells; four with excitatory RNA but inhibitory phenotype and one outside MOp were excluded, leaving 1,227.
claims.source: Methods, t-Type assignment, paragraphs 1 and 3
claims.quote: cells with the highest correlation below 0.4 (78 cells); cells that would be assigned to non-neural t-types, presumably owing to RNA contamination 51 (14 cells; see also Extended Data Fig. 2j–n ); cells with the highest correlation less than 0.02 above the maximal correlation in one of the other two large transcriptomic groups (5 cells). The remaining 1,232 cells passed quality control
claims.criterion: Default 10% tolerances, as the counts depend on the mapping. The code's metadata table lists 7 cells with exclusion reasons (6 mismatches between RNA and phenotype, 1 outside MOp); 2 of the 6 already failed quality control, which leaves the Methods' four contaminated cells and one outside MOp, so 1,232 less 5 gives 1,227. The final 1,227 is tested in fig1a-ttype-coverage.

claims.statement: Patch-seq expression profiles are most similar to the single-nucleus Smart-seq2 reference, and t-type assignments based on Smart-seq2 and 10x references agree well.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq of mouse primary motor cortex, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 2g-i
claims.quote: We found that Patch-seq expression profiles were most similar to the single-nucleus Smart-seq2 data (Extended Data Fig. 2g, h ). At the same time, there was good agreement between t-type assignments based on Smart-seq2 and those based on 10x reference data (Extended Data Fig. 2i )
claims.criterion: As the Methods (t-Type assignment) and the code (ttype-assignment.ipynb) do it. Reproduced when the median over cells of the maximal correlation is highest for the single-nucleus Smart-seq2 reference among the seven, and the single-cell Smart-seq2 and single-cell 10x v2 assignments fall in the same t-type for a majority of cells.

claims.statement: 646 neurons had staining good enough for reconstruction, 369 inhibitory and 269 excitatory among cells with a t-type; 73 t-types have at least one reconstructed neuron.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq of mouse primary motor cortex, paragraphs 1 and 3
claims.quote: Of these neurons, 646 had sufficient staining for their morphologies to be reconstructed.
claims.criterion: Counts of SWC files in the excitatory and inhibitory folders (the 30 dendrite-only Vip and Sncg reconstructions left out, Methods), matched to t-types; exact records.

claims.statement: A sparse reduced-rank regression predicting the 17 electrophysiological features from gene expression, with 25 genes and a rank-5 latent space, reaches a cross-validated R2 of 0.38, with cross-validated correlations of 0.90, 0.74 and 0.67 between the first three pairs of projections.
claims.source: Results, Distinct phenotypes of major families, paragraph 1; Figure 2; Methods, Reduced-rank regression
claims.quote: The selected model used 25 genes with a 5-dimensional latent space and achieved a cross-validated R 2 of 0.38. ... The cross-validated correlations between the first three pairs of projections were 0.90, 0.74, and 0.67, respectively.
claims.criterion: As the Methods and the code (reduced-rank-regression.ipynb, sparseRRR.py) do it. The 1,219 cells with all 17 features, a t-type and no exclusion; features standardized; genes the 1,000 most variable (Methods' selection on raw exon counts, threshold 32, decay 1.5); exon and intron counts over gene lengths summed, CPM, log2(x + 1), standardized. Rank 5, alpha 1, relaxed solutions; 10-fold cross-validation with the code's folds (one permutation with seed 42, contiguous folds); R2 and the correlations averaged over folds. For lambda, the Methods give 0.5 for the 25-gene fit, the code's cross-validation cell uses 0.45; both are run and the number of genes selected is reported. The Methods log-transform four features, the code's RRR notebook three (latency not); the Methods' choice is the main reading and the code's a variant. Reproduced when, under the main reading at either lambda, all four values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when R2 is and a correlation is not, or when only the variant matches.

claims.statement: A reduced-rank regression restricted to ion channel genes does not perform much worse than the full model, with cross-validated R2 0.33 and correlations 0.86, 0.71 and 0.56.
claims.source: Results, Distinct phenotypes of major families, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 5e, f
claims.quote: A reduced-rank regression model restricted to using only ion channel genes (Extended Data Fig. 5 ) did not perform much worse than the full model (cross-validated R 2 = 0.33 and correlations 0.86, 0.71, and 0.56, respectively, with regularization set to select 25 genes).
claims.criterion: As fig2-rrr, with genes the ion channel genes of HGNC group 177 (the code's ion-channel-genes-group-177.csv) with non-zero counts in at least 10 cells (307), lambda 0.303 (Methods and code), no variable-gene selection. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance under one of fig2-rrr's two log-transform readings.

claims.statement: The cDNA yield was not correlated with the recording hold time (Spearman correlation -0.01).
claims.source: Methods, Patch-seq recording procedures, last paragraph
claims.quote: The resulting cDNA yield was not correlated with the hold time (Spearman correlation −0.01).
claims.criterion: As the code does it (patch-seq-data-load.ipynb, last cell), the Spearman correlation over cells with both values between hold time and the log of cDNA yield (yield from the paper's metadata table; hold time from the dandiset where it is recorded, else from the same table). The default 10% of 0.01 is below any meaningful resolution for a correlation of about 1,300 cells, so the tolerance is 0.05, about one standard error (1 over the square root of n). A claim of absence; the paper gives no test, so it is judged on the value. Reproduced when the correlation is within tolerance.

claims.statement: The dandiset's cells can be matched by cell id to the paper's per-cell metadata table, and the matched records agree on what both describe.
claims.source: Data availability; the code's data/m1_patchseq_meta_data.csv (mini-atlas at commit 3bf98a524b8e48aa8647e1b9ae8f2351d9c712c9)
claims.criterion: Cells are matched by the files' cell id (DandiIcephysMetadata cell_id) to the table's Cell column. Reproduced when every dandiset cell matches a row and, for every matched cell, the records agree on mouse, slice, genotype, sex, Cre label, targeted and inferred layer, exon, intron and intergenic reads, sequencing batch, genes detected, t-type, family, t-type confidence and age; labels that differ only in spelling (PT for ET) are one label. Partially reproduced when at least 95% of cells match and agree; not reproduced otherwise. Fields of the files that agree with a differently named column of the table, and table columns absent from the files, are reported. The table supplies what the files lack (the exclusion of five cells with a t-type, the µm soma depths, hold time, cDNA yield) to the claims that list this claim under depends_on.

claims.statement: The electrophysiological features extracted from the dandiset's files with the paper's code match the paper's published per-cell feature table.
claims.source: Methods, Extraction of electrophysiological features; the code's data/m1_patchseq_ephys_features.csv and preprocess-ephys-files.ipynb (mini-atlas at commit 3bf98a524b8e48aa8647e1b9ae8f2351d9c712c9)
claims.criterion: Features are extracted from every file as in ed4-example-cell, and cells are matched by cell id. A value agrees when it equals the published one to a relative 1e-4, or both are undefined. Reproduced when every file matches a published row and at least 99% of cells agree on all 28 features other than the rheobase, which the code fits with RANSAC on random subsets without a seed; the rheobase agreement is reported. Partially reproduced when at least 90% agree; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Mice performed the delayed-response task at 77.6% correct on average, with 10.3% lick-early trials and 1.1% no-response trials.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 1
claims.quote: mean percent correct 77.6%; lick-early before ‘go’ cue 10.3%, no response 1.1%
claims.criterion: The paper does not say over which trials or sessions these are taken. Readings (a) all trials of all sessions pooled; (b) mean over sessions; (c) control (non-photoinhibition) trials only, pooled and per session. Percent correct excludes lick-early and no-response trials (Methods, Behavioral data analysis); lick-early and no-response are read as fractions of all trials (the paper does not give their denominator). Reproduced when all three values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Unilateral photoinhibition of ALM during the delay epoch biased responses to the ipsilateral side, lowering performance on contra trials and raising it on ipsi trials.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 1; Figure 1c
claims.quote: Unilateral photoinhibition of ALM during the delay epoch produced an ipsilateral response bias ... reducing performance for contralateral trials and increasing performance for ipsilateral trials ( P < 0.001; paired t -test, Fig. 1c )
claims.criterion: Per session, fraction correct (lick-early and no-response excluded) on contra and on ipsi trials, in control and in ALM photoinhibition trials (PV-IRES-Cre x Ai32 mice, left ALM; Methods, Photoinhibition). Two-sided paired t-test over sessions of photoinhibition against control, separately for contra and ipsi trials. Reproduced when contra performance is lower and ipsi performance higher under photoinhibition, both at p < 0.001; partially reproduced when the contra decrease holds at p < 0.001 and the ipsi increase does not.

claims.statement: Unilateral photoinhibition of thalALM during the delay epoch lowered performance on contra trials and caused a small, non-significant improvement on ipsi trials.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 3; Figure 1d
claims.quote: Similar to ALM, unilateral photoinhibition of thal ALM during the delay epoch reduced performance for contralateral trials and caused a small improvement in performance for ipsilateral trials ( P < 0.001 for contralateral trials, not significant for ipsilateral trials, paired t -test
claims.criterion: As fig1c-alm-photoinhibition-bias, for thalamus photoinhibition through an optical fibre over VM/VAL in Gad2-IRES-Cre mice with ChR2 in TRN (Methods, Photoinhibition). Reproduced when contra performance is lower under photoinhibition at p < 0.001 (paired t-test over sessions); the ipsi change and its p-value are reported (the paper finds it not significant, p >= 0.05).

claims.statement: Photostimulating TRN axons in thalamus of Gad2-IRES-Cre mice reduced thalALM spike rates, recorded near VM/VAL, to 67.8% of control during the delay epoch.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 2c
claims.quote: Photostimulating axonal terminals of TRN GABAergic neurons in thalamus reduced spike rates in thal ALM (recorded near VM/VAL, to 67.8% during the delay epoch
claims.criterion: Putative thalamic units recorded with the optrode in Gad2-IRES-Cre mice (Extended Data Fig. 2c, n = 26, 41 and 17 at 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0 mm from the fibre). The legend gives the measure as "mean spike rate during photoinhibition divided by mean spike rate during control". The window is open, readings (W1) the whole photostimulus (delay onset to delay end, as "during the delay epoch" says), (W2) 20 to 120 ms after photostimulus onset (convention P). Ratio readings Q1 to Q3 and trial readings T1, T2 of convention P. Reproduced when the value is within tolerance under one reading; the value per distance group is reported.

claims.statement: In VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice, thalamus photoinhibition reduced activity 0.5 to 1.1 mm from the fibre tip to 15.9% of control.
claims.source: Methods, Photoinhibition, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 2d
claims.quote: Photoinhibition reduced activity (0.5-1.1 mm from the tip of the optical fiber) to 15.9 ± 9.3%
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the paper's stated spread (called SEM in the Methods; the legend of Extended Data Fig. 2d calls its error bars standard deviations). Putative thalamic units recorded with the optrode in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice, 0.5 to 1.1 mm from the fibre (Extended Data Fig. 2d, n = 34, 42, 38). Measure, windows W1 and W2, and readings as gad2-thalamus-reduction. Reproduced when within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Small doses of muscimol infused near VM/VAL produced an ipsilateral bias in licking responses, while infusions outside thalALM, anterior or dorsal (1.1 to 1.6 mm anterior or 1.6 to 1.9 mm dorsal to VM/VAL in the Results; about 0.3 to 0.8 mm anterior to VM/VAL and 0.2 to 0.5 mm dorsal to MD in the legends), did not, even at ten-fold higher doses.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 3
claims.quote: Inhibition near VM/VAL produced ipsilateral bias in the licking response ( Extended Data Fig. 3a, b ). Inhibition outside of thal ALM (1.1 - 1.6 mm anterior or 1.6-1.9 dorsal to VM/VAL) did not cause ipsilateral bias, even at 10-fold higher doses
claims.criterion: Performance change is fraction correct over the 100 trials after infusion relative to the 100 trials before, separately for contra and ipsi trials, compared with the control condition (buffer, or the pause without infusion) by Student's t-test (Methods, Behavioral data analysis; Extended Data Fig. 3b). The legend does not say which side carries the star; open, readings (s1) the contra change near VM/VAL is lower than control, (s2) the ipsi change is higher than control, each at p < 0.05. Reproduced when the bias near VM/VAL holds under one reading, and neither anterior (n = 4 sites) nor dorsal (n = 4 sites) infusions show it against control at p < 0.05 under that reading. Open, which control, readings (a) buffer infusions, (b) pauses without infusion, (c) both pooled. The doses differ between Results (1.8 to 5.9 ng) and the legend (1.5 to 5 ng); and the distances outside VM/VAL differ between Results (1.1 to 1.6 mm anterior, 1.6 to 1.9 mm dorsal) and the legends (0.3 to 0.8 mm anterior, 0.2 to 0.5 mm dorsal of MD); sites are taken as the dataset labels them.

claims.statement: Of 1214 ALM units, 1006 were putative pyramidal neurons (spike width > 0.6 ms), 166 putative fast-spiking (< 0.4 ms) and 42 unclassified; the spike-width distribution was bimodal.
claims.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 4b
claims.quote: In ALM, 1214 single units were recorded across 57 behavioral sessions. ... units with width < 0.4 ms were defined as putative fast-spiking (FS) neurons (166/1214) and units with width > 0.6 ms as putative pyramidal neurons (1006/1214)
claims.criterion: Spike width is the trough-to-peak interval of the mean waveform (Methods). Bimodality is judged from the histogram, with the counts below 0.4 ms, between 0.4 and 0.6 ms, and above 0.6 ms reported. Class readings P1 and P2 of convention C; every claim that selects units by class runs both. Reproduced when the three counts are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Most ALM putative pyramidal neurons (70%, 704/1006) distinguished trial types; 145 had preparatory activity only, 272 peri-movement selectivity only and 287 both.
claims.source: Results, Preparatory activity in thalamus, paragraph 1; Figure 2e
claims.quote: For a majority of neurons, activity differed across trial types (70%, 704/1006; P < 0.05, t -test; Methods). ... subsets of neurons showed selective preparatory activity ( Fig. 2b , left column; Fig. 2e , 145/1006), selective peri-movement activity during the response epoch ( Fig. 2b , right column; Fig. 2e , 272/1006), or both ( Fig. 2b , middle column; Fig. 2e , 287/1006)
claims.criterion: Putative pyramidal ALM units. Whether photoinhibition trials enter is not said; readings (a) control trials only, (b) all trials. Selectivity by convention S, under response-epoch readings R1 and R2, t-test readings (a) and (b) and outcome readings c1 and c2. Reproduced when all four counts are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Approximately equal numbers of selective ALM neurons preferred contra and ipsi movements.
claims.source: Results, Preparatory activity in thalamus, paragraph 1; Figure 2e
claims.quote: Approximately equal numbers of neurons preferred contra- or ipsi-lateral movements ( Fig. 2e )
claims.criterion: Preference by total spike count over the three epochs (convention S), among the selective neurons of fig2e-alm-selectivity. The paper gives no test, number or threshold, so the judgement is open; readings (a) a two-sided binomial test of the contra count against one half does not reject at p < 0.05; (b) the contra fraction lies within 10% of one half (0.45 to 0.55), the registry's default tolerance on the implied value. Reproduced when both readings hold, not reproduced when neither does, methods_underspecified when they differ. The counts and the contra fraction are reported, under each reading of fig2e-alm-selectivity.

claims.statement: Of 790 thalamic units, 672 were putative thalamic neurons (spike width > 0.5 ms) and 313 lay within 0.4 mm of the VM/VAL centre; 295 VM/VAL units were analysed.
claims.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis, paragraph 3; Results, Preparatory activity in thalamus, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 4e
claims.quote: In thalamus, 790 single units were recorded across 73 behavioral sessions. ... Units with spike width > 0.5 ms were selected as putative thalamic neurons (672/790) ... units within 0.4 mm from the VM/VAL center ... were scored as VM/VAL neurons (313/790)
claims.criterion: Width as for alm-unit-classes (readings P1, P2 of convention C; the counts 672 and 295 rest on the width rule, so P3 does not apply to them); location under readings L1 and L2. The 295 of the Results are read as the units that pass both the width and the location rule (the paper does not say; a reading, since 295 is below both 313 and 672). Reproduced when all four counts are within tolerance under one location reading.

claims.statement: A majority of VM/VAL neurons (69%, 204/295) distinguished trial types, a fraction indistinguishable from ALM; 43 had preparatory activity only, 82 peri-movement selectivity only and 79 both, a distribution similar to ALM.
claims.source: Results, Preparatory activity in thalamus, paragraph 2; Figure 2f
claims.quote: A majority of VM/VAL neurons discriminated trial types (69%, 204/295; indistinguishable from ALM, chi-squared test, P = 0.79). ... VM/VAL neurons exhibited similar selectivity and time-course to ALM (chi-squared test, P > 0.5)
claims.criterion: VM/VAL units of thalamus-unit-classes, selectivity as in fig2e-alm-selectivity, same readings. Chi-squared tests (2 x 2 for selective against not; for the types, readings (i) 2 x 4 with non-selective as a class, (ii) 2 x 3 among selective neurons). Reproduced when the counts are within tolerance under one reading and neither chi-squared test finds a difference at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Strong photoinhibition of thalALM (VGAT-ChR2-EYFP) decreased ALM activity to 6% of control, inhibiting 309 of 314 neurons (155 significantly) and significantly activating none.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 3c
claims.quote: Thal ALM photoinhibition decreased ALM activity to 6% of control, reducing activity in nearly all neurons ( Fig. 3c , 309/314 inhibited, 3/314 activated, 155/314 significantly inhibited, 0/314 significantly activated, t -test, P < 0.05)
claims.criterion: ALM putative pyramidal units recorded during ipsilateral thalamus photoinhibition in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice, at 10 mW ("Laser power at the tip of optical fiber 10mW, n = 314 cells", Extended Data Fig. 2e), at least 5 photoinhibition trials. The text names only VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice for this experiment (Results, "using VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice"; Methods, Photoinhibition, lists PV-IRES-Cre x Ai32 for ALM photoinhibition only, "Fig. 1 and 6 , Extended Data Fig. 8 , 10"), so sessions of PV-IRES-Cre x Ai32 mice with thalamic photostimulation are not a reading; they may be shown as a variant, not judged (answer of 2026-10-20). Window, pooling and tests by convention P, under readings T1, T2 and Q1 to Q3. Reproduced when all values are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when, under every reading, activity falls, inhibited neurons outnumber activated ones and none is significantly activated, but some value is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: Thalamus photoinhibition reduced ALM activity across all cortical layers.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 3d
claims.quote: across all cortical layers ( Fig. 3d )
claims.criterion: Unit depth as recorded (manipulator reading verified by histology, Methods). The figure plots the number of modulated neurons by depth; the text gives neither its bins nor layer boundaries, and does not say whether "modulated" means the sign of the change or a significant change. The finding as worded is a reduction of activity at all depths. Open, readings for bins (a) 100 um, (b) 200 um, and for modulated (m1) sign of the change, (m2) significant by convention P. Reproduced when, under every reading, in every depth bin that holds neurons the inhibited neurons outnumber the activated ones; not reproduced when some bin fails under every reading; methods_underspecified otherwise. Counts per bin and the population rate ratio per bin are reported.

claims.statement: ALM neurons with preparatory activity, peri-movement selectivity or both were equally inhibited by thalamus photoinhibition.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 3b
claims.quote: neurons showing preparatory activity, peri-movement selectivity or both were equally inhibited; Fig. 3b , P > 0.2, t -test
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, two-sided t-tests between each pair of the three groups (preparatory only, peri-movement only, both; convention S) of the neurons of fig3-alm-collapse. The measure of inhibition is not named; readings (a) each neuron's rate under photoinhibition over control, (b) the difference of rates, both in the window of convention P. Reproduced when no pair differs at p < 0.05 under both measures; not reproduced when a pair does under both; methods_underspecified when the measures disagree. Group means and the p-values are reported, and whether they exceed 0.2.

claims.statement: Strong photoinhibition in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice abolished thalALM activity nearly completely, to 2% of control.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 3f
claims.quote: Photoinhibition abolished thal ALM activity nearly completely (to 2 % of control without photoinhibition) ( Fig. 3f )
claims.criterion: Thalamic units recorded during thalamus photoinhibition in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice (Fig. 3f, n = 148). Which units are meant is open, readings (a) all putative thalamic units of those recordings, (b) those in VM/VAL (convention L). Window and readings by convention P (the Methods use 20 to 120 ms for Fig. 3). Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Photoinhibition reduced thalALM activity 2.5 ms after photostimulus onset, and ALM spike rates were reduced 8.2 ms after onset, a latency difference consistent with direct thalamocortical drive.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 3; Figure 3e, f
claims.quote: Photoinhibition reduced thal ALM activity 2.5 ± 0.8 ms after photostimulus onset (mean ± SEM, activity reduction onset detected by 3 × std, Fig. 3f ). Hyperpolarization of ALM neurons and reduction of ALM spike rates were detected 7.9 ± 1.7 ms and 8.2 ± 1.5ms after photostimulus onset
claims.criterion: Onsets by convention O (readings O1, O2) on the populations of fig3f-thalamus-silenced (148) and fig3-alm-collapse (314), trial readings T1 and T2. Tolerances are the paper's SEMs. Reproduced when both onsets are within tolerance under one reading and the ALM onset is later than the thalamic one. The Vm onset (7.9 ms) is tested in wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization.

claims.statement: During the delay epoch the mean membrane potential of ALM neurons was close to spike threshold, 12.7 mV below it on average.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 2
claims.quote: the average membrane potential of ALM neurons was close to the spike threshold during the delay epoch (action potential threshold - mean basal membrane potential = 12.7 ± 0.7 mV; mean ± SEM, n = 60 cells)
claims.criterion: Whole-cell ALM recordings with more than 20 behavioural trials (Methods). The text does not define the spike threshold; it is read as the Vm at the kink of convention V, the only spike-onset rule the Methods give; per cell, mean threshold minus mean basal Vm, then the mean over cells. The basal Vm window differs between Results ("during the delay epoch") and Methods (0 to 0.5 s before trial onset); readings (a) the Methods window, (b) the delay epoch of control trials, spikes clipped. Reproduced when the value is within tolerance under one reading. Tolerance is the paper's SEM.

claims.statement: Thalamus photoinhibition hyperpolarized ALM neurons by 18.7 mV, preventing spiking, with an onset 7.9 ms after photostimulus onset.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 3g, 4b, c
claims.quote: Thal ALM photoinhibition caused hyperpolarization (Membrane potential, control trials –photoinhibition trials, -18.7 ± 1.1 mV; measured for 100 ms, starting 20 ms after photostimulus onset; mean ± SEM, n = 16 cells), preventing ALM neurons from spiking
claims.criterion: Whole-cell ALM recordings during thalamus photoinhibition in behaving VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice (n = 16). Mean Vm (spikes clipped, convention V) 20 to 120 ms after photostimulus onset, photoinhibition trials minus control trials, mean over cells. The text writes "control trials -photoinhibition trials" with a negative value; the sign is read as hyperpolarization. Onset by convention V, readings V1 and V2. Photostimulus onset (answer of 2026-10-20). The Methods put it "at the beginning of the delay epoch", which is 1.3 s after the onset of pole movement and 0.1 s after the pole started to retract, the pole travelling 0.2 s, staying 1 s and retracting 0.2 s (Methods, Behavior), so 0.1 s before retraction is complete. The paper does not say which of these events the files' pole_in_time and pole_out_time mark, nor give the laser time in these recordings. Readings (E) 1.3 s after pole_in_time, pole_in_time read as the onset of pole movement; (M) 0.1 s after pole_out_time, pole_out_time read as the start of retraction. Placing the onset from the Vm change itself is not a reading. The onset latency of 7.9 ms needs the true laser time, which no reading gives. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance (the paper's SEMs) under one reading.

claims.statement: The hyperpolarization of ALM neurons during thalamus photoinhibition was caused mainly by a loss of excitation, not by an increase in inhibition; it was larger with negative current injection.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 5c-h
claims.quote: Manipulating the membrane potential during recording revealed that hyperpolarization was mainly caused by a reduction in excitation, not an increase in inhibition
claims.criterion: Non-behaving Gad2-IRES-Cre mice with ChR2 in TRN (Extended Data Fig. 5c-h; n = 14 cells without, 9 with negative and 6 with positive current injection). Per cell and current condition, Vm in control and Vm change under photoinhibition, both 100 to 120 ms after light onset; cells with positive and negative injection pooled (cells without injection left out, as the legend does). Linear regression of the change on control Vm; p from a bootstrap of the slope. Resampling unit is open, readings (a) cells, (b) cell-condition points; iterations 1000 or 10000 (Methods, Statistics), a standard choice. Reproduced when the slope is positive with p < 0.0001 under one reading, partially reproduced when positive with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Photoinhibition of M1 during the delay epoch caused only a slight hyperpolarization (3.3 mV) and a small drop in spike rate (1.4 spikes per s) in ALM neurons.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 3; Figure 4d-f
claims.quote: direct photoinhibition of M1 during the delay epoch ... caused only a slight hyperpolarization of the membrane potential and spike rates of ALM neurons (-3.3 ± 1.0 mV; -1.4 ± 0.6 spikes per s; mean ± SEM, n = 11 cells)
claims.criterion: Whole-cell ALM recordings during M1 photoinhibition (n = 11), as wc-thalamus-hyperpolarization, window 20 to 120 ms after photostimulus onset (Fig. 4c legend, same format for f). Spike rate from the spikes detected in the whole-cell trace. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance (the paper's SEMs).

claims.statement: Photoinhibition of contralateral ALM barely changed the membrane potential of ALM neurons (1.4 mV).
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 4; Figure 4g-i
claims.quote: photoinhibiting contralateral ALM, the anatomically strongest input to ALM, barely changed membrane potential (-1.4 ± 0.5 mV; mean ± SEM, n = 9 cells)
claims.criterion: As wc-m1-small-effect, for contralateral ALM photoinhibition (n = 9).

claims.statement: thalALM drives ALM more strongly than M1 or contralateral ALM, the other reciprocally connected structures tested.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 4; Figure 4b vs 4e, h
claims.quote: Altogether thal ALM drives ALM directly and more strongly than other reciprocally connected structures (cf. Fig. 4b vs Fig. 4e,h )
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test for this comparison ("cf." the figure panels). Readings (a) the mean Vm change (20 to 120 ms) under thalamus photoinhibition is more negative than under M1 and under contralateral ALM photoinhibition; (b) as (a), with each difference significant by a two-sided t-test over cells at p < 0.05, the test the paper uses elsewhere. Reproduced when both readings hold, not reproduced when neither does, methods_underspecified when they differ.

claims.statement: The latency of ALM hyperpolarization is too short for the thalamus to M1 to ALM pathway; thalamus photoinhibition hyperpolarized M1 neurons after 11.0 ms and M1 photoinhibition hyperpolarized ALM neurons after 13.9 ms, so that pathway would give a latency difference above 14.3 ms against the 5.4 ms observed.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 6e-g
claims.quote: The thalamus → M1 → ALM pathway would produce a latency difference of > 14.3 ms, too slow by > 9 ms to explain the hyperpolarization in ALM
claims.criterion: Onsets by convention V (readings V1, V2) for whole-cell M1 neurons during thalamus photoinhibition (n = 9) and ALM neurons during M1 photoinhibition (n = 11), Extended Data Fig. 6e, f; tolerances are the paper's SEMs. The pathway latency difference is (M1 onset minus thalamic silencing onset) plus (ALM onset after M1 photoinhibition minus cortical silencing onset), as Extended Data Fig. 6e, f compute it (8.5 + 5.8 = 14.3 ms). Reproduced when both onsets are within tolerance under one reading and the pathway difference exceeds the direct one (ALM Vm onset minus thalamic silencing onset).

claims.statement: Photoactivating thalamus in Olig3-cre x Ai32 mice depolarized ALM neurons after 3.6 ms, an estimate of the thalamocortical conduction delay.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 6c
claims.quote: The time between photostimulation onset and depolarization onset was 3.6 ± 1.1 ms ( n = 9 cells)
claims.criterion: Whole-cell ALM recordings in non-behaving Olig3-cre x Ai32 mice during thalamus photoactivation (10 mW), onset of depolarization by convention V (readings V1, V2) as the Methods say ("a similar procedure"). Reproduced when within tolerance (the paper's SEM) under one reading.

claims.statement: A model ALM neuron with 200 thalamic inputs predicts at least 1.8 ms between full loss of thalamic input and a detectable change in membrane potential.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 6d; Supplementary information
claims.quote: Even when 100% of the input neurons were inhibited, we expect to observe latency of 1.8 ± 0.7 ms
claims.criterion: A simulation, not a test on recorded data; its parameters are in the Supplementary information, which is not in the text read. Cannot be specified from the text; recorded so the finding is covered.

claims.statement: Weak thalamus photoinhibition (20-fold weaker, 0.5 mW) significantly changed the spike rate of 83 of 160 ALM neurons, with a mean reduction of 1.2 spikes per s; 39% of the changed neurons (32/83) increased their rate.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus contributes to selectivity in ALM, paragraph 1; Figure 5b
claims.quote: 83 /160 of ALM neurons showed statistically significant changes in mean spike rate during photoinhibition ( t -test; average reduction of spike rate, 1.2 ± 0.2 spikes per s, mean ± SEM, n = 160; Fig. 5a, b ). A substantial fraction of these neurons (39%, 32/83) showed increases in spike rate
claims.criterion: ALM putative pyramidal units recorded during weak thalamus photoinhibition (VGAT-ChR2-EYFP, 0.5 mW) with at least 25 photoinhibition trials. Rates over 1300 ms from photostimulus onset (Fig. 5b legend), contra and ipsi trials pooled; trial readings T1, T2; significance by two-sided t-test at P < 0.05 (convention P, t-test readings of convention S). Reproduced when all values are within tolerance under one reading (the reduction's tolerance is the paper's SEM).

claims.statement: Weak thalamus photoinhibition reduced the selectivity of ALM neurons, both contra- and ipsi-preferring; the change in selectivity was anti-correlated with selectivity (slope -0.33, r = -0.75), even in neurons without a change in mean rate.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus contributes to selectivity in ALM, paragraph 1; Figure 5c; Extended Data Figure 7a, b
claims.quote: This unequal spike rate change reduced the selectivity of ALM neurons in both contra- and ipsi- preferring neurons ( Fig. 5c, d and Extended Data Fig. 7a, b )
claims.criterion: The neurons of fig5-weak-photoinhibition-rates with rates above 2 spikes per s in control and in photoinhibition (Methods, n = 73). Selectivity is contra minus ipsi rate (convention S), in control; the Fig. 5c legend gives no window, read as the 1300 ms window of Fig. 5b; its change is photoinhibition selectivity minus control selectivity; ordinary least squares of change on control selectivity. Trials, open, readings (a) correct only in both conditions (Methods, selectivity), (b) correct only in control and all outcomes under photoinhibition. Reproduced when slope and r are within tolerance under one reading. The paper gives no p-value for this regression. For Extended Data Fig. 7a, b (contra- and ipsi-preferring defined by a delay-epoch t-test, P < 0.05), the mean absolute selectivity under photoinhibition is lower than in control in each group; reported, and required for reproduced. For "even in neurons without a change in mean rate" (Fig. 5c white circles), the slope among the neurons not significantly modulated is reported; the paper gives no test for it.

claims.statement: The data are inconsistent with linear network models with specific or non-specific thalamocortical connectivity, but do not exclude non-linear models of either kind.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus contributes to selectivity in ALM, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 7c-e; Supplementary information
claims.quote: Our data are inconsistent with linear models with either specific (like-to-like) or non-specific (all-to-all) thalamocortical connectivity. However, our data do not exclude non-linear models
claims.criterion: A modelling result; its equations and parameters are in the Supplementary information, which is not in the text read. Cannot be specified from the text; recorded so the finding is covered.

claims.statement: ALM photoinhibition decreased the activity of VM/VAL neurons to 25% of control, inhibiting 190 of 201 neurons (139 significantly) and significantly activating none.
claims.source: Results, ALM drives thalamic preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 6c
claims.quote: ALM photoinhibition decreased activity in a majority of VM/VAL neurons (to 25% of control; 190/201 inhibited, 11/201 activated, 139/201 significantly inhibited, 0/201 significantly activated, P < 0.05, t -test, Fig. 6c )
claims.criterion: VM/VAL putative thalamic units (convention L) recorded during ipsilateral ALM photoinhibition (PV-IRES-Cre x Ai32), at least 5 photoinhibition trials; window, pooling and tests by convention P, readings T1, T2, Q1 to Q3 and L1, L2. Reproduced when all values are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when, under every reading, activity falls, inhibited neurons outnumber activated ones and none is significantly activated, but some value is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: VM/VAL neurons selective during the sample, delay or response epochs were equally inhibited by ALM photoinhibition.
claims.source: Results, ALM drives thalamic preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 6b
claims.quote: VM/VAL neurons selective during sample, delay or response epochs were equally inhibited ( Fig. 6b , P > 0.2, t -test)
claims.criterion: As fig3b-selectivity-types-equally-inhibited, on the neurons of fig6c-vmval-reduced. The groups are open, readings (a) preparatory only, peri-movement only and both (convention S, as for ALM); (b) selective in the sample, in the delay and in the response epoch (overlapping groups), as the sentence reads. A claim of absence; reproduced when no pair differs at p < 0.05 under every reading, not reproduced when a pair does under every reading, methods_underspecified otherwise.

claims.statement: The few VM/VAL neurons not changed by ALM photoinhibition were significantly less selective in the delay epoch, while neurons strongly reduced by it carried trial-type information; the change of rate and delay selectivity were negatively related (regression slope -0.73, r -0.33).
claims.source: Results, ALM drives thalamic preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 6c bottom
claims.quote: A small fraction of neurons in VM/VAL was not changed by ALM photoinhibition. These neurons also showed significantly less selectivity ( Fig. 6c , P = 0.002, t -test)
claims.criterion: Neurons of fig6c-vmval-reduced, split by the significance of their change (convention P). Delay-epoch selectivity on correct control trials; its form is open, readings (a) absolute contra minus ipsi rate, (b) preferred minus non-preferred rate, preference by total count over the three epochs (convention S). Two-sided t-test of delay selectivity, significantly against not significantly modulated. Regression of selectivity on rate change (photoinhibition minus control, convention P window); the axis order is open, readings (i) selectivity on change, (ii) change on selectivity. Reproduced when, under one reading, the unmodulated group is less selective at p < 0.05 and the slope and r are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the group difference holds and the correlation is negative but slope or r is out of tolerance. The paper gives no p-value for the regression.

claims.statement: The reduction of thalamic activity by ALM photoinhibition was mainly limited to VM/VAL; neurons within 1.0 mm of the VM/VAL centre were inhibited to 36% of control, and neurons farther away less.
claims.source: Results, ALM drives thalamic preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis, paragraph 3; Figure 6d; Extended Data Figure 8b, c
claims.quote: neurons within 1.0 mm from VM/VAL center showed robust inhibition (to 36% of control activity during the first 100 ms inhibition
claims.criterion: Thalamic units recorded during ALM photoinhibition, at least 5 photoinhibition trials, grouped by distance from the VM/VAL centre (Extended Data Fig. 8b; convention L, reading L2, or the dataset's coordinates with any centre it documents). The legend says "thalamic neurons"; open, readings (u1) putative thalamic units (width > 0.5 ms), (u2) all units. The window is "the first 100 ms" of photoinhibition (Methods; Extended Data Fig. 8c), open, readings (w1) 20 to 120 ms after photostimulus onset (convention P), (w2) 0 to 100 ms. Ratio and trials by convention P. Reproduced when the within-1.0 mm value and the group counts are within tolerance under one reading and the ratio is lower below 0.5 mm than at 1.0 mm or more.

claims.statement: Photoinhibiting vibrissal M1 did not reduce thalALM activity (Results), or reduced VM/VAL activity less than ALM photoinhibition in the same neurons (Extended Data Fig. 8g legend).
claims.source: Results, ALM drives thalamic preparatory activity, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 8f, g
claims.quote: photoinhibiting the nearby vibrissal primary motor cortex (vM1), which projects to parts of VA/VL, did not cause a reduction in thal ALM activity ( Extended Data Fig. 8d-g )
claims.criterion: VM/VAL units recorded with interleaved ALM and vM1 photoinhibition (Extended Data Fig. 8f, g; n = 46 cells, 3 mice). The paper names no test for either form, and its legend ("produced less reduction") is weaker than the Results ("did not cause a reduction"). The window is that of convention P, a reading (the legends show PSTHs only). Parts (a) absence, from the Results, a two-sided paired t-test over neurons of rates under vM1 photoinhibition against control finds no reduction at p < 0.05 (the population paired test is a reading; the paper's t-tests are per neuron); (b) comparison, from the legend, the reduction under vM1 is smaller than under ALM photoinhibition, by a two-sided paired t-test over neurons at p < 0.05 (a reading, as for a). Reproduced when (a) and (b) hold; partially reproduced when only (b) holds; not reproduced when (b) fails. The ratios under vM1 and ALM photoinhibition (Q1 to Q3) are reported either way. Site and power (answer of 2026-10-20). The text gives no coordinate or power for vM1 photoinhibition (Supplementary Table 1, not in the text read). The only vM1 coordinate in the text is an Allen Brain Atlas tracer injection (Extended Data Fig. 8e, "AP1, ML 0.75"), not the photostimulation site, and the paper does not say in what frame the galvo positions are given, so which deposited condition is vM1 is not given by the paper. The only power the Methods give for cortical photoinhibition in Extended Data Fig. 8 is 1.5 mW, so the ALM condition is ALM at 1.5 mW (convention P); ALM at a power matched to the vM1 condition is a variant, not judged.

claims.statement: After ALM photoinhibition onset, ALM pyramidal neurons were silenced after 8.1 ms and VM/VAL activity reduced after 10.9 ms; SNr neurons changed later, after 15.2 ms.
claims.source: Figure 6e; Extended Data Figure 6f; Extended Data Figure 10d
claims.quote: SNr neurons were affected by ALM photoinhibition with a relatively long latency difference (15.2 ± 4.6 ms, mean ± SEM, P < 0.05, t -test), longer than for reducing thal ALM activity (10.9 ± 2.9 ms; Fig. 6e )
claims.criterion: Onsets by convention O (O1, O2) for ALM putative pyramidal neurons during ALM photoinhibition (n = 256), VM/VAL neurons (n = 201) and the significantly modulated SNr neurons (Extended Data Fig. 10d, 48 inhibited; whether the 23 activated enter, with sign flipped, is open, readings (a) inhibited only, (b) both). The legend calls the SNr 15.2 ms and VM/VAL 10.9 ms values a "latency difference", while Extended Data Fig. 6f uses 8.1 ms as the time to silence cortex; open, readings (d1) onsets from photostimulus onset, (d2) onsets minus the ALM silencing onset for SNr and VM/VAL. Tolerances are the paper's SEMs. The paper does not say what its t-test of SNr against VM/VAL onsets compares; the onsets and their bootstrap SEMs are reported and the outcome does not rest on that test. Reproduced when the three onsets are within tolerance under one reading and SNr is latest.

claims.statement: ALM photoinhibition changed only a small fraction of SNr GABAergic neurons (48/181 significantly inhibited, 23/181 activated), more decreasing than increasing, and reduced SNr activity overall by 3.6 spikes per s (8.3%), which argues against SNr mediating the thalamic reduction.
claims.source: Results, ALM drives thalamic preparatory activity, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 10c
claims.quote: Photoinhibition of ALM changed only a relatively small fraction of SNr neurons (48/181 significantly inhibited; 23/181 significantly activated, P < 0.05, t -test,). Moreover, neurons that decreased their activity were more numerous than neurons that increased their activity (bootstrapping over neurons, P < 0.01, Methods). Overall, inhibiting ALM reduced SNr activity by 3.6 spikes per second (8.3% of control activity
claims.criterion: SNr units with trough-to-peak width below 0.45 ms (Methods; readings P1, P2 of convention C); window and tests by convention P (readings T1, T2), all such units (n = 181; the minimum of 5 photoinhibition trials is not stated for SNr, readings (a) none, (b) 5). Bootstrap as the Methods describe, resampling neurons with replacement, 1000 or 10000 rounds, p the fraction of rounds with up-modulated at least as many as down-modulated. Reproduced when the values are within tolerance under one reading and p < 0.01.

claims.statement: Putative GABAergic SNr neurons had high spike rates (40.9 spikes per s) compared with the other SNr units (23.4), and most of them (152/181) were selective for trial type, like ALM and VM/VAL.
claims.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis, paragraph 4; Extended Data Figure 4j, 10b
claims.quote: These units have high spike rates (40.9 ± 21.5, mean ± SD, n = 181). For comparison, neurons with longer spike widths have lower spikes rates (23.4 ± 17.0, mean ± SD, n = 46)
claims.criterion: Mean rate per unit over the session (the window is not given; readings (a) whole session, (b) all trials from trial start to end), then mean over units. Selectivity by convention S (readings R1, R2). Tolerances are 10% of the values, as the stated SDs describe spread over units, not uncertainty of the mean. Reproduced when all values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: ALM is reciprocally connected with ipsilateral thalamic nuclei, most consistently the VM/VAL complex; a retrograde injection into ALM labelled 17375 thalamic neurons, against 38062 in contralateral ALM and 26599 in M1.
claims.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 1d, f
claims.quote: Within thal ALM , the VM/VAL complex was most extensively and consistently labeled in experiments involving injections of multiple types of anterograde and retrograde tracers into ALM
claims.criterion: Histology (tracer injections, cell counts registered to the Allen CCF). The dataset is described as electrophysiology, behaviour and optogenetics; whether it holds these images is for the author to find.

claims.statement: In ALM and in VM/VAL, population selectivity emerged in the sample epoch and increased throughout the delay epoch; it peaked at the beginning of the response epoch in ALM and during the response epoch in VM/VAL.
claims.source: Results, Preparatory activity in thalamus, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 2e, f; Extended Data Figure 4c, f
claims.quote: Selectivity for movements emerged in the sample epoch, increased throughout the delay epoch, and reached a maximum at the beginning of the response epoch ... Selectivity emerged in the sample epoch, increased throughout the delay epoch, and reached a maximum during the response epoch
claims.criterion: Population selectivity as in the Extended Data Fig. 4c legend (applied to VM/VAL by 4f) on correct trials, contra and ipsi. Whether photoinhibition trials enter is not said (the Extended Data Fig. 4c legend names no trials; the Methods say only "Only trials in which mice correctly reported pole locations were included to compute selectivity"; answer of 2026-10-20); readings (t1) correct control trials only, (t2) all correct trials, as for fig2e-alm-selectivity. Each neuron's preferred trial type from spike counts in half of the trials, selectivity as preferred minus non-preferred rate in the other half, 200 ms averaging window, SEM by bootstrapping over neurons. The neurons entering are not said; readings (a) all ALM putative pyramidal and all VM/VAL neurons, (b) the selective neurons of fig2e-alm-selectivity and fig2f-vmval-selectivity. How the halves are drawn is open; a random split is a standard choice. The paper gives no test; "emerged" is read as the mean selectivity exceeding twice its bootstrap SEM (a standard choice) within the sample epoch, "increased" as the last 200 ms of the delay exceeding the first 200 ms, and the maximum is located in time. Reproduced when, under one reading, both areas show emergence in the sample epoch and the increase over the delay, and the maximum falls in the response epoch (ALM within its first 200 ms is reported against "at the beginning").

claims.statement: GABAergic neurons in ALM do not project to thalALM, so ALM photoinhibition does not inhibit thalamus directly.
claims.source: Results, ALM drives thalamic preparatory activity, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 8h, i
claims.quote: Second, GABAergic neurons in ALM do not project to thal ALM ( Extended Data Fig. 8h, i ), excluding direct photoinhibition of thal ALM
claims.criterion: Histology (AAV2/1-CAG-flex-EGFP injected into ALM of a Gad2-IRES-Cre mouse; no labelled axons in VM). The dataset is described as electrophysiology, behaviour and optogenetics; whether it holds these images is for the author to find. No quantity or test is given.

claims.statement: Mice in the object location discrimination task performed at 78.4% correct on average, and fewer than 13% of responses came before the go cue.
claims.source: Results, ALM is required for movement planning, paragraph 1
claims.quote: (mean per cent correct, 78.4%; responses before the go cue, ,13%)
claims.criterion: Performance is the fraction of correct reports excluding lick early trials (Methods, Behavioural data analyses), on trials without photostimulation. The paper does not say how the mean is formed. Readings are (a) all control trials pooled; (b) the mean over sessions; (c) the mean over mice of per-mouse performance. Reproduced when, under one reading, the per cent correct is within tolerance and the fraction of lick early trials among control trials (same three readings) is below 13% widened by 10% (14.3%). Trials without a lick in the 1.5 s window after the go cue ("did not lick", Methods, Behaviour) are not named among the exclusions; the Methods exclude only lick early trials. Readings are (x) no-lick trials kept in the denominator as not correct, the literal reading of the Methods, and (y) no-lick trials left out, reading "fraction of correct reports" as among trials with a report. Both are run; either may decide.

claims.statement: Unilateral photoinhibition of ALM during the delay epoch biases licking to the ipsilateral side, raising performance on ipsilateral (lick left for left ALM) trials and lowering it on contralateral trials, with the reverse pattern for right ALM.
claims.source: Results, ALM is required for movement planning, paragraph 2; Figure 1d
claims.quote: Inhibiting left ALM caused a tendency to lick the left port, resulting in increased performance in 'lick left' trials and decreased performance in 'lick right' trials (Fig. 1d). The reversed pattern of bias was observed when inhibiting right ALM
claims.criterion: Trials of the 8 photoinhibition mice. For left and right ALM separately, the change in performance (photoinhibition minus control) on lick right and lick left trials, with the delay-epoch photoinhibition trials. Significance by the Methods' bootstrap, resampling with replacement animals, then sessions within each animal, then trials within each session, 10^4 times; P is the fraction of resamples with a change of the opposite sign (one-tailed). Reproduced when, for both hemispheres, contralateral-trial performance falls with P < 0.05 and ipsilateral-trial performance rises (its P reported); partially reproduced when this holds for one hemisphere. The stars of Fig. 1d were not read, so which comparisons the paper found significant beyond the text is not fixed here.

claims.statement: The ipsilateral bias is smaller when ALM is photoinhibited during the sample epoch than during the delay epoch.
claims.source: Results, ALM is required for movement planning, paragraph 2; Figure 1d
claims.quote: This ipsilateral bias was smaller when photoinhibiting during the sample epoch
claims.criterion: Same trials and performance measure as fig1d-delay-inhibition-ipsi-bias. The paper gives no measure of the bias and no test. Readings are (a) the fall in contralateral-trial performance; (b) the ipsilateral-trial change minus the contralateral-trial change. Reproduced when, under each reading, the bias for sample-epoch inhibition is smaller than for delay-epoch inhibition in both hemispheres; partially reproduced when in one. A bootstrap of the difference (resampling as in the Methods) is reported as a variant.

claims.statement: 1,408 single units were recorded from left ALM in 19 mice over 99 sessions; by spike width 124 were fast-spiking, 1,245 putative pyramidal and 39 intermediate.
claims.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 1a
claims.quote: A total of 1,408 single units were recorded across 99 recording sessions ... Units with spike width ,0.35 ms were defined as fast-spiking neurons (124/1,408) and units with spike width .0.45 ms as putative pyramidal neurons (1,245/1,408)
claims.criterion: Spike width is the trough-to-peak interval of the mean spike waveform (Methods); fast-spiking below 0.35 ms, putative pyramidal above 0.45 ms, intermediate between. Each count is checked against its tolerance.

claims.statement: 73% (912 of 1,245) of putative pyramidal neurons distinguished the trial types in at least one trial epoch.
claims.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 1; Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, paragraph 2
claims.quote: A large fraction(73%,912/1,245)ofneuronsdistinguishedtrialtypes(P , 0.05, two-tailed t-test, not corrected for multiple comparisons) (Fig. 2b)
claims.criterion: Per neuron, spike counts in the sample, delay and response epochs compared between lick right and lick left trials with a two-tailed t-test, P < 0.05, uncorrected; selective when significant in any epoch (Methods). Sample epoch from pole movement onset, 1.3 s; delay epoch the 1.3 s before the go cue. Open, with readings - the trials, (a) correct trials only (as the Methods state for contra-selectivity and Fig. 2b shows) or (b) all non-early trials by instructed trial type; the response epoch, which no passage times, (i) 1.3 s after the go cue, like the other epochs, or (ii) the 1.5 s lick window after the go cue. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading. Trials with the antidromic tagging light, where a session has them, are not addressed by the paper. The Methods' only trial filter is correct reports ("Only trials in which mice correctly reported pole locations were included"), and the Results say the tagged neurons were recorded "during behaviour" without saying whether tagging overlapped the task trials. Readings for this and every electrophysiology claim of Figs 2 and 3 are (t1) all trials as the other readings select them, light or not, the literal reading of the Methods, and (t2) only trials without the tagging light. Both are run; either may decide.

claims.statement: Among selective neurons, 219 of 912 had selective preparatory activity only, 389 peri-movement activity only, and 304 both.
claims.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 1; Figure 2d
claims.quote: subsets of neurons showed selective preparatory activity (Fig. 2b, left column; Fig. 2d, 219/912 neurons), peri-movement activity during the response epoch (Fig. 2b, right column; 389/912), or both
claims.criterion: Preparatory means significant in the sample or delay epoch, peri-movement significant in the response epoch, by the test of fig2-selective-fraction (Methods), with its readings. Reproduced when all three counts are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Selectivity emerges in the sample epoch, increases through the delay epoch and peaks at the beginning of the response epoch.
claims.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 1; Figure 2c; Extended Data Figure 1d, f
claims.quote: Selectivityemergedinthesampleepoch,increasedthroughoutthedelay epoch, and reached a maximum at the beginning of the response epoch
claims.criterion: As Extended Data Fig. 1f, the number of putative pyramidal neurons significantly selective in 200 ms windows of spike counts (two-tailed t-test, P < 0.05), correct trials. Window step is not stated; readings are a 200 ms step (non-overlapping) and a 50 ms step, both run. Reproduced when, under each step, (1) the count in some sample-epoch window exceeds the 95th percentile of a binomial count with p = 0.05 over the neurons tested (the rate the test gives by chance) while the windows before sample onset do not exceed it on average; (2) the count in the last delay window exceeds that in the first delay window; (3) the maximum over the trial falls at the beginning of the response epoch, read as (a) the first window after the go cue or (b) any window starting within 0.5 s after the go cue.

claims.statement: Individual neuron responses are dynamic although selectivity is stable at the level of the population (Fig. 2c, bottom, population selectivity and the correlation of the population response with that at the go cue).
claims.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 1; Figure 2c, bottom; Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Individualneuronresponseswere dynamic, despite stable selectivity at the level of the population (Fig. 2c, bottompanelandExtended Data Fig.2a)
claims.criterion: As the Methods, a pseudo-population treated as simultaneously recorded, of (a) the 912 selective neurons (the neurons Fig. 2c shows) or (b) all 1,245 putative pyramidal neurons, both run; each neuron's response (correct trials, 200 ms bins) mean- subtracted and normalized to its variance over the trial; Pearson correlation of the population vector at each time with that at go cue onset (t = 0). Population selectivity is the spike rate difference between preferred and non-preferred trial types, the preference set from 10 trials and the selectivity computed on the remaining trials. Whether the population vector concatenates both trial types or uses their difference is open; both are run. The paper gives no number, and the curve of Fig. 2c was not read, so the claim is judged on shape, a reading of "dynamic" made here. Reproduced when, under each reading, the mean correlation over the sample epoch is lower than over the delay epoch, which is lower than 1, while the population selectivity stays above 0 through the delay epoch. Three details the paper leaves open, each with its readings. (1) Normalization, "normalized to the variance of its response" (Methods); (v) dividing by the variance, the text as written, and (s) dividing by the standard deviation (z-score). (2) The preference set "using spike counts from a subset of the trials (10 trials)" (Methods; Extended Data Fig. 1b, "from 10 trials"); (n10) 10 trials in all and (n20) 10 trials of each type. (3) The vector "at the onset of the go cue" (Methods; Fig. 2c legend, "t 5 0", "Averaging window, 200ms"); the 200 ms bin that (gs) starts at, (gc) is centred on, or (ge) ends at the go cue. These join the readings of the rule above, all combinations run.

claims.statement: On error trials ALM activity predicts the direction the mouse licked, so most selective neurons switch their trial-type preference relative to correct trials.
claims.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 2c
claims.quote: On error trials, when mice licked in the opposite direction to the instruction provided by object location (Fig. 1a), a majority of ALM neurons switched their trial type preference to predict the licking direction, as indicated by the negative correlations
claims.criterion: For the 912 selective neurons and each epoch (sample, delay, response), selectivity is (rate lick right) minus (rate lick left) by instructed trial type, on correct trials and on error trials; Pearson correlation across neurons between the two (Extended Data Fig. 2c). The minimum number of error trials per neuron is not stated; readings (a) at least one error trial of each type, (b) at least five. Reproduced when r < 0 in the delay and response epochs under each reading, with the sample epoch reported; partially reproduced when in one of the two.

claims.statement: Contra-preferring and ipsi-preferring neurons are present in equal proportions in left ALM, and the overall spike count shows no significant contralateral bias (P = 0.13; 8% spike rate modulation across all task-selective neurons).
claims.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 2; Figure 2e; Results, A movement command emerges in the pyramidal tract neurons, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Significant contralateral bias also did not appear in the overall spike count across the recorded population of neurons (Extended Data Fig. 1; P 5 0.13, two-tailed t-test against 0) ... The contra-preferring and ipsi-preferring neurons were present in equal proportions
