claims.statement: At the consonant time (-25 ms) k-means clustering of the cortical state-space groups syllables by major oral articulator (labial, coronal, dorsal), and three clusters are more parsimonious than two or four (mean silhouette 0.47 against 0.45 and 0.43).
claims.source: Results, Phonetic Organization of Spatial Patterns, paragraph 1; Figure 4a; Methods, Clustering Analysis, paragraph 2
claims.quote: On average across subjects, this analysis validated the claim that three clusters (Average Silhouette = 0.47) was a more parsimonious clustering scheme than either two (Average Silhouette = 0.45) or four clusters (Average Silhouette = 0.43)
claims.criterion: Per subject, k-means with Euclidean distance on the CVs' nine-PC states at -25 ms, for k = 2, 3 and 4; mean silhouette per k, averaged over subjects. k-means starts are a standard choice (100 random starts, the best kept) that is not expected to change the outcome. Reproduced when k = 3 has the highest mean silhouette and the three values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when k = 3 is highest but values are outside it. The cluster-articulator match is claim suppfig11-co-clustering.

claims.statement: Clusters of the cortical state-space match the major articulators at the consonant time (median co-clustering 0.50 against 0.32 by chance) and the vowels at the vowel time (0.65 against 0.37), across subjects.
claims.source: Results, Phonetic Organization of Spatial Patterns, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 11a, b
claims.quote: clustering of CV’s in the cortical state-space co-clustered with the major articulators significantly more than expected by chance (Red: observed distribution, median = 0.50, Black: null distribution from 1000 random permutations of articulator assignments of CVs, median = 0.32
claims.criterion: Per subject, k-means (k = 3) at -25 ms (consonants) and +250 ms (vowels) as in claim fig4a-consonant-clusters; the co-clustering coefficient of each CV against the major articulator labels (consonants) or vowel identity (vowels), Supplementary Methods Eq. 1, kappa = 1 - |NC delta AC| / (|NC| + |AC|); the null for each CV the mean of kappa over 1000 permutations of the labels within subject. Wilcoxon signed-rank, observed against null, over the 168 CVs. For consonants the two readings of the /h/ and /r/ labels in the header. Reproduced when both medians are within tolerance and both tests give p < 1e-10 (the main text's bound); partially reproduced when the tests hold and a median is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: Hierarchical clustering of the state-space puts the major oral articulator (dorsal, labial, coronal) at the top tier for consonants, superordinate to constriction location, with constriction degree only at the lowest level; for vowels the first split is lip rounding (/u/ against /a/ and /i/).
claims.source: Results, Phonetic Organization of Spatial Patterns, paragraph 2; Figure 4c, d
claims.quote: For consonants, this analysis confirmed that the primary tier of organization was defined by the major oral articulator features: dorsal, labial, or coronal ( Fig. 4c ) ... during the vowel period, a primary distinction was based upon the presence/absence of lip-rounding (/u/ vs. /a/ & /i/)
claims.criterion: Agglomerative clustering with Ward's method on Euclidean distances between the CVs' nine-PC states (Methods), at -25 ms and +250 ms. The paper does not say whether Fig. 4c, d is one subject or pooled; each subject is run. Consonants. The tree cut into three clusters; reproduced for a subject when the three clusters have different majority major articulators and at least two thirds of the labelled CVs fall in the cluster of their articulator's majority (OPEN, the paper gives no purity measure; the co-clustering coefficient of claim suppfig11-co-clustering for the cut is reported as well). Vowels. The tree cut into two clusters; reproduced for a subject when one cluster holds a majority of the /u/ syllables and the other a majority of the /a/ and /i/ syllables. The claim is reproduced when both hold in every subject and partially reproduced when they hold in some. The lowest-level manner grouping is shown, not judged.

claims.statement: Over early times (-375 to 120 ms) constriction location correlates with the state-space structure more than constriction degree, which correlates more than the upcoming vowel; over later times (125 to 620 ms) vowel configuration correlates most.
claims.source: Results, Phonetic Organization of Spatial Patterns, paragraph 3; Figure 4e, f
claims.quote: Across early time points (−375:120 ms), we found that consonant features describing constriction location yielded a significantly greater correlation with the cortical state-space than constriction degree, which in turn was significantly more correlated than the upcoming vowel ... across later time points (125:620 ms), we found that vowel features provided the greatest correlation
claims.criterion: Per subject and time, R(t) of Methods Eq. 7, the Pearson correlation between the unique pairwise Euclidean distances of the CVs' nine-PC states and those of the CVs in each feature set of Supplementary Figure 12 (location, degree/shape, vowel). The n of 297 is read as 99 time points in each window x 3 subjects, at 5 ms steps (OPEN, which end point is left out; the result is not expected to depend on it). Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests over these values. Reproduced when location > degree and degree > vowel in the early window, and vowel > location and vowel > degree in the late window, each with p < 1e-10; partially reproduced when some of the four comparisons hold. Distances in Hamming form for the feature sets are a variant (Methods say both gave the same result).

claims.statement: Cluster separability, averaged over subjects, rises from about -300 ms and peaks about 200 ms before the C-V transition for consonants, and rises from about 50 ms and peaks at +250 ms for vowels.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of Phonetic Representations, paragraph 2; Figure 5c
claims.quote: separability peaked ~200 ms before the CV transition for consonants (onset, ~−300 ms), and at +250 ms for vowels (onset, ~50 ms)
claims.criterion: Separability at each time is the mean distance between CVs in different clusters minus the mean distance within clusters (Methods, Cluster Separability), on nine-PC states, per subject, then averaged over subjects. OPEN, the clusters; readings (a) the phonetic groups, major articulator for consonants and vowel identity for vowels, (a') for consonants the four groups of the Fig. 5a legend (labial, coronal tongue, dorsal tongue, sibilant), (b) k-means (k = 3) at each time. OPEN, the onset; readings (a) the first time the mean exceeds its pre-epoch level by 2 bootstrap s.e. (1000 bootstrap samples of syllables, as the Methods), (b) the time at half the peak. The vowel onset tolerance is two 5 ms samples, as 10% would be a single sample. Reproduced when, under each reading of the clusters and one of the onset, all four values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the peaks are and an onset is not.

claims.statement: Cluster separability and the correlation of the state-space with phonetic features are tightly linked over time for consonants and vowels in each subject (R2 0.42 to 0.98, all P < 1e-10).
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of Phonetic Representations, paragraph 2; Figure 5c, d
claims.quote: Across subjects, we found that cluster separability and the correlation between cortical state-space organization and phonetic features were tightly linked for both consonants and vowels in a time-dependent fashion (R 2 range = [0.42–0.98], P < 10 −10 for all)
claims.criterion: Per subject, the separability time course of claim fig5c-separability-timing and R(t) of claim fig4ef-feature-correlations, constriction location for consonants and vowel configuration for vowels (OPEN; reading (b) the mean over the three feature sets); squared Pearson correlation over the epoch at 5 ms steps. Reproduced when the six R2 values lie within 0.38 to 1 (the reported range widened by 10% of each bound) with each p < 1e-10; partially reproduced when all are positive and significant but some fall below 0.38.

claims.statement: Consonant and vowel representations occupy distinct regions of the state-space; consonant-vowel distances are larger than consonant-consonant and vowel-vowel distances, and consonant-consonant distances are larger than vowel-vowel ones.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of Phonetic Representations, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 13
claims.quote: We found that the distribution of distances comparing consonants and vowels was significantly greater than the consonant-consonant comparison or vowel-vowel comparison, and the consonant-consonant comparison was greater than the vowel-vowel comparison
claims.criterion: Per subject, nine-PC states of each CV at -25 ms (consonant) and +250 ms (vowel). For each unordered pair of CVs in a subject, the consonant-consonant distance, the vowel-vowel distance and the consonant-vowel distance (OPEN, which of the pair at which time; readings (a) the mean of the two cross pairings, (b) i at -25 ms and j at +250 ms). 4623 is read as the pairs within subjects (1596 + 1596 + 1431). Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests over the pairs pooled over subjects, Bonferroni for 3. Reproduced when all three orderings hold with corrected p < 1e-10 and the pair count is 4623.

claims.statement: The first three PCs are weighted toward tongue over lips, and toward lips over jaw and larynx, while jaw and larynx do not differ.
claims.source: Supplementary Figure 9a legend
claims.quote: the magnitude of the articulator weightings (log10(|(PCNi*Wij)|)) was significantly biased towards tongue over lips (P < 0.05) over jaw and larynx (P < 0.001 for each), while the difference between jaw and larynx was not significant (P > 0.2)
claims.criterion: Methods Eq. 6, PCw_ij = M_ij beta_j, with beta_j the GLM weights of claim fig2a-lips-dorsal averaged over each articulator's window (W_jA) for every vSMC electrode (OPEN, all 266 electrodes or only the significant ones; the n reads as all), for PCs 1 to 3; log10 of the absolute value. Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank across electrodes for the six articulator pairs, per PC, Bonferroni for 6. The legend's "tongue over lips (P < 0.05) over jaw and larynx (P < 0.001 for each)" reads as (a) lips over jaw and over larynx, or (b) tongue and lips each over jaw and over larynx; it matches under either. Reproduced when, in each PC, tongue > lips at p < 0.05, the P < 0.001 comparisons of the reading hold, and jaw against larynx p > 0.05 (the absence judged on the paper's test); partially reproduced when this holds in one or two of the three PCs.

claims.statement: The dandiset's recordings can be matched to the paper's per-cell table (t-type and depth) by specimen ID, and the 18 features computed from them agree with the paper's feature table.
claims.source: Methods, Electrophysiology feature analysis; code data/human_IVSCC_excitatory_L23_consolidated_0131.csv and data/human_mouse_ephys_all_0127.csv at commit 3daf9f0
claims.criterion: Cells are matched to the code's cell table by specimen ID (SpecimenID). The paper names no identifier (Methods), and the code joins its tables on SpecimenID only (hivscc_data.load_data). Where the files carry no SpecimenID, the paper allows two readings of the match, (M1) only by a SpecimenID stored in the files, and (M2) by a SpecimenID recovered from each file, the code's SpecimenID of the same donor next above the file's ephys session id, with agreement of the computed features with the code's table as the check. M2 is a reconstruction that neither the paper nor the code states. Both are run and reported, with the missing identifier recorded as a finding; the claims that depend on this link name the reading they use. The 18 features are computed from each matched recording with IPFX, after the sweep QC of the Methods. For each feature, the median over matched cells of the absolute difference from the code's table relative to the table's absolute value is taken (10%, the protocol's default tolerance, as the bound). Reproduced when at least 283 of the 385 cells match and all 18 features are within 10%; partially reproduced when cells match and 9 to 17 features are within 10%; not reproduced otherwise. The number of matched cells, and how many of them carry a t-type or depth in the files themselves, is reported. The code's table is from the revision (316 human cells), so cells beyond the preprint's 283 are expected.

claims.statement: 385 Patch-seq neurons passing transcriptomic QC mapped to the five supragranular glutamatergic t-types, and 283 of them had recordings complete enough to compute electrophysiological features.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq pipeline for human neurosurgical tissue analysis, paragraph 2
claims.quote: A total of 385 neurons that passed transcriptomic data QC mapped with higher confidence to the five supragranular human glutamatergic t-types than to any other neuron type. ... Most neurons (283) also had sufficiently complete recordings to calculate electrophysiological features.
claims.criterion: Counts are records, so the tolerance is zero. The 385 is counted as the cells of the code's table that have a recording in the dandiset; the 283 as those whose recordings give the 18 features with IPFX (the paper does not say how many features may be missing; readings are (a) at least one feature, (b) all 18, (c) no more than 3 of 18 missing, the rule the Methods give for the projections). Reproduced when both counts match under one reading; partially reproduced when one does. The dandiset may hold other cells; they are counted and reported apart.

claims.statement: The neurons came from neurosurgical specimens of 90 tissue donors.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 2
claims.quote: across human neurosurgical specimens from 90 different tissue donors
claims.criterion: Donors are counted as distinct subjects. The paper allows two readings, (a) all subjects in the dandiset, or (b) the donors of the 385 cells of the code's table that are in the dandiset. Reproduced when either gives 90. The code's pathology table also lists 90 donors, which is reported.

claims.statement: The electrophysiology figures show 66 LTK, 25 GLP2R and 136 FREM3 neurons, and 21 deep FREM3, 17 CARM1P1 and 37 COL22A1 neurons.
claims.source: Figure 4a legend; Figure 6b legend
claims.quote: Bottom panels compare the intrinsic electrophysiological responses for 66 LTK, 25 GLP2R and 136 FREM3 neurons. ... Electrophysiological description of the intrinsic electrophysiology responses of 21 deep FREM3, 17 CARM1P1 and 37 COL22A1 neurons.
claims.criterion: Counts per t-type of the cells with features, under the readings of cohort-cells for which cells have features; deep FREM3 also needs a normalized depth above 0.575. Reproduced when all six match under one reading; partially reproduced when at least three do.

claims.statement: Human L2 and L3 together (1.23 +/- 0.15 mm) are on average 1.16 times thicker than the whole mouse cortex (1.06 +/- 0.01 mm).
claims.source: Results, Human supragranular cortex is more diverse than in mouse, paragraph 1; Figure 1a
claims.quote: The combined thickness of the relatively thin L2 and very thick L3 in human cortex (1.23 ± 0.15 mm) is on average 1.16 times greater than the thickness of the entire mouse cortex (1.06 ± 0.01 mm; Fig. 1a ).
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the reported spreads (SD across donors). Not tested on the dandiset. The human value is the mean and SD over the 5 human sections of each section's mean L2 plus L3 thickness, from the L1/L2 to the L3/L4 boundary line (Code6_cortical_depth_code_human.r, L23_depth; the code prints 1058, 1293, 1387, 1073 and 1344 um). The paper does not say where the mouse value of 1.06 mm comes from; the Methods (Quantification of soma size) describe only the L1/L2 and L3/L4 borders, and the code's mouse sections have no white matter line, so the mouse value and the ratio of 1.16 cannot be tested from the paper's materials and are not judged. The mouse L2/3 thickness the code computes (Code7, 281, 223 and 257 um) is reported, not compared. Reproduced when the human value is within tolerance; the outcome notes that the mouse value is untested.

claims.statement: Human supragranular neuron density is 27.7 +/- 4.5 thousand cells/mm3, highest in L2 and halving to a minimum in mid L3, while mouse VISp L2/3 has about 6 times that density (165 +/- 24.9 thousand cells/mm3), uniform with depth.
claims.source: Results, Human supragranular cortex is more diverse than in mouse, paragraph 1; Figure 1b
claims.quote: the average density of human neurons was 27.7 ± 4.5 thousand cells/mm 3 ( Fig. 1b ; left). This distribution is not homogeneous, with higher density in L2 that decreases by half to reach a low point in mid L3 ( Fig. 1b ; right). In contrast, supragranular layers of mouse VISp show 6 times the neuronal density of human (165 ± 24.9 thousand cells/mm 3 ) with a homogeneous distribution across cortical depth.
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the reported spreads. Method per the Methods (20 bins over L2/3, first and last dropped, one section per donor). Not tested on the dandiset.

claims.statement: Mean soma area doubles from L2 to deep L3 in human but is uniform across mouse L2/3; the interquartile ranges are 44 to 96 um2 in mouse and 107 to 253 um2 in human, and the largest human somata exceed 850 um2.
claims.source: Results, Human supragranular cortex is more diverse than in mouse, paragraph 1; Figure 1c
claims.quote: the average cross-sectional area of neuron somata doubles from L2 to deep L3 in human supragranular cortex in a graded fashion but in mouse is remarkably uniform across the depth of supraganular cortex ( Fig. 1c , left). The interquartile range of mouse and human somata were 44 - 96μm 2 and 107 - 253μm 2 , respectively, with the largest human somata exceeding 850μm 2 .
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset. The quartiles are over all somata of a species pooled across its sections (3 mouse, 5 human), as the code computes the values the text gives (Code7_cortical_depth_code_mouse.r, quantile over the concatenated areas; it prints 44.7 and 96.5 um2 for mouse, 107.5 and 252.6 um2 for human, and a largest human soma of 886 um2). The per-section quantiles the code also prints are reported, not judged. Reproduced when the four quartiles are within tolerance and the largest human soma exceeds 850 um2.

claims.statement: The variation of soma size in deep L3 is four times higher in human than in mouse.
claims.source: Results, Human supragranular cortex is more diverse than in mouse, paragraph 1; Figure 1c right
claims.quote: variation in deep L3 neuron soma size is four-fold higher in human compared to mouse ( Fig. 1c , right)
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset. The Methods do not say which bins make up deep L3 for this ratio; the code settles it. Of the 20 bins of scaled depth (breaks every 0.05, Code6), deep L3 is the five bins whose centres lie in scaled depth -0.95 to -0.7 (centres -0.925 to -0.725, normalized L2/3 depth 0.7 to 0.95). For each section and bin the SD of soma area is taken; these SDs are averaged over the deep L3 bins and sections of each species, and the human mean is divided by the mouse mean (Code7_cortical_depth_code_mouse.r, l3dex on het, printed as 4.0). Reproduced when this ratio is within tolerance. As a variant, deep L3 as the bins with centres deeper than the density minimum at normalized depth 0.575 (Methods, Quantification of soma size), without the deepest bin, which the Methods drop for boundary effects, is run and reported.

claims.statement: The human FREM3 t-type has more within-type transcriptomic heterogeneity (variance explained by PC1 above permuted data) than any other human or mouse supragranular t-type, which are similar to one another.
claims.source: Results, Human supragranular cortex is more diverse than in mouse, paragraph 3; Figure 1f
claims.quote: This analysis confirms high heterogeneity in FREM3 , with lower, generally similar, values for all other human and mouse t-types ( Fig. 1f ).
claims.criterion: Method per the Methods (80 cells per type, 80 most variable genes, 100 repeats against gene-shuffled data). Not tested on the dandiset.

claims.statement: The homologous types are similarly discrete from one another in mouse and in human, while CARM1P1 and COL22A1 have many more differentially expressed genes against the homologous types than the homologous types have against one another, in either species.
claims.source: Results, Human supragranular cortex is more diverse than in mouse, paragraph 3; Figure 1g
claims.quote: Homologous types are similarly discrete from one another in both mouse in human, whereas the deep L3 CARM1P1 and COL22A1 t-types had many more DE genes when compared to the homologous t-types ( Fig. 1g ).
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset.

claims.statement: Human Patch-seq cells and dissociated nuclei of matched t-types are highly correlated in gene expression (R = 0.85), more than mouse cells and human nuclei (R = 0.57); 177 genes are enriched in nuclei and 2,670 at least four-fold in Patch-seq.
claims.source: Results, High-confidence Patch-seq neuron t-type mapping, paragraph 2; Figure 3a
claims.quote: Expression data from dissociated mouse whole cells and human nuclei were moderately correlated (R=0.57, p~0, Fig. 3a , left), ... dissociated nuclei and Patch-seq cells from matched human t-types were highly correlated (R=0.85, p~0, Fig. 3a , right). Relatively few genes (177 genome-wide) showed enriched expression in dissociated nuclei relative to Patch-seq cells ... we identified 2,670 genes with at least four-fold enrichment in Patch-seq
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset.

claims.statement: Average pathology scores over six markers ranged from 0.06 to 1.83 across donors, and most cases had averages below 1.0, a range not considered overtly pathological.
claims.source: Results, Detailed histological assessment of human surgical tissue, paragraph 2; Figure 2c and 2d
claims.quote: images from the case with the lowest average score (mean of 6 marker scores = 0.06) are contrasted with images from the case with the highest average score (mean of 6 marker scores = 1.83) ( Fig. 2c ). ... However, this was rare, and most cases had average scores <1.0 ( Fig. 2d )
claims.criterion: The average is of GFAP, IBA1, Ki-67, SMI-32, NeuN and Nissl (cellularity) scores, as the code's pathology_analysis.ipynb sums them. "Most" is read as more than half of the donors with all six scores. Not tested on the dandiset.

claims.statement: The six pathology markers are very weakly correlated with one another across donors, with only Ki-67 and Nissl (cellularity) modestly correlated.
claims.source: Results, Detailed histological assessment of human surgical tissue, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 1
claims.quote: we found very low correlation of the 6 cellular markers with each other, with only Ki-67 and Nissl (cellularity) being modestly correlated ( Extended Data Fig. 1 )
claims.criterion: Pearson correlation across donors (Extended Data Fig. 1 legend). The paper gives no threshold for "modest"; reproduced when the Ki-67 and Nissl pair has the largest absolute correlation of the 15 pairs. Not tested on the dandiset.

claims.statement: Of 18 electrophysiological features compared between neurons from donors with low (0 to 1) and high (1 to 3) GFAP or IBA1 scores, only resting membrane potential under IBA1 differs, neurons from high-IBA1 donors being about 5 mV more hyperpolarized; the other 17 IBA1 and all 18 GFAP comparisons do not differ.
claims.source: Results, Detailed histological assessment of human surgical tissue, paragraph 3; Figure 2e and 2f
claims.quote: Among the 18 electrophysiological features analyzed for GFAP and IBA1, only one feature (resting membrane potential, RMP) related to IBA1 was significantly different between low versus high groups. Neurons in the high IBA1 group were approximately 5 mV more hyperpolarized at rest than neurons in the low IBA1 group ( Fig. 2f ). The remaining 17/18 features for IBA1 and all 18 features for GFAP were not statistically different between low and high groups
claims.criterion: Partly a claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. Cells are the supragranular glutamatergic neurons (the code's 385-cell table) with all 18 features defined (the code drops cells with any missing feature). The paper's text says "all supragranular glutamatergic neurons"; the original pathology notebook also keeps only temporal cortex cells of the hIVSCC-MET project, from a table not in the repository. So the readings are (a) temporal cells only (region temporal in the code's cell table), (b) all regions; the group counts above say which the paper used. Each donor's GFAP and IBA1 scores are the columns GFAP Cortex and Iba1 Cortex of the code's data/pathology_scoring.csv (the mean of three neuropathologists), low being at most 1 and high above 1 (the code; the text gives 0-1 and 1-3). The test is the code's, scipy's Mann-Whitney U with its default of scipy 1.4 (the pinned version), whose p is half the two-sided p, at the Bonferroni level 0.05/18 per marker (Figure 2f legend and the code). The paper does not say whether the 5 mV is a difference of group medians or of group means; both are computed, and the size part of the outcome is the one both give (methods_underspecified for the size when they differ). Reproduced when, under one reading of the cells, RMP under IBA1 is the only significant comparison of the 36, with the high group more hyperpolarized and the difference within tolerance; partially reproduced when the significance pattern holds but the size is outside tolerance; not reproduced when any other comparison is significant or RMP under IBA1 is not. The two-sided Mann-Whitney test is shown as a variant, as is the updated notebook's result.

claims.statement: LTK neurons lie mainly in L2 and at the L2/L3 border, GLP2R mainly in upper L3, FREM3 span L2 and L3 and continue into L4, and CARM1P1 and COL22A1 lie almost entirely in deep L3 and along the L3/L4 border.
claims.source: Results, High-confidence Patch-seq neuron t-type mapping, paragraph 4; Figure 3d
claims.quote: Human LTK neurons were found primarily in L2 and in the border region of L2 and L3. GLP2R neurons were found primarily in upper L3, with some neurons found in L2. FREM3 neurons spanned L2 and L3, continuing into L4, consistent with their heterogeneous gene expression profile. CARM1P1 and COL22A1 were found almost entirely in deep L3 and along the L3/L4 border.
claims.criterion: Normalized L2/3 depth per cell (0 at the L1/L2 border, 1 at the L3/L4 border; Figure 3d legend and Figure 1 legend). The L2/L3 border is not recorded per cell, so L2 is judged by order. Deep L3 is depth above 0.575 (the paper's density minimum) and L4 depth above 1. Reproduced when all of these hold; the median depth of LTK is below that of GLP2R; the GLP2R median is below 0.575; FREM3 includes cells shallower than the LTK median and cells deeper than 1; and, for CARM1P1 and COL22A1 each, "almost entirely" holds. The paper gives no number for "almost entirely"; the readings are (a) at least 90% and (b) at least 80% of cells deeper than 0.575. They are thresholds, so the outcome is the one both give, and the claim is methods_underspecified when they differ. Partially reproduced when the order of medians holds but not the rest. All cells of the code's table with a depth are used, whether or not they have features.

claims.statement: Among the three human homologous t-types (LTK, GLP2R, FREM3), 3 of 18 electrophysiological features explain more than 10% of variance by t-type (input resistance, f-I slope and rheobase), at FDR below 1e-5, with a maximum R2 of 0.16.
claims.source: Results, Increased morpho-electric specialization in human L2-3 t-types, paragraph 5; Figure 4e
claims.quote: For electrophysiological features ( Fig. 4e ), 3/18 showed differences between t-types that explained >10% of feature variance ( R 2 >0.1) for both human and mouse (FDR<0.05 for mouse features, <10 −5 for human). ... while the human types showed distinct firing properties (f-I slope and rheobase) in addition to input resistance, with a maximum R 2 =0.16.
claims.criterion: The t-type ANOVA on LTK, GLP2R and all FREM3 cells (the preprint's Methods say the three homologous t-types; the code's revision uses superficial FREM3 only, depth below 0.575, shown as a variant). Reproduced when exactly the three features named have R2 above 0.1, each at FDR below 1e-5, and the maximum R2 is within tolerance; partially reproduced when at least two of the three named features have R2 above 0.1 at FDR below 0.05.

claims.statement: Among the three mouse L2/3 t-types, 3 of 18 electrophysiological features explain more than 10% of variance (input resistance, AP width and AP downstroke rate), at FDR below 0.05, with a maximum R2 of 0.12, below the human maximum.
claims.source: Results, Increased morpho-electric specialization in human L2-3 t-types, paragraph 5; Figure 4e
claims.quote: However, the mouse types were distinct in input resistance and two related AP shape features (width and downstroke) with a maximum R 2 =0.12
claims.criterion: The t-type ANOVA on the mouse Adamts2, Rrad and Agmat cells. The mouse recordings are not in this dandiset and the paper does not say where they are (ref. 32 is the mouse Patch-seq study); the code's feature and cell tables hold their features and t-types. Reproduced when exactly the three features named have R2 above 0.1 at FDR below 0.05, the maximum R2 is within tolerance and is below the human maximum of fig4e-human-ephys-anova; partially reproduced when two of the three hold.

claims.statement: 16 of 60 morphological features have R2 above 0.15 between the human homologous t-types (FDR below 1e-3), against 12 of 60 for mouse (10 of them at FDR below 0.05).
claims.source: Results, Increased morpho-electric specialization in human L2-3 t-types, paragraph 5; Figure 4f
claims.quote: For morphological features ( Fig. 4f ), 16/60 features had R 2 >0.15 between the human t-types (FDR<10 −3 ), compared to 12/60 for the mouse t-types (with 10/12 significant at FDR<0.05).
claims.criterion: The t-type ANOVA on all 60 morphological features of the code's tables, human LTK, GLP2R and all FREM3 cells (the preprint's Methods; the code's revision uses superficial FREM3 only, shown as a variant) and mouse Adamts2, Rrad and Agmat cells. As in the code (run_regressions in morpho_electro_feature_analysis.ipynb), a feature with no p-value (constant among the cells) is dropped before the Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and R2 above 0.15 is counted over the features kept. Not tested on the dandiset.

claims.statement: GLP2R neurons, like LTK neurons, lack firing rate adaptation and have higher input resistance, but unlike LTK neurons (which have no sag) they have pronounced sag.
claims.source: Results, Increased morpho-electric specialization in human L2-3 t-types, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 4a
claims.quote: Electrophysiologically, GLP2R neurons exhibited LTK -like electrophysiology, lacking adaptation and higher input resistance, but differed from LTK neurons in that they had pronounced sag.
claims.criterion: Sag (sag ratio at about -100 pA) and adaptation (adapt_mean) compared between LTK and GLP2R with the pairwise test over the three homologous types (the paper's post hoc test for Figure 4e; the paper shows this finding only as traces). Reproduced when GLP2R sag is significantly higher than LTK sag (FDR below 0.05) and adaptation does not differ between them; partially reproduced when sag is higher but adaptation also differs. The higher input resistance is not judged, since the paper does not say what it is higher than (FREM3 is the likely comparison); the input resistance of the three types is reported.

claims.statement: Between human and mouse homologous t-types, 17 of 18 electrophysiological features differ at FDR below 0.05.
claims.source: Extended Data Table 1 legend
claims.quote: For homologous t-types, results are shown for unpaired t-tests across species for each feature ... 17out of 18 features are significant at FDR<0.05.
claims.criterion: Human LTK, GLP2R and FREM3 cells against mouse Adamts2, Rrad and Agmat cells (mouse features from the code's table), one test per feature, Benjamini-Hochberg over 18. The legend does not say whether the t-test assumes equal variances; readings are (a) Student's and (b) Welch's. A feature counts when its BH-corrected p is below 0.05 (the legend). Reproduced when both readings give 17; the claim is methods_underspecified when they differ in outcome. The code's test (scipy's Mann-Whitney with the scipy 1.4 default, on cells with all 18 features; AP width the one feature not significant) is shown as a variant, as is Cohen's d per feature.

claims.statement: A random forest predicts the homologous human t-type from electrophysiological features with 67% accuracy.
claims.source: Results, Increased morpho-electric specialization in human L2-3 t-types, paragraph 6; Extended Data Figure 6
claims.quote: Homologous human t-types were predicted with 67% accuracy using electrophysiological features, while mouse t-types were predicted with 54% accuracy.
claims.criterion: As the Methods (Analysis of features by t-type and species, paragraph 3) and the code (classifier_and_species_analysis.ipynb). LTK, GLP2R and FREM3 cells with all 18 features (the code drops any cell with a missing feature), features standardized over all cells, 1000 stratified random splits into 70% training and 30% test, a random forest of 600 trees (sklearn, with the code's settings class_weight balanced, max_features sqrt, min_samples_leaf 2), accuracy on the test set averaged over the splits. Reproduced when the mean accuracy is within tolerance. Accuracy with shuffled t-type labels (Methods) is reported for comparison. The code runs 10 splits (n_repeats = 10), not the Methods' 1000; the Methods are followed, and the number of splits changes only the precision of the mean.

claims.statement: The same classifier predicts mouse L2/3 t-types from electrophysiological features with 54% accuracy, lower than for human.
claims.source: Results, Increased morpho-electric specialization in human L2-3 t-types, paragraph 6; Extended Data Figure 6
claims.quote: Homologous human t-types were predicted with 67% accuracy using electrophysiological features, while mouse t-types were predicted with 54% accuracy.
claims.criterion: As edfig6-classifier-human-ephys, on mouse Adamts2, Rrad and Agmat cells (features from the code's table). Reproduced when the mean accuracy is within tolerance and below the human accuracy.

claims.statement: Combining morphological and electrophysiological features raises accuracy slightly, to 69% for human and 60% for mouse neurons.
claims.source: Results, Increased morpho-electric specialization in human L2-3 t-types, paragraph 6; Extended Data Figure 6
claims.quote: Classifying based on morphological and electrophysiological features combined resulted in slightly improved performance of 69% for human neurons and 60% for mouse neurons
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset alone; it needs the morphological features. The method of edfig6-classifier-human-ephys (and edfig6-classifier-mouse-ephys), on the cells of the three homologous types of each species with all 18 electrophysiological features and a reconstruction, the 18 features and the 60 morphological features side by side, as in the code (classifier_and_species_analysis.ipynb, "Human morpho-electric features" and "Mouse morpho-electric features"; 72 human and 50 mouse cells in its tables). No morphological value is missing in these cells, so the KNNImputer of the morphology-only classifier has no effect; the code does not standardize the combined matrix, which leaves a random forest unchanged. The notebook prints 0.686 for human and 0.640 for mouse over its 10 splits. Reproduced when both mean accuracies are within tolerance.

claims.statement: In FREM3 neurons, 9 of 18 electrophysiological features correlate with normalized depth at FDR below 0.05 (7 at FDR below 0.01); the strongest are increasing sag, increasing AP upstroke/downstroke ratio and decreasing latency at rheobase.
claims.source: Results, Human FREM3 t-type exhibits depth-dependent morpho-electro-transcriptomic variation, paragraph 2; Figure 5c
claims.quote: Nine out of 18 physiological features were significantly correlated with depth (FDR<0.05, 7/18 FDR<0.01; Supplementary Data 1). The three strongest electrophysiology correlations with depth were the increase in sag and AP (Action Potential) upstroke / downstroke ratio and the decrease in AP latency at rheobase ( Fig. 5c ).
claims.criterion: The depth regression on all FREM3 cells with a normalized depth, per feature, BH over the 18. "Strongest" is read as the largest R2, the measure the Methods report. Reproduced when both counts are within tolerance and the three features with the largest R2 are sag and upstroke/downstroke ratio (positive slope) and latency (negative slope), each at FDR below 1e-7; partially reproduced when those three are significant at FDR below 0.05 with those signs but the counts or the ranking differ.

claims.statement: In FREM3 neurons, 37 of 58 morphological features correlate with depth at FDR below 0.05 (28 at FDR below 0.01), including apical height, maximum basal dendrite length and soma radius.
claims.source: Results, Human FREM3 t-type exhibits depth-dependent morpho-electro-transcriptomic variation, paragraph 2; Figure 5b
claims.quote: 37 out of 58 morphological features were correlated with depth (FDR<0.05, 28/58 FDR<0.01).
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset. The depth regression on all FREM3 cells with a reconstruction and a normalized depth, for each of the 60 morphological features of the code's table (morph_df.columns), the two soma location features included. As in the code (run_regressions in morpho_electro_feature_analysis.ipynb), a feature with no p-value is dropped before the Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Two features are constant among these cells (apical_dendrite_pct_below_basal_dendrite_none, basal_dendrite_pct_above_apical_dendrite_none), which leaves the paper's 58; the notebook prints 37 at FDR below 0.05 and 28 below 0.01.

claims.statement: FREM3 gene expression varies with soma depth; 790 genes correlate with depth at FDR below 0.05, enriched for synaptic transmission, cell migration and neuron projection morphogenesis.
claims.source: Results, Human FREM3 t-type exhibits depth-dependent morpho-electro-transcriptomic variation, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 5a and 5d
claims.quote: 790 genes were correlated with depth (FDR<0.05) and GO (gene ontology) enrichment analysis on this gene set revealed a variety of significantly enriched functional categories ( Fig. 5d , Supplementary Data 1)
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset. The code's gene_depth_analysis.ipynb counts 1917 genes at FDR below 0.01 from its revision's results, so its table is not the preprint's.

claims.statement: The three deep L3 types (deep FREM3, CARM1P1, COL22A1) differ in 15 of 18 electrophysiological features (FDR below 0.05), with R2 above 0.4 for 4 of them, while no feature reaches R2 0.4 among the three homologous types.
claims.source: Results, Deep L3 human glutamatergic t-types are morpho-electrically distinct, paragraph 4
claims.quote: ANOVA differences were seen in 15 out of 18 electrophysiological features and 24 out of 60 morphological features (FDR<0.05) (Supplementary Data 1). Many of these features showed very large effect sizes, with the variance explained by type surpassing 40% ( R 2 >0.4) for 4 electrophysiological and 20 morphological features, while no features met this threshold for the three homologous types (maximum R 2 =0.26).
claims.criterion: The t-type ANOVA on deep FREM3, CARM1P1 and COL22A1 cells (21, 17 and 37 neurons in the Figure 6b legend; CARM1P1 and COL22A1 are not cut by depth, as in the code). A feature differs when its BH-corrected p is below 0.05. Reproduced when both counts are within tolerance and no electrophysiological feature has R2 above 0.4 in fig4e-human-ephys-anova; partially reproduced when one count is within tolerance. The maximum R2 of 0.26 for the homologous types is not tested, as the text does not say which modality gives it and the electrophysiological maximum is 0.16.

claims.statement: The deep L3 types differ in 24 of 60 morphological features (FDR below 0.05), with R2 above 0.4 for 20 of them.
claims.source: Results, Deep L3 human glutamatergic t-types are morpho-electrically distinct, paragraph 4; Figure 6d
claims.quote: ANOVA differences were seen in 15 out of 18 electrophysiological features and 24 out of 60 morphological features (FDR<0.05)
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset. The t-type ANOVA on deep FREM3, CARM1P1 and COL22A1 cells with a reconstruction (CARM1P1 and COL22A1 not cut by depth, as in the code), for each of the 60 morphological features of the code's table. As in the code (run_regressions in morpho_electro_feature_analysis.ipynb), a feature with no p-value is dropped before the Benjamini-Hochberg correction (one, basal_dendrite_pct_above_apical_dendrite_none, in these cells), and R2 above 0.4 is counted over the features kept; the notebook prints 24 and 20.

claims.statement: CARM1P1 neurons have a faster AP upstroke than deep FREM3 and COL22A1 neurons, and a higher input resistance than deep FREM3 neurons.
claims.source: Results, Deep L3 human glutamatergic t-types are morpho-electrically distinct, paragraph 2; Figure 6c
claims.quote: Electrophysiologically, CARM1P1 neurons exhibited a faster action potential upstroke than the other deep types ( Fig. 6c ). This extensive dendritic branching did not predict a lower input resistance, which was higher than deep FREM3 neurons ( Fig. 6c ).
claims.criterion: The pairwise test over the three deep types (Figure 6c legend; BH over the three pairs of a feature, as the code's plot_mw_bars). "Faster upstroke" is read as (a) the AP upstroke rate (upstroke_long_square) or (b) the upstroke/downstroke ratio, the feature the code plots for the deep types; both are run. The upstroke part is the one both readings give, and is methods_underspecified when they differ. Reproduced when CARM1P1 upstroke is significantly higher than both deep FREM3 and COL22A1, and CARM1P1 input resistance is significantly higher than deep FREM3; partially reproduced when one of the two parts holds.

claims.statement: COL22A1 neurons have very high input resistance and a steeper f-I gain than the other deep L3 types, and less sag than CARM1P1 neurons.
claims.source: Results, Deep L3 human glutamatergic t-types are morpho-electrically distinct, paragraph 3; Figure 6b and 6c
claims.quote: COL22A1 neurons exhibited very high input resistance ( Fig. 6c ) and thus were the most responsive to current injection, displaying a steeper firing frequency to current input gain relative to the other deep L3 t-types. Interestingly, COL22A1 neurons showed a smaller amount of sag than CARM1P1 neurons ( Fig. 6b )
claims.criterion: The pairwise test over the three deep types, for input resistance, f-I slope and sag. The sag and f-I gain findings are shown in the paper only in Figure 6b (traces, and f-I curves normalized to rheobase), with no test; the post hoc Mann-Whitney test of the Methods (Analysis of features by t-type and species, paragraph 2) and Figure 6c is used for them too, on the sag and fi_fit_slope features. Reproduced when COL22A1 input resistance and f-I slope are each significantly higher than both deep FREM3 and CARM1P1, and COL22A1 sag is significantly lower than CARM1P1 sag; partially reproduced when at least two of the three features hold.

claims.statement: CARM1P1 neurons have the largest total dendritic length of the L2 and L3 t-types, with extensive proximal oblique and basal branching, while COL22A1 neurons have very sparse branching.
claims.source: Results, Deep L3 human glutamatergic t-types are morpho-electrically distinct, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 6a
claims.quote: CARM1P1 neurons had the largest total dendritic length of all the L2 and L3 t-types, despite having a shorter apical dendrite length on average. ... COL22A1 had very sparse dendritic branching ( Fig. 6a ).
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset. The paper gives no measure, cell set or test for this claim, and the code computes none. The readings it allows are these. Total dendritic length is the sum of apical_dendrite_total_length_none and basal_dendrite_total_length_none per cell (the code's table has no total). "All the L2 and L3 t-types" is (a) the five t-types with FREM3 whole, or (b) with FREM3 split at 0.575 into superficial and deep. Largest is by (i) the mean, the paper's "on average" in the same sentence, or (ii) the median, over reconstructed cells, with no test, since the paper reports none. The apical part ("shorter apical dendrite length on average") is apical_dendrite_total_length_none below that of deep FREM3. Sparse branching of COL22A1 is the fewest apical and basal branches (apical_dendrite_num_branches_none, basal_dendrite_num_branches_none) among the three deep types, by the same mean or median. Reproduced when CARM1P1 is largest and COL22A1 sparsest under every reading; methods underspecified when the readings differ.

claims.statement: 219 marker genes distinguish deep FREM3, CARM1P1 and COL22A1, 77 of them also found in Patch-seq cells, enriched for axon, synapse, calcium ion binding and extracellular matrix terms.
claims.source: Results, Deep L3 human glutamatergic t-types are morpho-electrically distinct, paragraphs 5 and 6; Figure 6e; Extended Data Figure 9
claims.quote: we used genesorteR 44 with slightly relaxed parameters (quant = 0.7) to identify DE genes selective for one or two of these three t-type sets, and found 219 such marker genes ( Extended Data Fig. 9 ). ... Furthermore, 77 of these 219 marker genes (including four genes shown in Fig. 6e ) were also defined as marker genes by Patch-seq
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset.

claims.statement: Large FREM3 and CARM1P1 neurons in deep L3 are SMI-32 immunoreactive while COL22A1 neurons are not, and NEFH, the gene coding the SMI-32 epitope, is higher in deep FREM3 and CARM1P1 than in COL22A1 and the superficial types.
claims.source: Results, Deep L3 human glutamatergic t-types are morpho-electrically distinct, paragraph 7; Figure 6e and 6f
claims.quote: The large FREM3 and CARM1P1 neurons were SMI-32ir, while COL22A1 neurons were not SMI-32ir. Furthermore, the gene coding SMI-32, NEFH, also shows increased expression in deep FREM3 and CARM1P1 relative to COL22A1 and all the superficial glutamatergic t-types ( Fig. 6e ).
claims.criterion: Not tested on the dandiset. The paper gives no counts of labelled cells.

claims.statement: The dandiset holds the recordings the paper analyses and the files its notebooks name, with the properties the paper and the notebooks give.
claims.source: Results, opening paragraph; Data availability; the four notebooks at ee08fb6
claims.quote: The datasets are publicly available in NWB format on the DANDI archive
claims.criterion: Each of the five files named in the opening comment is present, and a recording of mouse 412804 with the properties below (the notebook's own file name is local). The real Neuropixels recording has a sampling rate of 30 kHz and lasts 15 min (27,000,000 frames), with 246 channels (the paper) or 248 (the notebook); the simulated recording lasts 10 min and its ground truth has 250 units; the rat recording has 384 channels at 30 kHz; the Biocam recording has 1024 channels at about 23199 Hz. Reproduced when all hold under one of the two channel counts; partially reproduced when a file is missing or a property differs, naming which.

claims.statement: On the real Neuropixels recording the six sorters return very different numbers of units: Tridesclous the fewest (187) and SpyKING Circus the most (628); HerdingSpikes2 210, Kilosort2 446, IronClust 233 and HDSort 317.
claims.source: Results, Spike sorters show low agreement for the same high-density dataset, paragraph 3; Figure 1B
claims.quote: with Tridesclous (TDC) finding the least units (187) and SpyKING Circus (SC) finding the most units (628). HerdingSpikes2 finds 210 units; Kilosort2 finds 446 units; IronClust finds 233 units; and HDSort finds 317 units
claims.criterion: Sorters, versions and parameters as in the opening comment, on the real Neuropixels recording. Reproduced when all six counts are within tolerance; partially reproduced when Tridesclous has the fewest units and SpyKING Circus the most but some count is outside tolerance. The notebook printed 448 for Kilosort2 and 234 for IronClust.

claims.statement: Of the 2031 units detected on the real recording, all six sorters agree on only 33, and two or more sorters agree on only 263.
claims.source: Results, Spike sorters show low agreement for the same high-density dataset, paragraph 4; Figure 1C
claims.quote: Of the 2031 total detected units, all six sorters agree on just 33 of the units ... We also find that two or more sorters agree on just 263 of the total units
claims.criterion: Sorters, agreement graph and k as in the opening comment. The counts of agreement units with k = 6 and with k >= 2 are compared with 33 and 263. The total is the sum of the six sorters' unit counts, the only reading the text allows ("total detected units"); the counts the paper gives in Figure 1B sum to 2021, not 2031, which is within tolerance. The number of agreement units (components) is reported as well. Reproduced when the three values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: For most sorters more than half of their units match no other sorter; IronClust and Tridesclous are the exceptions.
claims.source: Results, Spike sorters show low agreement for the same high-density dataset, paragraph 4; Figure 1D
claims.quote: For most sorters, over 50% of the units that they find do not match with any other sorter (with the exceptions of Ironclust and Tridesclous)
claims.criterion: Sorters, agreement graph and k as in the opening comment. Per sorter, the fraction of the agreement units holding one of its units that have k = 1, as the notebook's per-sorter table computes it. Reproduced when the fraction exceeds 0.5 for HerdingSpikes2, Kilosort2, SpyKING Circus and HDSort and is below 0.5 for IronClust and Tridesclous; partially reproduced when it exceeds 0.5 for at least four sorters but the exceptions are other sorters. The notebook printed 50.7% for Kilosort2, close to the boundary.

claims.statement: Matched units mostly agree closely: around 80% of the agreement scores of agreed-upon units are 0.8 or higher.
claims.source: Results, Spike sorters show low agreement for the same high-density dataset, paragraph 4; Figure 1, figure supplement 2
claims.quote: For agreed-upon units, around 80% of the agreement scores are 0.8 or higher, indicating that matched units typically have high spike train agreement
claims.criterion: Sorters, agreement graph and k as in the opening comment. Two details are open. The recording: the Results cite the supplement in the paragraph on the real recording, while its legend and the author response say it shows the simulated ground-truth recording; both are read. The scores: (a) the agreement scores of all matched pairs (the graph's edges, all at least 0.5), or (b) the average agreement of each agreement unit with k >= 2 (the code's avg_agreement). The legend says "over 80%" and "greater than 0.8"; the Results "around 80%" and "0.8 or higher"; the tolerance covers both. Reproduced when the fraction is within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: On a rat cortex Neuropixels recording (six sorters) and a mouse retina Biocam recording (the four sorters able to process it, HerdingSpikes2, Kilosort2, IronClust and HDSort) the sorters disagree as much as on the first recording.
claims.source: Results, Spike sorters show low agreement for the same high-density dataset, paragraph 5; Figure 1, figure supplements 3 and 4
claims.quote: In both cases, we find similar disagreement among the sorters
claims.criterion: Sorters, agreement graph and k as in the opening comment. The Biocam recording is first passed through blank_saturation, as in its notebook. The paper does not say how similarity was judged and its figures could not be read here, so the readings are the two measures it uses for the first recording: (a) Figure 1D, more than half of the sorters have over 50% of their units at k = 1 (the legends of both supplements say most sorters find many units that other sorters do not); (b) Figure 1C, agreement units found by all sorters are at most 8% of all detected units (the 7.24% of the simulated recording, which the paper calls a large disagreement, widened by 10%). The two readings are choices of measure, so each recording's outcome is the one both give, and the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ. Reproduced when both readings hold for both recordings; partially reproduced when they hold for one recording only.

claims.statement: On the simulated recording with 250 ground-truth units the sorters again return very different numbers of units: Tridesclous 189, HDSort 458, HerdingSpikes2 233, Kilosort2 415, IronClust 283 and SpyKING Circus 343.
claims.source: Results, Evaluating spike sorters on a simulated dataset, paragraph 2; Figure 2C
claims.quote: The number of detected units range from the 189 units found by Tridesclous to the 458 units found by HDSort. HerdingSpikes2 finds 233 units; Kilosort2 finds 415 units; IronClust finds 283 units; and SpyKING Circus finds 343 units
claims.criterion: Sorters as in the opening comment, with the same parameters as on the real recording, on the simulated recording. Reproduced when all six counts are within tolerance; partially reproduced when Tridesclous has the fewest and HDSort the most but some count is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: Sorters trade precision against recall differently: HerdingSpikes2, SpyKING Circus and HDSort favour precision, IronClust recall, Kilosort2 scores well on both, and Tridesclous shows no bias.
claims.source: Figure 2, figure supplement 1A legend; Results, Evaluating spike sorters on a simulated dataset, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Some sorters seem to favor precision (HerdingSpikes, SpyKING Circus, HDSort), others instead have higher recall (Ironclust) or score well on both measures (Kilosort2). Tridesclous does not show a bias towards precision or recall
claims.criterion: Precision and recall per ground-truth unit from the ground-truth comparison of the opening comment (the notebook's perf_by_units). The paper shows scatter plots and does not say how a bias is summarized, so the readings are the per-sorter median precision and median recall over (a) all 250 ground-truth units or (b) the ground-truth units with a Hungarian match. Under a reading, the claim holds when median precision exceeds median recall for HerdingSpikes2, SpyKING Circus and HDSort; median recall exceeds median precision for IronClust; both Kilosort2 medians are at least 0.8 (the Methods' well-detected score); and Tridesclous has a smaller absolute difference between the two than each of those four. Reproduced when all hold under one reading; partially reproduced when the directions for HerdingSpikes2, SpyKING Circus, HDSort and IronClust hold.

claims.statement: Accuracy depends on the SNR of the ground-truth units for every sorter except Kilosort2, which reaches almost perfect accuracy on low-SNR units.
claims.source: Results, Evaluating spike sorters on a simulated dataset, paragraph 2; Figure 2, figure supplement 1B
claims.quote: Moreover, the accuracy is modulated by the SNR of the ground-truth units for all spike sorters except Kilosort2 which achieves an almost perfect performance on the low-SNR units
claims.criterion: Accuracy per ground-truth unit as in fig2s1a-precision-recall-bias; ground-truth SNR as in the opening comment. The paper reports no test (its reporting form says it has none), so dependence is read as a Spearman correlation of accuracy with SNR over the 250 ground-truth units, positive with p < 0.05. Low-SNR units are open, read as (a) those below the median ground-truth SNR or (b) those below the mode of the ground-truth SNR histogram (bins of 1, a standard choice), the reference Figure 3, figure supplement 2 uses. The two cuts are thresholds the paper does not give, so the outcome is the one both give, blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ. Reproduced when the correlation is positive with p < 0.05 for HerdingSpikes2, IronClust, Tridesclous, SpyKING Circus and HDSort, Kilosort2 has the weakest correlation of the six, and, under both cuts, Kilosort2's median accuracy on low-SNR units is at least 0.8 and above every other sorter's; partially reproduced when the Kilosort2 parts hold but the correlation fails for one other sorter.

claims.statement: Kilosort2 scores higher than the other sorters for most ground-truth units.
claims.source: Results, Evaluating spike sorters on a simulated dataset, paragraph 2; Figure 2D
claims.quote: Kilosort2 attains significantly higher scores than the rest of the spike sorters for most ground-truth units
claims.criterion: Scores per ground-truth unit as in fig2s1a-precision-recall-bias. The paper reports no test behind "significantly", so the claim is judged by its words "for most ground-truth units": for each of the five other sorters, Kilosort2's score exceeds that sorter's for more than half of the 250 ground-truth units. "Scores" is read as (a) accuracy or (b) each of accuracy, precision and recall, the three metrics of Figure 2D. The two readings are choices of measure, so the outcome is the one both give, blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ. Reproduced when this holds for all five sorters; partially reproduced when it holds for three or four. A paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test per pair is shown, not used.

claims.statement: Kilosort2 has the most well-detected units (245) but also many false positive (147) and redundant (21) units, and two overmerged units.
claims.source: Results, Evaluating spike sorters on a simulated dataset, paragraph 3; Figure 2E
claims.quote: While Kilosort2 has the most well-detected units (245), this comes at the cost of a high percentage of false positive (147) and redundant (21) units ... In both cases two overmerged units are found
claims.criterion: Unit classes from the ground-truth comparison of the opening comment. The tolerance for the overmerged count is one unit, since 10% of 2 is below the smallest difference a count can show. Reproduced when the four counts are within tolerance and Kilosort2 has more well-detected units than each other sorter; partially reproduced when it has the most well-detected units but a count is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: With Kilosort2's own curation, which removes units with an estimated contamination above 20%, false positive and redundant units are fewer but persist: 241 well detected, 93 false positive, 18 redundant and 2 overmerged.
claims.source: Results, Evaluating spike sorters on a simulated dataset, paragraph 3 (parenthesis)
claims.quote: In that case the number of well-detected units is 241, false positives are 93, and redundant units are 18. In both cases two overmerged units are found
claims.criterion: Kilosort2's automated curation is the sorter wrapper's keep_good_only=True (spikesorters 0.3.3, the line commented out in the notebooks), which keeps the units Kilosort2 labels good. Applied to (a) the same Kilosort2 run as fig2e-ks2-unit-types, or (b) a run with keep_good_only=True; the paper does not say which. Classes as in fig2e-ks2-unit-types, overmerged tolerance one unit for the reason given there. Reproduced when the four counts are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when false positive and redundant counts fall below those of fig2e-ks2-unit-types but stay above zero.

claims.statement: Tridesclous detects very few false positive or redundant units while finding many well-detected units, and HDSort finds many more false positive units than any other sorter.
claims.source: Results, Evaluating spike sorters on a simulated dataset, paragraph 3; Figure 2E
claims.quote: Notably, Tridesclous detects very few false positive/redundant units while still finding many well-detected units. HDSort, on the flip side, finds many more false positive units than any other spike sorter
claims.criterion: Unit classes as in fig2e-ks2-unit-types. Reproduced when HDSort's false positive count is the highest of the six sorters, Tridesclous has the lowest fraction of its units that are false positive or redundant, and at least half of Tridesclous's units are well detected ("many"); partially reproduced when the HDSort part or the Tridesclous part holds alone.

claims.statement: On the simulated recording only 139 of the 1921 detected units (7.24%) are agreed upon by all six sorters.
claims.source: Results, Low-agreement units are mainly false positives, paragraph 1; Figure 3A
claims.quote: Again, we observe a large disagreement among the spike sorting outputs with only 139 units of the 1921 total units (7.24%) being in agreement among all sorters
claims.criterion: Sorters, agreement graph and k as in the opening comment. The 7.24% is 139 over 1921, the sum of the six sorters' unit counts, not over the number of agreement units; it is computed that way. Reproduced when the three values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: HDSort, SpyKING Circus and Kilosort2 are more prone to finding low-agreement units than HerdingSpikes2, IronClust and Tridesclous.
claims.source: Results, Low-agreement units are mainly false positives, paragraph 1; Figure 3B
claims.quote: highlighting that some sorters are more prone to finding low agreement units (HDSort, SpyKING Circus, Kilosort2) than other sorters (HerdingSpikes2, Ironclust, Tridesclous)
claims.criterion: Sorters, agreement graph and k as in the opening comment. Per sorter, the fraction of its agreement units with k = 1, as in fig1d-most-units-unmatched. Reproduced when each of HDSort, SpyKING Circus and Kilosort2 has a higher fraction than each of HerdingSpikes2, IronClust and Tridesclous; partially reproduced when two of the three named sorters are among the three highest.

claims.statement: Almost all false positive units are found by a single sorter, while most real units are matched by more than one sorter; false positives found by two or more sorters number 4 for HerdingSpikes2, Kilosort2 and IronClust, 2 for SpyKING Circus and HDSort and 1 for Tridesclous.
claims.source: Results, Low-agreement units are mainly false positives, paragraph 2; Figure 3C legend
claims.quote: The plots show that (almost) all false positive units are ones that are found by only a single sorter (not matched with any other sorters), while most real units are matched by more than one sorter
claims.criterion: Sorters, agreement graph and k as in the opening comment. True and false positive agreement units as in the opening comment (the notebook's rule; the Methods do not define them for this figure). The counts are from the legend; their tolerance is one unit, since 10% of a count below 5 is less than one unit. Reproduced when, for every sorter, the false positive units with k >= 2 are within tolerance, and its true positive units with k >= 2 outnumber those with k = 1; partially reproduced when this holds for four or five sorters.

claims.statement: With two sorters, combining Kilosort2 and IronClust identified true positives most reliably, with false positive and true positive detection rates of 96% and 95%.
claims.source: Results, Low-agreement units are mainly false positives, paragraph 2; Figure 3, figure supplement 1 legend
claims.quote: For two sorters, the most reliable identification of true positives for this dataset was achieved by combining Kilosort2 and Ironclust (96% and 95% false positive and true positive detection rate, respectively)
claims.criterion: No code for this figure was found; the legend gives the method: for each subset of sorters, the units of the other sorters are removed from the full comparison of fig3a, the units of the subset found by one sorter (k = 1) are predicted false positive and the others true positive, against the truth of fig3c-fp-found-by-one-sorter. The false positive detection rate is the fraction of false positive units predicted so, the true positive rate likewise. Open, with readings: removal (a) drops the nodes and recomputes connected components, or (b) keeps the full comparison's components and counts the subset's sorters in each; the rate is (i) pooled over the units of the subset's sorters or (ii) the mean of the per-sorter rates. The legend says the best pairs combine two of Kilosort2, IronClust and HDSort; the Results name Kilosort2 and IronClust. The four combinations of readings are choices of method, so the outcome is the one they all give, blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ. Reproduced when both rates are within tolerance and Kilosort2 with IronClust has the highest true positive rate of the 15 pairs; partially reproduced when the rates are within tolerance and the best pair is another pair of Kilosort2, IronClust and HDSort.

claims.statement: A pair of sorters suffices to isolate almost all false positive units, but with fewer than four sorters a significant fraction of true positive units, found by only one sorter, are wrongly classed as false positives; four or more sorters reliably identify most true positives.
claims.source: Results, Low-agreement units are mainly false positives, paragraph 2; Figure 3, figure supplement 1 legend
claims.quote: This analysis showed that using a pair of sorters is sufficient to isolate almost all false positive units in each sorter, yet when fewer than four sorter outputs are compared, a significant fraction of true positive units found by only one sorter can be wrongly classified as false positives with this approach
claims.criterion: Subsets of two to five sorters and the rates as in fig3s1-ks2-ic-best-pair, under the same readings. "Almost all" is read against the paper's own example of a pair, 96%, widened by 10%: the median false positive detection rate over the 15 pairs is at least 86.4%. "Most" true positives is more than half: every subset of four or five sorters has a true positive rate above 0.5. The loss with fewer sorters: the lowest true positive rate over pairs and over triples is below the lowest over subsets of four. The outcome is the one all the readings give, blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ. Reproduced when all three hold; partially reproduced when the false positive part holds and one true positive part fails.

claims.statement: Ground-truth units with higher SNR are found by more sorters.
claims.source: Results, Low-agreement units are mainly false positives, paragraph 3; Figure 3D
claims.quote: This shows, as expected, that higher SNR units have higher agreement among sorters
claims.criterion: Sorters, agreement graph and k as in the opening comment. For each sorter, its true positive units (as in fig3c-fp-found-by-one-sorter) with the SNR of the ground-truth unit each matches (ground-truth SNR as in the opening comment), as the notebook's Figure 3D cell pairs them. The paper reports no test; the claim is read as a positive Spearman correlation between k and SNR. Reproduced when the correlation is positive for all six sorters; partially reproduced when positive for four or five.

claims.statement: For Kilosort2, SNR is not a good predictor of false positives: many of its false positive units have an SNR above the mode of the ground-truth SNR.
claims.source: Results, Low-agreement units are mainly false positives, paragraph 3; Figure 3, figure supplement 2 legend
claims.quote: Many detected false positive units have an SNR above the mode of the ground-truth SNR, indicating that SNR is not a good measure to separate false and true positives in this case
claims.criterion: No code for this figure was found. The SNR of each Kilosort2 unit is computed with the same function and arguments as the ground-truth SNR (opening comment); the mode of the ground-truth SNR is the peak of its histogram in bins of 1 (a standard choice). Units "without matches" are read as (a) the Methods' false positive class (fig2e-ks2-unit-types) or (b) units that are the best match of no ground-truth unit (the rule of fig3c-fp-found-by-one-sorter). "Many" is open, read as more than half or as at least a quarter of those units above the mode. Reproduced when every reading holds; not reproduced when none does; blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ.

claims.statement: The two experts' manual curations of the Kilosort2 output agree on most curated units (226 of 351, 64.2%), and 174 Kilosort2 units are discarded by both.
claims.source: Results, Consensus units highly overlap with manually curated ones, paragraph 1; Figure 4A
claims.quote: most of the curated units (226 out of 351–64.2%) are agreed upon by both experts. Notably, 174 units found by Kilosort2 are discarded by both experts
claims.criterion: As the notebook's Venn diagram: compare_multiple_sorters on curated 1, curated 2 and the Kilosort2 run (defaults), and the counts of agreement units by which of the three they hold. Read as 226 = units holding both curators, 351 = units holding either curator, 174 = units holding Kilosort2 alone. For 226 and 351 a second reading is the pairwise compare_two_sorters(curated 1, curated 2): matched pairs, and the two counts summed less the matched pairs. Curated counts do not depend on a sorter run; 174 does, as the curators worked on the paper's run. Reproduced when the values are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when 226, 351 and 64.2% are and 174 is not.

claims.statement: Only a small percentage of each sorter's units match the curated units; IronClust matches best (59.83% and 61.1%), above Kilosort2 (50.67% and 56.25%), from whose output the curations were made.
claims.source: Results, Consensus units highly overlap with manually curated ones, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
claims.quote: The highest percentage match is actually IronClust which is surprising given that the initial sorting output was curated from Kilosort2’s output (IC ∩ C1 = 59.83%, IC ∩ C2 = 61.1%, KS ∩ C1 = 50.67%, KS ∩ C2 = 56.25%)
claims.criterion: Percentages as in the opening comment (comparisons with the curated sortings), for all of each sorter's units. Reproduced when the four values are within tolerance and IronClust has the highest percentage of the six sorters for both curators; partially reproduced when IronClust is highest but a value is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: Consensus units (found by at least two sorters) match the curated units at above 70% for every sorter; Kilosort2 is highest (84.55% and 89.55%), slightly above IronClust (82.63% and 83.83%).
claims.source: Results, Consensus units highly overlap with manually curated ones, paragraph 2; Figure 4C
claims.quote: The average match percentage is above 70% for all sorters showing that there is a large agreement between the manually curated outputs and the consensus-based output. Kilosort2 has the highest match (KS c ∩ C1 = 84.55%, KS c ∩ C2 = 89.55%), slightly higher than Ironclust (IC c ∩ C1 = 82.63%, IC c ∩ C2 = 83.83%)
claims.criterion: Consensus units and percentages as in the opening comment. "The average match percentage is above 70%" is read as (a) the mean of the two curators' percentages for each sorter, or (b) each curator's percentage (the legend says the percent is above 70% for all sorters). Reproduced when, under one reading, every sorter is above 70%, the four values are within tolerance and Kilosort2 is highest for both curators; partially reproduced when every sorter is above 70% but the Kilosort2 parts fail.

claims.statement: Units found by only one sorter rarely match the curated units; the only notable overlap is Kilosort2's (18.58% with C1 and 24.34% with C2).
claims.source: Results, Consensus units highly overlap with manually curated ones, paragraph 2; Figure 4D legend
claims.quote: The only significant overlap is between Curator one and Kilosort2, with a percent around 18% (KS nc ∩ C1 = 18.58%, KS nc ∩ C2 = 24.34%)
claims.criterion: Non-consensus units and percentages as in the opening comment. Reproduced when the two Kilosort2 values are within tolerance, every other sorter's percentage is below Kilosort2's for the same curator, and every sorter's non-consensus percentage is below its consensus percentage (fig4c), the contrast the Results draw; partially reproduced when the last two hold but a Kilosort2 value is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: After quality control, 1,227 Patch-seq neurons from mouse primary motor cortex were assigned to transcriptomic types, covering 77 of the 90 neuronal t-types of the reference taxonomy.
claims.source: Results, "Patch-seq of mouse primary motor cortex", paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 1a
claims.quote: leaving 1,227 neurons for further analysis ... The resulting data set covered 77 out of the 90 neuronal t-types (Fig. 1a)

claims.statement: A sparse reduced-rank regression of 17 electrophysiological features on gene expression, using 25 genes and a rank-5 latent space, reached a cross-validated R2 of 0.38, with cross-validated correlations of 0.90, 0.74 and 0.67 between the first three pairs of projections.
claims.source: Results, "Distinct phenotypes of major families", paragraph 1; Figure 2
claims.quote: The selected model used 25 genes with a 5-dimensional latent space and achieved a cross-validated R2 of 0.38 ... The cross-validated correlations between the first three pairs of projections were 0.90, 0.74, and 0.67, respectively.

claims.statement: A reduced-rank regression restricted to ion channel genes did not perform much worse than the full model, with a cross-validated R2 of 0.33 and correlations of 0.86, 0.71 and 0.56.
claims.source: Results, "Distinct phenotypes of major families", paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 5e-f
claims.quote: A reduced-rank regression model restricted to using only ion channel genes (Extended Data Fig. 5) did not perform much worse than the full model (cross-validated R2 = 0.33 and correlations 0.86, 0.71, and 0.56, respectively

claims.statement: In a k-nearest-neighbour classification of cells into seven transcriptomic families from electrophysiological features, the confusion matrix was mostly diagonal, with only the ET and IT subclasses strongly overlapping.
claims.source: Results, "Distinct phenotypes of major families", paragraph 3; Figure 3a, d
claims.quote: We quantified this separation using a confusion matrix for k-nearest neighbours (kNN) classification of cells into families: it was mostly diagonal, with only the ET and IT subclasses strongly overlapping (Fig. 3d).

claims.statement: Families were less separable by morphology than by electrophysiology among inhibitory neurons, and most separable when electrophysiological and morphological features were combined.
claims.source: Results, "Distinct phenotypes of major families", paragraph 4; Figure 3b-d
claims.quote: The separability between inhibitory families was weaker than with electrophysiological features (Fig. 3d). The between-family separability was strongest when we had combined electrophysiological and morphological features into a joint representation (Fig. 3c, d)

claims.statement: Across 200 pairs of t-types from the same family, the transcriptomic distance and the electrophysiological distance between t-types were correlated with r = 0.60.
claims.source: Results, "Continuous phenotypic variation", paragraph 2; Figure 4c
claims.quote: Pooling the pairs across all families, we found that these two distance measures were correlated, with r = 0.60 (Fig. 4c, n = 200 pairs

claims.statement: Among IT t-types, transcriptomic distances were strongly correlated with differences in average soma depth, r = 0.70.
claims.source: Results, "Continuous phenotypic variation", paragraph 3; Figure 4d
claims.quote: Transcriptomic distances between t-types were strongly correlated with the average soma depth differences (r = 0.70; Fig. 4d).

claims.statement: Most t-types were classified into their own family from electrophysiology, but some, such as Sst Pvalb Calb2, Lamp5 Egln3_1 and Vip Mybpc1, were often classified into another family.
claims.source: Results, "Variability in individual t-types", paragraph 1; Figure 5a
claims.quote: Most t-types could be unambiguously placed into the correct family (Fig. 5a), but some t-types were in between two families ... Vip Mybpc1 neurons often had Sst-like firing.

claims.statement: Many t-types had a normalized total variance of electrophysiological features well above that of k-means clusters, while some, such as Pvalb Vipr2_2, appeared homogeneous.
claims.source: Results, "Variability in individual t-types", paragraph 3; Figure 5b
claims.quote: We found that many t-types had total variance substantially above the variances of the k-means clusters (Fig. 5b) ... some of them, such as Pvalb Vipr2_2 (chandelier cells), appeared morpho-electrically homogeneous.

claims.statement: At physiological temperature, 185 neurons were sequenced from 8 adult mice (7 Sst-Cre/Ai9 and 1 Pvalb-Cre/Ai9); 177 got a t-type (110 Sst, 43 IT, 12 ET, 10 Pvalb, 2 NP); 175 were in layer 5; electrophysiological features were extracted for 184.
claims.source: Methods, "Experiments at physiological temperature", paragraph 2
claims.quote: We sequenced in total 185 neurons, obtained from 8 adult mice (7 Sst-Cre/Ai9 and 1 Pvalb-Cre/Ai9), of which 177 neurons passed the transcriptomic quality control and got a t-type assignment ... One hundred and ten cells mapped to the Sst subclass, 43 to IT, 12 to ET, 10 to Pvalb, and 2 to NP.
claims.criterion: The counts of neurons, mice and labels are exact records, so their tolerance is zero. The number of neurons with features depends on the feature extraction, so it takes the default 10%. A neuron counts as having features when all 17 features the paper uses are defined. Families are read from the t-type names in the files, as the paper names them (L5 PT types are ET). Reproduced if every count is within its tolerance; partially reproduced if the neuron, mouse and family counts match and others do not.

claims.statement: Cells at physiological temperature were stimulated with the same paradigm as the main data set, 600 ms current pulses from -200 pA upwards in 20 pA steps up to 1,380 pA, sometimes stopped earlier.
claims.source: Methods, "Patch-seq recording procedures", paragraph 4, and "Experiments at physiological temperature", paragraph 1
claims.quote: Each neuron was injected with 600-ms-long current pulses starting from −200 pA and up to 1,380 pA with 20-pA increment steps (in some cases stimulation was stopped before reaching 1,380 pA) ... Intrinsic electrophysiological recordings were obtained using the same stimulation paradigm as described above.
claims.criterion: For every file, the stimulus of each sweep is read from the file. A cell conforms when every step lasts 600 ms (to within 1 ms), the first step is -200 pA, consecutive sweeps differ by 20 pA (the 0 pA sweep included), and the largest step is at most 1,380 pA. Reproduced if all cells conform; partially reproduced if at least 90% do; not reproduced otherwise.
