claims.criterion: For each field and state, fp and fLFP from in-field spikes in speed bins of 20 cm/s from 20 to 120 cm/s (bins with at least 50 spikes). Pooling states, least-squares slopes of fp and of fLFP on bin speed over all field-bins. Reproduced when the fp slope is positive (P < 0.05) and larger than the fLFP slope (95% bootstrap interval of the difference over fields above 0), and in every speed bin with at least 10 fields measured in both states the median fp during cooling is below that before cooling. Partially reproduced when one of the two parts holds.

claims.statement: The theta-repeated cross-correlograms of place cell pairs had a period of about 85 ms before cooling, which lengthened during MS cooling (P = 0.002), while the period of the phase cross-correlograms was unaffected (P = 0.32).
claims.source: Figure 5D, 5E and 5F
claims.quote: Duration of the theta-repeated spike cross-correlograms (as in d), calculated for each session, significantly increased during MS cooling ... whereas the spike phase-lag correlations remained unaffected (n.s., P = 0.32).
claims.criterion: Pairs of place fields of different cells on the same segment whose bins overlap, in FIG5 sessions; spikes on forward runs above 10 cm/s within the union of the two fields; at least 50 spikes of each cell in the state. Each pair's cross-correlogram (1 ms bins, 60-bin Gaussian window, lags up to 400 ms) has a main peak (the largest local maximum within 70 ms of zero); the pair's period is the mean spacing from it to the largest local maxima 60 to 200 ms away on either side. The same on the theta phase axis (0.01 pi bins, main peak within pi, neighbours pi to 3 pi away). Per session and condition (control is pre and post combined), the median over pairs. Reproduced when the median control period over sessions is within tolerance, the cooling period is longer by a Wilcoxon signed-rank test over sessions at P < 0.05, and the phase period does not differ (P >= 0.05). Partially reproduced when the lengthening holds and one other part fails. The period of the summed cross-correlogram of all pairs is a variant.

claims.statement: Distance-time compression of place cell pairs (0.54 cm/ms before cooling) decreased during MS cooling (P = 0.02), while distance-phase compression was unchanged (P = 0.92).
claims.source: Figure 5C and 5G; Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Compression index, c (cm/ms; i.e., the slope in c), significantly decreased during MS cooling (* P = 0.02) but the distance/phase lag compression (cm/radian) remained unaffected (P = 0.92).
claims.criterion: Pairs as fig5d-ccg-period. Time lag tau is the lag of the largest local maximum of the smoothed pair cross-correlogram within 70 ms of zero (pairs without one are dropped), phase lag the same within pi of zero on the phase axis; Ltr is the signed distance of the field peaks. Compression is the least-squares slope of Ltr on tau (cm/ms), and on phase lag (cm/rad), in pairs with at least 50 spikes of each cell. Reproduced when the compression over all pre pairs pooled is within tolerance, the per-session compression is lower during cooling than in control by a Wilcoxon signed-rank test at P < 0.05, and the phase compression does not differ (P >= 0.05). Partially reproduced when the decrease holds and one other part fails. The inverse slope of tau on Ltr, and a window of half the state's theta period, are variants.

claims.statement: During MS cooling the theta time lags between place cell pairs increased compared with before and after cooling (P = 8e-5 and P = 0.00032), and did not differ between before and after (P = 0.79).
claims.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 3; Figure 5H
claims.quote: During MS cooling, the time lags increased significantly ... whereas they were not different from each other during precooling and post-cooling sessions (P = 0.79)
claims.criterion: The absolute time lag of each pair (as fig5cg-compression) in each state. Readings, (a) Wilcoxon signed-rank test over pairs measured in both states; (b) the same over sessions of the median absolute lag. Reproduced when, under one reading, cooling is longer than both pre and post at P < 0.05. Partially reproduced when one comparison holds. Pre against post is reported.

claims.statement: Theta phase lags between place cell pairs were not affected by MS cooling (P > 0.24 between all conditions).
claims.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 3; Figure 5I
claims.quote: In contrast, phase lags between spikes of place cell pairs were not affected by MS cooling (Fig. 5i; P > 0.24 between all conditions).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, on the paper's sign-rank test. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests over pairs measured in both states of the absolute phase lag, for pre against cooling, cooling against post and pre against post. Reproduced when all give P >= 0.05; not reproduced when any gives P < 0.05.

claims.statement: The fraction of place cells active in a theta cycle was not significantly affected by MS cooling (P = 0.2).
claims.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 4; Figure 5J
claims.quote: we found that the fraction of place cells active in a given theta cycle was not significantly affected by MS cooling (Fig. 5j; P = 0.2).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on pre against cooling, the comparison the text reports. Theta cycles (between upward zero crossings of the theta phase) during forward runs above 10 cm/s in trials of FIG5 sessions; per cycle, the fraction of the session's place cells with at least one spike. The paper's default unpaired test, a Wilcoxon rank-sum test over cycles pooled across sessions. Reproduced when P >= 0.05, not reproduced when P < 0.05. The per-session medians and a signed-rank test over sessions are shown as a variant.

claims.statement: The number of spikes emitted by all neurons per theta cycle was preserved during MS cooling (P > 0.058 between all conditions).
claims.source: Results, MS temperature effects on theta time/phase compression of place cells sequences, paragraph 4; Figure 5K
claims.quote: The number of spikes emitted by all neurons per theta cycle was also preserved after MS cooling (Fig. 5k)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Cycles as fig5j-fraction-active-unchanged; spikes of all good units per cycle. Wilcoxon rank-sum tests over cycles pooled across sessions for pre against cooling, cooling against post and pre against post. Reproduced when all give P >= 0.05, not reproduced when any gives P < 0.05.

claims.statement: The waveforms of hippocampal action potentials were not affected by MS cooling.
claims.source: Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 3 (Supplementary Figure 1G)
claims.quote: Finally, the waveforms of action potentials in the hippocampus ... were not affected by MS cooling (Suppl. Fig. 1g).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. For units of UNIT sessions with at least 30 spikes in each window, the mean waveform in 120 s of pre-cooling trials and in the 120 s around the coldest cooling trial; trough-to-peak time and peak-to-peak amplitude on the channel of largest amplitude. The paper's default paired test, Wilcoxon signed-rank over units, at 0.05 for each measure. Reproduced when neither differs; not reproduced when either does.

claims.statement: The theta oscillation frequency of putative fast-spiking interneurons decreased during MS cooling, commensurate with the LFP theta.
claims.source: Results, Effects of MS cooling on single neuron properties, paragraph 1 (Supplementary Figure 2D)
claims.quote: Theta frequency oscillation of putative fast spiking interneurons also decelerated (Suppl. Fig. 2d), commensurate with the downward frequency shift of LFP theta oscillation.
claims.criterion: Putative interneurons of UNIT sessions; oscillation frequency of spikes in frames of trials above 10 cm/s, per state. Reproduced when it is lower during cooling than pre by a Wilcoxon signed-rank test over units at P < 0.05.

claims.statement: Hippocampal temperature fell by less than 1.5 C at the time of the largest MS temperature decrease, and later than the MS cooling.
claims.source: Results, MS cooling decreases hippocampal theta frequency and power, paragraph 3 (Supplementary Figure 1H to 1K)
claims.quote: we measured temperature simultaneously in the MS and hippocampus, and found < 1.5° C decrease in the hippocampus at the time of the largest MS temperature decrease ... the mild temperature decrease in the hippocampus was considerably delayed
claims.criterion: Needs the hippocampal temperature recordings of the control experiment.

claims.statement: Over 61 sessions in 4 rats, 7,390 well-isolated units were recorded (rat 1, 2,444; rat 2, 1,294; rat 3, 1,138; rat 4, 2,514), of which 2,038 were in the BLA, 782 in the central nuclei, 1,560 in the piriform cortex and 1,210 in the hippocampus.
claims.source: Results, BLA recordings and sleep physiology, paragraph 1; Supplementary Table 1
claims.quote: Over the course of a total of 61 sessions, we recorded 7,390 well-isolated units (rat 1, 2,444; rat 2, 1,294; rat ... 3, 1,138; rat 4, 2,514). On the basis of histological reconstruction of probe placement and probe movement record, 2,038 of these were in the BLA, 782 in the central nuclei, 1,560 in the piriform cortex and 1,210 in the hippocampus
claims.criterion: Counts of distinct sorted units and sessions, per rat and per location label (M1). Reproduced when every count is within its tolerance; partially reproduced when the totals are and some location counts are not.

claims.statement: Rats learned the daily location of the air puff. The speed ratio between the previous and the current danger zone rises from pre-run to run and post-run, reversing between pre-run and post-run.
claims.source: Results, Rats learn the daily location of an aversive air puff on a linear track, paragraph 1; Figure 1b, right; Supplementary Fig. 1b
claims.quote: Therefore, the systematic reversal in the speed ratio (previous/current danger zone) between pre- and ... post-run indicates learning of the new air puff location (Fig. 1b and Supplementary Fig. 1b).
claims.criterion: Per session and run epoch (pre-run, run, post-run), the mean speed in the current danger zone (the 20 cm before the day's air puff location, on laps of the day's air puff direction) and in the previous danger zone (the 20 cm before the previous day's location, on laps of the previous day's direction); speed from positions smoothed over 5 samples (LinearVelocity(pos,5)); ratio = (previous - current)/(previous + current) (Online Methods; BehavioralMeasures.m). Laps per M8 under each reading of O1. Sessions with all three ratios defined enter (the first session of a rat has no previous day). A one-way repeated-measures ANOVA over the three epochs, then paired t-tests (BehavioralMeasures_Stats.m). Reproduced when the ANOVA has p < 0.05 and the post-run ratio exceeds the pre-run ratio by paired t-test at p < 0.05/3 (O5 reading a) or p < 0.05 (reading b); the run against pre-run and run against post-run tests are reported.

claims.statement: The speed ratio changes across pre-run, run and post-run in each of the four rats taken alone, indicating that every rat learned the new air puff location.
claims.source: Supplementary Fig. 1b legend
claims.quote: The reversal of ratio between pre and post RUN indicates that all animals learned the new location during RUN and remembered it during post-RUN
claims.criterion: The per-session speed ratios of rats-learn-puff-location (each O1 reading), split by rat. Per rat, a one-way repeated-measures ANOVA over the three epochs (Supplementary Fig. 1b legend). Reproduced when every rat has p < 0.05; partially reproduced when three of the four rats do. The legend's Bonferroni-corrected post hoc tests are shown but give no P values to match.

claims.statement: Speed in the current danger zone is lower in post-run than in pre-run, and in run and post-run rats run slower in the current than in the previous danger zone.
claims.source: Results, Rats learn the daily location of an aversive air puff on a linear track, paragraph 2; Figure 1b, left; Figure 1c
claims.quote: This was quantitatively reflected by the significantly slower speed in the current danger zone in post-run compared to pre-run (Fig. 1b,c).
claims.criterion: The danger-zone speeds of rats-learn-puff-location. A two-way repeated-measures ANOVA (epoch by danger zone) over sessions with all six speeds, then paired t-tests (BehavioralMeasures_Stats.m). Reproduced when current-zone speed is lower in post-run than in pre-run and current-zone speed is lower than previous-zone speed in run and in post-run, each by paired t-test at p < 0.05/4 (O5 reading a) or p < 0.05 (reading b); partially reproduced when the post-run against pre-run test holds and one of the other two does not.

claims.statement: The location of the air puff on the track does not correlate with the speed in the current danger zone in pre-run, run or post-run.
claims.source: Results, Rats learn the daily location of an aversive air puff on a linear track, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The location of the air puff on the track did not correlate with the speed in the current danger zone in pre-run, training or post-run
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The text names no test; the code computes Pearson correlations (corrcoef) across sessions between the air puff location normalised to the track (0 to 1, flipped for right-to-left days so that 0 is the start of the air puff run) and the current-zone speed of each epoch (AirpuffPositionDistribution_Plot.m). Reproduced when none of the three correlations has p < 0.05; not reproduced when any does. The code's second measure, the distance of the location from the track centre, is shown as a variant. r is reported.

claims.statement: The aversive valence of the air puff diminishes over training days; rats run more laps per unit time as they habituate.
claims.source: Results, Rats learn the daily location of an aversive air puff on a linear track, paragraph 2; Supplementary Fig. 1c
claims.quote: The aversive valence of the air puff gradually diminished with training days (Supplementary Fig. 1c).
claims.criterion: Habituation index per training session = laps / time on the track x 100 (Online Methods; Performance.m counts left-to-right laps over the run epoch duration). The laps counted are open between the Methods ("back-and-forth laps"), the Supplementary Fig. 1c legend ("airpuff laps") and the code (left-to-right laps); all three are run. The paper shows the index per day for each rat and gives no test. Readings of "gradually diminished" (a) a Spearman correlation between the training day rank within the rat and the index, sessions of all rats pooled, positive with p < 0.05; (b) a positive Spearman correlation in at least 3 of the 4 rats. Reproduced when the outcome holds under every reading; otherwise reported as methods_underspecified with all results. Laps per O1, on the readings the dataset allows; when it holds neither lap intervals nor position, the claim is judged on O1 reading (c) alone, the back-and-forth laps between the reward ends that the Methods count.

claims.statement: BLA pyramidal cells fire faster in REM sleep and, to a lesser extent, in NREM sleep than in wakefulness.
claims.source: Results, BLA recordings and sleep physiology, paragraph 1; Figure 2c
claims.quote: we found a specific increase in the firing rate of BLA pyramidal cells, but not interneurons, during REM sleep and, to a lesser extent, NREM sleep relative to wakefulness
claims.criterion: Per BLA pyramidal cell, firing rates over all REM, all NREM and all wake intervals of the session (StatesFiringRates.m); ratios (REM - wake)/(REM + wake) and (NREM - wake)/(NREM + wake) (Online Methods). A two-sided Wilcoxon signed rank test of each ratio against 0. Cells per O4. Reproduced when both ratios have a positive median with p < 0.05 and the REM median exceeds the NREM median; partially reproduced when both are positive and significant but the REM median does not exceed the NREM median.

claims.statement: BLA interneurons do not change their firing rate between REM sleep and wake, and fire slightly less in NREM sleep than in wake.
claims.source: Figure 2c legend
claims.quote: Interneurons do not change firing rates between REM and wake ... and slightly decrease firing rates during NREM compared to wake
claims.criterion: As bla-pyr-sleep-firing-increase, for BLA interneurons (cells per O4). The REM part is a claim of absence judged on the paper's test, a two-sided Wilcoxon signed rank test of the REM/wake ratio against 0 at p < 0.05. Reproduced when that test does not reach p < 0.05 and the NREM/wake ratio has a negative median with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when only one of the two holds.

claims.statement: Hippocampus-BLA pyramidal cell pair correlations of the run are reinstated in post-sleep NREM, measured as explained variance (EV) exceeding the reverse explained variance (REV) across sessions.
claims.source: Results, BLA-hippocampus coordinated reactivations during NREM sleep, paragraph 1; Figure 3a-c
claims.quote: The EV and REV, calculated using hippocampus–BLA pyramidal cell pairs, showed significant reactivations between the hippocampus and BLA during post-NREM (Fig. 3c).
claims.criterion: EV and REV per session (M4) over hippocampal and BLA pyramidal cells, NREM bins of pre- and post-sleep (M2, M3). A two-sided Wilcoxon signed rank test of EV against REV across sessions (Online Methods, Statistical analysis; ExplainedVarianceMean_Ultimate.m). Reproduced when EV exceeds REV with p < 0.05 and the expected values hold (the mean EV - REV of 3.13 +- 0.73% s.e.m. is from Results, BLA-hippocampus coordinated reactivations during NREM sleep, paragraph 2, the Fig. 3d test); partially reproduced when the test holds and an expected value does not.

claims.statement: Hippocampus-BLA NREM reactivation holds when pyramidal cells and interneurons are both included.
claims.source: Results, BLA-hippocampus coordinated reactivations during NREM sleep, paragraph 1; Supplementary Fig. 5a
claims.quote: Reactivations were maintained when both pyramidal cells and interneurons were included in the EV calculation (Supplementary Fig. 5).
claims.criterion: As hpc-bla-reactivation-post-sleep with all hippocampal and BLA units. Reproduced when EV exceeds REV with two-sided Wilcoxon signed rank p < 0.05 across sessions. The 20-min epochs are reported as in reactivation-decay.

claims.statement: Hippocampus-BLA reactivation decays over the first hour of post-sleep NREM (mean EV - REV 2.89, 1.72 and 1.31% in successive 20-min NREM periods).
claims.source: Results, BLA-hippocampus coordinated reactivations during NREM sleep, paragraph 1; Figure 3c, right
claims.quote: The gradual decay in reactivations over the first hour of NREM sleep ... paralleled the previously described decay for pairs of hippocampal neurons
claims.criterion: Pyramidal pairs, sessions of hpc-bla-reactivation-post-sleep. The post-NREM bins are concatenated in time order and cut into the first 24,000 bins (20 min), the next 24,000, and the next 24,000 or what remains when fewer; each period's EV and REV use the whole pre-NREM and the run (ExplainedVariance_Ultimate.m). Only sessions with EV > REV in the first period enter (Online Methods). A Kruskal-Wallis test of EV - REV across the three periods (Results) and two-sided Wilcoxon signed rank tests of EV against REV in each period. Reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.05 with the means falling from the first to the third period and the expected values hold; partially reproduced when the means fall and the test or an expected value fails.

claims.statement: Hippocampus-BLA and hippocampus-piriform cortex reactivations are not significant in REM sleep.
claims.source: Results, BLA-hippocampus coordinated reactivations during NREM sleep, paragraph 2; Figure 3c, left
claims.quote: Reactivations during REM sleep ... were not significant in any structure
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. EV and REV (M4) from the REM bins of pre- and post-sleep, sessions with more than 180 s of REM in each, pyramidal pairs; two-sided Wilcoxon signed rank test of EV against REV, for hippocampus-BLA pairs and for hippocampus-piriform pairs (piriform units per M1). Reproduced when neither test has p < 0.05, not reproduced when either does; the median EV - REV is reported. Hippocampus-BLA all cell pairs shown as a variant. Central nuclei REM is in cen-no-reactivation and intra-structure REM in intra-structure-reactivation.

claims.statement: Piriform cortex neurons show weaker reactivation with hippocampal CA1 neurons than BLA neurons do, though still significant in NREM.
claims.source: Results, BLA-hippocampus coordinated reactivations during NREM sleep, paragraph 2; Figure 3d
claims.quote: Neurons in the piriform cortex showed weaker experience-induced ... reactivation with their CA1 partner neurons (Fig. 3d
claims.criterion: EV and REV (M4) for hippocampus-piriform pyramidal pairs, piriform units as the paper's maps label them (M1). Reproduced when EV - REV of hippocampus-BLA sessions exceeds that of hippocampus-piriform sessions by one-tailed Wilcoxon rank sum p < 0.05, the hippocampus-piriform EV exceeds REV by two-sided signed rank p < 0.05, and the expected value holds. Partially reproduced when the comparison holds and one of the others does not. The paper gives 14 sessions for the comparison and 17 for Fig. 3d; both session sets are shown.

claims.statement: There are no reactivations between the central amygdala nuclei and the hippocampus.
claims.source: Results, BLA-hippocampus coordinated reactivations during NREM sleep, paragraph 2; Figure 3e
claims.quote: while there were no reactivations at all between the central nuclei and the hippocampus (Fig. 3e)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. EV and REV (M4) for all hippocampus-central nuclei cell pairs; two-sided Wilcoxon signed rank of EV against REV in NREM and in REM. Reproduced when neither has p < 0.05 with EV above REV; not reproduced when either does. Medians reported.

claims.statement: Within the hippocampus and within the BLA, pair correlations are reactivated in NREM but not in REM sleep.
claims.source: Supplementary Fig. 4; Results, BLA-hippocampus coordinated reactivations during NREM sleep, paragraph 1
claims.criterion: EV and REV (M4) over the distinct pairs within one structure (upper triangle of the correlation matrix, ExplainedVariance_Ultimate_IntraStruct.m), for all cells and for pyramidal cells, NREM and REM (REM sessions per M4). Two-sided Wilcoxon signed rank of EV against REV. Reproduced when all four NREM tests have EV above REV at p < 0.05 and none of the four REM tests reaches p < 0.05 (absence on the paper's test); partially reproduced when the NREM tests hold and a REM test does not, or three of four NREM tests hold.

claims.statement: A subset of BLA neurons is positively modulated during hippocampal SPW-Rs, 25.8% of interneurons (42 of 163) and 11.1% of pyramidal cells (137 of 1,233).
claims.source: Results, A subset of BLA cells are modulated during hippocampal SPW-Rs, paragraph 1; Figure 4a
claims.quote: A fraction of BLA neurons were significantly and positively modulated (‘upmodulation’; 42 of 163 interneurons (25.8%), 137 of 1,233 pyramidal cells (11.1%)) ... during hippocampal SPW-Rs (Fig. 4).
claims.criterion: M6 for every BLA unit of the sessions with ripple events (29 sessions, 3 rats, Fig. 4a legend), under both readings of O2; denominators are the BLA pyramidal cells and interneurons of those sessions (PoissonRippleModPercent.m counts all typed BLA cells in the table). An untested unit (no spikes in ripples or baseline) counts in the denominator as not modulated; the fractions excluding untested units are shown as a variant. Reproduced when both fractions are within tolerance; partially reproduced when both are above 0 and one is outside it.

claims.statement: Another subset of BLA neurons is negatively modulated during hippocampal SPW-Rs, 14.7% of interneurons (24 of 163) and 8.3% of pyramidal cells (102 of 1,233).
claims.source: Results, A subset of BLA cells are modulated during hippocampal SPW-Rs, paragraph 1; Figure 4a
claims.quote: or negatively modulated (‘downmodulation’; 24 of 163 interneurons (14.7%), 102 of 1,233 pyramidal cells (8.3%)) during hippocampal SPW-Rs (Fig. 4)
claims.criterion: As bla-ripple-up-subgroup, for the lower tail. Reproduced when both fractions are within tolerance; partially reproduced when both are above 0 and one is outside it.

claims.statement: Reactivation (EV - REV) is larger for hippocampus-BLA pairs whose BLA cell is ripple-modulated than for pairs with a non-modulated BLA cell.
claims.source: Results, A subset of BLA cells are modulated during hippocampal SPW-Rs, paragraph 1; Supplementary Fig. 5b
claims.quote: Moreover, reactivations calculated using SPW-R-modulated BLA cells were larger than for nonmodulated pairs (Supplementary Fig. 5b).
claims.criterion: Per session, EV and REV (M4) computed twice, with the BLA cells that are up- or downmodulated (M6) and with the non-modulated BLA cells; a session enters when it has more than 5 hippocampal and more than 5 modulated BLA cells of the type used (ExplainedVarianceMean_Ultimate.m). A two-sided Wilcoxon rank sum test on EV - REV of the two sets, as the paper names it (Supplementary Fig. 5b legend); the signed rank test on the same sessions is shown as a variant. Reproduced when, for all cells and for pyramidal pairs, modulated exceeds non-modulated with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when one of the two holds. The modulated cells are taken per M6, which is defined for every BLA unit and needs no cell type, so the all-cell test needs no other claim's result. When the pyramidal test cannot be run, the all-cell test is judged alone, as part of the claim; partially reproduced when it holds, not reproduced when it does not.

claims.statement: During run, 6.69% of hippocampus-BLA pyramidal pairs (2,521 of 37,660) are significantly positively correlated, 3.34% (1,258) negatively, and 89.96% (33,881) not reliably correlated.
claims.source: Results, Ripple-modulated BLA cells are preferentially involved in reactivations, paragraph 1; Supplementary Table 2
claims.quote: During run, a fraction of hippocampal–BLA pyramidal neuron pairs showed significantly positively correlated spike trains (2,521 of 37,660; 6.69%). Another small percentage (1,258 of 37,660; 3.34%) was negatively correlated, while the remaining majority (33,881 of 37,660; 89.96%) was not reliably correlated
claims.criterion: All hippocampus-BLA pyramidal pairs of the 29 sessions with simultaneous recordings and ripple events (Supplementary Fig. 6a legend; ExplainedVariance_PrePostCorr_Ultimate.m has no cell minimum), pooled. Run correlation is the Pearson correlation of 50-ms binned counts over the whole run epoch; positive when p < 0.01 and r > 0, negative when p < 0.01 and r < 0, otherwise not reliably correlated (Online Methods; the code's isnosig is p >= 0.01). Pairs with an undefined correlation (a silent cell) are left out of the fractions. Reproduced when every expected value holds; partially reproduced when the three fractions hold and a pair count does not.

claims.statement: Among nine groups of hippocampus-BLA pyramidal pairs formed by run correlation and BLA ripple modulation, the pairs with a significant positive run correlation and an upmodulated BLA partner show the largest pre-NREM to post-NREM increase in correlation, and differ from every other group.
claims.source: Results, Ripple-modulated BLA cells are preferentially involved in reactivations, paragraph 1; Figure 5a; Supplementary Fig. 6a; Supplementary Table 2
claims.quote: Hippocampus–BLA pairs with significant, positive run correlations and SPW-R upmodulation of the BLA partner showed the largest pre-NREM to post-NREM change
claims.criterion: The pairs and run-correlation classes of run-correlated-pair-fractions, crossed with the BLA partner's ripple modulation (M6, both O2 readings). Per pair, post-NREM correlation minus pre-NREM correlation (Pearson, 50-ms bins, M2). A one-way ANOVA across the nine groups, then post hoc comparisons (ExplainedVariance_PrePostCorr_Ultimate.m, anova1 and multcompare). Post hoc correction per O6, Bonferroni over the 36 pairwise comparisons (main) and Tukey-Kramer (variant). Reproduced when the ANOVA has p < 0.05, the upmodulated positive group has the largest mean, and it differs from each of the other eight groups at p < 0.01 after correction; partially reproduced when it has the largest mean and differs from at least five. The group counts are reported against Supplementary Table 2.

claims.statement: EV computed within each of the nine pair groups confirms the dominant contribution of the pairs with positive run correlation and an upmodulated BLA partner.
claims.source: Results, Ripple-modulated BLA cells are preferentially involved in reactivations, paragraph 1; Supplementary Fig. 6b
claims.quote: The dominant contribution of this specific subgroup of cell pairs to reactivations was confirmed by calculating the EVs across the nine subgroups
claims.criterion: For each group of reactivation-involves-ripple-up-cells, EV and REV (M4 formula) over the pooled pairs of the group, with pre-NREM, run and post-NREM correlations (ExplainedVariance_PooledCorr_Groups.m). The paper gives no test. Reproduced when the upmodulated positive group has the largest EV - REV of the nine. In the code the non-significant group is restricted to negative run correlations (run.signot); the Methods define it by p > 0.01 alone, so the Methods' groups are the main reading and the code's the variant.

claims.statement: Upmodulated BLA cells in the quartile contributing most to the reactivation increase their SPW-R gain from pre-NREM to post-NREM, while upmodulated cells of the other three quartiles do not.
claims.source: Results, Ripple-modulated BLA cells are preferentially involved in reactivations, paragraph 2; Figure 5b; Supplementary Fig. 8a
claims.quote: We found that upmodulated BLA neurons in the most strongly contributing quartile showed a specific increase in SPW-R gain (that is, firing rate during versus outside SPW-R) from pre-NREM to post-NREM compared to the upmodulated cells of the remaining three, low-contribution quartiles
claims.criterion: Contribution of a pair (Online Methods; ExplainedVariance_PooledCorr.m). Over all pooled pyramidal pairs with defined pre-NREM, run and post-NREM correlations, the global EV (M4 formula on pooled pairs) and, for each pair, the EV with that pair removed; contribution = EV without the pair minus global EV (negative is a positive contribution). A BLA cell's contribution is the mean over its pairs; BLA cells are split at the quartiles, the highest contribution quartile being the most negative. Gain (AllRippleCCGs_2.m, RippleMod_PrePost.m) is the cell's peri-ripple firing in 10-ms bins over -2 to +2 s around ripple peaks of pre-NREM, and of post-NREM, divided by the baseline rate of the same sleep epoch (NREM minus ripples widened by 100 ms); cells with an all-zero or undefined gain in either epoch are dropped; each curve is smoothed over 2 bins (the Methods' 20-ms Gaussian) and averaged over -250 to +250 ms. A one-tailed Wilcoxon signed rank test (post greater than pre) in the upmodulated cells (M6, both O2 readings) of the highest quartile and in those of the other three. Reproduced when the highest quartile has p < 0.05 and the other three do not; partially reproduced when the highest quartile has p < 0.05 and the other quartiles do too.

claims.statement: Hippocampus-BLA EV does not depend on firing rates; EV exceeds REV across firing-rate octiles of the pairs, of the BLA cells and of the hippocampal cells.
claims.source: Results, Ripple-modulated BLA cells are preferentially involved in reactivations, paragraph 2; Supplementary Fig. 9
claims.quote: This control showed that EV did not depend on firing rates (Supplementary Fig. 9).
claims.criterion: The pooled pyramidal pairs of run-correlated-pair-fractions, split into octiles of (a) the mean of the two cells' rates, (b) the BLA cell's rate, (c) the hippocampal cell's rate, rate being the spike count over the whole recording span of the scored states (StatesFiringRates.m, all-states rate, used by ExplainedVariance_PooledCorr_Groups.m); EV and REV (M4 formula) over the pairs of each octile. The paper gives no test. Readings of "did not depend" (a) EV exceeds REV in all eight octiles of each of the three splits; (b) the Spearman correlation between octile rank and EV - REV has p >= 0.05 in each split. Reproduced when the outcome holds under both readings; otherwise reported as methods_underspecified with all results.

claims.statement: Reactivation strength of the whole-run template around hippocampal ripple peaks is higher in post-NREM than in pre-NREM, for pyramidal pairs and for all cell pairs.
claims.source: Supplementary Fig. 11a
claims.quote: Mean z-scored peri-ripple reactivation strength of the whole training session ... reactivation strength in a 500ms window around ripple peaks (grey bar in a) was significantly higher in post-NREM
claims.criterion: R per M7 with the whole run epoch as template, pyramidal cells (and all cells as the second test). Per session, the ripple-peak value in pre-NREM and in post-NREM; a one-tailed Wilcoxon signed rank test, post greater than pre (ReplayInTime_All.m, tail left on pre against post). Reproduced when both tests have p < 0.05; partially reproduced when one does. Sessions enter by the M7 cell minimum for the cell type of each test, which needs no other claim's result. When the pyramidal test cannot be run, the all-cell test is judged alone, as part of the claim; partially reproduced when it has p < 0.05, not reproduced when it does not.

claims.statement: The hippocampus-BLA correlation pattern of the air puff trajectory is reactivated more around post-NREM ripples than around pre-NREM ripples.
claims.source: Figure 6a, top; Results, The aversive trajectory is reactivated during SPW-Rs, paragraph 1
claims.quote: reactivation strength in a 500-ms window around ripple peaks (gray bars) was significantly higher in post-NREM compared to pre-NREM for air puff trajectory
claims.criterion: R per M7, pyramidal cells, with the template built only from run bins inside air puff laps (M8, each O1 reading), the run counts z-scored within those bins (ReplayInTime_LapTypes.m). Per session, ripple-peak values in pre- and post-NREM; one-tailed Wilcoxon signed rank test, post greater than pre (ReplayInTime_LapTypes_All.m). Reproduced when p < 0.05 under every O1 reading; methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: The hippocampus-BLA correlation pattern of the safe trajectory is not significantly more reactivated around post-NREM ripples than around pre-NREM ripples (pyramidal pairs).
claims.source: Figure 6a, bottom; Results, The aversive trajectory is reactivated during SPW-Rs, paragraph 1
claims.quote: significantly higher in post-NREM compared to pre-NREM for air puff trajectory ... but not for safe trajectory
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. As airpuff-trajectory-ripple-reactivation with the template built from run bins inside safe laps. Reproduced when the one-tailed Wilcoxon signed rank test (post greater than pre) has p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The median post minus pre difference is reported. The O1 readings are each run and reported; absence is judged on each.

claims.statement: The post-NREM minus pre-NREM change in reactivation strength at the ripple peak is larger for the air puff trajectory than for the safe trajectory (pyramidal pairs).
claims.source: Figure 6b; Results, The aversive trajectory is reactivated during SPW-Rs, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The pre-NREM vs. post-NREM difference in reactivation strength (RS) at the ripple peak is significantly higher for the air puff trajectory compared to safe trajectory
claims.criterion: Per session, the post-NREM minus pre-NREM ripple-peak value (M7) for the air puff template and for the safe template of the two claims above. One-tailed Wilcoxon signed rank test across sessions, air puff greater than safe (ReplayInTime_LapTypes_Plot.m, signrank of safe against air puff, tail left). Reproduced when p < 0.05 under every O1 reading; methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: With all cell types included, both the air puff and the safe trajectory patterns are more reactivated around post-NREM than pre-NREM ripples, and the post minus pre difference does not differ significantly between the two trajectories.
claims.source: Supplementary Fig. 11b,c
claims.quote: Reactivation strength in a 500ms window around ripple peaks (grey bar in a) was significantly higher in post-NREM compared to pre-NREM for airpuff ... and safe trajectories ... Pre/Post peak differences (postNREM - preNREM; see methods) in reactivation strength are not significantly different for safe and airpuff trajectories when all cell types are included
claims.criterion: The three tests of airpuff-trajectory-ripple-reactivation, safe-trajectory-no-ripple-reactivation and aversive-direction-stronger with all cells (ctype all), using their procedure (M7, M8, laps per O1) but not their results; sessions enter by the M7 cell minimum for all cells (ReplayInTime_LapTypes_All.m). Reproduced when both within-trajectory tests have p < 0.05 and the between-trajectory test has p >= 0.05 (absence on the paper's one-tailed test); partially reproduced when two of the three hold.

claims.statement: Firing rates of BLA cells do not differ significantly between the safe and the air puff trajectories.
claims.source: Results, The aversive trajectory is reactivated during SPW-Rs, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Because the firing rates of BLA cells did not significantly differ between safe and air puff trajectories
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a two-sided Wilcoxon signed rank test across BLA cells, safe against air puff rate in the run epoch, for pyramidal cells and for all cells. The paper gives no n and does not say which sessions enter; readings (a) the BLA cells of the sessions entering aversive-direction-stronger (pyramidal) and direction-all-cell-pairs (all cells); (b) all BLA cells of sessions with a run epoch. The rate per O7, both readings, laps per O1. Reproduced when neither test has p < 0.05 under every reading; not reproduced when either test has p < 0.05 under every reading; methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. Median differences reported.

claims.statement: The occurrence rate of SPW-Rs does not differ between pre-NREM and post-NREM.
claims.source: Results, The aversive trajectory is reactivated during SPW-Rs, paragraph 1; Supplementary Fig. 11d
claims.quote: The occurrence rate of SPW-R was also not significantly different between the pre-NREM and postNREM epochs
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. Per session with ripple events, the number of ripple peaks in pre-NREM over pre-NREM duration and the same in post-NREM (RippleRatePrePost.m). A two-sided Wilcoxon signed rank test (Online Methods default; the printed P of 0.192 for z = -1.289 is two-sided, while RippleRatePrePost_All.m calls tail right; Supplementary Fig. 11d prints P = 0.1972 for the same test). Reproduced when p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. Median difference reported.

claims.statement: For the 2.5% most strongly contributing hippocampus-BLA pairs, the pre-run to post-run change in correlation correlates with the pre-NREM to post-NREM change (r = 0.27), but not for the 2.5% least contributing pairs.
claims.source: Results, NREM contributes to reinstatement of new place-threat representations, paragraph 1; Figure 7b; Supplementary Fig. 7c
claims.quote: We found that for strongly contributing, but not for weakly contributing, pairs the increase between pre-run and post-run coactivity was significantly correlated with the increase in coactivity between pre-NREM and post-NREM (Fig. 7b).
claims.criterion: Pair contributions as in contributing-up-cells-gain-increase. Strongly contributing pairs are those below the 2.5th percentile of contribution (most negative), weakly contributing those above the 97.5th (ExplainedVariance_PooledCorr.m, prctile 2.5 and 97.5). Per pair, post-NREM minus pre-NREM correlation, and post-run minus pre-run correlation (Pearson, 50-ms bins over the pre-run and post-run test epochs); pairs with an undefined run change left out. Pearson correlation of the two changes in each group. Reproduced when the strong group has r > 0 with p < 0.05 and r within tolerance, and the weak group has p >= 0.05; partially reproduced when the strong group's r is positive and significant but outside tolerance, or the weak group's p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The coupling between run and sleep correlation changes holds when the most and least contributing quartiles of pairs are compared (r = 0.13 against r = 0.013).
claims.source: Results, NREM contributes to reinstatement of new place-threat representations, paragraph 1; Figure 7c; Supplementary Fig. 7b
claims.quote: This result was maintained when the most strongly and the most weakly contributing quartiles (instead of 2.5th percentiles) of the distribution were compared (Fig. 7c).
claims.criterion: As contributing-pairs-run-sleep-coupling with the pairs split at the 25th and 75th percentiles of contribution (quantile), strongest quartile below the 25th. Reproduced when the strongest quartile has r > 0 with p < 0.05 and r within tolerance, and the weakest has p >= 0.05; partially reproduced when only the strongest quartile's test holds.

claims.statement: The dandiset's recording channels can be assigned to the prefrontal probe, the CA1 probe and the nose-poke sensors by the channel map of the CRCNS pfc-2 description of the same recordings (channels 1 to 64 prefrontal, 65 to 96 CA1, 97 right and 98 left nose-poke sensors), and the data agree with that map.
claims.source: Methods (8-shank, 64-site probe in mPFC); CRCNS pfc-2 data description, version 0.7
claims.criterion: Two checks in each of the eight sessions with the wideband signal, and the sensor check also in EE.088. (i) The median theta ratio (6 to 10 Hz over 1 to 40 Hz power, during trials) of the CA1 channels is above that of channels 1 to 64. (ii) In at least 90% of trials the sensor channel with more activity during the nose poke is the one of the trial's side. Reproduced when both hold in every session with the CRCNS channel numbers; partially reproduced when both hold in every session only with a per-rat correction of the channel numbers found in the data; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: 633 well-isolated units were recorded from the mPFC of four rats.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We recorded a total of 633 well-isolated units from the anterior cingulate area (area 24) and dorsal prelimbic area (area 32) of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC)... in four rats.
claims.criterion: Readings of the unit count, all over the eight sessions; (a) PFC single units; (b) PFC single units with a peak rate of at least 1 Hz during runs; (c) all units placed on the prefrontal probe, multi-unit clusters included. Reproduced when the dandiset holds four rats and one reading is within tolerance; partially reproduced when only one of the two holds; not reproduced when neither does.

claims.statement: Rats performed the odor-place matching task at 92% correct (91.9% in the recording sessions).
claims.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 1; Methods, Behavioral task
claims.quote: All rats performed the task at high proficiency (mean performance, 92% correct) at the time of neurophysiological data collection... In the recording sessions, the mean correct performance was 91.9%.

claims.statement: About 10% (layer 2/3) and 20% (layer 5) of the recorded neurons fire at least one spike in any 100 ms window, a fraction that is relatively constant along the maze.
claims.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 3; Figure 2c; Discussion
claims.quote: the population firing rates (Fig. 2b) and the fraction of simultaneously active neurons (10% and 20% in 100-ms windows, layers 2/3 and 5, respectively; Fig. 2c) were relatively constant in all segments of the maze
claims.criterion: Per session, the mean over the 100 ms windows tiling each run of the fraction of PFC single units with at least one spike, and the same mean in ten position bins of 0.1. Per rat, the median over its sessions. Reproduced when each rat's value is within 10% of 10% (9 to 11%) or of 20% (18 to 22%), at most one rat at 20%, and in every session the largest of the ten position-bin means is at most twice the smallest (the threshold for "relatively constant" is chosen here). Partially reproduced when one of the two parts holds.

claims.statement: Neurons are active over similar standardized distances of the maze, 0.27 (62 cm) plus or minus 0.17 (39 cm) (mean and s.d.), from the 50% boundaries of the peak firing rate.
claims.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 3; Figure 2a
claims.quote: most neurons were generically active for similar standardized distances of 0.27 (62 cm) ± 0.17 (39 cm) (mean ± s.d.) in the maze (as determined by the 50% firing boundaries of the peak firing rate
claims.criterion: Occupancy-normalized rate maps on 100 bins of the normalized track, by side, smoothed with the paper's Gaussian kernel (sigma 0.05). Units are PFC single units with a peak rate of at least 1 Hz on either side (the "Cells" rule of the CRCNS description; the paper states none). The tolerance of the mean is the paper's stated spread, as the protocol asks; the s.d. takes 10%. Readings; (a) the contiguous run of bins at or above half the peak around the peak, on the side with the higher peak; (b) the same on each side, each side a separate value; (c) all bins at or above half the peak on the side with the higher peak. Reproduced when, under one reading, both values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when only the mean is.

claims.statement: The fraction of neurons with significantly different firing on left and right trials is 16% (layer 2/3) and 18% (layer 5) in the central arm (positions 0 to 0.3), where the trajectories overlap, and 22% (layer 2/3) and 40% (layer 5) in the side arms (0.5 to 1).
claims.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 4; Figure 2b; Methods, permutation tests and global bands
claims.quote: The fraction of trajectory-selective neurons in the side arms (positions 0.5–1) was almost twice as large in deep (layer 5, 40%) than in superficial (layer 2/3, 22%) neurons... a sizable but smaller fraction of neurons in both layer 2/3 and layer 5 (16% and 18%, respectively; Fig. 2b) was also differentially active in the central arm
claims.criterion: The Methods' test; per-trial kernel densities of spike positions (sigma 0.05) on 101 points of the track, difference of left and right means, 1000 permutations of the trial labels, global band at alpha 0.05. A unit is selective in a segment when the difference breaks the global band anywhere in it. Units as in fig2-field-size. The chance rate is the same procedure on one random relabelling of each unit's trials. Per rat, reproduced when the central-arm fraction is within 14.4 to 19.8% (the range 16 to 18% widened by 10% of each bound) and the side-arm fraction is within 10% of the value of one layer (19.8 to 24.2% for layer 2/3, 36 to 44% for layer 5), with at most one rat in layer 5. The claim is reproduced when every rat is; partially reproduced when the pooled central-arm fraction is above the chance fraction (one-sided Fisher exact test, p < 0.05) but not every rat matches; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Left and right trajectories overlap in the central arm and begin to differ significantly at position 0.3.
claims.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 3
claims.quote: Left and right lap trajectories in segments 0 to 0.3 of the central arm overlapped; they began to differ significantly at position 0.3 (P < 0.01 with respect to differences in means; Supplementary Fig. 3 online).
claims.criterion: Written in the first revision, after the verifier asked whether the x coordinate separates the sides and before x was compared between sides. The only coordinate is x1, the x of the first head LED in pixels; frames with x1 at or below 0 (-1, no tracking) are left out. Per trial, the mean x1 in 50 bins of 0.02 of the normalized position. Per session and bin, a Welch t-test of left against right trials. The divergence point of a session is the start of the first bin from which every bin up to 0.6 differs at p < 0.01. Blocked (data_missing) when x1 does not differ between sides (p < 0.01) over 0.5 to 1 in at least half the sessions, as then x1 does not carry the side. Otherwise, reproduced when the median divergence point over sessions is within 0.27 to 0.33 (10% of 0.3); partially reproduced when it is above 0.33, since one coordinate can separate the paths later than both would; not reproduced when it is below 0.27.

claims.statement: About one quarter of the neurons fire at significantly different rates (P < 0.05 per cell) during nose poking for the two odors.
claims.source: Results, Medial prefrontal cortical units predict behavioral choice, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 6
claims.quote: Approximately one-quarter of the neurons showed significantly different (P < 0.05 per cell) firing rates in response to one of the two odorants
claims.criterion: The trial table holds correct trials only, so the odor is given by the side (chocolate for one side, cheese for the other). Per PFC single unit with at least 10 spikes in nose-poke periods, its rate in each trial from the start of the first nose poke to the end of the last; left against right trials by a two-sided Mann-Whitney test at P < 0.05 (the paper names no test). The tolerance is wider than 10% because the paper says "approximately". Reproduced when the pooled fraction is within tolerance; partially reproduced when it is outside but above the chance fraction from one random relabelling of each unit's trials (one-sided Fisher exact test, p < 0.05); not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Of all ordered pairs of simultaneously recorded neurons, 0.79% had short-latency, narrow peaks or troughs in their cross-correlograms (0.55% excitatory, 0.24% inhibitory), found with a jitter test.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 5; Figure 3a and 3e; Methods, identifying monosynaptic interactions
claims.quote: Of the 62,408 cell pairs (counting each literal pair twice, corresponding to the two directions), 495 (0.79%) had short latency (< 5 ms onset) and narrow significant peaks (≤ 2 ms) or troughs in their cross-correlograms... 0.55% excitatory connections and 0.24% inhibitory connections (single directions)
claims.criterion: Every ordered pair of PFC single units in a session, whole session. Cross- correlogram in 1 ms bins from -5 to 5 ms (the bin width is chosen here); 1000 surrogates with every spike jittered uniformly by +-5 ms; global bands at 99% from the maximum and minimum of each surrogate over the window. Excitatory when a bin from 1 to 4 ms is above the upper band and the run of bins above it is at most 2 ms wide; inhibitory when a bin from 1 to 4 ms is below the lower band and the pair is not excitatory in that direction. To save time, pairs whose correlogram is within the pointwise 1% Poisson quantiles of the exact jitter mean in every test bin are not given the Monte Carlo test; a random sample of them is, to show the screen misses nothing. Reproduced when all three rates are within tolerance; partially reproduced when one or two are; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: By their connections, 32.5% of units are putative pyramidal cells and 12.5% putative interneurons, a ratio of 2.82 plus or minus 0.51 (s.d.), and 50.7% of the postsynaptic targets of putative excitatory cells themselves inhibit other neurons.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 5
claims.quote: a sizable fraction of the recorded units could be classified as putative pyramidal cells (32.5%) or inhibitory interneurons (12.5%). A large percentage of the postsynaptic targets of the putative excitatory cells (50.7%) were suppressing other neurons... The ratio of putative principal cells to inhibitory interneurons... was 2.82 ± 0.51 (s.d.).
claims.criterion: A unit is a putative pyramidal cell when it has at least one excitatory outgoing connection, a putative interneuron when it has at least one inhibitory one; a unit with both is counted in neither. Fractions over all PFC single units. The ratio's tolerance is the paper's s.d. Readings of the ratio; (a) the mean of per-session ratios (sessions with at least one interneuron); (b) the pooled ratio; (c) the mean of per-rat pooled ratios. Targets; distinct postsynaptic units of excitatory connections that are putative interneurons. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when two or three are; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Most connected pairs were recorded on the same shank, and the probability of a connection falls with the distance between the neurons, though connections were found up to 1200 micrometres apart.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 6; Figure 3f
claims.quote: most functionally connected pairs were detected locally and recorded by the same probe shank. The probability of putative connections decreased rapidly as a function of distance between the somata of the recorded pair (Fig. 3f), but connections were detected between neurons up to 1,200 μm apart.
claims.criterion: Distance between two units taken as 200 micrometres times the number of shanks between them (the probe's shank spacing; positions within a shank are not used). Reproduced when the connection probability (excitatory or inhibitory, ordered pairs) is higher on the same shank than across shanks (two-sided Fisher exact test, p < 0.05), the Spearman correlation of probability with shank distance over distances 0 to 1400 micrometres is negative with p < 0.05, and some connection is at least 1000 micrometres apart; partially reproduced when the first two hold.

claims.statement: Out of 343 excitatory monosynaptic pairs, 67 showed position dependence of their short-latency coincidences in the maze (P < 0.01), beyond what the firing rates explain.
claims.source: Results, Behavioral modulation of monosynaptic interactions, paragraph 1; Figure 4; Methods, identifying position dependence
claims.quote: Across all sessions, out of 343 pairs with significant excitatory monosynaptic connections in all sessions, 67 pairs showed identifiable position dependence in monosynaptic interactions by this measure (P < 0.01).
claims.criterion: For each excitatory pair, coincident events (postsynaptic spike 1 to 4 ms after a presynaptic spike) during runs, located at the presynaptic spike; kernel density (sigma 0.05) on 101 points; 1000 surrogates with both trains jittered by +-5 ms; one-sided global band at 0.01. Readings; (a) left and right trials together, significant excess anywhere on the track; (b) left and right trials tested separately, significant in either. Reproduced when the fraction is within tolerance under one reading; not reproduced otherwise. The fraction of the track that is significant is reported for every pair.

claims.statement: About equal fractions of connected pairs show firing pattern-dependent depression (12.7%) and facilitation (10.7%), comparing the transmission of the first spike of a train with that of later spikes.
claims.source: Results, Behavioral modulation of monosynaptic interactions, paragraph 3; Figure 6c
claims.quote: we found that approximately equal percentages of neuron pairs showed firing pattern–dependent depressing (12.7%) and facilitating (10.7%) effects (Fig. 6c).
claims.criterion: Excitatory pairs with at least 20 first spikes (after at least 200 ms of presynaptic silence) and 20 later spikes (less than 40 ms after the previous presynaptic spike). Transmission of a set of presynaptic spikes is the mean number of postsynaptic spikes 1 to 4 ms after each, minus its expectation under +-5 ms jitter of the postsynaptic spikes (chosen here, as the supplementary definition was not available). 1000 permutations of the first and later labels, two-sided P < 0.10; depressing when first spikes transmit more, facilitating when later spikes do. Reproduced when both fractions are within tolerance; partially reproduced when both are above the 5% that the test gives each side under its null (one-sided binomial test, p < 0.05) but not both within tolerance; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Coincident firing of two or more presynaptic neurons within 5 ms on a common target is more effective than the sum of their separate effects (supralinear), while spikes spread over windows longer than 10 ms add linearly.
claims.source: Results, Behavioral modulation of monosynaptic interactions, paragraph 4; Figure 7
claims.quote: Coincident discharge of two presynaptic neurons within 5 ms was more effective than the sum of the effects of nonsynchronous spikes (Fig. 7a)... In contrast, spike occurrences of more than one neuron in time windows >10 ms showed only a linear additive effect
claims.criterion: Satellites are PFC single units with at least two excitatory presynaptic partners. Partner spikes are merged into events (a spike and every partner spike within 5 ms after it); for each event, whether the target fires 1 to 4 ms after its last spike, minus the chance of a target spike in any 3 ms window. Supralinear in a satellite when the excess for events with two partners exceeds twice that for events with one. Satellites with at least 20 two-partner events are tested. Reproduced when more than half of them are supralinear and a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of the difference gives p < 0.05; partially reproduced when more than half are but p is 0.05 or more; not reproduced otherwise. The same with 20 ms events is shown as a variant for the linear part.

claims.statement: Large fractions of putative pyramidal cells (72.2% in layer 2/3, 84.7% in layer 5) and of interneurons (58.3% and 83%) are trajectory specific.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraph 7
claims.quote: In addition to a large fraction of putative pyramidal cells (72.2% and 84.7% in layers 2/3 and 5, respectively), many interneurons (58.3% and 83% in layers 2/3 and 5, respectively) were also trajectory specific.
claims.criterion: A unit is trajectory specific when the test of fig2b-trajectory-selective finds a significant left-right difference anywhere on the track (units of any peak rate). Per rat, the fractions of its putative pyramidal cells and interneurons. Reproduced when every rat matches one layer's two values within 10% of each, at most one rat in layer 5; partially reproduced when in every rat both fractions are above the chance fraction of fig2b-trajectory-selective; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: In the example layer 2/3 session, 117 neurons gave 1172 pairs with 48 excitatory and 30 inhibitory connections, 39 of the 117 cells formed one connected hub, 15 of 36 excitatory connections were active in particular maze segments, and the example pairs (156-136, 197-201, 49-52, 186-201, 197 and 186 onto one interneuron, a satellite on cell 135) show position-dependent, depressing, facilitating and supralinear transmission.
claims.source: Figures 2a, 3b to 3d, 4, 5, 6b and 7a; Results, Characterization of mPFC neurons and their connections, paragraphs 6 and 7
claims.quote: Figure 3b illustrates significant peaks and troughs of cross-correlograms of 1172 pairs of layer 2/3 cells (13,572 matrix points) simultaneously recorded in a single session... a large portion of the active neurons (39 of the 117) belonged to a single interconnected circuit

claims.statement: The two array datasets, monkey J-array recorded 2009-09-18 and monkey N-array recorded 2010-09-23, each present 108 reach conditions and comprise 146 and 218 isolations (a mix of single and multi-unit isolations).
claims.source: Methods, Recordings and task design, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 3e and 3f legend
claims.quote: For the monkey J-array and N-array datasets, 108 conditions were presented in the same recording session ... These array-based datasets involved, respectively, 146 and 218 single isolations (each a mix of single and multi-unit isolations)
claims.criterion: Conditions are the distinct maze_condition values above 0 among the trials the Methods select; isolations are the rows of the Units table. Reproduced when both sessions are in the dandiset with all four values within tolerance; partially reproduced when the sessions and condition counts match but a unit count does not; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: In the first jPCA plane the neural state rotates in the same direction for all conditions of the J-array and N-array datasets, including reaches in opposite directions.
claims.source: Results, Quasi-rhythmic responses during reaching, paragraph 4; Figure 3e and 3f
claims.quote: Second, the neural state rotates in the same direction across conditions (different traces) ... Yet for each dataset the neural state rotates in the same direction across conditions
claims.criterion: For each condition, the net change of the polar angle of its state in the oriented jPC plane from -50 to +150 ms. Reproduced when at least 90% of the 108 conditions rotate counter-clockwise (positive) in each dataset; partially reproduced when at least 75% do in each, or 90% in one only; not reproduced otherwise. The values under the shuffle controls of suppfig3-shuffle-controls are shown as reference.

claims.statement: The rotations do not relate directly to reach curvature; the neural state rotates the same way for clockwise-curving, counter-clockwise-curving and straight reaches.
claims.source: Results, Quasi-rhythmic responses during reaching, paragraph 4; Figure 3e and 3f
claims.quote: Finally, state-space rotations do not relate directly to reach curvature ... Yet for each dataset the neural state rotates in the same direction across conditions
claims.criterion: Each condition's reach is classed by the net change of heading of its mean hand path from movement onset to the end of the window (+500 ms) as clockwise (below -20 degrees), counter-clockwise (above +20 degrees) or straight. Reproduced when, in each dataset, at least 90% of the conditions in each class with at least five conditions rotate counter-clockwise in the jPC plane; partially reproduced when this holds for every class at 75%; not reproduced otherwise. A logistic fit of rotation direction on curvature is reported as well.

claims.statement: The rotation phase follows from the preparatory state; knowing the initial state in the jPC plane, the subsequent states are reasonably predictable.
claims.source: Results, Quasi-rhythmic responses during reaching, paragraphs 4 and 5; Figure 3
claims.quote: Third, the rotation phase follows naturally from the preparatory state ... If one knows the initial population-level preparatory state (fig. 3, circles) subsequent states are reasonably predictable
claims.criterion: Writing each condition's state in the plane as a complex number, the state at +150 ms is predicted from the state at -50 ms by one complex gain (a rotation and a scaling) shared by all conditions, fitted leaving one condition out. Reproduced when the cross-validated R2 is at least 0.5 in each dataset and above the median R2 of shuffle 3 of suppfig3-shuffle-controls (which keeps preparatory states and reassigns the movement activity); partially reproduced when this holds in one dataset; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: The first jPCA plane captures an average of 28% of the total data variance (typically 20 to 35%).
claims.source: Results, Controls regarding rotational structure, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 5 legend
claims.quote: Those projections captured an average of 28% of the total data variance ... This was typically 20-35%
claims.criterion: The paper's average is over nine datasets, of which the dandiset holds two. The readings are (a) the mean of J-array and N-array within 28 +- 2.8%, (b) each of the two within the stated typical range 20 to 35%, widened by 10% of each bound to 18 to 38.5%. Reproduced when (a) or (b) holds.

claims.statement: The plane of PC2 and PC3 captures 29% of the total variance on average, about as much as the first jPCA plane, so the jPCA plane captures patterns already present in the top PCs.
claims.source: Results, Controls regarding rotational structure, paragraph 2
claims.quote: As a comparison, the dimensions defined by PC2 and PC3 (which by definition capture the second- and third-most data variance possible) together capture 29% of the total variance. Thus, the jPCA projection simply captures response patterns that were always present in the top PCs
claims.criterion: Readings (a) the mean of J-array and N-array within 29 +- 2.9%, (b) each dataset within it. Reproduced when (a) or (b) holds and, in each dataset, the jPCA plane captures at least 80% as much variance as PC2 and PC3 together; partially reproduced when only one of these two parts holds.

claims.statement: In J-array the first three jPCA planes found within the top 10 PCs capture 22%, 19% and 12% of the variance (54% together), against 64% for the top six PCs, and each plane holds rotations coherent across conditions.
claims.source: Supplementary Figure 4
claims.quote: All three planes contained rotational structure that was coherent (in the same direction and at a similar angular velocity) across conditions ... The top three jPCA planes (spanning six dimensions) captured 60% (monkey B) and 54% ... the top six PCs ... captured 72% and 64% of the variance
claims.criterion: Reproduced when all five values are within tolerance and at least 75% of the conditions rotate in the plane's direction in each of the three planes; partially reproduced when the three-plane total and the top-six-PC value are within tolerance; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Every dataset contains two, and usually three, planes with rotations, together capturing 50 to 70% of the variance.
claims.source: Supplementary Figure 4 legend; Results, Controls regarding rotational structure, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Together these captured 50–70% of the total data variance ... all datasets contained two, and usually three, planes that captured rotations
claims.criterion: jPCA on the top 10 PCs of J-array and N-array. Reproduced when in each dataset the first three planes together capture 45 to 77% (the stated range widened by 10% of each bound) and at least the first two planes have 75% or more of the conditions rotating in the plane's direction; partially reproduced when this holds in one dataset; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: The distribution of the angle between the neural state and its derivative in the first jPCA plane, over all conditions and times, peaks near pi/2 (rotation), not near 0.
claims.source: Figure 6a
claims.quote: The neural data and the generator model have distributions with peaks near π/2
claims.criterion: Peak of a 36-bin histogram over -pi to pi. The figure shows the peaks of the nine neural datasets between about 0.35 pi and 0.6 pi (read from the figure), against 0 to 0.3 pi for the kinematic models and EMG. Reproduced when the peak lies between 0.3 pi and 0.7 pi in each dataset; partially reproduced in one; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: For the neural data the rotational (skew-symmetric) dynamics matrix fits the data nearly as well as the best unconstrained linear dynamics matrix, both in the 6-D space and in the first jPCA plane.
claims.source: Results, Population-level quantification, paragraph 2; Figure 6b
claims.quote: For the neural data and generator model, the fit provided by Mskew was nearly as good as the fit provided by the best unconstrained M (fig. 6b) ... Results were similar whether we considered all six dimensions or just the plane with the strongest rotations
claims.criterion: The ratio R2(M_skew) / R2(M). Figure 6b shows the nine neural datasets at about 0.75 to 0.9 in 6-D and about 0.8 to 0.97 for the best plane, and the kinematic models at or below about 0.45 (6-D) and 0.75 (plane) (read from the figure). Reproduced when the 6-D ratio is at least 0.7 and the plane ratio at least 0.75 in each dataset; partially reproduced when both hold in one dataset, or one of the two holds in both; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: The rotations are brief and fast, up to about 2.5 Hz; the largest eigenvalues of M_skew in the monkey A and B datasets are 8.8 to 13.5 radians/s.
claims.source: Results, Quasi-rhythmic responses during reaching, paragraph 5, and Population-level quantification, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Their brevity and high frequency (up to ~2.5 Hz) makes them easy to miss ... the largest eigenvalues of Mskew were actually slightly smaller for fast reaches (8.8 versus 9.8 radians/s for monkey A, 12.2 versus 13.5 radians/s for monkey B)
claims.criterion: Frequency is the magnitude of the largest eigenvalue of M_skew (radians/s) over 2 pi. Reproduced when it lies within 1.26 to 2.75 Hz in each dataset (the range of the reported eigenvalues, 1.40 to 2.15 Hz, and the stated maximum of 2.5 Hz, widened by 10% of the bounds); partially reproduced when in one; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Three shuffle controls that keep preparatory activity and invert or reassign the peri-movement activity largely remove the rotational structure found by jPCA, so jPCA does not find rotations that are not there.
claims.source: Supplementary Figures 2 and 3; Results, Controls regarding rotational structure, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Multiple ‘shuffle’ controls demonstrate that jPCA does not find rotational structure when such structure is not present ... largely lost following shuffling
claims.criterion: The dividing point is 50 ms after the go cue, taken per dataset as the median go-cue time relative to movement onset plus 50 ms. Shuffle 1 (half the conditions inverted per unit) and 3 (movement activity reassigned) are run 20 times with fixed seeds, shuffle 2 once. Rotation strength is R2(M_skew) in 6-D. Reproduced when, in each dataset and for each shuffle, every run is below the original and the median is at most 75% of it; partially reproduced when this holds for at least two shuffles in each dataset or all three in one; not reproduced otherwise. The fraction of conditions rotating counter-clockwise and the R2 ratio are shown as well.

claims.statement: Analysed separately, the PMd and M1 arrays each show clear rotations; the jPCA plane captures 29% (PMd) and 29% (M1) in J-array and 32% and 28% in N-array.
claims.source: Supplementary Figure 5
claims.quote: Both PMd and M1 exhibited clear rotations of the neural state
claims.criterion: Units split by the electrode group of their array (PMd group 1, M1 group 2). Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance and at least 75% of conditions rotate counter-clockwise in each; partially reproduced when all four lie in the stated typical range widened to 18 to 38.5% with 75% rotating; not reproduced otherwise. The sub-Nitschke ses-20090910 session is shown against the N-9-10-2010 values (26% and 24%) as a variant.

claims.statement: The angular velocity of the rotations is slightly higher for M1 than for PMd in each dataset.
claims.source: Supplementary Figure 5 legend
claims.quote: Second, the angular velocity of the rotations was in each case slightly higher for M1
claims.criterion: Frequency of the first jPCA plane (largest eigenvalue of M_skew) per array. Reproduced when M1 is higher than PMd in both J-array and N-array; partially reproduced in one; not reproduced in neither. The sub-Nitschke ses-20090910 session is a variant.

claims.statement: A simulated population of units tuned to hand velocity and speed, with preparatory activity tuned to reach endpoint, matched to the recorded data, shows no robust or consistent rotations; M_skew fits it poorly and its angle distribution peaks slightly above zero.
claims.source: Results, Rotations, kinematics and EMG, paragraph 1; Results, Population-level quantification, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 4d and 4h; Figure 6a and 6b
claims.quote: For velocity-model populations, jPCA found no robust or consistent rotations (fig. 4a,d,h) ... the velocity-tuned model, the complex-kinematic model, and EMG all had distributions that peaked slightly above zero ... For the velocity-tuned and complex kinematic models, Mskew performed poorly
claims.criterion: One simulated dataset per array dataset from that session's condition-mean hand kinematics (`simulate_population`, fixed seed), analysed as the data. Reproduced when, in each dataset, its 6-D R2 ratio is below 0.6 and below the neural ratio and its angle peak is below pi/4; partially reproduced when this holds in one dataset; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: A simulated population tuned to hand position, velocity, acceleration and jerk (with the Methods' sensitivities) produces multiphasic responses but no consistent rotations; M_skew fits it poorly.
claims.source: Results, Rotations, kinematics and EMG, paragraph 1; Results, Population-level quantification, paragraph 2; Figure 4e and 4i; Figure 6a and 6b
claims.quote: This model produced multiphasic responses but not consistent rotations (fig. 4b,e,i) ... For the velocity-tuned and complex kinematic models, Mskew performed poorly
claims.criterion: As for fig6-velocity-model, with the complex kinematic model.

claims.statement: The population responses of the swimming leech and of premotor cortex in a walking monkey rotate in the jPCA plane, as expected for rhythmic movement.
claims.source: Results, Rhythmic responses in different systems, paragraph 1; Figure 1a, 1b, 1d and 1e
claims.quote: We projected the population response onto a two-dimensional state space and found rotations of the neural state for both the swimming leech (fig. 1d; projection of 164 simultaneously recorded neurons) and the walking monkey

claims.statement: Single neurons recorded with single electrodes show multiphasic, quasi-oscillatory responses lasting about 1 to 1.5 cycles, from 469 isolations in four monkeys averaging 810 trials per neuron.
claims.source: Results, Quasi-rhythmic responses during reaching, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 1c and Figure 2
claims.quote: We analyzed 469 single-neuron recordings from motor and premotor cortex of four monkeys (A,B,J,N) ... Yet there appear to be oscillations in many single-neuron responses, beginning just before movement onset and lasting for ~1–1.5 cycles

claims.statement: The rotations are seen in the seven single-electrode datasets (monkeys A, B, J1 to J4 and N), for example monkey B, A, J3 and N in Figure 3a to 3d.
claims.source: Figure 3a to 3d; Results, Quasi-rhythmic responses during reaching, paragraph 4
claims.quote: The resulting projections (fig. 3a-f) show four striking features. First, rotations of the neural state are prevalent during reaching

claims.statement: The recorded muscle populations (6 to 12 EMG recordings per dataset) show weak, inconsistent rotations, also when the neural population is down-sampled to their size.
claims.source: Results, Rotations, kinematics and EMG, paragraph 1; Figure 4c, 4f and 4j; Figure 6a and 6b; Supplementary Figure 6
claims.quote: Although EMG is strongly multiphasic, the population of muscles did not show consistent rotations (fig. 4c,f,j, summary data below). This was not due to the smaller size of the muscle population (supplementary fig. 6)

claims.statement: A generator model of two rotations of fixed frequency fits deltoid EMG with correlations of 0.97 to 0.99, and its simulated units resemble real neurons.
claims.source: Results, Rotations, kinematics and EMG, paragraphs 3 and 5; Figure 5; Supplementary Figures 7 to 9
claims.quote: This ‘generator model’ provided excellent EMG fits (fig. 5b,c; supplementary fig. 7,8). The fit/EMG correlation ranged from 0.97–0.99 across datasets ... Simulated units displayed multiphasic response patterns resembling those of real neurons

claims.statement: Rotations have similar angular velocity for instructed fast and slow reaches; the largest M_skew eigenvalues are 8.8 against 9.8 radians/s (monkey A) and 12.2 against 13.5 (monkey B), with larger amplitude for fast reaches.
claims.source: Results, Population-level quantification, paragraph 3; Figure 6c and 6d
claims.quote: the neural data exhibited rotations that were of similar angular velocity for fast and slow reaches (fig. 6c,d) ... the largest eigenvalues of Mskew were actually slightly smaller for fast reaches (8.8 versus 9.8 radians/s for monkey A, 12.2 versus 13.5 radians/s for monkey B). Rotation amplitude, rather than frequency, differed between speeds

claims.statement: The dandiset's behaviour labels can be named through the paper's code; "Mom agressing" is shepherding, "Virgin in rest" is nest entry (a nest dwell) and "Mom retrieval" is spontaneous pup retrieval by the dam.
claims.source: Methods (Spike train analysis, paragraph 1); Extended Data Fig. 7b; shepNestPup_xCorr_ForNature.m at GitHub commit 2db2a75
claims.quote: Distribution of durations of time in nest for virgins after entry events. ~70% of all nest dwell times are ≤40 s
claims.criterion: Records are matched by label text; a label that differs only in spelling ("Mom aggressing") is the same label. The link holds (reproduced) when (1) in the one file that carries both the code's labels and the paper's names (V116 03122018), every "Mom agressing" interval coincides with a "Shepherding" interval and every "Mom retrieval" interval with a "Self gen retrieval" interval (start and stop within 0.5 s), and (2) the fraction of "Virgin in rest" intervals lasting 40 s or less, pooled over all files that have the label, is within the tolerance of 70.5%. Partially reproduced when only one of (1) and (2) holds; not reproduced when neither does.

claims.statement: A significant fraction of virgin PVN units were activated during nest entry (6 of 21 OT-PVN and 33 of 126 PVN units; one-sided Fisher's exact test p = 0.01 and 0.0001).
claims.source: Fig. 2i; Extended Data Fig. 7a (middle); Source Data Fig. 2i
claims.quote: nest entry (middle; 6/21 OT-PVN neurons, p=0.01; 33/126 PVN neurons, p=0.0001
claims.criterion: Method as in the file header, on all units of the sessions that have at least one "Virgin in rest" episode. Two readings of the reported fraction, as OT identity is not in the dandiset; (a) OT-PVN and PVN pooled, 39 of 147 = 26.5%, and (b) PVN only, 33 of 126 = 26.2% (tolerance 2.62).
