Reproduced when the pooled fraction activated is within tolerance under either reading and the one-sided Fisher's exact test against zero gives p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when the Fisher test gives p < 0.05 but the fraction is outside both tolerances. Not reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: A significant fraction of virgin PVN units were activated during shepherding by the dam (5 of 21 OT-PVN and 9 of 97 PVN units; p = 0.02 and 0.001).
claims.source: Fig. 2e; Extended Data Fig. 7a (left); Source Data Fig. 2e
claims.quote: during shepherding (left; 5/21 OT-PVN neurons, Fisher's exact test, p=0.02; 9/97 PVN neurons, p=0.001)
claims.criterion: Method as in the file header, on all units of the sessions that have at least one "Mom agressing" episode, with the 10 s baseline of the Methods. Readings (a) pooled, 14 of 118 = 11.9%, and (b) PVN only, 9 of 97 = 9.3% (tolerance 0.93). Reproduced when the fraction is within tolerance under either reading and the Fisher test gives p < 0.05; partially reproduced when p < 0.05 but the fraction is outside both; not reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Spontaneous pup retrieval by the dam, in which the virgin was not involved, activated a significant fraction of virgin PVN units (5 of 17 OT-PVN and 10 of 69 PVN units; p = 0.02 and 0.0007).
claims.source: Fig. 3b, c; Extended Data Fig. 7a (right); Source Data Fig. 3c
claims.quote: Remarkably, retrieval by dams evoked responses in virgin PVN (Fig. 3b, c), although the virgin was not directly involved ... dam retrieval (right; 5/17 OT-PVN neurons, p=0.02; 10/69 PVN neurons, p=0.0007)
claims.criterion: Method as in the file header, on all units of the sessions that have at least one "Mom retrieval" episode, with the 10 s baseline of the Methods. Readings (a) pooled, 15 of 86 = 17.4%, and (b) PVN only, 10 of 69 = 14.5% (tolerance 1.45). Reproduced when the fraction is within tolerance under either reading and the Fisher test gives p < 0.05; partially reproduced when p < 0.05 but the fraction is outside both; not reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: PVN units fired more when the virgin entered the nest after being shepherded than when she entered it voluntarily (18 units, Wilcoxon matched-pairs signed rank test, p = 0.0056).
claims.source: Fig. 2j; Extended Data Fig. 7a; Source Data Fig. 2j
claims.quote: Spiking rate when virgin entered nest after shepherding (red) or voluntarily (grey) ... shepherding vs voluntary entry, p=0.005, Wilcoxon signed-rank test
claims.criterion: A nest entry ("Virgin in rest" start) is shepherded when it starts between the start of a "Mom agressing" episode and 10 s after its end, and voluntary otherwise; the paper does not give a rule. Each unit's change during nest entry (method of the file header, 40 s cap) is averaged separately over shepherded and voluntary entries. Units are all units of the sessions with at least one entry of each kind and a defined value for both. Reproduced when the shepherded value exceeds the voluntary one in the median over units and a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test gives p < 0.05; not reproduced otherwise. Variants, which do not change the outcome; windows of 5 and 30 s, and the units activated in ed7a-nest-entry-fraction.

claims.statement: Dams shepherded virgins more often than the 0.2 events per hour at which dams chased virgins without pups, at 3.5 +/- 0.9 events per hour with pups present.
claims.source: Fig. 1j; Extended Data Fig. 3b
claims.quote: summary of shepherding events per hour when pups were removed vs when pups were present (‘No pups’: 0.2±0.1 events/hour; ‘Pups’: 3.5±0.9 events/hour, N=4, p=0.03, Student’s two-tailed paired t-test)
claims.criterion: Rates are per session, "Mom agressing" (and "Mom aggressing") episodes over the session's length (the longer of the recording and the last annotation), over every session whose annotations include a label for the virgin ("Virgin in rest", "Virgin in nest" or "Virgin Agressing"), as only these appear scored for interactions. Reproduced when the mean per-session rate is above 0.2 with a two-sided one-sample t-test p < 0.05 and the mean is within 3.5 +/- 0.9; partially reproduced when only the t-test part holds; not reproduced when the t-test part fails. Per-mouse means are also shown.

claims.statement: About once every two hours, dams dropped and then retrieved pups during co-housing (daily means 0.34 to 0.60 retrievals per hour, N = 14 dams).
claims.source: Results, Social transmission of maternal behaviour, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 8a
claims.quote: About once every two hours, dams dropped and then retrieved pups, sometimes bringing pups to the virgin
claims.criterion: Rates are per session, "Mom retrieval" episodes over the session's length, over the same sessions as fig1j-shepherding-rate. Reproduced when the mean per-session rate is within 10% of 0.5 per hour or within the daily range of Extended Data Fig. 8a widened by 10% of each bound (0.31 to 0.66); not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Optically tagged OT-PVN units (21 units) were activated by shepherding, nest entry and dam retrieval, and pairs including OT-PVN units were more correlated than PVN pairs during these behaviours.
claims.source: Fig. 2b, e, g-i; Fig. 3b-d; Extended Data Figs. 5, 6a, 7a, 7d, 7e
claims.quote: Virgin PVN and OT-PVN units were activated by shepherding or initial nest entry ... found that pairs containing OT-PVN cells were more correlated during shepherding, nest entry and dam retrieval
claims.criterion: Needs the identity of the OT-PVN units, from the optical tagging recordings or the authors' list of identified units.

claims.statement: Units activated during shepherding fired less when the virgin chased the dam (6 units, Wilcoxon p = 0.03).
claims.source: Fig. 2f; Source Data Fig. 2f
claims.quote: Units with significant rate changes during shepherding (red) fired less during virgin→dam chases (grey)
claims.criterion: Needs a label for virgin-to-dam chases. The files have "Virgin Agressing", which no source names.

claims.statement: During 5-minute interactions, more virgin PVN units were activated by the dam than by pups (25 of 248 against 7 of 248), and units barely responded to pup calls (1 of 71).
claims.source: Extended Data Figs. 6c-e, 7c
claims.quote: interactions with dam activated more virgin PVN cells than interactions with pups (with dam: 25/248, with pup: 7/248, p=0.001, two-sided Fisher’s exact test) ... only 1/71 PVN units having significant responses to pup vocalizations
claims.criterion: Needs the 5-minute interaction periods and the pup call playback times.

claims.statement: Virgins co-housed with a dam and litter began retrieving pups earlier than virgins co-housed with pups alone (n = 14 and 10, P < 0.0001), and nest entry and shepherding on day 1 correlated with retrieval at the end of day 1 (r = 0.66 and 0.75).
claims.source: Fig. 1c, d, f, k; Extended Data Fig. 2
claims.quote: Virgins co-housed with dams and litters (D+ virgins, n = 14) began reliably retrieving ... earlier than virgins co-housed with pups but without dams (D− virgins, n = 10) ... the more virgins entered the nest, the more likely it was that retrieval occurred on day 1
claims.criterion: Needs the daily retrieval tests of each co-housed virgin.

claims.statement: Chemogenetic silencing of OT-PVN neurons delayed the onset of retrieval in co-housed virgins.
claims.source: Fig. 2a; Extended Data Fig. 4
claims.quote: found that retrieval onset in naive co-housed virgins was delayed (Fig. 2a)
claims.criterion: Needs the retrieval scores of the DREADD and control cohorts.

claims.statement: Non-co-housed virgins learned to retrieve after watching dams retrieve, with no barrier (11 of 15) or through a transparent barrier (12 of 19), but not through an opaque barrier (2 of 18) or when lacking the oxytocin receptor (3 of 10).
claims.source: Fig. 3e-g; Extended Data Fig. 8c, d
claims.quote: No barrier: 11 out of 15 virgins retrieving after 40 maternal demonstrations ... transparent: 12 out of 19 virgins retrieving ... opaque: 2 out of 18 virgins retrieving ... OXTR-KO: 3 out of 10 virgins retrieving
claims.criterion: Needs the retrieval scores of the observation cohorts.

claims.statement: PVN units of non-co-housed virgins were activated while watching dam retrievals (15 of 65), some also during the virgin's own retrievals (15 of 41), and only in virgins that went on to retrieve (learners against non-learners, P = 0.0001).
claims.source: Fig. 3h-j
claims.quote: 15 out of 65 PVN neurons increased activity during dam retrieval; right, 15 out of 41 of these units increased activity during self-performance) ... was elevated only in those non-co-housed virgins that eventually began retrieving
claims.criterion: Needs unit recordings from the observation sessions.

claims.statement: Auditory cortex photometry responses to pup calls increased over co-housing up to the day of retrieval onset (P = 0.003, n = 3).
claims.source: Fig. 4a-c; Extended Data Fig. 10a
claims.quote: We found a progressive increase in photometric signal before the day of retrieval onset
claims.criterion: Needs auditory cortex photometry with pup call playback times.

claims.statement: Single-trial PVN activity correlated with pup-call responses in auditory cortex during observation (r = 0.5, P = 0.00001, n = 4).
claims.source: Fig. 4d-f
claims.quote: Even before virgins began retrieving pups, single-trial PVN activity correlated with pup call-evoked responses in cortex
claims.criterion: Needs simultaneous PVN units and auditory cortex photometry.

claims.statement: PVN to auditory cortex projections were activated during observation of dam retrieval in virgins that learned to retrieve (P = 0.02) but not in those that did not (P = 0.5), three animals per group.
claims.source: Fig. 4g-i; Source Data Fig. 4i
claims.quote: In virgins that began retrieving, PVN→auditory cortex projections were activated during observation of dam retrieval ... PVN→auditory cortex projections were not significantly activated in virgins that did not learn after observation
claims.criterion: Per-animal responses to the dam's retrievals in the observation sessions, tested with a one-sample t-test per group as in the Source Data. Needs which animals learned.

claims.statement: An oxytocin receptor antagonist in auditory cortex prevented learning by observation (2 of 10 against 7 of 9), and stimulating OT-PVN fibres in auditory cortex enhanced it (4 of 4 against 2 of 4).
claims.source: Fig. 4j, k
claims.quote: Infusing a selective oxytocin receptor antagonist (OTA) into virgin left auditory cortex before transparent-barrier observational testing prevented virgins from learning to retrieve ... Optogenetic stimulation of OT-PVN→auditory cortex projections during observational testing with the opaque barrier enhanced retrieval learning
claims.criterion: Needs the retrieval scores of the infusion and optogenetic cohorts.

claims.statement: Superficial superior colliculus projects to OT-PVN neurons, and stimulating this input replaced visual experience (4 of 5 against 1 of 6 virgins retrieving).
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 9; Results, Social transmission of maternal behaviour, paragraph 4
claims.quote: found projections from medial superficial layers of ipsilateral superior colliculus ... Optogenetic sSC→PVN stimulation could replace visual experience in non-co-housed virgins exposed to maternal retrievals behind an opaque barrier
claims.criterion: Needs tracing histology and the retrieval scores of the stimulation cohort.

claims.statement: The analysis includes 24, 32, 23 and 33 behavioural sessions and 89, 85, 105 and 166 trial blocks for the four subjects.
claims.source: Figure 1D and 1E-F legends
claims.quote: n = 24, 32, 23, and 33 sessions per subject, respectively ... n = 89, 85, 105, and 166 trial blocks per subject, respectively
claims.criterion: Sessions are the full-task sessions of each subject, less sessions 1 and 3 of subject 1 (Methods, Spatial decoding). The paper does not say how sessions are numbered; the code selects them with a $gooddecode flag and a per-animal $session field of the task records, neither given in the repository. Two readings are allowed. (a) The first and third run sessions of subject 1 in order of recording. (b) The two sessions the Methods describe, the first with fewer than 75% of movement frames decoded on the same segment, the second with not all arms visited. Both are run and reported; when they give different outcomes the claim follows (b), which the Methods state, and (a) is a variant. Trial blocks are counted as in dfs_ripcontent.m part 2, blocks with at least four rewards at the goal (a trial of task phase >= 4, the code's any(ctphase>=4)), with the first valid trial after each goal change in the old block, as the opening comment says. Reproduced when all eight counts are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the session counts are and the block counts are not.

claims.statement: Aligned to the goal change, the outer-arm reward rate starts at chance (0.125) and rises; aligned to the first reward at the new goal, it is well above chance, so all subjects keep visiting a goal once found.
claims.source: Results, Rats learn to perform a flexible spatial memory task, paragraph 5; Figure 1E and 1F
claims.quote: Aligned to the first search trial of each trial block, the reward rate at the outer arms for all subjects began at chance (0.125) and rose (Figure 1E) ... the outer reward rate was well above chance, indicating that all subjects preferentially visited the goal location consistently after finding it (Figure 1F)
claims.criterion: As dfs_ripcontent.m part 2, per subject over trial blocks with at least four rewards, the final unrewarded trial of the block dropped; a trial scores 1 when rewarded; binomial S.E.M. sqrt(p(1-p)/n), trials 1 to 15. The paper gives no test, so the figure's S.E.M. band is read. Reproduced when, in all four subjects, the band on trial 1 of Figure 1E reaches 0.125 or lies below it, the rate rises over trials 1 to 15, and every point of Figure 1F (trials 1 to 15 after the first reward) has its band above 0.125.

claims.statement: SWRs occur mainly during reward consumption at the home port, the center ports and the rewarded goal arm, and are rarely detected at unrewarded outer ports.
claims.source: Results, Most SWRs contain interpretable spatial content, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 1C
claims.quote: SWRs occurred primarily during reward consumption (Supplementary Figure 1C) ... As expected, SWRs were rarely detected at non-goal outer arm ports, which did not provide reward
claims.criterion: SWRs detected as in the Methods (consensus ripple envelope, 150 to 250 Hz, over all CA1 cell-layer tetrodes, above 2 SD of the session mean for at least 15 ms, bounds at the mean crossing, immobility below 4 cm/s). Per session, time, SWR count and SWR rate in each trial phase (home port, center port before and after reward, rewarded outer port, unrewarded outer port), as dfs_ripcontent.m part 12. Reproduced when, in all four subjects, the median over sessions of the SWR count at unrewarded outer ports is the lowest of the five phases and its SWR rate is below that of each reward phase.

claims.statement: During movement the decoded position (posterior maximum) is usually on the same or an adjacent maze segment as the real position, and the median deviation between them is less than one 5 cm bin, on every maze segment.
claims.source: Results, Most SWRs contain interpretable spatial content, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 3A-C; Methods, Spatial decoding, paragraph 5
claims.quote: The median deviation between predicted and real position was less than a single spatial bin (5 cm), indicating that the maximum of the posterior and the subject's real position most often corresponded to the same spatial bin, and this was consistent across all segments of the maze
claims.criterion: Decoding as the Methods give it (clusterless, encoding on spikes above 100 uV at > 4 cm/s with a 20 uV Gaussian kernel on the four amplitudes and 5 cm bins, 2 ms steps, a continuous and a uniform fragmented movement state, 0.98 probability of staying in a state, acausal smoother, each session decoded alone, a spike's own position not used to decode it). For 30 Hz frames during movement, the frame is same/adjacent when the real and decoded segments match or one is the box; for those frames the deviation in 5 cm bins. Reproduced when, in every subject, the median deviation is 0 bins (less than one bin) on the pooled frames and on each of the nine segments. dfs_decodequant_movement.m part 2 plots the mean deviation per segment; it is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Decoding error on the goal arm shows no systematic change over the course of a trial block, so repeated reward does not change spatial coding at the ensemble level.
claims.source: Results, Most SWRs contain interpretable spatial content, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 3D-F
claims.quote: We found no systematic changes in the deviation over the course of the trial block, indicating that the changing reward location did not alter overall spatial coding at the ensemble level
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The legend names no test; dfs_decodequant_movement.m part 6 compares the mean deviation in the last 5 bins (25 cm) of the goal arm on the first against the last rewarded goal visit of each block with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test, and fits a line to the per-visit deviations of each block with at least 4 visits. Reproduced when the rank-sum test gives p >= 0.05 in each subject; the slope distributions (median and its sign) are reported either way.

claims.statement: About 95% of SWRs contain spatially continuous representations.
claims.source: Results, Most SWRs contain interpretable spatial content, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 3G
claims.quote: We found that the vast majority of SWRs (~95%) contained spatially continuous representations of the environment
claims.criterion: Per session, spatially continuous SWRs (as in the opening comment, with the 0.3 single-segment share) over all SWRs inside trial intervals, as dfs_ripcontent.m part 3 (fraccohall). Reproduced when the session mean of each subject is within tolerance.

claims.statement: A history-independent Bayesian decoder with 20 ms bins and no movement model assigns more than 90% of SWRs to the same maze segment as the state space decoder.
claims.source: Results, Most SWRs contain interpretable spatial content, paragraph 4
claims.quote: We found that >90% of SWRs decoded to the same maze segment and our main results were unchanged with the use of this simplified decoding approach
claims.criterion: The comparison is not described beyond the sentence. Readings, each run, (a) over all SWRs, the segment with the largest summed posterior during the SWR under each decoder; (b) over spatially continuous SWRs only. Reproduced when the fraction is above 0.9 under one reading, pooled over subjects and in each subject. The "main results unchanged" part is tested in robustness-controls.

claims.statement: A substantial fraction of all detected SWRs contain remote replay, 35.1%, 41.1%, 34.5% and 47.2% for the four subjects.
claims.source: Results, Most SWRs contain interpretable spatial content, paragraph 6; Figure 2F
claims.quote: Across all animals, we found that a substantial fraction of detected SWRs contained remote replay ... 35.1%, 41.1%, 34.5%, and 47.2% for the 4 subjects (Figure 2F)
claims.criterion: Per session, remote continuous events (segment other than the current one) over all SWRs in the trial intervals, then the mean over sessions, as dfs_ripcontent.m part 3 (fracremoteall, whose printed means are the reported values). Reproduced when all four are within tolerance; partially reproduced when two or three are.

claims.statement: The large majority of spatially continuous replay events occur in the box area, before the arm choice, and include local and remote events.
claims.source: Results, Replay content is enriched for previous goal locations, paragraph 1; Figure 3A
claims.quote: The large majority of spatially continuous replay events occurred in the box area, before arm choice, and included both local and remote representations (Figure 3A)
claims.criterion: Pooled over sessions per subject, the shares of continuous events that are box local, box remote, outer local, outer box and outer remote arm, as dfs_ripcontent.m part 3 (totalnums). Reproduced when, in all four subjects, box events are more than half of all continuous events and box local and box remote are each above zero. "Large majority" is not given a number; the box share is reported.

claims.statement: In search trials where the past, future and previous goal arms are distinct, the previous goal arm is consistently and strongly over-represented in pre-choice remote replay, about 20% of these events, in all subjects.
claims.source: Results, Replay content is enriched for previous goal locations, paragraph 2; Figure 3B
claims.quote: In contrast, we saw consistent and strong enrichment for replay of the previous goal arm ... such replay accounted for roughly 20% of all pre-choice remote replay events during these search trials (Figure 3B, previous goal)
claims.criterion: As the Methods (Quantification of replay content) and dfs_ripcontent.m part 4. Box remote events, sessions after the first trial block, search trials with past, future and previous goal all distinct, sessions with at least 5 such trials; per session the count of events of each category over all remote events. The null is the open detail; readings, each run, (a) Methods, per session 5000 draws of a random arm 1 to 8 for each event, the null values of all included sessions pooled; (b) dfs_ripcontent.m, 100 draws per session pooled; (c) 5000 draws over the subject's events pooled across sessions. Per subject, a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test of session fractions against the null. "Roughly 20%" does not say which summary; the session median (the boxplot's) and the session mean are both read. Reproduced when the previous goal fraction is above the null at p < 0.05 in all four subjects under every null reading and the median or the mean is within tolerance; partially reproduced when it is enriched in all four but neither is within tolerance.

claims.statement: In those search trials the immediately past arm is replayed far less often than chance.
claims.source: Results, Replay content is enriched for previous goal locations, paragraph 2; Figure 3B
claims.quote: we found far fewer replays of the immediate past arm than would be expected by chance (Figure 3B, past)
claims.criterion: Selection, measure, null readings and test as fig3b-search-prevgoal-enriched. Reproduced when the past fraction is below the null at p < 0.05 in all four subjects under every reading; partially reproduced in two or three.

claims.statement: In those search trials the upcoming (future) arm shows a small but significant enrichment in two of the four subjects only.
claims.source: Results, Replay content is enriched for previous goal locations, paragraph 2; Figure 3B
claims.quote: while we did see a small but significant enrichment for the upcoming arm in two out of four subjects, this enrichment was not consistent across animals (Figure 3B, future)
claims.criterion: Selection, measure, null readings and test as fig3b-search-prevgoal-enriched. Reproduced when the future fraction is significantly above the null (p < 0.05) in fewer than four subjects and its session median is below that of the previous goal in every subject. The count of subjects with significant enrichment is reported; the paper's count is two.

claims.statement: Each of the other arms is replayed at about chance per arm, yet the other arms together make up the majority of pre-choice remote replay.
claims.source: Results, Replay content is enriched for previous goal locations, paragraph 2; Figure 3B right
claims.quote: Finally, replay of other arms occurred at roughly chance levels per arm (Figure 3B, other), but the total fraction of "other" events comprised the majority of replay events overall (Figure 3B, right)
claims.criterion: Per session, other-arm events over all remote events divided by 5 (per arm) and not divided (total), as the Methods and dfs_ripcontent.m part 4. "Roughly chance" has no test in the text; the per-arm session median is compared with 0.125 using the protocol's 10% tolerance (0.1125 to 0.1375) and the rank-sum p against the null is reported. Reproduced when, in all four subjects, the per-arm median is within that range and the total-other median is above 0.5.

claims.statement: In repeat trials where past, future and current goal are the same arm and the previous goal is distinct, all animals still strongly over-replay the previous goal, while the future (past and goal) arm shows only a small and variable effect; other arms together are again the majority.
claims.source: Results, Replay content is enriched for previous goal locations, paragraph 3; Figure 3C
claims.quote: During the large subset of repeat trials in which the past, future, and goal arm refer to the same location, distinct from the previous goal arm, all animals still showed a strong and highly significant tendency to replay the previous goal location (Figure 3C, previous goal). In contrast, replay of the future arm still showed only a small and variable effect
claims.criterion: As fig3b-search-prevgoal-enriched, for repeat trials (task phase > 1) after the first block where past, future and current goal are one arm and the previous goal differs; other arms per arm are divided by 6. Reproduced when, under every null reading, the previous goal fraction is above the null at p < 0.01 ("highly significant", the figure's ** level) in all four subjects, the future/past/goal fraction is significantly above the null in fewer than four subjects or has a median below that of the previous goal in every subject, and the total-other median exceeds 0.5 in all four.

claims.statement: In a Poisson GLM over all search trials, being the previous goal roughly doubles an arm's replay rate, the strongest effect; the past arm is consistently replayed less; the future arm has a small increase significant in three of four subjects.
claims.source: Results, Replay content is enriched for previous goal locations, paragraph 5; Figure 3D
claims.quote: During search trials, previous goal arm status had the strongest impact on replay, such that if an arm was the previous goal, there was an approximately two-fold increase in replay rate from baseline (Figure 3D). The past arm showed a significant and consistent reduction in the rate of replay. The future category showed a small increase in replay rate that was significant in three of the four subjects but not in the fourth
claims.criterion: As the Methods (Generalized linear models to measure the effect of arm category) and dfs_ripcontent.m part 5. Per subject, eight rows per search trial (task phase <= 1), response the count of box remote continuous events of that arm, binary predictors future, past and previous goal, Poisson log link, 99% Wald intervals, exponentiated. The trial set is the open detail; (a) Methods, trials after the first block of each session (main); (b) dfs_ripcontent.m, all search trials with the previous goal predictor zero in the first block, whose trial counts appear to be those of the legend (711 here against 534 search trials after the first block in Figure 5A), run as a variant. Reproduced under (a) when, in all four subjects, the previous goal fold change has its interval above 1 and is the largest of the three, the past fold change has its interval below 1, and the future interval is above 1 in at most three subjects; the previous goal values are compared with 2 within tolerance, and partially reproduced when only that fails. The pooled fit of the code is shown too. The legend gives 711, 848, 725 and 1065 trials per subject.

claims.statement: In a Poisson GLM over all repeat trials the previous goal arm is again the strongest and most consistent driver of replay and the past arm is reliably replayed less.
claims.source: Results, Replay content is enriched for previous goal locations, paragraph 5; Figure 3E
claims.quote: Applying the GLM approach to repeat trials yielded similar results (Figure 3E), confirming that for both search and repeat phase, the previous goal arm was the strongest and most consistent driver of replay content, while the replay of the past arm was reliably reduced
claims.criterion: As fig3d-glm-search with a fourth predictor, current goal, over repeat trials (task phase > 1), with the same two trial-set readings. In dfs_ripcontent.m part 5 the current goal on the final unrewarded trial of a block is already the new goal; this is kept. Reproduced when, in all four subjects, the previous goal interval is above 1 and its fold change is the largest of the four predictors, and the past interval is below 1. The legend gives 1347, 1661, 1154 and 1730 trials per subject.

claims.statement: Replay of the current goal is consistently enhanced only late in the repeat phase (five or more rewards at the goal), while the effects of the other three categories do not differ much between early and late repeat trials.
claims.source: Results, Replay of current goal location increases with experience, paragraph 2; Figure 4A-B
claims.quote: Indeed, we found a consistent enhancement of current goal replay only in the late portion of the repeat phase. In contrast, the three other categories did not differ substantially between early and late conditions
claims.criterion: The repeat GLM of fig3e-glm-repeat fit separately to early and late repeat trials. Early is task phase > 1 and < 5, as dfs_ripcontent.m part 5 (the Figure 4A n equal the early correct plus early error counts of Supplementary Figure 7 for subjects 1 to 3, and differ by one trial for subject 4, 793 against 515 + 277). Late is open; readings, each run, (a) task phase >= 5, the complement of early; (b) the code's task phase > 4, under which errors after four rewards (4.3, 4.5, 4.8) enter both sets. The trial-set readings of fig3d-glm-search also apply. Reproduced when, under each reading, the current goal interval is above 1 in all four subjects for late trials and in fewer than four for early trials, and for future, past and previous goal the early and late 99% intervals overlap in at least three of four subjects. The legends give 594, 801, 573 and 793 early and 801, 895, 600 and 967 late trials per subject.

claims.statement: On correct repeat trials, the number of current goal replays correlates positively with the number of rewards already received at that goal in every subject, with low R2.
claims.source: Results, Replay of current goal location increases with experience, paragraph 2; Figure 4C
claims.quote: Quantified on a trial-by-trial basis, we found significant positive correlations between the number of replays of the current goal and the number of rewards already received at that location, although there was substantial variability across trials, as indicated by the low R2 values (R2=0.033, 0.015, 0.012, and 0.025; p=1.54e-6, 0.0003, 0.0004, and 2.87e-11; n=923, 1007, 847, and 1340 trials per subject, respectively)
claims.criterion: As dfs_ripcontent.m part 6. Correct repeat trials after the first block (task phase integer > 1 or n + 0.9, with the old goal kept on the n + 0.9 trial), per subject pooled over sessions (n = 923 is the Figure 5B correct count, so the first-block variant of fig5b-future-correct-error is run too); Pearson correlation (corrcoef) of the count of box remote events of the current goal with reward experience. Reward experience is open; (a) the code's ceil(task phase), the reward count including the current trial's (n + 1 on the final trial); (b) rewards received before the trial (n - 1 for a rewarded trial, n on the final trial). Reproduced when, under one reading, r > 0 with p < 0.05 in all four subjects and the R2 values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the correlations are significant and positive but some R2 is outside tolerance. The Figure 4C means per reward count (groups of at least 10 trials) are shown.

claims.statement: Replay of the future arm occurs on average less than once per trial, and more often in search than in repeat trials for three of the four subjects.
claims.source: Results, Subsequent arm choice is not biased by replay, paragraph 2; Figure 5A
claims.quote: Future replay per trial tends to occur less than once per trial, and more often during search trials than repeat trials for three of the four subjects ... Search vs repeat rate p = 0.001, 5.002e-11, 0.264, and 4.111e-5 for each subject, respectively, using Wilcoxon rank-sum test
claims.criterion: As dfs_ripcontent.m part 7. Per trial after the first block, the count of box remote continuous events of the arm visited on that trial; per subject the mean over search and over repeat trials, and a Wilcoxon rank-sum test of the pooled trial counts. Reproduced when all eight means are below 1 and the search mean is above the repeat mean at p < 0.05 in three subjects (any three); partially reproduced in two or four.

claims.statement: On repeat trials, future arm replay does not differ between correct and error trials in two subjects and is higher on error trials in the other two, the opposite of what planning predicts.
claims.source: Results, Subsequent arm choice is not biased by replay, paragraph 2; Figure 5B
claims.quote: However, we found no difference in future replay rate between correct and incorrect repeat trials for two out of the four subjects (Figure 5B). For the other two subjects, future arm replay was actually higher, on average, for error as compared to correct trials
claims.criterion: As dfs_ripcontent.m part 6. Repeat trials after the first block, correct and error as in the opening comment; per trial the count of box remote events of the visited arm; per subject a Wilcoxon rank-sum test of correct against error trials pooled over sessions. The trial set is open; (a) after the first block, as the Methods (Quantification of replay content) and part 6 (~isnan of the previous goal), the main reading; (b) all repeat trials, first block included, run as a variant, because the legend's correct plus error counts (1347, 1661, 1154, 1730) equal the Figure 3E counts, which part 5 takes with the first block included. Reproduced when no subject has significantly (p < 0.05) more future replay on correct than on error trials, and the number of subjects with significantly more on error trials is two. Partially reproduced when no subject is higher on correct trials but the count is not two. The p entry above records the figure's lowest marked level (**).

claims.statement: Current goal replay does not differ consistently between correct and error repeat trials for three subjects, and the fourth has more current goal replay on error trials.
claims.source: Results, Subsequent arm choice is not biased by replay, paragraph 4; Figure 5C
claims.quote: Again, we found no consistent significant difference between the amount of current goal replay on correct compared to error trials for three subjects (Figure 5C), and the fourth subject showed a significant increase
claims.criterion: As fig5b-future-correct-error, counting box remote events of the current goal arm (the old goal on the final unrewarded trial, as dfs_ripcontent.m part 6). Reproduced when no subject has significantly more current goal replay on correct trials and exactly one has significantly more on error trials; partially reproduced when none is higher on correct trials but the count of subjects higher on error trials is not one.

claims.statement: The lack of a correct over error difference in future and current goal replay holds both early and late in the repeat phase.
claims.source: Results, Subsequent arm choice is not biased by replay, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 7A-D
claims.quote: Importantly, these results were consistent for trials that occurred both early and late in the repeat phase of the trial block, indicating that familiarity with the goal location did not modulate the effect (Supplementary Figure 7A-D)
claims.criterion: As fig5b and fig5c, split into early (task phase < 5) and late (task phase >= 5) repeat trials, as dfs_ripcontent.m part 6 (its counts, 268 early correct and 326 early error trials for subject 1, are in the legend). Reproduced when, in both halves, for future and for current goal replay, no subject has significantly (rank-sum p < 0.05) more replay on correct than on error trials.

claims.statement: Error trials have more remote replay than correct trials regardless of content, while SWR amplitude, event duration and spike rate of remote events do not differ.
claims.source: Results, Subsequent arm choice is not biased by replay, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 7E
claims.quote: We also examined features of remote events on correct and error trials, independent of their content, and found that while characteristics such as SWR amplitude, event duration, and spike rate did not differ, the rate of remote replay was consistently higher on error trials
claims.criterion: As dfs_ripcontent.m part 14. Repeat trials (task phase > 1), error trials the n + 0.3, 0.5 and 0.8 trials; per trial the number of box remote continuous events, and the mean amplitude (SD threshold at which the event would still be detected), duration and spike rate of those events. The legend says number per trial; the code also shows events per second in the box, a variant. Per subject a Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Reproduced when the number per trial is significantly higher on error trials in all four subjects; the amplitude, duration and spike rate comparisons are judged as absence on the same test (p >= 0.05) and partially reproduce the claim when one of them differs in some subject.

claims.statement: Binomial GLMs predicting correct or error repeat trials from the counts of future arm, current goal, or all four category replays perform at or very near chance (50% misclassification), far worse than the animals.
claims.source: Results, Subsequent arm choice is not biased by replay, paragraph 6; Figure 5D
claims.quote: In all cases the models performed at or very close to chance levels, far worse than the animals (Figure 5D)
claims.criterion: As the Methods (Generalized linear models to predict correct and incorrect repeat phase trials). Per subject, repeat trials pooled, correct trials subsampled to the number of error trials, five folds, a binomial GLM (logit) on counts of future replay, of current goal replay, or of future, past, current goal and previous goal replay; misclassification is the mean over folds of the test-set error. Open details, each run, (a) number of subsamples, 1000 (Methods, main) or 100 (dfs_ripcontent.m part 6, variant); (b) how a test trial is classified, a draw from the fitted probability (the code's random(mdl, ...)) or a threshold at 0.5. Reproduced when every subject and model mean lies within tolerance under every reading; when readings differ, the claim is methods_underspecified with all results shown. The legend gives 848, 1308, 614 and 780 trials per subset per subject, twice the error trial counts of Figure 5B; the trial-set readings of fig5b-future-correct-error apply.

claims.statement: Across trial blocks, the rate of previous goal replay shows no consistent correlation with the number of visits to the previous goal during that block.
claims.source: Results, Subsequent arm choice is not biased by replay, paragraph 8
claims.quote: There was no consistent correlation between the rate of previous goal replay with the number of subsequent visits to the previous goal location during the subsequent trial block (for each subject: R2=0.008, 0.019, 0.021, and 0.023; p=0.49, 0.32, 0.18, and 0.08, respectively)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, on the paper's test as dfs_ripcontent.m part 16. Per trial block from the second on (trailing blocks with no trial of task phase above 3 dropped), previous goal replay rate is the count of box remote events of the previous goal over all the block's trials divided by its number of trials, and visits are the block's visits to the previous goal arm, search and repeat together; Pearson correlation across blocks per subject. Reproduced when p >= 0.05 in every subject; not reproduced when p < 0.05 with the same sign in all four ("consistent", as the paper uses it); otherwise partially reproduced. R2 and p are reported.

claims.statement: Pre-choice replay of the previous goal is no more or less likely to precede a visit to the previous goal than a visit to any other arm.
claims.source: Results, Subsequent arm choice is not biased by replay, paragraph 8; Figure 5E
claims.quote: However, we found that previous goal replay was no more or less likely to precede visits to the previous goal as it was to precede visits to any other arm (Figure 5E)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, per subject a Wilcoxon rank-sum test over sessions at p < 0.05. The measure is open; readings, each run, (a) dfs_ripcontent.m part 8, per session the fraction of trials visiting the previous goal that have at least one box remote event of the previous goal, against the same fraction among trials visiting any other arm; (b) the legend's "fraction of all trials", the count of trials with previous goal replay and a previous goal visit, and of those with previous goal replay and another visit, each over all trials with a defined previous goal. Trials after the first block, search and repeat. Reproduced when p >= 0.05 in every subject under reading (a), the code's; (b) is shown and its outcome recorded. The legend gives 23, 32, 23 and 33 sessions per subject and no p.

claims.statement: Replay of a goal arm stays enriched long after it stops being rewarded, peaking several trials after the switch, extended and significant in all subjects; two subjects also show elevated replay before the switch.
claims.source: Results, Previous goal replay persists through multiple trial blocks, paragraph 2; Figure 6A
claims.quote: The enrichment for replay of a goal location peaked several trials after it ceased to provide reward and continued for many subsequent trials. This enrichment was extended and significant for all subjects (Figure 6A). We also saw elevated replay before the transition for two out of the four subjects
claims.criterion: As the Methods (Trial-wise replay rate) and dfs_ripcontent.m part 9. Per session, count of box remote events per arm per trial, smoothed with a Gaussian kernel of five trials and SD one trial; for each block (blocks 1 to 8) the goal arm's trace from 40 trials before to 40 after the last rewarded trial, NaN beyond the session; the same window for every arm never a goal in the session. Per trial a Wilcoxon rank-sum test of goal against non-goal traces, Bonferroni corrected. The number of tests is 80 in the legend and 81 (0.05/81) in the code; both are run. Reproduced when, in all four subjects, the mean goal curve peaks after trial 0, some trials after 0 are significant with goal above non-goal, and two subjects (any two) have significant trials with goal above non-goal before trial 0. The number of significant trials after 0 is reported per subject.

claims.statement: The behavioural bias to the previously rewarded arm decays very quickly after the switch, returning to baseline within a few trials.
claims.source: Results, Previous goal replay persists through multiple trial blocks, paragraph 2; Figure 6B
claims.quote: In contrast, behavioral bias to the previously rewarded arm decays extremely quickly after the switch, returning to baseline levels within a few trials (Figure 6B)
claims.criterion: As fig6a-pg-replay-persists for visits (1 if the arm was visited on that trial), unsmoothed. "A few trials" has no number; readings, (a) no significant trial after trial +3, (b) after trial +5. Reproduced when, in all four subjects, the last trial after 0 with a significant goal over non-goal visit difference is no later than the bound under one reading and the replay enrichment of fig6a extends beyond it.

claims.statement: Enhanced replay of a previous goal persists for at least two complete trial blocks after it served as the goal, in all four animals.
claims.source: Results, Previous goal replay persists through multiple trial blocks, paragraph 3; Figure 6C
claims.quote: This analysis revealed that the enhanced replay of a previous goal location persisted for at least two complete trial blocks for all four animals (Figure 6C)
claims.criterion: As dfs_ripcontent.m part 9. Per session, blocks 1 to 8, each block split into search (task phase <= 1) and repeat (> 1) sub-blocks; a repeat sub-block counts only when the block reached a fourth reward; per sub-block the unsmoothed count of box remote events per arm over its number of trials. For each goal arm, the rates in the search and repeat sub-blocks of the three following blocks, against the same sub-blocks for arms never a goal in the session; per sub-block a Wilcoxon rank-sum test at 0.05/6. Reproduced when, in all four subjects, the first four sub-blocks (s1, r1, s2, r2) are each significant with goal above non-goal.

claims.statement: During search, never-rewarded arms not visited for 5 trials are replayed more than those visited one or two trials ago, and replay rate correlates with how long ago the arm was visited (1 to 5 trials) in every subject.
claims.source: Results, Pre-choice replay is biased toward non-recent past, paragraph 1; Figure 7
claims.quote: We found consistently higher replay rates for arms that had not been visited within 5 trials compared to those visited within one or two trials (Figure 7). Although highly variable, the replay rate of arms visited within 1-5 trials was strongly correlated with visit recency (for each subject: R2=0.011, 0.028, 0.012, and 0.018; p=1.04e-4, 4.04e-13, 7.94e-5, and 2.76e-8, respectively)
claims.criterion: As dfs_ripcontent.m part 8. Search trials (task phase <= 1) of all blocks; for each trial and each arm last visited k trials ago (lockout trials not counted), the count of box remote events of that arm. Open details, each run, (a) "never rewarded", the code's arms that were not a previous goal up to that trial, or the Results' arms never a goal in the session; (b) the "5 trials ago" bar, exactly 5 (the code's plotted and tested bar) or 5 or more (the Results' "not been visited within 5 trials"). Per subject, Wilcoxon rank-sum of the 5 bar against the 1 and the 2 bars, pooled trials, and Pearson correlation of count with k over k = 1 to 5. Reproduced when, under every reading, the 5 bar is significantly above the 1 and 2 bars (p < 0.05) and replay rises with k at p < 0.05 in all four subjects, with R2 within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when only R2 fails.

claims.statement: Replay at the rewarded outer arm port also favours the previous goal; beyond the expected strong over-representation of the current arm, the previous goal arm is replayed more than other arms, consistently in a GLM over all rewarded trials.
claims.source: Results, Enhanced replay of previous goal at outer arms, paragraph 2; Figure 8A-B
claims.quote: However, we also observed greater replay of the previous goal compared to other arms (Figure 8A). We used a Poisson GLM to quantify these effects during all rewarded trials and found that in addition to overrepresentation of the current arm (the goal arm), we also saw consistent, strong enrichment for replay of the previous goal arm (Figure 8B)
claims.criterion: Figure 8A as dfs_ripcontent.m part 10, outer events on rewarded trials (task phase >= 1) after the first block where past, current and goal arm are one arm distinct from the previous goal, sessions with at least 5 such trials, fractions over all continuous outer events (local included); other arms per arm divided by 6. Figure 8B as part 5, all rewarded trials (integer task phase >= 1), counts of outer continuous events per arm, predictors past, current goal and previous goal, Poisson GLM with 99% intervals; the trial-set readings of fig3d-glm-search apply. Reproduced when, in all four subjects, the session mean previous goal fraction exceeds the per-arm other fraction, and the previous goal and current arm intervals are above 1. The legends give 333, 958, 1161 and 3316 events (8A) and 948, 1026, 868 and 1372 trials (8B) per subject.

claims.statement: Among outbound remote events, and among the final remote event before each choice, the previous goal is still the most consistently enriched arm, and future and current goal replay still do not differ consistently between correct and error trials.
claims.source: Results, Subsequent arm choice is not biased by replay, paragraph 5; Supplementary Figure 8
claims.quote: For neither of these subsets of events did we see any difference in the relationships between content and behavior ... previous goal replay remained more strongly and consistently enriched compared to future arm or current goal replay and we still did not observe consistent differences between correct and error trials (Supplementary Figure 8)
claims.criterion: Outbound events as the Methods and dfa_ripcontent_ripspeed.m, the slope of a line fit through the posterior-maximum bin of each 2 ms step after correcting for linearisation, positive for box to arm; final events as dfs_ripcontent.m part 15, the last box remote event before the arm choice. For each subset, the search and repeat GLMs of fig3d and fig3e, and the correct against error rank-sum tests of fig5b and fig5c. Reproduced when, for both subsets, the previous goal interval is above 1 in all four subjects for search and repeat, no subject has significantly more future or current goal replay on correct than on error trials, and the future and current goal effects are not significant (p < 0.05) in the same direction in all four subjects.

claims.statement: The main results are unchanged with MUA-based event detection, with a more permissive definition of remote events, after excluding stationary events identified by a three-state decoder, and with a simple 20 ms Bayesian decoder.
claims.source: Results, Most SWRs contain interpretable spatial content, paragraphs 1, 4 and 5; Methods, Spatial decoding, paragraphs 4 and 7
claims.quote: Additionally, we verified that our conclusions were unchanged by using a multiunit activity-based event detection strategy ... instead of a SWR-based one ... Use of this alternative definition did not alter any of our conclusions
claims.criterion: The paper does not say which results were compared. Read as the patterns of Figures 3D and 3E (previous goal interval above 1 in all subjects, past interval below 1 in all subjects) and Figure 5B (no subject with more future replay on correct trials). Each control as the Methods give it and its script (dfs_muacontent.m, MUA 1 ms bins smoothed with a 15 ms Gaussian, events above 3 SD of the immobility mean; dfs_ripcontent_contentthresh.m, a local-majority event is remote when at least 30% of its density is on one remote segment; dfs_ripcontent_3state.m, the three-state decoder with stationary events excluded; dfs_likcontent.m, 20 ms non-overlapping bins without a movement model). Reproduced when the three patterns hold under all four controls; partially reproduced when they hold under some. The share of remote events classed stationary (paper, < 30%) is reported.

claims.statement: The sessions are those the Methods list for each target configuration; for monkey R, ring on 2017-01-24 and 25, horizontal on 2017-01-17 and 18, vertical on 2017-01-15 and 16, and 3-rings on 2017-01-19; for J, ring, vertical and 3-rings on the dates listed.
claims.source: Materials and methods, Experimental design, paragraph 3; Figure 1b
claims.quote: 36 for R (3577 over two sessions: 2017-01-24, 2017-01-25) ... For horizontal configuration ... 3699 trials over two sessions for R (2017-01-17, 2017-01-18). For vertical ... 4040 trials over two sessions for R (2017-01-15, 2017-01-16)
claims.criterion: Each session's configuration is inferred from its target positions (ring, all targets on one circle; horizontal, all targets on the x axis; vertical, all on the y axis; 3-rings, three circles of 16). Reproduced when every session of the dandiset has the configuration the Methods give for its date. Partially reproduced when the only mismatches are horizontal and vertical exchanged. Not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Monkey R performed 3577 ring trials over two sessions, 3699 horizontal over two, 4040 vertical over two, and 912 3-rings trials in one session.
claims.source: Materials and methods, Experimental design, paragraph 3
claims.quote: 36 for R (3577 over two sessions ... 3699 trials over two sessions for R ... 4040 trials over two sessions for R ... 912 trials from one session for R
claims.criterion: Sessions are grouped by the dates the Methods give. The count can be read as (a) successful center-out trials with a delay; (b) all center-out trials with a delay, successful or not; (c) successful center-out trials including those without a delay. Reproduced when all four counts are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when two or three are.

claims.statement: Monkey J contributed 6161 ring, 5017 horizontal, 6110 vertical and 7722 3-rings trials, over four sessions each.
claims.source: Materials and methods, Experimental design, paragraph 3
claims.quote: 24 targets for J (6161 trials over four sessions ... For horizontal configuration: 5017 trials over four sessions for J ... For vertical: 6110 trials over four sessions ... (7722 trials over four sessions for J

claims.statement: Delays were uniform from 300 to 700 ms for J and 400 to 900 ms for R, 10% of trials had no delay; average reaction time was 346 ms (J) and 311 ms (R), average reach time 582 ms (J) and 482 ms (R), and reaction time was negatively correlated with delay (p < 1e-4 for both).
claims.source: Materials and methods, Experimental design, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Delays were distributed uniformly from 300 to 700 ms for J and 400 to 900 ms for R ... The average reach time of successful trials was J: 582 ms, R: 482 ms and the average reaction time was J: 346 ms, R: 311 ms. Also, the reaction time was negatively correlated
claims.criterion: Successful center-out trials. Delays of delayed trials must lie in the stated range widened by 10% of each bound (J 270 to 770 ms, R 360 to 990 ms), and the no-delay fraction of successful center-out trials must be within 9 to 11%. Reaction time as fixed above. Reach time can be read as (a) first target acquisition after the go cue minus movement onset, or (b) first acquisition minus the go cue. Pearson correlation of reaction time with delay over delayed trials, per monkey. Reproduced when the delays, the four times (under one reading) and the negative correlations at p < 1e-4 all hold; partially reproduced when some do.

claims.statement: Of the 96 PMd electrodes, 74 for J and 80 for R had activity significantly correlated with the x and y location of the target (p < .05, Bonferroni over 96).
claims.source: Materials and methods, Neural recording and signal preprocessing, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Of the 96 electrodes, we found that 74 for J and 80 for R had significant correlation (p < .05, with Bonferroni correction where n = 96) with the task
claims.criterion: For each channel, an ordinary least-squares regression of its delay activity on target x and y over all analysed trials of the monkey, F-test p < 0.05/96. Reproduced when both counts are within tolerance; partially reproduced when one is. Counts per session and on the array the file labels PMd are shown as variants.

claims.statement: The top six PCs of the condition-averaged delay activity explain cumulatively 58, 82, 88, 92, 94 and 95% of the variance for J (120 conditions) and 81, 89, 92, 94, 95 and 96% for R (132 conditions).
claims.source: Materials and methods, Dimensionality reduction, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The top 6 PCs explained the following cumulative percentages of the variance: 58% 82% 88% 92% 94% 95% (J); 81% 89% 92% 94% 95% 96% (R)
claims.criterion: Reproduced when all values are within tolerance. Partially reproduced when those of R (complete data) are and those of J (5 of 16 sessions, 96 of 120 conditions) are not.

claims.statement: The spatial plane captures a large part of the variance of the condition-averaged activity for the ring, horizontal, vertical and 3-rings tasks; 66.8, 64.4, 47.7 and 68.2% for J and 33.7, 30.7, 31.0 and 30.1% for R (p < 1e-4).
claims.source: Results, Structure of neural activity during delay period, paragraph 2; Figure 2a
claims.quote: The spatial plane captures a large percentage of the overall variance of the trial-averaged neural responses for the ring, horizontal, vertical, and 3-rings tasks: 66.8%, 64.4%, 47.7%, and 68.2% (monkey J), 33.7%, 30.7%, 31.0%, 30.1% (monkey R)
claims.criterion: For each task, the variance of its condition averages (centred within the task) that lies in the plane (orthonormalised), as a share of (a) their total variance over all PMd channels, or (b) their variance within the top PCs. R's horizontal and vertical tasks are taken (a) by the dates of the Methods, or (b) by the target geometry in the files. J horizontal is not in the dandiset. Reproduced when, under one pairing of readings, all R values and all J values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when all R values are, or when at least four of the seven are. The p-value is compared with planes fit to target positions shuffled across conditions (1000 shuffles).

claims.statement: After target onset the neural state in the spatial plane starts at the center, diverges after 50 ms (R 75 ms) and converges to the steady delay state after 300 ms (R 400 ms).
claims.source: Results, Structure of neural activity during delay period, paragraph 2; Figure 2c
claims.quote: at target onset, the neural states projected onto this plane start at the center of this plane, start to diverge after 50 ms (R: 75 ms), and converge to the steady neural states after J: 300 ms, R: 400ms
claims.criterion: Tolerance of 50 ms because the times are round values read from a figure and the thresholds are chosen here. Delay activity in 20 ms bins aligned on target onset, smoothed with a 3-bin boxcar, projected onto the plane; condition averages at each time use trials whose go cue comes after the bin. d(t) is the mean over conditions of the distance of the condition's state from its converged delay state (the 200 ms before the go cue). With d0 the mean of d over the 100 ms before target onset and dmin its minimum after onset, D(t) = (d(t) - dmin) / (d0 - dmin). Divergence is the first bin after onset with D below 0.9, convergence the first with D below 0.1. Reproduced when all four times are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the times of one monkey are, or both divergence times are.

claims.statement: On single trials, on-axis and off-axis deviations of the neural state in the spatial plane are positively correlated with the on-axis and off-axis deviations of the hand position at maximum speed (on-axis p = 1e-3 J, 4e-3 R; off-axis p = 4e-4 J, 2e-4 R).
claims.source: Results, Structure of neural activity during delay period, paragraph 3; Figure 2d
claims.quote: Both on-axis ... and off-axis ... deviations in the neural state were positively correlated with on-axis and off-axis deviations in the position of max-speed for both monkeys
claims.criterion: Deviations are from the condition mean, of the plane coordinates and of the hand position at maximum speed, each split along the target direction and its normal. Pearson correlation of neural with kinematic deviation, separately on and off axis, per monkey, over (a) all tasks pooled, or (b) the 3-rings task alone. Reproduced when under one reading all four correlations are positive with two-sided p < 0.05; partially reproduced when two or three are.

claims.statement: The speed axis of delay activity varies with maximum speed for reaches to the same target distance, for 11 of 12 distances in J and 11 of 12 in R (p < 0.05), so it encodes speed independently of distance.
claims.source: Results, Structure of neural activity during delay period, paragraph 4; Figure 2e and 2f
claims.quote: We then tested whether the neural state in this dimension varied with speed for reaches to the same target, and found that for almost all distances it did (J: 11/12 distances in the vertical and horizontal tasks, R: 11/12, p < 0.05)
claims.criterion: Horizontal and vertical trials, grouped by target distance (1 to 12 cm, both sides and both tasks together). Per distance, Pearson correlation of the speed-axis projection with maximum speed, counted when positive with p < 0.05. The axis is fit (a) on all trials of all tasks, or (b) on the horizontal and vertical trials. Reproduced when both counts are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when one is. Projections cross-validated in 10 folds are shown as a variant. J has only vertical sessions here.

claims.statement: After regressing out speed from the neural activity, a positive correlation with target distance remains (p < 1e-4 for J and R).
claims.source: Results, Structure of neural activity during delay period, paragraph 4
claims.quote: we found that after regressing out speed from the neural activity, there is still a positive correlation
claims.criterion: Each channel's delay activity is regressed on maximum speed and the residuals kept. A linear regression from the residuals to target distance, over all trials of all tasks, is cross-validated in 10 folds (fixed seed); the Pearson correlation of the out-of-fold predictions with distance must be positive with p < 1e-4 in both monkeys for reproduced, in one for partially reproduced. The in-sample fit is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Projected onto the top PCs, the distance dimension is about half as large as the speed dimension.
claims.source: Results, Structure of neural activity during delay period, paragraph 4
claims.quote: when projecting the speed and distance dimensions onto the top PCs, the distance projection is approximately half compared to the projection of the speed dimension
claims.criterion: Tolerance of 20% as the paper says "approximately half". The speed axis as above; the distance axis is the regression of target distance on the speed-residualised activity (all trials). Each axis is normalised to unit length and projected onto the top PCs (6 J, 5 R); the ratio is the norm of the distance projection over that of the speed projection. Reproduced when both ratios are within tolerance; partially reproduced when one is.

claims.statement: Across all single trials the speed dimension explains 2% (J) and 1% (R) of the variance of the neural state, and the spatial plane 20% (J) and 10% (R).
claims.source: Results, Structure of neural activity during delay period, paragraph 4
claims.quote: This dimension explains J: 2%, R: 1% of the variance in the neural state across all trials; for reference, the spatial plane explains J: 20%, R: 10% for single trials
claims.criterion: The speed values are whole percentages, so the tolerance is the rounding interval (0.5 point), larger than 10%. Variance of the single-trial delay activity (centred over trials, all PMd channels) along the unit speed axis, and in the orthonormalised plane, as a share of the total. Reproduced when all four are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the values of one monkey are, or both plane values or both speed values are.

claims.statement: The distributions of single-trial neural states for each condition are elliptical, and for most conditions their major axis points along the direction of the mean neural state from the origin.
claims.source: Results, Neural state variability during delay, paragraph 2; Figure 3a and 3c
claims.quote: we found that the ellipses for most conditions were oriented in the direction of the mean neural state from the origin
claims.criterion: For each condition with at least 10 trials, the first PC of its trials in the plane; the axial angle (0 to 90 degrees) between it and the direction of the condition mean from the origin. Reproduced when, in each monkey, more than half of the conditions have an angle below 45 degrees and a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of the angles against 45 degrees has p < 0.05; partially reproduced when that holds in one monkey.

claims.statement: The mean absolute on-axis (distance) deviation of the neural state is larger than the off-axis (direction) deviation, in each task (J p = 9e-7 ring, 4e-7 horizontal, 1e-8 vertical, 3e-14 3-rings; R 8e-3, 4e-7, 2e-7 and 0.19).
claims.source: Results, Neural state variability during delay, paragraph 2; Figure 3
claims.quote: The mean absolute on-axis deviation for each target and for each monkey was systematically greater than the mean absolute off-axis deviations in the tasks
claims.criterion: Per target, the mean absolute on-axis and off-axis deviation from the condition mean in the plane. The test can be read as (a) a paired t-test over targets, (b) a Welch t-test over targets, or (c) a Welch t-test over trials. Six task and monkey pairs where the paper reports p < 0.05 are in the dandiset (J ring, vertical, 3-rings; R ring, horizontal, vertical; R tasks by the Methods' dates). Reproduced when on-axis exceeds off-axis with p < 0.05 in all six under one reading; partially reproduced when in three to five. R 3-rings is reported.

claims.statement: Relative deviations of the neural state (deviation as a fraction of reach distance), on and off axis, decrease with reach distance.
claims.source: Results, Neural state variability during delay, paragraph 3; Figure 3b and 3d
claims.quote: we found that the relative deviations in both distance and direction in the neural state decreased as a function of reach distance
claims.criterion: All tasks pooled, per monkey. Spearman correlation between target distance and the trial's absolute on-axis (and off-axis) deviation divided by target distance. Reproduced when all four correlations are negative with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when two or three are.

claims.statement: Direction classification of the ring targets reaches 32.2% for J (24 targets) and 16% for R (36 targets); distance classification over 12 targets reaches 18.9% (J) and 21.4% (R).
claims.source: Results, Accuracy of endpoint prediction from delay activity, paragraph 2; Figure 4a and 4b
claims.quote: direction was J:32.2% ± 0.6% accuracy for 24 targets (R:16% ±.5% for 36 targets) while distance classification for only 12 targets was lower for J (18.9% ±.1%) and comparable for R (21.4% ±.2% for R)
claims.criterion: The paper's SEMs (0.1 to 0.6%) are the spread over folds of one cross-validation, not the uncertainty of a repeat with other trials or with the paper's unreported hyperparameters, so the tolerance is 10%. SVM as fixed above. Distance is classified separately on each side (12 targets) of each of the horizontal and vertical tasks, and the accuracies are averaged weighted by trials. Reproduced when all four are within tolerance; partially reproduced when two or three are, or when only the R values are.

claims.statement: Classifying the 16 directions of each ring of the 3-rings task separately, accuracy increases with ring distance; 23, 36 and 43% for J and 22, 28 and 29% for R.
claims.source: Results, Accuracy of endpoint prediction from delay activity, paragraph 2; Figure 4c
claims.quote: when classifying targets in 3-rings separately for each distance, accuracy increases with ring distance (23%, 36%, 43% for J; 22%, 28%, 29% for R)
claims.criterion: Reproduced when all six values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the accuracy increases from the 4 cm to the 12 cm ring in both monkeys but some values are outside tolerance; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Angular errors of direction classification decrease with ring distance, but errors measured as arc length are not significantly different between rings (F test, p > .05 for J and R).
claims.source: Results, Accuracy of endpoint prediction from delay activity, paragraph 3; Figure 4c and 4d
claims.quote: When presenting the decoding accuracy in term of angular error, mean error decreases as a function target distance (Fig 4c). In contrast, when presenting the errors as arc-length ... the arc-length error distributions are not significantly different
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's F test, read as a one-way ANOVA of the per-trial arc-length errors (angle error in radians times ring radius, 0 for correct trials) across the three rings, per monkey. Reproduced when p > 0.05 in both monkeys and the mean angular error decreases from the 4 cm to the 12 cm ring in both; not reproduced when the ANOVA finds a difference (p < 0.05) in either. The test restricted to errors within the range of the 4 cm ring is shown as a variant, with the size of the differences.

claims.statement: Mean distance-classification error is slightly but significantly lower than the arc-length error of direction classification, and projecting the activity onto the spatial plane before classification raises it (J 2.64 to 3.03 cm; R given as 2.78 and 3.27 cm), to the level of the direction errors.
claims.source: Results, Accuracy of endpoint prediction from delay activity, paragraph 4; Figure 4d
claims.quote: we found that the mean classification error for distance classification was significantly (albeit only slightly) lower than the errors for directional classification ... The resulting classification error rate (Fig 4d, blue bars) is significantly greater than classification using the full dimensional neural activity
claims.criterion: The text gives R as "2.78 cm v.s. 3.27 cm" after J's "3.03 cm v.s. 2.64 cm" (projected first), so R can be read as (a) full 2.78 and projected 3.27, as the claim that projection raises the error implies, or (b) projected 2.78 and full 3.27. Distance errors are |true - predicted| in cm from the distance SVM. Reproduced when under one reading all four values are within tolerance and the projected error exceeds the full one by a Welch t-test over trials at p < 0.05 in both monkeys; partially reproduced when the increase holds in both but some values are outside tolerance, or when it holds in one monkey.

claims.statement: In the two-workspace experiment, the whole-arm model predicted neural activity better than the hand-only model for 238 of 288 neurons, with no significant difference for the other 50.
claims.source: Figure 4
claims.quote: Of the 288 neurons recorded across the 8 sessions, 238 were significantly better predicted by the whole-arm model than the hand-only model, and for the other 50, there was no significant difference

claims.statement: A whole-arm model trained on both workspaces explained as much neural variance as models trained within a single workspace.
claims.source: Figure 5
claims.quote: The symbols lying very close to the unity line in each panel of Figure 5 indicate that the full model explained just as much neural variance as did the individual models.

claims.statement: The whole-arm model predicted the shape of directional tuning curves in the two workspaces better than the hand-only model for 138 of 288 neurons, and worse for 2.
claims.source: Figure 6
claims.quote: Only two out of 288 neurons were significantly better predicted by the hand-only model (using p < 0.05), while 138 of 288 neurons were significantly better predicted by the whole-arm model.

claims.statement: The whole-arm model predicted the shifts of preferred direction between workspaces better than the hand-only model, with a circular variance accounted for of 0.75 against 0.57.
claims.source: Figure 7B
claims.quote: Figure 7B shows that the whole-arm model once again out-performed the hand-only model, with an average cVAF over all neurons of 0.75 compared to 0.57.

claims.statement: In the 120 ms after movement onset, average hand speed was similar in active reaches and passive bumps.
claims.source: Figure 8B
claims.quote: However, average movement speed was similar between active and passive trials in this 120 ms window, which we used for data analysis.

claims.statement: A linear discriminant classifier predicted whether a movement was active or passive 89% of the time from whole-arm kinematics in the analysis window.
claims.source: Results, Area 2 represents passive movements differently from active reaches, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Averaged over the sessions, a linear discriminant analysis (LDA) classifier could predict the movement type 89% of the time, using only the whole-arm kinematics in the analysis window

claims.statement: Many neurons had an above-chance separability index, the accuracy of a linear discriminant predicting the trial type from that neuron's firing.
claims.source: Figure 8E
claims.quote: we used LDA to classify movement type based on individual neurons, calling this prediction rate the neuron's 'separability index' (Figure 8E). We found that many neurons had an above chance separability index

claims.statement: In the active/passive experiment the whole-arm model again tended to out-perform the hand-only model, but for many more neurons than in the two-workspace experiment the difference was not significant.
claims.source: Figure 9
claims.quote: the whole-arm model again tended to out-perform the hand-only model (Filled circles above the dashed unity line in Figure 9). However, there were many more neurons (open circles) for which the difference between models was insignificant...

claims.statement: Unlike in the two-workspace experiment, many neurons had no consistent relationship with arm kinematics across active and passive movements, shown by negative pseudo-R2 for the model trained on both conditions.
claims.source: Figure 10
claims.quote: Surprisingly however, unlike our results from the two-workspace experiment (see Figure 5), many neurons in the active/passive task did not have this consistent relationship, indicated by the many neurons with negative pR2 values for the model trained over both conditions.

claims.statement: The consistency of the whole-arm model, its pseudo-R2 when trained on both conditions, correlated negatively with a neuron's separability index.
claims.source: Figure 11B
claims.quote: Interestingly, we found the opposite result—model consistency actually correlated negatively with the separability index.

claims.statement: The J-array dataset holds 146 single- and multi-unit isolations from two 96-electrode arrays, recorded on the maze task with 108 conditions, with a mean of 2166 trials per neuron.
claims.source: Results, Behavior and recordings, paragraph 1; Methods, Neural recordings and datasets
claims.quote: (27 and 108 conditions for ‘monkey J’ and ‘monkey J-array’ datasets) ... a pair of implanted 96-electrode arrays (J-array dataset, 146 single- and multi-unit isolations) ... High trial counts (mean trials/neuron = 311, 492, 388 and 2166 for monkey A, B, J, J-array)
claims.criterion: Counts from the dataset's units, conditions and trials. The trial count can be read as (a) all successful trials or (b) those kept by M1 (delay > 400 ms and the proto-trial selection); the Methods print 2155 where the Results print 2166, both within the tolerance. The condition count has tolerance 0 because it is a design count, not a measurement. Reproduced when all three are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: The single-electrode datasets hold 64, 74 and 172 single units for monkeys A, B and J, with means of 311, 492 and 388 trials per neuron.
claims.source: Results, Behavior and recordings, paragraph 1; Supplemental Experimental Procedures, Neural and EMG recordings
claims.quote: High trial counts (mean trials/neuron = 311, 492, 388 and 2166 for monkey A, B, J, J-array) ... A total of 310 single-electrode isolations (64, 74, and 172 single-unit isolations for monkeys A, B and J) were recorded from caudal PMd, surface M1 and sulcal M1.
claims.criterion: Testable only if the dataset holds the speed task or the single-electrode maze recordings. Reproduced when every count the dataset can give is within tolerance.

claims.statement: In the speed task one example neuron keeps its preparatory preference (reaches up and left) into the peri-movement epoch, with a preparatory to peri-movement tuning correlation of 0.72.
claims.source: Results, Neural responses during preparation and movement, paragraph 2; Figure 2B
claims.quote: This preference is shared between preparatory and peri-movement epochs. This agreement is not perfect (two green traces surpass the black trace) but the overall correlation is quite high ( r =0.72, see section on correlations below for details).
claims.criterion: Speed task only (monkey A or B); the paper does not name the neuron. Per neuron, the tuning correlation of claim fig4abc-mean-correlation-single-electrode. The paper gives no measure of "prefers reaches ending up and leftwards"; the Figure 2B legend shows the near distance and fast speed and shades traces by the rate 50 ms before the go cue. It is read as follows. Among those 7 conditions, the one with the highest rate 50 ms before the go cue has its target in the upper-left quadrant. Reproduced when at least one speed-task neuron has r within tolerance of 0.72 and that preference; blocked if the dataset holds no speed-task data.

claims.statement: Three other speed-task neurons with clear preparatory tuning do not keep their preferences into the peri-movement epoch; their preparatory and peri-movement tuning are negatively correlated, even for straight reaches at one distance and speed.
claims.source: Results, Neural responses during preparation and movement, paragraph 3; Figure 2C-E and legend
claims.quote: Despite clear preparatory tuning, preferences are not maintained between the preparatory and peri-movement epochs (color ordering differs between epochs). ... These neurons show negative correlations between preparatory and peri-movement tuning.
claims.criterion: Speed task only, neurons passing M6, tuning correlation as in M4. The paper does not say over which conditions the negative correlations of these neurons were computed. Readings (F1) the 7 far, fast conditions shown in the Figure 2C-E legend; (F2) all 28 conditions, as in Figure 4. Reproduced when at least three neurons have negative correlations under one reading; blocked if the dataset holds no speed-task data.

claims.statement: In the maze task some neurons keep similar tuning between the preparatory and peri-movement epochs, but most do not.
claims.source: Results, Neural responses during preparation and movement, paragraph 4; Figure 3
claims.quote: Some neurons maintained similar tuning between preparatory and peri-movement epochs (panel A ) but most did not.
claims.criterion: J-array (and J if present), neurons selected as for Figure 4 (M6, reading S1), tuning correlation as in M4. The paper sets no threshold for "similar tuning"; the one value it calls "quite high" is r = 0.72 (Figure 2B). Reproduced when at least one neuron has r of 0.72 or more and more than half of the neurons have r below 0.72.

claims.statement: In the J-array dataset the correlation between a neuron's preparatory and peri-movement tuning is positive on average but small (mean r = 0.13, p = 0.03; mean Spearman r = 0.11).
claims.source: Results, Correlations between preparatory and peri-movement tuning, paragraph 1; Figure 4D
