claims.source: Results, "ALM encodes upcoming sequences", paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 7b
claims.quote: Expert mice nevertheless usually initiated sequences from the correct side without exploring the other (Extended Data Fig. 7b)
claims.criterion: Standard trials of the 35 Figure 3 sessions. A trial is initiated without exploring when no lick before the first touch has theta_shoot on the other side of the midline from the lick that made the first touch. Reproduced when the fraction exceeds 0.5 in every mouse; partially when it does in most mice; not reproduced otherwise. A 5 degree margin around the midline is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Inhibiting S1TJ increased the across-trial variability of lick angle, SD(theta_shoot), without reducing the lateral reach |theta_shoot|, and did not shorten licks.
claims.source: Figure 2b; Extended Data Fig. 3j; Results, "Optogenetic inhibition screen", paragraph 2
claims.quote: SD(Θshoot) increased significantly compared with no inhibition (Fig. 2b, left). Despite disorganized targeting, the ability to direct licks to the sides (i.e. |Θshoot|) was uncompromised ... Inhibiting S1TJ also did not shorten the length of licks
claims.criterion: Needs the inhibited region of each opto session.

claims.statement: Inhibiting ALM/M1TJ reduced the ability to direct licks to the sides and decreased lick length; inhibiting M1B only slightly increased angle variability; inhibiting S1BF or S1Tr changed nothing.
claims.source: Figure 2b; Extended Data Fig. 3j; Results, "Optogenetic inhibition screen", paragraph 3
claims.quote: when inhibiting ALM/M1TJ, mice had reduced ability to direct licks to the sides ... and showed decreased length of lick (Fig. 2b, right). Inhibiting M1B caused only minor increases in lick angle variability ... Inhibiting S1BF or S1Tr changed no aspects of lick control.
claims.criterion: Needs the inhibited region of each opto session.

claims.statement: Inhibiting ALM/M1TJ at sequence initiation strongly suppressed licking (licks largely absent in 4 of 7 mice), and less strongly at mid-sequence.
claims.source: Figure 2c; Extended Data Fig. 3k; Results, "Optogenetic inhibition screen", paragraph 4
claims.quote: inhibiting ALM/M1TJ at sequence initiation strongly suppressed production of licking sequences (Fig. 2c, left; Supplementary Video 4). In 4 of 7 mice, licks were largely absent ... When applied at mid-sequence, ALM/M1TJ inhibition also suppressed the production of licks, although less strongly.
claims.criterion: Needs the inhibited region of each opto session.

claims.statement: Inhibiting S1TJ or M1B at water consumption impaired the stopping of ongoing licking.
claims.source: Figure 2c; Extended Data Fig. 3k; Results, "Optogenetic inhibition screen", paragraph 5
claims.quote: when inhibiting S1TJ or M1B at water consumption, mice were impaired at stopping ongoing sequences (Fig. 2c, right; Extended Data Fig. 3k, bottom row; example in Supplementary Video 5).
claims.criterion: Needs the inhibited region of each opto session.

claims.statement: With half the illumination power (2 mW) the effects were consistent with, though weaker than, those at 4 mW, and the termination deficit of S1TJ and M1B inhibition was similarly strong.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 3l,m; Results, "Optogenetic inhibition screen", paragraph 6
claims.quote: Effects of ALM/M1TJ inhibition ... remained largely consistent with, though weaker than, our previous results using higher power (4 mW). At consumption, inhibiting S1TJ or M1B resulted in similarly strong deficits in terminating ongoing sequences
claims.criterion: Needs the inhibited region of each opto session.

claims.statement: At 4 mW, light within 1 mm reduced the spike rate of putative pyramidal cells by 91%, at about 1.5 mm by 61% and at about 3 mm by 19%; FS neurons within 1 mm increased by 739%.
claims.source: Methods, "Photostimulation", paragraph 4; Extended Data Fig. 3c-f
claims.quote: light within 1 mm distance reduced mean spike rate of putative pyramidal cells (Extended Data Fig. 3c-e) by 91%, light at ~1.5 mm away by 61%, and ~3 mm away by 19% ... light shined within 1 mm increased the mean spike rate of FS neurons by 739%
claims.criterion: Needs the spike waveform widths (pyramidal against FS) and the distance of the fibre from the recording site in each efficiency session.

claims.statement: Hearing loss with earplugs did not increase missed licks during sequences.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 1i; Results, first section, paragraph 3; Methods, "Hearing loss"
claims.quote: Control experiments (Methods) showed that mice did not rely on auditory (Extended Data Fig. 1i) or olfactory (Extended Data Fig. 1j) cues
claims.criterion: Needs which of the two sessions of each mouse had earplugs.

claims.statement: Masking odours with an air flow did not change missed licks.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 1j; Results, first section, paragraph 3; Methods, "Odor masking"
claims.quote: Control experiments (Methods) showed that mice did not rely on auditory (Extended Data Fig. 1i) or olfactory (Extended Data Fig. 1j) cues
claims.criterion: Needs which part of each session had the air flow on.

claims.statement: Numbing the tongue with lidocaine increased missed licks, so mice require tactile feedback from the tongue.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 1k; Results, first section, paragraph 3; Methods, "Tongue numbing"
claims.quote: Control experiments (Methods) showed that mice ... did require tactile feedback from the tongue (Extended Data Fig. 1k).
claims.criterion: Needs which session of each mouse was lidocaine and which saline.

claims.statement: The maximal force of a lick was on average about 4 mN.
claims.source: Methods, "Two-axis optical force sensors", paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 1f
claims.quote: In contrast, the maximal force of a lick was on average about 4 mN (Extended Data Fig. 1f).
claims.criterion: Needs the calibration from sensor voltage to force.

claims.statement: Clustering the PETHs of all neurons by NNMF was most consistent with 13 clusters.
claims.source: Methods, "PETH and NNMF clustering", paragraph 5; Extended Data Fig. 4j,k
claims.quote: We ran this method with the number of clusters set to each value from 6 to 20, and found that 13 clusters achieved the best consistency (Extended Data Fig. 4j)
claims.criterion: Needs how cluster labels are matched across bootstrap iterations, which the Methods do not give.

claims.statement: In the Neuropixels data, 18 of 1,804 V1 RS units respond exclusively to the grating patch at the center position (the illusory gap region) of the receptive field mapping block.
claims.source: Methods, Definition of functional subsets of neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 1e legend
claims.quote: In the Neuropixels data, there were n = 18 exclusively center-responsive neurons of 1,804 V1 RS units
claims.criterion: V1 RS units as in the opening comment. Per RF trial (one presentation of the four directions, 1 s), the mean rate from 0 to 1000 ms after onset (code, postprocessnwb_v240130.m, every fourth row of the RFCI table), standard (not inverse) patches only. The Methods test each position against gray-screen trials with a Wilcoxon rank-sum test, Bonferroni-Holm corrected, and keep units significant at the center only. The RF block has no gray-screen trials (0 s ITI), so what forms the gray-screen sample is open. Readings, (a) the code (analyzeRFCI.m, RFsigexclclassic with RFindclassic = center), a Wilcoxon signed-rank test of each position's trial rates against the unit's mean rate in the longest spontaneous block, the position of largest mean response being the center and the only one significant after the Holm step; (b) the Methods, a rank-sum test of each position's trial rates against rates in 1 s windows tiled over the longest spontaneous (gray screen) block, Holm corrected over the 9 positions, center the only significant position. Reproduced when, under one reading, both counts are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Of the exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units, 66.7% respond substantially to the IC image and 77.8% to the real-edge (IRE) image of their preferred IRE orientation, although the IC image has no contrast in their receptive field.
claims.source: Figure 1f legend; Results, Mouse V1 neurons respond to ICs despite the absence of contrast within their receptive fields, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Bottom, individual neurons with substantially I C -responsive (left; 66.7%) and I RE -responsive (right; 77.8%) neurons marked in magenta on the y axis
claims.criterion: Units of fig1e-npx-exclusive-center. Preferred IRE orientation is the IRE image with the strongest mean IC response (Results, paragraph 2); the IC image is the one with the illusory bar of that orientation. Neither the Methods nor the code read fixes the test for "substantially responsive" or the block. Readings, test (a) the code's analyzeStaticICtxi.m, Kruskal-Wallis across blank, IC and IRE of that orientation at p < 0.05 with Tukey-Kramer comparison against blank at p < 0.05 and mean above blank (sigmcBICREl1/2); (b) a rank-sum test of those trials against blank trials at p < 0.05 with AUROC > 0.5. Block (i) ICwcfg1 only, two orientations (135 and 45 degrees); (ii) ICwcfg1 and ICwcfg0 together, four orientations. Reproduced when, under one combination, both fractions are within tolerance.

claims.statement: For IRE-responsive exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units, the preferred orientation of the illusory bar matches that of the real bar in 78.6% of units.
claims.source: Figure 1g legend; Results, Mouse V1 neurons respond to ICs despite the absence of contrast within their receptive fields, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Comparison of the preferred orientation between illusory bars (I C stimuli) and real bars (I RE stimuli) for I RE -responsive and exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units, showing a 78.6% match
claims.criterion: Preferred IC (IRE) orientation is that of the IC (IRE) image with the strongest mean IC response (Results, paragraph 2), among the IRE-responsive units of fig1f under the same readings. Reproduced when, under the reading that reproduces fig1f, the match is within tolerance; the fraction is reported for every reading.

claims.statement: The Neuropixels sessions hold 150 +/- 20 V1 RS units and 597 +/- 46 higher visual area RS units per session (mean +/- s.e.m., 12 sessions).
claims.source: Results, A subpopulation of V1 neurons respond to ICs but not to its inducing segments, paragraph 4
claims.quote: 12 sessions from 12 mice; mean ± s.e.m. = 150 ± 20 V1 RS units and 597 ± 46 higher visual area RS units across sessions
claims.criterion: RS units and areas as in the opening comment, with no further quality filter (the code computes an ISI, amplitude cutoff and presence ratio filter and does not apply it). Tolerances are the paper's s.e.m.

claims.statement: Across the ICwcfg0 and ICwcfg1 blocks, 159 of 1,804 V1 RS units are IC-encoders.
claims.source: Methods, Definition of functional subsets of neurons, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Across ICwcfg0 and ICwcfg1, 159 of 1,804 V1 RS units were identified as IC-encoders in the Neuropixels dataset
claims.criterion: IC-encoder and IC response as in the opening comment, in each block separately with that block's IC1 and IC2 images. "Across" is open. Readings, (a) units that are IC-encoders in at least one of the two blocks; (b) the sum of the two blocks' counts. Reproduced when the count is within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: The Neuropixels data hold 87 V1 IC-encoders and 636 V1 segment responders (the sets whose layer distribution Extended Data Fig. 6b shows).
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 6b legend
claims.quote: For the Neuropixels dataset, proportion of V1 IC-encoders (left, n = 87) and V1 segment responders (right, n = 636) in each layer
claims.criterion: IC-encoder and segment responder as in the opening comment (segment responders the union over BR, BL, TL, TR). Which units and block are open (Fig. 2d gives 79 and 526, the Methods 159 across two blocks). Readings, (a) RS units, block ICwcfg1; (b) all units not classified as noise, block ICwcfg1; (c) RS units, union of ICwcfg1 and ICwcfg0. Reproduced when both counts are within tolerance under one reading. The layer proportions are shown, with no value to match.

claims.statement: V1 IC-encoders (n = 79) are more likely than V1 segment responders (n = 526) to receive putative excitatory connections from higher visual areas, by cross-correlogram analysis.
claims.source: Figure 2d legend; Results, A subpopulation of V1 neurons respond to ICs but not to its inducing segments, paragraph 4
claims.quote: V1 IC-encoders ( n = 79) are substantially more likely than V1 segment responders ( n = 526) to receive putative excitatory connections from higher visual areas (LM, RL, AL, PM and AM)
claims.criterion: Methods, Cross-correlogram analysis. Spike trains of cortical RS units over the ICwcfg1 block in 1 ms bins; CCG(tau) = sum over t of x1(t) x2(t + tau) divided by the square root of the two spike counts, tau up to +/- 100 ms (code analyze_CCGfftlong.m); the CCG of the same trains smoothed with a 25 ms window is subtracted; a putative excitatory connection from an HVA unit to a V1 unit when the corrected CCG peak in the 1 to 10 ms window with the HVA unit leading exceeds 7 times the SD of the CCG flank (50 to 100 ms from zero). Groups as in the opening comment, in ICwcfg1 (larger repository, aggregate_ctxqcCCGfftlong.m lines 285 to 287). Open details, each could change the outcome. Smoothing window shape, (a) a 25-bin boxcar, (b) a Gaussian kernel 25 ms long with s.d. 5 ms, the kernel the paper uses for PSTHs (Extended Data Fig. 4b legend). Flank SD taken from (i) the uncorrected CCG (larger repository, line 77), (ii) the corrected CCG. Per V1 unit measure, (x) the fraction of the session's HVA RS units with a connection to it (larger repository, Pin_flank.HVA), (y) the number of such units. Reproduced when, under every combination, IC-encoders have the higher median and a two-sided rank-sum test gives p < 0.05; not reproduced when none does; when the readings differ the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified with all results shown. Group sizes are compared with the expected counts.

claims.statement: A linear SVM decodes the four images IC1, LC1, LC2 and IC2 from V1 activity in the Neuropixels data with tenfold cross-validation accuracy above the chance of 0.25.
claims.source: Figure 3a; Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 3
claims.quote: The tenfold cross-validation performance was substantially above chance, indicating that neural activity patterns evoked by these four images were highly distinct at the multivariate level
claims.criterion: The decoder of the opening comment on V1 RS units, sessions with >= 50 of them. The paper reports no test for Fig. 3a; the code tests the per-session accuracy against 0.25 with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test (aggregateICtxi_SVM_trainICRC_areas.m line 147). Reproduced when the mean accuracy exceeds 0.25 with that test at p < 0.05 under both decoder readings. Accuracy for the other five areas is reported.

claims.statement: In Neuropixels V1, TRE trials are decoded as the matching IC image more often than as the matching LC image (0.51 against 0.22), so IC inference is represented in V1.
claims.source: Figure 3c; Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Applying inference decoding to Neuropixels V1 recordings revealed that T RE was substantially more likely to be decoded as I C than as L C (Fig. 3c ; decoding probability for I C vs. L C was 0.51 vs. 0.22, P < 0.05 Wilcoxon signed-rank test)
claims.criterion: The decoder and inference score of the opening comment on V1 RS units. The IC value is the mean of P(TRE1->IC1) and P(TRE2->IC2), the LC value the mean of P(TRE1->LC1) and P(TRE2->LC2), each averaged over sessions. Reproduced when, under a decoder reading, both values are within tolerance and the signed-rank test of IC against LC gives p < 0.05 with IC higher; partially reproduced when the test holds and a value is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: In the Neuropixels data almost every visual area decodes TRE as IC more than as LC, significantly in V1, LM, RL, AL and PM and not in AM, with V1, LM and AL the strongest.
claims.source: Figure 3d legend; Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 5
claims.quote: In the Neuropixels dataset, almost every visual area was substantially biased toward decoding T RE as I C than L C , with V1, LM and AL showing the strongest representations of the IC
claims.criterion: The decoder and inference score of the opening comment per area, sessions with >= 50 RS units in the area (the paper keeps 12, 8, 11, 10, 12, 11 sessions for V1, LM, RL, AL, PM, AM; the counts found are reported). "Strongest" is open, readings (a) the three largest mean inference scores, (b) the three smallest p-values. Reproduced when at least five areas give p < 0.05 with IC above LC and V1, LM and AL are the strongest three under reading (a) or (b); partially reproduced when three or four areas are significant, or when five are and the ranking fails under both readings; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: No higher visual area shows a substantially larger inference performance than V1, although decoding accuracy and inference scores differ across areas.
claims.source: Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 9; Extended Data Fig. 7a and 7c legends
claims.quote: Notably, none of the higher visual areas showed a substantially larger inference performance compared to V1 (Extended Data Fig. 7a,c )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Per-session TRE inference scores (fig3d) and XRE inference scores (ed7b) per area. The paper's test is a Kruskal-Wallis across areas followed by pairwise comparisons it does not name. Readings, (a) two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank of V1 against each HVA over sessions with both, the pairwise test the code uses between areas (plot_SVM_trainICRC_areas.m line 245); (b) Tukey-Kramer comparisons after the Kruskal-Wallis (MATLAB multcompare default). Reproduced when no HVA has a significantly larger score than V1 (p < 0.05) for either score; not reproduced when one does. Extended Data Fig. 7c is said to show the data of panel b, which mixes the Neuropixels and 2p areas; its Kruskal-Wallis values are compared on the six Neuropixels areas and the reading is a deviation. The Kruskal-Wallis p-values found are reported against the paper's.

claims.statement: Decoders trained on the XRE real-bar images classify IC1 and IC2 trials as the XRE image whose real bar matches the illusory bar, above chance in all six Neuropixels areas.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 7b legend; Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 7
claims.quote: As with T RE inference decoding (Fig. 2 ), layer 2/3 of V1 and LM consistently show high inference scores (*p < 0.05, Wilcoxon signed-rank test compared to chance of 0.5
claims.criterion: The decoder of the opening comment trained on XRE1 against XRE2 trials (codes 1201, 1299) of ICwcfg1, probed with IC1 and IC2 trials (code svmdesc trainREx); XRE inference score (P(IC1->XRE1) + P(IC2->XRE2))/2 (Extended Data Fig. 7b legend) per session and area, sessions with >= 50 RS units. Reproduced when the score is above 0.5 with a signed-rank p < 0.05 in all six areas; partially reproduced in four or five; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: In the Neuropixels data, IC images do not evoke larger population average responses than LC images in any area, averaged over all units or over visually responsive units.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 6e and 6f legends
claims.quote: I C images do not evoke greater responses than L C images (*p < 0.05 one-tailed Wilcoxon signed-rank test for testing I C > L C ; note that none of the visual areas showed significance)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, on the paper's test. Same sessions as fig3d (>= 50 RS units in the area); ICwcfg1; per session, the IC response averaged over (e) all RS units of the area, (f) visually responsive RS units (Kruskal-Wallis across blank, IC1, LC1, LC2, IC2 at p < 0.05, Extended Data Fig. 6d legend), on IC trials (IC1 and IC2 pooled) and on LC trials (LC1 and LC2 pooled); one-tailed signed-rank test of IC > LC across sessions. Reproduced when no area gives p < 0.05 in either panel; not reproduced when any does. The mean IC minus LC difference per area is reported.

claims.statement: Limiting the Neuropixels analysis to fixed-gaze trials (pupil within 8 degrees of its modal position) leaves 11 exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units, and their responses to ICs and orientation match do not change the conclusion.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 2b to 2e legends; Results, Mouse V1 neurons respond to ICs despite the absence of contrast within their receptive fields, paragraph 3
claims.quote: When analyzing only fixed-gaze trials, there were n = 11 exclusively center-responsive V1 RS units; 10 sessions had eye tracking data and of these, 9 sessions had a valid receptive field mapping block where the fixed-gaze constraint left at least one trial in each position
claims.criterion: Fixed-gaze trials per the Methods (Eye tracking analysis), pupil position within 8 visual degrees of the modal pupil position throughout the trial. The code (analyzeMouseEye.m) uses the NWB EyeTracking pupil fits, a threshold of 20 camera pixels (its stand-in for 8 degrees) on the maximum distance from the mode during the trial, and drops likely blinks. The paper gives no pixel to degree conversion, so the threshold is open. Readings, (a) 8 visual degrees, when the dataset gives pupil or gaze position in degrees; (b) the code's 20 camera pixels. Then fig1e, fig1f and fig1g are repeated on fixed-gaze trials only, in the sessions whose fixed-gaze RF trials cover all 9 positions. Session counts must match exactly. The paper shows the match against a shuffle null (Extended Data Fig. 2e) and gives no threshold for it; the 95th percentile of 1,000 shuffles of the preferred IC orientations among those units is a standard choice, recorded as a deviation, and the match fraction is also compared with the 78.6% of fig1g. Reproduced when the unit count is within tolerance and the match exceeds that percentile; partially reproduced when one holds.

claims.statement: Receptive field positions mapped with fixed-gaze trials match those mapped with all trials for 81% of the 398 V1 RS units with significant receptive fields.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 2f legend
claims.quote: Match proportion is 0.81 among 398 V1 RS units with significant receptive fields (p < 0.05 Kruskal-Wallis test across responses to 9 positions in the receptive field mapping block)
claims.criterion: RF position is the position of largest mean RF-trial response (code analyzeRFCI.m, RFindclassic); significant receptive field when the Kruskal-Wallis across the 9 positions gives p < 0.05 (legend). Fixed-gaze trials as in ed2b, sessions with eye tracking. Open, which mapping must be significant. Readings, (a) significant with all trials; (b) significant with fixed-gaze trials; (c) both. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Pupil area during the presentation does not differ across the images of the IC block.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 2g legend
claims.quote: Pupil area, z-scored across each recording session, during visual presentation of various images in the IC block (n = 10 sessions with eye tracking data; p = 0.7220 Friedman test)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, on the paper's test. Pupil area from the NWB pupil fits, z-scored over the session; per trial its mean over the 0 to 0.4 s presentation (the code's aggregateMouseEye.m also computes the end and maximum value; the mean is used, the others shown); per session and image the mean over trials; a Friedman test with sessions as blocks. Open, which images. Readings, (a) IC1, LC1, LC2, IC2 of ICwcfg1, the images the code compares; (b) all 22 images of ICwcfg1. Reproduced when p >= 0.05 under the readings; when they differ, blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Eye gaze is confined to a small region that fits within the illusory gap, with no systematic difference in pupil position among IC1, LC1, LC2 and IC2 presentations.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 2a legend; Results, A subpopulation of V1 neurons respond to ICs but not to its inducing segments, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Mouse eye gaze is confined to a small region that fits within the illusory gap region. There are no systematic differences in pupil position among I C1 vs. L C1 vs. L C2 vs. I C2 presentations
claims.criterion: The paper names no test and gives no pixel to degree conversion. Pupil center from the NWB pupil fits during the 0 to 0.4 s presentation of IC1, LC1, LC2, IC2 trials in ICwcfg1. A claim of absence with no test in the paper, so any test is a reader's choice and is recorded as a deviation. "No systematic differences" is read as no difference consistent across sessions, a Friedman test with sessions as blocks of the per-session image means of x and of y (the test the paper uses for pupil area, Extended Data Fig. 2g). Reproduced when neither gives p < 0.05. Per-session Kruskal-Wallis tests across the four images (10 sessions, two coordinates, many trials each) are shown as a variant and do not decide the outcome. The confinement part is reported as the extent of the 0.01 isoline of each session's 2D density in camera pixels, with no conversion to degrees.

claims.statement: Decoders of other kinds (quadratic and radial basis function SVMs, a fully connected neural network) give results highly consistent with the linear SVM.
claims.source: Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 8; Supplementary Fig. 3 (not read); Methods, Decoding analysis, paragraph 3
claims.quote: In addition, different types of decoders yielded highly consistent results (Supplementary Fig. 3 )
claims.criterion: Supplementary Fig. 3 was not available, so which dataset and areas it shows is not known. Methods, SVMs with linear, quadratic polynomial and RBF kernels, and an ANN (input layer of one node per unit, two hidden layers of 100 nodes, four softmax outputs, Adam, cross-entropy loss, 50,000 epochs), all with tenfold cross-validation. Tested on the Neuropixels areas, a reading recorded as a deviation. Reproduced when each decoder gives the same sign and significance (signed-rank p < 0.05) as the linear SVM for the TRE inference score in V1, LM and AL; partially reproduced when two of three agree.

claims.statement: In the 2p data, 310 of 18,576 V1L2/3 neurons are exclusively center-responsive; 21.3% of them respond to the IC and 43.2% to the IRE image, and preferred IC and IRE orientations match in 54.5%.
claims.source: Figure 1i to 1k legend; Methods, Definition of functional subsets of neurons, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Bottom, individual neurons with substantially I C -responsive (left; 21.3%) and I RE -responsive (right; 43.2%) neurons marked in magenta on the y axis. There was a 54.5% match
claims.criterion: 2p imaging, 29 sessions from five mice, not in this dandiset. Methods as in fig1e to fig1g on z-scored fluorescence averaged over the 1 s presentation, with the same open details.

claims.statement: About 4.3% of V1L2/3 neurons are IC-encoders (selective for one of the two IC images with no substantial response to either LC image), 8.5% over both white-circle configurations.
claims.source: Results, A subpopulation of V1 neurons respond to ICs but not to its inducing segments, paragraph 3; Methods, Definition of functional subsets of neurons, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Using these stimuli, we identified approximately 4.3% of neurons in V1L2/3 with selectivity for one of the two I C images, and no substantial responses to either L C image
claims.criterion: 2p imaging, not in this dandiset. IC-encoder as in the opening comment on z-scored fluorescence over the 1 s presentation.

claims.statement: V1L2/3 IC-encoders are tuned to the orientation of the illusory bar of their IC image, measured with single long bars, for white-circle and black-circle blocks alike.
claims.source: Figure 2c legend; Extended Data Fig. 5b legend
claims.quote: Indeed, IC-encoders in V1L2/3 were tuned to the orientation of the illusory bar in the I C image (I C1 -encoders were tuned to 135°, and I C2 -encoders were tuned to 45°)
claims.criterion: 2p imaging, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when the response to the single bar at the illusory bar's orientation exceeds that at the orthogonal orientation by a signed-rank test at p < 0.05 over IC-encoders.

claims.statement: IC-encoders' receptive fields are not biased toward the illusory gap region, while segment responders' receptive fields are biased toward the segments that define them.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 4c legend; Results, A subpopulation of V1 neurons respond to ICs but not to its inducing segments, paragraph 6
claims.quote: IC-encoders’ receptive fields are not biased toward the illusory gap region (n = 367/386 I C1 /I C2 -encoders in 24 sessions from 4 mice). On the contrary, segment responders’ receptive fields are biased toward the image segments that are used to define them
claims.criterion: 2p imaging, not in this dandiset. The paper names no test for panel c; Extended Data Fig. 4g, a different set of sessions (images scaled up 1.5 times, 10 sessions from 5 mice), compares with 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals of IC-responsive and LC-responsive neurons; that comparison is borrowed for panel c, and the borrowing and the two rules below are a reader's reading, recorded as a deviation. Reproduced when the IC-encoders' fraction with RF at the center is inside that interval and each segment responder group's most common RF position is its segment.

claims.statement: IC-encoders do not have larger receptive fields than other V1L2/3 neurons, by size tuning and by the number of grating patches they respond to.
claims.source: Results, A subpopulation of V1 neurons respond to ICs but not to its inducing segments, paragraph 6; Extended Data Fig. 5c and 5d legends
claims.quote: Furthermore, IC-encoders did not have substantially larger receptive fields compared to other neurons in V1L2/3
claims.criterion: 2p imaging, not in this dandiset. A claim of absence; the paper's comparison is the 95% bootstrapped confidence interval of the number of patches IC-encoders respond to against that of IC-responsive neurons (Extended Data Fig. 5d). Reproduced when the intervals overlap.

claims.statement: Inference decoding is significant in V1L2/3 and not in V1L4, so V1L2/3 is the lowest region of the visual hierarchy where IC inference is represented.
claims.source: Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 4; Figure 3e legend
claims.quote: Whereas V1L2/3 showed substantial inference decoding performance, V1L4 did not (Fig. 3e )
claims.criterion: 2p imaging, not in this dandiset. Decoder and inference score of the opening comment on z-scored fluorescence over the 1 s presentation. Reproduced when V1L2/3 gives p < 0.05 with IC above LC and V1L4 does not.

claims.statement: In the 2p mesoscope data, V1 and LM show significant IC inference, and RL, AL, PM and AM do not.
claims.source: Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 5; Figure 3e legend
claims.quote: Similarly, L2/3 of V1 and LM showed the strongest IC representation in the 2p mesoscope dataset (Fig. 3e )
claims.criterion: 2p mesoscope, not in this dandiset. As fig3e-2p-l23-not-l4, areas with >= 100 neurons. Reproduced when V1 and LM give p < 0.05 with IC above LC.

claims.statement: XRE inference decoding gives results consistent with TRE inference decoding in the 2p data, significant in V1L2/3, mesoscope V1, LM and RL and not in V1L4, AL, PM or AM.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 7b legend; Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 7
claims.quote: When applying X RE inference decoding to different visual areas, we found consistent results as T RE inference decoding
claims.criterion: 2p imaging, not in this dandiset. As ed7b-npx-xre-inference on the 2p sessions, areas with >= 100 neurons. Reproduced when V1L2/3, mesoscope V1, LM and RL give p < 0.05 above 0.5 and V1L4 does not.

claims.statement: Inference decoding indicates IC inference in V1L2/3 for white-circle and for black-circle (inverted) blocks alike.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5e legend; Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 8
claims.quote: We found that inference decoding indicated the representation of IC inference in V1L2/3 regardless of black–white inversion (Extended Data Fig. 5e )
claims.criterion: 2p imaging, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when both block types give p < 0.05 with IC above LC.

claims.statement: With IC block images scaled up 1.5 times, decoding accuracy is above chance and the TRE inference score above zero in V1L2/3.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 4h and 4i legend
claims.quote: Decoder performance for images scaled up by 1.5× (n = 10 sessions from 5 mice)
claims.criterion: 2p imaging, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when both tests give p < 0.05 in the stated direction.

claims.statement: V1L2/3 neurons with receptive fields in the gap respond to illusory bars with the orientation selectivity of real bars also with larger gaps, dense receptive field mapping and contrast bars.
claims.source: Results, Mouse V1 neurons respond to ICs despite the absence of contrast within their receptive fields, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 3 legend
claims.quote: We further verified the illusory bar responsiveness and orientation selectivity for exclusively center-responsive V1 neurons using larger illusory gap sizes (Extended Data Fig. 3a–d ), denser receptive field mappings (Extended Data Fig. 3e–h ) and contrast bars instead of outline bars
claims.criterion: 2p imaging, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when in each variant the IC-IRE orientation match exceeds the 95th percentile of shuffled matches (the null the legends show).

claims.statement: Zeroing out IC-encoders in the input of a trained V1L2/3 decoder abolishes the TRE inference performance, while zeroing out segment responders does not.
claims.source: Figure 4a legend; Results, Neurons that respond emergently to ICs mediate the representation of inference in V1, paragraphs 2 and 4
claims.quote: Indeed, this abolished the IC inference performance; T RE -responses were no longer biased toward being classified as I C compared to L C (Fig. 4a , right)
claims.criterion: 2p holography sessions (visual block), not in this dandiset. The legend gives the per-subset p-values in the figure's order without naming the subsets in text; read from the Results, the non-significant one (0.1228) is the IC-encoders-zeroed decoder. Reproduced when zeroing IC-encoders gives a TRE inference test p >= 0.05 and zeroing segment responders gives p < 0.05 with IC above LC.

claims.statement: A decoder trained only on IC-encoders (30 +/- 4 per session) shows high TRE inference performance, while one trained only on segment responders (69 +/- 8) does not, though both discriminate IC from LC images.
claims.source: Figure 4b legend; Results, Neurons that respond emergently to ICs mediate the representation of inference in V1, paragraphs 3 and 4
claims.quote: Despite training this decoder on the activity of drastically fewer cells, it showed high levels of IC inference performance (Fig. 4b , right)
claims.criterion: 2p holography sessions, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when the IC-encoder-only decoder's TRE inference test gives p < 0.05 with IC above LC, the segment-responder-only decoder's does not, and both decoders' cross-validation accuracy is above 0.25 at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Photoactivating IC-encoders evokes larger activity in nonphotoactivated IC-responsive neurons than in non-IC-responsive neurons, while photoactivating segment responders does not.
claims.source: Results, Neurons that encode IC inference drive neural pattern completion within V1, paragraph 4; Figure 5c; Extended Data Fig. 8b legend
claims.quote: Despite this heterogeneity, targeting IC-encoders evoked substantially larger activity in I C -responsive neurons compared to non-I C -responsive neurons during the photoactivation window
claims.criterion: 2p holography, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when the IC-encoder test gives p < 0.05 and the segment responder test does not.

claims.statement: Photoactivating a sparse ensemble of V1L2/3 excitatory neurons leads on average to a prolonged suppression of the nonphotoactivated population.
claims.source: Results, Neurons that encode IC inference drive neural pattern completion within V1, paragraph 4; Figure 5c
claims.quote: Consistent with prior reports, photoactivating a sparse ensemble of excitatory neurons in V1L2/3 led to a prolonged suppression of the nonphotoactivated population on average
claims.criterion: 2p holography, not in this dandiset. No test is reported; reproduced when the mean baseline-subtracted response of nonphotoactivated neurons after the photoactivation window is below zero.

claims.statement: Holographic activation of IC-encoders is decoded as the corresponding IC image, both from all neurons and from nonphotoactivated neurons only (median 0.372), in the absence of any visual stimulus.
claims.source: Figure 5d legend; Results, Neurons that encode IC inference drive neural pattern completion within V1, paragraph 6
claims.quote: Indeed, the decoder constructed with nonphotoactivated neurons was able to classify IC-encoder photoactivation trials as the corresponding I C image
claims.criterion: 2p holography, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when both tests give p < 0.05 above chance (0.25).

claims.statement: Holographic activation of segment responders is decoded as the corresponding IC image from all neurons, but not from nonphotoactivated neurons (median 0.228).
claims.source: Figure 5e legend; Results, Neurons that encode IC inference drive neural pattern completion within V1, paragraph 6
claims.quote: In contrast, photoactivating a similar number of segment responders did not evoke decodable activity patterns (Fig. 5e , right, and Extended Data Fig. 9c,d,g,h )
claims.criterion: 2p holography, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when the all-neuron test gives p < 0.05 and the nonphotoactivated test does not.

claims.statement: Decoding IC-encoder holography trials with a decoder trained on visual trials approaches the cross-validation accuracy on held-out visual trials (0.4029 against 0.4818), and the effect correlates with the number of targets.
claims.source: Results, Neurons that encode IC inference drive neural pattern completion within V1, paragraphs 6 and 7; Extended Data Fig. 9b
claims.quote: mean ± s.e.m. performance for decoding holography trials as visual image labels was 0.4029 ± 0.0296, whereas cross-validation accuracy was 0.4818 ± 0.0165
claims.criterion: 2p holography, not in this dandiset. Tolerances are the paper's s.e.m.; the Spearman correlation with target number is reproduced when positive at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: LC-encoders are less potent than IC-encoders at driving pattern completion, even when matched in visual information.
claims.source: Results, Neurons that encode IC inference drive neural pattern completion within V1, paragraph 8; Extended Data Fig. 10e and 10g legends
claims.quote: LC-encoders were substantially less potent at driving pattern completion of L C representations compared to IC-encoders
claims.criterion: 2p holography, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when both Kruskal-Wallis tests give p < 0.05 and IC-encoders exceed LC-encoders in the corrected rank-sum test.

claims.statement: On the 2p holographic mesoscope, photoactivating V1 IC-encoders is decoded as the corresponding image from all neurons, but not from nonphotoactivated neurons in higher visual areas.
claims.source: Figure 6d legend; Results, IC encoding is mediated by a looped circuit in the visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 4
claims.quote: In stark contrast to pattern completion effects within V1L2/3 (Fig. 5d,e , right), V1 segment responders, but not V1 IC-encoders, drove IC representation in higher visual areas
claims.criterion: 2p holographic mesoscope, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when the all-neuron test gives p < 0.05 and the higher visual area test does not.

claims.statement: On the 2p holographic mesoscope, photoactivating V1 segment responders drives IC representations in nonphotoactivated neurons of higher visual areas.
claims.source: Figure 6e legend; Results, IC encoding is mediated by a looped circuit in the visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 4
claims.quote: These data demonstrate that V1 segment responders drive feedforward communication of the bottom-up sensory information to higher visual areas
claims.criterion: 2p holographic mesoscope, not in this dandiset. Reproduced when both tests give p < 0.05 above chance.

claims.statement: IC-encoders are found in every visual area, in the Neuropixels and in the calcium imaging data.
claims.source: Results, Representation of IC inference across the mouse visual cortical hierarchy, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 6c and 6d legends
claims.quote: Using the same approach as above for V1, we could identify IC-encoders throughout these visual areas both in the electrophysiology and in the calcium imaging datasets
claims.criterion: Neuropixels part. IC-encoder as in the opening comment, block ICwcfg1, RS units of each area, sessions with >= 50 RS units in the area (Extended Data Fig. 6 legend). Per session and area, the proportion of IC-encoders among all RS units (panel c) and among visually responsive RS units (panel d, Kruskal-Wallis across blank, IC1, LC1, LC2, IC2 at p < 0.05). The paper gives no numbers for the proportions; they are reported. Reproduced when each of V1, LM, RL, AL, PM and AM holds at least one IC-encoder; the 2p part is not in this dandiset.

claims.statement: The dandiset's subjects can be assigned to the paper's imaging groups (experienced or naive virgin, dam, right cortex, cohousing, CH+575, opto-OT; excitatory, inhibitory or pan-neuronal indicator), with stimulus identity (prototype or morph ISI) for each presentation.
claims.source: Methods, Data availability statement; Methods, In vivo two-photon calcium imaging
claims.quote: The data that support the findings of this study are further available at figshare
claims.criterion: Reproduced when every subject carries a group and indicator, from the dataset's own metadata or from the title of the figshare item (collection doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.c.5043830.v6) with the same mouse ID, and every imaging presentation can be assigned its call and ISI bin. The counts per group are compared with the paper's (EV excitatory N=9, NV excitatory N=12, EV interneurons N=5, NV interneurons N=6, EV right cortex N=4, dam N=1, CH+575 N=6, CH+575 opto-OT N=4, chronic cohousing N=13). Partially reproduced when groups can be assigned but stimulus identity cannot, or counts differ for some groups; not reproduced when groups cannot be assigned.

claims.statement: Pup distress call ISIs (5,355 intervals from 37 recordings of pups at postnatal days 1-8) follow a lognormal distribution; calls with ISIs around the median (175 +/- 25 ms) serve as prototypes, and ISIs of 575 ms or more essentially never occur.
claims.source: Figure 1a; Methods, Stimulus library and vocalization analysis
claims.quote: 5,355 inter-syllable intervals were measured from 37 audio recordings ... and a lognormal frequency distribution was generated
claims.criterion: From the vocalization recordings, the ISIs measured and binned at +/-25 ms. Reproduced when the counts match, a lognormal fits (the median lies in the 150-200 ms bin), and fewer than 1% of ISIs are 550 ms or longer. The 1% bound is not in the paper; it reads "essentially never".

claims.statement: Experienced females (dams and experienced virgins pooled) retrieve cold, silent pups on fewer trials than warm, vocalizing pups (32.0% against 80.0%).
claims.source: Figure 1c; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 1c
claims.quote: Experienced females retrieved cold, silent pups on fewer trials than warm, vocalizing pups (retrieval (cold) : 32.0% of trials, retrieval (warm) : 80.0%
claims.criterion: Reproduced when both rates are within tolerance and warm against cold is significant by two-tailed Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction at p < 0.05. The family of comparisons is not stated (Methods, Statistics, say only that FDR was corrected in Fisher's tests with multiple comparisons). The readings are (a) every condition tested (cold, prototypes, each morph tested, single syllables) against warm, (b) the three comparisons the legend reports (cold, single, 575 against warm). The outcome is the one both give; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. Uncorrected p-values are shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Cold pups dubbed over with prototypes (76.7%) or with morphs of ISIs 75 to 375 ms (73.7-81.0%) are retrieved at rates similar to warm pups.
claims.source: Figure 1c; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 1c
claims.quote: Cold pups dubbed over with prototypes (76.7%), as well as morphs with ISIs between 75:375 ms (73.7–81.0%), were retrieved at similar rates to warm pups
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Each of prototypes and morphs 75, 125, 225, 275, 375 ms against warm by two-tailed Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction over reading (a) of the family in fig1c-warm-vs-cold (reading (b) does not hold these comparisons). Reproduced when none differs at p < 0.05 and the rates lie within the range widened by 10% of each bound; the differences from warm are reported.

claims.statement: ISIs slower than 575 ms (27.3%) and single syllables (15.0%) do not effectively elicit retrieval, being retrieved less than warm pups.
claims.source: Figure 1c; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 1c
claims.quote: In contrast, ISIs slower than 575 ms (27.3%) and single syllables (15.0%) did not effectively elicit retrieval
claims.criterion: Reproduced when both rates are within tolerance and each is below warm by two-tailed Fisher's exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction (both family readings of fig1c-warm-vs-cold, with the same rule) at p < 0.05. The 975 ms morph is reported but not required, since the text names 575 ms.

claims.statement: Dams and experienced virgins do not differ in retrieval of warm pups, prototype-dubbed pups or cold pups.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 2a
claims.quote: Dams and EVs did not differ in their retrieval behavior
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Two-tailed Fisher's exact test, dams against EVs, for each of warm, prototype and cold. Reproduced when none has p < 0.05; the rates are reported.

claims.statement: On successful trials, latencies to retrieve cold pups and pups dubbed with slow stimuli (single syllables and 575 ms) are longer than for warm pups and for pups dubbed with 75 to 375 ms ISIs.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 2b
claims.quote: Latencies to retrieve cold pups and cold pups dubbed over with slow morphs (single syllables (‘SS’) and 575 ms ISIs) were longer than for warm pups (p=0.02) or cold pups dubbed over with morphs containing ISIs between 75:375 ms (p=0.001)
claims.criterion: Latencies of successful trials in three bins (warm; morphs 75 to 375 ms; cold, single syllable and 575 ms). Whether prototypes are in the 75 to 375 ms bin is not said; the readings are with and without prototypes. Reproduced when, under one reading, the Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's post hoc shows the slow bin longer than both others at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In a y-maze, experienced females show no preference between a prototype and a morph with ISIs 25 to 350 ms, but approach prototypes more than morphs slower than 350 ms (425 ms 25.0%, 575+ ms 15.8% of trials approaching the morph).
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 2d; main text, paragraph citing Extended Data Fig. 2c,d
claims.quote: Mice showed a significant preference to approach prototypes when ISIs were slower than 350 ms
claims.criterion: First room entry per trial, bins of +/-75 ms except 575+. Reproduced when the 425 and 575+ bins differ from 0.5 by two-tailed binomial test at p < 0.05 with values in tolerance, and the 62.5 and 275 ms bins do not.

claims.statement: About 16% of excitatory neurons in left auditory cortex respond to prototypes, regardless of maternal experience.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 3e; main text, paragraph citing it
claims.quote: We observed robust responses to prototypes in ~16% of excitatory neurons regardless of maternal experience
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the responsive ROIs (the imaging method, responsive to any of the 6-9 prototypes) over all ROIs. Whether ~16% is the mean over mice or over neurons pooled is not said; both readings are computed. Reproduced when, under one reading, the value is within tolerance and the per-mouse percentages of EV and NV do not differ by two-tailed unpaired t-test at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Excitatory neuronal tuning to temporal morphs is broader in experienced than in naive virgins across the ISIs that elicit retrieval; naive cortex responds less to morphs than to prototypes.
claims.source: Figure 1f; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 1e,f
claims.quote: Compared to naive virgins, temporal tuning was broader in experienced virgins across ISIs that reliably elicited pup retrieval
claims.criterion: Per-mouse population tuning curves of normalized dF/F (the imaging method, readings (vi) a and b). The ANOVA design is not given; the readings are (a) a one-way ANOVA over all group and ISI cells with Bonferroni-corrected EV against NV comparisons at each of the seven morph ISIs; (b) EV against NV t-tests per morph ISI, Bonferroni over the seven. Reproduced when the EV mean exceeds the NV mean at each of 75, 125, 225, 275 and 375 ms and the 375 ms comparison has p <= 0.05 under every reading (of the design and of (vi)); partially reproduced when EV exceeds NV at all five but no reading gives p <= 0.05 at 375 ms; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: Tuning width over 75 to 375 ms is broader for excitatory neurons in experienced than in naive virgins; in naive cortex interneurons are more broadly tuned than excitatory neurons; and interneuron tuning width does not differ between experienced and naive virgins.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 6c
claims.quote: Excitatory neuronal tuning curves were significantly broader in EVs (N=9 mice) than in NVs (N=12; p=0.001), and interneuron tuning was broader than excitatory tuning in naive cortex (Inh: N=6; p=0.04). Interneuron tuning width did not differ between experienced (N=5) and naive virgins (p>0.99; one-way ANOVA, Bonferroni correction)
claims.criterion: Per-mouse tuning widths (the imaging method, readings (vi) a and b) in four groups (EV and NV, excitatory and interneuron); one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni post hoc comparisons. Which pairs form the Bonferroni family is not stated; the readings are (a) the three pairs reported, (b) all six pairs. Reproduced when, under every reading (of the family and of (vi)), EV excitatory exceeds NV excitatory and NV interneurons exceed NV excitatory, each at p < 0.05, and EV against NV interneurons is not significant; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: The narrow tuning in naive cortex does not extend to temporally modulated pure tones; tuning width to tone sequences does not differ between experienced and naive virgins.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 3k; main text, paragraph citing Extended Data Fig. 3i-m
claims.quote: the narrow tuning in naive cortex did not extend to temporally-modulated pure tones
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Cells responsive to the best frequency and to the 175 ms (5 Hz) sequence by paired one-tailed t-test at p < 0.05; normalized dF/F of the 75, 375 and 575 ms sequences to the 175 ms one; width as the mean "across all stimuli" (the legend), the readings being with or without the 175 ms value (an affine change, so one is used). Unpaired two-tailed t-test. The legend gives both mice (3 and 4) and neurons (94 and 45) and does not say which is the unit; the readings are (a) neurons, (b) per-mouse mean widths. Reproduced when p >= 0.05 under both, not reproduced when p < 0.05 under both, blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree; the difference is reported.

claims.statement: In naive auditory cortex, normalized responses to temporally modulated tones are higher than to pup call morphs at 75, 375 and 575 ms.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 3m
claims.quote: We observed higher normalized ΔF/Fs to temporally-modulated tones (N=5 mice) than to pup call morphs (n=11–12) in naive auditory cortex
claims.criterion: Normalized dF/F to tone sequences (normalized to the 175 ms sequence, Methods) per naive mouse (N=5) against normalized dF/F to call morphs per naive excitatory mouse of Fig. 1f (n=11-12, the count varying by ISI), at 75, 375 and 575 ms. The legend gives N=5 tone mice where Extended Data Fig. 3k gives N=4 naive mice; the difference is not explained, and the mice reached are reported. Whether the per-mouse value is the mean of single-cell curves or comes from the mean raw curve is reading (vi). Reproduced when, under every reading, tones exceed calls at all three ISIs by unpaired two-tailed Mann-Whitney test at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Broad temporal tuning in experienced virgins is left-lateralized; tuning width (75 to 375 ms) is larger in left than in right auditory cortex.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 4a-c
claims.quote: broad temporal tuning was left-lateralized in experienced females
claims.criterion: Per-mouse tuning widths (the imaging method) of EV excitatory neurons, left (the nine of Fig. 1f) against right (N=4). The unit is mice, since panel c is "from animals in (b)", and p = 0.003 matches the smallest exact two-sided Mann-Whitney p for 9 against 4 mice (2/715, about 0.0028, complete separation). Reproduced when left exceeds right at p < 0.05 by unpaired two-tailed Mann-Whitney test over mice; single-cell curves are shown as a variant.

claims.statement: In experienced virgins, call-evoked dF/F across ISI bins is correlated with the probability of each ISI in natural pup calls.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 4d
claims.quote: In EVs (N=9 mice), evoked ΔF/Fs were correlated with ISI probability from the distribution in Fig. 1a (Pearson’s r=0.86, p=0.007; two-tailed)
claims.criterion: The mean dF/F per ISI bin over the nine EV mice (eight points, prototype and seven morphs) against the probability of that bin in the Fig. 1a distribution. The ISI distribution is not in the dataset; it comes from fig1a-isi-distribution or from the source data. The legend says "evoked ΔF/Fs", the term the paper uses for raw responses as against "normalized ΔF/F", so raw dF/F is used and normalized dF/F is shown as a variant. Reproduced when r is within tolerance and p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Qualitatively, the left auditory cortex of a lactating dam shows broad temporal tuning, similar to that of experienced virgins.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 4e; main text, paragraph citing Extended Data Fig. 4d,e
claims.quote: Qualitatively, we observed broad temporal tuning in the left auditory cortex of a lactating dam (N=1 dam, n=10 single-cell tuning curves)
claims.criterion: The dam's mean normalized curve (10 single-cell curves). The paper gives no test ("we observed similar tuning in a lactating dam", main text). Reproduced when its tuning width lies within the range of the nine EV mice's widths and above the NV median; these bounds are a reading of "similar" and "broad", not the paper's.

claims.statement: In virgins retrieving on 10-30% of trials, temporal tuning was sharper before the onset of reliable retrieval; more neurons are broadly tuned once they retrieve on 100% of trials.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 4f,g
claims.quote: A larger proportion of neurons were more broadly tuned (higher normalized ΔF/Fs) when EVs retrieved on 100% of trials (p<0.0001; two-tailed unpaired Kolmogorov-Smirnov test)
claims.criterion: Single-cell tuning widths of the two virgins before (n=78) and after (n=52) reliable retrieval (Extended Data Fig. 4f, the 10% virgin day 0 n=21 and day 2 n=26, the 30% virgin day 1 n=57 and day 2 n=26). Reproduced when the after distribution lies to the right (higher median) and the two-sample KS test has p < 0.0001; partially reproduced when p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In pup-naive auditory cortical slices, IPSCs depress faster than EPSCs at the prototypical stimulation rate (175 ms), while EPSCs and IPSCs depress similarly at 75 or 575 ms.
claims.source: Figure 1g; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 1g
claims.quote: whole-cell recordings in pup-naive auditory cortical slices revealed that IPSCs adapted out faster than EPSCs at prototypical repetition rates, while PSCs were similarly depressed at faster or slower stimulation rates
claims.criterion: Peak PSCs normalized to the first (Sn/S1) per cell; 75 ms n=10 cells, 175 ms n=14, 575 ms n=13; one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni correction (legend). The p-value is not printed (the legend marks significance with asterisks), and the ANOVA factors are not given; the readings are (a) IPSC against EPSC Sn/S1 at each pulse, Bonferroni over pulses, per rate; (b) the mean Sn/S1 over pulses 2 to 5, IPSC against EPSC, per rate. The number of pulses per train is not given in the text. Reproduced when, under every reading, IPSCs are lower than EPSCs at p < 0.05 at 175 ms and not at 75 or 575 ms; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: Of naive virgins able to silence playback with a lever press, only those hearing prototypes significantly increased their press duration by session 8.
claims.source: Figure 1h,i; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 1h,i
claims.quote: Only virgins listening to prototypes exhibited a significant increase in press duration by session 8 (p=0.03)
claims.criterion: Touch-time files of 30 min sessions (KAMB_OperantTask_*.m write the time of each polling sample with a touch). A press is a run of consecutive touch samples; the gap that ends a press is not given, and the readings are gaps above (a) the median inter-sample interval times 2, (b) 100 ms. The mean press duration per session; files marked b (e.g. v4b) are joined to their session. The comparison is not stated; the readings are (a) session 1 against session 8, (b) the mean of sessions 1-2 against 7-8. Reproduced when, under every reading, prototypes give p < 0.05 by paired two-tailed t-test with an increase and the other groups do not; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: The number of lever presses per session did not increase by session 8 in any of the three groups.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5b
claims.quote: The total number of levers presses in a session (which turns off continuously playing prototypes or morphs) did not increase by session 8, regardless of the stimulus group
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Presses counted as in fig1i-operant-prototypes, under both of its press readings and both of its comparison readings; paired two-tailed t-test per group (N=7). Reproduced when no group shows an increase at p < 0.05 under every reading, not reproduced when one does under every reading, blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Interneurons are broadly tuned regardless of experience, but their tuning curve slopes at the transition between retrieved (75:375 ms) and ignored (575:975 ms) ISIs are sharper in experienced virgins.
claims.source: Figure 2c,d; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 2
claims.quote: tuning curve slopes at the transition between ISIs eliciting retrieval (75:375 ms, Fig. 1c ) and ignored ISIs (575:975 ms) were significantly sharper in experienced virgins (p=0.03
claims.criterion: Per-mouse population curves of interneurons (the imaging method, readings (v) and (vi)); slope 375 to 975 ms. Reproduced when the EV slope is more negative than the NV slope at p < 0.05 by unpaired two-tailed t-test under every reading of (v) and (vi); blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Population tuning slopes at the behavioural transition (375:975 ms) are significantly negative in experienced virgins, for excitatory neurons and interneurons, and not in naive virgins.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 6d; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 2e
claims.quote: Slopes in EVs were significantly negative
claims.criterion: Per-mouse population slopes (readings (v) and (vi)). The mice counts (7 and 11) are fewer than in Fig. 1f (9 and 12); which were left out is not said, so all mice with a 975 ms response are used and the counts reported. Reproduced when both EV groups have slopes below zero at p < 0.05 and neither NV group does, under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: In experienced virgins, excitatory and inhibitory single-cell tuning are matched across behaviourally salient ISIs and differ at 575 and 975 ms.
claims.source: Figure 2e
claims.quote: Excitatory and inhibitory neuronal tuning were also matched in experienced virgins, responding similarly across behaviorally-salient ISIs and with negative slopes between 375:975 ms
claims.criterion: Single-cell normalized curves of EV excitatory and inhibitory neurons; one-way ANOVA over cell type and ISI cells with Bonferroni-corrected comparisons, excitatory against inhibitory at each morph ISI. The direction at 575 and 975 is not stated in the text; it is reported. Reproduced when 575 and 975 differ at p < 0.05 and none of 75 to 375 ms does.

claims.statement: In naive cortex, interneurons are more broadly tuned than excitatory neurons but lack a sharp boundary at the behavioural transition.
claims.source: Figure 2f; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 2f
claims.quote: while interneurons in naive cortex were more broadly tuned than excitatory neurons, the lack of a sharp boundary suggests interneurons were still relatively untuned to relevant statistics
claims.criterion: The sentence cites Fig. 2f and Extended Data Fig. 6c,d. Fig. 2f (268 excitatory and 128 inhibitory NV single-cell curves, one-way ANOVA, Bonferroni) prints no p, so the claim is judged on the Extended Data tests. Reproduced when NV interneuron width exceeds NV excitatory width as in ed6c-tuning-width-groups and the NV interneuron slope does not differ from zero as in ed6d-slopes-negative-in-ev (one-sample t-test, p >= 0.05). The Fig. 2f per-ISI comparisons are reported.

claims.statement: In experienced females, prototype- and morph-evoked EPSCs are similar and negatively correlated with ISI; in naive cortex morph-evoked EPSCs are weaker than prototype-evoked ones and uncorrelated with ISI.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 6e,f; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 2g
claims.quote: In experienced females, prototype- and morph-evoked EPSCs were similar in magnitude and negatively correlated with ISI duration
claims.criterion: PSC area over the window from call onset to 250 ms after offset, divided by its length, minus the 1 s baseline, mean of the largest 5-10 trials (the readings 5 and 10 are both run). Experienced cells are dams and EVs pooled (Methods, In vivo whole-cell recordings). The legends use 125, 175, 275 and 575 ms, while the Methods list morphs of 125, 225 and 575 ms; the legends' ISIs are used. Correlation over all cell and ISI points (n=12 cells by 4 ISIs, matching the p for r=-0.37). Reproduced when, under every reading, NV prototype exceeds 125, 275 and 575 ms at p < 0.05 by repeated measures ANOVA with Bonferroni, no EV pair differs, the EV correlation is negative at p < 0.05 and the NV one is not significant.

claims.statement: Prototype-evoked EPSCs are similar between groups, but EPSCs evoked by non-prototypical ISIs are larger in experienced than in naive females.
claims.source: Figure 2h; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 2h
claims.quote: While prototype-evoked EPSCs were similar, responses to non-prototypical ISIs were enhanced in experienced females
claims.criterion: EPSC magnitudes as in ed6ef-epsc-tuning. Reproduced when EV exceeds NV at 125, 275 and 575 ms at p < 0.05 by unpaired one-tailed t-test and the prototype comparison is not significant.

claims.statement: IPSCs are broadly tuned in both groups but weaker in naive virgins at every ISI.
claims.source: Figure 2i; Extended Data Fig. 6i-k
claims.quote: IPSCs were broadly tuned in both groups ( Extended Data Figure 6i – k ), albeit weaker in naive virgins
claims.criterion: IPSC magnitudes as in ed6ef-epsc-tuning. Reproduced when EV exceeds NV at all four ISIs at p < 0.05 by unpaired two-tailed t-test, and neither correlation with ISI is significant.

claims.statement: In experienced females the IPSC-EPSC ratio is positively correlated with ISI, so that the balance shifts toward inhibition for slower ISIs; not so in naive females.
claims.source: Figure 2j; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 2j
claims.quote: In experienced females, this ratio was positively correlated with ISI duration (Pearson’s r=0.47, p=0.02
claims.criterion: (IPSC - EPSC)/(IPSC + EPSC) per cell and ISI, from cells with both currents recorded, correlated with ISI over all cell and ISI points. Reproduced when the EV r is within tolerance with p < 0.05 and the NV correlation is not significant.

claims.statement: Within cells of experienced cortex, 575 ms-evoked IPSCs are stronger than EPSCs, while the two do not differ at 125, 175 or 275 ms.
claims.source: Figure 2k; Extended Data Fig. 6l
claims.quote: 575-evoked IPSCs were significantly stronger than EPSCs (p=0.03
claims.criterion: Reproduced when IPSC exceeds EPSC at 575 ms at p < 0.05 by paired two-tailed t-test and the other ISIs are not significant.

claims.statement: Prototype- and morph-evoked EPSCs do not differ between lactating dams and experienced virgins, justifying their pooling.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 6g,h
claims.quote: Prototype and morph-evoked EPSCs did not differ between dams (n=4 cells) and EVs (n=8)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Unpaired two-tailed t-test, dams (n=4) against EVs (n=8), per ISI. Reproduced when none has p < 0.05.

claims.statement: During cohousing prototype-responsive interneurons are relatively stable while the set of prototype-responsive excitatory neurons changes; about 18.8% of excitatory and 72.3% of inhibitory neurons responsive at baseline remain responsive in the final session.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 7a-c; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 3b
claims.quote: Of the neurons that were prototype-responsive at baseline and successfully tracked, ~18.8% of excitatory neurons and ~72.3% of inhibitory neurons remained responsive in the final imaging session
claims.criterion: Chronic imaging virgins. ROIs matched across days by spatial cross-correlation of the 100x100-pixel image around each ROI; cells below the 95th percentile of the across-ROI null are dropped. Prototype dF/F at baseline and in the final session (+24 to 96 h), zero for non-responsive cells. Reproduced when the percentages and r values are within tolerance and both correlations have p < 0.0001; partially reproduced when the signs and p < 0.05 hold.

claims.statement: During cohousing, excitatory single-cell tuning broadens between 75 and 375 ms after retrieval onset, while interneuron tuning does not broaden; excitatory and inhibitory tuning, mismatched at first, become similar 24 hours after first retrieval.
claims.source: Figure 3e-g; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 3e
claims.quote: Excitatory population tuning broadened between 75:375 ms ( Fig. 3e , f ), elaborating on the initial preference for prototypes. Interneurons did not broaden their tuning
claims.criterion: Chronic imaging, sessions aligned to first retrieval, binned +/-12 h. "Before and after retrieval onset" is naive (baseline) against +24 h; the counts fix it (Fig. 3e +24 h n=70 excitatory and 86 inhibitory, the "retrieving" n of Extended Data Fig. 8a,b). Reproduced when the excitatory width distribution shifts up with KS p < 0.0001, the interneuron KS has p >= 0.05, and, by one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni-corrected excitatory against inhibitory comparisons at each morph ISI (Fig. 3e legend), the two differ at one or more ISIs at baseline and at none of 75 to 375 ms at +24 h ("matched ... over the range of behaviorally-relevant ISIs (+24 hours, Fig. 3e)", main text). The ANOVA design is open as in fig1f-ev-broader-than-nv and both designs are run, the outcome being the one both give. Partially reproduced when the width parts hold and the matching part does not.

claims.statement: Both excitatory and inhibitory population tuning sharpen at the transition 375 to 975 ms after virgins start retrieving.
claims.source: Figure 3h
claims.quote: both excitatory and inhibitory tuning selectively sharpened between 375:975 ms
claims.criterion: Per-mouse population slopes (readings (v) and (vi)) before cohousing against after retrieving. "After virgins were successfully retrieving" is read as (a) +24 h after first retrieval, (b) the last session. Reproduced when, under every reading, slopes become more negative at p < 0.05 by one-tailed paired t-test in both cell types; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. The single-cell slopes of Fig. 3i (one-way ANOVA against baseline, Bonferroni; no p printed) are reported.

claims.statement: Retrieval onset ranged from 12 to 109 hours of cohousing in the 13 chronically imaged virgins.
claims.source: Methods, In vivo two-photon calcium imaging
claims.quote: Retrieval onset ranged from 12–109 hours of cohousing in N=13 virgins

claims.statement: Pup-naive virgins imaged on three consecutive days without cohousing show no systematic change in temporal tuning.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 8c,d
claims.quote: non-cohoused controls only exposed to calls during consecutive imaging sessions showed no systematic tuning changes
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Single-cell normalized curves, session 1 (N=4 mice, n=53) against session 3 (N=5, n=48), one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni-corrected session 1 against session 3 at each morph ISI. No p is reported. Reproduced when no ISI differs at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Virgins that heard slow morphs (575 ms) during cohousing have excitatory tuning broader at 575 ms than standard cohoused virgins.
claims.source: Figure 4b; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 4b
claims.quote: prototype-responsive neurons in virgins that heard slow exemplars were more broadly tuned to 575 ms ISIs
claims.criterion: Population curves 24 h after first retrieval, CH+575 against CH (the +24 h mice of Fig. 3e, per Methods; reading (vi)). The ANOVA design is open as in fig1f-ev-broader-than-nv. Reproduced when CH+575 exceeds CH at 575 ms at p < 0.05 with Bonferroni over the seven morph ISIs, under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Virgins exposed to slow morphs during cohousing retrieve pups dubbed with slow morphs more reliably than standard cohoused virgins (75% against 14.3% of trials).
claims.source: Figure 4c; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 4c
claims.quote: virgins in the CH+575 group retrieved cold pups dubbed over with slow morphs (ISI:575 ms; 75% of trials) more reliably than controls (14.3%
claims.criterion: CH are the experienced virgins of Fig. 1c (Methods, Statistics, item 1). Reproduced when both rates are within tolerance and the two-tailed Fisher's exact test gives p < 0.05. Latencies (Extended Data Fig. 8f, p=0.73, Mann-Whitney) are reported.

claims.statement: Photoinhibiting left auditory cortex only during slow morph playback blocks the learning of slow ISIs (18.8% against 66.7% in shams) without affecting retrieval of prototypes or latencies.
claims.source: Figure 4d; Extended Data Fig. 8g
claims.quote: Photoinhibiting left auditory cortex (ACtx) exclusively during slow morph playback selectively blocked the learning of slow ISIs compared to shams
claims.criterion: Reproduced when both rates are within tolerance, slow differs at p < 0.05 by two-tailed Fisher's exact test, prototypes do not, and latencies on successful trials do not differ by unpaired two-tailed Mann-Whitney test (p >= 0.05).

claims.statement: Virgins hearing single syllables during cohousing do not learn to retrieve pups dubbed with single syllables.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 8h,i; main text, paragraph citing it
claims.quote: virgins hearing single syllables (ISI:30s) during cohousing were unable to associate these calls with isolated pups
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Two-tailed Fisher's exact test, CH against CH+SS, single syllable trials. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; the rates are reported.

claims.statement: Oxytocin enhances spiking to repeated 575 ms pulses in auditory cortical slices from stimulus 2 on, while stimulation without oxytocin does not change spike probability.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 9a,b
claims.quote: evoked spike probability was significantly enhanced 15–30 minutes following the onset of oxytocin wash
claims.criterion: Spike probability per pulse, baseline against 15-30 min after wash onset. Reproduced when stimuli 2 to 5 increase at p < 0.05 by Friedman test with Dunn's post hoc, stimulus 1 does not, and ACSF controls (n=7) show no change at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Inhibiting oxytocin neurons during slow morph playback lowers retrieval of warm pups (43.8% against 92.3%), prototype-dubbed pups (36.8% against 83.3%) and slow-morph-dubbed pups (33.3% against 83.3%), and changes retrieval latencies.
claims.source: Figure 4e; Extended Data Fig. 9d
claims.quote: we observed deficits in retrieval rates for warm pups (CH+575 sham : 92.3% vs. CH+575 opto-OT : 43.8% of trials), as well as cold pups dubbed over with prototypes (83.3% vs. 36.8%) and slow morphs (83.3% vs. 33.3%
claims.criterion: Reproduced when all six rates are within tolerance, each pair differs at p < 0.05 by two-tailed Fisher's exact test, and latencies on successful trials differ at p < 0.05 by unpaired two-tailed Mann-Whitney test. The text does not give the direction of the latency change; it is reported.

claims.statement: Virgins with oxytocin neurons inhibited during cohousing have uncharacteristically narrow tuning 24 hours after first retrieval, narrower than cohoused virgins' excitatory and inhibitory tuning.
claims.source: Figure 4f,g; Extended Data Fig. 9e
claims.quote: These behavioral deficits were associated with uncharacteristically narrow temporal tuning in auditory cortex 24 hours after first retrieval
claims.criterion: Per-mouse tuning widths (reading (vi)); CH is all retrieving virgins imaged (Methods), excitatory N=14 and inhibitory N=10. Reproduced when opto-OT is lower than both at p < 0.05 by Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post hoc. Which mice make up the 14 and 10 is not listed; the counts reached are reported.

claims.statement: Single-cell tuning in opto-OT virgins is narrower than in reliably retrieving virgins but similar to virgins retrieving on 10-30% of trials.
claims.source: Figure 4h; main text, paragraph citing Fig. 4h
claims.quote: Single-cell tuning curves in CH+575 opto-OT virgins were significantly narrower compared to reliably retrieving virgins
claims.criterion: Single-cell widths of opto-OT (N=4, n=40) and the two virgins of Extended Data Fig. 4g before (n=78) and after (n=52) reliable retrieval. Reproduced when opto-OT is lower than CH 100% at p < 0.05 and does not differ from CH 10-30%, by Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post hoc.

claims.statement: Neuropil correction has no significant effect on prototype-evoked dF/F in excitatory or inhibitory neurons.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 3a-c; Methods, Image processing and analysis
claims.quote: Neuropil correction had no significant effect on call-evoked ΔF/Fs in excitatory or inhibitory neurons
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. F_true = F_raw - r F_neuropil, r = F_blood_vessel / F_neuropil, on one excitatory and one inhibitory region; which regions is not said, so every region is run and the claim judged on the regions with 52 and 64 responsive neurons if they can be identified, and on all otherwise. Reproduced when the two-sample KS test of corrected against uncorrected prototype dF/F gives p >= 0.05 in both.

claims.statement: In the ten-finger task, N-PPC yielded 111 neurons per session (102 to 119) over 10 sessions of 100 trials, J-PPC 160 (159 to 160) and J-MC 130 (120 to 130) over 2 sessions of 100 trials.
claims.source: Results, Decoding individual finger presses of either hand, paragraph 2
claims.quote: participant N: 100 trials / session for 10 sessions; participant J: 100 trials / session for 2 sessions). We recorded 111 neurons per session (min: 102; max: 119) from N-PPC, 160 neurons per session (min: 159; max: 160) from J-PPC, and 130 neurons per session (min: 120; max: 130) from J-MC
claims.criterion: Neurons counted after the 0.5 Hz exclusion under both readings of O1, and before it. Reproduced when the session and trial counts match and, under one reading, each mean count is within tolerance and each range is within 10% of its bounds.

claims.statement: 1111 N-PPC neurons were recorded across the 10 sessions of the ten-finger task.
claims.source: Supplementary Figure 11 legend
claims.quote: 1111 N-PPC neurons were recorded across 10 sessions
claims.criterion: Counted under both readings of O1 and before the exclusion; reproduced when one count is within tolerance.

claims.statement: Most neurons discriminate firing rates across the ten fingers (N-PPC 66%, J-PPC 57%, J-MC 78%, q < 0.05).
claims.source: Results, Decoding individual finger presses of either hand, paragraph 2
claims.quote: most neurons (N-PPC: 66%; J-PPC: 57%; J-MC: 78%) discriminated firing rates across fingers (q < 0.05)
claims.criterion: As in Methods, Single-neuron selectivity. Per neuron, a one-way ANOVA of Go-window firing rates (200 to 700 ms after Go, by O11) across the ten finger conditions; Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over all neurons of the participant's array pooled across sessions; discriminative when q < 0.05; neurons pooled across sessions for the percentage (Methods). J-PPC and J-MC are corrected separately, as each legend gives an array's own neuron count. Reproduced when, under one reading of O1, all three percentages are within tolerance; partially reproduced when one or two are.

claims.statement: A linear classifier discriminates all ten fingers well above the 10% chance level (cross-validated accuracy N-PPC 70%, J-PPC 66%, J-MC 75%).
claims.source: Results, Decoding individual finger presses of either hand, paragraph 3; Figure 7c to 7e
claims.quote: A linear classifier (Methods) was able to discriminate between all ten fingers (cross-validated classification accuracy, N-PPC: 70%; J-PPC: 66%; J-MC: 75%; chance: 10%)
claims.criterion: As in Methods, Offline classification with cross-validation.
