claims.quote: This early wave of activity was followed substantially later by significant visual encoding in other areas, including the MRN, SCm, PRNr, IRN and GRN (latencies of about 100−120 ms
claims.criterion: Only IRN and GRN are loaded (MRN, SCm and PRNr would add many sessions). The reported range 100 to 120 ms widened by 10% of each bound is 90 to 132 ms, written as 111 +/- 21. Reproduced when both latencies (Methods' definition) are in 90 to 132 ms and both regions' distances are significant; partially reproduced for one region.

claims.statement: The stimulus trajectory distance was significant in 104 regions.
claims.source: Results, Representation of visual stimulus, paragraph 6; Fig. 4c
claims.quote: Altogether, this analysis indicated that distance was a significant result in 104 regions (Fig. 4c,f).
claims.criterion: Trajectories as in traj-latency-visual (0 to 150 ms after stimulus onset, analysed trials, 1000 permutations of stimulus side within block and choice, P = (n + 1) / (M + 1) on the amplitude) for every canonical region, pooling its canonical units over its sessions with valid blocks; a region with fewer than 20 such units is not tested and counts as not significant. Readings (a) Benjamini-Hochberg at q = 0.01 over the regions (Methods, multiple comparisons), (b) P < 0.01 without correction (Methods, trajectory analysis). Reproduced when the count is within 104 +/- 10.4 under one reading. The code's Benjamini-Yekutieli correction and the variant with the 64 sessions of invalid blocks are shown and do not decide; agreement of each region with the stim_euc_sig column of region_info.csv is reported and does not decide.

claims.statement: During reward delivery, activity showed coherent oscillations of about 10 Hz that were missing after negative feedback and were closely related to licking.
claims.source: Results, Representation of feedback, paragraph 4; Fig. 6j-l; Extended Data Fig. 12
claims.quote: multiple brain areas exhibited coherent approximately 10 Hz oscillatory dynamics during reward delivery that was phase-locked across brain areas ... These oscillatory dynamics were missing during negative feedback and were closely related to licking behaviour
claims.criterion: In IRN, the paper's example region, the session mean PSTH over units (5 ms bins, 0 to 1 s after feedback) on correct and on incorrect trials, and the lick PSTH of the same sessions. Reproduced when (i) the median over sessions of the peak frequency (4 to 20 Hz) of the correct PSTH is within 9 to 11 Hz, (ii) power within 1 Hz of each session's correct peak is higher on correct than incorrect trials (Wilcoxon signed-rank p < 0.05), and (iii) the median lick PSTH peak is within 1 Hz of the neural one. Partially reproduced when (ii) and (iii) hold and (i) does not.

claims.statement: Wheel speed was decodable from 163 of the 201 regions.
claims.source: Results, Representation of wheel movement, paragraph 2; Fig. 7a
claims.quote: Wheel speed was decodable from 81% of the reportable areas (163 out of 201)

claims.statement: In the encoding model the kernel for correct feedback explained the most variance of all kernels (mean delta R2 of 8.6e-3 over all neurons).
claims.source: Results, Representation of feedback, paragraph 6; Extended Data Fig. 13
claims.quote: The kernel for correct feedback was the largest single contributor to neural response variance across each trial (mean ΔR2 of 8.6 × 10−3 averaged across all neurons; Extended Data Fig. 13), which exceeded all other kernels

claims.statement: More than half of the neurons in most brain regions were significantly correlated with at least one behavioural variable from video (nose, paw, pupil, tongue).
claims.source: Results, Representation of wheel movement, paragraph 5; Extended Data Fig. 15
claims.quote: More than half of the neurons in most brain regions were significantly correlated with at least one behavioural variable (Extended Data Fig. 15b).

claims.statement: High Granger interaction scores were found for region pairs from all major brain regions, weakly correlated with anatomical distance and mostly bidirectional.
claims.source: Results, Neural analyses, paragraph 8; Extended Data Fig. 4
claims.quote: High Granger interaction scores were obtained for region pairs from all major brain regions, which were weakly correlated with anatomical distance and mostly bidirectional.

claims.statement: All five rats acquired the task faster in the novel environment than during de novo learning; proportion correct over the first 50 trials is higher in novel learning.
claims.source: Figure 1B; Results, Rats generalize learned rules across contexts, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Compared with de novo learning, all animals acquired the inbound and outbound task rules faster in the novel environment
claims.criterion: Proportion correct is the state-space estimate of the probability of a correct trial (Smith et al. 2004, ref 84; Methods), with background probability 1/3 for inbound and outbound trials combined, as cal_behavperform.m sets it. As behavperform_gather.m does, the novel curve is trials 1 to 50 of the novel sessions (N and N' run together) and the de novo curve is trials 1 to 50 of de novo learning. Reproduced when, for every one of the five rats, the mean of the novel curve over the 50 trials exceeds the mean of the de novo curve. Needs the de novo learning sessions.

claims.statement: Final performance at the end of de novo learning was 84.3% correct (SD 7.7%).
claims.source: Results, Rats generalize learned rules across contexts, paragraph 2
claims.quote: final performance, 84.3% ± 7.7%, mean ± SD
claims.criterion: Per rat, the mean of the state-space estimate over the trials of the last de novo session (behavperform_gather.m, which takes the last session in its de novo file); the mean over the five rats. Tolerance is the stated SD. Which session is last is open for the three rats trained 2 more days in the familiar room (Methods). Readings are (a) the last W-track session before the N-F-N' day ("final performance of de novo learning before N-F-N′ sessions", Figure 1C legend), on those extra days for the three rats, (b) the eighth session of the de novo day. Needs the de novo learning sessions.

claims.statement: Proportion correct differs across de novo session 1, final de novo session, N, F and N', with performance in N above the first de novo session.
claims.source: Figure 1C
claims.quote: Proportion correct against session number (data points for individual animals; repeated-measures ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc, F = 40.48 , n.s., p > 0.75 , ***p = 0.0002, **p = 0.0045)
claims.criterion: Per rat and session, the mean of the state-space estimate over the session's trials (behavperform_gather.m), for de novo session 1, final de novo session (readings as in fig1-denovo-final-performance), N, F and N'. A repeated-measures ANOVA over the five groups with Tukey's post hoc; the legend gives F = 40.48 and no p for the ANOVA. The legend does not say which pairs the three post hoc values belong to. Reproduced when the ANOVA has p < 0.05 and Tukey's test puts N above de novo session 1 at p < 0.05; the post hoc p for every pair is reported. Needs the de novo learning sessions.

claims.statement: In both groups of rats, performance in the familiar environment is higher than in the novel one whatever the order of exposure (N-F-N' group in Figure 1C, F-N-F'-N' group in Figure S1C).
claims.source: Results, Rats generalize learned rules across contexts, paragraph 2; Figure 1C; Figure S1C
claims.quote: We found that for both animal groups, the performance in the familiar environment was significantly higher than that in the novel one regardless of the order of experience
claims.criterion: Session means of the state-space estimate as in fig1c-session-performance. For the N-F-N' rats, reproduced when Tukey's post hoc of the repeated-measures ANOVA of Figure 1C puts F above N at p < 0.05 (F above N' is reported too). The F-N-F'-N' rats are from earlier experiments; their part is tested only if their behaviour is in the dataset, the same way (F and F' above N and N', p < 0.05).

claims.statement: In the first session, both inbound and outbound performance are higher in novel learning (N) than in de novo learning.
claims.source: Figure S1B
claims.quote: Note the higher performance for both inbound and outbound during novel learning than de novo learning (****p < 0.0001, rank-sum tests)
claims.criterion: The legend does not give the unit of the rank-sum test; with five rats a p below 0.0001 needs more samples, so the samples are trials. The state-space estimate of proportion correct is computed separately for inbound and outbound trials with background probability 0.5, as cal_behavperform.m notes for that split. Readings for the samples are (a) the trial-by-trial estimates of all five rats pooled, first de novo session against N; (b) the binary correct or incorrect outcomes of the same trials. Reproduced when, under each reading, the rank-sum test gives p < 0.05 with novel higher, for inbound and for outbound. Needs the de novo learning sessions.

claims.statement: Cells were tracked across environments, with 30.5 (SD 9.8) CA1 and 37.4 (SD 19.3) PFC cells per session per animal.
claims.source: Results, PFC spatial map generalizes, while CA1 completely remaps, across contexts, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Cells were stably tracked across environments (mean ± SD = 30.5 ± 9.8 CA1 and 37.4 ± 19.3 PFC cells per session per animal
claims.criterion: Cells as the Methods select them, well isolated units with at least 100 spikes in the session, putative interneurons excluded; for the interneurons, the code's rules (CA1 mean rate below 7 Hz, the per-animal exclusion lists). Counted per animal and per session (N, F, N'), giving 15 counts per region; mean and SD over them. Tolerance is the stated SD. The paper does not say whether a cell recorded in all three sessions is counted once per session (the reading used) or once per animal; the second is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: CA1 spatial similarity between the two environments is no different from that of cell-ID shuffles, that is, CA1 remaps globally.
claims.source: Results, PFC spatial map generalizes, while CA1 completely remaps, across contexts, paragraph 1; Figure S3A
claims.quote: Notably, the distributions of CA1 spatial-representation similarity between two environments were not different from distributions obtained by shuffling cell identities in the same environment
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a one-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc (Figure S3A legend) over the CA1 groups N-N', F-N' and shuffle. Spatial similarity is the Pearson correlation of a cell's linearized rate maps (4 trajectories, 2-cm bins) between two sessions (Methods). The shuffle pairs a cell's map in F with a different cell's map in the novel environment (Methods). Cells are the spatially tuned cells of the PV analysis (peak above 3 Hz in either session of the pair, cal_PVsimilarity.m), which the paper's text does not restate for this panel. Reproduced when Tukey's test finds no difference (p > 0.05) between CA1 F-N' and shuffle; the effect size is given either way. Rate maps use the open smoothing width named in fig2d-pv-similarity.

claims.statement: Single-cell rate overlap and spatial correlation of PFC cells across environments (F-N') are as large as across repeated exposures to the novel environment (N-N'), whereas in CA1 they are lower across environments.
claims.source: Figure S3A
claims.quote: Note that the similarity of PFC firing across familiar-novel environments (F-N’) was as large as with repeated exposures of the novel environment (N-N’; n.s., p > 0.05), in contrast to CA1 (*p = 0.012, ****p < 0.0001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc)
claims.criterion: Rate overlap is the mean rate in the less active session over that in the more active one; spatial similarity is the Pearson correlation of linearized rate maps (Methods). The paper does not say how the mean rate is taken; readings are (a) the mean of the linearized rate map, (b) spikes over time in the session's run periods. One-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc per measure and region over N-N', F-N' and shuffle. Reproduced when, for both measures, PFC F-N' does not differ from N-N' (p > 0.05, judged on the paper's test) and CA1 F-N' is below N-N' at p < 0.05; partially reproduced when this holds for one measure. Cells as in figs3a-ca1-global-remapping.

claims.statement: PFC population-vector similarity across environments (F-N') is as high as across repeated exposures to the novel environment (N-N'), while CA1 PV similarity is lower across environments than within the novel environment, where the CA1 map is reinstated.
claims.source: Figure 2C and 2D; Results, PFC spatial map generalizes, while CA1 completely remaps, across contexts, paragraphs 1 and 2
claims.quote: the PFC spatial-representation similarity between two different environments was just as large as with repeated testing in the same environment
claims.criterion: As cal_PVsimilarity.m computes it, per animal and region. Cells pass the Methods' rules for either session of the pair (more than 100 spikes, interneurons excluded) and are spatially tuned (linearized peak rate of at least 3 Hz in either session, Methods; the code's "above 3 Hz" is a variant). Each trajectory's linearized rate map is interpolated to 101 bins of normalized length (about 2 cm, as the Methods' 2-cm bins), NaN runs filled linearly, the four trajectories concatenated. PV similarity is the Pearson correlation, bin by bin, of the PVs of two sessions; per animal, the mean over bins. Pairs are N-N' (epochs 2 and 6) and F-N' (epochs 4 and 6). The 1D smoothing width is garbled in the text; the readings are (a) 8 cm, the σ given for the 2D maps in the sentence before, and (b) no width the text fixes, so 4 cm and 2 cm are run as variants; the outcome is the one (a) gives if (a) and the variants agree, and is otherwise methods_underspecified. Rate maps use run periods above 5 cm/s with SWR times excluded and occupancy above 20 ms (Methods). The legend gives F = 83.24 and no p for the ANOVA. Reproduced when a repeated-measures ANOVA over the four groups (CA1 N-N', CA1 F-N', PFC N-N', PFC F-N') has p < 0.05, Tukey's test finds CA1 F-N' below CA1 N-N' (p < 0.05), and PFC F-N' does not differ from PFC N-N' (p > 0.05, a claim of absence on the paper's test).

claims.statement: Decoding with N' rate maps, CA1 position error is higher in F than in N, and in F no better than with cell-ID shuffled templates.
claims.source: Figure 2E; Results, PFC spatial map generalizes, while CA1 completely remaps, across contexts, paragraph 4
claims.quote: the error between actual and reconstructed positions in the familiar environment was significantly higher than that in the novel environment and no better than chance for CA1
claims.criterion: Decoder as the Methods give it. A memoryless Bayesian decoder with Poisson spiking and a uniform prior over position and trajectory type; templates are the N' linearized rate maps of cells with peak rate at least 3 Hz; spikes in N and F in 200-ms windows; run periods above 5 cm/s; positions within 15 cm of a reward well excluded; the decoded position is the maximum of the posterior, the error the linear distance from the actual position. The Methods say the window moves "with 50 ms overlap", a 150-ms step; the code (decoding_position_*_novelfamiliar_cross.m) steps by 50 ms and keeps only bins in its theta periods, which are variants. As the code does, a bin is decoded when its positions lie on one trajectory and at least one cell fires, and the error is measured along the four trajectories laid end to end, so a decode onto the wrong trajectory is far. Time bins pooled over the five rats. Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post hoc; the legend does not say which groups enter one test, so the readings are (a) CA1 N, CA1 F, PFC N and PFC F together, (b) N and F per region. The shuffle permutes cell identities of the N' rate maps (Methods). The paper does not say how many shuffles or what the Wilcoxon test pairs; readings are (a) each bin's error against its error under one shuffle, (b) against its median error over 100 shuffles (a standard number; the paper gives none). Reproduced when, under each grouping reading, Dunn's test puts CA1 F above CA1 N at p < 0.05 and, under each shuffle reading, the CA1 F errors do not differ from the shuffle at p < 0.05 (a claim of absence on the Wilcoxon paired test).

claims.statement: Decoding with N' rate maps, PFC position error is similar in N and F, and in both well above chance (below the cell-ID shuffles).
claims.source: Figure 2E; Results, PFC spatial map generalizes, while CA1 completely remaps, across contexts, paragraph 4
claims.quote: whereas PFC decoding was well above chance and similar across environments
claims.criterion: Decoding, groups, test and shuffle readings as in fig2e-ca1-error-familiar. Reproduced when, under each grouping reading, Dunn's test finds no difference between PFC N and PFC F (p > 0.05, a claim of absence on the paper's test) and, under each shuffle reading, PFC errors in N and in F are below their shuffles by the Wilcoxon paired test at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: After the switch from N to F, CA1 decoding error rises within the first trial, while PFC decoding error stays stable.
claims.source: Figure 2F; Results, PFC spatial map generalizes, while CA1 completely remaps, across contexts, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Interestingly, the decoding error rapidly increased during the first trial after environment switching for CA1 but remained stable for PFC
claims.criterion: Decoding with N' templates as in fig2e-ca1-error-familiar, per trial, errors pooled over the five rats. Methods' decoder settings are the main reading; the code's (decoding_position_*_novelfamiliar_trial.m) are a variant (non-overlapping 200-ms bins, no speed or theta filter, more than one active cell, the decode restricted to the current trajectory, absolute error). The paper does not define trial -1. Readings are (a) the last N trial before the switch; (b) the code's, which takes the first 10 trials of N and of F and labels the N trials -10 to -1, so trial -1 is the tenth N trial. Kruskal-Wallis over the trials from -10 to 10 with Dunn's post hoc, per region. Reproduced when, under each reading, CA1 trial 1 exceeds trial -1 at p < 0.05 and PFC trial 1 does not differ from trial -1 (p > 0.05, a claim of absence on the paper's test).

claims.statement: PFC PV similarity across environments grows with experience (F-N' higher than F-N), while CA1 does not change (F-N against F-N' not different) and stays below N-N'.
claims.source: Figure S3C; Results, PFC spatial map generalizes, while CA1 completely remaps, across contexts, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Furthermore, there was greater assimilation of PFC representations across environments with experience, while CA1 place cells maintained their independent representations
claims.criterion: PV similarity per spatial bin as in fig2d-pv-similarity, bins pooled over the five rats (the cumulative distributions of the panel), for F-N, F-N' and N-N'. One-way ANOVA per region with Tukey's post hoc. Reproduced when PFC F-N' exceeds PFC F-N at p < 0.05, CA1 F-N and F-N' do not differ (p > 0.05, a claim of absence on the paper's test), and CA1 F-N' is below CA1 N-N' at p < 0.05. The PFC F-N' against N-N' difference is reported.

claims.statement: Over trials in the novel environment, PFC similarity to the familiar map rises from the first to the last trial, while CA1 similarity does not change.
claims.source: Figure S3D
claims.quote: PV similarity between novel and familiar environments over trials in the novel environment
claims.criterion: Single-trial rate maps in the novel environment against session-averaged F rate maps; only trials with at least 80% of spatially tuned cells active (legend); PV similarity per bin as in fig2d-pv-similarity. The paper does not say which novel trials. Readings are (a) the trials of N followed by those of N', (b) N alone, (c) N' alone. The single-trial map smoothing is that of the session maps (open, as in fig2d-pv-similarity). One-way ANOVA over trials with Tukey's post hoc on per-bin values. Reproduced when, under each reading, PFC last trial exceeds first trial at p < 0.05 and CA1 first and last do not differ (p > 0.05).

claims.statement: Ramping cells make up 16.4% of CA1 cell samples (81 of 495) and 18.1% of PFC cell samples (115 of 636), a cell sample being one cell on one trajectory type.
claims.source: Figure S4A and S4B legend
claims.quote: ramping cells identified here (CA1 ... 81/495 = 16.4% cell samples; PFC ... 115/636 = 18.1% cell samples across all sessions
claims.criterion: A session-averaged linearized rate map on one trajectory is ramping when the linear regression of rate on traversed position toward the reward has Pearson r > 0.5 and p < 0.05, its peak rate is at least 3 Hz, and its peak lies within 20 cm of the reward location (Methods). The paper does not say which positions enter the regression or which cells form the denominator. Readings for the denominator are (a) cell samples of all three sessions pooled ("across all sessions"), (b) N' only ("identified in N'"), each over cells with a valid rate map on the trajectory. The regression runs over the whole trajectory up to the reward well. Reproduced when the two fractions are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: PFC ramping cells generalize their reward representation across environments, whereas CA1 ramping cells remap, and the generalization of ramping cells is similar to that of other cells in each region.
claims.source: Results, PFC spatial map generalizes, while CA1 completely remaps, across contexts, paragraph 3; Figure S4A to S4C
claims.quote: We found that PFC ramping cells generalized reward representations, but the CA1 representation remapped across environments ... In addition, the generalization for reward ramping cells was seen to a similar degree to other cells within regions
claims.criterion: PV similarity per bin as in fig2d-pv-similarity, computed separately for ramping cells (identified in N', figs4-ramping-fraction) and other cells, for N-N' and F-N', bins pooled over rats. Kruskal-Wallis over the eight groups (region, ramping or other, environment pair) with Dunn's post hoc. Reproduced when (1) CA1 ramping F-N' is below CA1 ramping N-N' at p < 0.05; (2) PFC ramping F-N' does not differ from PFC ramping N-N' (p > 0.05); (3) ramping and other cells do not differ (p > 0.05) for the same region and environment pair. Parts (2) and (3) are claims of absence on Dunn's test. Partially reproduced when (1) and (2) hold but not (3).

claims.statement: PV similarity between the environments at the reward wells is the same as at other locations, in both regions.
claims.source: Results, PFC spatial map generalizes, while CA1 completely remaps, across contexts, paragraph 3; Figure S4D
claims.quote: Finally, in both regions, the similarity of population activity across different environments at reward wells was the same as other locations
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the paper's test. PV similarity between the novel and familiar environments per linear bin over the four trajectories, mean over the five rats (fig2d-pv-similarity; the legend shows SEM shading), per region. The legend does not name the novel session; readings are F-N' (the pair of the other panels) and F-N. Grubbs' test (two-sided, alpha 0.05) on the bin values. The legend says "PV similarity was consistent across locations (all p’s > 0.05...)", so the test finds no outlier at any location, not only at the wells. It does not say what one test covers; readings are (a) all bins of a region, (b) the bins of each trajectory in a region. Reproduced when Grubbs' test finds no outlier (p > 0.05) in every test; whether the bins at the reward wells (the trajectory ends) are extreme is reported.

claims.statement: PFC cells show stronger path equivalence (similar firing at the same trajectory phase across trajectory types) than CA1 cells.
claims.source: Figure S5D; Results, Distinct geometries of CA1 and PFC representations, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Stronger path equivalence in PFC than CA1 (***p = 0.0004, ****p < 0.0001, F = 25.37, one-way ANOVA with Tukey’s post hoc)
claims.criterion: The path-equivalent coefficient R of a cell is the median, over the six pairs of the four trajectory types, of the Pearson correlation of rate maps aligned from trajectory start to end (Methods; cal_path_equivalence.m, which reverses the inbound maps, interpolates to the first trajectory's bins and drops NaN bins). Cells are those found in all three sessions. Groups are the six region by session groups (N, F, N'), as the code plots them. One-way ANOVA with Tukey's post hoc. Reproduced when, in each session, PFC R exceeds CA1 R at p < 0.05; partially reproduced when it holds in one or two sessions.

claims.statement: The path-equivalent coefficient of PFC cells is strongly correlated between environments (r = 0.64), more so than that of CA1 cells (r = 0.21).
claims.source: Figure S5E
claims.quote: Path-equivalent coefficient is more strongly correlated between environments for PFC than CA1 (****p < 0.0001, Z = 4.25, comparing correlation coefficients; PFC, r = 0.64, p = 8.43e-21; CA1, r = 0.21, p = 0.035; Pearson correlation)
claims.criterion: R as in figs5d-path-equivalence. The legend does not say which novel session; readings are F against N', F against N. The test comparing the two r values is taken as Fisher's z for independent correlations, the usual test of that name. Reproduced when under one reading both r values are within tolerance and Fisher's z gives p < 0.05 with PFC higher; partially reproduced when PFC r is significantly above CA1 r but a value is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: Path equivalence and task-sequence selectivity are uncorrelated across cells.
claims.source: Figure S5F
claims.quote: Path equivalence and task-sequence selectivity are two uncorrelated measures (n.s., all p’s > 0.05; Pearson correlation)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the paper's test, Pearson correlation per region of R (figs5d-path-equivalence) against SI(IN) and against SI(OUT) (fig3d-selectivity-index), cell samples per session. The paper does not say whether the signed or absolute SI is used; both are run. Reproduced when no correlation has p < 0.05 under the signed reading and under the absolute one; when only one reading finds a correlation the claim is methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Inbound and outbound trajectory selectivity indices are negatively correlated in PFC (r = -0.5), reflecting task-sequence selectivity, and positively correlated in CA1 (r = 0.56), reflecting spatial coverage.
claims.source: Figure 3D; Results, Distinct geometries of CA1 and PFC representations, paragraph 1
claims.quote: As a result, the selectivity indices of IN (IN L vs. IN R ) and OUT (OUT L vs. OUT R ) trajectories exhibited a positive correlation for CA1 and an opposite, negative correlation for PFC
claims.criterion: SI = (FR_L - FR_R)/(FR_L + FR_R) with FR the mean rate of the linearized rate map on the left or right trajectory, for IN (IN_L, IN_R) and OUT (OUT_L, OUT_R) (Methods). As cal_SI.m does, the right map is interpolated to the left map's bins, means over bins valid on both, and a cell sample counts when the peak rate is at least 3 Hz on the IN pair and on the OUT pair (Methods; cal_SI.m's "> 3" is a variant). Cells found in all three sessions. Each dot is a cell sample in one session (legend; Methods, "rate maps in different sessions were analyzed separately"); the paper does not say which sessions enter the panel. Readings are (a) N, F and N' pooled, (b) N' alone, (c) F alone. Reproduced when, under one reading, both r are within tolerance and p < 0.05 with the signs given; when no reading puts both in tolerance but every reading gives PFC r < 0 and CA1 r > 0 at p < 0.05, partially reproduced. The p-values printed "1.35e16" and "1.39e11" have lost their minus signs in the text; they are read as 1.35e-16 and 1.39e-11.

claims.statement: Trajectory selectivity is stable across environments for PFC cells (r = 0.49 between familiar and novel) but not for CA1 cells (r = 0.12, not significant).
claims.source: Figure 3E; Results, Distinct geometries of CA1 and PFC representations, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Finally, consistent with spatial remapping results, these properties were stable across environments for PFC neurons but not CA1
claims.criterion: SI as in fig3d-selectivity-index, with SI(IN) and SI(OUT) pooled in one correlation per region (both shown in the panel, one r given). The legend says "novel environment" without naming the session; readings are N' and N. Reproduced when, under one reading, both r are within tolerance, PFC r has p < 0.05 and CA1 r is not significant (p > 0.05, Pearson, the paper's test). Partially reproduced when the PFC correlation is significant and the CA1 one is not but a value is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: The pseudo-populations pooled across animals for the manifold analyses hold 98 CA1 and 171 PFC cells.
claims.source: STAR Methods, Characterization of neural manifold, paragraph 1; Figure 3F and 3G legend
claims.quote: all spatially-tuned units that were active in both environments were pooled across animals to build a pseudo-population of neurons ( n = 98 CA1 and 171 PFC cells, respectively)
claims.criterion: The Methods select spatially tuned units active in both environments; the code (cal_UMAP.m with matchidx_acrossep.m) takes every unit found in all three sessions that passes the inclusion rules, with no tuning threshold. Readings are (a) the Methods' (units active in N, F and N' with a linearized peak rate of at least 3 Hz in at least one session), (b) the code's. Reproduced when both counts are within tolerance under one reading; the reading that matches is used for the manifold claims, and if both match, (a).

claims.statement: UMAP embeddings show that PFC population activity lies on a ring-shaped manifold, whereas the CA1 manifold has a double V shape resembling the W-maze.
claims.source: Figure 3F and 3G; Results, Distinct geometries of CA1 and PFC representations, paragraph 2
claims.quote: This unsupervised algorithm revealed that the population activity of PFC cells resides on a ring-shaped manifold, making it distinct from the CA1 neural manifold with a double “V” shape that topologically resembles the physical spatial structure of the W-maze
claims.criterion: Embedding as the Methods give it. Single-trial linearized rate maps of the pseudo-population cells (manifold-cell-counts) in N', with the minimum number of trials per trajectory type across animals from the first trial, binned at 1 cm. Bins with fewer than 5 active cells are dropped. UMAP with 3 dimensions, cosine metric, 50 neighbours, min_dist 0.6. The code bins each trajectory at 1/200 of its normalized length (201 bins), a variant. The random seed and the UMAP implementation are standard choices (the paper's fitted templates are not public; the code notes that a new fit gives a quantitatively similar result). The paper gives no measure of the ring or V shapes; it validates the embedding by the distance tests of Figure 3H to 3J. The embedding is shown, and the outcome is that of fig3h-inseq-outseq-distance and fig3i-phase-location-distance (reproduced when both are, partially when one is).

claims.statement: In the PFC manifold, trajectories of the same task sequence (InSeq) are closer than trajectories out of sequence (OutSeq); in the CA1 manifold, OutSeq pairs with the same spatial coverage are closer than InSeq pairs.
claims.source: Figure 3H; Results, Distinct geometries of CA1 and PFC representations, paragraph 3
claims.quote: we found that the distance between two InSeq trajectories was significantly smaller than two OutSeq ones in the PFC manifold, whereas OutSeq pairs with same spatial coverages had smaller distances than InSeq pairs in the CA1 manifold
claims.criterion: Embedding as in fig3fg-manifold-shapes. InSeq pairs are OUT_L with IN_R and OUT_R with IN_L; OutSeq pairs are OUT_L with IN_L and OUT_R with IN_R. For every pair of single trials of the two types, the mean Euclidean distance over matched bins in the 3D embedding (cal_UMAP_INSeq_distance.m). The Methods do not say how bins are matched for this panel; the code matches by spatial location for CA1 and by trajectory phase for PFC, which is followed. Matching both regions the same way (by phase, by location) is shown as a variant. Rank-sum test of InSeq against OutSeq trial-pair distances per region. Reproduced when PFC InSeq < OutSeq and CA1 OutSeq < InSeq, each at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: PFC neural states at the same trajectory phase are closer than those at the same spatial location, while CA1 shows the opposite.
claims.source: Figure 3I; Results, Distinct geometries of CA1 and PFC representations, paragraph 3
claims.quote: As a result, the distances between PFC neural states for the same trajectory phases were significantly smaller than those for the same spatial locations, while the opposite is true for CA1
claims.criterion: Embedding as in fig3fg-manifold-shapes. The Methods take same-phase distances from pairs of the same task sequence and same-location distances from pairs on the same side of the maze, which is the main reading. The code (cal_UMAP_TrajPhase_vs_Spatial_distance.m) takes both from the same-side pairs (OUT_L with IN_L, OUT_R with IN_R), aligned by phase or by location, a variant. Distances are Euclidean in the 3D embedding between all states at the matched bins of the two types, pooled. Rank-sum test of phase against location distances per region. Reproduced when PFC phase < location and CA1 location < phase, each at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The PFC manifold is preserved across environments (F states lie closer to N' states than cell-ID shuffles do), while the distortion of the CA1 manifold is similar to that of random shuffles.
claims.source: Figure 3J; Results, Distinct geometries of CA1 and PFC representations, paragraph 3
claims.quote: We found that the geometric structure of the PFC manifold was largely preserved across environments, whereas the distortion of the CA1 manifold was similar to that from random shuffles
claims.criterion: F single-trial activity embedded with the UMAP fitted on N' (template transform, Methods). For each N' state, the mean Euclidean distance to all F states of the same trajectory type and location (Methods; cal_UMAP_FNdistance.m). The chance level shuffles cell identities of the N' activity and embeds it with the same fit; the code draws a new permutation for each trial and runs it once (cal_UMAP_FNdistance_shuffle.m), which is followed. Rank-sum of real against shuffle distances per region. Reproduced when PFC F-N' distances are below the shuffle at p < 0.05 and CA1 F-N' distances do not differ from the shuffle (p > 0.05, a claim of absence on the paper's test).

claims.statement: The distance relationships of Figure 3H to 3J hold in the original high-dimensional neural space.
claims.source: Figure S6; Results, Distinct geometries of CA1 and PFC representations, paragraph 3
claims.quote: In all the cases above, the distance relationship of neural states, which determines the representational geometry, was preserved between the low-dimensional manifold space and the original high-dimensional neural space
claims.criterion: As fig3h-inseq-outseq-distance, fig3i-phase-location-distance and fig3j-familiar-novel-manifold, with Euclidean distances between population vectors of the pseudo-population (Methods, "distance was computed identically, except for the number of dimensions"; Figure3/Supplemental/cal_PV_*.m). Reproduced when all three reproduce in the neural space; partially reproduced when one or two do.

claims.statement: In PFC, the cross-condition generalization performance (CCGP) for trajectory phase, task sequence and environment is high and above trial-label shuffles for every decoder.
claims.source: Figure 4D; Results, Distinct abstraction in CA1 and PFC, paragraph 2
claims.quote: We found that the CCGP for all three task variables showed high accuracy for PFC
claims.criterion: Clusters are the N' (and for the environment, F) embedded states at 20% to 30% and 70% to 80% of trajectory length from the start of each of the 4 trajectory types, 8 clusters (Methods; cal_all_dichotomies.m); features are the 3 UMAP coordinates. Linear C-SVM (libsvm, linear kernel, default cost 1), accuracy balanced over the two classes (decoding_CCGP_linearSVM_simple.m). Trajectory phase is trained on 3 trajectory types and tested on the fourth (4 decoders). Task sequence (IN_R and OUT_L against IN_L and OUT_R) follows CCGP_taskSeq.m. Each decoder is tested on the two outbound clusters (OUT_L, OUT_R) or the two inbound clusters (IN_L, IN_R) at one phase, and trained on the four clusters of the other direction (4 decoders); the Methods' "holding out two clusters belonging to the same trajectory phase of two different OutSeq trajectories" allows this reading, and training on all six clusters left is a variant. Environment applies the decoders trained in N' to F (8 decoders, CCGP_environment.m). Significance permutes the labels of training and test sets 1,000 times; p is the fraction of shuffles above the real CCGP. Reproduced when every one of the 16 PFC decoders has p < 0.001 (no shuffle above it).

claims.statement: In CA1, CCGP for trajectory phase, task sequence and environment is at or below chance by the trial-label permutation test.
claims.source: Figure 4D; Results, Distinct abstraction in CA1 and PFC, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Note that all dichotomies can be accurately decoded in PFC (****p < 0.001) but not in CA1 (n.s., p > 0.05 , trial-label permutation test)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the paper's test. CCGP as in fig4d-pfc-ccgp for the 16 CA1 decoders. Reproduced when no CA1 decoder has p < 0.05; the CCGP values are reported either way.

claims.statement: Against a geometric random model that keeps within-condition noise but destroys the geometry, PFC CCGP is significant while CA1 CCGP is not.
claims.source: Figure S7B; Results, Distinct abstraction in CA1 and PFC, paragraph 2
claims.quote: CCGP for trajectory phases (circles), task sequences (triangles), and environments (diamonds; horizontal lines, median) against the null-distributions of the geometric random model (red horizontal line shown the 95th percentile; n.s., p > 0.05, **p = 0.0026, ****p <0.0001)
claims.criterion: Each cluster's noise cloud (trial-by-trial values of the condition) is rotated by permuting the axes of the firing rate space, separately per cluster, and CCGP is recomputed (fig4d-pfc-ccgp), 100 times (Methods). No code for this model is in the repository. The paper does not say in which space the axes are permuted or what is done with the cluster centres (the legend of S7A says "rotation-translation"). Readings are (a) permute the 3 UMAP coordinates of each cluster's points about its centroid; (b) permute the neuron axes of each cluster's population vectors and embed them with the N' fit. Reproduced when, under each reading, the PFC CCGP of each variable exceeds the 95th percentile of its null and no CA1 CCGP does.

claims.statement: With traditional cross-validated decoders, most of the 35 dichotomies of the 8 clusters are decoded accurately in both CA1 and PFC, with similar accuracy in the two regions.
claims.source: Figure S7D; Results, Distinct abstraction in CA1 and PFC, paragraph 2
claims.quote: we found that most of the dichotomies were accurately separated in both CA1 and PFC, suggesting that both regions contain a similar amount of decodable variables
claims.criterion: The 35 balanced dichotomies of the 8 clusters of fig4d-pfc-ccgp (4 against 4), each decoded by a linear C-SVM with 4-fold cross-validation (libsvm -v 4; decoding_dichotomy_*.m) on the 3 UMAP coordinates; significance by 1,000 trial-label shuffles, p the fraction of shuffles above. Reproduced when more than half of the 35 dichotomies have p < 0.05 in each region ("most") and the rank-sum test of PFC against CA1 accuracies does not find a difference (p > 0.05, a claim of absence on the paper's test).

claims.statement: Superficial stimulation sites lay 0.41 +/- 0.04 mm and deep sites 1.06 +/- 0.05 mm below the brain surface.
claims.source: Results, Global evoked responses are modulated by the depth of the cortical stimulation site, paragraph 3
claims.quote: in layer 2/3 (superficial: 0.41±0.04 mm below the brain surface) or in layer 5/6 (deep: 1.06±0.05 mm below the brain surface
claims.criterion: Mean over stimulation sites of the depth below the brain surface recorded for the stimulating electrode. The Methods give per-group depths too (MOs L2/3 0.37 +/- 0.04, MOs L5/6 1.15 +/- 0.06, SSp L2/3 0.47 +/- 0.06, SSp L5/6 0.92 +/- 0.05 mm), which are reported as a variant. Reproduced when both means are within tolerance.

claims.statement: After artifact masking and visual inspection, an average of 23 +/- 4 of the 30 EEG electrodes per subject were kept as artifact-free.
claims.source: Methods, Data processing, EEG
claims.quote: leaving an average of 23±4 artifact-free electrodes out of 30 for each subject
claims.criterion: Tested only if the dataset marks good or bad EEG electrodes; the paper's selection is by eye and cannot be redone. The mean over subjects of the number marked good is compared with 23, tolerance the stated spread of 4.

claims.statement: Deep (layer 5/6) stimulation in the awake state usually evokes an ERP with two prominent peaks, near 25 ms and near 180 ms; the late component is not evident with superficial stimulation, in MOs or SSp.
claims.source: Results, Global evoked responses are modulated by the depth of the cortical stimulation site, paragraph 3; Figure 1C and 1D
claims.quote: when we stimulated layer 5/6 during the awake period, we usually observed two prominent peaks in the ERP: an initial response around 25 ms and a secondary peak at around 180 ms post-stimulation ... The early component was preserved, whereas the second, late component was not evident when stimulating superficially in either area
claims.criterion: The paper gives no peak detection method. ERP is the trial average of the average-referenced EEG (0.1 to 100 Hz, third-order Butterworth, epochs -2 to +2 s, -2 to +2 ms excluded; Methods, EEG and ERPs); global field power (GFP) is the SD across good electrodes at each time, z-scored to -2 to 0 s (Methods, ERP magnitude and duration). Readings of a peak, in windows taken from the paper's own phases (initial excitation 2 to 25 ms, rebound 150 to 300 ms, chosen to align with the ERP peaks; Results, paragraph before Figure 4) and from the stated latencies; (a) a local maximum of the z-scored GFP above z = 3 within 2 to 50 ms and another within 150 to 300 ms; (b) the same with windows 2 to 25 ms and 100 to 300 ms (the late window of Figure 7G). Reproduced when, under one reading, more than half of deep sites show both peaks and more than half of superficial sites show no late peak.

claims.statement: In the example deep MOs session, the ERP lasts 1.01 s and has a magnitude of 11.13 SD.s.
claims.source: Figure 1, figure supplement 1B legend
claims.quote: The duration of this example is 1.01 s ... The magnitude of this example is 11.13 SD∙s
claims.criterion: Duration and magnitude as in fig1e-erp-duration. The paper names the example only as the deep MOs subject of Figure 1C and 1D (bottom left); a session is accepted as the example if it is a deep MOs session and it matches the paper's description, and the author reports how it was identified. Reproduced when one deep MOs session matches both values under one reading of duration and magnitude; blocked if no session can be identified as the example.

claims.statement: ERPs evoked by superficial stimulation were shorter than those evoked by deep stimulation (0.4 +/- 0.0 against 0.5 +/- 0.1 s), but the difference was not significant.
claims.source: Results, Global evoked responses are modulated by the depth of the cortical stimulation site, paragraph 3; Figure 1E
claims.quote: The total duration of the ERP was shorter when stimulating superficial layers compared to deep layers although not significant (mean ERP duration for superficial stimulation: 0.4±0.0 s; deep stimulation: 0.5±0.1 s; Student’s two-tailed t-test, p=0.0843
claims.criterion: The superficial SEM is printed as 0.0, so its tolerance is the printing precision (half of 0.1 s). Per session, GFP of the awake ERP (as in fig1d-two-erp-peaks), z-scored to the baseline -2 to 0 s; duration is the time the z-scored GFP exceeds z = 3 within 0 to +2 s (Methods, ERP magnitude and duration). Open, with readings; (a) the total time above z = 3; (b) the time from onset to the last sample above z = 3 (the legend of Figure 1, figure supplement 1 marks the duration by a single vertical line). A claim of absence for the depth effect, judged on the paper's test, scipy ttest_ind (two-sided, equal variances) on per-session durations. Reproduced when both means are within tolerance under one reading and the t-test gives p >= 0.05 with superficial below deep; the p-value is reported either way.

claims.statement: ERPs evoked by superficial stimulation had a significantly smaller normalized magnitude than those evoked by deep stimulation (3.3 +/- 0.8 against 6.2 +/- 0.9 SD.s).
claims.source: Results, Global evoked responses are modulated by the depth of the cortical stimulation site, paragraph 3; Figure 1F
claims.quote: When stimulating superficially, ERPs had a significantly smaller normalized magnitude compared to stimulating deep layers (mean ERP magnitude for superficial stimulation: 3.3±0.8 SD∙s; deep stimulation: 6.2±0.9 SD∙s; Student’s two-tailed t-test, p=0.0354
claims.criterion: Per session, z-scored GFP as in fig1e-erp-duration. The Methods and the figure supplement legend differ on the magnitude; readings (a) the area between the z-scored GFP and z = 3 where it is above 3, within 0 to +2 s, in SD.s (Figure 1, figure supplement 1B legend); (b) that area divided by the area under the baseline window (-2 to 0 s), as the Methods text says. Reproduced when, under one reading, both means are within tolerance and scipy ttest_ind (two-sided) gives p < 0.05 with superficial smaller.

claims.statement: The amplitude of the first ERP peak decays with distance from the stimulation site and eventually flips sign, while the second component changes in a different spatial pattern.
claims.source: Results, Global evoked responses are modulated by the depth of the cortical stimulation site, paragraph 3; Figure 1, figure supplement 2
claims.quote: The amplitude of the first peak in the ERP decays systematically when moving away from the stimulation site until it eventually flips its sign, most likely reflecting volume conduction
claims.criterion: The paper shows one deep MOs session as an interpolated map and gives no measure. Signed ERP voltage at each good electrode at the time of the early GFP peak (2 to 50 ms), with the sign set so that the electrode nearest the stimulation site is positive, against distance from the stimulation site on the skull. Readings; (a) the example deep MOs session; (b) every deep session. Reproduced when, under one reading (for (b) in more than half of sessions), the Spearman correlation of signed amplitude with distance is negative with p < 0.05 and both signs occur. Needs electrode and stimulation coordinates; blocked without them. The second component's pattern is described, not tested.

claims.statement: Stimulating superficial MOs evoked a local spike, LFP and CSD response followed by quiescence of 94.2 +/- 16.1 ms in MO neurons, with minimal to no responses in other sampled areas.
claims.source: Results, The spiking response pattern of the stimulated cortex echoes the ERP, paragraph 2; Figure 2C and 2D to 2F, left
claims.quote: Stimulating superficial MOs evoked a local spike, LFP and CSD response, followed by a period of quiescence lasting 94.2±16.1 ms in MO neurons
claims.criterion: The paper does not define how quiescence is measured, and the Discussion gives a different value for the same quantity (44.3 +/- 16.4 ms), so both values are readings of the target. Population rate is the mean over MO RS units of the firing rate in the awake state, one value per superficial MOs session. Readings of quiescence; (a) the time after the initial excitation (after 25 ms) for which the population rate stays below its pre-stimulus mean; (b) the time for which it stays at zero spikes. Bin width is not given; 1 ms and 5 ms bins are both run. Reproduced when the session mean is within tolerance of 94.2 or of 44.3 (tolerance 16.4) under one reading. The part on other areas is not judged here; spiking outside the stimulated area is tested in fig3d-magnitudes, where the paper finds superficial stimulation did modulate non-stimulated LFP and CSD.

claims.statement: Stimulating deep MOs evokes in local cortex an initial excitation within 25 ms (peak population rate 38.1 +/- 4.2 Hz), quiescence of 125.0 +/- 5.5 ms, and a longer rebound excitation (peak 7.9 +/- 0.7 Hz).
claims.source: Results, The spiking response pattern of the stimulated cortex echoes the ERP, paragraph 2; Figure 2C, right
claims.quote: an initial excitation within 25 ms (peak population firing rate 38.1±4.2 Hz), followed by quiescence (duration 125.0±5.5 ms) and a longer period of strong excitation (peak population firing rate 7.9±0.7 Hz
claims.criterion: Population rate is the mean firing rate over RS units of the stimulated cortex, per session, peak taken within 2 to 25 ms and within 150 to 300 ms (the paper's windows for initial and rebound excitation). Quiescence as in fig2c-superficial-quiescence, readings (a) and (b); the Discussion gives 127.8 +/- 4.1 ms for the same quantity, accepted as an alternative target. Open; which sessions (readings, deep MOs sessions as in Figure 2, or all deep sessions) and bin width (1 ms and 5 ms). Reproduced when all three values are within tolerance under one combination of readings; partially reproduced when the triphasic sequence (peak above baseline, a period below baseline, a second peak above baseline) holds in more than half of deep sessions but a value is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: The triphasic pattern of deep stimulation is replicated, shifted in time, in SM-TH; a brief excitation (peak 22.3 +/- 3.2 Hz), 74.6 +/- 15.5 ms of suppression, and rebound excitation (peak 14.7 +/- 1.0 Hz). It is absent with superficial stimulation.
claims.source: Results, CTC interactions underlie features of the ERPs, paragraph 1; Figure 2F
claims.quote: we observed a brief excitation (peak population firing rate 22.3±3.2 Hz), a 74.6±15.5 ms long period of suppression, followed by rebound excitation (peak population firing rate 14.7±1.0 Hz). This is not the case when stimulating superficial layers
claims.criterion: As fig2c-deep-triphasic-cortex, with all SM-TH units (thalamic units are not split into RS and FS in Figure 2F), early peak within 2 to 25 ms and rebound peak within 75 to 300 ms (the late window of Figure 5F). The paper gives no measure for the absence of the pattern with superficial stimulation; readings (a) no peak of the SM-TH population rate in 75 to 300 ms above z = 3 of its pre-stimulus rate (the z = 3 threshold of the paper's ERP duration); (b) no SM-TH unit significantly increased in 150 to 300 ms by the test of fig4ad-initial-excitation. Reproduced when all three values are within tolerance under one combination of readings and more than half of the superficial sessions show no rebound under that reading; partially reproduced when the pattern holds but a value is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: In the example deep MOs session, evoked LFP, CSD and spiking magnitudes are large near the stimulation site (54.0, 51.4 and 30.9 SD.s in MO) and smaller in distant VIS (18.0, 4.8 and 1.8 SD.s).
claims.source: Results, Global ERPs are associated with widespread evoked cortical activity, paragraph 1; Figure 3A to 3C
claims.quote: The magnitude of the LFP near the stimulation site is greater than background activity (54.0 SD∙s in MO) and decays with distance from the stimulation site (18.0 SD∙s in VIS
claims.criterion: Magnitudes as in fig3d-magnitudes, for the session identified in fig1-supp1-example. Reproduced when the MO value exceeds the VIS value for all three signals and all six values are within tolerance under one combination of readings; partially reproduced when the ordering holds but a value is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: Superficial stimulation modulated local LFP, CSD and spiking and non-local LFP and CSD, but evoked no spiking outside the stimulated area; deep stimulation evoked LFP, CSD and spiking both locally and in non-stimulated cortical regions.
claims.source: Results, Global ERPs are associated with widespread evoked cortical activity, paragraph 2; Figure 3D
claims.quote: Together, these data show that cortical stimulation evoked widespread changes in the LFP and CSD, but only evoked ipsilateral cortical spiking outside of the stimulated area when stimulating deep layers
claims.criterion: Method from Methods, LFP, CSD, and population spiking magnitude, and Data processing. LFP after artifact masking, downsampled to 1.25 kHz, first-order Butterworth high-pass (cutoff not given; open, readings 0.1 Hz and 1 Hz), re-referenced to the median of channels in the ACSF above the brain; CSD as the second spatial derivative after Chebyshev channel rejection (+/- 7 SD), smoothing 8 ms in time and 26 then 4 channels in space; spiking as single RS unit spike density functions (kernel not given; open, readings Gaussian SD 5 ms and 10 ms). For a region, the spatial average of the rectified trial-averaged signal over its channels (units) in all layers except layer 1, z-scored to the pre-stimulus baseline (window not given; open, readings -2 to 0 s and -0.5 to 0 s), and its area under the curve from 0 to +0.5 s; background by shuffling the onset time per trial 1000 times; magnitude is (AUC minus the mean of the shuffled AUCs) over their SD. How onsets are shuffled is not given; readings, uniform within the epoch (-2 to +2 s) and uniform over the recording. Each group of values is tested against zero with the two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test (scipy), Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the tests. The unit of the test is open; the printed p-values (0.0313, 0.0078, 1.221E-4, 3.052E-5) are the smallest exact two-sided signed-rank values for n = 6, 8, 14 and 16, which indicates one value per mouse; readings (a) one value per mouse, non-stimulated regions averaged within mouse; (b) one value per region. Reproduced when, under one combination of readings, every test the paper finds significant has corrected p < 0.05 with a positive median, superficial non-stimulated spiking is not significant (claim of absence, judged on this test), and all 11 medians are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the significance pattern holds but a median is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: Figure 4 rests on 870 RS units from stimulated and 4110 from non-stimulated cortex in 7 mice with superficial stimulation, and 2559 and 9363 in 17 mice with deep stimulation.
claims.source: Figure 4 legend
claims.quote: Panels A–C are derived from 870 RS neurons from stimulated cortex and 4110 RS neurons from non-stimulated cortical regions in N=7 mice and panels D–F from 2559 RS neurons from stimulated cortex and 9363 RS neurons from non-stimulated cortical regions in N=17 mice
claims.criterion: Counts of high-quality RS units (waveform duration > 0.4 ms) in stimulated and non-stimulated ipsilateral cortex, summed over sessions of each depth. Reproduced when all four are within tolerance and the session counts are 7 and 17.

claims.statement: In the initial excitation window (2 to 25 ms), the fraction of activated RS neurons is always higher in stimulated cortex than elsewhere; across 24 animals an average of 0.5% (0 to 2.6%) of neurons in non-stimulated regions were modulated against 17.8% (0 to 83.3%) in stimulated cortex, and about three times more cortical neurons respond to deep than to superficial stimulation.
claims.source: Results, Global ERPs are associated with widespread evoked cortical activity, paragraph 4; Figure 4A and 4D; Results, The spiking response pattern of the stimulated cortex echoes the ERP, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Indeed, across all 24 animals, only an average of 0.5% (minimum 0% and maximum 2.6%) of the neurons was modulated in the initial excitation, compared to an average of 17.8% (minimum 0% and maximum 83.3%) in stimulated cortex
claims.criterion: Modulated neurons by the Methods (Significantly modulated neurons); per RS unit, spike counts in the post-stimulus window and a pre-stimulus window of the same length, per trial, two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at 0.05 over all RS units in all areas of interest, sign from the mean change. Open, with readings; pre-stimulus window (a) immediately before onset with the same length (-23 to 0 ms for 2 to 25 ms), (b) mirrored about onset (-25 to -2 ms); FDR family (a) per session and window, (b) all sessions pooled per window. Units with no spikes in either window are not modulated (a test that scipy cannot run is counted as not significant, a standard choice). Fractions are per area per session; the non-stimulated value is per non-stimulated region (readings, per region, or pooled over the non-stimulated regions of a session). The "about three times" is the ratio of mean fractions of significantly responding stimulated-cortex units, deep over superficial, in the 2 to 25 ms window (reading (a)) or in any of the three windows (reading (b)), reproduced between 2 and 4. Reproduced when, under one combination of readings, the fraction of significantly increased units in stimulated cortex exceeds that in non-stimulated regions in every session (the paper's "activated"), the means and maxima are within tolerance (minima 0) and the ratio is between 2 and 4; partially reproduced when the ordering holds but values do not.

claims.statement: In the off period (25 to 150 ms) very few neurons increased their spiking (mean 0.4%, maximum 2.8%), spiking was significantly reduced in 18 of 22 subjects, and non-stimulated areas showed decreases only with deep stimulation (mean 10.1%, maximum 55.7%).
claims.source: Results, Global ERPs are associated with widespread evoked cortical activity, paragraph 4; Figure 4B and 4E
claims.quote: There were very few neurons with increased spiking, regardless of stimulation depth and area (mean 0.4%, minimum 0%, and maximum 2.8%; Figure 4B and E ). In contrast, spiking in 18/22 subjects was significantly reduced from baseline following either superficial or deep stimulation. Interestingly, some non-stimulated areas showed decreased spiking but only in response to deep stimulation (mean 10.1%, minimum 0%, and maximum 55.7%)
claims.criterion: Modulated units as in fig4ad-initial-excitation, window 25 to 150 ms. "Spiking significantly reduced" in a subject is open; readings (a) at least one RS unit of the stimulated cortex significantly decreased; (b) at least one in any cortical area; (c) the population count of the stimulated cortex lower after than before by the same signed-rank test. The count of 22 subjects (against 24 elsewhere) is not explained and is reported. Reproduced when, under one combination of readings, the five values are within tolerance and no superficial session has decreased units in non-stimulated areas; partially reproduced when the qualitative pattern (few increases, most subjects reduced, non-stimulated decreases only with deep) holds.

claims.statement: In the rebound window (150 to 300 ms), all 16 deep-stimulation subjects showed significant rebound excitation in stimulated cortex against 1 of 6 superficial subjects; 6 of 16 deep subjects showed it in non-stimulated areas, and none of 7 superficial subjects did.
claims.source: Results, Global ERPs are associated with widespread evoked cortical activity, paragraph 4; Figure 4C and 4F
claims.quote: All 16 subjects who received deep stimulation showed significant rebound excitation in the stimulated cortex, whereas only 1/6 superficial stimulation subjects did ( Figure 4C and F ). Some subjects who received deep stimulation showed significant rebound excitation in the non-stimulated areas (6/16; Figure 4F ), but it was nonexistent amongst the superficial stimulation subjects (0/7
claims.criterion: Modulated units as in fig4ad-initial-excitation, window 150 to 300 ms; a subject shows rebound excitation in an area when at least one of its RS units there is significantly increased (reading (a)); or (b) the population spike count of the area higher after than before by the same signed-rank test, as reading (c) of fig4be-off-period. The paper defines a subject's rebound in neither way. Counts are reported against the denominators found; the paper's denominators (16, 6, 7) differ from Figure 4's N of 17 and 7. Reproduced when, under one reading, at least 90% of deep subjects and at most a sixth of superficial subjects show rebound in stimulated cortex, the non-stimulated deep count is within 10% of 6/16 as a fraction, and no superficial subject shows it in non-stimulated areas.

claims.statement: FS neurons behave like RS neurons in their modulation by stimulation depth and time window.
claims.source: Results, Global ERPs are associated with widespread evoked cortical activity, paragraph 3; Figure 4, figure supplement 1
claims.quote: We separately analyzed FS neurons and found they behave like RS neurons
claims.criterion: The analyses of fig4ad, fig4be and fig4cf repeated on FS units (waveform duration <= 0.4 ms; FDR over FS units). The paper gives no test of likeness. Reproduced when the qualitative findings of those three claims (stimulated above non-stimulated at 2 to 25 ms; decreases dominate at 25 to 150 ms; rebound in stimulated cortex in most deep and few superficial sessions) hold for FS units, and the unit counts (legend, 7 superficial and 16 deep mice) are within tolerance.

claims.statement: SM-TH neurons were almost eight times more likely to be modulated by deep than by superficial stimulation (37.9 +/- 20.6% against 5.0 +/- 4.1%).
claims.source: Results, CTC interactions underlie features of the ERPs, paragraph 1; Figure 5A
claims.quote: the neurons were almost eight times more likely to be modulated by deep than superficial stimulation (superficial: 5.0±4.1% of SM-TH population, N=5; deep: 37.9±20.6%, N=14; Student’s two-tailed t-test, p=0.0037
claims.criterion: The spread is taken as the SEM, as the Methods say text values are mean +/- SEM. Units are all high-quality SM-TH units (the legend does not restrict them to RS), tested as in fig4ad-initial-excitation. The window "between 2 ms and 300 ms" is open; readings (a) one window 2 to 300 ms against a matched pre-stimulus window; (b) a unit significantly increased or decreased in any of the three windows 2 to 25, 25 to 150, 150 to 300 ms. Reproduced when, under one reading, both means are within tolerance and scipy ttest_ind (two-sided) gives p < 0.05 with deep higher.

claims.statement: Deep stimulation was significantly more likely than superficial stimulation to evoke SM-TH bursts 75 to 300 ms after the stimulus (median 0.12 [0.02 to 0.2] against 0 [0 to 0.02]).
claims.source: Results, CTC interactions underlie features of the ERPs, paragraph 2; Figure 5C
claims.quote: deep stimulation had a significantly higher likelihood of evoking bursts (superficial stimulation: median 0 [0–0.02 IQR]; deep stimulation: median 0.12 [0.02–0.2 IQR]; Mann-Whitney U test, p=0.0258
claims.criterion: A burst is two or more consecutive spikes with inter-spike interval below 4 ms preceded by at least 100 ms of silence (Results, paragraph 2 of CTC interactions), counted when its first spike falls 75 to 300 ms after onset. The probability is the fraction of trials (Figure 5C legend); open whether (a) per session, the fraction of trials in which any SM-TH unit bursts, or (b) the mean over SM-TH units of each unit's fraction of trials with a burst. Reproduced when, under one reading, the deep median is within tolerance, the superficial median is 0, and the two-sided Mann-Whitney U test (scipy) gives p < 0.05 with deep higher.

claims.statement: During the initial excitation, stimulated cortical RS cells fired first (median first-spike latency 4.4 +/- 0.9 ms), followed by the thalamus (11.4 +/- 2.8 ms), a mean difference of 6.9 ms.
claims.source: Results, CTC interactions underlie features of the ERPs, paragraph 3; Figure 5E
claims.quote: during the initial excitation, stimulated cortical RS cells had a median first-spike latency of 4.4±0.9 ms, with the thalamic population following at 11.4±2.8 ms (mean latency difference of 6.9 ms; paired t-test, p=4.838E-6
claims.criterion: Responsive units are those significantly increased in the 2 to 25 ms window (as in fig4ad-initial-excitation; RS units in stimulated cortex, all units in SM-TH). Per unit, the first spike from 2 to 25 ms on each trial with a spike; per population, the median latency over its units. Open; the per-unit summary over trials, readings median and mean. The Discussion gives 6.7 ms for the difference, accepted as an alternative target. Reproduced when, under one reading, the three values are within tolerance and the paired t-test (scipy ttest_rel) gives p < 0.05 with SM-TH later.

claims.statement: During the rebound, the order flips; SM-TH fires first (median latency 148.2 +/- 21.2 ms) and cortex follows (184.2 +/- 17.3 ms), a mean difference of -36.0 ms.
claims.source: Results, CTC interactions underlie features of the ERPs, paragraph 3; Figure 5F
claims.quote: During the rebound excitation window, the temporal relationship flipped: the thalamic population had a median rebound spike latency of 148.2±21.2 ms, with cortex following at 184.2±17.3 ms (mean latency difference –36.0 ms; paired t-test, p=2.136E-4
claims.criterion: As fig5e-early-latency, with the first spike in the late window. The window is 75 to 300 ms in the Figure 5F legend and 100 to 300 ms in the Figure 7G legend; both are run. Responsive units are open; readings (a) significantly increased in 150 to 300 ms; (b) significantly increased in the late window used. The Discussion gives 37.0 ms for the difference, accepted as an alternative target. Reproduced when, under one combination of readings, the three values are within tolerance and ttest_rel gives p < 0.05 with SM-TH earlier.

claims.statement: After deep MOs stimulation, a pronounced current sink near the border of layers 2/3 and 5 in MOs coincided with the thalamic rebound burst (about 180 ms), consistently across subjects.
claims.source: Results, CTC interactions underlie features of the ERPs, paragraph 4; Figure 6A
claims.quote: We observed a pronounced current sink near the border of layers 2/3 and 5 in MOs (near the deep stimulation site) that coincided with the timing of the thalamic rebound burst (~180 ms). This was consistent across subjects (N=9, Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p<0.05
claims.criterion: CSD as in fig3d-magnitudes, trial-averaged per session in MOs after deep MOs stimulation. Each trace is mapped to 10 bins per layer by a non-linear transform (Methods, Population CSD; the transform is not given, reading, linear interpolation within each layer's CCF bounds); per bin, a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test across sessions against zero at p < 0.05, uncorrected; isolated significant bins (not neighboured by significant bins in both space and time) removed. Reproduced when a cluster of significant negative bins (sinks) lies within the bins adjacent to the L2/3 to L5 border and spans about 180 ms (the paper's timing), inside the rebound window 150 to 300 ms of Figure 4.

claims.statement: On single trials, EEG signals correlate more strongly with the CSD of deep than of superficial cortical layers.
claims.source: Results, CTC interactions underlie features of the ERPs, paragraph 4; Figure 6, figure supplement 1
claims.quote: We also analyzed the correlation between the ERP and laminar CSD on a trial-by-trial basis and found that the EEG signals correlated more strongly with CSD of deep compared to superficial layers
claims.criterion: The legend gives "time-resolved correlation of EEG with layer-specific CSD power" across trials, Pearson and Spearman, N=9, and no test. Open; the EEG signal (readings, GFP; the electrode nearest the stimulation site), CSD power (reading, squared CSD averaged over the layer's bins) and the time resolution (reading, each sample from 0 to 0.5 s). Reproduced when, under one reading, the mean over sessions of the across-trial correlation, averaged over 0 to 0.5 s, is higher for L5 and L6 than for L1 and L2/3 with both Pearson and Spearman.

claims.statement: On a trial-by-trial basis, the fraction of bursting SM-TH neurons correlated with the cortical population firing rate in the rebound window (8 of 13 mice significant, mean r 0.4 +/- 0.04).
claims.source: Results, CTC interactions underlie features of the ERPs, paragraph 5; Figure 6B
claims.quote: The fraction of bursting SM-TH neurons was correlated with the cortical population firing rate (8/13 mice with a significant correlation [p<0.05], mean Pearson r value: 0.4±0.04
claims.criterion: Per deep session, per trial in 75 to 300 ms; the fraction of SM-TH units with a burst (definition as in fig5c-burst-probability-depth) against the peak cortical population rate (Figure 6B legend; mean over stimulated-cortex RS units, bin width open, readings 5 ms and 10 ms). Pearson r and its p per session; p < 0.05 counts a session as significant (the paper's threshold). Reproduced when, under one reading, the mean r is within tolerance and the count of significant sessions is within the tolerance of 8 of 13 (proportionally, if the number of sessions differs).

claims.statement: The cortical population firing rate correlated trial by trial with the magnitude of the late ERP component (9 of 13 mice significant, mean r 0.5 +/- 0.04).
claims.source: Results, CTC interactions underlie features of the ERPs, paragraph 5; Figure 6C
claims.quote: The cortical population firing rate was likewise correlated with the magnitude of the second, late component in the ERP (9/13 mice with a significant correlation [p<0.05], mean Pearson r value: 0.5±0.04
claims.criterion: As fig6b-bursts-cortical-rate, against the single-trial peak amplitude of the late ERP component in 75 to 300 ms (Figure 6C legend). How the single-trial amplitude is taken is open; readings (a) the peak of the single-trial GFP (SD across good electrodes); (b) the peak absolute voltage at the electrode with the largest trial-averaged late component. Reproduced when, under one reading, the mean r is within tolerance and the count of sessions with p < 0.05 is within the tolerance of 9 of 13 (proportionally, if the number of sessions differs).

claims.statement: The late ERP component correlated trial by trial with the fraction of bursting SM-TH neurons in every mouse (13 of 13, mean r 0.5 +/- 0.07), much more than with the SM-TH population firing rate.
claims.source: Results, CTC interactions underlie features of the ERPs, paragraph 5; Figure 6, figure supplement 2
claims.quote: the late component in the ERP was significantly correlated with the fraction of bursting SM-TH neurons (13/13 mice with a significant correlation [p<0.05], mean Pearson r value: 0.5±0.07 ... much more so than it was correlated with the SM-TH population firing rate
claims.criterion: Late ERP amplitude as in fig6c-cortical-rate-late-erp, burst fraction as in fig6b-bursts-cortical-rate, and peak SM-TH population rate (mean over SM-TH units) in 75 to 300 ms. The paper gives no test of "much more so". Reproduced when, under one reading, the mean r with burst fraction is within tolerance, every session (or all but one, given the 13 against 12 discrepancy) has p < 0.05, and the mean r with the population rate is lower with fewer significant sessions.

claims.statement: Per animal, the state comparisons averaged a median of 97 quiet-wakefulness, 21 running and 120 anesthetized trials, across 17 animals.
claims.source: Results, Behavioral states modulate the ERP and the cortico-thalamic interactions, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We then compared average responses from 97 (median, [86–104 IQR]) quiet wakefulness, 21 (median, [16–27 IQR]) active wakefulness, and 120 (median, [120–120 IQR]) anesthetized trials across 17 animals
claims.criterion: Trials split by wheel speed from -0.5 to +0.5 s; quiet when the speed is 0 cm/s throughout (Methods, EEG ERPs), running when the average speed exceeds 0 (Results); speed from the wheel's angular velocity (wheel radius from the dataset). Counts over the pulses of one intensity (see the opening comment). The paper does not say which 17 animals Figure 7 uses; readings (a) one deep-stimulation session per animal (17 matches the deep mice of Figure 4D to 4F, and the Figure 7 examples are deep MOs); (b) one session per animal with any stimulation and an anesthetized stage. The Figure 7 claims use the same readings. Reproduced when, under one reading of the intensity and the session set, the three medians are within tolerance.

claims.statement: ERP duration decreased from quiet wakefulness (0.5 +/- 0.1 s) to running (0.3 +/- 0.0 s) and anesthesia (0.3 +/- 0.0 s); the late component is diminished when running and absent under anesthesia.
claims.source: Results, Behavioral states modulate the ERP and the cortico-thalamic interactions, paragraph 1; Figure 7C
claims.quote: The second component in the ERP was diminished when running and nonexistent during anesthesia; this was captured by the decrease in ERP duration (quiet wakefulness 0.5±0.1 s, running 0.3±0.0 s, anesthetized 0.3±0.0 s; Friedman test
claims.criterion: Duration as in fig1e-erp-duration (both readings), per animal and state. SEMs printed as 0.0 take the printing precision as tolerance. Whether trial numbers were matched across states for the ERP metrics is open (the Methods match them only for PCIst); readings, unmatched and matched by random subsampling to the smallest state (seeded). Reproduced when, under one combination of readings, the three means are within tolerance, the Friedman test (scipy friedmanchisquare) gives p < 0.05, and quiet wakefulness is the longest.

claims.statement: ERP magnitude decreased from quiet wakefulness (6.1 +/- 0.9) to running (1.6 +/- 0.3) and anesthesia (1.6 +/- 0.3).
claims.source: Results, Behavioral states modulate the ERP and the cortico-thalamic interactions, paragraph 1; Figure 7D
claims.quote: the decrease in ERP magnitude (quiet wakefulness 6.1±0.9, running 1.6±0.3, anesthetized 1.6±0.3; Friedman test
claims.criterion: Magnitude as in fig1f-erp-magnitude (both readings), trial matching as in fig7c-erp-duration-state. Reproduced when, under one combination of readings, the three means are within tolerance, the Friedman test gives p < 0.05, and quiet wakefulness is the largest.

claims.statement: Baseline firing rates in stimulated cortex and SM-TH were higher during running and lower during anesthesia than in quiet wakefulness (cortex 3.5, 5.2, 1.1 Hz; SM-TH 9.0, 16.4, 0.8 Hz).
claims.source: Results, Behavioral states modulate the ERP and the cortico-thalamic interactions, paragraph 2; Figure 7E
claims.quote: In both regions, the baseline firing rates (measured during the pre-stimulus epoch) were higher during running and lower during anesthesia compared to quiet wakefulness
claims.criterion: Per animal and state, the mean pre-stimulus firing rate of RS units in stimulated cortex and of SM-TH units. The pre-stimulus epoch is open; readings (a) -2 to 0 s, the epoch the Methods cut; (b) -0.5 to 0 s, the window that classifies the state. The Discussion prints other values for the same quantities (cortex 3.3 +/- 0.2, 5.0 +/- 0.5, 1.1 +/- 0.2; SM-TH 9.4 +/- 1.5, 16.8 +/- 1.6, 0.8 +/- 0.4 Hz), accepted as alternative targets. Reproduced when, under one reading, the six means are within tolerance of one set of values, the one-way RM ANOVA (cortex) and Friedman test (SM-TH) give p < 0.05, and running > quiet > anesthetized in both regions.

claims.statement: First-spike latencies of the initial excitation did not differ across states, in cortex (4.5, 4.0, 4.6 ms) or SM-TH (11.5, 11.3, 10.9 ms); the region effect was significant.
claims.source: Results, Behavioral states modulate the ERP and the cortico-thalamic interactions, paragraph 2; Figure 7F
claims.quote: The median first spike latencies for cortical and thalamic populations were the same when looking at the initial excitation
claims.criterion: Latencies as in fig5e-early-latency, per state. A claim of absence judged on the paper's test, a two-way repeated-measures ANOVA (state by region) on per-animal median latencies; reproduced when the state effect has p >= 0.05 and the region effect p < 0.05. The six means are compared with their tolerances and reported either way.

claims.statement: Rebound spike latencies in cortex and thalamus were earlier during running than in quiet wakefulness (cortex 186.7 against 163.8 ms; SM-TH 156.0 against 123.1 ms), and were not consistently timed during anesthesia.
claims.source: Results, Behavioral states modulate the ERP and the cortico-thalamic interactions, paragraph 2; Figure 7G
claims.quote: However, the rebound spike latencies for cortex and thalamus were earlier during running compared to quiet wakefulness
claims.criterion: Latencies as in fig5f-rebound-latency, per state; the late window of Figure 7G is 100 to 300 ms (75 to 300 ms is run as the variant). Two-way repeated-measures ANOVA (state by region), post hoc pairs with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Reproduced when, under one reading, the state effect has p < 0.05, running is earlier than quiet wakefulness in both regions by the corrected post hoc test (paired t-tests, Methods, Statistics), and all six means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the state effect and the running against quiet order hold but a mean is out of tolerance. The printed interaction (F = 6.6 with p = 0.053) is internally odd for F(2, 24) and is reported, not judged.

claims.statement: The probability of evoked thalamic bursts decreased during running compared to quiet wakefulness and was very low under anesthesia (medians 0.1, 0, 0).
claims.source: Results, Behavioral states modulate the ERP and the cortico-thalamic interactions, paragraph 2; Figure 7H
claims.quote: The probability of evoking thalamic bursts decreased during running compared to quiet wakefulness and was very low (zero for many subjects) during anesthesia (N=13; median probability: quiet wakefulness 0.1 [0.01–0.24 IQR], running 0 [0–0.07 IQR], anesthetized 0 [0–0.002 IQR]; Friedman test
claims.criterion: Burst probability as in fig5c-burst-probability-depth (both readings), 75 to 300 ms, per animal and state. The Discussion gives the quiet median as 9.5%, accepted as an alternative target (tolerance 0.0095). Reproduced when, under one reading, the medians match, the Friedman test gives p < 0.05, and quiet wakefulness is the highest.

claims.statement: PCIst was higher in the awake than in the isoflurane-anesthetized state in all subjects (45.5 +/- 3.6 against 16.5 +/- 2.4).
claims.source: Results, Thalamo-cortical interactions affect perturbational complexity in head-fixed mice, paragraph 1; Figure 8B
