claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 10A
claims.quote: Postsonication, we found the correlation from S1 RSUs to POm FSUs and POm RSUs to S1 RSUs significantly decreased, representing the desynchronization of spikes
claims.criterion: The 3000 Hz, 60% DC sessions, dSTTC (M5, O6, O7) from S1 RSUs to POm FSUs and from POm RSUs to S1 RSUs. The paper does not name the postsonication window or give the p-values; the readings are each 67 ms window from 67 to 268 ms, and 201 to 268 ms, the postsonication window of the rate analyses. One-tailed less against prestimulation at p < 0.05 (M6). Reproduced when both directions are significant in at least one common window; partially reproduced when one is.

claims.statement: With 30 Hz PRF, S1 RSUs show a time-locked increase in correlation to POm FSUs, while POm RSUs show decreased correlation to S1 FSUs during sonication.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 10B
claims.quote: When delivering 30 Hz ultrasound, S1 RSUs to POm FSUs higher correlated (p = 0.0058), while POm RSUs showed decreased correlation to S1 FSUs during sonication (p = 0.0058)
claims.criterion: The 30 Hz, 0.6% DC sessions, dSTTC (M5, O6, O7, O8), 0 to 67 ms against prestimulation (M6), S1 RSU to POm FSU one-tailed greater and POm RSU to S1 FSU one-tailed less, at p < 0.05. Reproduced when both hold under every reading; partially reproduced when one holds.

claims.statement: With constant 200 us pulse duration, the change of STTC between S1 RSUs and POm RSUs during sonication does not depend on PRF, though 1500 Hz gives a higher change than 30 Hz.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 2; Figure 10C
claims.quote: When applying tFUS with constant 200 μs PD, varying the DC and PRF, the correlation did not show PRF-dependent change. A total of 1,500 Hz PRF did show a higher correlation change compared with 30 Hz PRF (Fig. 10C; p = 0.02).
claims.criterion: Pairs of S1 RSUs and POm RSUs in the constant-PD series; STTC (Cutts and Eglen 2014) with Delta t 20 ms, change during 0 to 67 ms from prestimulation normalized by O7. The absence of PRF dependence is judged on the paper's test, Kruskal-Wallis across the five PRFs at p < 0.05 (M6), holding when not significant. The 1500 against 30 Hz part holds when 1500 Hz is greater, one-tailed, p < 0.05. Reproduced when both hold under every O7 reading; partially reproduced when one holds.

claims.statement: With constant 60% DC, the change of correlation between S1 RSUs and POm RSUs depends on PRF, with a preference for 1500 and 3000 Hz.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 2; Figure 10D legend
claims.quote: Unlike the neuronal responses (Fig. 9), the correlation showed the preference to 1,500 and 3,000 Hz (Fig. 10D)
claims.criterion: As fig10c-sttc-constant-pd, for the 60% DC series. Reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis test across the five PRFs is significant at p < 0.05 and 1500 and 3000 Hz have the two highest mean changes; partially reproduced when the test holds and one of them is among the two highest.

claims.statement: At 30 Hz PRF the change of correlation between S1 RSUs and POm RSUs depends on DC, largest at middle DCs (6, 30, 60%) and smaller at 0.6% and 90%.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 2; Figure 10E legend
claims.quote: For 30 Hz PRF (Fig. 10E), the correlation tended to change most at a middle range (6, 30, 60%) and respond less to lower (e.g., 0.6%) and higher DC (e.g., 90%)
claims.criterion: As fig10c-sttc-constant-pd, for the 30 Hz DC series. Reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis test across the five DCs is significant at p < 0.05 and each of 6, 30 and 60% has a higher mean change than both 0.6% and 90%; partially reproduced when the test holds and the lowest two means are 0.6% and 90% in either order but the middle order is otherwise.

claims.statement: At 3000 Hz PRF the change of correlation between S1 RSUs and POm RSUs does not depend on DC.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 2; Figure 10F
claims.quote: For 3,000 Hz PRF, the pathway correlation showed DC independence (Fig. 10F).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, Kruskal-Wallis across the five DCs of the 3000 Hz series, STTC change as in fig10c-sttc-constant-pd, at p < 0.05. Reproduced when not significant; not reproduced when significant; H and p reported.

claims.statement: The PRFs that elicit the strongest local S1 RSU responses (1500 and 3000 Hz) also give the highest POm responses and the strongest correlation change, so pathway modulation is PRF dependent.
claims.source: Discussion, The feedback and feedforward cortico-thalomo-cortical circuits activated by cell-type selective tFUS, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Our results show S1 RSUs’ preference for 1,500 and 3,000 Hz, and the POm highest responses as well as the strongest correlation change were induced by the same PRF range
claims.criterion: From the results of the claims it depends on. Reproduced when the PRF with the highest mean 0 to 67 ms response of S1 RSUs in the constant-PD series is 1500 or 3000 Hz, the PRF with the highest mean response of POm RSUs in that series is 1500 or 3000 Hz, and the two highest STTC changes in the 60% DC series are at 1500 and 3000 Hz; partially reproduced when two of the three hold. The Discussion does not say which window "the POm highest responses" means; the readings are 0 to 67 ms and 201 to 268 ms (where Figure 6C puts the highest delayed response at 1500 Hz), and the POm part holds under either.

claims.statement: The auditory-confound analysis rests on 453 AC neurons over the PRFs, with 83, 107, 104 and 100 neurons in the 30, 1500, 3000 and 4500 Hz sessions.
claims.source: Results, Auditory confound on CTC pathway modulation using tFUS, paragraph 1; Figure 11 legend
claims.quote: The comparison of the responses of sorted 453 neurons from AC to different PRFs was conducted using Kruskal–Wallis
claims.criterion: AC units selected by M1, untyped, counted per session condition of the AC group. Reproduced when at least four of the five counts are within tolerance; partially reproduced for two or three. Which PRF series the AC sessions follow (constant PD or other) the paper does not say; the readings are the constant-PD series and any series the dataset labels with these PRFs.

claims.statement: AC neurons show time-locked responses to 1500 and 3000 Hz PRF tFUS targeting S1 and postsonication responses to 30, 1500, 3000 and 4500 Hz, with the least response to 300 Hz.
claims.source: Results, Auditory confound on CTC pathway modulation using tFUS, paragraph 1; Figure 11A and the PRF panel of Figure 11 (labelled B in the text, C in the legend)
claims.quote: During sonication, the AC neurons showed time-locked responses to 1,500 Hz (n = 107, p = 9.9 × 10−5) and 3,000 Hz PRF (n = 104, p = 1.98 × 10−7). Postsonication, neuronal responses were activated by 30 Hz (n = 83, p = 1.77 × 10−20), 1,500 Hz, (n = 107, p = 1.36 × 10−5), 3,000 Hz (n = 104, p = 4.47 × 10−13), and 4,500 Hz (n = 100, p = 1.66 × 10−40)
claims.criterion: AC units of the AC group (M1), normalized rate (M3) in 0 to 67 ms and 201 to 268 ms (the postsonication window of the parameter comparisons; the paper does not name it for AC), tests of M4 under O2 to O4. Reproduced when both Kruskal-Wallis tests are significant, 1500 and 3000 Hz (and not 30, 300, 4500 Hz) are significant against baseline during sonication, 30, 1500, 3000 and 4500 Hz (and not 300 Hz) postsonication, one-tailed greater, corrected p < 0.01, and 300 Hz has the lowest mean in both windows. Partially reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis tests and at least four of the six named PRF-window results hold.

claims.statement: With 30 Hz PRF, the directional correlation from AC neurons to S1 RSUs increases significantly during sonication and lasts about 150 to 200 ms, indicating that the auditory cortex is activated directly by 30 Hz tFUS.
claims.source: Results, Auditory confound on CTC pathway modulation using tFUS, paragraph 2; Figure 11 legend, panel C
claims.quote: During tFUS sonication with 30 Hz PRF, the correlation from 878 paired AC neurons to S1 RSUs significantly increased (p = 0.0014) which lasting for ∼150 ms
claims.criterion: Pairs of AC neurons (A) and S1 RSUs (B) recorded together in the 30 Hz sessions (O8); dSTTC (M5, O6, O7), 0 to 67 ms against prestimulation, one-tailed greater, p < 0.05 (M6). The duration is given as about 150 ms (legend) and about 200 ms (Results); it holds when the windows from onset that stay significant reach at least 134 ms (two 67 ms windows) and end by 268 ms. Reproduced when the during-sonication increase holds under every reading and the duration holds; partially reproduced when the increase holds alone.

claims.statement: With 30 Hz PRF, the directional correlation from AC neurons to S1 FSUs also changes during and right after sonication; the legend says it decreased, while the Results say the same synchronization as with S1 RSUs was found.
claims.source: Figure 11 legend, panel C; Results, Auditory confound on CTC pathway modulation using tFUS, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The correlation of AC neurons to S1 FSUs decreased during and right after sonication.
claims.criterion: The two sentences give opposite directions, so the claim is tested as a change. dSTTC from AC neurons to S1 FSUs of the 30 Hz sessions (M5, O6, O7, O8), 0 to 67 ms and 67 to 134 ms against prestimulation, one-tailed less (the legend) and one-tailed greater (the Results), p < 0.05 (M6). Reported as reproduced in the legend's reading when the decrease is significant in either window, in the Results' reading when the increase is; the direction found is reported and the paper's disagreement recorded as a deviation.

claims.statement: With 3000 Hz PRF, AC neurons show no directional correlation change with S1 RSUs, while the correlation of AC neurons with S1 FSUs changes only postsonication, at about 200 to 300 ms.
claims.source: Results, Auditory confound on CTC pathway modulation using tFUS, paragraph 2; Figure 11 legend, panel D
claims.quote: However, when delivering 3,000 Hz PRF ultrasound energy to S1, auditory neurons did not show directional correlation change with S1 RSUs. The correlation change of AC neurons with S1 FSUs only occurred ∼200–300 ms.
claims.criterion: Pairs of the 3000 Hz sessions of the AC group (O8), dSTTC (M5, O6, O7). The absence with S1 RSUs is judged on the paper's test, dSTTC from AC neurons to S1 RSUs (the direction the Figure 11 legend names), each 67 ms window from 0 to 268 ms against prestimulation at p < 0.05 (M6), one-tailed by O5; it holds when none is significant. S1 RSU to AC is shown as a variant only. The FSU part holds when dSTTC from AC neurons to S1 FSUs increases or decreases significantly (the legend's "bidirectional") in 201 to 268 ms (the windows nearest 200 to 300 ms; 268 to 335 ms as a second reading) and none in 0 to 134 ms. Reproduced when both parts hold; partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: With 1500 Hz PRF, 200 us PD, 67 ms UD and 5 V input, the in situ peak-to-peak pressure with beam steering to S1, measured ex vivo through a rat skull, is 88 kPa, with ISPTA 29.42 mW/cm2 (free-water spatial peak 1626.4 kPa).
claims.source: Methods, Transcranial focused ultrasound stimulation, paragraph 2; Figure 1C
claims.quote: The measured peak-to-peak in situ ultrasound pressure magnitude with beam steering (targeting S1) was 88 kPa (Fig. 1C) and spatial-peak temporal average (ISPTA) was 29.42 mW/cm2.
claims.criterion: From the hydrophone scans of Figure 1C, which the paper describes recording but does not say it deposited; tested only if the dataset holds them.

claims.statement: Both 4-methyl-3-hexanol and 6MHO cause wild-type ants to leave the initial nest pile and the initial nest chamber, compared with the vehicle control.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromones elicit a range of behavioral responses, paragraph 1; Figure 1C-D
claims.quote: Both compounds caused ants to leave the initial nest pile (consisting of at least 2 adult workers and at least 1 egg) and the initial nest chamber
claims.criterion: The paper's test (Methods, Colony alarm bioassay) on hand-scored counts of ants outside the nest pile and outside the nest chamber, from 1 minute before to 2 minutes after the stimulus, two-way repeated measures ANOVA and Dunnett's test against vehicle at each timepoint. Reproduced when, for each compound and each of the two measures, at least one post-stimulus timepoint differs from vehicle at p < 0.05. The spacing of the scored timepoints is not given in this paper (the Methods refer to Lopes et al. 2023, ref. 22) and is open. The behaviour videos are not named among the paper's deposits.

claims.statement: In blinded categorization, 4-methyl-3-heptanone, 4-methyl-3-heptanol, their blend and 4-methyl-3-hexanol caused immediate panic alarm (nest pile disassembled within one minute) in at least 80% of trials, while the most common response to 6MHO was "ants leave nest", the nest pile persisting for more than one minute.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromones elicit a range of behavioral responses, paragraph 1; Figure 1E
claims.quote: all caused the ants to rapidly leave and disassemble the nest pile ... within one minute after exposure in at least 80% of trials. We call this response "immediate panic alarm". The most common response to 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one was for the majority of ants to slowly walk away from the nest, while the nest pile persisted for more than one minute
claims.criterion: Each video classified as in the Methods (immediate panic alarm, ants leave nest, no immediate response). Reproduced when each of the four compounds gives immediate panic in at least 72% of trials (80% less 10%) and "ants leave nest" is the most frequent class for 6MHO. Trials per compound are taken as Table S2's n for the same bioassays (Figure 1F legend), 17, 11, 9, 10 and 10 (heptanone, heptanol, blend, hexanol, 6MHO); the paper does not print the trial counts of Figure 1E.

claims.statement: 4-methyl-3-hexanol disassembles the nest pile as fast as the native O. biroi alarm pheromones; the time the initial pile persists does not differ from 4-methyl-3-heptanone, 4-methyl-3-heptanol or the blend.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromones elicit a range of behavioral responses, paragraph 1; Figure 1F; Table S2
claims.quote: treatment with 4-methyl-3-hexanol led to similarly rapid disassembly of the nest as 4-methyl-3-heptanone, 4-methyl-3-heptanol, and the blend
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. The percentage of the first two minutes after the stimulus during which the initial pile (at least one egg and two adults in the same area) persists, per trial; one-way ANOVA over the six treatments and Sidak's test, the family being the nine comparisons of Table S2 (hexanol, 6MHO and the vehicle, each against heptanone, heptanol and the blend). Reproduced when none of the three hexanol comparisons has adjusted p < 0.05; the mean differences are reported either way.

claims.statement: With 6MHO the initial nest pile persists significantly longer than with each native alarm pheromone, and its outcomes vary widely.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromones elicit a range of behavioral responses, paragraph 1; Figure 1F; Table S2
claims.quote: treatment with 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one produced a wide range of outcomes, and the average response was significantly different from responses to clonal raider ant alarm pheromones
claims.criterion: As for fig1f-hexanol-like-native. Reproduced when all three 6MHO comparisons have adjusted p < 0.05 with 6MHO persisting longer; partially reproduced for one or two.

claims.statement: After the vehicle control the initial nest pile persists far longer than after any native alarm pheromone.
claims.source: Figure 1F; Table S2
claims.quote: non- O. biroi alarm pheromones and the vehicle control were compared to known O. biroi alarm pheromones for (F)
claims.criterion: As for fig1f-hexanol-like-native. Reproduced when all three comparisons have adjusted p < 0.05 with the vehicle persisting longer.

claims.statement: piggyBac injection of eggs yielded at least one transgenic line from the four pooled treatments (overall efficiency 0.00021, transformation efficiency 0.026), the line that gave the stable population used in all later experiments, and at least one from the last treatment (0.0028 and 0.059); higher rates of fluorescent G0s came from eggs under 3 hours old, and mixes above 110 ng/uL mRNA gave low hatch rates and no fluorescent G0s.
claims.source: Results, Creation of transgenic ants; Methods, Egg collection, microinjection, and larval rearing; Table 1
claims.quote: Higher rates of fluorescent G0s were obtained when eggs were <3 hours old ... than <5 hours old at the time of injection. Mixes with >110ng/μL mRNA concentrations produced low hatch rates and no fluorescent G0s
claims.criterion: Efficiencies as Table 1 defines them (lines over eggs injected; lines over G0 adults eclosed). Injection records are not named among the paper's deposits.

claims.statement: Transgenic pupae show GCaMP6s fluorescence in the antennae and broadly visible DsRed under epifluorescence, unlike wild type.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of transgenic ants, paragraph 1; Figure 2B; Figure S1A
claims.quote: Transgenic pupae had detectable GCaMP6s fluorescence in the antennae, consistent with expression in OSNs, and DsRed was broadly visible under epifluorescence
claims.criterion: A qualitative comparison of transgenic and wild-type pupae images; the epifluorescence images are not named among the paper's deposits.

claims.statement: GCaMP6s labels the great majority of Orco-positive cells in the antennal club, and in the ALs GCaMP6s co-localizes with Orco in OSN afferents.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of transgenic ants, paragraph 1; Figure 2C-D
claims.quote: GCaMP6s labels the great majority of Orco-positive cells ( Fig. 2C ). In the ALs, high levels of GCaMP6s co-localized with Orco, which labels OSN afferents
claims.criterion: The paper gives no count. Anti-GFP and anti-Orco confocal stacks of the antennal club; the fraction of Orco-positive cells that are GFP-positive is reported, and "great majority" is read, by the reader, as more than half (the weakest reading); reproduced when more than half are GFP-positive and AL GFP and Orco signals overlap. Which deposited stacks are these is not stated.

claims.statement: DsRed is expressed at a low level in the ALs, and GCaMP6s is also expressed in parts of the subesophageal zone and central complex; these patterns are consistent across individuals.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of transgenic ants, paragraph 1; Figure S1B-D
claims.quote: DsRed is expressed at a low level in the ALs, possibly due to leaky expression from ObirOrco ... GCaMP6s is also expressed in parts of the sub-esophageal zone and central complex
claims.criterion: Qualitative, from the confocal stacks; reproduced when anti-DsRed signal is present in the ALs and GCaMP6s fluorescence in the subesophageal zone and central complex.

claims.statement: Reconstructions of two GCaMP6s ALs found 505 (anti-SYNORF1) and 508 (phalloidin) glomeruli, within the wild-type range; in the second, 502 glomeruli were Orco-positive and all of them GCaMP6s-positive, the 6 Orco-negative ones were the T7 cluster, and 4 of these had weak GCaMP6s.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of transgenic ants, paragraph 2; Figure S2A-B
claims.quote: From the first AL, we reconstructed 505 glomeruli using anti-SYNORF1 signal ... we reconstructed 508 glomeruli ... we counted 502 Orco-positive glomeruli, all of which were also GCaMP6s-positive ... The 6 glomeruli of the T7 cluster were the only Orco-negative glomeruli
claims.criterion: Manual segmentation (LABKIT, 1 um z resolution) of the right AL (anti-SYNORF1) and the left AL (anti-Orco and phalloidin), as in the Methods. The segmentations themselves are not named among the deposits, so the stacks would have to be segmented again.

claims.statement: GCaMP6s robustly labels glomeruli of clusters T1 to T6, while T7 signal is weaker and often undetectable and the antennal mechanosensory and motor center is unlabeled, so the line can report from about 99% of glomeruli.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of transgenic ants, paragraph 2; Figure 2E
claims.quote: While glomeruli in T1-T6 were always robustly labeled by anti-GFP, signal in the T7 glomeruli was consistently weaker than in other glomeruli and was often undetectable
claims.criterion: Qualitative, from anti-GFP and anti-SYNORF1 confocal stacks; reproduced when T7 anti-GFP intensity is below that of the other glomeruli and the AMMC shows no anti-GFP signal.

claims.statement: After unilateral antennal ablation, GCaMP6s and anti-Orco signals are greatly reduced across the AL on the ablated side, with no glomerular labeling left, while GCaMP6s in the subesophageal zone and central complex is unaffected; AL GCaMP6s thus comes from the antennae.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of transgenic ants, paragraph 2; Figure 2F; Figure S1E
claims.quote: While GCaMP6s signal in the sub-esophageal zone and central complex was unaffected ( Fig. S1E ), GCaMP6s and anti-Orco signals were greatly reduced across the entire AL connected to the ablated antenna, and no clear glomerular labeling remained
claims.criterion: Qualitative; reproduced when AL GCaMP6s and anti-Orco intensity on the ablated side is below that on the intact side and the SEZ and CC signals are bilaterally present.

claims.statement: One month after unilateral antennal ablation, the AL on the ablated side tends to be smaller (mean 165,360 against 209,412 um3), not significantly (n=3).
claims.source: Methods, Immunohistochemistry, last paragraph
claims.quote: We therefore reconstructed AL volumes from several brains (n=3) and found a non-significant trend toward smaller volumes on the ablated side (means of 165,360μm 3 and 209,412μm 3 for ablated vs. non-ablated ALs, respectively; p=0.073, paired values T-test)
claims.criterion: AL volumes reconstructed from confocal stacks of three ablated brains; a paired t-test. A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test at p < 0.05. Reproduced when both means are within tolerance, the ablated side is the smaller and the test gives p of 0.05 or more; p is reported. Sidedness is not stated; two-sided (the GraphPad default) is the main reading and one-sided is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: GCaMP6s ants, like wild type, leave the nest pile in response to 4-methyl-3-heptanone, 4-methyl-3-heptanol and the 9:1 blend; leaving the nest chamber differs significantly from control only for 4-methyl-3-heptanone and the blend.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of transgenic ants, paragraph 3; Figure S2C-F
claims.quote: The ants left the nest cluster in response to 4-methyl-3-heptanone, 4-methyl-3-heptanol and the blend, similar to wild types ( Fig. S2C – D ). The effect on leaving the nest chamber was only significantly different from control for 4-methyl-3-heptanone and the blend
claims.criterion: As in fig1cd-new-pheromones-leave-nest, with all GCaMP6s treatments compared with one shared set of vehicle trials (Figure S2 legend), 15 to 20 ants per arena. Reproduced when all three compounds differ from vehicle at some post-stimulus timepoint for ants outside the nest pile, and for ants outside the chamber heptanone and the blend do while heptanol does not.

claims.statement: The GCaMP6s line carries a single haploid transgene insertion on chromosomal scaffold 2, at Chr2 3,870,844 to 3,870,847, within an intron of trace amine-associated receptor 9; normalized read depth is about 1.5 at ObirOrco and about 0.5 over the rest of the insert.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of transgenic ants, paragraph 3; Figure S3; Methods, Genome sequencing and genomic analyses
claims.quote: The line contains a single, haploid transgene insertion on the 2 nd chromosomal scaffold ( Fig. S3A – B ). The insertion occurred at location Chr2:3,870,844–3,870,847, within an intron of the gene trace amine-associated receptor 9
claims.criterion: The Methods pipeline (Trimmomatic 0.36, bwa mem to Obir_v5.4 GCA_003672135.1 and the linearized plasmid, Picard deduplication, samtools depth -aa, normalization to heterozygous SNPs below twice the genome-wide median depth, junction reads). Reproduced when the depths are within tolerance and the junction reads place the insert at the stated position.

claims.statement: Each general odorant activates a unique combination of glomeruli, and the same odorant activates similar AL regions in different individuals.
claims.source: Results, Recording calcium responses to general odorants, paragraph 2; Figure 3F
claims.quote: each odorant activated a unique combination of glomeruli, and responses to the same odorant occurred in similar regions of the AL in different individuals
claims.criterion: The paper judged this by eye from M1 maps (n=6 ants, 48%). The rule below is the reader's, not the paper's. Within each ant, the M2 sets of responding ROIs differ between every pair of the odorants that ant was given (each odorant was tested in 2 to 6 ants). Across ants, the centroid of each odorant's responding pixels (at least 0.2, trial-averaged map), in coordinates scaled to the AL's bounding box in raw fluorescence, lies closer to the same odorant's centroids in the other ants than to other odorants' centroids, in more than half of the ant and odorant cases. Reproduced when both hold under every M2 reading.

claims.statement: The breadth of responses varies across general odorants; most activate a few glomeruli, while 3-hexanone activates large regions of the ventral and medial AL.
claims.source: Results, Recording calcium responses to general odorants, paragraph 2; Figure 3F-G
claims.quote: the breadth of glomerular responses varied dramatically across odorants, with most odorants activating a few glomeruli, while 3-hexanone activated large regions of the ventral/medial AL
claims.criterion: The paper gives no measure; one is fixed here. Breadth is the area of pixels of at least 0.2 (the Methods threshold) in each ant's trial-averaged M1 map. Reproduced when 3-hexanone has the largest area of the five odorants in every ant where it was tested, and its median area across ants is at least twice that of each other odorant.

claims.statement: Responses to 4-methyl-3-hexanol are bilaterally symmetrical in the two ALs imaged together, so later experiments imaged only the right AL.
claims.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 1; Figure S4A
claims.quote: we first imaged responses to 4-methyl-3-hexanol in both ALs simultaneously (n=3 ants) and found that response patterns were bilaterally symmetrical
claims.criterion: The paper gives no measure; one is fixed here. In each of the three bilateral ants (1X zoom, 4-methyl-3-hexanol 48%), M1 maps split at the midline between the ALs, the left mirrored. Reproduced when in every ant both ALs have responding ROIs (M2) and their counts differ by at most one, and the mirrored-left and right maps of responding pixels correlate better than the right map does with itself shifted by half its width.

claims.statement: Sparse, unique subsets of glomeruli respond to each alarm pheromone, while the paraffin oil vehicle generates no responses.
claims.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 1; Figure 4B-C
claims.quote: Sparse, unique subsets of AL glomeruli responded to all pheromones, while the paraffin oil vehicle did not generate responses
claims.criterion: A claim of absence for the vehicle, on the paper's rule (M2, peak fold change at least 0.2). Reproduced when no ROI responds in any ant's vehicle trials, and each pheromone has at least one responding ROI in most ants at their higher concentration, under every M2 reading; the largest vehicle ROI value is reported.

claims.statement: Odors cause no fluorescence decreases; only small non-specific decreases from shifts in AL position and photobleaching occur.
claims.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We did not observe any fluorescence decreases in response to odor, although we did detect small, non-specific decreases in fluorescence due to minor shifts in AL position and photobleaching
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The Methods judged it ("We determined that all responses were positive") from the per-plane peak fold change maps of the first look, so those are used. Per plane, Image Stabilizer, 1-sigma Gaussian blur, F0 the mean of frames 1 to 5, peak fold change the mean of dF/F0 over frames 9 to 14, all 33 planes examined. The paper's only threshold is 0.2; it is applied with the sign reversed, a choice of the reader. Reproduced when no glomerulus-sized region (10 to 20 um) reaches -0.2 or below in at least two trials of the same odor and concentration without doing so in that ant's vehicle trials; the most negative such region is reported.

claims.statement: Fluorescence increases to alarm pheromones are often large (1 to 2-fold change) and outlast the 5 s odor pulse.
claims.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Fluorescence increases were frequently large (1–2-fold change) and lasted longer than the 5s odor presentation
claims.criterion: Over responding ROI-trials (M2) at each ant's higher concentration, the ROI peak fold change. The paper reports a range, 1 to 2, and no single value. "Frequently large" is read as the median lying in 1 to 2 widened by 10% of each bound (0.9 to 2.2), a reading of the reader, under each ROI value reading (i) and (ii). "Lasted longer" is read with the paper's onset rule (Methods, temporal dynamics); reproduced when, in more than half of those ROI-trials, dF/F0 at the first volume after the pulse ends (8 s) is still above the baseline mean plus 3 SD.

claims.statement: Each alarm pheromone activates few of the roughly 500 glomeruli; even at the highest concentration the median number of responding glomeruli is at most 6.
claims.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 2; Figure S5A; Figure 6 legend
claims.quote: Even at the highest concentration tested, the four pheromones activated a median of at most 6 glomeruli
claims.criterion: Counts per ant from M2 (each reading). "The highest concentration tested" is read as (a) 48%, the 8 ants of Figure 6, or (b) each ant's higher concentration (13 ants). Reproduced when, under a reading, the median over ants is at most 6.6 for every pheromone.

claims.statement: Higher concentrations give more robust responses and a few more glomeruli passing the threshold, while the overall spatial pattern stays similar across concentrations.
claims.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 2; Figure S5A; Figure S6
claims.quote: Higher concentrations produced more robust responses, with a few more glomeruli passing the threshold, but overall spatial response patterns were similar across concentrations
claims.criterion: The paper shows box plots and no test; a rule is fixed here. Within each ant and pheromone, M2 counts at the higher minus the lower concentration. Reproduced when, pooled over pheromones, positive differences outnumber negative ones by a two-sided sign test at p < 0.05, and in more than half of ant and pheromone pairs every ROI that responds at the lower concentration also responds at the higher one. Shown under every M2 reading.

claims.statement: The three compounds that elicit panic alarm (4-methyl-3-heptanone, 4-methyl-3-heptanol, 4-methyl-3-hexanol) activate partly overlapping sets of glomeruli, with a single glomerulus, PGb, activated by all three.
claims.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 2; Figure S5B
claims.quote: we observed consistent partial overlap in the response patterns activated by the three compounds eliciting panic alarm responses ... with a single glomerulus activated by all three
claims.criterion: Per ant, the number of M2 ROIs responding to all three, at (a) each ant's higher concentration (13 ants) or (b) 48% (the 8 ants of Figure 6, whose medians are at 48%); Figure S5B plots each concentration and the text names none. Reproduced when, under each M2 reading and under (a) or (b), the median over ants is 1 and more than half of the ants have exactly one such ROI.

claims.statement: 6MHO only rarely and inconsistently activates glomeruli shared with 4-methyl-3-heptanone or 4-methyl-3-hexanol.
claims.source: Results, Pheromone representation is sparse, paragraph 2; Figure S5C
claims.quote: while we sometimes observed responses to 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one and either 4-methyl-3-heptanone or 4-methyl-3-hexanol in an overlapping region, those occurrences were rare and inconsistent
claims.criterion: Per ant, at (a) its higher concentration or (b) 48% (as in figs5b-shared-glomerulus), the number of M2 ROIs responding to 6MHO and to any other pheromone (overlaps at different depths excluded, as in the Methods). Reproduced when, under each M2 reading and under (a) or (b), the median over ants is 0 and the count is non-zero in fewer than half of the ants.

claims.statement: PGb lies in the anterior ventral hemi-lobe next to a gap without glomeruli, about halfway between the dorsal and ventral AL surfaces, with two neighbouring alarm-responsive glomeruli in the same plane; PGb and 6G were found in 13 of 13 ants and PGa in 11 of 13.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 1; Figure 5A-B
claims.quote: PG b is located approximately halfway between the dorsal and ventral AL surfaces, and is neighbored by two additional glomeruli that respond to alarm pheromones, with all three visible in the same optical plane ... Both glomeruli were identified in 13/13 individuals. In 11/13 individuals, we identified a third neighboring glomerulus
claims.criterion: Identification by M4 on each ant's higher-concentration ROIs (M2, each reading). Reproduced when the counts are within tolerance (12 or 13, 12 or 13, 10 to 12) and, in most ants with PGb, its centre plane lies in the middle third of the AL depth (from the top plane, the dorsal surface, to the deepest plane with AL fluorescence, Methods).

claims.statement: PGb, PGa and 6G each respond to a unique combination of pheromones, with several pheromone and glomerulus pairs giving no response; PGb responds to 4-methyl-3-heptanone, 4-methyl-3-heptanol and 4-methyl-3-hexanol and not to 6MHO, PGa to 4-methyl-3-heptanol and 4-methyl-3-hexanol, and 6G to 6MHO.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 2; Figure 5C; Figure S6
claims.quote: while PG b , PG a , and 6G are spatially adjacent, they each reliably respond to unique combinations of odorants, with several pheromone/glomerulus combinations producing no detectable responses ... PG b did not respond to 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one
claims.criterion: Peak fold change per trial from M3 (each reading), all concentrations, 13 ants (11 for PGa). The Methods model, peak response on concentration with a random effect for individual, fitted with "the glm function", which has no random effects; readings (a) a linear model with individual as a fixed factor, (b) a linear mixed model with a random intercept per ant. Concentration log-transformed (Figure S6 legend; the base is a standard choice that cannot change the outcome). A combination responds when the model's prediction at 48% is at least 0.2 (the Methods threshold) with its 95% CI above 0, and gives no response when the 95% CI at 48% includes 0. Reproduced when the six named combinations respond, PGb to 6MHO does not, and the three glomeruli's sets of responding pheromones all differ.

claims.statement: Responses in PGb and PGa peak and then decline close to baseline by the end of the 48 s recording, while 6G responses to 6MHO are very slow, with a plateau of tens of seconds.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 2; Figure 5C
claims.quote: while responses in PG b and PG a peaked and then declined close to baseline by the end of the recording, responses in 6G were extremely slow, with a fluorescence plateau of tens of seconds
claims.criterion: Mean M3 traces for the robust combinations of the Methods (heptanone in PGb; heptanol and hexanol in PGb and PGa; 6MHO in 6G). The concentration of Figure 5C is not stated; readings (a) 48% (8 ants, as Figure S7C), (b) all concentrations pooled. Thresholds are fixed here. Reproduced when the PGb and PGa mean traces over the last five volumes are below 0.2 (the Methods threshold) and below a quarter of their peak, while the 6G trace stays at or above half its peak for at least 20 s.

claims.statement: In 144 s recordings, 6G responses to 6MHO plateau for about 30 s and return to baseline about 80 s after odor presentation, sometimes taking more than 100 s.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 2; Figure S7A
claims.quote: Fluorescence plateaued for ~30s before declining and returning to baseline ~80s after odor presentation
claims.criterion: Single 144 s trials from five ants at 48%, M3 traces of 6G, and their mean. Plateau and return are not defined in the paper. Readings, return to baseline as the first volume after the peak where the mean trace falls (a) below baseline mean plus 3 SD (the Methods onset rule) or (b) below 0.2; plateau as the time the mean trace stays at or above (c) 90% or (d) 80% of its peak; the 90% and 80% levels are the reader's, not the paper's. Odor presentation read as (e) odor onset at 3 s or (f) odor offset at 8 s. Reproduced when, under one reading, both values are within tolerance and at least one trial takes more than 100 s.

claims.statement: Onset and peak times differ by pheromone and glomerulus; for PGb and PGa responses to 4-methyl-3-heptanol and 4-methyl-3-hexanol, onset time depends on pheromone, glomerulus and their interaction, and time to maximum on pheromone and glomerulus but not their interaction.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 2; Figure S7C legend
claims.quote: Time to response onset: significant effects of pheromone (p=0.0034), glomerulus (p<0.0001), and the interaction (p=0.0030). Time to response maximum: significant effects of pheromone (p<0.0001) and glomerulus (p=0.047), but not the interaction (p=0.88)
claims.criterion: M3 traces at 48%; baseline the first five frames; onset the latency from stimulus start (3 s) to the first volume where dF/F0 exceeds baseline mean plus 3 SD; time to maximum the latency to the largest dF/F0; traces that never exceed the bound excluded (Methods). Volume times taken as (index - 1) x 1.2 s, a standard choice that shifts all latencies alike. Model per parameter, pheromone, glomerulus and their interaction, random effect for trial nested in ant (lme). How the p-values were taken is not stated; readings (a) anova of the lme fit, sequential F-tests in the order the Methods list, (b) marginal F-tests, (c) the t-tests of the coefficients in its summary. Reproduced when, under every reading, the five effects have p < 0.05 and the time-to-maximum interaction has p of 0.05 or more (a claim of absence on the paper's test); partially reproduced when three or four of the five hold.

claims.statement: PGa is always anterior (12.9 +/- 1.9 SD um) and slightly lateral (5.1 +/- 2.9 um) to PGb, and 6G always lateral to PGb (13.1 +/- 2.6 um) at a similar anterior-posterior position (0.6 +/- 2.2 um); the SDs are much smaller than a glomerulus diameter, so the three occupy stereotyped positions.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 3; Figure 5D
claims.quote: PG a was always located anterior (mean distance between centers: 12.9±1.9SD μm), and slightly lateral (mean distance: 5.1±2.9SD μm) to PG b ( Fig. 5D ). In comparison, 6G was always lateral to PG b (mean distance: 13.1±2.6SD μm), and in a similar position along the anterior-posterior axis (mean distance: 0.6±2.2SD μm)
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's SDs. One plane per ant where all three are visible (n=11 for PGa, 13 for 6G), PGb at (0,0), 0.289 um per pixel. The centres were placed by hand; readings (a) the centroid of each glomerulus's responding pixels (at least 0.2) to its defining odor (M4) in that plane, (b) its peak pixel; and the plane from (c) one higher-concentration trial or (d) the mean over that ant's higher-concentration trials. These are method details the paper leaves open (markers placed by hand). Reproduced when, under every reading, the four means are within tolerance, PGa is anterior in every ant and 6G lateral in every ant, and each SD is below 10 um (the lower bound of the 10 to 20 um glomerulus diameter); when the readings give different outcomes, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified. If the files give no orientation, only distances are tested and the claim is at most partially reproduced.

claims.statement: The three pheromones with overlapping AL responses all elicit panic alarm, while 6MHO does not elicit panic and gives a non-overlapping response, pointing to a shared pathway for panic alarm centred on PGb.
claims.source: Results, Alarm pheromone-responsive glomeruli are spatially stereotyped, paragraph 4; Figure 6
claims.quote: The three pheromones with overlapping calcium response patterns all robustly elicited panic alarm behavior, while 6-methyl-5-hepten-2-one did not elicit panic alarm behavior and generated a non-overlapping response
claims.criterion: The synthesis of the claims it depends on. The imaging half is tested here; the behaviour half rests on fig1e-categorical-response, whose data are not in the dataset. Reproduced in its imaging half when figs5b-shared-glomerulus and figs5c-mho-rarely-overlaps are reproduced; the claim is reported as partially tested.

claims.statement: The dataset holds 41 recording sessions from 21 patients, every patient with a Sternberg session and all but one (P47HMH) with a screening session.
claims.source: Methods, Subjects, paragraph 1; Table 1 and its legend
claims.quote: In total, 41 recording sessions were completed across 21 patients with intractable localization-related epilepsy (Table 1 ). ... Screening sessions are available for all subjects except for 'P47HMH', for whom screening was not performed.
claims.criterion: Counted from the subjects and the session files. Counts of subjects and sessions are exact, so the tolerance is zero. The text gives ages of 17 to 71, while Table 1 lists ages of 17 to 70; the ages are reported against both and do not decide the claim.

claims.statement: In the Sternberg task 902 units were recorded, 190 in the hippocampus, 259 in the amygdala, 171 in the dACC, 250 in the pre-SMA and 32 in the vmPFC.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Data recorded and spike sorting quality metrics, paragraph 1; Figure 3b
claims.quote: In the Sternberg task, we recorded a total of 902 neurons (190 hippocampus, 259 Amygdala, 171 dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, 250 pre-supplementary motor area, 32 ventromedial prefrontal cortex) (Fig. 3b ).
claims.criterion: Units in the units table of the ses-2 files, assigned to an area by the location of their electrode, left and right merged, as in NWB_countAreas.m and translateArea_SB.m. Tolerances are the protocol's 10%; the exact counts are reported.

claims.statement: In the screening task 907 units were recorded, 449 of them in the MTL.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Data recorded and spike sorting quality metrics, paragraph 1; Figure 3a
claims.quote: In the screening task, we recorded 907 neurons (Fig. 3a ). Of these, 449 were recorded in the MTL.
claims.criterion: Units in the ses-1 files, assigned to areas as for sternberg-unit-yield. The MTL count of 449 equals the Sternberg MTL count (190 + 259), while the screening percentages of claims screening-concept-mtl and screening-concept-mfc imply about 421 MTL and 486 MFC units (138 / 0.3278 and 26 / 0.0535). Both 449 and 421 are readings of the MTL count; the claim holds when the count is within 10% of either, and the notes say which.

claims.statement: Subjects answered on average 88.73% of Sternberg trials correctly.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Behavior, paragraph 1; Figure 1d
claims.quote: During the working memory task (Fig. 1b ), subjects answered on average 88.73% of trials correctly (Fig. 1d ).
claims.criterion: As in NWB_QA_graphs.m, the percent of trials with response_accuracy 1 in each Sternberg session, over all trials, averaged over sessions (Fig. 1d shows the session values with mean and s.e.m.).

claims.statement: Reaction times grew with memory load; a repeated-measures ANOVA of per-session median reaction times found a load effect.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Behavior, paragraph 1; Figure 1c
claims.quote: Accuracy and reaction time varied as a function of load as expected (Fig. 1c ), with higher loads resulting in slower and less accurate answers (F 2,40 = 7.92, P = 0.0013, repeated-measures ANOVA of median reaction times).
claims.criterion: As in NWB_QA_graphs.m, the reaction time is timestamps_Response minus timestamps_Probe, on correct trials only (filter_correct = 1; the paper does not say, the code settles it); the median per session and load; an ANOVA (anovan) with session as a random factor and load as a fixed factor, the code's form of the repeated-measures ANOVA. Reproduced when the load effect has p < 0.05, F is within tolerance, and the mean of the session medians rises from load 1 to load 3; partially reproduced when p < 0.05 and the rise hold but F is outside tolerance. The same test on all trials is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Accuracy was lower at higher memory loads.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Behavior, paragraph 1; Figure 1c
claims.quote: Accuracy and reaction time varied as a function of load as expected (Fig. 1c ), with higher loads resulting in slower and less accurate answers
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test for accuracy and the code computes none. Percent correct per session and load, averaged over sessions. Reproduced when the mean accuracy falls from load 1 to load 2 to load 3; partially reproduced when load 3 is below load 1 but the order is not monotonic; not reproduced otherwise. The per-load values are reported.

claims.statement: Across Sternberg units, refractory period violations (ISIs shorter than 3 ms) were 0.41% of ISIs on average, with a standard deviation of 0.50%.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Data recorded and spike sorting quality metrics, paragraph 2; Figure 3d
claims.quote: On average across all neurons in the Sternberg task, ( i ) refractory period violations were 0.41% ± 0.50% of interspike intervals (ISIs) (Fig. 3d )
claims.criterion: Per unit, the percent of consecutive spike time differences below 3 ms over the whole session, as in NWB_QA_graphs.m. The text says all neurons; the code averages only the units whose value is below 4% (thresh_isi = 4). The text gives the main reading (all units); the code's filter is a variant, and the claim is reproduced when either reading puts both values within tolerance, the notes saying which. The 0.50% is the spread of the units, not an uncertainty of the mean, so each value has the protocol's 10%.

claims.statement: Sternberg units fired at 2.55 Hz on average, ranging from 0.11 to 33.82 Hz.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Data recorded and spike sorting quality metrics, paragraph 2; Figure 3e
claims.quote: (ii) average firing rate was 2.55 Hz, with a range of 0.11–33.82 Hz (Fig. 3e )
claims.criterion: Per unit, the number of spikes divided by the time from first to last spike, as in NWB_QA_graphs.m, over all Sternberg units; mean, minimum and maximum. The range holds when the minimum and maximum lie within 10% of each bound.

claims.statement: The pairwise projection distance between units isolated on the same wire was 13.77 plus or minus 7.32 s.d. of the signal.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Data recorded and spike sorting quality metrics, paragraph 2; Figure 3i
claims.quote: ( iii ) the pairwise projection distance in clustering space between neurons isolated on the same wire was 13.77 ± 7.32 (projection test; in units of s.d. of the signal)
claims.criterion: The stored waveforms_mean_proj_dist of the Sternberg units, zeros removed, mean and standard deviation, as in NWB_QA_graphs.m. The text cites Fig. 3g; the legend places the projection distance in panel i.

claims.statement: The ratio between the s.d. of the noise and the peak amplitude of the mean waveform (an SNR) was 6.62 plus or minus 3.63 across Sternberg units.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Data recorded and spike sorting quality metrics, paragraph 2; Figure 3g,h
claims.quote: ( iv ) the ratio between the s.d. of noise and the peak mean waveform amplitude was 6.62 ± 3.63 (Fig. 3g,h )
claims.criterion: The sentence describes the peak SNR (Fig. 3g) but cites panels g and h, the second being the mean SNR. Readings are (a) the stored waveforms_peak_snr and (b) the stored waveforms_mean_snr, each as mean and standard deviation over Sternberg units, as NWB_QA_graphs.m computes them. Reproduced when either reading puts both values within tolerance; the notes say which.

claims.statement: The modified coefficient of variation of the ISIs (CV2) was 0.94 plus or minus 0.14 across Sternberg units.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Data recorded and spike sorting quality metrics, paragraph 2; Figure 3f
claims.quote: (v) the modified coefficient of variation of the ISIs (CV2 52 ) was 0.94 ± 0.14 (Fig. 3f )
claims.criterion: Per unit, CV2 as in calcCV2.m with ignoreMode 1, the mean over pairs of consecutive ISIs of 2 times the absolute difference over the sum, leaving out pairs in which either ISI exceeds 1 s; over the whole session; mean and standard deviation over Sternberg units, as in NWB_QA_graphs.m.

claims.statement: The median isolation distance of Sternberg units was 31.14.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Data recorded and spike sorting quality metrics, paragraph 2; Figure 3j
claims.quote: (vi) median isolation distance 53 was 31.14 (Fig. 3j )
claims.criterion: The stored waveforms_isolation_distance of the Sternberg units, undefined (NaN) values removed as in NWB_QA_graphs.m, median.

claims.statement: In the screening task, 138 MTL units (32.78%) qualified as concept cells.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Proportion of selective cells, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Screening task: Of the MTL cells, 138 (32.78%) qualified as concept cells (Fig. 4 shows examples).
claims.criterion: Per screening unit, the firing rate 200 to 1000 ms after each image onset (trial start_time; image from StimulusPresentation), all presentations, as in NWB_calcSelective_SC.m. Following the Methods (Cell selection, concept cells), a concept cell passes a permuted one-way ANOVA on image identity (54 to 64 groups) at P < 0.05, and then a permutation t-test of the presentations of the image with the highest mean rate against all other presentations at P < 0.05. The number of permutations is not given; 2000 is used, as in the code's commented permutation alternative (a resolution detail). The Methods say the preferred response must be significantly larger; the code's test is two-sided. Readings of the second test are (a) two-sided and (b) one-sided, larger. The code's parametric version (anovan, then a binarized anovan) is a variant. MTL is amygdala and hippocampus; the percent is taken over the MTL screening units (see screening-unit-yield for the 421 against 449 denominator). Reproduced when the count and percent are within tolerance under both readings of the test; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. Every result is shown.

claims.statement: In the screening task only 26 MFC units (5.35%) were concept cells, far fewer than in the MTL, so that concept cells are largely found in the MTL.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Proportion of selective cells, paragraph 2
claims.quote: In contrast, only 26 (5.35%) of cells in the MFC were concept cells, reproducing our earlier finding that concept cells are largely only found in the MTL.
claims.criterion: The concept cell test and its readings as in screening-concept-mtl, over MFC screening units (dACC, pre-SMA and vmPFC). Reproduced when the count and percent are within tolerance and the MFC percent is below the MTL percent of screening-concept-mtl; partially reproduced when only the comparison holds. The paper reports no test of the comparison.

claims.statement: Five example screening units (Fig. 4a to e) are concept cells.
claims.source: Figure 4 legend
claims.quote: Shown are five ( a – e ) neurons classified as concept cells.
claims.criterion: The units listed for Fig. 5a to e (the paper's Fig. 4) in NWB_SB_plotCell_Screening.m, given as subject ID and 1-based unit index (NWB units id plus 1) of the ses-1 files, are (4, 16), (7, 24), (15, 3), (16, 22) and (21, 15). Reproduced when all five pass the concept cell test of screening-concept-mtl, under the readings named there; partially reproduced for three or four.

claims.statement: In the Sternberg task, 94 MTL units (20.94%) qualified as concept cells during the encoding period.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Proportion of selective cells, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Working memory task: In the MTL, 94 (20.94%) neurons qualified as concept cells during the encoding period (Fig. 5 shows examples).
claims.criterion: Per Sternberg unit, the firing rate 200 to 1000 ms after Encoding 1 onset, all trials, grouped by the Encoding 1 image (5 groups). The Methods say only following stimulus onset; the code (NWB_calcSelective_SB.m) settles it as Encoding 1 only. The tests follow the Methods, a permuted one-way ANOVA at P < 0.05, then a permutation t-test of the trials of the image with the highest mean rate against all other trials at P < 0.05, with 2000 permutations as in screening-concept-mtl and the same two readings of the second test's sidedness. The code's parametric version (anovan twice) is a variant. Percent over the 449 MTL Sternberg units. Reproduced when count and percent are within tolerance under both readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: As a group, concept cells fired more during the maintenance period when their preferred image was held in memory than when it was not (4.76 against 2.67 Hz).
claims.source: Technical Validation, Proportion of selective cells, paragraph 3
claims.quote: As a group, concept cells continued to fire during the maintenance period if their preferred stimulus was held in WM (4.76 ± 4.71 Hz vs. 2.67 ± 3.66 Hz; p = 1.38 × 10 −21 for pref. vs. non-pref. trials, paired one-sided t-test).
claims.criterion: The preferred image is the Encoding 1 image with the highest mean rate in the concept cell test (code). Per cell, the mean maintenance rate 0 to 2500 ms after maintenance onset (the window of the Methods for maintenance cells) over preferred trials and over non-preferred trials; a paired one-sided t-test across cells (paper); values are mean and standard deviation over cells (the code prints std). Two readings of which cells, from the text, are (a) the MTL concept cells of sternberg-concept-mtl, as the sentence follows that count, and (b) all Sternberg concept cells in any area, as the code tests. Two readings of preferred trials, which the paper does not fix, are (i) trials in which the preferred image was shown in any encoding period, as the Fig. 5 maintenance raster in the code splits them, and (ii) trials whose Encoding 1 image is the preferred image, as the code's hzPref is labelled. Both trial readings are run for each cell reading. Reproduced when, for one cell reading, both trial readings give p < 0.05 with preferred higher and put all four expected values (means and standard deviations) within tolerance; blocked as methods_underspecified when the trial readings disagree for that cell reading; not reproduced otherwise. The code as written compares Encoding 1 window rates (200 to 1000 ms), with a mask that leaves no non-preferred trial; the same comparison in the Encoding 1 window with the intended mask is shown as a variant, as it may be what produced the printed numbers.

claims.statement: Two example amygdala units (Fig. 5a,b) are concept cells in the Sternberg task that also show persistent activity during maintenance.
claims.source: Figure 5 legend
claims.quote: ( a,b ) Example responses from 2 neurons classified as concept cells in the Sternberg task that also exhibited persistent activity during the maintenance period. Both cells were recorded in the amygdala.
claims.criterion: The units listed for Fig. 5a,b in NWB_SB_plotCell_Sternberg.m, subject ID and 1-based unit index of the ses-2 files, are (7, 9) and (16, 16). Reproduced when both pass the concept cell test of sternberg-concept-mtl, both electrodes are in the amygdala, and both have a higher mean maintenance rate (0 to 2500 ms) on trials in which the preferred image was shown in any encoding period than on the other trials (the split the code plots). The paper gives no per-cell test of persistence, so none decides the claim. Partially reproduced when one unit meets all three.

claims.statement: In the MFC, 144 units (31.79%) qualified as maintenance cells.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Proportion of selective cells, paragraph 3
claims.quote: In the MFC, 144 (31.79%) cells qualified as maintenance cells and 122 (26.93%) as probe cells.
claims.criterion: Per Sternberg unit, all trials, the mean rate 0 to 2500 ms after maintenance onset against the rate 0 to 500 ms after fixation cross onset, by a one-sided permutation test (increase) at P < 0.05 (Methods; the Methods give the 500 ms baseline length, and the code, NWB_calcSelective_SB.m, places it at fixation onset; the fixation cross lasts 900 to 1000 ms). A unit that is also a concept cell (by the test of sternberg-concept-mtl) must in addition pass the same test on its non-preferred trials. The Methods do not say how the permutation is formed; readings are (a) shuffling the labels of the trial rates between the two periods, as the code's commented alternative permutationTest with sidedness larger, and (b) flipping the sign of the per-trial differences, a paired form. Non-preferred trials are read as (i) trials whose Encoding 1 image is not the preferred image (the code's intent), and (ii) trials in which the preferred image was not shown in any encoding period. 2000 permutations, as in the code's comment. The code's paired one-sided t-tests are a variant. Percent over MFC Sternberg units (dACC, pre-SMA, vmPFC; 453 by sternberg-unit-yield). Reproduced when count and percent are within tolerance under all readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: In the MFC, 122 units (26.93%) qualified as probe cells.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Proportion of selective cells, paragraph 3
claims.quote: In the MFC, 144 (31.79%) cells qualified as maintenance cells and 122 (26.93%) as probe cells.
claims.criterion: Per Sternberg unit, all trials, the rate 200 to 1000 ms after probe onset against the encoding rate (200 to 1000 ms) and, separately, against the maintenance rate (0 to 2500 ms), each by a one-sided permutation t-test (probe higher) at P < 0.05; a probe cell passes both (Methods). The Methods do not fix the encoding rate; readings are (i) the rate pooled over the 200 to 1000 ms windows of every encoding period shown in the trial, as the code intends, and (ii) Encoding 1 only. The permutation is read as (a) label shuffling and (b) paired sign flipping, as in maintenance-cells-mfc; 2000 permutations. The code's paired one-sided t-tests, with its Encoding 3 window taken at Encoding 2 onset, are a variant. Percent over the 453 MFC Sternberg units. Reproduced when count and percent are within tolerance under all readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: In head-fixed mice moving a free floating chamber with a single cue, 14.0% of RSC neurons (373 of 2665) are heading selective, with no head movement.
claims.source: Results, Neurons in the RSC represent heading in the absence of physical head movements, paragraph 2; Figure 1D, E
claims.quote: revealing that a proportion of neurons in RSC faithfully represent heading (14.0%, 373/2665 neurons
claims.criterion: The 4 free-chamber recordings over 3 mice. Method from the Methods (Analysis of calcium data, paragraph 2) and code FreelyMoving.m. The Rayleigh vector length of each neuron's tuning curve (inferred spikes, 6 degree bins, 15 degree smoothing) is compared with 1000 values from the spike data circularly shifted in time by a random amount; a neuron is selective when its RVL meets or exceeds the 99th percentile (Methods). The code keeps only frames with chamber speed above 2 (FreelyMoving.checkIsMoving), which the Methods do not mention; and its default threshold is the 95th percentile. Readings, run in turn, (a) all frames, 99th percentile; (b) moving frames only, 99th percentile; (c) the code's 95th percentile on moving frames, as a variant. Reproduced when (a) or (b) gives a percentage within tolerance; (c) is reported.

claims.statement: With the chamber rotated by a motor (single cue), 14.2% of RSC neurons (452 of 3179, 16 recordings over 5 mice) are heading selective by the paper's reliability and Gaussian-fit test, a percentage similar to the free-chamber experiments.
claims.source: Results, Neurons in the RSC represent heading in the absence of physical head movements, paragraph 3; Figure 1G
claims.quote: we found a similar percentage heading neurons as in the experiments without controlled rotation, comprising 14.2% (452/3179 neurons) of the total number of cells recorded (n = 16 recordings over 5 mice
claims.criterion: The heading-selection test of the opening comment (Methods; code ControlledRotation.calculateHeadDirection) with a single-term Gaussian, on inferred spikes of every neuron of the 16 single-cue controlled-rotation recordings. Reproduced when the percentage is within tolerance. The test uses random splits and shuffles; the random seed is a standard choice that should not change the count beyond a few cells.

claims.statement: Run on pre-shuffled data, the heading-selection test passes no cells, so the count of heading-selective cells is not due to chance.
claims.source: Methods, Analysis of calcium data, paragraph 4
claims.quote: When repeating these procedures using pre-shuffled data, no cells passed these criteria, suggesting that the number of heading selective cells is accurate, and not due to chance
claims.criterion: The test of fig1g-rotation-heading-fraction, run after circularly shifting each trial's tuning curve by an independent random amount before the test, as in the commented calculateHeadDirection_shuff of Cue.m (code). The Methods do not say on which recordings; the single-cue controlled-rotation recordings are used, as the claim follows that test. Reproduced when no cell passes; partially reproduced when some pass but no more than 1% of cells (the combined significance of p = 0.01 the Methods give for the thresholds); not reproduced above 1%.

claims.statement: The preferred headings of heading-selective cells tile the whole circumference of the chamber, including headings with the cue outside the visual field, with a moderate overrepresentation near 0 degrees, where the cue is centered in front of the mouse.
claims.source: Results, Neurons in the RSC represent heading in the absence of physical head movements, paragraph 3; Figure 1H
claims.quote: showing that heading-responsive cells tile the entire circumference of the chamber, even when the cue card is outside of the visual field of the mouse; though we note there is a moderate overrepresentation of responses when the cue is centered in front of the mouse near 0°
claims.criterion: The cells selected in fig1g-rotation-heading-fraction; the preferred heading of each is the peak bin of its trial-mean tuning curve, cross-validated as in the Methods (sorted by "cross-validated angle of peak response", Figure 1H legend). Heading 0 is the cue centered in front of the mouse (Results); how the dataset's heading maps to the cue is the author's to find. The paper gives no measure of tiling or of overrepresentation, so both are open, with these readings, (a) every one of the 60 bins of 6 degrees holds at least one preferred heading; (b) every 90 degree quadrant, including the one centered on 180 degrees, holds at least 10% of the preferred headings. For the overrepresentation, the share of preferred headings within 45 degrees of 0 exceeds 25% (its share under uniformity). Reproduced when the overrepresentation holds and tiling holds under (a) or (b).

claims.statement: Matched ROIs have on average the same preferred heading relative to the wall pattern whether the head is rotated in a fixed chamber or the chamber is rotated around a fixed head (V-test against 0 degrees, V = 14.1, p = 2.5e-4), though not all cells keep their preference.
claims.source: Results, Heading cells exhibit similar preferred directions during rotation of the animal or the environment; Figure 2E, F
claims.quote: matched ROIs on average have the same heading preference with respect to wall pattern across conditions ... (V32 = 14.1, p = 2.5 × 10−4, V-test for nonuniformity against 0°
claims.criterion: The 5 head-rotation recordings, each paired with its chamber-rotation recording of the same field; ROIs matched across the two (a single set of ROIs after derotation, manually checked, Results). Per ROI the difference in preferred heading, head rotation minus chamber rotation, wrapped to +-180; circ_vtest against 0. Open, with readings, the cells, (a) matched ROIs heading-selective in both conditions, (b) in either condition, (c) in the chamber-rotation condition; the preferred heading, (i) the peak of the trial-mean tuning curve (Figure 2F legend, "peak heading preference"), (ii) the code's 'fit' method (Cue.calculatePreferredDirection, recommended in the code's README). Reproduced when a reading gives p < 0.05 with V > 0; the V and n of each reading are reported, and the one whose n is 32 is named.

claims.statement: When all the wall cues are replaced, heading cells remap coherently, each shifting its preferred heading by about the same angle as the rest of the population in its recording (V-test of the Delta phase offsets against 0 degrees, V = 25.6, p = 4.9e-6).
claims.source: Results, Changing visual cues elicits coherent remapping in RSC neurons; Figure 3C
claims.quote: changing contexts caused the population of heading cells to coherently remap, as indicated by low Δ phase offsets (V66 = 25.6, p = 4.9 × 10−6
claims.criterion: The 12 remapping recordings (single-cue class in the code, RemappingExperiment). Per neuron n, Delta phase offset = (pref A(n) - pref B(n)) minus the expected offset of the other neurons of its recording, wrapped to +-180; circ_vtest against 0 over all neurons of all recordings (Methods, Calculation of coherent remapping). Open, with readings, the expected offset, (i) the median over the other neurons of their differences pref A - pref B (Methods text) or (ii) the median of their pref A minus the median of their pref B (the Methods equation); the cells, (a) heading-selective in both contexts, (b) in either; the preferred heading, the peak of the trial-mean tuning curve or the code's 'fit' method. Reproduced when a reading gives p < 0.05 with V > 0; every reading's V and n are reported.

claims.statement: In the light-on condition with two symmetric cues, ADN axons in RSC show unimodal heading tuning curves, while visual cortical (AM/PM) axons show bimodal tuning curves with peaks about 180 degrees apart.
claims.source: Results, The ADN and visual cortex send distinct information to RSC, paragraph 2; Figure 4D, E
claims.quote: In the light-on condition, ADN axons show a unimodal tuning curve, whereas visual cortical axons show a bimodal tuning curve
claims.criterion: The 17 ADN and 7 AM/PM axon recordings (AxonExperiment, three light/dark repeats). Light-on tuning curves, cross-validated alignment on light-on trials. The paper's measure of bimodality is the flip score (Methods). The axons shown are open, with readings, (a) axons passing the heading-selection test with a two-term Gaussian; (b) all axons. Reproduced when, under a reading, the flip score of the mean aligned light-on curve is below 0 for ADN and above 0 for visual axons, and the mean flip score of single visual axons exceeds that of ADN axons (two-sample KS test, p < 0.05, the paper's test for two distributions).

claims.statement: In the light-off condition ADN axons keep their heading tuning for several trials, while visual cortical axons lose their tuning.
claims.source: Results, The ADN and visual cortex send distinct information to RSC, paragraph 2; Figure 4D, E legends
claims.quote: In the light-off condition, ADN axons maintain their response for several trials, whereas visual cortical axons lose their tuning
claims.criterion: Same recordings, axons and readings as fig4-axons-light-on-shape; light-off trials aligned with the light-on shifts (Methods). The paper gives no test; the measure is the paper's heading-selection test run on light-off trials only (the code's 'dark' option of calculateHeadDirection), with a two-term Gaussian. Reproduced when the fraction of axons selective in light-off is higher for ADN than for visual axons (two-sample comparison of per-recording fractions; Fisher's exact test on the pooled counts as a variant), and the mean aligned light-off curve of ADN axons peaks within 18 degrees (the decoder's accuracy window) of the light-on peak bin while that of visual axons has a peak-to-trough range under half of its light-on range. "For several trials" is not tested further.

claims.statement: The diversity of RSC responses (a second peak in light, as in visual axons, and a single peak in the dark, as in ADN axons) persists regardless of the direction of chamber rotation (bootstrapped KS test, p = 0.0094, 4 recordings over 2 mice).
claims.source: Results, A functional class of RSC neurons coregisters visual and heading signals, paragraph 1; Figure S5
claims.quote: These responses persisted regardless of rotation direction (Figure S5, p = 0.0094, bootstrapped KS-test, n = 4 recordings over 2 mice)
claims.criterion: Figure S5, where the test is shown, was not read (supplement missing). The Methods give the test (p is one minus the fraction of bootstrap iterations in which a two-sample KS test passes at alpha 0.05) but not what is compared. Readings the text allows, (a) the distribution of differences in preferred heading between clockwise and counterclockwise rotation for heading-selective cells against the same differences with cells paired at random (as the shuffles of Figures 2F and 3C); (b) the correlations of each cell's clockwise and counterclockwise tuning curves against those of randomly paired cells. Reproduced when a reading gives p < 0.05 with the real pairs closer than the random ones. The number of bootstrap iterations is not given for this test; 1000, as for the decoding, is the reading.

claims.statement: The diversity of RSC responses persists whether or not the mouse is in control of the arena (bootstrapped KS test, p = 0.031, 7 recordings over 3 mice).
claims.source: Results, A functional class of RSC neurons coregisters visual and heading signals, paragraph 1; Figure S6
claims.quote: or whether or not the animal was in control of the arena (Figure S6, 0.031, bootstrapped KS-test, n = 7 recordings over 3 mice)
claims.criterion: As for figs5-rotation-direction, with animal-controlled against motor-controlled rotation in place of the two directions. Figure S6 was not read (supplement missing), so what is compared is open, with the readings (a) and (b) of figs5-rotation-direction. Reproduced when a reading gives p < 0.05 with the real pairs closer than the random ones.

claims.statement: Clustering the Gaussian-fit coefficients of RSC somatic tuning curves in light-on and light-off conditions gives an optimum of three functional classes (heading, landmark and alignment cells), though the responses span a continuum.
claims.source: Results, A functional class of RSC neurons coregisters visual and heading signals, paragraph 1; Figure 5B; Methods, Clustering of RSC soma responses
claims.quote: We found that the data were optimally clustered into three functional classes ... although we note that the responses span a continuum
claims.criterion: The 36 dual-cue RSC soma recordings over 6 mice; heading-selective cells only (two- term Gaussian test of the opening comment), as the reviewer code clusters is_head_direction cells and the Results speak of tuned cells. For each cell, the light-on and light-off tuning curves are aligned (cross-validated, light-on shifts), rescaled together to [0, 1] (code rowrescale on the concatenation) and each fitted with the two-term Gaussian (Methods, eq. 4; code LightDarkExperiment.calculateTuningFits2); the features are a1, a2, c1, c2 of both fits (8 values; Methods). Silhouette evaluation of Gaussian mixture models (Methods) for k = 2, 3 and 4. The cells clustered are open, with readings, (a) heading-selective cells only, as above (the Results give class shares "of the total number of tuned cells"); (b) all cells (Methods, "all cells were fit with a sum of Gaussians"). Both are run. Reproduced when the silhouette value at k = 3 exceeds those at k = 2 and k = 4 (a local maximum, Methods). The reviewer code's fit (calculateTuningFits, on unaligned curves centered on their peak) is a variant and is reported.

claims.statement: 12.1% of RSC neurons are tuned in the dual-cue experiment; of these, landmark cells are the plurality (33%), followed by alignment cells (28%) and heading cells (22%).
claims.source: Results, A functional class of RSC neurons coregisters visual and heading signals, paragraph 3; Figure 5C to E
claims.quote: Of the total number of tuned cells (12.1 ± 1.1%), landmark cells made up the plurality of cells (33 ± 3.5%), followed by alignment cells (28 ± 1.9%, mean ± s.e.m.), and heading (22 ± 2.3%) cells
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e.m. Classes from a 3-component GMM on the features of fig5-three-classes (the reviewer code fits it with 20 replicates and up to 1000 iterations, followed). Then, per the Methods, cells whose minimum Mahalanobis distance to the component centroids is "significantly greater" go to a null cluster; archetypal light-on and light-off curves are built from each component's mean coefficients (eq. 4, with b1 and b2 at the code's pi/2 and 3pi/2); each cell goes to the class whose archetypes have the smallest summed cosine distance to its two curves. Classes are named by their archetypes as in the Results (heading, unimodal in light and dark; landmark, bimodal in light and absent in dark; alignment, bimodal in light and unimodal in dark). Open, with readings, the outlier rule, (a) squared Mahalanobis distance beyond the 95th percentile of a chi-square with 8 degrees of freedom, (b) no outlier step (the reviewer code); the averaging, (i) mean over recordings, (ii) mean over mice, (iii) pooled cells. The F-test degrees of freedom of Figure 5F to H imply 332 heading, 522 landmark and 409 alignment cells (2n - 2), and 332 is the smallest class in the decoding Methods; those counts are reported for comparison. The heat-map axis labels of Figure 5, as extracted from the PDF text (the figure could not be viewed), read 332, 409 and 552 cells for the three classes and 1569 for Figure 5A; pooled, 332, 552 and 409 of 1569 are 21%, 35% and 26%, close to the reported shares, so 552 may be the landmark count, which disagrees with the 522 implied by F(1,1042). Reproduced when a reading puts all four values within tolerance with landmark > alignment > heading; partially reproduced when the order holds but a value falls outside.

claims.statement: In alignment cells the single light-off peak is always at the location of one of the two light-on peaks, so landmark and heading responses are coregistered.
claims.source: Results, A functional class of RSC neurons coregisters visual and heading signals, paragraph 2; Figure 5E
claims.quote: The light-off peak in these alignment cells was always at the same location as one of the two peaks in the light-on condition
claims.criterion: The alignment cells of fig5-class-proportions; aligned light-on and light-off tuning curves (light-on shifts applied to both, Methods). The paper gives no test; the paper's test for angles clustered at a value is the V-test (Methods), which is used. Per cell, the offset of the light-off peak bin from the nearer of the two light-on peaks (the peak bin and the peak bin of the other half circle), wrapped to +-180; circ_vtest against 0. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with V > 0; the share of cells with an offset within 18 degrees is reported.

claims.statement: Heading cells show no significant difference in flip score between light-on and light-off conditions.
claims.source: Results, A functional class of RSC neurons coregisters visual and heading signals, paragraph 3; Figure 5F
claims.quote: Heading cells showed no significant difference in flip score across conditions (F1,662 = 0.18, p = 0.67
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Flip score (Methods, eq. 5; code Cue.calculateFlipScore) of each heading cell's light-on and light-off tuning curve. The paper's test is an F-test on the light condition in a (generalized) linear mixed-effects model with mouse as random effect (Methods, Statistical information, mixed models control for cells within the same animal; the residual df 2n - 2 fit one fixed effect and an intercept), run as fitlme-style flip ~ light + (1|mouse). Reproduced when p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The difference in mean flip score is reported either way, and a model with a random intercept per cell as well is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Landmark and alignment cells have significantly lower flip scores in light-off than in light-on (landmark F(1,1042) = 1062.5, p = 3.1e-161; alignment F(1,816) = 209.5, p = 2.0e-42).
claims.source: Results, A functional class of RSC neurons coregisters visual and heading signals, paragraph 3; Figure 5G, H
claims.quote: both landmark (F1,1042 = 1062.5, p = 3.1 × 10−161) and alignment (F1,816 = 209.5, p = 2.0 × 10−42) cells have significantly lower flip scores in the light-off than the light-on condition
claims.criterion: As fig5f-heading-flip-unchanged, for landmark and for alignment cells. Reproduced when both classes have p < 0.05 with the light-off flip score lower; partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: Projected into the soma clusters' discriminant space, ADN axons fall mostly within the heading cluster and visual axons mostly within the landmark cluster, with some overlap with the alignment cluster.
claims.source: Results, A functional class of RSC neurons coregisters visual and heading signals, paragraph 4; Figure 5I
