claims.statement: Below the crossover, paired pulses enhance electroporation up to about three-fold over single pulses at 90 to 100 degrees for both frequencies, followed by a plateau down to 0 degrees, so pulses at 90 degrees and at smaller angles are as efficient as co-directional pulses.
claims.source: Results, 2.1, paragraphs 3 and 4; Figure 2; Discussion, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Further reduction of the angle enhanced electroporation, up to about three-fold at 90–100° for both nsEP frequencies, followed by a plateau all the way to 0°
claims.criterion: Measure as in fig2-180-cancellation. The level "about three-fold at 90-100 degrees, followed by a plateau" has two readings of the reported number, (1) the mean of the ROI values between 90 and 100 degrees and (2) the mean of the ROI values from 100 degrees to the smallest angle; it holds when it matches under either, with either normalization. The paper defines neither the plateau nor where it is reached and gives no test. Readings of the plateau, both run (a choice that could change the outcome) over the ROI means from 0 to 90 degrees, (P1) a linear fit of value against angle whose slope has a 95% confidence interval that includes zero, and (P2) the mean of the ROIs below 10 degrees within 10% (the claim's tolerance) of the mean of the ROIs between 90 and 100 degrees. The angle where the plateau is reached is the largest angle at which the mean value first comes within 10% of the level, a standard choice tied to the tolerance. Reproduced when, under each background reading, the levels hold for both frequencies, that angle lies within 81 to 110 degrees, and the plateau holds at both frequencies; blocked as methods_underspecified when the plateau readings or the background readings give different outcomes.

claims.statement: Pairing pulses enhances electroporation at small angles and inhibits it at large angles in a frequency-dependent manner, with stronger cancellation at 833 kHz than at 1 Hz.
claims.source: Figure 2 legend; Results, 2.1, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Note that applying pulses in pairs enhanced electroporation at small angles but inhibited them at large angles in a frequency-dependent manner
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test, and Results 2.1 reads the frequency dependence from the 180 degree values ("Stronger cancellation at sub-MHz frequencies") and the crossover angles. Measure as in fig2-180-cancellation and fig2-crossover-angle. Reproduced when, under each background reading, the mean paired-pulse value at the 180 degree reading is lower at 833 kHz than at 1 Hz and the 833 kHz crossover angle is smaller than the 1 Hz one, with values above 100% at the smallest angles and below 100% at the largest at both frequencies, under one normalization reading at least; blocked as methods_underspecified when background readings (a) and (b) give different outcomes.

claims.statement: At 833 kHz, co-directional and counter-directional pulse pairs differ about 60-fold in electroporation efficiency.
claims.source: Results, 2.3, paragraph 1; Figure 2
claims.quote: The profound, 60-fold difference in electroporation efficiency of co- and counter-directional nsEPs at 833 kHz ( Figure 2 )
claims.criterion: Measure as in fig2-180-cancellation, at 833 kHz. The paper does not say which values form the ratio. Readings of the reported number, (a) the ROI of smallest angle over the ROI of largest angle, and (b) the plateau level of fig2-facilitation-plateau over the 180 degree value of fig2-180-cancellation (3-fold over 1/20 gives the paper's 60, so (b) is the paper's arithmetic). Reproduced when one of these, under one normalization reading, is within tolerance, under each background reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when background readings (a) and (b) give different outcomes.

claims.statement: In the square array at 1 Hz, co-directional and cross-directional (90 degree) paired pulses have the same electroporation efficiency at the array center.
claims.source: Results, 2.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3
claims.quote: Consistently with the measurements in Figure 2 , co- and cross-directional pulses at 1 Hz had the same electroporation efficiency ( Figure 3 )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Per dish, the mean YP intensity in the single 200 x 200 um ROI at the array center (Methods 4.4), after 4 paired pulses at 10 kV/cm (Figure 3 legend), under background readings (a) and (b). The paper's test, from the Figure 3 legend, a two-tailed Student's t-test (unpaired, equal variance) of co- against cross-directional dishes at 1 Hz, n = 6 each, at p < 0.05. Reproduced when p >= 0.05, not reproduced when p < 0.05; the ratio of means and p are reported either way. The outcome is taken under background reading (b), the correction Methods 4.4 names; reading (a) and Welch's test are variants.

claims.statement: Raising the pulse frequency from 1 Hz to 770 kHz enhances electroporation by co-directional paired pulses, attributed to temporal summation of the induced membrane potential.
claims.source: Results, 2.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3
claims.quote: Increasing the pulse frequency to 770 kHz enhanced electroporation by the co-directional pulses because of the temporal summation of the induced membrane potential
claims.criterion: Measure as in fig3-1hz-co-equals-cross. A two-tailed Student's t-test (unpaired, equal variance; Figure 3 legend) of co-directional dishes at 770 kHz against 1 Hz. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with the 770 kHz mean higher, under each background reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The explanation by temporal summation is not tested.

claims.statement: Cross-directional paired pulses at 770 kHz are just as effective as at 1 Hz; charging two different membrane regions does not cause summation.
claims.source: Results, 2.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3
claims.quote: Interestingly, charging two different regions of the cell membrane did not cause summation, making cross-directional pulses at 770 kHz just as effective as at 1 Hz
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Measure as in fig3-1hz-co-equals-cross. A two-tailed Student's t-test (unpaired, equal variance; Figure 3 legend) of cross-directional dishes at 770 kHz against 1 Hz, at p < 0.05. Reproduced when p >= 0.05, not reproduced when p < 0.05; the ratio of means and p are reported either way. Background reading (b) decides; reading (a) and Welch's test are variants.

claims.statement: Unlike with long pulses, YP uptake after nsEP does not depend on whether the same or a larger area of the cell membrane is electroporated.
claims.source: Results, 2.2, paragraph 1 (last sentence)
claims.quote: Contrary to data with “long” pulses [ 10 , 11 ], electroporative dye uptake after nsEP did not depend on whether we electroporated the same or a larger area of the cell membrane
claims.criterion: The sentence closes the Figure 3 paragraph, whose evidence is the 1 Hz comparison, where co- and cross-directional pulses differ only in the membrane area charged. Judged by the outcome of fig3-1hz-co-equals-cross. The Discussion, paragraph 1, draws the same conclusion from Figure 2; the outcome of fig2-facilitation-plateau is reported alongside and does not decide.

claims.statement: With single-pulse trains on one base electrode, YP uptake follows the electric field map; with paired pulses on both base electrodes at 833 kHz, uptake is strong near the grounded apex electrode and weak or absent near the base electrodes despite the strong field there.
claims.source: Results, 2.3, paragraph 1; Figure 4A to 4C
claims.quote: In control cell monolayers exposed to a train of five single pulses applied to one of the base electrodes (833 kHz, 4 kV), the distribution of YP fluorescence ( Figure 4 A) simply followed the electric field strength map ... produced a strong effect near the apex electrode (ground) but weak or no effect near the base electrodes, despite the strong electric field there
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test. From Results 2.3 and Methods 4.4, the mean YP intensity in 200 x 200 um ROIs adjacent to the apex electrode and to each base electrode, under each background reading. Reproduced when, in the paired-pulse sample, uptake next to the apex exceeds uptake next to each base electrode, and in the single-pulse sample uptake next to the energized base electrode exceeds uptake next to the apex. "Near" is not defined; the readings are ROIs touching the edge of the electrode footprint (1.5 mm outer diameter, Methods 4.2) and ROIs 200 um farther out, both run, and the outcome is the one all readings give, else blocked as methods_underspecified. The match to the field map is reported as the Spearman correlation of ROI uptake with field strength (field from the angle-reading models of the opening comment), with no threshold, as the paper gives none.

claims.statement: Cells between the base electrodes show sawtooth-like membrane potential changes in synchrony with the alternating pulses, about a 10% FluoVolt emission increase at the cathode-facing pole and a 10% decrease at the anode-facing pole.
claims.source: Results, 2.4, paragraph 2; Figure 5
claims.quote: Cells placed between the base electrodes displayed sawtooth-like changes in membrane potential in synchrony with the applied pulses ( Figure 5 ). Depolarization at the cathode-facing pole of the cell manifested as a ~10% emission increase, and hyperpolarization at the anode-facing pole caused a ~10% emission decrease
claims.criterion: From Methods 4.5 and the Figure 5 legend, emission changes at the two poles in the direction of the maximum field gradient, normalized to whole-cell emission, averaged over the time-increment and decrement series and over 5 cells. Reproduced when both peak changes are within tolerance and the pole signals reverse sign with each change of pulse direction.

claims.statement: Cells near the apex reach a much larger polarization, about 25% FluoVolt emission change, more than twice that near the base electrodes, which follows the envelope of the pulse train and not the individual pulses.
claims.source: Results, 2.4, paragraph 2; Figure 5
claims.quote: In stark contrast, the cells near the apex reached a much higher polarization (~25% change in FluoVolt emission), which followed the envelope of the pulse train but not the individual pulses of it
claims.criterion: Measure as in fig5-base-sawtooth, at the apex location. Reproduced when the peak change is within tolerance, more than twice the base-location peak change ("More than a twofold larger polarization", same paragraph), and does not reverse sign at each pulse through the train.

claims.statement: At 1 Hz, co-directional and cross-directional (90 degree) paired pulses in the square array have the same electroporation efficiency, measured as YP uptake at the array center.
claims.source: Results, 2.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3
claims.quote: Consistently with the measurements in Figure 2 , co- and cross-directional pulses at 1 Hz had the same electroporation efficiency ( Figure 3 )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Measure, per dish, the mean YP (FITC) intensity in the single 200 x 200 um ROI at the center of the square array, 10 min after 4 paired pulses at 10 kV/cm (Methods 4.2 and 4.4; Figure 3 legend), under background readings (a) and (b) of the opening comment. Test, from the Figure 3 legend, a two-tailed Student's t-test (unpaired, equal variance) of the co-directional against the cross-directional dishes at 1 Hz, n = 6 each. Reproduced when p >= 0.05 under the paper's test, not reproduced when p < 0.05; the ratio of the group means and the p-value are reported either way. Background reading (b) is the one used for the outcome when the footprints can be located, as the Methods name it as the correction for spontaneous uptake; reading (a) and Welch's test are variants.

claims.statement: Raising the pulse frequency from 1 Hz to 770 kHz enhances electroporation by co-directional paired pulses, attributed to temporal summation of the induced membrane potential.
claims.source: Results, 2.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3
claims.quote: Increasing the pulse frequency to 770 kHz enhanced electroporation by the co-directional pulses because of the temporal summation of the induced membrane potential
claims.criterion: Measure as in fig3-1hz-co-equals-cross. A two-tailed Student's t-test (unpaired, equal variance) of co-directional dishes at 770 kHz against co-directional dishes at 1 Hz (Figure 3 legend). Reproduced when p < 0.05 and the 770 kHz mean is higher, under each background reading that can be computed; blocked as methods_underspecified when the two readings disagree. The temporal summation explanation is not tested.

claims.statement: Cross-directional paired pulses at 770 kHz are just as effective as at 1 Hz; charging two different regions of the membrane does not cause summation.
claims.source: Results, 2.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3
claims.quote: Interestingly, charging two different regions of the cell membrane did not cause summation, making cross-directional pulses at 770 kHz just as effective as at 1 Hz
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Measure as in fig3-1hz-co-equals-cross. A two-tailed Student's t-test (unpaired, equal variance) of cross-directional dishes at 770 kHz against cross-directional dishes at 1 Hz (Figure 3 legend). Reproduced when p >= 0.05, not reproduced when p < 0.05; the ratio of means and the p-value are reported either way. Background reading (b) decides as in fig3-1hz-co-equals-cross; reading (a) and Welch's test are variants.

claims.statement: At 770 kHz, co-directional paired pulses electroporate more than cross-directional ones.
claims.source: Results, 2.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3
claims.criterion: Measure as in fig3-1hz-co-equals-cross. A two-tailed Student's t-test (unpaired, equal variance) of co-directional against cross-directional dishes at 770 kHz. Reproduced when p < 0.05 and the co-directional mean is higher, under each background reading that can be computed; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Unlike with long pulses, YP uptake after nsEP does not depend on whether the same or a larger area of the membrane is electroporated.
claims.source: Results, 2.2, paragraph 1 (last sentence); Discussion, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Contrary to data with “long” pulses [ 10 , 11 ], electroporative dye uptake after nsEP did not depend on whether we electroporated the same or a larger area of the cell membrane
claims.criterion: The Results sentence closes the Figure 3 paragraph, and its evidence is the 1 Hz comparison of Figure 3, where co- and cross-directional pulses differ only in the membrane area charged. Judged by the outcome of fig3-1hz-co-equals-cross. The Discussion, paragraph 1, also cites Figure 2 (pulses at 90 degrees and smaller angles "just as efficient as co-directional pulses"); the outcome of fig2-facilitation-plateau is reported alongside and does not decide.

claims.statement: At a 180 degree change of field direction, paired-pulse trains give less YP uptake than single-pulse trains, 2-fold less at 1 Hz and 20-fold less at 833 kHz.
claims.source: Results, 2.1, paragraph 3; Figure 2
claims.quote: Maximum cancellation was expectedly observed at the 180° vector change, reducing YP uptake compared to single-pulse trains 2-fold at 1 Hz and as much as 20-fold at 833 kHz
claims.criterion: From the Figure 2 legend and Methods 4.4, per ROI along the bisecting line of the triangular array, paired-pulse YP intensity as % of the single-pulse train in the same ROI, averaged over the n = 3 experiments; the angle of each ROI from the field simulation (Figure 7). "At the 180 degree vector change" is read as (1) the ROI nearest the base (largest angle) or (2) the ROI of lowest mean uptake ("maximum cancellation"); with the normalization readings (i) and (ii) of the opening comment these are readings of the reported numbers, and a value holds when it matches under any of them. The background readings (a) and (b) are method details and are both run, and the claim is reproduced when, under each, both values hold and the 833 kHz cancellation is stronger than at 1 Hz; when (a) and (b) give different outcomes it is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Cancellation weakens as the angle is reduced, and paired and single pulses become equally effective at about 160 degrees at 1 Hz and about 130 degrees at 833 kHz.
claims.source: Results, 2.1, paragraph 3; Figure 2
claims.quote: Cancellation weakened as the angle was reduced, and at about 160° (1 Hz) or 130° (833 kHz), the effects of paired-pulse trains became the same as those of single-pulse ones
claims.criterion: Measure as in fig2-180-cancellation. The crossover is the angle at which the mean paired-pulse uptake crosses 100%, by linear interpolation between neighboring ROIs (the paper does not say how it was located; interpolation is a standard choice that cannot move the value by more than one ROI spacing). Reproduced when both angles fall within tolerance under one normalization reading at least, for each background reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when background readings (a) and (b) disagree.

claims.statement: Below the crossover, paired pulses enhance electroporation up to about three-fold over single pulses at 90 to 100 degrees for both frequencies, followed by a plateau down to 0 degrees.
claims.source: Results, 2.1, paragraph 3; Figure 2
claims.quote: Further reduction of the angle enhanced electroporation, up to about three-fold at 90–100° for both nsEP frequencies, followed by a plateau all the way to 0°
claims.criterion: Measure as in fig2-180-cancellation. "Up to about three-fold at 90-100 degrees, followed by a plateau" allows two readings of the level, (1) the mean of the ROIs between 90 and 100 degrees and (2) the mean of the ROIs from 100 degrees to the apex; the level holds when it matches under either, and under either normalization reading. The paper defines neither the plateau nor where it is reached and gives no test. As standard choices, named as such, the plateau holds when a linear fit of uptake against angle over 0 to 90 degrees has a slope whose 95% confidence interval includes zero, and the angle where it is reached is the largest angle at which the mean uptake first comes within 10% of the level (the claim's tolerance). Reproduced when, under each background reading, the levels are within tolerance for both frequencies, that angle lies within 81 to 110 degrees, and the plateau holds; blocked as methods_underspecified when background readings (a) and (b) disagree.

claims.statement: At 833 kHz the electroporation efficiency of co-directional and counter-directional pulse pairs differs about 60-fold.
claims.source: Results, 2.3, paragraph 1; Figure 2
claims.quote: The profound, 60-fold difference in electroporation efficiency of co- and counter-directional nsEPs at 833 kHz ( Figure 2 )
claims.criterion: Measure as in fig2-180-cancellation, at 833 kHz. The paper does not say which values form the ratio; the readings are (a) the ROI nearest the apex over the ROI nearest the base, and (b) the plateau level of fig2-facilitation-plateau over the value of fig2-180-cancellation (3-fold over 1/20 gives the paper's 60, so (b) is the paper's arithmetic). Reproduced when one of these readings, under one normalization reading, is within tolerance, for each background reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when background readings (a) and (b) disagree.

claims.statement: With single-pulse trains on one base electrode, YP uptake follows the electric field map; with paired pulses on both base electrodes at 833 kHz, uptake is strong near the (grounded, never energized) apex electrode and weak or absent near the base electrodes despite the strong field there, forming a comet-shaped region pointing from the apex toward the base.
claims.source: Results, 2.3, paragraph 1; Figure 4A to 4C; Discussion, paragraph 3
claims.quote: In control cell monolayers exposed to a train of five single pulses applied to one of the base electrodes (833 kHz, 4 kV), the distribution of YP fluorescence ( Figure 4 A) simply followed the electric field strength map ... produced a strong effect near the apex electrode (ground) but weak or no effect near the base electrodes, despite the strong electric field there
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test. From Results 2.3, measure the mean YP intensity in 200 x 200 um ROIs (the ROI size of Methods 4.4) adjacent to the apex electrode and to each base electrode, with background reading (b) where footprints can be found. Reproduced when, in the paired-pulse sample, uptake next to the apex exceeds uptake next to each base electrode, and in the single-pulse sample uptake next to the energized base electrode exceeds uptake next to the apex. "Near" is not defined in the paper; as standard choices, the readings are ROIs touching the edge of the electrode footprint (1.5 mm outer diameter, Methods 4.2), and ROIs one ROI width (200 um) farther out; the outcome is the one both give. The match to the field map is reported as the Spearman correlation of ROI uptake with field strength, with no threshold, as the paper gives none; the simulated field map (Figure 7B) is not given as numbers, so this is reported only where the field can be computed from the electrode positions.

claims.statement: Cells between the base electrodes show sawtooth-like membrane potential changes in synchrony with the alternating pulses, about a 10% FluoVolt emission increase at the cathode-facing pole and a 10% decrease at the anode-facing pole.
claims.source: Results, 2.4, paragraph 2; Figure 5
claims.quote: Cells placed between the base electrodes displayed sawtooth-like changes in membrane potential in synchrony with the applied pulses ( Figure 5 ). Depolarization at the cathode-facing pole of the cell manifested as a ~10% emission increase, and hyperpolarization at the anode-facing pole caused a ~10% emission decrease
claims.criterion: From Methods 4.5 and the Figure 5 legend, emission changes at the two poles in the direction of the maximum field gradient, normalized to whole-cell emission, averaged over 5 cells and over the time-increment and decrement series. Reproduced when the peak changes are within tolerance and the pole signals reverse sign with each change of pulse direction.

claims.statement: Cells near the apex reach a much larger polarization, about 25% FluoVolt emission change, which follows the envelope of the pulse train and not the individual pulses, more than twice that near the base electrodes.
claims.source: Results, 2.4, paragraph 2; Figure 5
claims.quote: In stark contrast, the cells near the apex reached a much higher polarization (~25% change in FluoVolt emission), which followed the envelope of the pulse train but not the individual pulses of it
claims.criterion: Measure as in fig5-base-sawtooth, for the apex location. Reproduced when the peak change is within tolerance, more than twice the base-location change, and holds through the train without reversing sign at each pulse.

claims.statement: At a 180 degree change of field direction, trains of paired pulses electroporate less than trains of single pulses, about 2-fold less at 1 Hz and about 20-fold less at 833 kHz, so cancellation is stronger at the higher rate.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.1, paragraph 2; Figure 2
claims.quote: Maximum cancellation was expectedly observed at the 180° vector change, reducing YP uptake compared to single-pulse trains 2-fold at 1 Hz and as much as 20-fold at 833 kHz
claims.criterion: As in Section 2.1 and the Figure 2 legend, YP uptake per ROI under paired pulses as % of single pulses in the same ROI, mean over the n = 3 experiments, with each ROI's angle taken from the field simulation of Methods 4.3 (an outside input, not deposited). Open details, each a reading to run. (1) Spontaneous uptake measured in the electrode footprints (Methods 4.4) is (a) subtracted from each ROI before the ratio, or (b) not subtracted. (2) The 180 degree value is (a) the ROI nearest the base, or (b) the value at 180 degrees read from a fit of the curve (the paper fitted in Grapher 16 but does not name the function). Reproduced when both folds fall within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: As the angle falls from 180 degrees, cancellation weakens, and paired-pulse trains equal single-pulse trains at about 160 degrees at 1 Hz and about 130 degrees at 833 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.1, paragraph 2; Figure 2
claims.quote: Cancellation weakened as the angle was reduced, and at about 160° (1 Hz) or 130° (833 kHz), the effects of paired-pulse trains became the same as those of single-pulse ones
claims.criterion: The curves of claim fig2-cancellation-at-180, under its readings. The crossing is the angle where the mean curve crosses 100%, found by (a) linear interpolation between the two adjacent ROIs (a standard choice the paper does not fix) or (b) the fitted curve. Reproduced when both angles fall within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Below the crossover, paired pulses facilitate electroporation, up to about three times the single-pulse effect at 90 to 100 degrees at both rates, and the effect then stays on a plateau down to 0 degrees.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.1, paragraph 2; Figure 2; Discussion, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Further reduction of the angle enhanced electroporation, up to about three-fold at 90–100° for both nsEP frequencies, followed by a plateau all the way to 0°
claims.criterion: The curves of claim fig2-cancellation-at-180, under its readings. The value at 90 to 100 degrees is (a) the mean of the ROIs whose angle lies in 90 to 100 degrees or (b) the ROI nearest 95 degrees. The paper gives no test or bound for the plateau; it is read as the mean over the ROIs below 90 degrees lying within the same tolerance (270 to 330%) at each rate, a choice that uses the default 10% tolerance of the three-fold value. Reproduced when both values and both plateaus hold under one reading; partially reproduced when the three-fold values hold and the plateau does not.

claims.statement: At 833 kHz co-directional pulse pairs electroporate about 60 times more than counter-directional ones.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.3, paragraph 1; Figure 2
claims.quote: The profound, 60-fold difference in electroporation efficiency of co- and counter-directional nsEPs at 833 kHz
claims.criterion: The 833 kHz curve of claim fig2-cancellation-at-180, under its readings. The paper does not say which co-directional value is meant; the readings are the ratio to the 180 degree value of (a) the plateau value (claim fig2-facilitation-plateau) or (b) the ROI nearest 0 degrees. Reproduced when the ratio is within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: At 1 Hz, paired pulses that keep their direction and pairs whose second pulse turns by 90 degrees electroporate the cell monolayer equally.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3
claims.quote: Consistently with the measurements in Figure 2 , co- and cross-directional pulses at 1 Hz had the same electroporation efficiency
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. YP uptake in the 200 x 200 um ROI at the array center (Methods 4.4), n = 6 per group, co-directional against cross-directional at 1 Hz with the paper's two-tailed Student's t-test (Figure 3 legend), read as the unpaired test with equal variances, which is what the name denotes; the paper reports no pairing of samples. The p-values are printed in Figure 3 only and were not read. Spontaneous uptake measured in the electrode footprints is subtracted, as Methods 4.4 says it was measured to account for it; the unsubtracted values are shown as a variant only. The threshold is not stated; the conventional p < 0.05 is used. Reproduced when the test finds no difference; the difference of means is reported either way.

claims.statement: Raising the rate to 770 kHz increases electroporation by co-directional pulse pairs, through temporal summation of the induced membrane potential.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3
claims.quote: Increasing the pulse frequency to 770 kHz enhanced electroporation by the co-directional pulses because of the temporal summation of the induced membrane potential
claims.criterion: Measure and test as in claim fig3-1hz-co-cross-same, comparing co-directional pairs at 770 kHz with co-directional pairs at 1 Hz. Reproduced when the 770 kHz mean is higher and the two-tailed t-test gives p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Cross-directional pulse pairs at 770 kHz are as effective as at 1 Hz, so charging two different regions of the membrane does not summate.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.2, paragraph 1; Figure 3
claims.quote: Interestingly, charging two different regions of the cell membrane did not cause summation, making cross-directional pulses at 770 kHz just as effective as at 1 Hz
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged as in claim fig3-1hz-co-cross-same, comparing cross-directional pairs at 770 kHz with cross-directional pairs at 1 Hz. Reproduced when the t-test finds no difference; the difference of means is reported either way.

claims.statement: Under a train of five single pulses applied to one base electrode (833 kHz, 4 kV), YP uptake is distributed as the electric field strength map.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.3, paragraph 1; Figure 4A
claims.quote: In control cell monolayers exposed to a train of five single pulses applied to one of the base electrodes (833 kHz, 4 kV), the distribution of YP fluorescence ( Figure 4 A) simply followed the electric field strength map
claims.criterion: The paper shows this as an image beside the simulated field map (Methods 4.3, Figure 7B), which is not deposited and whose values the text does not give; the comparison needs that map as an outside input, computed as Methods 4.3 states (Sim4Life, 1.6 S/m solution 3.5 mm deep, 1 V on the energized electrode, field in the plane 1 um above the glass, scaled to 4 kV). The paper names no measure of agreement. Readings, each to run. Background-subtracted YP (footprint background, Methods 4.4) in 200 x 200 um ROIs over the image, compared with the field in the same ROIs by (a) Spearman rank correlation or (b) the order of the three electrode neighbourhoods by YP matching their order by field. Both measures are choices, as the paper names none. Reproduced when both readings agree with the map (correlation positive with p < 0.05, and the same order), not reproduced when both fail, and methods_underspecified when they disagree. Without the map the claim is blocked.

claims.statement: Under five paired pulses applied to the two base electrodes in alternation (833 kHz, 4 kV), electroporation is strong near the grounded apex electrode and weak or absent near the base electrodes, despite the strong field there.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.3, paragraph 1; Figure 4B,C; Discussion, paragraph 2
claims.quote: energizing two base electrodes in alternation (five paired pulses, 600 + 600 ns, 833 kHz, 4 kV) produced a strong effect near the apex electrode (ground) but weak or no effect near the base electrodes, despite the strong electric field there
claims.criterion: The paper shows this as images only (Figure 4B and the 3D rendering in 4C) and gives no measure. From Methods 4.4, YP intensity in 200 x 200 um ROIs with the footprint background subtracted. How near "near" is, is open; the readings are ROIs centered (a) 100 um and (b) 500 um outside the edge of each electrode footprint (1.5 mm needles), on the line from that electrode toward the array center. Reproduced when, under both readings, the YP near the apex in the paired-pulse image exceeds that near each base electrode, and the ratio of apex to base YP is higher in the paired-pulse image than in the single-pulse image of Figure 4A (the contrast the paper draws between the panels); not reproduced when either fails under both readings; the readings disagreeing makes the claim methods_underspecified. The values near each electrode in both images are reported.

claims.statement: Under paired pulses the electroporated cells form a comet-shaped region pointing from the apex electrode towards the base.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 2; Figure 4B,C
claims.quote: The electroporated cells formed a comet-shaped region pointing from the apex electrode towards the base
claims.criterion: Shown in images only, with no measure. The paper does not say what counts as electroporated; the readings for the electroporated region are background-subtracted YP above (a) half and (b) a quarter of its maximum in the paired-pulse image, after smoothing over 200 x 200 um (the ROI size of Methods 4.4). Reproduced when, under both readings, the region touches the apex footprint and extends further along the bisecting line toward the base than across it.

claims.statement: Cells between the base electrodes show sawtooth changes of membrane potential in step with the alternating pulses, about a 10% rise of FluoVolt emission at the cathode-facing pole and a 10% fall at the anode-facing pole.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.4, paragraph 2; Figure 5
claims.quote: Cells placed between the base electrodes displayed sawtooth-like changes in membrane potential in synchrony with the applied pulses ... Depolarization at the cathode-facing pole of the cell manifested as a ~10% emission increase, and hyperpolarization at the anode-facing pole caused a ~10% emission decrease
claims.criterion: As in Methods 4.5 and the Figure 5 legend, emission at the two opposite poles along the field gradient, normalized to whole-cell emission, mean of 5 cells over the 220 time points. The peak is (a) the largest excursion over the train or (b) the mean of the per-pulse peaks (the paper does not say). Reproduced when both magnitudes are within tolerance under one reading and the sign of the change alternates with each pulse.

claims.statement: Cells near the apex reach a polarization of about 25% FluoVolt emission change, more than twice that between the base electrodes, which follows the envelope of the train and not its individual pulses.
claims.source: Results, Section 2.4, paragraph 2; Figure 5
claims.quote: In stark contrast, the cells near the apex reached a much higher polarization (~25% change in FluoVolt emission), which followed the envelope of the pulse train but not the individual pulses of it
claims.criterion: As in claim fig5-base-sawtooth, with its readings. Reproduced when the apex value is within tolerance, exceeds twice the base value, and the apex trace keeps one sign through the train. How to judge "not the individual pulses" is not fixed by the paper; it is reported as the size of the pulse-to-pulse alternation relative to the peak, without a threshold.

claims.statement: The dandiset's NWB files can be matched to the paper's per-cell metadata and feature tables in its code repository, and features recomputed from the files agree with those tables.
claims.source: Data and materials availability; github.com/AllenInstitute/human_patchseq_gaba commit 5eb357a, data/README.md, LeeDalley_manuscript_metadata_v2.csv and LeeDalley_ephys_fx.csv
claims.criterion: Files are matched to rows of LeeDalley_manuscript_metadata_v2.csv by its nwb_id column (or by specimen id where the NWB metadata carry it). The link holds (reproduced) when at least 90% of the rows with Has_ephys true are found in the dandiset, and, for the matched cells, rheobase_i, input_resistance, sag and width_rheo computed here with IPFX are within 10% of the LeeDalley_ephys_fx.csv values for at least 90% of the cells with both values. It is partially reproduced when the matching holds and the features agree for 50 to 90% of cells, and not reproduced otherwise. The number of NWB files without a metadata row is reported.

claims.statement: The study characterized 778 human GABAergic neurons in layers 2 to 6, covering 44 of the 45 GABAergic t-types, with electrophysiology from 75 LAMP5/PAX6, 99 VIP, 149 SST and 352 PVALB neurons.
claims.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraphs 1 and 3
claims.quote: properties of 778 neurons from the four canonical GABAergic subclasses in human cortex. We described neurons in cortical layers 2 to 6 (L2–6) across 44 transcriptomic types ... LAMP5/PAX6 ( n = 75), VIP ( n = 99), SST ( n = 149), and PVALB ( n = 352)
claims.criterion: Counted over the dandiset's NWB files that pass the cell inclusion criteria of the Methods and have at least one QC-passing long square sweep, labelled through cell-metadata-link. The subclass counts are read two ways, as the text does not say which is meant, (a) Revised_subclass_label (SST FRZB in PVALB, as for subclass-level analyses) or (b) subclass_label. The 778 and 44 are counted over all labelled cells, as they include cells without electrophysiology; that the dandiset holds fewer cells than 778 is expected and reported. Reproduced when the four subclass counts are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Patch-seq neurons from slices in culture (2 to 16 days) had more genes detected than neurons from acute slices.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 1; Figure 1B
claims.quote: Patch-seq neurons from culture preparations recorded at 2 to 16 days in culture (DIC) had significantly ( P < 0.0001) higher genes detected as compared with the acute paradigm
claims.criterion: Genes detected per cell, culture against acute (condition column), two-sided Mann-Whitney test. Reproduced when the culture median is higher at p < 0.0001.

claims.statement: Culture neurons fall into two clusters, with and without a microglial gene signature, and the signature is also present, less strongly, in a subset of acute neurons.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 1; fig. S1B and S1C
claims.quote: These neurons clustered into two domains, with or without microglial gene expression signatures ... This microglial signature ( data S2 ) was also observed in a subset of neurons collected with the acute paradigm, although the effect was less pronounced
claims.criterion: As in Methods (Assigning cells a microglial signature) and the notebook (chunk "identify immune signature cells in culture and acute"), Seurat clustering of culture cells at resolution 0.001 into two clusters, then of culture and acute cells separately on the 269 culture microglial genes at resolution 0.1. Reproduced when the culture cells form two clusters, one with high microglial gene expression, and some acute cells are called microglial, with the effect less pronounced in acute cells. "Less pronounced" is not defined; its readings are (a) a lower fraction of acute than of culture cells called microglial and (b) lower mean expression of the 269 genes in acute than in culture microglial cells. The outcome is the one both give; blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ.

claims.statement: For the top differentially expressed genes of each GABAergic subclass, average expression in acute and culture neurons is strongly correlated.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 1; Figure 1C
claims.quote: Upon examination of key differentially expressed genes responsible for GABAergic subclass discrimination, average gene expression was strongly correlated ( P < 0.0001), demonstrating alignment between acute and culture paradigms
claims.criterion: For each subclass, the top 25 genes differentially expressed for that subclass (Fig. 1C legend), mean expression over acute cells against mean over culture cells. The text and legend name no test, no expression scale and no source of the 25 genes, so these are open. Readings are Pearson's correlation (the Methods' test for continuous variables, stated for feature relationships) or Spearman's, on log2(CPM + 1) or CPM, per subclass (the four panels) or pooled over the 100 genes; genes ranked by differential expression in the snRNA-seq reference or in the Patch-seq cells. Reproduced when p < 0.0001 and r > 0 in every subclass (or pooled, for that reading) under all readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ.

claims.statement: The normalized marker sum score does not differ between acute and culture neurons.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 1; Figure 1D
claims.quote: we found no difference between the acute and culture paradigms ( Fig. 1D )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a two-sided Mann-Whitney test of NMS, acute against culture (Fig. 1D legend). Reproduced when p >= 0.05; the medians and the effect size are reported either way.

claims.statement: Fifty morphological features of depth-matched PVALB WFDC2 neurons do not differ between culture (n = 9) and acute (n = 10) slices.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure 1G; fig. S2A
claims.quote: We also evaluated 50 morphological features of cortical depth–matched PVALB WFDC2 neurons ( Fig. 1F ) from culture ( n = 9) and acute paradigms ( n = 10) and didn’t find any difference among the two conditions
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a Mann-Whitney U test per feature with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across the 50 features (Methods, Statistical analysis of variability; preprint, P > 0.05). Reproduced when no feature has FDR-corrected p < 0.05. Which 9 and 10 cells were depth-matched is not given; readings are (a) the cells with a reconstruction in the culture and acute groups, if that gives 9 and 10, and (b) those cells after matching soma depth, the method of matching being open.

claims.statement: In PVALB WFDC2 neurons, 43 of 84 electrophysiological features differ between the acute and culture paradigms.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; fig. S2B; preprint, same section
claims.quote: Analysis of electrophysiological responses from PVALB WFDC2 neurons revealed that 43 of 84 features differed across the two paradigms
claims.criterion: PVALB WFDC2 cells (Transcriptomic_type) with electrophysiology, acute against culture (condition). Per feature a two-sided Mann-Whitney test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across features, counted at FDR-corrected p < 0.05 (preprint, "P < 0.05, false discovery rate (FDR)-corrected Mann–Whitney test"). The feature set is reading (a), the 84 non-chirp columns of LeeDalley_ephys_fx.csv; the count over all 93 columns is shown as a variant and does not decide the outcome, as the paper counts 84 features. Whether the microglial groups are pooled is not said; they are pooled, as condition has only acute and culture, and the split by condition2 is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: In PVALB WFDC2 neurons AP width and sag differ between acute and culture slices (sag is higher in culture), while interspike interval and input resistance do not.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure 1L; preprint Discussion, paragraph 2 (direction of sag)
claims.quote: AP width and sag are two of the key features that were different between the two groups ( Fig. 1L ); however, multiple other cardinal intrinsic membrane properties, such as interspike interval or input resistance, were not
claims.criterion: PVALB WFDC2 cells, acute against culture, two-sided Mann-Whitney tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across the features of figs2b-wfdc2-ephys-43-of-84 (reading a). Reproduced when sag and AP width each differ at FDR-corrected p < 0.0001 with sag higher in culture, and ISI and input resistance (the absence part, judged on the same test) have FDR-corrected p >= 0.05. AP width is read as width_rheo, width_hero, width_short_square or width_ramp, and ISI as mean_isi_rheo or mean_isi_hero; the outcome is the one all readings give, and the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ. The direction of the width change is reported.

claims.statement: The features that differ in culture already differ at 2 days in culture and do not change with further days in culture.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; fig. S2C (preprint Supplementary Figure 2C, sag and AP width against days in culture)
claims.quote: The features that were different between the two paradigms were observed at the earliest time point (2 DIC) and did not change with additional days in culture
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the test the Methods give for continuous variables, Pearson's correlation of sag and of AP width with Days_In_culture over culture PVALB WFDC2 cells (the two features the preprint's Supplementary Figure 2C plots), FDR-corrected across the two. Reproduced when neither correlation is significant at FDR-corrected p < 0.05 and the 2 DIC cells already differ from the acute median in the direction of the culture group. The same test over all features found in figs2b-wfdc2-ephys-43-of-84 is shown as a variant. The AP width readings are those of fig1l-width-sag-differ.

claims.statement: In electrophysiology UMAP space of all 84 features, acute and culture PVALB WFDC2 neurons occupy a similar space.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure 1I
claims.quote: When projecting all 84 electrophysiological features through the UMAP, PVALB WFDC2 neurons from both paradigms occupied a similar space
claims.criterion: The paper gives no UMAP parameters and no overlap measure, so one is fixed here. All cells with electrophysiology, features of reading (a) z-scored with missing values set to the feature median; for each acute PVALB WFDC2 cell, the fraction of its 15 nearest neighbours (Euclidean, in feature space and in a umap-learn embedding with default parameters) among the PVALB WFDC2 cells that are culture cells, and the same for culture cells. Reproduced when both groups' mean cross-group fraction is at least half of what random labels with the same group sizes give (median of 1000 shuffles), in both spaces. The neighbour count and the one-half threshold are choices, not the paper's; the fractions are reported against the shuffle distribution and for 10 and 30 neighbours.

claims.statement: Of 114 voltage-gated ion-channel genes, only seven differ in expression between culture and acute neurons.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 3; fig. S2D; Discussion, paragraph 2
claims.quote: We examined 114 voltage-gated ion-channel genes and found only seven that were different in culture versus acute paradigm
claims.criterion: The Methods give no test; the notebook settles it (chunks "linear model gene expression WFDC2" and "fold change and ion channels WFDC2"). PVALB WFDC2 cells, genes kept by the notebook with mean expression > 0.01, a linear model expression ~ condition + isImmune + condition x isImmune per gene, p-values of the condition term adjusted with R's p.adjust default (Holm, though the code comment says FDR), channel genes from vgic_genes.csv, counted at adjusted p <= 0.01. Reproduced when the count is 7 and the channel genes tested number about 114 (within 10%). The notebook's all-subclass model is a variant.

claims.statement: The four GABAergic subclasses are separable in electrophysiology feature space, with PVALB neurons occupying the most distinct region.
claims.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 1; Figure 2B
claims.quote: PVALB, SST, VIP, and LAMP5/PAX6 interneurons were separable when visualized by electrophysiological ( Fig. 2B ) and morphological ( Fig. 2C ) features in UMAP space, with PVALB neurons occupying the most distinct subregions in both UMAPs
claims.criterion: No UMAP parameters or separability measure are given, so one is fixed here. Features of reading (a), z-scored, missing values set to the median; for each cell the fraction of its 15 nearest neighbours (in feature space and in a default umap-learn embedding) of its own subclass. Reproduced when every subclass's mean same-subclass fraction exceeds its share of all cells by at least 0.2, and PVALB has the highest mean same-subclass fraction, in both spaces.

claims.statement: The four subclasses are separable in morphological feature space, PVALB the most distinct.
claims.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 1; Figure 2C
claims.quote: PVALB, SST, VIP, and LAMP5/PAX6 interneurons were separable when visualized by electrophysiological ( Fig. 2B ) and morphological ( Fig. 2C ) features in UMAP space
claims.criterion: As for fig2b-ephys-umap-subclasses, on the morphology features of the 140 reconstructed neurons.

claims.statement: LAMP5/PAX6 neurons have the shortest soma-to-branch-tip Euclidean distance for both axon and dendrite.
claims.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 2; Figure 2E
claims.quote: They also had the shortest soma–to–branch tip Euclidean distance for both axon and dendrite
claims.criterion: axon_max_euclidean_distance and basal_dendrite_max_euclidean_distance by subclass, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post hoc, FDR-corrected (Fig. 2E legend). Reproduced when the LAMP5/PAX6 median is the lowest of the four for both and Kruskal-Wallis is significant at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: APs of the PVALB subclass have the fastest kinetics, and LAMP5/PAX6 APs have the highest peak amplitude of the four subclasses.
claims.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 3; Figure 2F
claims.quote: APs from PVALB subclass had the fastest kinetics, whereas LAMP5/PAX6 had the highest peak amplitude versus other subclasses
claims.criterion: Figure 2F shows APs to a current pulse, a 3 ms pulse in the preprint, so short square features are the first reading; rheobase-sweep features are the second. Kinetics is read as AP width (width_short_square or width_rheo) and as upstroke/downstroke ratio; peak as peak_deltav (peak relative to threshold) of the same sweep. Kruskal-Wallis across the four subclasses with Dunn's post hoc, FDR-corrected (the tests of Fig. 2H). The ratio is peak upstroke over peak downstroke (Methods), so faster repolarization gives a lower ratio. Reproduced when PVALB has the narrowest width and the lowest upstroke/downstroke ratio, and LAMP5/PAX6 the highest peak, each with Dunn's p < 0.05 against every other subclass, under all readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when readings disagree.

claims.statement: LAMP5/PAX6 and VIP neurons have minimal sag compared with PVALB and SST neurons.
claims.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 3; Figure 2G
claims.quote: LAMP5/PAX6 and VIP subclasses had minimal sag compared with PVALB and SST subclasses
claims.criterion: Sag as IPFX computes it at the hyperpolarizing sweep closest to -100 mV (Methods), by subclass, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post hoc, FDR-corrected. Reproduced when the LAMP5/PAX6 and VIP medians are both below the PVALB and SST medians and all four of those pairs differ at Dunn's p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Several additional electrophysiological features differ between the subclasses.
claims.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 3; Figure 2H
claims.quote: Several additional features further demonstrated the electrophysiological distinctness of each subclass
claims.criterion: The features plotted in Figure 2H are not named in any text read. Kruskal-Wallis across subclasses for every feature of reading (a), Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across features. "Several" is read as at least three. Reproduced when at least three features other than width, upstroke/downstroke ratio, peak and sag have FDR-corrected p < 0.05 and at least one Dunn's pair significant at p < 0.05. The count of significant features is reported.

claims.statement: Most SST FRZB neurons colocalize with the PVALB subclass in electrophysiology space.
claims.source: Results, Revising subclass assignment based on multimodal data, paragraph 2; Figure 3C
claims.quote: Examination of all 84 electrophysiological features, visualized using a UMAP, revealed that most of the SST FRZB neurons colocalized with the PVALB subclass
claims.criterion: Groups are SST (subclass_label SST without SST FRZB), PVALB (without SST FRZB) and SST FRZB (Transcriptomic_type). No UMAP parameters are given, so a measure is fixed here. Features of reading (a), z-scored over SST and PVALB cells; for each SST FRZB cell, its 15 nearest SST or PVALB neighbours (feature space, and a default umap-learn embedding). Reproduced when more than half of the SST FRZB cells have a majority of PVALB neighbours in both spaces.

claims.statement: The AP upstroke/downstroke ratio and AP width of SST FRZB neurons align with fast-spiking PVALB neurons and differ from SST neurons.
claims.source: Results, Revising subclass assignment based on multimodal data, paragraph 2; Figure 3D, 3E and 3I
claims.quote: We observed the AP kinetics, such as upstroke/downstroke ratio, AP width, and AP firing pattern of SST FRZB neurons aligned with fast-spiking interneurons of the PVALB subclass
claims.criterion: Groups as in fig3c-frzb-ephys-with-pvalb. Kruskal-Wallis over the three groups with Dunn's post hoc, FDR-corrected (Fig. 3E legend). Reproduced when, for both features, SST FRZB differs from SST at Dunn's p < 0.0001 and the SST FRZB median is nearer the PVALB median than the SST median. Which pairs carry the legend's asterisks is not said; the SST FRZB against PVALB result is reported. Features are read as upstroke_downstroke_ratio and width of the rheobase sweep, the short square and the rheobase + 40 pA sweep; the outcome is the one all readings give.

claims.statement: The upstroke/downstroke ratio and AP width of SST subclass neurons do not differ between acute and culture recordings.
claims.source: Results, Revising subclass assignment based on multimodal data, paragraph 2; fig. S6
claims.quote: Additionally, these select features of the SST subclass were not different in recordings from acute versus culture paradigms
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the test used for acute against culture elsewhere in the paper (FDR-corrected Mann-Whitney, Fig. 1 legend), since the fig. S6 legend is missing. SST subclass cells (subclass_label SST, read with and without SST FRZB), the two features of fig3e-frzb-ap-like-pvalb under its sweep readings. Reproduced when no feature differs at FDR-corrected p < 0.05 under every reading; the effect sizes are reported.

claims.statement: SST FRZB neurons express SST higher than PVALB but lack several key genes of each subclass while expressing several others, and most SST FRZB Patch-seq samples lie with the PVALB subclass in transcriptomic UMAP space.
claims.source: Results, Revising subclass assignment based on multimodal data, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 3A and 3B
claims.quote: Whereas neurons belonging to the SST FRZB transcriptomic type did express SST higher than PVALB, they lacked expression of multiple key genes that define each subclass ... the vast majority of SST FRZB samples localized to the PVALB subclass within the transcriptomic UMAP space in our Patch-seq dataset
claims.criterion: Top 20 genes differentially expressed between all PVALB and all SST types (excluding SST FRZB) in the snRNA-seq data (Methods); SST against PVALB expression in the SST FRZB nuclei of the snRNA-seq data (Fig. 3A legend, a heat map of snRNA-seq data); for the UMAP, the integrated space of the Methods (Visualization of integrated transcriptomic space; the notebook's chunk "run Seurat integration by condition"). Reproduced when the SST FRZB median SST expression exceeds its PVALB expression, at least two subclass genes of each list are not expressed (median CPM 0) and at least two are (median CPM > 0), thresholds the paper does not give, and more than half of the SST FRZB Patch-seq cells have a majority of PVALB among their 15 nearest SST or PVALB neighbours.

claims.statement: SST FRZB neurons overlap more with PVALB than with SST neurons in morphology space, their horizontal axon extent and axon versus dendrite earth mover's distance resemble PVALB basket cells, and in co-clustering they fall more often into PVALB-dominated types.
claims.source: Results, Revising subclass assignment based on multimodal data, paragraph 3; Figure 3F to 3H
claims.quote: Morphological features such as horizontal axon extent and a measure of the dissimilarity of the axon and dendrite compartments (axon versus dendrite earth mover’s distance) showed that SST FRZB neurons had individual morphological features that were more similar to PVALB basket cells than to SST neurons
claims.criterion: axon_extent_x and axon_emd_with_basal_dendrite for SST, SST FRZB and PVALB, Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's post hoc, FDR-corrected (Fig. 3G legend); co-clustering as the Methods give it (95% subsamples, shared nearest neighbour graph, fast-greedy community detection, 500 resamplings, Ward linkage on the co-clustering matrix). The features entering the graph, the number of neighbours of the graph and where the Ward tree is cut are not given; the paper names types 1 to 6, so the tree is cut at six clusters, and the features are all columns of LeeDalley_morpho_features.csv; these are choices, and 10 and 20 graph neighbours are both run. A cluster is PVALB- or SST-dominated by its majority subclass. Reproduced when the SST FRZB medians are nearer the PVALB than the SST medians for both features, SST differs from SST FRZB at p < 0.01 for at least one (the legend does not say which pairs carry the asterisks; the preprint gave P > 0.05 for this panel, the version of record gives ** P < 0.01, and the version of record is followed), and more SST FRZB cells fall in PVALB-dominated clusters than in SST-dominated ones under both neighbour counts.

claims.statement: The SST CALB1 t-type contains four qualitative morphology types, Martinotti cells, double bouquet cells, one basket-like cell and sparse SST cells.
claims.source: Results, Morphological heterogeneity within SST CALB1, paragraph 1; Figure 4A and 4B
claims.quote: In humans, we qualitatively identified four morphological types within SST CALB1. Three of these types resembled previously described neurons
claims.criterion: The types were assigned by eye; the test is that the reconstructions labelled with each type in the metadata show the defining traits the Results give. Reproduced when MCs have more axon length in L1 than below their soma layer, DBCs have the narrowest axon_extent_x relative to dendrite width (axon_over_basal_dendrite_extent_x) of the four, the basket-like cell has the least L1 axon, and sparse SST cells have fewer axon branches per length than MCs.

claims.statement: Within SST CALB1, sparse SST neurons tend to have lower sag, higher adaptation ratio and slightly delayed AP onset than DBCs and MCs, and MCs have the highest AP peak.
claims.source: Results, Morphological heterogeneity within SST CALB1, paragraph 2; Figure 4C
claims.quote: sparse SST neurons show a lower degree of sag, a higher adaptation ratio, and a slightly delayed onset of AP firing as compared with DBCs and MCs, whereas the peak of the AP is highest in MCs
claims.criterion: SST CALB1 cells with Qualitative_morphology_type MC, DBC, sparse SST or basket-like, with electrophysiology. The paper calls these trends from few neurons and does not say which pairs are significant, so the claim is judged on medians, with Kruskal-Wallis and Dunn's FDR-corrected results reported. Sag is sag; adaptation ratio is the Methods' ISI adaptation ratio (first to third spike, isi_adapt_ratio), as the Methods keep "adaptation ratio" for these first-to-third spike ratios and call adapt_rheo and adapt_hero the adaptation index, which is shown as a variant only; onset as latency_rheo and latency_hero; peak as peak_deltav_rheo and peak_deltav_hero. Reproduced when, under every reading, the sparse SST median sag is below, its adaptation and latency medians above, those of DBC and MC, and the MC peak median is the highest of the four types; partially reproduced when three of the four statements hold.

claims.statement: A UMAP on 253 genes differentially expressed between DBC, MC and sparse SST neurons splits SST CALB1 neurons into three clusters that largely separate the morphology types.
claims.source: Results, Morphological heterogeneity within SST CALB1, paragraph 3; Figure 4D
claims.quote: With this variable gene set, three distinct clusters appeared with morphological types largely separated across clusters
claims.criterion: The Methods (Calculating differentially expressed genes, case iv) give Seurat FindMarkers, t test, min.pct 0, logfc.threshold 0, Bonferroni, between any pair of DBC, MC and sparse SST cells; the genes are the union over the three pairs. The notebook (chunks "morpho of immune culture cells" and "morpho of immune culture cells dex", read at 5eb357a) instead runs FindAllMarkers (t test, logfc.threshold 0) on SST CALB1 culture_immune cells of known morphology, after dropping immune genes and genes with median expression below 1. The UMAP is over all SST CALB1 neurons (Fig. 4D legend) with the DE genes as variable genes; the Methods say it follows the procedure of the integrated space (scaling, PCA with 30 PCs, 2D UMAP) without integration, while the notebook uses 6 PCs and 5 neighbours. Clusters are not in the Methods; the notebook's Louvain clustering on the UMAP at resolution 1 is used. The Methods' reading (pairwise FindMarkers, 30 PCs) is the main one and the notebook's a variant, as the protocol puts the Methods first. The cells entering the DE test are open, read as the culture_immune cells of the notebook or all SST CALB1 cells with a DBC, MC or sparse SST call; the adjusted p cut is open, read as 0.05 (Seurat's default report). For the 253, reproduced when the count is within tolerance under one reading. For the clusters, reproduced when three clusters form and each of DBC, MC and sparse SST has most of its cells in a different cluster under the main reading; the variant is shown. The notebook warns that this is "somewhat circular", which is reported.

claims.statement: Morphologically classic double bouquet cells map to two t-types, SST CALB1 and SST ADGRG6.
claims.source: Results, Double bouquet cells, paragraph 1; Figure 5A
claims.quote: We found that these classical DBC morphologies map to two closely related transcriptomic types, SST CALB1, mentioned above, and L3–5 SST ADGRG6
claims.criterion: Reproduced when the cells called DBC in dbc_calb1_ADGRG6.csv include cells of both t-types (Tree_first_cl), seven in SST CALB1 and four in SST ADGRG6 (the counts of figs7a-dbc-regions), and the tree mapping of their transcriptomes gives the same t-types.

claims.statement: In MERFISH, SST CALB1 is mostly restricted to L2 and SST ADGRG6 to L3, in line with the Patch-seq soma positions, and SST CALB1 DBC axon peaks more superficially.
claims.source: Results, Double bouquet cells, paragraph 1; Figure 5A and 5B
claims.quote: MERFISH analysis to map the spatial distributions of all types in the MTG taxonomy revealed that the SST CALB1 transcriptomic type was mostly restricted to L2, whereas SST ADGRG6 was mostly restricted to L3
claims.criterion: The modal layer of MERFISH cells mapped to each t-type. Reproduced when it is L2 for SST CALB1 and L3 for SST ADGRG6. The Patch-seq soma layers (Cortical_layer) of the two t-types are reported; they can be tested on the labels alone. The axon part is tested on the layer-aligned DBC reconstructions (Brain Image Library), by the depth of the peak of each DBC's axon branch-length histogram (5 um bins, Methods, Morphology feature analysis); reproduced for that part when the SST CALB1 median peak depth is shallower than the SST ADGRG6 median. No test is reported.

claims.statement: Six of seven DBCs in SST CALB1 come from temporal cortex and three of four DBCs in SST ADGRG6 from frontal cortex.
claims.source: Results, Double bouquet cells, paragraph 1; fig. S7A (preprint Supplementary Figure 3A)
claims.quote: We also found that six out of seven DBCs in the SST CALB1 transcriptomic type were from the temporal cortex, whereas three out of four DBCs in the SST ADGRG6 transcriptomic type were from the frontal cortex
claims.criterion: Counts are exact (tolerance 0, as they are small integers). DBC calls from dbc_calb1_ADGRG6.csv, region from the NWB metadata where present and otherwise from the lobe column of the metadata table. The counts are taken over all DBCs and, as a variant, over those with an NWB file in the dandiset. No test is reported.

claims.statement: Most DBCs strongly express CALB1, only one expresses CALB2, all but one express some SST, and TAC1, NOS1 and NPY expression is mixed, so no gene specific to DBCs was found.
claims.source: Results, Double bouquet cells, paragraph 2; fig. S7A
claims.quote: Most DBCs showed strong expression of CALB1 (calbindin), whereas only one showed expression of CALB2 (calretinin). All but one neuron showed some degree of SST expression and mixed expression of TAC1, NOS1, and NPY
claims.criterion: Expression (CPM, detected when > 0) of CALB1, CALB2, SST, TAC1, NOS1 and NPY in the DBCs of dbc_calb1_ADGRG6.csv. "Strong" is read as log2(CPM + 1) above 5, a threshold the paper does not give; the CALB1 values are reported. Reproduced when more than half of DBCs strongly express CALB1, exactly one has CALB2 > 0, all but one have SST > 0, and each of TAC1, NOS1 and NPY is detected in some but not all DBCs.

claims.statement: A higher sag ratio is a consistent and prominent feature of all DBCs.
claims.source: Results, Double bouquet cells, paragraph 3; Figures 4C and 5C
claims.quote: One main feature that was consistent and prominent with all DBCs was a higher sag ratio
claims.criterion: The comparison group is not named; readings are (a) non-DBC neurons of SST CALB1 and SST ADGRG6 (Fig. 5C) and (b) MC and sparse SST neurons of SST CALB1 (Fig. 4C). Sag as in fig2g-sag-by-subclass. No test is reported. Reproduced when, under both readings, the DBC median sag is higher and every DBC with electrophysiology has sag above the comparison group's median; partially reproduced when the median is higher but some DBCs fall below. A two-sided Mann-Whitney test is reported.

claims.statement: In electrophysiology space, DBCs of the SST CALB1 and SST ADGRG6 types are intermingled with other SST neurons.
claims.source: Results, Double bouquet cells, paragraph 3; Figure 5D, middle
claims.quote: Furthermore, in the electrophysiological UMAP space, DBCs from the SST CALB1 and SST ADGRG6 transcriptomic types were intermingled with other SST neurons
claims.criterion: No UMAP parameters are given, so a measure is fixed here. SST subclass cells, features of reading (a) z-scored; for each DBC, the fraction of its 10 nearest SST neighbours (feature space and default umap-learn embedding) that are DBCs. Reproduced when the mean fraction is no more than twice the DBC share of SST cells in both spaces, that is, DBCs do not form their own cluster.

claims.statement: Bouton density does not differ between DBCs of the two t-types.
claims.source: Results, Double bouquet cells, paragraph 4; Figure 5E; fig. S7B (preprint Supplementary Figure 3C)
claims.quote: Bouton density measurements did not show differences between the two types
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The test is not named in any text read; the Methods give the Mann-Whitney test for binary comparisons of morphological features, so a two-sided Mann-Whitney test of bouton density, SST CALB1 against SST ADGRG6 DBCs, at p < 0.05. Reproduced when it is not significant. How boutons were counted is not given in the text read.

claims.statement: For homologous types Pvalb 2 and Sst 5, human neurons have less axonal and dendritic branching but a larger spatial extent than mouse neurons, with no difference in total axon length.
claims.source: Results, Human versus mouse, paragraph 2; Figure 6B
claims.quote: Human neurons had less axonal and dendritic branching yet occupied a larger spatial extent. We found no variation in axon total length between the homologous types
claims.criterion: Homologous types as the Results define them. Human versus mouse two-sided Mann-Whitney per feature, FDR-corrected (Fig. 6B legend), on axon_num_branches, basal_dendrite_num_branches, axon and dendrite extent (extent_x, extent_y, max euclidean distance) and axon_total_length. Reproduced when, in both homologous types, branch numbers are lower and at least one extent feature is higher in human at FDR p < 0.05, and axon total length does not differ (the absence part, same test).

claims.statement: In electrophysiology UMAP space human and mouse neurons separate clearly for both Pvalb 2 and Sst 5.
claims.source: Results, Human versus mouse, paragraph 3; Figure 6C
claims.quote: In the electrophysiological UMAP, both Pvalb 2 and Sst 5 showed clear separation between humans and mice
claims.criterion: Human cells of the homologous types (as in fig6e-species-sag-rheobase-width), mouse cells of the mouse t-types the Results list, from Gouwens et al. 2020 (ref. 16). Features computed with IPFX on both. No UMAP parameters are given, so a measure is fixed here; for each cell, the fraction of its 15 nearest neighbours (z-scored features, and a default umap-learn embedding) of its own species. Reproduced when the mean is at least 0.9 for both homologous types in both spaces.

claims.statement: Human and mouse neurons of homologous types Pvalb 2 and Sst 5 differ in sag, rheobase and AP half-width.
claims.source: Results, Human versus mouse, paragraph 3; Figure 6D and 6E
claims.quote: Average traces from each type and species shown in Fig. 6D and quantified in Fig. 6E highlight the differences in sag, rheobase, and AP half-width
claims.criterion: Human Pvalb 2 is PVALB WFDC2 and L4-6 PVALB SULF1, human Sst 5 is SST CALB1 (M_H_Hodge_cross_species_types in the metadata as a check); mouse Pvalb 2 is Pvalb Calb1 Sst, Pvalb Reln Itm2a, Pvalb Reln Tac1 and Pvalb Sema3e Kank4, mouse Sst 5 is Sst Calb2 Necab1, Sst Calb2 Pdlim5, Sst Mme Fam114a1, Sst Tac1 Htr1d and Sst Tac1 Tacr3 (ref. 16). The Results restrict to supragranular neurons; read as (a) somas in L2 or L3 in human and L2/3 in mouse and (b) all layers, the layer of mouse cells as ref. 16 gives it. Human acute and culture cells are pooled, as the main analysis does (fig. S9 separates them). Two-sided Mann-Whitney human against mouse, FDR-corrected across the features tested. Reproduced when sag, rheobase_i and AP width (width_rheo; width_short_square as a second reading) each differ at FDR p < 0.0001 in both types, under every reading; the directions are reported, as the Results do not state them.

claims.statement: Average firing rate and f-I slope differ between species for Pvalb 2 but not for Sst 5.
claims.source: Results, Human versus mouse, paragraph 3; Figure 6D; fig. S8B
claims.quote: Features related to AP firing such as average firing rate and AP frequency-current curve slope were found to differ across species for the Pvalb 2 but not for the Sst 5 homologous type
claims.criterion: Cells and readings as in fig6e-species-sag-rheobase-width; avg_rate (rheobase + 40 pA sweep as first reading, rheobase sweep as second) and fi_fit_slope. Two-sided FDR-corrected Mann-Whitney (Fig. 6 legend). Reproduced when both differ at FDR p < 0.05 for Pvalb 2, and neither does for Sst 5 (the absence part, judged on the same test), under every reading.

claims.statement: Only the Pvalb 2 species difference in AP width is driven mainly by the culture condition; the other species differences in electrophysiology hold for acute and for culture human neurons alike.
claims.source: Results, Human versus mouse, paragraph 4; fig. S9
claims.quote: Only the species difference in AP width for Pvalb 2 was driven primarily by the culture condition, whereas all other species differences in electrophysiological features were robustly detected irrespective of acute versus culture paradigm
claims.criterion: The fig. S9 legend is missing, so the test is read from the Results. For each feature that differs between species in fig6e-species-sag-rheobase-width and figs8b-firing-differs-pvalb2-only, human acute cells against mouse and human culture cells against mouse, each by two-sided Mann-Whitney, FDR-corrected across features. Reproduced when every such feature except Pvalb 2 AP width differs at FDR p < 0.05 in the same direction in both comparisons, and Pvalb 2 AP width differs for culture but not for acute human cells.

claims.statement: Neurons labelled with the VIP enhancer AAV CN2039 did not map only to VIP types but were strongly enriched for VIP types.
claims.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 2; fig. S5
claims.quote: Although the viral-labeled neurons recorded by Patch-seq did not exclusively map to VIP types, we found strong enrichment for diverse VIP neuron types with small cell bodies and bipolar dendrites in L2 and L3
claims.criterion: Cells with Virus CN2039 against other cells, by Revised_subclass_label. The comparison group is not named; readings are (a) all cells without CN2039 and (b) cells labelled with CN1390 only. No test is reported, so "strong enrichment" is judged by a two-sided Fisher exact test, a choice. Reproduced when not all CN2039 cells are VIP, and the VIP fraction among CN2039 cells exceeds that among the comparison cells at Fisher p < 0.05, under both readings. Whether more than half of CN2039 cells are VIP is reported; the paper does not say.

claims.statement: The higher number of genes detected in culture is present at every day in culture sampled and stays consistent across days in culture.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 1; fig. S1A (preprint Supplementary Figure 1A, genes against days in culture)
claims.quote: This elevation was prevalent and remained consistent across all days sampled in culture
claims.criterion: No test is reported (the fig. S1 legend is missing; the preprint shows a scatter plot). The consistency part is a claim of absence, judged on the test the Methods give for days in culture, Pearson's correlation of genes detected with Days_In_culture over culture cells; it holds when p >= 0.05. The elevation part holds when the median genes detected at every day in culture sampled exceeds the acute median. Reproduced when both hold; the correlation and the per-day medians are reported.

claims.statement: Acute and culture PVALB WFDC2 neurons overlap in transcriptomic UMAP space.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure 1E
claims.quote: For this transcriptomic type, the acute and culture datasets exhibited overlap in transcriptomic UMAP space
claims.criterion: The space is the integrated transcriptomic space of the Methods (Visualization of integrated transcriptomic space; four groups, anchors on the tree-mapping markers, 30 PCs), restricted to the PVALB subclass (Fig. 1E legend). The paper gives no overlap measure, so the measure of fig1i-wfdc2-ephys-umap-overlap is used, on the 30 PCs and on the 2D UMAP. Reproduced when it holds in both.

claims.statement: In morphological UMAP space, culture and acute PVALB WFDC2 neurons occupy similar space in the PVALB-rich portion.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure 1H
claims.quote: dimensionality reduction of the morphological features showed that PVALB WFDC2 neurons from the culture and acute paradigms occupied similar space in the PVALB-rich portion of morphological UMAP
claims.criterion: No UMAP parameters or overlap measure are given, so the measure of fig1i-wfdc2-ephys-umap-overlap is used on the morphology features of all reconstructed neurons (z-scored, missing values set to the median), with 5 neighbours as the groups are small (9 and 10 depth-matched cells, or all PVALB WFDC2 reconstructions as a second reading). The PVALB-rich part holds when most of each PVALB WFDC2 cell's 5 nearest neighbours among all cells are PVALB subclass cells, for most cells of each group. Both neighbour count and thresholds are choices. Reproduced when both parts hold in feature space and in a default umap-learn embedding.

claims.statement: Microglial signatures do not impair mapping, as neurons of the same tree-mapped subclass colocalize in transcriptomic UMAP space, whether integrating by paradigm and microglial signature or using marker genes only.
claims.source: Results, Morphological, electrophysiological, and transcriptomic features in the slice culture paradigm, paragraph 1; fig. S1D and S1E (preprint Supplementary Figure 1D)
claims.quote: Microglial gene signatures did not impact the ability to accurately map transcriptomic types, as neurons of the same subclass defined from tree mapping colocalized when visualizing the transcriptome through a uniform manifold approximation projection (UMAP)
claims.criterion: Two spaces, the integrated space of the Methods (Visualization of integrated transcriptomic space) and a space built on the tree-mapping marker genes only without integration (the notebook's chunk "no data integration", read at 5eb357a). No measure is given, so the same-subclass neighbour measure of fig2b-ephys-umap-subclasses is used, within each of the four groups (acute, acute microglial, culture, culture microglial). Reproduced when every subclass's mean same-subclass fraction exceeds its share of cells by at least 0.2 in every group and both spaces; thresholds as in fig2b-ephys-umap-subclasses, choices.

claims.statement: In Seurat-aligned transcriptomic UMAP space, the Patch-seq GABAergic neurons overlap with the human MTG snRNA-seq data.
claims.source: Results, Comparison of features across human GABAergic subclasses, paragraph 1; Figure 2A
claims.quote: When visualized in Seurat-aligned transcriptomic space through UMAP, the Patch-seq dataset overlapped with single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) human MTG dataset
claims.criterion: The integrated space of the Methods (Visualization of integrated transcriptomic space). No overlap measure is given, so one is fixed here, a choice. For each Patch-seq cell, the subclass held by most of its 15 nearest snRNA-seq nuclei (30 PCs). Reproduced when this equals the tree-mapped subclass for at least 80% of Patch-seq cells; the fraction is reported by subclass.

claims.statement: In morphological UMAP space, DBCs of the SST CALB1 and SST ADGRG6 types cluster near each other.
claims.source: Results, Double bouquet cells, paragraph 3; Figure 5D, right
claims.quote: In morphological UMAP space, we saw DBCs from these two transcriptomic types cluster near each other with perhaps some separation at the transcriptomic-type level
claims.criterion: No UMAP parameters are given, so a measure is fixed here, a choice.
