claims.quote: There was a significant interaction of phenotype and training time ... only DPR mice showed a significant increase in shocks received across the probes
claims.criterion: RI60 mice with both probes, stored labels. Two-way mixed ANOVA (phenotype between, probe within). Reproduced when the interaction has p < 0.05, the DPR paired t-test late against early has Bonferroni-corrected (x3) p < 0.05, and neither PR nor PS does. Partially reproduced when the interaction holds and DPR increases significantly but another group also changes significantly.

claims.statement: During RI60 training PR and DPR mice nosepoke at higher rates than PS mice (main effect of phenotype, p < 0.0001).
claims.source: Results, Three punishment-related phenotypes emerge with extended RI60 training, paragraph 3; Figure 2C
claims.quote: PR and DPR mice had higher rates of nosepoking than PS mice
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the mean over RI60 training sessions of active nosepokes per minute. A one-way ANOVA across phenotypes with Tukey's test. Reproduced when the ANOVA has p < 0.05 and both PR > PS and DPR > PS have Tukey p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when only one of the two pairs does. A mixed model over sessions is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: PR mice take longer than PS mice to complete the omission probe (PR 51.50 +- 17, PS 27.92 +- 13.65; one-way ANOVA F2,18 = 4.36, p < 0.05; Tukey PR vs PS p < 0.05).
claims.source: Results, Three punishment-related phenotypes emerge with extended RI60 training, paragraph 3; Figure 2D
claims.quote: PR mice took significantly longer than PS mice to complete the omission probe
claims.criterion: The text gives the unit as seconds but the Methods' median split is at 29 minutes and a session lasts at most 60 minutes, so the values are read as minutes. Tolerances are the stated SDs. Reproduced when both means are within tolerance and Tukey PR vs PS has p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when PR > PS but one of these fails. Not reproduced when PR <= PS.

claims.statement: After a reward PS mice wait longer before nosepoking again (38 +- 15 s) than PR (21 +- 5 s) and DPR (22 +- 4 s) mice (one-way ANOVA p < 0.01; Tukey p < 0.01 for each).
claims.source: Results, Three punishment-related phenotypes emerge with extended RI60 training, paragraph 4; Figure 2K
claims.quote: PS mice waited an average of 38 ± 15 seconds, significantly longer than the other groups
claims.criterion: Per reward, the rewarded port entry is the first port entry after the reward, and the wait is the time from it to the next active nosepoke; per mouse the mean over all RI60 training rewards. Tolerances are the stated SDs. Reproduced when all three means are within tolerance and Tukey PS > PR and PS > DPR have p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when PS has the longest wait but a mean or a test fails. Not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: PS mice make fewer extra nosepokes between a rewarded nosepoke and the rewarded port entry than PR mice (PS 1.28 +- 0.85, PR 3.23 +- 1.65, DPR 2.1 +- 2.63; Tukey PS vs PR p < 0.05).
claims.source: Results, Three punishment-related phenotypes emerge with extended RI60 training, paragraph 4; Figure 2L
claims.quote: PS mice made significantly fewer extra nosepokes than PR mice
claims.criterion: Extra nosepokes are active nosepokes after a rewarded nosepoke and before the rewarded port entry; per mouse the mean over RI60 training rewards. Tolerances are the stated SDs. Reproduced when all three means are within tolerance and Tukey PS < PR has p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when PS < PR but a mean or the test fails.

claims.statement: PS mice have longer inter-reward intervals (79.77 +- 26.54 s) than PR (71.2 +- 32.3 s) and DPR (69.58 +- 35.18 s) mice (Kolmogorov-Smirnov, p < 0.0001 for each).
claims.source: Results, Three punishment-related phenotypes emerge with extended RI60 training, paragraph 5; Figure 2M
claims.quote: PS mice pay for their efficiency with longer inter-reward intervals (Fig. 2M). The average inter-reward interval for PS mice is 79.77 ± 26.54s compared to 71.2 ± 32.3s for PR and 69.58 ± 35.18s for DPR
claims.criterion: Intervals between consecutive rewards within each RI60 training session, pooled per phenotype. Tolerances are the stated SDs. Reproduced when the means are within tolerance, PS has the longest mean, and two-sample KS tests PS vs PR and PS vs DPR both have p < 0.0001. Partially reproduced when PS is longest but a KS test has p >= 0.0001 or a mean is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: Averaged over RI60 training, PS mice earn fewer rewards per session (39.91 +- 7.39) than DPR mice (46.56 +- 4.49; PR 45.33 +- 4.33); one-way ANOVA p < 0.05, Tukey PS vs DPR p < 0.05.
claims.source: Results, Three punishment-related phenotypes emerge with extended RI60 training, paragraph 5; Figure 2N
claims.quote: when the number of rewards per session was averaged over all days, PS mice received significantly fewer rewards
claims.criterion: Per mouse the mean number of rewards over RI60 training sessions. Tolerances are the stated SDs. Reproduced when the three means are within tolerance and the ANOVA and Tukey PS vs DPR both have p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when PS is lowest but a test or a mean fails.

claims.statement: PR mice escalate their nosepoking as soon as they enter RI30, while DPR mice escalate later, during RI60.
claims.source: Results, Three punishment-related phenotypes emerge with extended RI60 training, paragraph 6; Figure 2O
claims.quote: PR mice escalate their nosepoking as soon as they enter RI30 (Fig. 2O). DPR mice escalate their nosepoking later in RI60
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the mean active nosepokes per minute over its RI30 sessions, and the slope of active nosepokes per minute against RI60 day (training sessions up to the late probe). (i) PR exceed both DPR and PS in RI30 rate (Mann-Whitney, p < 0.05 for each); (ii) the median RI60 slope of DPR mice is above that of PR mice. Reproduced when both hold, partially when one holds.

claims.statement: RI60-trained mice earn more rewards per training session than RR20-trained mice (unpaired t-test, p < 0.0001).
claims.source: Results, A random interval schedule of reinforcement promotes punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 4; Figure S1I (legend not available)
claims.quote: RI60-trained mice ... earned significantly more rewards per training session than RR20-trained mice
claims.criterion: Per mouse the mean rewards per training session (RI60 or RR20, up to the late probe). Reproduced when RI60 is higher with an unpaired t-test p < 0.05; notes say whether p < 0.0001.

claims.statement: Male mice accept more shocks than female mice in the shock probes (main effect of sex, F1,35 = 26.19, p < 0.0001).
claims.source: Results, Three punishment-related phenotypes emerge with extended RI60 training, paragraph 2; Figure S2B (legend not available)
claims.quote: Male mice tolerated more shocks than females
claims.criterion: RI60 fiber photometry mice with both probes. Two-way mixed ANOVA (sex between, probe within). Reproduced when the sex main effect has p < 0.05 with males higher; notes say whether p < 0.0001.

claims.statement: Peaks in DMS dopamine axon activity at rewarded nosepokes emerge during RI30 in PR mice, and more slowly across RI60 in DPR mice.
claims.source: Results, Dopamine axon signals in the DMS predict punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 2; Figure 3E
claims.quote: Peaks in response to rewarded nosepokes emerged during RI30 in PR mice, whereas peaks emerged more slowly across RI60 training in DPR mice
claims.criterion: Needs photometry recorded during RI30.

claims.statement: The DMS rewarded-unrewarded peak score differs by phenotype (F2,33 = 8.16, p < 0.01) and changes across training (p < 0.001).
claims.source: Results, Dopamine axon signals in the DMS predict punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 2; Figure 3F
claims.quote: The rewarded-unrewarded peak score changed across training ... and was significantly different by phenotype
claims.criterion: Early and late RI60 sessions only (no RI30 photometry is in the dandiset). Linear mixed model score ~ phenotype * stage with a random intercept per mouse. Reproduced when the phenotype main effect (likelihood ratio, model without phenotype terms) has p < 0.05 and the PR and DPR means exceed the PS mean. Partially reproduced when this holds in one stage only (one-way ANOVA per stage). The stage effect is reported in the notes.

claims.statement: The DMS rewarded-unrewarded peak score correlates with the shocks a mouse receives in the shock probes (r = 0.53, p < 0.0001).
claims.source: Results, Dopamine axon signals in the DMS predict punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 3; Figure 3G
claims.quote: the shocks received were significantly correlated with DMS rewarded-unrewarded peak score on a mouse-by-mouse basis
claims.criterion: Readings, before the analysis. (a) Pooled pairs of the early RI60 score with the early probe count and the late RI60 score with the late probe count; (b) late pairs only; (c) early pairs only. Reproduced when under one reading r is within tolerance and p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when r > 0 with p < 0.05 but no reading is within tolerance. Not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: The DMS rewarded-unrewarded peak score does not correlate with omission completion time (r = 0.1, ns).
claims.source: Results, Dopamine axon signals in the DMS predict punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 3; Figure 3H
claims.quote: Performance on the omission probe was not correlated with this score
claims.criterion: Absence claim. Pearson correlation of each mouse's late RI60 score with its omission completion time. Reproduced when p >= 0.05, not reproduced when p < 0.05. Pooled early and late scores are a variant.

claims.statement: The DLS rewarded-unrewarded peak score has no significant effect of phenotype.
claims.source: Results, Dopamine signals in the DLS do not predict punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 1; Figure 4F
claims.quote: There was a significant effect of training stage ... but no significant effect of group
claims.criterion: Absence claim. The model of fig3f-dms-score-phenotype on DLS scores. Reproduced when the phenotype effect has p >= 0.05, not reproduced when p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The DLS rewarded-unrewarded peak score does not correlate with shocks received (r = -0.01, ns).
claims.source: Results, Dopamine signals in the DLS do not predict punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 1; Figure 4G
claims.quote: We also looked at whether these signals correlated with shock or omission probe performance on an individual basis and found no correlations
claims.criterion: Absence claim. Pearson correlation on the pooled pairs of reading (a) of fig3g-dms-score-shock-correlation. Reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: The DLS rewarded-unrewarded peak score does not correlate with omission completion time (r = -0.21, ns).
claims.source: Results, Dopamine signals in the DLS do not predict punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 1; Figure 4H
claims.quote: We also looked at whether these signals correlated with shock or omission probe performance on an individual basis and found no correlations
claims.criterion: Absence claim, as fig3h-dms-score-omission-no-correlation on DLS scores. Reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Mice receiving DMS dopamine terminal stimulation on rewarded nosepokes (ChR2) escalate their nosepoking faster than EYFP and ChR2 Scrambled controls during FR1 and RI30.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic excitation of DMS dopamine terminals at the time of a rewarded nosepoke accelerates the development of punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 3; Figure 5F
claims.quote: ChR2 mice escalated their nosepoking much faster than the control groups during FR1 and RI30
claims.criterion: Per stage (FR1, RI30), an ordinary least squares fit of active nosepokes per minute on the session's index within the stage, with a group by index interaction, over the sessions of all mice of the three DMS excitatory groups. Reproduced when the ChR2 slope exceeds both control slopes with interaction p < 0.05 in both stages. Partially reproduced when this holds in one stage or for one control. Not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: On the first shock probe ChR2 mice accept more shocks than EYFP mice (interaction of time and manipulation, F2,35 = 3.65, p < 0.05; Tukey p < 0.05); the difference fades by the second probe.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic excitation of DMS dopamine terminals at the time of a rewarded nosepoke accelerates the development of punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 3; Figure 5G
claims.quote: On the first shock probe, ChR2 mice were significantly more resistant to punishment than EYFP mice ... This difference faded by the second probe
claims.criterion: DMS excitatory mice with both probes. Two-way mixed ANOVA (group between, probe within). Reproduced when the interaction has p < 0.05 and Tukey ChR2 vs EYFP on the first probe has p < 0.05 with ChR2 higher. Partially reproduced when only one of the two holds.

claims.statement: ChR2 mice are very likely to be classified PR, while EYFP and ChR2 Scrambled mice are distributed across phenotypes as expected.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic excitation of DMS dopamine terminals at the time of a rewarded nosepoke accelerates the development of punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 3; Figure 5H
claims.quote: ChR2 mice were extremely likely to be categorized as PR, whereas EYFP and ChR2 Scrambled mice were distributed as expected across groups
claims.criterion: Phenotypes by the Methods rule. Reproduced when more than half of ChR2 mice are PR, the PR fraction is higher in ChR2 than in EYFP and in Scrambled, and a Fisher exact test of PR against not PR, ChR2 against both controls pooled, has p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when the fractions are ordered so but the test has p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Under DMS ChR2 stimulation 100% of male mice and about 71% of female mice are PR.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic excitation of DMS dopamine terminals at the time of a rewarded nosepoke accelerates the development of punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 3; Figure S5F (legend not available)
claims.quote: Notably, under ChR2 stimulation, 100% of male mice were PR mice (Fig. S5F). A large majority of female mice (~71%) were also PR
claims.criterion: Phenotypes by the Methods rule. Reproduced when both are within tolerance; partially reproduced when one is.

claims.statement: DMS dopamine terminal stimulation does not change omission probe performance.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic excitation of DMS dopamine terminals at the time of a rewarded nosepoke accelerates the development of punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 3; Figure 5I
claims.quote: We also looked to see whether DMS dopamine terminal stimulation influenced performance on the omission probe. It did not
claims.criterion: Absence claim. One-way ANOVA of omission completion time across the three DMS excitatory groups. Reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: DMS dopamine terminal inhibition impairs initial learning; 25% of NpHR and 22% of NpHR Scrambled mice in group 1 failed FR1, and 29% of NpHR mice in group 2 failed RI30, and were dropped.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic inhibition of dopamine terminals in DMS delays the development of punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 2; Figure 6F
claims.quote: 25% of NpHR mice and 22% of NpHR Scrambled mice were dropped from the study after >14 days (mean+2SD) of unsuccessful FR1 training ... In this case, 29% of NpHR mice were dropped from the study because they could not learn RI30
claims.criterion: The dandiset marks mice that did not learn in its notes. Reproduced when the marked mice (or mice without any RI60 session) number 4 NpHR (2 of 8 and 2 of 7), 2 NpHR Scrambled and 0 EYFP. Partially reproduced when the marked mice are only NpHR or Scrambled but the counts differ. Blocked when the dandiset does not say which mice were dropped. Group 1 and group 2 cannot be told apart unless the files say which group a mouse is in.

claims.statement: DMS dopamine terminal inhibition on rewarded nosepokes delays punishment resistance; NpHR mice accept fewer shocks than EYFP mice on the second probe (Tukey p < 0.01).
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic inhibition of dopamine terminals in DMS delays the development of punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 3; Figure 6G
claims.quote: NpHR inhibition of DMS dopamine terminals during RI60 training delayed the development of punishment-resistant reward-seeking, with a significant effect on the second shock probe
claims.criterion: DMS inhibitory mice with both probes. Tukey's test on second probe counts across the three groups. Reproduced when NpHR < EYFP with p < 0.05 (notes say whether p < 0.01). Partially reproduced when NpHR < EYFP with p >= 0.05. A two-way mixed ANOVA is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: The NpHR group has more PS mice, and the NpHR Scrambled group more PR mice, than the EYFP group.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic inhibition of dopamine terminals in DMS delays the development of punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 3; Figure 6H
claims.quote: the NpHR group had an increased incidence of PS mice, while the NpHR Scrambled group had an increased incidence of PR mice
claims.criterion: Phenotypes by the Methods rule. Reproduced when the PS fraction of NpHR exceeds that of EYFP and the PR fraction of Scrambled exceeds that of EYFP. Partially reproduced when one holds. A Fisher exact test of each is reported.

claims.statement: DMS dopamine terminal inhibition does not change omission completion time.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic inhibition of dopamine terminals in DMS delays the development of punishment-resistant reward-seeking, paragraph 3; Figure 6I
claims.quote: No significant differences in omission time were observed
claims.criterion: Absence claim. One-way ANOVA across the three DMS inhibitory groups. Reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Mice receiving DLS dopamine terminal stimulation (ChR2, EYFP, ChR2 Scrambled) escalate their nosepoking at the same rates.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic excitation of dopamine terminals in DLS at the time of a rewarded nosepoke does not influence instrumental learning or behavioral flexibility, paragraph 2; Figure 7F
claims.quote: All groups of mice (ChR2, EYFP, and ChR2 Scrambled) behaved similarly, escalating their nosepoking at the same rates
claims.criterion: Absence claim. The fit of fig5f-dms-chr2-escalation on DLS excitatory mice. Reproduced when no group by index interaction has p < 0.05 in FR1 or RI30. No test is given in the paper.

claims.statement: DLS dopamine terminal stimulation does not change the number of shocks received.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic excitation of dopamine terminals in DLS at the time of a rewarded nosepoke does not influence instrumental learning or behavioral flexibility, paragraph 2; Figure 7G
claims.quote: All groups of mice (ChR2, EYFP, and ChR2 Scrambled) behaved similarly ... and receiving similar numbers of shocks
claims.criterion: Absence claim. Two-way mixed ANOVA (group between, probe within) on DLS excitatory mice with both probes. Reproduced when neither the group main effect nor the interaction has p < 0.05.

claims.statement: DLS ChR2, EYFP and ChR2 Scrambled mice have similar distributions of PR, DPR and PS.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic excitation of dopamine terminals in DLS at the time of a rewarded nosepoke does not influence instrumental learning or behavioral flexibility, paragraph 2; Figure 7H
claims.quote: All groups had similar distributions of PR, DPR, and PS mice
claims.criterion: Absence claim; the paper gives no test. Chi-square test of the 3 x 3 table of group by phenotype (Methods rule). Reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: DLS dopamine terminal stimulation does not change omission completion time.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic excitation of dopamine terminals in DLS at the time of a rewarded nosepoke does not influence instrumental learning or behavioral flexibility, paragraph 2; Figure 7I
claims.quote: No significant differences were observed in omission completion time

claims.statement: Whole-head activity of 196 sex-shared and 6 male-specific neurons was studied in 22 hermaphrodites and 25 males.

claims.statement: Of the 89 head neuron classes, 84 (94%) responded to at least one stimulus in at least one sex.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 9; Figure 5B
claims.quote: Of the 89 neuron classes in the head, 84 were responsive (94%)

Male-specific CEM and MCM are not among the 89 (code removes them). Reproduced when the count is within tolerance under both exclusion readings (opening comment, EXCLUSION).

claims.statement: Of the 89 head neuron classes, 80 (90%) responded dimorphically to at least one stimulus.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 9; Figure 5B
claims.quote: and 80 classes (90%) were sexually dimorphic

The code (Fig5.ipynb) counts a class as dimorphic only when it is also responsive; the Methods do not say so. Readings are (a) dimorphic and responsive, as the code; (b) dimorphic alone. Each is run with both exclusion readings. Reproduced when the count is within tolerance under (a) or (b), with both exclusion readings giving that outcome.

claims.statement: Responsive and dimorphic classes per layer are 23 and 22 of 24 sensory, 34 and 33 of 36 inter, 14 and 13 of 15 motor, and 13 and 12 of 14 pharyngeal classes.

claims.quote: Of the 24 sensory neuron classes, 23 classes (96%) were responsive, and 22 classes (92%) were dimorphic. Of the 36 interneuron classes, 34 classes (94%) were responsive, and 33 classes (92%) were dimorphic. Of the 15 motor neuron classes, 14 classes (93%) were responsive, and 13 classes (87%) were dimorphic. Of the 14 pharyngeal neuron classes, 13 classes (93%) were responsive, and 12 classes (86%) were dimorphic
claims.criterion: As the two claims it depends on, split by layer. The layer assignment is OPEN (opening comment, CLASSES). Reproduced when all eight counts are within tolerance under reading (a) or (b) of fig5b-dimorphic-classes; partially reproduced when six or seven are. claims.statement: For every stimulus at least one neuron class responds dimorphically and at least one monomorphically.

claims.quote: For each stimulus tested, we observed at least one neuron class respond in a sexually dimorphic manner, and one class respond in a monomorphic manner
claims.criterion: Per cue, a class is dimorphic to it when DIMORPHISM gives p <= 0.05 at onset or offset, and monomorphic to it when RESPONSIVE holds for that cue and DIMORPHISM gives p > 0.05 at both onset and offset (Figure 5B legend counts per-stimulus responsive and dimorphic classes; code Fig5.ipynb). Reproduced when all 8 cues have at least one of each, under each exclusion reading.

claims.statement: Nearly every sensory neuron class responds dimorphically to at least one stimulus and monomorphically to at least one other.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 1; Figures 3 and 5A
claims.quote: nearly every sensory neuron responds in a sexually dimorphic manner to at least one stimulus while responding monomorphically to at least one other stimulus
claims.criterion: Dimorphic and monomorphic to a cue as defined in fig3-each-stimulus-mixed, over the 24 sensory canonical classes. The paper gives no count for the pair of conditions; "nearly every" is read from the paper's own use of it for 22 of 24 sensory classes and 80 of 89 classes, as at least 90% (22 of 24). Reproduced when at least 22 sensory classes meet both conditions.

claims.statement: Dimorphic and monomorphic responses are less present in interneurons than in sensory neurons, and less still in motor neurons.
claims.source: Summary; Figures 3A, 3B and 5B
claims.quote: This dimorphic and monomorphic activity was present to a lesser extent in downstream interneurons and even less so in motoneurons
claims.criterion: The paper gives no measure for this. Its class counts (Figure 5B, 92% of sensory, 92% of inter and 87% of motor classes dimorphic) do not order sensory above inter, so the statement is read from the per-stimulus counts of Figure 5B and the cells of Figure 3A and 3B. Over the 8 cues, with canonical classes and layers as in fig5b-layer-counts, per layer, readings are (a) the fraction of class-cue combinations with a dimorphic response (DIMORPHISM, onset or offset); (b) the fraction of class-cue combinations that are responsive (RESPONSIVE, dimorphic or monomorphic); (c) as (a) over subclass-cue-window cells of Figure 3A and 3B. Reproduced when, under one reading, sensory > inter > motor; each reading is reported.

claims.statement: At the onset of osmotic stress ASER and ASH respond monomorphically while AWA and AWB respond dimorphically.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 5; Figures 2B and 3A
claims.quote: in response to the onset of osmotic stress, the gustatory neuron ASER and the nociceptive neuron ASH ... show monomorphic responses, whereas olfactory neurons AWA and AWB ... show dimorphic responses
claims.criterion: DIMORPHISM, representation 1, onset window, 800 mM sorbitol. Reproduced when AWA and AWB have p <= 0.05, and ASER and ASH have p > 0.05 (the absence is judged on the same test) and are responsive to sorbitol at onset (RESPONSIVE, in at least one sex), since Figures 3 and 5 count a class as monomorphic only when it responds. The four p-values and normalized differences are reported, under both exclusion readings.

claims.statement: AWA's response to osmotic stress is dimorphic and BAG's response to high odor is monomorphic.
claims.source: Figure 2B legend
claims.quote: exemplifying sexually dimorphic (e.g., AWA responding to osmotic stress) and monomorphic neural activity (e.g., BAG responding to high odor)
claims.criterion: DIMORPHISM, representation 1. The legend does not say onset or offset; Figure 2B plots the whole presentation. Readings are (a) onset, (b) offset, (c) either window for AWA and both windows for BAG. Reproduced when, under one reading, AWA has p <= 0.05 and BAG with 1e-2 isoamyl alcohol has p > 0.05 and is responsive to it in the same window (RESPONSIVE, in at least one sex), since Figures 3 and 5 count a class as monomorphic only when it responds.

claims.statement: ASH responds monomorphically to osmotic and toxic stress but dimorphically to high salt.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 5; Figures 2B and 3A
claims.quote: the ASH neuron's response to osmotic and toxic stress is monomorphic, but its response to high salt is dimorphic
claims.criterion: DIMORPHISM, representation 1, onset window (the text cites Figure 3A, onset). Reproduced when ASH has p <= 0.05 for 450 mM NaCl, and p > 0.05 for sorbitol and for CuSO4 while responsive to each at onset (RESPONSIVE, in at least one sex; monomorphic as in Figures 3 and 5).

claims.statement: ASER responds dimorphically to low salt but monomorphically to high salt.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 5; Figures 2B and 3A
claims.quote: the ASER neuron's response to a low concentration of salt is dimorphic, but its response to a higher concentration of salt is monomorphic
claims.criterion: DIMORPHISM, representation 1, onset window (Figure 3A), ASER alone. Reproduced when the 100 mM NaCl response has p <= 0.05, and the 450 mM NaCl response has p > 0.05 while responsive at onset (RESPONSIVE, in at least one sex; monomorphic as in Figures 3 and 5).

claims.statement: Pharyngeal interneuron I2 responds dimorphically to pheromone, osmotic stress and salt.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 7; Figure 2E
claims.quote: pharyngeal interneuron I2 exhibited sexually dimorphic responses to pheromone, osmotic stress, and salt
claims.criterion: DIMORPHISM, representation 1, class I2. The text fixes neither the window nor which salt. Reproduced when ascr#3, sorbitol and at least one NaCl concentration each give p <= 0.05 at onset or offset; the readings (onset only, offset only, low salt, high salt) are all reported.

claims.statement: The pharyngeal (enteric) neurons respond dimorphically to food, salt and pheromone.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 4; Figure 2E
claims.quote: the enteric nervous system of the worm responds to food, salt, and (most strikingly) pheromone in a sexually dimorphic manner
claims.criterion: DIMORPHISM, representation 1, over the pharyngeal subclasses (layer OPEN, opening comment). Reproduced when at least one pharyngeal class has p <= 0.05, at onset or offset, for OP50, for ascr#3, and for at least one NaCl concentration.

claims.statement: Olfactory neurons AWA and AWB also respond to osmotic and toxic stress.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 7; Figure 2B
claims.quote: in addition to responding to odors, olfactory neurons AWA and AWB also responded to nociceptive stimuli, including osmotic and toxic stress
claims.criterion: RESPONSIVE per class and cue (in at least one sex, onset or offset). Reproduced when AWA and AWB are each responsive to sorbitol and to CuSO4.

claims.statement: ADF responds to food in hermaphrodites but to pheromone in males, and pharyngeal neuron M2 shows a similar switch between food and pheromone.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 7; Figures 2B and 2E
claims.quote: ADF responds to food in hermaphrodites, but in males it responds to pheromones ... More surprising was a similar dimorphic switch in the M2 pharyngeal neuron, also to food and pheromone
claims.criterion: Per sex, RESPONSIVE (onset or offset) of ADF and M2 to OP50 and to ascr#3. For M2 the text does not say which sex responds to which cue. Readings are (a) ADF responsive to food and not to pheromone in hermaphrodites, and to pheromone and not to food in males; M2 responsive to one cue and not the other in each sex, with the cues opposite between sexes; (b) DIMORPHISM gives p <= 0.05 for both cues in each of ADF and M2, in the direction of a switch (for ADF the absolute mean response to OP50 larger in hermaphrodites and to ascr#3 larger in males; for M2 the larger sex opposite between the two cues), since a dimorphism without direction does not test the switch the statement names. Reproduced when ADF and M2 meet one reading; partially reproduced when one of the two does.

claims.statement: The male-specific head neuron classes CEM and MCM were predominantly unresponsive to the stimuli.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 2; Figure S2D (the text cites S2C; the legend of S2D shows the male-specific neurons)
claims.quote: The male-specific head neuron classes (sensory neuron CEM and interneuron MCM) were predominantly unresponsive to stimuli
claims.criterion: RESPONSIVE in males, for CEMD, CEMV and MCM as the code separates them, over 8 cues and 2 windows (16 tests per class). "Predominantly" is read as most of the tests. Reproduced when fewer than half of each class's tests are significant; the number significant is reported.

claims.statement: Tail neurons did not appear to respond to cues presented to the head.
claims.source: Results, Broad chemosensory stimulation activates the whole brain of both sexes, paragraph 3
claims.quote: tail neurons did not appear to be responsive to cues presented to the head
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test on tail neurons; its test of responsiveness is RESPONSIVE. A claim of absence, judged on that test, applied to each tail class the dandiset identifies. Reproduced when no tail class is responsive; not reproduced when any is, with the number of classes and tests reported. Not testable if the dandiset holds no identified tail neurons.

claims.statement: Neurons within the same class usually have equivalent activity, with left and right neurons more correlated with each other than with neurons of other classes.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 3; Figure S2F
claims.quote: Neurons within the same class usually exhibit equivalent neural-activity traces
claims.criterion: Figure S2F legend, the within-animal Pearson r between the left and right neurons of each class against the mean r of each of them with neurons of other classes. The traces are OPEN. Readings are (a) the band-passed traces of CORRELATION; (b) the raw traces. Reproduced when, in each sex, the mean left-right r exceeds the mean other-class r for more than half of the bilateral classes, under both readings.

claims.statement: Restricting the test to the first cycle or to per-animal averages makes specific neuron-stimulus pairs less clearly dimorphic but leaves the pattern of dimorphic neuron classes largely unchanged.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 10; Figure S3A to S3E
claims.quote: Overall, while specific odor-neuron pairs are not as clearly dimorphic in these more conservative analyses, the pattern of neurons that we find to respond dimorphically is largely unaffected
claims.criterion: DIMORPHISM under representations 1, 2 and 3 (Methods), per subclass, at p <= 0.05; a class is dimorphic when any cue and window is (Figure S3E legend). The paper fixes no measure of "largely". Readings are (a) more than half of the classes dimorphic under representation 1 are dimorphic under all three (S3E's robust classes); (b) more than half of them are dimorphic under each of representations 2 and 3 separately. Reproduced when one reading holds and the number of dimorphic neuron-cue-window pairs is lower under representations 2 and 3 than under 1.

claims.statement: Response amplitude does not depend on the position of the stimulus in the presentation order.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 10; Figure S2E
claims.quote: We also verified that there was no dependence on response amplitude as a function of stimulus order
claims.criterion: Figure S2E legend, onset responses (RESPONSE) of cycle 1 only, against position 1 to 10, for all stimuli combined and for each stimulus. The paper names no test and does not say which neurons enter. Readings are (a) a linear regression of response on position over all neuron responses, slope p >= 0.05; (b) the same on per-animal means over neurons; (c) a one-way ANOVA over positions on all neuron responses, p >= 0.05. A claim of absence with no test in the paper, so all readings are run; reproduced when all find no dependence for all stimuli combined, not reproduced when all find one, otherwise blocked as methods_underspecified. Per-stimulus results are reported.

claims.statement: Motor-state-dependent sexual dimorphism is more prominent in interneurons than in sensory or motor neurons.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 11; Figure S3F and S3G
claims.quote: These state-dependent responses were more prominent in interneurons than in sensory or motor neurons
claims.criterion: State per presentation from AVA (Methods, Classifying motor state); the AVA trace is divided by an exponential fit of its baseline, the 5 s before onset is a transition if it changes by more than 20%, otherwise reverse when its mean is above the global mean and forward when below. OPEN, with all combinations run. AVA as AVAL, AVAR, or their mean; "changes by more than 20%" as (max - min) / mean of the window, or as |last - first| / first; the fit subtracted or divided. Per neuron-cue pair and window, a two-way ANOVA of RESPONSE values (representation 1) on sex and state (forward and reverse; transitions out), interaction p (Methods, Identifying state-dependent...), BH over the pairs of each window. Per layer, the fraction of neuron-cue pairs with interaction q < 0.05 (black borders in S3F, S3G), and as a second reading p < 0.05. Reproduced when the interneuron fraction exceeds both the sensory and the motor fraction.

claims.statement: The structure of AIB's sexual dimorphism to high salt or pheromone differs between forward and backward motor states.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 11; Figure S2C
claims.quote: In some responses, such as AIB responding to high salt or pheromones (Figure S2C), the structure of the sexual dimorphism is different when animals are (fictively) moving forward in comparison to backward
claims.criterion: States and readings as in figs3fg-state-dependence-interneurons. Per state, DIMORPHISM of AIB (S2C legend, two-sample t-test). Reproduced when, for 450 mM NaCl or for ascr#3, at onset or offset, either the sex x state interaction has p < 0.05 or the response is dimorphic (p <= 0.05) in one state and not in the other.

claims.statement: Average responses are mostly insensitive to the animal's motor state, and many dimorphic sensory responses persist after conditioning on it.
claims.source: Results, Most sensory neurons in the head exhibit sexually dimorphic responses, paragraph 11; Discussion, paragraph 3; Figure S8A to S8D
claims.quote: Overall, however, average responses were mostly insensitive to the motor state of the animal
claims.criterion: States and readings as in figs3fg-state-dependence-interneurons, onset state, over the classes and cues of Figure 2B to 2E (code Fig2&3_prepare_data, ADF, ADL, ASEL, ASER, ASH, ASI, AWA, AWB, BAG, AIA, AIB, AVE, AVH, RIA, RIR, DB1, VB2, M2, I2, MC, M3). The paper names no test of insensitivity; with its two-sample t-test, per class, cue, window and sex, forward against reverse responses. Reproduced when more than half of these comparisons have p > 0.05, and more than half of the sensory class-cue-window responses dimorphic under DIMORPHISM stay dimorphic (p <= 0.05) within the forward state or within the reverse state.

claims.statement: Pairwise functional connectivity is highly similar between the sexes (R2 = 0.8 for a linear fit of male on hermaphrodite mean correlations).
claims.source: Results, Functional correlations between sex-shared neurons are predominantly shared between sexes, paragraph 2; Figure 4C
claims.quote: the functional connectivity between hermaphrodites and males is highly similar (80% or R2 = 0.8 for a linear fit)
claims.criterion: CORRELATION over the pairs of the 110 subclasses with stimuli left out (code Fig4.ipynb, no_odor_score_df); R2 of an ordinary least-squares line (scipy linregress, as the code). Reproduced when R2 is within tolerance under CORRELATION reading (b), the Methods'; reading (a), the code's, is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: In both sexes stimuli are more correlated or anti-correlated with sensory neurons than with interneurons or motor neurons.
claims.source: Results, Functional correlations between sex-shared neurons are predominantly shared between sexes, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
claims.quote: In both sexes, stimuli were more correlated (or anti-correlated) with sensory neurons than with interneurons ... or motor neurons
claims.criterion: CORRELATION per stimulus-subclass pair (880 pairs), the per-sex mean r. The paper gives no test or summary. Readings are (a) the mean |r| over the pairs of each layer; (b) the root mean square r (as Figure S14's global correlation). Reproduced when, in each sex, the sensory value exceeds the interneuron and the motor value under both readings, with CORRELATION reading (b); CORRELATION reading (a) is a variant.

claims.statement: Pharyngeal neurons show some correlations with each other but are largely uncorrelated with the rest of the brain.
claims.source: Results, Functional correlations between sex-shared neurons are predominantly shared between sexes, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
claims.quote: Neurons within the pharynx show some correlations with each other but are largely uncorrelated with the rest of the brain
claims.criterion: CORRELATION, per-sex mean r per subclass pair. The paper gives no measure; mean |r| is used, with root mean square r as the second reading. Reproduced when, in each sex, pharyngeal to non-pharyngeal pairs have a lower value than pharyngeal to pharyngeal pairs and than non-pharyngeal to non-pharyngeal pairs, under every reading.

claims.statement: Almost all neuron pairs have a functional dimorphism below 0.4, on a scale of 0 to 2.
claims.source: Results, Functional and synaptic sexual dimorphisms are distinct, paragraph 2; Figure 4E
claims.quote: we observed that almost all neuronal pairs had a functional dimorphism of less than 0.4
claims.criterion: CORRELATION, functional dimorphism per pair of subclasses (stimuli left out, "neuronal pairs"). "Almost all" is read as (a) at least 95% or (b) at least 99% of pairs. Reproduced when one reading holds under CORRELATION reading (b); the fraction is reported under both CORRELATION readings, (a) as a variant.

claims.statement: Functional and synaptic dimorphisms are uncorrelated.
claims.source: Results, Functional and synaptic sexual dimorphisms are distinct, paragraph 3; Figure 4D
claims.quote: We found no clear relationship between synaptic and functional dimorphism
claims.criterion: Functional dimorphism (CORRELATION) and synaptic dimorphism degree (CONNECTOME) per pair of subclasses present in the connectome, pairs without synapses set to 0 (code Fig4.ipynb). A claim of absence. The test is the code's linear regression (scipy linregress); the paper reports no value or threshold, so the paper's alpha of 0.05 is used. Reproduced when the slope has p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05; R2 and slope reported either way. The code's regularization of 3 is a variant.

claims.statement: The neuron pairs with the highest synaptic dimorphisms are functionally uncorrelated in both sexes and show little to no functional dimorphism.
claims.source: Results, Functional and synaptic sexual dimorphisms are distinct, paragraph 3; Figure 4F; Figure S4B
claims.quote: These pairs were functionally uncorrelated in both sexes
claims.criterion: The top 36 pairs by dimorphism degree after removing pairs with combined SEM >= 5 (Methods, Selecting neuron pairs...), and the six of Figure 4F (code, RIM-SAAD, AIB-AIM, URYD-RMDV, AVK-RMF, URX-RIR, ASH-AVA). Functional dimorphism p from CORRELATION. Readings of "no functional dimorphism" are (a) p > 0.05 (Figure 4F asterisks); (b) p >= 0.01 (Figure 4E white). Reproduced when more than half of the 36 and of the six have no functional dimorphism under one reading; their mean r per sex is reported. The text's "functionally uncorrelated in both sexes" has no measure or test in the paper (the Figure 4F legend states only little to no functional dimorphism), so that part is reported descriptively and does not decide the outcome.

claims.statement: The neuron pairs with the highest functional dimorphisms are mostly not synaptically connected, and where connected their connectivity is essentially not dimorphic.
claims.source: Results, Functional and synaptic sexual dimorphisms are distinct, paragraph 3; Figure 4G; Figure S4C
claims.quote: We found that these pairs were mostly not synaptically connected. When they were connected, the connectivity was essentially not dimorphic
claims.criterion: The top 36 pairs by functional dimorphism with p < 0.01 (Methods; the code's p < 0.001 is a variant), stimulus pairs, sensory-sensory pairs and pairs absent from the connectome left out (Methods, Selecting neuron pairs...). The order of these exclusions is OPEN. The Methods name them after the top 36, and the Figure S4C legend says the 36 include pairs that Figure 4G drops (sensory-sensory pairs). Readings are (i) the exclusions applied before taking the 36; (ii) the top 36 by p < 0.01 alone, with stimulus pairs and pairs absent from the connectome then left out of the counts. Both are run and must give the outcome. Not connected is read as (a) zero summed weight in both sexes, or (b) both sums below 3 (the code drops these). Not dimorphic is a difference below 5 (Methods, the bar for a substantial dimorphism). Reproduced when, under one reading, more than half of the 36 are not connected and more than half of the connected ones are not dimorphic.

claims.statement: Indirect multi-hop synaptic connections are stronger between all pairs but still fail to match functional dimorphisms.
claims.source: Results, Functional and synaptic sexual dimorphisms are distinct, paragraph 4; Figure S20
claims.quote: these multi-hop indirect synaptic connections were higher between all pairs of neurons, but they failed to match the dimorphisms measured in functional connectivity
claims.criterion: Figure S20 legend, a weighted graph per sex with edge cost 1 / synaptic strength (CONNECTOME sums), Dijkstra shortest paths, indirect strength 1 / path cost; dimorphism degree as CONNECTOME on the indirect strengths. Judged as fig4d-functional-synaptic-uncorrelated (linregress slope p >= 0.05) on these values.

claims.statement: Normalizing the three hermaphrodite connectomes by their 95% quantiles cut the mean SEM across them from 1.14 (SD 2.07) to 0.62 (SD 0.87).
claims.source: STAR Methods, Normalization of connectome data
claims.quote: This average SEM was 1.14 with a standard deviation of 2.07 ... the average SEM decreased to 0.62 (down from the initial 1.14), and the standard deviation of the SEM decreased to 0.87
claims.criterion: CONNECTOME only; the dandiset is not used. SEM per directed synapse over the three hermaphrodite datasets (pandas sem, ddof 1), its mean and SD (ddof 1) before and after normalization. Which synapses enter is OPEN. The Methods say "across all synapses", the code (Fig4_prepare_data) keeps synapses with both neurons among the recorded head neurons. Readings are (a) the code's set; (b) every directed neuron pair with a synapse in at least one hermaphrodite dataset. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance under one reading, as these are readings of what the reported numbers were computed over.

claims.statement: The stimuli evoke behavioral responses in wild-type and in the imaged NeuroPAL GCaMP6s strain, with preferences that are monomorphic for some stimuli and dimorphic for others.
claims.source: Results, Broad chemosensory stimulation activates the whole brain of both sexes, paragraph 1; Figure 1A and 1C; Figure S1A and S1B
claims.quote: These stimuli evoked robust behavioral responses in both wild-type (N2) worms and the NeuroPAL;GCaMP6s (OH16230) worms
claims.criterion: Drop-test avoidance indices (Methods, Behavioral assays; code FigS2.ipynb). Per stimulus and strain, hermaphrodite against male, two-sample t-test (S1 legend; equal variances, as the code). "Robust" has no test in the paper or code and is reported descriptively. Reproduced when, in each strain, at least one stimulus differs between the sexes (p <= 0.05) and at least one does not. The paper does not say these data are in the dandiset.

claims.statement: The RSC dataset holds 570 units recorded in 14 sessions from 3 mice.
claims.source: STAR Methods, Behavioral procedures, paragraph 2; Experimental model and study participant details, paragraph 2; Figure 5F legend
claims.quote: A total of 570 units were recorded from 14 sessions.
claims.criterion: Counts of the dandiset's sessions, distinct subjects and sorted units over all sessions. The tolerance is zero, as these are counts of the deposited records themselves, which the archive's description gives with the same numbers. Reproduced when all three match; partially reproduced when sessions and mice match and the unit count is within 10%.

claims.statement: In retrosplenial cortex, as in PoSub, units with a larger firing-rate overshoot at UP state onset (peak-to-mean ratio, PMR) enter the UP state earlier; UP onset delay and PMR are negatively correlated (Kendall tau = -0.28, n = 570 units from 14 sessions in 3 mice, p = 6.76e-21).
claims.source: Figure 5F legend; Results, Post-DOWN rebound suggests a widespread role for Ih in neuronal activation at UP onset, paragraph 4
claims.quote: We found a similar relationship in the frontal cortex ... and RSC (data available at DANDI:000987) (Figure 5F).
claims.criterion: Method from Figure5F.py and detectDOWNs_RSC.py (commit 4ee34f3), which agree with the STAR Methods (UP and DOWN state detection; Peri-Event Time Histograms; Sequential Activation at UP onset) and the Results definition of PMR. NREM epochs are those of the sleep scoring (SleepScoreMaster). DOWN states are the ones the dandiset carries as the study's, if it carries them; they are also re-detected as the code does it, and the re-detection is shown as a check. Re-detection, per session, from the spikes of all units in NREM, counted in 10 ms bins, smoothed with a Gaussian of 20 ms s.d. (pandas rolling window of 100 bins, std 2 bins) and summed; DOWN states are the intervals below the 20th percentile of that rate; intervals shorter than 10 ms are dropped, those closer than 20 ms merged, and then those shorter than 30 ms or longer than 500 ms dropped; UP states are the intervals between consecutive DOWN states, and the DOWN states are then restricted to NREM. Per unit, the PETH of its spikes around each UP state start (the DU transition) is pynapple's compute_eventcorrelogram with 5 ms bins, a 0.255 s window, ep = the UP states and norm = True (spikes and events restricted to UP states, the PETH divided by the unit's mean rate in UP states), smoothed with a Gaussian of 2 bins s.d. (10 ms, rolling window of 8 bins) and cut to 0 to 0.155 s after DU. UP onset delay is the first time in that interval at which the normalized PETH exceeds 0.5; PMR is the maximum of the normalized PETH in that interval; a unit that never exceeds 0.5 is left out. Units of all sessions are pooled and scipy's kendalltau is computed between UP onset delay and PMR. Which units enter is open. The text allows two readings. (a) All sorted units, as Figure5F.py does (no cell-type selection) and as the legend's n of 570 units, the total recorded per the Methods, implies. (b) Putative EX units only, per the Methods sentence "only EX units were used for analyses", classified by trough-to-peak duration above 0.35 ms and mean rate below 10 Hz in open-field exploration (Spike sorting and unit classification). Both are run. Reproduced when tau is negative with p < 0.05 under both readings and within tolerance of -0.28 under at least one; partially reproduced when tau is negative with p < 0.05 under both but outside tolerance under both; not reproduced when tau is not negative with p < 0.05 under either; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree on sign or significance. The number of units entering the test is reported under each reading. The pynapple version is not pinned by the code; any version whose compute_eventcorrelogram takes these arguments is a standard choice and is reported. The Figure 5F legend reads "Same as (D)", an Isomap plot, but Figure5F.py draws the 2D histogram of UP onset delay against PMR with its fit line, as Figure5C.py does; only the correlation is tested.

claims.statement: In PoSub, PMR is negatively correlated with UP onset delay; earlier-activating EX units show a larger overshoot, and virtually no late-activating unit has a large PMR (Kendall tau = -0.19, n = 1,096, p = 8.34e-20).
claims.source: Figure 5C; Results, Post-DOWN rebound suggests a widespread role for Ih in neuronal activation at UP onset, paragraph 2
claims.quote: As predicted, PMR was negatively correlated with UP state onset timing, with earlierspiking cells showing a larger overshoot (Figure 5C). Critically, virtually no units with a late activation at UP onset had a large PMR.
claims.criterion: As fig5f-rsc-pmr-onset, with the PoSub DOWN states (detectDOWNs_PoSub.py, or the event files in Analysis/OutputFiles) and EX units only, as Figure5C.py does with the CellTypes ex and gd flags. Reproduced when tau is negative with p < 0.05 and within tolerance.

claims.statement: An Isomap projection of the DU-aligned PETHs of all PoSub EX units shows a continuous gradation of profiles whose first dimension correlates strongly with PMR (Pearson R = 0.88, n = 1,096).
claims.source: Figure 5D; Results, Post-DOWN rebound suggests a widespread role for Ih in neuronal activation at UP onset, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Isomap decomposition of the DU-PETHs of all PoSub units (Figure 5D) revealed a continuous gradation of temporal profiles at the UP state onset, which was largely attributable to a single dimension strongly correlated with PMR
claims.criterion: PETHs as in fig5c-posub-pmr-onset, for the units that enter that test; sklearn Isomap with 2 components and 50 neighbours on the stacked PETHs, as Figure5D.py and the Methods (Peri-Event Time Histograms) give; the absolute Pearson R of the first dimension with PMR, since the sign of an Isomap axis is arbitrary. The window of the PETHs given to Isomap differs between the sources. The Methods (PETHs on an interval of +/- 250 ms from DU) and the Figure 5D legend (PETHs aligned to DU, +/- 250 ms) give -250 to +250 ms, which is the main result; Figure5D.py passes the PETHs cut to 0 to 0.155 s, which is run as a variant. Reproduced when |R| is within tolerance and p < 0.05 under the Methods window; the variant is reported.

claims.statement: In rat frontal cortex, UP onset delay and PMR are also negatively correlated (Kendall tau = -0.22, n = 950 EX units from 25 sessions in 11 rats, p = 5e-21).
claims.source: Figure 5E legend; Results, Post-DOWN rebound suggests a widespread role for Ih in neuronal activation at UP onset, paragraph 4
claims.quote: We found a similar relationship in the frontal cortex (FC; data from Watson et al.
claims.criterion: As fig5f-rsc-pmr-onset, with the dataset's own UP states (SlowWaves events), excitatory units by its CellClass, as Figure5E.py does. Reproduced when tau is negative with p < 0.05 and within tolerance.

claims.statement: At the DOWN-to-UP transition PoSub EX units activate in sequence, dorsal units entering the UP state before ventral ones; the per-session correlation of UP onset delay with depth is consistently non-zero for DU and not for UD transitions.
claims.source: Figure 1E to 1G; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 1
claims.quote: This sequential activity followed an anatomical pattern... dorsally located units tended to enter the UP state before ventrally located units (Figure 1G; one-sample Wilcoxon test; DU, W = 1, n = 16
claims.criterion: Per session, the Kendall tau between UP onset delay and depth of EX units, onset delay as in fig5f-rsc-pmr-onset (first bin above 0.5 of the rate-in-UP normalized PETH, 0 to 150 ms after DU), and for UD the last bin above 0.5 between -150 and -5 ms of the PETH around DOWN starts for units that also cross after +5 ms, as Figure1G.py does. Reproduced when the DU coefficients differ from 0 by a two-sided one-sample Wilcoxon test at p < 0.05 with the sign of dorsal-first, the UD coefficients do not (p >= 0.05), and DU and UD differ by a Mann-Whitney U test at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: PoSub neurons activate with reliable delays after the DU transition, ranging from 5 to 100 ms (99th percentile range).
claims.source: Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 1; Figures 1D to 1F
claims.quote: Unlike UD transitions, neurons activated with reliable delays with respect to the DU transition (Figures 1D-1F and S1I), ranging from 5 to 100 ms (99th percentile range)
claims.criterion: UP onset delays of all PoSub EX units as in fig5c-posub-pmr-onset. "99th percentile range" is not defined. Readings are (a) the 0.5th to 99.5th percentiles and (b) the 1st to 99th percentiles of the pooled delays. Reproduced when under one reading both bounds are within the range widened by 10% of each bound.

claims.statement: DOWN states detected from ventral PoSub last longer than those detected from dorsal PoSub (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, W = 9, n = 16, p = 0.01).
claims.source: Figure 1H; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 1
claims.quote: we found that the DOWN state durations were significantly longer in the ventral half when detected separately from the dorsal half of PoSub (Figure 1H; p = 0.01, Wilcoxon signed-rank test).
claims.criterion: As Figure1H.py and the Methods (UP and DOWN state detection, paragraph 2). Units split into dorsal and ventral halves by depth (two equal-width depth bins); the pooled spikes of each half form a PETH around each DOWN start, normalized by its mean rate in UP states and smoothed as in fig5f-rsc-pmr-onset; the DOWN duration of a half is the first time after +5 ms where the normalized rate exceeds 0.2 minus the last time between -150 and -5 ms where it exceeds 0.2. The code uses all units with the gd flag; the Methods' general rule would use EX units only; both are run. Reproduced when ventral exceeds dorsal by a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test at p < 0.05 under both; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: HD information, linear speed and angular head velocity tuning of PoSub EX cells do not vary with DV position; resultant vector length and peak rate show weak but significant correlations with it.
claims.source: Figure 1B; Figure S1D to S1F; Results, opening paragraph
claims.quote: Across all behavioral correlates tested, we saw either no significant correlations (Figures 1B and S1D) or, at most, weak but significant correlations with DV location (Figures S1E and S1F)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence for HD information, speed and AHV scores, judged by the paper's test, a two-sided Kendall tau against depth at p < 0.05 over all EX cells; the measures as the Methods define them (HD tuning curves and tuning metrics). Reproduced when those three are not significant and resultant vector length and peak rate are positively correlated with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The DOWN state resets the virtual HD signal; the angle at the start of an UP state is unrelated to the angle at the end of the previous UP state.
claims.source: Figure 1J; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 2
claims.quote: We found that the DOWN state resets this virtual HD signal, as there was no relationship between the angle represented at the end of an UP state and the beginning of the subsequent UP state (Figure 1J).
claims.criterion: Angles from the Isomap ring as in the Methods (Isomap Projection and Decoding), the first post-DU bin whose radius exceeds one third of the mean wake radius against the angle at the preceding UD transition, which the legend names as the shuffled quantity; the paper does not fix which bin gives the angle at UD, and the last above-threshold bin before UD and the mean of the last 150 ms before UD are both run. A claim of absence, judged as the legend does, the histogram of angular differences against 1,000 shuffles of the angle at UD; reproduced when no bin lies outside the minimum to maximum of the shuffled counts. The histogram's bin width is not given; 20 bins over the circle is a standard choice, and 10 and 36 are shown.

claims.statement: During the UP onset sequence the represented HD changes less rapidly than later in the UP state (diffusion coefficients, Mann-Whitney U test, U = 54, n = 16, p = 0.006).
claims.source: Figure 1K; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Following the DOWN state, the represented HD maintained a specific direction throughout the duration of the UP onset sequence (Figure 1I) and changed less rapidly than later in the UP state (Figure 1K).
claims.criterion: As the Methods (Isomap Projection and Decoding) give it. UP states longer than 500 ms; angles 0 to 150 ms (traveling) and 150 to 300 ms (control) after DU; cumulative circular variance from the first three bins; the diffusion coefficient is the mean numpy gradient of it between 35 and 150 ms. Per session, one coefficient per interval. Reproduced when traveling is lower than control by a two-sided Mann-Whitney U test at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: During NREM sleep, dorsal and ventral PoSub represent the same HD; the decoded angular difference is not different from that with shuffled cell depths.
claims.source: Figure S1J; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 1
claims.quote: during NREM sleep, dorsal and ventral PoSub consistently represented the same HD
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Bayesian decoding with pynapple decode_1d in 50 ms UP-state bins with at least 5 HD cells spiking in each half; per session, the mean absolute angular difference z-scored against 100 shuffles of cell depth. Reproduced when the two-sided one-sample Wilcoxon test against 0 gives p >= 0.05; the effect is reported either way. The paper has no code for Figure S1J. How the dorsal and ventral halves are split is not given; the equal-width depth split of Figure1H.py and the median split are both run. The legend z-scores "the difference between data and mean of the shuffled distribution" but does not say how the per-bin angular differences of a session are summarized; the mean and the median of the absolute circular difference are both run.

claims.statement: The rise in high gamma (70 to 150 Hz) power at UP onset travels along the DV axis, while its drop at the UD transition is synchronous.
claims.source: Figure 2B to 2F; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 3
claims.quote: gh traveled in the DV direction during the UP state onset, mirroring the wave observed in single unit activity (Figures 2B- 2F; one-sample Wilcoxon test; DU, W = 21, n = 16, p = 0.013; UD, W = 68, n = 16, p = 1)
claims.criterion: Per channel, LFP downsampled to 625 Hz, filtered 70 to 150 Hz (third-order Butterworth), smoothed with a 32 ms s.d. Gaussian, averaged around the event; UP onset delay is the time of maximal derivative (Methods, Peri-Event Time Histograms and Sequential Activation at UP onset). Per session, Kendall tau of delay against channel depth. The paper has no code for Figure 2 and leaves these details open, each run under the readings named. (1) How power is taken from the filtered signal is not given; the absolute value of its Hilbert transform and its square are both run. (2) The event; the Methods align to DU (DU-triggered average, +/- 1 s), the Figure 2D legend shows delta-peak-aligned power (delta peaks as in Methods, Delta peak detection); both are run. (3) The UD measure is not defined for the LFP; it is read as the time of maximal negative derivative around the DOWN start (or the delta peak). (4) The window in which the maximal slope is searched is not given; 0 to 150 ms after the event (as for units) and -250 to 250 ms are both run. Reproduced when, under all readings, DU coefficients differ from 0 (two-sided one-sample Wilcoxon, p < 0.05) and UD do not; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: For sessions with a significant delay-depth correlation, the speed of the traveling UP onset is similar from spikes and from LFP (6.72 +/- 4.08 against 9.89 +/- 5.51 mm/s, Mann-Whitney U = 58, n = 13 and 15, p = 0.072).
claims.source: Figure S2E; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 3
claims.quote: the speed of the traveling activity for significant sessions was similar when computed using either the LFP or spiking activity
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged by the paper's two-sided Mann-Whitney U test at p < 0.05; reproduced when it does not find a difference. Speed is the slope of the delay-depth relation (Figure S2E legend) in sessions whose Kendall correlation is significant; whether speed is the inverse of the regression slope of delay on depth or the slope of depth on delay is not given, and both are run. Tolerances are the reported s.d. The unit is printed "mm/s" in the text read, whose extraction also renders micro as "m" (as in "25 mm vertical separation"); mm/s fits delays of 5 to 100 ms over the PoSub DV extent, so the expected values are compared in mm/s; a match only after a factor of 1000 is reported as a match under the um/s reading.

claims.statement: At UP state onset ADN cells activate more synchronously than PoSub cells (s.d. of delays 10.38 +/- 5.74 ms against 15.54 +/- 5.42 ms), suggesting the PoSub sequence is generated locally.
claims.source: Figure S2F and S2G; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 4
claims.quote: At UP state onset, ADN cells activated more synchronously than in the PoSub (Figures S2F and S2G; standard deviation of delays, 10.38 ± 5.74 ms in ADN versus 15.54 ± 5.42 ms in PoSub
claims.criterion: As FigureS2G.py. Per session, onset delays as in fig5f-rsc-pmr-onset, PoSub EX units only and all ADN units (location adn), with the DOWN states detected from the ADN units as detectDOWNs_ADn.py does; the s.d. of delays per session; two-sided Mann-Whitney U test. detectDOWNs_ADn.py drops ADN DOWN states shorter than 50 ms, while the Methods (UP and DOWN state detection) give 30 ms for all detection; the Methods' 30 ms is the main result and the code's 50 ms is run as a variant. The Results and the legend give different U and p; either is accepted. Reproduced when ADN is lower at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Across halves of a session, the delays of PoSub units at UP state onset are more stable than their timing at the UD transition (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, W = 4, n = 16, p = 0.0002).
claims.source: Figure S1I legend; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Half-session correlation for UP state onset and the UD transition suggests that the UP state onset is overall more stable than the UD transition
claims.criterion: Per session, UP onset delays (DU) and UD times of EX units as in fig1g-dv-sequence-du, computed separately in two halves of the session; the correlation of each across units between halves; the DU and UD correlations compared over sessions by a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The paper has no code or Methods text for this panel. Open, each run under the readings named; how the session is halved (first against second half of the NREM DOWN states, or odd against even DOWN states) and which correlation is used (Pearson, as plotted against the unity line, or Kendall, the paper's default rank correlation). Reproduced when DU exceeds UD at p < 0.05 under all readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: UP onset delays of PoSub EX units are explained by DV position better than by NREM firing rate; per animal, the regression coefficients of delay on position exceed those on firing rate (Wilcoxon signed-rank, W = 19, n = 16, p = 0.009) and differ from 0 (one-sample Wilcoxon, W = 0, n = 16, p = 3.052e-5).
claims.source: Figure S1K and S1L legends; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Finally, these neuronal activation sequences were not accounted for by differences in neuronal firing rates
claims.criterion: Per animal, a linear regression of the UP onset delays of EX units (as in fig1g-dv-sequence-du) on DV position and NREM firing rate together (Figure S1L legend). The paper has no code or Methods text for this panel. Open, each run under the readings named; whether the predictors are z-scored before the fit (needed for the coefficients to be comparable) or used raw, and whether "better" compares absolute or signed coefficients. Reproduced when, under all readings, the position coefficients exceed the firing-rate coefficients by a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test at p < 0.05 and differ from 0 by a two-sided one-sample Wilcoxon test at p < 0.05; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Per session, the delay-depth correlation computed from units agrees with that computed from high gamma LFP power (Pearson R = 0.62, n = 16, p = 0.01).
claims.source: Figure S2D legend; Results, Neuronal activity at the DU transition travels along the PoSub DV axis and is locally generated, paragraph 3
claims.quote: The correlation coefficients between UP onset delay and depth for individual sessions were well correlated between LFP and spikes (Figure S2D)
claims.criterion: The per-session DU Kendall coefficients of fig1g-dv-sequence-du against those of fig2f-gamma-travels, under each reading of the latter; two-sided Pearson test. Reproduced when R is within tolerance and p < 0.05 under at least one reading and positive with p < 0.05 under all; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree on sign or significance.

claims.statement: In an adapting Wilson-Cowan array, gradients of excitability, recurrence or adaptation produce an inactivation sequence at the UD transition, not the observed activation sequence at DU only, over all parameter values tested.
claims.source: Figures 3B to 3D and S3B to S3D; Results, An Ih gradient can account for DV sequential activation at UP state onset, paragraph 2
claims.quote: we found that none of these parameter gradients were able to account for our primary observation... synchronous deactivation at the UD transition but sequential activation at UP state onset
claims.criterion: Run Figure3.m and FigureS3b.m to FigureS3d.m with the parameters of the Methods table (Parameters for AdWC model). Reproduced when, for each of the three gradients, the slope of threshold-crossing time against position is non-zero at UD in all parameter combinations swept, as the scripts compute it.

claims.statement: A gradient of an h current (Ih) in the model produces synchronous UD transitions and a DV activation sequence at DU, robustly over a range of parameters.
claims.source: Figure 3E, 3F and S3F; Results, An Ih gradient can account for DV sequential activation at UP state onset, paragraph 3
claims.quote: As a result, an Ih gradient led to synchronous UD and sequential activation at UP state onset at the DU transition, as observed in our recordings (Figure 3F). Importantly, this property of the network was robust to a wide range of parameters (Figure S3F).
claims.criterion: Run Figure3.m and FigureS3f.m with the Ih parameters of the Methods table. Reproduced when the DU slope is non-zero and the UD slope near zero in the main simulation and over the sweep, as the scripts compute and plot them. "Near zero" is not quantified in the paper; the slopes are reported.

claims.statement: Ex vivo, the Ih-mediated voltage sag of layer III PoSub EX cells decreases along the DV axis (Pearson R2 = 0.22, n = 59 cells from 11 mice, p = 0.0004), and the gradient is abolished by the HCN blocker ZD-7288 (R2 = 0.05, n = 19 cells from 8 mice, p = 0.36).
claims.source: Figure 4D; Results, An Ih gradient can account for DV sequential activation at UP state onset, paragraph 4
claims.quote: We found a gradient of decreasing sag along the DV axis (Figure 4D) that was sensitive to an HCN-channel blocker
claims.criterion: Sag from -500 pA steps as (peak minus steady state) over peak, averaged over at least 3 repetitions, against distance from the dorsal pole (Methods, Whole-cell patch clamp recordings). Reproduced when control R2 is within tolerance with a negative slope and p < 0.05, and ZD-7288 gives p >= 0.05. The ex vivo data are not deposited.

claims.statement: Resting potential, input resistance, membrane time constant, F-I slope and the fast time constant of sag do not vary with DV position in PoSub.
claims.source: Figure S4A to S4G; Results, An Ih gradient can account for DV sequential activation at UP state onset, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Critically, no other DV gradients in passive properties or excitability were found in PoSub cells (Figure S4).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged by the paper's two-sided Pearson tests at p < 0.05 on the control cells; reproduced when none is significant. The ex vivo data are not deposited.

claims.statement: A single unipolar 600-ns pulse at 15 kV/cm causes by far the strongest YP uptake in individual CHO cells, 126 +/- 14 a.u. at the end of the 10-min recording (n = 25), and sham exposure causes no gain in YP fluorescence.
claims.source: Results, 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 4
claims.quote: Sham-exposed cells showed no gain in YP fluorescence during the 10 min of observation. ... A single 600-ns pulse at 15 kV/cm caused by far the strongest YP uptake, reaching 126±14 a.u. (n=25) by the end of recording.
claims.criterion: Per cell, F minus F0 as Section 2.2 defines it (F0 the mean of the six images before the pulses), at the last image of the 600-s series (the paper's "end of recording"). The value holds when the mean over cells is within the paper's s.e. (14 a.u.) of 126. The sham claim holds when the sham group's mean F minus F0 at the end of recording does not differ from zero by a two-sided one-sample Student's t-test at p < 0.05 (the Methods' test, Section 2.4, applied to the one group), and is reported with its size.

claims.statement: Bipolar signals that start with the same pulse cause significantly weaker YP uptake than the single unipolar pulse (p < 0.001), reaching 20.8 +/- 2.0 a.u. for the 4-phase signal, 6.9 +/- 1.6 a.u. for the 8-phase signal and 25.4 +/- 2.8 a.u. for the 8-phase signal with 5-us delays; the 8-phase signal gives about 20-fold cancellation.
claims.source: Results, 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 4 legend
claims.quote: Bipolar signals started with exactly the same pulse (600 ns, 15 kV/cm) but caused significantly weaker effects (p<0.001). By the end of recording, YP signal reached only 20.8±2.0 a.u. for the 4-phasic signal; 6.9±1.6 a.u. for the 8-phasic signal; and 25.4±2.8 a.u. for the 8-phasic signal with 5-μs delays between phases. The impressive 20-fold bipolar cancellation achieved with the 8-phasic signal
claims.criterion: Values as in fig4-unipolar-strongest, each within the paper's s.e. The test is not named in Section 2.2 or the Fig. 4 legend; the only test the Methods name is the two-sided Student's t-test (Section 2.4), which is used here, comparing each bipolar group with the unipolar group at the last image (Welch's t-test is shown as a variant only). Reproduced when all three bipolar groups are below the unipolar group with p < 0.001 and the values are within tolerance. The ratio uses the group means. The "4-5-fold" cancellation of the other two signals (Section 3.4) is reported alongside.

claims.statement: Packet 2 applied 40 times from e1 enhances electroporation in the center of the array despite the weakening field, while the unipolar train control electroporates more strongly throughout and follows the field distribution; without rotation the region near e1 stays stronger than the center.
claims.source: Results, 3.2, paragraph 1; Figure 5A
claims.quote: The lack of cancellation caused a much stronger electroporation throughout the array, and the distribution of YP uptake expectedly followed the electric field strength distribution in Fig. 3C . In contrast, Packet 2 enhanced electroporation in the center of the array, despite gradual weakening of the electric field with distance from e1. However, the bipolar cancellation only partially offset the electric field weakening, and electroporation near e1 remained stronger than in the center.
claims.criterion: Along the e1 to e3 diagonal (Fig. 5A legend), dish means of ROI values. Three parts, each tested with the Methods' two-sided Student's t-test at p < 0.05 over dishes (n = 4 to 5). (1) "40 Trains" above "40 Packets" at the most peripheral ROI next to e1, at the center ROI and at the trough. (2) For "40 Packets", the center ROI above the trough, the trough being the ROI with the lowest mean between the center and e1 (the paper's "least affected area ... between the center and the electrodes", Section 3.3). (3) For "40 Packets", the ROI next to e1 above the center ROI. Reproduced when all three hold under the readings of the opening comment that apply (ROI count, center ROI, raw or LOESS); partially when two hold.

claims.statement: Rotating the first-energized electrode with Packet 2 (1Px40) smears the effect at the perimeter and emphasizes a remote effect in the center, while the same rotation of the unipolar train (1Tx40) leaves a void of electroporation in the center; the difference is clearest in fluorescence normalized to the most peripheral ROI.
claims.source: Results, 3.2, paragraph 1; Figure 5B and 5C
claims.quote: Rotation with Packet 2 “smeared” the electroporation effect at the perimeter and emphasized the remote effect in the center. This remote effect contrasted with a void of electroporation in the center when the pulse train was applied in the same manner instead of the packet.
claims.criterion: Both diagonals averaged (Fig. 5B legend), normalized to the most peripheral ROI (Fig. 5C). Reproduced when (1) the normalized center value of 1Px40 exceeds that of 1Tx40 and (2) for 1Px40 the center ROI exceeds the trough (the lowest ROI between center and periphery), each by the Methods' two-sided Student's t-test at p < 0.05 over dishes, and (3) for 1Tx40 the center shows a void. The paper does not define a void; readings, (a) the normalized center value of 1Tx40 is below 100% by the same test, (b) the center ROI is the lowest point of the 1Tx40 mean profile. Part (3) is judged under both, and blocked as methods_underspecified if they disagree. The paper gives no number for Fig. 5C, so no value is expected; the normalized center values of both treatments are reported. The readings of the opening comment for normalization and center ROI are each run.

claims.statement: Increasing the total number of rotated Packet 2 packets from 4 to 20 and 40 strongly increases YP uptake throughout the array, and the central peak is discernible for all three.
claims.source: Results, 3.3, paragraph 1; Figure 6A
claims.quote: Increasing the total number of applied packets from 4 to 20 and 40 profoundly enhanced the electroporative YP dye uptake throughout the electrode array ( Fig. 6A ). The peak of electroporation in the center was clearly discernable for all tested treatments.
claims.criterion: Dish means (n = 3 to 4) at the most peripheral ROI, the trough and the center ROI. Reproduced when, at all three positions, the means increase from 1Px4 to 5Px4 to 10Px4 and 10Px4 exceeds 1Px4 by the Methods' two-sided Student's t-test at p < 0.05, and for each treatment the center ROI exceeds the trough. Partially reproduced when the increase holds at one or two of the positions.
