claims.quote: Percent increase in transient amplitude for the largest versus smallest quintile of decelerations/accelerations: Vglut2 = 214%, Calb1 = 243%, Anxa1 = 206%. P values: Vglut2 = 0.01, Calb1 = 0.002, Anxa1 = 0.002 (two-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction).
claims.criterion: As AccDecSizeAnalysis.m does, accelerations and decelerations are reselected from the acceleration trace with their peaks, split per recording into quintiles of peak size, and averaged; the amplitude is the change from the trigger to the largest excursion within 1 s. The ratio is the mean over recordings for the largest quintile over that for the smallest; the test is a paired two-sided signed-rank test of the two quintiles, multiplied by 3. Reproduced when the three ratios are within tolerance with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when all three ratios exceed 100% with p < 0.05 but a ratio is outside tolerance, or when two of the three subtypes meet the full criterion.

claims.statement: Vglut2 and Calb1 axons respond to unexpected rewards (means 7.9 and 12.4 normalized dF/F s), as do DAT recordings (5.9).
claims.source: Figure 4d,g; Results, Subtypes show different responses to rewards and aversive stimuli, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Means (m) and P values for reward: Vglut2 mice = 7.9 normalized ΔF/F s ... Calb1 mice = 12.4, P = 0.001 ... DAT mice = 5.9
claims.criterion: Per recording, the mean over consumed rewards of the integral after minus before the reward (Methods windows; the code's windows as a variant). Two-sided signed-rank test against 0 per group, multiplied by 4. Reproduced when the three means are within tolerance and positive with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when the three are positive with p < 0.05 but a mean is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: Reward responses are almost entirely absent from Anxa1 axons (mean -0.5, P = 0.1, not significant).
claims.source: Figure 4d,g; Results, Subtypes show different responses to rewards and aversive stimuli, paragraph 2
claims.quote: unexpected reward responses were almost entirely absent from Anxa1+ axons (Fig. 4c–e,g; integral of response: mean = −0.5, P = 0.1, NS)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of the per-recording reward responses against 0, multiplied by 4. Reproduced when p >= 0.05, not reproduced when p < 0.05. The mean, the code-window variant and the fraction of recordings with a positive response are reported either way.

claims.statement: Air puffs evoke increases in Vglut2 (15.8), Calb1 (5.3) and DAT (5.3) axons and a decrease in Anxa1 axons (-3.7).
claims.source: Figure 4f,g; Results, Subtypes show different responses to rewards and aversive stimuli, paragraphs 1 and 2
claims.quote: Means (m) and P values for air puff: Vglut2 mice = 15.8 ... Calb1 mice = 5.3, P = 0.007, Anxa1 mice = −3.7 ... DAT mice = 5.3, P = 0.02 (two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction)
claims.criterion: As for rewards, over all air puffs. Reproduced when the four means are within tolerance and each differs from 0 in the stated direction with p < 0.05 (signed-rank test multiplied by 4); partially reproduced when the four directions are significant but a mean is outside tolerance, or when three of the four groups meet the full criterion.

claims.statement: Vglut2 axons respond more to air puffs than to rewards, and Calb1 axons more to rewards than to air puffs.
claims.source: Figure 4h; Results, Subtypes show different responses to rewards and aversive stimuli, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Vglut2+ axons displayed larger responses to air puffs than reward, whereas Calb1+ axons displayed larger responses to rewards than air puffs (Fig. 4h).
claims.criterion: Per recording with both responses, a paired two-sided signed-rank test of reward against air puff responses, multiplied by 4, as the code does. Reproduced when Vglut2 air puff > reward and Calb1 reward > air puff, both with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when one holds.

claims.statement: Calb1 axons respond more to large than to small rewards (mean difference 3.9, P = 9e-3), as do DAT recordings (1.9, P = 8e-5), while Vglut2 (0.9, P = 0.6) and Anxa1 (0.04, P = 1) do not.
claims.source: Figure 4i; Results, Subtypes show different responses to rewards and aversive stimuli, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Mean difference (m) and P values: Vglut2 mice = 0.9 normalized ΔF/F s, P = 0.6 (NS); Calb1 mice = 3.9 ... Anxa1 mice = 0.04, P = 1 (NS); DAT mice = 1.9
claims.criterion: Per recording with at least 3 small and 3 large rewards, paired two-sided signed-rank test of large against small, multiplied by 4. The Vglut2 and Anxa1 parts are claims of absence judged on that test. Reproduced when Calb1 and DAT are larger for large rewards with p < 0.05, Vglut2 and Anxa1 have p >= 0.05, and the Calb1 and DAT differences are within tolerance; partially reproduced when Calb1 is significantly larger for large rewards but another part fails; not reproduced when Calb1 is not.

claims.statement: Reward responses of Vglut2 and Calb1 axons are the same for rewards delivered at rest as for the others (P = 1 for both), so the reward signal is not a movement response.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 8e,f; Results, Subtypes show different responses to rewards and aversive stimuli, paragraph 1
claims.quote: the amplitude of the reward signals was the same at rest (Extended Data Fig. 8e,f; P = 1 (not significant (NS)) for both Vglut2+ and Calb1+, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Bonferroni correction)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a paired two-sided signed-rank test of the responses to rewards at rest against rewards not at rest (each with at least 3 events), multiplied by 4. Reproduced when Vglut2 and Calb1 both have p >= 0.05, not reproduced when either has p < 0.05. Anxa1 and DAT are reported.

claims.statement: Unsupervised k-means clustering on locomotion (PC1, PC2 scores), reward and air puff responses assigns recordings to clusters that match the genetic subtypes with 91% accuracy (14/16 Vglut2, 10/11 Calb1, 15/16 Anxa1).
claims.source: Figure 6c; Results, Dopamine neuron functions differentially map onto genetic subtypes, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Unsupervised k-means classification distinguished subtypes based on locomotion (PC1 and PC2 scores), reward and air puff responses, with total accuracy of 91% ... 14/16 Vglut2, 10/11 Calb1 and 15/16 Anxa1 recordings correctly classified
claims.criterion: Recordings that pass both the locomotion and the stimulus selection with reward and air puff responses; the four features z-scored; k-means with 3 clusters, k-means++ starts and one start, as MATLAB's default; each subtype is matched to the median cluster label of its recordings, as the code does. The code's random seed cannot be repeated, so the result is the median accuracy over 100 seeds. Reproduced when it is within tolerance, partially reproduced when it is above 66% (twice chance), not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Within genetic subtypes, simultaneously recorded SNc somas and striatal axons are highly correlated (mean peak cross-correlation 0.65 Vglut2, 0.67 Calb1, 0.58 Anxa1), more than in DAT recordings (0.37); P = 3e-4, 3e-3, 3e-4.
claims.source: Figure 7e,f; Results, Axons track somatic signaling within subtypes, paragraph 4
claims.quote: On average, the cross-correlation between soma and axon ΔF/F recordings was significantly higher compared to DAT+ recordings (Fig. 7e,f; mean = 0.65 for Vglut2+, 0.67 for Calb1+ and 0.58 for Anxa1+, compared to 0.37 for DAT
claims.criterion: Dual recordings with one SNc and one striatal fiber, both with signal-to-noise ratio above 10, 405/470 cross-correlation peak below 0.12 and no artifact exclusion, as the code selects them. Peak of the smoothed cross-correlation over 1 s of lags. Two-sided rank-sum tests of each subtype against DAT, multiplied by 3 (the legend states Bonferroni; the code prints uncorrected values, also shown). Reproduced when the four means are within tolerance and each subtype exceeds DAT with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when each subtype mean exceeds DAT but a test or a tolerance fails.

claims.statement: Like their axons, Vglut2 and Calb1 somas in SNc respond to rewards and air puffs, while reward responses are largely undetectable in Anxa1 somas.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 9a-c; Results, Axons track somatic signaling within subtypes, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Indeed, just as in the axonal recordings, Calb1+ and Vglut2+ somas responded to rewards and air puffs, whereas reward responses were largely undetectable in Anxa1+ somas (Extended Data Fig. 9a–f).
claims.criterion: SNc recordings selected as for the striatum (stimulus selection with SNc fibers); responses and tests as in fig4g-reward-response. Reproduced when Vglut2 and Calb1 reward and air puff responses are positive with p < 0.05 (x4) and the Anxa1 reward test gives p >= 0.05; partially reproduced when three of these five parts hold. Counts are reported against the legend (reward 25, 10, 23, 39; air puff 25, 10, 25, 47 for Vglut2, Calb1, Anxa1, DAT).

claims.statement: The striatal PCs explain most of the variance of the SNc cross-correlations, 77.6% (PC1 52.4%, PC2 25.2%).
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 9k legend; Methods, Analysis of signaling during locomotion, paragraph 16
claims.quote: Striatal PCs explain 77.6% of SNc variance (52.4% PC1, 25.2% PC2).
claims.criterion: SNc recordings selected by the locomotion criteria; their cross-correlations projected on the striatal PCs, with the uncentered variance as the code computes it. The legend gives PC1 52.4% and PC2 25.2%, the Methods 53.2% and 24.3%; both readings are listed, and the claim is reproduced when the total and both components are within 10% of one reading, partially reproduced when only the total is.

claims.statement: Aldh1a1 axons are heterogeneous; dorsal recordings are acceleration-correlated (Type 1) and more ventral ones deceleration-correlated (Type 2).
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 1h; Results, opening paragraph 2 (before the first subsection)
claims.quote: Distribution of locomotion response (integral of the cross-correlation at positive lags) along the dorso-ventral axis of the striatum ... showing how in Aldh1a1 dorsal recordings show acceleration correlation (Type 1) while more ventral recordings show deceleration correlation (Type 2).
claims.criterion: For Aldh1a1 recordings in the locomotion selection, the integral of the cross-correlation over lags 0 to 1 s against fiber depth. The paper gives no test; chosen here, a Spearman correlation below 0 with p < 0.05. Reproduced when it holds, and the mean integral is positive above 2.5 mm depth and negative below 3 mm; partially reproduced when only the correlation holds.

claims.statement: In Aldh1a1 recordings, larger reward responses go with deceleration-correlated signaling, and small or negative reward responses with acceleration-correlated signaling.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 1i; Results, opening paragraph 2 (before the first subsection)
claims.quote: Relationship between reward response and locomotion response for each recording of each subtype, showing how in Aldh1a1 larger reward responses correspond with deceleration correlation (Type 2), while small or negative reward responses correspond with acceleration correlation (Type 1).
claims.criterion: Aldh1a1 recordings with a reward response and a cross-correlation (both selections), reward response against the cross-correlation integral over 0 to 1 s. The paper gives no test; chosen here, a Spearman correlation below 0 with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Where Calb1 and Anxa1 axons overlap in striatum, Calb1 recordings remain deceleration-correlated and Anxa1 recordings acceleration-correlated (Calb1 4 mice, 5 recordings; Anxa1 5 mice, 16 recordings).
claims.source: Figure 3a; Results, Genetic subtypes show different signaling patterns during locomotion, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Comparison of locomotion response (cross-correlation between ΔF/F and acceleration) for Calb1 and Anxa1 recordings only from a region of striatum where their axons overlap ... Calb1 mice = 4, n = 5 recordings; Anxa1 mice = 5, n = 16 recordings.
claims.criterion: Recordings of the locomotion selection within 0.5 mm (in the coronal plane) of the code's two circle centres, converted from its image pixels to mm with its own scale and offsets; (ML 1.51, DV 3.50) at AP +0.86 and (ML 1.84, DV 3.51) at AP +0.50. The paper gives no test; chosen here, the cross-correlation integral over 0 to 1 s is negative on average for Calb1 and positive for Anxa1, and a two-sided rank-sum test between them gives p < 0.05. Counts are reported against the legend.

claims.statement: Where Calb1 and Anxa1 axons overlap, Calb1 recordings respond to rewards and Anxa1 recordings do not, and Anxa1 recordings decrease to air puffs (Calb1 4 mice, 9 recordings; Anxa1 5 mice, 13 for rewards, 17 for air puffs).
claims.source: Figure 4l; Results, Subtypes show different responses to rewards and aversive stimuli, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Notably, these differences persist even in regions where axons from different subtypes may overlap (Fig. 4l), indicating that they were intrinsic to each subtype and not simply defined by striatal projection location.
claims.criterion: The same region as fig3a-overlap-locomotion, recordings of the stimulus selection. The paper gives no test; chosen here, Calb1 reward responses exceed Anxa1 ones by a two-sided rank-sum test at p < 0.05, the Calb1 mean reward response is positive and the Anxa1 mean air puff response negative. Partially reproduced when the test holds but a sign does not.

claims.statement: Single-nucleus RNA-seq of dopamine neurons from five DAT-Cre, Sun1-GFP mice yields 12,065 nuclei after quality control, with a mean of 3,435 UMIs and 1,683 genes per nucleus.
claims.source: Methods, Analysis of snRNA-seq data, paragraph 1; Figure 1a,b
claims.quote: nuclei with fewer than 500 unique features were removed from each dataset ... In total, the integration resulted in a final dataset of 12,065 nuclei, with a mean UMI count of 3,435 and a mean of 1,683 features.
claims.criterion: Nuclei with 500 or more detected genes, as the Methods filter, from the two samples' count matrices. Reproduced when the three values are within tolerance, partially reproduced when the count is and a mean is not.

claims.statement: Anxa1 expression is limited to a subset of Aldh1a1-expressing dopamine neurons.
claims.source: Figure 1c; Extended Data Figure 2b; Results, Anxa1+, a new subtype within Aldh1a1+, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Expression of Aldh1a1 and Anxa1, the latter of which is expressed only within a subset of Aldh1a1-expressing neurons.
claims.criterion: Without clustering, from raw counts of the nuclei that pass quality control, a gene is detected with one or more UMI. Reproduced when (i) Anxa1 and Aldh1a1 detection are associated (Fisher exact test, odds ratio above 1, p < 0.05), (ii) more than half of the Anxa1-detected nuclei have Aldh1a1 detected and (iii) fewer than half of the Aldh1a1-detected nuclei have Anxa1 detected; partially reproduced when (i) and (iii) hold but not (ii).

claims.statement: Clustering of the snRNA-seq nuclei gives 15 clusters; cluster 4 is enriched for Anxa1 (FDR-adjusted P = 9.4e-118) within the Aldh1a1 clusters, and clusters 9 and 11 are the Vglut2 and Calb1 subtypes.
claims.source: Figure 1b-d; Extended Data Figures 3 and 4; Results, Anxa1+, a new subtype within Aldh1a1+, paragraph 2
claims.quote: This approach resulted in the unbiased identification of 15 clusters ... we infer that clusters 9 and 11 represent the SNc Vglut2+ and Calb1+ subtypes ... Cluster 4 was, again, significantly enriched for Anxa1 expression

claims.statement: Integrating four published single-cell datasets gives eight clusters, one of them defined by co-expression of Aldh1a1 and Anxa1.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 2; Results, Anxa1+, a new subtype within Aldh1a1+, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We observed eight clusters, one of which was defined by co-expression of Aldh1a1 and Anxa1 (Extended Data Fig. 2a).

claims.statement: With packets at the maximum rate, heating followed the field and was largest near the electrodes; after 2 bursts it was confined to about 2 mm next to the electrodes and could exceed 30 C but not 44 C; after 6 bursts it spread further, exceeding 30 C even near the centre, yet never exceeded 44 C.
claims.source: Methods 2.3, paragraph 1; Figure 2
claims.quote: With 2 bursts ( Fig. 2A ), heating was restricted to an approximately 2-mm zone next to electrodes, where it could reach over 30 °C but did not exceed 44 °C. With 6 bursts ( Fig. 2B ), heating was more widespread ... Temperature could exceed 30 °C even near the center of the array, but did not exceed 44 °C even near the electrodes.
claims.criterion: Film images at the end of the 2nd and 6th burst (Methods 2.3). Temperature classes from the calibrated colour transitions, black to red, green, blue and back to black at 25, 26, 30 and 44 C (Methods 2.3). The hue limits of the colours are not given; readings (a) red below 45, green 75 to 165, blue 180 to 270 degrees of hue, (b) red below 30, green 90 to 150, blue 195 to 255 degrees, with black any pixel of value below 0.2 (standard choices). Above 30 C is blue; above 44 C is black after blue, that is a dark pixel inside a blue region. "Near the center" is not given as a distance; readings (a) within 1 mm, (b) within 2 mm of the centre. Reproduced when, under every reading, the 2-burst image has blue pixels only within 2.2 mm of an electrode edge ("approximately 2-mm", widened by 10%), the 6-burst image has blue pixels near the centre, and neither image has a dark pixel enclosed by blue outside the electrode footprints. Blocked when the dataset holds no film images.

claims.statement: Every CANCAN protocol enhanced electroporation at the array centre, while in the control (single unipolar pulse per packet) YP uptake decreased gradually toward the centre.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 3A
claims.quote: All CANCAN protocols visibly enhanced electroporation at the center of the array, in contrast to its gradual decrease toward the center in the control ( Fig. 3A ).
claims.criterion: Set S1, F1 to F3, O1, O2. For each CANCAN rate, the mean diagonal profile has its maximum at x = 0 (reading (b) of O1 allows the ROI nearest 0); for the control, the mean at x = 0 is below the means at 6 and 7 mm by a gap larger than the error bars (F8). Reproduced when both hold for every rate under every reading.

claims.statement: Raising the packet rate from 1 Hz to 0.2 MHz suppressed electroporation better both near the electrodes (diagonal profile) and at the perimeter between electrodes (profile parallel to the sides).
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 3B, 3C
claims.quote: The most conspicuous effect of increasing the packet rate from 1 Hz to 0.208333 MHz (abbreviated to 0.2 MHz below and in figure legends) was better suppression of electroporation both near electrodes ( Fig. 3B ) and at the perimeter between electrodes ( Fig. 3C ).
claims.criterion: Set S1, F1 to F3, F8, O1, O2. Near electrodes is YP at 6 and 7 mm on the diagonals. The perimeter is not given as a distance; readings (a) the outermost ROIs of the parallel profile, (b) the mean of the parallel ROIs at 4 mm or more from the centre. Reproduced when, under every reading, mean YP at 0.2 MHz is below that at 1 Hz with a gap larger than the error bars (F8) at 6 mm, at 7 mm and at the perimeter; a two-sided t test at each is reported. Blocked for the perimeter part when the dataset has no parallel measurements.

claims.statement: The decline of YP emission from the centre was bell-shaped and fitted a Lorentzian function over -4 to 4 mm nearly perfectly (R > 0.9, p < 0.001) for every packet rate.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 3; Figure 3B, 3C legend; Methods 2.5
claims.quote: The fit correlation with data in the −4 to 4 mm radius was nearly perfect (R>0.9, p<0.001).
claims.criterion: Set S1, F1 to F4, F6, O1, O2. For each CANCAN rate, the Lorentzian (F4) is fitted to the mean diagonal profile over -4 to 4 mm and to the parallel profile where present. R is the Pearson correlation of fitted and measured values over that range, and p its test. Reproduced when R exceeds 0.9 with p < 0.001 for every rate and profile under every reading; the threshold 0.9 is the paper's bound, so the tolerance is zero.

claims.statement: Beyond the fitted range, the data deviated from the Lorentzian fit less as the packet rate increased.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 3; Figure 3B, 3C
claims.quote: The deviation of experimental data from the fits at larger distances from the center diminished with increasing the packet repetition rate, highlighting better suppression of the off-target electroporation.
claims.criterion: Set S1, fits of fig3-lorentzian-profile extended to all distances (Figure 3B legend, the plots were extended to the x-axis limits). The deviation is the mean of (data - fit) over ROIs beyond 4 mm. The paper does not say in which units; readings (a) a.u., (b) percent of the fitted peak a. Reproduced when, under every reading, the deviation is largest at 1 Hz and smallest at 0.2 MHz, and its Spearman correlation with rate over the tested rates is negative (a standard measure of a monotone trend, as the paper names none).

claims.statement: YP uptake at the array centre showed no significant effect of packet rate.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 4; Figure 4B
claims.quote: YP intensity in the center showed no significant effect of the packet rate ( t -test with Bonferroni correction, Fig. 4B ).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. Set S1, F1 to F3, O2; per experiment the background-subtracted YP at x = 0. Two-sided Student's t tests with Bonferroni correction (F7). The set of comparisons is not given; readings (a) each rate against 1 Hz (as in Figure 4C), (b) all pairs of rates. Reproduced when no corrected comparison has p < 0.05; not reproduced when any does. Group means and the largest ratio between rates are reported either way.

claims.statement: In contrast to the centre, YP uptake at 6 and 7 mm from the centre (1.65 and 0.65 mm from the electrodes) declined steeply as the packet rate increased.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 4; Figure 4B
claims.quote: It contrasted with a steep, packet rate-dependent decline of YP uptake at 6 and 7 mm from the center (i.e., 1.65 and 0.65 mm from electrodes).
claims.criterion: Set S1, F1 to F3, O2. At 6 mm and at 7 mm, a power function YP = c rate^k is fitted to YP against packet rate (Figure 4B legend, best fits using power function), by least squares. Whether the fit uses the plotted means or the individual experiments is not given; readings (a) group means, (b) per-experiment values. Reproduced when, under every reading, k < 0 at both distances and mean YP at 0.2 MHz is below that at 1 Hz with a gap larger than the error bars (F8) at both.

claims.statement: At 0.2 MHz, YP uptake at the centre was 40 times that near the electrodes, despite the field there being about 4 times weaker (3.3 against about 14 kV/cm).
claims.source: Results 3.1, the sentences on the ratio of YP uptake in the center and near electrodes; Figure 4B; Abstract
claims.quote: Now, by increasing the packet repetition rate to 0.2 MHz, we achieved a 40-fold difference ( Fig. 4B ), despite using a bigger array with larger reduction of the electric field from electrodes to the center.
claims.criterion: Set S1 at 0.2 MHz, F1 to F3, F9, O2, O5. The ratio of group-mean background-subtracted YP at x = 0 to that at the near-electrode distance. Reproduced when the ratio is within 36 to 44 under one reading of O5 and O2 (the paper names one number for a choice it leaves open).

claims.statement: Higher packet rates focused electroporation into a smaller spot; the FWHM fell from about 4 mm at 1 Hz to about 2 mm at 1 kHz, 10 kHz and 0.2 MHz (p = 0.03, 0.02 and 0.09 against 1 Hz), and could be under 15% of the inter-electrode gap.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraphs 5 and 6; Figure 4C
claims.quote: FWHM decreased from ~4 mm at 1 Hz to ~2 mm at 1 kHz, 10 kHz, and 0.2 MHz packet rates (p = 0.03; 0.02, and 0.09, respectively; t -test with Bonferroni correction).
claims.criterion: Set S1, F1 to F7, F10, O1, O2. Per experiment, the Lorentzian fitted over -4 to 4 mm gives b; FWHM per rate is the mean over experiments. Two-sided t tests of each rate against 1 Hz, Bonferroni over the rates compared with 1 Hz. Reproduced when the four means are within tolerance, 1 kHz and 10 kHz differ from 1 Hz at corrected p < 0.05 (the legend marks them with *p<0.05), and at least one rate has mean FWHM below 15% of 15.3 mm (2.3 mm). Partially reproduced when the tests hold but a mean is outside tolerance. The 0.2 MHz comparison (p = 0.09) is reported, not required.

claims.statement: FWHM fell logarithmically with packet rate from 1 Hz to 10 kHz (R = 0.77, p < 0.001; n = 15), with no further narrowing from 10 kHz to 0.2 MHz.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 5; Figure 4C legend
claims.quote: FWHM decrease followed the logarithmic dependence from 1 Hz to 10 kHz (correlation coefficient R = 0.77, p<0.001), but there was no further focality increase when the packet rate increased from 10 kHz to 0.2 MHz.
claims.criterion: Per-experiment FWHM from fig4c-fwhm-falls-with-rate, rates 1 Hz to 10 kHz, 0.2 MHz left out (Figure 4C legend). FWHM = m log(rate) + c by least squares; R is the absolute Pearson correlation of FWHM with log rate; the slope is tested by a two-sided t test. Reproduced when R is within tolerance, the slope is negative with p < 0.001, and mean FWHM at 0.2 MHz is not below that at 10 kHz by a gap larger than the error bars (F8). Partially reproduced when the slope is negative with p < 0.05 but R or p falls short.

claims.statement: Since with MHz-CANCAN there was practically no YP staining near electrodes (a finding the text cites to Figure 4), the only clear effect of raising the electrodes 1 or 2 mm above the monolayer was a weakening of electroporation in the central spot.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 1; Figure 5A, 5B
claims.quote: With MHz-CANCAN (CT26 cells, 2 bursts (x4), Fig. 4 ), there was practically no YP staining near electrodes to start with, so the only clear effect of raising electrodes was the weakening of electroporation in the central spot.
claims.criterion: Set S2, F1 to F3, F8, O2. YP in percent of the mean 0-mm peak (Figure 5B legend). The centre is x = 0. Reproduced when mean centre YP at 1 mm and at 2 mm elevation are each below 0 mm with a gap larger than the error bars (F8). Two-sided t tests are reported. The near-electrode part is the Figure 4 finding and is judged by fig4b-40-fold-ratio; mean YP at 6 and 7 mm at each elevation is reported.

claims.statement: The central spot of YP staining (electroporation) was only slightly larger than the spot of Pr staining (cell killing).
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 1; Figure 5A, 5B
claims.quote: Somewhat unexpectedly, the central spot of YP staining (electroporation) was just slightly larger than the spot of Pr staining (cell killing; Fig 5A and B ).
claims.criterion: Set S2, each elevation, F1 to F4, F6, O2. FWHM of the Lorentzian fit to mean YP and of the Gaussian fit to mean Pr over -5 to 5 mm (Figure 5B legend); the Gaussian FWHM is 2.4 sigma as the Methods give it, and 2.355 sigma as a variant. The paper bounds "slightly" by no number; readings (a) YP FWHM / Pr FWHM between 1 and 1.25, (b) between 1 and 1.5. Reproduced when the ratio falls in the range under every reading at 0 mm elevation (the panel the text cites first); other elevations are reported.

claims.statement: Pr intensity declined from the peak as a Gaussian and YP as a Lorentzian; for the 0-mm data (the left panel of Figure 5B, read as the 0-mm panel) the R2 was 0.92 (Lorentzian) against 0.96 (Gaussian) for Pr, and 0.98 against 0.95 for YP, fitted from -5 to 5 mm with p < 0.0001.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 2; Figure 5B
claims.quote: For Pr data in the left panel of Fig. 5B , the coefficient of determination increased from 0.92 for Lorentzian fit to 0.96 for Gaussian fit. YP data showed the opposite trend, with the coefficients of 0.98 and 0.95 for Lorentzian and Gaussian fits, respectively (for all these fits, the fitted region was from −5 to 5 mm, p<0.0001).
claims.criterion: Set S2, 0-mm elevation. The left panel of Figure 5B is not named; it is read as the 0-mm panel, the one whose peak is 100% (legend). Mean profiles in percent, F4 fits over -5 to 5 mm, O1, O2. R2 is 1 - SSres / SStot over the fitted points. Reproduced when every R2 is within tolerance and the ordering holds (Gaussian above Lorentzian for Pr, Lorentzian above Gaussian for YP) under every reading; partially when the values are within tolerance but an ordering fails.

claims.statement: In the central spot cells showed bright nuclear YP staining, indicating irreversible damage, while farther out reversibly electroporated cells were weakly stained with less contrast between nucleus and cytoplasm; cells inside the electrode footprint were unstained though present (Hoechst).
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 1; Figure 5C
claims.quote: Indeed, a closer examination of the central spot confirmed bright YP staining of cell nuclei ( Fig. 5C , zone 1), which is indicative of the irreversible membrane damage and cell death. Reversible electroporation is distinguished by a much weaker YP staining and smaller difference in staining of the nucleus and cytoplasm, such as in zones 2 and 3 in Fig. 5C .
claims.criterion: Set S2 at 0 mm. Zone locations are shown only in Figure 5A, not seen. Zone 3 straddles an electrode wall (Results 3.2, its right portion lies inside the footprint; Figure 5C legend, dotted lines mark the wall), so its outside part is the band within 0.5 mm outside a wall, and the footprint is inside the wall. Zone 1 is in the central spot and zone 2 is not placed by the text; readings, zone 1 within 1 mm of the centre, zone 2 (a) 2 to 4 mm, (b) 3 to 5 mm from the centre along a diagonal. Nuclei are Hoechst-positive objects (Otsu threshold, a standard choice); the cytoplasm is a ring around each nucleus, readings (a) 2 to 4 um, (b) 4 to 8 um. Reproduced when, under every reading, median nuclear YP in zone 1 exceeds that in zones 2 and 3, the median nucleus to cytoplasm YP ratio is higher in zone 1, footprint YP is below zones 2 and 3, and the footprint has Hoechst-positive nuclei. Blocked when the dataset lacks full-resolution Hoechst and YP images of these wells.

claims.statement: The central YP peak was highest for 900-ns pulses, but not significantly different from 300- or 600-ns pulses.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 6B
claims.quote: The central peak of YP uptake was higher for 900-ns pulses, but the difference from the other two pulse durations was not statistically significant (CT26 cells, 2 bursts (x4), Fig. 6B ).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. Set S3, F1 to F3, O2; per experiment YP at x = 0. Two-sided t tests of 900 ns against 300 ns and against 600 ns, Bonferroni over the two (F7). The paper does not say whether Bonferroni covers these two comparisons or all three pairs; both are run. Reproduced when the 900-ns mean is the highest and no corrected p is below 0.05; not reproduced when one is. Effect sizes are reported.

claims.statement: Normalized to the central peak, the sideways decline of YP was similar for the three pulse durations.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 6C
claims.quote: When the peak YP emission was taken as 100%, its decline sideways was similar for the three tested pulse durations ( Fig. 6C ).
claims.criterion: Set S3, F1 to F3, O1, O2, each profile in percent of its value at x = 0 (Methods 2.5; Figure 6C legend, the same data normalized to the peak). Whether each experiment or each mean is normalized is not given; readings (a) each experiment, then mean +/- s.e., (b) the mean profile, with s.e. scaled by the same factor. Judged by the paper's error-bar rule (F8). Reproduced when, under every reading, no distance has two durations whose means differ by a gap larger than the error bars.

claims.statement: Longer pulses focused electroporation into a smaller spot; the FWHM fell with pulse duration (slope p = 0.003), 600- and 900-ns pulses differed from 300 ns, and 900-ns packets gave FWHM 1.7 +/- 0.08 mm, 11.1 +/- 0.6% of the gap between electrodes.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 6D legend
claims.quote: However, a more detailed analysis based on fitting of individual experiments (as described in 3.1 ) revealed significant sharpening of the central peak when packets were built from 600- and 900-ns pulses ( Fig. 6D ). The slope coefficient of the logarithmic fit of the data was different from zero at p = 0.003 (one sample, 2-sided t -test). 900-ns pulse packets reduced FWHM to 1.7 ± 0.08 mm, that was 11.1 ± 0.6% of the gap between electrodes.
claims.criterion: Set S3, F1 to F5, F7, F10, O1 to O4. Per-experiment Lorentzian FWHM. The trend's form is open, as the text says "logarithmic fit" and the legend "best linear fit"; readings (a) FWHM against duration, (b) FWHM against log duration, each slope tested by a two-sided t test. Two-sided t tests of 600 ns and 900 ns against 300 ns, Bonferroni over the two. Reproduced when, under every reading, the slope is negative with p < 0.05, both comparisons have corrected p < 0.05 and the 900-ns FWHM is within tolerance (the paper's s.e.). Partially reproduced when the slope holds but a comparison or the value fails.

claims.statement: The central YP peak grew linearly with the number of bursts in both CT26 and CHO cells (slope p < 0.001), except that it saturated after 6 bursts (x4) in CT26 cells.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 7B, 7E legend
claims.quote: Increasing the number of bursts increased the amplitude of the central peak of YP uptake in both CT26 and CHO cells ( Fig 7A and D ). The increase was linear in both cell lines, except when it reached saturation after 6 bursts (x4) in CT26 cells ( Fig. 7B and E ).
claims.criterion: Set S4, F1 to F3, F7, O2, O4. Per experiment YP at x = 0 against the number of bursts; linear least squares, the CT26 6-burst point left out (Figure 7B legend). The paper gives no test of saturation; it is read from the legend's 95% confidence band (a choice made here, not the paper's), that the CT26 6-burst mean lies below the band of the fit extrapolated to 6 bursts. Reproduced when both slopes are positive with p < 0.001 and the saturation holds; partially when a slope is positive with p < 0.05 only, or saturation fails.

claims.statement: The FWHM of the central peak increased in proportion to the number of bursts in CT26 cells (slope p < 0.001) but not in CHO cells (p = 0.44).
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 7C, 7F legend
claims.quote: Concurrently, FWHM of the central peak increased proportionally to the burst number in CT26 cells, but not in CHO cells ( Fig. 7C and F ).
claims.criterion: Set S4, F1 to F5, F7, O1 to O4. Per-experiment Lorentzian FWHM against burst number, linear least squares, slope tested two-sided. CHO 1-burst wells are left out (Figure 7 legend, too small to measure FWHM). Whether the CT26 6-burst point enters the FWHM fit is not said (the legend excludes it only from 7B); readings (a) included, (b) excluded. Reproduced when, under every reading, the CT26 slope is positive with p < 0.001 and the CHO slope has p >= 0.05 (a claim of absence on the paper's test). Partially when the CT26 slope is positive with p < 0.05 only.

claims.statement: One burst (x4) in CT26 cells gave the sharpest peak of the study, FWHM 1.1 +/- 0.1 mm, 7.3% of the inter-electrode gap and 2.3% of the array area, with YP near the electrodes 40 to 50 times smaller than at the centre.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 3; Figure 7A, 7C
claims.quote: That being said, 1 burst (x4) in CT26 cells produced the sharpest peak of electroporation seen in this study ... at FWHM of 1.1 ± 0.1 mm, it occupied just 7.3% of the inter-electrode gap and 2.3% of the electrode array area. Off-target effects, characterized by YP emission near electrodes, were 40–50 times smaller than at the remote target.
claims.criterion: Set S4, CT26 1-burst wells, FWHM as in fig7cf-fwhm-bursts with every reading of O3. The ratio uses group means at x = 0 and near the electrodes (O5); the reported range 40 to 50 widened by 10% of each bound gives 36 to 55, coded as 45.5 +/- 9.5. The area percentage is not tested, as the paper does not say how it was computed from the FWHM. Reproduced when the FWHM is within the paper's s.e. and is the smallest mean FWHM of any group in sets S1 to S4 ("seen in this study"), the percent is within tolerance, and the ratio is within 36 to 55, under one reading of O3 and O5 (the paper names one value for choices it leaves open).

claims.statement: Neurons were selected for APs peaking above 5% dF and lasting about 10 ms; typical APs were 11.3% dF high and 8 ms long, excluding the afterhyperpolarization (mean of 22).
claims.source: Methods, Recording of the optical APs and data analyses
claims.quote: we selected neurons whose APs peaked at a more than 5% Δ F and lasted about 10 ms (typical values ... 11.3% ± 0.9% Δ F and 8 ± 0.7 ms duration, excluding afterhyperpolarization; mean ± SEM, n = 22)
claims.criterion: F1 to F3, O1 to O3, FluoVolt sessions with APs. Per neuron, the mean peak dF and duration of its APs, then the mean over neurons. Which APs are measured is not given; readings (a) every AP, (b) the first AP of each session. The duration measure is not given; readings (a) width at half height, (b) time from the rise to the first return to F0 (leaving out the afterhyperpolarization). Reproduced when both means are within the paper's SEM under every reading.

claims.statement: Unmodulated 250-ms sine waves at 2 and 20 kHz excited every neuron tested; near threshold isolated APs came 100 to 200 ms after onset, and stronger fields shortened the delay and evoked sustained firing whose maximum rate rose linearly to a ceiling of 60 to 90 Hz.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 2; Figures 1A to 1C and inset
claims.quote: Pure sine waves at 2 and even 20 kHz excited 100% of neurons ... at near-threshold electric field strengths, isolated APs emerged with a delay of 100–200 ms after the sine wave onset ... Increasing the field strength reduced this delay and evoked sustained firing ... The maximum firing rate increased linearly until reaching a ceiling of 60–90 Hz
claims.criterion: F1 to F5, O1 to O3, FluoVolt sessions with unmodulated waves. A neuron's threshold is its lowest field with at least one AP (F5). Reproduced when, under every reading, at least 90% of neurons are excited at each frequency, the median first-AP latency at threshold lies within 90 to 220 ms (100 to 200 ms widened by 10% of each bound), latency falls with field (Spearman rho below 0 over a neuron's sessions with APs, in most neurons; the paper gives no measure, so Spearman and "most" are standard choices), and the median over neurons of the highest maximum firing rate lies within 54 to 99 Hz. The linear rise below the ceiling is shown only in the inset for three neurons, with no measure or test; a straight-line fit of maximum rate on field over each neuron's sessions below its ceiling is reported and does not decide the claim. Whether the ceiling is meant for the median neuron or for each neuron is open (the inset shows three neurons); readings (a) the median, (b) at least 75% of neurons within 54 to 99 Hz; both are run under the header's rule.

claims.statement: At the highest fields, unmodulated sine waves merged APs into low-amplitude oscillations on a continuous depolarization, which could flatten and leave the membrane depolarized for the rest of the stimulus (an excitation block), and this depolarization reversed immediately when the stimulus stopped.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 2; Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure 1
claims.quote: At the highest field strengths, multiple APs coalesced into low-amplitude oscillations on top of a continuous depolarization. These oscillations could flatten after several cycles, leaving the membrane depolarized for the rest of the sine wave ... The sustained depolarization induced by intense unmodulated sine waves ( Figures 1 and 3 ) was immediately reversible upon stimulus cessation
claims.criterion: F1 to F3, O1 to O4. The paper gives no count of neurons that reached the block. Reproduced when, under every reading, most neurons tested at fields above the one giving their highest maximum firing rate show sustained depolarization (O4) at their highest field, and in those sessions the mean dF over the 50 ms after the stimulus ends is below the O4 level. The 50-ms window is a standard choice.

claims.statement: All excitation thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
claims.quote: All thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz ( p < 0.0001, two-tailed unpaired t test)
claims.criterion: Thresholds (F5) for 1 and 5 APs, modulated and unmodulated, under O1 to O3. The paper gives one p for "all thresholds"; readings (a) one test per stimulus type and AP count, each p < 0.0001, (b) one test pooling the four. Reproduced when the four ratios are within tolerance and the test reaches p < 0.0001, under every reading.

claims.statement: All thresholds to elicit 5 APs were higher than those for 1 AP.
claims.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
claims.quote: All thresholds to elicit 5 APs were expectedly higher than those for 1 AP
claims.criterion: Thresholds as in fig1-20khz-needs-twice-the-field. The paper reports no test. Reproduced when, for each of the four stimuli (2 and 20 kHz, modulated or not), the mean 5-AP threshold is above the mean 1-AP threshold, under every reading.

claims.statement: Thresholds for sine waves modulated at 20 Hz were significantly higher than for pure sine waves at the same carrier frequency for 5 APs at 2 kHz and for 1 and 5 APs at 20 kHz, so modulation did not lower excitation thresholds; the 2-kHz unmodulated AP threshold was 57.7 ± 3.6 V/cm.
claims.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D and legend; Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, last paragraph
claims.quote: thresholds for modulated sine waves, which emulate the TI stimulus at the target, were significantly higher than those for pure sine waves at the same frequency (for 2 kHz, 5 APs ... p = 0.0079; for 20 kHz, 1 and 5 APs, respectively ... p = 0.0142 and p = 0.0037). Thus, modulated sine waves were equally or less efficient than pure ones at eliciting APs
claims.criterion: Thresholds as in fig1-20khz-needs-twice-the-field; two-tailed unpaired t tests, as the Figure 2D legend names them (the Methods allow paired tests, and the thresholds come from the same neurons; a paired test is shown as a variant). Reproduced when, under every reading, the three modulated thresholds are higher at p < 0.05, the 2-kHz 1-AP thresholds do not differ in the other direction at p < 0.05, and the mean 2-kHz unmodulated threshold is within the paper's SEM. The paper calls 57.7 V/cm "the AP threshold" without saying 1 or 5 APs, so the number has two readings, (a) the 1-AP threshold (the excitation threshold of Figure 3B, the more likely), (b) the 5-AP threshold; the expected value holds when it matches under either, and the notebook shows both.

claims.statement: With 20-Hz modulation, firing above threshold locked to the beats, one AP near the peak of each of the five beats and at most two per beat (ten in all), and modulated sine waves triggered no sustained firing or sustained depolarization.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 1; Figures 2A and 2B
claims.quote: single APs emerged near the peak of each beat, so the firing rate equaled the modulation rate ... At the highest field strengths, each beat could elicit a pair of APs, so the maximum number of APs evoked by five beats was limited to ten. Unlike pure sine waves, modulated stimuli did not trigger sustained firing or sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: F1 to F3, O1 to O4, modulated sessions only. The 250-ms wave holds five 50-ms beats (Results). The dataset's stimulus record is used when it gives the envelope. Otherwise the envelope phase is open; readings (a) the wave starts at minimal amplitude, as the Methods say of the single-beat strobe waves (Pulsed laser fluorescence microscopy), so each beat peaks 25 ms into it, (b) the wave starts at maximal amplitude, as the in-phase superposition of 1.99- and 2.01-kHz waves the Results describe would give, so beats peak at 0, 50, 100, 150 and 200 ms. "Near the peak" is not quantified; as standard choices, reproduced when no session has more than 10 APs, in sessions with at least 5 APs most APs fall within 12.5 ms of a beat peak, and no session shows sustained depolarization (O4), under every reading.

claims.statement: In the same neuron, the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated sine waves, and at the same field strength pure sine waves triggered more APs than modulated ones.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 2; Figures 2A to 2C
claims.quote: When modulated and unmodulated sine waves of the same carrier frequency were tested in the same cell, the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated signals ( Figures 2A - 2C ). At the same field strengths, pure sine waves triggered a larger number of APs
claims.criterion: F1 to F3, O1 to O3. Pairs are a neuron's modulated and unmodulated sessions at the same carrier and field. The paper reports no test. Reproduced when, under every reading, the unmodulated AP count is larger in more pairs than the reverse and the unmodulated 1-AP threshold is lower in more neurons than the reverse. A two-sided paired t test of the counts (F6) is reported.

claims.statement: Replacing NaCl with sodium gluconate, which lowered the solution conductivity from 16.4 to 8.4 mS/cm, reversibly lowered excitation thresholds about 2-fold at every sine wave frequency from 2 to 20 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 2; Figures 3A and 3B
claims.quote: Switching to the NaGlu-based solution reversibly and reproducibly decreased excitation thresholds ~2-fold across all sine wave frequencies tested
claims.criterion: 1-AP thresholds (F5) for unmodulated waves per frequency and solution, 4 to 8 neurons per point (Figure 3B legend), O1 to O3. Reproduced when the ratio is within tolerance at every frequency, under every reading. That the threshold returns on switching back to NaCl (reversibly) is reported per neuron where the dataset holds a return; the paper gives no measure of it.

claims.statement: Extrapolated to a 2 mS/cm solution, excitation by 2-kHz sine waves would be expected at about 7 V/cm.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Extrapolating this trend to still lower conductivities, excitation by 2-kHz sine waves would be expected at ~7 V/cm in a 2 mS/cm solution
claims.criterion: From the mean 2-kHz 1-AP thresholds in NaCl and NaGlu of fig3b-low-conductivity-halves-threshold. The paper does not name its extrapolation (the Figure 3B fits are over frequency, not conductivity), but its own numbers settle it. The "trend" is a halving of threshold for a halving of conductivity (16.4 to 8.4 mS/cm, ~2-fold), and threshold proportional to conductivity gives 57.7 x 2/16.4 = 7.0 V/cm, the paper's ~7, while a straight line through the two points gives about 5.8 V/cm and an exponential about 16.6 V/cm. The value is the NaCl mean times 2/16.4. Reproduced when it is within tolerance. The straight-line and exponential extrapolations are shown as variants.

claims.statement: Excitation by pure sine waves was not caused by heating; the adiabatic temperature rise was 2.5 C after 250 ms at 63 V/cm in NaCl, at most 1.24 C for the same stimulus in the low-conductivity solution, where it evoked sustained firing, and 4.1 C at 81 V/cm in NaCl.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 3; Figure 3A
claims.quote: the maximum theoretical temperature rise (assuming no heat dissipation 43 ) was 2.5°C after 250 ms of near-threshold stimulation at 2 kHz, 63 V/cm, in the NaCl-based solution ( Figure 3A ). The same stimulation in the low-conductance solution elicited sustained neuron firing while the temperature rise would not exceed 1.24°C ... 81 V/cm in the NaCl solution, which would heat by 4.1°C in the adiabatic conditions. These observations prove that excitation by pure sine waves was not caused by heating
claims.criterion: The rise is conductivity times E squared times duration over the volumetric heat capacity (no dissipation, reference 43). The paper does not give the heat capacity or whether E is the peak or the RMS field; readings (a) peak, (b) RMS, each with the heat capacity of water (4.18 J per cm3 per K, a standard choice). From the paper's values neither gives 2.5 C (peak about 3.9 C, RMS about 1.95 C), while the ratios 4.1/2.5 and 1.24/2.5 follow the scaling with E squared and conductivity. Reproduced when all three are within tolerance under a reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when none is but both ratios are within 10%; not reproduced when the ratios fail. That the Figure 3A neuron fired in NaGlu at 63 V/cm (O3) and showed firing in NaCl at 81 V/cm like that in NaGlu at 63 V/cm is reported where the dataset holds it.

claims.statement: In the low-conductivity solution, a 2-s unmodulated 2-kHz sine wave ramped up over 250 ms evoked firing for its whole duration; the firing rate rose with field until replaced by a firing block with sustained depolarization, which developed before the end of the ramp.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 4; Figure 3C
claims.quote: we observed sustained firing for the entire duration of the sine wave ( Figure 3C ). The rate of firing increased with the electric field strength until it was replaced by a firing block and sustained depolarization. The block had already developed before the end of the 250-ms ramp-up period
claims.criterion: F1 to F3 (with the bleaching correction of F2), O1 to O3. Reproduced when, under every reading, some field has APs in the last 250 ms of the 2-s stimulus, the AP count rises with field up to some field, and the highest field shows no AP and a mean dF above the O4 level from 250 ms after onset to the end. The windows follow the 250-ms ramp of the legend; the last-250-ms window is a standard choice.

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS in place of FluoVolt, in eight neurons, 2-kHz sine waves near threshold elicited one or a few delayed APs, and stronger fields shortened the delay and induced sustained firing ending in sustained depolarization, as with FluoVolt.
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 2; Figure S1
claims.quote: Experiments were performed on eight neurons using different electric field strengths tested in a random sequence ... Stimulation near the threshold elicited one or a few delayed APs. Increasing the electric field strength reduced the delay and induced sustained firing that culminated in sustained depolarization. Overall, stimulation effects were not different from those observed with FluoVolt dye
claims.criterion: F1 (traces inverted), F2, F3, O1 to O4; O3 reading (a) uses 5% of the inverted trace only if the Di-8-ANEPPS APs reach it, as its traces are noisier (Results), otherwise reading (b) alone. The paper gives no test of "not different". Reproduced when eight neurons are found and, under every reading, most show one to three APs at their lowest field with APs ("one or a few"; three is a standard choice), a first-AP latency that falls with field, and sustained firing or sustained depolarization (O4) at higher fields.

claims.statement: 1 uM tetrodotoxin abolished both the APs and the sustained depolarization evoked by intense unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves, while the vehicle did not.
claims.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure S2 legend
claims.quote: the inhibition of sodium channels with 1 μM tetrodotoxin not only abolished the APs but also fully blocked the sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: F1 to F3, O1 to O4, sessions before and about 5 min after the change of solution (Figure S2 legend). Reproduced when, under every reading, every TTX neuron has APs or sustained depolarization before and neither after at the same fields, and every vehicle neuron keeps APs or sustained depolarization at the same fields. The paper gives no count of neurons or test.

claims.statement: Membrane charging by 2-us pulses is fast; pooled over 19 experiments, charging and discharging time constants averaged 0.7 and 0.91 us at the cathodic pole and 0.65 and 0.8 us at the anodic pole, so the membrane charges fully within each sine wave cycle up to 100 to 200 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
claims.quote: The time constants pooled together for all cells averaged 0.7 ± 0.08 (charging) and 0.91 ± 0.08 (discharging) μs for the cathodic cell pole and 0.65 ± 0.05 and 0.8 ± 0.07 μs for the anodic pole, respectively (mean ± SEM, n = 19)
claims.criterion: F7, O5. Per experiment (a cell in one field direction) and pole, dF averaged over the eight replicates (Results) and fitted by least squares with the charging function from pulse onset to pulse end and the discharging function from pulse end to the last frame; means over the 19 experiments. Where the discharging fit starts and whether dFmax is shared between the two fits are not given; readings (a) separate dFmax per fit, (b) the discharging fit's amplitude fixed to the dF at pulse end. Reproduced when all four means are within the paper's SEM under every reading.

claims.statement: Aligning elongated cells with the field doubled the time constants compared with the same cells perpendicular to it or with randomly shaped cells; dFmax and the time constants did not differ between the cathode- and anode-facing poles; and discharging was slower than charging except in elongated cells aligned with the field.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the two paragraphs after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E and legend
claims.quote: Δ F max did not differ at the cathodic and anodic cell poles, indicating the lack of rectification of the applied electric field. Charging and discharging time constants did not differ between the two poles either. Aligning elongated cells with the electric field doubled the time constants, as compared to either the same cells oriented perpendicular to the field ( p < 0.001, paired t test) or to randomly shaped cells ( p < 0.01, unpaired t test). Interestingly, discharging time constants were always larger than the charging ones in the same cell ( p < 0.001, paired t test), with the exception of elongated cells aligned with the field
claims.criterion: Fits of fig4-pooled-time-constants; groups as in the Figure 4D and 4E legend (parallel n = 3, perpendicular n = 6, random n = 10, field orientations pooled for random cells). The Figure 4 legend gives other bounds for two of these tests (p < 0.01, paired two-tailed, charging against discharging; p < 0.01, unpaired two-tailed, between orthogonal orientations), and a paired test needs the same cells in both orientations though the groups differ in size; readings (a) the Results' tests, (b) the legend's. Reproduced when, under every reading, parallel time constants are about twice the perpendicular ones (within tolerance) and larger than random at p < 0.05, the pole differences in dFmax and time constants are not significant by paired two-sided t tests (F6, the absence judged on that test), and discharging exceeds charging at p < 0.05 when elongated parallel cells are left out.

claims.statement: Sine waves polarized the two poles of a cell more asymmetrically than 2-us pulses; in the Figure 5 cell the depolarized ROI 2 was 30% smaller than the hyperpolarized ROI 1 with the pulse and up to 90% smaller with sine waves, and in the Figure S3 cell the hyperpolarized ROI 1 was 20% smaller than the depolarized ROI 2 with the pulse and 40% smaller with sine waves, the oscillations not migrating to other regions.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraphs 1 to 4; Figures 5 and S3
claims.quote: in this cell, the oscillations in ROI 2 were up to 90% smaller than those in ROI 1 (compared to just 30% smaller when the same cell was polarized with the 2-μs pulse) ... With the 2-μs pulse, polarization in ROI 1 was 20% smaller than in ROI 2 ( Figure S3B ); however, with sine waves, it became 40% smaller
claims.criterion: F7, O5, O6; ROIs 1 and 2 as in the dataset (cells C7 and C8 of Figure 6B). Pulse asymmetry is 1 minus the smaller ROI's polarization over the larger's. The Results speak of the "maximum depolarization" for Figure 5B, while Figure 6B averages 1 to 2 us into the pulse; readings (a) the peak of the 5-point running average (Figure 5B legend), (b) the mean from 1 to 2 us (Figure 6B legend). Sine asymmetry from the oscillation amplitudes after LOESS subtraction. "Up to 90%" is the largest per-cycle difference; the 40% is not said to be a maximum, so readings (a) the regression sensitivities of Figure 6C, (b) the largest per-cycle difference; the 100- and 154-Hz waves are both run. Reproduced when the four values are within tolerance under every reading, and the sine asymmetry exceeds the pulse asymmetry in both cells.

claims.statement: Across 9 cells FluoVolt sensitivity to 2-us pulses was 15% to 47% per 1 kV/cm (mean 28%); sensitivity to 2-kHz sine waves, linearly correlated with the field, was 1.5% to 28.4% (mean 11.8%), smaller in every ROI, and 42% of the pulse value.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraphs 5 and 6; Figures 6B to 6D
claims.quote: The electric field sensitivity of FluoVolt ranged between a 15% and 47% change per 1 kV/cm, with an average value of 28% ± 2.5% across all ROIs in all the cells ... The regression coefficient, which was the FluoVolt sensitivity to sine waves, varied from 1.5% to 28.4% ( Figure 6C ). All numbers were invariably smaller than those measured for the same ROIs with the pulse ( Figure 6D ). The electric field sensitivity averaged across all ROIs in all the cells was 11.8% ± 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, just 42% of the value for the 2-μs pulses
claims.criterion: F7, O5, O6, on the 2-kHz waves modulated at 100 Hz (Figure 6C legend). Pulse sensitivity per ROI is dF averaged over the 21 frames from 1 to 2 us, divided by the field in kV/cm, with sign removed; sine sensitivity per ROI the slope of the oscillation dF on the instantaneous field. Whether the slope is fitted on signed values or on per-cycle amplitudes is not given; readings (a) signed dF on the signed field, sign removed after, (b) per-cycle peak-to-peak amplitude on the cycle's peak field. Reproduced when, under every reading, the means and the ratio are within tolerance, the ranges within the widened bounds, the sine value is below the pulse value in every ROI, and the regression p is below 0.0001 for both ROIs in eight of the nine cells.

claims.statement: The 2-kHz AP threshold of 57.7 V/cm times the sine wave sensitivity gives a 0.68% emission change, about 6.8 mV with FluoVolt's calibration, so the threshold depolarization is 5 to 15 mV, as with intracellular current injection.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, last paragraph
claims.quote: This threshold corresponds to a 0.68% ± 0.11% FluoVolt emission change (11.8 × 57.7/1,000) ... Then, a 0.68% emission change corresponds to a 6.8-mV depolarization at the AP threshold. Considering the calibration factor variability, the threshold TMP depolarization can be conservatively estimated in the range from 5 to 15 mV
claims.criterion: The mean sine sensitivity of fig6-sine-less-than-pulse times the mean unmodulated 2-kHz threshold of fig2d-modulated-thresholds-higher, divided by 1,000, under the two readings of 57.7 V/cm given there (1-AP or 5-AP threshold), matching under either, and that times 10 mV per 1% (the calibration of reference 47, about 10% per 100 mV, as the paper uses it). Tolerances are the paper's, the second being 0.11% times 10 mV per 1%. Reproduced when both are within tolerance and the depolarization lies within 4.5 to 16.5 mV (5 to 15 mV widened by 10%).

claims.statement: During a single beat of a modulated 2-kHz sine wave, the optical TMP in ROIs 1 and 2 oscillated with the carrier in opposite phases, with amplitudes proportional to the sine wave amplitude, on top of a gradual depolarization of the whole cell that developed as the amplitude rose.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 2; Figures 5C, 5D and legend; Figure S3
claims.quote: Optical TMP oscillated in synchrony with the carrier sine wave in the opposite phases, i.e., the peak depolarization in ROI 1 corresponded to the peak hyperpolarization in ROI 2, and vice versa. These oscillations, proportional to the sine wave amplitude, were superimposed on the gradual depolarization of the entire cell
claims.criterion: F7, O5, O6, on the Figure 5 and Figure S3 cells, 100- and 154-Hz waves. The whole-cell response is the LOESS fit of each ROI (Figure 5 legend) and the oscillation the data minus that fit (Figure 5H). The paper gives no measure or test. As standard choices, reproduced when, under every reading, in both cells the oscillations of ROIs 1 and 2 have a negative Pearson correlation (two-sided p < 0.05), the per-cycle peak-to-peak amplitude in each ROI rises with the cycle's peak field (positive slope), and the LOESS fit at the envelope peak is above F0 in both ROIs.

claims.statement: Of 106 mice entering SHIELD surgery, 79 passed all quality checks, 14 passed after a flag that resolved and 13 failed, a final passing rate of 87.7%, on par with 90% (122 of 135) for the earlier 5-mm cranial window surgery.
claims.source: Results, Installation of SHIELD implant and QC evaluation, paragraph 3; Figure 3B
claims.quote: Of the 106 mice entering surgery for this study, 79 passed all quality checks with no issues, 14 passed with a flag that eventually resolved, and 13 mice failed ... The final passing rate of 87.7% is on par with the success rate for our previous 5 mm cranial window surgery
claims.criterion: Counts of surgical outcomes from the paper's surgery records. The Methods list failures as 4 detached headposts, 1 recurring seizures, 2 implant issues, 1 brain health, 3 unexpected deaths (11, not 13); both totals are reported. The earlier-surgery rate (122 of 135) is from references 18 and 28 and is not tested.

claims.statement: Intrinsic signal imaging through the implant maps the retinotopic boundaries of VISp and many higher visual areas.
claims.source: Results, Installation of SHIELD implant and QC evaluation, paragraph 4; Figure 3C
claims.quote: We found that standard procedures successfully mapped retinotopic boundaries of VISp and many higher visual cortical areas (Figure 3C)
claims.criterion: Sign maps computed as in the Methods (Intrinsic signal imaging) from at least three averaged trials show VISp and higher visual areas as contiguous regions. Shown in the paper by example only; the paper gives no count of mice.

claims.statement: The implanted left hemisphere shows little GFAP activation or loss of DAPI and NeuN staining compared with the unaltered right hemisphere (6 mice, 56 days after surgery).
claims.source: Results, Installation of SHIELD implant and QC evaluation, paragraph 5; Figures 3D and S3E
claims.quote: found little evidence of GFAP activation or cell loss, indicating that the implant did not compromise the underlying tissue
claims.criterion: The paper shows example sections only and reports no measure or test. Open. Readings (a) visual comparison of the two hemispheres as in Figure 3D; (b) GFAP, DAPI and NeuN intensity or cell density, implanted against control hemisphere per mouse, by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (the Methods' default paired test), reproduced when no difference at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Inserted probes rarely caused significant intracranial bleeding, in 3 of 547 tracks.
claims.source: Results, Installation of SHIELD implant and QC evaluation, paragraph 5
claims.quote: We found that inserted probes rarely caused significant intracranial bleeding (3/547 tracks).

claims.statement: In MRI, the 5-mm cranial window deforms the brain under the window, while the brain under SHIELD implants (250 and 400 micrometre inserts) is close to naive mice; the thicker insert trended toward less deformation.
claims.source: Results, Installation of SHIELD implant and QC evaluation, paragraph 6; Figures 3F to 3H
claims.quote: revealed clear brain deformation for the non-contoured 5-mm window over the visual cortex ... the area between surface contours for SHIELD mice was more similar to naive mice ... though the thicker design trended toward less deformation
claims.criterion: Area between the mirrored right and the left brain surface contours at ten coronal planes, summed over the 4 most posterior, per mouse (Methods, Magnetic resonance imaging; Figure 3H legend). The naive volumes are from Qiu et al. 2018 (reference 35). The legend does not say which pairs carry the asterisk; open. Readings (a) each implant group against naive; (b) all six pairs. Reproduced when, after Benjamini-Hochberg, the 5-mm window group is larger than naive at p < 0.05 and neither SHIELD group differs from naive at p < 0.05. The 250 against 400 trend is reported only.

claims.statement: SHIELD mice and 5-mm window mice learn the change detection task at similar rates (median sessions to criterion 12.5 against 14, p = 0.17).
claims.source: Results, Installation of SHIELD implant and QC evaluation, paragraph 7; Figure 3I
claims.quote: Mice with either implant had similar learning rates (Figure 3I; median number of sessions to criterion: SHIELD 12.5 ± 2; 5-mm window 14 ± 3; p = 0.17, Wilcoxon rank-sum test)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a Wilcoxon rank-sum test of sessions to criterion between the groups at p < 0.05; reproduced when it is not significant. Criterion and training stages as in references 36 and 37. The paper does not say where the 5-mm window mice's training records are, nor how many mice each group has. Tolerances are the paper's stated spread.

claims.statement: A typical 6-probe session records 1,821 non-noise units (SD 341.9) from 28.1 areas (SD 5.1).
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
claims.quote: we recorded activity from over 1,800 units spanning ... 25 brain areas (this includes all non-noise units, as described in STAR Methods; 1,821 ± 341.9 units; 28.1 ± 5.1 areas, mean ± SD
claims.criterion: As in DynamicGating_ephys_metrics.ipynb cells 36 to 39, over the 87 QC-passing sessions. Units in an annotated area (structure_acronym not No Area, out of brain or Track not annotated); 6-probe sessions are those whose such units come from exactly six probes; units counted are non-noise (quality good); areas counted are distinct structure_acronym values among all such units. Mean and SD across sessions. Tolerances are the paper's stated SD.

claims.statement: Across recording days each mouse received about 20 probe insertions (SD 4.1) into about 10 implant holes (10.4, SD 2.3).
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 2; Figures S4A and S4B
claims.quote: we typically made ... probe insertions (20 ± 4.1, mean ± SD; Figure S4A) targeting ... implant holes (10.4 ± 2.3, mean ± SD; Figure S4B)
claims.criterion: Insertions per mouse are the distinct probe insertions with units (code cell 32, distinct probe_id per mouse_id). Which sessions count is open. Readings (a) the 87 QC-passing sessions, as the code; (b) all sessions of each mouse, as the S4A legend says "over all recording days". Under (a) the mean is at most 467 / 25 = 18.7. Holes per mouse need the implant hole of each insertion; no code. Tolerances are the paper's stated SD.

claims.statement: Stable recordings were made from 25 mice in 87 experiments with 467 probe insertions.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 2
claims.quote: high-quality recordings from 25 mice, totaling 87 experiments and 467 probe insertions
claims.criterion: Counted over the 87 QC-passing sessions of code cell 26 (code cell 34). The dandiset's description lists 99 sessions; the 12 others are reported.

claims.statement: On average 5.46 of the 6 intended probes per session were successfully inserted.
claims.source: STAR Methods, Neuropixels recordings, Probe insertion, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Overall, we achieved a penetration success of 5.46 probes per session
claims.criterion: Insertions with recorded units divided by sessions. The code's counts give 467 over 87 (5.37); which insertions or sessions give 5.46 is not stated. Readings (a) over the 87 QC-passing sessions; (b) over all sessions in the dandiset.

claims.statement: Insertions along the same trajectory (same hole and probe orientation) enter the brain at similar CCF locations, with a median absolute deviation of 150 micrometres medial-lateral and 200 micrometres anterior-posterior over 15 trajectories.
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 3; Figure 4B
claims.quote: for 15 unique trajectories, we found the median absolute deviation in CCF coordinates was 150 mm in the medial-lateral axis and 200 mm in the anterior-posterior axis
claims.criterion: Per trajectory, the median absolute deviation across its insertions of the entry point's CCF coordinate; the median across trajectories. No code. How the entry point is located is open. Readings (a) the CCF coordinate of the most superficial channel in a brain structure; (b) the most superficial channel with units. Which insertions share a trajectory needs the hole and orientation of each insertion.

claims.statement: Discontinuous or abrupt shifts in unit depth in the drift map occurred in 5.1% of insertions (23 of 454).
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 4; Figure 4C
claims.quote: We rarely observed discontinuous or abrupt shifts in the depth of units in the drift map (5.1% of insertions; 23/ 454)
claims.criterion: The paper judged drift maps by eye and gives no rule for an abrupt shift, and no code. Open; the only reading the paper allows is inspection of drift maps (unit depth against time, marker intensity by amplitude).

claims.statement: Unit drift with SHIELD is only slightly higher than with the 5-mm window (median 25.1 against 22.82 micrometres).
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 4; Figure 4D
claims.quote: found it was only slightly higher than that observed in our previous recordings using the 5-mm insertion window method (SHIELD: 25.1 ± 0.1 mm, 5-mm window: 22.82 ± 0.05; median ± SEM
claims.criterion: The max_drift metric of all non-noise units (quality good) of the 87 QC-passing sessions (143,828 units) against VBN non-noise units (262,177), as in code cells 41 and 46; median of each. Tolerances are the paper's SEM. VBN units come from DANDI:000713 (reference 29).

claims.statement: The distributions of unit quality metrics (presence ratio, amplitude cutoff, ISI violations, SNR, isolation distance, drift, amplitude) are comparable for SHIELD and the 5-mm window.
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 5; Figure 4D
claims.quote: We found that the distribution of QC metrics was comparable with both surgical preparations (Figure 4D).
claims.criterion: Non-noise units as in fig4d-unit-drift, seven metrics as in code cell 46. The paper reports no test or measure of comparability. Open. Readings (a) the code's two-sided Mann-Whitney U test per metric (its printed output gives p = 1.4e-156 for presence ratio and 6.0e-18 for amplitude cutoff), comparable when not significant at 0.05; (b) each SHIELD median within 10% of the 5-mm window median. Both readings are run and every median and p value shown.

claims.statement: The fraction of units passing the standard quality filter is very similar for SHIELD (41.1%) and the 5-mm window (40.7%).
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 5
claims.quote: the percentage of units passing our standard quality metrics filter (see STAR Methods) was very similar for the SHIELD versus 5-mm window implants (% units passing quality metrics criteria: SHIELD: 41.1, 5-mm window: 40.7)
claims.criterion: Passing means isi_violations < 0.5, amplitude_cutoff < 0.1 and presence_ratio > 0.95 (Methods), as a fraction of non-noise units (code cell 42).

claims.statement: About 300 units are recorded per probe on each day, and unit yield does not differ across the four recording days with SHIELD (p = 0.48).
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 6; Figure 4E
claims.quote: On each recording day, we measured the activity of roughly 300 units from each probe (Figure 4E). ... unit yield was not significantly different across days for SHIELD mice (p = 0.48, Kruskal-Wallis H test)
claims.criterion: Non-noise units per insertion (mouse, probe and session type EPHYS_1 to EPHYS_4), over the 87 QC-passing sessions, as in code cells 48 and 49. A claim of absence, judged on the paper's Kruskal-Wallis test across the four days at p < 0.05; reproduced when not significant and each day's median is within tolerance. The insertion counts in the figure are 129, 126, 121, 91.

claims.statement: With the 5-mm window, unit yield decreased on the second recording day (p = 6e-22).
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 6; Figure 4E
claims.quote: In contrast to the 5-mm window preparation, for which unit yield decreased on the second recording day (p = 6e–22, Kruskal-Wallis H test)
claims.criterion: VBN non-noise units per insertion by session number (code cell 47). The code's p = 6e-22 is a Kruskal-Wallis test over six groups (two VBN days and four SHIELD days, cell 51), not VBN day 1 against day 2. Readings (a) VBN day 1 against day 2; (b) the code's six groups. Reproduced when p < 0.05 under a reading and the VBN day-2 median is below day 1.

claims.statement: The average firing rate of recorded units is similar across the four recording days (p = 0.21).
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 6; Figure 4E
claims.quote: Additionally, the average firing rate of recorded units was similar across days (p = 0.21 Kruskal-Wallis H test).
claims.criterion: Per session the median firing rate of non-noise units; Kruskal-Wallis across session types EPHYS_1 to EPHYS_4 (code cells 54 and 55). A claim of absence on that test; reproduced when p >= 0.05. The code's output and the figure give p = 0.26, the text 0.21; both are reported.

claims.statement: A consistent fraction of VISp units has significant spatial receptive fields on each of the four recording days (p = 0.38).
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 7; Figures 4E and 4F
claims.quote: we measured a consistent fraction of units with well-defined spatial receptive fields (RFs) (Figure 4E and 4F; p = 0.38 Kruskal-Wallis H test)
claims.criterion: Per session the fraction of QC-passing units labelled VISp (ISI label) whose receptive field is significant, a chi-square test on the 9 x 9 spike-count map at p < 0.01 (Methods, Receptive Field Mapping; the code's units table uses 0.01); Kruskal-Wallis across days. The Figure 4E code uses p < 0.05 (cell 58); shown as a variant. A claim of absence; reproduced when p >= 0.05 under the Methods threshold. Figure 4E prints p = 0.39 for this panel, the text 0.38; both are reported.

claims.statement: VISp receptive fields recorded through adjacent holes on successive days lie where the ISI-based retinotopic map predicts.
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 7; Figure 4F
claims.quote: the region of visual space preferred on each day matched the expected location indicated by the ISI-based retinotopic map
claims.criterion: Shown for one example mouse; the paper gives no measure. Open. Reading, the RF centres (azimuth, elevation) of significant VISp units on each day against the retinotopic location the ISI sign map predicts at that day's insertion site. Needs the ISI maps and insertion images.

claims.statement: The population response of VISp units to an image is highly similar across the four recording days.
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 7; Figure 4G
claims.quote: In addition, the stimulusevoked temporal dynamics were highly similar across the 4 recording days (Figure 4G).
claims.criterion: Units with significant RFs labelled VISp, PSTHs at 1 ms to active-behavior presentations of image im115_r (the Figure 4G legend gives unit counts only, 595, 482, 536 and 446 from 12, 11, 12 and 11 mice; the selection by significant RF is the code's, run_im115_responses.py; that script keeps presence_ratio > 0.9 and ephys_metrics cell 64 then applies the 0.95 filter); day means baseline-subtracted by the 10 ms before onset and divided by their maximum (cell 66). The paper gives no measure of similarity. Open. Readings take the paper's test for stability across days (Kruskal-Wallis, Figure 4E) on per-unit (a) mean baseline-subtracted response 0 to 250 ms and (b) time of peak response 0 to 250 ms; reproduced when neither differs across days at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Task performance is stable across the four recording days despite repeated insertions (median rewards 59.5, 63.5, 56.5, 60.5; p = 0.96).
claims.source: Results, High-quality multi-Neuropixels recordings, paragraph 8
claims.quote: we found that mouse behavioral performance on the visual task was stable across the 4 recording days despite repeated probe insertions (median rewards received: day 1, 59.5; day 2, 63.5; day 3, 56.5; day 4, 60.5; Kruskal-Wallis test: p = 0.96)
claims.criterion: Rewards per session, median across sessions of each session type EPHYS_1 to EPHYS_4, Kruskal-Wallis across days; a claim of absence, reproduced when p >= 0.05. No code.
