Which rewards count is open. Readings (a) all rewards delivered; (b) rewards earned by hits, auto-rewards left out. Sessions are the 87 QC-passing ones; all sessions as a variant.

claims.statement: Activity is transiently suppressed after probe insertion and recovers with a time constant of 25 to 30 minutes.
claims.source: STAR Methods, Neuropixels recordings, Probe insertion, paragraph 1; Figure S4I
claims.quote: we find that activity is transiently suppressed directly after probe insertion and gradually recovers with a time constant of 25-30 minutes (Figure S4I)
claims.criterion: Reported as the range 25 to 30 min; the claim holds inside 22.5 to 33 min. Spikes of QC-passing non-noise units summed in 1 s bins from the first stimulus onset per session (dg_plot_firing_rate_drift_over_session.py); the S4I legend plots the mean change across 85 SHIELD experiments. The normalisation and fit are not given. Open. Readings (a) each session's rate divided by its mean, averaged across sessions, fitted with a - b exp(-t / tau); (b) the same with rates divided by the mean of the last 10 minutes. The 5-mm comparison (103 experiments) needs VBN data and is a variant.

claims.statement: Retracting probes 100 micrometres after insertion reduces unit drift (unit means 24.48 against 30.25 micrometres; session means 24.23 against 30.56).
claims.source: Figure S4D and S4E legends; STAR Methods, Probe insertion, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Units from sessions where probes were retracted had lower drift (mean = 24.48 μm) than those from sessions where probes were not retracted (mean = 30.25 μm; Kolmogrov-Smirnov test, p < .001)
claims.criterion: Which sessions were retracted (23 per the Methods) must be found in the dandiset. The drift measure is the legend's point-to-point drift per unit over the session; open. Readings (a) max_drift; (b) cumulative_drift. The unit set (102,747 units over 83 sessions) is smaller than all non-noise units; readings (a) QC-passing units; (b) non-noise units. Reproduced when the KS test gives p < 0.001 with retracted lower, and the means are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Retracted and non-retracted sessions record similar numbers of good units (means 1125 against 1280, p = 0.318).
claims.source: Figure S4F legend
claims.quote: Number of good units recorded per session is similar across retracted and non-retracted sessions. ... Distributions did not differ significantly (Kolmogrov-Smirnov test, p = 0.318).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the paper's KS test at p < 0.05. Good units read as (a) QC-passing units (Methods); (b) non-noise units.

claims.statement: Sharpened probes show drift comparable to unsharpened probes and a lower insertion failure rate (p = 0.0004).
claims.source: Figure S4G and S4H legends
claims.quote: Sharpened Neuropixels probes show comparable drift to unsharpened probes. ... Sharpened Neuropixels probes have a lower insertion fail rate than unsharpened probes (p = 0.0004, Fisher’s exact test).
claims.criterion: Needs which probes were sharpened and the failed insertion attempts; no code. Drift comparison has no test in the paper; reported as medians (21,894 and 80,673 units).

claims.statement: Dura-Gel can stay on the implant for at least 2 weeks without visible brain deterioration or a drop in unit yield.
claims.source: Results, Dual-hemisphere SHIELD implant, paragraph 1 (end, page 10); Figures S3B and S3D
claims.quote: Dura-Gel can remain in place for at least 2 weeks without visible signs of brain deterioration (Figure S3B) or a drop in unit yield (Figure S3D).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the paper's test, the Wald test for a nonzero slope of unit yield against days since Dura-Gel application over 24 insertions (S3D legend); reproduced when the slope is not significantly negative at p < 0.05. The unit set for yield is not stated; readings (a) non-noise units; (b) QC-passing units.

claims.statement: Simultaneous Neuropixels recordings from both hemispheres are feasible with the dual-hemisphere implant.
claims.source: Results, Dual-hemisphere SHIELD implant, paragraph 1; Figures 5C and 5D
claims.quote: In preliminary experiments, we demonstrate the feasibility of simultaneous, bilateral Neuropixels recordings with the SHIELD method (Figures 5C and 5D).
claims.criterion: Reproduced when a session recorded through a dual-hemisphere implant has units on probes in both hemispheres (cortex and striatum, Figure 5D). Two sessions in the paper.

claims.statement: Blue light through the implant in a VGAT-ChR2 mouse silences visually evoked activity of VISp regular-spiking units at the recording site, with activity near baseline 2 mm away, and the effect depends on distance and power.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD is compatible with optogenetics, paragraph 2; Figures 6B and 6C
claims.quote: Stimulusevoked activity of regular spiking (RS) units in VISp was silenced when a 2-mW laser spot was targeted to the recording location but returned to near baseline at a distance of 2 mm (Figure 6B). The dependence of this silencing effect on distance and laser power (Figure 6C)
claims.criterion: RS units are VISp units with peak-to-trough duration > 0.4 ms; laser at 1, 2 and 12 mW at 0, 0.5, 1 and 2 mm anterior, with a 500 ms grating (Methods, Optogenetic silencing). The measure is not given. Open. Readings (a) mean rate in the 500 ms stimulus window; (b) the same minus the pre-stimulus rate. Reproduced when, with 2 mW at 0 mm, the RS population response is below the no-laser response by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test across units (the Methods' default paired test) at p < 0.05, and at 2 mm it is not different at p < 0.05; the dependence on distance and power is reported.

claims.statement: Red light through the implant evokes reliable short-latency spikes from ChrimsonR-tagged Vglut2 midbrain units, found up to 4 mm below the brain surface.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD is compatible with optogenetics, paragraph 3; Figures 6E and 6F
claims.quote: Photo-stimulation with pulses (10 ms) of red light (638 nm) evoked reliable, short-latency spiking responses from units recorded in the midbrain (Figure 6E). Such optotagged units were found up to 4 mm below the surface of the brain
claims.criterion: Tagged units show a significant increase (p < 0.05) in rate during all five 10 ms pulses at 20 Hz (Methods, Optotagging in the midbrain); the test is not named; per pulse, the Wilcoxon signed-rank test across trials of the spike count in the 10 ms pulse against an equal window before the train (the Methods' default paired test). Which trials enter is open, since trials ran at several laser powers (50 per power, powers not given). Readings (a) all powers pooled; (b) each power separately, a unit tagged when it passes at any power. Reproduced when tagged units exist and the deepest is within tolerance.

claims.statement: VISp alpha events are rhythmic at 3 to 5 Hz, and MOp events occur in a slightly higher band, 5 to 7 Hz.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD recordings reveal multi-regional subnetworks, paragraphs 3 and 4; Figure 7A
claims.quote: we observed rhythmic 3–5 Hz waves of activity in VISp (Figure 7A, left) ... These MOp alpha-like events occurred in a slightly higher frequency band (5–7 Hz)
claims.criterion: Qualifying events as in the header. No method is given for the frequency. Open. Readings (a) the inverse of the median interval between successive detected maxima in each event; (b) the peak frequency of the event's autocorrelogram spectrum. Reproduced when, under a reading, the median VISp frequency lies in 2.7 to 5.5 Hz, the median MOp frequency in 4.5 to 7.7 Hz (the ranges widened by 10% of each bound), and MOp is higher by the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (the Methods' default unpaired test) at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: VISp and MOp alpha events occur when the mouse is immobile and the pupil constricted, with pupil diameter about 25% smaller than at random session times.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD recordings reveal multi-regional subnetworks, paragraph 5; Figure 7B
claims.quote: VISp and MOp events tended to occur during periods of lower arousal, when the animal was immobile and the pupil was constricted (during alpha events, pupil diameter was ... 25% smaller relative to randomly chosen session times)
claims.criterion: As in DynamicGating_4hz_analysis.ipynb cells 13 to 15, on qualifying events (header). Pupil (blinks removed) and running speed resampled at 10 ms with forward fill; event value the mean over 0 to 1 s after event onset, windows with fewer than 1000 samples dropped. Pupil change is (event value minus the session's mean over random times) over that mean, pooled over events, Wilcoxon signed-rank against zero; running at events against running at random times by the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (code). The code uses pupil area while the text says diameter; open. Readings (a) pupil area; (b) diameter, the square root of area. The summary of the pooled changes is not stated; readings (c) mean; (d) median. The text gives the 25% for alpha events without naming the area; readings (e) VISp events; (f) MOp events; (g) both pooled. Reproduced, for each of VISp and MOp, when pupil is smaller and running lower at events at p < 0.05 and the change is within tolerance under a reading.

claims.statement: VISp alpha events are often triggered by the offset of visual stimuli, while the timing of MOp events is not related to visual stimuli.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD recordings reveal multi-regional subnetworks, paragraph 5; Figure 7B, right
claims.quote: The VISp events were often triggered by the offset of visual stimulation (Figure 7B) ... The timing of MOp events was not related to visual stimuli (Figure 7B).
claims.criterion: As in code cell 12, for each qualifying event the last stimulus presentation starting before it; onset minus that stimulus's end time, histogram 0 to 0.5 s in 50 ms bins. The paper reports no test. Open. Readings (a) chi-square goodness of fit of the ten bins against uniform; (b) Kolmogorov-Smirnov against uniform on [0, 0.5) s. Reproduced when, under a reading, VISp differs from uniform at p < 0.05 with the largest bin in the first 250 ms after offset, and MOp does not differ at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Activity during post-stimulus VISp alpha events is weakly but significantly correlated with activity during the preceding stimulus (r = 0.77, p = 1.8e-6), as if events replay recent stimulation.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD recordings reveal multi-regional subnetworks, paragraph 5; Figure S6
claims.quote: Activity during post-stimulus alpha events was weakly but significantly correlated with activity during the preceding stimulus, indicating that alpha events tend to replay recent sensory stimulation (Figure S6; r = 0.77
claims.criterion: No code. Per S6 legends, for each VISp unit the mean response to each of the four stimuli of the session and the response during the alpha event following each stimulus (event assigned to the last stimulus before it, as in code cell 12); rows normalised; per session the column average over units; Pearson correlation across sessions with four points per session (S6F inset). Open details and readings. Evoked window (a) 0 to 250 ms after onset (image duration, Methods); (b) 0 to 500 ms. Event window (c) 0 to 1 s after onset (as the code's pupil window); (d) the event's 1.25 s detection window. Which four stimuli is not stated; the sessions' stimulus names must show it. A per-unit correlation (S6E) is shown as a variant. The paper's numbers favour the S6F inset, since a Pearson r of 0.77 gives p = 1.8e-6 at about 28 points (7 sessions of four), while a per-unit correlation over hundreds of units would give a far smaller p. The text prints the p value with a garbled minus sign (1.8e?6).

claims.statement: During VISp events, VISp is tightly coupled to LP and VISl (sharp CCG peaks near zero lag and a 3 to 7 Hz coherence peak), but not to PO or SSp.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD recordings reveal multi-regional subnetworks, paragraph 6; Figures 7C and 7D
claims.quote: During VISp events, VISp activity was tightly coupled to the secondary visual thalamus (LP) and higher-order lateral visual cortex (VISl), as evidenced by sharp peaks in the CCG at near-zero lag. VISp was not strongly coupled to somatosensory thalamus (PO) or SSp. Indeed, coherence analysis revealed a prominent peak in the 3–7 Hz band between VISp population spiking activity and LP and VISl, but not PO or SSp (Figure 7D)
claims.criterion: Header method. Coherence part, the pair test, reproduced when VISp-LP and VISp-VISl are significant with positive band coherence and VISp-PO and VISp-SSp are not (the absence on the same test). CCG part, the mean of event CCGs pooled across sessions; near zero is not defined; open. Readings (a) peak within 20 ms of zero lag; (b) within 50 ms. Reproduced when the CCG peaks of LP and VISl lie near zero and are higher than those of PO and SSp.

claims.statement: During MOp events, MOp is coupled to PO and SSp but not to LP or VISl.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD recordings reveal multi-regional subnetworks, paragraph 6; Figures 7C and 7D
claims.quote: Conversely, MOp showed the opposite pattern: strong coupling to PO and SSp, but not to LP or VISl.
claims.criterion: As fig7cd-visp-coupling with MOp as reference. Reproduced when MOp-PO and MOp-SSp are significant with positive band coherence and MOp-LP and MOp-VISl are not, and the CCG peaks of PO and SSp lie near zero and are higher than those of LP and VISl.

claims.statement: In the 3 to 7 Hz band, time lags between VISp or MOp and their associated regions straddle zero; neither consistently leads or follows.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD recordings reveal multi-regional subnetworks, paragraph 7 (top of page 13); Figure 7E
claims.quote: Time lags between VISp and MOp and their associated regions in the 3–7 Hz band straddled zero lag, indicating that these areas did not consistently lead or follow activity in the other network nodes (Figure 7E).
claims.criterion: As in code cell 26, per qualifying event the median over 3 to 7 Hz frequency bins of the phase delay (nitime CoherenceAnalyzer, default settings) between the reference population rate and the other area's, both at the event, for VISp with VISl, VISal, LGd, LP, CP and MOp with SSp, PO, those significant in fig7f. A claim of absence. The paper's text names no test; the code tests lags against zero with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test and Benjamini-Hochberg, and its printed output gives p from 2.4e-49 to 0.010 for all seven pairs. Judged on that test at 0.05; reproduced for a pair when not significant. The median lag and the fraction of positive lags are reported for each pair.

claims.statement: Beyond visual cortex and thalamus, VISp alpha events enhance coherence of VISp with ACA, RSP and CP.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD recordings reveal multi-regional subnetworks, paragraph 8 (page 13; the text cites it as Figure 6F); Figure 7F
claims.quote: In addition to visual corticothalamic regions, VISp alpha events enhanced coherence between VISp and medial cortical structures anterior cingulate area (ACA) and RSP, as well as CP
claims.criterion: The header's pair test with VISp as reference. Areas are the units' structure_acronym values with at least 20 units, so ACA and RSP appear as ACAd, ACAv, RSPd, RSPv and so on; readings (a) any subdivision significant; (b) all recorded subdivisions significant. Reproduced when ACA, RSP, CP, LGd, LP and VISl are each significant with positive band coherence.

claims.statement: MOp alpha events enhance coherence of MOp with SSp, PO, MRN and the deep layers of the superior colliculus (SCiw).
claims.source: Results, SHIELD recordings reveal multi-regional subnetworks, paragraph 8 (page 13; the text cites it as Figure 6F); Figure 7F
claims.quote: Conversely, MOp events enhanced coherence between MOp and SSp/PO, as well as motor-related midbrain structures MRN and deep layers of the superior colliculus (SCiw).
claims.criterion: The header's pair test with MOp as reference. Reproduced when SSp, PO, MRN and SCiw are each significant with positive band coherence (SSp under the same subdivision readings as fig7f-visp-network).

claims.statement: Neither VISp nor MOp alpha events engage the hippocampus.
claims.source: Results, SHIELD recordings reveal multi-regional subnetworks, paragraph 4; Figures 7A and 7F
claims.quote: Neither visual nor motor events appeared to engage the hippocampus.
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the pair test of the header (the paper's test for engagement, Figure 7F) for every hippocampal formation region recorded (CA1, CA2, CA3, DG, SUB, ProS and the like, by the CCF tree in the code's ccf_structure_tree_2017.csv). Reproduced when none is significant with positive band coherence for either reference area.

claims.statement: CP units with significant spatial receptive fields lie mostly in the medial dorsal striatum, midway along the anterior-posterior extent of CP.
claims.source: Results, Fine-scale alpha rhythm coupling between visual cortex and striatum, paragraph 2; Figures 8B and 8C
claims.quote: These units were biased toward the medial dorsal striatum mid-way along the anteriorposterior extent of the CP
claims.criterion: CP units (structure_acronym CP) passing QC, split by RF significance (chi-square, p < 0.01, Methods). The paper gives no test. Open. Reading, CCF medial-lateral and dorsal-ventral coordinates of CP-RF against CP-noRF units by the Wilcoxon rank-sum test (the Methods' default unpaired test); reproduced when CP-RF units are more medial and more dorsal at p < 0.05. The anterior-posterior part is reported as the CP-RF median against the CP extent sampled; the paper notes the lateral and posterior striatum were not sampled.

claims.statement: CP units with receptive fields respond more strongly to the task's full-field images than CP units without receptive fields.
claims.source: Results, Fine-scale alpha rhythm coupling between visual cortex and striatum, paragraph 3; Figure 8D
claims.quote: CP-RF units showed significantly larger visual responses to this stimulus compared with CPnoRF units (Figure 8D).
claims.criterion: As in code cells 31 to 35, the five sessions 1182628226, 1182871514, 1183071525, 1194850630 and 1195036753; spikes at 1 ms from 250 ms before to 500 ms after every active-behavior image presentation (make_dg_unit_tensor.py); the group's mean over -50 to 0 ms subtracted; exponential smoothing with tau 2 ms; mean over presentations per unit; per 1 ms bin a Wilcoxon rank-sum test of CP-RF against CP-noRF units, Benjamini-Hochberg (Figure 8D legend). Units passing QC (Methods); the code's presence_ratio > 0.9 filter is a variant. Reproduced when significant bins occur within 250 ms after onset with CP-RF higher in all of them.

claims.statement: CP-RF responses lag VISp by about 20 ms, and CP-noRF responses lag CP-RF by about another 20 ms.
claims.source: Results, Fine-scale alpha rhythm coupling between visual cortex and striatum, paragraph 3; Figure 8D
claims.quote: CP-RF lagged behind VISp responses by ... 20 ms, whereas CP-noRF had slower responses that lagged behind CP-RF units by an additional 20 ms
claims.criterion: Population mean responses as in fig8d-cp-rf-larger-response. Tolerance 5 ms because the paper gives the lags as approximate and to the nearest 10 ms. The latency measure is not given; open. Readings (a) time of the population peak; (b) time at which the population mean first reaches half its peak.

claims.statement: Triggered on VISp alpha events, CP-RF firing rates are more modulated than CP-noRF rates, particularly in the troughs of the oscillation.
claims.source: Results, Fine-scale alpha rhythm coupling between visual cortex and striatum, paragraph 4; Figure 8E
claims.quote: We found that CP-RF firing rates were significantly more modulated, particularly during the troughs of the oscillation when the visual thalamo-cortical network is suppressed.
claims.criterion: Qualifying VISp events (header) in sessions with CP recorded (code cell 37); per event the CP-RF and CP-noRF population mean rate in 10 ms bins from -0.5 to 2 s, exponential smoothing tau one bin (cell 39). Per bin test, the legend's Wilcoxon rank-sum with Benjamini-Hochberg; the code's paired signed-rank test is a variant. More modulated is not defined; open. Readings (a) the peak-to-trough range of the event-triggered mean over 0 to 1 s is larger for CP-RF; (b) the same on rates divided by each group's mean over -0.5 to 0 s. Reproduced when significant bins exist at the troughs of the VISp rate and the range is larger for CP-RF under a reading.

claims.statement: During VISp alpha events, CP-RF units are more coherent with VISp in the 3 to 7 Hz band than CP-noRF units (p = 3.8e-14, 439 events).
claims.source: Results, Fine-scale alpha rhythm coupling between visual cortex and striatum, paragraph 4; Figure 8F
claims.quote: As predicted, CP-RF units displayed higher coherence with VISp in the 3–7 Hz band, indicating that alpha events coordinate functionally related cortico-striatal subnetworks.
claims.criterion: As in code cells 37 and 38, per qualifying VISp event (header) the coherence of each CP group's population rate (10 ms bins, 4 s) with the VISp population rate minus the random-time coherence (readings R1 and R2), mean over 3 to 7 Hz; paired Wilcoxon signed-rank of CP-RF against CP-noRF over events. Reproduced when CP-RF is higher at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Tissue came from 58 macaques, 23 male and 35 female, 48 Macaca nemestrina and 10 Macaca mulatta, aged 2 to 19 years.
claims.source: STAR Methods, Experimental model and study participant details, Macaque specimens
claims.quote: Male ( n = 23) and female ( n = 35) Macaca Nemestrina ( n = 48) and Macaca Mulatta ( n = 10) from 2 to 19 years old
claims.criterion: Counted over the subjects of the dataset's files, by subject identifier, sex and species. The 58 animals include donors whose tissue gave no recording in this dataset (the Methods count animals used in the study); the count of animals with at least one file is reported against 58.

claims.statement: The physiology analysis rests on 333 recordings, 300 of them new in this study, plus 20 cells from a previous M1 study and 13 from a Patch-seq methods study.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq reveals subclass and areal distinctions, paragraph 2; STAR Methods, Neurophysiology features, paragraph 1
claims.quote: For the current study, we presented data from 300 new patch-clamp/Patch-seq experiments, 168 of which were included in transcriptomic analyses. We also included data from 20 cells from a previously published study on M1 ... and 13 cells from a Patch-seq methods manuscript
claims.criterion: Counted as cells with current clamp data in the dataset. Two readings of what the dataset should hold, both reported, are (a) all 333 cells; (b) the 300 new cells only, as the 33 earlier cells were published with other datasets. Reproduced when the count matches either reading within tolerance.

claims.statement: 177 Patch-seq samples passed transcriptomic quality control (66 failed) and mapped to infragranular glutamatergic types of the reference taxonomy.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq reveals subclass and areal distinctions, paragraph 1; Figure 2D, 2E; Figure S2A
claims.quote: Using this approach, we collected 177 high-quality Patch-seq samples
claims.criterion: QC as in STAR Methods, Patch-seq sample mapping. A sample passes when its normalized marker sum (NMS) exceeds 0.7 and its correlation score to the MTG reference is at least 0.525, after correlation-based mapping with scrattch.mapping to the macaque MTG reference (Jorstad et al. 2023).

claims.statement: Retrogradely labelled corticospinal neurons map to the L5 ET subclass, 15 of 16 with the MTG reference and 16 of 16 with the M1 reference.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq reveals subclass and areal distinctions, paragraph 1; Figure 2F; Figure S2E
claims.quote: Retrogradely labeled CS neurons mapped to the L5 ET subclass in both the MTG (15 of 16 samples) and M1 (16 of 16 samples) reference taxonomy
claims.criterion: The CS samples are those tdTomato-positive after the spinal AAV-retro injection that passed QC (cell_counts.ipynb selects projection_type CS among QC-passing samples). Reproduced when the counts match within tolerance.

claims.statement: In the UMAP of the physiology features, CS neurons lie only among the transcriptomic L5 ET neurons and overlap little with non-ET neurons, regardless of preparation, area and species.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq reveals subclass and areal distinctions, paragraph 3; Figure 3A to 3C; Figure S3A
claims.quote: CS neurons (triangles) exclusively distributed with the transcriptomically defined L5 ET neurons ( Figure 3A ) and had little overlap with non-L5 ET neurons. This separation did not depend upon slice preparation type
claims.criterion: The embedding as in STAR Methods, Physiology UMAP and classification, and UMAPprojections_020724.ipynb: the 40 features of the code's list; cells with more than 75% of features missing excluded; missing values imputed as the mean of the 2 nearest neighbours (KNNImputer) and features z-scored, separately for acute and cultured cells; PCA, keeping components that explain at least 1% of variance; UMAP with 25 neighbours, min_dist 0.1, Euclidean metric, random_state 20. The paper gives no measure of "exclusively distributed with". Two readings, both the reader's, both run: (a) in the two-dimensional embedding, the nearest transcriptomically labelled non-CS neighbour of every CS neuron is an L5 ET neuron; (b) in the space of the retained PCs, at least 9 of the 10 nearest labelled non-CS neighbours of each CS neuron are L5 ET, for at least 90% of CS neurons. Reproduced when both hold; partially when one does. The same rule is reported within each preparation, area and species.

claims.statement: A logistic regression classifier trained on physiology predicts transcriptomic subclass (L5 ET, L5 IT, L5/6 NP, L6 IT) with 92.8% accuracy weighted across subclasses on the whole dataset, 87.9% holding out 50% and 82.2% holding out 75%; for L5 ET it is 98.6% and 93.8% (75% held out).
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq reveals subclass and areal distinctions, paragraph 4; Figure 3E to 3G
claims.quote: Classifiers trained and tested on 100% of the dataset had an average accuracy of 92.8% weighted across subclasses ... Classification was especially robust for the L5 ET subclass, where accuracy was 98.6% when trained on 100% of the dataset and dropped to 93.8% when holding out 75% of the dataset for cross-validation.
claims.criterion: Training cells are QC-passing Patch-seq samples and CS neurons (labelled L5 ET); subclasses with 5 or fewer cells are dropped (classifier_features_070523.ipynb), leaving L5 ET, L5 IT, L5/6 NP and L6 IT. Features preprocessed as in fig3a-cs-with-l5et. Multiclass logistic regression on the feature z-scores; 100 repeats each of training on 100%, a random 50% and a random 25% of cells, testing on the held-out cells (on all cells for 100%), predictions aggregated. Open, as predict_subclass was not deposited: the regularization and solver (standard choice: scikit-learn defaults, L2 with C = 1, lbfgs, max_iter raised until convergence) and whether the random split is stratified (both run). The score: the Results say "average accuracy weighted across subclasses", the Methods "average f1 scores", and the code prints per-class f1 (0.986 for L5 ET at 100%, matching the 98.6%). Readings, all run: (a) support-weighted mean of per-class f1; (b) per-class recall (diagonal of the row-normalized confusion matrix) averaged with class weights. Reproduced when, under one reading, every value is within tolerance.

claims.statement: Classifiers built on sparse principal components of the physiology features perform similarly to those built on the features.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq reveals subclass and areal distinctions, paragraph 4; Figure S3B
claims.quote: Similar results were obtained by building classifiers using sparse principal components (sPC) of physiology features
claims.criterion: Sparse PCA with 8 components, alpha 7, random_state 0 on the preprocessed features (classifier_features_070523.ipynb), then the procedure of fig3e-classifier-accuracy on the 8 component scores. "Similar" has no measure in the paper; the reader's reading is that each of the five scores of fig3e is within 10 percentage points of the feature-based score computed here. Reproduced when all five are; partially when three or four are.

claims.statement: In three-way ANOVAs of each physiological feature on projection type, preparation and cortical area, effect sizes are on average largest for projection type.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq reveals subclass and areal distinctions, paragraph 5; Figure 3H
claims.quote: While preparation type and cortical area contributed to some variance, effect sizes, on average, were largest for neuronal projection type
claims.criterion: Cells with a subclass (transcriptomic, CS, or predicted by the classifier trained on all labelled cells; predicted_subclass in L5_physiology_121223.csv), projection class L5 ET against all others. For each of the 40 features, OLS with projection class, preparation, area and all their interactions, type II sums of squares (UMAPprojections_020724.ipynb); Figure 3H plots the median effect size per factor over the 40 features. Effect size as in the Methods, partial eta squared SS_effect/(SS_effect + SS_residual); the code's formula (opening comment) is run as a variant. Reproduced when the median partial eta squared over features is larger for projection class than for preparation and for area.

claims.statement: Among features differing between L5 ET and non-ET neurons, the largest effect sizes are for subthreshold, HCN-related properties, resonant frequency, input resistance and the 3 dB cutoff.
claims.source: Results, L5 ET and non-ET neurons are differentiated, paragraph 1; Figure 4A
claims.quote: The features with the largest effect size were those related to subthreshold membrane properties and HCN conductance (resonant frequency, input resistance, and 3dB cutoff).
claims.criterion: From the ANOVAs of fig3h-projection-largest-effect, the features whose projection effect has BH-corrected p at most 0.05 (the code corrects across the 40 features for each main effect) ranked by the projection effect size. "Input resistance" can be the maximum or the steady-state input resistance (both are features); either counts. Reproduced when the three highest-ranked features are resonant frequency, an input resistance and the 3 dB cutoff; partially when two of them are in the top three and the third in the top five.

claims.statement: L5 ET neurons have a higher resonant frequency than non-ET neurons in both the MCx and the TCx, and in both acute and cultured slices.
claims.source: Results, L5 ET and non-ET neurons are differentiated, paragraph 1; Figure 4B, 4C; Figure S3C
claims.quote: L5 ET neurons had a higher resonant frequency ... and a lower input resistance than non-L5 ET neurons regardless of other factors
claims.criterion: Resonant frequency as defined in the opening comment, on the cells of Figure 4C (147 L5 ET and 177 non-ET with the feature). Reproduced when the projection effect in the three-way ANOVA of fig3h has BH-corrected p < 0.05 and the L5 ET mean exceeds the non-ET mean within each area and within each preparation; partially when the effect holds but the direction fails in one area or preparation. Cell counts are reported against 147 and 177.

claims.statement: Maximum input resistance is lower in L5 ET than in non-ET neurons in both the MCx and the TCx, and in both preparations.
claims.source: Figure 4D, 4E legend; Figure S3C
claims.quote: Maximum input resistance is lower in L5 ET neurons ( n = 145) than non-ET neurons ( n = 173) in both the MCx and TCx.
claims.criterion: Maximum input resistance as defined in the opening comment, on 145 L5 ET and 173 non-ET cells. Reproduced when the projection effect of the three-way ANOVA has BH-corrected p < 0.05 and the L5 ET mean is below the non-ET mean within each area and each preparation; partially when the effect holds but the direction fails in one group.

claims.statement: L5 ET neurons have faster action potential kinetics than non-ET neurons, with larger maximum and minimum dV/dt and a shorter half-width, and faster repolarization in both areas and preparations.
claims.source: Results, L5 ET and non-ET neurons are differentiated, paragraph 1; Figure 4F, 4G; Figure S3C
claims.quote: exhibiting faster action potential kinetics ... Action potential repolarization was faster in L5 ET neurons compared with non-ET neurons in both neocortical areas and preparations
claims.criterion: Max dV/dt, min dV/dt and half-width of the first spike at rheobase of the 1 s steps, as defined in the opening comment; Figure 4G has 148 L5 ET and 176 non-ET cells. For each of the three features the projection effect of the three-way ANOVA (BH-corrected p < 0.05) with L5 ET faster (larger max dV/dt, more negative min dV/dt, shorter half-width). Reproduced when all three hold and min dV/dt is faster in L5 ET within each area and each preparation; partially when min dV/dt holds and one of the other two does not.

claims.statement: Projection type by area interactions are small; no feature differs strongly between L5 ET and non-ET neurons in one area and not the other.
claims.source: Results, L5 ET and non-ET neurons are differentiated, paragraph 1; Figure S3D
claims.quote: Notably, projection type-by-area interactions were small, suggesting that no features were strongly different between L5 ET and non-ET neurons in one area and not the other
claims.criterion: A claim stated as small effect sizes, not as a test. From the three-way ANOVAs of fig3h, the projection by area interaction effect size of each feature. The paper gives no threshold; the reader's readings, both run, are (a) every interaction partial eta squared is below the median projection main effect over the 40 features; (b) for every feature whose interaction has p < 0.05 (uncorrected, as the code selects them for Figure S3D), L5 ET and non-ET differ in the same direction in both areas. Reproduced when both hold.

claims.statement: A four-way ANOVA on species, preparation, area and subclass finds no significant effect of species on any of the 40 physiological features.
claims.source: STAR Methods, Neurophysiology features, last paragraph
claims.quote: Initial analyses involving a 4-way ANOVA with species, preparation, area, and subclass as the factors revealed no significant effects of species on any of the 40 physiological features extracted for analysis.
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the paper's test, a four-way ANOVA per feature. The code for it was not deposited. Taken from the code's other ANOVAs: OLS with all interactions, type II sums of squares, BH correction across the 40 features for the species main effect (the Methods say p values were FDR adjusted). "Subclass" is open: (a) projection class, L5 ET against non-ET, as in the three-way ANOVA; (b) the predicted subclass. Species from the subject metadata. Reproduced when the corrected species p is at least 0.05 for every feature under the reading run; when the readings differ the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified. The smallest species p and its feature are reported, and the uncorrected count is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Within TCx, physiological features do not differ significantly between L5 ET transcriptomic types (FDR-corrected p > 0.066), though some effect sizes are large.
claims.source: Results, L5 ET and non-ET neurons are differentiated, paragraph 2; Figure S3G, S3H
claims.quote: Although we did not detect statistically significant differences between L5 ET types (FDR-corrected p > 0.066), effect sizes for some features were large
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. TCx L5 ET neurons with a t-type from the MTG mapping (cluster_Corr_label_MTG in cell_list_L5.csv), the types with enough cells (Figure S3H names ET_1 with 25 and ET_2 with 19). The test is not named; the Methods list ANOVAs, t-tests, Mann-Whitney U tests and BH correction. Readings, all run: (a) two-sided Welch t-test per feature, as the code's other two-group comparisons, BH across the 40 features; (b) two-way ANOVA on type and preparation, type effect, BH across features. Reproduced when no feature reaches corrected p < 0.05 under every reading; not reproduced when one does under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings differ. The smallest corrected p and the largest Cohen's d are reported.

claims.statement: In the Patch-seq data, 47 ion channel, neurofilament and axonal targeting genes differ between L5 ET and non-ET neurons (partial eta squared at least 0.05), 21 of them also found in the snRNA-seq data, including HCN1 and PEX5L higher in L5 ET.
claims.source: Results, L5 ET and non-ET neurons are differentiated, paragraph 3; Figure 4H; Figure S4A to S4C
claims.quote: we identified 47 ion channel, neurofilament, and axonal targeting genes from our Patch-seq data with significantly different expression between L5 ET and non-ET neurons
claims.criterion: As in STAR Methods, Gene expression analysis, and Interareal_Project_Patch_seq_Tdata_Comparisons_wStats.ipynb. log2(CPM + 1) of the 442 curated genes (gene_list.csv); genes with at least 0.5 log2 difference of medians between L5 ET and non-ET; three-way ANOVA on area, projection type and preparation; projection effect FDR-corrected p < 0.05 and effect size at least 0.05 (standard partial eta squared, the code's formula as variant). Reproduced when the counts are within tolerance.

claims.statement: In the Patch-seq data, 43 curated genes differ between L5 ET neurons of MCx and TCx (partial eta squared at least 0.05), 10 of them also found in the snRNA-seq data, among them KCNN2, KCNN3, KCNC2, DPP6 and CACNA1A.
claims.source: Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations in the L5 ET subclass, paragraphs 1 and 5; Figure S4D to S4F; Figure S6E
claims.quote: We identified 43 genes with significantly different expression and with η 2 ≥ 0.05 between L5 ET neurons from the MCx versus TCx
claims.criterion: As fig4h-patchseq-genes-et, restricted to L5 ET samples, with the 0.5 log2 difference between areas and a two-way ANOVA on area and preparation (Figure S4E), area effect, BH-corrected p < 0.05 and effect size at least 0.05. The overlap is counted against the genes of fig1-snrna-genes-area. Reproduced when both counts are within tolerance.

claims.statement: In the human and macaque snRNA-seq references, 29 curated genes differ between L5 ET and non-ET subclasses (at least 0.5 log2-fold, partial eta squared at least 0.05), including KCNN1, KCNN2, SCN4B, HCN1 and NEFH.
claims.source: Results, Differences in ion channel- and neurofilament-related gene expression, paragraph 3; Figure 1D; Figure S1E, S1F
claims.quote: we identified 29 genes with ... between L5 ET and non-ET neuronal subclasses
claims.criterion: As in STAR Methods, Gene expression analysis, and RNA_seq10x_human and macaque.ipynb. 50 nuclei sampled per subclass, species and area (random_state 1); log2(CPM + 1); at least 0.5 log2 difference of medians; three-way ANOVA (area, projection type, species), type II; projection effect BH-corrected p < 0.05 and effect size at least 0.05 (standard partial eta squared, the code's formula as variant). Reproduced when the count is within tolerance.

claims.statement: Within the L5 ET subclass, 30 curated genes differ between M1 and MTG in the snRNA-seq references, including SK channel genes, KCNC2 and KCNIP1.
claims.source: Results, Differences in ion channel- and neurofilament-related gene expression, paragraph 4; Figure 1E; Figure S1G
claims.quote: We identified 30 genes with significantly different expression and with ... between L5 ET neurons in M1 versus MTG datasets
claims.criterion: As fig1-snrna-genes-et, restricted to L5 ET nuclei, with the 0.5 log2 difference between areas and a two-way ANOVA on area and species, area effect.

claims.statement: Several MCx L5 ET neurons, including CS neurons, have long "tap root" basal dendrites reaching about 1.4 mm from the soma; TCx L5 ET neurons have none but have more complex apical tufts.
claims.source: Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations in the L5 ET subclass, paragraph 2; Figure 5A; Figure S5A, S5B
claims.quote: possessed prominent ... basal dendrites that, in the most extreme cases, extended ~1.4 mm from the soma
claims.criterion: On the 12 MCx and 11 TCx reconstructions. The paper defines no measure of a tap root, and "extended ~1.4 mm from the soma" can be read as (a) the maximum Euclidean distance of a basal dendrite tip from the soma or (b) the maximum basal path distance (basal_dendrite_max_path_distance, a feature of the morphology code); both are run. Reproduced when, under one reading, the MCx maximum is within tolerance of 1.4 mm and every TCx value is below the MCx median (the reader's measure of "lacked tap root dendrites altogether"; the paper gives none).

claims.statement: L5 ET neurons in TCx have more dendrite in L1, those in MCx more dendrite in deeper layers.
claims.source: Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations in the L5 ET subclass, paragraph 2; Figure 5B
claims.quote: The total length of dendrites in each layer differed between neocortical areas, with L5 ET neurons in the TCx having more dendrites in L1 and L5 ET neurons in the MCx having more dendrites in deeper layers
claims.criterion: Dendrite length per layer from the reconstructions aligned to the pia-white matter axis (skeleton_keys). Layer boundaries are not given for these slices; the paper's own layer-aligned features are the reading. The paper reports no test; reproduced when the mean L1 dendrite length is larger in TCx and the mean length in L5 and L6 is larger in MCx.

claims.statement: MCx L5 ET neurons have longer basal dendrites extending farther horizontally, and TCx L5 ET neurons have more apical branches and a higher maximum apical branch order.
claims.source: Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations in the L5 ET subclass, paragraph 2; Figure 5C, 5D
claims.quote: Basal dendrites were longer (FDR-corrected p = 0.0008, two-sided t test, d = 2.22) and extended farther in the horizontal direction (FDR-corrected p = 0.0006, two-sided t test, d = 2.65) in the MCx compared to the TCx, and L5 ET neurons in the TCx had both more apical dendrite branches (FDR-corrected p = 0.009, two-sided t test, d = 1.56) and higher-order apical dendrite branches
claims.criterion: Features from skeleton_keys and neuron_morphology after shrinkage correction (STAR Methods, Morphology feature analysis). As in morphology.ipynb, Welch t-test per feature, BH correction across all features (apical depth PCs and axon features excluded), absolute Cohen's d with pooled SD. The features are read as basal_dendrite_max_path_distance (or total length, both run) for "longer", basal_dendrite_extent_x for "horizontal", apical_dendrite_num_branches and apical_dendrite_max_branch_order. The deposited notebook printed other values (extent_x corrected p 0.0015, d 2.79; max branch order d 2.11), so the paper's numbers came from another run. Reproduced when all four differ at corrected p < 0.05 in the stated direction; the d values are compared with tolerance.

claims.statement: A classifier predicts the area of an L5 ET neuron from dendritic features with 100% accuracy on the whole dataset, 91.9% weighted f1 holding out 50% and 76.1% holding out 75%.
claims.source: Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations in the L5 ET subclass, paragraph 3; Figure 5E
claims.quote: the classifier obtained an accuracy of 100% when trained and tested on the whole dataset and maintained better-than-chance levels of performance when holding out 50% (average weighted f1 score = 91.9%) or 75% (average weighted f1 score = 76.1%)
claims.criterion: As in morphology.ipynb, imputation and scaling as for physiology, logistic regression, 100 repeats per training fraction (100%, 50%, 25%), weighted f1. Classifier settings open as in fig3e-classifier-accuracy. The deposited notebook printed 0.900 and 0.741.

claims.statement: Two-way ANOVAs (preparation and area) show substantial cross-areal variation in subthreshold and suprathreshold properties of L5 ET neurons.
claims.source: Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations in the L5 ET subclass, paragraph 4; Figure 6A
claims.quote: This analysis revealed substantial cross-areal variation in subthreshold and suprathreshold properties
claims.criterion: L5 ET neurons as in the code (predicted_subclass L5 ET, L5ET_121223.csv; Figure 6 has 77 or 78 MCx and 70 TCx cells). For each of the 40 features, OLS on area, preparation and their interaction, type II, BH correction across features per term (L5ET.ipynb; its feature list now also holds three AHP features, AHP_area, AHP_duration and AHP, which the deposited ET_cross_p.csv does not hold, so the 40 are the reading). The code's corrected area p values (ET_cross_p.csv) are below 0.05 for 19 of the 40 features, among them Fr, cutoff, zap_tau, initial_ifreq_gain, max_ifreq_gain, up_down_ratio, f_AHP, MaxRn, SSRn, MaxZ, AP_HW, min_dvdt and threshold_current. "Substantial" has no measure; reproduced when at least one subthreshold (chirp or input resistance) and one suprathreshold (spike or firing) feature have corrected area p < 0.05, and the count of such features is reported against 19.

claims.statement: L5 ET neurons in the MCx have a higher resonant frequency and a higher 3 dB cutoff than those in the TCx.
claims.source: Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations in the L5 ET subclass, paragraph 4; Figure 6B
claims.quote: Resonant frequency and the 3dB cutoff in response to the chirp stimulus were higher in L5 ET neurons in the MCx compared to the TCx
claims.criterion: From the two-way ANOVAs of fig6a, the area effects for resonant frequency (77 MCx, 70 TCx in Figure 6B) and 3 dB cutoff. Reproduced when both have BH-corrected p < 0.05 with the MCx mean higher; partially when one does. The paper's code obtained means of 5.16 and 3.30 Hz (fR) and 10.99 and 8.10 Hz (cutoff), MCx and TCx, corrected p 5.7e-5 and 3.1e-4 (ETmean_sem.csv, ET_cross_p.csv); these are reported alongside, not as targets.

claims.statement: L5 ET neurons in the MCx have a more pronounced fast AHP and faster, more symmetrical action potentials (lower ratio of max to min dV/dt) than those in the TCx.
claims.source: Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations in the L5 ET subclass, paragraph 4; Figure 6C to 6E
claims.quote: L5 ET neurons in the MCx had a more pronounced fast afterhyperpolarization (fAHP) and exhibited faster, more symmetrical ... action potentials compared to those in the TCx
claims.criterion: The Figure 6D and 6E legend says the opposite for the fAHP and for symmetry ("TCx ... have a deeper fast AHP ... than ... MCx ... and are more symmetrical"); the Results and the code's means (fAHP -14.18 mV MCx, -10.74 mV TCx; up/down ratio 2.84 and 3.57) agree with each other, so the Results are tested and the legend is recorded as a paper inconsistency. From the ANOVAs of fig6a: fAHP (more negative relative to threshold in MCx), up/down ratio (lower in MCx), and "faster" read as (a) shorter half-width and (b) more negative min dV/dt (the code finds max dV/dt not different, corrected p 0.13). Reproduced when fAHP, the up/down ratio and one reading of "faster" have corrected area p < 0.05 in the stated direction; partially when two of the three do.

claims.statement: The input resistance of L5 ET neurons is lower in MCx than in TCx, in both acute and cultured slices.
claims.source: Figure S6B legend, left
claims.quote: the input resistance of L5 ET neurons is lower in MCx (n = 76) compared with TCx (n = 68) in both acute and culture preparations (FDR corrected p = 0.003, area effect, 2-way ANOVA)
claims.criterion: The legend does not say which input resistance; the code's corrected area p is 0.0033 for steady-state (SSRn) and 0.0081 for maximum input resistance (MaxRn), so SSRn matches the printed p. Both are run. Reproduced when the area effect has corrected p < 0.05 with MCx lower, and MCx is lower within each preparation, for SSRn; MaxRn is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: MCx L5 ET neurons need more current to start spiking than TCx L5 ET neurons.
claims.source: Figure S6B legend, middle; Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations, paragraph 5
claims.quote: the current required to generate spiking in L5 ET neurons is higher in MCx (n = 78) compared to TCx (n = 70; FDR corrected p = 0.0496, area effect 2-way ANOVA)
claims.criterion: Rheobase as the lowest 1 s step amplitude that evokes a spike (the code's threshold_current; its corrected area p is 0.049). Reproduced when the area effect has corrected p < 0.05 with MCx higher. As p is near 0.05, the uncorrected p and the effect size are reported.

claims.statement: The slope of the average-rate FI curve (maximum gain) does not differ between MCx and TCx L5 ET neurons.
claims.source: Figure S6B legend, right; Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations, paragraph 5
claims.quote: the slope of the average firing rate FI curve (max gain) is not different between areas (MCx, n = 78; TCx, n = 70; FDR corrected p = 0.869, area effect 2-way ANOVA)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the paper's test, the area effect of the two-way ANOVA with BH correction across features. Maximum gain as in the code, the largest step-to-step increase in spike count of the 1 s steps divided by the current step (Hz/pA). The code's corrected p is 0.850, not the printed 0.869. Reproduced when corrected p is at least 0.05; the means and partial eta squared are reported either way.

claims.statement: TCx L5 ET neurons fire onset doublets or bursts, so both the initial and the maximum slope of the maximum instantaneous FI curve are higher in TCx than in MCx.
claims.source: Results, Regional morpho-electric specializations in the L5 ET subclass, paragraph 5; Figure 6F to 6H
claims.quote: In the TCx, L5 ET neurons exhibited doublets or high-frequency bursts of action potentials at the onset of the current that were rarely observed elsewhere in the sweep or in MCx L5 ET neurons
claims.criterion: The paper quantifies the bursts through the slopes of the maximum instantaneous rate (1/ISI min) against current on the 1 s steps: initial gain is the slope where the neuron begins firing (the first suprathreshold step and the step before it) and maximum gain the largest step-to-step slope, each divided by the current step (Figure 6H has 69 TCx and 78 MCx). From the ANOVAs of fig6a, reproduced when both have corrected area p < 0.05 with TCx higher; partially when only the initial slope does. The code obtained corrected p 5.7e-5 and 4.7e-4 and initial-slope means of 0.28 (TCx) and 0.10 (MCx) Hz/pA.

claims.statement: At maximal current injections MCx L5 ET neurons sustain higher average firing rates than TCx L5 ET neurons.
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 2; Figure S6C
claims.quote: L5 ET neurons in the MCx sustained higher average spike counts compared to L5 ET neurons in the TCx at maximal current injections ... maximal average firing rate, p = 0.0002, two-sided t test, d = 1.0
claims.criterion: Cells: the L5 ET neurons recorded with 1 s steps increasing by 200 pA up to 4 nA (STAR Methods), 42 MCx and 26 TCx (keys of MCx.pkl and TCx.pkl). Per cell the maximum over steps of the spike count in the 1 s step; Welch t-test and pooled-SD Cohen's d (ExtendedFI.ipynb, which printed means 101.6 MCx and 76.0 TCx, p 0.00024, d 1.00). Reproduced when p < 0.05 with MCx higher and d within tolerance; partially when only the test holds.

claims.statement: TCx L5 ET neurons reach higher instantaneous rates below 1 nA, but at up to 4 nA MCx L5 ET neurons fire at equivalent maximal instantaneous rates.
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 2; Figure S6D
claims.quote: MCx neurons were capable of firing equivalently at higher current injection amplitudes ... maximal instantaneous firing rate, p = 0.99, two-sided t test, d = 0.003
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the paper's test. Per cell the maximum over all steps of the maximum instantaneous rate 1/ISI(min); Welch t-test (ExtendedFI.ipynb printed 243.8 Hz TCx and 244.1 Hz MCx, p 0.99). Reproduced when p is at least 0.05; Cohen's d is reported. The first clause (TCx higher below 1 nA) rests on Figure S6D alone with no test; the mean maximum instantaneous rate per area at each step below 1 nA is shown and does not decide the outcome.

claims.statement: At high current amplitudes, TCx L5 ET neurons undergo depolarization block far more often than MCx L5 ET neurons (14 of 26 against 1 of 42).
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 6J, 6K and S6C, S6D (arrows)
claims.quote: L5 ET neurons in the TCx were more likely to undergo depolarization-induced block of action potential generation in response to these higher current injection amplitudes (MCx = 1 of 42 neurons; TCx = 14 of 26 neurons)
claims.criterion: Block is "a negative slope in the average rate FI curves" (STAR Methods). The readings are (a) any decrease of spike count from one step to the next; (b) the spike count at the largest step below the maximum of the curve. Reproduced when, under one reading, both counts are within tolerance (1 of 42 exactly, 13 to 15 of 26); partially when, under one reading, the TCx proportion exceeds the MCx proportion but a count is outside tolerance. The paper reports no test; a Fisher exact test is shown as a variant and does not decide the outcome.

claims.statement: At the maximal average firing rate, spike width more than doubles from first to last spike in TCx L5 ET neurons but increases only 1.5 times in MCx L5 ET neurons.
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 6J
claims.quote: At the maximal average firing rates, the spike width in TCx L5 ET neurons more than doubled, whereas MCx L5 ET neuron spike widths only increased 1.5 times ... p = 1.7e−09, two-sided t test, d = 2.02
claims.criterion: Per cell, the step with the most spikes; at that step the ratio of the half-width of the last spike to that of the first; Welch t-test and Cohen's d (ExtendedFI.ipynb printed 2.27 TCx, 1.53 MCx). The code takes the argmax over steps with nonzero spike counts and uses that index into the full array; when steps without spikes precede firing this picks a later step. Readings, both run: (a) the step with the most spikes; (b) the code's indexing. Reproduced when the TCx mean exceeds 2, the MCx mean is within tolerance of 1.5, p < 0.05 and d within tolerance, under one reading.

claims.statement: At the maximal average firing rate, max dV/dt of the last spike falls to about 20% of the first in TCx L5 ET neurons but only to about 50% in MCx.
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 6K
claims.quote: Similarly, the maximum dVdt decreased to ~20% of the first spike value in TCx neurons versus only ~50% in the MCx ... p = 3.2e−10, two-sided t test, d = 1.69
claims.criterion: As fig6j-spike-width-ratio, for the ratio of max dV/dt of the last to the first spike (ExtendedFI.ipynb printed 0.221 TCx and 0.520 MCx, p 3.2e-10, d 1.69). The values are "~20%" and "~50%"; reproduced when both means and d are within tolerance and p < 0.05 under one reading; partially when the test holds and one mean is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: During 10 s near-rheobase steps, MCx L5 ET neurons fire more irregularly (higher CV of ISIs) than TCx L5 ET neurons across a wide range of firing rates.
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 3; Figure S7F, S7G
claims.quote: which revealed more variable ISIs in MCx L5 ET neurons across a wide range of average firing rates during the 10-s current step
claims.criterion: Sweeps of the 10 s steps with at least 10 spikes; spikes in the first 100 ms excluded; CV = SD/mean of the ISIs (STAR Methods); each sweep is an observation. The second factor of the two-way ANOVA is not named; Figure S7G bins CV by the number of spikes in the sweep, so the reading is area by spike-count bin. The bin edges are not given; readings, both run: (a) bins of 10 spikes; (b) bins of 25 spikes. The code was not deposited. Reproduced when the area effect has p < 0.001 with MCx higher under both readings; partially when p < 0.05; observation and cell counts are reported against the legend's.

claims.statement: The peak frequency of subthreshold oscillations between spikes increases with membrane potential in MCx L5 ET neurons but not in TCx, by autocorrelation and by Fourier analysis.
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 3; Figure 7I, 7J
claims.quote: However, the peak frequency of these oscillations increased with membrane potential only in the MCx, whether measured from autocorrelation
claims.criterion: Method from STAR Methods (the R code was not deposited): sweeps of the 10 s steps with at least one spike and at most 200; interspike segments from the return to baseline after the AHP (found by fitting a curve) to 50 ms before the next spike; filtered 3 to 50 Hz; segments longer than 650 ms analysed by FFT (peak frequency and strength per segment) and a smoothing spline over segments for the sweep's peak frequency and strength; autocorrelogram over the last 1 s of segments longer than 1 s, frequency from its peaks and troughs; segments aggregated into 5 mV bins of membrane potential per cell, each cell-bin an observation; Pearson correlation over observations. Open, with standard choices: the curve fitted to find the return to baseline (standard: an exponential fit to the AHP decay, baseline reached within 1 mV of its asymptote), the filter (standard: zero-phase 4th-order Butterworth band-pass), the spline (standard: R smooth.spline defaults), and the autocorrelogram frequency (standard: 1 over the lag of the first peak after zero lag). These could change the values; the readings are run as stated and the counts of observations reported against the legend's. Reproduced when the MCx correlations are positive with p < 0.001 and the TCx correlations have p at least 0.05, for both measures; the r2 values are compared with tolerance. TCx r2 below 0.001 with p 0.146 on 82 observations is not self-consistent (such an r2 gives p near 0.8), so only p is used for TCx.

claims.statement: Oscillation strength increases modestly with membrane potential, significantly in MCx L5 ET neurons and not significantly in TCx.
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 3; Figure 7K
claims.quote: increased in power modestly as a function of membrane potential
claims.criterion: Method as fig7-oscillation-frequency-vm, with the spline-fitted FFT peak strength. Reproduced when the MCx correlation is positive with p < 0.001 and the TCx correlation is positive with p at least 0.05; partially when the MCx part holds only; the r2 values are compared with tolerance.

claims.statement: Subthreshold oscillations persist with fast synaptic transmission blocked, at a slightly reduced frequency, so they are intrinsic to the neuron.
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 3; Figure S7D, S7E
claims.quote: Oscillations occurred in the presence of blockers of fast synaptic transmission, albeit at a slightly reduced frequency
claims.criterion: Blockers (DNQX with d-APV and gabazine or picrotoxin) per cell from the recording metadata. Oscillation frequency as in fig7-oscillation-frequency-vm. The legend bins by number of spikes in the sweep; the two-way ANOVA is read as blocker by spike-count bin, with the bin edges open (bins of 10 and of 25 spikes, both run). Reproduced when oscillations are detected in cells with blockers and the blocker effect has p < 0.05 with lower frequency under both readings; partially when oscillations are present but the effect is not significant.

claims.statement: In MCx L5 ET neurons the modal instantaneous firing rate during spiking epochs is well correlated with the subthreshold oscillation frequency; in TCx it is not.
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 4; Figure 7L
claims.quote: Consequently, the instantaneous firing rate during spiking epochs was well correlated with the prominent subthreshold oscillatory frequency in L5 ET neurons in the MCx
claims.criterion: Modal firing rate is the most common value of 1/ISI over the 10 s step (STAR Methods); the binning of instantaneous rates to find a mode is not given (readings, both run, 1 Hz and 2 Hz bins). Observations as in Figure 7L, each a sweep with an FFT peak frequency. Reproduced when the MCx correlation is positive with p < 0.001 and r2 within tolerance and the TCx p is at least 0.05; partially when the MCx correlation holds with r2 outside tolerance.

claims.statement: MCx L5 ET neurons reach modal firing rates near 30 Hz while still having ISIs longer than 650 ms, whereas no TCx neuron with such ISIs has a modal rate above about 8 Hz.
claims.source: Results, Functional specializations of MCx L5 ET neurons, paragraph 4; Figure S7G
claims.quote: In the MCx, L5 ET modal firing rates were as high as ~30 Hz, accompanied with ISIs longer than 650 ms
claims.criterion: Over the 10 s sweeps that contain at least one ISI longer than 650 ms, the largest modal firing rate per area, modal rate as in fig7l. The TCx value is a bound in the paper ("no TCx neurons had modal firing rates greater than ~8 Hz"), so reproduced when, under one binning reading, the MCx maximum is within tolerance of 30 Hz and the TCx maximum is at most 8.8 Hz (8 Hz plus its tolerance).

claims.statement: Imaging a MORSE hydrogel through the GRIN lens shows 100 to 200 green sensor cells spread through the full thickness of the gel.
claims.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 1; Figure 1C
claims.quote: 3D two-photon imaging of the resultant hydrogel through the GRIN lens (30 planes/volume, ~600×600×270 μm 3 volume) demonstrated a uniformly distributed set of 100–200 green cells spanning the full thickness of the gel
claims.criterion: Neither the Methods nor the code say how the cells were counted. Readings (a) the number of cell masks extracted per recording before curation (CNMF components); (b) the number of curated cell masks per recording. Reproduced when the per-probe counts of a reading lie in 90 to 220 for most probes (more than half) and the cells occupy all depths of the gel (cell centres found in the top, middle and bottom thirds of the gel thickness). Needs masks or imaging.

claims.statement: Hydrogels of pure Matrigel deform substantially over tens of minutes; a mixture of Matrigel and collagen I deforms less.
claims.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 2; Figure 1D
claims.quote: The small hydrogel volume (~40 nL) on the GRIN lens tip, when composed of pure Matrigel, exhibited substantial global and local deformations over tens of minutes. We minimized these deformations using an optimized mixture of Matrigel and collagen I
claims.criterion: Deformation is the local strain magnitude, the mean over the hydrogel volume of the magnitude of the displacement field minus its mean (Figure 1D legend, Figure S1C; morse_figs1 cells 3, 92, 97), from demons registration of Cellpose probability maps to a reference volume. With n=6 probes per recipe imaged for 9 h, reproduced when the mean deformation across probes of the 50:50 recipe stays below that of pure Matrigel over the recording (mean over the 9 h lower, and lower at the end). The paper gives no test. Needs the deformation fields or raw imaging.

claims.statement: Treating the silicone surface with KOH before applying the gel strongly reduces gel warping and detachment during dipping; with the optimized protocol (40:60 Matrigel:collagen I with 2.5% KOH, against 50:50 without KOH) probe stability rose from about 10% to about 65% in initial tests.
claims.source: Methods, Optimization of MORSE manufacture, paragraph 1; Figure 1F; Figure S1D-E; Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 2
claims.quote: This allowed us to increase probe stability from ~10% to ~65% in initial tests ( Figure 1F )
claims.criterion: A probe is early warp when the 3D translation of the hydrogel (the norm of the mean displacement over the gel) exceeds 25 um in the first hour, late warp when it exceeds 25 um in the second hour, and stable otherwise (Figure 1F legend). Stable fraction over the 9 probes of 50:50 without KOH and the 24 of 40:60 with KOH. Variant (code, morse_figs1 cell 139), late warp as more than 50 um within 2 h. The code's comments (cell 126) give "~66% success" for the KOH group. The two groups differ in both recipe and KOH (Figure 1F legend), so the comparison does not separate the two. Of 9 probes, "~10%" can only be 1 (11%), recorded as a count. Needs the deformation fields or raw imaging.

claims.statement: In the revision experiments more than 90% of probes were stable, 10 of 13 in vitro dipping, 9 of 9 slice and 13 of 14 in vivo CSF experiments.
claims.source: Methods, Optimization of MORSE manufacture, paragraph 1
claims.quote: In revision experiments, >90% probe stability was achieved (n=10/13 in vitro dipping experiments, n=9/9 brain slice experiments, n=13/14 in vivo CSF experiments).
claims.criterion: The paper does not define stability for the revision experiments. Read as in fig1f-koh-stability (no translation above 25 um), the only definition the paper gives, made for dipping; for slice and in vivo recordings this is a reading. Counts are exact. The ">90%" does not follow from 10/13; the counts decide the claim. Needs deformation fields or raw imaging, and a record of which recordings were revision experiments.

claims.statement: Ten ten-sensor probes yielded 506 identified single-cell masks; per probe a median of 9 sensors were active (IQR 8 to 9), with on average 6.02 cells per sensor per probe.
claims.source: Figure 1G and legend; Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 4
claims.quote: we could assign clear sensor identities across several hundred cells from ten representative MORSE probes (median of 9 active sensors per probe, interquartile range 8–9; average of 6.02 cells per sensor per probe)
claims.criterion: From SENSOR IDENTITY on the identification dipping recordings of the ten ten-sensor probes. A sensor is active on a probe when at least one cell carries its label; there is no threshold (morse_figs3_rev cells 139-143). Cells per sensor per probe is the total number of cells divided by the number of (probe, sensor) pairs with at least one cell (cells 139, 144, 506/84). Percentiles by numpy's default linear interpolation (cell 142, which prints 8.25).

claims.statement: Dipping ten-sensor probes into each ligand in turn gave rapid, strong and consistent responses in a subset of cells for each ligand, and all ten sensors were activated.
claims.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 4; Figure 1G, Figure S3A
claims.quote: This resulted in rapid, strong, and consistent patterns of elevated fluorescence in subsets of cells evenly spread throughout the gel in response to each ligand
claims.criterion: Reproduced when each of the ten sensor labels is carried by cells on at least one of the ten probes, and the mean peak-normalized dF/F0 of each sensor's cells is highest during the well of its own ligand (Figure 1G heatmap; peak normalization by Eq. 28, mean of the highest 10% minus mean of the lowest 10%), except that the DA and NE sensors and the AVP and OXT sensors may also respond to each other's ligand (fig1h-crosstalk-pairs). Background correction by an exponential fit to the signal before activation (Methods), as in morse_figs3_rev cells 21-24.

claims.statement: Among the ten sensors, only the DA and NE sensors, and to a lesser extent the AVP and OXT sensors, show crosstalk in their ligand responses.
claims.source: Methods, Quantification and statistical analysis; Figure 1H, Figure S3B; Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Calculating the means of the derivative time courses across each cell cluster and cross-corelating them with each other consistently demonstrated that only the DA2.9 dopamine and the NE2h norepinephrine sensors, as well as to a lesser extent the AVP0.2 vasopressin and OXT1.7 oxytocin sensors, exhibited crosstalk in their ligand responses
claims.criterion: Per cell, the time derivative of the peak-normalized dF/F0 by a Savitzky-Golay filter (1-min window, order 1; Methods, which decide; morse_figs3_rev cell 216 uses 10 frames, shown as a variant), each divided by its own maximum (cell 218); the mean per sensor (cell 224); the Pearson correlation at zero lag between the ten sensor means (cell 227). The paper and the code set no threshold for crosstalk. Reproduced when the DA-NE correlation is the largest off-diagonal value, the AVP-OXT correlation is the second largest, and every other pair is lower than both. Variant (code, cell 219), a band-pass 3-minute dipping artefact subtracted before averaging.

claims.statement: The MORSE EC50 of each sensor for its own ligand, from consensus dose-response fits, is AVP 355 nM, OXT 2.19 uM, 5-HT 687 nM, CCK 245 nM, NE 4.04 uM, DA 1.70 uM, ACh 7.03 uM, ATP 75.2 uM, MT 22.0 nM and HA 6.39 uM.
claims.source: Table 1, EC50 (MORSE) column; Figure 1I, Figure S3C
claims.quote: We found that the sensors’ half-maximal effective concentrations (EC 50 , equivalent to a sensor’s apparent dissociation constant K d ) could be reliably estimated for all sensors ( Table 1 ; Figures 1I , S3C )
claims.criterion: Dose-response dipping of the ten probes of Figure 1G (two mixtures at 10-fold steps; Video S6). Per cell matched to a sensor identity, background corrected by an exponentially decaying fit and peak-normalized (Methods); the plateau in each well is the mean over the third minute (Methods). Fit Eq. 9 with Hill coefficient 1, y = F/(1 + Kd/[L]), by least squares (morse_figs3_rev cell 365, Powell minimization), to the cells of all probes pooled (consensus fit, Figure 1I). Variants (code, cell 339) the plateau as the median of sorted frames 47 to 78 of the 93-frame well, peak normalization to the 6th or 7th well, a stretched exponential background, cells dropped by a noise cut, and ACh, ATP, MT and HA pooled with an older probe set (cell 365, groups_merge_rev). The Methods and the code disagree on the plateau; the Methods reading decides and the code's is shown. Each value within 10%.

claims.statement: The crosstalk sensors respond to the partner ligand with EC50s of 28.7 uM (AVP sensor to OXT), 247 nM (OXT sensor to AVP), 9.35 uM (NE sensor to DA) and 8.20 uM (DA sensor to NE).
claims.source: Table 1, EC50 (MORSE) column; Figure S3C
claims.criterion: As table1-ec50-on-target, each sensor's cells fitted against the partner ligand's concentrations in the mixture wells, signals peak-normalized to the on-target maximum and scaled by the crosstalk ratio (morse_figs3_rev cells 365 and 368). Each value within 10%.

claims.statement: On MORSE probes the peak dF/F0 of each sensor to a saturating dose of its ligand is 0.37 (AVP), 0.24 (OXT), 0.36 (5-HT), 0.40 (CCK), 0.34 (NE), 0.27 (DA), 0.37 (ACh), 0.28 (ATP), 0.30 (MT) and 0.38 (HA), and to the partner ligand 0.10 (AVP sensor, OXT), 0.05 (OXT sensor, AVP), 0.15 (NE sensor, DA) and 0.21 (DA sensor, NE).
claims.source: Table 1, Peak dF/F0 (MORSE) column; Figure S3B
claims.criterion: Identification dipping of the ten probes of Figure 1G (Figure S3B ligands, 10 uM AVP, 100 uM OXT, 100 uM 5-HT, 10 uM CCK, 1 mM NE, 100 uM DA, 1 mM ACh, 1 mM ATP, 10 uM MT, 1 mM HA). Per cell, dF/F0 after background correction; the cell's peak is the maximum within the third minute of the ligand's well (morse_figs3_rev cell 160); the table value is the median across cells with a positive peak (cells 248 and 263; the S3B legend draws the median). For AVP, NE and CCK the code takes the well after the ligand well (cell 248); readings (a) the ligand well, (b) the code's well. Each value within 10%.

claims.statement: Dose-response relationships, after peak normalization and averaging over cells of the same sensor, are precise and consistent across probes.
claims.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 5; Figure 1I-J
claims.quote: peak-normalizing each cell’s signal and averaging across cells expressing the same sensor produced precise dose-response relationships that were consistent across probes ( Figures 1I - J , S3C )
claims.criterion: Per-probe EC50s are fitted as in table1-ec50-on-target to each probe's cells alone, for probes with more than one cell of the sensor (morse_figs3_rev cell 662); Figure 1J shows their mean and SEM across 5 to 8 probes per sensor (cells 677, 685). The paper does not say what consistent means. Readings (a) for every sensor, every per-probe EC50 lies within one 10-fold dose step of the consensus EC50 (between a tenth and ten times it); (b) for every sensor, the SEM across probes is less than half the mean. Reproduced when both hold; blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ.

claims.statement: Ligands diffuse quickly through the hydrogel; almost all sensors show an onset time constant under 1 minute, and most signals plateau within 1 minute.
claims.source: Figure S3E legend; Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Almost all sensors demonstrate a t-on under 1 minute, reflecting rapid diffusion of all ten ligands through the hydrogel to reach their sensors
claims.criterion: Per cell, an exponential rise (x0 - xinf)*exp(-t/tau) + xinf fitted to the first three minutes in the well with the lowest concentration of its ligand above the sensor's EC50 (Methods; S3E legend; morse_figs3_rev cells 688-692, which fit frames 0 to 78 after a 31-frame median filter, set xinf to the median of frames 47 to 78, and drop tau above 200 frames). Done on the peak-normalized dF/F0 and on the Eq. 8 concentration. "Almost all sensors" read as at least 8 of the 10 sensors with a median tau-on across cells under 60 s. The S3E legend plots both fits and does not say which one its sentence is about, and the Methods treat the concentration fit as the diffusion measure; readings (a) the dF/F0 fits, (b) the concentration fits (larger by construction, S3E legend). The outcome is the one both give; if they differ, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Onset times increase only modestly with cell depth in the gel, with a positive slope for all sensors except ATP.
claims.source: Figure S3F legend; Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Notably, all but one sensor demonstrate a small increase in t-on with increasing cell depth
claims.criterion: The concentration tau-on of figs3e-tau-on-under-one-minute against each cell's depth, the z centre of mass of its mask measured from the front face of the gel (morse_figs3_rev cells 712-718, 9.89 um per plane), a least-squares line per sensor. Reproduced when 9 of the 10 slopes are positive (tau-on rising with distance from the front face) and the ATP slope is the negative one. "Modest" is read as a slope below 1 s per um. Needs masks with depth.

claims.statement: Registration using probability maps of the GRAB signal stabilizes the images as well as or better than registration using the tdTomato channel, in dipping, slice and in vivo recordings.
claims.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 3; Figure S2C
claims.quote: Registration using Cellpose2.0 probability maps derived from the GRAB signals performed similarly to or better than those from tdTomato signals ( Figure S2C ; Video S4 )
claims.criterion: Image stability is the normalized cross-correlation of the GRAB probability map at each time with the first, restricted to voxels with at least 50% cell probability at the first timepoint (S2C legend; Methods, MORSE hydrogel deformation quantification; morse_figs2 cells 3-12 use skimage match_template on maps downsampled 4-fold in x and y). Over the dipping (n=36), slice (n=11) and in vivo (n=11) recordings with both channels, reproduced when both alignments raise the mean cross-correlation above the unaligned one and the GRAB-aligned mean is at least the tdTomato-aligned mean minus its SEM at most times. Needs raw imaging.

claims.statement: About 70 to 130 active sensor cells per probe can be tracked across 2 to 8 recordings in different contexts.
claims.source: Results, MORSE probe development and characterization, paragraph 3; Figure S2F
claims.quote: we could reliably track ~70–130 active sensor cells per probe across 2–8 sequential recordings in different contexts across up to 8 hours in total
claims.criterion: The number of cells matched across recordings of the same probe (S2F, dipping n=40 recordings over 10 probes, slice n=15, in vivo n=25). Reproduced when the per-probe mean of the matched counts lies in 63 to 143 for most probes. The code's printed counts (morse_figs2_2 cell 4) range from 53 to 108, which is noted.

claims.statement: Bath application of 50 mM KCl to dLGN slices activates the NE, DA and 5-HT sensors.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2; Figure 2B-C
claims.quote: Bath application of 50 mM KCl activated GRAB sensors for NE, DA, and 5-HT ( Figures 2B - C , top ; Video S7 )
claims.criterion: In the 9 dLGN recordings, POOLED-SLICE before peak normalization. Reproduced when, in most recordings, the NE, DA and 5-HT sensors' pooled dF/F0 rise during the KCl wash-on above 1.96 times their SD over the pre-KCl period (the Methods' robustness rule applied to dF/F0). The DA rise is accounted for by NE in fig2c-dlgn-da-explained-by-ne.

claims.statement: In dLGN slices the KCl responses of both the NE and the DA sensors are explained by release of NE alone, not a combination of DA and NE.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2; Figure 2C bottom, Figure S4B
claims.quote: Responses to KCl at both the NE and DA sensors could be explained solely by release of NE
claims.criterion: CONC by Eq. 19 on the pooled NE and DA sensor signals (POOLED-SLICE, CONSTANTS). Reproduced when, in most of the 9 recordings, the KCl-evoked NE concentration exceeds THRESH while the DA concentration stays below its THRESH during the KCl response window (PEAK readings). A claim of absence for DA; the paper uses the threshold, and its value is given either way.

claims.statement: KCl evoked robust NE responses in 9 of 9 dLGN slices and robust 5-HT responses in 7 of 9, with robustness thresholds of 348 nM (NE), 116 nM (DA) and 62.7 nM (5-HT).
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2; Figure 2C-D
claims.quote: Robust responses to KCl (defined as a peak-normalized ΔF/F 0 signal increases exceeding the 95% confidence interval above pre-wash-on baseline) were detected for NE in n=9/9 slices and for 5-HT in n=7/9 slices ( Figure 2D )
