claims.criterion: POOLED-SLICE, CONC (NE and DA by Eq. 19, 5-HT by Eq. 8), THRESH over the 9 dLGN recordings, PEAK with readings (a) and (b) for the KCl window, combined with the two readings of the peak normalization in POOLED-SLICE. Counts are exact. The THRESH variant is shown. The code that made these numbers is not in the repository (morse_fig2 gives other thresholds), so no code detail binds beyond the shared methods.

claims.statement: KCl-evoked peak concentrations at the dLGN were about 4.61 uM NE and 0.44 uM 5-HT.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2; Figure 2E
claims.quote: KCl-evoked peak concentrations were estimated at ~4.61 μM for NE and ~0.44 μM for 5-HT ( Figure 2E )
claims.criterion: PEAK of the CONC traces of fig2d-dlgn-robust-counts, averaged over recordings. Which recordings enter the mean is open. Readings (a) all 9 for both ligands; (b) all 9 for NE and the 7 robust ones for 5-HT. Each combined with the PEAK and POOLED-SLICE readings. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one combination.

claims.statement: In the dLGN the rise of the 5-HT sensor activation was delayed relative to the NE sensor by 111 s on average.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2; Figure 2F
claims.quote: The rise time of activation of the 5-HT sensor was delayed relative to that of the NE sensor by an average of 111 sec ( Figure 2F )
claims.criterion: TAU-RISE of the NE and 5-HT concentration traces of fig2d-dlgn-robust-counts, timed from KCl wash-on. Readings (a) the mean over the 7 recordings with both robust of the within-recording difference; (b) the mean 5-HT tau-rise over the 7 robust minus the mean NE tau-rise over all 9. Figure S4D's numbers imply mean tau-rise of about 240 s (NE) and 351 s (5-HT), whose difference is 111 s; these are reported beside the delay. Each combined with the PEAK and POOLED-SLICE readings.

claims.statement: Deconvolving the hydrogel transfer function sharpens the dLGN responses; the average NE and 5-HT tau-rise fall by 44.6 s (18.6%) and 63.9 s (18.2%), and the average peaks rise by 682 nM (14.8%) and 146 nM (33.3%), so true peaks occur up to 19% sooner and up to 33% higher.
claims.source: Figure S4D-E legends; Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 2
claims.quote: This resulted in sharper and narrower peak responses for each ligand, suggesting that the true peak concentrations at the slice surface occurred up to 19% sooner and were up to 33% higher than those recorded at the sensors within the hydrogel
claims.criterion: Deconvolve h(t) = (1/tau) exp(-t/tau) from each concentration trace of fig2d-dlgn-robust-counts (Methods Eq. 25-26) with tau per sensor the median of the dipping tau-on of figs3e-tau-on-under-one-minute; the code (morse_fig2_rev cell 160, morse_fig2 cell 427) uses scipy.signal.deconvolve after a Savitzky-Golay filter (20 frames, order 1). Open, whether tau comes from the dF/F0 fits or the concentration fits (S3E shows both); readings (a) dF/F0, (b) concentration. Then TAU-RISE and PEAK with and without deconvolution; percent changes are of the means across recordings (n=9 NE; 5-HT over the 7 robust, S4C-E legends). Reproduced when, under one reading, the four percentages are within tolerance; the absolute changes are reported.

claims.statement: KCl did not release enough AVP, OXT or HA from dLGN or PVH slices to drive their sensors; those sensor cells, present on the probes, responded only to post hoc dipping.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 2B right, Figure S5B
claims.quote: Most of these cells did not have matching cell masks in the slice experiment, indicating that they did not respond to bath application of NE, DA, or 5-HT, and that KCl did not elicit sufficient release of AVP, OXT, or HA from the slice to drive the respective sensors
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's robustness rule. In the dLGN and PVH recordings followed by dipping, the AVP, OXT and HA sensor cells identified by dipping either have no mask in the slice recording or, where matched, show no KCl response above 1.96 times their pre-KCl SD (POOLED-SLICE dF/F0). Reproduced when no recording shows such a response; the largest response is given either way. Needs the dipping-only cells and the matching.

claims.statement: Dipping a probe into KCl solutions does not drive the NE or DA sensors, so the slice responses come from KCl-evoked release, not a direct effect of KCl on the sensors.
claims.source: Figure S5C legend
claims.quote: Neither sensor is driven by dipping into any KCl solution, indicating that the KCl responses on the left heatmap in B correspond to KCl-induced ligand release from the PVH slice
claims.criterion: In the first post hoc dipping recording of the PVH probe of Figure S5B, the mean dF/F0 of the NE and DA sensor cells in each KCl well (1.56 to 50 mM) against the aCSF wells. A claim of absence, judged as the paper does on the robustness rule; reproduced when no KCl well raises either sensor above 1.96 times its SD over the preceding aCSF wells, while the DA and NE wells do. Sizes reported either way.

claims.statement: In the PVH, KCl activates the NE, DA and 5-HT sensors, and demixing shows that NE alone explains the NE and DA sensor responses.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 3; Figure S5B-E
claims.quote: quantitative estimation of NE and DA concentrations along with demixing of their combined effects at the DA sensor suggested that NE alone could explain the activation of both sensors in the PVH
claims.criterion: As fig2c-dlgn-da-explained-by-ne, on the 6 PVH recordings with THRESH computed over them. Reproduced when the NE concentration exceeds threshold during 25 or 50 mM KCl and the DA concentration stays below its threshold, in most recordings, and the two thresholds are within tolerance. The S5D legend gives them on one example, but the Methods define one threshold per dataset (the maximum SD across its recordings), so they are the PVH dataset's thresholds.

claims.statement: KCl drove robust elevations of both NE and 5-HT in all 6 PVH experiments.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 3; Figure S5F
claims.quote: KCl drove robust elevations in both NE and 5-HT in n=6/6 experiments ( Figure S5F )
claims.criterion: Robustness on the pooled NE and 5-HT sensor dF/F0 (S5F plots dF/F0 with thresholds; 5-HT was not converted to concentration, S5D legend), the threshold being 1.96 times the largest pre-KCl SD across the 6 recordings (THRESH before conversion). In 4 of the 6 the 5-HT identity is inferred from responding to KCl but not to DA or NE (S5F legend); the dataset's labels are used.

claims.statement: NE sensor cells in the PVH were reliably driven by 25 mM KCl, while 5-HT sensor cells needed 50 mM KCl to be fully activated.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 3; Figure S5G
claims.quote: While NE sensor cells were reliably driven by 25 mM KCl, 5-HT sensor cells consistently required a higher dose of KCl (50 mM) to be fully activated ( Figure S5G )
claims.criterion: Per recording, the peak pooled dF/F0 of each sensor at each KCl dose. The code (morse_fig2 cell 642) takes the median of the last 10 frames before the end of each lower dose, and the peak for 50 mM, with hand-set dose ends; the main reading is PEAK of dF/F0 within each dose period (from that dose's onset to the next onset), the code's as variant. "Reliably driven" and "fully activated" are not defined. Readings (a) the NE peak at 25 mM exceeds the threshold of figs5f-pvh-robust-counts in all 6, and the 5-HT peak at 25 mM is below it in all 6 and above it at 50 mM; (b) the NE peak at 25 mM is at least half its 50 mM peak, and the 5-HT peak at 25 mM is below half its 50 mM peak, in all 6.

claims.statement: The average NE concentration at the PVH with 50 mM KCl was 21.4 uM, nearly five times that at the dLGN.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 3; Figure S5F, H, I
claims.quote: The average NE concentration detected at the PVH in response to 50 mM KCl was 21.4 μM – nearly five-fold higher than at the dLGN
claims.criterion: PEAK of the CONC NE trace (Eq. 19) during the 50 mM dose period over the 6 PVH recordings, mean across recordings (S5I, not deconvolved). The ratio is to the mean of fig2e-dlgn-peak-concentrations; 21.4/4.61 = 4.6, which "nearly five-fold" states. The ratio's expected value is that quotient, not a printed number.

claims.statement: Optogenetic stimulation of LC releases NE and DA together with distinct time courses; DA reaches its peak (248 nM on average) before NE (347 nM).
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 4; Figure 2H, 2K, Figure S4F
claims.quote: Quantification of NE and DA release while accounting for sensor crosstalk demonstrated that both ligands were released simultaneously and with distinct time courses, with the DA concentration reaching its peak (248 nM, on average) before the NE concentration (347 nM
claims.criterion: POOLED-SLICE and CONC (Eq. 19) on the LC recordings; PEAK in the 5 to 12.5 min window (morse_fig2_rev cell 139); mean over the 5 recordings with robust NE (cells 145 and 157 print 347 and 248 nM for these). The paper does not say how "before" is measured. Readings (a) the DA TAU-RISE earlier than the NE TAU-RISE (fig2l-lc-ne-delay, Figure 2L); (b) the time of the maximum of the mean DA concentration trace in the window earlier than that of NE. The outcome is the one both give; if they differ, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: After each of the first several optogenetic trains, NE and DA concentrations rose in discrete steps of 100 to 300 nM, so 20 s between trains let the released ligands equilibrate with the hydrogel.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 4; Figure 2I legend
claims.quote: In fact, discrete 100–300 nM increments in the concentrations of both ligands were evident after each of the first several trains of optogenetic stimulation
claims.criterion: The example probe of Figure 2H-I. The NE and DA concentration (CONC, Eq. 19) with a 5-frame median filter (morse_fig2_rev cell 205), train onsets from the stimulation record (45 trains 20 s apart). The increment is open. Readings (a) the code's, concentration from 4 to 15 frames after the train onset minus the value 4 frames after (cells 224-231); (b) the value at the next train's onset minus that at this train's onset. Over the first 5 trains, reproduced when the increments of both ligands lie in 90 to 330 nM. The legend's "100-200 nM" (90 to 220 nM) is reported as a second range. The paper names no number of trains; "several" is read as 5.

claims.statement: Of five LC slices with robust NE elevations, four also had robust DA elevations and none had robust 5-HT elevations; thresholds were 148 nM (NE), 84.3 nM (DA) and 30.3 nM (5-HT).
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 4; Figure 2H, 2J-K
claims.quote: Out of five brain slices with robust elevations in NE, four also had robust elevations in DA, while none had robust elevations in 5-HT ( Figures 2J - K )
claims.criterion: THRESH as the Methods give it (SD of the pooled peak-normalized signal before stimulation) decides; the code's variant (morse_fig2_rev cells 120, 144, 146, the SD of the unnormalized pooled dF/F0 over the first 5 min) is shown, and is the one whose printed values match the paper's thresholds. Which recordings form the "dataset" over which the maximum SD is taken is open (the Methods do not define it); readings (a) the LC recordings, (b) the code's 12 quantified opto recordings (LC and DRN; the paper mentions no DRN optogenetic recordings). PEAK in 5 to 12.5 min. The code picks the five NE responders by hand (cells 116, 183, 195); here a slice is an NE responder when its NE peak exceeds the threshold. Counts are exact.

claims.statement: In LC slices the rise of NE concentration lagged the rise of DA by 31 s, or 1 to 2 optogenetic trains.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 4; Figure 2L
claims.quote: Rise times of NE concentration were consistently delayed relative to DA concentration by 31 sec, or 1–2 trains of optogenetic stimulation ( Figure 2L )
claims.criterion: TAU-RISE from stimulation onset of the NE and DA concentration traces, in the 4 slices with robust NE and DA (morse_fig2_rev cells 170-174 print 1.432 and 0.920 min, 30.7 s). "Consistently" is read as the NE tau-rise later than the DA tau-rise in each of the 4.

claims.statement: MORSE probes stayed stable for over an hour of slice recording (46 of 48 probes) and over the following 1.5 or more hours of dipping (15 of 17).
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects regionalized neuromodulator release in brain slices, paragraph 4
claims.quote: these hydrogel probes remained stable for over an hour during slice recordings (46/48 probes) and over a subsequent 1.5+ hours of post hoc dipping (15/17 probes)
claims.criterion: Stability as in fig1f-koh-stability (hydrogel translation not above 25 um), which the paper defines only for dipping. Counts are exact. Not in the code. Needs all 48 slice recordings with deformation fields or raw imaging.

claims.statement: In awake mouse CSF, IP AVP, OXT and 5-HT each evoked a response in the corresponding sensor within at most 10 to 15 min, followed by washout.
claims.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 2; Figure 3B-F
claims.quote: Upon peripheral delivery of each ligand, we reliably observed a specific corresponding sensor response in the CSF within at most 10–15 minutes, followed by washout
claims.criterion: POOLED-INVIVO on the three-sensor recordings (n=11 mice in the legend; the code uses 10, morse_fig3_rev cell 96). Onset is open. Readings (a) TAU-RISE of the per-mouse trace within 0 to 45 min; (b) the first time after injection at which the trace exceeds 1.96 times the largest pre-injection SD across mice (the Methods' threshold rule). Reproduced when, for each ligand, the onset is at most 16.5 min in every mouse (or in the mean trace, reported both), the mean peak dF/F0 of the matching sensor in 0 to 45 min exceeds that of the other two sensors (specificity, read from Figure 3D-F), and the mean trace at 45 min is below its peak by more than the threshold (washout). The code prints tau-rise of 11 to 36 min for older data (morse_fig3 cells 142-150), which is noted.

claims.statement: Single-sensor fiber photometry probes in CSF show AVP and OXT time courses after IP injection with kinetics similar to MORSE two-photon recordings.
claims.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 2; Figure S6D-F, Figure 3D-E
claims.quote: This approach demonstrated similar kinetics of CSF AVP and OXT time courses following IP injection as compared to the MORSE technique involving two-photon imaging ( Figures 3D - E )
claims.criterion: Photometry at 50 Hz, a 2-s median filter, an exponential background fitted over the tens of minutes before activation, dF/F0 against the 15 min before each IP injection (Methods). n=4 mice per sensor. Kinetics compared through TAU-RISE of the mean traces (photometry against MORSE of fig3df-ip-responses). "Similar" is not defined; readings (a) the photometry tau-rise lies within the range of per-mouse MORSE tau-rise; (b) the two mean tau-rise differ by less than 5 min. Not in the code. Needs the photometry recordings.

claims.statement: With ten-sensor probes in CSF of four mice, up to 9 sensors per probe were recovered (median 8.5), with on average 3.8 cells per sensor per probe.
claims.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 3G
claims.quote: Across four animals, we were able to successfully recover simultaneous signals from up to 9 distinct sensors per probe ... 8.5 sensors; average of 3.8 cells per sensor) ( Figure 3G )
claims.criterion: SENSOR IDENTITY on the four ten-sensor in vivo recordings; a sensor is recovered on a probe when at least one cell carries its label; cells per sensor per probe is total cells over (probe, sensor) pairs with a cell (morse_fig3_rev cells 192-203 print sensors per probe 9, 8, 9, 5 and 119/31 = 3.84).

claims.statement: Each of the ten sensors responded after IP injection of its ligand, with kinetics that differ across ligands.
claims.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 3H
claims.quote: Each sensor demonstrated a response following IP injection of the respective ligand, with diverse response kinetics across ligands that likely reflect differential permeability from blood into CSF ( Figure 3H )
claims.criterion: POOLED-INVIVO for each sensor around the IP mixture that contains its ligand (and the ICV 5-HT), on the ten-sensor probes (Figure 3H uses 5 probes, morse_fig3_rev cells 337-346, 31-frame median filter). Reproduced when, for every sensor recorded, the mean dF/F0 after its ligand's injection exceeds 1.96 times the largest pre-injection SD across probes (Methods threshold rule) within 0 to 45 min, and the TAU-RISE of the sensors' mean traces span more than a factor of 2 (diverse kinetics). Sensors with no cell in any probe are listed.

claims.statement: IP delivery raised CSF concentrations to tens of nanomolar for 5-HT and hundreds of nanomolar for AVP and OXT.
claims.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 4A, D, G and 4B, E, H left
claims.quote: We found that IP delivery drove CSF levels in the tens of nanomolar (5-HT) or hundreds of nanomolar (AVP, OXT) range ( Figures 4A , D , G )
claims.criterion: CONC-INVIVO on the mice with ICV of the same ligand (AVP 5, OXT 6, 5-HT 5; morse_fig3_rev cell 224). Which value is meant is open. Readings (a) the mean across mice of the value at 30 min after injection, a single timepoint (Figure 4B, E, H left; code cells 294-297); (b) the mean across mice of the peak within 0 to 45 min. Reproduced when, under one reading, 5-HT lies in 9 to 109 nM and AVP and OXT each in 90 to 1099 nM.

claims.statement: In naive mice, IP injections raised serum levels of the injected ligands 30 min later, and raised AVP and OXT in CSF as well.
claims.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 4B-C, E-F, H-I
claims.quote: We found that the IP injections drove elevated levels in serum, with AVP and OXT increases also detected in CSF.
claims.criterion: ELISA (AVP, OXT) and mass spectrometry (5-HT, 5-HIAA) of cisterna magna CSF and cardiac serum 30 min after IP ligand (n=3 AVP, n=3 OXT, n=4 5-HT) or saline (n=2, 2, 4), as in the Figure 4 legends; values as tabulated (the code loads AVP_all_samples.csv, OXT_all_samples.csv, vandy_core.csv, morse_fig3_rev cells 298-323). No test is reported. Readings (a) the IP group mean exceeds the saline mean; (b) every IP sample exceeds every saline sample. Reproduced when both hold for serum AVP, OXT and 5-HT and for CSF AVP and OXT; not reproduced when neither does; blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ. Needs the ELISA and mass spectrometry tables.

claims.statement: CSF concentrations measured ex vivo were over two orders of magnitude lower than those MORSE estimated in vivo 30 min after the same IP injection.
claims.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 4B, E, H
claims.quote: Notably, the levels quantified in these ex vivo CSF samples were over two orders of magnitude lower than those estimated in vivo by MORSE at the same 30-minute timepoint following IP injection.
claims.criterion: For AVP and OXT, the mean across mice of the MORSE 30-min value (fig4-ip-csf-concentrations reading a) divided by the mean ELISA CSF value of the IP group; reproduced when both ratios exceed 100. The sentence follows the one on AVP and OXT increases in CSF, and does not say whether 5-HT is included. For 5-HT the ratio of the MORSE 30-min value to the mean mass spectrometry CSF value of the IP group (Figure 4H) is reported, or to the detection limit (0.050 pg/uL, about 0.28 nM; Methods) where values lie below it; the paper does not say whether they do. Not computed in the code (a note in morse_fig3_rev cell 334).

claims.statement: AVP concentrations estimated by MORSE dipping into serum samples ex vivo were similar to ELISA values from the same kind of samples.
claims.source: Results, Real time, quantitative tracking of CSF composition with MORSE in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure S6G-J
claims.quote: AVP concentration estimated by MORSE ex vivo by dipping in serum samples was similar to that obtained with ELISA
claims.criterion: A ten-sensor probe dipped in serum from IP AVP mice (n=3); AVP concentration by Eq. 8 from the AVP sensor signal calibrated in the same recording (S6H). The code takes twice the median over the last part of each well (morse_fig2 cell 56, 2*median of frames 104 to 156) and prints 13.9, 31.0 and 39.5 nM (morse_fig3_rev cell 320); the factor 2 is not explained, so readings with and without it are shown. "Similar" is not defined; readings (a) the MORSE and ELISA ranges overlap; (b) the ratio of means lies within a factor of 10 (against the "two orders of magnitude" contrast the paper draws). Reproduced when both hold; not reproduced when neither does; blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ.

claims.statement: In 3 of 7 recordings of undisturbed mice, CSF 5-HT rose spontaneously within the first 60 to 90 min, in all 5-HT sensor cells and in none of the other sensor cells.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects endogenous CSF signals at concentrations that impact downstream signaling, paragraph 1; Figure 5A-B
claims.quote: In a subset of experiments (n=3/7), we observed a spontaneous elevation in CSF 5-HT that was evident in all 5-HT sensor cells (but none of the other sensor cells) within the first 60–90 min of the recording
claims.criterion: The 7 three-sensor recordings with 2 h of quiet imaging before IP injections. The code picks the 3 by hand (morse_fig3 cells 232-243, l_vals 1, 2, 5) and gives no rule. Reading, an elevation is a rise of the per-mouse median 5-HT sensor dF/F0 (F0 the mean of the lowest 1/15 of values, 51-frame median filter, code cell 232) above 1.96 times its SD over the first 15 min, peaking within the first 90 min and before the first IP injection, with every 5-HT cell rising above its own baseline and no AVP or OXT sensor median doing so. Count exact.

claims.statement: The spontaneous CSF 5-HT fluctuations were as large as or larger than responses to IP 5-HT, and rose and decayed over tens of minutes.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects endogenous CSF signals at concentrations that impact downstream signaling, paragraph 1; Figure 5C-D
claims.quote: These fluctuations were of similar magnitude or larger than the signals we observed in CSF following IP 5-HT delivery (c.f. Figure 3F ) and slowly rose and decayed over tens of minutes ( Figures 5C - D )
claims.criterion: On the 3 recordings of fig5ab-spontaneous-5ht, the per-mouse mean 5-HT trace; FWHM as the last minus the first time above half the maximum, tau-off as the last time above max/e minus the time of the peak (morse_fig3 cells 238-243, which print FWHM 79.8, 94.6 and 87.6 min and tau-off 91.1, 84.8 and 76.1 min). Reproduced when the FWHM and tau-off of each lie between 10 and 99 min (tens of minutes) and each peak dF/F0 is at least 0.9 times the mean peak dF/F0 of the 5-HT sensor after IP 5-HT in fig3df-ip-responses (same F0 rule across both, readings with the Figure 3 F0 and with the Figure 5 F0).

claims.statement: IP and ICV 5-HT drove calcium responses of similar amplitude in choroid plexus epithelial cells, both lasting at least 60 min.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects endogenous CSF signals at concentrations that impact downstream signaling, paragraph 2; Figure 5G-H
claims.quote: Both routes of 5-HT administration drove similar amplitudes of calcium activity in the ChP epithelial cells, and both responses persisted for at least 60 minutes following delivery.
claims.criterion: GCaMP6f in FoxJ1-Cre::Ai95D mice, ICV n=3 and IP n=6. A square ROI over several epithelial cells, the mean signal; an exponential fitted to the signal before injection and subtracted where it decays; dF/F0 against the first 5 min (Methods, ChP signal processing). The code (morse_fig3 cells 334-405) median filters over about 100 s and divides by the mean over the 15 min before injection; both F0 readings are shown. Peak = maximum after injection. Code prints peaks ICV 0.72, 0.75, 1.47 and IP 0.58, 0.50, 0.34, 0.61, 1.28, 0.59. "Similar" read as the IP and ICV mean peaks within a factor of 2 of each other. Persistence read as the mean dF/F0 at 60 min after delivery still above 1.96 times the pre-injection SD, for both routes. Needs the ChP traces.

claims.statement: GRAB sensors expressed in the choroid plexus epithelium report IP 5-HT, AVP and OXT with time courses similar to those seen with MORSE in CSF.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects endogenous CSF signals at concentrations that impact downstream signaling, paragraph 3; Figure 6C, E, G against Figure 3F, D, E
claims.quote: In subsets of mice, IP delivery of 5-HT, AVP, or OXT drove associated sensor signals in ChP with similar time courses as observed previously with MORSE
claims.criterion: ChP GRAB dF/F0 as in fig5gh-chp-calcium (5-HT 5 injections in 4 mice, AVP 9 in 4, OXT 3 in 2), TAU-RISE per injection (morse_fig3 prints 5-HT 1.9 to 6.8 min, AVP 4.4 to 42.9, OXT 4.2 to 29.3). "Similar" is not defined; readings (a) the mean ChP tau-rise of each ligand lies within the range of per-mouse MORSE tau-rise of fig3df-ip-responses; (b) the mean tau-rise differ by less than a factor of 2. Needs the ChP traces.

claims.statement: IP 5-HT reached the apical choroid plexus membrane fast enough to explain the choroid plexus calcium response.
claims.source: Results, MORSE detects endogenous CSF signals at concentrations that impact downstream signaling, paragraph 3; Figure 6C, Figure 5H
claims.quote: Furthermore, IP 5-HT reached the apical ChP membrane ( Figure 6C ) fast enough to explain the ChP calcium response ( Figure 5H )
claims.criterion: TAU-RISE after IP 5-HT of the ChP GRAB-5-HT2h signal (Figure 6C right, 5 injections) against the GCaMP6f signal (Figure 5H right, 6 mice). The paper does not say what "fast enough" means. Readings (a) the mean GRAB tau-rise is not later than the mean GCaMP tau-rise plus its SEM; (b) the mean GRAB signal exceeds 1.96 times its pre-injection SD (the Methods' threshold rule) no later than the mean GCaMP signal does. The outcome is the one both give; if they differ, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified. The code's printed values (below) fail reading (a), so it may not be what the authors meant. The code prints GRAB 6.8, 5.5, 1.9, 5.0, 3.8 min and GCaMP 1.4, 4.4, 0.6, 1.3, 1.6, 3.0 min (morse_fig3), which is noted; the code's exclusion of one GCaMP mouse from the mean is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: MORSE probe implantation caused no asymmetry in microglial (Iba1) or astrocytic (GFAP) staining, nor in diffusion of labeled BSA from CSF into tissue.
claims.source: Figure S6A-C legends
claims.quote: No Iba1 or GFAP signal asymmetry between left and right hemispheres induced by MORSE probe implantation into one of the cannulae was noted in any animals (n=12) across the span of the ventricular system.
claims.criterion: Histology of 12 mice. A claim of absence with no test in the paper; reproduced when the Iba1 and GFAP intensities on the implanted side are within the range of the other side in every mouse, and the BSA profile (S6C) is symmetric. Needs histology images, which the paper does not say are deposited.

claims.statement: Activity was recorded from 113 WT-background animals, each for up to 40 min, while a neuron was stimulated once every 30 s with a 0.5 s train of light pulses.
claims.source: Results, "Population imaging and single-cell activation", paragraph 1; Methods, "Stimulus delivery and pulsed laser", paragraph 3
claims.quote: We recorded activity from 113 wild-type (WT)-background animals, each for up to 40 min, while stimulating a mostly randomly selected sequence of neurons one by one every 30 s ... a 500-ms (300-ms for the unc-31-mutant strain) train of light pulses was used to optogenetically stimulate that neuron
claims.criterion: Reproduced when 113 recordings hold both calcium traces and a stimulation table, the median interval between stimulations is within 10% of 30 s, and at least 90% of recordings last no more than 44 min (40 min plus 10%). Partially reproduced when the interval and duration conditions hold and between 100 and 112 recordings hold traces and stimulations. The stated 0.5 s duration is reported, with whether the files could show any other.

claims.statement: Responses to stimulation were imaged for 23,433 pairs of neurons (66% of all possible pairs in the head), from 186 of the 188 head neurons, and some pairs were observed as many as 59 times.
claims.source: Results, "Signal propagation map", paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 4a
claims.quote: We imaged activity in response to stimulation for 23,433 pairs of neurons (66% of all possible pairs in the head). Measured pairs were imaged at least once, and some as many as 59 times ... This includes activity from 186 of 188 neurons in the head
claims.criterion: An observation of pair (i, j) is a stimulation of the neuron labelled j that evoked an autoresponse, while an ROI labelled i had a usable trace (5% NaN rule and a nonzero local standard deviation); both labels must be among the 188 head neurons. The paper's text allows these readings, (a) pairs including i = j (the Source Data count of 23,433 includes the diagonal), (b) pairs with i different from j, (c) as (a) without requiring the autoresponse. Reproduced when under one reading all three values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when one or two are. Counts per animal are reported.

claims.statement: Stimulation of the interneuron AVJR evoked activity in AVDR.
claims.source: Fig. 1e
claims.quote: Stimulation of the interneuron AVJR evoked activity in AVDR (Fig. 1e)
claims.criterion: Over all AVJR stimulations with an autoresponse in which AVDR was observed, the mean <dF/F0>_t of AVDR is above 0 and the response classifier detects an AVDR response in at least one of them. Reproduced when both hold; not reproduced otherwise. The value per animal and the number of trials are reported.

claims.statement: Activation of the premotor interneuron AVER evoked activity transients in AVAR.
claims.source: Fig. 1f
claims.quote: Activation of the premotor interneuron AVER evoked activity transients in AVAR (Fig. 1f)
claims.criterion: As for fig1e-avjr-avdr, with AVER stimulated and AVAR observed.

claims.statement: Activation of SAADL inhibited the activity of the sensory neuron OLLR.
claims.source: Fig. 1g
claims.quote: Activation of the turning-associated neuron SAADL ... inhibited the activity of the sensory neuron OLLR
claims.criterion: Over all SAADL stimulations with an autoresponse in which OLLR was observed, the mean <dF/F0>_t of OLLR is below 0 and the classifier detects an OLLR response in at least one of them. Reproduced when both hold; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: The per-pair measurements computed from the dandiset agree with the paper's published per-pair values, the number of observations (Extended Data Fig. 4a) and the mean response <dF/F0>_t (Extended Data Fig. 3a).
claims.source: Source Data of Extended Data Figs. 3a and 4a
claims.criterion: Pairs are matched by the names of the responding and the stimulated neuron. Reproduced when at least 90% of the paper's observed pairs are observed here, the Spearman correlation of the observation counts over pairs observed in both is at least 0.9, and the Pearson correlation of mean <dF/F0>_t over pairs observed in both is at least 0.7. Partially reproduced when at least 70% are observed here and the two correlations are at least 0.7 and 0.5. Not reproduced otherwise. The mean over all observations is the main reading; the mean over detected responses only and the code's correction of decaying traces are shown as variants.

claims.statement: The dandiset's recordings can be linked to the recordings the paper exported to its OSF repository, and the stimulated neuron found here from the target position agrees with the one the paper's pipeline assigned.
claims.source: Data availability (OSF doi 10.17605/OSF.IO/E2SYT, raw_extracted_data)
claims.quote: Machine-readable datasets containing the measurements from this work are publicly accessible through on Open Science Foundation repository at 10.17605/OSF.IO/E2SYT
claims.criterion: Recordings are matched by the date and time in the dandiset's session id and in the folder name the export gives for each recording. Reproduced when at least 95% of the 110 recordings with traces match one exported recording with the same number of stimulations and ROIs, and, over stimulations that both assign to an ROI, at least 80% are assigned to the same ROI. Partially reproduced when at least 80% of recordings match and the agreement is at least 60%. The labels of matched ROIs are compared as well, and the head-pair count of pairs-measured is shown with the exported assignment as a variant.

claims.statement: 11% of the functional connections at q < 0.05 are inhibitory.
claims.source: Results, "Signal propagation map", paragraph 5; Fig. 2d
claims.quote: Our measurements indicate that 11% of q < 0.05 functional connections are inhibitory (Fig. 2d)
claims.criterion: The q values cannot be computed from the dandiset (see fig2c-1310-connected), so the pairs with q < 0.05 are taken from the paper's Source Data (Extended Data Fig. 4b), and the sign of each pair's mean <dF/F0>_t is computed from the dandiset. Readings, (a) all q < 0.05 pairs observed here, including i = j; (b) excluding i = j. Reproduced when the fraction with a negative mean is within tolerance under one reading; the fraction from the paper's own Source Data means is given for reference.

claims.statement: Stimulation does not elicit responses in most close neighbours of the targeted neuron; at 75% of the cumulative distribution, neighbours' responses are below a dF/F0 of 0.1.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 2i,j and legend; Methods, "Characterization of the size of the two-photon excitation spot", paragraph 2
claims.quote: Cross-hairs in j, 75% cumulative distribution at ΔF/F0 = 0.1 ... we show that stimulations do not elicit responses in most of the close neighbours of the targeted neurons
claims.criterion: Over stimulations with an autoresponse, <dF/F0>_t of the targeted ROI (0 um) and of every other ROI with a usable trace whose centroid lies 4 to 10 um or 10 to 16 um away, with 0.42 um per pixel and the imaging file's plane spacing. The legend does not say which neighbours the 75% refers to; readings, (a) both bands pooled (4 to 16 um), (b) 4 to 10 um, (c) 10 to 16 um. Reproduced when under one reading the fraction below 0.1 is within tolerance and the median of the targeted ROI is at least three times that of the 4 to 10 um band. Partially reproduced when only the second condition holds.

claims.statement: 1,310 of the 23,433 measured neuron pairs (6%) are functionally connected at q < 0.05.
claims.source: Results, "Signal propagation map", paragraph 3; Fig. 2c
claims.quote: A total of 1,310 of the 23,433 measured neuron pairs, or 6%, pass our stringent criteria to be deemed functionally connected at q < 0.05 (Fig. 2c)

claims.statement: Bilaterally symmetric neurons are eight times more likely to be functionally connected than pairs chosen at random.
claims.source: Results, "Signal propagation map", paragraph 4; Fig. 2c
claims.quote: As expected, bilaterally symmetric neurons are (eight times) more likely to be functionally connected than are pairs of neurons chosen at random (Fig. 2c)

claims.statement: The probability of a functional connection decreases with the minimal anatomical path length, functionally connected pairs are on average 2.1 hops apart, and pairs with long paths are more often functionally non-connected.
claims.source: Results, "Signal propagation map", paragraph 6; Fig. 2e-g
claims.quote: the likelihood of functional connections decreased as the minimal path length through the anatomical network increased (Fig. 2e) ... neurons that had large minimal path lengths through the anatomical network were more likely to be functionally non-connected ... Functionally connected (q < 0.05) neurons were on average connected by a minimal anatomical path length of 2.1 hops

claims.statement: Signal propagation differs from predictions of a connectome-constrained model; pairs predicted to respond strongly respond more, but agreement over all pairs is poor (R2 < 0), improves when weights and signs are fitted, and is better in unc-31 animals.
claims.source: Results, "Functional measurements differ from anatomy", paragraphs 2 to 4; Fig. 3b-d
claims.quote: Neuron pairs that the model predicted to have large responses (ΔV > 0.1) were significantly more likely to have larger measured responses ... poor agreement between anatomy-based prediction and measurement when considering the response amplitudes of all neuron pairs ... Fitting the weights and signs ... improved the agreement ... signal propagation in these animals showed better agreement with anatomy than it did in WT animals

claims.statement: Kernels of one neuron pair are more similar to each other than to kernels of other pairs, and kernel rise times characterize the speed of signal propagation.
claims.source: Results, "Signal propagation map", paragraph 7; Extended Data Fig. 6b-f
claims.quote: As expected, kernels from one neuron pair were more similar to each other than to kernels from other pairs (Extended Data Fig. 6f) ... Kernel rise time for each measured neuron pair in WT is a metric of signal propagation speed

claims.statement: unc-31 mutants have a smaller proportion of functionally connected pairs than WT animals.
claims.source: Results, "Extrasynaptic signalling also drives neural dynamics", paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 7b
claims.quote: Consistent with this, unc-31 animals had a smaller proportion of functional connections than did WT animals (Extended Data Fig. 7b)

claims.statement: URX, ADL and AWB, predicted from anatomy to have no response, respond strongly to RID stimulation in WT animals.
claims.source: Results, "Extrasynaptic signalling also drives neural dynamics", paragraph 4; Fig. 4a-d; Extended Data Fig. 7c
claims.quote: Many neurons responded to RID activation (Extended Data Fig. 7c), including URX, ADL and AWB, three neuron subtypes that were predicted from anatomy to have no response (Fig. 4a). These three neurons showed strong responses in WT animals
claims.criterion: RID stimulations are those whose stimulated ROI, found as in the other claims, carries the NeuroPAL label RID. As the Methods state for Fig. 4, no autoresponse is required and values of <dF/F0>_t beyond 2 in absolute value are excluded; the dandiset holds only the regular traces, not the matchless ones. Readings, (a) URX, ADL and AWB with left and right pooled; (b) the neurons shown in Fig. 4, URXL, ADLR and AWBR. For each of the three, over RID stimulations in which it is observed, the mean <dF/F0>_t is above 0 and the classifier detects a response in at least one trial. Reproduced when this holds for all three under one reading; partially reproduced when it holds for one or two; not reproduced when for none. Blocked (other) when none of the three is observed after a RID stimulation. Where each mean falls among the means of all head pairs is reported for "strongly".

claims.statement: The responses of URXL, ADLR and AWBR to RID stimulation are reduced or absent in unc-31 mutants.
claims.source: Results, "Extrasynaptic signalling also drives neural dynamics", paragraph 4; Fig. 4b-d
claims.quote: These three neurons showed strong responses in WT animals but their responses were reduced or absent in unc-31 mutants (Fig. 4b–d)
claims.criterion: In the 18 unc-31 recordings of the OSF export (exported_data_unc31.tar.gz), RID stimulations are those whose exported stimulated ROI carries the exported label RID. The exported traces are processed as the dandiset's, with the inclusion rules of fig4-rid-wt and the same two readings. A neuron's response is reduced when its mean <dF/F0>_t in unc-31 is below its WT mean in fig4-rid-wt. Reproduced when the response is reduced for every one of the three neurons observed in both strains under one reading; partially reproduced when for some; not reproduced when for none. Blocked (other) when none is observed in both. Because the WT values come from the dandiset and the unc-31 values from the export, the WT values computed in the same way from the WT export are shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Fifty-three pairs are functionally connected in WT (q < 0.05) and functionally non-connected in unc-31 (q_eq < 0.05), with timescales similar to all functional connections.
claims.source: Results, "Extrasynaptic-dependent signal propagation screen", paragraph 1; Fig. 5a; Extended Data Fig. 9
claims.quote: Fifty-three pairs of neurons met our criteria (Extended Data Fig. 9) ... The timescales of signal propagation for those neuron pairs that passed our screen were similar to that of all functional connections (Fig. 5a)

claims.statement: Correlations derived from the measured kernels predict spontaneous activity correlations better than anatomical weights or the connectome-constrained model.
claims.source: Results, "Signal propagation predicts spontaneous activity", paragraph 1; Fig. 6
claims.quote: We conclude that functionally derived predictions based on our measured signal propagation kernels better agree with spontaneous activity than do either a bare description of anatomical weights or an established model constrained by the connectome

claims.statement: In a D1-cre mouse expressing GCaMP7f in D1 spiny projection neurons, fluorescence under 470 nm excitation shows Ca2+ transients across fibers that are absent under 405 nm (isosbestic) excitation.
claims.source: Figure 1C; Results, Chronic measurements of large-scale calcium and neuromodulator signals in head-fixed mice, paragraph 1
claims.quote: 470 nm excitation light (green trace) was alternated with 405nm light (black) at 18hz to provide a quasi-simultaneous isosbestic control. Significant transients are absent with 405 illumination
claims.criterion: Mouse 842, session 2022-11-23 (the session the paper's Fig01/C code reads), the 61 fibers flagged included. For each fiber, the standard deviation of DF/F under 470 nm divided by that under 405 nm. Reproduced when the ratio exceeds 1 in at least 90% of fibers and its median is at least 2; partially reproduced when the median is above 1 but either condition fails; not reproduced otherwise. The other session of the mouse (2022-11-18) is a variant.

claims.statement: Pairwise correlations of D1 SPN Ca2+ signals are generally low but variable, and drop off significantly with the distance between fiber tips.
claims.source: Results, Chronic measurements of large-scale calcium and neuromodulator signals in head-fixed mice, paragraph 1; Figure S2D; code SuppFig02/DEF/surface_brain_dist.m
claims.quote: Pairwise correlations of SPN Ca2+ signals were generally low, but were highly variable and dropped off significantly with distance between fibers (Figure S2D)
claims.criterion: Mouse 842, session 2022-11-23, 470 nm DF/F of the included fibers. As the code does, the Pearson correlation of each pair of fibers over the session, and the Pearson correlation across pairs between these coefficients and the Euclidean distance between fiber tips. Reproduced when this correlation is negative with p < 0.05 and the median pairwise coefficient is below 0.3 ("generally low"); partially reproduced when only the distance effect holds.

claims.statement: After accounting for distance in the brain, signal correlations do not depend on the distance between fibers on the bundle surface, so nearby fibers in the bundle do not cross-talk.
claims.source: Results, Chronic measurements of large-scale calcium and neuromodulator signals in head-fixed mice, paragraph 1; Figure S2E-F; code SuppFig02/DEF/surface_brain_dist.m
claims.quote: No relationship was observed between signal correlations and distance on the bundle surface after accounting for brain distance, indicating no cross-talk between nearby fibers in the bundle (Figure S2E–F)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test as its code runs it, a linear model of the pairwise correlation coefficient on Euclidean, AP, ML and DV tip distances and the distance between the fibers' ROI centroids on the bundle image (ROICentroids). Reproduced when the bundle-distance coefficient has p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The coefficient, its sign (crosstalk would make correlations fall with bundle distance) and its confidence interval are reported either way.

claims.statement: Dopamine release to unpredicted water reward is reliable and of comparable amplitude over at least 12 weeks after implantation (median over 44 fibers, normalized to week 5).
claims.source: Figure 1D; Results, Chronic measurements of large-scale calcium and neuromodulator signals in head-fixed mice, paragraph 1; code Fig01/D
claims.quote: DA release at a single location to unpredicted water reward delivery was highly reliable and comparable in amplitude over at least 12 weeks following stable expression of dLight1.3b
claims.criterion: Mouse DL15, the 44 included fibers. As the code does, DF/F aligned to the first lick after each reward (consumption), the weekly mean response over 0 to 4 s, its peak over the first 1 s, divided by the fiber's peak in the first week; the median over fibers per week. Weeks are counted from the first session, taken as week 5 as in the figure (the files do not give the implantation date; the code's date puts the first session on day 35). Rewards are taken as unpredicted only in sessions with 25 rewards or fewer, as the code does; in larger sessions the code keeps rewards by a task phase or cue signal the files do not hold. Reproduced when the weekly median stays between 0.7 and 1.3 in every week tested and the weeks tested reach week 12; partially reproduced when it stays in that band in every week tested but they end before week 12; not reproduced when any week falls outside it. All rewards of all sessions are shown as a variant.

claims.statement: The dandiset's DF/F traces, fibers and stimulus times are those behind the paper's salient-stimulus analysis, so that its per-fiber responses can be linked to the paper's.
claims.source: Figure 4E-F; the paper's intermediate file glm_spline_results.mat (Zenodo, Fig04)
claims.criterion: Fibers are matched by order within each mouse (the included fibers of the files in table order against the code's striatal ROIs). The link holds (reproduced) when, for every mouse, the published per-fiber triggered averages of raw DF/F to light (cue1_roi_mu) equal those computed from the dandiset within 1e-6, and those to tone do as well in every mouse but DL18; when the GLM spline estimates of the dandiset analysis correlate with the published ones at r >= 0.99 for each stimulus; and when the significance of increases and decreases agrees for at least 90% of fiber and stimulus pairs. Partially reproduced when the raw averages match but either of the other two fails; not reproduced when the raw averages do not match. DL18's 12 kHz tones are identified by matching the published per-trial activity (cue2_loco_regr_act) to the dandiset's tone presentations.

claims.statement: The light evokes transient increases in dopamine release across many striatal locations.
claims.source: Figure 4B, 4E; Results, Spatial topography of modality specific dopamine release magnitudes over large-scale 3-dimensional volumes, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The light evoked transient increases in DA release across many locations
claims.criterion: Over the 280 fibers, by the GLM and null test fixed above. Reproduced when at least half of the fibers have a significant increase to light and significant increases outnumber significant decreases; partially reproduced when increases outnumber decreases but fewer than half of fibers have one.

claims.statement: Light-evoked dopamine increases follow an amplitude gradient from the anterior striatum into the posterior tail, where increases are less prevalent and smaller.
claims.source: Figure 4E; Figure S4A; Results, Spatial topography of modality specific dopamine release magnitudes over large-scale 3-dimensional volumes, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The light evoked transient increases in DA release across many locations with an amplitude gradient extending from the anterior striatum into the posterior tail, where increases were less prevalent and smaller amplitude
claims.criterion: Over the 280 fibers, the light value (signed largest point of the spline estimate). (a) Spearman correlation of AP and the light value positive with p < 0.05; (b) the fraction of fibers with a significant light increase lower in the tail (AP <= -1.0 mm) than elsewhere (Fisher exact test, one-sided, p < 0.05); (c) the tail's light values lower than elsewhere (Mann-Whitney, one-sided, p < 0.05). Reproduced when all three hold; partially reproduced when (a) holds and one of (b) and (c) does.

claims.statement: The tone evokes the strongest dopamine increases at sites in the posterior tail, while anterior to the tail it evokes primarily decreases.
claims.source: Figure 4D, 4F; Figure S4C; Results, Spatial topography of modality specific dopamine release magnitudes over large-scale 3-dimensional volumes, paragraph 1
claims.quote: the tone evoked the strongest increases in DA release at sites in the posterior tail, while anterior to the tail, the tone evoked primarily decreases in DA release
claims.criterion: Over the 280 fibers, the tone value. (a) The tail's tone values higher than elsewhere (Mann-Whitney, one-sided, p < 0.05) and their median positive, and at least 6 of the 10 fibers with the largest tone values in the tail; (b) among fibers anterior to the tail with a significant tone response, those whose value is a decrease outnumber those whose value is an increase (binomial test, one-sided, p < 0.05). Reproduced when (a) and (b) hold; partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: Tone-evoked decreases are slightly more prevalent in the anterior lateral and ventral striatum, with many sites showing both increases to the light and decreases to the tone.
claims.source: Figure 4F; Results, Spatial topography of modality specific dopamine release magnitudes over large-scale 3-dimensional volumes, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Decreases were slightly more prevalent in the anterior lateral and ventral striatum, with many sites exhibiting both increases to the light and decreases to the tone (Figure 4F)
claims.criterion: Fibers anterior to the tail. Fibers whose tone value is a significant decrease have larger ML (more lateral) and larger DV (more ventral) coordinates than the other fibers (Mann-Whitney, one-sided, p < 0.05 each). Reproduced when both hold; partially reproduced when one does. The number of fibers with a significant light increase and a significant tone decrease is reported for the second part of the statement, read as "many" when it is at least 20% of the anterior fibers.

claims.statement: The modality-specific release patterns are consistent within and across mice.
claims.source: Results, Spatial topography of modality specific dopamine release magnitudes over large-scale 3-dimensional volumes, paragraph 1 (Figure S4A, C)
claims.quote: These distinct release patterns were consistent within and across mice (Figure S4A, C)
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the Spearman correlation of AP with the light value and with the tone value. Reproduced when the light correlation is positive in at least 5 of the 7 mice and the tone correlation is negative in at least 5 of the 7; partially reproduced when one of the two holds.

claims.statement: Locomotor changes to the stimuli are variable and bi-directional, while the dopamine release patterns to light and tone are consistent, so the patterns are stimulus and not movement driven.
claims.source: Results, Spatial topography of modality specific dopamine release magnitudes over large-scale 3-dimensional volumes, paragraph 1 (Figure S4); Methods; code SuppFig04/EFGH/sal_stim_bubbles_loco.m
claims.quote: Locomotor changes to stimuli were variable, bi-directional, and differed across mice and individual stimulus presentations, while DA release patterns to light and tone were consistent, indicating that modality-specific patterns were stimulus, not movement driven
claims.criterion: As the code does, presentations are split by the sign of the largest-magnitude overall acceleration in the 1 s after onset; per fiber and split, the signed largest point of the mean raw DF/F over 0 to 1 s. Reproduced when, for both light and tone, the values of the two splits correlate across fibers at Pearson r >= 0.5 and the tone pattern (tail median positive, anterior median negative) holds in both splits; partially reproduced when this holds for one stimulus. The number of presentations followed by acceleration and by deceleration in each mouse is reported for the first part of the statement.

claims.statement: With isosbestic (415 nm) excitation, large fluorescence changes and spatial patterns to light and tone are not observed, ruling out a hemodynamic origin of the release patterns.
claims.source: Results, Spatial topography of modality specific dopamine release magnitudes over large-scale 3-dimensional volumes, paragraph 1 (Figure S5E-H); code SuppFig05/EFGH
claims.quote: Large fluorescence changes and spatial patterns were not observed with 405nm or 415mn (dLight1.3 isosbestic point) illumination, ruling out a significant impact of hemodynamic changes on the spatial DA release patterns
claims.criterion: Mice DL31 and DL32 (18 Hz, interleaved 470 and 415 nm), included fibers, the GLM of the code at 18 Hz (window -1 to 2 s, tone shift of 6 frames, lags within 9 frames) with 10000 null refits for each channel. Reproduced when, for both light and tone, the median absolute value at 415 nm is below half that at 470 nm and fewer fibers are significant at 415 than at 470 nm; partially reproduced when this holds for one stimulus. The 470 and 405 nm sessions of Figure S5A-D are not in the dandiset.

claims.statement: Latencies to half-maximum are shorter for dopamine increases to light than to tone, and shorter for increases than decreases to tone (light increase 221.6 ms, SD 42.5; tone increase 305.4 ms, SD 100.0; tone decrease 428.3 ms, SD 197.1).
claims.source: Figure 5A-B; Results, Modality specific gradients of dopamine release timing across the striatum, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Response latencies (from stimulus onset to the half-max or half-min amplitude) were shorter, on average, for DA increases to light, and shorter for DA increases than for decreases to the tone
claims.criterion: Tolerance is 10% of each mean; the stated SDs describe the spread across fibers, not the uncertainty of the mean. Latency of the spline estimate to half its peak (or trough), from the code's rule, over fibers with a significant increase (or decrease), pooled over mice. Following the Methods, time is counted from the onset frame (index 0); the code counts one frame later (its 1-based index divided by the frame rate), which is shown as a variant. Reproduced when all three means are within tolerance and the order light increase < tone increase < tone decrease holds; partially reproduced when the order holds but not every mean is within tolerance.

claims.statement: Dopamine release latencies to light follow an anterior-posterior gradient, with faster increases in the anterior striatum, consistent with wave-like dynamics.
claims.source: Figure 5C, E, G; Results, Modality specific gradients of dopamine release timing across the striatum, paragraph 1; code Fig05/general_functions
claims.quote: DA release latencies (time to half-max) for light presentations followed a spatial gradient along the anterior-posterior axis, with relatively faster latencies to increase in the anterior striatum than in the posterior striatum, consistent with wave-like dynamics
claims.criterion: As the code does, per presentation and fiber, the half-maximum latency of the trial activity with locomotion regressed out, for fibers with a significant mean increase whose trial activity exceeds the null band for 3 consecutive frames; latency relative to the fastest fiber of that presentation; per fiber the mean over presentations. Reproduced when the Spearman correlation of AP with the mean relative latency over fibers of all mice is negative with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Dopamine release latencies to tone follow a different gradient, faster in the posterior striatum than in the anterior striatum.
claims.source: Figure 5D, F, H; Figure S6A-B; Results, Modality specific gradients of dopamine release timing across the striatum, paragraph 1
claims.quote: DA release latencies to tone presentations followed a different spatial gradient with faster latencies in the posterior striatum relative to the anterior striatum (Figure 5D, F, H)
claims.criterion: As for fig5g-light-latency-gradient, with the earlier of the increase and decrease latencies of each trial ("either" in the code). Reproduced when the Spearman correlation of AP with the mean relative latency is positive with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The spatial latency gradients are also present in individual mice.
claims.source: Results, Modality specific gradients of dopamine release timing across the striatum, paragraph 1 (Figure S6C-D)
claims.quote: Spatial gradients were also present at the level of individual mice (Figure S6C–D)
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the Spearman correlations of fig5g and fig5h, for mice with at least 5 fibers with a latency. Reproduced when the light correlation is negative in at least 5 of the 7 mice and the tone correlation is positive in at least 5 of the 7; partially reproduced when one holds.

claims.statement: In the mouse with ChR2 in dopamine axons and rDAm3.0 in the striatum, 24 recording locations lie within or on the border of the striatum; 18 of the 24 stimulated locations evoke a significant response at another location, and 22 of the 24 recording locations respond to at least one stimulation.
claims.source: Methods, "DA release to optogenetic stimulation", paragraph 4; Figure 6G legend
claims.quote: the position of the fiber tip had to be within, or on the border of, the striatum ... (24 recording locations) ... (18 out of 24 included locations) ... (22 out of 24 included locations)
claims.criterion: Mouse Opto2. Locations in or bordering the striatum are the fibers flagged included. In each session the stimulated fiber is the one whose DF/F crosses 0.4 at the laser epochs (as the code finds the epochs); sessions where more than one fiber shows the laser artefact are left out. Responses as the Methods define them (mean DF/F over one frame to 0.5 s after laser offset, bootstrap band of 10000 random onsets, 3 consecutive frames). Counts within tolerance decide the claim, each separately (all three within tolerance, reproduced; one or two, partially reproduced; none, not reproduced). The code's further exclusion of two 35 um fibers and one broken fiber is a variant.

claims.statement: Stimulating dopamine axons through one fiber evokes release at neighbouring non-stimulated sites that drops off sharply with distance in all three dimensions.
claims.source: Figure 6E-H; Results, Local control of striatal dopamine release through micro-fiber arrays, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Significant transient increases in stimulation-evoked DA release were detected at sites neighboring the targeted fiber which dropped off sharply with distance in all 3 dimensions (Figure 6E–H)
claims.criterion: Mouse Opto2, included stimulated and recording locations as in fig6-inclusion-counts, responses at non-stimulated sites only. The exponential y = a exp(b d) fitted to the response against Euclidean distance, as the code does. Reproduced when b is negative with a 95% bootstrap interval over stimulation sites that excludes 0, and the Spearman correlation of response with distance is negative (p < 0.05) along each of ML, AP and DV (absolute distances); partially reproduced when b < 0 is supported but not all three axes are.

claims.statement: Evoked release drops off less with distance dorsal to the stimulated fiber than ventral to it, consistent with dorsally extending dopamine axon branches.
claims.source: Figure 6G (D/V distance); Results, Local control of striatal dopamine release through micro-fiber arrays, paragraph 1
claims.quote: activation dorsal to the stimulation location dropped off less with distance than ventral (Figure 6G, D/V Distance, right) ... consistent with the dorsally extending axon morphology of branching DA axons
claims.criterion: Recording sites dorsal (DV smaller) and ventral (DV larger) to the stimulated fiber, non-stimulated sites, Opto2. The exponential decay rate b fitted separately to each group against Euclidean distance. Reproduced when b is less negative dorsally than ventrally with the 95% bootstrap interval of the difference (over stimulation sites) excluding 0; partially reproduced when the point estimates are in that order but the interval includes 0; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: In control mice expressing tdTomato in place of rDAm3.0, single-fiber stimulation evokes no significant fluorescence increase at non-stimulated sites (0 of 48 sites, 26 stimulations in 2 mice), so the release is not a hemodynamic effect.
claims.source: Results, Local control of striatal dopamine release through micro-fiber arrays, paragraph 1; Figure 6G controls
claims.quote: there were no significant stimulation-evoked fluorescent increases in control mice which were injected with tdTomato instead of rDAm3.0 (0/48 non-stimulated sites for 26 single-site stimulations across 2 mice
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test (the bootstrap of fig6-inclusion-counts) in mice Opto4 and Opto9 (tdTomato, 13 sessions each). The laser epochs are found from the fiber with the largest laser artefact, which is taken as the stimulated fiber. Reproduced when no included non-stimulated fiber has a significant increase in any session; not reproduced when any does. The number and size of significant increases are reported either way, with the same count in Opto2 for comparison.

claims.statement: In mice expressing rDAm3.0 without opsin, light through one fiber raises fluorescence at the stimulated site by photoswitching, but at no other site (0 of 22 non-stimulated sites for 3 stimulations).
claims.source: Results, Local control of striatal dopamine release through micro-fiber arrays, paragraph 1; Figure 6E, Figure S7A
claims.quote: Photoswitching in controls, but not opsin expressing mice, was entirely confined to the stimulated site (0/22 non-stimulated sites for 3 single-site stimulations
claims.criterion: Mouse UG21 (3 sessions, 22 included fibers), the test of fig6-inclusion-counts. Reproduced when the stimulated fiber has a significant increase in each session and no other included fiber does in any session; partially reproduced when the non-stimulated sites show none but the stimulated fiber is not significant in every session; not reproduced when a non-stimulated site does.

claims.statement: Neuronal density is not reduced under 50 um fiber tips or between neighbouring fibers relative to unimplanted tissue.
claims.source: Results, Microfiber array design, paragraph 1; Figure S1
claims.quote: there was no significant reduction in neuronal density under 50μm fiber tips or between neighboring fibers, relative to unimplanted tissue (Figure S1)

claims.statement: The magnitude and type of targeting errors (fiber tip relative to its intended target) vary across mice and fibers.
claims.source: Results, Micro-CT based method for precise fiber localization and atlas alignment, paragraph 1; Figure S3
claims.quote: found that the magnitudes and types of targeting errors varied across mice and fibers (Figure S3)

claims.statement: Fiber arrays imaged with a miniscope in freely moving mice show robust D1 SPN Ca2+ signals during locomotion, and dopamine transients associated with the approach to food rewards.
claims.source: Figure 3; Results, Chronic measurements of large-scale calcium and neuromodulator signals in freely moving mice, paragraph 1
claims.quote: This revealed robust, high-SNR signals from GCaMP7f expressed in D1 spiny projection neurons that varied dynamically during locomotion (Figure 3B) ... large transients that appeared to be reliably associated with the initial approach toward food rewards

claims.statement: Stimulating D1 SPNs through a group of ventral striatum fibers, but not dorsal ones, increases jaw movement, an effect absent in a control mouse (interaction p = 7.4e-7; ventral p = 0.0002, dorsal p = 0.45).
claims.source: Figure 7D; Results, Targeted optogenetic manipulations can localize region-specific behavioral effects in the striatum at multiple scales, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We found that stimulating regions in the ventral, but not the dorsal striatum led to rapid increases in jaw movement, which were not present in the non-opsin expressing control mouse
claims.criterion: Jaw velocity change index per stimulation as the code barJawMov.m computes it; the two-way ANOVA with interaction and the two-sample t-tests as in the code. Reproduced when the interaction has p < 0.05, opto against control differs for the ventral group (p < 0.01) and not the dorsal group (p >= 0.05).

claims.statement: Of the eight ventral fibers stimulated singly in each mouse, only one per mouse has a significant effect on jaw movement (3 mice), located in the posterior medial striatum.
claims.source: Figure 7E-F, Figure S7B; Results, Targeted optogenetic manipulations can localize region-specific behavioral effects in the striatum at multiple scales, paragraph 2
claims.quote: We found that only one of the eight ventral fibers from each mouse produced a significant effect on jaw movements ... Post-hoc CT scanning (Figure 7F) localized these fibers to the posterior medial striatum
claims.criterion: The change index per fiber with the code's bootstrap (barJawMov_singleFib.m). Reproduced when exactly one fiber per mouse is significant at p < 0.01.

claims.statement: During mating the probability of accepting behaviours (lordosis, wiggle) increases gradually over the interaction, while resistance behaviours (dart, top up, kick, turn) first increase and then slowly decrease.
claims.source: Figure 1b, Extended Data Figure 1a, Results "Dynamics of female behaviours in mating", paragraph 1
claims.quote: The behaviours were dynamic, with the probability of accepting behaviours gradually increasing, whereas resistance behaviours initially increased and then slowly decreased (Fig. 1b and Extended Data Fig. 1a).
claims.criterion: Per trial, the fraction of each 20-s bin occupied by each group, from male entry (into_male_cage) to 600 s after it, averaged over trials (bins with fewer than 5 trials are dropped). Accepting escalates if the Spearman correlation of the mean curve with time is positive with p below 0.05 and the mean of the last third of the bins exceeds that of the first third. Resistance rises then falls if the peak of the mean curve, after a 3-bin running mean, is later than the first bin and within the first two thirds, and the mean of the last third is below the peak. Trial sets read in turn are all trials with female annotations, and only receptive trials (any lordosis or wiggle), because the paper's 74 trials are not identified. Reproduced if both parts hold under a reading; partially if one part holds.

claims.statement: Females spend 83.9% of their mating behaviour time in male-responsive behaviours (accepting, resistance, staying) and 16.1% in self-initiated ones (approach, sniff, check genital area).
claims.source: Figure 1c, Results "Dynamics of female behaviours in mating", paragraph 2
claims.quote: Females spent six times longer displaying male-responsive (83.9%) versus self-initiated behaviours (16.1%; Fig. 1c).
claims.criterion: Responsive time is the summed duration of lordose, wiggle, stay, dart, top up, kick and turn; self-initiated is approach, sniff and check genital. Readings are the mean over trials of the per-trial fraction, and the pooled fraction over all trials, each on all annotated trials and on receptive trials. Reproduced if any reading is within the tolerance.

claims.statement: Males spend 11.3 times more time in self-initiated mating behaviours (sniff, mount, intromission) than females do in theirs (approach, sniff, check genital area).
claims.source: Figure 1d, Results "Dynamics of female behaviours in mating", paragraph 2
claims.quote: Male spent 11.3 times more time displaying self-initiated mating behaviours than females (Fig. 1d), indicating that males largely drive mating interaction.
claims.criterion: Readings are the mean over trials of the per-trial ratio (trials with some female self-initiated time), the ratio of summed times, and the median per-trial ratio, each on all annotated trials and on receptive trials. Reproduced if any reading is within the tolerance; partially if every reading is above 1 but none within it.

claims.statement: Male copulation (mounting and intromission) comes in bouts separated by interbout intervals with a mean of 13.7 s (1,685 bouts and 1,611 intervals in 74 trials).
claims.source: Figure 1e legend, Results "Neural dynamics in female VMHvl", paragraph 1
claims.quote: Distribution of the durations of male copulation bouts (left; n = 1,685) and IBIs (right; n = 1,611) ... a duration longer than the mean copulation IBI (13.7 s; Fig. 1e, right).
claims.criterion: A bout is a run of mount and intromission annotations. Readings for the merging of annotations into bouts are gaps of at most 0.1 s, gaps of at most 1 s, and no merging; trial sets are all trials with female annotations, receptive trials, and all distinct sessions with male annotations outside the male-inhibition experiment. Reproduced if any reading is within the tolerance. The counts of bouts and intervals are reported but not judged, as the trial set differs.

claims.statement: Females show social behaviours (accepting, resistance and appetitive) for 62% of the duration of each male copulation bout and continue them for 23% of each interbout interval.
claims.source: Figure 1g, Results "Dynamics of female behaviours in mating", paragraph 3
claims.quote: During copulation bouts, females primarily exhibited social behaviours (62% of the duration for each bout) ... they continued social behaviours initiated during the preceding bout (Fig. 1g, right; 23% of IBI duration).
claims.criterion: Social behaviours are lordose, wiggle, dart, top up, kick, turn, approach and sniff (the Methods' grouping, which leaves out stay). Bouts merge annotations with gaps of at most 0.1 s. Readings are the mean over bouts (or intervals) of the per-bout fraction and the pooled time fraction, on all annotated trials and on receptive trials. Reproduced if both numbers are within tolerance under one reading; partially if one is.

claims.statement: Only a small percentage of VMHvl alpha-cells (approximately 2 to 13%) are tuned to any one mating behaviour by choice probability; most show mixed selectivity.
claims.source: Figure 2c, Extended Data Figure 2a,b, Results "Tuning of female VMHvl neurons in mating", paragraph 2, Methods "Choice probability"
claims.quote: a relatively small percentage of VMHvl α-cells (approximately 2–13%) were ‘tuned’ to specific mating behaviours (Fig. 2c and Extended Data Fig. 2a,b), whereas the majority exhibited ‘mixed selectivity’
claims.criterion: In the 15 receptive sessions, 1-s bins of the z-scored trace; a bin belongs to a behaviour when the behaviour covers at least half of it. Choice probability is the ROC area for behaviour bins against the other bins of the interaction (male entry to end of annotation); a cell is tuned if it is above 0.7 or below 0.3 and outside 2 SD of 1000 label shuffles. Behaviours with at least 10 bins in at least 5 mice are analysed. Reproduced if the pooled percentage of tuned cells is between 1% and 15% for every behaviour analysed (the paper says "approximately"); partially if the median over behaviours is in that range.

claims.statement: A linear model of each neuron's activity from behaviour explains little of its variance, with mean cross-validated R2 of 0.08 from female behaviours, 0.14 from male behaviours and 0.15 from both.
claims.source: Figure 2e, Extended Data Figure 2c,d, Results "Tuning of female VMHvl neurons in mating", paragraph 3, Methods "GLM"
claims.quote: only approximately 8% of the variance in neural activity was explained by female mating behaviours (Fig. 2e; mean cross-validated R2 (cvR2) = 0.08; n = 15 mice); approximately 14% by male mating behaviours ... approximately 15% of the variance were explained by combined female and male behaviours
claims.criterion: In the 15 receptive sessions, during the interaction, ridge regression of each z-scored trace on binary behaviour rasters at lags of 0 to 10 s, tenfold contiguous cross-validation, R2 of the pooled held-out predictions. Readings are the mean over all cells and the mean of per-mouse means. Reproduced if all three values are within tolerance under a reading; partially if the ordering (female below male, both at least male) holds and all three are below 0.25, the paper's point being that behaviour explains little.

claims.statement: Adding the activity of the other simultaneously imaged neurons as regressors raises the mean cross-validated R2 to 0.46.
claims.source: Figure 2f, Results "Tuning of female VMHvl neurons in mating", paragraph 4, Methods "GLM"
claims.quote: The introduction of neuronal coupling dramatically increased variance explained by the GLM ... (Fig. 2f,g; mean cvR2 = 0.46; n = 15 mice).
claims.criterion: As for fig2e-glm-behaviour-explains-little, with the instantaneous activity of every other cell added. Reproduced if the value is within tolerance under a reading; partially if it is at least twice the behaviour-only value but outside tolerance.

claims.statement: About 30% of cells have an autocorrelation half-width (ACHW) longer than 25 s, and the mean ACHW is 20 s, longer than the mean interbout interval.
claims.source: Figure 2i, Results "Neural dynamics in female VMHvl", paragraph 1, Methods "Calculation of ACHW"
claims.quote: Of cells, 30% displayed ACHWs longer than 25 s (mean ACHW of 20 s; Fig. 2i), a duration longer than the mean copulation IBI (13.7 s; Fig. 1e, right).
claims.criterion: ACHW as in the authors' code (MATLAB-style autocorrelation, the lag whose value is closest to 0.5, lags to 50 s), on the 15 receptive sessions. Readings are the whole recording and the interaction only, each smoothed as in the code (9-frame moving average) and unsmoothed, pooled over cells. Reproduced if both numbers are within tolerance under one reading; partially if one is.

claims.statement: The ACHW of the same cells is shorter when the male is behind a perforated pencil cup (14.3 s) than during free interaction (19.6 s), 470 neurons from 5 mice.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 3a-c, Results "Neural dynamics in female VMHvl", paragraph 1
claims.quote: the ACHW of the same female cells was significantly lower when the male was confined in a perforated enclosure (pencil cup) than during free mating interaction (mean ACHW for pencil cup of 14.3 ± 0.42 s, mean ACHW for free interaction of 19.64 ± 0.58 s

claims.statement: An rSLDS fit to each receptive mating trial explains 64.08% (SD 6.8) of the variance of the neural trajectories, n = 15 mice.
claims.source: Figure 3a, Results "Neural dynamics in female VMHvl", paragraph 2
claims.quote: directly to neural data during individual trials (Fig. 3a,d,e; n = 15 mice; mean variance explained (calculated as cvR2 between observed and predicted neural trajectories) of 64.08 ± 6.8%).

claims.statement: The rSLDS reveals one integration dimension with a long time constant (110.7 +- 13.6 s) compared with the next (24.5 +- 5.1 s), forming an approximate line attractor; n = 15 mice, P = 6.5e-5.
claims.source: Figure 3b,c,e, Results "Neural dynamics in female VMHvl", paragraphs 2 (Figure 3c legend) and 3
claims.quote: Distribution of time constants across animals fit by the rSLDS ... mean time constant of dimension 1: 110.7 ± 13.6 and dimension 2: 24.5 ± 5.1 ... revealed that the fit dynamical system contains a line attractor (Fig. 3e)

claims.statement: A single-state linear dynamical system driven by male sniff, mount and intromission predicts activity in the integration dimension with cvR2 of 0.88 +- 0.02 and an intrinsic time constant above 200 s.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 3r-u, Results "Neural dynamics in female VMHvl", paragraph 5
claims.quote: We found that the model fits with high accuracy (cvR2 of 0.88 ± 0.02) and possess a large intrinsic time constant (more than 200 s), revealing that it does indeed function as an integrator (Extended Data Fig. 3s).

claims.statement: Of neurons contributing to the integration dimension, 56% correlate with an ideal ramp with r2 above 0.5, but they peak at different times.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 4a-d, Results "Neural dynamics in female VMHvl", paragraph 6
claims.quote: some single cells exhibited ramping-like activity (Extended Data Fig. 4a,b; 56% of neurons r2 > 0.5), but that different cells peaked at different times during the mating interaction

claims.statement: Transient optogenetic inhibition of VMHvl pushes population activity off the line attractor, after which it relaxes back to the attractor, as the flow field fit to unperturbed data predicts; n = 3 mice.
claims.source: Figure 3h-k, Extended Data Figure 5c-j, Results "Perturbations of the female line attractor", paragraph 1
claims.quote: transient optogenetic inhibition creates consistent transient off-manifold responses in neural state space during the period of photostimulation, with the neural trajectory returning to the nearest fixed point along the line attractor post-inhibition (Fig. 3h–k and Extended Data Fig. 5e–j).

claims.statement: Activity in the integration dimension during copulation interbout intervals is as high as in the preceding bout, so a decoder cannot tell bouts from intervals (0.52 against a shuffle of 0.49, n = 4 mice, P = 0.2).
claims.source: Figure 4a,b, Results "Perturbations of the female line attractor", paragraph 2
