claims.quote: the average value of the integration dimension during copulation IBIs was relatively high, similar to and statistically indistinguishable from that measured during the preceding copulation bout (Fig. 4a) ... (n = 4 mice, P = 0.2, Mann–Whitney U-test, mean value of data of 0.52 ± 0.007, shuffle of 0.49 ± 0.03).

claims.statement: When male mating is stopped for minutes by optogenetic activation of the male's VMH, activity in the female's integration dimension stays elevated; n = 4 mice.
claims.source: Figure 4c,d, Results "Perturbations of the female line attractor", paragraph 3
claims.quote: Nevertheless, activity in the integration dimension in the female brain remained elevated for minutes while the male was prevented from resuming mating (Fig. 4d)

claims.statement: Activity in the integration dimension peaks just before ejaculation and drops immediately after; n = 4 mice.
claims.source: Figure 4g,h, Results "Perturbations of the female line attractor", paragraph 5
claims.quote: We examined activity in the integration dimension during ejaculation and observed that it peaked just before ejaculation, and immediately dropped thereafter (Fig. 4g,h)

claims.statement: Over the natural oestrus cycle, rSLDS models fit on receptive days have a line attractor and those fit on unreceptive days do not (line-attractor score 1.9 +- 0.2 against 0.05 +- 0.02, n = 4 mice, P = 0.02).
claims.source: Figure 5b-f, Results "Attractor encodes level of receptivity", paragraphs 1 (Figure 5c legend) and 2
claims.quote: Line-attractor scores for dynamical systems fit during receptive and unreceptive days (n = 4 mice, mean ± s.e.m. of 0.05 ± 0.02 (unreceptive) and 1.9 ± 0.2 (receptive) ... Models fit to data from unreceptive days failed to identify a single dimension with a very long time constant, indicating the absence of a line attractor

claims.statement: Projected onto the integration dimension found on the receptive day, activity on unreceptive days does not ramp and stays low during male mounting (normalised value 0.09 on unreceptive against 0.69 on receptive days, n = 4 mice).
claims.source: Figure 5g,h, Extended Data Figure 6c-f, Results "Attractor encodes level of receptivity", paragraph 3
claims.quote: Although male mounting occurred on unreceptive days (Fig. 5h, purple rasters), activity in the first rSLDS dimension was low during this behaviour (Extended Data Fig. 6e) ... mean value during unreceptive day: 0.09 ± 0.04, receptive day: 0.69 ± 0.05
claims.criterion: Uses the authors' deposited rSLDS weights for the two mice that have them (m541, and the file labelled m542, whose cells are those of mouse 543). The receptive day is the one whose recording is also deposited as the mouse's receptive session. The integration factor is the one whose receptive-day projection has the longer ACHW, signed so that it is higher after male entry than before. The projection is the weights times each day's z-scored activity, min-max normalised over the three days together (variant, normalised by the receptive day's range). Reproduced if in both mice the mean normalised value during mounting is higher on the receptive day than on each unreceptive day; partially if in one mouse. The paper's values are compared, not judged, since n differs.

claims.statement: Cells weighted on the integration dimension have shorter ACHW on unreceptive than on receptive days (16.1 +- 0.8 s against 25.2 +- 1.5 s, P < 0.001), while cells that do not contribute to it do not change.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 7a-h, Results "Attractor encodes level of receptivity", paragraph 4
claims.quote: the lower ACHW of cells weighted on the first rSLDS dimension on unreceptive versus receptive days (Extended Data Fig. 7a,b; distribution mean for ACHW on unreceptive days 16.1 ± 0.8 s, and on receptive days 25.2 ± 1.5 s; P < 0.001)
claims.criterion: Same mice, days, factor and data as ed6e-projection-unreceptive-days. Weighted cells have an absolute weight above one SD of the weights (the authors' code). ACHW as in fig2i-persistent-cells, smoothed as in the code. Two-sample KS test, as in Extended Data Figure 7c,d, of receptive against unreceptive days (both pooled, and each separately). Reproduced if, in both mice, weighted cells have a longer mean ACHW on the receptive day with KS p below 0.05 and other cells show no difference at p 0.05; partially if the first part holds in both mice or both parts in one.

claims.statement: Attractor dynamics disappear after ovariectomy and return after hormone priming.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 9j-n, Results "Attractor encodes level of receptivity", paragraph 5
claims.quote: The results indicated that attractor dynamics disappeared following OVX and were reinstated following hormone priming (Extended Data Fig. 9j).

claims.statement: In oestrogen-injected females, the area under the curve of the integration dimension correlates with the percentage of time spent in accepting behaviours (r2 = 0.62, P < 0.0001, n = 50 trials), and not with resistance or appetitive behaviours.
claims.source: Figure 5i-l, Extended Data Figure 10b, Results "Attractor encodes level of receptivity", paragraph 7
claims.quote: The area under the curve was strongly and positively correlated with the percentage of time that females performed acceptance behaviours during each mating interaction (Fig. 5k,l; r2 = 0.62; P < 0.0001; n = 50 trials).

claims.statement: In the same trials, the area under the curve of the population mean of all neurons does not correlate with the percentage of time spent in accepting behaviours.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 10c,d, Results "Attractor encodes level of receptivity", paragraph 7
claims.quote: Finally, the population mean of neural activity did not show any correlation with the percentage of time that females performed acceptance behaviours
claims.criterion: The 42 oestrogen-injected sessions (WT_7d). Accepting percentage is lordose plus wiggle time over the time from male entry to the end of the annotation. The area under the curve of the population mean of the z-scored traces is read three ways, because the window is not given; from male entry to the end of annotation after subtracting the mean of the 60 s before entry, the same without subtraction, and the 200 s from first male contact after subtraction. The test is linear regression, as in the paper. Following the protocol's rule for readings, reproduced if the slope is not significant (p at least 0.05) under any reading, and not reproduced if it is significant under all; the r2 of every reading is given either way.

claims.statement: About 78% of Esr1+ VMHvl cells express Oxtr mRNA, and about 61% of these also express Avpr1a mRNA, in a single-cell RNA-seq atlas of VMHvl.
claims.source: Results, Most Esr1+ neurons co-express Oxytocin and Vasopressin receptors, paragraph 1; Figure 1E
claims.quote: Overall, ~78% of Esr1 + cells in VMHvl expressed Oxtr mRNA, and ~61% of these cells also expressed Avpr1a mRNAs
claims.criterion: Uses the outside atlas of Kim et al. 2019 (doi:10.1016/j.cell.2019.09.020), analysed "as described previously" (STAR Methods, Transcriptomic analysis); the expression threshold is not given. Reproduced when both fractions are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Bath application of OXT plus AVP (400 nM each), or of either peptide alone, evokes strong calcium responses (dF/F about 500-600%) in VMHvl Esr1 neurons in acute slices.
claims.source: Results, Most Esr1+ neurons co-express Oxytocin and Vasopressin receptors, paragraph 2; Figure 1F, S1F-G
claims.quote: Perfusing a mixture of 400nM (each) OXT plus AVP or individually administering these peptides elicited strong (ΔF/F ~500–600%) responses in VMHvl Esr1 cells
claims.criterion: The paper reports a range, 500 to 600%; the claim holds inside the range widened by 10% of each bound (450 to 660%), for the mean response of the 124 cells of Figure 1F. Which measure of the response (peak of the mean trace, or mean of per-cell peaks) is not given; either reading counts.

claims.statement: In slices from mice with Cre-dependent Oxtr/Avpr1a gRNAs, the fraction of GCaMP8s-expressing cells responsive to OXT plus AVP is reduced from 42.6 +/- 3% (scrambled gRNA) to 13 +/- 3.3%.
claims.source: Results, Altered VMHvl Esr1 neural activity during social interactions, paragraph 1; Figure 2E
claims.quote: The fraction of GCaMP8s-expressing cells responsive to mixed AVP and OXT peptides was reduced from 42.6± 3% in Scr gRNA controls to 13± 3.3% (~70% reduction) in Oxtr/Avpr1a gRNAs
claims.criterion: The criterion for a responsive cell is not given in the Methods. Reproduced when both fractions are within tolerance (the paper's stated spread) and the Mann-Whitney test across slices gives p < 0.01, the level printed in the Figure 2 legend.

claims.statement: Bilateral co-editing of Oxtr and Avpr1a in VMH (LV gRNAs plus Cas9 AAV) reduces attack towards male intruders (number, probability, total time and bout duration of attacks) and lengthens the latency to the first attack.
claims.source: Results, Oxtr/Avpr1a-mediated neuropeptidergic signaling in VMH is required for male territorial aggression, paragraph 3; Figure 2G, S2B-C
claims.quote: Experimental mice displayed a notable reduction in aggression towards male intruders, as evidenced by significant decreases in the number and time-varying probability of attack bouts, the total time spent attacking and the average duration of each attack bout; in addition, the latency to the 1st attack bout was significantly increased
claims.criterion: Per mouse, over the first 15 min of the male-male assay (STAR Methods, Behavior annotations), the number of attack bouts, total attack time, mean attack bout duration and latency to the first attack, compared between groups with a Mann-Whitney test. Reproduced when each measure differs in the stated direction with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when some do.

claims.statement: Bilateral co-editing does not change time spent sniffing male intruders, nor sniffing or mounting of female intruders.
claims.source: Results, Oxtr/Avpr1a-mediated neuropeptidergic signaling in VMH is required for male territorial aggression, paragraph 3; Figure 2G-H, S2D
claims.quote: the time spent in close investigation (sniffing) of male intruders did not differ significantly between experimental and control male residents ... Experimental males also did not differ significantly from controls in their sniffing or mounting behavior towards female intruders
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the Mann-Whitney test between groups per mouse (n=11 each) on male-directed sniff time over the first 15 min of the male-male assay, and female-directed sniff time and the mounting measures of S2D over 10 min of male-female interaction (STAR Methods, Behavior annotations); for the inter-mount interval, mice with at most 1 mount bout are left out (same section). The percentage of animals mounting (S2Di) is a group proportion and is reported without a per-mouse test. Reproduced when none gives p < 0.05; the effect sizes are reported either way.

claims.statement: Bilateral Cre-dependent co-editing in VMHvl Esr1 neurons reduces most measures of aggression towards males, less strongly than the constitutive system, while sniffing duration is unaffected.
claims.source: Results, Altered VMHvl Esr1 neural activity during social interactions, paragraph 2; Figure 3C, S3C
claims.quote: Bilateral co-disruption of Oxtr/Avpr1a in VMHvl Esr1 neurons significantly reduced most metrics of aggression towards male intruder compared to control mice, although to a somewhat lower extent than observed with the Cre-independent system
claims.criterion: Per mouse, over 15-20 min of male-male interaction, the attack measures of Figure 3C and S3C (percent attacking, attack bout duration, latency, inter-bout interval, number and probability of attack bouts) and sniff duration, Mann-Whitney between groups. Reproduced when more than half of the attack measures are significantly lower (or latency longer) at p < 0.05 and sniff duration is not significantly different.

claims.statement: Bulk calcium activity of VMHvl Esr1 neurons during male-directed sniffing and attack is reduced in mice with bilateral Cre-dependent co-editing.
claims.source: Results, Altered VMHvl Esr1 neural activity during social interactions, paragraph 2; Figure 3E-H
claims.quote: we observed a significant reduction in overall VMHvl Esr1 neuronal activity during the infrequent attack bouts exhibited by experimental mice ... A reduction in VMHvl Esr1 activity during sniffing episodes was also observed in these mice
claims.criterion: From the STAR Methods (Fiberphotometry recordings and analysis), the 470 nm signal corrected by a least-squares fit of the 405 nm signal, dF/F = (F470 - F405)/F405, normalized to a 2-s pre-bout baseline (mean and SD); AUC and peak over 10 s after bout onset, per bout; for sniffing, the first 1 min of sniffing after intruder entry. Mann-Whitney on bouts between groups. Reproduced when AUC and peak are lower in experimental mice at p < 0.05 for both sniffing and attack.

claims.statement: During interactions with females, bulk calcium activity during sniffing and mounting does not differ between experimental and control males.
claims.source: Results, Altered VMHvl Esr1 neural activity during social interactions, paragraph 2; Figure S3E-F
claims.quote: during male-female interactions, calcium signals in experimental males were not significantly different from controls
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, Mann-Whitney between groups on the AUC of the z-scored behavior-triggered average for female-directed sniffing (1 min) and mounting, computed as in fig3fh-photometry-reduced. Reproduced when neither gives p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Mice with unilateral editing and imaging (the CRISPRoscopy mice) show no deficit in sniffing or aggression compared with controls.
claims.source: Results, Single cell CRISPRoscopy imaging, paragraph 1; Figure S4A
claims.quote: Indeed, unilateral injected experimental animals displayed no deficits in sniffing or aggression compared to controls
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The S4 legend names no test for panel A; the paper's test for the same measures in Figures 2, 3 and S3 is the Mann-Whitney test, used here. Per mouse, total sniff time, sniff bout duration, total attack time, attack bout duration, latency to first attack, inter-attack interval and attack probability, during the male-intruder period. Reproduced when none differs at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: CRISPRoscopy recorded 585 units from 5 control mice and 546 units from 7 experimental mice.
claims.source: STAR Methods, Micro-endoscopic data extraction, last sentence
claims.quote: A total of 585 units (n=5 mice) from control and 546 units (n=7 mice) from experimental mice were recorded
claims.criterion: Counts are exact; tolerance 0 because they are counts of recorded units and mice, not measurements. A difference is reported per mouse.

claims.statement: During interactions with a male intruder, the activity of all VMHvl Esr1 units (sigma above pre-intruder baseline, and z-scored) is slightly but significantly lower in experimental than in control mice.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on VMHvl Esr1 activity and intruder sex representations, paragraph 1; Figure 4Ei, 4Fi, S4Di
claims.quote: During interactions with a male intruder, the experimental cumulative distribution function (ECDF) and mean activity of all units (pooled from n=4 control and n=7 experimental animals) were slightly but significantly decreased in experimental mice
claims.criterion: Per unit, the mean activity in units of sigma above the pre-intruder baseline over the first part of the first male interaction, and the same for z-scored traces (z relative to the cell's mean over the whole recording). The window is open; the Results say "the first two minutes" and the Figure 4E-F legend "1 minute of interaction" (S4D also 1 min); readings 1 min and 2 min. Tests as named, under the file-level readings of "nested" and of the baseline. Reproduced when, under a reading, experimental activity is lower than control at p < 0.05 by both the Mann-Whitney and the KS test for sigma-normalized activity.

claims.statement: During interactions with females, activity in units of sigma above baseline does not differ between experimental and control mice, while z-scored activity is slightly but significantly higher in experimental mice.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on VMHvl Esr1 activity and intruder sex representations, paragraph 1; Figure 4Eii, 4Fii, S4Dii
claims.quote: During interactions with females there was no significant difference in activity (measured in σ above baseline) between experimental and control animals ... although z-scored activity showed a slight but significant increase
claims.criterion: As in fig4ef-male-activity-slightly-lower, for the first female interaction. The absence part is judged on the paper's tests (Mann-Whitney on mean activity, KS on the distribution, sigma-normalized). Reproduced when neither finds a difference at p < 0.05 and the KS test on z-scored activity finds experimental higher at p < 0.05. Under several readings of window and nesting, the outcome is the one they all give.

claims.statement: Among male-responsive units (at least 2 sigma above baseline), mean activity does not differ between control and experimental mice.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on VMHvl Esr1 activity and intruder sex representations, paragraph 1; Figure S4E
claims.quote: However, the mean activity among cells considered as “active” (≥ 2σ above baseline 66 ) did not differ between control and experimental mice
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Units with mean activity of at least 2 sigma above the pre-intruder baseline during the male interaction window (readings as in fig4ef-male-activity-slightly-lower); nested Mann-Whitney between groups under the file-level readings. Reproduced when the test finds no difference at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The fraction of male-activated units (selective or mixed) is slightly smaller in experimental than in control mice (34.6% against 38.3%), and male-selective units are reduced by about 56% (6.3 +/- 2% against 14.4 +/- 4%).
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on VMHvl Esr1 activity and intruder sex representations, paragraph 2; Figure 4G, S4F
claims.quote: The percentage of all male-activated neurons (selective or mixed) was slightly smaller in experimental than control mice (34.6% vs. 38.3%, respectively ... while there was a ~56% reduction in the small fraction of male-selective neurons (6.3 ± 2% vs. 14.4 ± 4%, respectively
claims.criterion: A unit is male-selective when its activity is at least 2 sigma above the pre-intruder baseline during the male interaction and below 2 sigma during the female interaction, and mixed when at least 2 sigma during both (Results; Figure 4G legend). Window and baseline as in fig4ef-male-activity-slightly-lower. The percentages can be read as (a) pooled over units of all mice of the group, or (b) the mean over mice (the +/- values suggest b for the selective fractions). Reproduced when, under a reading, all four values are within tolerance; partially when the experimental male-selective fraction is lower than control but values fall outside.

claims.statement: During female interactions the fractions of female-selective and of mixed-selectivity units are increased by about 4% and 44% in experimental mice.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on VMHvl Esr1 activity and intruder sex representations, paragraph 2; Figure 4G, S4F
claims.quote: Conversely, during female interactions the fraction of female-selective and mixed selectivity neurons was increased by ~4% and ~44%, respectively, in experimental mice
claims.criterion: Fractions defined as in fig4g-male-selective-reduced. "Increased by" can be read as (a) a relative change, (experimental - control) / control, or (b) a difference in percentage points; and the fractions as pooled or per-mouse means. Reproduced when, under one reading, both increases are within tolerance; partially when both fractions are higher in experimental mice but outside tolerance.

claims.statement: Linear SVM decoders trained on VMHvl Esr1 activity from either control or experimental mice predict intruder sex with virtually 100% accuracy.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on VMHvl Esr1 activity and intruder sex representations, paragraph 3; Figure 4D
claims.quote: linear SVM decoders trained on imaging data from either control or experimental mice correctly predicted intruder sex with virtually 100% accuracy
claims.criterion: From the STAR Methods (Decoding intruder sex), per mouse, frame-wise linear SVM on N-unit population vectors from all frames of social interaction, equal numbers of male and female frames, stratified five-fold cross-validation, repeated 100 times, accuracy averaged per mouse; shuffle control with labels assigned at random to each behavior bout, 500 repeats. Reproduced when the mean accuracy of each group is at least 90% and above the shuffled accuracy at p < 0.05 (Mann-Whitney across mice). The SVM regularization is not given; readings C = 0.1, 1 and 10, and the outcome is the one they all give.

claims.statement: Partial least-squares regression of population activity against intruder sex separates responses to males and females in both control and experimental mice.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on VMHvl Esr1 activity and intruder sex representations, paragraph 3; Figure 4C, S4B-C
claims.quote: This analysis revealed a clear separation of responses during encounters with males vs. females in both control and experimental animals
claims.criterion: From the STAR Methods (Dimensionality reduction), per mouse, PLS of all unit traces against a vector that is -1 with a male intruder present, 1 with a female, 0 otherwise. The paper gives no measure of "clear separation". Readings of it (a) the mean PLS1 score differs in sign between male and female frames; (b) the area under the ROC curve of PLS1 scores, male against female frames, is above 0.75 or below 0.25. Reproduced when, under both readings, every mouse of both groups separates; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The PLS1 variance explained per group (S4C) is reported.

claims.statement: Single-unit activity during male-directed sniffing and attack is slightly but significantly lower in experimental than in control mice, while activity during female-directed sniffing and mounting is similar.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on behavior representation in VMHvl, paragraph 1; Figure 5A, 5C, S5A-B
claims.quote: The ECDF and average single unit activity during male-directed sniffing or attack was slightly but significantly lower in experimental than in control mice ... In contrast, during social interactions with females, activity during sniffing and mounting was similar
claims.criterion: Per unit, mean activity (sigma above pre-intruder baseline; z-scored in S5) over all frames annotated as each behavior. Tests as named under the file-level readings. Reproduced when male-directed sniffing and attack are both lower in experimental mice at p < 0.05 and, for female-directed sniffing and mounting, the paper's tests on sigma-normalized activity find no difference at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Mean bout-triggered activity is slightly but significantly lower in experimental mice during male-directed sniffing and attack, higher during female-directed sniffing, and unchanged during mounting.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on behavior representation in VMHvl, paragraph 1; Figure S5C
claims.quote: The mean activity during male-directed sniffing or attack was slightly but significantly lower in experimental than in control mice ... while it was significantly higher during female-directed sniffing, but unchanged during mounting
claims.criterion: From the STAR Methods (Micro-endoscopic data extraction), for each unit and bout, the z-scored trace minus the mean of a 2-3 s pre-bout baseline, averaged over 15 s after onset. The baseline length is open; readings 2 s and 3 s. Nested Mann-Whitney under the file-level readings. Reproduced when all four directions hold (male sniff and attack lower at p < 0.05, female sniff higher at p < 0.05, mounting not different at p < 0.05).

claims.statement: During male interactions, sniff-selective units are reduced from 8.9 +/- 3% to 3.9 +/- 2% and attack-selective units from 6 +/- 0.9% to 1.8 +/- 0.7% in experimental mice; the mixed-selectivity fraction is reduced by about 22%, and units active during male-directed behaviors fall from 36.2% to 22.4%; female-directed selective fractions are similar.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on behavior representation in VMHvl, paragraph 2; Figure 5B, 5D
claims.quote: In experimental mice, during male interactions the fraction of sniff-selective units was reduced by ~40% relative to controls (3.9 ± 2% in OARs gRNAs mice vs. 8.9 ± 3% in Scr gRNAs mice) while the small proportion of attack-selective units was reduced by ~70% (1.8 ± 0.7% vs. 6 ± 0.9% ... The fraction of neurons exhibiting mixed behavioral selectivity (i.e., active during both behaviors) was moderately reduced (~22% ... Overall, there was a ~38% reduction in the fraction of active units during all male-directed behaviors (from 36.2% in control to 22.4% in experimental mice). In contrast, the fraction of female-directed sniffing- or mount-selective units was similar between control and experimental males
claims.criterion: Per unit, mean activity in sigma above the pre-intruder baseline over all frames of each behavior; selective for sniff when at least 2 sigma during sniffing and below 2 sigma during attack, and conversely; mixed when at least 2 sigma during both (Results; Figure 5B legend). "Active during all male-directed behaviors" read as (a) at least 2 sigma during sniffing or attack, or (b) the sum of the selective and mixed fractions as plotted in 5Di. Fractions as (a) pooled or (b) per-mouse means. Reproduced when, under one reading, all expected values are within tolerance; partially when the directions hold for sniff- and attack-selective and active fractions but some values fall outside. Female-directed selective fractions are reported with a Mann-Whitney test across mice; the text gives no test for them.

claims.statement: By choice probability, the percentages of attack- and sniff-tuned units during male-male interactions are reduced by about 80% and 70% in experimental mice, mixed-selectivity units increase by about 18%, and units tuned to sniffing females against sniffing males rise from 28.8 +/- 3% to 41.1 +/- 3%.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on behavior representation in VMHvl, paragraph 3; Figure 5E, S5D
claims.quote: We observed an ~80% and ~70% reduction in the percentage of attack- and sniff-tuned units, respectively, in experimental vs. control mice during male-male interactions ... with a concomitant ~18% increase in the fraction of units exhibiting mixed selectivity ... In contrast, the percentage of units tuned to sniffing females (vs. sniffing males) was increased in experimental mice (28.8 ± 3% vs. 41.1 ± 3%
claims.criterion: From the STAR Methods (Choice probability), per unit and pair of behaviors, the area under the ROC curve built from histograms of the unit's dF/F values in frames of each behavior; shuffled 100 times by shuffling behavior bout timings; tuned when CP > 0.7 and more than 2 shuffled SDs above the shuffled mean (the Results print "p < 0.5"; the Methods' 2-SD rule is used). Open details and their readings. Direction, (a) CP(A vs B) > 0.7 means tuned to A and CP(B vs A) > 0.7 tuned to B, (b) only CP(A vs B) is computed and tuned to B means CP < 0.3 with the mirrored shuffle test. Bout shuffling, (a) circular shift of the bout sequence by a random offset, (b) random reassignment of bout onsets within the interaction period. The trace used for "dF/F", (a) the sigma-normalized trace, (b) the z-scored trace. Fractions as pooled or per-mouse means, and "reduction" or "increase" as relative change. For the sniff female against sniff male fractions, the values are assigned as the word "increased" requires (control 28.8%, experimental 41.1%); elsewhere in this section the paper lists the experimental value first, which would give the opposite assignment and contradict the text, so that reading is reported and does not decide. Every combination is run; reproduced when all the expected values are within tolerance under one combination and the direction of each change holds under all; blocked as methods_underspecified when the directions differ between combinations.

claims.statement: Linear decoders distinguish attack from sniffing equally well in control and experimental mice.
claims.source: Results, Effect of Oxtr/Avpr1a co-editing on behavior representation in VMHvl, paragraph 3; Figure S5E
claims.quote: there was no significant difference between control and experimental mice in the performance of linear decoders trained to distinguish attack from sniffing based on VMHvl Esr1 activity
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. From the STAR Methods (Decoding behavior from neural activity), per mouse, frame-wise linear SVM on attack against sniffing frames towards male intruders, equal numbers of frames of each, 20 repeats, accuracy averaged per mouse; the cross-validation scheme is not given for this decoder, and the stratified five-fold scheme of the sex decoder is used as the paper's nearest stated choice. The Methods say frames are "sampled at 15 Hz" while traces are at 10 Hz; the data's own rate is used. Reproduced when the Mann-Whitney test across mice finds no difference between groups at p < 0.05; both groups' accuracy against shuffled decoders is reported.

claims.statement: rSLDS models with 5 latent dimensions and 3 discrete states, fit to each mouse with at least 31 units, capture about 85% of the variance, with similar performance in control and experimental mice; attack occurs within a single rSLDS state in both groups.
claims.source: Results, VMHvl Esr1 line attractor dynamics require Oxtr/Avpr1a-mediated signaling, paragraph 2; Figure S6D
claims.quote: In both the control and experimental groups, the fit models reduced the dimensionality of the data to 5 latent factors and three states (S1-S3) capturing ~85% of the observed variance in neural activity. Model performance (cvR 2) was similar between control and experimental mice ... During male-male interactions, attack behavior occurred during a single rSLDS state in both control and experimental males
claims.criterion: The rSLDS settings for all claims below are these. From the Results, one model per mouse with at least 31 units, 5 latent dimensions, 3 discrete states. From the ssm notebook the paper's code links, transitions recurrent_only, dynamics diagonal_gaussian, emissions gaussian_orthog, single subspace, Laplace-EM with a structured mean-field posterior, 100 iterations. Time bins of 0.1 s (traces downsampled to 10 Hz, STAR Methods). Open details and their readings. Which frames are fit, (a) the whole male-intruder part of the session from intruder entry to removal plus the post-intruder period, (b) the whole session (STAR Methods say the model relates "the activity of recorded neurons (y) during male directed behavior (sniffing, dominant mounting and attack)"). The trace, (a) z-scored, (b) sigma-normalized. Seeds and restarts are not given; fits are run with seeds 0 (the DJALab notebook's npr.seed(0)) to 3, and each claim's outcome is the one all seeds give. Performance is the forward-simulation score of the STAR Methods (normalized MSE of predictions over a short horizon, computed on held-out folds), with the horizon and folds not given (readings 1 s and 5 s; five folds over time); variance explained as the R2 of the emissions reconstruction. Reproduced when variance explained is within tolerance in both groups, performance does not differ at p < 0.05 (Mann-Whitney), and in each mouse attack "occurred during a single rSLDS state", read as (a) a majority of attack frames fall in one state, (b) at least 90% do.

claims.statement: In control mice, the time constant of the first rSLDS dimension (about 100-120 s) is significantly larger than that of the second (about 40 s).
claims.source: Results, VMHvl Esr1 line attractor dynamics require Oxtr/Avpr1a-mediated signaling, paragraph 2; Figure 6A
claims.quote: In control mice, the time constant (τ) of the 1 st rSLDS dimension (derived from the first eigenvalue of the fit dynamics matrix; see Methods ) was significantly higher than that of the 2 nd dimension (~100–120s vs. ~40s
claims.criterion: tau = |1 / log(|lambda|)| for each eigenvalue lambda of the dynamics matrix, in time bins, times 0.1 s (STAR Methods, Estimation of time constants), sorted in decreasing order. Which dynamics matrix is open; readings (a) the matrix of the discrete state in which attack occurs, (b) the mean of tau over the three states' matrices. rSLDS settings and readings as in fig6-rslds-fit-quality. Tau 1 reproduces inside the reported range widened by 10% of each bound (90 to 132 s); tau 2 within 10% of 40 s. Reproduced when, under a reading, the group means are within tolerance and the Kruskal-Wallis test across the five dimensions' tau values (mice as samples) gives p < 0.05 with dimension 1 the largest. The Figure 6 legend names no pairwise test after the Kruskal-Wallis test; readings (a) the Kruskal-Wallis test alone, (b) Dunn's multiple comparison of dimension 1 with dimension 2, the correction the paper pairs with Kruskal-Wallis in the S1F and S7 legends. With 4 mice a pairwise test may be unable to reach p < 0.05; the attainable minimum p is reported.

claims.statement: In experimental mice the first two rSLDS dimensions have statistically indistinguishable time constants (below 50 s), because the first dimension's time constant is reduced relative to controls.
claims.source: Results, VMHvl Esr1 line attractor dynamics require Oxtr/Avpr1a-mediated signaling, paragraph 2; Figure 6C, S6E
claims.quote: In contrast, in experimental mice the first two rSLDS dimensions had statistically indistinguishable τ values (<50s; Figure 6C ) due to a reduced 1 st dimension τ
claims.criterion: Tau and readings as in fig6a-control-tau1-greater. Reproduced when, under a reading, the experimental mean tau 1 and tau 2 are below 55 s (50 s plus 10%), the test of tau 1 against tau 2 in experimental mice finds no difference at p < 0.05 (the absence is judged on the paper's Kruskal-Wallis test), and tau 1 is lower in experimental than in control mice at p < 0.01 by Mann-Whitney (the S6E image shows two stars).

claims.statement: The line attractor score, log2 of the ratio of the two largest time constants, is about 1.6 in control mice and close to zero in experimental mice.
claims.source: Results, VMHvl Esr1 line attractor dynamics require Oxtr/Avpr1a-mediated signaling, paragraph 2; Figure 6F
claims.quote: This yielded a line attractor score (calculated as the log 2 of the ratio of the τ ‘s of the 1 st and 2 nd dimensions) of ~1.6 ... and consequently a line attractor score close to zero
claims.criterion: Score = log2(tau_n / tau_n-1), the two largest time constants (STAR Methods), per mouse; tau and readings as in fig6a-control-tau1-greater. "Close to zero" is judged by the Methods' own reading, a score below 1 (the Methods say it "is greater than one for systems that possess a line attractor"). Reproduced when, under a reading, the control mean is within tolerance, the experimental mean is below 1, and Mann-Whitney finds control higher at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: During mounting of female intruders, co-editing does not significantly reduce the first-dimension time constant or the line attractor score.
claims.source: Results, VMHvl Esr1 line attractor dynamics require Oxtr/Avpr1a-mediated signaling, paragraph 2; Figure S6F
claims.quote: during mounting behavior towards female intruders, co-perturbation of Oxtr/Avpr1a-mediated signaling did not significantly reduce the 1st dimension τ values or the line attractor score in experimental mice compared to controls
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's Mann-Whitney test. rSLDS fit to the female-intruder part of each session (readings for the frames as in fig6-rslds-fit-quality, with female-directed behavior in place of male-directed), mice with at least 31 units; tau 1 and score as in fig6a-control-tau1-greater and fig6f-line-attractor-score, with the state in which mounting occurs in place of attack for reading (a). Reproduced when neither tau 1 nor the score is lower in experimental mice at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Flow fields of the fit rSLDS in the plane of the first two principal components show a line attractor (a roughly linear region of low flow) in control mice and a point attractor in experimental mice.
claims.source: Results, VMHvl Esr1 line attractor dynamics require Oxtr/Avpr1a-mediated signaling, paragraph 3; Figure 6G-H, S6C
claims.quote: The 2D flow field of control mice (Scr gRNAs) revealed a roughly linear region of low vector flow constituting the line attractor ... In contrast, in experimental mice (OARs gRNAs) this line attractor was absent and was replaced by a point attractor
claims.criterion: The flow field is drawn from the fit dynamics as in the DJALab notebook (dx = A x + b on a grid, speed = norm of dx, the 3D landscape its height), in the plane of the first two principal components of the latent trajectories. The paper gives no measure of the shape of the low-flow region; its only measure of a line against a point attractor is the line attractor score (STAR Methods, score above 1 for a line attractor, near 0 for a point attractor). Judged per mouse, reproduced when the score is above 1 in a majority of control mice and below 1 in a majority of experimental mice. The flow field and landscape of every mouse are shown and described, and do not decide the outcome.

claims.statement: In control mice the activity of the first rSLDS dimension ramps up during sniffing and attack and stays elevated after the intruder is removed; in experimental mice it decays rapidly between attack bouts and is significantly lower in the post-intruder interval.
claims.source: Results, VMHvl Esr1 line attractor dynamics require Oxtr/Avpr1a-mediated signaling, paragraph 4; Figure 6B, 6D, 6E, S6A-B
claims.quote: in control mice this activity ramped up during the progression from male-directed sniffing to attack, eventually reaching a plateau where it decayed slowly between attack bouts towards a single intruder and remained elevated between sequential trials with different intruders ... In contrast, in experimental mice 1 st dimension neural activity decayed rapidly between attack bouts, displaying a “sawtooth” profile, and was significantly lower during the post-intruder (i.e., inter-trial) interval
claims.criterion: The weighted average of unit activity on dimension 1 (the latent x1 of the fit, equivalently the emission-weighted projection), normalized to 0-1 per mouse; rSLDS readings as in fig6-rslds-fit-quality. Per mouse, its mean over all frames of male-directed behavior bouts and over the post-intruder period. The post-intruder window is not given; readings (a) from removal of the intruder to the next intruder's entry or the end of the male part, (b) the first 60 s after removal. Reproduced when, under a reading, the paired t-test across experimental mice finds post-intruder lower than during bouts at p < 0.05 and the same test across control mice does not; partially when the experimental drop is significant and the control drop is also significant but smaller.

claims.statement: The mean autocorrelation half-width of units weighted on the first rSLDS dimension, over the entire male-male interaction, is shorter in experimental (9.86 +/- 1 s) than in control mice (28.6 +/- 1.23 s); the reduction is about 66%, against about 61% for second-dimension units.
claims.source: Results, Oxtr/Avp1ra-mediating signaling controls VMHvl Esr1 persistent neural activity, paragraph 1; Figure 7B, S7A
claims.quote: The mean ACHW of these neurons across the entire social interaction was significantly shorter in experimental (9.86 ± 1 s) than in control mice (28.6 ± 1.23 s), by ~20 seconds ... A reduction in the average ACHW was also observed among 2 nd rSLDS dimension cells
claims.criterion: ACHW per unit is the lag at which the unit's autocorrelation first falls to half its zero-lag value, in seconds (an "approximate measure of the decay constant", Results; the computation is cited to Remedios et al. 2017 and not given here). Open details and their readings. The trace, (a) z-scored, (b) sigma-normalized. Which units are "weighted on" a dimension, (a) each unit assigned to the dimension of its largest absolute emission weight, (b) the units in the top 25% by absolute weight on that dimension (the Results' "~20–25%" of units). "Average" ACHW per unit, (a) one autocorrelation over the whole male-intruder period, (b) the mean over intruder trials. rSLDS readings as in fig6-rslds-fit-quality. Every combination is run; reproduced when, under one, the three expected values are within tolerance and the paper's tests (under the file-level readings of "nested") give p < 0.05 with experimental shorter; blocked as methods_underspecified if combinations disagree on the direction or significance.

claims.statement: Across all VMHvl Esr1 units, the mean ACHW during the first 1-2 minutes of male-male interaction is reduced in experimental mice (by about 50.9%), less than for first-dimension units.
claims.source: Results, Oxtr/Avp1ra-mediating signaling controls VMHvl Esr1 persistent neural activity, paragraph 1; Figure 7C
claims.quote: A reduction in the average ACHW was also observed among 2 nd rSLDS dimension cells, as well as in the VMHvl Esr1 population as a whole ... the difference in mean ACHW between experimental and control animals was larger for 1 st dimension-weighted units (~66%) than for 2 nd dimension and total Esr1 + neurons (~61% and 50.9%, respectively
claims.criterion: ACHW and its readings as in fig7b-achw-first-dimension, all units of each mouse, over the first part of the first male interaction; the window is "the first 1–2 minutes" (Figure 7C legend), readings 1 min and 2 min. Reproduced when, under a reading, the reduction is within tolerance and the experimental mean is lower at p < 0.05 by the paper's tests.

claims.statement: During male-female interactions, the mean ACHW of all VMHvl Esr1 units is only slightly reduced in experimental mice (by about 22%).
claims.source: Results, Oxtr/Avp1ra-mediating signaling controls VMHvl Esr1 persistent neural activity, paragraph 1; Figure S7B
claims.quote: In contrast, the average and cumulative distribution of ACHWs among all VMHvl Esr1 neurons were only slightly reduced (by ~22%) during male-female interactions
claims.criterion: As fig7c-achw-all-units, for the first 1-2 minutes of the first female interaction (S7B legend). The S7 legend names no test for panel B; the tests of the matching male panel (Figure 7C, nested Mann-Whitney on the mean, Kolmogorov-Smirnov on the distribution) are run and reported, and do not decide the outcome. The S7B image is read as showing one and two stars, and p < 0.05 is recorded. Reproduced when, under a reading, the reduction is within tolerance.

claims.statement: An rSLDS fit to slice calcium responses to OXT plus AVP captures 85% of the variance, with a first-dimension time constant (about 90 s) 8-9 times that of the second (about 15 s).
claims.source: Results, OXT and AVP evoke persistent responses in VMHvl Esr1 neurons ex vivo, paragraph 1; Figure S7C-D
claims.quote: This fit model captured 85% of the observed variance in neural activity. The time constant of dimension x1 (~90s) was ~8–9 -fold greater than that of x2 (~15s
claims.criterion: rSLDS settings as in fig6-rslds-fit-quality; the number of latent dimensions and states for the slice fit is not given (Figure S7D shows two dimensions), and the frame rate is about 1.2 Hz (STAR Methods). Readings (a) 2 latent dimensions, (b) 5 latent dimensions with the two largest tau reported; the number of states read as 1 and 3. The paper's numbers are not consistent with each other (90 s over 15 s is 6, not 8-9), so the fold ratio is not an expected value; the ratio found is reported. Reproduced when, under one reading, all three values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Slice responses to OXT plus AVP fall into persistent responses that outlast the perfusion window and transient responses that decay within it.
claims.source: Results, OXT and AVP evoke persistent responses in VMHvl Esr1 neurons ex vivo, paragraph 1; Figure S7F-K
claims.quote: Plotting the time-varying weighted average activity of x1 and x2 neurons revealed that the former exhibited slowly decaying responses to OXT+AVP application, while the latter exhibited more transient responses
claims.criterion: From the Figure S7K legend, a cell is transient when its response decays to 20% of the peak within the peptide perfusion window and persistent when it decays to 20% after the window. Reproduced when both classes contain cells and the x1-weighted cells (largest absolute weight on x1) are mostly persistent while x2-weighted cells are mostly transient.

claims.statement: Bilateral Cre-dependent co-editing in VMHvl Esr1 neurons does not change mounting of female intruders.
claims.source: Results, Altered VMHvl Esr1 neural activity during social interactions, paragraph 2; Figure 3D, S3D
claims.quote: consistent with the lack of an effect on mounting behavior
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the Mann-Whitney test between groups per mouse (Figure 3 legend) on the measures of Figure 3D and S3D (mean mount bout duration, latency to the first mount, interval between mount bouts) over 10 min of male-female interaction (STAR Methods, Behavior annotations); for the interval, mice with at most 1 mount bout are left out (same section). Reproduced when none gives p < 0.05; the effect sizes are reported either way.

claims.statement: In slices, synaptic transmission blockers (CNQX and MK-801) only slightly increase the decay rate of the peptide-evoked calcium response, during its later phases.
claims.source: Results, OXT and AVP evoke persistent responses in VMHvl Esr1 neurons ex vivo, paragraph 1; Figure S7L
claims.quote: the inclusion of synaptic transmission blockers (20 μ M CNQX and 10 μ M MK-801) only slightly increased the decay rate during later phases of the peptide response
claims.criterion: From the S7L legend, the mean response of 45 cells to 100 nM AVP with 20 uM CNQX and 10 uM MK-801. The S7 legend names a Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's correction over time points 0-1000 s, and the text does not say the effect is significant, so no p-value is recorded; the test is run and reported. The comparison condition is not given (readings, the response to AVP without blockers, or to OXT plus AVP without blockers), nor which time points are "later phases". Reproduced when, under a reading, the blocker response decays faster than the comparison after its peak and not before it.

claims.statement: The mouse block-protocol data (four odors, 5 s pulses, 55 s between trials, blocks of ten, 15 min between blocks) come from seven imaging sessions in four mice, with a median of 215 glomeruli per imaging session.
claims.source: Results, OFF responses form anticorrelated odor afterimages across species, paragraph 5; Figure 2H and 4B legends; Methods, Odor delivery to mice
claims.quote: With this approach, we monitored calcium signals from hundreds of glomeruli (median: 215 glomeruli per imaging session) ... Summary of the median angular distances for 4 odors (n = 7 imaging sessions from 4 mice)
claims.criterion: Sessions are classed by protocol from the trials tables; glomeruli are the ROIs of the three fields of view. The median can be read over (a) the seven block-protocol sessions or (b) every imaging session in the dandiset. Reproduced when the session and mouse counts match and the median is within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: The dandiset's raw fluorescence of the 198-glomerulus session is the data the paper deposited for its Figure 2D to 2F and 4C (Figshare data1_mouse_glom198.mat), up to the normalisation, with glomeruli in the same order.
claims.source: Methods, Time-bin-by-time-bin correlation analysis (n = 198 glomeruli for Fig. 2F); the paper's Figshare record
claims.quote: For mouse data, dF/F values were taken to be a n-dimensional population glomerular activity vectors (where n=198 glomeruli for Fig. 2F
claims.criterion: Records are matched by ROI count (the one dandiset session with 198 ROIs) and by ROI order (FOV1, FOV2, FOV3 concatenated), and the deposited solitary blocks 1 to 4 by recorded order to the session's four solitary blocks. Windows are taken as the code does, 912 consecutive frames from 32 frames before each onset. Reproduced when the median over trials and glomeruli of the within-trial Pearson r between the raw F and the deposited array is at least 0.9 and, for at least 90% of glomeruli, the deposited glomerulus correlates best with the dandiset ROI of the same index. Partially reproduced when the median r is at least 0.9 but the order check fails. The same median r with windows placed in seconds is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: In the mouse OB the angle between glomerular ON and OFF response vectors is greater than 90 degrees for each odor (mean 121.8 +/- 2.98 SEM, 4 odors, 7 sessions), so ON and OFF responses are inverted relative to each other.
claims.source: Results, OFF responses form anticorrelated odor afterimages across species, paragraph 6; Figure 2G and 2H
claims.quote: the angle between ON and OFF trajectories was greater than 90° for each odor presented (mean = 121.8° +/- 2.98 SEM, n = 4 odors, 7 sessions) (Fig. 2G, H), revealing that, as in the locust, odor ON and OFF responses in mouse OB glomeruli are inverted relative to each other
claims.criterion: As Script_Fig2.m (mouse) does, per session and odor, trial-averaged dF/F frames of the 5 s ON and 5 s OFF windows, minus the median across glomeruli at each frame, centred over the 160 frames; the median angle over all ON x OFF frame pairs. "Greater than 90 degrees for each odor" is read as (a) each odor's mean over sessions above 90, or (b) every session and odor value above 90. Reproduced when the mean over the 28 values is within tolerance and the 90-degree condition holds under one reading; partially reproduced when the 90-degree condition holds but the mean is outside tolerance; not reproduced otherwise. Shown as variants, uncentred vectors (the Methods' wording), no median subtraction, per-trial z-scored traces, the ON-ON and OFF-OFF medians, and random Gaussian vectors.

claims.statement: Time-averaged glomerular ON and OFF responses to the same odor are anticorrelated; glomeruli active during the odor tend to be suppressed after it and the reverse.
claims.source: Results, OFF responses form anticorrelated odor afterimages across species, paragraph 6; Results, ON and OFF responses occupy distinct regions of feature space, paragraph 3; Figure 2D, 2F and 4C
claims.quote: glomeruli responding to odors during odor presentation tended to be suppressed following odor offset, and that glomeruli responding most strongly to odor offset were suppressed during the odor presentation ... odor ON and OFF responses were not just distinct, but were anticorrelated.
claims.criterion: Per session and odor, Pearson r across glomeruli between the trial- and time-averaged dF/F of the ON window and of the OFF window, each minus the median across glomeruli (as Script_Fig3.m does for Fig 3e). Reproduced when the median over the 28 session-odor values is below 0 with a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p < 0.05 and each odor's median over sessions is below 0; partially reproduced when the first part holds and not every odor's median is below 0. The values without the median subtraction are shown as a variant.

claims.statement: In the mouse OB the ON response to a reference odor is closer in angle to the ON responses of the other odors than to any OFF response, including its own, and this holds for every odor of the panel.
claims.source: Results, ON and OFF responses occupy distinct regions of feature space, paragraph 3; Figure 4B and S4B
claims.quote: As in locusts, angular separations between a reference odor and all other odor ON responses were smaller than angular separations between the reference ON response and all odor OFF responses (Fig. 4B). This result was true for all odors in the panel (Fig. S4B).
claims.criterion: Per session, as the code does for the locust (Script_Fig3.m, Fig 3c), PCA of the trial-averaged, median-subtracted ON and OFF frames of the four odors, mean score vector of each odor and period on the top three components, and the angles from each reference odor's ON vector. "True for all odors" is read as (a) for each reference odor, the session-mean ON-ON angle (three other odors) is smaller than the session-mean ON-OFF angle (four odors) by a paired two-sided t-test over the seven sessions at p < 0.05, or (b) in every session and for every reference odor, the largest ON-ON angle is smaller than the smallest ON-OFF angle. Reproduced when one reading holds for all four reference odors; partially reproduced when reading (a) holds for one to three. The full-dimensional vectors are shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Hierarchical clustering of glomerular responses cleanly separates ON responses from OFF responses.
claims.source: Results, ON and OFF responses occupy distinct regions of feature space, paragraph 3; Figure 4D
claims.quote: Supporting this, hierarchical clustering of mouse odor responses cleanly separated ON and OFF responses (Fig. 4D)
claims.criterion: As Script_Fig3.m (Fig 3h), per session, complete linkage on cosine distance between the trial- and time-averaged dF/F vectors of the four ON and four OFF periods; the tree is cut into two clusters. Reproduced when the two clusters are exactly the ON and the OFF vectors in the 198-glomerulus session (the session of Figure 2F and 4C) and in at least four of the seven sessions; partially reproduced when only one of the two holds.

claims.statement: Methyl salicylate presented 1 s after another odor evokes a response less correlated with that odor's solitary response than the solitary methyl salicylate response is (history dependent contrast enhancement; one-tailed t-test p < 0.01, 3 sessions from 2 mice).
claims.source: Results, History-dependent suppression enhanced between sequentially presented odors, paragraph 3; Figure 6D and 6E (left)
claims.quote: Correlation values between solitary presentations of msc and other odors (left boxes in D) compared to correlation values between sequential msc and odors across imaging sessions (right boxes in D, n = 3 imaging sessions from 2 mice; one-tailed t test, p < 0.01)
claims.criterion: As Script_Fig4.m (Fig 4i), per session and first odor X (ace, als, eug), Pearson r across glomeruli between the trial- and time-averaged dF/F of solitary X (ON window) and of solitary msc (ON window), and between solitary X and msc in the (X)msc pairs (its own 5 s, 6 to 11 s after the pair's onset), with F0 from the 2 s before the first onset. The paper's three sessions are not identified, so all seven block sessions are used. Reproduced when the solitary r exceeds the sequential r by a paired one-tailed t-test over the 21 session-odor pairs at p < 0.01; partially reproduced when 0.01 <= p < 0.05. Per session (mean over X) and per X are shown as well.

claims.statement: Acetophenone presented 1 s after another odor evokes a response less correlated with that odor's solitary response than solitary acetophenone (one-tailed t-test p < 0.05, 4 sessions from 2 mice).
claims.source: Figure 6E (right) and Figure S6
claims.quote: Correlation values between solitary presentations of ace and the three other odors (see also Figure S5) compared to correlation values between sequential ace and odors across imaging sessions (n = 4 imaging sessions from 2 mice; one-tailed t test, p < 0.05).

claims.statement: After odor offset the glomerular population activity stays negatively correlated with the odor-evoked ON response for several tens of seconds, although overall activity returns to baseline quickly.
claims.source: Results, Odor OFF responses persist long after odor offset, paragraph 1; Figure 7B, 7D and S7C
claims.quote: neuronal activity in the AL and OB maintained negative correlations with the odor-evoked ON responses for several tens of seconds following stimulus termination ... although the overall neural activity after stimulus termination returns rapidly to pre-stimulus levels, network activity remains negatively correlated
claims.criterion: Per session and odor, Pearson r across glomeruli between the trial- and time-averaged ON vector and the trial-averaged vector in each 5 s bin from 0 to 50 s after offset, both minus the median across glomeruli (as Script_Fig2.m does for the temporal correlation), dF/F with F0 from the 2 s before onset. "Several tens of seconds" is read as at least 20 s. Reproduced when, in each of the four bins from 0 to 20 s, the median over the 28 session-odor values is below 0 with a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p < 0.05; partially reproduced when this holds for the first bin but not all four. All bins are reported; without the median subtraction, and with F0 from the 15 min before each block, as variants.

claims.statement: Glomerular activity averaged over the 50 s after each odor offset classifies the preceding odor with high accuracy (k-NN, k = 20).
claims.source: Results, Odor OFF responses persist long after odor offset, paragraph 2; Figure 7G and 7H; Methods, Classification analysis of average ITI periods
claims.quote: We observed a similar clustering of 55-second ITI activity from the mouse OB (Fig. 7G), which contributed to highly accurate classification of odors from ITI glomerular responses (Fig. 7H).
claims.criterion: In the 318-glomerulus session (the Methods' n for Fig. 7H), per trial the mean dF/F (session-median F0) over 0 to 50 s after offset, 40 vectors; leave-one-out k-NN with k = 20 (the legend; the Methods' k = 50 exceeds the 39 other vectors) on angular distance in full dimension (Methods). Reproduced when the accuracy is at least 50% and above the 99th percentile of 1000 label permutations; partially reproduced when above that percentile but below 50%; not reproduced otherwise. The code's choice (cosine on the top three PCs) and the other six sessions are shown as variants.

claims.statement: A time-bin k-NN classifier identifies the preceding odor from glomerular activity throughout the 55 s inter-trial interval; accuracy stays high for its whole duration and falls to chance with shuffled labels.
claims.source: Results, Odor OFF responses persist long after odor offset, paragraph 3; Figure 7J and S8C
claims.quote: We found that classifier accuracy remained high for the duration of the 55-second ITI (Fig.7J) ... Shuffling odor labels results in chance-level classifier performance throughout the ITI (Fig. S8C).
claims.criterion: In the 318-glomerulus session, dF/F (session-median F0) over 0 to 50 s after offset, averaged over 4-frame bins, per trial (code, Script_Fig6.m), 4 odors x 10 trials; k-NN with k = 10 and correlation distance, neighbours from other trials only. Accuracy is averaged over odors in 10 s segments. Reproduced when every segment is at least 50% (twice chance) and above the 99th percentile of 200 permutations of the trial labels; partially reproduced when every segment is above that percentile but not all reach 50%; not reproduced when any segment is not above it. The other six sessions are shown as variants.

claims.statement: During the 15 min between blocks odor-specific information is no longer present; classification of 1-min bins of the inter-block interval by the preceding odor is near chance (34.8%).
claims.source: Results, Odor OFF responses persist long after odor offset, paragraph 2; Figure S7D and S7E, Figure 7K
claims.quote: during the IBI, network activity ceased to contain odor-specific information ... The overall classification rate of the glomerular IBI activity was 34.8%.
claims.criterion: The IBI is the 15 min from the end of each solitary block's last ITI (last onset plus 60 s), in 1-min bins of dF/F (session-median F0), only bins before the next presentation and the end of imaging. Leave-one-out k-NN with k = 50 and angular distance (Methods) needs 60 bins, so it is run on the sessions with four complete IBIs. Reproduced when the mean rate over those sessions is at most 38.3% (the expected value plus its tolerance; the claim is that the rate is near chance, 25%). The 318-glomerulus session with k = 20, and a 1000-permutation null for each session, are shown as well.

claims.statement: When eleven odors are presented in random order (1 s pulses, 19 s apart), odor information after offset is variable across odors and on average declines to chance after several seconds.
claims.source: Results, Odor OFF responses persist long after odor offset, paragraph 4; Figure S8D and S8E
claims.quote: Classifier accuracy across the ITI was variable across odors (Fig. S8D), but, on average, declined to chance after several seconds (Fig. S8E).
claims.criterion: The dandiset's random-order sessions; the first 10 presentations of each of the 11 odors (not Empty), dF/F (session-median F0) over 0 to 17 s after offset in 4-frame bins; k-NN with k = 10 and correlation distance, neighbours from other trials only (Methods). Per session, accuracy averaged over odors; early is 0 to 2 s after offset, late is 12 to 17 s. Reproduced when, in at least three of the sessions, early accuracy is above the 99th percentile of 200 permutations of the trial labels and late accuracy is not above the 95th; partially reproduced when early accuracy is above it in at least three sessions but late accuracy is too.

claims.statement: Photoionization detector recordings at the nostril show odor concentration rising and decaying quickly at onset and offset, for every odor.
claims.source: Figure S2; Results, Odor OFF responses persist long after odor offset, paragraph 3; Methods, Odor delivery to mice
claims.quote: PID recordings confirmed that, for all odors, concentrations near the nares decayed rapidly after odor offset (Fig. S2).

claims.statement: In the locust antennal lobe the median angle between PN population ON and OFF response vectors exceeds 90 degrees for every one of 11 odors (mean 106.7 +/- 0.84 SEM).
claims.source: Results, OFF responses form anticorrelated odor afterimages across species, paragraph 4; Figure 1F and 1G, S1
claims.quote: For every odor the median angle between the ON and OFF responses was more than 90 degrees (mean = 106.7° +/- 0.84 SEM, n = 11 odors)
claims.criterion: As Script_Fig2.m (locust), per odor, trial-averaged spike counts of 66 PNs in 50 ms bins over the 4 s ON and 4 s OFF windows, centred over the 160 bins (PCA scores); median angle over all ON x OFF bin pairs. Reproduced when all 11 medians exceed 90 and the mean is within tolerance; partially reproduced when all exceed 90 and the mean is outside it; not reproduced when any is at most 90. Uncentred and baseline-subtracted vectors are shown as variants.

claims.statement: In the locust the ON response to a reference odor is closer to other odors' ON responses than to OFF responses for most reference odors, significantly for 5 of 11.
claims.source: Results, ON and OFF responses occupy distinct regions of feature space, paragraph 1; Figure 3B and S4A
claims.quote: While this finding was consistent for most reference odors, the difference in angular separation was significant for 5 out of 11 odors in the panel (Fig. S4A).
claims.criterion: As Script_Fig3.m (Fig 3c), PCA of the trial-averaged ON and OFF bins of all 11 odors, mean score vectors on the top three components per odor and period, angles from each reference ON vector; two-sample t-test of the 11 ON angles against the 11 OFF angles at p < 0.05, with ON smaller. The tolerance is one odor, as counts of 5 cannot take a 10% tolerance. Reproduced when the count is within tolerance and ON angles are smaller on average for most (at least 6) reference odors.

claims.statement: In the locust, PN responses to geraniol presented 0.5 s after another odor are less correlated with that odor's solitary response than solitary geraniol is (one-tailed t-test p < 0.05, 5 odor pairs).
claims.source: Results, History-dependent suppression enhanced between sequentially presented odors, paragraph 2; Figure 5D and 5E
claims.quote: we found that the correlation between high-dimensional odor response vectors was lower when the odors were sequentially presented, compared to when the odors were presented in isolation (Fig. 5D, E).
claims.criterion: As Script_Fig4.m (Fig 4d,e), Pearson r across 85 PNs of trial- and time-averaged spike counts, solitary first odor (ON window) against solitary ger (ON window) and against ger in the pair (its 4 s window); paired one-tailed t-test over the five first odors. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with solitary r higher; not reproduced otherwise. The same for hexanol as second odor is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: In the locust, PN activity averaged over the 20 s after odor offset classifies the preceding odor (k-NN on angular distance), so ITI activity is odor specific.
claims.source: Results, Odor OFF responses persist long after odor offset, paragraph 2; Figure 7E and 7F; Methods, Classification analysis of average ITI periods
claims.quote: A k-nearest neighbor classifier, using angular distances of the full-dimensional ITI data, robustly discriminated odors (Fig. 7F). This confirmed the interpretation from the PCA analysis and showed that ITI activity was odor-specific.
claims.criterion: Per trial the mean spike count of each PN over the 20 s after offset, 7 odors x 10 trials; leave-one-out k-NN with k = 10 on angular distance in full dimension (Methods). Reproduced when the accuracy is at least 50% and above the 99th percentile of 1000 label permutations; partially reproduced when above that percentile but below 50%. The code's choice (k = 4, cosine on the top three PCs) is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: In the locust a time-bin k-NN classifier's accuracy decays across the 20 s after offset to about 40% averaged over odors, but for most odors does not fall to chance.
claims.source: Results, Odor OFF responses persist long after odor offset, paragraph 3; Figure 7I
claims.quote: Classifier accuracy decreased to ∼40% across odors throughout the 20-second post stimulus ITI, but notably, for most odors, accuracy did not fall to chance levels during the entire ITI period (Fig.7I).
claims.criterion: As Script_Fig5.m and the Methods, 200 ms bins (four 50 ms bins) over the 21 s after offset, 7 odors x 10 trials, k-NN with k = 10 and correlation distance, neighbours from other trials only. "At the end" is the last 5 s. Reproduced when the mean over odors in the last 5 s is within tolerance and, for at least 4 of 7 odors, that odor's accuracy in the last 5 s is above the 99th percentile of 200 permutations of the trial labels; partially reproduced when one of the two holds.

claims.statement: The paper's Allen parcel masks, from its code, can be laid on the dandiset's ΔF/F pixels, so that the areas the paper names can be found in the data.
claims.source: Methods, Preprocessing of imaging data and Post-processing analysis; parcells_updated121519.mat and brainMask.mat in the paper's code at commit c337686
claims.criterion: The pixels with non-zero ΔF/F in the blue and green ΔF/F movies of every session used must equal the code's brainMask.mat under exactly one of the eight rotations and reflections (agreement of at least 99.9% of the 65536 pixels, all others below 99%). In one visual stimulus session per mouse, the calcium response to 100% contrast gratings (mean ΔF/F 0 to 1 s after onset minus -2 to 0 s, averaged over trials) is then computed for each of the 46 parcels. The code takes the left VISp parcel as the visually driven one. Reproduced when the mask match holds and left VISp has the largest response of the 46 parcels in at least 3 of 4 mice, with left VISp above right VISp in all 4. Partially reproduced when the mask match holds and the largest response is in a left visual parcel in at least 3 mice. Not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: The variance of ACh3.0 and jRCaMP1b signals explained by a ridge regression on FaceMap PCs 1 to 25, locomotion speed and pupil area differs across cortical areas (Friedman's ANOVA p < 0.001 for both, n = 6 mice).
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 1; Figure 2a,b
claims.quote: For ACh3.0 and jRCaMp1b, the variance explained ... using this full model differed significantly across cortical areas
claims.criterion: Ten-fold cross-validated R2 (ten contiguous blocks) of a ridge model with the penalty chosen per parcel by marginal likelihood, as ridgeMML does, fitted per session on the 23 left parcels and averaged over each mouse's sessions. Friedman's test across the 23 parcels with mice as blocks. Reproduced when p < 0.05 for both signals; partially reproduced when for one. With 4 mice the paper's p < 0.001 is not required.

claims.statement: The coupling of behaviour to fluorescence has anterior-posterior gradients that are inverted between the signals, with ACh most strongly linked to behaviour in frontal areas and calcium in posterior areas.
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 1; Figure 2b
claims.quote: We also observed significant anterior-posterior gradients in the coupling between behavioral state and fluorescence activity that were inverted for cholinergic versus calcium signals ... with ACh release and calcium signaling most strongly linked to behavioral state variables in frontal and posterior areas, respectively
claims.criterion: Spearman correlation between the mean full-model R2 over mice and the anterior-posterior rank of the 23 left parcels (1 = MOs, the most anterior), as in the code. Reproduced when ACh has rho < 0 with p < 0.05 and calcium rho > 0 with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when one of the two holds; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: For ACh3.0, facial movement (FaceMap PC1) predicts activity better than locomotion or pupil, in single-variable models (Friedman p = 0.006, face against locomotion and against pupil p = 0.031) and as unique contribution (Friedman p = 0.003).
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 1; Figure 2c
claims.quote: Facial movements yielded the strongest prediction accuracy compared to locomotion and pupil variation for Ach 3.0
claims.criterion: Single-variable cross-validated R2 (face PC1, pupil area, wheel speed) averaged over the 23 left parcels, with negative values set to 0 as in the code, per mouse. Reproduced when Friedman's test across the three variables gives p < 0.05 and face PC1 has the highest R2 in every mouse. Partially reproduced when face PC1 has the highest mean R2 over mice but not in every mouse, or Friedman p >= 0.05. Not reproduced when face PC1 does not have the highest mean. The unique contributions (full model R2 minus the model with that variable shuffled in time; for face, PC1 is shuffled) are reported with the same rule and do not change the outcome.

claims.statement: For jRCaMP1b, facial movement (FaceMap PC1) is the most robust predictor of activity (single-variable Friedman p = 0.006; face against locomotion and pupil p = 0.031).
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 1; Figure 2c
claims.quote: Again, facial movement (PC1) was the most robust predictor
claims.criterion: As for fig2c-face-best-predictor-ach, on calcium.

claims.statement: Facial movement onset without locomotion is associated with significant whole-cortex transients in ACh (0.64 ± 0.09 ΔF/F, p = 0.001) and calcium (0.69 ± 0.15 ΔF/F, p = 0.006).
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 2; Figure S7
claims.quote: Facial movement onset (quantified using FaceMap PC1) in the absence of locomotion was associated with desynchronization of local neuronal firing as estimated by ECoG and significant whole cortex-averaged transients in both ACh ... and calcium ... signals
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's stated spread (SEM over 6 mice). Face onsets as in the code (a high face state during sustained quiescence preceded by at least 4 s of low face state ending at most 0.5 s before). Per trial the mean of -4 to -2 s is subtracted; trials are averaged per mouse over sessions; the peak in 0 to 1 s is taken per parcel and averaged over the 23 left parcels. Reproduced when both means are within tolerance and both are above 0 by a one-sample t-test at p < 0.05 over mice. Partially reproduced when both are above 0 at p < 0.05, or positive in every mouse, but a mean is outside tolerance. Not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Locomotion onset is associated with transient increases in ACh (0.68 ± 0.17 ΔF/F, p = 0.010) and calcium (1.50 ± 0.11 ΔF/F, p < 0.001).
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 2; Figure S7
claims.quote: Locomotion onset co-occurred with an increase in facial movement and local desynchronization and was also associated with transient increases in ACh ... and calcium ... signals
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's SEM. Locomotion onsets are those of the dandiset's WheelActivation table (the code's onsets with at least 5 s of running preceded by at least 10 s of quiescence). Baseline -5 to -3 s; peak in 0 to 1 s; otherwise as s7-face-onset-transients, with the same rule.

claims.statement: ACh transients vary across cortical areas (p < 0.001) but do not differ between locomotion and facial motion onsets (p = 0.734, two-way repeated measures ANOVA).
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 2; Figure S7
claims.quote: ACh transients varied significantly across cortical areas ... but were not significantly different between locomotion and facial motion onsets
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. Two-way repeated measures ANOVA of the per-mouse parcel peaks (23 left parcels by 2 onset types). Reproduced when the onset-type effect has p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The area effect and the size of the onset-type difference are reported either way.

claims.statement: Calcium transients vary across cortical areas (p < 0.001) and states (p = 0.005), with locomotion onset associated with the largest signal.
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 2; Figure S7
claims.quote: Calcium transients varied significantly across cortical areas ... and states ... with locomotion onset associated with the largest signal
claims.criterion: The same ANOVA on calcium. Reproduced when the onset-type effect has p < 0.05 and the whole-cortex locomotion transient exceeds the face transient in every mouse. Partially reproduced when it exceeds it in every mouse but p >= 0.05. Not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Transient magnitudes show a significant anterior-posterior gradient for ACh but not for calcium.
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 2; Figure S7
claims.quote: We also found a significant anterior-posterior gradient in the transient magnitudes for cholinergic but not calcium signals
claims.criterion: The paper does not say which onsets. Spearman correlation of the mean peak over mice with the anterior-posterior rank, for each signal and onset type. Reproduced when ACh has p < 0.05 for at least one onset type and calcium p >= 0.05 for both; partially reproduced when the ACh part holds but calcium is significant for one onset type; not reproduced when ACh has p >= 0.05 for both.

claims.statement: Sustained facial movement and locomotion are associated with progressively increasing 30 to 100 Hz ECoG power.
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 3; Figure 3b
claims.quote: Sustained increases in facial movement and locomotion were associated with progressively increasing local circuit desynchronization, as evidenced by an increase in high frequency power

claims.statement: Sustained facial motion elevates whole-cortex ACh (low face -0.13 ± 0.04, high face 0.18 ± 0.08 ΔF/F; low against high p = 0.046, post hoc LSD), with a main effect of state (p = 0.015).
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 3; Figure 3c
claims.quote: ACh activity varied significantly across cortical areas ... and differed by state ... Sustained facial motion significantly elevated whole-cortex Ach activity
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's SEM. Sustained states and epoch matching as in the code's SustainedStatesCorrelation.m; per epoch the mean ΔF/F, averaged over epochs and sessions per mouse, then over the 23 left parcels. Two-way repeated measures ANOVA (area by state, three states) and Fisher's LSD on the state means using the ANOVA's state-by-mouse error. Reproduced when both means are within tolerance and high exceeds low with LSD p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when high exceeds low in every mouse but a mean is outside tolerance or p >= 0.05. Not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Locomotion does not further increase whole-cortex ACh beyond high facial motion (locomotion 0.16 ± 0.06 ΔF/F; locomotion against high face p = 0.717).
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 3; Figure 3c
claims.quote: but locomotion did not further increase the Ach signal
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the LSD comparison of locomotion with high face in the ANOVA of fig3c-ach-sustained-face. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The locomotion mean, its tolerance (0.06) and the size of the difference are reported either way.

claims.statement: Sustained facial movement and locomotion both increase whole-cortex calcium (low face -0.02 ± 0.02, high face 0.17 ± 0.04, locomotion 0.63 ± 0.19 ΔF/F; low against high p = 0.020, locomotion against high p = 0.044), with a main effect of state (p = 0.005).
claims.source: Results, Calcium and cholinergic signals encode behavioral state, paragraph 3; Figure 3c
claims.quote: Similarly, sustained calcium activity varied significantly for cortical area ... and state ... Sustained facial movement and locomotion both increased whole cortex calcium activity
claims.criterion: As fig3c-ach-sustained-face, on calcium. Reproduced when all three means are within tolerance and both comparisons (high above low, locomotion above high) have LSD p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when both orderings hold in every mouse but a mean is outside tolerance or a p >= 0.05. Not reproduced otherwise.
