claims.quote: The results suggested that the SYN-P (onset, 113 ms and peak, 480 ms) occurred earlier than SEM (122 ms and 524 ms) and SYN-C (283 ms and 579 ms) in terms of both onset and peak of the response, respectively.
claims.criterion: Latencies L per electrode and condition, averaged (mean, as Fig. 3a's box centre is the mean) over electrodes. Open, the electrodes, (a) for each condition the electrodes passing V for it; (b) the electrodes of E+ (pars opercularis, pars triangularis and precentral, the set of the Fig. 3d legend, n = 106), each giving latencies for all three conditions; with L1, L2, L3 and the readings of E and V. Reproduced when, under one combination, all six values are within tolerance and SYN-P precedes SEM and SYN-C in both onset and peak; partially reproduced when the order holds under every combination but no combination puts all six within tolerance. The n of each reading is reported against 106.

claims.statement: Onset and peak latencies differ significantly between each pair of SYN-P, SYN-C and SEM.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 10; Figure 3d legend
claims.quote: we estimated the latency differences based on ANOVA (Fig. 3d, P < 0.001, one-way ANOVA, two tailed, Bonferroni, corrected for ten participants.
claims.criterion: For each pair of conditions and for onset and peak, a one-way ANOVA (f_oneway) of the electrodes' latencies of the two conditions, p multiplied by 10 (Bonferroni "for ten participants", as printed). Electrodes and latencies under the readings of fig3-latency-values. Reproduced when, under every combination of readings, all six corrected p are below 0.001; partially reproduced when at least four are under every combination; not reproduced when fewer than four are under every combination; blocked otherwise. The paper's p for SEM against SYN-P onset (1.83e-5) with means 9 ms apart is noted as surprising; it is matched as printed.

claims.statement: Onset and peak latencies vary more across electrodes for SYN-C than for SYN-P.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 10; Figure 3c and 3d
claims.quote: This possibility may help explain the results that relatively later (and also greater variations of) onset and peak were observed for SYN-C than SYN-P.
claims.criterion: The paper gives no measure or test of the variation. Electrodes and latencies under the readings of fig3-latency-values; the spread is the standard deviation of the latencies across electrodes (a standard choice; the interquartile range, which Fig. 3a's boxes show, as a variant). Reproduced when the SYN-C spread exceeds the SYN-P spread for both onset and peak under every reading; not reproduced when it does for neither under every reading; blocked otherwise.

claims.statement: Response latencies do not depend on the location of the electrodes along the anterior-posterior or superior-inferior axis, or across pars opercularis, pars triangularis and precentral gyrus.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 11; Figure 3e; Supplementary Figure 10c and 10d
claims.quote: Moreover, response latencies did not depend on the spatial location of the electrodes (Fig. 3e and Supplementary Fig. 10c,d).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a linear regression of latency on electrode coordinate with its 95% confidence interval (Fig. 3e legend), for onset and peak, each condition, and each axis. The legend calls the axes the x and y coordinates, while the panel names the anterior-posterior and superior-inferior axes; on MNI152 these are y and z. Open, (a) MNI y and z; (b) MNI x and y, as the legend prints. Reproduced when every slope's 95% CI includes zero; not reproduced when any excludes it, under the readings of fig3-latency-values and of the axes (blocked when they differ). Slopes are reported in ms per mm. The comparison across the three areas (Supplementary Fig. 10c) has no test in the paper; a one-way ANOVA of latency on area at p < 0.05 is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: The accuracy of classifying the conditions after the keyword peaks about 400 to 700 ms after keyword onset.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 10; Supplementary Figure 10a legend
claims.quote: The accuracies for classifying different conditions peaked at about 400–700 ms after the keywords, which indicated they were most separable in this time frame
claims.criterion: The paper does not name the classifier, features, time resolution or cross-validation of this panel. Readings, each of the three classifiers with the Methods settings (SVM, logistic regression, kNN), classifying CORR, SYN-P, SYN-C and SEM trials together, or each violation against CORR (the legend says "classification accuracy of each violation type"), from the HGA of the responding electrodes of fig2b-violation-electrodes within each participant at each 10 ms sample (or in 100 ms windows), 5-fold stratified cross-validation (a standard choice), accuracy averaged over participants. Reproduced when, under every reading, the time of maximum accuracy lies in 360 to 770 ms (the range widened by 10% of each bound); not reproduced when it lies outside under every reading; blocked otherwise.

claims.statement: The total length of the significant difference from CORR differs between SYN-P, SYN-C and SEM electrodes.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 11; Supplementary Figure 10b legend
claims.quote: The discrepancy in terms of the total length of the significant difference between respect violation and correct sentence of each electrode (ANOVA). This also indicated temporal differences in processing each linguistic component
claims.criterion: For each electrode and each violation it passes V for, the total length of significant samples (times 10 ms). One-way ANOVA of these lengths across SYN-P, SYN-C and SEM, and pairwise one-way ANOVAs Bonferroni-corrected for three pairs (the paper does not say what is corrected; the three pairs are read). Reproduced when the three-group ANOVA has p < 0.001 and at least one corrected pair has p < 0.001 under every reading of E and V; the group medians are reported.

claims.statement: In the non-linguistic task, the violation enhances activity mainly at lower frequencies (4 to 10 Hz), where many electrodes respond to both linguistic and non-linguistic tasks, unlike the high-gamma band.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figures 4 and 7c
claims.quote: In contrast, in the NL task, the violation condition showed an enhanced activity mainly at the lower frequency (Supplementary Fig. 4), indicating that neural oscillations during linguistic and NL tasks may arise in different frequency bands.
claims.criterion: Needs the 4 to 10 Hz amplitude, which a high-gamma dataset does not hold. If the broadband signal is present, the test of V for NL-VIO against NL-CORR at P < 0.01 corrected (Supplementary Fig. 4b) on the 4 to 10 Hz amplitude and on HGA; reproduced when more electrodes pass at 4 to 10 Hz than in high gamma. The measure of Supplementary Fig. 4a (peak power during NL-VIO against peak power during NL-CORR, per electrode and band) is shown with it.

claims.statement: Keyword frequencies are matched between CORR (shared by SYN-P and SEM; mean 31.88 per million) and SYN-C (30.25 per million).
claims.source: Methods, The Chinese language and stimuli design, paragraph 3
claims.quote: the word frequencies were matched between CORR (same in SYN-P and SEM, mean frequency = 31.88 per million, s.d. = 35.14) and SYN-C (mean frequency = 30.25 per million, s.d. = 73.58) (t(62) = 0.11, P = 0.91)
claims.criterion: Keywords from the supplement's sentence lists (word 4 of CORR and SYN-C), frequencies from the corpus the paper names (lingua.mtsu.edu/chinese-computing, the Modern Chinese word frequency list). Reproduced when both means are within tolerance and an independent two-sample t-test gives p > 0.05.

claims.statement: At the resting membrane potential, photostimulation of DRN-DAT terminals evoked both excitatory and inhibitory post-synaptic potentials in downstream cells of the BNST, CeA and BLP (19, 36 and 48 cells recorded).
claims.source: Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 2; Figure 6D-F
claims.quote: Optical stimulation at the resting membrane potential evoked both excitatory and inhibitory post-synaptic potentials (EPSPs and IPSPs) in downstream cells
claims.criterion: Counts are compared exactly (tolerance 0) because they are cell counts the dataset either holds or not; a count that differs is reported, and the claim is then judged on the cells present. Per cell, the average of the light sweeps at rest (Methods, Ex vivo electrophysiology); the EPSP peak and IPSP trough are measured against the 5 s before stimulation (Methods). A cell is 'excitation' with an EPSP only, 'inhibition' with an IPSP only, 'mix' with both, 'none' otherwise (Methods; Figure 6D-F legend). The paper gives no threshold for calling a deflection an EPSP or an IPSP; the readings run are a peak (EPSP) or trough (IPSP) of the average trace within 0-5.5 s of light onset (the window the Methods use for total voltage area) beyond (a) 2 or (b) 3 standard deviations of the 5 s baseline of the average trace. Reproduced when, under the readings, each of the three regions has at least one cell with an EPSP and the pooled cells include cells with an IPSP; the proportions of the four classes per region are reported. If the readings disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: In cells made to fire by constant current, photostimulation increased firing in all BNST cells (5 of 5), while CeA (20 cells) and BLP (17 cells) cells showed either an increase or a decrease in firing.
claims.source: Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 2; Figure 6G-I
claims.quote: During spontaneous firing, BNST cells were universally excited whereas more diverse responses were observed with the BLP and CeA
claims.criterion: Per cell, the action potential inter-event interval (IEI) in the 5 s before and the 5 s after the first light pulse; a decrease is 'excitation', an increase 'inhibition' (Methods, Ex vivo electrophysiology). The paper does not say how sweeps are combined or which summary of the IEIs is compared; readings (a) mean IEI over all intervals pooled across sweeps, (b) mean over sweeps of each sweep's mean IEI. The Figure 6 supplement 1G legend plots 5.5 s before the light, so a 5.5 s baseline is shown as a variant. Action potentials are detected as upward crossings of 0 mV, a standard choice. Reproduced when every BNST cell is excited and both classes occur among CeA cells and among BLP cells, under each reading.

claims.statement: The peak amplitude of the optically evoked EPSP differed between regions, larger in the CeA than in the BLP.
claims.source: Figure 6J, left
claims.quote: peak amplitude (Kruskal-Wallis statistic = 6.790, p=0.0335; Dunn’s posts-hoc tests: CeA vs BLP p=0.0378)
claims.criterion: EPSP peak of the average trace at rest against the 5 s baseline (Methods), one value per cell with an EPSP. Which cells enter is open; readings (a) cells with an EPSP (excitation and mix), (b) excitation-only cells. Reproduced when, under the readings, a Kruskal-Wallis test across the three regions gives p < 0.05, Dunn's test gives CeA against BLP p < 0.05, and the CeA median exceeds the BLP median.

claims.statement: The trough amplitude of the optically evoked IPSP differed between regions, deeper in the CeA than in the BLP.
claims.source: Figure 6K, left
claims.quote: trough amplitude (one-way ANOVA, F2,31=8.150, p=0.0014, CeA vs BLP: **p=0.0014)
claims.criterion: IPSP trough of the average trace at rest against the 5 s baseline (Methods), one value per cell. Readings for the cells (a) inhibition and mix cells, (b) inhibition-only cells; the single BNST point in Figure 6K beside the absence of BNST inhibition-only cells in Figure 6D favours (a), but both are run. The post hoc test is not named; Tukey's test (the Prism default after a one-way ANOVA) and Holm-Sidak are the readings. Reproduced when the one-way ANOVA gives p < 0.05, CeA against BLP p < 0.05 and the CeA mean trough is more negative than the BLP mean.

claims.statement: The optically evoked EPSP and the slow component of the IPSP persisted after TTX/4AP, so the responses were typically monosynaptic.
claims.source: Figure 6 supplement 1D-E; Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 2
claims.quote: the optically-evoked EPSP (upper panels) and slow component of the IPSP (lower panels) was maintained following application of TTX/4AP
claims.criterion: Per cell, the EPSP peak or IPSP trough after TTX/4AP divided by that before (normalized amplitude, Figure 6 supplement 1E). The paper gives no threshold for 'maintained'; the response is counted as maintained when it is still detected under the readings of fig6df-epsp-ipsp-at-rest. Reproduced when it is maintained in most cells of each group. The normalized amplitudes are reported.

claims.statement: Hierarchical clustering of CeA cells on four baseline properties gave two clusters, late-firing cells (cluster 1) that were excited by DRN-DAT input and regular-firing cells (cluster 2) that were mostly inhibited.
claims.source: Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 3; Figure 6L, 6N-O
claims.quote: CeA cells in cluster 1 represented ‘late-firing’ neurons, whereas cluster 2 were typical of ‘regularfiring’ neurons ... with cluster 1 ‘late-firing’ neurons excited and cluster 2 ‘regular-firing’ neurons mostly inhibited
claims.criterion: Features from the Methods (Ex vivo electrophysiology). Ramp ratio, mean Vm 900-1000 ms over mean Vm 100-200 ms after step onset at the largest subthreshold step; max instantaneous frequency, the highest firing frequency in the first 100 ms of the depolarizing steps; firing delay, step onset to first spike at rheobase; voltage sag, peak minus steady-state Vm in the -120 pA step. Each feature max-min normalized, Ward linkage on Euclidean distance (scipy linkage), two clusters at the top split. Response label per cell (Methods), from IEI when firing data exist, else EPSP only = excitation, IPSP only = inhibition, mix by the sign of the voltage area 0-5.5 s after light onset. Open details and their readings, all run. (1) Ramp ratio from absolute Vm (as written) or from the deflections from the pre-step baseline. (2) Steady state for the sag, the mean of the last 100 ms or of the last 200 ms of the step. (3) Normalization is max-min, as the Methods and legend say; Figure 6L shows the normalized values on a 0-100 scale, which accounts for the dendrogram's axis (to 200) and does not change the partition. (4) Cells, those with all four features (26 from t24). The cluster with the longer firing delay is the late-firing cluster. Proportions are over all cells of a cluster, as the Figure 6O pie charts include cells with no response. Reproduced when, under the readings, every cell of the late-firing cluster is excited and more than half of the cells of the other cluster are inhibited; blocked as methods_underspecified if the readings disagree.

claims.statement: The two CeA clusters differed in all four input properties (ramp ratio, maximum instantaneous frequency, firing delay and voltage sag).
claims.source: Figure 6 supplement 1H
claims.quote: Unpaired t-tests for CeA – ramp ratio: t24=3.502, p=0.0018; max instantaneous firing frequency (max freqinst.): t24=4.698, p<0.0001, firing delay: t24=5.050, p<0.0001, voltage sag: t24=3.983, p=0.0006
claims.criterion: Unpaired two-sided t-tests (Statistical analyses) between the clusters of fig6no-cea-clusters on the raw feature values. Reproduced when all four give p < 0.05 under the readings of that claim.

claims.statement: BLP cells clustered into putative pyramidal neurons (cluster 1) and putative GABAergic interneurons (cluster 2); 93% of the putative pyramidal neurons were inhibited by DRN-DAT input and 62% of the putative interneurons were excited.
claims.source: Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 3; Figure 6M, 6P-Q
claims.quote: with 93% of putative pyramidal neurons showing an inhibitory response, and 62% of putative GABAergic interneurons showing an excitatory response
claims.criterion: As fig6no-cea-clusters, with capacitance in place of ramp ratio (Methods). Capacitance from the 5 mV, 250 ms hyperpolarizing step in voltage clamp at -70 mV by the Q-method (charge of the transient over 5 mV; Methods cite the Q-method, the paper's MATLAB code is not published). Cells, those with all four features (27 from t25). The cluster with the larger capacitance and lower maximum frequency is the pyramidal cluster. The same open reading (steady state for the sag) is run, with max-min normalization. Denominators are all cells of each cluster, as the Figure 6Q pie for cluster 2 includes cells with no response, and 93% and 62% fit 13 of 14 and 8 of 13 cells (27 in all), not the response-labelled cells alone. Reproduced when both percentages are within tolerance under the readings; partially reproduced when the direction holds (most pyramidal cells inhibited, most interneurons excited) but a percentage is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: The two BLP clusters differed in capacitance, maximum instantaneous frequency, firing delay and voltage sag.
claims.source: Figure 6 supplement 1I
claims.quote: unpaired t-tests for BLP – capacitance: t25=4.803, p<0.0001, max freqinst.: t25=15.48, p<0.0001, firing delay: t25=2.743, p=0.0111, voltage sag: t25=2.705, p=0.0121
claims.criterion: Unpaired two-sided t-tests between the clusters of fig6pq-blp-clusters on the raw feature values. Reproduced when all four give p < 0.05 under the readings of that claim.

claims.statement: The total voltage area evoked by DRN-DAT stimulation differed between the two clusters in both the CeA and the BLP, and the EPSP peak amplitude differed between the BLP clusters but not between the CeA clusters.
claims.source: Figure 6 supplement 1J-K
claims.quote: EPSP peak amplitude, CeA: unpaired t-test, t17=1.40, p=0.180; BLP: unpaired t-test t22=2.34, p=0.029. ... Total voltage area, CeA: Mann-Whitney U = 22, p=0.0023; BLP: Mann-Whitney U = 29, p=0.0019
claims.criterion: Total voltage area, the integral of Vm against the 5 s pre-light baseline from 0 to 5.5 s after the first pulse, on the average trace at rest (Methods). Mann-Whitney U for the area and unpaired t-test for the EPSP peak between clusters, as the legend names them. Reproduced when the area tests give p < 0.05 in both regions, the BLP EPSP test gives p < 0.05, and the CeA EPSP test gives p >= 0.05 (a claim of absence, judged on the paper's t-test).

claims.statement: Clustering CeA and BLP cells together gave two clusters with a response pattern very similar to that of the separate clusterings.
claims.source: Figure 6 supplement 1L-N; Results, DRNDAT input has divergent effects on downstream cellular excitability, paragraph 3
claims.quote: In addition, clustering CeA and BLP cells together yielded a very similar result
claims.criterion: The five features used in the separate clusterings (ramp ratio, capacitance, maximum instantaneous frequency, firing delay, voltage sag; Figure 6 supplement 1L), max-min normalized, Ward linkage, two clusters, on the cells with all five. The paper gives no number for 'very similar'; what it shows (Figure 6 supplement 1N) is the response of CeA and BLP cells in each combined cluster. Reproduced when, under the readings of the two claims it depends on, in each region one combined cluster has more than half of its cells excited and the other more than half inhibited, with the excited cluster the same for both regions, as in the separate clusterings (late-firing CeA and putative interneurons excited, regular-firing CeA and putative pyramidal inhibited). The agreement of each cell's combined and separate cluster is reported.

claims.statement: With the expression and illumination parameters used, social preference of ChrimsonR mice did not differ significantly across GH off, GH on and SI off.
claims.source: Figure 7E; Results, DRNDAT input enables a functional shift in CeA dynamics, paragraph 4
claims.quote: We successfully optimized viral expression and illumination parameters to minimize changes in social preference with DRNDAT-CeA with ChrimsonR
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. Social:object ratio per session, time in the social side over time in the object side during the 10 min test (Methods, Three chamber sociability assay; the imaging chamber has the same dimensions). Sides are the left and right compartments (23 cm each) of the 57.5 cm chamber, the 11.5 cm centre excluded. A mixed-effects model with condition as the repeated factor (Prism's mixed-effects analysis, restricted maximum likelihood, with the Geisser-Greenhouse correction that the fractional degrees of freedom F(1.897, 30.36) show) on the ChrimsonR mice. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; the condition means are reported either way. Total social time (Figure 7E right) is shown as a variant, under both readings the paper allows (social side time, as the axis label says, and social cup interaction time, as the legend says).

claims.statement: CeA response strength to the social cup relative to the object cup (social minus object auROC) tended to be larger with DRN-DAT stimulation (GH on) than without (GH off), a trend with a significant Kruskal-Wallis test across conditions but a non-significant pairwise test.
claims.source: Figure 7G-H; Results, DRNDAT input enables a functional shift in CeA dynamics, paragraph 5
claims.quote: did find a trend indicating stronger responses toward social stimuli compared to object stimuli in the GH on condition compared to the GH off condition in mice expressing ChrimsonR
claims.criterion: auROC per cell and stimulus as in the Methods (In vivo microendoscopic calcium imaging). A binary vector of social (or object) cup interaction in 40 ms bins against the cell's raw CNMF-E trace z-scored and thresholded at 100 steps from its minimum to its maximum; area under the ROC curve. Interaction, from pose, when the nose is within 1.3 times the cup diameter and the cup lies in a 90 degree cone in front of the head (Methods). Open details, readings all run. (1) Distance, nose to cup centre below 0.65 cup diameters (inside a circle 1.3 times the cup) or below 1.3 cup diameters. (2) Head direction, from the neck or the head keypoint to the nose; the cone is 45 degrees either side. (3) Time base, traces and behaviour resampled to 40 ms bins as written, or the 50 ms imaging frames. (4) Period, the 10 min test only, or the whole session with habituation counted as no interaction. (5) Mice, ChrimsonR mice only (the panel is labelled DRNDAT-CeA:ChrimsonR) or all mice imaged. Kruskal-Wallis on social minus object auROC across the three conditions with cells as samples, then Dunn's test. Reproduced when, under the readings, Kruskal-Wallis gives p < 0.05 and the GH on median or mean exceeds that of GH off; the Dunn p-values are reported. If the readings disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Single cells did not change significantly in response strength or in the proportion of neurons significantly excited or inhibited by the social or object cup across the three conditions (social cup excited 6.0%, 7.2% and 5.9%, inhibited 4.8%, 4.0% and 6.0%; object cup excited 4.1%, 2.4% and 3.6%, inhibited 5.0%, 3.6% and 5.1%, for GH off, GH on and SI off).
claims.source: Figure 7G and 7J (percentages read from the figure); Figure 7K-L for the per-mouse proportions; Results, DRNDAT input enables a functional shift in CeA dynamics, paragraph 5
claims.quote: At a single-cell level, we did not observe significant changes in CeA response strength or proportion of neurons significantly responding to social or object stimuli across the three conditions
claims.criterion: A cell is significantly excited when its auROC exceeds the 97.5th percentile of 1,000 auROCs from random circular shifts of the behaviour vector, inhibited when below the 2.5th (Methods); shifts drawn uniformly over the session length and the seed are standard choices. The auROC readings of fig7gh-delta-auroc-trend are all run. The expected percentages hold when within tolerance under one reading. The paper names no test for the proportions (the legend of 7J-L is missing). Readings for the absence part are a chi-square test of the 3 by 2 table of responsive against other cells per stimulus and sign (pooled proportions, Figure 7J); for the per-mouse percentages (Figure 7K-L), a one-way repeated measures ANOVA, or Prism's mixed-effects model when a mouse lacks a session (Statistical analyses, three or more groups), and a Kruskal-Wallis test (the test the paper uses on the auROCs in Figure 7H). For response strength the paper reports no test on the auROCs of Figure 7G; a Kruskal-Wallis test across conditions on the social and on the object auROC is the reading, and the paper's own Kruskal-Wallis on social minus object auROC (fig7gh-delta-auroc-trend) gives p = 0.0457, so this part of the statement sits uneasily with Figure 7H; the results are reported. Reproduced when the percentages are within tolerance and no proportion test finds p < 0.05; partially reproduced when the tests find no difference but percentages fall outside tolerance.

claims.statement: Among 202 cells co-registered between GH off and GH on, 16 GH off and 18 GH on cells were excited by the social cup, and only 2 in both sessions, suggesting that stimulation may recruit separate CeA ensembles to represent social stimuli.
claims.source: Figure 7I; Results, DRNDAT input enables a functional shift in CeA dynamics, paragraph 5
claims.quote: in co-registered neurons, we found little overlap between CeA neurons excited by the social stimulus in both GH on and GH off conditions
claims.criterion: Co-registration with CellReg on the CNMF-E spatial footprints, with translation and rotation and its probabilistic model on spatial correlation and centroid distance (Methods); the paper gives no CellReg parameters, so its defaults are used, a stated choice. The tolerance on the 'both' count is one cell, since 10% of 2 is below a cell. Reproduced when the counts are within tolerance under one auROC reading. Whatever the counts, the overlap is reported against the number expected if the two sets were independent (16 x 18 / 202, about 1.4 in the paper). The figure's inhibitory overlap (12 GH off, 11 GH on, 2 both) is reported as well.

claims.statement: Across mice, the proportion of socially excited CeA neurons correlated positively with social preference in the GH on condition (r = 0.679, p = 0.045), but not in GH off or SI off.
claims.source: Figure 7M (r and p read from the figure); Results, DRNDAT input enables a functional shift in CeA dynamics, paragraph 5
claims.quote: we did find a significant positive correlation between the proportion of socially-excited CeA neurons and social preference in the GH on condition, but not in the GH off or SI off conditions
claims.criterion: Per mouse and condition, the fraction of its cells significantly excited by the social cup (fig7j-proportions-unchanged) against its social:object ratio (fig7e-no-behavioural-change, labelled soc:obj zone ratio in the figure); Pearson correlation per condition (Statistical analyses). Which mice enter is not stated and the counts disagree (the Figure 7G legend says 15 mice, Figure 7E 12 ChrimsonR mice, Figure 7 supplement 1N-O 9, 8 and 9 mice, while r = 0.679 with p = 0.045 fits 9 mice in GH on and the supplement's p-values fit 10, 9 and 10); readings (a) ChrimsonR mice with that session, (b) all mice imaged in that session. Reproduced when, under one reading together with each auROC reading, GH on gives r > 0 with p < 0.05 and GH off and SI off give p >= 0.05; r is within tolerance for full agreement, else partially reproduced. If the readings disagree on the sign or significance, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified with every result shown.

claims.statement: Social preference did not correlate with the proportion of object-excited CeA neurons or of socially inhibited CeA neurons in any condition.
claims.source: Figure 7 supplement 1N-O; Results, DRNDAT input enables a functional shift in CeA dynamics, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Importantly, we do not observe a correlation between social preference and object-excited CeA neurons
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's Pearson correlations, as in fig7m-social-excited-predicts-preference with object-excited and social-inhibited fractions. Reproduced when all six give p >= 0.05; r is reported either way. The printed values are not self-consistent. The two GH off p-values appear swapped between panels N and O (r = -0.3231 gives p = 0.3625 and r = 0.1729 gives p = 0.6328 with 10 mice), and every printed r and p fits 10, 9 and 10 mice, not the printed N = 9, 8 and 9. The r values are taken as printed and the absence is judged on each correlation's own p.

claims.statement: In TdTomato control mice, the social minus object auROC did not differ across GH off, GH on and SI off.
claims.source: Figure 7 supplement 1L
claims.quote: Difference in response strength (Δ auROC) of CeA neurons to social and object cups in DRNDAT-CeA:TdTomato control mice
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's one-way ANOVA across conditions with cells as samples, on the auROC readings of fig7gh-delta-auroc-trend. Reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Hierarchical clustering of trial-averaged CeA responses to social and object cup interactions gave 12 functional clusters.
claims.source: Figure 7 supplement 2A-B; Methods, In vivo microendoscopic calcium imaging, last paragraph
claims.quote: The dendrogram (left) reveals 12 functional clusters of neurons
claims.criterion: Trials are interactions lasting at least 1 s, at least 5 s after the previous interaction, merging pauses under 1.5 s (Methods). Per neuron, the z-scored average trace from 5 s before to 5 s after onset for the social and the object cup, concatenated; MATLAB-style agglomerative clustering cut at 0.770 times the largest linkage distance (Methods). Open details, readings all run. (1) Linkage, MATLAB's default (single) or Ward or average, since the Methods name the 'cluster' function but no method. (2) Z-scoring of the whole trace before averaging, or of the averaged trace. (3) Neurons, pooled across the three conditions (the figure gives percentages per condition from one dendrogram). Reproduced when one reading gives 11 to 13 clusters; the counts under all readings are reported.

claims.statement: Ex vivo, red light evoked ChrimsonR-mediated potentials in CeA cells with much larger peak amplitude and area than the blue light (0.3 or 0.2 mW) used for imaging.
claims.source: Figure 7 supplement 1D-F; Results, DRNDAT input enables a functional shift in CeA dynamics, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Red light evoked a PSP with a significantly greater peak amplitude
claims.criterion: Per cell, the PSP peak amplitude and the area 0-5.5 s after light onset. The paper does not say how a PSP with both EPSP and IPSP (Figure 7 supplement 1D) gives one peak amplitude; the readings run are (a) the largest absolute deflection from the 5 s baseline, whichever sign, and (b) the EPSP peak, or the IPSP trough magnitude in cells with only an IPSP. Amplitude and area are measured for each light condition against the 5 s baseline (Methods, Ex vivo electrophysiology). Repeated measures one-way ANOVA across the three lights. Reproduced when both ANOVAs give p < 0.05 and red exceeds each blue power in most cells.

claims.statement: Red light still evoked PSPs during constant blue light, though they were significantly smaller than with red light alone.
claims.source: Figure 7 supplement 1G-I
claims.quote: Red light evoked a significantly smaller PSP in the presence of continuous blue light
claims.criterion: As fig7-s1ef-red-vs-blue, red alone against red during constant 0.3 mW blue light, paired two-sided t-tests. Reproduced when both give p < 0.05 with smaller PSPs during blue light, and a PSP is still detected during blue light in most cells.

claims.statement: DRN-DAT and VTA-DAT neurons innervate distinct targets; VTA-DAT fluorescence is greater in striatal subregions, DRN-DAT fluorescence is greater in the oval BNST and the lateral CeA.
claims.source: Figure 1C; Results, DRNDAT neurons project to and exhibit dense collateralization, paragraph 1
claims.quote: and significantly greater following DRN injection in the BNST oval nucleus (unpaired ttest: t22=3.95, p=0.0007) and CeA lateral division

claims.statement: Dual retrograde tracing shows that many TH+ DRN neurons project to both the BNST and the CeA (46% of BNST projectors, 55% of CeA projectors), while few project to both the BLP and the BNST or CeA (7.6% and 9.7%).
claims.source: Figure 1H
claims.quote: dual CTB-labelled TH+ cells constituted 46% of all BNST projectors and 55% of all CeA projectors ... (7.6% of BNST projectors and 9.7% of CeA projectors)

claims.statement: TH+ BNST and CeA projectors per slice were similar in number, while BLP projectors were significantly fewer.
claims.source: Figure 1 supplement 2D
claims.quote: The total number of TH+ BNST and CeA projectors per slice was similar (n=27.9 BNST projectors and n=27.2 CeA projectors per slice), whereas TH+ BLP projectors were significantly fewer

claims.statement: Photostimulation of the DRN-DAT to BLP projection, but not the projections to the BNST or CeA, produced avoidance of the stimulation zone in real-time place preference relative to eYFP controls.
claims.source: Figure 2B-G; Results, DRNDAT-BLP photostimulation promotes place avoidance, paragraph 2
claims.quote: we found that photostimulation of the DRNDAT-BLP projection, but not the projection to the BNST or CeA, produced avoidance of the stimulation zone, relative to eYFP controls
claims.criterion: As the paper tests it, ON minus OFF percent zone time in ChR2 against eYFP mice per projection, unpaired two-sided t-test. Reproduced when BLP gives p < 0.05 with ChR2 lower and BNST and CeA give p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Photostimulation of none of the three projections supported intracranial self-stimulation.
claims.source: Figure 2 supplement 2A-C
claims.quote: did not support intra-cranial self-stimulation (ICSS) as shown by a lack of preference for the active nosepoke

claims.statement: Photostimulation of the projections had no significant effect on open arm time in the elevated plus maze; BNST stimulation gave only a weak trend toward more open arm time.
claims.source: Figure 3A-C; Results, DRNDAT-BNST photostimulation promotes non-social exploration
claims.quote: resulted in a weak trend toward increased time spent in the open arm of the EPM

claims.statement: Photostimulation did not change time in the centre or distance travelled in the open field for any projection.
claims.source: Figure 3 supplement 1
claims.quote: Photostimulation had no significant effect on time spent in the center of the open field

claims.statement: Photostimulation of the DRN-DAT to BNST projection increased rearing during the juvenile intruder assay; CeA and BLP stimulation did not.
claims.source: Figure 3G-I; Results, DRNDAT-BNST photostimulation promotes non-social exploration
claims.quote: photoactivation of the DRNDAT-BNST projection increased rearing behavior

claims.statement: Photostimulation of the DRN-DAT to CeA projection increased the social:object ratio in the three-chamber assay; BNST and BLP stimulation had no significant effect.
claims.source: Figure 4D-F; Results, DRNDAT-CeA photostimulation promotes sociability, paragraph 1
claims.quote: This revealed that optical stimulation of the DRNDAT-CeA projection increased social preference, but no significant effect was observed

claims.statement: In DRN-DAT to CeA ChR2 mice the light-induced change in social zone time correlated positively with social dominance.
claims.source: Figure 4H; Results, DRNDAT-CeA photostimulation promotes sociability, paragraph 1
claims.quote: we found that the optically-induced change in social preference in DRNDAT-CeA mice was positively correlated with social dominance

claims.statement: Photostimulation of the DRN-DAT to CeA projection modestly increased face investigation of a juvenile in the home cage.
claims.source: Figure 4J-L; Results, DRNDAT-CeA photostimulation promotes sociability, paragraph 2
claims.quote: photoactivation of the DRNDAT-CeA projection modestly increased face sniffing of the juvenile mouse

claims.statement: In a two-state Markov model of juvenile intruder behaviour, CeA photostimulation changed the probability of transitions between social and nonsocial states but not of transitions within a state.
claims.source: Figure 4P-R; Results, DRNDAT-CeA photostimulation promotes sociability, paragraph 4
claims.quote: did not significantly change the probability of transitioning within social and nonsocial state (Figure 4Q ), but did significantly change the probability of transitioning between social and nonsocial states

claims.statement: Across baseline behaviour, social dominance correlated weakly and negatively with open arm time, and social sniffing correlated robustly and negatively with rearing.
claims.source: Figure 4 supplement 2D; Results, DRNDAT-CeA photostimulation promotes sociability, paragraph 3
claims.quote: This showed a weak, negative correlation between social dominance and open arm time in the elevated plus maze ... revealed a robust negative correlation between the time spent engaged in social sniffing and time spent rearing

claims.statement: In the BNST and CeA terminal fields neuropeptide receptors (Vipr2, Npbwr1) were densely and co-expressed, with Drd2 more abundant than Drd1, while the BLP terminal field was dominated by Drd1.
claims.source: Figure 5; Results, DRNDAT terminal fields contain spatially-segregated dopamine and neuropeptide receptor populations, paragraph 2
claims.quote: dopamine receptor expression was relatively more sparse, with Drd2 more abundant than Drd1 ... The DRNDAT terminal field of the BLP displayed a markedly different receptor expression pattern, dominated by Drd1

claims.statement: Photoinhibition of DRN-DAT terminals in the CeA, but not the BNST or BLP, blocked the increase in social preference after 24 h of isolation.
claims.source: Figure 8C; Results, DRNDAT-CeA photoinhibition blocks isolation-induced sociability
claims.quote: However, inhibition of DRNDAT terminals in CeA, but not BNST or BLP, blocked the rebound in sociability associated with acute social isolation

claims.statement: In CeA NpHR mice the change in social zone time after isolation correlated negatively with social dominance.
claims.source: Figure 8D
claims.quote: showing significant negative correlation in NpHRCeA mice
claims.criterion: Pearson correlation of relative dominance with the change in social zone time (isolated minus grouped) in CeA NpHR mice (Figure 8D legend). The printed values are not self-consistent (r = -0.500 with N = 20 gives p = 0.025; p = 0.0414 fits 17 mice), so r is judged within tolerance and the sign and p < 0.05 are required.

claims.statement: Photoinhibition of the terminals in group-housed mice did not change social preference in any region.
claims.source: Figure 8 supplement 1B
claims.quote: Photoinhibition had no significant effect on social:object ratio in group-housed mice

claims.statement: Simultaneous S1 and POm recordings were made in 16 rats, and S1 and auditory cortex recordings in a further 12 rats.
claims.source: Materials and Methods, Animal surgery, paragraph 3
claims.quote: multiunit activities were recorded from the S1 and POm (N = 16) ... To check the auditory confound, another group of rats was used (N = 12)
claims.criterion: Counts of distinct rats with sessions of each recording pair under the paper's conditions (S1-targeted tFUS, sham or CG1 control). The tolerance is zero as these are counts of animals, which the paper gives exactly. Reproduced when both counts match; partially reproduced when the dataset holds a subset of the rats (fewer, none extra), with the counts given.

claims.statement: High-pressure tFUS (about 170 kPa) aimed at the electrode site produces an artifact aligned with sonication that vanishes off target or at lower pressure, and extracted waveforms show tail oscillations at the 1,500 Hz PRF.
claims.source: Materials and Methods, Transcranial focused ultrasound stimulation, paragraph 4; Figure 2
claims.quote: Once the ultrasound was delivered at the desired target, high “artifact” would appear and align with the stimulation duration (Fig. 2A). To lower the pressure or move off the target could eliminate the “artifact” (Fig. 2B). The extracted spike waveform also showed oscillations at the tail due to the displacement of electrode (Fig. 2C). The frequency of the oscillations was 1,500 Hz which aligned with PRF.
claims.criterion: Needs the target-determination trials (10 to 20 trials at about 170 kPa, 1,500 Hz PRF, Methods) and a lower-pressure recording at the same site. The paper gives no measure of the artifact; it shows traces. Reproduced when the voltage aligned to sonication onset shows a deflection confined to 0 to 67 ms at high pressure and not at lower pressure, and the dominant frequency of the mean waveform tail (after the AHP) is within tolerance of 1,500 Hz. The spectral method is a standard choice (FFT peak), named as one.

claims.statement: In the constant-PD sessions at 3,000 Hz there were 312 RSUs and 54 FSUs in S1 and 233 RSUs and 17 FSUs in POm; at 30 Hz there were 148 RSUs and 61 FSUs in S1 and 189 RSUs and 43 FSUs in POm.
claims.source: Figure 4 legend
claims.quote: There are 312 RSUs and 54 FSUs recorded from S1, 233 RSUs and 17 FSUs recorded from POm for PRF 3,000 Hz. There are 148 RSUs and 61 FSUs recorded from S1 and189 RSUs and 43 FSUs recorded from POm for PRF 30 Hz.
claims.criterion: Units selected and typed as in U, in the 3,000 Hz/200 us and 30 Hz/200 us sessions of the S1 and POm rats, counted once per session. Reproduced when all eight counts are within 10% under a reading of U; partially reproduced when at least six are.

claims.statement: During 3,000 Hz PRF (60% DC) sonication of S1, RSUs in S1 (n = 312) and in POm (n = 233) increase their firing above baseline.
claims.source: Results, Synchronizing neuronal responses to tFUS in CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 4A, 4B
claims.quote: RSUs from S1 (n = 312, p = 3.13 × 10−7) and POm (n = 233, p = 0.0003) were both activated during 3,000 Hz PRF sonication.
claims.criterion: Units as in U in the 3,000 Hz/200 us sessions; normalized rate (R) in 0 to 67 ms; test T, one-tailed for an increase, at corrected p < 0.01. Reproduced when both S1 RSUs and POm RSUs are significant with mean normalized rate above 100%; partially reproduced when one is. Run under R1 and R2, T1 and T2, B1 and B2; the outcome is the one they all give.

claims.statement: After 3,000 Hz PRF sonication, from 134 ms, S1 RSUs, POm RSUs and S1 FSUs (n = 54) show increased firing.
claims.source: Results, Synchronizing neuronal responses to tFUS in CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 4A, 4B
claims.quote: Postsonication activations were presented for S1 RSUs (p = 5 × 10−18), POm RSUs (p = 0.0007), and S1 FSUs (n = 54, p = 4.03 × 10−8) from 134 ms.
claims.criterion: As fig4-timelocked-rsu-3000, in the 67 ms windows of W starting at or after 134 ms (134 to 201, 201 to 268 ms; the paper reports this window range for Fig. 4 and 201 to 268 ms in Fig. 6). Reproduced when each of the three groups is significantly above baseline in at least one of these windows; partially reproduced when one or two are.

claims.statement: At 30 Hz PRF (0.6% DC), S1 RSUs (n = 148) decrease firing at 67 to 134 ms after onset, and POm RSUs (n = 189) show a delayed increase at 134 to 268 ms.
claims.source: Results, Synchronizing neuronal responses to tFUS in CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 4 legend
claims.quote: At 30 Hz PRF, the S1 RSUs showed an inhibitory response after sonication (67–134 ms, n = 148, p = 0.0029) and POm RSUs expressed delayed excitatory activities (n = 189, p = 2 × 10−9).
claims.criterion: Units as in U in the 30 Hz/200 us sessions; R; T at corrected p < 0.01, one-tailed for a decrease in S1 RSUs in 67 to 134 ms, and for an increase in POm RSUs in at least one of the windows 134 to 201 and 201 to 268 ms (Fig. 4 legend, 134–268 ms). Reproduced when both hold, partially when one does, across the readings of R, T and B.

claims.statement: S1 FSUs show no activity change to 30 Hz PRF, POm FSUs show none to either PRF, and S1 FSUs show no time-locked response at 3,000 Hz.
claims.source: Results, Synchronizing neuronal responses to tFUS in CTC pathway, paragraphs 1 and 3; Figure 4 legend
claims.quote: There was no activity change among S1 FSUs (n = 61) to 30 Hz PRF and POm FSUs to both PRFs (3,000 Hz, n = 17; 30 Hz, n = 43).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, T at corrected p < 0.01, in each 67 ms window of W from 0 to 268 ms, for S1 FSUs at 30 Hz, POm FSUs at 30 Hz and 3,000 Hz, and S1 FSUs at 3,000 Hz in 0 to 67 ms only. The direction the absence is tested in is not stated; the readings are an increase only (the one-tailed direction of the paper's activations) and either direction (both one-tailed tests). Reproduced when no test finds a change under either reading; not reproduced when a test for an increase finds one; when only a decrease is found the readings differ and the claim is methods_underspecified. The S1 FSU part at 3,000 Hz is read from the Fig. 4 legend, which names time-locked responses in S1 and POm RSUs only, and from paragraph 3 ("only S1 RSUs showed time-locked responses to 3,000 Hz PRF"). The mean normalized rates are reported either way, under each reading of R, T and B.

claims.statement: Sham sessions held 31 RSUs and 53 FSUs in S1 and 67 RSUs and 67 FSUs in POm; CG1 control sessions held 12 RSUs and 34 FSUs in S1 and 55 RSUs and 42 FSUs in POm.
claims.source: Figure 5 legend
claims.quote: There are 31 RSUs and 53 FSUs recorded from S1 and 67 RSUs and 67 FSUs recorded from POm for sham condition. There are 12 RSUs and 34 FSUs recorded from S1 and 55 RSUs and 42 FSUs recorded from POm for control condition.
claims.criterion: As fig4-unit-counts, for the sham and CG1 control sessions. Reproduced when all eight counts are within 10% under a reading of U; partially reproduced when at least six are.

claims.statement: Without tFUS (sham), S1 and POm RSUs and FSUs show no time-locked or delayed (201 to 268 ms) change in activity.
claims.source: Results, Synchronizing neuronal responses to tFUS in CTC pathway, paragraph 2; Figure 5A
claims.quote: In sham condition (no tFUS), S1 neurons and POm neurons showed no time-locked (S1 RSUs: n = 31, p = 1.0; S1 FSUs: n = 53, p = 0.55; POm RSUs: n = 67, p = 1.0; POm FSUs: n = 67, p = 1.0) and delayed
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, T at corrected p < 0.01, in 0 to 67 ms and 201 to 268 ms, for the four groups of the sham sessions, aligned to the sham trial times the dataset gives. The direction of the one-tailed tests is not stated; the readings are an increase only (the direction of the responses this control is set against) and either direction. Reproduced when none of the tests is significant under either reading; not reproduced when a test for an increase is; when only a decrease is significant the readings differ and the claim is methods_underspecified. The effect sizes (mean normalized rates) are reported. Run under each reading of R, T and B; the outcome is the one they all give.

claims.statement: With tFUS aimed at the cingulate cortex (CG1) at 3,000 Hz PRF, S1 and POm neurons show no time-locked or delayed (201 to 268 ms) change in activity.
claims.source: Results, Synchronizing neuronal responses to tFUS in CTC pathway, paragraph 2; Figure 5B
claims.quote: In control condition (tFUS targeted at CG1), S1 neurons and POm neurons showed no time-locked (S1 RSUs: n = 12, p = 1.0; S1 FSUs: n = 34, p = 1.0; POm RSUs: n = 55, p = 1.0; POm FSUs: n = 42, p = 0.33) and delayed responses (201–268 ms, S1 RSUs: p = 1.0; S1 FSUs: p = 0.10; POm RSUs: p = 0.32, POm FSUs: p = 1.0).
claims.criterion: As fig5a-sham-no-response, for the CG1 control sessions.

claims.statement: Across the five constant-PD PRF conditions, 1,050 RSUs and 247 FSUs were sorted in S1 and 913 RSUs and 106 FSUs in POm.
claims.source: Figure 6 legend
claims.quote: The comparison of neuronal responses for sorted 1,050 RSUs (A) and 247 FSUs (B) recorded from S1 ... The comparison of neuronal responses for sorted 913 RSUs (C) and 106 FSUs (D) recorded from POm
claims.criterion: Units as in U in the five 200 us PD sessions (30, 300, 1,500, 3,000, 4,500 Hz), summed over conditions with each unit counted once per session. Reproduced when all four totals are within 10% under a reading of U; partially reproduced when two or three are. The per-condition counts are reported and compared with those the Results give (S1 RSUs 284 at 1,500 Hz, 312 at 3,000 Hz, 152 at 4,500 Hz; POm RSUs 153 at 1,500 Hz; POm FSUs 26 at 4,500 Hz).

claims.statement: With constant 200 us PD, S1 RSU time-locked responses depend on PRF and are elicited only by 1,500, 3,000 and 4,500 Hz, with the highest level, 123.34 +/- 4.3%, at 1,500 Hz.
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 6A
claims.quote: time-locked S1 RSUs’ responses could only be elicited from high PRFs ... 1,500 Hz (n = 284, p = 2.74 × 10−6 compared with baseline), 3,000 Hz (n = 312, p = 3.13 × 10−7), and 4,500 Hz (n = 152, p = 0.0028), among which 1,500 Hz evoked highest response level of 123.34 ± 4.3%.
claims.criterion: S1 RSUs (U) of the five 200 us PD sessions; R in 0 to 67 ms; Kruskal-Wallis across the five PRFs at p < 0.01, then T against baseline per PRF, one-tailed for an increase, corrected p < 0.01. The tolerance is the paper's SEM. Reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis test is significant, 1,500, 3,000 and 4,500 Hz are significant and 30 and 300 Hz are not, 1,500 Hz has the highest mean, and the 1,500 Hz mean is within tolerance; partially reproduced when the pattern of significance holds but the 1,500 Hz value or rank does not. Run under each reading of R, T and B.

claims.statement: S1 RSU postsonication (201 to 268 ms) responses depend on PRF, occur at PRFs above 30 Hz, and are highest at 4,500 Hz (148.39 +/- 5.41%).
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 6A legend
claims.quote: The delayed responses (201–268 ms) of RSUs could be observed at PRFs higher than 30 Hz and the highest response occurred at 4,500 Hz (148.39 ± 5.41%).
claims.criterion: As fig6a-s1-rsu-timelocked-high-prf, in 201 to 268 ms. Reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis test is significant, 300, 1,500, 3,000 and 4,500 Hz are significantly above baseline and 30 Hz is not, 4,500 Hz has the highest mean, and its mean is within the paper's SEM; partially reproduced when the significance pattern holds without the value or the rank.

claims.statement: S1 FSUs show no time-locked response to any PRF, and delayed responses only at the higher PRFs, highest at 4,500 Hz (158.75 +/- 10.75%), with PRF-dependent postsonication activity.
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 6B
claims.quote: FSUs did not show time-locked responses to any PRFs and only presented delayed responses at PRFs higher than 1,500 Hz, with the highest response level at 4,500 Hz (158.75 ± 10.75%).
claims.criterion: S1 FSUs (U) of the five 200 us PD sessions, R, T as in fig6a-s1-rsu-timelocked-high-prf. "Higher than 1,500 Hz" is read as (a) 3,000 and 4,500 Hz significant and 1,500 Hz not, or (b) 1,500 Hz and above significant. Reproduced when no PRF gives a significant increase in 0 to 67 ms, the postsonication Kruskal-Wallis is significant, the postsonication pattern matches a reading, 4,500 Hz has the highest mean and that mean is within the SEM; partially reproduced when the absence of time-locked responses and the postsonication pattern hold without the value.

claims.statement: POm RSUs respond during sonication to 1,500 Hz (n = 153) and 3,000 Hz (n = 233), and their delayed responses are induced by the higher PRFs and highest at 1,500 Hz (141.68 +/- 2.38%).
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 6C legend
claims.quote: time-locked responses (Fig. 6B) from POm RSUs could be elicited by 1,500 Hz (n = 153, p = 0.003) and 3,000 Hz PRFs (n = 233, p = 0.0003). However, the delayed responses (201–268 ms) of POm RSUs were induced by PRFs higher than 1,500 Hz and were highest (141.68 ± 2.38%) at 1,500 Hz.
claims.criterion: POm RSUs (U) of the five 200 us PD sessions, R, T as in fig6a-s1-rsu-timelocked-high-prf. During sonication, 1,500 and 3,000 Hz significantly above baseline and 30, 300 and 4,500 Hz not. The paper says the delayed responses come at PRFs "higher than 1,500 Hz" yet are highest at 1,500 Hz; the readings are (a) 3,000 and 4,500 Hz significant, (b) 1,500, 3,000 and 4,500 Hz significant. Reproduced when both Kruskal-Wallis tests are significant, the time-locked pattern holds, the postsonication pattern matches a reading, and 1,500 Hz has the highest postsonication mean within the SEM; partially reproduced when the time-locked pattern holds and the postsonication part holds only in part.

claims.statement: POm FSUs show no time-locked responses relative to baseline at any PRF (though 30 and 1,500 Hz differ), and a delayed response only to 4,500 Hz (n = 26).
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 6D legend
claims.quote: The FSUs did not show any time-locked responses and only expressed the delayed responses to 4,500 Hz (n = 26, p = 4.2 × 10−6).
claims.criterion: POm FSUs (U) of the five 200 us PD sessions, R, T as in fig6a-s1-rsu-timelocked-high-prf. Reproduced when no PRF is significantly above baseline in 0 to 67 ms, only 4,500 Hz is in 201 to 268 ms, and the postsonication Kruskal-Wallis is significant; partially reproduced when the 4,500 Hz response holds and one other part fails. The 30 against 1,500 Hz comparison in 0 to 67 ms is reported, one-tailed in each direction since the paper does not give one.

claims.statement: The DC series at 3,000 Hz held 645 S1 RSUs, 171 S1 FSUs, 286 POm RSUs and 129 POm FSUs; the DC series at 30 Hz 442 S1 RSUs and 147 S1 FSUs; the 60% DC series 759 S1 RSUs and 151 S1 FSUs.
claims.source: Figure 7, 8 and 9 legends
claims.quote: sorted 645 RSUs recorded from S1 ... sorted 171 FSUs recorded from S1 ... sorted 286 RSUs from POm ... sorted 129 FSUs ... sorted 442 RSUs recorded from S1 with 30 Hz PRF ... sorted 147 FSUs ... The comparison of 759 RSU’s responses ... The comparison of 151 FSU’s responses
claims.criterion: As fig6-unit-counts, for the three series of the header. Reproduced when all eight totals are within 10% under a reading of U; partially reproduced when at least five are.

claims.statement: At 3,000 Hz PRF, S1 RSU responses depend on DC; time-locked responses are elicited at 30% and 60% DC and delayed responses at 6%, 30% and 60%.
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 3; Figure 7A
claims.quote: with 3,000 Hz PRF, the time-locked responses of S1 RSUs were dependent on DCs which can be elicited with DC of 30% (n = 194, p = 3.38 × 10−6) and 60% (n = 312, p = 5.96 × 10−6). Delayed activities of RSUs were found at 6% (n = 56, p = 0.001), 30% (n = 194, p = 9.64 × 10−32), and 60% (n = 312, p = 1.38 × 10−15).
claims.criterion: S1 RSUs (U) of the five 3,000 Hz sessions (PD 2, 20, 100, 200, 300 us); R in 0 to 67 and 201 to 268 ms; Kruskal-Wallis across DCs at p < 0.01 in each window; T against baseline per DC, one-tailed for an increase, corrected p < 0.01. Reproduced when both Kruskal-Wallis tests are significant, exactly 30% and 60% are significant during sonication, and exactly 6%, 30% and 60% postsonication; partially reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis tests hold and the per-DC pattern differs by one DC. Run under each reading of R, T and B.

claims.statement: At 3,000 Hz PRF, S1 FSUs show delayed responses at 6%, 30% and 60% DC, the same range as S1 RSUs, and 0.6% differs from 30% postsonication.
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 3; Figure 7B
claims.quote: Delayed responses of FSUs could be elicited by 6% (n = 22, p = 1.29 × 10−8), 30% (n = 49, p = 2.32 × 10−11), and 60% (n = 54, p = 2.38 × 10−8) DCs (Fig. 7B), which were the same range of S1 RSUs.
claims.criterion: As fig7a-s1-rsu-dc-3000 for S1 FSUs in 201 to 268 ms. The legend does not give the direction of the 0.6% against 30% difference; both one-tailed directions are read, the claim holding under the one the data's means give. Reproduced when exactly 6%, 30% and 60% are significantly above baseline and 0.6% and 30% differ significantly; partially reproduced when the per-DC pattern differs by one DC.

claims.statement: At 3,000 Hz PRF, POm RSU time-locked responses do not depend on DC and are highest at 60% (106 +/- 0.77%); their delayed responses depend on DC and are activated at the middle and high DCs.
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 3; Figure 7C legend
claims.quote: The POm RSUs’ time-locked responses did not show DC dependence and were highest at 60% (106 ± 0.77%; Fig. 7C). Delayed responses could be activated by DC higher than 6% (6%, n = 22, p = 1.55 × 10−6; n = 7, p = 0.001; 60%, n = 233, p = 1.28 × 10−6; 90%, n = 18, p = 0.006).
claims.criterion: POm RSUs (U) of the five 3,000 Hz sessions, R, T as in fig7a-s1-rsu-dc-3000. The absence of DC dependence during sonication is judged on the paper's test, Kruskal-Wallis across the five DCs in 0 to 67 ms, at p < 0.01 (the spiking level). "Higher than 6%" with 6% listed is read as (a) 6%, 30%, 60% and 90% significant and 0.6% not, or (b) 30%, 60% and 90% significant; the unlabeled n = 7 entry is taken as 30% by its order. Reproduced when the during-sonication Kruskal-Wallis is not significant, 60% has the highest mean within the paper's SEM, the postsonication Kruskal-Wallis is significant and the postsonication pattern matches a reading; partially reproduced when the two Kruskal-Wallis results hold and the rest holds in part.

claims.statement: At 3,000 Hz PRF, POm FSUs show no time-locked response against baseline but DC-dependent activity during sonication, with 30% above 0.6% and 6%, and delayed responses at 30%, 60% and 90%.
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 3; Figure 7D legend
claims.quote: There was no time-locked responses of POm FSUs compared with baseline while 30% DC showed higher activities compared with 0.6% (p = 0.0001) and 6% DC (p = 0.0003). The delayed activities of POm FSUs occurred at 30% (n = 18, p = 0.003), 60% (n = 17, p = 0.005), and 90% (n = 52, p = 6.8 × 10−5) DCs
claims.criterion: POm FSUs (U) of the five 3,000 Hz sessions, R, T as in fig7a-s1-rsu-dc-3000. Reproduced when no DC is significantly above baseline in 0 to 67 ms, the during-sonication Kruskal-Wallis is significant, 30% is significantly above 0.6% and 6% (one-tailed), and exactly 30%, 60% and 90% are significant in 201 to 268 ms; partially reproduced when at least three of these four parts hold.

claims.statement: At 30 Hz PRF, S1 RSUs respond during sonication at 6%, 30% and 90% DC and after sonication only at 90% DC, with DC-dependent activity in both windows.
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 3; Figure 8A
claims.quote: With 30 Hz PRF stimulation (Fig. 8A), the S1 RSUs showed time-locked responses to DC of 6% (n = 81, p = 1.19 × 10−8), 30% (n = 61, p = 0.001), and 90% (n = 66, p = 2.17 × 10−6) and delayed responses to 90% DC (n = 66, p = 1.5 × 10−24).
claims.criterion: S1 RSUs (U) of the five 30 Hz sessions (PD 200, 2,000, 10,000, 20,000, 30,000 us), R, T as in fig7a-s1-rsu-dc-3000. Reproduced when both Kruskal-Wallis tests are significant, exactly 6%, 30% and 90% are significantly above baseline in 0 to 67 ms and only 90% in 201 to 268 ms; partially reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis tests hold and the per-DC pattern differs by one DC.

claims.statement: At 30 Hz PRF, 90% DC induces a time-locked increase in S1 FSUs (n = 28), whose activity during sonication depends on DC; after sonication they respond only to 90% DC, while the legend reports no DC difference postsonication.
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 3; Figure 8B legend
claims.quote: Moreover, 90% DC with 30 Hz PRF induced positive time-locked response in S1 FSUs (Fig. 8B; n = 28, p = 4.57 × 10−11). Like S1 RSUs, S1 FSUs only showed delayed responses to 90% DC (n = 28, p = 0.007) with 30 Hz PRF.
claims.criterion: S1 FSUs (U) of the five 30 Hz sessions, R, T as in fig7a-s1-rsu-dc-3000. Reproduced when the during-sonication Kruskal-Wallis is significant, 90% is significantly above baseline in 0 to 67 ms, and in 201 to 268 ms 90% is significantly above baseline and no other DC is; partially reproduced when the time-locked part holds without the delayed part. The postsonication Kruskal-Wallis is reported against the legend's "no difference to DCs postsonication".

claims.statement: At constant 60% DC, only 30 Hz PRF differs from the other PRFs in S1 RSU activity during sonication, and postsonication activity is highest at 4,500 Hz; activity depends on PRF in both windows.
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 3; Figure 9A legend
claims.quote: only 30 Hz PRF showed different effects to other PRFs (300 Hz, p = 0.008; 1,500 Hz, p = 0.006; 3,000 Hz, p = 0.007; 4,500 Hz, p = 0.0003) on S1 RSUs during sonication, while postsonication activities preferred 4,500 Hz.
claims.criterion: S1 RSUs (U) of the five 60% DC sessions (30 Hz/20,000 us, 300/2,000, 1,500/400, 3,000/200, 4,500/133 us), R in 0 to 67 and 201 to 268 ms, Kruskal-Wallis at p < 0.01, pairwise one-tailed rank-sum tests between PRFs under B1 (the five PRFs compared with baseline) and B2 (the ten pairs), corrected p < 0.01. The direction of the 30 Hz difference is not stated; both directions are read, the claim holding under the one the data's means give. Reproduced when both Kruskal-Wallis tests are significant, 30 Hz differs from each of the other four PRFs in one direction during sonication and no other pair differs, and 4,500 Hz has the highest postsonication mean; partially reproduced when 30 Hz differs from three of the four or the postsonication rank fails.

claims.statement: At constant 60% DC, S1 FSUs respond to 1,500 Hz PRF during sonication (n = 48) and postsonication prefer 4,500 Hz (n = 18), with PRF-dependent activity in both windows.
claims.source: Results, tFUS parameters on affecting neuronal activities of CTC pathway, paragraph 3; Figure 9B legend
claims.quote: S1 FSUs responded to 1,500 Hz PRF (n = 48, p = 3.35 ×10−6) during sonication and preferred 4,500 Hz post sonication (n = 18, p = 5.84 × 10−10; Fig. 9B).
claims.criterion: S1 FSUs (U) of the five 60% DC sessions, R and T as in fig9a-s1-rsu-60dc. Reproduced when both Kruskal-Wallis tests are significant, 1,500 Hz is significantly above baseline during sonication, and 4,500 Hz is significantly above baseline postsonication with the highest mean; partially reproduced when two of these three parts hold.

claims.statement: During 3,000 Hz PRF, 60% DC sonication, the directional correlation from S1 RSUs to POm RSUs and from POm RSUs to S1 FSUs increases, while S1 RSU to POm FSU and POm RSU to S1 RSU do not change.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 10A legend
claims.quote: When 3,000 Hz PRF was applied, S1 RSUs showed an increased correlation to POm RSUs during sonication (p = 0.01). At the same period, POm RSUs showed enhanced correlation to S1 FSUs (p = 0.02). The other directional correlation did not show significant change during sonication.
claims.criterion: Pairs from the 3,000 Hz/200 us sessions, types as in U, normalized dSTTC as in D in 0 to 67 ms against the prestimulus window, one-tailed rank-sum at p < 0.05, after Kruskal-Wallis across the windows. Reproduced when S1 RSU to POm RSU and POm RSU to S1 FSU increase significantly and S1 RSU to POm FSU and POm RSU to S1 RSU do not change (tested in either direction, the paper's "no significant change"); partially reproduced when one of the two increases holds. Run under D1 and D2, D3 and D4, C1 and C2, R-independent; the outcome is the one they all give.

claims.statement: After 3,000 Hz PRF sonication, the directional correlation from S1 RSUs to POm FSUs and from POm RSUs to S1 RSUs decreases.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 10A
claims.quote: Postsonication, we found the correlation from S1 RSUs to POm FSUs and POm RSUs to S1 RSUs significantly decreased, representing the desynchronization of spikes.
claims.criterion: As fig10a-dsttc-3000-during, one-tailed for a decrease, in the postsonication windows of D1 or D2 (the paper does not say which postsonication window; 201 to 268 ms is the window of the spiking analysis, and the claim holds when the decrease is significant in at least one window after 67 ms). Reproduced when both decrease; partially when one does.

claims.statement: During 30 Hz PRF sonication, the directional correlation from S1 RSUs to POm FSUs increases and that from POm RSUs to S1 FSUs decreases.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 1; Figure 10B legend
claims.quote: When delivering 30 Hz ultrasound, S1 RSUs to POm FSUs higher correlated (p = 0.0058), while POm RSUs showed decreased correlation to S1 FSUs during sonication (p = 0.0058).
claims.criterion: As fig10a-dsttc-3000-during, for the 30 Hz/200 us sessions in 0 to 67 ms. Reproduced when the S1 RSU to POm FSU increase and the POm RSU to S1 FSU decrease are both significant at p < 0.05; partially reproduced when one is.

claims.statement: With constant 200 us PD, the change in S1 RSU to POm RSU correlation during sonication does not depend on PRF, though 1,500 Hz gives a larger change than 30 Hz.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 2; Figure 10C
claims.quote: When applying tFUS with constant 200 μs PD, varying the DC and PRF, the correlation did not show PRF-dependent change. A total of 1,500 Hz PRF did show a higher correlation change compared with 30 Hz PRF (Fig. 10C; p = 0.02).
claims.criterion: S1 RSU and POm RSU pairs of the five 200 us PD sessions, STTC change from prestimulus to 0 to 67 ms as in D (D3 or D4). The absence is judged on the paper's test, Kruskal-Wallis across the five PRFs at p < 0.05, not significant; the 1,500 against 30 Hz one-tailed rank-sum at p < 0.05. Reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis test is not significant and 1,500 Hz exceeds 30 Hz significantly; not reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis test is significant; partially reproduced when it is not and the pairwise test fails. Effect sizes (median change per PRF) are reported.

claims.statement: At constant 60% DC, the S1 RSU to POm RSU correlation change depends on PRF, with a preference for 1,500 and 3,000 Hz.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 2; Figure 10D legend
claims.quote: Then we fixed the DC to 60% and varied PRF. Unlike the neuronal responses (Fig. 9), the correlation showed the preference to 1,500 and 3,000 Hz (Fig. 10D).
claims.criterion: As fig10c-sttc-constant-pd, for the five 60% DC sessions. Reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis test is significant at p < 0.05 and 1,500 and 3,000 Hz have the two highest changes; partially reproduced when it is significant and one of them is among the two highest. The paper does not say whether the preference is read from means or medians; both are read.

claims.statement: At 30 Hz PRF, the S1 RSU to POm RSU correlation change depends on DC, changing most at the middle DCs (6, 30, 60%) and less at 0.6% and 90%.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 2; Figure 10E
claims.quote: For 30 Hz PRF (Fig. 10E), the correlation tended to change most at a middle range (6, 30, 60%) and respond less to lower (e.g., 0.6%) and higher DC (e.g., 90%).
claims.criterion: As fig10c-sttc-constant-pd, for the five 30 Hz sessions. "Tended to" is judged on the means, and on the medians as a second reading (the paper names neither); reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis test is significant at p < 0.05 and each of 6%, 30% and 60% has a larger mean change than both 0.6% and 90%; partially reproduced when the test is significant and two of the three middle DCs exceed both ends.

claims.statement: At 3,000 Hz PRF, the S1 RSU to POm RSU correlation change does not depend on DC.
claims.source: Results, tFUS elicited correlation change in CTC pathway, paragraph 2; Figure 10F
claims.quote: For 3,000 Hz PRF, the pathway correlation showed DC independence (Fig. 10F).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, Kruskal-Wallis across the five 3,000 Hz DC sessions at p < 0.05, measure as in fig10c-sttc-constant-pd. Reproduced when not significant, not reproduced when significant, under each reading of D3 and D4; the H statistic and the per-DC means are reported.

claims.statement: Auditory cortex neurons respond during sonication to 1,500 and 3,000 Hz PRF and after sonication to 30, 1,500, 3,000 and 4,500 Hz, with PRF-dependent responses and the least response at 300 Hz.
claims.source: Results, Auditory confound on CTC pathway modulation using tFUS, paragraph 1; Figure 11 legend (panel B, printed as C)
claims.quote: During sonication, the AC neurons showed time-locked responses to 1,500 Hz (n = 107, p = 9.9 × 10−5) and 3,000 Hz PRF (n = 104, p = 1.98 × 10−7). Postsonication, neuronal responses were activated by 30 Hz (n = 83, p = 1.77 × 10−20), 1,500 Hz, (n = 107, p = 1.36 × 10−5), 3,000 Hz (n = 104, p = 4.47 × 10−13), and 4,500 Hz (n = 100, p = 1.66 × 10−40).
claims.criterion: AC units of the 12 S1 and AC rats with more than 2,000 spikes (U, not typed), R, T as in fig6a-s1-rsu-timelocked-high-prf, 0 to 67 and 201 to 268 ms. Which PD the PRF series used is not stated ("varying combination of PRFs and DCs"); the reading is the 200 us PD series of Fig. 6, and any other PRF series the AC sessions hold is shown as a variant. Reproduced when both Kruskal-Wallis tests are significant, exactly 1,500 and 3,000 Hz are significant during sonication, exactly 30, 1,500, 3,000 and 4,500 Hz postsonication, and 300 Hz has the lowest mean in both windows; partially reproduced when the patterns differ by one PRF. The total count is within 10%.

claims.statement: During 30 Hz PRF sonication the directional correlation from AC neurons to S1 RSUs increases and lasts about 150 to 200 ms, while the correlation of AC neurons to S1 FSUs changes during and right after sonication.
claims.source: Figure 11 legend (second panel C); Results, Auditory confound on CTC pathway modulation using tFUS, paragraph 2
claims.quote: During tFUS sonication with 30 Hz PRF, the correlation from 878 paired AC neurons to S1 RSUs significantly increased (p = 0.0014) which lasting for ∼150 ms (left). The correlation of AC neurons to S1 FSUs decreased during and right after sonication.
claims.criterion: Pairs of AC neurons and S1 units (U) in the 30 Hz/200 us sessions of the AC rats, normalized dSTTC from AC to S1 as in D, against the prestimulus window, one-tailed rank-sum at p < 0.05. The legend gives 1,421 AC and S1 RSU pairs and 878 pairs for 30 Hz; the readings are (a) 878 is the number of pairs in the 30 Hz sessions and 1,421 those of all sessions, (b) 878 are the pairs with a defined dSTTC among 1,421 in the 30 Hz sessions. The Results say the increase lasted about 200 ms and that the same synchronization was found from AC to S1 FSUs, while the legend says about 150 ms and a decrease to S1 FSUs. Reproduced when the AC to S1 RSU increase is significant in 0 to 67 ms and stays significant in consecutive windows to between 134 and 268 ms (covering both durations); partially reproduced when only the 0 to 67 ms increase holds. The AC to S1 FSU change is reported with its direction, set against both passages, and the pair count is compared under each reading.

claims.statement: With 3,000 Hz PRF, AC neurons show no directional correlation change with S1 RSUs, while the correlation of AC neurons to S1 FSUs changes in both directions after sonication, at about 200 to 300 ms.
claims.source: Figure 11 legend (panel D); Results, Auditory confound on CTC pathway modulation using tFUS, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The 1,714 paired neurons recorded from 3,000 Hz PRF sessions were compared. There was no correlation change of AC neurons to S1 RSUs. While there were postsonication bidirectional correlation change from 1,016 paired AC neurons to S1 FSUs.
claims.criterion: As fig11c-ac-to-s1-30hz, for the 3,000 Hz/200 us sessions. The absence for AC to S1 RSUs is judged on the paper's test, one-tailed rank-sum against the prestimulus window at p < 0.05, in each window of D, in either direction; reproduced for that part when none is significant. The AC to S1 FSU part holds when windows between about 200 and 300 ms (D1 windows 201 to 268 and 268 to 335 ms) show significant changes, an increase in one and a decrease in another ("bidirectional"; the paper does not say whether this means both signs over time or both directions of the pair, which is the second reading, AC to S1 FSU and S1 FSU to AC both changing). Reproduced when both parts hold, partially when one does.

claims.statement: The tdTomato+ cell densities computed from the dandiset's whole-brain images agree, brain by brain, with the densities in the paper's deposited table (tdTomato_summary.csv on Figshare) that its Figure 2 code reads.
claims.source: Data availability; Figure 2.ipynb at GitHub commit 4e98c43, cell 4
claims.quote: Whole brain FosTRAP activity mapping data is available on DANDI
claims.criterion: Densities computed here as in fig2c-brain-wide-increase (ClearMap registration to the Unified Anatomical Atlas, ilastik segmentation, count per region over region volume). The trained classifier is not deposited, so it is retrained as the Methods describe (10 random chunks of 1.8 x 1.8 mm x 100 um from four subjects). The link holds (reproduced) when the 14 brains fall into groups of 4, 5 and 5 matching the table's Stim labels and, for each brain, the median over level-6 regions of the absolute relative difference from the table's density of the matched subject is within 10% (the protocol's default tolerance). Partially reproduced when the groups match but fewer than 10 of the 14 brains meet the 10% bound. The per-brain correlation over regions is reported. The table is outside data (Figshare doi:10.6084/m9.figshare.27642768.v1).

claims.statement: TRAP-labeled (tdTomato+) cell density increases brain-wide when 4-OHT is given after male ejaculation, compared with the appetitive phase.
claims.source: Results, Brain-wide mapping of neural response to male ejaculation, paragraph 1; Figure 2C and 2D
claims.quote: As a result, we found the level of tdTomato expression increased in a brain-wide manner during the post-ejaculatory period when compared to the appetitive phase
claims.criterion: Method from the Methods (Brain-wide analysis) and the Figure 2 legend, with the code where they are silent. Per brain, tdTomato+ cells per atlas region (Unified Anatomical Atlas, Kim lab, outside data; Figure 2.ipynb reads its label table atlas_info_KimRef_FPbasedLabel_v2.9) divided by region volume (cells per mm3), at hierarchy level 4. Per region a one-way ANOVA over the three groups (appetitive n=4, consummatory n=5, post-ejaculatory n=5), Benjamini-Hochberg correction at FDR 0.05 (Methods and legend; the code uses 0.1, shown as a variant), then Tukey's HSD (FWER 0.05) post-ejaculatory against appetitive for regions significant in the ANOVA. Open, and named here because it could change the outcome; (1) the level-4 family is the ten regions of the code or the twelve of the Figure 2C legend (adding VERM and HEM); (2) region volume is the atlas volume or the region's volume in each brain's own space; the paper gives neither. Supplementary file 2, which lists which regions were significant, is not in the text read, so "brain-wide" is read as follows, stated before analysis. Reproduced when the post-ejaculatory mean exceeds the appetitive mean in at least 80% of the level-4 regions of the family and at least half of the family is significant (ANOVA q < 0.05 and Tukey p < 0.05, post-ejaculatory higher). Partially reproduced when the direction holds in at least 80% but fewer than half are significant. Not reproduced otherwise. Every reading is run; when they give different outcomes the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Regions known for social behavior, including the paraventricular hypothalamic areas (PVHd, PVH, PaV), the medial amygdala and the BNST, have significantly higher tdTomato+ density in the post-ejaculatory group than in the appetitive group.
claims.source: Results, Brain-wide mapping of neural response to male ejaculation, paragraph 1; Figure 2E to 2H; Figure 2-figure supplement 2
claims.quote: regions well known to be related to social behavior had significantly higher tdTomato density in the post-ejaculatory group compared to appetitive group ... This includes paraventricular hypothalamic areas (PVHd, PVH, PaV) which are important for endocrinological regulations, medial amygdala (MeA) which is critical for olfactory sensory information processing, and the BNST
claims.criterion: Densities as in fig2c-brain-wide-increase, at hierarchy level 6. Per region a one-way ANOVA over the three groups with Benjamini-Hochberg correction at FDR 0.10 over the level-6 family (Methods; Figure 2-figure supplement 2 legend), then Tukey's HSD at FWER 0.05 (Methods; p-values from scipy tukey_hsd as in Figure 2.ipynb). A region is significantly higher when q < 0.10, Tukey p < 0.05 and the post-ejaculatory mean is higher. The medial amygdala is the atlas label Me (Figure 2H legend); the other names are matched to atlas acronyms at level 6, or at the nearest level that holds them when level 6 does not (open; named before analysis). The level-6 family is (a) the code's, regions under the ten level-4 regions, or (b) all level-6 regions. Reproduced when all five regions (PVHd, PVH, PaV, Me, BNST) are significantly higher under the readings; partially reproduced for three or four; not reproduced below three. Per-region q and Tukey p are reported.

claims.statement: The medial preoptic nucleus (MPN) has significantly higher tdTomato+ density in the post-ejaculatory group than in the appetitive group.
claims.source: Results, Brain-wide mapping of neural response to male ejaculation, paragraph 1; Figure 2F and 2H
claims.quote: The medial preoptic area nucleus (MPN), a subregion of the MPOA, had significantly higher tdTomato density in the post-ejaculatory group compared to the appetitive group
