claims.criterion: As in fig2ei-social-regions-higher, for the atlas region MPN. Reproduced when the level-6 ANOVA q < 0.10 (under both family readings) and Tukey's HSD post-ejaculatory against appetitive p < 0.05 with the post-ejaculatory mean higher. Partially reproduced when Tukey p < 0.05 but q >= 0.10. The density ratio of the two group means is reported.

claims.statement: The MPN shows the fourth largest difference in mean tdTomato+ density between the post-ejaculatory and appetitive groups among all brain regions.
claims.source: Results, Brain-wide mapping of neural response to male ejaculation, paragraph 1; Figure 2F
claims.quote: The MPN also had the fourth largest difference of density between the post-ejaculatory group and appetitive group among all the brain regions
claims.criterion: Difference is the post-ejaculatory group mean minus the appetitive group mean of density (Figure 2F, "difference of average tdTomato density"). The set ranked is open; the readings the text allows are (a) the level-6 family of the code, (b) all level-6 regions, (c) all atlas regions at every level. The rank is a reported count (tolerance 0); the claim is reproduced when the MPN ranks fourth under one reading. The ranks under every reading and the three regions above the MPN are shown.

claims.statement: The consummatory group tends to have higher MPN tdTomato+ density than the appetitive group, without reaching significance.
claims.source: Results, Brain-wide mapping of neural response to male ejaculation, paragraph 1; Figure 2G and 2H
claims.quote: While it was not statistically significant, the consummatory group also tended to have a larger tdTomato density than the appetitive group in the MPN as well
claims.criterion: For the MPN, Tukey's HSD consummatory against appetitive (FWER 0.05), as in Figure 2G and Figure 2.ipynb. The absence part is judged on that test alone; the claim is reproduced when Tukey p >= 0.05 and the consummatory mean is above the appetitive mean; partially reproduced when p >= 0.05 and the mean is not higher; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The mean difference and p are reported.

claims.statement: The whole-brain mapping indicates increased TRAP labeling in the dorsal raphe after male ejaculation.
claims.source: Discussion, Neural circuitry for female sexual behavior regulation, last paragraph; Figure 2-figure supplement 1 and 2
claims.quote: Our whole brain activity mapping data also indicates increased Fos activity in the dorsal raphe
claims.criterion: For the atlas dorsal raphe region at level 6 (DR, or the label the atlas gives it), as in fig2ei-social-regions-higher. Reproduced when the post-ejaculatory mean exceeds the appetitive mean and the ANOVA q < 0.10 (the significance marked in Figure 2-figure supplement 2); partially reproduced when the mean is higher but q >= 0.10.

claims.statement: In hormone-primed females, zone transitions decrease and time in the isolation zone increases after male ejaculation, compared with before ejaculation and with the control trial.
claims.source: Figure 1G and 1H; Results, Female sexual motivation is suppressed after male ejaculation, paragraph 2
claims.quote: we found that there was a significant decrease in the number of zone transitions as well as a significant increase in the time spent in the isolation zone after male ejaculation
claims.criterion: As in the Figure 1 legend and Figure 1.ipynb; repeated-measures ANOVA (statsmodels AnovaRM) over control, pre- and post-ejaculation, then Tukey's HSD (FWER 0.05). Reproduced when both ANOVAs have p < 0.05 and post differs from pre and from control in the stated direction at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Latency to return to the interaction zone is longest after male ejaculation, longer than after sniffing or mounting.
claims.source: Figure 1I; Results, Female sexual motivation is suppressed after male ejaculation, paragraph 2
claims.quote: This was the largest after the female experienced male ejaculation when compared to after sniffing or after mounting
claims.criterion: RM ANOVA then Tukey's HSD as in the Figure 1 legend. Reproduced when ejaculation latency exceeds both others at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: After ejaculation, female-to-male sniffing does not change, while mounting and intromission decrease and self-grooming increases (hormone-primed females).
claims.source: Figure 1J to 1M; Results, Female sexual motivation is suppressed after male ejaculation, paragraph 2
claims.quote: while there was no change in the amount of female-to-male sniffing, there was a significant decrease in the number of mounting and intromission episodes ... There was also a significant increase in the number of self-grooming behavioral episodes
claims.criterion: Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test pre against post on counts per 10 min (legend; Figure 1.ipynb, scipy wilcoxon). Reproduced when mounting and intromission decrease and grooming increases at p < 0.05, and sniffing is not significant (the absence judged on this test).

claims.statement: Naturally cycling estrus females show the same post-ejaculatory changes, with a strong reduction of sniffing and no change in self-grooming.
claims.source: Figure 1N to 1T; Results, Female sexual motivation is suppressed after male ejaculation, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Animals that were in their natural estrus cycle showed similar behavior changes after experiencing male ejaculation ... showed a strong reduction of sniffing after experiencing male ejaculation but no changes in self-grooming behaviors
claims.criterion: Tests as in the Figure 1 legend (RM ANOVA and Tukey's HSD for N to P; Wilcoxon signed-rank for Q to T). Reproduced when the three ANOVAs, sniffing, mounting and intromission are significant at p < 0.05 (counts lower after ejaculation) and grooming is not (the absence judged on the Wilcoxon signed-rank test).

claims.statement: Virgin females spend more time in the isolation zone than sexually experienced females; the number of isolation zone entries also differs between the two groups.
claims.source: Figure 1-figure supplement 1; Results, Female sexual motivation is suppressed after male ejaculation, paragraph 2
claims.quote: the virgin female mice stayed in the isolation zone significantly longer than sexually experienced females
claims.criterion: Two-sided Mann-Whitney U test (legend; Figure S1.ipynb, scipy mannwhitneyu). The legend does not say which part of the session is compared; Figure S1.ipynb (cell 8) compares the pre-ejaculation epoch of the sexual interaction trial, which is followed. Reproduced when the time difference is significant at p < 0.05 with virgin females higher and the entries difference is significant at p < 0.05. The text does not state the direction of the entries difference, which is reported.

claims.statement: The post-ejaculatory reduction in sexual motivation does not depend on the state of the male; with a novel sexually active male after ejaculation, females still make fewer isolation zone entries and spend more time there.
claims.source: Figure 1-figure supplement 2; Results, Female sexual motivation is suppressed after male ejaculation, paragraph 2
claims.quote: When the female animal was introduced to a novel sexually motivated male animal immediately after they experienced male ejaculation from another mouse, they showed a similar reduction in zone transition and an increase in the time spent in the isolation zone
claims.criterion: Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, pre- against post-ejaculation assay (legend; Figure S2.ipynb). Reproduced when both are significant at p < 0.05 in the stated direction.

claims.statement: By HCR, the proportion of Fos+ cells is higher after ejaculation than in the appetitive group in the MPN but not in nearby regions (MPA, BNST, LPO, VLPO).
claims.source: Figure 3D; Results, Male ejaculation is represented by both inhibitory and excitatory cell types in the MPOA, paragraph 2
claims.quote: we found that the number of Fos + cells in the post-ejaculatory group was significantly higher than the appetitive group in the MPN but not in the nearby regions
claims.criterion: Per mouse and region, the proportion of Fos+ cells averaged over sections (Figure S5.ipynb groupby mean). Student's t-test with Bonferroni correction over the five regions (legend; Figure S5.ipynb, scipy ttest_ind and multipletests). Reproduced when only the MPN is significant at corrected p < 0.05, higher after ejaculation.

claims.statement: In the MPN, both Vglut2+ and Vgat+ cells expressing Fos increase after ejaculation, with a higher proportion of Fos+ cells in the Vgat population.
claims.source: Figure 3I; Results, Male ejaculation is represented by both inhibitory and excitatory cell types in the MPOA, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Vglut2 and Vgat cells expressing Fos were significantly higher in the post-ejaculatory group than in the appetitive group, suggesting that male ejaculation activates both excitatory and inhibitory neurons ... The proportion of Fos+ cells was higher in the Vgat population
claims.criterion: As in the Figure 3 legend. Reproduced when both are significant at corrected p < 0.05 and the post-ejaculatory Fos+ proportion is higher in Vgat than in Vglut2 cells (no test is reported for the latter, so it is judged on the means).

claims.statement: Fos induction after ejaculation is found in Vglut2 cells only when they co-express Calcr, and in Vgat cells co-expressing Calcr, Gal or Prlr; among clusters, the Vglut2, Vgat and Gal types have more Fos+ cells after ejaculation, while the Nts type does not.
claims.source: Figure 3J to 3M; Results, Male ejaculation is represented by both inhibitory and excitatory cell types in the MPOA, paragraph 2
claims.quote: in the Vglut2 cells, we found that Fos induction was only observed in the cells that co-expressed Calcr ... Type 1 ... and type 3 ... had significantly more Fos+ cells from the post-ejaculatory group compared to the appetitive group ... In contrast, Fos+ cells were not induced in type 4
claims.criterion: Student's t-tests with Bonferroni correction as in the Figure 3 legend; clusters from Seurat 3.1.1 as in the Methods and Figure S5_Seurat clustering.R. The legend prints t(8)=-3.9487 for every Vglut2 row and for Vgat+ Prlr+, so those statistics are not recorded. Reproduced when the named groups are significant at corrected p < 0.05 and the Nts cluster is not.

claims.statement: Vgat cells show higher average response magnitude than Vglut2 cells after sniffing, self-grooming, male anogenital sniffing and ejaculation, but not after mounting or intromission.
claims.source: Figure 4H; Results, A subpopulation of MPOA Vgat cells responds to male ejaculation, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Vgat cells showed significantly higher average response magnitude after sniffing, self-grooming, anogenital sniffing, and male ejaculation than the Vglut2 cells
claims.criterion: Per cell, z-scored signal (z-scored on the background period) from -5 to +15 s around each onset, averaged over events, baseline (-5 to 0 s) subtracted, magnitude the mean of 0 to +5 s (Methods; the code's parameter_dict also sets after_window_for_quantification to 5 s). The Results say "for 15 s after behavior onset"; the Methods' 0 to 5 s is followed. Sniffs after the first mount are excluded (Methods). Student's t-test per behavior over the six behaviors with Bonferroni correction (legend; Figure 3, 4, 5, S6, S7, S8.ipynb, scipy ttest_ind and multipletests). Grooming has t = -7.25, that is Vgat lower, against the Results sentence; the sign is reported and grooming is left out of the outcome. Reproduced when ejaculation, sniff and anogenital sniffing are significant with Vgat higher and mount and intromission are not.

claims.statement: A larger proportion of Vgat than Vglut2 cells respond positively to ejaculation (184/522 against 35/271) and to sniffing (29/522 against 1/271).
claims.source: Figure 4I; Results, A subpopulation of MPOA Vgat cells responds to male ejaculation, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Vgat cells also contained a significantly higher proportion of cells that positively respond (>2δ) to sniff and male ejaculation onset
claims.criterion: Responding when the magnitude of fig4h-response-magnitude exceeds 2 (Methods; abs value above 2 in the code, sign giving positive or negative). Chi-square test of proportions (statsmodels proportions_chisquare) over the six behaviors with Bonferroni correction (legend and Figure 3, 4, 5, S6, S7, S8.ipynb). Reproduced when the counts match and ejaculation and sniff differ at corrected p < 0.05 with Vgat higher.

claims.statement: Among cells responding to sniff, mount or ejaculation, ejaculation-specific cells are the most numerous (177, against 46 mount and 12 sniff), and most ejaculation responders are specific (Vgat 80%, Vglut2 82%).
claims.source: Results, A subpopulation of MPOA Vgat cells responds to male ejaculation, paragraph 2; Figure 5A to 5D
claims.quote: the number of cells that specifically responded was largest to male ejaculation with 177 cells, next to mount with 46 cells, and to sniff with 12 cells
claims.criterion: The Figure 5 legend gives n=48 mount and 178 ejaculation cells, against 46 and 177 in the Results; both are readings. "Specific" is read as (a) positive (>2) to that behavior only, among sniff, mount and ejaculation, recomputed from the per-behavior positive responder flags of fig4i-ejaculation-responders, or (b) the precomputed magnitude_cell_types column of male_analysis_magnitude.csv, whose values Sniff_only_cells, Mount_only_cells and Ejaculation_only_cells the code uses for Figure 5 (the legend says the cells "were categorized based on response magnitude"). The counts hold if they match under one reading.

claims.statement: Sniff-specific and ejaculation-specific cells respond more strongly than the other classes only to sniff and to ejaculation, respectively; mount-specific cells respond more strongly than the other classes to mount, intromission and anogenital sniffing, but not to sniff or ejaculation.
claims.source: Results, A subpopulation of MPOA Vgat cells responds to male ejaculation, paragraph 2; Figure 5C
claims.quote: sniff cells and completion cells only showed significantly stronger responses than the other cells to sniff and male ejaculation, respectively ... Mount responsive cells showed significantly stronger response than the other cells to mount, intromission and anogenital sniffing, but not to sniffing and male ejaculation
claims.criterion: Cells are the sniff, mount and ejaculation-specific classes of fig5-ejaculation-specific; the measure is the response magnitude of fig4h-response-magnitude for each of the six behaviors. Per behavior a one-way ANOVA over the three classes and Tukey's HSD (FWER 0.05), as the panel C entries of the Figure 5 legend give them and as Figure 3, 4, 5, S6, S7, S8.ipynb runs them (statsmodels ols with anova_lm, pairwise_tukeyhsd). The legend's closing line names Student's t-test with Bonferroni correction for C; the reported F and Tukey values and the code both use ANOVA and Tukey, which is followed. Reproduced when, at p < 0.05, sniff cells exceed both other classes for sniff, ejaculation cells exceed both for ejaculation, mount cells exceed both for mount and exceed ejaculation cells for intromission and anogenital sniffing, and mount cells do not exceed sniff cells for sniff nor ejaculation cells for ejaculation.

claims.statement: Ejaculation-responding Vgat cells have a longer decay length than Vglut2 cells.
claims.source: Figure 6C; Results, MPOA Vgat cells display prolonged activity, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Vgat cells had significantly longer decay length compared to the Vglut2 cells
claims.criterion: Signal from -5 to +120 s around ejaculation onset, baseline (-5 to 0 s) subtracted (Methods). Decay length is "the time the z-scored signal was smaller than 0" (Methods) or "the time for the increased calcium signal to return to baseline" (Results); the code reads it precomputed. Readings, (a) time from onset to the first sample below 0, (b) total time below 0 in 0 to 120 s. Student's t-test (scipy ttest_ind). Reproduced when Vgat is longer at p < 0.05 under the readings.

claims.statement: Spectral clustering of ejaculation responses gives five types; the late-response type 3 has the longest decay length and contains only Vgat cells, while Vglut2 cells are more often fast responders.
claims.source: Figure 6D to 6K; Results, MPOA Vgat cells display prolonged activity, paragraph 1
claims.quote: all the cells in type 3 were Vgat cells, suggesting that the increased activity in the MPOA late after the onset of male ejaculation is mediated by inhibitory neurons
claims.criterion: Cells are the ejaculation responders of fig4i-ejaculation-responders (184 Vgat, 35 Vglut2). PCA of the -5 to +120 s traces (whitened in Figure 5 Spectral clustering.ipynb), 4 components (Methods; the code picks the number at the elbow of the scree plot), spectral clustering (scikit-learn, nearest_neighbors affinity) with the number of clusters (2 to 11 in the code) and nearest neighbours (10 to 70 in steps of 5 in the code) chosen by maximal silhouette score, computed with the cosine metric in the code (the paper reports 5 clusters, 55 neighbours, silhouette 0.405). Proportions compared by chi-square test with Bonferroni correction over the five types (legend). Reproduced when the cluster with the latest response and longest decay holds no Vglut2 cells and its Vgat proportion differs at corrected p < 0.05, and the fast-response cluster holds a larger proportion of Vglut2 than of Vgat cells at corrected p < 0.05. The clustering has no fixed random seed in the code; cluster membership may vary between runs, which is reported.

claims.statement: CNO activation of post-ejaculatory TRAP-labeled MPOA neurons reduces zone transitions and increases time in the isolation zone; activation of appetitive or consummatory ensembles and eYFP controls do not.
claims.source: Figure 7F and 7G; Results, An activity-defined subset of neurons in the MPOA, paragraph 4
claims.quote: only post-ejaculatory-hM3Dq group showed significantly fewer number of transitions and spent more time in the isolation zone on the CNO trial than on the saline trial
claims.criterion: Saline against CNO trial within each group, Bonferroni over the four groups. The legend names a Wilcoxon rank sum test; Figure 6.ipynb runs scipy wilcoxon (paired signed-rank), and 0.03125 is 4 times the smallest two-sided signed-rank p for 8 mice. Methods first; the rank-sum test is the main reading and the signed-rank test is the variant. Reproduced when only post-ejaculatory-hM3Dq is significant at corrected p < 0.05 in both measures.

claims.statement: Activation of post-ejaculatory TRAP neurons lowers intromissions and receptivity in the self-paced assay; the text also reports fewer self-grooming and mounting episodes, which the legend gives as p = 0.0625.
claims.source: Figure 7H to 7L; Results, An activity-defined subset of neurons in the MPOA, paragraph 4
claims.quote: post-ejaculatory-hM3Dq group displayed fewer numbers of self-grooming, mounting, intromission and lower receptivity score on the CNO trial than on the saline trial
claims.criterion: Tests as in fig7fg-activation-suppresses. Reproduced when intromission and receptive score are lower on CNO at corrected p < 0.05; grooming and mounting are reported.

claims.statement: The number of TRAP-labeled cells does not differ between groups, but the proportion located in the MPN is higher in the post-ejaculatory group; most MPN TRAP cells are Vgat (0.76) and few Vglut2 (0.15).
claims.source: Figure 7-figure supplement 1B, 1C and 1G; Results, An activity-defined subset of neurons in the MPOA, paragraph 1
claims.quote: while the overall number of TRAP-labeled cells had no difference between the post-ejaculatory groups, consummatory group and appetitive group, the proportion of cells located in the MPN was significantly higher in the post-ejaculatory group ... most TRAP-labeled cells in the MPN were Vgat (Vgat: 0.76±0.16. Vglut2: 0.15±0.13)
claims.criterion: One-way ANOVA and Tukey HSD as in the legend (Figure S9.ipynb, pairwise_tukeyhsd). Tolerances are the stated spread. The text does not say over which mice the 0.76 and 0.15 are taken; the readings are (a) the appetitive-hM3Dq and post-ejaculatory-hM3Dq mice of panel G pooled (13), (b) the post-ejaculatory mice alone (7). The Vgat against Vglut2 test of G is not named; the degrees of freedom (2n - 2) fit an unpaired Student's t-test, which is the main reading, with the paired test as a variant. Reproduced when the count ANOVA is not significant, the MPN proportion ANOVA is, post-ejaculatory above appetitive at p < 0.05, the Vgat proportion exceeds the Vglut2 proportion at p < 0.05 in both groups, and the proportions match under one reading.

claims.statement: In the home cage, activation of post-ejaculatory TRAP neurons reduces sniffing and intromission compared with post-ejaculatory eYFP controls, without changing mounting; it does not induce place preference or aversion.
claims.source: Figure 7-figure supplement 2C to 2J; Results, An activity-defined subset of neurons in the MPOA, paragraphs 3 and 4
claims.quote: post-ejaculatory-hM3Dq group but not the appetitive-hM3Dq and consummatory-hM3Dq group showed significantly fewer sniffing events compared to post-ejaculatory-eYFP group ... there were significantly less intromission episodes
claims.criterion: Each hM3Dq group against post-ejaculatory-eYFP by Mann-Whitney U test with Bonferroni correction (legend; Figure S10.ipynb). Reproduced when sniff and intromission are significant for post-ejaculatory-hM3Dq only, and mounting and the place preference measures are not.

claims.statement: Chemogenetic inhibition of post-ejaculatory TRAP neurons does not change behavior in the self-paced assay, but increases intromission and receptivity in the home cage assay.
claims.source: Figure 7-figure supplement 3; Results, An activity-defined subset of neurons in the MPOA, paragraph 5
claims.quote: the post-ejaculatory-hM4Di group experienced did not show significant changes in sniffing, self-grooming, or mounting, but showed more intromission and higher sexual receptivity than in the post-ejaculatory-eYFP group
claims.criterion: Home cage, post-ejaculatory-hM4Di against post-ejaculatory-eYFP by two-sided Mann-Whitney U test without correction (legend, O to R; Figure S11.ipynb, scipy mannwhitneyu). Self-paced assay, saline against CNO trial within each group with Bonferroni correction (E to L); the legend names a Wilcoxon rank sum test and Figure S11.ipynb runs scipy wilcoxon (paired signed-rank), so, as in fig7fg-activation-suppresses, the rank-sum test is the main reading and the signed-rank test the variant. The absence in the self-paced assay is judged on the main reading. Reproduced when both home cage measures are higher in hM4Di at p < 0.05, sniffing and mounting are not, and no self-paced measure is significant.

claims.statement: The simulations hold spikes from 1,388 model neurons within 50 um of the Neuropixels probe in the spontaneous regime, 1,836 in the 1-hour evoked regime at 20 kHz and 1,552 in the 10-minute evoked regime at 40 kHz, and every one of them fired at least once in the first 10 minutes.
claims.source: Methods, Datasets and simulations, Biophysical model, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We detected spikes from 1,388 model neurons during the spontaneous activity condition, 1,836 model neurons during the 1-hour evoked condition sampled at 20 kHz, and 1,552 neurons during the 10 minute evoked condition sampled at 40 kHz, within 50 µm of the Neuropixels probe ... All model neurons fired at least once in the first 10 minutes
claims.criterion: Count the ground truth units of each simulation (the 50 um rule is in the opening comment). Reproduced when the counts are within tolerance and, for each simulation, every unit has at least one spike in the first 600 s; the number of silent units is reported. A simulation the dataset lacks is reported as not testable.

claims.statement: After gain and noise fitting, the maximal amplitude of the spontaneous Neuropixels simulation (361 uV) matches that of the Marques-Smith recording (362 uV), and the evoked simulation reaches 387 uV.
claims.source: Methods, Fitting amplitude and background noise, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The spontaneous regime’s maximal amplitude (361 µV) closely matched Marques-Smith’s (362 µV), while the evoked regime produced a slightly higher value (387 µV)
claims.criterion: The paper does not say whether the maximum is taken before or after preprocessing, nor over which duration or sites. Readings, (a) the maximum absolute value of the fitted traces after preprocessing (300 Hz high-pass and common median reference) over cortical sites, as in the code (fig2_M_amplitude_npx, maximum of the absolute trace per site over the loaded trace); (b) the same on the raw fitted traces. Which evoked simulation is meant is not stated; both are shown. Reproduced when, under one reading, the three values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: In both in vivo datasets the median peak amplitude of the traces increased with cortical depth, and the biophysical models reproduced this trend, although their medians differed from in vivo.
claims.source: Results, Validation of recording traces, paragraph 2; Figure 2m, o
claims.quote: In both Marques-Smith and Horvath’s data, median peak amplitude increased with cortical depth ... While the models’ median peak amplitudes differed from in vivo (most p < 0.01, Mann-Whitney U test), all captured the in vivo trend
claims.criterion: Per site, the peak amplitude is the maximum absolute value of the preprocessed trace (code, fig2_M_amplitude_npx; the paper says "peak amplitudes of the electrode traces"), sites grouped by layer, cortical sites only; first 10 minutes (Methods, Amplitude-to-noise ratio, for all validation metrics; the code reads the whole trace, shown as a variant). For each of NS, E and DS, a Kruskal-Wallis test across layers. The paper does not say how "increased with depth" is judged beyond the test; the criterion takes the test at p < 0.001 and the layer medians rising from layer 1 to layer 6 with at most one inversion between neighbouring layers. Reproduced when this holds for every model; partially reproduced when it holds for some. The in vivo trend and the per-layer Mann-Whitney U tests against M (Neuropixels models) and H (dense model) are reported, with the share of layers at p < 0.01.

claims.statement: Background noise increased with cortical depth in vivo, and the biophysical models reproduced this trend.
claims.source: Results, Validation of recording traces, paragraph 2; Figure 2n, p
claims.quote: In vivo background noise also increased with cortical depth ( p < 0.001, Kruskall Wallis, Fig. 2n, p ), a trend reproduced by the biophysical models
claims.criterion: Noise per site as the Methods give it for the fit, the mean absolute deviation of the preprocessed trace (Methods, Fitting amplitude and background noise); the code (src/nodes/validation/noise.py) takes the mean absolute deviation in 1-s segments and keeps the minimum over segments, which is followed. The median absolute deviation (Methods, Amplitude-to-noise ratio) is a variant. First 10 minutes, cortical sites, grouped by layer. Reproduced when, for each of NS, E and DS, a Kruskal-Wallis test across layers has p < 0.001 and the layer medians rise from layer 1 to 6 with at most one inversion between neighbours; partially reproduced when this holds for some models.

claims.statement: The amplitude-to-noise ratio distributions of the models span a wide dynamic range and lie within the in vivo range, with data between -10 and 10 times the noise level.
claims.source: Results, Validation of recording traces, paragraph 2; Figure 2q
claims.quote: The distributions of ANRs observed in vivo and in the models showed a wide dynamic range, with alignment of data points between -10 and 10 times the noise level ( Fig. 2q ), particularly in layers 1, 5, and 6. Despite deviations from in vivo due to difference in peak amplitudes, simulated ANRs remained within the in vivo range
claims.criterion: ANR is the preprocessed trace divided by its median absolute deviation, per site, first 10 minutes, cortical sites; the range of all experiments split into 100 bins, the probability per bin per site, averaged over sites (Methods, Amplitude-to-noise ratio). "Within the in vivo range" is not defined; the criterion reads it as the minimum and maximum ANR of each model lying within those of its in vivo reference (M for NS and E, H for DS), widened by 10%. Reproduced when this holds for all three models, and every distribution has data from -10 to 10.

claims.statement: In simulated and real traces, power decreased with frequency in the spiking band (0.3 to 6 kHz) and followed a power law in all layers.
claims.source: Results, Validation of recording traces, paragraph 3; Figure 2r
claims.quote: In both the simulated and real traces, power decreased with increasing frequency in the frequency band of spiking activity (0.3 - 6 KHz) and followed a power law in all layers
claims.criterion: Welch PSD at 1 Hz resolution with a Hann window (Methods, Spectral composition), of the preprocessed traces, first 10 minutes (code, src/pipes/validation/psd/multiprocess.py), normalised by total power, median over the sites of each layer; a linear regression of log power on log frequency in 300 to 6000 Hz per site (Methods; code eval_freq_scaling). The paper gives no goodness-of-fit rule; the criterion reads "followed a power law" as a negative slope and R2 of at least 0.9 of the log-log fit for the median PSD of every layer of every experiment. Reproduced when this holds for all; the slopes and R2 are reported.

claims.statement: In the biophysical models the power in the spike frequency band and the power-law scaling slope in the spiking band increased with cortical depth, as in vivo; the dense probe model had weaker power and slope than in vivo but within the in vivo range.
claims.source: Results, Validation of recording traces, paragraph 3; Figure 2s-v
claims.quote: The biophysical models’ median power in the frequency band of a spike waveform and the scaling slope in the spiking band also increased with cortical depth as in vivo (2s-v, all p < 0.001, Kruskall Wallis) ... Nonetheless the dense probe’s AP power and frequency scaling remained within in vivo range
claims.criterion: AP power per site is the PSD power in 0.3 to 2 kHz (Results, paragraph 3); the code's revised notebook uses the median PSD in 0.3 to 1 kHz (fig2_R_AP_power_npx_revised), shown as a variant. Both the median PSD value in the band and the summed power in the band are read, since the text says "median power" and "power". The slope alpha is from the 0.3 to 6 kHz fit of fig2r-power-law-spiking-band. For each model (NS, E, DS), a Kruskal-Wallis test across layers. Reproduced when both measures (AP power and alpha) have p < 0.001 in every model, with layer medians rising from layer 1 to 6 with at most one inversion between neighbours; for AP power in 0.3 to 2 kHz the median and summed readings are both run and the outcome is the one both give (methods_underspecified when they differ); the 0.3 to 1 kHz band is a variant, not used for the outcome. Partially reproduced when this holds for one measure or some models. Whether the DS values lie within the range of H's site values is reported.

claims.statement: The Horvath traces are dominated by slow (0.5 to 1.5 Hz) and delta (1 to 4 Hz) waves of slow-wave sleep, which the Marques-Smith traces and the biophysical models lack.
claims.source: Results, Validation of recording traces, paragraph 4; Supplementary figure "Validation of raw simulated traces"
claims.quote: In Horvath’s data but not in Marques-Smith’s, the traces were dominated by high-amplitude slow (0.5 - 1.5Hz) and δ waves (1 - 4Hz) characteristic of slow-wave sleep ... The biophysical models did not replicate these oscillations
claims.criterion: Raw traces (mean subtracted), Welch PSD on the first 10 minutes divided by total power, averaged over sites (legend of the supplementary figure). The paper gives no threshold; the criterion reads "dominated" as the fraction of the 0.5 to 4 Hz power in the 0.5 to 300 Hz power being larger in H than in M and in every model (NS, E, DS) by a factor of 2 or more. Reproduced when this holds.

claims.statement: The peak-to-peak amplitude of a model cell's spikes drops by more than half within 75 um of the soma, and the trace is strongly distorted by noise beyond 200 um.
claims.source: Results, Validation of single unit spike waveforms, paragraph 1; Figure 3d, e
claims.quote: The peak-to-peak amplitude of the spikes rapidly decayed between nearby electrodes, dropping by more than half within 75 µm ( Fig. 3e ), therefore making the summed extracellular potentials difficult to isolate at 75 µm from the somata. The extracellular traces was strongly distorted by noise beyond 200 µm
claims.criterion: The figure uses the most active layer 5 pyramidal cell, recorded isolated and in the full circuit at 128 electrode positions on a grid (Figure 3d, e legend); the code writes these traces to NWB as biophy_isolated_reyes and biophy_summed_reyes (cell 3754013, 40 s). Spike-triggered average on the isolated trace at each electrode, peak-to-peak amplitude against distance to the soma. Reproduced when the amplitude at every electrode 75 um or more from the soma is below half the amplitude at the nearest electrode. For the 200 um part the paper gives no measure; the spike-triggered average on the summed trace is reported against the trace's MAD at each distance, and that part holds when the peak-to-peak amplitude is below 5 MAD beyond 200 um (a choice made here, as the paper gives none; reported, not used for the outcome). Not testable when the dataset lacks these traces.

claims.statement: Spikes sorted with Kilosort3 from the spontaneous Neuropixels simulation qualitatively match the five temporal profiles reported in humans and cats.
claims.source: Results, Validation of single unit spike waveforms, paragraph 1; Figure 3a-c
claims.quote: The simulated temporal waveforms qualitatively matched the five shapes reported in cats [ 46 ] and humans [ 9 ]
claims.criterion: A qualitative comparison with panels copied from other papers, with no stated measure. The paper's own measure of profile diversity is the WaveMap clustering of fig3fg-wavemap-six-profiles, on which this claim depends; this claim is judged with that one and otherwise reported as not testable by a fixed rule.

claims.statement: WaveMap clustering of multi-electrode spike waveforms identifies six distinct profiles in the simulation, as in the Marques-Smith data.
claims.source: Results, Validation of single unit spike waveforms, paragraph 2; Figure 3f, g
claims.quote: Consistent with the experimental data, the algorithm identified six distinct profiles from the simulations
claims.criterion: Tolerance 0 because a cluster count is an integer and 10% of 6 is below one. Kilosort3 single units of NS and M (Results, paragraph 1 of the section). Spike-triggered averages; the six nearest sites with the largest average amplitude, ordered by the largest of first peak, trough or second peak; aligned at the trough over 12 ms, reduced to 6 ms; amplitudes scaled to 0 to 1; UMAP (umap-learn 0.5.3) to two dimensions; Louvain clustering (python-louvain 0.16) (Methods, WaveMap). The legend shows three electrodes. The paper does not give UMAP's n_neighbors or the Louvain resolution; the code uses n_neighbors 15 and picks the resolution that maximises modularity over 0.1 to 6.9 in steps of 0.1 (fig3_H_wavemap_shapes), which is followed; its notebook markdown says resolution 1.5, a variant. Which simulation (NS, E or both pooled) is meant is open; the legend of Fig. 3c names the spontaneous regime, so NS is the main reading and E and pooled are variants. Reproduced when NS and M each give six clusters with six electrodes (Methods) and the code's resolution choice, which decide; the 1.5 resolution and the three electrodes of the legend (a display choice) are variants, reported and not used for the outcome. The code's saved outputs printed 7 to 10 clusters for NS and 7 for M.

claims.statement: The firing rates of single units sorted by Kilosort4 from the spontaneous and evoked simulations are distributed log-normally across layers, as in Marques-Smith's data.
claims.source: Results, Validation of firing rates, paragraph 2; Figure 4a
claims.quote: Like Marques-Smith’s sorted unit firing rates, the firing rates from the spontaneous (red dots, Fig. 4a ) and evoked (orange dots) biophysical simulations were distributed log-normally across layers
claims.criterion: Kilosort4 single units, first 10 minutes, firing rate as spike count over 600 s, by layer (code fig4_A_B_C_firing_rate_ks4). The paper fits lognormal distributions and judges the match qualitatively. The criterion reads "log-normal" as a Shapiro-Wilk test of log10 rates not rejecting normality at p < 0.05 in layers 5 and 6 (the layers with enough units, Results, paragraph 1) for NS, E and M. Reproduced when this holds in all; partially reproduced when it holds for M and one simulation. Which evoked simulation is open (the code's "npx_evoked" config, 10 minutes); both the 10-minute 40 kHz recording and the first 10 minutes of the 1-hour recording are run.

claims.statement: Single-unit yields are low in superficial layers and high in layers 5 and 6; in vivo the yields in these layers are at least 20 times that of layer 4 and no unit is found in layers 1 and 2/3, a trend also seen in the simulated data.
claims.source: Results, Validation of firing rates, paragraph 1; Figure 4a (unit counts)
claims.quote: In vivo , the yields in these layers were at least 20 times that in layer 4, and no units were found in layers 1 and 2/3, a trend also reflected in the simulated data
claims.criterion: Kilosort4 single units of the first 10 minutes, by layer. Reproduced when, for M, each of layers 5 and 6 has at least 20 times the count of layer 4 and layers 1 and 2/3 have none, and for NS and E the counts of layers 5 and 6 each exceed those of layers 1, 2/3 and 4. "At least 20 times" can be read per layer or for layers 5 and 6 pooled; both are shown, and the claim holds under either. With 0 units in layer 4 the ratio is infinite and holds.

claims.statement: The median firing rate of sorted single units over layers 5 and 6 is 2.8 spikes/s in Marques-Smith's data, 1.2 in the spontaneous and 0.7 in the evoked simulations, and 5 in Buccino's synthetic simulation.
claims.source: Results, Validation of firing rates, paragraph 2; Figure 4b
claims.quote: The overall median firing rate averaged over layer 5 and 6 differed but only by a small margin (Marques-Smith: 2.8 ± 1% (95% CI) spikes/secs, spontaneous biophysical simulation: 1.2 ± 0.2%, evoked simulation: 0.7 ± 0.1% and Buccino’s full synthetic simulation: 5 ± 0.4% (95% CI))
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's 95% CI half-widths, printed with a stray "%" that the code shows to be spikes/s (fig4_A_B_C_firing_rate_ks4, cell 13 prints 2.85 +- 1.14, 1.15 +- 0.21, 0.655 +- 0.083, 4.92 +- 0.42 Hz). Kilosort4 single units, first 10 minutes. "Median averaged over layer 5 and 6" is read two ways - (a) the median of the pooled layer 5 and 6 rates, as the code does; (b) the mean of the layer 5 median and the layer 6 median. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance under one reading. Which evoked simulation is open, as in fig4a-lognormal-firing-rates; both are run.

claims.statement: Compared with in vivo, the biophysical simulations have lower median firing rates and narrower firing rate distributions across layers, while the synthetic model has a lower variance in layer 5 but a higher median.
claims.source: Results, Validation of firing rates, paragraph 2; Figure 4b, c
claims.quote: Specifically, the biophysical simulations had lower median firing rates ( Fig. 4b , p < 0.001, Mann-Whitney) and distributions were narrower ( c, p < 0.001) than in vivo across layers. For reference, the synthetic model distribution also had a lower variance in layer 5 (all p < 0.01) but it displayed higher median firing rate ( p < 0.01)
claims.criterion: Kilosort4 single units, first 10 minutes, log10 firing rates per layer (Methods, Firing rate). Medians - two-sided Mann-Whitney U test of each simulation's log10 rates against M's, per layer. Variances - 100 bootstrap resamples (with replacement) of each group's log10 rates, the variance of each, and a Mann-Whitney U test of the 100 variances against M's (Methods, Firing rate; code bootstrap_varlogfr). Layers with units in M (5 and 6, and 4 if any). Reproduced when NS and E are lower than M with p < 0.001 in each tested layer for both medians and variances, and S in layer 5 has a lower variance and a higher median than M at p < 0.01; partially reproduced when the medians or the variances part holds alone.

claims.statement: With other sorters, Kilosort3 gives log-normal firing rate distributions that match in vivo, older sorters give bimodal distributions, and across regimes the simulated medians and variances tend to be lower than in vivo.
claims.source: Results, Validation of firing rates, paragraph 3; Supplementary figure "Validation of firing rate distributions"
claims.quote: While newer sorters like Kilosort3 produced log-normal distributions ( Supplementary Fig. 4a ) that better matched in vivo data (b, p > 0.15), older sorters often generated bimodal distributions ... firing rate medians (b, p < 0.05) and variances ( c, p < 0.01) in simulations tended to be reduced
claims.criterion: As fig4bc-lower-median-narrower-distribution, for Kilosort, 2, 2.5 and 3 (all units for Kilosort, single units for the others), per layer. The Kilosort3 part is a claim of absence, judged on the paper's test - reproduced when no layer's Mann-Whitney U test of Kilosort3 against M has p <= 0.15 (the code's notebooks supp_fig4_ABC_ks3 run the same per-layer test). Which quantity the p > 0.15 refers to is open - the Results call panel b the medians (and c the variances), while the supplementary legend calls panel a the rate statistics and panel b the variances; both medians and bootstrapped variances are run, and the outcome is the one both give. "Bimodal" has no stated test; reported with Hartigan's dip test as a description, not for the outcome. The "tended to be reduced" part holds when, over the sorter, layer and simulation comparisons, a majority have lower medians (p < 0.05) and lower variances (p < 0.01). Reproduced when both parts hold; partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: For the spontaneous Neuropixels simulation sorted by Kilosort4, on average 41% of sorted units are single units, and the proportion of single units differs between experiments.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 2; Figure 5a
claims.quote: We found that for spontaneous activity recorded with Neuropixels and sorted by Kilosort4, on average 41% of sorted units were ‘single-units’. This proportion differed between experiments
claims.criterion: Kilosort4, first 10 minutes, cortical units; fraction = single units / all units. The paper does not say which 5 experiments enter the test (df 4) or how it is formed, and the code holds no such test. The code forms its other tests in this panel as a goodness-of-fit chi-square of the per-experiment single-unit percentages against equal values (scipy chisquare, fig5_A_yield); its experiments in that order are M, NS, NS-2X, E and S. Readings, (a) that goodness-of-fit test on M, NS, NS-2X, E and S; (b) a chi-square contingency test of single against multi-unit counts in the same five; (c) as (b) on M, H, NS, E and DS. "On average 41%" is read three ways - (i) the fraction for NS (the sentence names it); (ii) the mean of NS and NS-2X; (iii) the mean of the M, NS and NS-2X fractions. The paper's own counts favour (iii) - the unit totals it prints (M 200, NS 504, H 358, DS 562, Results paragraph 4, checked against its N values) and N = 1,212 for M, NS and NS-2X give NS-2X 508 units, so NS is 182 / 504 = 36%, NS-2X 193 / 508 = 38% and M 96 / 200 = 48%, whose mean is 40.7%; reading (iii) also reproduces the paper's chi2 = 2.0 of fig5a-single-unit-counts. Reproduced when the fraction is within tolerance and the test has p < 0.001 under one reading.

claims.statement: The simulations give at least twice as many single units as in vivo (182 and 193 against 96 for Neuropixels, 206 against 93 for the dense probe), yet the fractions of single units are similar.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 2; Figure 5a
claims.quote: At least twice more ‘single-units’ were detected from the simulations than in vivo , with the largest difference being 206 vs. 93 for the dense probe ( Fig. 5a , 182 and 193 vs. 96 for Neuropixels). Yet the fractions of ‘single-units’ were similar
claims.criterion: Kilosort4, first 10 minutes, cortical single units. The text does not name the two Neuropixels simulations; the code's test with N = 1,212 is on M, NS and NS-2X, and 193 / 182 is the 6% gain of fig5a-downsampling-small-gain, so 182 is NS and 193 NS-2X (code, fig5_A_yield, cells 10 and 19). NS-2X is NS with every second sample kept and the sampling rate left at 40 kHz (Methods, Unit isolation ratio). The fractions are a claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, which the code gives as a goodness-of-fit chi-square of the single-unit percentages against equal values (scipy chisquare); a contingency chi-square of single against multi-unit counts is shown as a variant. Reproduced when the counts are within tolerance and both tests have p >= 0.05; not reproduced when either has p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Most units sorted from Buccino's synthetic traces are single units, four times more than in vivo.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 2; Figure 5a
claims.quote: In contrast with the in vivo yield, the majority of units sorted from the synthetic traces were ‘single-units’, four times more than in vivo
claims.criterion: In "S 377 vs. 163", 163 is S's multi-unit count - N = 740 is S's 540 units (377 + 163) plus M's 200 units (96 single, 104 multi, Results paragraphs 2 and 4), and the goodness-of-fit chi-square of the single-unit percentages (S 69.8%, M 48.0%) against equal values gives 4.0, the printed value. "Four times more than in vivo" is S's 377 single units against M's 96 (3.9). Kilosort4, first 10 minutes. Reproduced when the two S counts are within tolerance, S has more than half single units, S's single units are 3.6 to 4.4 times M's (four widened by 10%), and the goodness-of-fit chi-square of the single-unit percentages of M and S (code fig5_A_yield, cell 14) has p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The model predicts that in a stimulus-evoked regime the number of sorted units increases at least threefold and the single-unit yield doubles, while the ratio shifts toward multi-units.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 3; Figure 5a
claims.quote: The model predicts that the number of sorted units should increase at least three times in a stimulus-evoked regime. Although the ratio should strongly shift to ‘multi-units’, a key prediction is that the single-unit yield should double
claims.criterion: Kilosort4, first 10 minutes, cortical units, E against NS. Reproduced when E has at least 3 times NS's total units, a lower single-unit fraction, and between 1.8 and 2.2 times NS's single units (2 widened by 10%). Which evoked recording is open (the 10-minute 40 kHz or the first 10 minutes of the 1-hour 20 kHz); the code uses the 10-minute sortings of its "npx_evoked" config; both are run, and the claim holds under either.

claims.statement: In vivo, multi-units were twice as frequent with the dense probe as with Neuropixels, which the model did not reproduce; despite its higher-resolution sampling the dense probe did not give a higher single-unit yield than Neuropixels.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 4; Figure 5a
claims.quote: These were mostly ‘multi-units’, which were twice more frequent for the dense probe in vivo (M:104, H:265, χ 2 (1, N = 558) = 6.6, p = 0.01). The model did not reproduce this effect (NS:182, DS:206, χ 2 (1, N = 1066) = 0.004, p = 0.9)
claims.criterion: Kilosort4, first 10 minutes, cortical units, dense probe counts summed over the three depths. The unit totals are M 200, H 358, NS 504 and DS 562 ("358 vs 200 units and 562 vs. 504 units respectively", which the N values 558 = 200 + 358 and 1066 = 504 + 562 confirm). The test, as in the code (fig5_A_yield, cells 21 and 22), is a goodness-of-fit chi-square of the two experiments' single-unit percentages against equal values; a contingency chi-square of single against multi-unit counts is a variant. Reproduced when M against H has p < 0.05 with H's multi-unit share higher, and NS against DS has p >= 0.05 (absence, on the same test).

claims.statement: Down-sampling the simulated traces by two to shorten spikes improves the Kilosort4 single unit yield only marginally, by 6%.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 5; Figure 5a (NS-2X)
claims.quote: We applied this approach but observed only a marginal 6% improvement in single-unit yield
claims.criterion: NS-2X as in fig5a-single-unit-counts. Gain = NS-2X single units / NS single units - 1. The 10% default tolerance is 0.006, below one unit's change at these counts (1 / 182 = 0.0055); reproduced when the gain is within 0.054 to 0.066, or when it is positive and below 0.10 as a marginal gain (a reading of "marginal"); both are reported, and the first decides.

claims.statement: Raw single-unit yields per site are an order of magnitude lower than the theoretical yields (active neurons within 50 um per site, NS 6.9, NE 8.4, S 0.65, DS 5.3) and do not differ significantly between probes or sorters.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 6; Figure 5b legend
claims.quote: For the biophysical models, the raw single-unit yields were an order of magnitude lower than the theoretical yields and were not significantly different between probes or spike sorters (5b)
claims.criterion: Theoretical yield - ground truth neurons within 50 um with at least one spike, counted per layer of their soma, divided by the number of sites in that layer, median over layers (legend; code get_gt_yield_per_site); S is 250 / 384. Sorted yield - single units per layer divided by the sites in that layer, averaged over layers (legend "median yield per electrode, averaged across layers"; the code plots the mean over layers with seaborn's bootstrap 95% CI), for Kilosort4 and the other sorters (Supplementary figure "Single-unit yield and quality ... all tested spike sorters"). "An order of magnitude lower" is read two ways - (a) theoretical / sorted of 10 or more; (b) of 10^0.5 (3.2) or more, the nearest power of ten being 10. Neither the paper nor the code names a test for "not significantly different"; it is reported, with the yields and their CIs, and not used for the outcome. Reproduced when the theoretical yields are within tolerance and the biophysical models' Kilosort4 yields are lower by an order of magnitude under one reading. Partially reproduced when only one of the two parts holds.

claims.statement: In Buccino's synthetic model, Kilosort4 produces more single units than there are modelled neurons, which indicates redundant units.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 6; Figure 5b (blue)
claims.quote: In Buccino’s full synthetic model, Kilosort4 produced more ‘single-units’ than the number of modeled neurons, indicating the production of redundant units
claims.criterion: Kilosort4 single units on the first 10 minutes of S. Reproduced when their number exceeds 250.

claims.statement: Most single units isolated by Kilosort4 are less than 80% accurate, contain spikes of several true neurons (merged) and miss at least 20% of their matched neuron's spikes; Kilosort4 produces no false positives.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 7; Figure 5c, d
claims.quote: The majority of the isolated ‘single-units’ were less than 80% accurate and degraded across layers ( Fig. 5d , white area) and spike sorters ( Supplementary Fig. 5b ). They contained spikes from multiple true units (’merged unit’) and missed at least 20% of the matched true units spikes ( Fig. 5c , green). Kilosort4 did not produce false positives
claims.criterion: Kilosort4 single units of NS and E (first 10 minutes), each given its best agreement score with any ground truth neuron and its quality tags (opening comment). Reproduced when, in each simulation, more than half of the single units have a best score below 0.8, more than half are tagged merged, and none is a false positive; partially reproduced when the first part holds and one other fails. The other sorters (Supplementary figure, panel b) are reported. Which evoked recording is open; both are run.

claims.statement: A logistic regression on unit quality metrics classifies good against degraded Kilosort4 single units with 89% and 93% precision and 61% and 55% recall in the spontaneous and evoked simulations.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 8; Figure 5e, f
claims.quote: The model achieved 89% ± 2% (95% CI) and 93% ± 2% precision and 61% ± 3% and 55% ± 2% recall in the spontaneous ( Fig. 5e ) and evoked simulations (f) respectively
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's 95% CI half-widths. Units - Kilosort4 single units with all metrics computable (182 of 184 in NS). Label - good when the best agreement score is 0.8 or more (Methods, Logistic regression). Features - the quality metrics of ref. 16 named by the code (src/nodes/models/Flc), amplitude_cutoff, firing_range, firing_rate, isi_violations_ratio, rp_contamination, rp_violations, sd_ratio, snr, silhouette and mad_ratio (presence_ratio dropped as constant), z-scored. Model - Binomial GLM with logit link (statsmodels). The Figure 5 legend calls it lasso-regularized but gives no penalty; the Methods (Logistic regression model) describe a GLM with no penalty and the code fits it unpenalised, which is followed. A unit is predicted good when its probability is 0.8 or more (code; the paper is silent). Splits are open - (a) 80% train and 20% test (Methods), (b) 75% and 25% (legend "25% test units", code split_ratio 0.75); 100 random splits each. The value is the median over splits; the CI is 1.96 SD / sqrt(100) (code get_metrics_stats). The split is a method detail on which the Methods and the legend disagree, so both are run and the outcome is the one both give (methods_underspecified when they differ). Which evoked recording is meant is a reading of the reported number; both are run and either may match. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance under both splits.

claims.statement: The new mad_ratio metric has the largest correlation with unit sorting accuracy (R = -0.46), and the firing rate statistics and the spike trough variability metrics (mad_ratio, sd_ratio) are the key significant predictors of a good unit.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 8; Figure 5g
claims.quote: We also introduced a new metric, which we called the “mad_ratio” (see Methods), which better reflected contamination by multiple units, displaying the largest correlation with unit sorting accuracy ( R = − 0.46). The model offered the additional insight that two key predictive features of a good unit are its firing rate statistics ( Fig. 5g , including firing rate and range, p < 0.001) and the variability of its spike troughs compared to background noise variability (mad_ratio and sd_ratio, p < 0.001)
claims.criterion: NS Kilosort4 single units as in fig5ef-curation-precision-recall. The mad_ratio is not defined in this text's Methods; the code defines it as the mean absolute deviation of the unit's negative-peak spike amplitudes over that of all waveform samples on its extremum channel (get_mad_ratio). The code's R is the Pearson correlation of mad_ratio with the binary good label (fig5_G_curation_metrics_npx_spont, cell 13); the text says "accuracy", so the Pearson correlation with the continuous best agreement score is a second reading. Weights - the unpenalised GLM on all units, z-scored metrics, Wald p-values. Reproduced when R is within tolerance and is the largest in magnitude among the metrics under one reading, and the weights of firing_rate, firing_range, mad_ratio and sd_ratio have p < 0.001.

claims.statement: A CEBRA embedding of full waveforms with a k-nearest neighbour classifier gives better recall (82% and 90%) but lower precision (61% and 55%) than the logistic regression in the spontaneous and evoked regimes.
claims.source: Results, Model predicts low yield, quality and biases, paragraph 9; Supplementary figure "Single-unit yield and quality ...", panels c, d
claims.quote: The model achieved better recall (82%, ± 3% and 90% ± 2% for the spontaneous ( Supplementary Fig. 5c ) and evoked (d) regimes respectively) but lower precision (61% ± 3% and 55% ± 3%) than the logistic regression
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's CI half-widths. Settings from the Methods (cebraspike model) and the code (src/nodes/models/CebraSpike) - Kilosort4 units with more than 25 spikes; the first 25 spike waveforms, +-3 ms on the extremum channel, with the quality metrics appended; good = best score 0.8 or more, poor = merged and partial without good (code); CEBRA offset10-model, cosine distance, 40 iterations, learning rate 0.001, output dimension 3, temperature auto, seed 0; KNN decoder with 20 neighbours, cosine; stratified 80 / 20 splits, 100 seeds; median and 1.96 SD / sqrt(100). The code appends the metrics in sorted unit order while the waveforms keep their own order; a version with the rows aligned is shown as a variant. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance, under the code's version or the aligned one.

claims.statement: On Buccino's synthetic simulation most spike sorters detect most neurons, with accuracies ranging from 50% for herdingspikes to 99% for Kilosort2.
claims.source: Results, Biological factors of sorting failures, paragraph 2; Figure 6a
claims.quote: As previously reported, for the synthetic simulation [ 16 ] most spike sorters detected most neurons with accuracies ranging from 50% for herdingspikes to 99% for Kilosort2
claims.criterion: The ground truth of S is its 250 units. Accuracy per neuron and the 0.8 rule as in the opening comment; the fraction of neurons with accuracy of 0.8 or more per sorter (Figure 6a legend). Which sorted units enter the best match - the Methods (Sorting accuracy) say only "its best-matching sorted unit", and the code settles it - single units for Kilosort 2 to 4 and all units for Kilosort and herdingspikes (code get_accuracy), which decides; all units for every sorter is shown as a variant. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance and a majority of the six sorters have a fraction above 0.5.

claims.statement: For the biophysical models the sorters well-sort similarly low proportions of ground truth neurons, on average 15% of the neurons within 50 um of the electrodes.
claims.source: Results, Biological factors of sorting failures, paragraph 2; Figure 6a, b
claims.quote: However, the sorters produced similarly low proportions of well-sorted ground truth neurons for the biophysical models ( Fig. 6a ), on average 15% of the neurons within 50 µm of the electrodes across the simulations
claims.criterion: Figure 6 legend - the 10-minute evoked simulation at 40 kHz and NS; accuracy of 0.8 or more. Per sorter, the well-sorted neurons summed over the ground truths divided by the neurons within 50 um summed (Figure 6b legend). N = 3,190 is 250 + 1,388 + 1,552, so the code sums S, NS and E (fig6_A_B_sorting_accuracy, cell 5); the "biophysical" sum over NS and E alone is a second reading. Best-match units as in fig6a-synthetic-accuracy-range (the code's choice decides). The test, as in the code (cell 12), is a goodness-of-fit chi-square of the six per-sorter percentages against equal values; a contingency chi-square of well-sorted against other neurons per sorter is a variant. Reproduced when the mean over sorters is within tolerance under one reading and the chi-square has p >= 0.05 (the paper's "similarly", on its test).

claims.statement: The dense probe gives five times fewer neurons sorted with above 80% accuracy than the Neuropixels probe, on average 3% against 15% across sorters.
claims.source: Results, Biological factors of sorting failures, paragraph 3; Figure 6a, b
claims.quote: We found that the dense probe produced five times fewer neurons sorted with above 80% accuracy across spike sorters than the Neuropixels probe (on average 3% vs. 15%)
claims.criterion: DS depths pooled (Figure 6b legend), well-sorted neurons divided by ground truth neurons within 50 um. The 10% default tolerance on 3% is below the resolution of a sum over a few hundred neurons per sorter; reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading of fig6ab-biophysical-accuracy-15-percent, or when the Neuropixels value is within tolerance and the ratio of Neuropixels to dense is within 4.5 to 5.5 (five widened by 10%).

claims.statement: A fractional regression of Kilosort4 sorting accuracy on 21 neuron features fits the data (R2 = 0.42 spontaneous, 0.34 evoked) and finds seven significant features in both regimes; accuracy rises with firing rate and spike spatial extent, is higher for pyramidal cells and in layer 5, and falls with distance to the nearest electrode.
claims.source: Results, Biological factors of sorting failures, paragraph 4; Figure 6c-f
claims.quote: The model provided a good fit to the data ( Fig. 6 , R 2 = 0.42 and R 2 = 0.34 in the spontaneous (c) and evoked (d) regimes respectively) and identified seven significantly predictive features out of 21 in both regimes. Accuracy improved as neuronal firing rates increased and spike spatial extent (or ‘footprint’ [ 6 ]) expanded. It was also higher for pyramidal cells compared to interneurons and in layer 5 compared to other cortical layers. Sorting accuracy decreased when neuron’s distance to the nearest electrode increased
claims.criterion: Tolerance 0 on the feature count because it is an integer and 10% of 7 is below one. Neurons - ground truth neurons within 50 um; NS and the 1-hour evoked simulation at 20 kHz (Figure 6 legend), Kilosort4 on the first 10 minutes (code). Target - accuracy as the best agreement score with any Kilosort4 unit (code, all units). Features - the 21 of the code (fig6_C_E_fracreg_NS_ks4, cell 4) - firing_rate, synapse_class, etypes bAC, bNAC, bSTUT, cACint, cADpyr, cNAC, cSTUT, dNAC, dSTUT, layers 1, 2/3, 4, 5 and 6, distance to the nearest site, snr, spatial_extent, exc_mini_frequency and dynamics_holding_current, z-scored. Model - Binomial GLM, logit link, statsmodels fit_regularized elastic_net with L1_wt 1, maxiter 100, cnvrg_tol 1e-10 (Methods). The lasso penalty strength is not given anywhere; the code passes none, so statsmodels' alpha 0 applies, which is followed. With alpha 0 no weight is set to zero, which does not match the Methods' account of the lasso selecting features; this is recorded as a deviation, and a penalised fit cannot be run from the paper. R2 - McFadden's pseudo-R2 on test sets of 100 random 75 / 25 splits, median (code); in-sample R2 is a variant. Significance - Wald p < 0.05 of the weights of a one-step unpenalised refit on all neurons (code). Reproduced when both R2 are within tolerance, each regime has seven significant features, and the signs are positive for firing rate, spatial extent, synapse class (excitatory) and layer 5 and negative for distance in both regimes. Partially reproduced when the signs hold but R2 or the counts do not.

claims.statement: Because sorting favours highly active units, mean firing rates in most layers are overestimated three to four times by sorted spike trains compared with the ground truth.
claims.source: Results, Biological factors of sorting failures, paragraph 4; Supplementary figure "Ground truth firing rate distribution"
claims.quote: Notably, the bias for high firing units led to mean firing rates in most layers being overestimated by a factor of three to four from sorted spike trains compared to the ground truth
claims.criterion: A reported range of 3 to 4 widened by 10% of each bound gives 2.7 to 4.4 (written as 3.5 +- 0.9 above). NS; true rates of all ground truth neurons within 50 um over the first 600 s, sorted rates of Kilosort4 single units of the first 10 minutes, per layer (legend; code supp_fig7_ABCDE_true_firing_rates_revised, which also bootstraps 100 draws of 100 values). Ratio of the means per layer, assigned by soma layer for true and by site layer for sorted. Reproduced when the ratio lies in 2.7 to 4.4 in a majority of the layers that have sorted units.

claims.statement: Pyramidal neurons, 91% of the ground truth, are under-represented after sorting by about a factor of two in every layer except layer 5, where they are over-represented by about two; most interneurons are represented in proportion, but rare interneuron types are over-represented by 2.9 to 8.1 by some sorters, mainly Kilosort 1 to 2.5.
claims.source: Results, Biological factors of sorting failures, paragraph 5; Figure 6g, h
claims.quote: Excitatory pyramidal neurons, which made up 91% of the ground truth population ( Fig. 6g ), were consistently underrepresented across all layers by approximately a factor of 2, except in layer 5, where they were over-represented by the same factor ( Fig. 6h , ratios in blue; Fisher’s exact test, two-tailed, p < 0.05). In contrast, most interneurons were proportionally represented relative to the ground truth, except for rare interneuron types, which were over-represented by factors ranging from 2.9 to 8.1 by some spike sorters, particularly Kilosort (1 to 2.5)
claims.criterion: The 1-hour evoked simulation at 20 kHz (Figure 6 legend). Types are synapse class, layer and electrical type. Ground truth - all neurons within 50 um. Sorted - single units of Kilosort 2 to 4, all units of Kilosort and herdingspikes, each given the synapse class and electrical type of its best-matching neuron (Results). Its layer is the matched neuron's layer, as the Results and the Figure 6h legend say ("assigned the biophysical features of its best ground truth match"), which decides; the code's site layer (fig6_G_H_selection_bias, get_feature_data_for) disagrees with them and is a variant. Which sorting duration is open; the code's table is named "1h" but its generator sorts 600 s; both are run where possible, and the outcome is the one both give (methods_underspecified when they differ). Ratio - share of a type among sorted units / its share in the ground truth. Test - per type and sorter, two-sided Fisher's exact test on [[ground truth of the type, sorted of the type], [ground truth others, sorted others]] (code cell 18), p < 0.05, uncorrected. Reproduced when, for a majority of sorters, the excitatory types of layer 5 have ratios of 1.5 or more and those of the other layers ratios of 0.67 or less, with p < 0.05 for those that differ; and the largest ratio of an interneuron type is within 2.6 to 8.9 for at least one of Kilosort, 2 or 2.5. Partially reproduced when only the excitatory part holds.

claims.statement: The ground truth neural manifold has a ring-like geometry tracking stimulus direction; spike sorting distorts it for all sorters, but the recent sorters (Kilosort2 to 4) still preserve the stimulus mapping.
claims.source: Results, Spike sorting degrades stimulus representation, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 7a
claims.quote: The ground truth neural manifold exhibited a ring-like geometry ( Fig. 7a ), which continuously reflected changes in the stimulus direction across trials. Spike sorting distorted the manifold’s geometry for all spike sorters, but the most recent sorters still preserved stimulus mapping (from Kilosort2 to 4)
claims.criterion: A visual finding with no stated measure. Responses are spike counts per unit in each 200 ms stimulus presentation, 8 directions 45 degrees apart, 50 trials each, 1-hour evoked simulation (Results; Figure 7 legend; code get_evoked_responses), reduced to 3 dimensions by PCA. The criterion reads "ring-like, continuously reflecting direction" as the trial-averaged centroids of the 8 directions, in the plane of the first two PCs, having angular order equal to the direction order (cyclic, either sense), and "preserved mapping" as the same for a sorter's population. Reproduced when the ground truth and Kilosort2, 2.5, 3 and 4 keep the cyclic order.

claims.statement: Spike sorting significantly reduces the information capacity of the population, on average by 50% across sorters, from 25% above the lower bound.
claims.source: Results, Spike sorting degrades stimulus representation, paragraph 3; Figure 7b
claims.quote: Distortions in manifold geometry were associated with significant reductions in information capacity, averaging 50% decrease across spike sorters, from 25% above the lower bound ( Fig. 7b , t(199) ranging from -68 to -24, all p < 0.001, t-test)
claims.criterion: Method (Methods, Manifold information geometry; Figure 7 legend; code igeom.py) - 1-hour evoked simulation, 8 directions, 50 trials each, spike counts in each 200 ms presentation; sorted populations are single units of Kilosort 2 to 4 and all units of Kilosort and herdingspikes; neural_manifolds_replicaMFT, kappa 0, n_t 200; each population projected to 200 dimensions (the code uses a Gaussian random projection with unit-norm rows, as in ref. 52); capacity divided by that of the same data with shuffled direction labels. Bootstraps - 200 (legend, code) or 1000 (Methods); the code varies only the projection and shuffle seeds, which is followed, with 200; 1000 is a variant. Test - the code's two-sample t-test (scipy ttest_ind) of the sorter's against the ground truth's values; a one-sample t-test against the ground truth mean (matching the printed df 199) is a variant. "50% decrease from 25% above the lower bound" is read two ways - (a) normalised capacity falls by half of its ground truth value; (b) the excess above the lower bound falls by half (from 0.25 to about 0.125). Reproduced when the ground truth ratio is within tolerance, every sorter is lower with p < 0.001, and the mean decrease is within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Randomly under-sampling ground truth neurons to the sorters' yields does not change information capacity, but also matching the neuron type distribution of the sorted units reduces it by an average 21% across sorters.
claims.source: Results, Spike sorting degrades stimulus representation, paragraph 4; Figure 7d-f
claims.quote: Under-sampling ground truth neurons to match sorting yields neither disrupted the manifold’s structure nor its information capacity (example for Kilosort4, Fig. 7d , and all sorters in f, red boxes vs. red line, t(199) ranging from -0.71 to -0.02, all p > 0.47, t-test). However, also matching neuron type distribution to that of sorted units visibly degraded the manifold structure and its information capacity by an averaged 21% across sorters
claims.criterion: Capacity as in fig7b-sorting-halves-capacity. Random sample - as many ground truth neurons as the sorter's sorted units, without replacement, a new draw per bootstrap (code get_igeom_stats_for_gt_and_random_sampling). Type-matched sample - for each type (layer, synapse class, electrical type), as many ground truth neurons of that type as the sorter has sorted units of it, without replacement unless too few (code sample_gt_based_on_sorting_distribution). The undersampling part is a claim of absence judged on the paper's t-test (both forms of fig7b-sorting-halves-capacity shown; the code's two-sample test decides) - holds when no sorter's random sample differs from the ground truth at p < 0.05. Type-matched part - every sorter lower at p < 0.001 and the mean decrease within tolerance under one of the two readings of a decrease in fig7b-sorting-halves-capacity. Reproduced when both parts hold; partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: Good and degraded sorted units differ in type distribution; good units have on average 37% lower capacity than the ground truth, and degraded units, matched to the good units' type distribution, a further 12% lower for most sorters.
claims.source: Results, Spike sorting degrades stimulus representation, paragraph 5; Figure 7g
claims.quote: Unit type distributions differed significantly between biased and good units across spike sorters ( p < 0.001, Fisher exact test with Monte Carlo simulations) ... On average, the information capacity of good units was 37% lower than the ground truth across spike sorters ( Fig. 7g , red boxes vs. red line, t(199) ranging from -0.31 to -15, all p < 0.001, t-test). Degraded units exhibited even lower capacity, averaging a 12% decrease from good units’ capacity across most sorters (Kilosort4, 2.5, 1, and herdingspikes)
claims.criterion: Capacity as in fig7b-sorting-halves-capacity. Good units are tagged good; degraded units are merged or partial and not good (code - "mixed good + overmerger + oversplitter" against "mixed overmerger + oversplitter"). Degraded units resampled per type to the good units' type counts, with replacement (code sample_pop_based_on_ref_distribution; the code then drops duplicates with np.isin and does not reset its arrays between the two classes, both shown as variants of a corrected version, which decides). Type distribution test - a Fisher exact test on the type by class table with Monte Carlo p-values (R fisher.test simulate.p.value, 10^5 replicates, a standard choice). The paper's printed range includes t(199) = -0.31, which gives p of about 0.76, so its "all p < 0.001" and its t range disagree; the per-sorter t and p are reported and the disagreement is a deviation. Reproduced when the type test has p < 0.001 for every sorter, good units are below the ground truth at p < 0.001 for every sorter with a mean decrease within tolerance under one reading of a decrease, and degraded units are below good units for Kilosort4, 2.5, 1 and herdingspikes with a mean decrease within tolerance. Partially reproduced when the first two parts hold.

claims.statement: The capacity loss comes with larger direction manifold radii (6% on average, except a 3% decrease for Kilosort), larger dimensions (6% on average, except a 19% decrease for Kilosort and Kilosort2) and slightly more correlated centroids (1% for Kilosort3, 2, 1 and herdingspikes).
claims.source: Results, Spike sorting degrades stimulus representation, paragraph 6; Figure 7h-j
claims.quote: Except for Kilosort which showed a 3% decrease, direction mani-folds’ radii increased by an averaged 6% across sorters ( Fig. 7h , t(199) ranging from -87 to 0.18, all p < 0.001, t-test). Except for Kilosort and Kilosort2 which displayed a 19% decrease in direction manifold’s dimension, dimension also increased by an averaged 6% across sorters (i, t(199) ranging from -59 to 234, all p < 0.001). A marginal but significant increase in center correlation of 1% was observed for Kilosort3, 2, 1, and Herdingspikes
claims.criterion: Radius, dimension and centre correlation from neural_manifolds_replicaMFT, as in fig7b-sorting-halves-capacity, relative to the ground truth's. The printed radius range includes t(199) = 0.18, which cannot give p < 0.001, so "all p < 0.001" and the t range disagree; per-sorter t and p are reported. Whether the averages include the excepted sorters is open; both are shown, and the expected values are read over the other sorters. Reproduced when the radius increases for every sorter except Kilosort and the dimension for every sorter except Kilosort and Kilosort2, each at p < 0.001, with mean increases within tolerance, and the centre correlation is higher for Kilosort3, 2, 1 and herdingspikes. Partially reproduced when the directions hold but the means do not.

claims.statement: Peak pure-tone responses of A1 principal cells, contrasts combined, vary with baseline PD in an inverse U, largest at intermediate baseline PD (Kruskal-Wallis p = 5.91e-7, 295 tone-responsive cells from eight animals).
claims.source: Results, CGC is more robust at intermediate baseline PD, paragraph 2; Figure 1f
claims.quote: we also observed an inverse U relationship, where pure-tone response amplitudes are largest at baseline PDs that are within ... the intermediate range of an animal's PD [Fig. 1f, relative to maximum animal PD; p = 5.91 × 10−7, one-way Kruskal–Wallis test, 295 tone-responsive cells
claims.criterion: Group A mice, all trials (the 50% limit applies to evoked pupil analyses, not Fig. 1). Per cell and baseline PD bin, the average peak pure-tone response over that cell's trials of both contrasts in the bin (shared methods, both peak readings). Kruskal-Wallis across the seven bins on the cell-bin values. Reproduced when p < 0.05 and the bin with the highest mean is neither the first nor the last. The lower edge of bin 1 is open, (a) all trials below 21% or (b) 10 to 21%; both run.

claims.statement: Response reliability (trial-to-trial zero-lag cross-correlation of pure-tone responses at 2-3.2 s) is highest at intermediate baseline PD, along with response amplitude (Kruskal-Wallis p = 3.25e-8).
claims.source: Results, CGC is more robust at intermediate baseline PD, paragraph 2; Figure 1g
claims.quote: increased trial-to-trial consistency in the timing of pure-tone responses, termed reliability, coincides with increased pure-tone response amplitudes at intermediate baseline PD (Fig. 1g; reliability calculated as average zero lag trial-to-trial cross-correlation between all pairs of pure-tone response ΔF/F traces at 2–3.2 s; p = 3.25 × 10−8, one-way Kruskal–Wallis test)
claims.criterion: Group A, cells and bins as in fig1f-tone-response-inverse-u. Per cell and bin, the mean over all pairs of trials in the bin of the zero-lag cross-correlation of the pure-tone response traces at 2 to 3.2 s (Methods and Results). The normalization is open, (a) Pearson correlation of the two traces (the axis reads "reliability (C.C.)"), (b) the normalized cross-correlation without mean removal; both run. Cell-bins with fewer than two trials have no value. Reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis test across bins has p < 0.05 and the bin with the highest mean is neither the first nor the last.

claims.statement: The contrast scaling factor (CGC magnitude) is largest at intermediate baseline PD (Kruskal-Wallis p = 3.03e-5).
claims.source: Results, CGC is more robust at intermediate baseline PD, paragraph 3; Figure 1h
claims.quote: the magnitude of CGC is, like pure-tone response amplitudes (Fig. 1f), largest at intermediate baseline PDs (Fig. 1h; p= 3.03 × 10−5, one-way Kruskal–Wallis test)
claims.criterion: Group A, cells responsive in both contrasts. Per cell and bin with trials of both contrasts, the contrast scaling factor (shared methods, both peak readings). Kruskal-Wallis across the seven bins. Reproduced when p < 0.05 and the bin with the highest mean factor is neither the first nor the last.
