claims.statement: CGC is evident throughout the baseline PD range, the contrast scaling factor being significantly above 1 in every baseline PD bin.
claims.source: Results, CGC is more robust at intermediate baseline PD, paragraph 3; Figure 1h; Discussion, paragraph 3
claims.quote: We deemed CGC evident when contrast scaling factors were significantly >1. Contrast scaling factors plotted across baseline PD reveal that CGC is evident throughout the baseline PD range
claims.criterion: Values as in fig1h-cgc-largest-intermediate. The paper names no test for "significantly >1", no sidedness and no correction. Readings, (a) one-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank test of the cell factors against 1, (b) one-sample t-test against 1, each run one-sided and two-sided at p < 0.05 per bin, uncorrected. Reproduced when, under each reading, every bin's mean factor is above 1 and the test is significant in every bin; the bins and p-values are shown.

claims.statement: Peak pure-tone responses depend on baseline PD (F(6,1871) = 10.74, p = 9.04e-12), with a significant interaction between contrast and baseline PD (F(6,1871) = 6.01, p = 3.10e-6).
claims.source: Results, CGC is more robust at intermediate baseline PD, paragraph 3; Figure 1i
claims.quote: we observed a significant association between baseline PD and response amplitude (Fig. 1i; F(6,1871) = 10.74, p =9.04× 10−12, two-way ANOVA). Notably, we found a significant interaction between contrast and baseline PD (Fig. 1i; F(6,1871)= 6.01, p = 3.10 × 10−6)
claims.criterion: Group A. Per cell, bin and contrast, the average peak pure-tone response (shared methods, both peak readings). Two-way ANOVA with bin (7 levels) and contrast (2), with interaction. Which cell-bins enter is open, (a) every cell-bin-contrast with trials, (b) only cell-bins with trials of both contrasts; both run. Reproduced when, under one reading whose count of values is within tolerance, both the bin effect and the interaction have p < 0.05; partially reproduced when only the bin effect does.

claims.statement: Only at the intermediate baseline PD bin of 43-54% do peak pure-tone responses differ significantly between low and high contrast (Bonferroni corrected post hoc, p = 3.65e-5).
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 3; Figure 1i, fourth bin
claims.quote: solely at the intermediate baseline PD range where CGC is maximal, we observed a significant effect of contrast on pure-tone responses between low and high contrast (p = 3.65 × 10−5, Bonferroni’s corrected post hoc test)
claims.criterion: On the ANOVA of fig1i-baseline-contrast-interaction, low against high contrast within each of the seven bins, Bonferroni corrected. The paper names Bonferroni and no family, so the family is open, (a) the seven contrast comparisons, one per bin, (b) all 91 pairs of the 14 bin by contrast groups (as a post hoc test of all group means after a two-way ANOVA gives); both run. Reproduced when, under both, the fourth bin is significant at corrected p < 0.05 and no other bin is; methods_underspecified if they disagree.

claims.statement: Evoked PD averaged over the DRC (0-8 s) is larger in high than in low contrast (Wilcoxon rank sum p = 0.0066).
claims.source: Results, Sound-evoked PD responses are contrast-dependent but do not predict CGC magnitude, paragraph 1; Figure 2a, b
claims.quote: We found that evoked PD responses to high-contrast sound are significantly larger than those in low contrast across a temporal average of the DRC stimulus (Fig, 2a; 0–8 s; Wilcoxon rank sum test, p = 0.0066)
claims.criterion: Per trial, the mean evoked PD (% baseline) over 0 to 8 s from DRC onset, trials with baseline PD < 50% of animal max, CTRL trials of the CGC assay (DRC with the pure tone, as Fig. 2a shows). Open, run under each reading - the mice, (a) group A, (b) group B before ZX1, (c) groups A and B pooled, if they are distinct mice (the Methods list both for Fig. 2a-c); the unit of the test, (a) trials, (b) per-animal means per contrast. Two-sided Wilcoxon rank sum, high against low. Reproduced when high exceeds low with p < 0.05 under every reading; if the readings differ, methods_underspecified with every result shown.

claims.statement: Before the pure tone, evoked PD averaged over 1-2 s is also larger in high than in low contrast (Wilcoxon rank sum p = 0.043).
claims.source: Results, Sound-evoked PD responses are contrast-dependent but do not predict CGC magnitude, paragraph 1; Figure 2c
claims.quote: we analyzed responses at 1–2 s and again observed significantly larger evoked PD during high contrast (Fig. 2c; 1–2 s; Wilcoxon rank sum test, p = 0.043)
claims.criterion: As fig2b-evoked-pd-whole-drc, with the per-trial mean over 1 to 2 s, under the same readings.

claims.statement: A1 principal cell responses averaged over the first 2 s of the DRC do not differ between low and high contrast, before or after ZX1 (520 tone-responsive cells from 14 mice).
claims.source: Results, Sound-evoked PD responses are contrast-dependent but do not predict CGC magnitude, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 2d, e
claims.quote: we averaged cell response magnitude across 0–2 s (Fig. 2e). We did not observe any significant difference in response magnitude in either control or ZX1 (Wilcoxon rank sum test for control: z = 0.0073, p = 0.9942; after ZX1, z = −1.2425, p = 0.2141)
claims.criterion: Group B. Per cell and condition, the mean over 0 to 2 s of the trial-averaged dF/F (F0_DRC over -1.2 to 0 s). A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test - two-sided Wilcoxon rank sum of cell values, low against high, in CTRL and in ZX1 separately. Reproduced when neither is significant at p < 0.05; not reproduced when either is; the median difference is given either way. Cell inclusion readings as in the shared methods; the count is checked under each.

claims.statement: In an LME model of cell peak pure-tone responses, baseline PD contributes significantly (F(1,165.06) = 8.70, p = 3.64e-3), while evoked PD at 1-2 s (p = 0.108) and its interaction with contrast (p = 0.756) do not.
claims.source: Results, Sound-evoked PD responses are contrast-dependent but do not predict CGC magnitude, paragraph 2; Figure 3b; Methods, Pupillometry, analysis, paragraph 3
claims.quote: we found that the baseline PD model coefficient significantly differed from zero and thus significantly contributed to neuronal responses (F(1,165.06) = 8.70; p = 3.64 × 10−3). Neither sound-evoked PD responses (F(1,167.17)= 2.61; p = 0.108) nor their interaction with contrast (F(1,169.59) = 0.0971; p = 0.756) contributed to predicting neuronal pure-tone responses
claims.criterion: Group A. Which cells is open, (a) cells responsive in both contrasts (the Methods rule for CGC analyses), (b) all tone-responsive cells of fig1f-tone-response-inverse-u; both run. Model as in the Methods, peakPureToneResponse ~ baseline_PD + contrast x pupil_at_1-2s + (1 | subject) + (1 | baseline_PD) + (1 | pupil_at_1-2s), baseline_PD in % animal max (Fig. 3a axis), pupil_at_1-2s the trial's mean evoked PD over 1 to 2 s in % baseline; F tests of the fixed effects with Satterthwaite df. Rows are cell by trial (the pupil terms are per trial), with the trial peak response. Open, run under each reading - trials, (a) all, (b) baseline PD < 50%. The positive claim (baseline PD) is reproduced when p < 0.05 under every reading; the absence parts (evoked PD and its interaction) are judged on the paper's test, reproduced when neither has p < 0.05. The claim is reproduced when all three parts hold, partially when the baseline part or the absence parts hold alone.

claims.statement: The full LME model with evoked PD and its contrast interaction does not predict pure-tone responses better than a null model with baseline PD alone (likelihood ratio test p = 0.330).
claims.source: Results, Sound-evoked PD responses are contrast-dependent but do not predict CGC magnitude, paragraph 2; Figure 3c
claims.quote: The full model including sound-evoked PD responses and their interaction with contrast did not significantly improve neuronal pure-tone response prediction when compared with the null model (p = 0.330)
claims.criterion: Data and full model as in fig3b-lme-coefficients; null model peakPureToneResponse ~ baseline_PD + (1 | subject) + (1 | baseline_PD) (Methods). Both fitted by maximum likelihood (needed to compare models with different fixed effects; a standard choice). A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test - reproduced when the likelihood ratio test has p >= 0.05, under each trial reading.

claims.statement: In ZnT3-WT mice, contrast and ZX1 both affect the GCA intercept and slope of evoked PD, and contrast interacts with ZX1 (F(1,7921.6) = 24.2, p = 8.85e-7).
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraph 1; Figure 4a, c, e
claims.quote: In ZnT3-WT mice, we observed a significant effect of both contrast and ZX1 on the intercept ... and on the first-order (linear) time polynomial coefficient (slope) ... We also observed a significant interaction between contrast and ZX1 treatment (Fig. 4c, F(1,7921.6) = 24.2, p = 8.85 × 10−7)
claims.criterion: Group C, CTRL and ZX1 trials of DRC without the tone, baseline PD < 50%. GCA as in the shared methods, under both model readings and both coding readings. Reproduced when, under every reading, all five terms have p < 0.05; partially reproduced when the contrast x ZX1 term and at least two of the four main terms do; methods_underspecified if the readings disagree. The signs of the terms and the row count against the df (about 7930 rows) are shown.

claims.statement: In ZnT3-WT mice, post hoc Tukey tests show an effect of contrast before but not after ZX1, and an effect of ZX1 only on high-contrast evoked PD (p < 0.0001).
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraph 1; Figure 4c
claims.quote: Pairwise post hoc Tukey tests revealed a significant effect of contrast before, but not after ZX1 treatment, and solely a significant effect of ZX1 on high-contrast–evoked PD (p < 0.0001 for both comparisons)
claims.criterion: On the model of fig4c-wt-contrast-zx1-effects (each model reading), emmeans of the four contrast x treatment cells at the time polynomials' mean (zero for orthogonal polynomials, emmeans' default), Tukey adjusted pairwise comparisons with Satterthwaite df (Methods). Reproduced when HIGH exceeds LOW in CTRL at p < 0.05 and not in ZX1, and ZX1 lowers HIGH at p < 0.05 and does not change LOW at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In ZnT3-KO mice, neither contrast nor ZX1 affects the GCA intercept of evoked PD and they do not interact; contrast does not affect the slope.
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraph 2; Figure 4b, d, f
claims.quote: In ZnT3-KO mice (Fig. 4b), we did not observe a significant effect of either contrast or ZX1 on evoked PD intercept (Fig. 4d,f; contrast, F(1,4500.8) = −1.14, p = 0.255; ZX1, F(1,4502.4) = 1.45, p = 0.147), nor a significant interaction between the two (F(1,4500.2) = −0.540, p = 0.589)
claims.criterion: Group D, as fig4c-wt-contrast-zx1-effects. A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test - reproduced when the contrast intercept, ZX1 intercept, contrast x ZX1 and contrast slope terms all have p >= 0.05, not reproduced when any has p < 0.05; under each model and coding reading, estimates given. The model readings are part of how the test is written, so a disagreement between them is reported as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: In ZnT3-KO mice ZX1 still reduces the GCA slope (p = 0.0129), but its slope weight (-0.64) is less than half that in ZnT3-WT mice (-1.41).
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraph 2; Figure 4e, f
claims.quote: however, we observed a significant effect of ZX1 (F(1,4500.0) = −2.49, p = 0.0129) ... the GCA slope coefficient (weight) for ZX1 in the ZnT3-KO mice (−0.64, Fig. 4f) was less than half that of ZnT3-WT (−1.41, Fig. 4e)
claims.criterion: Models of fig4c-wt-contrast-zx1-effects and fig4f-ko-no-contrast-effect; the weight is the tPoly1 x treatment coefficient. Reproduced when, under one model and coding reading, the KO term is negative with p < 0.05 and the KO weight is less than half the WT weight in magnitude; the two weights are checked against the expected values, which also depend on the polynomial scaling (unit norm, as R poly() gives, is used; the paper does not state it).

claims.statement: ZX1 infused into the contralateral (left) ACtx increases sound-evoked responses of right A1 principal neurons (one-way repeated measures ANOVA F = 33.44, p = 4.1e-5; control against contralateral ZX1 p = 0.016, Bonferroni; three mice).
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraph 4; Figure 5c-e
claims.quote: infusion of ZX1 to the contralateral ACtx increased the sound-evoked responses of ipsilateral A1 PNs (Fig. 5c–e; three mice, one-way repeated measure ANOVA, F = 33.44, p = 4.1 × 10−5; control vs ZX1 in contralateral ACtx, p = 0.016, Bonferroni's multiple-comparisons test)
claims.criterion: Group E, widefield dF/F of right A1 to broadband noise (6 to 64 kHz, 100 ms, 30 to 80 dB SPL, Fig. 5b axis, d legend), F0 the 1 s mean before sound onset (carried over from Methods, Widefield imaging, which states it for the pure-tone mapping, not for Fig. 5). The paper does not give the A1 region, the response measure or window, or what the repeated measures are. Readings, run each - measure, (a) peak dF/F, (b) mean dF/F, in the 1 s after onset (standard window). Repeated units - with three conditions, F = 33.44 gives p = 0.0032 on (2,4) df (three mice), 9e-9 on (2,34) df (three mice by six levels), and 3.7e-5 on (2,10) df, close to the reported 4.1e-5; so the units are read as the sound levels (six on the Fig. 5b axis, 30 to 80 dB SPL), with values averaged over mice, and with and without a Greenhouse-Geisser correction. Units of mice, and of mouse by level, are variants shown. A1 is the region the dataset marks as A1, if it does; else this claim is blocked. Reproduced when the ANOVA has p < 0.05 and contralateral ZX1 exceeds control at Bonferroni p < 0.05 under every measure reading; methods_underspecified if they disagree.

claims.statement: Subsequent ZX1 infusion into the ipsilateral ACtx reduces sound-evoked A1 responses compared with contralateral ZX1 (p = 3.2e-5, Bonferroni).
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraph 4; Figure 5d-f
claims.quote: subsequent infusion of ZX1 to ipsilateral ACtx reduced the sound-evoked responses of A1 PNs (Fig. 5d–f; ZX1 in contralateral vs ipsilateral ACtx, p = 3.2 × 10−5, Bonferroni's multiple-comparisons test)
claims.criterion: As fig5-contralateral-zx1-increases. Reproduced when ipsilateral ZX1 is below contralateral ZX1 at Bonferroni p < 0.05 under every reading.

claims.statement: After infusion of ZX1 with Alexa Fluor 594 into the left ACtx, no Alexa Fluor 594 is seen in the right ACtx, suggesting ZX1 does not travel to the other hemisphere.
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraph 3; Figure 5c
claims.quote: We found that the infusion of ZX1 + Alexa Fluor 594 to the left (contralateral) ACtx does not show the presence of Alexa Fluor 594 in the ipsilateral ACtx under the red channel (Fig. 5c)
claims.criterion: Shown with a representative red-channel image and no measure. Testable only if the dataset holds the red-channel images of the right ACtx before and after contralateral infusion; the paper gives no threshold for presence, so the claim is reported as methods_underspecified with the mean red intensities shown, unless the images make the answer plain both ways (no change at all, or a change of the order seen after the ipsilateral infusion).

claims.statement: Baseline PD increases with recording time in both ZX1 (slope 95% CI 0.0798 to 0.183, p = 1.26e-6) and ACSF experiments (95% CI 0.0159 to 0.279, p = 0.0282), and the intervals overlap.
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraph 5; Figure 6a
claims.quote: We observed a significant time-dependent increase in baseline PD across the recording duration of ZX1 experiments [Fig. 6a; slope 95% CI = (0.0798, 0.183), p = 1.26 × 10−6] ... we used ACSF as a control and found a similar time-dependent increase in baseline PD [Fig. 6a; slope 95% CI = (0.0159, 0.279), p = 0.0282]
claims.criterion: Per trial, baseline PD (% animal max, over -4 to 0 s) against recording time in minutes (Fig. 6a axes; the time origin, the first trial, changes no slope), all trials of the experiment, pooled over mice, ordinary least squares (Methods, Statistics). Which ZX1 experiments is open, run each - (a) groups C and D, (b) group C only, (c) groups B, C and D. ACSF is group F. Reproduced when both slopes are positive with p < 0.05 and their 95% CIs overlap, under every ZX1 reading; the slopes and intervals are compared with the reported ones.

claims.statement: After ACSF injection the contrast effect on evoked PD remains, on both the GCA intercept (F(1,2558.3) = 46.22, p = 1.31e-11) and slope (F(1,2558) = 15.076, p = 1.10e-4).
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraph 5; Figure 6b
claims.quote: following ACSF injection, unlike following ZX1 injection (Fig. 4a,c,e), we observed a significant effect of contrast on both the intercept and fitted slope coefficient of the first-order time polynomial (Fig. 6b; intercept, F(1,2558.3) = 46.22, p = 1.31 × 10−11; slope, F(1,2558)= 15.076, p = 1.10× 10−4)
claims.criterion: Group F, baseline PD < 50%. Open, run each - (a) trials after ACSF only, pupil ~ (tPoly1 + tPoly2) x contrast + (1 | subject); (b) trials before and after ACSF, the model of fig4c-wt-contrast-zx1-effects with ACSF as treatment, the contrast terms (and the contrast effect within ACSF from emmeans). Reproduced when the contrast intercept and slope terms both have p < 0.05 with HIGH above LOW under every reading; methods_underspecified if they disagree. Row counts are shown against the df (about 2560 rows).

claims.statement: Below 50% of animal max baseline PD, baseline PD and evoked PD at 1-2 s are not significantly correlated (r(238) = -0.0928, p = 0.1537).
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraph 5; Figure 6c
claims.quote: we limited our pupil response analyses to the 50th percentile of baseline PD ... at which there was no significant correlation between baseline PD and evoked PD (Fig. 6c; Pearson's correlation coefficient, r(238) = −0.0928, p = 0.1537)
claims.criterion: Per trial, baseline PD (% animal max) against mean evoked PD over 1 to 2 s (% baseline), both contrasts, baseline PD < 50% (Fig. 6c legend). Which experiments is not given; the readings are each group (A, B before ZX1, C, D, F) and the CTRL or all trials of each, and the reading used is the one whose count of responses is within tolerance of 240. A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test - reproduced when that reading's Pearson correlation has p >= 0.05. If no reading or more than one matches the count, every result is shown, and the claim is methods_underspecified unless all agree.

claims.statement: Evoked pupil responses are negatively correlated with baseline PD over all responses (r(624) = -0.35, p = 1.20e-19), and the correlation is small and not significant below 50% of animal max PD (r(382) = -0.055, p = 0.285).
claims.source: Materials and Methods, Pupillometry, analysis, paragraph 2
claims.quote: evoked pupil responses are significantly negatively correlated with baseline PD (data not shown; r(624) = −0.35, p = 1.20 × 10−19). At PDs <50% of maximum animal PD, this correlation becomes much smaller and is no longer significant (Fig. 6b; r(382) = −0.055, p = 0.285)
claims.criterion: Measures as in fig6c-no-baseline-evoked-correlation (evoked PD at 1-2 s; the paper does not name the window here, 0 to 2 s and 0 to 8 s are variants). The data set is not named (the text cites Fig. 6b, an ACSF panel, which has no correlation); the readings are those of fig6c-no-baseline-evoked-correlation, and the one used is the one whose counts are within tolerance of 626 and 384. Reproduced when, on that reading, the correlation over all responses is negative with p < 0.05 and within tolerance, and the one below 50% has p >= 0.05. If no reading or more than one matches the counts, every result is shown, and the claim is methods_underspecified unless all agree.

claims.statement: Before ZX1, ZnT3-KO mice have smaller evoked PD increases to high-contrast sound than ZnT3-WT mice, a genotype effect on the GCA slope (F(1,3869) = 22.37, p = 2.33e-6).
claims.source: Results, Cortical synaptic zinc signaling is necessary for the increased evoked PD in high- versus low-contrast sound, paragraphs 6 and 7; Figure 6d
claims.quote: observed a significant effect of genotype on the slope coefficient of the first-order time polynomial (Fig. 6d; F(1,3869) = 22.37, p = 2.33 × 10−6). Namely, ZnT3-KO mice have reduced PD responses in high contrast
claims.criterion: CTRL high-contrast trials of groups C and D (Fig. 6d legend, the light orange responses of Fig. 4a, b), baseline PD < 50%. GCA as in the shared methods with pupil ~ (tPoly1 + tPoly2) x genotype + (1 | subject) (Methods); the factor coding is open as in the shared methods, (a) reference coding with WT as reference, (b) effects coding, both run. Reproduced when the tPoly1 x genotype term has p < 0.05 and the KO slope is below the WT slope. Row count shown against the df (about 3870 rows).

claims.statement: After ZX1, high-contrast PD responses of ZnT3-WT mice peak at about 110% of baseline, like the high-contrast responses of ZnT3-KO mice, and with zinc signaling blocked both contrasts resemble low-contrast responses.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraphs 6 and 7; Figure 4c, d
claims.quote: upon blockade, responses to both low and high contrast resembled low-contrast responses, which were of comparable magnitude in ZnT3-WT and ZnT3-KO mice (Fig. 4) ... the magnitude of PD responses to high-contrast sound after ZX1 infusion in ZnT3-WT mice (Fig. 4c; peak at ∼110% PD) is not different from the magnitude of high-contrast PD responses in ZnT3-KO mice (Fig. 4d; peak at ∼110% PD)
claims.criterion: The peaks are given as approximate ("∼110%"), read from Fig. 4c, d, and no test is named for "not different". The quantity is the maximum of the trial-mean trace (% baseline, baseline PD < 50%) within 0 to 2 s (the Fig. 4c, d window), minus 100. The tolerance is a quarter of the 10 point rise, as the paper gives the values only to the nearest few percent; 10% of the 110 would accept no rise at all. Which KO trials is open, (a) CTRL, (b) CTRL and ZX1 pooled; both run, and the claim holds when the WT value and the KO value under one reading are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Dataset KI holds 24,248 single units from 99 Neuropixels recordings in awake head-fixed mice, 52% of them in the PFC and 48% in other brain regions.
claims.source: Results, Capturing the diversity of spontaneous firing patterns, paragraph 1; Methods, Unit quality control
claims.quote: We recorded the firing activity of 24,248 single units from awake, head-fixed mice (dataset KI; Fig. 1a–c ). Overall, 52% of the units originated from the PFC and 48% from other brain regions
claims.criterion: Units counted under both readings of G3. The PFC fraction is the share of units whose location is one of the 11 PFC subregions the Results list. The recording count has no tolerance, as it is a count of files the paper names; a dandiset holding only part of dataset KI is reported as such (the author finds what 001260 holds), and the expected values are then compared for the whole of dataset KI only if 000473 is used as well.

claims.statement: Peak-to-trough durations are bimodal, splitting units into 19,186 ww units (81.1%) and 4,200 nw units (17.7%), with 862 intermediate units left unclassified.
claims.source: Figure 1h and legend; Results, Capturing the diversity of spontaneous firing patterns, paragraph 2
claims.quote: As expected, spike widths were bimodally distributed, allowing us to distinguish ww ( n = 19,186; 81.1%) and nw ( n = 4,200; 17.7%) units (Fig. 1h )
claims.criterion: Thresholds from the Methods (Waveform classification), < 0.38 ms nw and > 0.43 ms ww, on the peak-to-trough duration of each unit's mean waveform. The percentages do not follow from the counts given (19,186 of 24,248 is 79.1%); they match a total of 23,667 units, the preprint's count. Readings of the denominator are (a) all units, classified and unclassified (the legend's 24,248); (b) ww plus nw units only. The fractions hold if they match under either reading; the conflict between counts and percentages is recorded as a paper inconsistency. Bimodality is shown by the histogram (1-ms bins as in the legend are too coarse for a 0.4 ms valley; a finer bin is a plotting choice).

claims.statement: Narrow-waveform units have significantly higher firing rates, burstiness and memory than wide-waveform units.
claims.source: Figure 1i; Results, Capturing the diversity of spontaneous firing patterns, paragraph 2
claims.quote: indeed, nw units displayed significantly higher firing rates, along with higher burstiness and memory compared to ww units (Fig. 1i )
claims.criterion: For each metric (log10FR, B, M), a linear mixed-effect model Metric ~ 1 + Unittype + (1|Mouse) (Methods, equation 6), with the unit-type effect tested by a post hoc F test with Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom and Tukey's correction for multiple comparisons (Methods; Fig. 1i legend; code Fig1i__MixModel_Statistics.jl, emmeans pairwise contrast). The VoR text gives no p-value; the figure marks are not in the text. Reproduced when, for all three metrics, the nw estimate is higher than the ww estimate with p < 0.05; partially reproduced for one or two metrics. The code also drops units with log10FR < 0.1 and pools active and other epoch states; shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Firing metrics in sleep-like epochs differ from those in active spontaneous epochs, which is why sleep-like epochs are excluded.
claims.source: Results, Capturing the diversity of spontaneous firing patterns, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 1d,e
claims.quote: Epochs contaminated by ‘sleep-like’ periods 27 were excluded due to their fundamentally different, nonstationary firing characteristics
claims.criterion: Sleep-like periods detected as in Methods (Detection of sleep-like periods; mean cortical rate in 10-ms bins, Savitzky-Golay 11 points order 3, troughs below 0.2 of the geometric mean for longer than 5 ms, extended to the geometric mean, merged within 1.5 s, padded by 1 s or 0.3 s). Sleep-like epochs overlap such a period. Per unit, metrics computed over active epochs (all ww units with enough active epochs, n = 19,186) and over sleep-like epochs (ww units with at least 12 sleep-like epochs of at least 6 spikes, n = 11,599), as the Extended Data Fig. 1 legend gives the two samples. A mixed model Metric ~ 1 + EpochType + (1|Mouse) (Methods, equation 7) per metric and unit type, post hoc F test with Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom and Tukey's correction (Methods). The legend's per-metric marks and any direction are in the figure only, so the count of metrics required is this file's rule. Reproduced when the epoch-type effect has p < 0.05 for all three metrics in ww units; partially reproduced for one or two; the direction of each is reported.

claims.statement: Sleep-like episodes occupy a median 6% (IQR 0 to 18%) of recording time; sessions hold a median 227 (IQR 172 to 284) spontaneous active epochs and 19 (IQR 1 to 84) sleep-like epochs.
claims.source: Methods, Detection of sleep-like periods and Epoch selection; Extended Data Fig. 1 legend, Data (unit count)
claims.quote: Sleep-like episodes occupied 6% (IQR, 0–18%) of the time in recording sessions ... Recording sessions contained 227 (IQR, 172–284) spontaneous active epochs and 19 (IQR, 1–84) sleep-like epochs
claims.criterion: Sleep-like detection and epoch rules as in extfig1d-sleep-like-differ. Whether a "recording session" is one probe recording (99) or one session of up to 3 probes is open; both readings are shown, and the values hold under either.

claims.statement: Across ww units, a linear correlation does not reveal a dependence between burstiness and memory.
claims.source: Results, Brain regions have distinct firing repertoires, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 1f,g
claims.quote: Note that linear correlation did not reveal this empirical dependence between burstiness and memory (Extended Data Fig. 1f,g )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The paper's test is a mixed model Metric1 ~ 1 + Metric2 + (1|Mouse) (Methods, equation 8) across all ww units, reported as the marginal R2 and marked n.s. in the legend. Reproduced when the fixed effect of memory on burstiness is not significant at p < 0.05; not reproduced when it is. The marginal R2 and the effect size are given either way, with burstiness on memory as a variant.

claims.statement: On the ww SOM, burstiness and firing rate vary along perpendicular gradients, while high memory occurs only with medium to low burstiness, so high memory and high burstiness are mutually exclusive.
claims.source: Figure 2a; Results, Brain regions have distinct firing repertoires, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The SOM displayed perpendicular gradients of burstiness and firing rate, showing that these two metrics vary independently of each other. In contrast, high memory patches coincided with medium to low burstiness, indicating that high memory and high burstiness are mutually exclusive
claims.criterion: The paper shows this in the component planes and gives no measure. Across the nodes of the ww SOM trained as in the header, using the de-standardized prototype values. Part 1 (perpendicular gradients) is judged by the angle between the directions of steepest increase of B and of log10FR over the node grid, from a linear fit of each prototype value on the node coordinates; reproduced when the angle is between 60 and 120 degrees. Part 2 is judged by the nodes with the highest memory, read as (a) the top 10% of nodes or (b) the top 25%; reproduced when, under both, none of these nodes lies in the top quartile of node burstiness. The angle bounds and the quantiles are this file's, as the paper gives none, and are recorded as a deviation; the claim is reproduced only when both parts hold under both readings, and blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: PFC ww units are widely spread on the SOM, with many matching regular-firing (low burstiness) nodes and few in anti-memory territory, while units from other regions populate different territories.
claims.source: Figure 2b; Extended Data Fig. 2e; Results, Brain regions have distinct firing repertoires, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Overall, PFC units were widely distributed on the SOM, with many units matching best to regular firing (that is, low burstiness) and avoiding anti-memory territories (Fig. 2b ), while units from other brain regions populated different territories
claims.criterion: The paper shows this as SOM hit maps and gives no measure or test, so the comparison below is a reading of this file, not the paper's, and is recorded as a deviation. Compared with all non-PFC ww units, reproduced when PFC ww units have a lower median burstiness and a smaller fraction of units with negative memory (M < 0, "anti-memory" as in Fig. 1e), each by a two-sided Mann-Whitney test (burstiness) or a chi-square test (fraction) at p < 0.05. The 54% is the share of PFC units among the ww units the SOM is trained on (all regions and layers).

claims.statement: About 57% of ww units keep their category from one block of about 50 spontaneous epochs to the next, far above the 18% expected by chance from the marginal distributions.
claims.source: Figure 2e; Results, Stable classification of single-unit firing patterns, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Consistently, around 57% of units remained in the category they had in the previous block, which is considerably above the 18% expected from chance (marginal distributions; Fig. 2e )
claims.criterion: Blocks as in Methods (Stability analyses), the recording's own blocks of 50 or 100 epochs (100 split in two) where the setting has them, else blocks of about 50 epochs; blocks with fewer than 12 epochs of at least 6 spikes dropped for that unit (Methods; the code uses at least 3 valid epochs per block and 5 per transition, shown as a variant). Block metrics standardized to the full-data ww SOM and assigned their best matching node's category. Stability per transition t is the trace of the summed transition matrix M_t over its total, and chance is the same for the matrix expected from the marginals of M_t (Methods, Assessment of overall stability per transition; Fig. 2e plots it per transition). The paper does not say how "around 57%" summarizes the transitions; readings (a) the mean over transitions, (b) the pooled matrix summed over transitions. Both are shown with the per-transition values, and the value holds under either. The dataset may not mark the recordings' inherent block structure; if it does not, blocks of about 50 consecutive epochs are used and this is a deviation.

claims.statement: Block-wise category assignment is less stable for low-rate categories (1 to 3, 7 and 8) than for high-rate categories, and low-rate regular categories 1 to 3 mostly transition among themselves, as do the low-rate bursty categories 7 and 8.
claims.source: Figure 2f; Extended Data Fig. 3d; Results, Stable classification of single-unit firing patterns, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Indeed, the block-wise assignment of categories to units was substantially less stable for low-rate categories (1–3, 7 and 8) compared to high-rate categories (Fig. 2f and Extended Data Fig. 3d ) ... low-rate, regular-firing categories (1–3) mostly transitioned among themselves, as did the low-rate, bursty categories (7 and 8)
claims.criterion: From the summed transition count matrix of fig2e-category-stability, the transition probability matrix P (rows sum to 1, Methods). Part 1, the stability of a category read as its diagonal entry of P; reproduced when the mean diagonal of categories 1 to 3, 7 and 8 is lower than the mean diagonal of 4 to 6, with the diagonal of the coincidence coefficient matrix X (Methods, equation 4) shown as a second reading that must agree. Part 2, for each category in 1 to 3, the summed probability of moving to the other two categories of 1 to 3 exceeds that of moving to any other single category outside the group, and likewise for 7 and 8. Reproduced when both parts hold; partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: Superficial cortical layers (L2/3) are enriched in bursty ww units, while deep layers (L5 to 6) are enriched in regular-firing ww units.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 3f,g; Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 1
claims.quote: E-score analysis of ww unit activity revealed substantial enrichment in bursty units in the superficial cortical layers (L2/3), while deep cortical layers (L5–6) were enriched in regular-firing units
claims.criterion: E-scores of cortical layer against ww category, all cortical ww units, with each combination of region and behavioral setting as a group (Methods, Group-bias control), 1,000 shuffles. Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 (the p-values) were not read. Reproduced when L2/3 has a significant positive E-score for at least one of the bursty categories 6 to 8, and L5 and L6 each have a significant positive E-score for at least one of categories 1 to 3. Layers as labeled in the dataset (L6a and L6b counted as L6). Under G1 and G2.

claims.statement: Most PFC subregions (ILA, PL, ACAd, ACAv, ORBm and ORBvl) are enriched in low-rate, regular-firing ww units (categories 1 to 3).
claims.source: Figure 2g; Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The majority of the cytoarchitectural PFC subregions, that is, ILA, PL, ACAd, ACAv, ORBm and ORBvl, were generally enriched in low-rate, regular-firing units (categories 1–3)
claims.criterion: E-scores of brain (sub)region against ww category, deep-layer units for cortical regions and all units elsewhere, against all such units (the code's refall), grouped by behavioral setting (Methods), 1,000 shuffles, regions with more than 20 units. "Generally enriched" is read as (a) a positive sum of the E-scores of categories 1 to 3, or (b) a significant positive E-score in at least one of categories 1 to 3. Reproduced when all six subregions meet the reading, under both readings; partially reproduced when at least four do under both. Under G1 and G2; readings that disagree block the claim as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: ILA and PL are both strongly and significantly enriched in the most regular-firing category 1.
claims.source: Figure 2g; Supplementary Table 3 (not read); Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Interestingly, ILA and PL were both heavily and significantly enriched in units of the most regular-firing category 1 (Supplementary Table 3 )
claims.criterion: The E-scores of fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment. Reproduced when the category 1 E-score is positive and significant (P < 0.05) for both ILA and PL; partially reproduced for one.

claims.statement: ORBl, MOs and AIv are significantly enriched in bursty category 8 units, setting them apart from the activity-defined prefrontal entity.
claims.source: Figure 2g,h; Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The ORBl, MOs and AIv, in contrast, were significantly enriched in bursty category 8 units
claims.criterion: The E-scores of fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment. Reproduced when the category 8 E-score is positive and significant for all three; partially reproduced for one or two.

claims.statement: Thalamus and hippocampal formation are strongly and significantly enriched in bursty units (categories 6 to 8), unlike the PFC.
claims.source: Figure 2g; Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Other brain regions like thalamus (TH) and hippocampal formation (HPF) were heavily and significantly enriched in bursty units (categories 6–8)
claims.criterion: The E-scores of fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment, with TH and HPF as the code's parent groups. Readings (a) a significant positive E-score in each of categories 6, 7 and 8; (b) in at least one of them. Reproduced when both TH and HPF meet the reading under both readings; when they differ, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified with both shown.

claims.statement: Regional enrichment profiles of dataset KI are highly similar to those of dataset IBL Passive; for category 1, enrichment across 14 cortical (sub)regions correlates between the two datasets.
claims.source: Figure 2i; Extended Data Fig. 4; Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Repeating the analyses with spontaneous activity obtained from the International Brain Laboratory (dataset IBL Passive 31 ) revealed a high degree of similarity between the regional enrichment profiles of the two datasets
claims.criterion: IBL Passive units' metrics from the 99 epochs of 3 s of the spontaneous block, standardized to dataset KI's ww features and assigned to dataset KI's ww SOM (Methods, Projection of the dataset IBL Passive). E-scores for the 14 cortical (sub)regions both datasets share (deep layers), as in fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment (grouping for IBL Passive is open, as it has one setting; no grouping is the reading). Pearson correlation of the category 1 E-scores across the 14, two-sided (Fig. 2i legend). The r and p are in the figure only. Reproduced when r > 0 with p < 0.05 for category 1, and at least half of categories 2 to 8 (Extended Data Fig. 4d to j) have r > 0.

claims.statement: Among nw units, ILA, PL and ACAd/v are significantly enriched in high-rate, regular-firing units with high memory, and ORBl in high-rate, bursty units.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5g; Supplementary Table 4 (not read); Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 4
claims.quote: ILA, PL and ACAd/v were significantly enriched in high-rate, regular-firing nw units with high memory (Extended Data Fig. 5g and Supplementary Table 4 ). ORBl was consistently and significantly enriched in high-rate, bursty units
claims.criterion: An nw SOM of 220 nodes and 5 categories as in the header, E-scores as in fig2g-pfc-regular-enrichment for nw units. The text does not number the nw categories. The regular high-memory category is read as the nw category with above-median log10FR whose median B is lowest, and the bursty one as the category with above-median log10FR whose median B is highest (by category medians); under the code's labels (G2 a) the category numbers are shown as well. Reproduced when ILA, PL and at least one of ACAd and ACAv have a significant positive E-score for the first, and ORBl for the second; partially reproduced when either part holds.

claims.statement: Brain (sub)regions enriched in low-rate, regular-firing ww units are enriched in high-rate, regular-firing nw units, and regions enriched in low-rate bursty ww units are enriched in high-rate bursty nw units.
claims.source: Figure 2j; Results, Enrichment of low-rate, regular-firing units in the PFC, paragraph 4
claims.quote: we observed that brain (sub)regions enriched in low-rate, regular-firing ww units were enriched in high-rate, regular-firing nw units. Similarly, regions enriched in low-rate, bursty ww units were enriched in high-rate, bursty nw units
claims.criterion: Pearson correlation across the n = 9 regions with sufficient nw units (Fig. 2j legend), between ww and nw category E-scores. The text does not define "sufficient"; the code's Nmin_maps (more than 20 nw units) is used and the number of regions it keeps is reported against 9. Reproduced when the mean r between ww categories 1 to 3 and the nw regular high-memory category of extfig5g-nw-enrichment is positive, and the mean r between ww categories 7 and 8 and the nw high-rate bursty category is positive. The full 8 by 5 matrix is shown.

claims.statement: In dataset KI, enrichment of cortical (sub)regions in low-rate, regular-firing units (categories 1 to 3, category 2 shown) correlates positively with the Harris cortical hierarchy score, driven by the split between low-hierarchy sensory regions and high-hierarchy PFC subregions.
claims.source: Figure 3a,c; Extended Data Fig. 6a; Results, Enrichment in units displaying regular spontaneous firing reflects high cortical hierarchy, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We found a positive correlation between cortical hierarchy and enrichment in low-rate, regular-firing units (categories 1–3). This positive correlation was not driven by a continuous relationship but due to a bimodal distribution of hierarchical scores
claims.criterion: Harris et al. 2019 cortical hierarchy scores (the code reads 'CC+TC+CT iterated', cortex rows of hierarchy_summary_CreConf.xlsx, Zenodo 14205018). E-scores of the n = 17 cortical (sub)regions with a score, deep-layer ww units (Fig. 3a legend), grouped by behavioral setting as the Methods give for (sub)regions; the code's Fig. 3 script shuffles without groups, shown as a variant. Pearson correlation, two-sided. The r values are in the figure only. Reproduced when category 2 has r > 0 with p < 0.05 and categories 1 and 3 have r > 0; partially reproduced when category 2 holds alone. Under G1 and G2.

claims.statement: In dataset IBL Passive, across 32 cortical (sub)regions, enrichment in the PFC's signature categories 1 to 3 correlates positively with cortical hierarchy.
claims.source: Figure 3b,c; Extended Data Fig. 6b; Results, Enrichment in units displaying regular spontaneous firing reflects high cortical hierarchy, paragraph 1
claims.quote: we repeated the analysis with the dataset IBL Passive and found positive correlations between cortical hierarchy and the PFC’s signature categories 1–3
claims.criterion: IBL Passive units projected on dataset KI's ww SOM as in fig2i-ibl-replication; n = 32 cortical (sub)regions, deep layers; Pearson, two-sided. Reproduced when categories 1, 2 and 3 each have r > 0 and at least one has p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Cortical hierarchy correlates even more strongly, and negatively, with enrichment in bursty, low-memory units (categories 6 to 8), in both datasets.
claims.source: Figure 3c; Extended Data Fig. 6a,b; Results, Enrichment in units displaying regular spontaneous firing reflects high cortical hierarchy, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We identified even stronger, negative correlations between cortical hierarchy and enrichment in bursty, low-memory units (categories 6–8; Fig. 3c and Extended Data Fig. 6a,b )
claims.criterion: As fig3a-harris-regular-positive for dataset KI (and fig3b for IBL Passive, shown as a part counted with that claim's data). Reproduced for dataset KI when categories 6, 7 and 8 each have r < 0, at least one with p < 0.05, and the largest |r| among 6 to 8 exceeds the largest |r| among 1 to 3.

claims.statement: Restricted to PFC subregions, enrichment in unit categories shows no relationship to cortical hierarchy.
claims.source: Results, Enrichment in units displaying regular spontaneous firing reflects high cortical hierarchy, paragraph 1; Supplementary Table 5 (not read)
claims.quote: Importantly, when we limited the correlation analysis to PFC subregions, we found no direct relationship between cortical hierarchy and enrichment/depletion in unit categories (Supplementary Table 5 )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The test, from the Results and the Fig. 3 methods, is a two-sided Pearson correlation of E-scores with the Harris score across the PFC subregions among the 17 of fig3a-harris-regular-positive, per category. Supplementary Table 5, which gives it, was not read, so whether a multiple-comparison correction was applied is unknown; none is applied. Reproduced when no category has p < 0.05; not reproduced when any does; r per category given.

claims.statement: The PFC flatmap is parcellated into 42 dataROIs that respect subregion boundaries, each holding about 200 deep-layer ww units.
claims.source: Figure 4b; Extended Data Fig. 7a; Methods, Parcellation into ROIs of similar unit count
claims.quote: we parcellated the PFC subregions into smaller ROIs (dataROIs, n = 42), each containing a similar number of deep-layer ww units (~200
claims.criterion: Per subregion, n = (unit count)/200 rounded down (code, int()), FRP not split; flatmap (u, v) of deep ww units clustered by constrained k-means. Methods give 160 to 240 units per ROI; the code uses 180 to 220 (marg 0.1 around 200). The Methods' bounds are the main reading and the code's a variant; the count holds if either is within tolerance. Needs each unit's flatmap position, which the paper takes from Gao et al.'s projection code (not public; positions are in the Zenodo 14205018 metrics files); a dataset without flatmap positions blocks this and the dataROI and GaoROI claims as data_missing unless those files are used as an input (then data with_inputs).

claims.statement: Low-rate, regular-firing categories 1 and 3 are significantly enriched in dataROIs in ILA and PL, while low-rate, bursty categories 7 and 8 are enriched in dataROIs in MOs and ORBl, the ORBl enrichment pinpointed to its most ventral dataROI.
claims.source: Figure 4c,d; Extended Data Fig. 7b,c; Supplementary Table 6 (not read); Results, Toward an activity-defined map of the PFC, paragraphs 1 and 2
claims.quote: Low-rate, regular-firing units (categories 1 and 3) were significantly enriched in dataROIs located in ILA and PL, while low-rate, bursty units (categories 7 and 8) were enriched in dataROIs located in the MOs and the ORBl
claims.criterion: E-scores of dataROI against ww category, deep-layer PFC ww units, grouped by behavioral setting (Methods), 1,000 shuffles. The reference population is open; readings (a) all PFC deep ww units (the code's refPFC, used for its flatmaps); (b) all units as for regions. Reproduced when, under both readings, at least one dataROI in ILA and one in PL have a significant positive E-score in category 1 or 3, and at least one dataROI in MOs and one in ORBl have a significant positive E-score in category 7 or 8. Disagreeing readings block it. The ORBl part of the statement (most ventral dataROI) is not tested, as the flatmap's dorsoventral axis is not given in the text; the ORBl dataROI with the highest category 7 and 8 E-scores is reported.

claims.statement: Clustering dataROIs by enrichment profile gives activity modules; ILA forms a homogeneous ILA-specific module bordering a similar module in adjacent PL and ACAd, while other modules cross cytoarchitectural boundaries and occur in several places.
claims.source: Figure 4e; Extended Data Fig. 7c,d; Results, Toward an activity-defined map of the PFC, paragraph 1
claims.quote: This revealed a homogeneous enrichment profile in ILA, creating an ILA-specific activity module that bordered a module with similar firing patterns in the adjacent parts of PL and ACAd (Fig. 4e ). Other activity modules stretched over cytoarchitectural boundaries and occurred in multiple places
claims.criterion: dataROI E-score profiles (8 categories) standardized and clustered by Ward linkage into 5 modules (Extended Data Fig. 7d; Methods, Hierarchical clustering analyses). Reproduced when all ILA dataROIs fall in one module, and at least two other modules each hold dataROIs of more than one subregion. "ILA-specific" is read as (a) the module holds only ILA dataROIs, or (b) it holds all ILA dataROIs and most of its dataROIs are in ILA; the first part must hold under both, else the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Across GaoROIs, enrichment in low-rate, regular-firing category 1 units correlates positively with the intra-PFC hierarchy score of Gao et al.
claims.source: Figure 4g,h; Results, Toward an activity-defined map of the PFC, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Enrichment in low-rate, regular-firing units (category 1) was positively correlated with intra-PFC hierarchy (Fig. 4g )
claims.criterion: Units assigned to the 60 GaoROIs (polygons from Gao et al.; Zenodo 14205018 flatmap_PFCrois.h5); E-scores per GaoROI as for dataROIs; GaoROIs with at least 20 deep ww units (Extended Data Fig. 7i; > 20 as in the code is a variant) and a hierarchy score (ROI_Gao_hierarchy_index.csv), n = 30 (Fig. 4g legend). Pearson, two-sided. The r and p are in the figure only. Reproduced when r > 0 with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Across GaoROIs, enrichment in high-rate, bursty category 6 units correlates negatively with intra-PFC hierarchy.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 7n; Results, Toward an activity-defined map of the PFC, paragraph 3
claims.quote: while enrichment in high-rate, bursty units (category 6) was negatively correlated to intra-PFC hierarchy (Extended Data Fig. 7n )
claims.criterion: As fig4g-gao-category1 for category 6. Reproduced when r < 0 with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: GaoROIs 19, 20 and 41 in PL have exceptionally high hierarchy scores and the strongest category 1 enrichment, while GaoROI 23 in ventral ORBl has the lowest hierarchy score and the strongest category 1 depletion.
claims.source: Figure 4g; Results, Toward an activity-defined map of the PFC, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Specifically, GaoROIs (19, 20, 41) located in PL displayed exceptionally high hierarchy scores and the strongest enrichment in unit category 1, while the GaoROI (23) located in the ventral part of ORBl featured the lowest hierarchy score and most prominent depletion in unit category 1
claims.criterion: Among the GaoROIs of fig4g-gao-category1, GaoROI IDs as in Gao's table. Reproduced when GaoROIs 19, 20 and 41 are the three highest category 1 E-scores and GaoROI 23 the lowest; partially reproduced when at least two of 19, 20, 41 are in the top three or 23 is lowest. The hierarchy-score ranks are a property of the outside table, checked as a link.

claims.statement: Deep-layer PFC ww tone responses cluster into eight categories ordered by peak delay; most units have flat or negative responses (category 8), categories 1 to 4 have sharp peaks with consistent onsets, and categories 5 to 7 have variable onsets and persistent responses.
claims.source: Figure 5b; Extended Data Fig. 8a to c; Results, Tone response maps do not align with cytoarchitecture, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Most units displayed flat or negative response traces (category 8). Units belonging to tone response categories 1–4 exhibited well-defined peaks and consistent response peak onsets. In contrast, units belonging to tone response categories 5–7 had variable peak onset latencies and persistent responses
claims.criterion: PSTHs from tone response epochs (−2 to 0.7 s, dropping licking, sleep-like and saturation epochs), 0.5-ms bins, Gaussian kernel sd 10 ms, z-scored to the prestimulus window, units below 0.1 Hz overall or prestimulus dropped, 0 to 0.65 s trace; PCA over nw and ww units pooled, 8 components; SOM of 400 nodes on ww units (code somsettings_carlenResp.yml), Ward into 8 categories numbered by mean peak delay, the flat or negative category last (Methods). The units the SOM is trained on are open; readings (a) deep-layer ww units of all regions, n = 15,352 (Results, Tone response maps, paragraph 1); (b) all ww units of all regions and layers, as the code's runCresp*_brain settings (layerlist all). The claim is judged on the PFC deep-layer ww units with tone responses, n = 7,184 (Fig. 5 legend), under both readings. The code drops units beyond 5 sd on any component; shown as a variant. Reproduced when the category whose mean trace has no positive peak is the largest, and the across-unit spread (IQR) of ZETA onset times of significant units is smaller in each of categories 1 to 4 than in each of 5 to 7; partially reproduced when only the first holds. ZETA as in fig5e.

claims.statement: Tone-response enrichment maps of the PFC do not follow cytoarchitectural boundaries; the earliest-responding units (category 1) are enriched in anterior ACAd and ORBvl and parts of PL, and tone response modules reveal heterogeneity within subregions.
claims.source: Figure 5c,d; Extended Data Fig. 8d to f; Results, Tone response maps do not align with cytoarchitecture, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Units displaying the earliest responses (category 1) were enriched in anterior parts of ACAd and ORBvl and in parts of PL (Fig. 5c ). Neither this response map nor the maps of the other response types (categories 2–8) obeyed cytoarchitectural boundaries
claims.criterion: dataROI E-scores for tone categories, units as in fig5b, grouped by behavioral setting, reference population read both ways as in fig4cd-dataroi-enrichment. Ward into 4 tone modules (Extended Data Fig. 8e). Reproduced when at least one dataROI in each of ACAd, ORBvl and PL has a significant positive category 1 E-score, and the dataROIs of at least two subregions fall in more than one module. "Anterior" is not tested, as the flatmap's anterior axis is not given in the text.

claims.statement: Tone-responsive ww units (ZETA test) are enriched in spatial patches distributed across the PFC.
claims.source: Figure 5e; Results, Tone response maps do not align with cytoarchitecture, paragraph 2
claims.quote: classifying units as either tone-responsive or nonresponsive (Zenith of event-based time-locked anomalies (ZETA) test 32 ; Methods ) confirmed that tone-responsive units were enriched in spatial patches distributed across the PFC
claims.criterion: ZETA test on the 700 ms after tone onset, two-sided, responsive at P < 0.01 (Methods, ZETA test). The number of resamplings and the zetapy version are not given in the paper or the code (results are loaded from Zenodo); the zetapy default is a standard choice and the seed is fixed. dataROI E-scores for responsive against nonresponsive. Reproduced when significantly enriched dataROIs occur in at least three different subregions and at least one subregion holds both a significantly enriched and a significantly depleted dataROI.

claims.statement: In dataset IBL, of 16,148 PFC ww units, only 105 are tuned to visual stimulus side, 1,109 to choice and 2,868 to feedback.
claims.source: Results, Mapping task variables during goal-directed behavior, paragraphs 2 and 3; Fig. 5g
claims.quote: Only 105 of 16,148 PFC units were tuned to the position of the visual stimulus ... Choice-tuned units ( n = 1,109 units) ... Feedback-tuned units ( n = 2,868 units)
claims.criterion: Windows 0 to 0.1 s after stimulus, 0.1 s before to first wheel movement, 0 to 0.2 s after feedback; trials with first movement 0.08 to 2 s after stimulus (Methods). Combined-condition Mann-Whitney U within conditions of block and stimulus side (choice) or block and choice (stimulus, feedback), 2,000 within-condition shuffles; tuned when P < 0.05 and the unconditioned Mann-Whitney P < 0.001 (Methods). The code also requires the same preferred side in both tests and a combined statistic of at least 0.52; shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Across 73 IBL ROIs, choice-tuned units are enriched in a territory spanning central MOs, FRP and anterior ACAd, ORBvl and PL, and consistently depleted in ILA, ORBm, ORBl and ACAv; feedback-tuned units are enriched in AId, FRP and anterior MOs, ORBvl and PL, and depleted in ILA, ORBm and ACAd/ACAv; visual stimulus tuning is strongly enriched in a single IBL ROI in MOs.
claims.source: Figure 5g; Extended Data Fig. 9c; Results, Mapping task variables during goal-directed behavior, paragraphs 2 and 3
claims.quote: with a single IBL ROI in the MOs showing strong enrichment (Fig. 5g ). Choice-tuned units ( n = 1,109 units) were enriched in a spatially cohesive territory spanning central MOs, the FRP and the anterior parts of ACAd, ORBvl and PL; ILA, ORBm, ORBl and ACAv were consistently depleted in choice-tuned units (Fig. 5g ). Feedback-tuned units ( n = 2,868 units) were enriched in AId, FRP and anterior parts of MOs, ORBvl and PL, while they were depleted in ILA, ORBm and ACAd/ACAv
claims.criterion: IBL ROIs from the dataset IBL deep-layer PFC ww units, parcellated as in fig4b-dataroi-parcellation (Methods, Parcellation into ROIs of similar unit count). E-scores of tuned against untuned units per IBL ROI with at least 20 units, 1,000 shuffles (Methods); the grouping is not stated (readings as in fig5h-choice-gao-hierarchy; the code's 2,000 shuffles grouped by 'task', calc_statsdict_tuning.py, a variant). The text gives no rule for "enriched" or "depleted" in a territory; readings (a) a significant E-score of that sign, (b) an E-score of that sign. Enriched is judged per subregion as at least one IBL ROI of the subregion enriched; "consistently depleted" and "depleted" as every IBL ROI of the subregion with a negative E-score (under (a), none significantly positive and at least one significantly negative). Reproduced when every named subregion meets its part for choice and for feedback, and exactly one IBL ROI, in MOs, has a significant positive E-score for visual tuning, under both readings; partially reproduced when choice or feedback holds alone. "Anterior" and "central" are not tested, as the flatmap axes are not given in the text.

claims.statement: Across GaoROIs, enrichment in choice-tuned units correlates with the intra-PFC hierarchy score (R = 0.48, P = 0.002), while correlations are weak for visual tuning and absent for feedback tuning.
claims.source: Figure 5h; Extended Data Fig. 9d,f,g; Results, Mapping task variables during goal-directed behavior, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Enrichment in choice-tuned units correlated strongly with intra-PFC hierarchy score ( R = 0.48, P = 0.002; Fig. 5h and Extended Data Fig. 9d ), whereas correlations were weak for visual tuning and absent for feedback tuning
claims.criterion: Tuned units as in fig5g; E-scores per GaoROI with at least 20 units (Extended Data Fig. 9d) and a hierarchy score (n = 39), 1,000 shuffles as in Methods, Enrichment statistics (the grouping for dataset IBL is not stated; no grouping is one reading and grouping by recording a second; both shown). The code (calc_statsdict_gaoRois_tuning.py) uses 2,000 shuffles grouped by its 'task' label; shown as a variant. The R holds when within tolerance with P < 0.05 under a reading. Feedback "absent" is judged as a claim of absence, P >= 0.05 for the feedback correlation.

claims.statement: Enrichment in tone-responsive units does not correlate with intra-PFC hierarchy across GaoROIs.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 9e; Results, Mapping task variables during goal-directed behavior, paragraph 4
claims.quote: whereas correlations were weak for visual tuning and absent for feedback tuning and tone responsiveness (Extended Data Fig. 9e–g )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Pearson, two-sided, n = 29 GaoROIs (legend), E-scores of ZETA-responsive units (fig5e) per GaoROI. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05; r given.

claims.statement: No pair of PFC maps is strongly congruent, but the choice-tuning map is most similar to the spontaneous category 1 map, the feedback-tuning map to the category 6 map, and the tone-responsiveness map to the category 8 map.
claims.source: Figure 5i; Results, Relationship between spontaneous and evoked activity patterns at spatial and single-unit level, paragraphs 1 and 2
claims.quote: the map of choice-tuned units (Fig. 5g ) was most similar to the map of low-rate, regular-firing units (spontaneous category 1; Fig. 4c ) ... The map of feedback-tuned units was most similar to the map of high-rate, bursty units (spontaneous category 6), while the map of overall tone responsiveness (Fig. 5e ) was most similar to the map of low-rate, bursty units (spontaneous category 8; Fig. 4d )
claims.criterion: Each map rasterized on the PFC flatmap (311,563 pixels in the paper), each pixel taking the E-score of its ROI, cosine similarity between vectors (Results, Relationship between spontaneous and evoked activity patterns, paragraph 1). The code offers Gaussian blurring of the rasters; the unblurred map is the paper's text and is used. Pixels outside any analyzed ROI are left out. Reproduced for the dataset part when, among the eight spontaneous category maps, the tone-responsiveness map has its highest cosine with category 8; the choice and feedback parts, which use dataset IBL, are reported with this claim and hold when choice is highest with category 1 and feedback with category 6.

claims.statement: At the single-unit level, tone-responsive units (tone categories 1 to 7) are more often than expected high-rate spontaneous units (categories 4 to 6), and units without clear positive tone responses (category 8) tend to have low spontaneous rates (categories 1 to 3, 7 and 8).
claims.source: Figure 5j; Results, Relationship between spontaneous and evoked activity patterns at spatial and single-unit level, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Surprisingly, we found that tone-responsive units (tone response categories 1–7) were more likely than expected to have high spontaneous firing rates (spontaneous categories 4–6; Fig. 5j ). Conversely, units lacking clear positive tone responses (tone response category 8) tended to have low spontaneous firing rates
claims.criterion: Mutual enrichment with spontaneous category as population and tone category as attribute, 1,000 shuffles grouped by behavioral setting (Methods, Group-bias control); the code groups by region and setting, shown as a variant. Reproduced when the summed E-score of tone categories 1 to 7 is positive in each of spontaneous categories 4, 5 and 6, at least one significantly, and the tone category 8 E-score is positive in at least four of spontaneous categories 1 to 3, 7 and 8.

claims.statement: Units with choice tuning and units with feedback tuning are associated with high-rate, Poissonian spontaneous firing (category 4).
claims.source: Figure 5k; Results, Relationship between spontaneous and evoked activity patterns at spatial and single-unit level, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Similarly, analysis of goal-directed task variables revealed that units with choice tuning, as well as units displaying feedback tuning, were associated with high-rate, Poissonian firing (spontaneous category 4; Fig. 5k )
claims.criterion: Mutual enrichment of spontaneous category (IBL Passive units on dataset KI's ww SOM) as population against tuning as attribute (Methods, Mutual enrichment), 1,000 shuffles (Methods, Enrichment statistics). The Methods name no grouping for Fig. 5k; readings (a) no grouping, (b) the code's grouping by its 'task' label and region (calc_statsdict_tuning.py). The code's 2,000 shuffles are a variant, as the Methods give 1,000. Reproduced when choice-tuned and feedback-tuned units each have a significant positive E-score in spontaneous category 4, under both readings; readings that disagree block the claim as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Firing metric distributions do not differ significantly across behavioral settings.
claims.source: Methods, Habituation and behavioral settings
claims.quote: Importantly, although the mice were engaged in various behavioral tasks, firing metric distributions were not significantly different across behavioral settings
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, but the paper names no test in the text read; the Supplementary Methods, which may give it, were not read. The claim is blocked as methods_underspecified unless a reader answers with the paper's test. As a variant only, a mixed model Metric ~ 1 + Setting + (1|Mouse) per metric for ww units, with the size of the setting effects.

claims.statement: Electrophysiology was analysed for 48 BLA-projecting cholinergic and 46 BLA-projecting noncholinergic NBM/SI neurons from 27 mice (56 slices) and 46 BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons from nine macaques (38 slices); morphology for 31 mouse cholinergic and 44 mouse noncholinergic neurons.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 1; Table 1; Results 3.1, paragraph after Figure 1; Results 3.3, paragraph 3
claims.quote: In total, we obtained complete analyses of 94 BLA-projecting neurons (48 cholinergic and 46 noncholinergic for electrophysiology; 31 cholinergic and 44 noncholinergic for morphology) from 27 mice (56 slices) and 46 BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons from nine macaques (38 slices)
claims.criterion: Counts of neurons by species and group (Groups, opening comment) and of subjects. Counts are exact, as the dataset should hold the paper's neurons. For NC, both readings of the group (ChAT-negative only; with ChAT-unknown neurons added, as getindices.m does) are counted. Slices and sexes (mouse 18 male, 9 female; macaque 7 male, 2 female, Table 1) are reported where the dataset holds them.

claims.statement: In mouse, BLA-projecting cholinergic and noncholinergic NBM/SI neurons differ in 15 of the 18 electrophysiological features; spike width, upstroke and downstroke do not differ.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph after the Figure 2 legend; Figure 2D; Figure S2-2C
claims.quote: Cholinergic and noncholinergic BLA-projecting neurons within the region of the NBM/SI differed electrophysiologically in all but three features
claims.criterion: F1 to F18 (opening comment), every reading and variant computed; S per feature. Reproduced when, under one set of readings (the code's variants are shown but do not decide), 14 to 16 features differ and AP width, upstroke and downstroke (Fig. S2-2C) are among those that do not; partially reproduced when the count is in range but the features that do not differ are others. The p-values of all 18 are reported. F1 is counted only if it can be computed; if not, the count is out of 17 and the range becomes 13 to 15 (the paper reports F1 as different).

claims.statement: Mouse noncholinergic BLA-projecting neurons are more excitable than cholinergic ones, with a maximum firing rate about six times larger (39.0 +- 24.9 against 7.3 +- 4.3 Hz).
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph after the Figure 2 legend; Figure 2D
claims.quote: Overall, noncholinergic neurons were much more excitable than cholinergic ones, with a maximum firing rate almost six times larger (cholinergic 7.3 ± 4.3 Hz, noncholinergic 39.0 ± 24.9 Hz, p < 0.0001)
claims.criterion: F16 (Methods and code), S. Reproduced when the rank-sum p < 0.0001 with NC higher and the means are within tolerance. Partially reproduced when the test holds and a mean is outside tolerance. The 200 pA reading (Fig. S2-1 legend) is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Mouse cholinergic BLA-projecting neurons have a more depolarized spike threshold (-33 +- 4.6 against -37.1 +- 6.3 mV) and a larger rheobase (64.3 +- 41.2 against 42.2 +- 33.2 pA) than noncholinergic ones.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph after the Figure 2 legend; Figure 2D
claims.quote: spike threshold: cholinergic -33 ± 4.6 mV, noncholinergic -37.1 ± 6.3 mV, p < 0.001; rheobase current: cholinergic 64.3 ± 41.2 pA, noncholinergic 42.2 ± 33.2 pA, p < 0.001
claims.criterion: F6 and F5, S. Reproduced when both tests give p < 0.001 in the reported direction and the four means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when one feature holds. The SDs (4.6, 6.3, 41.2, 33.2) are reported against the paper's.

claims.statement: Mouse cholinergic BLA-projecting neurons have a larger AHP (28.9 +- 8.3 against 12.4 +- 6.1 mV) and a wider AHP (177.9 +- 89.3 against 85.0 +- 118.6 ms) than noncholinergic ones.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph after the Figure 2 legend; Figure 2D
claims.quote: AHP amplitude: cholinergic 28.9 ± 8.3, noncholinergic 12.4 ± 6.1 mV, p < 0.0001; AHP width: cholinergic 177.9 ± 89.3 ms, noncholinergic 85.0 ± 118.6 ms, p < 0.0001
claims.criterion: F12 and F14 with the Methods' window (rheobase step, 100 ms after threshold), S. Reproduced when both tests give p < 0.0001 with cholinergic larger and the four means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the tests hold and a mean is outside tolerance. The code's window (first step with two spikes) is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Mouse cholinergic BLA-projecting neurons have a higher adaptation index than noncholinergic ones (0.83 +- 0.56 against 0.64 +- 0.29).
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph after the Figure 2 legend; Figure 2D
claims.quote: with concomitant effects on spike frequency adaptation (adaptation index: cholinergic 0.83 ± 0.56, noncholinergic 0.64 ± 0.29, p < 0.05)
claims.criterion: F17 under both readings of the step (200 pA; the step with the most spikes), S. Reproduced when, under one reading, p < 0.05 with cholinergic higher and both means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the test holds under a reading and no reading puts both means within tolerance.

claims.statement: Mouse cholinergic BLA-projecting neurons have a more depolarized resting potential (-54.4 +- 8.4 against -58.7 +- 8.2 mV) and a longer membrane time constant (34.6 +- 14.3 against 22.3 +- 9.8 ms) than noncholinergic ones.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph after the Figure 2 legend; Figure 2D
claims.quote: Passive electrophysiological properties, such as resting membrane potential (cholinergic -54.4 ± 8.4 mV, noncholinergic -58.7 ± 8.2 mV, p < 0.05) and membrane time constant tau (cholinergic 34.6 ± 14.3, noncholinergic 22.3 ± 9.8 ms, p < 0.0001), also exhibited significant differences
claims.criterion: F1 under readings (a) and (b) as the dataset allows, and F4 on the -20 pA step (Methods), S. Each feature is judged alone; reproduced when both hold (test at the reported level in the reported direction, means within tolerance), partially reproduced when one does. If F1 cannot be computed, the claim is judged on tau and F1 is reported as untestable. The code's step for tau is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: In mouse, spike amplitude, the CV of interspike intervals and sag also differ between cholinergic and noncholinergic BLA-projecting neurons, with cholinergic neurons having larger spikes, a lower CV and a smaller sag.
claims.source: Figure S2-2A
claims.quote: Additional electrophysiological features that distinguish BLA-projecting, cholinergic from noncholinergic neurons and features that are shared in mouse NBM/SI
claims.criterion: F7, F18 (both step readings) and F2, S. The figure marks the bounds as p <= 0.001, 0.01 and 0.01; directions are read from the figure's box plots. Reproduced when each feature differs at its figure level in the stated direction (F18 under one reading); partially reproduced when one or two do.

claims.statement: A UMAP of the 18 electrophysiological features separates mouse cholinergic from noncholinergic BLA-projecting neurons almost completely, with only two neurons on the wrong side of the boundary.
claims.source: Results 3.1, last paragraph; Figure 2C
claims.quote: shows almost complete separation between the BLA-projecting cholinergic and noncholinergic neurons within the NBM/SI; only two neurons fall on the "wrong" side of the boundary
claims.criterion: U on F1 to F18 (the readings of F set by fig2-mouse-c-nc-15-of-18, the Methods' choices first) of the 48 C and 46 NC neurons. The boundary is open (opening comment, U); the measure is the number misclassified by a linear boundary in the two UMAP dimensions. Reproduced when, under both readings of missing values, the median over seeds is at most 2 and the separation beats every label permutation; not reproduced when it fails under both; methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The count is reported either way.

claims.statement: Mouse cholinergic and noncholinergic BLA-projecting neurons differ in 3 of 13 morphological features; cholinergic neurons have more branch points (8.1 +- 5.4 against 6.6 +- 5.4), a smaller total process area (4.6 +- 2.7 against 6.6 +- 3.6 x 10^3 um^2) and a smaller centripetal bias (12.9 +- 14.9 against 15.2 +- 10.1).
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figure 4D; Figure S4-1B
claims.quote: Three of the 13 features assayed were statistically significantly different ... cholinergic neurons had more branch points (cholinergic 8.1 ± 5.4, noncholinergic 6.6 ± 5.4, p < 0.05), a smaller total proximal process area ... and a smaller centripetal bias (cholinergic 12.9 ± 14.9, noncholinergic 15.2 ± 10.1, p < 0.05)
claims.criterion: The 13 stored morphological features (Methods 2.7), S. Reproduced when exactly these three differ at p < 0.05 and the six means are within tolerance. Partially reproduced when the three differ and other features also differ, or a mean is outside tolerance. The count tolerance is 0 because 10% of 3 is under one feature.

claims.statement: Sholl intersections as a function of distance from the soma do not differ between mouse cholinergic and noncholinergic BLA-projecting neurons.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figure S4-1A
claims.quote: On a standard Sholl analysis of intersections as a function of distance from the soma, cholinergic and noncholinergic neurons were also not significantly different
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The paper names no test for the Sholl curves; its only named test is the Wilcoxon rank-sum at p < 0.05 (Methods 2.8). Readings (a) a rank-sum at each 10 um radius from 10 to 200 um (the range of Fig. S4-1A), uncorrected, absence when no radius has p < 0.05; (b) a rank-sum on each neuron's total intersections over those radii. Reproduced when both find no difference, not reproduced when both find one, blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. The differences at each radius are reported.

claims.statement: A UMAP of the morphological features does not separate mouse cholinergic from noncholinergic BLA-projecting neurons.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figure 4C
claims.quote: Dimensionality reduction via PCA and subsequent display via UMAP likewise indicated that proximal neuritic morphology was similar between the two types of mouse BLA-projecting neurons
claims.criterion: U on the 13 morphological features of the 31 C and 44 NC neurons. The paper gives no test; the measure of U is used. Reproduced when, under each reading of missing values, the separation of the true labels is not better than that of 95% of the label permutations (p >= 0.05); not reproduced when it is, under both; methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The misclassified count is reported.

claims.statement: A linear discriminant analysis of the electrophysiological features clearly separates mouse cholinergic from noncholinergic BLA-projecting neurons.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph before the Figure 5 legend; Figure 5A
claims.quote: Given the clean separation between these groups on the unsupervised electrophysiological UMAP plot ... supervised LDA revealed a clear separation
claims.criterion: L on F1 to F18 of the 48 C and 46 NC neurons. Reproduced when the resubstitution accuracy exceeds that of 95% of the shuffles under both shuffle readings, for both scalings; not reproduced when it does under none; methods_underspecified when they disagree. The Fig. 5A legend says the populations separate "but not from the distribution of shuffled data", which contradicts the Results and the Fig. 5C legend; the Results are followed. The accuracy, and a 10-fold cross-validated accuracy as a variant, are reported.

claims.statement: AHP amplitude has the highest weight in the LDA separating mouse cholinergic from noncholinergic BLA-projecting neurons.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph before the Figure 5 legend; Figure 5B
claims.quote: The feature with the highest weight in the LDA vector was AHP amplitude
claims.criterion: L on F1 to F18 as in fig5a-mouse-lda-electrophysiology, z-scored. Reproduced when AHP amplitude ranks first under both readings of the weights (a) and (b); not reproduced when it ranks first under neither; methods_underspecified when they disagree. The top five under each reading are reported.

claims.statement: An LDA of the morphological features fails to separate mouse cholinergic from noncholinergic BLA-projecting neurons; the result is like that of shuffled features.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph before the Figure 5 legend; Figure 5C
claims.quote: By contrast, even supervised LDA failed to separate cholinergic and noncholinergic neurons morphologically ... Indeed, the distribution was equivalent to the LDA plots that resulted when feature values were randomly shuffled
claims.criterion: L on the 13 morphological features of the 31 C and 44 NC neurons. Reproduced when the resubstitution accuracy is not above that of 95% of the shuffles (p >= 0.05) under both shuffle readings; not reproduced when it is under both; methods_underspecified when they disagree.
