claims.statement: Macaque BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons are more excitable than mouse ones, with a maximum firing rate three times larger (26.3 +- 23.1 against 7.3 +- 4.3 Hz), a rheobase a third as large (23.3 +- 16.5 against 64.3 +- 41.2 pA) and an f-I slope twice as large (0.13 +- 0.10 against 0.06 +- 0.03 Hz/pA).
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph after the Figure 7 legend; Figure 7D
claims.quote: The maximum firing rate was three times larger (macaque 26.3 ± 23.1 Hz, mouse 7.3 ± 4.3 Hz, p < 0.0001), the rheobase current was only a third as large (macaque 23.3 ± 16.5 pA, mouse 64.3 ± 41.2 pA, p < 0.0001), and the slope of the f - I curve was twice as large (macaque 0.13 ± 0.10, mouse 0.06 ± 0.03, p < 0.0001)
claims.criterion: F16, F5 and F15, S, macaque C against mouse C. The mouse means of firing rate and rheobase are those of fig2d-mouse-max-firing-rate and fig2d-mouse-threshold-rheobase. Reproduced when all three tests give p < 0.0001 in the reported direction and the means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the tests hold and a mean is outside tolerance, or when two of the three tests hold.

claims.statement: Macaque BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons have a more hyperpolarized spike threshold (-39.7 +- 5.9 against -33.0 +- 4.6 mV), a smaller AHP (19.1 +- 8.8 against 28.9 +- 8.3 mV) and a narrower AHP (106.6 +- 71.9 against 177.9 +- 89.3 ms) than mouse ones.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph after the Figure 7 legend; Figure 7D
claims.quote: spike threshold: macaque -39.7 ± 5.9 mV, mouse -33.0 ± 4.6 mV, p < 0.0001) and in afterhyperpolarization properties (AHP amplitude: macaque 19.1 ± 8.8 mV, mouse 28.9 ± 8.3 mV, p < 0.0001; AHP width: macaque 106.6 ± 71.9 ms, mouse 177.9 ± 89.3 ms, p < 0.0001)
claims.criterion: F6, F12 and F14 (Methods' window; the code's as a variant), S, macaque C against mouse C. Reproduced when all three tests give p < 0.0001 in the reported direction and the macaque means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the tests hold and a mean is outside tolerance, or when two of the three tests hold.

claims.statement: Macaque BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons have wider spikes than mouse ones (1.32 +- 0.45 against 1.15 +- 0.43 ms).
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph after the Figure 7 legend; Figure S7-1C
claims.quote: Macaque neurons also differed from mouse neurons in basic spike shape (spike width: macaque 1.32 ± 0.45 ms, mouse 1.15 ± 0.43 ms, p < 0.01)
claims.criterion: F8, S. Reproduced when p < 0.01 with macaque wider and both means within tolerance; partially reproduced when the test holds and a mean is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: Macaque BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons also differ from mouse ones in spike amplitude, CV of interspike intervals, sag and upstroke, each larger in macaque, while the downstroke does not differ.
claims.source: Figure S7-1A and C
claims.quote: Population scatter plus box plots of additional features that differ in the action potential time course of BLA-projecting, NBM/SI cholinergic neurons from macaque ... Population scatter plus box plots showing features of AP width and Upstroke are distinct, but feature of downstroke is shared
claims.criterion: F7, F18 (both step readings), F2, F10 and F11 (both readings), S, macaque C against mouse C. The figure marks the bounds as p <= 0.01, 0.0001, 0.05 and 0.0001; directions are read from its box plots. The four differences are reproduced when each holds at its figure level in the stated direction (F18 under one reading); partially reproduced when two or three do. The shared downstroke is a claim of absence on the rank-sum at p < 0.05, judged under both F11 readings (methods_underspecified if they disagree); a downstroke difference makes the claim at most partially reproduced.

claims.statement: Most of the 18 electrophysiological features differ between macaque and mouse BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons; the text gives the number as 15 of 18, and the figure legends imply 17.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph after the Figure 7 legend; Figure 7D legend; Figure S7-1
claims.quote: In all, 15 of the 18 electrophysiological features were insignificantly different between macaque and mouse
claims.criterion: The sentence as printed (15 not different, so 3 different) is contradicted by the same paragraph, which reports 7 features that differ; it is read as a slip. Readings of the count of differing features (a) 15, the sentence with "insignificantly" read as "significantly"; (b) 17, from the legends (12 features "that distinguish" in Fig. 7D, 3 in Fig. S7-1A, AP width and upstroke in Fig. S7-1C; downstroke shared). F1 to F18 as in fig2-mouse-c-nc-15-of-18, S. Reproduced when the count is within 10% of either reading (14 to 16, or 16 to 18 capped at 18); not reproduced below 14. Fig. 7D itself could not be read (no PDF), so which 12 features it shows is not known; the per-feature p-values are reported.

claims.statement: Macaque BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons have a larger input resistance and a smaller rheobase than mouse ones, the opposite of what larger cells would show.
claims.source: Discussion 4.2, paragraph 3; Figure 7D
claims.quote: If macaque neurons were simply larger than mouse neurons, everything else kept constant, one would predict that their input resistances would be smaller and their rheobase currents larger. However, in fact, the opposite is true in both cases
claims.criterion: F3 (the -20 pA step; the code's slope as a variant) and F5, S. The paper gives no values for input resistance; Fig. 7D, which shows it, could not be read. Reproduced when the macaque input resistance is higher at p < 0.05 and the rheobase lower at p < 0.05; partially reproduced when one holds.

claims.statement: A UMAP of the 18 electrophysiological features shows a strong separation between macaque and mouse BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons.
claims.source: Results 3.3, last paragraph; Figure 7C; Discussion 4.3, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The resulting 2D UMAP plot is given in Figure 7C . It exhibits a strong separation between groups
claims.criterion: U on F1 to F18 (as in fig2-mouse-c-nc-15-of-18) of the 46 macaque and 48 mouse C neurons. "Strong" is not quantified. Readings (a) as clean as the paper's "almost complete separation" of Fig. 2C, at most 2 of the 94 neurons misclassified (median over seeds); (b) separation better than every label permutation. Reproduced when (a) and (b) hold under both readings of missing values; methods_underspecified when (b) holds and (a) does not, or when the readings of missing values disagree; not reproduced when (b) fails under both.

claims.statement: Macaque BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons have a larger convex hull than mouse ones, in volume (2.19 +- 1.63 against 0.94 +- 0.77, units below), area (1.15 +- 0.59 against 0.83 +- 0.45 x 10^5 um^2) and sphericity (0.65 +- 0.08 against 0.51 +- 0.09).
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph after the Figure 8 legend; Figure 9D
claims.quote: Most notably, those related to convex hull were different (convex hull volume: macaque 2.19 ± 1.63 × 10 3 ... convex hull sphericity: macaque 0.65 ± 0.08, mouse 0.51 ± 0.09, p < 0.0001)
claims.criterion: Stored convex hull volume, area and sphericity (Methods 2.7), S. The volume's unit is open: the text prints x 10^3 um^3, while the axis of Fig. S4-1B (the same mouse neurons) is x 10^6 um^3; both readings are compared. Reproduced when the three tests hold at the reported levels with macaque larger and the means are within tolerance (volume under one reading); partially reproduced when the tests hold and a mean is not.

claims.statement: Of the 13 morphological features, five (text) or six (Figure 9 legend) differ between macaque and mouse BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons; the other seven are similar.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph after the Figure 8 legend; Figure 9 legend; Figure S9-1B
claims.quote: five of the 13 measured parameters exhibited significant differences
claims.criterion: The 13 stored features, S. The text says five, the Figure 9 legend six ("differ from those in mouse in six of the 13 morphological parameters"), and Fig. S9-1B shows seven not marked (centripetal bias, root angle, total process area, primary and first-order process numbers, total process length and its normalized form), which leaves six. Readings 5 and 6. Reproduced when the count is 5 or 6 and none of the seven features of Fig. S9-1B differs; partially reproduced when the count is 5 or 6 but the set differs.

claims.statement: The proximal arbors of macaque BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons tend to have fewer branch points than those of mouse.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 2; Figure 9D
claims.quote: the soma-proximal arbors of macaque BLA-projecting NBM/SI cholinergic neurons tend to have fewer branch points and occupy larger 3D space than those of mouse
claims.criterion: Stored number of branch points, S. No value or p-value is printed and Fig. 9D could not be read; the claim is that it is among the differing features. Reproduced when macaque has fewer branch points at p < 0.05; not reproduced otherwise. The normalized branch points are reported as well.

claims.statement: In a UMAP of the morphological features, macaque neurons tend to cluster away from mouse neurons, but the separation is weak compared with the electrophysiological UMAP.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph before Figure 10; Figure 9C
claims.quote: There was a tendency for macaque neurons to cluster away from mouse neurons ... but the effect of clustering based on morphology alone was weak
claims.criterion: U on the 13 morphological features of the 52 macaque and 31 mouse neurons, and on the electrophysiological features as in fig7c-macaque-mouse-umap-separation. Reproduced when the morphological separation is better than 95% of label permutations and its misclassified fraction is larger than the electrophysiological one (same seeds, same reading of missing values), under both readings of missing values; partially reproduced when only the second holds; methods_underspecified when the readings of missing values disagree.

claims.statement: Combining the 18 electrophysiological and 13 morphological features separates macaque from mouse BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons, in a UMAP and clearly in an LDA, unlike shuffled data.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph before Figure 10; Figure 10A and B
claims.quote: Examination of combined morphoelectric features distinguishes macaque versus mouse basal forebrain neurons despite common projection target, anatomical location, and cholinergic phenotype ... Note the clear separation in clustering of the two populations from one another and its distinct nature from the distribution of shuffled data
claims.criterion: The 46 macaque and 27 mouse cholinergic neurons with both. LDA (L, both scalings): the resubstitution accuracy exceeds that of 95% of the shuffles under both shuffle readings. UMAP (U): separation better than every label permutation, under both readings of missing values. Reproduced when both hold; partially reproduced when the LDA holds and the UMAP does not; methods_underspecified when the shuffle or missing-value readings disagree.

claims.statement: The features with the highest LDA weights separating macaque from mouse are convex hull (morphology) and rheobase, AHP width and maximum firing rate (physiology).
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph before Figure 10; Figure 10C
claims.quote: The features with the highest weight in the LDA vector analysis differentiating macaque from mouse were convex hull in morphology and rheobase, AHP width, and maximum firing rate in physiology
claims.criterion: L as in fig10-combined-separation, z-scored. "Convex hull" may name any of its three features. Readings of the ranking (i) the four highest weights are rheobase, AHP width, maximum firing rate and one convex hull feature; (ii) the same, with the three convex hull features taken together as one (their largest weight). Each under weights (a) and (b). Reproduced when one ranking reading holds under both weight readings; not reproduced when no ranking reading holds under either; methods_underspecified when the weight readings disagree. The top eight weights are reported.

claims.statement: Sholl intersections as a function of distance from the soma are similar in macaque and mouse BLA-projecting cholinergic neurons.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph after the Figure 8 legend; Figure S9-1A
claims.quote: Although many morphological features were similar
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the Sholl counts of the 52 macaque and 31 mouse cholinergic neurons. The sentence cites only Fig. S9-1A (Sholl intersections against sphere radius, no difference marked). The paper names no test for the Sholl curves; readings as in figs4-1a-mouse-sholl-not-different, (a) a rank-sum at each 10 um radius from 10 to 200 um, uncorrected, (b) a rank-sum on each neuron's total intersections over those radii. Reproduced when both find no difference at p < 0.05, not reproduced when both find one, methods_underspecified when they disagree. The differences at each radius are reported.

claims.statement: The dataset holds 104 experiments (gerbils) with 1160 single auditory nerve fibres; 60 young-adult (32 female), 13 middle-aged (7 female) and 31 old (11 female) gerbils, with 759, 87 and 314 single units.
claims.source: Data Records, Files that help users search through the dataset, paragraph 2; Table 1
claims.quote: The dataset consists of 104 experiments, with a total of 1160 single auditory nerve fibres ... Number of animals (number of females) 60 (32) 13 (7) 31 (11) ... Total number of single units 759 87 314
claims.criterion: Counts of the records a data descriptor says it deposits, so the tolerance is zero, not the default 10%; any difference is reported with the units or animals it concerns. Animals are counted by animal ID (files of one experiment split in sequence numbers are one animal, as check_dataset_metadata.m merges them); age groups by age in days as the code defines them (young <= 365, middle > 365 and <= 1095, old > 1095). A unit counts towards its animal's group. Reproduced when all eleven counts match; partially reproduced when the totals match and a group count differs.

claims.statement: Mean ages of the groups are 5.5, 22.5 and 38.3 months, mean ABR thresholds 18.1, 34.2 and 49.0 dB SPL, and mean weights 74.6, 83.4 and 86.4 g (young adult, middle aged, old).
claims.source: Table 1
claims.criterion: As check_dataset_metadata.m computes them, over animals (one value per animal), ignoring missing values, with age in months as days / (365/12) and the code's age groups. The SDs and ranges of Table 1 are reported beside the means; the outcome rests on the means alone, as the statement does. Reproduced when all nine means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when at least six are.

claims.statement: Best frequencies range from 428 to 15,825 Hz in young adults, 350 to 15,091 Hz in middle-aged and 620 to 15,762 Hz in old gerbils.
claims.source: Table 1
claims.quote: Range of best frequency in Hz 428–15,825 350–15,091 620–15,762
claims.criterion: As check_dataset_metadata.m computes it, a unit's BF is its stored BF.analysis.bf, or its CF.analysis.cf when it has no BF recording; the group's range is the minimum and maximum over its units. Each reported range is widened by 10% of each bound (young 385 to 17,408 Hz; middle 315 to 16,600 Hz; old 558 to 17,338 Hz). Reproduced when, for every group, the minimum lies within 10% of the reported lower bound and the maximum within 10% of the reported upper bound; partially reproduced when that holds for two of the three groups.

claims.statement: ABR thresholds rise with age, and hearing loss varies widely among the old animals.
claims.source: Data Records, Files that help users search through the dataset, paragraph 2; Figure 3; Table 1
claims.quote: a rough estimate of hearing sensitivity, as determined by the auditory brainstem response (ABR) to chirps (0.3–19 kHz), is plotted as a function of the animal’s age (Fig. 3 ). Note the large variability in age-related hearing loss among the old animals
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test; its support is Table 1. Over animals, with the code's age groups, reproduced when the mean ABR threshold increases from young to middle aged to old and the SD of old animals is the largest of the three (Table 1 gives 5.3, 10.2 and 18.0 dB). The range of old thresholds is reported (Table 1, 20 to 85 dB SPL).

claims.statement: Old gerbils are skewed towards males (11 of 31 female), which the paper attributes to ovarian cancer and early death of old females.
claims.source: Data Records, Files that help users search through the dataset, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Note the slightly skewed distribution of quiet-aged gerbils towards more males
claims.criterion: Reproduced when fewer than half the old animals are female and the fraction is lower than in young adults (Table 1, 32 of 60). The cause (ovarian cancer) is not tested.

claims.statement: Of the 104 gerbils, 78 received additional oxygen throughout the experiment.
claims.source: Methods, Surgical procedures, Anaesthesia, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Of the total of 104 gerbils, 78 received additional oxygen (flow 1.5 l/min) in front of the tracheotomy or snout throughout the experiment
claims.criterion: A count of a metadata field (exp.info.anesthesia.oxygen, as read by check_dataset_metadata.m), so the tolerance is zero. Counted once per animal.

claims.statement: Responses to paired noise bursts were recorded in 21 of 104 experiments, Schroeder-phase stimuli in 5, and consonant-vowel-consonant logatomes in 17.
claims.source: Methods, Data acquisition, Complex acoustic stimuli, paragraph 1
claims.quote: in 21 of 104 experiments, responses to two 1-s noise bursts were recorded ... in 5 of 104 experiments, responses to Schroeder-phase harmonic tone complexes ... In 17 of 104 experiments, responses to consonant-vowel-consonant logatomes were recorded
claims.criterion: As check_dataset_metadata.m counts them, an experiment counts when at least one of its units has a non-empty NOISE, SPS or CVC recording. Counts, tolerance zero.

claims.statement: CF recordings were obtained for 119 fibres, CLICK for 261, SR for 203, NOISE for 143, SPS for 22 and CVC for 135.
claims.source: Figure 7 legend
claims.quote: For fibres for which a CF recording was obtained (n = 119) ... For fibres for which a CLICK recording was obtained (n = 261) ... For fibres for which a SR recording was obtained (n = 203) ... NOISE (n = 143, panel d ), SPS (n = 22, panel e ), and CVC (n = 135, panel f )
claims.criterion: Counted as check_dataset_units.m prints them. CF, units with a non-NaN stored CF; CLICK, units with exactly one CLICK recording and a non-NaN 2-bin latency; SR, units with a non-NaN stored SR from an SR recording; NOISE, SPS and CVC, units with a non-empty recording of that type. Counts, tolerance zero. A second reading counts units with any recording of the type, whatever its analysed value; reproduced when every count matches under one reading, partially reproduced when four of six do.

claims.statement: No SR, SPS or CVC recordings were obtained in middle-aged gerbils, and SPS responses were recorded only in young adults.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Sampling across best frequency for the different recording types, paragraph 1; Figure 7c to 7f
claims.quote: No SR, SPS, and CVC recordings were obtained in middle-aged gerbils, while SPS responses were only recorded in young-adult gerbils
claims.criterion: With the code's age groups, reproduced when no middle-aged unit has an SR, SPS or CVC recording and no middle-aged or old unit has an SPS recording.

claims.statement: Units with multiple inter-spike intervals below 0.6 ms, the absolute refractoriness of auditory nerve fibres, were excluded from the dataset.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Verification of single-unit recording and specificity to the auditory nerve bundle, paragraph 1; Figure 4b
claims.quote: Units with multiple inter-spike intervals <0.6 ms, which is the absolute refractoriness of auditory nerve fibres ... were excluded from the dataset
claims.criterion: Inter-spike intervals are taken within trials, between successive spike times of a trial, as checkAN.m does. The paper does not say over which recordings a unit's ISIs are counted, nor fix "multiple"; the readings are (a) any single recording of the unit with two or more ISIs < 0.6 ms, (b) two or more ISIs < 0.6 ms pooled over all the unit's recordings, (c) as (a) for the BF recording only, the one shown in Fig. 4. checkAN.m counts the ISIs < 0.6 ms of one recording, which is closest to (a) and (c). These readings concern a method detail, so the outcome is the one they all give - reproduced when no unit fails under any of them, not reproduced when units fail under all of them, otherwise blocked as methods_underspecified. The number of failing units under each reading and the distribution of their counts of short ISIs are reported.

claims.statement: No median spike waveform showed a prepotential, which would mark a ventral cochlear nucleus bushy cell.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Verification of single-unit recording and specificity to the auditory nerve bundle, paragraph 2, first criterion; Figure 4d
claims.quote: We did not encounter any prepotentials in our recordings
claims.criterion: The paper's check was a visual inspection of the median waveform (checkAN.m); it and its code give no quantitative rule for a prepotential. The claim cannot be judged by a criterion fixed from the paper and is blocked as methods_underspecified unless a reader can supply one.

claims.statement: Rate-level functions were checked for atypical shapes (auditory nerve rate-level functions are typically straight, sloping saturating or flat saturating), and units whose rate-level function was nonmonotonic at levels below 80 dB SPL were excluded.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Verification of single-unit recording and specificity to the auditory nerve bundle, paragraph 2, second criterion; Figure 5a
claims.quote: When a rate-level function showed nonmonotonicity at levels lower than 80 dB SPL, it indicated that the spikes derived from a non-primary cell receiving inhibitory input. The unit was then excluded from the dataset
claims.criterion: The check was visual ("carefully checked for atypical shapes"); the paper and its code give no rule for nonmonotonicity. The claim cannot be judged by a criterion fixed from the paper and is blocked as methods_underspecified unless a reader can supply one. As a description only, the number of units whose stored RLF mean rate falls between successive levels below 80 dB SPL by more than the stored standard deviation is reported.

claims.statement: The example fibre of Fig. 5b (animal G220908, unit 3p_181) had a best frequency of 7.6 kHz and a threshold of 19 dB SPL.
claims.source: Figure 5b legend
claims.quote: This fibre had a best frequency of 7.6 kHz and a threshold at 19 dB SPL
claims.criterion: The stored BF.analysis.bf and RLF.analysis.threshold of the unit. The legend's other details (BF recording at 30 dB SPL with 5 repetitions, RLF recording at 40 dB SPL with 10 repetitions) are reported as found.

claims.statement: Fibres of young-adult gerbils show two regions of best sensitivity separated by a region around 3 to 4 kHz with higher thresholds and fewer fibres; the highest thresholds are at 3.5 kHz.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Consistency with data from other labs, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 6a
claims.quote: Fibres of young-adult gerbils exhibited two regions of best sensitivity (lowest thresholds), separated by a frequency region (around 3–4 kHz) with slightly less sensitive and fewer fibres ... For the young-adult gerbils in the current dataset, highest thresholds were at 3.5 kHz
claims.criterion: As check_dataset_units.m builds the Fig. 6a moving average, young-adult units with a stored BF and RLF threshold, mean threshold in 24 logarithmic BF bins from 0.3 to 20 kHz (edges logspace(log10(0.3), log10(20), 25) kHz, a bin includes its upper edge), each plotted at its upper edge, so "at 3.5 kHz" is the bin from 2.92 to 3.48 kHz. The text does not say whether "highest" is over all bins or within the mid-frequency region; readings (a) the largest bin mean over all bins; (b) the largest bin mean between the two sensitive regions, that is a local maximum flanked on each side by bins with lower means. Reproduced when, under one reading, the highest bin mean is in the bin plotted at 3.48 kHz, with bins of lower mean threshold on both sides (two regions of best sensitivity). The code's bins are the resolution of the figure, so the neighbouring bins (plotted at 2.92 and 4.14 kHz) count as partially reproduced. All bin means and counts are reported.

claims.statement: Among young-adult fibres, the fewest best frequencies fall in the bin bordered by 2.5 and 3.0 kHz.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Consistency with data from other labs, paragraph 2; Figure 6b
claims.quote: fewest fibres were in the bin bordered by 2.5 and 3.0 kHz (Fig. 6b )
claims.criterion: The histogram of check_dataset_units.m, stored BF.analysis.bf of young-adult units, 24 logarithmic bins with edges logspace(log10(200), log10(20000), 25) Hz; the bin the text names is the one from 2423 to 2936 Hz. The empty bins outside the recorded BF range cannot be meant, so readings (a) the bin has the fewest units of all bins between the lowest and the highest non-empty bin (ties allowed); (b) the bin is a local minimum, with fewer units than both its neighbours. Reproduced when (a) holds; partially reproduced when only (b) holds. All bin counts are reported.

claims.statement: Among high-frequency fibres (BF above 3.5 kHz) there is a cluster with low spontaneous rates, and low-frequency fibres have a bimodal distribution of spontaneous rate with modes near 5 and 60 spikes/s.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Consistency with data from other labs, paragraph 3; Figure 6c
claims.quote: Among the high-frequency fibres (>3.5 kHz), there was a cluster of fibres with low spontaneous rates ... The low-frequency fibres show a bimodal distribution of spontaneous rate, with a mode around 5 spikes/s and one around 60 spikes/s
claims.criterion: Young-adult units (Fig. 6c plots them only, in check_dataset_units.m), BF from the stored BF.analysis.bf, spontaneous rate as the code's best estimate (SR recording, else PH, else RLF, else BF), split at BF 3.5 kHz (<= 3500 Hz low, > 3500 Hz high), in the code's histogram of 5 spikes/s bins from 0 to 200 spikes/s. The tolerances are the bin width set by the code - the lower mode must be one of the bins 0 to 5 or 5 to 10, the upper one of the bins from 50 to 70 (60 plus or minus 10%, widened to the bin edges). The paper does not say how a mode is found; the reading is the two largest local maxima of that histogram (a bin with more units than both neighbours, or the first bin when it exceeds the second), separated by a bin with fewer units than both. For the high-BF cluster, the paper's low-SR cutoff is 18 spikes/s (Fig. 6d legend); the paper does not define a cluster, and the reading is that the histogram of high-BF units has its largest local maximum below 18 spikes/s. Reproduced when both parts hold; partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: The highest best frequency at which significant phase locking was recorded in young-adult gerbils was 4.6 kHz.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Consistency with data from other labs, paragraph 4; Figure 6d
claims.quote: The maximum best frequency at which significant phase locking was recorded in young-adult gerbils was 4.6 kHz
claims.criterion: Young-adult units with a PH recording and a stored BF.analysis.bf; a unit phase locks significantly when any level's PH.analysis.prob is not NaN and below 0.001 (Methods; check_dataset_units.m). The value is the largest BF among them.

claims.statement: The highest vector strengths are found among fibres with low best frequencies (below 1.5 kHz) and low spontaneous rates (below 18 spikes/s).
claims.source: Technical Validation, Consistency with data from other labs, paragraph 4; Figure 6d
claims.quote: the highest vector strength values were found among the fibres with low best frequencies (<1.5 kHz) and low spontaneous rates (<18 spikes/s, shown in open markers Fig. 6d )
claims.criterion: Maximum vector strength per unit as check_dataset_units.m takes it (largest PH.analysis.vs over levels with prob not NaN and < 0.001), SR as the code's best estimate, BF from BF.analysis.bf. The paper does not say which age groups the sentence covers (it follows a sentence on young adults; Fig. 6d plots all three) or how "highest values" is judged. Readings, each for young adults alone and for all ages - (a) the unit with the largest maximum vector strength has BF < 1.5 kHz and SR < 18 spikes/s; (b) of the four groups the two cutoffs form, the median maximum vector strength is highest in the low-BF low-SR group. Reproduced when every reading holds; when they differ, blocked as methods_underspecified with all shown.

claims.statement: Characteristic frequency from the CF recordings correlates strongly with best frequency from the BF recordings, with no systematic deviation towards higher or lower frequencies.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Sampling across best frequency for the different recording types, paragraph 1; Figure 7a
claims.quote: these figures confirm that the characteristic frequency derived from the CF recordings correlated strongly with the best frequency derived from the BF recordings, with no systematic deviation towards higher or lower frequencies (Fig. 7a )
claims.criterion: Units with stored CF.analysis.cf and BF.analysis.bf, all ages, as Fig. 7a plots them on logarithmic axes against y = x. The paper reports no test, coefficient or threshold for "strongly". The correlation of log CF with log BF (Pearson, and Spearman as a variant) is reported with its p-value; the deviation is the median of log2(CF/BF) with a 95% bootstrap interval (10,000 resamples, a standard choice). Reproduced when the correlation is positive with p < 0.05 and the median CF/BF ratio lies within 10% of 1 (the default tolerance applied to the y = x line). "Strongly" is judged from the reported coefficient only.

claims.statement: Click latency is strongly negatively correlated with best frequency, reflecting the travelling wave delay along the cochlea.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Sampling across best frequency for the different recording types, paragraph 1; Figure 7b
claims.quote: Click latency had a strong negative correlation to best frequency, illustrating the travelling wave delay along the cochlea (Fig. 7b )
claims.criterion: Units with exactly one CLICK recording, a non-NaN stored latency_2bins and a stored BF, all ages (check_dataset_units.m, type 3). The paper reports no test; Fig. 7b plots latency against log BF. The Pearson correlation of latency with log BF is reported, with the Spearman correlation as a variant. Reproduced when both are negative with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The best-frequency distributions of the units with CF and with CLICK recordings are representative of the distribution of the full dataset.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Sampling across best frequency for the different recording types, paragraph 1; Figure 7a and 7b
claims.quote: BF distributions of two large datasets, CF and CLICK (Fig. 7a,b , respectively), are representative of the distribution of the full dataset (Fig. 6b )
claims.criterion: The paper gives no test, and Fig. 6b, which it compares with, shows young adults only while Figs. 7a and 7b show all ages. Readings - the reference is (i) young-adult BFs, as in Fig. 6b, or (ii) all units' BFs; the comparison is (a) a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of log BF, subset against the reference, finding no difference at p < 0.05, or (b) the subset's median BF within 10% of the reference's median. Reproduced when every reading holds for both CF and CLICK; not reproduced when none does; otherwise blocked as methods_underspecified with all shown.

claims.statement: Successful single-fibre recordings were obtained in 43% of old gerbils that were tried, against 88% of young adults.
claims.source: Background & Summary, paragraph 3
claims.quote: successful recordings of single auditory-nerve fibres were obtained in only 43% of the experimental old gerbils (compared to 88% in young adults)
claims.criterion: The denominators are animals that were operated on but gave no single units; the paper does not say they are in the dataset, which holds animals with recorded fibres. The claim needs those animals; whether the dataset lists them is the author's to find.

claims.statement: Responses to tones at 20 and 30 dB above threshold were examined for non-primary-like shapes, using BF, RLF and PH recordings combined when available, and units with clearly non-primary-like responses were excluded.
claims.source: Technical Validation, Verification of single-unit recording and specificity to the auditory nerve bundle, paragraph 2, third criterion; Figure 5b
claims.quote: The responses to tones at 20 and 30 dB above threshold were examined for non-primary-like shapes. When the response was clearly non-primary like, the unit was excluded from the dataset
claims.criterion: The check was visual; makePSTH.m builds the PSTH of BF, RLF and PH responses at or near a level above threshold (TestLevel), but the paper and its code give no rule for a non-primary-like shape. The claim cannot be judged by a criterion fixed from the paper and is blocked as methods_underspecified unless a reader can supply one.

claims.statement: The dandiset's files are the recordings the paper's Source Data index assigns to figure panels, so that example panels can be found by file name.
claims.source: Data availability; Source Data file, sheet "Raw data in Dandi_Archive"; dandiset description
claims.quote: The voltage imaging data generated in this study are on the DANDI archive under accession code 001266
claims.criterion: Files are matched by the name in the index's column "File name on DandiArchive" against the dandiset's subject and session names. Reproduced when every file the index names is found; partially reproduced when at least half are; not reproduced otherwise. Where the index's file name and the legend's label differ (Fig. 2 "D1 stim" is listed as file ..._D3; Fig. 3 lists files D1, D2, D4, soma and D4+soma for the legend's D2, soma and Soma + D2), the file for each panel is the one whose trial and event counts match the legend (54 trials each; Fig. 2, 8 dSpikes; Fig. 3 D2, 49 -dSpikes and 35 +dSpikes; soma, 161 and 6; Soma + D2, 116 and 54; Fig. S8a, 80 and 12; Fig. S8c-d D4, 85 and 11). The readings for the legend's D2 are (a) file D2 and (b) file D4 (the combined file is named D4+soma); both are reported.

claims.statement: In the Fig. 2 neuron, stimulation of proximal oblique dendrites evoked two somatic spikes per trial; in most trials the distal dendrites showed only an attenuated copy, and in 8 of 54 trials a single rapid dSpike, always on the second somatic spike.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 1; Figure 2a, 2c
claims.quote: Each stimulus evoked two spikes at the soma ... in some cases (8 of 54 trials), the dendrites produced a single rapid spike ... the dendritic excitations always emerged from the second somatic spike, never the first
claims.criterion: In the Fig. 2 recording (index entry "branch_stim (Fig.2)"), bAPs and dSpikes are counted per trial as in the shared method, distal region > 300 µm (legend). Reproduced when the count is within tolerance under both filter readings and no dSpike follows the first somatic spike of a trial.

claims.statement: Spike amplitudes have a unimodal distribution at the soma and a bimodal one in the distal dendrite.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 1; Figure 2b
claims.quote: A histogram of event amplitudes in the soma and dendrites showed a unimodal distribution at the soma and a clearly bimodal distribution in the distal dendrites
claims.criterion: The paper names no test of modality. For the Fig. 2 recording, the amplitude (-dF/F at the bAP's peak) of every bAP at the soma and in the distal region (> 300 µm). Readings, from the figure (a histogram with a threshold between two groups) and two standard tests, (a) Hartigan's dip test, p < 0.05 for the distal amplitudes and p >= 0.05 for the soma; (b) a two-component Gaussian mixture preferred over one component by BIC in the distal amplitudes and not at the soma. Reproduced when both readings agree that the distal distribution is bimodal and the somatic one is not; when they differ, methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: bAPs without a dSpike are confined to the soma and proximal dendrites, while bAPs with a dSpike are amplified in the distal dendrites.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 2; Figure 2e, 2f
claims.quote: In the -dSpike trials the bAP was primarily confined to the soma and proximal apical and basal dendrites ... In the +dSpike trials, the depolarization was amplified in the distal dendrites
claims.criterion: For the Fig. 2 recording, spike-triggered averages of -dF normalized by dF_ref (the fluorescence change during the passive return to baseline, Methods; Fig. 1d legend, mean from 10 to 20 ms after the spike) along the apical trunk in 10-pixel segments (Methods, Kymographs). Reproduced when the -dSpike average at > 300 µm is below half its value at the soma and the +dSpike average at > 300 µm is at least its value at the soma. The paper gives no number; half and equal are the readings of "confined" and "amplified" used here, and the ratios are reported.

claims.statement: The peak amplitude of bAPs without a dSpike decays exponentially along the apical trunk with a length constant of 255 ± 10 µm (mean ± s.e.m., 93 spikes).
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 2; Figure 2h
claims.quote: Plots of the peak spike amplitude along the apical trunk showed exponential decay of the -dSpike events (length constant 255 ± 10 μm, mean ± s.e.m., n = 93 spikes)
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the paper's s.e.m. The amplitude (-dF/F_ref) of each -dSpike bAP in 10-pixel segments along the trunk is fitted with an exponential in distance from the soma, one fit per spike, and the length constants are averaged. Open, as the paper does not say, (1) which 93 spikes; readings (a) the -dSpike bAPs of the Fig. 2 recording, (b) the -dSpike bAPs of all Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 recordings of that neuron; (2) the fit; readings (a) A exp(-x/lambda), (b) A exp(-x/lambda) + c. Reproduced when the mean is within tolerance under one reading of (1) for both readings of (2), and each reading is shown.

claims.statement: Subthreshold depolarization follows the stimulus location and decays smoothly outside it; dSpikes never initiated in the dendrites.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 3; Figure 3d-f, S10, S11
claims.quote: We only observed diffusive-like propagation of the subthreshold voltages, never dSpikes that initiated in the dendrites.
claims.criterion: In the branch, soma and soma plus dendrite recordings, every dSpike is checked for a somatic spike whose peak precedes the distal peak (shared method, item 3). Reproduced when no dSpike lacks a preceding somatic spike.

claims.statement: Neurons produced only two kinds of excitation, perisomatic bAPs and distal dSpikes, and neither spatial profile depended on which dendrite was stimulated.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 4; Figures S9 to S11
claims.quote: the neurons produced precisely two kinds of excitations ... neither spatial profile depended on the location of the driving stimulus
claims.criterion: The paper names no measure. For the neuron of Figs. 2, 3 and S8 (index entries branch_stim), the -dSpike and the +dSpike spike-triggered amplitude profiles along the trunk (-dF/F_ref, 10-pixel segments) for each stimulus location. Reproduced when, for each class, every pair of locations' profiles has Pearson r >= 0.9 and the +dSpike profiles all exceed the -dSpike profiles beyond 300 µm. The threshold 0.9 is a reading of "precisely two kinds", not the paper's; the correlations are reported.

claims.statement: The amplitude of dSpikes relative to the first bAP peaks in the distal trunk, 313 ± 41 µm from the soma (mean ± s.d., 22 stimulated regions, 17 neurons).
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 4; Figure 3g, 3h
claims.quote: was maximum in the distal dendritic trunk (313 ± 41 µm from the soma, mean ± s.d., n = 22 stimulated regions (soma or proximal branch), 17 neurons, 15 animals
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the paper's s.d. For each recording with soma or proximal (< 200 µm) stimulation, dF_1 is the amplitude of the first bAP after stimulus onset and dF_max the amplitude of a later dSpike (Fig. 3h legend) in each trunk segment; the distance of the segment with the largest ratio is taken, and the mean over stimulated regions is compared. Open, the paper does not say whether ratios are of trial averages or averaged over trials; readings (a) ratio of the averages, (b) average of single-trial ratios. Reproduced when the mean is within tolerance under both.

claims.statement: Later bAPs that carry a dSpike have a larger amplitude ratio to the first bAP than later bAPs without one.
claims.source: Figure 3g
claims.quote: g Amplitude ratio of later bAPs to the first bAP (∆F max /∆F 1 ). Data sorted by the presence ( + dSpike) vs. absence (-dSpike) of dSpike.
claims.criterion: Per stimulated region (soma or proximal < 200 µm, 22 regions), the mean ratio at the distal region for later bAPs with and without dSpikes. The paper reports no test; the Methods' paired two-tailed t-test across regions is applied. Reproduced when the +dSpike ratio is higher with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: bAPs propagate along the apical trunk at 141 ± 30 µm/ms (mean ± s.d., 17 neurons).
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 4; Figure S12
claims.quote: Mean propagation velocity of bAPs along the apical trunk was 141 ± 30 µm/ms (mean ± s.d., n = 17 neurons, 15 animals
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the paper's s.d. Per neuron, with soma stimulation (Fig. S12a), the time of each spike's peak along the trunk; sub-frame timing by SNAPT (Methods, time at 50% of the local maximum from a quadratic spline fit to the spike-triggered average). Open, how velocity is taken from the delays; readings (a) the slope of a line fitted to distance against delay, (b) the mean of segment-wise distance over delay. Reproduced when the mean over neurons is within tolerance under both readings. The Source Data (sheet Supplementary Fig 12) gives the 17 per-neuron values for comparison.

claims.statement: In the Fig. 3 neuron, soma stimulation never evoked dSpikes on the first two bAPs and evoked one on the third bAP in 6 of 54 trials.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 5; Figure 3e
claims.quote: Stimulation of the soma alone never evoked dSpikes on the first two bAPs, and occasionally evoked a dSpike on the third bAP (6 of 54 trials)
claims.criterion: The soma recording of the Fig. 3 neuron (index entry "branch_stim (Fig.3)", file ..._soma). Reproduced when no first or second bAP carries a dSpike and the count is within tolerance.

claims.statement: In the Fig. 3 neuron, stimulation of distal dendrite D2 evoked a dSpike on the first bAP in 35 of 54 trials (65%).
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 5; Figure 3d
claims.quote: Stimulation of distal dendrite D2 alone evoked dSpikes on the first bAP, with 65% probability (35 of 54 trials
claims.criterion: The recording for the legend's D2 is identified as in source-data-index (readings, file D2 or file D4). Reproduced when the count is within tolerance under the reading whose total counts match the legend; when neither matches, both are shown and the claim is methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: In the Fig. 3 neuron, simultaneous soma and D2 stimulation gave two quick bAPs without dSpikes and then a third bAP that evoked a dSpike in all 54 trials.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 5; Figure 3f
claims.quote: Simultaneous stimulation at soma and D2 produced two quick bAPs which failed to evoke dSpikes, and then the third bAP (12 – 17 ms after stimulus onset) triggered a dSpike with 100% probability (54 of 54 trials
claims.criterion: The combined recording (file ..._D4+soma). Reproduced when the count is within tolerance and at most 10% of first and second bAPs carry a dSpike.

claims.statement: The probability that the first bAP evokes a dSpike rises sigmoidally with the distance of the stimulus from the soma, reaching a plateau of about 80% beyond 300 µm, and is near zero for stimuli within 200 µm.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 5; Figure 3i
claims.quote: Proximal stimuli ( < 200 μm from the soma) almost never evoked dSpikes on the first bAP ... the probability of evoking a dSpike with the first bAP followed a sigmoidal distance dependence, with a plateau of ~80% success rate for stimuli > 300 µm from the soma
claims.criterion: For each of the 35 dendrite stimulations, the fraction of trials whose first bAP carries a dSpike, against the distance of the stimulus from the soma (Fig. 3i legend). Open, the paper does not say how the distance of a stimulus region is taken or what the plateau is; readings for distance, (a) the centroid of the stimulus polygon's eYFP fluorescence, (b) the point of the polygon nearest the soma; readings for the plateau, (a) the upper asymptote of a logistic fit, (b) the mean probability of stimuli beyond 300 µm. Reproduced when every reading gives a plateau within tolerance and the mean probability for stimuli within 200 µm is below 10% (a reading of "almost never", not the paper's number).

claims.statement: dSpikes arise if and only if the distal dendrites have been depolarized for at least 15 ms before the bAP arrives.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 6
claims.quote: dSpikes arose if and only if the distal dendrites had been depolarized for at least 15 ms prior to arrival of a bAP.
claims.criterion: The paper states the rule from its examples and gives no test. For every bAP in the branch, soma and soma plus dendrite recordings, the time the distal region (> 300 µm) has been depolarized before the bAP, from the first frame after stimulus onset at which the stimulus-triggered average distal -dF exceeds 2 s.d. of its pre-stimulus baseline (a standard onset choice). Reproduced when at least 90% of dSpikes follow >= 15 ms of distal depolarization and at least 90% of bAPs that follow < 15 ms fail; the full table is reported.

claims.statement: Under a gradual optogenetic ramp to the soma or proximal dendrites, the first somatic spike almost always evokes a dSpike (92%).
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 7; Figure S13
claims.quote: For this stimulus waveform, the first somatic spike almost always evoked a dSpike (92%, 188 ramps, 56 cells, 44 animals
claims.criterion: The ramp recordings (3 s linear ramps, soma or proximal < 150 µm). The text says 188 ramps and the Fig. S13d legend "92% out of 225 bAPs". Readings, (a) the fraction of ramps whose first bAP carries a dSpike, (b) the fraction of all first bAPs counted over recordings including repeats. Reproduced when one reading is within tolerance; both are shown.

claims.statement: In the Fig. 4a neuron, a step stimulus to a proximal apical dendrite evoked a bAP without a dSpike, then two bAPs with dSpikes, then a series of bAPs without dSpikes.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 1; Figure 4a
claims.quote: a step stimulus to a proximal apical dendrite evoked a bAP without a dSpike, then two bAPs with dSpikes, then a series of bAPs without dSpikes
claims.criterion: The recording of index entry "branch_adaptation (Fig.4a)". Reproduced when the sequence of failures and dSpikes in at least one trial is failure, dSpike, dSpike, then only failures, and the most common sequence over trials is reported.

claims.statement: Under step stimulation dSpikes fail for the first 18 ± 7 ms, succeed until 83 ± 47 ms after onset, and then fail (mean ± s.d., 43 stimulated branches, 16 cells).
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 1; Figure 4b
claims.quote: dSpikes failed for the first 18 ± 7 ms (mean ± s.d.), then there was a period where dSpikes succeeded which lasted until 83 ± 47 ms after stimulus onset, followed by subsequent dSpike failures
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.d. The step recordings (> 200 ms, soma or proximal dendrites). Open, the paper does not say how the two times are taken per branch; readings, (a) per stimulated branch, the time of the first and of the last dSpike in each trial, averaged over trials, then mean over branches; (b) per branch, the first and last time at which the trial-pooled dSpike fraction per 10 ms bin is above zero. Reproduced when both means are within tolerance under both readings.

claims.statement: Sustained somatic spiking produced very few dSpikes later than 100 ms after stimulus onset, whatever the stimulus strength or location.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 1; Figure 4b
claims.quote: Sustained spiking at the soma led to very few dSpikes later than 100 ms after stimulus onset, regardless of stimulus strength or location.
claims.criterion: In the step recordings, the percent of bAPs carrying a dSpike before and after 100 ms from onset (Fig. 4b bottom). Reproduced when the later percent is below one fifth of the earlier and below 10% (a reading of "very few"); both percents are reported.

claims.statement: Wide-field optogenetic stimulation evoked a period-doubling bifurcation, bAPs alternately succeeding and failing to evoke dSpikes, with all bAPs after about 180 ms failing (9 cells).
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 3; Figure 4c-e
claims.quote: this stimulus reliably evoked a period-doubling bifurcation ... ( n = 9 cells from 9 animals, Fig. 4c, d ). The dSpike window persisted to ~180 ms after stimulus onset, but, despite the stronger stimulus, all bAPs after ~180 ms failed to evoke dSpikes
claims.criterion: In the wide-field recordings, bAP frequency from inter-peak intervals and amplitude normalized to the mean of the final 5 bAPs of the epoch (Methods, Period doubling; Fig. 4e). Alternation holds in a cell when successive normalized amplitudes alternate above and below 1 for at least 4 consecutive bAPs (the alternating motif of Fig. 4e right). Reproduced when at least 7 of 9 cells alternate and the time of the last dSpike, averaged over cells, is within tolerance. The paper gives neither number; 4 consecutive bAPs and 7 of 9 cells are readings of "alternately" and "reliably", not the paper's, and the counts are reported.

claims.statement: In the Fig. 4c-d neuron, the first 12 bAPs under wide-field stimulation showed two bAP failures followed by alternating dSpikes and failures.
claims.source: Figure 4d
claims.quote: Amplitude maps of the first 12 bAPs showing two bAP failures, followed by alternating dSpikes and bAP failures.
claims.criterion: The recording of index entry "branch_bifurcation (Fig.4c,d)". Reproduced when the first 12 bAPs read failure, failure, then alternate dSpike and failure, in at least one trial.

claims.statement: Even stronger wide-field stimuli evoked an epoch of seemingly random interplay of bAPs and dSpikes, varying from trial to trial while somatic spiking stayed regular, followed by sustained dSpike failures.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 3; Figure S15
claims.quote: Even stronger stimuli evoked an epoch of seemingly random interplay of bAPs and dSpikes (Fig. S15 ), followed by sustained dSpike failures.
claims.criterion: The recording of index entry "period_doubling (Fig. S15)". Reproduced when the sequence of dSpikes and failures differs between at least two trials while somatic spike times stay within 2 ms of each other across trials for the same bAP index, and later bAPs fail.

claims.statement: With somatic current pulses at 3 Hz, distal bAP amplitudes attenuate progressively, without dSpikes.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 2; Figure S14d
claims.quote: At low frequencies (e.g., 3 Hz), membrane depolarization did not accumulate sufficiently to trigger dSpikes; instead, we observed a progressive attenuation of bAP amplitudes in the distal dendrites
claims.criterion: In the patch clamp pulse recordings (2 nA, 2 ms), the distal (> 300 µm) -dF/F of each spike relative to the last spike at 3 Hz (Fig. S14d, 29 recordings). The paper reports no test; the Methods' paired two-tailed t-test is applied to the first against the last spike's distal amplitude across recordings. Reproduced when the first exceeds the last with p < 0.05 and no dSpike is found at 3 Hz.

claims.statement: With somatic current pulses at 80 Hz or more, bAPs first fail, then a series of dSpikes arises, then failures again.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 2; Figure S14e, f
claims.quote: At frequencies ≥ 80 Hz, however, we observed a characteristic motif of bAP failure, then a series of dSpikes, and then failures again
claims.criterion: Maximum distal amplitude per frequency normalized to each dataset's minimum (Fig. S14e), and the sequence of successes at 80 Hz (Fig. S14f). Reproduced when dSpikes occur at 80 Hz and above and not below, and the 80 Hz sequence in most recordings starts with at least one failure and ends with failures.

claims.statement: BaCl2 (150 µM) increased the dSpike probability under soma stimulation from 11 ± 2% to 64 ± 10% (mean ± s.e.m., 9 cells).
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 4; Figure S16e-g
claims.quote: BaCl 2 : 11 ± 2% before to 64 ± 10% after, mean ± s.e.m., n = 9 cells from 6 animals, p < 0.001, paired t-test
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e.m. dSpike probability is the percent of bAPs carrying a dSpike (Source Data column "dSpike (%)"), per cell, for 20 or 30 ms soma stimuli at 5 Hz (59 repeats). Reproduced when both means are within tolerance and a two-sided paired t-test gives p < 0.001 for an increase. The Source Data sheet gives per-cell values.

claims.statement: 4-AP (5 mM) increased the dSpike probability from 19 ± 4% to 92 ± 4% (mean ± s.e.m., 4 cells).
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 4; Figure S16b-d
claims.quote: 4-AP: 19 ± 4% before to 92 ± 4% after, mean ± s.e.m., n = 4 cells from 3 animals, p < 0.001, paired t-test
claims.criterion: As figs16-ba-increases-dspikes. The text gives p < 0.001 and the legend p = 0.001; reproduced when both means are within tolerance and a two-sided paired t-test gives p <= 0.001 for an increase. Note that the example recording of the index ("after_4AP (Fig.S16c)") is named TTX20nM+4AP5mM.

claims.statement: Low TTX (20 nM) did not affect somatic spiking but decreased the dSpike probability from 44 ± 15% to 11 ± 8% (mean ± s.e.m., 4 cells).
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 4; Figure S17a-d
claims.quote: This low TTX dose did not affect spiking at the soma, but the mean dSpike probability was significantly decreased (control: 44 ± 15%, TTX: 11 ± 8%, mean ± s.e.m., n = 4 cells from 3 animals, p = 0.008, paired t-test
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e.m. dSpike probability as figs16-ba-increases-dspikes, for stimuli over about 100 µm across the soma and proximal dendrites (20 ms, 5 Hz, 59 to 118 repeats). Reproduced when both means are within tolerance and a two-sided paired t-test gives p < 0.05 for a decrease; the number of somatic spikes per stimulus before and after is reported.

claims.statement: At 100 nM, TTX eliminated distal dSpikes while somatic spiking continued.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 4; Figure S17e
claims.quote: In some experiments, a higher concentration of TTX (100 nM) eliminated all dSpikes at distal dendrites, while preserving somatic spiking
claims.criterion: The example of index entries "after_TTX (100nM; Fig.S17e)" and its baseline. Reproduced when the 100 nM recording has somatic spikes and no distal dSpike, while the baseline has dSpikes.

claims.statement: The CaV blocker Ni2+ (100 to 500 µM) did not affect dSpikes.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 4; Figure S18a-e
claims.quote: The dSpikes were not affected by addition of the Ca V blocker Ni 2+ (100-500 µM; Fig. S18a–e ), suggesting that they are not mediated by VGCCs.
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The legend names no test; the Methods' test for paired treatment data is the two-sided paired t-test at 0.05 (n = 5 cells from 4 animals), on dSpike probability as figs16-ba-increases-dspikes. Which Ni2+ concentration Fig. S18e pools is not said (the example has 100 and 500 µM). The Source Data sheet for Fig. S18e gives the per-cell values the paper tested; the recordings whose dSpike probabilities match them are the ones tested. Where they cannot be matched, the readings are (a) the highest concentration each cell received, (b) 100 µM, (c) 500 µM, all run. Reproduced when the test gives p >= 0.05 on the matched recordings, or under every reading; when the readings disagree, methods_underspecified. The mean change is reported either way.

claims.statement: Under strong drive, dSpikes occasionally triggered broad (> 20 ms) dendritic spikes; Ni2+ (500 µM) eliminated them while preserving dendritic Na+ spikes, and reduced their frequency significantly (6 cells).
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 4; Figure S18f-h
claims.quote: Addition of Ni 2+ (500 μM) eliminated these broad spikes, confirming their dependence on VGCC activation.
claims.criterion: Putative Ca2+ spikes are distal depolarizations lasting > 20 ms (Fig. S18f legend), counted per ramp (3 s), mean of three trials per cell, pooled from the wide-field and the Ba2+ ramp experiments (Fig. S18h legend). Open, how duration is measured; readings (a) full width at half maximum, (b) time above the dSpike threshold. Reproduced when under both readings the count falls with Ni2+ with p < 0.05 in a two-sided paired t-test and dSpikes remain under Ni2+.

claims.statement: Adding Ba2+ (150 µM) increased the incidence of putative dendritic Ca2+ spikes under soma-targeted ramp stimulation.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 4; Figure S18g
claims.quote: Addition of K V blocker Ba 2+ (150 µM) to otherwise untreated neurons increased the prevalence of putative Ca 2+ spikes
claims.criterion: The example of index entries "baseline (Fig.S18g)", "after_Ba2+ (Fig.S18g)" and "after_Ba2+_NiCl (Fig.S18g)", with Ca2+ spikes as in figs18-ni-blocks-calcium-spikes. Reproduced when the count is higher after Ba2+ than at baseline and lower again after Ni2+.

claims.statement: In the multi-compartment CA1 model, step stimulation at the soma gives a dSpike motif of failure, success, success, failures, and wide-field stimulation gives alternating successes and failures followed by repeated failures.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 5; Figure 4f, 4g
claims.quote: a simulated step-wise optogenetic stimulation at the soma led to a dSpike motif of failure, success, success, failures ... Simulated wide-field optogenetic stimulation with the same model parameters evoked a period-doubling bifurcation with alternating dSpike successes and failures, followed by repeated failures
claims.criterion: Supplementary Software 1 run as provided with the Table 1 parameters; a bAP succeeds when the compartment 500 µm from the soma peaks above -40 mV (Methods, Parameter fitting). Reproduced when the soma run gives the motif and the wide-field run alternates and then fails.

claims.statement: In the model, the accelerometer motif of bAP failure, dSpikes, then failure persists over a wide range of dendritic NaV density, NaV slow inactivation, A-type KV density and stimulus strength.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 6; Figure S20c-e
claims.quote: the spike-rate accelerometer motif of bAP failure, dSpikes, and then failure persisted over a wide range of parameters
claims.criterion: The parameter sweeps of Supplementary Software 1 (Model Robustness, parameters_list.py) with the -40 mV at 500 µm rule. Reproduced when the motif occupies a contiguous region in each of the three phase diagrams that includes the Table 1 parameters.

claims.statement: In the model, a 2 nA dendritic current injection evokes dendrite-localized sodium spikes, while optogenetic stimulation of the same dendrite evokes a somatic spike first that then back-propagates, explaining the absence of dendrite-initiated dSpikes in the experiments.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 3; Figure S20a, b
claims.quote: the absence of dendrite-initiated dSpikes in our experiments was likely due to the more gradual, weaker, and spatially distributed nature of optogenetic vs. patch clamp stimuli
claims.criterion: The "Oblique Patch Clamp and Optogenetic Stimulus" runs of Supplementary Software 1. Reproduced when the current injection peaks first in the stimulated dendrite and the optogenetic stimulus peaks first at the soma.

claims.statement: A two-compartment Izhikevich model reproduces the opening and closing of the dSpike window under soma stimulation and period-doubling under combined soma and dendrite stimulation.
claims.source: Results, Dendritic spike-rate accelerometer, period-doubling, and stochastic back-propagation, paragraph 6; Figure S21
claims.quote: which also captured the opening and closing of the dSpike window (i.e. spike-rate accelerometer) and the period-doubling under simultaneous distal and proximal stimulation
claims.criterion: Two_compartment_Izhikevich.m with the Methods' parameters (gs = 0.16, gD = 0 for soma only; gs = 0.3, gD = 0.05 combined; vrs = -55 and initial u_D = -13), and as a variant with the script's own (-65, -18). Reproduced when the soma run gives dendritic failure, spikes, then failure, and the combined run alternates, under the Methods' parameters.

claims.statement: Combining soma optogenetic stimulation with EFS of distal synaptic inputs evoked a long-lasting (about 120 ms) dendritic plateau potential and a burst of somatic spikes, unlike either stimulus alone.
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 2; Figure 5a
claims.quote: Remarkably, combining optogenetic and electrical stimuli evoked a long-lasting ( ~ 120 ms) plateau potential in the dendrites and a burst of spikes on top of a strong subthreshold depolarization at the soma
claims.criterion: The recording of index entry "Plateau_induction (Fig.5a)". Duration is the time the distal (> 200 µm) -dF stays above half its peak (a standard measure; the paper names none). Reproduced when the combined stimulus gives a duration within tolerance, more somatic spikes than the optogenetic stimulus alone, and neither single stimulus gives a distal event lasting over 60 ms.

claims.statement: The distal AUC for combined stimulation was on average 3.1 ± 0.7-fold the sum of the AUCs for optical and EFS stimuli alone (mean ± s.e.m.), and more than twice that sum in 15 of 28 cells.
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 3; Figure 5b
claims.quote: The average AUC combined was 3.1 ± 0.7-fold greater than AUC optical + AUC electrical (mean ± s.e.m.) and for more than half of the cells studied (15 of 28 cells from 12 animals)
claims.criterion: Tolerance of the mean is the paper's s.e.m. AUC as in the shared method (both window readings), at a distal dendrite > 200 µm, with 30 ms soma stimulation and one 0.1 ms EFS pulse. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under both window readings; when the window readings disagree, methods_underspecified. The Source Data sheet Figure 5 gives per-cell values.

claims.statement: Nonlinear amplification was greatest when optical and electrical stimuli overlapped; for EFS before bAPs it fell sigmoidally, by half in 87 ms, and for EFS after bAPs exponentially with a 35 ms time constant.
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 3; Figure 5c, 5d
claims.quote: For ‘EFS before bAPs’, the amplification followed a sigmoidal profile, decaying by half in 87 ms. For ‘EFS after bAPs’, the amplification decayed exponentially with a time constant of 35 ms.
claims.criterion: Per cell (8 cells, 30 ms stimulus), combined AUC against dTime, scaled to [0, 1] (Methods; Fig. 5d legend). Fits to the pooled points, an exponential from -245 to 0 ms and a sigmoid from 0 to +245 ms (legend). The legend's fit ranges place EFS after bAPs at negative dTime; the file names (interval_-100ms and so on) are read the same way. Open, the fits' forms; readings (a) exp(dTime/tau) and 1/(1 + exp((dTime - t_half)/k)), both without offset, (b) the same fitted to the per-time means. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under both readings and the per-time mean is highest at the dTime nearest 0 (stimuli overlapping, Results paragraph 3); when the readings disagree, methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: A single bAP (10 ms soma stimulus) did not evoke a nonlinear dendritic response at any timing relative to EFS (5 cells).
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 4; Figure 5c, 5d
claims.quote: Triggering a single bAP by a 10 ms optogenetic stimulus targeted to the soma did not evoke a nonlinear dendritic response, regardless of timing relative to the EFS
claims.criterion: Per cell and dTime, combined AUC over AUC optical plus AUC electrical, as fig5b-supralinear-auc. The paper's threshold for a nonlinear response is "> 200% nonlinearity" (Results, paragraph 3). Reproduced when no cell's ratio exceeds 2 at any dTime.

claims.statement: During a 3 s optogenetic ramp, EFS early (0.5 s) evoked plateau potentials but EFS late (2.5 s, somatic rate 24 ± 4 Hz) did not (AUC 5.6 ± 3.6 against 1.6 ± 1.0, mean ± s.d.).
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 5; Figure 5e, 5f
claims.quote: The early EFS reliably evoked plateau potentials (AUC 5.6 ± 3.6, mean ± s.d.), whereas the late EFS, which occurred when the average spike rate was 24 ± 4 Hz (mean ± s.d.), did not (AUC 1.6 ± 1.0, mean ± s.d., n = 7 cells from 5 animals, p = 0.01, paired t-test
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.d. The AUC unit is not given (the Source Data label is "Area (a.u.)"); the Source Data sheet Figure 5 gives per-cell values, and the AUCs here are compared with them in the same units after the same integration. Open, the sample, 7 cells (text) or 8 (legend); both are run. Reproduced when, under one sample and both window readings, the means are within tolerance and a two-sided paired t-test gives p < 0.05 for early above late; when the window readings disagree, methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Under a weak 3 s optogenetic step, EFS at 0.5 s and at 2.5 s were equally effective at inducing plateau potentials (AUC 4.5 ± 2.0 and 4.0 ± 2.0, mean ± s.d., p = 0.19).
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 5; Figure 5g, 5h
claims.quote: In this case EFS at 0.5 s and at 2.5 s were equally effective at inducing plateau potentials (0.5 s: AUC 4.5 ± 2.0, mean ± s.d., 2.5 s: AUC 4.0 ± 2.0, mean ± s.d., p = 0.19, n = 7 cells from 5 animals, paired t-test
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's two-sided paired t-test at 0.05, on the 7 cells of the text, with the legend's 8 as a variant. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; the mean difference is reported either way.

claims.statement: Blocking NMDARs with D-AP5 (50 µM) reduced the plateau area to 42 ± 7% of baseline, against 107 ± 5% for vehicle (mean ± s.e.m.).
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 6; Figure 6a, 6b
claims.quote: Block of NMDARs by D-AP5 (50 µM) reduced the plateau area to 42 ± 7% of baseline ( n = 6 cells from 5 animals, mean ± s.e.m.) compared to vehicle control (107 ± 5% of baseline, n = 11 cells from 8 animals; p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA with Bonferroni’s post hoc test
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e.m. Per cell, combined-stimulus (30 ms soma, 0.1 ms EFS) AUC after treatment over AUC before (Methods, % baseline), at > 200 µm. A one-way ANOVA over vehicle, D-AP5, TTX and Ni2+ with Bonferroni post hoc tests against vehicle. Reproduced when the means are within tolerance and the D-AP5 comparison has p < 0.001.

claims.statement: Blocking VGCCs with Ni2+ (100 µM) largely eliminated the plateau potential (18 ± 5% of baseline, mean ± s.e.m.).
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 6; Figure 6a, 6b
claims.quote: Block of voltage-gated Ca 2+ channels (VGCCs) by Ni 2+ (100 µM) largely eliminated the plateau potential (AUC 18 ± 5% of baseline, n = 4 cells from 4 animals, mean ± s.e.m.
claims.criterion: As fig6-dap5-reduces-plateau; reproduced when the mean is within tolerance and the Ni2+ comparison has p < 0.001.

claims.statement: Blocking dendritic NaV channels with TTX (20 nM) also eliminated plateau potentials (26 ± 8% of baseline, mean ± s.e.m.).
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 8; Figure 6a, 6b
claims.quote: Block of dendritic Na V channels by TTX (20 nM) also eliminated plateau potentials (AUC 26 ± 8% of baseline, n = 4 cells from 3 animals, mean ± s.e.m.
claims.criterion: As fig6-dap5-reduces-plateau; reproduced when the mean is within tolerance and the TTX comparison has p < 0.001.

claims.statement: The drugs' effects on the plateau were much larger than their effects on the AUC for EFS or optogenetic stimulation alone.
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 8; Figure S24
claims.quote: The drug effects on the plateau were much larger than their effects on the AUC for EFS or optogenetic stimulation alone
claims.criterion: The Fig. S24 legend does not say which response its p-values compare; the readings are (a) the combined response, (b) each response. Per cell and drug, AUC after over AUC before for optical alone, EFS alone and combined. Reproduced when for every drug the mean fall of the combined AUC exceeds the mean fall of each single-stimulus AUC, and the combined comparison has p < 0.05 in a two-sided paired t-test.

claims.statement: Subtracting the somatic signal from the dendritic signal reveals a slowly rising and falling dendritic depolarization lasting up to about 300 ms after the optogenetic stimulus, which drives the high-frequency somatic firing.
claims.source: Results, Plateau potentials are evoked by collision of synaptic inputs and dSpikes, paragraph 9; Figure S23
claims.quote: This procedure revealed the slowly rising and falling dendritic depolarization (presumably dominated by VGCC and NMDAR currents) which persisted for up to ~300 ms after the end of the optogenetic stimulus to the soma
claims.criterion: In the combined-stimulus recordings (Fig. S23, 9 neurons), -dF/F at the dendritic region with the largest plateau minus that at the soma. Persistence is the time after the 30 ms stimulus ends until the difference returns within 2 s.d. of its pre-stimulus baseline (a standard choice). Reproduced when the longest persistence over cells is within tolerance and the difference is positive in most cells.

claims.statement: Cooling from 34 to 24 °C increased the dSpike probability (first bAP 0% against 29 ± 16%; any bAP 16 ± 3% against 50 ± 12%, mean ± s.e.m., 6 cells).
claims.source: Methods, Slice preparation, paragraph 2; Figure S25f, g
claims.quote: We observed a significant increase in dSpike probability at 24 °C (0% vs. 29 ± 16% by the first bAP, p = 0.09; 16 ± 3% vs. 50 ± 12% by any bAP, p = 0.02; mean ± s.e.m., n = 6 cells from 4 animals, paired t-test)
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e.m.; a reported 0% needs a count of 0. Soma stimulation 30 ms at 5 Hz. "By the first bAP" is the percent of trials whose first bAP carries a dSpike. "By any bAP" is open; readings (a) the percent of all bAPs carrying a dSpike, (b) the percent of trials with a dSpike on any bAP. Reproduced when, under one reading, all four values are within tolerance and the any-bAP increase has p < 0.05 in a two-sided paired t-test.

claims.statement: Optopatch-V expression did not change resting potential, rheobase, capacitance, input resistance or spike rates relative to neighboring non-expressing neurons.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 2; Figure S1
claims.quote: No significant difference was found between the groups (p > 0.05, two-sided paired Student’s t-test).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's two-sided paired t-test at 0.05 for each property (16 pairs of an expressing and a neighboring non-expressing cell). Rheobase is the smallest 500 ms step that evokes a spike (Methods). Reproduced when no property gives p < 0.05; the differences are reported.

claims.statement: Optical recording at 1 kHz detected every spike up to 90 Hz with no false positives or negatives (7 cells, 2212 spikes), with a single-trial noise-equivalent voltage of 1.2 ± 0.5 mV (2.5 ± 0.8 mV at 2 kHz) and sensitivity of about 12% dF/F per 100 mV.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 2; Figure S2
claims.quote: The single-trial optical noise-equivalent voltage was 1.2 ± 0.5 mV at 1 kHz and 2.5 ± 0.8 mV at 2 kHz (mean ± s.d., n = 7 neurons, 4 animals) ... with zero false-positives or false-negatives up to the maximum observed spike rate of 90 Hz (n = 7 cells, 2212 spikes)
claims.criterion: The paired patch and imaging recordings listed in the index for Fig. S2 (7 cells). The paper does not define the noise-equivalent voltage; readings, (a) the s.d. of the bleach-corrected subthreshold fluorescence divided by the dF/F per mV from the -70 to +20 mV step (Fig. S2d), (b) the s.d. of the difference between the optical trace scaled to mV and the patch trace down-sampled to the frame rate (Fig. S2a), in subthreshold periods. Optical spikes are matched to patch spikes within one frame. Reproduced when all values are within tolerance (tolerances are the paper's s.d. or 10%).

claims.statement: Fluorescence changes for a step from -70 to +20 mV were the same at 1 kHz and 2 kHz.
claims.source: Figure S2d
claims.quote: Fluorescence changes upon a voltage step from -70 to +20 mV were the same for 1 kHz vs. 2 kHz camera frame rates (p > 0.05, two-sided paired Student’s t-test)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's two-sided paired t-test at 0.05, on dF/F at +20 mV per cell at the two frame rates. Reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Dosimetry by eYFP fluorescence had 7.8-fold lower variance than dosimetry by blue laser power (0.084 against 0.66).
claims.source: Figure S3f
claims.quote: Dosimetry via eYFP fluorescence had 7.8-fold lower variance than did dosimetry via raw blue laser power (0.084 vs. 0.66, n = 18 cells and 6 animals; p = 9.9 x 10-5, F-test)
claims.criterion: Per cell, slopes of charge against blue intensity and against cumulative eYFP in the linear regime (I < 1 mW/mm2), each normalized to its group mean (legend). Reproduced when both variances are within tolerance and an F-test of equal variances gives p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Patterned optogenetic stimuli are localized; somatic photocurrent fell to half when stimuli were offset by 11 ± 4 µm and to 20% at 23 ± 7 µm (10 cells), and dendritic responses fell to half at 11 ± 5 µm and to 20% at 34 ± 14 µm (29 branches) (mean ± s.d.).
claims.source: Results, paragraph 2; Figure S4d, S4h
claims.quote: The induced photocurrent fell to half maximum when stimuli were offset by 11 ± 4 μm and to 20% of maximum at 23 ± 7 μm ... Evoked responses, |∆F|, fell to half maximum for stimuli at 11 ± 5 μm offset and to 20% of maximum at 34 ± 14 μm offset
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.d. Per cell or branch, responses normalized to 0 µm offset and the offsets of half and 20% found by linear interpolation (a standard choice). Reproduced when all four means are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Voltage signals fall to half at 4 µm transverse offset from an in-focus branch and plateau at 11% (IQR 7 to 24%) beyond 20 µm.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 2; Figure S5b
claims.quote: The |∆F| signal fell to half maximum at transverse offsets of 4 μm (n = 49 branches, 21 cells, median). At offsets > 20 μm, the fluorescence signal plateaued at 11% (median, IQR: 7 - 24%) of maximum
claims.criterion: Rectangular ROIs shifted in 5 µm steps up to 25 µm from the branch centre; -dF during bAPs normalized to 0 µm (legend). Half offset by linear interpolation (a standard choice). Open, the plateau; "offsets > 20 μm" with 5 µm steps up to 25 µm allows (a) the 25 µm point, (b) the mean of the 20 and 25 µm points. Reproduced when both medians are within tolerance. The 5 µm step makes the half offset coarse; the tolerance of 0.4 µm is the protocol's 10%. The plateau's tolerance is the paper's spread, the narrower side of its IQR (11 - 7; the IQR runs to 24%).

claims.statement: The first principal components of the pixel waveforms hold more than 96% of their variance (the first five, Fig. S7b; the first three, Methods).
claims.source: Methods, PCA-based filtering; Figure S7b
claims.quote: The first 5 PCA eigenvectors account for > 96% of the pixel-to-pixel waveform variance
claims.criterion: For the stimulus-triggered average movie of Fig. S7a (distal stimulus, 11 trials, the Fig. 3a recording), PCA of the pixel waveforms.
