The paper gives a bound, > 96%, for the first five components (Fig. S7b legend) and for the first three (Methods); readings (a) five, (b) three. Reproduced when under one reading the share is at least 86.4% (the bound less the 10% tolerance); both shares are reported. The Results' > 93% is of the 2D and 3D voltage maps from the whole reconstruction (Figs. S6, S7), which this claim does not test.

claims.statement: From cumulative eYFP fluorescence, dendrite-targeted optogenetic stimulation drives dendritic CheRiff currents of about 130 pA.
claims.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Based on the cumulative eYFP fluorescence evoked by our dendrite-targeted optogenetic stimulation, we estimate dendritic CheRiff currents of ~130 pA
claims.criterion: The Peer Review File (response to Reviewer 2, page 5 of the manuscript) gives the method; the Fig. 3a distal stimulus (the legend's D2, file as in source-data-index) "generated ~69 eYFP counts. Using the calibration in Fig. S3e, this corresponds to ~130 pA". The calibration is a fit of charge against cumulative eYFP over the soma recordings of Fig. S3e (0.5 s pulses, Fig. S3b). Open, how charge becomes current; readings (a) charge over the 0.5 s calibration pulse, (b) charge over the 20 ms stimulus (the eYFP image may be cumulative over either). Reproduced when the eYFP count and the current are within tolerance, by the header's rule for method readings; if the calibration recordings or the eYFP image are not in the dataset, the claim cannot be tested.

claims.statement: The tetrodotoxin experiment was replicated in several neurons, with vehicle controls; the representative traces of Figure S2 come from at least 4 independent replications in different cells.
claims.source: Figure S2 legend; Methods, Quantification and statistical analysis
claims.quote: Representative traces of the optical membrane potentials were selected from at least 4 and usually 8-15 independent replications in different cells
claims.criterion: Neurons are counted from the dataset's subjects, sessions or cell identifiers, each recording counted once (author, step 1), and split into TTX and vehicle by the dataset's session metadata. The paper does not say whether the 4 replications count TTX neurons alone; readings (a) at least 4 TTX neurons, (b) at least 4 neurons over TTX and vehicle together. As a reported number read two ways, reproduced when either reading holds (protocol, step 3). The tolerance is 0 on a lower bound. The number of vehicle neurons is reported; the legend gives no count and the figure shows one, so at least one vehicle neuron is expected and its absence is reported as a finding.

claims.statement: Before the drug, unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves evoked repetitive APs at lower fields and, at the most intense fields, a sustained depolarization in which APs merged into small oscillations.
claims.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure S2
claims.criterion: F1 to F3, under O1 to O4, sessions before the change only. Per neuron, the session at its highest field and its sessions at lower fields. Reproduced when every neuron (TTX and vehicle) has APs in some session, and more than half of them (a standard choice; the paper gives no fraction) show sustained depolarization (O4) at their highest field and APs without sustained depolarization at a lower field. The AP count and the maximum firing rate (F5) per session are reported against field.

claims.statement: The sustained depolarization induced by intense unmodulated sine waves reversed immediately when the stimulus ended, so it was not membrane electroporation, which would take seconds or longer to repair.
claims.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The sustained depolarization induced by intense unmodulated sine waves ( Figures 1 and 3 ) was immediately reversible upon stimulus cessation. It was not related to membrane electroporation, which would take seconds or longer to repair
claims.criterion: F1 to F3, under O1 to O4, all sessions with sustained depolarization (O4), before the change and in vehicle neurons. "Immediately" is not quantified; readings of the window after the stimulus (a) 10 to 40 ms after its end, (b) the last 40 ms of the recording (the Methods give about 90 ms after the stimulus). Reproduced when, in every such session, the mean dF in the window is below the O4 level of that reading. A further check, from the paper's "seconds or longer", is that F0 of the next session of the same neuron (20 to 60 s later) is within 10% (a standard choice) of the F0 of the session before; it is reported, not judged. Windows are standard choices; the claim is tested on the Figure S2 neurons, while the paper's sentence cites Figures 1 and 3.

claims.statement: 1 uM tetrodotoxin abolished the APs evoked by unmodulated 250-ms, 2-kHz sine waves.
claims.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure S2 legend
claims.quote: the inhibition of sodium channels with 1 μM tetrodotoxin not only abolished the APs
claims.criterion: F1 to F4, under O1 to O3 and O5. Per TTX neuron, session pairs at the same field before and after TTX. Reproduced when, in every TTX neuron, no AP is detected in any session after TTX at a field where APs were detected before; not reproduced when any such session has an AP. The AP counts before and after per pair are reported.

claims.statement: Tetrodotoxin also fully blocked the sustained depolarization caused by intense sine waves, consistent with the depolarization arising from repeated activation of voltage-gated sodium channels by the cycling de- and hyperpolarization of the membrane.
claims.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure S2 legend
claims.quote: Consistent with this hypothesis, the inhibition of sodium channels with 1 μM tetrodotoxin not only abolished the APs but also fully blocked the sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: F1 to F4, under O1, O2, O4 and O5. Per TTX neuron, the session pairs at the same field where sustained depolarization (O4) was present before TTX. Reproduced when, in every such pair, sustained depolarization is absent after TTX, and the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus after TTX is below the O4 level. "Fully" is read as that level; the mean dF over the window before and after is reported per pair, with a two-sided paired t test (F6) over pairs shown as a variant, not judged. Blocked (other) when no TTX neuron has sustained depolarization before TTX.

claims.statement: In vehicle controls, recorded about 5 min after the solution was replaced by the same solution without TTX, the firing and sustained depolarization persisted.
claims.source: Figure S2 legend; Methods, Quantification and statistical analysis
claims.criterion: F1 to F4, under O1 to O5. Per vehicle neuron, session pairs at the same field before and after the change. Reproduced when, in every vehicle neuron, every pair with APs before has APs after, and every pair with sustained depolarization (O4) before has it after. AP counts and the maximum firing rate (F5) per pair are reported; the paper does not say whether the response must be unchanged, so a decline is reported, not judged. Blocked (other) when the dataset holds no vehicle neuron.

claims.statement: Neurons were selected for APs peaking above 5% dF and lasting about 10 ms; typical APs were 11.3% dF high and 8 ms long, excluding the afterhyperpolarization.
claims.source: Methods, Recording of the optical APs and data analyses
claims.quote: we selected neurons whose APs peaked at a more than 5% Δ F and lasted about 10 ms (typical values ... 11.3% ± 0.9% Δ F and 8 ± 0.7 ms duration, excluding afterhyperpolarization ... mean ± SEM, n = 22)
claims.criterion: F1 and F2, under O1 to O3, sessions before the change. The paper does not say which 22 neurons these are or which experiments they come from; the neurons of this dataset are tested as neurons the same selection was applied to, and a mismatch may come from that. Per neuron, the mean peak dF and duration of its APs. Which APs are measured is not given; readings (a) all APs before the change, (b) the first AP of each session, which is not merged with others. The duration measure is not given; readings (a) width at half height, (b) time from the rise to the return to F0 on the decay, ending at the first crossing of F0 (so the afterhyperpolarization is left out). These readings are method details that can change the outcome, so the header's rule applies. Reproduced when the means over neurons are within the paper's SEM under every reading; partially reproduced when, under every reading, every neuron has APs above 5% dF and lasting 2 to 20 ms (O3) but a mean falls outside; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings give different outcomes. The number of neurons with APs above 5% is reported.

claims.statement: Unmodulated 250-ms sine waves at 2 and 20 kHz excited every neuron tested, with APs 100 to 200 ms after onset near threshold, firing rate rising to a ceiling of 60 to 90 Hz, and sustained depolarization at the highest fields.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figures 1A to 1C and inset
claims.quote: Pure sine waves at 2 and even 20 kHz excited 100% of neurons ... at near-threshold electric field strengths, isolated APs emerged with a delay of 100-200 ms after the sine wave onset ... The maximum firing rate increased linearly until reaching a ceiling of 60-90 Hz
claims.criterion: F1 to F3, F5, O1 to O4 of the header, for FluoVolt sessions of unmodulated sine waves. A neuron's threshold is the lowest field of a session with at least one AP during the stimulus (Figure 2D legend). Reproduced when, under every reading, at least 90% of neurons are excited at each frequency, the median over neurons of the highest maximum firing rate lies within 54 to 99 Hz (60 to 90 Hz widened by 10% of each bound) and the median first-AP latency at threshold lies within 90 to 220 ms (100 to 200 ms widened the same way). Whether the ceiling is meant for the median neuron or every neuron is open (the inset shows three); both are reported and the median decides. Sustained depolarization (O4) at the highest field is reported, not judged, as the paper gives no fraction of neurons.

claims.statement: All excitation thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
claims.quote: All thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz ( p < 0.0001, two-tailed unpaired t test)
claims.criterion: Thresholds for at least 1 and at least 5 APs during the 250-ms stimulus (Figure 2D legend), from the threshold search of the Methods (5% to 10% steps), with the AP readings of the header. The paper gives one p over "all thresholds"; readings (a) one test per stimulus (modulated or not) and AP count, each p < 0.0001, (b) one test pooling the four. Reproduced when each ratio is within tolerance and 20 against 2 kHz reaches p < 0.0001 under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Thresholds for sine waves modulated at 20 Hz were significantly higher than for pure sine waves at the same carrier, for 5 APs at 2 kHz and for 1 and 5 APs at 20 kHz, so modulation did not lower excitation thresholds; the 2-kHz unmodulated 1-AP threshold was 57.7 V/cm.
claims.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D; Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging, last paragraph
claims.quote: thresholds for modulated sine waves, which emulate the TI stimulus at the target, were significantly higher than those for pure sine waves at the same frequency ... p = 0.0079 ... p = 0.0142 and p = 0.0037
claims.criterion: Thresholds as in fig1-20khz-needs-twice-the-field. Two-tailed unpaired t tests, as the Figure 2D legend names them. Reproduced when the three modulated thresholds are higher with p < 0.05 (Methods), the 1-AP threshold at 2 kHz is not lower for modulated waves at p < 0.05, and the mean 2-kHz unmodulated 1-AP threshold is within the paper's SEM, under every AP reading. The paper calls 57.7 V/cm "the AP threshold" for unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves (Figure 2D) without saying 1 or 5 APs; it is read as the 1-AP threshold, the excitation threshold of Figures 2D and 3B, and the 5-AP mean is reported beside it; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: With 20-Hz modulation, firing above threshold locked to the beats, one AP near the peak of each of the five beats and at most two per beat (ten in all), and modulated sine waves triggered no sustained firing or sustained depolarization.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 1; Figures 2A and 2B
claims.quote: single APs emerged near the peak of each beat, so the firing rate equaled the modulation rate ... the maximum number of APs evoked by five beats was limited to ten. Unlike pure sine waves, modulated stimuli did not trigger sustained firing or sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: AP readings of the header, modulated sessions only. The 250-ms wave holds five 50-ms beats (Results), and modulated waves begin and end at minimal amplitude (Methods, Pulsed laser fluorescence microscopy), so each beat peaks 25 ms into it; the dataset's stimulus record is used instead when it gives the envelope. The paper does not quantify "near the peak"; as standard choices, reproduced when no session has more than 10 APs, in sessions with 5 APs or more most APs fall within 12.5 to 37.5 ms of each 50-ms beat, and no session shows sustained firing or sustained depolarization (O4).

claims.statement: In the same neuron at the same field strength, pure sine waves triggered more APs than modulated ones, and the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated signals.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 2; Figures 2A to 2C
claims.quote: the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated signals ( Figures 2A - 2C ). At the same field strengths, pure sine waves triggered a larger number of APs
claims.criterion: AP readings of the header. Pairs are a neuron's modulated and unmodulated sessions at the same carrier and field. The paper reports no test; reproduced when the unmodulated count is larger in more pairs than the reverse, and the unmodulated threshold lower in more neurons than the reverse, under every reading. A two-sided paired t test (F6) of the counts is reported.

claims.statement: Lowering solution conductivity from 16.4 to 8.4 mS/cm with sodium gluconate reversibly lowered excitation thresholds about 2-fold at all sine wave frequencies from 2 to 20 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 1; Figures 3A and 3B
claims.quote: Switching to the NaGlu-based solution reversibly and reproducibly decreased excitation thresholds ~2-fold across all sine wave frequencies tested
claims.criterion: 1-AP thresholds for 250-ms unmodulated sine waves per frequency and solution, 4 to 8 neurons per point (Figure 3B legend), AP readings of the header. Reproduced when the ratio is within tolerance at every frequency under every reading.

claims.statement: Excitation by pure sine waves was not caused by heating; the adiabatic temperature rise was 2.5 C after 250 ms at 63 V/cm in NaCl solution, at most 1.24 C for the same stimulus in the low-conductivity solution, and 4.1 C at 81 V/cm in NaCl.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 2; Figure 3A
claims.quote: the maximum theoretical temperature rise (assuming no heat dissipation 43 ) was 2.5°C after 250 ms of near-threshold stimulation at 2 kHz, 63 V/cm, in the NaCl-based solution ... These observations prove that excitation by pure sine waves was not caused by heating
claims.criterion: The rise is sigma E^2 t over the volumetric heat capacity (reference 43, cited for the adiabatic assumption). The paper does not give the heat capacity or whether E is the peak or the RMS field; readings (a) peak, (b) RMS, each with the heat capacity of water (4.18 J per cm3 per K, a standard choice). Reproduced when all three are within tolerance under a reading; since these are calculated numbers read two ways, that reading is reported. Computed from the paper's own values (1.64 S/m, 63 V/cm, 0.25 s), neither reading gives 2.5 C (peak about 3.9 C, RMS about 1.95 C), while the ratios 4.1/2.5 and 1.24/2.5 follow the formula's scaling with E^2 and with conductivity. The heat capacity or field definition the paper used is therefore not known; when no reading matches the absolute values but the two ratios are within 10%, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified, and it is not reproduced only when the ratios fail as well. That the Figure 3A neuron fired at 63 V/cm in NaGlu as at 81 V/cm in NaCl is tested as in fig3b-low-conductivity-halves-threshold.

claims.statement: In the low-conductivity solution, a 2-s unmodulated 2-kHz sine wave ramped over 250 ms evoked firing for its whole duration, rising with field until replaced by a firing block with sustained depolarization.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 3; Figure 3C
claims.quote: we observed sustained firing for the entire duration of the sine wave ( Figure 3C ). The rate of firing increased with the electric field strength until it was replaced by a firing block and sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: Traces corrected for bleaching by subtracting a trace without APs (Methods); AP readings of the header. Reproduced when an intermediate field has APs in the last 250 ms of the stimulus, the AP count rises with field up to some field, and the highest field shows sustained depolarization (O4, over the last 250 ms of the stimulus). The windows are standard choices.

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS in place of FluoVolt, in eight neurons, the effects of 2-kHz sine waves were not different, so the excitation by unmodulated sine waves is not a sensitization by FluoVolt.
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
claims.quote: Experiments were performed on eight neurons using different electric field strengths tested in a random sequence ... Overall, stimulation effects were not different from those observed with FluoVolt dye
claims.criterion: As in the claims file for DANDI:001272 (figs1-eight-neurons and figs1-effects-same-as-fluovolt), which tests this finding on its own data.

claims.statement: Membrane charging by 2-us pulses is fast; pooled over 19 experiments, charging and discharging time constants averaged 0.7 and 0.91 us at the cathodic pole and 0.65 and 0.8 us at the anodic pole, so membranes charge fully within each sine wave cycle up to 100 to 200 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
claims.quote: The time constants pooled together for all cells averaged 0.7 ± 0.08 (charging) and 0.91 ± 0.08 (discharging) μs for the cathodic cell pole and 0.65 ± 0.05 and 0.8 ± 0.07 μs for the anodic pole, respectively (mean ± SEM, n = 19)
claims.criterion: Fits and readings as in the claims file for DANDI:001273 (fig4-pooled-time-constants), which tests this claim on its own data; tolerances are the paper's SEMs.

claims.statement: Aligning elongated cells with the field doubled the time constants; the maximum optical TMP and the time constants did not differ between the cathode- and anode-facing poles; and discharging was slower than charging except in elongated cells aligned with the field.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
claims.quote: Δ F max did not differ at the cathodic and anodic cell poles, indicating the lack of rectification of the applied electric field ... Aligning elongated cells with the electric field doubled the time constants ... discharging time constants were always larger than the charging ones in the same cell ( p < 0.001, paired t test)
claims.criterion: As in the claims file for DANDI:001273 (fig4-orientation-time-constants, fig4-no-pole-difference and fig4-discharging-slower), which tests each part on its own data; reproduced when all three are reproduced there. The Figure 4 legend gives other bounds and test types for these comparisons (p < 0.01, paired two-tailed, charging against discharging; p < 0.01, unpaired two-tailed, between orthogonal orientations); the statistics above are the Results'.

claims.statement: FluoVolt sensitivity to 2-kHz sine waves (11.8% per 1 kV/cm) was 42% of that to 2-us pulses (28% per 1 kV/cm) and smaller in every ROI, with sine waves polarizing the two poles more asymmetrically than pulses.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraphs 2 to 5; Figures 5, 6B to 6D and S3
claims.quote: All numbers were invariably smaller than those measured for the same ROIs with the pulse ( Figure 6D ). The electric field sensitivity averaged across all ROIs in all the cells was 11.8% ± 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, just 42% of the value for the 2-μs pulses
claims.criterion: Measures and readings as in the claims file for DANDI:001274 (fig6b-pulse-sensitivity, fig6c-sine-sensitivity, fig6d-sine-less-than-pulse, fig5-sine-asymmetry-c7 and figs3-sine-asymmetry-c8), which tests this finding on its own data; tolerances are the paper's SEMs, and 10% for the ratio.

claims.statement: The 2-kHz AP threshold of 57.7 V/cm times the sine wave sensitivity gives a 0.68% emission change, about 6.8 mV, so the threshold depolarization is 5 to 15 mV, as with intracellular current injection.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, last paragraph
claims.quote: This threshold corresponds to a 0.68% ± 0.11% FluoVolt emission change (11.8 × 57.7/1,000) ... a 0.68% emission change corresponds to a 6.8-mV depolarization at the AP threshold
claims.criterion: Mean sine sensitivity of fig6-sine-less-than-pulse times the mean unmodulated 2-kHz 1-AP threshold of fig2d-modulated-thresholds-higher, divided by 1,000, and that times 10 mV per 1% (the calibration of reference 47 as the paper uses it). Tolerances are the paper's, the last being 0.11% times 10 mV per 1%. Reproduced when both are within tolerance.

claims.statement: The Di-8-ANEPPS control experiments were made on eight neurons, at field strengths tested in a random sequence.
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
claims.quote: Experiments were performed on eight neurons using different electric field strengths tested in a random sequence
claims.criterion: Neurons are counted from the dataset's subjects, sessions or cell identifiers, each recording counted once (author, step 1). The tolerance is 0, as a count of neurons is whole and 10% of 8 admits no other value. The order of fields over each neuron's sessions is reported (the number of neurons whose fields rise monotonically with session order), not judged, since the Methods also allow escalating sequences.

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS, APs appear as brief reductions of emission, opposite in sign to FluoVolt.
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Methods, Recording of the optical APs and data analyses; Figure S1 legend
claims.quote: APs were identified by the reduction instead of the increase of emission
claims.criterion: F1 and F2, under the readings O1 and O2. Per neuron, over the sessions at fields above its threshold (F4, under O3), the largest brief deflections of dF during the stimulus are negative. Detection under O3 is run on the trace as recorded (not inverted) and on the inverted trace; reproduced when in every neuron with APs the inverted trace yields more APs than the trace as recorded, in more than 75% of its sessions with APs (a standard choice). The counts each way are reported.

claims.statement: Near threshold, 2-kHz sine waves elicited one or a few delayed APs in Di-8-ANEPPS neurons.
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
claims.quote: Stimulation near the threshold elicited one or a few delayed APs
claims.criterion: F1 to F4, under O1 to O5. Per neuron, the near-threshold sessions (O4); their AP count and first-AP latency from the onset (F3). The paper gives no count for "a few"; at most 3 APs is a standard choice. Reproduced when, in more than half of the neurons with APs (a standard choice), the median near-threshold session has 1 to 3 APs and its first AP is delayed (O5). Counts and latencies per neuron are reported.

claims.statement: In Di-8-ANEPPS neurons, increasing the field strength reduced the delay to the first AP and induced sustained firing.
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
claims.quote: Increasing the electric field strength reduced the delay and induced sustained firing
claims.criterion: F1 to F4, under O1 to O3 and O6. Per neuron with sessions with APs at 3 or more fields, the Spearman correlation of first-AP latency with field over those sessions. The paper reports no test; reproduced when the correlation is negative in more than half of those neurons and more than half of all neurons show sustained firing (O6) in some session. The majority and the Spearman correlation are standard choices. The maximum firing rate (F5) against field is reported per neuron.

claims.statement: In Di-8-ANEPPS neurons, the strongest fields replaced firing with sustained depolarization (excitation followed by inhibition of firing).
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1 legend
claims.quote: induced sustained firing that culminated in sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: F1 to F4, under O1 to O3 and O6. Per neuron, its sessions at its highest field. The paper gives no fraction of neurons; reproduced when more than half of the neurons (a standard choice) show sustained depolarization (O6) at their highest field and sustained firing or more APs at some lower field. The Figure S1 legend's "Excitation and inhibition of firing" describes one neuron; the number of neurons with each is reported.

claims.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS traces were noisier than FluoVolt traces, as the dye has a lower voltage sensitivity.
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Compared to FluoVolt recordings, the traces were expectedly noisier (Di-8-ANEPSS has a lower voltage sensitivity)
claims.criterion: F1 to F3, under O1 to O3, for the Di-8-ANEPPS neurons of this dataset and for the FluoVolt neurons stimulated with 250-ms unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves in NaCl solution in DANDI:001030 and 001032 to 001035 (assigned from their titles; FluoVolt traces not inverted). Per neuron, the signal to noise ratio is the median AP height over the SD of dF before the onset. "Noisier" is not defined; readings (a) that ratio, (b) the SD of dF before the onset. Reproduced when the Di-8-ANEPPS median is worse (lower ratio, larger SD) than the FluoVolt median under both. A two-sided unpaired t test (F6) is reported. As a variant on this dataset alone, the median Di-8-ANEPPS AP height is compared with the 11.3% typical of FluoVolt (Methods).

claims.statement: Overall, the effects of 2-kHz sine waves in Di-8-ANEPPS neurons did not differ from those with FluoVolt, so the excitation by unmodulated sine waves is not a sensitization by FluoVolt.
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Discussion, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Overall, stimulation effects were not different from those observed with FluoVolt dye
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, for which the paper names no test, and the paper does not say which effects were compared; the threshold comparison below is a reading of "not different", not a measure the paper names. The response pattern holds when figs1-near-threshold-delayed-aps, figs1-stronger-field-shorter-delay-sustained-firing and figs1-culminates-in-sustained-depolarization are reproduced. The paper's own concern is a sensitization by FluoVolt (Discussion, "we ruled out possible sensitization"), which would show as lower thresholds with FluoVolt; so the 1-AP threshold (F4) of the Di-8-ANEPPS neurons is compared with that of the FluoVolt neurons of figs1-noisier-than-fluovolt by a two-sided unpaired t test at p < 0.05 (F6). Reproduced when the pattern holds and the test finds no difference; not reproduced when the test finds a difference in either direction. The mean FluoVolt threshold of the neurons used is reported beside the paper's 57.7 ± 3.6 V/cm (Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging, last paragraph, from Figure 2D) as a check on the reference group, not judged. A one-sample t test of the Di-8-ANEPPS thresholds against 57.7 V/cm is shown as a variant on this dataset alone. The difference of means and its 95% interval are reported. The Di-8-ANEPPS sessions may not have been a threshold search (fields in a random sequence), so the threshold is the lowest exciting field tested, which is an upper bound; the notebook reports the gap to the next lower field tested.

claims.statement: Unmodulated 250-ms sine waves at 2 and 20 kHz excited every neuron tested, with APs 100 to 200 ms after onset near threshold, firing rate rising to a ceiling of 60 to 90 Hz, and an excitation block with sustained depolarization at the highest fields.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figures 1A to 1C and inset
claims.quote: Pure sine waves at 2 and even 20 kHz excited 100% of neurons ... The maximum firing rate increased linearly until reaching a ceiling of 60-90 Hz
claims.criterion: F1 to F5 and O1 to O3 and O6 of the header, applied to FluoVolt traces without inversion. Reproduced when, under every reading, at least 90% of neurons are excited at each frequency, the median ceiling lies within 54 to 99 Hz (60 to 90 Hz widened by 10% of each bound, written above as its midpoint and half-width) and the median first-AP latency at threshold lies within 90 to 220 ms (100 to 200 ms widened the same way); blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. Whether the ceiling is meant for the median neuron or every neuron is open (the inset shows three); the median is a standard choice and the range over neurons is reported. The block is reported under O6, not judged.

claims.statement: Responses to 20 kHz needed about 2-fold stronger fields than at 2 kHz, and all thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
claims.quote: All thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz ( p < 0.0001, two-tailed unpaired t test)
claims.criterion: Thresholds for at least 1 and at least 5 APs (Figure 2D legend), as F4, with the AP readings of the header. The paper gives one p over "all thresholds"; readings (a) one test per stimulus (modulated or not) and AP count, each p < 0.0001, (b) one test pooling the four. Reproduced when each ratio is within tolerance and 20 against 2 kHz reaches p < 0.0001 under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Thresholds for sine waves modulated at 20 Hz were significantly higher than for pure sine waves at the same carrier, for 5 APs at 2 kHz and for 1 and 5 APs at 20 kHz, so modulation did not lower excitation thresholds.
claims.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
claims.quote: thresholds for modulated sine waves, which emulate the TI stimulus at the target, were significantly higher than those for pure sine waves at the same frequency ... p = 0.0079 ... p = 0.0142 and p = 0.0037
claims.criterion: Thresholds as in fig1-20khz-needs-twice-the-field. Two-tailed unpaired t tests, as the Figure 2D legend names them. Reproduced when the three modulated thresholds are higher with p < 0.05 (Methods) and the 1-AP threshold at 2 kHz is not lower for modulated waves at p < 0.05, under every AP reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: With 20-Hz modulation, firing above threshold locked to the beats, one AP near the peak of each of the five beats and at most two per beat (ten in all), and modulated sine waves triggered no sustained firing or sustained depolarization.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 1; Figures 2A and 2B
claims.quote: single APs emerged near the peak of each beat, so the firing rate equaled the modulation rate ... the maximum number of APs evoked by five beats was limited to ten. Unlike pure sine waves, modulated stimuli did not trigger sustained firing or sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: AP readings of the header, modulated sessions only. The 250-ms wave holds five 50-ms beats (Results), and modulated waves begin and end at minimal amplitude (Methods, Pulsed laser fluorescence microscopy, F0 for sine waves), so each beat peaks 25 ms into it; the stimulus record of the dataset is used instead when it gives the envelope. The paper does not quantify "near the peak"; as standard choices, reproduced when no session has more than 10 APs, in sessions with 5 APs or more most APs fall within 12.5 to 37.5 ms of each 50-ms beat, and no session shows sustained depolarization (O6). The AP phase histogram is reported.

claims.statement: In the same neuron at the same field strength, pure sine waves triggered more APs than modulated ones, and the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated signals.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 2; Figures 2A to 2C
claims.quote: the threshold was typically lower for unmodulated signals ( Figures 2A - 2C ). At the same field strengths, pure sine waves triggered a larger number of APs
claims.criterion: AP readings of the header. Pairs are a neuron's modulated and unmodulated sessions at the same carrier and field. The paper reports no test; reproduced when the unmodulated count is larger in more pairs than the reverse, and the unmodulated threshold lower in more neurons than the reverse, under every reading. A two-sided paired t test (F6) of the counts is reported.

claims.statement: Lowering solution conductivity from 16.4 to 8.4 mS/cm with sodium gluconate reversibly lowered excitation thresholds about 2-fold at all sine wave frequencies from 2 to 20 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 1; Figures 3A and 3B
claims.quote: Switching to the NaGlu-based solution reversibly and reproducibly decreased excitation thresholds ~2-fold across all sine wave frequencies tested
claims.criterion: 1-AP thresholds (F4) for 250-ms unmodulated sine waves per frequency and solution, 4 to 8 neurons per point (Figure 3B legend), AP readings of the header. Reproduced when the ratio is within tolerance at every frequency under every reading.

claims.statement: In the low-conductivity solution, a 2-s unmodulated 2-kHz sine wave ramped over 250 ms evoked firing for its whole duration, rising with field until replaced by a firing block with sustained depolarization.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 3; Figure 3C
claims.quote: we observed sustained firing for the entire duration of the sine wave ( Figure 3C ). The rate of firing increased with the electric field strength until it was replaced by a firing block and sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: Traces corrected for bleaching by subtracting a trace without APs (Methods); AP readings of the header. Reproduced when an intermediate field has APs in the last 250 ms of the stimulus, the AP count rises with field up to some field, and the highest field shows sustained depolarization (O6, over the last 250 ms of the stimulus). The windows are standard choices.

claims.statement: 1 uM tetrodotoxin abolished both the APs and the sustained depolarization caused by intense unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves, while the vehicle did not.
claims.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure S2 legend
claims.quote: the inhibition of sodium channels with 1 μM tetrodotoxin not only abolished the APs but also fully blocked the sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: Per neuron, sessions before and about 5 min after TTX or vehicle at the same field (Figure S2 legend), AP readings of the header. Reproduced when, in every TTX neuron, APs present before are absent after and sustained depolarization (O6) present before is absent after, while vehicle neurons keep their response.

claims.statement: Membrane charging by 2-us pulses is fast; pooled over 19 experiments, charging and discharging time constants averaged 0.7 and 0.91 us at the cathodic pole and 0.65 and 0.8 us at the anodic pole, so membranes charge fully within each sine wave cycle up to 100 to 200 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
claims.quote: The time constants pooled together for all cells averaged 0.7 ± 0.08 (charging) and 0.91 ± 0.08 (discharging) μs for the cathodic cell pole and 0.65 ± 0.05 and 0.8 ± 0.07 μs for the anodic pole, respectively (mean ± SEM, n = 19)
claims.criterion: Fits and readings as in the claims file for DANDI:001273 (fig4-pooled-time-constants), which tests this claim on its own data; tolerances are the paper's SEMs.

claims.statement: Aligning elongated cells with the field doubled the time constants; the maximum optical TMP and the time constants did not differ between the cathode- and anode-facing poles; and discharging was slower than charging except in elongated cells aligned with the field.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
claims.quote: Δ F max did not differ at the cathodic and anodic cell poles, indicating the lack of rectification of the applied electric field ... Aligning elongated cells with the electric field doubled the time constants ... discharging time constants were always larger than the charging ones in the same cell ( p < 0.001, paired t test)
claims.criterion: As in the claims file for DANDI:001273 (fig4-orientation-time-constants, fig4-no-pole-difference and fig4-discharging-slower), which tests each part on its own data; reproduced when all three are reproduced there. The Figure 4 legend reports these tests differently from the Results (p < 0.01, paired two-tailed, charging against discharging; p < 0.01, unpaired two-tailed, between the orthogonal orientations, with n = 3 parallel and n = 6 perpendicular); the statistics above are the Results', and the legend's are a reading the paper also allows.

claims.statement: FluoVolt sensitivity to 2-kHz sine waves (11.8% per 1 kV/cm) was 42% of that to 2-us pulses (28% per 1 kV/cm) and smaller in every ROI, with sine waves polarizing the two poles more asymmetrically than pulses.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraphs 2 to 5; Figures 5, 6B to 6D and S3
claims.quote: All numbers were invariably smaller than those measured for the same ROIs with the pulse ( Figure 6D ). The electric field sensitivity averaged across all ROIs in all the cells was 11.8% ± 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, just 42% of the value for the 2-μs pulses
claims.criterion: Measures and readings as in the claims file for DANDI:001274 (fig6b-pulse-sensitivity, fig6c-sine-sensitivity, fig6d-sine-less-than-pulse, fig5-sine-asymmetry-c7 and figs3-sine-asymmetry-c8), which tests this finding on its own data; tolerances are the paper's SEMs, and 10% for the ratio.

claims.statement: The 2-kHz AP threshold of 57.7 V/cm times the sine wave sensitivity gives a 0.68% emission change, about 6.8 mV, so the threshold depolarization is 5 to 15 mV, as with intracellular current injection.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, last paragraph
claims.quote: This threshold corresponds to a 0.68% ± 0.11% FluoVolt emission change (11.8 × 57.7/1,000) ... a 0.68% emission change corresponds to a 6.8-mV depolarization at the AP threshold
claims.criterion: Mean sine sensitivity of fig6-sine-less-than-pulse times the mean unmodulated 2-kHz 1-AP threshold (F4), divided by 1,000, and that times 10 mV per 1% (the calibration of reference 47 as the paper uses it). Tolerances are the paper's SEMs, the last being 0.11% times 10 mV per 1%. Reproduced when all three are within tolerance.

claims.statement: A 2-us pulse polarizes mainly the membrane facing the electrodes, depolarized at the cathode-facing pole and hyperpolarized at the anode-facing one, while even large neurites show little or no polarization.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4A to 4C
claims.quote: In neurons of all shapes, the electric field primarily polarized membrane portions facing the electrodes ... Unexpectedly, even large neurites showed little to no polarization and did not seem to impact the charging of cell soma
claims.criterion: Per experiment, the filtered RATIO image of the Methods (mean of the frames in the last 0.5 us of the pulse over the mean of the frames before the pulse and late after it, each low-pass filtered over 12 x 12 pixels). The field direction per experiment is taken from the dataset. The paper gives no measure; reproduced when, in more than half of the experiments of each shape group of the Figure 4D and 4E legend (or of all 19 when the labels are missing, O4), the extreme depolarized and extreme hyperpolarized pixels of the cell lie on opposite sides of its centroid along the field axis (the angle between their separation and the field axis below 45 degrees). The majority, the centroid and the 45 degrees are standard choices. The part on neurites needs a neurite mask that the paper does not give and is reported, not judged.

claims.statement: In elongated neurons, charging was about 2-fold faster with the field orthogonal to the long axis; aligning elongated cells with the field doubled the time constants compared with the same cells perpendicular to it or with randomly shaped cells.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4A, 4D and 4E
claims.quote: Aligning elongated cells with the electric field doubled the time constants, as compared to either the same cells oriented perpendicular to the field ( p < 0.001, paired t test) or to randomly shaped cells ( p < 0.01, unpaired t test)
claims.criterion: Fits as in the header (F1 to F4), groups from the dataset's labels (O4), as in the Figure 4D and 4E legend (parallel n = 3, perpendicular n = 6, random n = 10, random cells with both orientations pooled). The tau compared are charging and discharging, at each pole. The text names a paired t test (p < 0.001) for parallel against perpendicular; the legend marks p < 0.01 between orientations with an unpaired two-tailed t test (O5). Readings of that test (a) paired, on elongated cells imaged in both orientations, (b) unpaired, on the legend's groups. Which time constants "the time constants" means is not given, and the text's first sentence names charging only; readings of the subset (i) charging tau, (ii) charging and discharging tau, each at both poles. Reproduced when, under one subset reading, the parallel mean is within tolerance of twice the perpendicular mean and of twice the random mean, and parallel against random reaches p < 0.01 and the orientation test its stated p (0.001 paired, 0.01 unpaired) at one pole at least, under every reading of the header (O1 to O3, F2) and both readings of the test; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. The ratios at each pole are reported.

claims.statement: The maximum optical TMP and the charging and discharging time constants did not differ between the cathode- and anode-facing poles, indicating no rectification of the field.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
claims.quote: Δ F max did not differ at the cathodic and anodic cell poles, indicating the lack of rectification of the applied electric field. Charging and discharging time constants did not differ between the two poles either
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The text names no test for it; the Methods' test is a two-sided Student's t test, paired or unpaired as appropriate, at p < 0.05, and the two poles are in the same experiment, so a two-sided paired t test over the 19 experiments of |dFmax|, charging tau and discharging tau, cathodic against anodic. Fits as in the header. Reproduced when none of the three is significant at p < 0.05 under every reading of the header; not reproduced when any is under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The mean differences and their 95% intervals are reported either way.

claims.statement: Discharging time constants were larger than charging ones in the same cell, except in elongated cells aligned with the field.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E
claims.quote: discharging time constants were always larger than the charging ones in the same cell ( p < 0.001, paired t test), with the exception of elongated cells aligned with the field
claims.criterion: Fits as in the header. Two-sided paired t test of discharging against charging tau. The pooling behind the text's p < 0.001 is not given; readings (a) all 19 experiments, both poles, (b) the experiments other than elongated parallel, both poles, (c) as (b), each pole alone, and per group and pole for the legend's marks. Reproduced when, under one of (a) to (c), discharging tau is larger with p < 0.001, and the elongated parallel group shows no difference at p < 0.05 at either pole (which needs the labels, O4), with every reading of the header giving that outcome; blocked as methods_underspecified when the header's readings disagree.

claims.statement: Pooled over all 19 experiments, charging and discharging time constants averaged 0.7 and 0.91 us at the cathodic pole and 0.65 and 0.8 us at the anodic pole.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend; Figures 4D and 4E (ALL)
claims.quote: The time constants pooled together for all cells averaged 0.7 ± 0.08 (charging) and 0.91 ± 0.08 (discharging) μs for the cathodic cell pole and 0.65 ± 0.05 and 0.8 ± 0.07 μs for the anodic pole, respectively (mean ± SEM, n = 19)
claims.criterion: Fits as in the header. The mean over all 19 experiment fits, as the text (n = 19) and the Figure 4D and 4E legend (ALL, n = 19, all cells and all orientations) give it. Tolerances are the SEMs the paper gives. Reproduced when all four are within tolerance, with every reading of the header (O1 to O3, F2) giving that outcome; blocked as methods_underspecified when the header's readings disagree. The SEMs are reported.

claims.statement: Membranes exceed 95% of full charge in under 3 us, even in the largest neurons and with the least efficient alignment with the field, so each cycle of a sine wave fully polarizes the membrane even at 100 to 200 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, the paragraph after the Figure 4 legend
claims.quote: It will take <3 μs to exceed 95% of the full charge, even in the largest neurons and with the least efficient cell alignment with the field
claims.criterion: Under the paper's exponential model (Methods), 95% of full charge is reached at 3 tau (ln 20 = 3.0). Charging tau from the fits of the header. The paper does not say whether the bound holds for every cell or for the least efficient group; readings (a) 3 times the mean charging tau of the elongated parallel group (the least efficient alignment, Figure 4D and 4E) is below 3 us at both poles, (b) 3 times the largest charging tau of any experiment is below 3 us. Reproduced when (a) holds under every reading of the header; partially reproduced when (a) holds and (b) does not. The 100 to 200 kHz part is an inference and is not tested.

claims.statement: Unmodulated 250-ms sine waves at 2 and 20 kHz excited every neuron tested, with APs 100 to 200 ms after onset near threshold, firing rate rising to a ceiling of 60 to 90 Hz, and an excitation block with sustained depolarization at the highest fields.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figures 1A to 1C and inset
claims.quote: Pure sine waves at 2 and even 20 kHz excited 100% of neurons ... The maximum firing rate increased linearly until reaching a ceiling of 60-90 Hz
claims.criterion: AP detection is given only as "brief emission upticks" in neurons whose APs peak above 5% dF and last about 10 ms (Methods, Recording of the optical APs); readings (a) a peak above 5% dF over F0, (b) a rise of at least 5% dF within 5 ms. The maximum firing rate of a session is the inverse of the interval between its first two AP peaks (Methods). Reproduced when, under both readings, at least 90% of neurons are excited at each frequency and the median ceiling lies within 54 to 99 Hz (the reported 60 to 90 Hz widened by 10% of each bound, written above as its midpoint and half-width), and the median first-AP latency at threshold lies within 90 to 220 ms (the reported 100 to 200 ms widened the same way); blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The median over neurons is a standard choice. The block is reported, not judged.

claims.statement: Thresholds for 1 and 5 APs at 20 kHz were about 2-fold those at 2 kHz, and thresholds for sine waves modulated at 20 Hz were significantly higher than for pure sine waves for 5 APs at 2 kHz and for 1 and 5 APs at 20 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
claims.quote: All thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz ( p < 0.0001, two-tailed unpaired t test) ... thresholds for modulated sine waves, which emulate the TI stimulus at the target, were significantly higher than those for pure sine waves at the same frequency
claims.criterion: The threshold of a neuron for a stimulus is the lowest field of a session with at least 1 (or 5) APs during the 250-ms stimulus (Figure 2D legend), AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, both readings. Two-tailed unpaired t tests as the text names them. The paper gives one p for 20 against 2 kHz over "all thresholds"; readings (a) one test per stimulus and AP count, each p < 0.0001, (b) one test pooling the four. Reproduced when each ratio is within tolerance, 20 against 2 kHz reaches p < 0.0001 under both readings of that test, and the three modulated pairs are higher with p < 0.05 (Methods), under both AP readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: With 20-Hz modulation, firing above threshold locked to the beats, one AP near the peak of each of the five beats and at most two per beat (ten in all), and modulated sine waves triggered no sustained firing or sustained depolarization.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 1; Figures 2A and 2B
claims.quote: single APs emerged near the peak of each beat, so the firing rate equaled the modulation rate ... the maximum number of APs evoked by five beats was limited to ten. Unlike pure sine waves, modulated stimuli did not trigger sustained firing or sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, both readings. Modulated sessions only. Reproduced when no session has more than 10 APs, in sessions with 5 APs or more most APs fall in the half of each 50-ms beat around its peak (12.5 to 37.5 ms into the beat), and no session has, over the last 100 ms of the stimulus, no APs with mean dF above 5% (the block test of fig3c-sustained-firing-2s applied to that window). The paper does not quantify "near the peak"; the window, the majority and the block test are standard choices, and the AP phase histogram is reported.

claims.statement: In the same neuron at the same field strength, pure sine waves triggered more APs than modulated ones.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 2; Figure 2C
claims.quote: At the same field strengths, pure sine waves triggered a larger number of APs
claims.criterion: AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, both readings. Pairs are a neuron's modulated and unmodulated sessions at the same carrier and the same field. The paper reports no test; reproduced when the unmodulated count is larger in more pairs than the reverse under both readings. A two-sided paired t test of the counts (the Methods' general test) is reported.

claims.statement: Lowering solution conductivity from 16.4 to 8.4 mS/cm with sodium gluconate reversibly lowered excitation thresholds about 2-fold at all sine wave frequencies from 2 to 20 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 1; Figures 3A and 3B
claims.quote: Switching to the NaGlu-based solution reversibly and reproducibly decreased excitation thresholds ~2-fold across all sine wave frequencies tested
claims.criterion: 1-AP thresholds for 250-ms unmodulated sine waves (Figure 3B legend) as in fig2d-modulated-thresholds-higher, per frequency and solution, 4 to 8 neurons per point. Reproduced when the ratio is within tolerance at every frequency under both AP readings.

claims.statement: In the low-conductivity solution, a 2-s unmodulated 2-kHz sine wave ramped over 250 ms evoked firing for its whole duration, rising with field until replaced by a firing block with sustained depolarization.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 3; Figure 3C
claims.quote: we observed sustained firing for the entire duration of the sine wave ( Figure 3C ). The rate of firing increased with the electric field strength until it was replaced by a firing block and sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: Traces corrected for bleaching by subtracting a trace without APs (Methods); AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, both readings. Reproduced when an intermediate field has APs in the last 250 ms of the stimulus, the AP count rises with field up to some field, and the highest field has no APs after 250 ms with mean dF above F0 by more than 5% over the rest of the stimulus. The 5% is the Methods' AP selection level, used here as a standard choice.

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS instead of FluoVolt, in eight neurons, near-threshold stimulation elicited one or a few delayed APs and stronger fields induced sustained firing ending in sustained depolarization, as with FluoVolt.
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
claims.quote: Stimulation near the threshold elicited one or a few delayed APs. Increasing the electric field strength reduced the delay and induced sustained firing that culminated in sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: Traces inverted, as Di-8-ANEPPS emission falls with depolarization (Methods). AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, with a third reading of 5 SD of the pre-stimulus trace, as the paper notes the dye is less sensitive. Reproduced when, under every reading, every neuron fires, first-AP latency falls with field in more than half, and the highest field ends in depolarization as in fig3c-sustained-firing-2s in more than half.

claims.statement: 1 uM tetrodotoxin abolished both the APs and the sustained depolarization caused by intense unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves.
claims.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure S2
claims.quote: the inhibition of sodium channels with 1 μM tetrodotoxin not only abolished the APs but also fully blocked the sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: Per neuron, sessions before and about 5 min after TTX or vehicle at the same field (Figure S2 legend). Reproduced when, in every TTX neuron, APs (as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all) present before are absent after and the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus is above 5% before and below it after, while vehicle neurons keep their response. The window and level are standard choices.

claims.statement: FluoVolt sensitivity to 2-us pulses averaged 28% plus or minus 2.5% per 1 kV/cm (15% to 47%), and to 2-kHz sine waves 11.8% plus or minus 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, 42% of the pulse value, smaller in every ROI.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraphs 4 and 5; Figures 6B to 6D
claims.quote: All numbers were invariably smaller than those measured for the same ROIs with the pulse ( Figure 6D ). The electric field sensitivity averaged across all ROIs in all the cells was 11.8% ± 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, just 42% of the value for the 2-μs pulses
claims.criterion: Pulse sensitivity is |dF| averaged from 1 to 2 us into the 257 V/cm pulse, per kV/cm (Results; Figure 6B legend). Sine sensitivity is the regression coefficient of the emission change on the electric field after subtracting the LOESS fit of the whole-cell response (Figure 5H and 6C legends); the LOESS span and the form of the regression are not given, and their readings are those of the claims file for DANDI:001274, which tests this claim on its own data. Reproduced when the ratio is below 1 in all 18 ROIs and the expected values are within tolerance under every reading.

claims.statement: In single cells, sine waves polarized the two poles more asymmetrically than a 2-us pulse (ROI 2 up to 90% smaller than ROI 1 with sine waves against 30% with the pulse in Figure 5; 40% against 20% in Figure S3), with carrier oscillations antiphasic in the two ROIs on a gradual whole-cell depolarization.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figures 5B to 5D and S3
claims.quote: Unexpectedly, in this cell, the oscillations in ROI 2 were up to 90% smaller than those in ROI 1 (compared to just 30% smaller when the same cell was polarized with the 2-μs pulse)
claims.criterion: Measures and readings as in the claims file for DANDI:001274 (fig5-sine-asymmetry-c7, figs3-sine-asymmetry-c8, fig5-carrier-antiphasic and fig5-whole-cell-depolarization), which tests this finding on its own data. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance and the antiphasic oscillations and whole-cell depolarization are found, under the readings that file names.

claims.statement: The 2-kHz AP threshold of 57.7 V/cm times the sine wave sensitivity gives a 0.68% emission change, about 6.8 mV, so the threshold depolarization is 5 to 15 mV, as with intracellular current injection.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 6
claims.quote: This threshold corresponds to a 0.68% ± 0.11% FluoVolt emission change (11.8 × 57.7/1,000) ... a 0.68% emission change corresponds to a 6.8-mV depolarization at the AP threshold
claims.criterion: Mean sine sensitivity of fig6-sine-less-than-pulse times the mean unmodulated 2-kHz 1-AP threshold of fig2d-modulated-thresholds-higher, divided by 1,000, and that times 10 mV per 1% (the calibration of reference 47 as the paper uses it). Tolerances are the SEMs the paper gives, the last being the 0.11% times 10 mV per 1%. Reproduced when all three are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Unmodulated 250-ms sine waves at 2 kHz and at 20 kHz excited every neuron tested, never as an on-off response.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 1A to 1C
claims.quote: Pure sine waves at 2 and even 20 kHz excited 100% of neurons. It was never an "on-off" response
claims.criterion: Per neuron, excited when at least one session with an unmodulated 2- or 20-kHz sine wave has an AP during the 250-ms stimulus. The Methods give no detection rule beyond "brief emission upticks" in neurons whose APs peak above 5% dF and last about 10 ms (Recording of the optical APs); readings (a) a peak of dF above 5% over F0, (b) a rise of at least 5% dF within 5 ms, which also counts APs riding on a depolarization. Reproduced when, under each reading, at least 90% of neurons tested with each frequency are excited; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: Near threshold, isolated APs appear 100 to 200 ms after the sine wave onset, and stronger fields shorten this delay and evoke sustained firing.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 1A to 1C
claims.quote: at near-threshold electric field strengths, isolated APs emerged with a delay of 100-200 ms after the sine wave onset ... Increasing the field strength reduced this delay and evoked sustained firing
claims.criterion: AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, both readings. Per neuron and frequency, the near-threshold session is the session of lowest field with at least one AP. Reproduced when the median first-AP latency of those sessions lies within 90 to 220 ms (the range widened by 10% of each bound) and, per neuron, the first-AP latency falls with field (Spearman correlation below zero in more than half of the neurons with at least three sessions with APs). The paper gives no test for either part; the median, the Spearman sign and the majority are standard choices.

claims.statement: The maximum firing rate increases linearly with field strength until it reaches a ceiling of 60 to 90 Hz.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 1 inset
claims.quote: The maximum firing rate increased linearly until reaching a ceiling of 60-90 Hz
claims.criterion: The maximum firing rate of a session is the inverse of the interval between the peaks of its first two APs (Methods, Recording of the optical APs); AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, both readings. The ceiling of a neuron is its highest maximum firing rate over sessions with unmodulated sine waves. Reproduced when the median ceiling over neurons lies within 54 to 99 Hz (60 to 90 Hz widened by 10% of each bound). The rise below the ceiling is reported as the slope of a linear fit of rate on field over the sessions before the ceiling; the inset shows three neurons only.

claims.statement: At the highest field strengths, APs coalesce into low-amplitude oscillations on a continuous depolarization, which can flatten and leave the membrane depolarized for the rest of the sine wave (an excitation block).
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz unmodulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 1A to 1C
claims.quote: At the highest field strengths, multiple APs coalesced into low-amplitude oscillations on top of a continuous depolarization. These oscillations could flatten after several cycles, leaving the membrane depolarized for the rest of the sine wave
claims.criterion: The paper gives no measure. Per neuron, the session of highest field with an unmodulated sine wave is compared with the near-threshold session (as in fig1-onset-delay). Reproduced when, in more than half of the neurons, the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus in the highest-field session exceeds the pre-stimulus F0 by more than 5% dF (the Methods' AP selection level) and exceeds that of the near-threshold session. The windows are a standard choice; the mean over the whole second half of the stimulus is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: All excitation thresholds at 20 kHz were about twice those at 2 kHz, for modulated and unmodulated sine waves and for 1 and 5 APs.
claims.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
claims.quote: All thresholds at 20 kHz were about 2-fold higher than at 2 kHz ( p < 0.0001, two-tailed unpaired t test)
claims.criterion: The threshold of a neuron for a stimulus is the lowest field of a session that evoked at least 1 (or at least 5) APs during the 250-ms stimulus (Figure 2D legend; Methods, 5% to 10% amplitude steps); AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, both readings. For each of the four groups (unmodulated and modulated, 1 and 5 APs) the ratio of mean 20-kHz to mean 2-kHz threshold, and a two-tailed unpaired t test of the two (Methods, Quantification and statistical analysis). The paper gives one p for "all thresholds", so which comparison it is open; readings (a) one test per group, each p < 0.0001, (b) one test pooling the four groups, 20 kHz against 2 kHz. Reproduced when each ratio is within tolerance and the test gives p < 0.0001 under both readings of the test; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The field per session is taken from the dataset's metadata; the paper gives the conversion from volts to V/cm only as the simulated profile of Figure S4C, with no number in the text, so a session without a recorded field is open.

claims.statement: Thresholds for sine waves modulated at 20 Hz were significantly higher than for pure sine waves of the same carrier, for 5 APs at 2 kHz and for 1 and 5 APs at 20 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Excitation thresholds are similar or lower for pure 2- and 20-kHz sine waves than those for modulated sine waves, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
claims.quote: thresholds for modulated sine waves, which emulate the TI stimulus at the target, were significantly higher than those for pure sine waves at the same frequency (for 2 kHz, 5 APs ... p = 0.0079; for 20 kHz, 1 and 5 APs, respectively ... p = 0.0142 and p = 0.0037)
claims.criterion: Thresholds as in fig2d-20khz-twofold-threshold. For each of the three pairs, a two-tailed unpaired t test of modulated against unmodulated thresholds, as the Results and the Figure 2D legend name it, although the same neurons were often tested with both; the paired test on neurons with both is shown as a variant. Reproduced when all three have the modulated mean higher with p < 0.05 (the Methods' level; the legend marks p < 0.02); partially reproduced when one or two do. The 2-kHz 1-AP pair, for which the paper reports no difference, is reported.

claims.statement: The AP threshold for unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves was 57.7 plus or minus 3.6 V/cm.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 6; Figure 2D
claims.quote: the AP threshold of 57.7 ± 3.6 V/cm for unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves ( Figure 2D )
claims.criterion: The mean over neurons of the 1-AP threshold as in fig2d-20khz-twofold-threshold, under both AP readings; reproduced when both are within tolerance (the SEM the paper gives), blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: With 20-Hz modulation, firing above threshold is locked to the beats, one AP near the peak of each of the five beats and at most two per beat (ten in all), and modulated sine waves trigger no sustained firing or sustained depolarization.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 1; Figures 2A and 2B
claims.quote: single APs emerged near the peak of each beat, so the firing rate equaled the modulation rate ... the maximum number of APs evoked by five beats was limited to ten. Unlike pure sine waves, modulated stimuli did not trigger sustained firing or sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, both readings. For sessions with modulated sine waves, reproduced when (i) no session has more than 10 APs, (ii) in sessions with 5 APs or more, at least 80% of APs fall within the middle half of a 50-ms beat (12.5 to 37.5 ms from the beat's start, the peak at 25 ms), and (iii) no session meets the excitation block test of fig1-excitation-block. The 80% and the window are a reading of "near the peak", which the paper does not quantify; the AP phase histogram over the beat is reported.

claims.statement: In the same neuron at the same field strength, pure sine waves trigger more APs than modulated ones.
claims.source: Results, Stimulation by 2- and 20-kHz sinusoids modulated at 20 Hz, paragraph 2; Figure 2C
claims.quote: At the same field strengths, pure sine waves triggered a larger number of APs
claims.criterion: AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, both readings. Pairs are a neuron's modulated and unmodulated sessions at the same carrier and the same field. Reproduced when the unmodulated AP count exceeds the modulated count in more pairs than the reverse, with a two-sided paired t test of the counts at p < 0.05 (Methods, Quantification and statistical analysis); the paper reports no test, so the test is its general one.

claims.statement: Replacing NaCl with sodium gluconate, lowering conductivity from 16.4 to 8.4 mS/cm, reversibly lowered excitation thresholds about 2-fold at all sine wave frequencies from 2 to 20 kHz.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 1; Figures 3A and 3B
claims.quote: Switching to the NaGlu-based solution reversibly and reproducibly decreased excitation thresholds ~2-fold across all sine wave frequencies tested
claims.criterion: The 1-AP threshold for 250-ms unmodulated sine waves (Figure 3B legend), as in fig2d-20khz-twofold-threshold, per neuron, frequency and solution; 4 to 8 neurons per point. Reproduced when the ratio of mean NaCl to mean NaGlu threshold is within tolerance at every frequency tested; partially reproduced when it is above 1 at every frequency but outside tolerance at some.

claims.statement: In the low-conductivity solution, a 2-s unmodulated 2-kHz sine wave ramped up over 250 ms evoked sustained firing for the whole stimulus; firing rate rose with field strength until replaced by a firing block with sustained depolarization, which developed before the end of the ramp.
claims.source: Results, Decreased extracellular conductivity lowers excitation thresholds, paragraph 3; Figure 3C
claims.quote: we observed sustained firing for the entire duration of the sine wave ( Figure 3C ). The rate of firing increased with the electric field strength until it was replaced by a firing block and sustained depolarization. The block had already developed before the end of the 250-ms ramp-up period
claims.criterion: Traces corrected for bleaching by subtracting a trace without APs (Methods); AP detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all, both readings. Reproduced when (i) at an intermediate field, APs occur in the last 250 ms of the 2-s stimulus, (ii) the AP count rises with field up to some field, and (iii) at the highest field there are no APs after 250 ms with dF above F0 by more than 5% (as in fig1-excitation-block) over the rest of the stimulus.

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS instead of FluoVolt, in eight neurons, stimulation near threshold elicited one or a few delayed APs and stronger fields induced sustained firing ending in sustained depolarization, as with FluoVolt.
claims.source: Results, Sensitivity to unmodulated sine waves was not caused by FluoVolt dye, paragraph 1; Figure S1
claims.quote: Stimulation near the threshold elicited one or a few delayed APs. Increasing the electric field strength reduced the delay and induced sustained firing that culminated in sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: Traces inverted, as Di-8-ANEPPS emission falls with depolarization (Methods). AP detection and the tests of fig1-onset-delay and fig1-excitation-block, applied to the eight neurons; the 5% dF level is the FluoVolt one, and the paper notes Di-8-ANEPPS is less sensitive, so the readings add a level of 5 times the pre-stimulus SD of each trace. Reproduced when, under every reading, every neuron is excited, latency falls with field in more than half, and the highest field meets the block test in more than half; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: 1 uM tetrodotoxin abolished both the APs and the sustained depolarization caused by intense unmodulated 2-kHz sine waves.
claims.source: Results, Tetrodotoxin blocks sustained depolarization, paragraph 1; Figure S2
claims.quote: the inhibition of sodium channels with 1 μM tetrodotoxin not only abolished the APs but also fully blocked the sustained depolarization
claims.criterion: Per neuron, the session in normal solution and the session about 5 min after TTX at the same field (Figure S2 legend). Reproduced when, in every TTX neuron, APs (detection as in fig1-pure-sine-excites-all) present before are absent after, and the mean dF over the last 100 ms of the stimulus (as in fig1-excitation-block) is above 5% before and below 5% after, while the vehicle neuron keeps its response.

claims.statement: Elongated neurons aligned with the field have about twice the charging and discharging time constants of the same cells perpendicular to it, or of randomly shaped cells.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, paragraph 3; Figures 4A, 4D and 4E
claims.quote: Aligning elongated cells with the electric field doubled the time constants, as compared to either the same cells oriented perpendicular to the field ( p < 0.001, paired t test) or to randomly shaped cells ( p < 0.01, unpaired t test)
claims.criterion: Per cell, pole and orientation, dF in the most de- and hyperpolarized ROIs averaged over the eight replicates and fitted with dF = dFmax (1 - exp(-t/tau)) during the pulse and dF = dFmax exp(-t/tau) after it (Methods), with and without debris scaling. Groups as in the Figure 4D and 4E legend (parallel n = 3, perpendicular n = 6, random n = 10). The text names a paired t test (p < 0.001) for parallel against perpendicular, while the legend marks p < 0.01 between the orthogonal orientations with an unpaired two-tailed t test, and the group n differ; readings for that test are (a) paired, on the elongated cells imaged in both orientations, (b) unpaired, on the legend's groups. The time constants compared are the charging tau and the discharging tau, at each pole. Reproduced when, for both, the parallel mean is within tolerance of twice the perpendicular mean and of twice the random mean, and the parallel against random test reaches p < 0.01 and the orientation test its stated p (0.001 paired, 0.01 unpaired) in at least one pole, under both readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: The maximum optical TMP and the charging and discharging time constants did not differ between the cathode- and anode-facing poles, indicating no rectification of the field.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, paragraph 3; Figures 4D and 4E
claims.quote: Δ F max did not differ at the cathodic and anodic cell poles, indicating the lack of rectification of the applied electric field. Charging and discharging time constants did not differ between the two poles either
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The paper does not name the test; the Methods use a two-sided Student's t test, paired or unpaired as appropriate, at p < 0.05, and the two poles are in the same cell, so the test is a two-sided paired t test over all 19 experiments of |dFmax|, charging tau and discharging tau, cathodic against anodic. Fits as in fig4-orientation-time-constants. Reproduced when none of the three is significant; the mean differences are given either way.

claims.statement: Discharging time constants were larger than charging ones in the same cell, except in elongated cells aligned with the field.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, paragraph 3; Figures 4D and 4E
claims.quote: discharging time constants were always larger than the charging ones in the same cell ( p < 0.001, paired t test), with the exception of elongated cells aligned with the field
claims.criterion: Fits as in fig4-orientation-time-constants. Two-sided paired t test of discharging against charging tau over cells and poles. The pooling is not given; readings (a) all 19 experiments, both poles, (b) the cells other than elongated parallel ones, both poles, (c) as (b), each pole alone (the legend's hash sign marks p < 0.01 per group). Reproduced when, under one reading, discharging tau is larger with p < 0.001, and the parallel group shows no significant difference at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Pooled over all 19 experiments, the charging and discharging time constants were 0.7 and 0.91 us at the cathodic pole and 0.65 and 0.8 us at the anodic pole, so membranes exceed 95% of full charge within 3 us.
claims.source: Results, Kinetics of membrane charging by pulsed electric fields, paragraph 3; Figures 4D and 4E (ALL)
claims.quote: The time constants pooled together for all cells averaged 0.7 ± 0.08 (charging) and 0.91 ± 0.08 (discharging) μs for the cathodic cell pole and 0.65 ± 0.05 and 0.8 ± 0.07 μs for the anodic pole, respectively (mean ± SEM, n = 19)
claims.criterion: Fits as in fig4-orientation-time-constants; for random cells both field orientations are pooled (Figure 4D and 4E legend). Whether ALL averages per cell or per cell and orientation is open (the paper's n = 19 counts experiments); readings (a) the mean over all cell and orientation fits, (b) the mean over cells of each cell's mean over its orientations. Reproduced when, under one reading, all four are within tolerance (the SEMs the paper gives).

claims.statement: During a single beat of a 2-kHz sine wave, the optical TMP in ROIs 1 and 2 oscillates with the carrier in opposite phases, with amplitude proportional to the sine wave amplitude, on top of a gradual whole-cell depolarization.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 2; Figures 5C, 5D and 5H
