claims.quote: Optical TMP oscillated in synchrony with the carrier sine wave in the opposite phases ... These oscillations, proportional to the sine wave amplitude, were superimposed on the gradual depolarization of the entire cell
claims.criterion: Cell C7 (O4), both modulation rates (100 and 154 Hz), dF per frame averaged over its sessions, LOESS-subtracted (O2, all readings). Reproduced when, under every reading, (i) the largest peak of the power spectrum of each subtracted trace above 500 Hz is at 2 kHz within one frequency bin, (ii) the Pearson correlation of the ROI 1 and ROI 2 subtracted traces is below zero with p < 0.05 (the Methods' level), and (iii) the regression of fig6c-sine-sensitivity (O3, reading a) has opposite signs in the two ROIs. The paper gives no test; the spectral peak, the Pearson correlation and the sign of the regression are standard choices, with the Methods' p < 0.05. The whole-cell depolarization is tested in fig5-whole-cell-depolarization.

claims.statement: During the sine wave beat the whole cell gradually depolarizes as the sine wave amplitude grows, then repolarizes.
claims.source: Figure 5C and 5D legend; Figures 5C and 5D
claims.quote: These high-frequency oscillations superimpose a gradual whole-cell depolarization that develops as the sine wave amplitude increases
claims.criterion: Cell C7 (O4), each modulation rate and ROI. The whole-cell response is the LOESS fit of the raw dF (Figure 5 legend; O2, all readings), fitted per session. The paper gives no test; its general test is the two-sided t test at p < 0.05 (Methods). The measure is open; readings (a) the mean of the LOESS fit over the beat, (b) the LOESS fit at the beat's peak (half the beat), each tested against zero over sessions with a one-sample two-sided t test. Reproduced when, under every reading, both ROIs are depolarized (positive, FluoVolt emission rising with depolarization) with p < 0.05 at both rates; partially reproduced when that holds at one rate. The same measure in the other eight cells is reported.

claims.statement: In the cell of Figure 5, the 2-us pulse depolarized ROI 2 about 30% less than it hyperpolarized ROI 1, while the sine wave oscillations in ROI 2 were up to 90% smaller than in ROI 1.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figures 5B to 5D
claims.quote: Unexpectedly, in this cell, the oscillations in ROI 2 were up to 90% smaller than those in ROI 1 (compared to just 30% smaller when the same cell was polarized with the 2-μs pulse)
claims.criterion: Cell C7 (O4). Pulse, readings (p1) the dF averaged 1 to 2 us into the pulse (Figure 6B measure), (p2) the largest |dF| of the 5-point running average during the pulse (Figure 5B legend). Sine wave, at 100 and 154 Hz, the larger of the two reductions, under readings (s1) the ratio of the ROIs' sensitivities as in fig6c-sine-sensitivity (O3 a and b), (s2) per carrier cycle half the peak-to-peak of the subtracted dF, taking the largest reduction over cycles whose ROI 1 amplitude is at least half its maximum ("up to"). Each with all O2 readings. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one pulse and one sine reading for every O2 reading.

claims.statement: In a second neuron (Figure S3), polarization in ROI 1 was 20% smaller than in ROI 2 with the 2-us pulse and 40% smaller with sine waves, and the antiphasic oscillations did not move to a new area.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 3; Figure S3
claims.quote: With the 2-μs pulse, polarization in ROI 1 was 20% smaller than in ROI 2 ( Figure S3B ); however, with sine waves, it became 40% smaller
claims.criterion: Cell C8 (O4), measures and readings as in fig5-sine-asymmetry-c7, except that the sine wave value is not qualified by "up to", so reading (s2) uses the median over cycles whose ROI 2 amplitude is at least half its maximum. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one pulse and one sine reading for every O2 reading. The part on migration needs the ROIs of Figure S3E and S3F and is reported, not judged, as their positions are only in the figure.

claims.statement: Over 16 further ROIs around the cell of Figure 5, strong oscillations were found on one side only, and the relatively large oscillations of ROIs 12 to 14 on the other side were not antiphasic to them, so the small ROI 2 oscillations did not come from migration of the polarized area.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 2; Figures 5E to 5G
claims.quote: strong oscillations were observed on one side only ( Figure 5F ), and the relatively large oscillations in ROIs 12-14 in Figure 5G were not antiphasic to those in Figure 5F
claims.criterion: Needs the 16 ROIs of Figure 5E with the paper's numbering (O1); blocked as metadata_insufficient if the dataset lacks them. Cell C7, the 154-Hz beat (Figures 5F and 5G are "same as (D)"), sensitivity per ROI as in fig6c-sine-sensitivity with its sign (O2 and O3 readings). Reproduced when, under every reading, the signed sensitivities of ROIs 12, 13 and 14 have the sign of the Figure 5F ROIs' median, and the largest |sensitivity| among the Figure 5G ROIs is below the largest among the Figure 5F ROIs. Which of the 16 ROIs belong to Figure 5F and which to 5G is shown only in the figure (the text says only that they lie on opposite sides of the cell, with 12 to 14 in 5G); without that split from the dataset the claim is blocked as metadata_insufficient.

claims.statement: The FluoVolt response to 2-us pulses, averaged 1 to 2 us into the pulse, ranged from 15% to 47% per 1 kV/cm, averaging 28% plus or minus 2.5% over all ROIs in the nine cells.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 4; Figure 6B
claims.quote: The electric field sensitivity of FluoVolt ranged between a 15% and 47% change per 1 kV/cm, with an average value of 28% ± 2.5% across all ROIs in all the cells
claims.criterion: Per cell C1 to C9 and ROI 1 and 2 (O1), |dF| averaged over the 21 frames from 1 to 2 us into the 257 V/cm pulse, divided by 0.257 kV/cm (or the field recorded for the cell), with and without debris scaling. Reproduced when, under both, the mean over the 18 ROIs is within tolerance (the SEM the paper gives) and every ROI lies within 13.5% to 51.7% (15% to 47% widened by 10% of each bound); blocked as methods_underspecified when the two disagree.

claims.statement: The sine-wave-induced TMP oscillations were linearly correlated with the electric field (p below 0.01% for both ROIs in eight of the nine cells), with sensitivities from 1.5% to 28.4% per 1 kV/cm.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 5; Figure 6C
claims.quote: The oscillations displayed a robust linear correlation with the electric field ... <0.01% for both ROIs in eight cells. The regression coefficient, which was the FluoVolt sensitivity to sine waves, varied from 1.5% to 28.4%
claims.criterion: Per cell C1 to C9 and ROI 1 and 2 (O1), the 2-kHz beat modulated at 100 Hz (Figure 6C legend), dF from the sine wave F0, averaged over sessions, LOESS-subtracted (O2), regressed on the field (O3, readings a and b, with and without debris scaling); sensitivity is |slope| in % per kV/cm. Reproduced when, under every O2 and O3 reading, both ROIs have p < 0.0001 in at least eight cells and every sensitivity lies within 1.35% to 31.2% (1.5% to 28.4% widened by 10% of each bound); blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: Every ROI's sensitivity to sine waves was smaller than to the pulse; averaged over all ROIs it was 11.8% plus or minus 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, 42% of the pulse value.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 5; Figures 6C and 6D
claims.quote: All numbers were invariably smaller than those measured for the same ROIs with the pulse ( Figure 6D ). The electric field sensitivity averaged across all ROIs in all the cells was 11.8% ± 1.7% per 1 kV/cm, just 42% of the value for the 2-μs pulses
claims.criterion: Sensitivities as in fig6b-pulse-sensitivity and fig6c-sine-sensitivity, with the same scaling in both. The Figure 6D legend's "ratio of values in (D) and (C)" is read as sine (C) over pulse (B). Reproduced when, under every O2 and O3 reading, the sine to pulse ratio is below 1 in all 18 ROIs and both expected values are within tolerance; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: Combining the sine wave sensitivity (11.8% per kV/cm) with the 2-kHz AP threshold (57.7 V/cm) gives a 0.68% emission change, about 6.8 mV at FluoVolt's calibration of about 10% per 100 mV, so the threshold depolarization is 5 to 15 mV.
claims.source: Results, Asymmetric and less-efficient membrane charging by sine waves compared to pulses, paragraph 6
claims.quote: This threshold corresponds to a 0.68% ± 0.11% FluoVolt emission change (11.8 × 57.7/1,000) ... a 0.68% emission change corresponds to a 6.8-mV depolarization at the AP threshold
claims.criterion: The product of the mean sine wave sensitivity of fig6d-sine-less-than-pulse and the mean threshold of threshold-2khz-unmodulated, divided by 1,000, and that times 10 mV per 1% (the calibration of reference 47, as the paper uses it). Reproduced when both are within tolerance under one reading of each claim it depends on.

claims.statement: In both CT26 and CHO cells, YP uptake at the array center increases linearly with the number of bursts (slopes different from zero at p < 0.001), except for saturation at 6 bursts (x4) in CT26 cells.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 1; Figure 7B and 7E and legend
claims.quote: The increase was linear in both cell lines, except when it reached saturation after 6 bursts (x4) in CT26 cells
claims.criterion: Center YP is the background-subtracted intensity of the ROI at 0 mm, by the profile method, in a.u. A linear fit of center YP on burst number (1, 2, 4, 6 bursts (x4)), with the 6-burst point excluded in CT26 as the Fig. 7 legend says, and its slope tested against zero by a 2-sided one-sample t test (Fig. 7 legend). The paper does not say whether the fit is to individual experiments or to group means; the readings are (a) individual experiments and (b) group means. Burst number counted as 1, 2, 4, 6 or as 4, 8, 16, 24 total bursts gives the same p. Reproduced when, under one reading, both slopes are positive with p < 0.001; partially reproduced when that holds in one cell line only. A cell line absent from the dataset is reported as untested and the claim judged on the other.

claims.statement: In CT26 cells the central YP uptake saturates at 6 bursts (x4), falling below the linear increase seen from 1 to 4 bursts, while CHO cells show no saturation.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 7B and 7E legend
claims.quote: Considering that even 2 bursts (x4) caused strong cell death in the center ( Fig. 5 ), saturation was expected and indicated that all cells were already killed and YP staining reached its maximum
claims.criterion: The paper gives no test of saturation; it shows it by excluding the 6-burst point from the CT26 fit and by the 95% confidence band of that fit (Fig. 7 legend). Reproduced when the CT26 mean center YP at 6 bursts (x4) lies below the lower edge of the 95% confidence band of the linear fit through 1, 2 and 4 bursts, extrapolated to 6, and the CHO 6-burst mean lies within the band of the CHO fit through 1, 2 and 4 bursts. This band test is the file's reading; the paper's own CHO fit (Fig. 7E) uses all four burst numbers, and its significant slope is tested in fig7be-center-linear-with-bursts. Partially reproduced when the CT26 point lies below the fitted line but within the band. Readings (a) and (b) of fig7be-center-linear-with-bursts apply.

claims.statement: The FWHM of the central YP peak increases in proportion to the number of bursts in CT26 cells (slope p < 0.001) but not in CHO cells (p = 0.44).
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 7C and 7F and legend
claims.quote: Concurrently, FWHM of the central peak increased proportionally to the burst number in CT26 cells, but not in CHO cells
claims.criterion: FWHM from Lorentzian fits of each experiment's diagonal profile, by the profile method. CHO uses 2, 4 and 6 bursts (x4), since after one burst YP uptake was too small to measure FWHM (Fig. 7 legend); CT26 uses all four burst numbers (the legend excludes the 6-burst point from panel B only). Linear fit of FWHM on burst number with its slope tested by a 2-sided one-sample t test. Open details and their readings, the fit range (-4 to 4, -5 to 5, -6 to 6 mm), the ROI spacing (1 or 0.5 mm), and whether the linear fit is to individual experiments or to group means. Reproduced when, under one reading, the CT26 slope is positive with p < 0.001 and the CHO slope has p >= 0.05; partially reproduced when only one of the two holds.

claims.statement: One burst (x4) in CT26 cells gives the sharpest peak of the study, FWHM 1.1 +/- 0.1 mm, 7.3% of the inter-electrode gap and 2.3% of the electrode array area.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 7C
claims.quote: 1 burst (x4) in CT26 cells produced the sharpest peak of electroporation seen in this study ... at FWHM of 1.1 ± 0.1 mm, it occupied just 7.3% of the inter-electrode gap and 2.3% of the electrode array area
claims.criterion: Mean over CT26 experiments of the per-experiment Lorentzian FWHM at 1 burst (x4), by the profile method, with its tolerance the paper's stated spread (+/- 0.1 mm, a s.e.). The gap is the 15.3 mm diagonal (Results 3.3 gives 1.7 mm as 11.1%). The paper does not say how the area percentage is computed. Readings, (a) a disk of diameter FWHM over the square with 15.3 mm diagonals (117 mm2); (b) a disk of radius FWHM over the square of the electrode centers (12.8 mm sides, 164 mm2), the one reading found that gives 2.3% from 1.1 mm; (c) a disk of diameter FWHM over the square of the electrode centers. Reproduced when the FWHM and the gap percentage are within tolerance and the area percentage is within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when the FWHM alone is. Open details of the profile method (fit range, ROI spacing) are run under each reading.

claims.statement: With 1 burst (x4) in CT26 cells, YP uptake near the electrodes is 40 to 50 times smaller than at the remote target in the center.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Off-target effects, characterized by YP emission near electrodes, were 40–50 times smaller than at the remote target
claims.criterion: The reported range 40 to 50, widened by 10% of each bound, is 36 to 55, which the value and tolerance give. Background-subtracted YP by the profile method. Readings the text allows, near electrodes as (a) 6 mm or (b) 7 mm from the center (Results 3.1); the ratio as (i) of group means or (ii) the mean of per-experiment ratios. The group meant is also open. The sentence follows the 1 burst (x4) result, giving reading (A), 1 burst (x4) only; it closes a paragraph on all CT26 burst numbers, and a range of 40 to 50 can be the span over groups, giving reading (B), the ratios for 1, 2 and 4 bursts (x4) in CT26 (6 bursts saturates) each lie in 36 to 55. Reproduced when the ratio lies in 36 to 55 under one reading.

claims.statement: CANCAN remote focusing of electroporation found in CT26 cells also holds in CHO cells, which show a central peak of YP uptake that grows with burst number.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 1; Conclusion; Figure 7D
claims.quote: Increasing the number of bursts increased the amplitude of the central peak of YP uptake in both CT26 and CHO cells ( Fig 7A and D )
claims.criterion: Diagonal profiles of CHO monolayers by the profile method. Reproduced when, for each burst number from 2 bursts (x4) up (after one burst CHO uptake was too small to measure FWHM, Fig. 7 legend; the 1-burst profile is reported), the mean center YP exceeds the mean YP at both 6 and 7 mm (the paper's measure of focusing, center against near electrodes, Results 3.1); together with the CHO part of fig7be-center-linear-with-bursts.

claims.statement: At a packet rate of 0.2 MHz, YP uptake in the center was 40-fold higher than near the electrodes, despite a roughly 4-fold stronger electric field near the electrodes.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 3; Figure 4B
claims.quote: Now, by increasing the packet repetition rate to 0.2 MHz, we achieved a 40-fold difference ( Fig. 4B ), despite using a bigger array with larger reduction of the electric field from electrodes to the center
claims.criterion: Background-subtracted YP by the profile method, CT26, 2 bursts (x4), 0.2 MHz. Readings as for fig7-offtarget-40-50-fold, near electrodes at (a) 6 mm or (b) 7 mm, ratio (i) of group means or (ii) the mean of per-experiment ratios. Reproduced when the ratio is within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: All CANCAN protocols enhance electroporation at the center of the array, while the unipolar control produces electroporation that decreases toward the center.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 3A to 3C
claims.quote: All CANCAN protocols visibly enhanced electroporation at the center of the array, in contrast to its gradual decrease toward the center in the control
claims.criterion: CT26, 2 bursts (x4), diagonal profiles by the profile method. The paper's measure of focusing is the ratio of YP uptake in the center to that near electrodes (Results 3.1, paragraph 3). Reproduced when the group-mean ratio of center YP to YP at 6 mm and to YP at 7 mm exceeds 1 for every CANCAN packet rate and is below 1 for the control.

claims.statement: Increasing the packet rate from 1 Hz to 0.2 MHz suppresses electroporation near the electrodes and at the perimeter between electrodes, so that the excess of YP uptake over the Lorentzian fit at larger distances from the center diminishes with packet rate.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraphs 2 and 4; Figure 3B and 3C
claims.quote: The deviation of experimental data from the fits at larger distances from the center diminished with increasing the packet repetition rate, highlighting better suppression of the off-target electroporation
claims.criterion: CT26, 2 bursts (x4), CANCAN packet rates, group-mean profiles along the diagonals (Fig. 3B) and along the lines through the center parallel to the sides (Fig. 3C), with the Lorentzian fitted from -4 to 4 mm as in fig3bc-lorentzian-profile. The paper gives no measure or test of the deviation. The measure used is the mean of observed minus fitted YP over the ROIs beyond 4 mm from the center, in % of the fitted peak a, which is the plain reading of "deviation of experimental data from the fits at larger distances". Reproduced when, in both directions, it is smaller at 0.2 MHz than at 1 Hz; the values for every rate are reported.

claims.statement: The decline of YP uptake sideways from the center is bell-shaped and follows a Lorentzian, with a nearly perfect fit within 4 mm of the center (R > 0.9, p < 0.001).
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 4; Figure 3B and 3C; Methods 2.5
claims.quote: The fit correlation with data in the −4 to 4 mm radius was nearly perfect (R>0.9, p<0.001)
claims.criterion: CT26, 2 bursts (x4), CANCAN packet rates. Lorentzian fitted to the group-mean profile from -4 to 4 mm (the dotted fits of Fig. 3B and 3C), along the diagonals (Fig. 3B) and along the lines through the center parallel to the sides (Fig. 3C); the correlation R of fitted and observed values within that range. Reproduced when R > 0.9 with p < 0.001 for every rate and both directions; partially reproduced when it holds for most of them.

claims.statement: YP uptake in the center of the array shows no significant effect of the packet rate.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 5; Figure 4B
claims.quote: YP intensity in the center showed no significant effect of the packet rate ( t -test with Bonferroni correction, Fig. 4B )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. Center YP (ROI at 0 mm) of CT26, 2 bursts (x4), at each packet rate compared with 1 Hz by two-sided Student's t-tests with Bonferroni correction over the comparisons, the same family as the Fig. 4C legend uses for the same experiments. Reproduced when no comparison has corrected p < 0.05; not reproduced when any does. Effect sizes are given either way; all pairs of rates are shown as a variant.

claims.statement: YP uptake at 6 and 7 mm from the center (near the electrodes) declines steeply with increasing packet rate, so that higher rates suppress off-target electroporation despite a stronger electric field there.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraphs 2 and 5; Figure 4A and 4B
claims.quote: It contrasted with a steep, packet rate-dependent decline of YP uptake at 6 and 7 mm from the center (i.e., 1.65 and 0.65 mm from electrodes)
claims.criterion: CT26, 2 bursts (x4), YP at 6 and at 7 mm by the profile method. The paper fits a power function of packet rate (Fig. 4B legend) and gives no test. Reproduced when, at both distances, the power-function exponent fitted to YP against packet rate is negative and YP at 0.2 MHz is lower than at 1 Hz by a two-sided t-test at p < 0.05 (Methods 2.5). The paper does not say whether the power function is fitted to group means or to individual experiments; both are run.

claims.statement: Higher packet rates focus electroporation into a smaller spot, FWHM decreasing from about 4 mm at 1 Hz to about 2 mm at 1 kHz, 10 kHz and 0.2 MHz, less than 15% of the gap between electrodes.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraphs 6 and 7; Figure 4C
claims.quote: FWHM decreased from ~4 mm at 1 Hz to ~2 mm at 1 kHz, 10 kHz, and 0.2 MHz packet rates (p = 0.03; 0.02, and 0.09, respectively; t -test with Bonferroni correction)
claims.criterion: CT26, 2 bursts (x4); per-experiment Lorentzian FWHM by the profile method, fitted from -4 to 4 mm (Results 3.1, Fig. 3 legend), averaged per rate. Each value is checked against its expected value. Each rate against 1 Hz by two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction (Fig. 4C legend). The paper's p for 0.2 MHz (0.09) is not below 0.05, so the claim's test is that the means fall within tolerance and the 1 kHz and 10 kHz comparisons reach corrected p < 0.05; the 0.2 MHz p is reported. Reproduced when all that holds and the smallest mean FWHM is below 15% of 15.3 mm; partially reproduced when the decrease is present but values miss tolerance or the tests fail.

claims.statement: FWHM decreases with the logarithm of packet rate from 1 Hz to 10 kHz (R = 0.77, p < 0.001), with no further gain in focality from 10 kHz to 0.2 MHz.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 6; Figure 4C legend
claims.quote: FWHM decrease followed the logarithmic dependence from 1 Hz to 10 kHz (correlation coefficient R = 0.77, p<0.001), but there was no further focality increase when the packet rate increased from 10 kHz to 0.2 MHz
claims.criterion: Per-experiment FWHM as in fig4c-fwhm-decreases-with-rate; linear regression of FWHM on log of packet rate over the 15 experiments below 0.2 MHz (Fig. 4C legend), slope tested by a 2-sided one-sample t test. Reproduced when the slope is negative with p < 0.001 and |R| is within tolerance, and the 0.2 MHz mean FWHM is not lower than the 10 kHz mean by a two-sided t-test at p < 0.05 (Methods 2.5).

claims.statement: With MHz-CANCAN there is practically no YP staining near the electrodes, and raising the electrodes 1 or 2 mm above the monolayer weakens electroporation in the central spot.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 1; Figure 5A and 5B
claims.quote: there was practically no YP staining near electrodes to start with, so the only clear effect of raising electrodes was the weakening of electroporation in the central spot
claims.criterion: CT26, 0.2 MHz, 2 bursts (x4); center YP (ROI at 0 mm) by the profile method, in % of the 0 mm elevation peak (Fig. 5B legend). The paper gives no test. Reproduced when center YP at 1 mm and at 2 mm elevation is each lower than at 0 mm by a two-sided t-test with Bonferroni correction over the two comparisons at p < 0.05 (Methods 2.5); partially reproduced when only the 2 mm comparison holds. YP at 6 and 7 mm in % of the center is reported.

claims.statement: The Pr (cell killing) profile is better fitted by a Gaussian than by a Lorentzian (R2 0.96 against 0.92), while the YP profile is better fitted by a Lorentzian (0.98 against 0.95).
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 3; Figure 5B
claims.quote: For Pr data in the left panel of Fig. 5B , the coefficient of determination increased from 0.92 for Lorentzian fit to 0.96 for Gaussian fit. YP data showed the opposite trend, with the coefficients of 0.98 and 0.95 for Lorentzian and Gaussian fits, respectively
claims.criterion: CT26, 0.2 MHz, 2 bursts (x4), electrodes at 0 mm elevation (the left panel of Fig. 5B is read as the 0 mm panel; the text does not name it). Group-mean diagonal profiles of YP and Pr in % of the peak, fitted from -5 to 5 mm (Results 3.2), with the Lorentzian and Gaussian of Methods 2.5. Since 10% tolerances on R2 near 1 are loose, the claim also needs the ordering. Reproduced when all four R2 are within tolerance, the Gaussian R2 exceeds the Lorentzian R2 for Pr and the Lorentzian exceeds the Gaussian for YP.

claims.statement: The central spot of YP staining (electroporation) is just slightly larger than the spot of Pr staining (cell killing).
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 2; Figure 5A and 5B
claims.quote: Somewhat unexpectedly, the central spot of YP staining (electroporation) was just slightly larger than the spot of Pr staining (cell killing; Fig 5A and B )
claims.criterion: The spot size is read as the FWHM, the paper's measure of spot size (Results 3.1); YP FWHM from the Lorentzian and Pr FWHM as 2.4 sigma of the Gaussian (Methods 2.5), fitted to group-mean profiles from -5 to 5 mm at each elevation. Reproduced when the YP FWHM exceeds the Pr FWHM at 0 mm elevation. "Slightly" is not quantified in the paper and is not tested; the ratio is reported, and the 1 and 2 mm elevations as variants.

claims.statement: The central spot shows bright YP staining of nuclei, indicating irreversible damage, while zones farther out show much weaker staining typical of reversible electroporation, and cells inside the electrode footprint are unstained though present.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 2; Figure 5C
claims.quote: a closer examination of the central spot confirmed bright YP staining of cell nuclei ( Fig. 5C , zone 1), which is indicative of the irreversible membrane damage and cell death. Reversible electroporation is distinguished by a much weaker YP staining
claims.criterion: The paper judges nuclear staining by eye from high-resolution images and gives no measure of it, so that part is not tested. The testable part is the intensity. The zones are located only by rectangles in Fig. 5A (not seen); zone 1 is at the center, zone 3 reaches into an electrode footprint, zone 2 lies between. Reproduced when background-subtracted YP in a 325 x 406 um ROI at the center exceeds YP in ROIs at every distance from 2 mm to 7 mm along the diagonal (the paper places reversible electroporation from about 2 mm out, Results 3.2, paragraph 3), and Hoechst intensity inside the footprint is above background.

claims.statement: The central YP peak is higher for 900 ns pulses, but its difference from 300 and 600 ns pulses is not statistically significant.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 6B
claims.quote: The central peak of YP uptake was higher for 900-ns pulses, but the difference from the other two pulse durations was not statistically significant
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. CT26, 0.2 MHz, 2 bursts (x4), center YP (ROI at 0 mm) by the profile method, n = 5 per duration. The paper does not name the test; Methods 2.5 names ANOVA and two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction, and Fig. 6D compares each duration with 300 ns. Tests run, (a) 900 ns against 300 ns and against 600 ns by two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction for two comparisons; (b) one-way ANOVA over the three durations. Reproduced when neither finds a difference at p < 0.05; not reproduced when both do; when they disagree, blocked as methods_underspecified with both shown. The 900 ns mean must be the highest for the first part of the statement; effect sizes are given.

claims.statement: Normalized to the central peak, the sideways decline of YP uptake looks similar for 300, 600 and 900 ns pulses.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 6C
claims.quote: When the peak YP emission was taken as 100%, its decline sideways was similar for the three tested pulse durations
claims.criterion: A claim of absence of a difference, for which the paper gives no test. Profiles in % of each group's center value, by the profile method. Judged by the tests Methods 2.5 names, a one-way ANOVA over the three durations at each distance with Bonferroni correction over the distances. Reproduced when no distance shows a difference at corrected p < 0.05; not reproduced when any does, with the distances and effect sizes reported. The finer per-experiment FWHM analysis of fig6d-fwhm-sharper-longer-pulses is a separate claim.

claims.statement: Packets of 600 and 900 ns pulses give a significantly sharper central peak than 300 ns pulses; 900 ns pulses reduce the FWHM to 1.7 +/- 0.08 mm, 11.1 +/- 0.6% of the gap.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 6D and legend
claims.quote: a more detailed analysis based on fitting of individual experiments (as described in 3.1 ) revealed significant sharpening of the central peak when packets were built from 600- and 900-ns pulses ( Fig. 6D ). The slope coefficient of the logarithmic fit of the data was different from zero at p = 0.003 (one sample, 2-sided t -test). 900-ns pulse packets reduced FWHM to 1.7 ± 0.08 mm, that was 11.1 ± 0.6% of the gap between electrodes
claims.criterion: CT26, 0.2 MHz, 2 bursts (x4), per-experiment Lorentzian FWHM by the profile method, tolerances the paper's stated spread (s.e.). Open details and their readings. The fit range is -5 to 5 mm (Fig. 6B legend) or -4 to 4 mm ("as described in 3.1"). The fit of FWHM on pulse duration is linear in the legend and logarithmic in the text; both are run. Each of 600 and 900 ns against 300 ns by two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction for two comparisons. Reproduced when, under one reading, both comparisons have corrected p < 0.05 with 600 and 900 ns sharper, the slope is negative with p < 0.05, and the 900 ns values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the sharpening holds but the values miss tolerance or only one comparison is significant.

claims.statement: Even in the worst-case heating protocol, temperature under the electrodes did not exceed 44 C, with heating above 30 C confined to about 2 mm from the electrodes after 2 bursts.
claims.source: Methods 2.3, paragraph 2; Figure 2
claims.quote: With 2 bursts ( Fig. 2A ), heating was restricted to an approximately 2-mm zone next to electrodes, where it could reach over 30 °C but did not exceed 44 °C
claims.criterion: Thermochromic film images of Fig. 2 after 2 and 6 bursts at 0.2 MHz without rotation. Reproduced when no part of the film shows the transition back to black (44 +/- 2 C) and, after 2 bursts, the blue color (30 +/- 2 C) occurs only within about 2 mm of an electrode.

claims.statement: In the simulation, 7.2 kV on one electrode produces 3.3 kV/cm in the center of the array and 9.4 and 13.5 kV/cm at 6 and 7 mm from the center toward the active electrode.
claims.source: Methods 2.2, paragraph 4; Figure 1E
claims.quote: Specifically, 7.2 kV applied to one electrode produced the electric field of 3.3 kV/cm in the center, and 9.4 and 13.5 kV/cm at 6 and 7 mm from the center towards the active electrode, respectively
claims.criterion: These are outputs of the paper's Sim4Life Lite 7.0.1.8169 model (Methods 2.2), not measurements; the model files are not published, and the paper names no other source for them. Settled by the expected values if a public copy of the model is found; otherwise not testable from recordings.

claims.statement: The central peak of YP uptake is highest for 900-ns pulse packets, but its difference from 300- and 600-ns packets is not statistically significant.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 6B
claims.quote: The central peak of YP uptake was higher for 900-ns pulses, but the difference from the other two pulse durations was not statistically significant
claims.criterion: Per experiment (well, n=5 per pulse duration, Fig. 6B legend), the background-subtracted YP intensity at the centre ROI (0 mm), as in Methods 2.5. The paper does not name the test for this comparison; the Methods allow ANOVA or two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction, and the matching comparison at the array centre in Results 3.1 (Fig. 4B) used t-tests with Bonferroni correction. Readings are (a) two-sided t-tests of 900 ns against 300 ns and against 600 ns, Bonferroni over the three pairwise comparisons, and (b) a one-way ANOVA over the three durations, each at p < 0.05. The claim of absence is reproduced when the test finds no significant difference and the 900-ns mean is the highest; not reproduced when the test finds a difference. If (a) and (b) disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified. The centre value from the Lorentzian fit (parameter a) is shown as a variant. Effect sizes are reported.

claims.statement: With the peak YP emission taken as 100%, the decline of YP emission away from the centre looks similar for 300-, 600- and 900-ns pulses.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 6C
claims.quote: When the peak YP emission was taken as 100%, its decline sideways was similar for the three tested pulse durations
claims.criterion: Per experiment, YP intensity along the diagonals divided by its value at 0 mm and expressed in percent; mean and s.e. over the n=5 experiments per duration at each distance, as in Fig. 6C. The paper reports no test; its Methods say significance in the graphs is read from the gap between error bars (a gap longer than the error bars means p < 0.05). Reproduced when at no compared distance do two durations' mean profiles show a gap between their s.e. bars longer than the bars; not reproduced otherwise. The text does not limit the distances; readings are -5 to 5 mm (the fit range of the Fig. 6 legend) and every measured distance. ROI spacing readings are 1-mm steps and contiguous ROIs. The outcome is the one all readings give; blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ.

claims.statement: FWHM of the central YP peak, fitted per experiment, decreases with pulse duration from 300 to 900 ns, with a trend slope different from zero (p = 0.003).
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 6D
claims.quote: revealed significant sharpening of the central peak when packets were built from 600- and 900-ns pulses ... The slope coefficient of the logarithmic fit of the data was different from zero at p = 0.003 (one sample, 2-sided t-test)
claims.criterion: For each experiment, the Lorentzian of Methods 2.5 (centre fixed at 0, a and b free, no offset) fitted by least squares to the background-subtracted YP intensity along the diagonals; FWHM is b. Then a regression of FWHM on pulse duration and a two-sided t-test of its slope. The Fig. 6D legend does not say whether the trend was fitted to the 15 individual values or to the 3 means; readings are individual values (as Fig. 4C, whose legend gives n=15 for fitting) and the 3 means. Further readings are the fit half-range (4, 5 or 6 mm, from Methods, Results 3.1 and the Fig. 6 legend), the trend (linear in pulse duration, Fig. 6D legend, or linear in log pulse duration, Results 3.3), the ROI spacing (1-mm steps or contiguous) and the pooling of diagonals (averaged at each signed distance, or all points fitted). Reproduced when the slope is negative with p < 0.05 under every reading; not reproduced when it is under none; blocked as methods_underspecified when readings differ. The p-value under each is reported.

claims.statement: FWHM for 600-ns and for 900-ns packets is each significantly smaller than for 300-ns packets (Bonferroni-corrected t-tests, p = 0.028 for one and p = 0.0072 for the other).
claims.source: Figure 6D legend
claims.quote: *p=0.028, **p=0.0072 for the difference from 300-ns pulse exposure (2-sided t -test with Bonferroni correction)
claims.criterion: Per-experiment FWHM as in fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak. Two-sided Student's t-tests of 600 against 300 ns and 900 against 300 ns, Bonferroni-corrected. The number of comparisons is not stated; readings are 2 (each against 300 ns, as the legend frames them) and 3 (all pairs). Reproduced when both corrected p-values are below 0.05 with smaller FWHM at the longer duration, under every reading of the fit range, ROI spacing, pooling and comparison count; partially reproduced when only one of the two comparisons is significant; blocked as methods_underspecified when readings differ. The legend's asterisks are not assigned to durations in the text, so the p-values are compared with 0.028 and 0.0072 in either order and shown.

claims.statement: Packets of 900-ns pulses reduce FWHM to 1.7 +/- 0.08 mm (mean +/- s.e.), 11.1 +/- 0.6% of the 15.3-mm gap between electrodes.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 6D
claims.quote: 900-ns pulse packets reduced FWHM to 1.7 ± 0.08 mm, that was 11.1 ± 0.6% of the gap between electrodes
claims.criterion: Mean over the n=5 experiments of per-experiment FWHM as in fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak. The gap is the 15.3-mm diagonal (1.7/15.3 = 11.1%, and Fig. 4C gives FWHM in % of the diagonal distance between electrodes). Tolerances are the paper's stated s.e. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading of fit range, ROI spacing and pooling; the result under each reading is shown.

claims.statement: All CANCAN protocols enhance electroporation at the centre of the array, while in single-pulse controls YP uptake decreases gradually toward the centre.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 3A
claims.quote: All CANCAN protocols visibly enhanced electroporation at the center of the array, in contrast to its gradual decrease toward the center in the control
claims.criterion: Diagonal YP profiles per experiment (Fig. 3B; n=3 per CANCAN rate, n=5 controls). The statement is of a peak at the centre; the paper names no positions for this visual reading of Fig. 3A. Reproduced when, for every CANCAN packet rate, mean YP at 0 mm exceeds mean YP at 4 mm (the edge of the Lorentzian fit range, Fig. 3 legend and Results 3.1), and in controls mean YP at 0 mm is below that at 4, 6 and 7 mm; each comparison read with the Methods' error-bar gap rule (a gap longer than the s.e. bars). Whether CANCAN YP at 0 mm also exceeds YP at 6 and 7 mm (the near-electrode positions of Fig. 4B) is shown per rate and not judged here, since the paper reports the near-electrode suppression as rate dependent (fig4b-suppression-near-electrodes).

claims.statement: Under CANCAN, the decline of YP emission from the centre is bell-shaped and well fitted by a Lorentzian within -4 to 4 mm (R > 0.9, p < 0.001).
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 3; Figure 3B and 3C
claims.quote: The decline of YP emission sideways from the center was bell-shaped and followed Lorentzian distribution ... The fit correlation with data in the −4 to 4 mm radius was nearly perfect (R>0.9, p<0.001)
claims.criterion: The Methods' Lorentzian fitted to the mean diagonal and side-parallel profiles of each CANCAN rate over -4 to 4 mm. Reproduced when the correlation of fit with data exceeds 0.9 with p < 0.001 for every rate.

claims.statement: Higher packet rates suppress YP uptake at 6 and 7 mm from the centre (near electrodes) in a rate-dependent way, so that at 0.2 MHz uptake in the centre is 40-fold larger than near electrodes despite a field of about 14 kV/cm there against 3.3 kV/cm in the centre.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraphs 2 and 4; Figure 4A and 4B
claims.quote: Now, by increasing the packet repetition rate to 0.2 MHz, we achieved a 40-fold difference
claims.criterion: Per experiment, background-subtracted YP at 0, 6 and 7 mm on the diagonals (Fig. 4B, n=3 per rate). The field values are the paper's simulation (Methods 2.2) and are not recomputed. The paper does not say which near-electrode distance or which ratio form gives 40; readings are 6 mm or 7 mm, and the ratio of means or the mean of per-experiment ratios. The rate dependence is judged as Fig. 4B shows it, a power function of packet rate fitted to the mean YP at 6 and at 7 mm, with a negative exponent, and 1 Hz above 0.2 MHz by the error-bar gap rule. Reproduced when both hold at 6 and 7 mm and the ratio is within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: YP intensity in the centre of the array shows no significant effect of packet rate.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 4; Figure 4B
claims.quote: YP intensity in the center showed no significant effect of the packet rate ( t -test with Bonferroni correction, Fig. 4B )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, two-sided t-tests with Bonferroni correction between packet rates of YP at 0 mm (n=3 per rate). The pairs compared are not stated; readings are each rate against 1 Hz (as in Fig. 4C) and all pairs. Reproduced when no corrected p is below 0.05 under either reading; not reproduced when some corrected p is below 0.05 under both; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings differ. Effect sizes are reported.

claims.statement: FWHM decreases from about 4 mm at 1 Hz to about 2 mm at 1 kHz, 10 kHz and 0.2 MHz, following a logarithmic dependence from 1 Hz to 10 kHz with no further gain at 0.2 MHz.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 5; Figure 4C
claims.quote: FWHM decreased from ~4 mm at 1 Hz to ~2 mm at 1 kHz, 10 kHz, and 0.2 MHz packet rates (p = 0.03; 0.02, and 0.09, respectively; t -test with Bonferroni correction). FWHM decrease followed the logarithmic dependence from 1 Hz to 10 kHz (correlation coefficient R = 0.77, p<0.001)
claims.criterion: Per-experiment Lorentzian FWHM (fit range -4 to 4 mm, Results 3.1 and Fig. 3 legend; 6 mm as the Methods' other bound is shown as a variant). FWHM regressed on log packet rate over the 15 experiments below 0.2 MHz. No further gain at 0.2 MHz is read with the Methods' error-bar gap rule; it holds when mean FWHM at 0.2 MHz is not below the 10-kHz mean by a gap longer than the s.e. bars. Reproduced when the slope is negative with p < 0.05, the 0.2-MHz condition holds and the means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when only the slope holds.

claims.statement: Raising the electrodes 1 or 2 mm above the monolayer weakens electroporation in the central spot, with practically no YP staining near electrodes at any height.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 1; Figure 5A and 5B
claims.quote: there was practically no YP staining near electrodes to start with, so the only clear effect of raising electrodes was the weakening of electroporation in the central spot
claims.criterion: Diagonal YP profiles at 0, 1 and 2 mm elevation (n=6-7). Reproduced when mean central YP at 0 mm exceeds that at 1 mm and at 2 mm by the Methods' error-bar gap rule. The paper sets no threshold for "practically no" staining near electrodes, so YP at 6 and 7 mm, as percent of the 0-mm centre, is reported and not judged.

claims.statement: The decline of Pr staining (cell killing) from the centre fits a Gaussian better than a Lorentzian (R2 0.96 against 0.92), while YP fits a Lorentzian better (0.98 against 0.95), fitted from -5 to 5 mm.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 3; Figure 5B, left panel
claims.quote: For Pr data in the left panel of Fig. 5B , the coefficient of determination increased from 0.92 for Lorentzian fit to 0.96 for Gaussian fit. YP data showed the opposite trend, with the coefficients of 0.98 and 0.95 for Lorentzian and Gaussian fits
claims.criterion: Fits of the Methods' Lorentzian and Gaussian to the mean diagonal profiles at 0 mm elevation (the left panel is read as 0 mm), from -5 to 5 mm. Reproduced when the Gaussian R2 exceeds the Lorentzian R2 for Pr and the reverse for YP; the values are compared with expected.

claims.statement: The central spot of YP staining (electroporation) is only slightly larger than the spot of Pr staining (cell killing).
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 2; Figure 5A and 5B
claims.quote: the central spot of YP staining (electroporation) was just slightly larger than the spot of Pr staining (cell killing
claims.criterion: FWHM of the YP Lorentzian and Pr Gaussian (FWHM about 2.4 sigma, Methods) on the mean diagonal profiles, -5 to 5 mm (Fig. 5B legend), at each elevation. Reproduced when YP FWHM exceeds Pr FWHM at 0 mm elevation. The paper sets no bound for "just slightly", so the ratio is reported and not judged.

claims.statement: The central YP peak grows linearly with the number of bursts in CT26 and CHO cells, except for saturation after 6 bursts (x4) in CT26 cells.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 7B and 7E
claims.quote: The increase was linear in both cell lines, except when it reached saturation after 6 bursts (x4) in CT26 cells
claims.criterion: Central YP (0 mm) regressed linearly on burst number, CT26 without the 6-burst point (Fig. 7B legend), CHO with all, slope tested by the two-sided one-sample t test of the legend. The legend does not say whether individual experiments or means were fitted; readings are both, and the outcome is the one both give (blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ). Reproduced when both slopes are positive at p < 0.05. Saturation is read with the Methods' error-bar gap rule; it holds when the CT26 6-burst mean is not above the mean at the next lower burst number by a gap longer than the bars.

claims.statement: FWHM increases with the number of bursts in CT26 cells but not in CHO cells (p = 0.44).
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 7C and 7F
claims.quote: FWHM of the central peak increased proportionally to the burst number in CT26 cells, but not in CHO cells
claims.criterion: Per-experiment Lorentzian FWHM regressed linearly on burst number (CHO without 1 burst, which was too small to fit). The CHO part is a claim of absence judged on the paper's test, the two-sided t-test of the slope at p < 0.05. Reproduced when the CT26 slope is positive at p < 0.05 and the CHO slope is not significant. Fit-range, ROI spacing, pooling and fitted-points (individual values or means) readings as in fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak; blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ.

claims.statement: One burst (x4) in CT26 cells gives the sharpest peak of the study, FWHM 1.1 +/- 0.1 mm, 7.3% of the inter-electrode gap and 2.3% of the array area, with YP near electrodes 40 to 50 times smaller than at the target.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 3; Figure 7A and 7C
claims.quote: 1 burst (x4) in CT26 cells produced the sharpest peak of electroporation seen in this study ... at FWHM of 1.1 ± 0.1 mm, it occupied just 7.3% of the inter-electrode gap and 2.3% of the electrode array area. Off-target effects, characterized by YP emission near electrodes, were 40–50 times smaller than at the remote target
claims.criterion: Per-experiment FWHM as in fig6d-longer-pulses-sharper-peak; gap is the 15.3-mm diagonal. Sharpest means the mean FWHM is below that of every other condition the study fitted (Figs 4C, 6D, 7C and 7F); this is shown and judged. The ratio range 40 to 50 widened by 10% of each bound is 36 to 55 (value 45.5, tolerance 9.5); the near-electrode readings are as in fig4b-suppression-near-electrodes. The paper does not say how 2.3% of the array area is computed; a circle of diameter 1.1 mm over a square of 15.3-mm diagonal gives 0.8%, so the area figure is reported under that reading and not used for the outcome.

claims.statement: In the worst-case heating protocol (600-ns packets with no interval, 2 or 6 bursts), temperature did not exceed 44 C even near the electrodes; it could exceed 30 C within about 2 mm of the electrodes after 2 bursts and even near the centre after 6 bursts.
claims.source: Methods 2.3; Figure 2
claims.quote: Temperature could exceed 30 °C even near the center of the array, but did not exceed 44 °C even near the electrodes
claims.criterion: Read from thermochromic film colour (black, red, green, blue, black at 25, 26, 30 and 44 C). Reproduced when no frame at the end of a burst shows the return to black that marks 44 C or above. These are film images, not cell data.

claims.statement: In all 10 subjects, during induction, the probability of response to clicks was below that to verbal stimuli in the transition between EON and LOC.
claims.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 2; Figure 1C
claims.quote: During induction, in 10 of 10 subjects, we observed that Pclicks < Pverbal during the transition between EON and LOC
claims.criterion: Common method, with Open A and B. Per subject, Pclicks < Pverbal holds where the posterior Pr{Pclicks < Pverbal} exceeds 0.95, which is where the 95% credibility interval of Pverbal - Pclicks excludes 0 (Results, paragraph 2). The text does not say over how much of the EON to LOC interval this must hold. Readings, (i) at some time in the interval; (ii) over more than half of it. The subject count is compared with the expected value.

claims.statement: The transition from EON to LOC took a median of 23.9 min across subjects (range 6.7 to 32.8 min, quartiles 16.4 and 28.6 min).
claims.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The transition between EON and LOC required a median of 23.9 min (minimum, 6.7 min; 25th percentile, 16.4 min; 75th percentile, 28.6 min; maximum 32.8 min)
claims.criterion: EON and LOC per subject by the common method, with Open A and B. Reproduced when the median is within tolerance under a reading; partially reproduced when the median is and fewer than three of the other four values are. If the dataset holds the paper's LOC and EON times, they are used as well and reported as a variant.

claims.statement: At the group level, aligned at LOC, Pclicks was below Pverbal during the transition to LOC, and the difference grew as subjects approached LOC.
claims.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 2; Figure 1 D and E
claims.quote: The group-level analysis corroborated the individual subject analyses, showing that Pclicks < Pverbal during the transition to LOC (Pr{Pclicks < Pverbal} > 0.95; Fig. 1E). Moreover, the group-level curves showed a gradual increase in the difference between these response probabilities as subjects approached LOC
claims.criterion: Group behavior by the common method, with Open A and B. Reproduced when Pr{Pclicks < Pverbal} > 0.95 at the group level before LOC, within the window from the median EON (about 24 min before LOC) to LOC, and the posterior estimate of Pverbal - Pclicks is higher in the last third of that window than in its first third. The window and the thirds are a reading of "during the transition" and "gradual increase", named here before the analysis. Partially reproduced when only the first part holds.

claims.statement: During emergence, at the group level aligned at ROC, Pclicks was below Pverbal, while individual curves were more variable.
claims.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 3; Figure 1E
claims.quote: During emergence, individual response-probability curves were more variable, but again we found that Pclicks < Pverbal at the group level
claims.criterion: Group behavior by the common method, aligned at ROC, with Open A and B. Reproduced when Pr{Pclicks < Pverbal} > 0.95 at some time after ROC, within the window from ROC to the median ROC to EOFF time (about 25 min).

claims.statement: During emergence 6 of 10 subjects did not reach EOFF, as Pclicks did not stay above 0.95 for 5 min or longer.
claims.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 3
claims.quote: During emergence, 6 of 10 subjects did not reach EOFF because they did not achieve Pclicks > 0.95 for 5 min or longer
claims.criterion: EOFF per subject by the common method, with Open A and B. The tolerance is one subject, as 10% of 6 is less than one subject and a count can only move by whole subjects.

claims.statement: The transition from ROC to EOFF (or the end of the recording when EOFF was not reached) took a median of 25.5 min (range 4.9 to 47.6 min, quartiles 12.8 and 38.0 min).
claims.source: Results, Continuous Transitions Between Consciousness and Unconsciousness, paragraph 3
claims.quote: We found that the transition between ROC and EOFF required a median of 25.5 min (minimum, 4.9 min; 25th percentile, 12.8 min; 75th percentile, 38.0 min; maximum, 47.6 min)
claims.criterion: ROC and EOFF per subject by the common method, with Open A and B, the end of the recording standing for EOFF when it is not reached. Reproduced when the median is within tolerance under a reading; partially reproduced when the median is and fewer than three of the other four values are.

claims.statement: Gamma and beta power rose significantly above baseline in the 30 min before LOC and stayed elevated during unconsciousness.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 1; Figure 2 B and C
claims.quote: gamma (25–40 Hz) and beta (13–24Hz) power increased significantly above baseline levels during the 30 min before LOC ... and remained elevated during the unconscious period
claims.criterion: Common method, frontal channel near Fz, Laplacian, with Open C to G. For each band, a time bin counts as significant when the sign test of the subjects' baseline-normalized power has p < 0.05, with power (i) averaged over the band's frequencies (Fig. 2C) or (ii) taken per frequency as in Fig. 2B, the bin counting when more than half of the band's frequencies are significant. The paper does not say what share of the window must be significant; readings (a) more than half the time bins of LOC - 30 min to LOC, and (b) every bin of the last 10 min before LOC. Both band definitions (Results; Fig. 2 legend) are run. Reproduced when, under a reading, gamma and beta both pass in the 30 min before LOC and are significant in more than half the bins of LOC to LOC + 30 min (the unconscious period, as the 10 to 40 min after LOC of claim fig5-peak-max lies within it); partially reproduced when one band does.

claims.statement: At LOC, alpha (8 to 12 Hz) and low-frequency (0.1 to 1 Hz) power both increased significantly.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 1; Figure 2 B and C
claims.quote: At LOC, both alpha (8–12 Hz) and low-frequency (0.1–1 Hz) power increased significantly
claims.criterion: As in fig2bc-gamma-beta-before-loc, readings (i) and (ii) of the measure. "At LOC" is not given a window. Readings, (a) the band is significant in more than half the bins from LOC to LOC + 5 min (5 min being the paper's equilibration interval for the markers) and not in more than half the bins from LOC - 10 min to LOC - 5 min; (b) the band is significant in more than half the bins from LOC to LOC + 5 min. Reproduced when both bands pass under a reading; partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: Fifteen minutes after LOC, the alpha power increase was concentrated in frontal channels and the low-frequency increase was spread broadly over temporal and parietal channels.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
claims.quote: Fifteen minutes after LOC, the increases in alpha power were concentrated in frontal channels, whereas those for low-frequency power were distributed broadly across temporal and parietal channels
claims.criterion: Common method, all kept channels, Laplacian, Open C to F. At LOC + 15 min, per subject and channel, baseline-normalized band power; the group map is the median across subjects (Methods, Spectral Analysis, group scalp maps). The paper gives no channel groups; they are read from the 10-20 labels, frontal Fp, AF, F (not FT, FC), temporal T, TP, FT, parietal P, CP (not PO), occipital O, PO. Reproduced when the frontal group has the highest median alpha increase of the groups, and the low-frequency increase is above 1 in more than half of the temporal and parietal channels and its frontal median is not more than twice the temporal and parietal median. The second part is a reading of "distributed broadly"; it is named so here, before the analysis.

claims.statement: During emergence the changes reversed with a similar time course, frontal alpha and low-frequency power decreasing at ROC while gamma and beta power stayed elevated after ROC.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 1; Figure 2 B and C
claims.quote: During emergence, these changes in power occurred in reverse, following a similar time course: Frontal alpha and low-frequency power decreased at ROC, whereas gamma/beta power remained elevated throughout the post-ROC period when Pclicks < Pverbal
claims.criterion: As in fig2bc-alpha-slow-at-loc mirrored at ROC. Alpha and low-frequency power are significant in more than half the bins from ROC - 5 min to ROC and in fewer than half from ROC to ROC + 5 min; gamma and beta significant in more than half the bins from ROC to ROC + the median ROC to EOFF time (claim roc-eoff-duration). Readings (i) and (ii) of the measure and both band definitions. Reproduced when all four bands pass under a reading; partially reproduced when two or three do.

claims.statement: Low-frequency power increased more than 10-fold in the unconscious state compared with baseline.
claims.source: Results, Changes in Spatially Coherent Alpha Activity Mark Unconsciousness, paragraph 2
claims.quote: low-frequency power increased by more than 10-fold in the unconscious state compared with baseline
claims.criterion: Common method, Laplacian, Open C to F. The paper cites Fig. 2 and does not say which channel or time. Readings, (a) the frontal channel near Fz at the Unconscious midpoint; (b) the same channel at LOC + 15 min (Fig. 2D); (c) the median over kept channels at LOC + 15 min. Group value is the median across subjects of mean 0.1 to 1 Hz power over mean baseline power. Reproduced when the ratio exceeds 9 (10 less 10%) under a reading.

claims.statement: In the transition before LOC, the median frequency of the frontal spectrum fell from 23.1 to 12.0 Hz and its bandwidth (interquartile range) from 17.4 to 9.1 Hz.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 3; Figure 3A
claims.quote: During induction, in the transition period before LOC, the median frequency decreased from 23.1 to 12.0 Hz, and the bandwidth decreased from 17.4 to 9.1 Hz
claims.criterion: Methods, Spectral Analysis, paragraph 2. Group-level spectrogram of the frontal channel near Fz, aligned at LOC, baseline- and total-power-normalized; at each time the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles of the 2 to 40 Hz power distribution; the bandwidth is the 75th minus the 25th; each series smoothed with a random-walk fixed-interval smoother whose observation variance is the sample variance of the series' first 10 s and whose state variance is the square of (yN - y1)/N (the equation is lost in the text; read from "the square of the end-to-end rate of change"). Open details. "Total power-normalized" is read as the baseline-normalized spectrum (linear ratio) divided by its sum over 2 to 40 Hz, so the percentiles are those of its cumulative sum; the group median is taken (a) before or (b) after this normalization. The start of the transition is not given; readings (i) the median EON time before LOC (claim eon-loc-duration), (ii) LOC - 30 min (Fig. 2, "the 30 min before LOC"). The end value is at LOC. Open C to F apply. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance under a reading; partially reproduced when the median frequency falls by at least half the reported drop and the bandwidth falls.

claims.statement: In the transition after ROC, the median frequency rose from 11.8 to 21.9 Hz and the bandwidth from 9.9 to 12.8 Hz.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 3; Figure 3A
claims.quote: During emergence, in the transition period after ROC, the median frequency increased from 11.8 to 21.9 Hz, and the bandwidth increased from 9.9 to 12.8 Hz
claims.criterion: As fig3a-induction-traveling-peak, aligned at ROC. The start value is at ROC; the end is not given, readings (i) ROC + the median ROC to EOFF time (claim roc-eoff-duration), (ii) ROC + 30 min. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance under a reading; partially reproduced when the median frequency rises by at least half the reported rise and the bandwidth rises.

claims.statement: Power at the median frequency had a frontal distribution at each behavioral time point.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 4; Figure 3B
claims.quote: We found that the power at the median frequency had a frontal distribution across the different behavioral time points
claims.criterion: Per subject and channel, power at the group median frequency of claim fig3a-induction-traveling-peak (or its emergence counterpart) at each time point EON, Pre-LOC, LOC, Unconscious, ROC, Post-LOC, EOFF; group map the median across subjects (Results, paragraph 3). The text says the analysis is "for each subject" and does not say whose median frequency is used; readings (x) the group median frequency at the time point's offset from LOC or ROC, (y) the subject's own median frequency, computed as in fig3a-induction-traveling-peak on the subject's spectrogram. Whether power is raw or baseline-normalized is not given; readings (a) power in dB, (b) baseline-normalized. Channel groups as in fig2d-spatial-loc15 (frontal, temporal, parietal, occipital). Reproduced when the frontal group has the highest median of the four groups at every time point under a reading; partially reproduced when it does at five or six of the seven.

claims.statement: Gamma and beta power were frontal from Pre-LOC through LOC; during unconsciousness the frontal power moved into the beta and alpha bands; during emergence it shifted back toward beta and gamma, and frontal gamma power persisted through EOFF.
claims.source: Results, Dynamics of the EEG Spectrum Covary with Changes in Probability of Response and LOC/ROC, paragraph 4; Figure S2
claims.quote: Gamma and beta power showed a frontal distribution from Pre-LOC through LOC; during unconsciousness the frontal power distribution moved to the beta and alpha bands ... In addition, frontal gamma power appeared to persist through EOFF
claims.criterion: Group maps of band power (in dB, as Fig. S2 shows) at the seven time points as in fig3b-frontal-median-frequency-power, bands of Fig. S2 (alpha 8 to 12, beta 12 to 25, gamma 25 to 35 Hz). Each band's frontal excess is the frontal group median minus the occipital group median, in dB, minus the same at baseline. Reproduced when the gamma and beta frontal excesses are positive at Pre-LOC and LOC; at Unconscious the alpha excess is above the gamma excess; at Post-ROC the gamma excess is above that at Unconscious (the shift back toward beta and gamma); and the gamma excess is positive at EOFF. Partially reproduced when two or three of the four hold. The thresholds are a reading of "frontal distribution", "moved" and "shifted", named here before the analysis.

claims.statement: At baseline the principal mode of the alpha band is spatially coherent over occipital channels; its modal projection dissipates at LOC and returns at ROC, remaining prominent after ROC.
claims.source: Results, Changes in Spatially Coherent Alpha Activity Mark Unconsciousness, paragraph 2; Figure 4 A and B
claims.quote: Occipital prominence of the principal mode was present while the subjects were awake, ended at LOC, and returned, and remained prominent after ROC
claims.criterion: Methods, Eigenvalue and Modal Projection Analyses. Per subject, multitaper cross-spectral matrices (parameters as for spectrograms) in nonoverlapping 2-s windows over the full baseline (Open C); the median over windows of the real and imaginary parts of each entry; the first eigenvector u1(f) is the principal mode. Modal projection in nonoverlapping 20-s windows, the power within u1 over total power (equation lost; read as u1^H S u1 over trace S, with S the window's cross-spectral matrix). Significance per Methods, a random circular shift per channel, 200 times, resampled 500 times with replacement, the 95% limit averaged across subjects and compared with the mean modal projection. Occipital means the channel group of fig2d-spatial-loc15 with the largest median |u1| at 10 Hz. Reproduced when the baseline mode at 10 Hz is largest over occipital channels, and the group mean modal projection of the baseline mode at 8 to 12 Hz is significant in more than half of the windows in the 10 min before LOC and after ROC + 10 min, and in fewer than half from LOC + 10 min to ROC - 10 min. The 10-min windows are a reading of "ended at LOC" and "returned" (the paper gives no window), named here before the analysis. Partially reproduced when the mode is occipital but the timing fails. Open E and F apply.

claims.statement: During unconsciousness the principal alpha mode (about 10 Hz) is spatially coherent over frontal channels; its modal projection begins after LOC and ceases at ROC.
claims.source: Results, Changes in Spatially Coherent Alpha Activity Mark Unconsciousness, paragraph 2; Figure 4 C and D
claims.quote: Activity within this frontal alpha mode, characterized by the modal projection, begins after LOC and ceases at ROC ... during unconsciousness, the principal mode in the alpha range was prominent in a frontal distribution
claims.criterion: As fig4ab-occipital-alpha-mode, with the unconscious cross-spectral matrix. The Methods' "segments of at least 5 min extending from LOC to ROC" allows readings (a) the whole LOC to ROC period, (b) the 5 min after LOC. Reproduced when the unconscious mode at 10 Hz is largest over frontal channels, and its group mean modal projection at 8 to 12 Hz is significant in more than half the windows from LOC + 10 min to ROC - 10 min and in fewer than half of the windows in the 10 min before LOC and after ROC + 10 min, under a reading. Partially reproduced when the mode is frontal but the timing fails.

claims.statement: Low frequencies showed no prominent principal mode, although low-frequency power rose more than 10-fold in unconsciousness.
claims.source: Results, Changes in Spatially Coherent Alpha Activity Mark Unconsciousness, paragraph 2
claims.quote: In contrast, low frequencies did not show a prominent principal mode
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The test is the paper's permutation test of the modal projection (fig4cd-frontal-alpha-mode, both readings of the segment), on the unconscious mode at 0.1 to 1 Hz. Reproduced when the group mean modal projection is not significant in more than half the windows from LOC to ROC; not reproduced when it is. The modal projection values at 0.1 to 1 Hz and at 8 to 12 Hz are reported either way. The 2-s windows resolve 0.5 Hz steps, so the low band holds the 0.5 and 1 Hz bins only; this is the paper's method and is said so.

claims.statement: From about 20 min before LOC to about 10 min after it, alpha/beta (8 to 14 Hz) amplitude was largest at the troughs of the low-frequency (0.1 to 1 Hz) oscillation (trough-max), significant in 9 of 10 subjects within 10 min of LOC.
claims.source: Results, Different Patterns of Phase-Amplitude Modulation, paragraph 2; Figure 5 B and C
claims.quote: During induction, beginning ∼20 min before LOC and extending ∼10 min after LOC, the alpha/beta amplitudes were largest at the troughs of low-frequency oscillations (Fig. 5 B and C; P < 0.05 in 9 of 10 subjects within 10 min of LOC by permutation test
claims.criterion: Methods, Phase-Amplitude Modulation Analysis, and SI. Frontal channel near Fz, Laplacian, data at 250 Hz; bandpass 0.1 to 1 Hz and 8 to 14 Hz; Hilbert phase and amplitude; 18 equal phase bins; per 2-min epoch, mean amplitude per bin over the epoch's mean. Phase 0 is the low-frequency peak (SI, "psi(t) = 0"), so trough-max is a modulogram whose largest bin has |phase| > pi/2. Open, filter design (ref. 36), readings (a) zero-phase FIR, (b) zero-phase Butterworth. Open, the permutation test (ref. 36 only), readings (a) amplitude series circularly shifted by a random offset within the epoch, statistic the modulation index of ref. 35 (Tort et al.), (b) the same shuffle, statistic the modulogram's largest bin; 200 shuffles, p < 0.05. Open, "within 10 min of LOC", readings (i) any 2-min epoch from LOC - 10 to LOC + 10 min significant and trough-max, (ii) the pooled 20 min. The tolerance is one subject (10% of 9 is less than one subject). Reproduced when the count is within tolerance under a reading, and the group modulogram (mean across subjects) is trough-max in more than half the epochs from LOC - 20 to LOC + 10 min. Partially reproduced when one of the two holds. Open C, E and F apply.

claims.statement: During profound unconsciousness, 10 to 40 min after LOC, the modulation shifted by 180 degrees, alpha/beta amplitude being largest at low-frequency peaks (peak-max), significant in 8 of 10 subjects.
claims.source: Results, Different Patterns of Phase-Amplitude Modulation, paragraph 2; Figure 5 B and D
claims.quote: During profound unconsciousness, i.e., from 10–40 min after LOC, the phase–amplitude modulation shifted by 180°, such that the alpha/beta amplitudes were largest at the peaks of low-frequency oscillations (Fig. 5 B and D; P < 0.05 in 8 of 10 subjects by permutation test
claims.criterion: As fig5-trough-max-induction, with peak-max a modulogram whose largest bin has |phase| < pi/2, over LOC + 10 to LOC + 40 min, readings (i) any epoch and (ii) the pooled 30 min. Reproduced when the count is within tolerance under a reading and the group modulogram is peak-max in more than half the epochs of that window; partially reproduced when one of the two holds.

claims.statement: During emergence, the modulation reverted to trough-max about 15 min before ROC, significant in 9 of 10 subjects.
claims.source: Results, Different Patterns of Phase-Amplitude Modulation, paragraph 2; Figure 5B
claims.quote: During emergence, the phase–amplitude modulation reverted to the trough-max pattern at ∼15 min before ROC (Fig. 5B; P < 0.05 in 9 of 10 subjects, permutation test)
claims.criterion: As fig5-trough-max-induction, aligned at ROC. The window is not given; readings (i) any epoch from ROC - 15 min to ROC, (ii) the pooled 15 min. Reproduced when the count is within tolerance under a reading and the group modulogram turns from peak-max to trough-max between ROC - 25 and ROC - 5 min (about 15 min, widened by 10 min either way, named here before the analysis); partially reproduced when one of the two holds.

claims.statement: The low-frequency phase modulates a broad range of higher frequencies, from theta through gamma, in both the trough-max and the peak-max regimes.
claims.source: Figure S3; SI Materials and Methods; Results, Different Patterns of Phase-Amplitude Modulation, paragraph 2
claims.quote: These results show that the low-frequency oscillation modulates a broad range of higher frequencies spanning theta through gamma bands in both the trough-max and peak-max regimes
claims.criterion: SI Materials and Methods. Peaks of the low-frequency oscillation where its phase is 0; spectrograms in windows of +-2 s around each peak (T = 4 s, TW = 1, K = 1, no overlap, 0.5 Hz resolution); median over windows within a 2-min epoch, normalized per frequency by the mean over lags; epochs centered at LOC (trough-max) and at LOC + 30 min (peak-max); averaged across subjects. The SI states T = 4 s windows but also +-2 s lags, so the windows are read as the 4-s window centered on each peak, with the spectrogram's time axis giving the lag; the step along the lag is open, readings (a) 0.1 s, (b) 0.25 s. The SI also says "Within each 10-min epoch" before giving the 2-min epoch; the 2-min epochs it names for LOC and LOC + 30 min are used, and a 10-min epoch centered at the same times is shown as a variant. Reproduced when, in both epochs, the normalized power in each of theta (4 to 8 Hz), alpha, beta and gamma (25 to 35 Hz) varies with lag by more than 0.1 of the mean (the colour range of Fig. S3 is -0.2 to 0.2), at lag 0 in the opposite direction for the two epochs. Partially reproduced when this holds for alpha and beta only.

claims.statement: In the fast-motion macaque recording, DREDge's spike-based (AP) motion estimate follows the drift visible in the unregistered spike raster.

claims.quote: a Spike raster before registration, with AP DREDge displacement estimate overlaid in red.
claims.criterion: The legend shows the estimate over the raster and states no result in words; that it follows the slow drift is read from the Methods ("First, slower timescale motion is estimated using DREDge"). Run the pipeline (opening comment, steps 1 and 2) on the whole recording. The paper shows this only as a figure, so the measure is the paper's own registration quality metric, the mean template correlation (Methods, Spike registration quality metrics) on a 1 um by 1 s raster of mean spike amplitudes, bins outside the probe after correction masked. Reproduced when, under readings (a) and (b) of step 2 and (i) and (ii) of step 1, the mean template correlation after DREDge correction exceeds that of the unregistered raster; not reproduced when it is lower under all; methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The size of the estimated displacement (range and s.d. in um) and the plot of the trace over the raster are reported. That a small improvement may reflect little drift in an anesthetized, paralyzed animal is noted, not judged.

claims.statement: A smoothing spline fit to the centered positions of the clustered spikes captures sub-second displacement left after AP DREDge registration.

claims.criterion: Pipeline step 3 under each combination of its open readings. The paper gives no number and no test for this panel. The control is borrowed from another panel of the paper, the "randomly permuted or 'scrambled'" motion estimate of Fig. 2e (legend), which the paper uses for ISI violations, not for this figure, and whose permutation unit it does not give. For each combination, the pooled within-cluster s.d. of corrected depth of the clustered spikes is computed after correction by the spline and after correction by the same spline trace with its time bins randomly permuted. The permutation bin (0.4 s, the knot spacing), the 100 permutations with a fixed seed and the one-sided 5% level are choices of this file, not of the paper. Reproduced when, in every combination, the spline-corrected s.d. is below the 5th percentile of the scrambled s.d. values; not reproduced when in none; methods_underspecified otherwise. The spline trace's range and s.d. (um) and its power spectrum are reported, as is the noted circularity that the spline is fit to the spikes it is evaluated on.

claims.statement: Correcting the AP-registered spikes with the spline estimate of sub-second displacement gives a more stable spike raster and tighter spike localizations than AP DREDge registration alone.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 3d and 3e legends; Results, DREDge rescues spike sorting and LFP features in human brain activity, paragraph 1
claims.quote: d Top, AP registered spike raster. Bottom, AP registered spike raster corrected using the spline estimate of sub-second displacement. e Localizations of detected spikes after AP DREDge registration (left), and spline correction (right).
claims.criterion: The legends show the comparison and state no result in words; the improvement is read from the Results, which call the spline estimate "a faster timescale AP-based estimate". Two measures, one per panel, both from the paper. Panel d, the mean template correlation (Methods, Spike registration quality metrics) of all detected spikes, on the 1 um by 1 s raster of mean amplitudes, after AP DREDge correction and after AP DREDge plus spline correction (the spline displacement subtracted from each spike's registered depth at its time). Panel e, the pooled within-cluster s.d. of corrected depth over the HDBSCAN clusters, before and after spline correction; the paper names no measure for panel e, so this one is the file's choice, and since the spline is fit to minimize these residuals it is reported with that circularity noted. The 1 s bins of the template correlation are the Methods' and cannot show motion faster than 1 s, so the panel d measure is also reported at 0.1 s bins as a variant that does not enter the outcome. Reproduced when both measures improve (higher correlation, lower s.d.) under every combination of the open readings of steps 2 and 3; not reproduced when neither improves under any; partially reproduced when one measure improves under every combination and the other does not; methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The size of each change is reported.
