claims.criterion: Participants with preinfusion normalized affective closure above 0.5 (fig. S14G legend); change defined as infusion minus the mean of pre- and postinfusion (legend) or as ketamine minus preinfusion (table S3), both shown. Reproduced when, under either, rho is within tolerance with p < 0.05, taking the sign of the change so that a larger loss scores higher.

claims.statement: In the human participants, activity along the persistent (0.5 to 1.5 s) beta-power coding dimension fell during ketamine (1.36 to 0.41) and recovered after infusion (0.72).
claims.source: Figure 6C; table S3, Fig. 6C
claims.quote: Across species we observed a decrease, caused by ketamine, in eyepuff-triggered persistence that recovered post infusion

claims.statement: In the human participants, activity along the fast (50 to 100 ms) coding dimension was not changed by ketamine.
claims.source: Figure 6E; table S3, Fig. 6E
claims.quote: Fast population activity is not significantly altered by ketamine in humans
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test (paired t-tests with FDR correction). Reproduced when neither corrected p is below 0.05.

claims.statement: In the human participants, the intrinsic timescale of the persistent dimension at baseline was shorter during ketamine (0.09 s) than before (0.11 s).
claims.source: Figure 6G; table S3, Fig. 6G
claims.quote: In both humans and mice, we observed that ketamine robustly accelerated the baseline intrinsic timescale of the population
claims.criterion: The Methods (Intrinsic timescale) take an eight-minute period before the eyepuff assay; table S3 says the ten minutes before. Both are shown. Exponential a*exp(-x/b) + c fitted from the autocorrelation peak to 2.5 s, initial a=1, b=0.2, c=0. Reproduced when, under either period, both means are within tolerance and the paired t-test gives p < 0.05 with ketamine shorter.

claims.statement: In the human participants, beta phase locking among the most persistent channels at baseline fell during ketamine (0.979 of preinfusion).
claims.source: Figure 6I; table S3, Fig. 6I
claims.quote: in both mice and humans, we discovered that ketamine decreased coupling among these sites
claims.criterion: The top 10% of sites per participant by persistent-dimension weight, white matter excluded (Methods, Phase-locking Value); table S3 says channels above the 90th percentile. Sliding 5 s windows, preinfusion 25 min before infusion and the final 25 min of infusion outside the assay; the Methods also name the ten minutes before the eyepuff assay (table S3), shown as a variant. Reproduced when the normalized value is within tolerance and the paired t-test gives p < 0.05 with ketamine lower.

claims.statement: In mice, ketamine (50 mg/kg) reduced late eye closure normalized by early closure on the first puff of each series (0.26 under saline, -0.07 under ketamine).
claims.source: Figure 1K; table S3, Fig. 1K
claims.quote: Late eye closure, normalized by early eye closure (0.1 to 0.2 s afterpuff onset), decreases during ketamine ( n = 5 mice

claims.statement: Compared with preinfusion, normalized late closure was unchanged by saline but reduced by ketamine (50 mg/kg) and PCP (20 mg/kg).
claims.source: Figure 1L; table S3, Fig. 1L
claims.quote: dissociative drugs such as ketamine and phencyclidine [(PCP), uniquely enabled for mice] similarly reduced late but not early eye closure

claims.statement: Under ketamine the early (reflexive) closure of mice was reduced but present (0.78 to 0.45), while late (affective) closure was abolished (0.34 to -0.02).
claims.source: Figure S2B and S2C; table S3, fig. S2 B and C
claims.quote: Late eye ... closure (during 0.3 to 0.8 s after puff onset) is abolished by ketamine

claims.statement: Late eye closure accumulated across the eight puffs of a series and decayed slowly after the last puff, with a Kaplan-Meier median persistence of 15.16 s.
claims.source: Figure 1M; fig. S2E; table S3, fig. S2 E
claims.quote: We found that late-phase eye closure in mice accumulated across a sequence of eyepuffs and decayed slowly after the final eyepuff in the sequence
claims.criterion: Preinfusion trials, 20 per mouse in 5 mice (table S3, fig. S2 E). Reproduced when the Kaplan-Meier median is within tolerance and the mean late closure (0.3 to 0.8 s) after the eighth puff exceeds that after the first, with non-overlapping mean +- 1.96 s.e.m. across mice. The paper does not state the event that ends survival; that detail is open.

claims.statement: In mice, normalized late eye closure was larger after the eighth puff of a series than after the first at each of three puff pressures (8, 18 and 28 PSI), while it did not differ between pressures at the eighth puff.
claims.source: Figure S2F and S2G; table S3, fig. S2 G
claims.quote: Late (normed by early) eye closure scales with puff number but not puff intensity, comparing air puffs of different pressure
claims.criterion: The paper's tests (table S3, fig. S2 G), paired t-tests across 8 mice with FDR correction over the six comparisons, on per-mouse means of late (0.3 to 0.8 s) divided by early (0.1 to 0.2 s) closure, preinfusion. Reproduced when the three puff 1 against puff 8 tests give corrected p < 0.05 with puff 8 higher and the three pressure comparisons give corrected p >= 0.05 (the absence is judged on the paper's test); the differences are reported either way.

claims.statement: The dissociative reduction of normalized late eye closure began around 35 mg/kg ketamine and 10 mg/kg PCP; lower doses did not significantly reduce it.
claims.source: Figure S2H to S2J; table S3, fig. S2 H; Results, Precisely timed affective behavior in mice and humans
claims.quote: Dose-response investigation showed that these robust dissociative effects begin around 35 mg/kg ketamine and 10 mg/kg PCP
claims.criterion: The paper's tests (table S3, fig. S2 H), paired t-tests of preinfusion against infusion of normalized late closure after the eighth puff at each dose, FDR-corrected. The family of the correction is not given; the readings are (a) all ten comparisons of the table together (saline included), (b) each drug apart. Reproduced when, under both readings, ketamine 35 and 50 mg/kg and PCP 10 and 20 mg/kg give corrected p < 0.05 with a decrease and the lower doses give corrected p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: A general anesthetic dose of ketamine with xylazine abolished both reflexive and affective eye closure, while ketamine or PCP alone kept the reflexive blink.
claims.source: Figure 1N to 1P; fig. S5D and S5E; Results, Precisely timed affective behavior in mice and humans
claims.quote: By contrast, general anesthesia, achieved through addition of xylazine to ketamine ... abolished both reflexive and affective responses
claims.criterion: The paper's tests (table S3, fig. S5 D and E), paired t-tests with FDR correction of reflexive (0.1 to 0.2 s) and affective (0.3 to 0.8 s) closure after the eighth puff, 5 mice, 15 trials each. Reproduced when both K/X tests give corrected p < 0.05 with K/X lower, the K/X values are within tolerance, and the reflexive closure under ketamine and under PCP is within tolerance (present, unlike K/X). Fig. 1N to 1P themselves carry no test.

claims.statement: Buprenorphine and diazepam did not reduce normalized late closure, unlike ketamine and PCP.
claims.source: Figure S5C; table S3, fig. S5 C
claims.quote: Only ketamine (50 mg/kg) and PCP (20 mg/kg) decrease late normalized by early eye closure
claims.criterion: The paper's test, paired t-tests with FDR correction on normalized late closure of the eighth puff. Reproduced when ketamine and PCP give corrected p < 0.05 with a decrease and buprenorphine and diazepam give corrected p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Inhibiting VPM thalamus with muscimol reduced normalized affective closure (0.60 after saline injection, 0.11 after muscimol) while the fast early closure remained.
claims.source: Figure S6B, S6C and S6H; table S3, fig. S6 C
claims.quote: With muscimol, there is early eye closure after each puff, but no accumulating late eye closure

claims.statement: Eyepuff series persistently reduced licking for a liquid reward, which recovered slowly after the last puff.
claims.source: Figure S4B
claims.quote: Lick probability decreased persistently during the air puff sequences and slowly recovered after the final air puff of the sequence
claims.criterion: Lick probability in 3 s bins, both series per mouse combined, averaged over 6 mice (Methods and fig. S4B). Reproduced when the mean lick probability over the series (0 to 24 s from the first puff) is below that of the 24 s before it, with non-overlapping mean +- 1.96 s.e.m. across mice. The paper reports no test.

claims.statement: Varying only the persistence timescale of the two-phase model explained much of the variation in affective eye closure across doses of ketamine and of PCP.
claims.source: Figure 5H and 5I; table S3, Fig. 5H, I
claims.quote: We found that varying τ PERSIST alone across different doses of ketamine explained substantial variance across doses
claims.criterion: Fit as for fig5g-tau-persist-model on the dose series (ketamine 6, 13, 25, 35 mg/kg; PCP 1, 5, 10 mg/kg; 5 mice), 750 ms after each puff masked (Methods, Model fitting, behavioral data; analysis.py filter_reflex). Variance explained is 1 - MSE_model/MSE_null against the fit with no parameter varying. The paper gives no value and no threshold; reproduced when the variance explained is positive for each drug and the fitted persistence timescale falls with dose.

claims.statement: Many thousands of single units were recorded across 13 sessions from 10 mice, with dozens of regions recorded simultaneously.
claims.source: Figure 4C; fig. S29A and S29B; table S2; table S3, Fig. 4E
claims.quote: We obtained recordings from many thousands of single units throughout the brain, with simultaneous recording of dozens of regions
claims.criterion: Counts of sessions and mice must match exactly. Units counted after the paper's quality criteria (Methods); "dozens of regions" holds when the median session has units in at least 24 Allen CCFv3 regions at the finest level, a reading of "dozens" as two dozen since the paper gives no count. The puff-modulated count uses the selection in the opening comment and depends on it.

claims.statement: The recorded mice showed affective eye closure after the first puff of each series, and ketamine reduced it.
claims.source: Figure 4B; fig. S28A; table S3, Fig. 4B
claims.quote: In response to eyepuffs, mice showed affective eye closure that was reduced by ketamine
claims.criterion: Eye closure of the 13 recorded sessions, baseline-subtracted with the 1 s before the puff (table S3), first puff of each series, Pre series 1 to 20 against Ketamine series 23 to 32 (code; Methods-literal 22 to 32 as a variant); the code normalizes each session's trace by its maximum before averaging, shown with and without. Late closure is the mean over 0.3 to 0.8 s (the paper's late window). Reproduced when the across-session mean of Pre minus Ketamine late closure has a 95% interval (1.96 s.e.m., table S3) above zero. The paper reports no test.

claims.statement: In the recorded mice, eye closure accumulated across each puff series, and ketamine abolished the accumulation.
claims.source: Figure 5B; table S3, Fig. 5B
claims.quote: recorded animals exhibited progressively accumulating eye closure behavior during each eyepuff series, which was abolished by ketamine
claims.criterion: 11 sessions from 9 mice (the excluded animal is open, see fig5d-emotion-dimension-accumulates), eye closure baseline-subtracted with the 1 s before each series (table S3). Accumulation is the late closure (0.3 to 0.8 s) after puff 8 minus that after puff 1. Reproduced when the 95% interval (1.96 s.e.m. across sessions) of accumulation is above zero for Pre and includes zero or lies below the Pre mean for Ketamine (series 23 to 32). The paper reports no test.

claims.statement: Unsupervised clustering of peri-puff responses of puff-modulated units from all sessions gave twelve clusters spread over many regions, some responding rapidly and briefly and others persistently after rapid (clusters 0 and 1) or delayed (cluster 2) onset.
claims.source: Figure 4D and 4E; fig. S31A; table S3, Fig. 4E
claims.quote: Some clusters responded rapidly and briefly to the eyepuff whereas others responded persistently after either rapid (clusters 0 and 1) or delayed onset (cluster 2)
claims.criterion: Method from the Methods (Unsupervised clustering) and analysis.py get_cell_clusters. Puff-modulated units of all 13 sessions; per unit, the z-scored rate from -1 to 2 s around each puff averaged over the 160 Pre puffs, minus its mean over -1 to 0 s; scanpy PCA (arpack), neighbors (n_neighbors 30, n_pcs 20), UMAP, Leiden with default resolution, seeds 42. The Methods say Leiden runs on the UMAP embedding; scanpy's leiden, as the code calls it, runs on the neighbor graph, which is followed. Cluster sizes are compared in descending order, since the numbering of table S3 is by size while the figure numbers clusters top to bottom after a hierarchical reordering; which numbering the text's "clusters 0, 1 and 2" uses is open, and the response shapes are judged under both. Rapid and brief means the cluster mean decays to 25% of its post-puff peak (Methods, Cumulative fraction of cells, and code find_decay) within 0.25 s of onset; persistent means it is still above 25% of its peak over 1 to 2 s, the window the Methods use to quantify persistent activity. The 25% level is the paper's; the 0.25 s bound and the use of the 1 to 2 s window for "persistent" are readings, since the paper gives no cut-off for "rapidly and briefly" or "persistently". Reproduced when the cluster count and sizes are within tolerance and at least one cluster is rapid and brief while three are persistent, two with peaks in the first 250 ms and one later.

claims.statement: Clusters overrepresented in the periaqueductal gray and VPM thalamus had fast, sharp responses, while clusters overrepresented in frontal cortex and limbic regions responded more slowly and persistently.
claims.source: Figure 4G; fig. S31A and S31B; table S3, fig. S31 B
claims.quote: Indeed, clusters overrepresented in midbrain (PAG) and thalamus (VPM) exhibited fast and sharp response dynamics, whereas clusters overrepresented in frontal cortex and limbic regions responded more slowly and persistently following the eyepuff
claims.criterion: As in table S3, fig. S31 B and analysis.py get_cluster_null_distribution. Regions with more than 30 clustered cells; for each region and cluster, the fraction of the region's cells in the cluster against 20,000 draws of uniformly random labels, two-sided, FDR across regions. The threshold is 0.05 in the Methods and the code and 0.01 in table S3; both are shown. Clusters are ranked by the time their mean falls to 25% of its post-puff peak. Reproduced when PAG and VPM are each significantly overrepresented in a cluster from the faster half, and at least one frontal cortical or limbic region (ORB, ACA, PL, ILA, MOs, AI, as Supplemental Note 1 maps them) in a cluster from the slower half.

claims.statement: Ketamine substantially changed the responses of clusters with slow, persistent preinfusion dynamics but left fast clusters little changed.
claims.source: Figure 4G; fig. S31C; table S3, Fig 4G
claims.quote: Clusters with more rapid preinfusion dynamics were minimally altered or unaltered by ketamine, whereas clusters with slower and more persistent preinfusion dynamics were substantially altered
claims.criterion: Cluster means as in table S3 (all cells of the cluster pooled, baseline-subtracted with the 1 s before the puff, z-scored over the peri-puff window within cluster and condition), Pre series 1 to 20 against Ketamine series 23 to 32 (code plot_avg_psth_prepost_ket, 10 series). Table S3 gives 64 Ketamine puffs per cluster (8 series), which the code does not reproduce and the paper does not place; the code is followed and the conflict is a deviation. The paper gives no measure of change. The readings are (a) the cosine distance between the Pre and Ketamine mean traces from -1 to 2 s, the similarity measure of the Methods (Analysis of similarity); (b) the absolute difference of the means over 1 to 2 s. Reproduced when, under both, the change correlates positively with the Pre decay time (to 25% of peak) across clusters by Spearman correlation at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Most regions responded to the puff with fast rise times, and ketamine did not change regional rise times.
claims.source: Figure 4I; fig. S31D to S31F; table S3, Fig. 4H, I
claims.quote: On a regional basis as well, the rise times of average neural activity were not altered by ketamine
claims.criterion: Method from the Methods (Regional rise and decay time), table S3 and analysis.py region_time_course. Regions merged across cortical layers (code reduce_region) with more than 30 puff-modulated units (code; the Methods say at least 30, shown as a variant); per region and cluster (cluster 11 skipped, as the code does) the first two puffs of each series, baseline-subtracted, turned into d' against the 1 s before the puff; rise is the time to 25% of the peak, combined across clusters weighted by the region's cell fractions; regions whose peak comes after 750 ms dropped; 1000 bootstraps over puffs; Ketamine series 23 to 32. Regions are excluded when their peak d' is below 1.3 (Methods and code) or below 2 (table S3); both are shown. The paper reports no test of absence. Reproduced when, under both thresholds, the median over regions of the bootstrap median change in rise time (Ketamine minus Pre, as fig. S31F) lies within one 10 ms bin of zero and the Pre median rise time is below 0.1 s in most regions.

claims.statement: Ketamine shortened the time for regional puff responses to decay from their peak.
claims.source: Figure 4H; fig. S31G
claims.quote: whereas regional times to decay from peak response were shortened
claims.criterion: Decay time is the time from the d' peak to fall to 25% of the peak, computed as for fig4i-rise-times-unchanged, under both d' thresholds. Reproduced when the median of the distribution of bootstrapped changes (Ketamine minus Pre) across regions, as fig. S31G draws it, is below zero and more than half the regions have a Ketamine median decay below their Pre median. The paper reports no test.

claims.statement: Before ketamine, regional decay times followed a progression from subcortical to frontal cortical regions, with long decays in frontal and limbic cortex and in VPM and MD thalamus.
claims.source: Figure 4H; Results, Brain-wide activity screen during emergence of affect in mice
claims.quote: decay times of regional neural activity were more variable and followed a general anatomical progression from subcortical to frontal cortical regions
claims.criterion: Pre decay medians per region, computed as for fig4i-rise-times-unchanged under both d' thresholds. Frontal and limbic cortex is ORB, ACA, PL, ILA, MOs, MOp and AI (the mouse regions Supplemental Note 1 maps to the human frontal and limbic regions); midbrain is the regions under MB in the Allen hierarchy. Reproduced when the median decay of the frontal and limbic regions exceeds that of the midbrain regions, and VPM and MD each lie above the median decay of all regions. The paper reports no test.

claims.statement: Population activity along an emotion-like dimension (after the series against before it) rose and saturated across the puff series and decayed over tens of seconds afterwards; under ketamine it did not accumulate.
claims.source: Figure 5C and 5D; table S3, Fig. 5D
claims.quote: Measuring neural activity along this dimension revealed emotion-like properties of scalability through a saturating rise across the series of eyepuffs and of persistence through a decay lasting tens of seconds following each eyepuff series before returning to baseline
claims.criterion: Sessions. 11 sessions from 9 mice; the paper does not name the excluded animal, so each mouse with more than one session whose removal leaves 11 sessions from 9 mice is a reading, and the outcome must hold under all of them. Dimension (Methods, Emotion-like neural dimension, and analysis.py get_affective_projections), per session from puff-modulated units (sessions with at least 20). Target window is the 1 s starting 5 s after the last puff onset (Methods); the code's window falls 3 to 4 s after it (bins 400 to 500 of a post-series window that its plotting places 1 s before the last puff), shown as a variant. Reference is the 750 ms ending 250 ms before the first puff. Weights are mean differences normalized by per-unit variance (Methods; the code divides by the variance pooled over all units, a variant), made orthogonal by QR to an eye-reflex dimension from the last four puffs (200 ms after against 200 ms before onset), signed so that puff 8 exceeds puff 1 (code). Projections are baseline- subtracted per series with the 250 ms before the first puff. Reproduced when, for Pre, the 95% interval across sessions (1.96 s.e.m., table S3) of the mean projection in the 250 ms before puff 8 is above zero and higher than before puff 2, the projection 10 to 11 s after the last puff onset is still above zero and the last 5 s of the 45 s shown after the series include zero; and, for Ketamine (series 23 to 32), the interval before puff 8 includes zero or lies below the Pre mean.

claims.statement: On the first puff of a series, late emotion-like activity (2 to 3 s after onset) was reduced by ketamine (0.546 to 0.005).
claims.source: Figure 5E; table S3, Fig. 5E
claims.quote: late changes along the emotion-like dimension (seconds after each eyepuff) were reduced
claims.criterion: Dimension and readings as in fig5d-emotion-dimension-accumulates; per session the mean over series of the first-puff projection in 2 to 3 s, baseline the 250 ms before the puff (analysis.py plot_affective_firstpuff_persist); two-sided paired t-test across sessions, FDR over the two windows. Reproduced when corrected p < 0.05 with Ketamine lower. The expected values are met when, under one weight scaling (unit vector or sum of absolute values), both are within tolerance; otherwise the claim is partially reproduced if the test holds.

claims.statement: The rapid emotion-like response to the first puff (0 to 0.25 s) did not differ between preinfusion and ketamine.
claims.source: Figure 5E; table S3, Fig. 5E
claims.quote: These transient increases on ketamine were not different from those prior to ketamine
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the two-sided paired t-test with FDR over the two windows, as for fig5e-late-reduced. Reproduced when corrected p >= 0.05; the difference is reported either way.

claims.statement: A two-phase first-order model in which only the persistence timescale differs between preinfusion and ketamine closely matched the emotion-like population activity.
claims.source: Figure 5F and 5G; table S3, Fig. 5G
claims.quote: Despite only varying the single parameter τ PERSIST across preinfusion and ketamine conditions, we observed a close match between the model and the experimental data
claims.criterion: Model and fit from the Methods (Theoretical model) and analysis.py (model_system, theoretical_persist, compare_model). Inputs are eight 250 ms steps 3 s apart; broadcast phase x = (S - x0)(1 - exp(-t/tauB)) + x0, persistence phase x = x0 exp(-t/tauP). Fitted with scipy curve_fit to the across-session mean of Pre and Ketamine traces concatenated, from -0.25 to 23 s and 25 to 70 s after the first puff (the dimension's training window left out), S and tauB shared, tauP times a factor in [0, 1] per condition (null factor in [0.99999, 1]), bounds [0, 100]. Variance explained is 1 - MSE_model/MSE_null. The paper gives no value for "close match". Reproduced when the variance explained is positive and the fitted Ketamine persistence timescale is shorter than the Pre one, under each reading of the dimension.

claims.statement: Alternative models in which ketamine changes the input scale S or the broadcast rate, or a symmetric single-timescale model, fit the ketamine puff-series activity worse than the model in which ketamine changes the persistence timescale.
claims.source: Figure S33A to S33D; Results, Brain-wide activity screen during emergence of affect in mice
claims.quote: other alternative models in which ketamine modulated the input scale S or the broadcast rate τ BROADCAST instead of τ PERSIST also did not fit the data well
claims.criterion: The same fit with the factor on S (theoretical_saturation), on tauB (theoretical_broadcast), or a single timescale (theoretical_symmetric). Variance explained on the Ketamine puff-series segment (fig. S33D). Reproduced when the tauP model has the highest variance explained there of the four.

claims.statement: Emotion-like dimensions computed within each high-level brain area all showed accumulating persistent dynamics before ketamine that ketamine abolished.
claims.source: Figure S32C
claims.quote: All high-level brain areas ... exhibit some ... degree of accumulating persistent dynamics during preinfusion that is abolished by ketamine
claims.criterion: As fig5d-emotion-dimension-accumulates, with units restricted per session to one high-level area (Methods, emotion-like dimension, last sentences); areas and sessions with at least 20 simultaneously recorded puff-modulated units (code min_cells). High-level areas are the Allen top-level divisions; the paper does not list them. Reproduced when every area that has at least two qualifying sessions meets the Pre and Ketamine conditions of that criterion for the value before puff 8; partially reproduced when most do.

claims.statement: The neurons carrying the persistent peri-puff dimension were not focally localized but distributed over much of the brain.
claims.source: Figure 6B; fig. S36A
claims.quote: We found that the persistent dimension was not focally localized in either mice or humans; instead, a distribution spanning much of the brain was observed across both species
claims.criterion: Persistent-dimension weights as in fig6d-mouse-persistent. The paper gives no measure. Reproduced when the units with the top 10% of absolute weight in each session (the paper's "persistent neurons", table S3, Fig. 6J) are found in every Allen top-level division that holds at least 30 included units (the Methods' regional minimum) and no single division holds more than half of them.

claims.statement: In mice, activity along the persistent (0.5 to 1 s) coding dimension 1 to 2 s after the puff fell during ketamine (0.86 to 0.02) and partly recovered afterwards (0.52).
claims.source: Figure 6D; table S3, Fig. 6D
claims.quote: Across species we observed a decrease, caused by ketamine, in eyepuff-triggered persistence that recovered post infusion
claims.criterion: Method from the Methods (Coding dimension, mouse peri-puff), table S3 and analysis.py plot_coding_dimension_early_late. Per session (sessions as in fig5d-emotion-dimension-accumulates), weights from Pre puffs of puff-modulated units, mean over 0.5 to 1 s against the 1 s before the puff, normalized by variance (per unit, Methods; pooled, code variant). The projection is averaged over series, z-scored over -1 to 2 s within session and condition and baseline- subtracted over -1 to 0 s (code); quantified as its mean over 1 to 2 s. The code projects the first puff of each series only; all eight puffs is a variant. Pre series 1 to 20, Ketamine 23 to 32, Post 35 to 40. Two paired t-tests, FDR over the two. Reproduced when both corrected p < 0.05 with Ketamine lowest and the means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when only Pre against Ketamine holds.

claims.statement: In mice, activity along the fast (0 to 70 ms) coding dimension was not changed by ketamine.
claims.source: Figure 6F; table S3, Fig. 6F
claims.quote: whereas similar analysis of a dimension encoding fast eyepuff-triggered activity exhibited no decrease during infusion
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, two-sided paired t-tests with FDR over the two comparisons. Target window 0 to 70 ms after onset; the Methods compare it with the 1 s before the puff, the code (cd_end 107) with the 70 ms before, and the Methods are followed with the code as a variant. Projection over all series and all eight puffs, z-scored over -1 to 2 s within session and condition, quantified over 0 to 70 ms (code). Reproduced when the Pre against Ketamine corrected p >= 0.05; the differences are reported either way.

claims.statement: In mice, the intrinsic timescale of the persistent dimension in the 30 s before each series was shorter during ketamine (0.14 s) than before (0.45 s).
claims.source: Figure 6H; fig. S34B; table S3, Fig. 6H
claims.quote: In both humans and mice, we observed that ketamine robustly accelerated the baseline intrinsic timescale of the population
claims.criterion: Method from the Methods (Intrinsic timescale analysis, mouse) and analysis.py stimulus_timescales and extract_timescale. Rates in the 30 s before the first puff of each series projected on the persistent weights of fig6d-mouse-persistent; autocorrelation (scipy.signal.correlate) normalized to its maximum, a*exp(-x/b) + c fitted over the 2.5 s after the peak, initial a=1, b=0.2, c=0; b is the timescale. Series used are Pre 11 to 20 and Ketamine 23 to 32 (code, ten each as table S3). Two readings of how series are combined (a) per series fits averaged within session (Methods and table S3); (b) one fit to the series concatenated (code). Reproduced when, under both, the paired t-test gives p < 0.05 with Ketamine shorter and both means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the test holds but the means do not.

claims.statement: In mice, correlations among the most persistent neurons in the 30 s before each series fell during ketamine to 0.49 of their preinfusion value.
claims.source: Figure 6J; table S3, Fig. 6J
claims.quote: in both mice and humans, we discovered that ketamine decreased coupling among these sites
claims.criterion: Persistent neurons and coupling. The Methods take edges between neurons in the top 10% of absolute persistent weight, Pearson correlation averaged within session; the code (plot_coding_dimension_early_late) takes neurons whose signed weight exceeds the 90th percentile of absolute weights and the median absolute correlation of z-scored rates over the concatenated 30 s windows of Pre series 1 to 10 and Ketamine series 23 to 32. Readings are (a) the Methods, per-series 30 s windows, mean r over edges, averaged over series (table S3), on the code's series (Pre 1 to 10, Ketamine 23 to 32), since table S3 gives ten series per condition without naming them; (b) the code. Ketamine values divided by Pre within session; paired t-test across sessions. Reproduced when, under both, p < 0.05 with Ketamine lower; the expected value is met under either.

claims.statement: Mice did not close their eyes appreciably to a series of auditory tones, before or during ketamine.
claims.source: Figure S34C; table S3, fig. S34 C
claims.quote: mice do not increase eye closure during tone presentation
claims.criterion: Eye closure across the tone series, 7 sessions from 7 mice, Pre 10 series, Ketamine 5 (table S3). Reproduced when the 95% interval across sessions (1.96 s.e.m.) of the mean closure from 0.3 to 0.8 s after each tone, averaged over the eight tones, lies below the corresponding eyepuff value of the same sessions and below 0.1 of full closure. The 0.1 bound is a reading of "not substantial"; the paper reports no test.

claims.statement: Fast tone-related population activity (0 to 70 ms) was not changed by ketamine.
claims.source: Figure S34D; table S3, fig. S34 D
claims.quote: Whereas fast tone-related neural activity was unchanged on ketamine
