claims.statement: After trial cleaning 20,952 trials (about 68% of the data) remain across 34 sessions with valid dopamine recordings.
claims.source: Methods, Neural data analysis, paragraph 2
claims.quote: After this cleaning, we were left with 20952 trials ( ~ 68 % of the dataset) across 34 sessions with valid dopamine recordings
claims.criterion: Sessions and cleaning as in the opening comment, under both SO_lat limits. Reproduced when, under one reading, the session count is 34 and the trial count within tolerance; partially reproduced when the trial count is within tolerance with another session count.

claims.statement: RPEs of BIfp and BRLfwr explain outcome dopamine better than RL4p RPEs and better than RLCF, RLFQ3p, RL_meta and PearceHall, by cross-validated log-likelihood.
claims.source: Results, Predictions from BRLfwr and BIfp, paragraph 4; Fig 4F
claims.quote: we found that both BIfp and BRLfwr models yielded larger relative log-likelihood ( Δ llk CV ) than the RL4p baseline, evaluated on cross validation sets (70-30) for each animal ... Both Bayesian models also outperformed other complex RL models on this measure
claims.criterion: Cleaned trials of the 34 sessions. Per model, the Methods' regression outcome_DA_PT ~ rpe:rpe_pos + rpe:rpe_neg + port_dur:rpe_pos + port_dur:rpe_neg + ego_action + session_num + log__MVMT + log__center_dur, by OLS (Gaussian likelihood), with rpe the model RPE of the opening comment, rpe_pos and rpe_neg indicators of rpe >= 0 and < 0, ego_action the choice contralateral or ipsilateral to the recorded hemisphere, session_num numeric, natural logs. Per animal, 70% of trials to fit and 30% to test, test log-likelihood with the training residual variance; Δllk_CV = llk(model) - llk(RL4p) on the same split. Not given ("featurized covariates", the split, the number of splits, the unit of the bootstrap); readings (a) random trial splits, 100 repeats per animal, Δ summed over animals per repeat, bootstrap over repeats; (b) the same with Δ per animal and bootstrap over animals and repeats; (c) splits by session. BIfp RPE and RLFQ3p forgetting with both variants of the opening comment. Reproduced when, under every reading, BRLfwr and BIfp have Δllk_CV > 0 with CI above 0 and each exceeds RLCF, RLFQ3p, RL_meta and PearceHall, and under one reading the six values lie inside the paper's intervals. Partially reproduced when this order holds but no reading puts the values inside the intervals, or when one Bayesian model meets the order.

claims.statement: Relative AIC, relative BIC, cross-validated R2 and cross-validated log-likelihood of the dopamine regressions all favour the Bayesian models' RPEs.
claims.source: S3 Fig legend; Methods, Neural data analysis, paragraph 2
claims.quote: All metrics converged on favoring Bayesian model predictions of dopamine at outcome phase
claims.criterion: The regressions of fig4f-bayesian-rpe-fit; AIC and BIC from the fit to all cleaned trials per animal, R2 and log-likelihood from the test sets, each relative to RL4p. Reproduced when, for every metric, BIfp and BRLfwr are better than RL4p and than each of RLCF, RLFQ3p, RL_meta and PearceHall; partially reproduced when this holds for at least two metrics.

claims.statement: On consecutive stay trials, dopamine responses to reward decrease as recent rewards accumulate (from aaa to AAA) but do not flatten to no response.
claims.source: Results, Predictions from BRLfwr and BIfp, paragraph 5; Fig 4G
claims.quote: As mice encountered more rewards in their recent history, dLight dopamine responses to reward gradually decreased (consistent with decreased RPE) but did not completely flatten to no response
claims.criterion: Rewarded trials t with t-3, t-2, t-1 and t at the same port (Fig 4G legend), by the outcomes at t-3 to t-1 (aaa to AAA). Cleaned trials. The paper reports no test. Read as (1) the Spearman correlation between the number of rewards in the history (0 to 3) and DA-PT is negative with p < 0.05; (2) on AAA trials the mean de-based Z(DA) over 0 to 1 s (DA-PT of a rewarded trial cannot fall below 0, so it cannot show flattening) has a 95% bootstrapped CI above 0. Reproduced when both hold.

claims.statement: OLS models predicting dopamine from each model's RPE alone fit best for BRLfwr (cross-validated log-likelihood -985.89, against -991.80 to -995.02 for the RL models).
claims.source: Results, Predictions from BRLfwr and BIfp, paragraph 5; Fig 4H
claims.quote: We compared the model fitness across different cognitive models with cross validated log-likelihood (BRLfwr ... Indeed, BRLfwr RPE predictions achieved the highest model fitness to dopamine data
claims.criterion: Per model, an OLS of DA-PT on the model RPE only, with cross-validation as in fig4f-bayesian-rpe-fit. Not given; readings of the RPE terms (a) rpe:rpe_pos + rpe:rpe_neg, (b) one rpe slope; of the trials (i) the Fig 4G subset (rewarded consecutive stay trials), (ii) all cleaned trials. Reproduced when, under every reading, BRLfwr has the highest llk_CV of the six and, under one reading, the six values are within tolerance (10% is loose here, as the values differ by under 1%); partially reproduced when the order holds and no reading gives the values. BIfp, which the sentence omits, is shown.

claims.statement: BRLfwr and BIfp predict a small but non-negative RPE on rewarded stay trials after consecutive rewards, as dopamine shows, while RL_meta and PearceHall drive the RPE toward zero as rewards accumulate.
claims.source: Results, Predictions from BRLfwr and BIfp, paragraphs 6 and 7; Fig 4H
claims.quote: This also allowed the best fitting BRLfwr and BIfp model to predict a small but non-negative RPE response on rewarded stay trials ( Fig 4H )
claims.criterion: On the Fig 4G trials, mean model RPE per history. Reproduced when on AAA trials the mean RPE of BRLfwr and of BIfp is above 0 and above that of each of RL4p, RLCF, RLFQ3p, RL_meta and PearceHall; partially reproduced when one of the two Bayesian models meets this.

claims.statement: Among trials following a reward at t-1, the dopamine response is consistent whatever the more distant history, and only BRLfwr captures this.
claims.source: Results, Predictions from BRLfwr and BIfp, paragraph 7; Fig 4G and 4H
claims.quote: Furthermore, we observed that among trials after an immediate past trial reward, the dopamine response was highly consistent, independent of more distant outcome histories. Only BRLfwr captured this phenomenon qualitatively
claims.criterion: The Fig 4G trials with A at t-1 (aaA, AaA, aAA, AAA). No test is given. Read as (1) a one-way ANOVA of DA-PT across the four histories has p >= 0.05; (2) the range (max - min) of the four mean model RPEs, divided by the model's range over all eight histories, is smallest for BRLfwr among BRLfwr, BIfp, RL4p, RLCF, RLFQ3p, RL_meta and PearceHall. Reproduced when both hold; partially reproduced when (1) holds alone.

claims.statement: On switch trials, past rewards at the chosen port reduce outcome dopamine (slope -0.128) and past rewards at the other port increase it (slope 0.126).
claims.source: Results, Predictions from BRLfwr and BIfp, paragraph 8; Fig 4I
claims.quote: LMER fitting revealed a significantly negative effect of R_chosen on dopamine at outcome phase during animal switch trials (slope estimate ... and a significantly positive effect of R_unchosen on dopamine during animal switch trials
claims.criterion: Cleaned trials. R_chosen is the number of rewarded trials among t-1 to t-4 at the port chosen at t, R_unchosen at the other port; Reward the outcome at t; Switch and Stay indicators of trial t. The Methods' lme4 formula DA ~ Reward:Switch + R_chosen:Switch + Switch + R_unchosen:Switch + 1 + Reward:Stay + R_chosen:Stay + R_unchosen:Stay, each term with a by-Subject random effect. Not given; readings of the random part (a) (term | Subject) for each term, (b) uncorrelated random slopes (0 + term | Subject) plus (1 | Subject); of DA, (i) DA-PT, (ii) mean de-based Z(DA) over 0 to 1 s; Wald CIs. Reproduced when, under one reading, both slopes have the paper's sign with CI excluding 0 and lie in the paper's intervals; partially reproduced when the signs hold with CI excluding 0 but a value lies outside.

claims.statement: On stay trials, past rewards at the chosen port reduce outcome dopamine (slope -0.09), as all models predict.
claims.source: Results, Predictions from BRLfwr and BIfp, paragraph 8; Fig 4J
claims.quote: All models predicted a negative relationship between R_chosen and RPE signal, matching the dopamine observation (slope estimate
claims.criterion: The same model and readings as fig4i-lmer-switch, the R_chosen:Stay term; model predictions as in fig4i-model-runchosen. Reproduced when, under one reading, the slope is negative with CI excluding 0 inside [-0.11, -0.07] and every model's R_chosen:Stay coefficient is negative; partially reproduced when the data slope holds outside its interval.

claims.statement: On switch trials BIfp, BRLfwr and RLCF predict a positive effect of past rewards at the other port on the RPE, while the other RL models predict little or none.
claims.source: Results, Predictions from BRLfwr and BIfp, paragraph 8; Fig 4I right
claims.quote: On animal switch trials, both BIfp, BRLfwr, and RLCF predicted a positive effect of R_unchosen, but other RL models predicted little to no effect
claims.criterion: Model RPEs regressed with the fixed part of the fig4i-lmer-switch formula by OLS, without subject effects (Methods, Linear mixed effects modeling). The Methods speak of model simulated data with a uniform sample size per simulated session; readings (a) the code's generate with each mouse's fitted parameters, one simulated session per real session of the same length, on 7 to 23 or 8 to 15 reward blocks; (b) RPEs of the models run on the mice's own trials. "Little to no effect" is read as not significantly positive at p < 0.05, or below half the smallest of the three positive coefficients. Reproduced when, under every reading, the R_unchosen:Switch coefficient is positive with p < 0.05 for BIfp, BRLfwr and RLCF and "little to no" for RL4p, RLFQ3p, RL_meta and PearceHall.

claims.statement: Dopamine results are qualitatively consistent across animals; per-animal regressions on switch trials resemble the Bayesian model predictions in all but one animal, and switch-stay differences in outcome responses are consistent across animals.
claims.source: S5 Fig legend
claims.quote: All but one animal showed a strong qualitative resemblance to Bayesian model predictions for Switch trials
claims.criterion: Per animal, OLS with the fixed part of the fig4i-lmer-switch formula. Read as resemblance when the R_chosen:Switch coefficient is negative and R_unchosen:Switch is positive, the sign pattern BRLfwr and BIfp predict. Reproduced when 4 of the 5 animals show it and, in at least 4 animals, mean DA-PT of rewarded switch trials exceeds rewarded stay trials and unrewarded stay trials are below unrewarded switch trials (S5 Fig A); partially reproduced when 3 animals show the regression pattern.

claims.statement: Only 94 trials start a reward, switch, reward sequence, out of 30,707 trials.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Yet in our dataset, there are only 94 trials initiating such sequences out of 30,707 trials in total
claims.criterion: A trial rewarded at one port followed, in the same session, by a choice of the other port that is rewarded. Readings of the trial set (a) the 34 sessions with valid recordings (20,952 is about 68% of 30,707, which fits this), (b) all recorded sessions, (c) all 70 sessions. Reproduced when, under one reading, both counts are within tolerance.

claims.statement: In cross-validated R2 of dopamine regressions, the 3R+Sw feature set (Reward, R_chosen and R_unchosen, each split by switch and stay trials) captures a similar level of variance to L0:R, the standard set of trial-back choice and reward interactions; 4 lags were used at the expense of about 1% of variance explained.
claims.source: S4 Fig legend; Methods, Linear mixed effects modeling
claims.quote: Together we found that 3R+Sw was enough to capture similar levels of variance compared to L0:R. We used 4 lags because it allows us to capture a relatively high amount of past outcome levels, with only the expense of 1% variance explained
claims.criterion: Cleaned trials, DA-PT as the output (the legend keeps dopamine as the output variable). Feature sets from the S4 Fig legend, L0:R (choice, reward and their interaction for each trial back) and 3R+Sw (the fixed part of the fig4i-lmer-switch formula). Not given (the regression type, the cross-validation scheme, the lags compared, and what the 1% is measured against); readings (a) OLS with the 70-30 splits of fig4f-bayesian-rpe-fit, (b) the LMER of fig4i-lmer-switch with the same splits; lags 1 to 8. Read "similar" as a cross-validated R2 of 3R+Sw at 4 lags within 0.01 of L0:R at 4 lags, and the 1% as the R2 of 3R+Sw at 4 lags within 0.01 of its best over lags, or of L0:R's best. Reproduced when both hold under every reading; partially reproduced when the first holds. All R2 values are shown.

claims.statement: The recordings comprise 13 ephys sessions and 6 behaviour-only sessions, one per animal, with the numbers of accepted single units and of trials per animal listed in Table S1, and with the units and OL turn trials of the example sessions given in Fig. 1J-K and Fig. S4.
claims.source: SI Appendix, Table S1; Fig. 1J-K legend; Fig. S4 legend
claims.criterion: Unit counts are single units that passed the acceptance criteria (Table S1 footnote; SI Spike sorting and unit filtering) and must match exactly, as must the OL_L plus OL_R counts of Fig. 1J-K and Fig. S4, which the legends give per turn type (489 266 and 265; 503 305 and 304; 528 95 and 95; 530 402 and 403; 482 350 and 350; 480 185 and 190; 517 270 and 268); the per-type counts are compared as well. Table S1 trials are "Total number of trials including CL straight, randomzied left and right turns" and are matched within 10%. Reproduced when every unit count and every OL count matches and at least 17 of the 19 total trial counts are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the unit counts match for at least 10 of the 13 ephys animals. The notes list each mismatch and the inconsistencies the header names.

claims.statement: In the C2 principal barrel column, population spiking across all layers is strongly and synchronously modulated during OL turns, in five consecutive epochs (stable spiking, a sharp peak, suppression, a ramp for contralateral turns, and a return to stable spiking).
claims.source: Results, Population dynamics in C2 barrel column..., paragraph 2; Fig. 1J-O
claims.quote: Spiking activity across all cortical layers is strongly modulated during navigation decisions and can roughly be divided into five consecutive epochs
claims.criterion: Animal 489, all units, population-averaged spike rate (header) over the 266 OL_L trials and, separately, the 265 OL_R trials. Reproduced when, for OL_L, the rate shows in order a peak between 0 and 0.065 s above the epoch 1 mean (the paper gives only t < 0; readings -1 to 0 s and -0.5 to 0 s, as in fig1n-epoch-rates), a minimum between 0.065 and 0.14 s below the epoch 1 mean, a maximum between 0.12 and 0.3 s above the epoch 1 mean, and a mean rate from 0.5 to 1.8 s that is below that maximum; and, for OL_R, the same epoch 2 peak and epoch 3 suppression. Each "above" or "below" is judged by a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test over units at p < 0.05 on per-unit trial-averaged rates in the two windows (the paper gives no test; the windows are the paper's, the test is this file's). Partially reproduced when the OL_L sequence holds but one OL_R part fails.

claims.statement: For animal 489, the population rate is about 2 Hz during straight running before the turn, peaks sharply at t = 0.026 s (epoch 2), drops to about 0.7 Hz (epoch 3) for both turn directions, and, for contralateral turns only, ramps to a maximum at about t = 0.25 s (epoch 4); for ipsilateral turns the suppression lasts to the end of the turn.
claims.source: Results, Population dynamics in C2 barrel column..., paragraph 2; Fig. 1N
claims.quote: the stable spiking (t < 0 s, 2 ± 0.1 Hz, mean ± SD) of epoch 1 during CL straight running is disrupted by a sharp peak we refer as epoch 2 (t = 0.026 s) ... Epoch 3 follows, which exhibits strong suppression of spiking activity down to 0.7 ± 0.1 Hz (mean ± SD) for both left and right turns ... While for ipsilateral turns the suppression lasts until the turn end ... contralateral turns produce a strong ramping activity labeled as epoch 4, (t = 0.25 s
claims.criterion: Animal 489, population-averaged rate in Hz (header), OL_L and OL_R separately. Tolerances are the paper's stated spread for the rates, one 5 ms bin for the epoch 2 peak time (10% of 0.026 s is smaller than the bin), and 10% for the epoch 4 time. The epoch 1 window is not given beyond t < 0; readings (a) -0.5 to 0 s and (b) -1 to 0 s. Epoch 2 peak is the maximum bin between 0 and 0.065 s; epoch 3 minimum is the minimum bin between 0.065 and 0.14 s (both windows from the Results); the epoch 4 maximum is the maximum bin between 0.12 and 0.5 s of OL_L. The rates must hold for both turn types where the paper says so. Smoothing is not named by the SI; the main reading is unsmoothed 5 ms bins, and because a single-bin minimum or maximum depends on noise, a variant with the rates averaged over three bins is shown. Reproduced when all four values match under some epoch 1 reading and the OL_R rate between 0.14 and 1.8 s has no maximum above the epoch 1 mean (suppression to the turn end).

claims.statement: All five epochs dominate the activity of every one of the 65 simultaneously recorded units of animal 489, reproducibly across 531 randomized trials with a jitter of about 30 ms.
claims.source: Results, Population dynamics in C2 barrel column..., paragraph 2; Fig. 1J-K; Fig. S5
claims.quote: all five epochs are major features that dominate the activity for all 65 simultaneously recorded units ... highly reproducible across 531 randomized trials with jitter of just 30 ms
claims.criterion: Animal 489, z-scored trial-averaged rate per unit (SI Spike rates, Fig. 1J-K) over OL_L trials. The paper gives no per-unit test and no definition of jitter; both are open. For the units, readings (a) the unit's trial-averaged rate is lower in the epoch 3 window (0.065 to 0.14 s) than in epoch 1 (-1 to 0 s) and higher at its maximum in 0.12 to 0.3 s than in the epoch 3 window, as signs only; (b) the same two differences tested over trials by a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test at p < 0.05. The unit part is reproduced when at least 90% of the 65 units show both under a reading ("all", with a 10% margin), partially reproduced when a majority do. For jitter, readings (a) the SD over trials of the time of the population epoch 2 peak (maximum of the trial's summed spike count, 5 ms bins, 0 to 0.065 s); (b) the SD over trials of the time of the epoch 4 maximum (0.12 to 0.5 s); jitter is reported under both and holds when either is within 10% of 30 ms. The outcome is the unit part; jitter is reported in the notes. When the unit readings disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: For animal 489 the linear slope of the epoch 4 ramp in contralateral (OL_L) trials is 12.25 (12.25 ± 0.88, mean ± SEM, in Fig. 4B; 12.25 ± 0.76 in Fig. 1N).
claims.source: Results, Ramping neural activity reflects temporal accumulation..., paragraph 2; Fig. 4B bottom; Discussion, paragraph 2; Fig. 1N
claims.quote: This is noticeably close to the linear slope of ramping peak 4 of 12.25 ± 0.88 (mean ± SEM)
claims.criterion: Animal 489, 266 OL_L trials, population-averaged rate (header), linear regression of rate on time over the ramp. The paper does not give the slope's units, the fit window or the normalisation range, so readings are named. Rate units (a) min-max normalised to 0 and 1 (SI Spike rates, "For comparison with DDM results (Fig.4B ...) ... normalized"), per second; (b) Hz per second (Fig. 1N plots the unnormalised rate and its triangle gives the same slope). Fit window (c) 0.12 to 0.17 s (start and end of linear ramping in Fig. 4F, SI Analysis of VarCE); (d) 0.12 to 0.18 s (Fig. 4G arrows, SI); (e) 0.12 s to the epoch 4 maximum (0.25 s in Fig. 1N). Normalisation range, for (a), the minimum and maximum over 0 to 1 s (the Fig. 1N window) and over 0 to 1.8 s; these coincide unless the extremes fall after 1 s, and both are shown. The SEM is the regression's standard error. The tolerance is the paper's SEM. The claim is reproduced when the slope matches under any reading; the notebook shows all.

claims.statement: At the end of the turn, when the contralateral wall moves back out at t = 1.8 s, the contralateral population shows a peak (2'), a longer suppression with ramp onset at t = 2.0 s, and a slower ramp (4') that peaks at t = 2.58 s with a slope of 2.05, about 7 times smaller than the slope of the first ramp.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 2; Fig. 1O; Results, Stages of decision-making..., paragraph 2
claims.quote: Epoch 3′ suppression is significantly longer with the onset of ramping activity at t = 2.0 s (0.21 s delay) suggesting regulation of integration onset to task demand. Ramping in epoch 4′ is much slower reaching maximum at t = 2.58 s (0.78 s delay). The fitted linear slope (2.05 ± 0.05, mean ± SEM, black triangle in Fig. 1O ) is 7× smaller than for the first turn at trial start (12.25 ± 0.76, mean ± SEM, triangle Fig. 1N )
claims.criterion: Animal 489, OL_L population-averaged rate (header) over the last 1.4 s of the trial (Fig. 1O, from about 1.6 to 3.0 s; the window's end is not given, readings end at 3.0 s and at 3.2 s). Epoch 2' peak is the maximum bin from 1.8 to 1.9 s (paper 1.84 s, tolerance two bins); ramp onset is not defined by the paper and takes the two readings of fig4b-ddm-matches-ramp applied between the 2' peak and the 4' maximum (tolerance 10% of the 0.21 s delay); the 4' maximum is the maximum bin from 2.0 to 3.0 s (tolerance 10% of the 0.78 s delay). The slope uses the readings of fig1n-ramp-slope for units, with the fit window from the 4' onset to the 4' maximum, the only window the text gives; the tolerance is the paper's SEM. The ratio uses the first-ramp slope under the same reading. Also reported, from the same section of the Results, the time of the OL_R 2' peak (paper 2.15 s). Reproduced when the times and the slope ratio match under one reading; the absolute slope is reported and judged as well.

claims.statement: The ramps of epochs 4 and 4' appear only in contralateral (OL_L) turns, while the epoch 2 and 2' peaks appear for both turn directions, showing strong lateralization.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 5; Fig. 1J-O; Fig. 5C-D
claims.quote: While epochs 2 (at trial start) and 2′ (at trial end) are present for both left and right turns, the ramping in epochs 4 and 4′ is exclusively presented only for contralateral left turn trials indicating extraordinarily strong lateralization
claims.criterion: For each ephys animal in Fig. 5C-D (480, 489, 503, 528, 482, 517, 530; Table S1), the population-averaged rate (header) in OL_L and OL_R trials. Epoch 4 size is the mean rate from 0.12 to 0.25 s minus the mean rate from 0.065 to 0.12 s (end of suppression), and epoch 4' size the mean rate from 2.0 to 2.58 s minus that from 1.9 to 2.0 s (windows from the times the paper gives for animal 489). Per animal, the OL_L size is compared with the OL_R size by a two-sided Mann-Whitney test over trials of the per-trial window means (the paper gives no test; this is the test of this file). Reproduced when epoch 4 is larger for OL_L in every animal at p < 0.05 and in at least 5 of 7 for epoch 4'; partially reproduced when epoch 4 holds in at least 5 of 7. Epoch 2 and 2' peaks for both directions are reported.

claims.statement: Mice run at fast speeds, 21 ± 4 cm/s (mean ± SD).
claims.source: Results, Ethological decision-making..., paragraph 1; SI Fig. S1A; SI Animal preparation
claims.quote: running at fast speeds (21 ± 4 cm/s, mean ± SD
claims.criterion: Speed is the absolute speed of the sphere, from forward and lateral velocities. The paper cites Fig. S1A, the speed histogram of animal 503 in the 481-trial experiment of Fig. 2A, while Table S1 gives animal 503 a mean running speed of 16.1 cm/s; the population it refers to is open. Readings (a) animal 503, mean over samples of the session's absolute speed; (b) the same restricted to running, mean trial speed above 10 cm/s (Table S1 footnote); (c) across all 19 animals, the mean of the per-animal mean running speeds (Table S1 definition); the per-animal values are also compared with Table S1's mean speeds (10% each). The SI (Animal preparation) gives the same 21 ± 4 cm/s for a mouse on habituation day 3, running above 10 cm/s; reading (d), habituation sessions, applies only if the dataset holds them, and the author says whether it does. Reproduced when the mean lies within 4 cm/s of 21 under any reading.

claims.statement: In the unrewarded task, with a correct trial defined as ±1 cm lateral clearance at t = 1 s, animal 503 succeeds in 95% of 414 randomized turn trials (14 failed trajectories).
claims.source: Results, Behavioral correlates of decision-making..., paragraph 1; Fig. 2A
claims.quote: Defining threshold for correct trials as ±1 cm lateral clearance at t = 1 s, the success rate reaches 95% (14 failed red trajectories in Fig. 2A
claims.criterion: Animal 503, OL_L and OL_R trials, lateral position integrated from the sphere's lateral velocity. Open details and readings. The zero of lateral position is not given; readings (e) relative to the position at t = 0; (f) the readings of fig2b-lateral-spread (Fig. 2B puts the t = 0 mean at 0.14 cm, so these differ little). Which 414 trials (animal 503 has 609 OL trials in Fig. S4A and Fig. S7) is not said; readings (a) all OL trials; (b) the first 414 consecutive OL trials ("414 consecutive randomized left and right turn trials"). What "±1 cm clearance" means is not defined; readings (c) displacement at t = 1 s of at least 1 cm in the turn direction (left for OL_L); (d) absolute displacement of at least 1 cm, the deviation rule of Fig. S1B. Reproduced when the success rate is within 10% of 0.95 under any reading; the number of failed trials is reported for each.

claims.statement: Lateral positions are tightly confined during the straight CL section (0.14 ± 0.55 cm, mean ± SD, at t = 0) and their distribution widens over time after the turn (t = 1 s and 3 s), about twice as wide at 3 s as at 2 s (SD 2.30 against 1.49).
claims.source: Results, Behavioral correlates of decision-making..., paragraph 1; Fig. 2B; Discussion, paragraph 2; Fig. S6B
claims.quote: While the straight CL section produces trajectories tightly confined within 0.14 cm ± 0.55 (mean ± SD) ... distributions of lateral distances after the turn widen over time ... (2.30 SD at 3 s trial time vs. 1.49 SD at 2 s time for Fig. 2 B , Top , and SI Appendix , Fig. S6 B , Top )
claims.criterion: Animal 503 (Fig. 2B), and animal 489 for Fig. S6B. Lateral distance is not defined beyond Fig. 2B; since the values at t = 0 are not zero, it is not relative to t = 0. Readings (a) the lateral position as the dataset stores it; (b) lateral velocity integrated from the start of the trial's CL section. The SD at 2 s and 3 s are attributed jointly to Fig. 2B top (animal 503, t = 3 s) and Fig. S6B top (animal 489, t = 2 s); readings (c) 2.30 for animal 503 at 3 s and 1.49 for animal 489 at 2 s; (d) both values for animal 503; (e) both for animal 489. Units are taken as cm. The widening holds when the SD rises from t = 0 to 1 s to 3 s. Reproduced when the t = 0 values and the widening hold and the 2 s and 3 s SDs match under one reading; partially reproduced when only the t = 0 values and the widening hold.

claims.statement: The success rate rises steeply as the approaching wall comes closer to the snout, from 8 mm (whisker barely touching) to 1 mm (whisker strongly bent).
claims.source: Results, Behavioral correlates of decision-making..., paragraph 1; Fig. 2C; Fig. S6E-G
claims.quote: The resulting success rate as a function of wall distance ( Fig. 2C ) exhibits a strong increase toward shorter distances
claims.criterion: Behaviour-only psychometric animals of Table S1 (474, 475, 499, 518); the text says n = 7 and the legend n = 5, so any other animal whose session varies the OL wall distance is also used and listed. Per animal and turn direction, success fraction (correct as in fig2a-success-rate, both readings of "±1 cm clearance") at each wall distance with at least 20 trials (Fig. 2C legend). Reproduced when the population average (mean over animals) has a negative Spearman correlation with distance and the average at the two shortest distances exceeds that at the two longest in at least 3 of 4 animals; the paper reports no test and this rule is this file's.

claims.statement: Turns are steeper (larger mean turn angle) when the wall comes closer.
claims.source: Results, Behavioral correlates of decision-making..., paragraph 1; Fig. 2D
claims.quote: Better threshold clearance is achieved by steeper turn angles ( Fig. 2D ) at closer wall distances
claims.criterion: Same animals and trials as fig2c-psychometric. Turn angle is the run angle of Eq. 1, theta = atan(D_lat/D_for), positive for left turns (SI Behavioral tactile virtual reality rig); turns to the right are sign-flipped. How the "mean turn angle" of a trial is taken is not given; readings (a) the mean of theta over the turn, 0 to 1.8 s; (b) the angle of the displacement from t = 0 to t = 1 s, atan of lateral over forward displacement. Reproduced when the population-average angle has a negative Spearman correlation with wall distance under either reading.

claims.statement: During straight CL running the C2 whisker whisks at 15 ± 2 Hz with an amplitude of 39 ± 5 degrees around a set point of 58 ± 5 degrees; once the wall is close (t > 0.2 s) the whisker angle is clamped at 68 ± 12 degrees.
claims.source: Results, Behavioral correlates of decision-making..., paragraph 2; Fig. 2E-F
claims.quote: Whisking during CL straight run (t < 0) is executed at 15 ± 2 Hz (mean ± SD) with an amplitude of just 39 ± 5° (mean ± SD) around a set point of 58 ± 5° (mean ± SD) ... (whisker angle clamped at 68° ± 12 (mean ± SD) for t > 0.2 s
claims.criterion: Contralateral (right) C2 whisker angle, 0 degrees perpendicular to the head's AP axis, from the two tracked points nearest the base (SI Whisker tracking), in OL_L trials of the whisker-tracking animal of Fig. 2E-F (573 per Table S1; 589 also has whisker tracking and is shown as a variant). Phase and amplitude from the Hilbert transform (SI Multiparameter GLM); set point is not defined, readings (a) the slowly varying mean of the angle (mean per whisk cycle); (b) the mean angle over t < 0. Frequency is the inverse cycle duration. Window for the CL values is t < 0 within the trial (-1 to 0 s, open); clamped angle is the mean angle for t from 0.2 to 1.8 s. Tolerances are the paper's SD. Reproduced when all four means fall within tolerance under one set-point reading.

claims.statement: The choice period lasts 0.32 s, between the mean first whisker touch of the approaching wall (0.06 ± 0.03 s) and the mean reaction time defined by the stereotypic hind-leg push (0.38 ± 0.07 s).
claims.source: Results, Behavioral correlates of decision-making..., paragraph 3; Fig. 2I
claims.quote: Corresponding time histograms for FT and RT ( Fig. 2I ) indicate the choice period of 0.32 s between the mean FT (0.06 ± 0.03 s, mean ± SD) and mean RT (0.38 ± 0.07 s, mean ± SD)
claims.criterion: Animal of Fig. 2I. Table S1 assigns Fig. 2I to both 573 ("2EFI") and 480 ("2IL"); readings (g) 573, (h) 480, (i) both pooled; OL_L trials. FT is the first whisker-wall touch after t = 0 to the approaching wall (Fig. 2F; Fig. 3Q); touches of the retracting wall in the first 11 ms (Fig. 3P) are excluded, reading (a), or not, reading (b). RT is the time of the largest peak of the lateral acceleration after t = 0 (SI Fitting of drift diffusion models), in the turn direction (positive for left turns, Fig. 2H). Open details and readings. The signal, (c) the derivative of the run angle theta of Eq. 1, (d) the derivative of the lateral velocity (the SI treats these as the same); the search window, (e) 0 to 1 s, (f) 0 to 1.8 s (the turn). Tolerances are the paper's SD for FT and RT, 10% for the choice period (mean RT minus mean FT). Reproduced when all three match under one combination. RT under the same readings is also reported for every ephys animal, for use by fig4-ddm-fit.

claims.statement: During straight CL running, over 80% of units encode more than one behavioural or sensory variable (whisking kinetics and kinematics, speed, gait), and the wall feedback signal V_wall is among the strongest encoded variables.
claims.source: Results, Stages of decision-making..., paragraph 2; Fig. 2J-K; SI Multiparameter GLM regression
claims.quote: In fact, multidimensional tuning is characteristic for the majority of population (over 80% of units, Fig. 2K ) ... Unsurprisingly, among the strongest correlations is the feedback signal V wall
claims.criterion: Animal 579 (Table S1, "2JK"). Poisson GLM with exponential link (SI Eq. 3). The SI gives "13 regressors" and then says V_wall (Eq. 2) was "additionally" included; Fig. S12A shows 13 variables. The SI names whisking phase and amplitude (Hilbert transform of the angle), run angle derivative (lateral acceleration), RH and LH leg push times, forward and absolute speed, run angle and lateral speed; the Results (Fig. 2K) add set angle, curvature and its derivative. These are 12 variables plus V_wall; whether a 13th variable exists, and which, is open, and the fit uses the 12 named plus V_wall. The same 3 s segment of 40 randomly chosen CL trials (SI; the Fig. 2J legend says 55 trials, a reading); spikes in 20 ms bins smoothed with a Savitzky-Golay filter; five-fold cross-validation with ridge regularisation; for each variable, the log likelihood ratio of full against reduced model averaged over the five folds, referred to a chi-squared distribution with 1 degree of freedom. Open details. The Savitzky-Golay window and order, the ridge penalty, the regressor lags or bases, which 3 s segment, and the significance threshold for "encoding" are not given; readings for the threshold are p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, and for the penalty the values a five-fold cross-validated search selects and no penalty. "Among the strongest" is not defined; readings V_wall among the three variables (a) encoded by the most units, (b) with the largest mean log likelihood ratio over units. Reproduced when at least 72% of units encode at least two variables and V_wall is among the strongest under either of these, under all readings; when readings disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: The epoch 2 peaks appear within 10 ms of the first whisker touch, consistent with the afferent delay from follicle to barrel cortex, which marks them as sensory (mismatch) signals.
claims.source: Results, Stages of decision-making..., paragraph 3; Fig. 1N-O; Fig. 2F
claims.quote: In all cases, epoch 2 peaks appear within 10 ms range from FT, which is consistent with the expected afferent delay from whisker follicle to barrel cortex
claims.criterion: Needs, in the same session, spikes and whisker touch times. Per ephys session with whisker touch times, the population epoch 2 peak time (maximum bin from 0 to 0.065 s, OL_L and OL_R) is compared with the mean FT of the same trials (FT as in fig2i-ft-rt, readings (a) and (b)), and in a second reading, the peak of the population rate aligned to each trial's FT. Reproduced when the absolute difference is at most 10 ms in every such session under a reading. The header notes that the paper's own numbers (epoch 2 at 0.026 s, FT at 0.06 to 0.07 s) disagree with this; the notes give the difference either way.

claims.statement: The epoch 4 ramp dominates the response only when the animal is actively running; during brief stops with active whisking the epoch 2 peak dominates and the ramp is absent.
claims.source: Results, Stages of decision-making..., paragraph 4; Fig. 2L
claims.quote: peak 4 activity dominates the modulation only when the animal is actively navigating
claims.criterion: OL_L trials split into sitting, the animal stopped for about 2 s with whisking maintained (Fig. 2L legend, 20 trials), and running (96 trials). The animal is 480 (Table S1, "2IL"); every other ephys animal with at least 10 sitting trials is reported as a variant. Sitting is not defined; readings (a) mean speed below 10 cm/s over -1 to 1 s (Table S1 defines running as above 10 cm/s); (b) mean speed below 10 cm/s over -2 to 0 s. Population-averaged rate (header). Epoch 2 size is the maximum from 0 to 0.065 s and epoch 4 size the maximum from 0.12 to 0.3 s, each minus the epoch 1 mean (-1 to 0 s). Reproduced when, in running trials, epoch 4 exceeds epoch 2, and in sitting trials epoch 2 exceeds epoch 4, in animal 480, under either reading; when readings disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Population activity is high-dimensional during epoch 1 and collapses to a single dimension after first touch during epochs 2 to 4, staying one-dimensional through the choice period and rising again at decision execution and in epoch 5.
claims.source: Results, Stages of decision-making..., paragraph 5; Fig. 2M; SI Dimensionality reduction
claims.quote: confirms the high-dimensional neural coding during epoch 1 that collapses rapidly to just a single dimension following the FT during epochs 2, 3, and 4 ... the neural population remains one-dimensional ( 46 ) during choice period between FT and RT and starts to increase only at the onset of decision execution and later, in epoch 5
claims.criterion: Animal 489 (Table S1, "2M"), OL_L trials. As the SI Dimensionality reduction gives it, spikes in 1 ms bins, smoothed with a 2 ms Gaussian kernel, units below 1 Hz removed, cut in 100 ms segments; for each segment, the matrix of trial-averaged rates (units by 1 ms time points) is analysed by PCA and the number of components that explain 90% of the variance is its dimensionality. Open details and readings. The kernel width as (a) SD of 2 ms or (b) FWHM of 2 ms; the 1 Hz rate taken (c) over the whole session or (d) over the OL_L trial window; PCA on time points as samples and units as variables, centred per unit (the standard method of the cited references). Reproduced when, under all readings, dimensionality is 1 in every segment from 0.1 to 0.3 s and greater than 1 in the epoch 1 segments (-1 to 0 s), and rises above 1 in a segment after 0.4 s; when readings disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Fitted separately to CL straight running and to OL turn decisions, the GLM shows that most units lose during the decision the significant tuning to sensory and behavioural variables they show during straight running (epoch 1).
claims.source: Results, Stages of decision-making..., paragraph 5; SI Fig. S12B-C
claims.quote: When analyzed with reduced GLM (examples in SI Appendix , Fig. S12 B and C ), the majority of units show no significant tuning for both sensory and behavioral variables during decision that they previously exhibited during epoch 1
claims.criterion: The GLM, likelihood ratio test and readings of fig2jk-glm-mixed-tuning, fitted separately to CL straight periods and to OL turn decisions, 100 trials per condition with a 2 s segment from each trial (Fig. S12B legend). Open details and readings. The animal; Table S1 lists Fig. S12 under 589, a behaviour-only animal with no units, and 579, the Fig. 2J-K animal, has 55 trials in all, fewer than 100 per condition; readings (a) 579 with all its CL and OL_L trials, (b) each ephys animal with whisker tracking and at least 100 CL and 100 OL_L trials. Where in each trial the 2 s segment lies is not said; readings (c) OL from t = 0 to 2 s and CL the 2 s straight section before an OL trial's t = 0, (d) OL as in (c) and CL the first 2 s of CL straight trials. Turn direction, OL_L trials (contralateral), and OL_R as a variant. Among units encoding at least one variable in the CL fit, the claim holds when more than half encode none of those variables in the OL fit. The paper gives only examples and no count; the majority rule is the text's "majority of units". Reproduced when it holds under the GLM readings in the animal of reading (a) or in most animals of reading (b); when GLM readings disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: At turn onset the wall retracts to its maximum 12 mm distance within a mean of 11 ms, so most (>80%) first touches are on the approaching wall; during the epoch 3 suppression the wall approaches from 8.7 to 4.4 mm, and it reaches its final 2 mm position at 200 ms.
claims.source: Results, Could the neural activity modulation be explained by simple sensory drive?, paragraphs 2 and 3; Fig. 3A, 3P-Q
claims.quote: The wall retracts very rapidly ( Fig. 3P ), reaching the maximum 12 mm distance at a mean delay as fast as 11 ms. Therefore, the majority (>80%) of first whisker touch (FT) events ( Fig. 3Q ) correspond to whisker palpating approaching ... when the wall is not retracting but fast approaching from 8.7 mm to 4.4 mm ... at a constant speed until the final position of 2 mm is reached at 200 ms
claims.criterion: Approaching-wall position in OL_L trials of the session of Fig. 3A and 3P (50 trials; animal 589, which Table S1 lists for "3ABCD, 3G-P"; 489 is shown as a variant). The FT distribution of Fig. 3Q is from 489 per Table S1 ("3EFQR") but "from the same trials as in O" (589) per its legend; readings 489 and 589. Time of maximum distance per trial, then its mean. Wall distances at 0.065 and 0.14 s are the mean trace at the ends of the epoch 3 window the Results give. FT on the approaching wall means FT after the time of maximum distance in that trial. The fraction holds when above 0.72 (">80%" with a 10% margin). Reproduced when all values match in at least one of the two sessions; the wall values are expected in all sessions and are reported for each.

claims.statement: The whisker touches the wall about 48 ± 4% of the time, in touches of median duration 21 ms; touch probability increases during epoch 4, reaching 90% in epoch 5.
claims.source: Results, Could the neural activity modulation be explained by simple sensory drive?, paragraph 3; Fig. 3B-D, 3M-O
claims.quote: The whisker stays in direct contact with the wall about 48 ± 4% of the time ( Fig. 3C ) with median touch duration of 21 ms ... Whisker touch probability ( Fig. 3C ) increases monotonously during epoch 4, as does mean whisker curvature ( Fig. 3D ), reaching 90% in epoch 5
claims.criterion: Animal 589 (Table S1, "3ABCD"), the 75 OL_L trials of Fig. 3B-C (which 75 is not said; all OL_L trials with touch annotations are used, and the first 75 as a variant). Touch probability is the fraction of trials in contact per 1 ms frame. The 48% is taken during epochs 2 to 3 (0 to 0.14 s, where the paragraph places it; reading a) and over epochs 1 to 3 (reading b); the median duration over all touches in the trials (reading c) and in epochs 2 to 3 (Fig. 3N; reading d); epoch 5 is 0.3 to 1.8 s. The increase in epoch 4 holds when the touch probability averaged over 0.2 to 0.3 s exceeds that over 0.12 to 0.2 s. Reproduced when all hold under one reading.

claims.statement: Across epochs 1, 2-3 and 4-5 the whisker palpates the wall at a constant 15 ± 2 Hz, with statistically identical amplitudes, set angles and per-cycle curvature maxima.
claims.source: Results, Could the neural activity modulation be explained by simple sensory drive?, paragraph 3; Fig. 3I-L
claims.quote: The whisker palpates the wall at a constant 15 ± 2 Hz frequency ( Fig. 3I ), with statistically identical amplitudes ( Fig. 3J ), and set angles ( Fig. 3K ) ... producing periodically modulated curvature with statistically identical maximum per each cycle ( Fig. 3L )
claims.criterion: Animal 589 (Table S1, "3G-P"), 25 OL_L trials (Fig. 3I legend; which 25 is not said, all tracked OL_L trials are used and the first 25 as a variant). Per whisk cycle (Hilbert phase), frequency, amplitude, set angle (cycle mean angle) and maximum curvature, grouped into epoch 1 (t < 0), epochs 2-3 (0 to 0.14 s) and epochs 4-5 (0.14 to 1.8 s). This is a claim of absence judged on the paper's test, two-sample t tests between groups (each pair) at p < 0.05. The samples of the test are not given; readings (a) whisk cycles, (b) per-trial means within each group (n = 25 trials). Reproduced when frequency stays within 15 ± 2 Hz in each group and no amplitude, set angle or curvature comparison is significant; not reproduced when they are, which is what the legends' P < 0.0001 report. The notes give each effect size and say whether the legends' result is what was found.

claims.statement: While sensory input is monotonous during the turn (constant whisking, wall contact rising steadily), neural activity is highly nonstationary (peak, suppression, ramp, return), so the modulation is not explained by simple sensory drive.
claims.source: Results, Could the neural activity modulation be explained by simple sensory drive?, paragraph 3; Fig. 3
claims.quote: However, while sensory input is monotonous, in stark contrast to the “simple sensory drive” hypothesis, the neural activity is highly nonstationary
claims.criterion: An interpretation resting on the claims it depends on. Reproduced when fig1lm-staged-modulation is reproduced and, in fig3c-touch-statistics, touch probability does not decrease from 0.065 to 0.3 s (mean per 10 ms bin is non-decreasing in its linear trend), so that the epoch 3 drop and epoch 4 rise are not matched by a drop and rise of contact. Whisking constancy (fig3ijkl-whisking-across-epochs) is reported, not required.

claims.statement: A classical drift-diffusion model fitted to the reaction-time distribution of animal 489 gives a nondecision time of 0.12 s, drift 2.91, bound 0.59 and noise 0.25 (BIC -664); a generalized DDM with collapsing bounds and leak fits better (BIC -705), with normalized drift K/B of 11.12.
claims.source: Results, Ramping neural activity reflects temporal accumulation..., paragraph 1; Fig. 4B-E; SI Table S2
claims.quote: Fitting classical DDM ( Materials and Methods ) to experimental distribution of RT ( Fig. 4B ) produces best fit (Bayesian information criterion, BIC of −664, Fig. 4C ) for nondecision time (NDT) of 0.12 s ( Fig. 4D ), drift K = 2.91, bound B = 0.59 ( Fig. 4E ), and noise σ = 0.25 ... that produce a better fit (BIC of −705). Normalized drift K/B that defines the time needed to reach the bound in absence of noise and decay is 11.12
claims.criterion: Animal 489 (Fig. 4B; Table S2), OL_L trials; which trials is not said, readings (e) the 266 OL_L trials of Fig. 4B bottom, (f) the 520 OL_L trials whose RT histogram is Fig. S7C-D. RT as in fig2i-ft-rt, correct and error trials as in fig2a-success-rate, fitted with PyDDM (SI Fitting of drift diffusion models). Models as the Results describe them. DDM, constant drift K, constant bounds at ±B, noise sigma, nondecision time; full DDM, adding uniform variability of the starting point X0 and of the nondecision time; GDDM, the DDM with exponentially collapsing bounds and a leaky integrator. Open details. Table S2's parameter list could not be read here, and the paper does not say which parameters were free, the fitting loss, the time step or the RT window. Readings (a) sigma free with K, B and NDT (as the reported sigma = 0.25 implies), PyDDM's default likelihood loss; (b) sigma fixed at 0.25 and the rest free. The RT readings of fig2i-ft-rt are carried. The K/B value is taken from the GDDM under reading (c), from the DDM under reading (d) (the header notes the reported DDM values give 4.93). Reproduced when NDT is within 10% of 0.12 s and the GDDM BIC is lower than the DDM BIC under some reading, and each other value is reported against its tolerance; partially reproduced when only one of these two holds.

claims.statement: The DDM nondecision time (0.12 s) matches the 0.12 s onset of the epoch 4 ramp, and the normalized drift (11.12) is close to the ramp's slope (12.25), so the ramp is consistent with accumulation of evidence to a bound.
claims.source: Results, Ramping neural activity reflects temporal accumulation..., paragraphs 1 and 2; Fig. 4B
claims.quote: appreciable NDT = 0.12 s from both DDM and full DDM ( Fig. 4D ) fits well to the 0.12 s delay of experimentally observed ramping onset at end of epoch 3 for this example animal
claims.criterion: Animal 489. Ramp onset is the end of the epoch 3 suppression in the OL_L population-averaged rate; it is not defined further, readings (a) the time of the minimum between 0.065 s and the epoch 4 maximum; (b) the last bin before the epoch 4 maximum at or below the epoch 3 minimum plus 10% of the range between them. Reproduced when the ramp onset and the DDM nondecision time from fig4-ddm-fit both lie within 0.012 s of 0.12 s and the fitted K/B lies within the 10% tolerance of the ramp slope of fig1n-ramp-slope under the normalised reading; partially reproduced when only the timing agrees.

claims.statement: Across seven animals, the epoch 4 ramp slope is 13.05 ± 4.59 (mean ± SD).
claims.source: Results, Ramping neural activity reflects temporal accumulation..., paragraph 2; Fig. 5E; Fig. S9
claims.quote: (other examples in SI Appendix , Fig. S9 and Fig. 5E below, n = 7, 13.05 ± 4.59, mean ± SD)
claims.criterion: The seven animals of Fig. 5C-E (480, 489, 503, 528 in C2; 482, 517, 530 in neighbouring barrels; Table S1), OL_L trials, slope per animal under the readings of fig1n-ramp-slope, with the fit window per animal from its own ramp onset (readings of fig4b-ddm-matches-ramp) to (a) its onset plus 0.05 s, (b) plus 0.06 s, (c) its epoch 4 maximum (the windows of 489 carried over by duration; the paper gives no per-animal rule). Fig. 5 uses normalised rates (SI Spike rates), so the normalised reading is the main one. Tolerance is the paper's SD. Reproduced when the mean lies within it under some reading.

claims.statement: For an example high-rate unit (489101), the Fano factor is 0.74 ± 0.04 in epochs 1 and 2 and drops to 0.29 at the epoch 4 peak (t = 0.23 s) as total variance saturates, and its VarCE rises quickly at the start of epoch 4 (0.12 to 0.17 s).
claims.source: Results, Ramping neural activity reflects temporal accumulation..., paragraph 3; Fig. 4F; SI Analysis of VarCE, paragraph 2; Fig. S10A
claims.quote: results in a Fano factor (Fig.S10A, top, black) of 0.74±0.04 (mean ± s.d.). Total variance saturates midway through a strong increase of mean firing rate during ramping that results in a Fano factor dropping down to 0.29 at the peak of epoch 4 at t=0.23s
claims.criterion: Unit 489101 of animal 489, 266 OL_L trials, spike counts in 10 ms bins (SI Analysis of VarCE). Fano factor per bin is variance over mean across trials. The epochs 1 and 2 value is the mean ± SD over bins from -1 to 0.065 s (window open; reading -0.5 to 0.065 s also shown). VarCE = variance minus phi times mean, phi the lowest Fano factor in the trial (SI Eq. 4). Reproduced when the three values match and VarCE averaged over 0.15 to 0.17 s exceeds that over 0.10 to 0.12 s. If the dataset's unit identifiers do not include 489101, the unit is the highest-rate RS unit in L5A or L5B of animal 489 (the paper's description, "an outlier with the highest spiking rate"), and the notes say so.

claims.statement: Population VarCE increases linearly between decision onset (0.12 s) and decision termination (0.18 s), whether computed over all units, without outliers, or on residuals, and then declines to a minimum at t = 0.23 s when the decision is executed.
claims.source: Results, Ramping neural activity reflects temporal accumulation..., paragraph 3; Fig. 4G-I; SI Analysis of VarCE
claims.quote: When VarCE is calculated from residuals ( 5 , 51 ) ( Materials and Methods ), it is similar ( Fig. 4G , black) showing linear increase between decision onset ( Fig. 4G , up arrow) and decision termination ( Fig. 4G , down arrow) times. VarCE exhibits a fast decline at decision end, reaching minimum at t = 0.23 when the decision is executed
claims.criterion: Animal 489, 266 OL_L trials, 10 ms bins, per-unit VarCE with phi the unit's lowest Fano factor that keeps VarCE positive in the choice period (SI Eq. 4). Population VarCE is the "union" of unit VarCEs (SI); readings (a) sum over units, (b) mean over units. Three versions as the SI gives them; all units; without the four outliers of Fig. 4I (the four units with the largest summed VarCE over the choice period, taken as 0.06 to 0.38 s, mean FT to mean RT of fig2i-ft-rt); and on residuals (each unit's per-bin trial mean subtracted from its counts). The paper gives no test of the increase; the regression rule below is this file's. Reproduced when, in all three versions under a reading, the linear regression of VarCE on time over 0.12 to 0.18 s has a positive slope with p < 0.05 and the VarCE minimum between 0.18 and 0.4 s lies within 0.023 s of 0.23 s; partially reproduced when the increase holds in all three but the minimum's time does not.

claims.statement: The CorCE matrix, computed on residuals, shows correlation rising with time along the diagonal and decaying with time lag along a row, a pattern that disappears when bins are shuffled, as expected for a diffusion process.
claims.source: Results, Ramping neural activity reflects temporal accumulation..., paragraph 4; Fig. 4J; Fig. S10C
claims.quote: The calculated ( Materials and Methods ) CorCE matrix ( Fig. 4J ) indeed exhibits characteristic increase of correlation as a function of time and, for given time (e.g., along the top row), shows sequential decay as often observed ( 5 , 51 ) during decision-making. This correlation disappears when bins are randomly shuffled
claims.criterion: Animal 489, OL_L trials, residual spike counts in 10 ms bins (SI Analysis of VarCE and CorCE, SI Eq. 6), covariance of conditional expectation across bins with VarCE on the diagonal, normalised to correlation. The bins of the matrix are not given; readings (a) 0.12 to 0.18 s (the ramp's VarCE window); (b) 0.06 to 0.38 s (the choice period, mean FT to mean RT). How units are combined is not given; readings (c) residuals summed over units per trial; (d) per-unit matrices averaged. The paper gives no test or shuffle count; the trend measures, the 100 shuffles and the ±0.2 bound below are this file's. Reproduced when, under a reading, the diagonal's linear trend is positive, the top row's correlation decreases with lag (negative Spearman correlation), and in 100 shuffles of bin order within trials (seeded) the top-row trend is gone (shuffled mean Spearman within ±0.2 of zero).

claims.statement: Trial-by-trial streak index analysis during ramping shows random local spike count fluctuations with close to zero mean (0.06 ± 1.36, mean ± SD), indicating a gradual, not step-like, transition in each trial.
claims.source: Results, Ramping neural activity reflects temporal accumulation..., paragraph 4; Fig. 4K; SI Streak Index analysis
claims.quote: showed randomness of local spike count fluctuations with close to zero mean (0.06 ± 1.36, mean ± SD, Fig. 4K ), indicated gradual
claims.criterion: Animal 489, OL_L trials. The SI gives 8 successive 5 ms bins, counts compared with the across-trial median per bin, 1 above and 0 below, and the number of 0-1 switches per trial. Open details and readings. The statistic, (a) the switch count as the SI describes it, which cannot have a mean near zero; (b) the z-scored runs statistic of the cited methods (observed number of runs minus its expectation under randomness, over its SD, Wald-Wolfowitz). Placement of the 40 ms window during the ramp, (c) 0.12 to 0.16 s; (d) 0.14 to 0.18 s. Counts, (e) all units summed per trial ("from all layers combined", SI); (f) per unit and trial ("all units across all trials", Fig. 4K legend). Ties with the median, (g) assigned 0; (h) bins at the median left out. Reproduced when mean and SD match under some reading; the notes say which.

claims.statement: All epochs, including the suppression and ramp of epochs 3 and 4, are present in layer 4 FS and RS units and in the units of every cortical layer and of each cell class, so the modulation is not confined to a subpopulation.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 3; Fig. 5B
claims.quote: All epochs including epochs 3 and 4 are already present in thalamo-recipient Layer 4 populations of fast spiking (FS, putative inhibitory, Fig. 5 B , Top ) and regular spiking (RS, putative excitatory, Fig. 5 B , Top ) units. They also dominate the activity in subpopulations of all units across different cortical laminae
claims.criterion: Animal 489, OL_L trials, normalised population rate (SI Spike rates) of each subpopulation; layers and FS/RS (waveform duration threshold 0.4 ms, SI) as the dataset labels them, and FS/RS recomputed from waveform duration when durations are available. In each subpopulation (L4 FS, L4 RS, each layer, all FS, all RS), the epoch sequence of fig1lm-staged-modulation is tested on that subpopulation's units. Reproduced when the sequence holds in L4 FS and L4 RS and in at least 6 of the 7 others; the counts are reported against the legend's.

claims.statement: Similar synchronous modulation epochs are seen in the other animals recorded in the C2 principal column (n = 4) and in animals recorded in neighbouring barrel columns of the same or a different row (n = 3).
claims.source: Discussion, paragraphs 3 and 4; Fig. 5C-D; Fig. S4
claims.quote: Similar synchronous modulation is observed for other animals (n = 4, Fig. 5C ) with recordings from principal barrel column ... similar characteristic modulation epochs were observed in animals where recordings were done in a neighboring barrel column in the same or even a different row (n = 3, Fig. 5D )
claims.criterion: Animals 480, 489, 503, 528 (C2) and 482 (B2), 517 (C3), 530 (C1), per Table S1 and Fig. S4, OL_L and OL_R trials; the test of fig1lm-staged-modulation applied per animal. Reproduced when it holds in at least 3 of the 4 principal and 2 of the 3 neighbouring animals; partially reproduced when it holds in at least half of each group.

claims.statement: The delay of the epoch 2 peak, the delay of ramp onset at the end of epoch 3, and the ramp slope do not differ between recordings in the principal C2 column (n = 4) and in neighbouring columns (n = 3).
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 4; Fig. 5E
claims.quote: delay of epoch 2 ( Fig. 5 E , Left ), start of ramping at end of epoch 3 ( Fig. 5 E , Middle ) and the linear slope of ramping activity in epoch 4 ( Fig. 5 E , Right ) shows no statistically significant difference (two-sample t test, P > 0.05) between principal C2 whisker and neighboring barrel columns
claims.criterion: Animals as in fig5cd-other-animals, OL_L trials, normalised population rate. Per animal, epoch 2 delay is the time of the maximum bin from 0 to 0.065 s; ramp onset delay under the readings of fig4b-ddm-matches-ramp; slope under the readings of fig5e-slope-across-animals. A claim of absence on the paper's test. Reproduced when a two-sample t test (equal variances, the default reading of "two-sample t test") of the 4 against the 3 per-animal values gives p > 0.05 for all three measures; not reproduced when any gives p < 0.05. The group means, their difference and Welch's test as a variant are reported. When the measure readings give different outcomes the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: In the adult corpus callosum SRF-cKO mice have a lower percentage of myelinated axons than SRF-Flox littermates (about 22% against about 37%, read from the figure), so the hypomyelination seen in optic nerve persists into adulthood in corpus callosum.
claims.source: Figure 2C; Results, Conditional Knockout of SRF Causes CNS Hypomyelination, paragraph 2
claims.quote: This degree of hypomyelination of SRF-cKO mice persisted into adulthood in both the optic nerve ... and the corpus callosum
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the percent of axons myelinated, from the counts of myelinated and unmyelinated axon objects (SI Methods, Corpus callosum TEM; Figure 2C legend), under the readings O1, O2, O4 and O7 of the opening comment. claims.statement: In acute hippocampal slices, PAGER-Gi-expressing CA1 neurons show a greater hyperpolarizing shift in resting membrane potential with 100 nM DCZ plus 1 uM mCherry than with DCZ alone (mixed linear model, Z = 3.17, P = 0.0015).

claims.quote: Neurons displayed a greater hyperpolarizing shift in RMP when presented with DCZ plus mCherry than with DCZ alone
claims.criterion: Measures from the Methods (Slice electrophysiology). Per sweep, RMP is the mean membrane potential over the 500 ms before any current injection. Rin is the steady-state voltage change to the -100 pA, 200-ms step (step voltage minus that sweep's RMP) divided by -100 pA; the steady-state window is not given, and the readings are the last 50 ms and the last 100 ms of the step. Cells whose initial Rin (first sweep) exceeds 500 megaohms are excluded (the paper prints "mΩ"), and sweeps with RMP above -50 mV or with no action potential during the ramp. Action potential detection is not given; the readings are (A1) an upward crossing of 0 mV and (A2) dV/dt above 20 V/s. The change "upon 2-min DCZ addition" is not defined beyond "before, during and after" the application; the readings are (W1) mean over included sweeps from DCZ onset to 2 min after onset minus the mean over included sweeps before onset, and (W2) mean over included sweeps from onset to the end of the recording minus the same baseline. Onset is the application time the dataset records. The test is a mixed linear model (statsmodels, as the Methods name) with treatment as fixed effect and a random intercept per mouse (Methods, Statistical analysis); the unit is not given, and the readings are (M1) one change per cell and (M2) every included sweep's change from baseline, with cell as a variance component within mouse. Under each combination of readings, the result is reproduced when the DCZ plus mCherry change is more negative than the DCZ change, the treatment effect has p < 0.05, and |Z| is within tolerance; partially reproduced when direction and p < 0.05 hold but |Z| is outside tolerance; not reproduced otherwise. The outcome is the one all combinations give; if they differ, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified with every result shown. Group means and s.e.m. of the change are reported, as the figure plots them.

claims.statement: The rheobase current needed to evoke action potentials increases more with DCZ plus mCherry than with DCZ alone (mixed linear model, Z = 2.60, P = 0.0093).

claims.quote: Similarly, the rheobase current needed to evoke action potentials increased in DCZ plus mCherry neurons, compared with DCZ-only samples
claims.criterion: Rheobase per sweep is the current being delivered when the first action potential of the ramp (-150 to +500 pA over 2 s) is evoked (Methods), read from the recorded stimulus at the time of detection; the ramp formula is shown as a check. Whether the holding current is included is not stated; it cancels in a change if constant, and the author shows whether it is. Exclusions, action potential detection (A1, A2), change windows (W1, W2), the mixed model (M1, M2) and the Rin windows used for the cell exclusion are as in fig4i-rmp. Under each combination, reproduced when the DCZ plus mCherry rheobase change is larger than the DCZ change, p < 0.05, and |Z| within tolerance; partially reproduced when direction and p < 0.05 hold but |Z| is outside tolerance; not reproduced otherwise. The outcome is the one all combinations give; if they differ, blocked as methods_underspecified with every result shown.

claims.statement: PAGER-Gi expression level (mEGFP intensity) is not correlated with baseline rheobase or input resistance, in either group, including in the presence of soluble mCherry.

claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The paper's test is a Pearson correlation (Extended Data Fig. 12 legend) between each cell's mEGFP mean intensity, measured in a freehand soma ROI of a widefield image taken before the recording, and its baseline value, within each group. Under each combination, reproduced when no correlation (rheobase and Rin, each group) has P < 0.05; not reproduced when any does; r and P are reported for all four. If the combinations disagree, blocked as methods_underspecified with every result shown. The ROIs are freehand and not published, so the test uses the per-cell intensities or ROIs the dataset holds.

claims.statement: In penetration M2p6, 24 well-isolated neurons were recorded over about 2,400 um; a group of superficial neurons (1 to 9, over 540 um) had similar shape tuning at both contrasts, and with dark shapes neurons 1 to 9, 14 and 17 had a significant positive Isimilarity with a negative slope, while most other, deeper neurons did not.

For some neurons (Neurons #1-9, #14, and #17), regression lines were characterized by a large positive y-intercept (Isimilarity) significantly different from zero (p < 0.05, solid lines) and a negative slope (Ssimilarity)

claims.statement: In M2p6, neurons 3 and 8, 260 um apart, have tuning similarity 0.82 at both contrasts, while neurons 18 and 19, 80 um apart, have similarity 0.00 (dark) and -0.25 (bright), though both pairs respond over a broad range.

The paper gives the distances between the contacts nearest each neuron's center of mass (Figure 2A legend); the template center-of-mass distance is shown as a variant. The tolerance of the zero value is 0.1, since 10% of zero is no tolerance; 0.1 is 5% of the measure's range of 2. Reproduced when every value is within tolerance; partially reproduced when the 3 and 8 values are and an 18 and 19 value is not, or the reverse.

claims.statement: In M2p6, shape tuning was contrast-invariant (invariance above 0.5) for 19 of the 24 neurons, whatever their Isimilarity.

claims.statement: The CSD shows a current sink taken as layer 4 at about 1,073 um below the most superficial neuron, 53 ms after stimulus onset, in M2p6, and at 570 um, 52 ms, in M1p12, with no other sink deeper in M1p12.

LF downsampled to 1 kHz, mean subtracted, scaled to volts, third-order Butterworth band-pass 0.5 to 100 Hz; the LF after the first stimulus of each trial averaged over trials, Gaussian smoothed over 10 adjacent contacts, second spatial derivative over three neighboring contacts, Gaussian smoothed over 10 contacts again, sign inverted, per column of contacts. OPEN, the Gaussian's width, the column shown, and how the sink is located are not given; the readings are (a) the earliest sink peak after stimulus onset and (b) the largest sink in 0 to 100 ms, each on every column, reproduced when one column under one reading gives all values within tolerance. Depth is relative to the most superficial good unit. Needs the LF signal. OPEN, "no other sinks were evident deeper" in M1p12 has no criterion in the paper (it gives no rule for what counts as a sink); that part is shown as the CSD profile and not judged.

claims.statement: In penetration M1p12, 42 neurons over 2,580 um showed no clustered shape tuning at either contrast; only one neuron had a significant Isimilarity, although most had high contrast invariance of shape tuning.

(1) The coefficient; "the correlation coefficient between shape responses" may be (a) Pearson's r of mean rates over the 120 shapes or (b) the noise-corrected similarity. (2) The contrast; (a) dark, (b) bright, (c) both contrasts as separate pairs. Reproduced when both tests give p < 0.0001 in the stated direction under every reading and all four means are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when the directions and p hold under every reading and no reading matches the means. claims.statement: Tuning similarity computed from orientation x spatial frequency fits (12 Gabor filters) to the shape responses is also diverse among nearby neurons, and its Isimilarity correlates with the Isimilarity from the shape responses (Spearman's r = 0.588, n = 1,848).

claims.criterion: Materials and Methods, Feature models; shape responses fit as a linear weighted sum of the outputs of 12 Gabor filters (4 orientations x 3 spatial frequencies) applied to the shape images; similarity is Pearson's r of fitted responses; Isimilarity as in the opening comment. Needs the shape images (Pasupathy and Connor 2001). OPEN, able to change the result; the filters' spatial frequencies, envelope, phase and pooling, and the fitting method, are not given (the paper cites Portilla and Simoncelli 2000 for the filters and David et al. 2006 for the orientation x SF model). The readings are (a) the energy of each subband of a steerable pyramid with 4 orientations and 3 scales summed over the image, (b) quadrature Gabor energy at 4 orientations and 3 octave-spaced frequencies summed over the image, and (c) the image's Fourier power pooled in 4 orientation x 3 SF bands, as in the spectral model of David et al. 2006, each fit by least squares; with the contrast readings of the opening comment. Reproduced when all readings give r within tolerance and p < 0.0001; blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ in outcome.

claims.statement: Assayed at a coarse scale with two orthogonal orientations of the spindle shape, some penetrations consist entirely of neurons preferring horizontal or vertical, and in others the preference switches along the probe, as with optical imaging, even where single-neuron shape clustering is not extensive.

claims.criterion: Materials and Methods, Feature models; per neuron the AUC between spike counts (30 to 200 ms, per presentation) for shape 1 at 0 and 180 degrees and at 90 and 270 degrees, both contrasts pooled, above 0.5 meaning vertical; averaged over neurons in 100 um depth bins. The examples are M2p6 and M1p5 (Figure 6C, D). The paper defines neither kind of penetration; the plain readings of "entirely" and "switched" are used, not taken from the paper. A penetration is all-one-preference when every occupied bin is on one side of 0.5, and switching when occupied bins lie on both sides, each side in a contiguous run of depth. OPEN which rotation is horizontal depends on the dataset's rotation labels and on shape 1 being the spindle (Figure 1B). Reproduced when at least one penetration of each kind exists among the 74 and M2p6 and M1p5 are each of one kind; the counts of each kind are reported.

claims.statement: Along angular position and curvature separately, clustering of tuning peaks is sparse; of 59 penetrations with at least four neurons well fit by the APC model, only 7 (angular position) and 5 (curvature) show a significant positive correlation between peak difference and distance, and only 9 and 5 sessions have smaller mean and STD of the differences than a permutation null.
claims.source: Results, Tuning for curvature or angular position, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Across 59 penetrations which included at least four neurons well-fit by the angular position × curvature model, only 7 (5) penetrations exhibited statistically significant positive correlation between the ΔAP (ΔCV) and inter-neuron distance (data not shown) ... we found that a minority (nine and five) of sessions exhibited smaller mean and STD than the null distributions (data not shown). These results indicate that evidence for clustered tuning ... is sparse in our dataset
claims.criterion: Materials and Methods, Feature models and Statistical tests; shape responses fit with the 4D APC Gaussian of Pasupathy and Connor (2001) (one angular position Gaussian, three curvature Gaussians for adjoining segments); well fit means goodness of fit r > 0.5 (Figure 7A legend); delta AP is the circular absolute difference of AP peaks (0 to 180 degrees), delta CV the absolute difference of central curvature peaks; per penetration Pearson's r of the difference against inter-neuron distance over all pairs; the permutation null shuffles AP and CV values across penetrations, 1,000 times, and a session counts when its mean and STD are below the one-tailed 95% limit. Needs the shapes' boundary curvature descriptions (Pasupathy and Connor 2001). OPEN, able to change counts; (1) the fitting procedure and which contrast's responses are fit (readings dark, bright, both); (2) "statistically significant positive correlation" as (a) two-sided p < 0.05 with r > 0 or (b) one-sided p < 0.05; (3) "mean and STD" as (a) both below the limit or (b) either. Reproduced when every reading gives a minority of penetrations and sessions (under half of the 59) and one reading puts the counts within tolerance; partially reproduced when the minority holds and no reading matches the counts.

claims.statement: In M2p51, 33 neurons well fit by the APC model show mild clustering of angular position peaks (superficial neurons near 330 degrees, deeper ones near 180), with a significant positive correlation between delta AP and distance (r = 0.407) and none in that direction for curvature (r = -0.109).

This relationship can be visualized by the statistically significant positive correlation between inter-neuron distance and difference in angular position tuning peaks (ΔAP) for all pairs of neurons (Fig. 7B). No such relationship is evident along the curvature dimension (Fig. 7C)
claims.criterion: Method and readings as in apc-peaks-sparse-clustering; M2p51 found as in ex-m2p6-cluster, accepted when its well-fit count is within tolerance. Reproduced when the three values are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when the AP correlation is significantly positive and the CV correlation is not significantly positive, without matching values.

claims.statement: Restricted to the 18 M2 penetrations centered on the V4 gyrus, the percentage of neurons with significant Isimilarity is consistent with the whole population, also when only neurons within about 1,500 um of the most superficial neuron are kept.
claims.source: Results, Penetration trajectory, paragraph 1; Figure 8C
claims.quote: When we restricted our analyses to 18 penetrations centered on the V4 gyrus (Fig. 8B, rectangles), our results were consistent withwhat we observedacross the population (Fig. 8C, compare gray and black dots) ... clusters were sparse even when we restricted our analyses to the superficial cortex in those 18 penetrations, e.g., by considering neurons within ∼1,500 μm of the superficial neuron in each penetration
claims.criterion: The 18 penetrations are those at the eight grid locations away from both meridians (Figure 8B legend), identified in the paper only graphically (Figure 5A diamonds, Figure 8B); the paper lists neither the sessions nor their grid coordinates, so the claim needs the dataset to identify them. The paper reports no test of "consistent"; it compares the 18 by eye with the population of Figure 5C, whose stated result is the ~20% level of pop-asymptote-20-percent. The 18 are judged against that result. Over those of the 18 with more than 30 neurons, the percentage of neurons with significant Isimilarity, under the readings of pop-asymptote-20-percent, is within its tolerance. A two-sided Mann-Whitney test of per-penetration percentages, the 18 against the other 56, is shown as a variant and does not decide. The 1,500 um restriction recomputes Isimilarity on neurons within 1,500 um of depth zero. Reproduced when the rule holds with and without the restriction.

claims.statement: For textures, of 979 neurons in 51 sessions (6 to 83 per penetration), a small subset (207; 18 in M1, 189 in M2) across 34 of 51 penetrations (7 in M1, 27 in M2) showed clustered selectivity, and 16 penetrations had five or more neurons with significant Isimilarity.
claims.source: Results, Population results, texture tuning, paragraph 1; Figure 9A
claims.quote: We studied the responses of 979 neurons across 51 sessions (M1, 17; M2, 34) ... (ranging from 6 to 83 per penetration). As with shape stimuli, we found that a small subset of neurons (207/ 979; M1, 18; M2, 189) across 34/51 (M1, 7; M2, 27) penetrations showed clustered selectivity ... Across the 51 penetrations, 16 penetrations had five or more neurons that exhibited regression lines with statistically significant intercepts (Fig. 9A, asterisks)
claims.criterion: As pop-significant-isimilarity, over the 40 textures with original and contrast-reversed versions in place of dark and bright (contrast readings (a) original, (b) contrast-reversed, (c) either), rotations pooled per texture as the Methods present them (rotation is randomized to remove local orientation). The Methods exclude 48 of 979 neurons with too few reliable similarities. Reproduced when one reading puts the counts within tolerance; partially reproduced when the total and penetration counts are and a per-monkey count is not.

claims.statement: Texture Isimilarity from original and contrast-reversed textures is consistent across neurons (Spearman's r = 0.464, n = 905).
claims.source: Results, Population results, texture tuning, paragraph 1; Figure 9B
claims.quote: Tuning similarity based on both sets of texture data (original and contrast-reversed) was highly consistent (Fig. 9B)
claims.criterion: Reproduced when r is within tolerance with p < 0.0001, under either reliability reading.

claims.statement: For textures as for shapes, the fraction of neurons with a significant intercept levels off at about 20% when many neurons are recorded.
claims.source: Results, Population results, texture tuning, paragraph 1; Figure 10
claims.quote: Our results from texture (Fig. 10, black symbols) are consistent with those from shape (Fig. 10, gray symbols): the fraction of neurons with a significant intercept asymptote to ∼20% when the number of recorded neurons was large
claims.criterion: As pop-asymptote-20-percent, on the texture penetrations, taking more than 30 neurons as "large", the yield the paper uses for shapes. Readings (a) median of per-penetration percentages and (b) pooled percentage. Reproduced when one reading is within tolerance.

claims.statement: In 33 M2 penetrations (723 neurons), Isimilarity computed from responses at each neuron's optimal stimulus position correlates positively with Isimilarity at the aggregate RF center (r = 0.325), so stimulus position and RF scatter do not explain the sparse clusters.
claims.source: Results, Position invariance for shape tuning similarity, paragraph 1; Figure 12B
claims.quote: We found a statistically significant positive correlation between Isimilarity in the RF aggregate center versus RF optimal positions (r = 0.325, p < 0.0001, Fig. 12B). These results provide evidence against the possibility that stimulus position and RF variability contributed to the sparsity of clusters
claims.criterion: Materials and Methods, RF localization, paragraph 2; per neuron the optimal position is the one of the five with the greatest variance-to-mean ratio of mean rates over the 15 shapes; similarity between two neurons uses each neuron's responses at its own optimal position; Isimilarity as in the opening comment. The Results text says the comparison is with "responses to stimuli at the aggregate RF center" of the position test, while the Figure 12B axis says "Isimilarity (shape test)".
