The readings are (a) the center position of the position test and (b) the main shape test with dark shapes (the position test's contrast). Spearman's r as Figure 12B names it. Reproduced when every reading gives a positive r with p < 0.0001 and one gives r within tolerance.

claims.statement: In two example penetrations, the pattern of tuning similarity is the same at all five stimulus positions; a small cluster at every position in M2p9 and none at any position in M2p28.
claims.source: Results, Position invariance for shape tuning similarity, paragraph 1; Figures 11A and 11C
claims.quote: Results from two representative recording sessions are shown in Figure 11A,C, and in both cases, tuning similarity patterns were similar across all five positions
claims.criterion: The paper shows the matrices and gives no measure. Sessions found as in ex-m2p6-cluster, accepted when the neuron counts match Figure 11 (16 in M2p9, 55 in M2p28) within 10%. Similarity matrices over the 15 shapes at each position, as in the opening comment. OPEN, the paper gives no measure of "similar across positions"; neither reading below is taken from the paper. (a) Pearson's r between the reliable off-diagonal similarities at each displaced position and at the center; holds when all eight correlations (four positions, two penetrations) are positive with p < 0.05. (b) The paper's own cluster measure, Isimilarity (opening comment) at each position; holds when M2p9 has two or more neurons with significant positive Isimilarity at every position and M2p28 has at most one at every position (M1p12, with one such neuron, is the paper's example of no cluster). Reproduced when both readings hold; blocked as methods_underspecified when they differ.

claims.statement: Simulated oblique penetrations through gradual tuning progressions in angular position and curvature give similarity matrices unlike the V4 data, while random tuning peaks interleaved with short stretches of similar tuning reproduce the observed localized clusters.
claims.source: Results, Simulation of tuning progression, paragraph 1; Figure 13
claims.quote: The resulting similarity matrices (Fig. 13A-C, bottom panels) were quite unlike our V4 data (compare with Figs. 3, 4). Random choice of tuning peaks in the APC space produced similarity matrices reminiscent of the majority of V4 data ... the observed patterns correspond best to random selectivity interspersed with small domains of similar tuning for shapes
claims.criterion: A simulation, not a test on recorded data, judged by eye in the paper. Its parameters are partly given (30 model neurons, 2D Gaussian tuning in APC space with SDs drawn from normal distributions of mean 60 degrees, SD 10, and mean 0.5, SD 0.1; Poisson spike counts; three repeats in the Figure 13 legend, 200 ms trains in the Methods); peak amplitudes and the progression step sizes are not. Recorded so the finding is covered; it cannot be tested on the dataset.

claims.statement: After each reward switch, every switch mouse improved its anticipatory licking before the new reward zone and kept that precise licking, as measured by the anticipatory lick ratio over blocks of ten trials.
claims.source: Results, Monitoring neural activity during a reward learning task, paragraph 2; Figure 1h
claims.quote: All mice improved and retained precise licking preceding the new reward zone (Fig. 1h ; n = 11 mice), demonstrating accurate spatial learning and memory
claims.criterion: The anticipatory lick ratio as the Methods define it (Quantification of licking behavior), (lick in - lick out)/(lick in + lick out), lick in being the mean lick rate in the 50 cm before the reward zone start and lick out the mean rate outside that zone and the reward zone, licks binned in 10 cm bins and divided by occupancy, trials with sensor errors (more than 30% of frames with a cumulative lick count above 2) removed; computed per trial and averaged over blocks of ten trials within each reward zone, as Fig1_Ext1.md:474-690 and behavior.py:876-951 do (np.array_split into ceil(n/10) blocks). The paper reports no test and does not say what "improved" is measured against. Readings (a) for each mouse and each switch day, the mean ratio of the last block after the switch exceeds that of the first block after the switch; (b) for each mouse, the mean over its switch days of (last block after minus first block after) is positive. Reproduced when all 11 mice improve under a reading and, for "retained", each mouse's mean ratio over the first block of the day after each switch day (a stay day, or the next switch day's pre-switch trials) is above 0. Partially reproduced when 9 or 10 mice meet it.

claims.statement: On switch days, 459 +/- 263 of 954 +/- 453 imaged cells per session were place cells, 48.5 +/- 14.5% (mean +/- s.d. across 11 mice and seven switch sessions).
claims.source: Results, Moving reward induced remapping spanning the environment, paragraph 1
claims.quote: we identified place cells as cells with significant spatial information (SI) either before or after the reward switch (means ± s.d. across 11 mice, seven switch sessions... 459 ± 263 place cells out of 954 ± 453 cells imaged; 48.5 ± 14.5% identified as place cells)
claims.criterion: Place cells as the Methods define them (Place cell identification), from deconvolved activity in 45 bins of 10 cm at speed of 2 cm/s or more, SI as the Methods' formula, 100 shuffles per cell circularly shifting position against activity independently on each trial by ~1 s to the trial length, significant when the cell's SI exceeds 95% of the shuffled SI of all cells of the animal in that session and trial set pooled (code, spatial.py:39-56 and 1260-1289, make_multi_anim_sess.md:79-141), in trial set 1 or 2. Putative interneurons excluded first. Means over the 77 mouse and switch-day sessions. The values match when the three means are within tolerance. The paper's "means +/- s.d. across 11 mice, seven switch sessions" can also be read as the mean over mice of per-mouse means; that reading is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: After a switch within an environment, 21.4 +/- 7.9% of place cells kept a field at the same track position (track-relative, TR), 11.2 +/- 7.0% lost their field (disappearing), 6.8 +/- 4.0% gained one (appearing), 4.8 +/- 3.3% followed the reward within 50 cm of both zone starts (remap near reward) and 15.6 +/- 3.6% remapped with fields far from reward (remap far from reward).
claims.source: Results, Moving reward induced remapping spanning the environment, paragraph 1; Figure 2a; Extended Data Fig. 2a-d
claims.quote: a subset of place cells maintained a stable field at the same track location (‘track-relative’ (TR) cells, 21.4 ± 7.9% of place cells, mean ± s.d. across six switches within environment, 11 mice ... We observed cells with place fields that disappeared (‘disappearing’; 11.2 ± 7.0%), appeared (‘appearing’; 6.8 ± 4.0%) or precisely followed the reward location ... (‘remap near reward’; 4.8 ± 3.3%) ... (‘remap far from reward’; 15.6 ± 3.6%
claims.criterion: Categories as the Methods define them (Remapping category definitions) on the six within-environment switch days (3, 5, 7, 10, 12, 14; the code takes day != 8, Fig2_Ext2_identifyRewardRelative.md:365-408), over place cells, with spatial peaks from the trial-averaged unsmoothed binned dF/F (Spatial peak firing identification). TR, significant SI before and after, peaks no more than 50 cm apart; disappearing, significant before only, mean binned dF/F after below the 50th percentile of the per-trial mean dF/F before; appearing, significant after only, mean after above the mean before plus one s.d. of the per-trial means; near reward, significant before and after, both peaks within 50 cm of their zone starts; far, significant before and after, not TR, a peak more than 50 cm from at least one zone start. The Methods remove RR cells (claim rr-cell-fractions) from the appearing and disappearing groups only; the code removes them from every category (dayData.py:2156, exclude_rr_from_others=True). Readings (a) the Methods' removal, (b) the code's. The values match under a reading when all five are within tolerance.

claims.statement: A reward switch within a constant environment induced more remapping than a stay day with a fixed reward and environment, and less than a reward switch combined with a novel environment.
claims.source: Results, Moving reward induced remapping spanning the environment, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 2b-d
claims.quote: At the population level, a reward switch within a constant environment induced more remapping than a fixed reward and environment 28 , 29 but less remapping than the introduction of a novel environment
claims.criterion: As the Extended Data Fig. 2b,c legend gives it. For each mouse and day, the unsmoothed 2D histogram of place-cell peaks (cells with significant SI before and after) in 10 cm bins, before against after the switch (first against second half on stay days), as a fraction of those cells; "diagonal" is peaks within 50 cm of the same position before and after, excluding near-reward bins, "near reward" peaks within 50 cm of both zone starts, "all other remapping" the rest. Each mouse's mean over stay days (1, 2, 4, 6, 9, 11, 13), switch-within days (3, 5, 7, 10, 12, 14) and day 8; logit-transformed; pairwise paired two-sided t-tests, Holm-corrected within the category (pingouin pairwise_ttests, Fig2_Ext2_identifyRewardRelative.md:1292-1666). Reproduced when "all other remapping" is ordered stay < switch within < across environment and "diagonal" stay > across environment and switch within > across environment, each at corrected p < 0.05; partially reproduced when the order holds for one category only. The code's diagonal band (np.tri, offsets of -4 to +5 bins) is shown as a variant of the legend's symmetric 50 cm.

claims.statement: The distance run in the teleport zone did not predict the next lap's spatial firing error for ~93% of RR cells; 6.7% of RR cells had a significant Spearman correlation on trials before the switch and 7.5% after.
claims.source: Results, Reward-relative remapping both near and far from reward, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 2e,f
claims.quote: The distance run in the teleport zone did not predict spatial firing variability on the following lap in the vast majority (~93%) of RR cells
claims.criterion: As the Methods give it (Relationship between distance run in the teleport zone and trial-to-trial variability), for each RR cell and trial set, the distance run in the teleport period after each trial (speed integrated from the first teleport frame to the last frame before the track restarts) against the next trial's signed spatial peak error (the trial's peak minus the set's trial-averaged peak, circular error converted to cm), Spearman correlation, significant at p < 0.05 (Extended Data Fig. 2f). The code holds no version of this analysis. The values match when both percentages are within tolerance.

claims.statement: On the first switch day the fraction of remapping place cells whose firing kept the same position relative to reward exceeded a random-remapping shuffle.
claims.source: Results, Reward-relative remapping both near and far from reward, paragraph 2; Figure 2d,e
claims.quote: We found that the fraction of place cells that exhibited RR remapping across animals (Fig. 2d ) exceeded chance on the first switch day (Fig. 2e , top)
claims.criterion: As the Methods give it (Quantification of RR remapping compared to chance). Cells with significant SI before and after the switch, TR cells (peaks within 0.698 rad, 50 cm) removed; peaks re-computed on circular coordinates (0-450 cm to -pi..pi) and expressed relative to each zone start; the circular difference of relative peaks (after minus before), pooled over mice, histogrammed in 45 bins of 2pi/45 as a fraction of cells; the shuffle keeps each pre-switch peak and circularly shifts the post-switch trial-averaged map 1,000 times by 0-44 bins. The above-chance fraction is the summed excess over the per-bin 95th percentile of the shuffle, over bins whose centres lie within 0.698 rad of zero (dayData.py:1541-1741). Reproduced when on day 3 at least one such bin exceeds the shuffle's 95th percentile and the above-chance fraction is positive. The code's 2pi/44 map bins and 0 to nbins-1 offsets are shown as a variant.

claims.statement: The above-chance fraction of RR remapping cells grew linearly with task experience over the seven switch days.
claims.source: Results, Reward-relative remapping both near and far from reward, paragraph 2; Figure 2h; Extended Data Fig. 2h
claims.quote: Above-chance fraction of RR remapping cells grows linearly with task experience
claims.criterion: The above-chance fraction as in fig2e-rr-remapping-above-chance, per switch day. Figure 2h, pooled over mice per day, a linear regression on switch number 1-7 (regression.linear_reg, p from scipy.stats.linregress, Fig2_Ext2_identifyRewardRelative.md:665-680). Extended Data Fig. 2h, per mouse and day, the logit of the fraction in a linear mixed-effects model with switch index as fixed effect and a random intercept per mouse (statsmodels mixedlm, REML, Wald test; fractions of exactly 0 or 1 dropped, Fig2_Ext2_identifyRewardRelative.md:744-755). The paper prints neither p. Reproduced when both slopes are positive at p < 0.05; partially reproduced when one is.

claims.statement: The mean reward-relative firing position of cells remapping within 50 cm relative to reward was significantly after the reward zone start, 0.441 rad on the first switch day (n = 453 cells) and 0.292 rad on the last (n = 645 cells).
claims.source: Results, Reward-relative remapping both near and far from reward, paragraph 2; Figure 2e,g (bottom) legend
claims.quote: The mean of the distribution of RR firing positions was significantly greater than zero (Fig. 2e , bottom), indicating that more RR place fields are in locations following reward delivery
claims.criterion: The cells of fig2e-rr-remapping-above-chance whose relative peaks before and after lie within 0.698 rad of each other, pooled over mice; each cell's value is the circular mean of its two relative peaks (dayData.py:1714-1719); pycircstat mtest against 0 at alpha 0.05 gives the 95% interval. Reproduced when on both days the mean is positive, the interval excludes zero, and the means are within tolerance.

claims.statement: After excluding cells with peaks within increasing distances on either side of both reward zone starts, above-chance RR remapping remained, spanning nearly the whole track by the last switch day.
claims.source: Results, Reward-relative remapping both near and far from reward, paragraph 3; Figure 2i
claims.quote: With these exclusions, we observed that above-chance RR remapping spans nearly the entire track length by the last switch day
claims.criterion: As fig2e-rr-remapping-above-chance, after removing cells with peaks within an exclusion distance of both zone starts, for exclusion distances of 10 to 190 cm in 10 cm steps (Fig2_Ext2_identifyRewardRelative.md:775-795). The paper gives no number for "nearly the entire track". Reproduced when on day 14 the above-chance fraction is positive at every exclusion distance up to 190 cm, the largest the code tests; partially reproduced when it is positive up to at least 50 cm (the exclusion of Extended Data Fig. 2i-l) but not to 190 cm. The largest distance with a positive fraction is reported for days 3 and 14.

claims.statement: Excluding cells within 50 cm of both reward zone starts, RR remapping still exceeded the shuffle, and the mean reward-relative position of the remaining RR remapping cells was 1.145 rad (n = 285) on the first switch and 1.245 rad (n = 303) on the last.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 2i-l legend
claims.quote: The fraction of cells remapping relative to reward at distances greater than ±50 cm still exceeds the shuffle
claims.criterion: As fig2e-rr-remapping-above-chance and fig2eg-mean-rr-position-after-reward with cells within 50 cm (0.698 rad) of both zone starts removed. Reproduced when on both days the above-chance fraction is positive, the circular-mean interval excludes zero and the expected values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: More RR cells fired after than before the reward zone start, after excluding cells within distances up to 50 cm on the first switch and up to 80 cm on the last.
claims.source: Results, Reward-relative remapping both near and far from reward, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 2m
claims.quote: more RR firing fields were located at positions following than preceding the reward zone at distances up to ±80 cm
claims.criterion: RR cells (claim rr-cell-fractions) pooled over mice on days 3 and 14, excluding cells whose post-switch relative peak is within each exclusion distance (10 to 190 cm in 10 cm steps) of the zone start; statsmodels proportions_ztest of the number after the start against all, value 0.5, at the legend's level p < 0.00263 (0.05/19, Fig2_Ext2_identifyRewardRelative.md:1292-1666). Reproduced when the after fraction exceeds 0.5 at that level for every exclusion distance from 10 to 50 cm on day 3 and from 10 to 80 cm on day 14; partially reproduced when it does so on one day.

claims.statement: After excluding cells within 50 cm of the reward zone start, the above-chance fraction of RR remapping cells did not increase significantly across days.
claims.source: Results, Reward-relative remapping both near and far from reward, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 2n
claims.quote: However, there was no significant increase in remapping at these distances across days (Extended Data Fig. 2n )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The above-chance fraction of ed2jl-rr-remapping-beyond-50cm per switch day, linear regression on switch number 1-7 as in Figure 2h (the legend names a linear regression; the code holds no version of panel n). Reproduced when the slope's p is 0.05 or more; not reproduced when the slope is positive at p < 0.05. Slope and p reported either way.

claims.statement: Under the additional criteria, RR cells were 16.3 +/- 5.3% of place cells over all switch days, 13.7 +/- 3.9% on the first switch and 19.4 +/- 5.2% on the last; non-RR remapping cells were 11.9 +/- 3.0%, and 31.4 +/- 14.3% of place cells fell in no category.
claims.source: Results, Reward-relative remapping both near and far from reward, paragraph 3
claims.quote: We implemented additional criteria ( Methods and Extended Data Fig. 2o–q ) to identify a robust subpopulation of RR cells for further analysis (mean ± s.d., 16.3 ± 5.3% of place cells averaged over all switch days; 13.7 ± 3.9% on the first switch, 19.4 ± 5.2% on the last switch). We refer to cells that remapped independently of RR position as ‘non-RR remapping’ (11.9 ± 3.0% of all place cells). A remaining 31.4 ± 14.3% of place cells did not show sufficiently stereotyped remapping patterns
claims.criterion: RR cells as the Methods define them (Criteria to define RR cells). Place cells (significant SI before or after), interneurons excluded, whose peaks relative to the zone start before and after lie within 0.698 rad (50 cm) of each other, and whose trial-averaged reward-aligned dF/F before and after has a cross-correlation peak above the 97.5th percentile of 500 shuffles (each post-switch trial circularly shifted by 1 to 45 bins) at a lag within 5 bins of zero. Non-RR remapping, the "remap far from reward" cells less the RR cells (code). Unclassified, place cells in none of the categories (RR, TR, disappearing, appearing, near, far). Over the 77 switch sessions for the RR fractions. The text does not say which days the non-RR and unclassified percentages cover; readings (a) all seven switch days, (b) the six within-environment days, as the code does for non-RR. The values match under a reading when all five are within tolerance. The code's shuffle of 1 to 44 bins and 2pi/44 bins is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: RR cells had higher pre- against post-switch correlations of their reward-aligned activity maps than TR and non-RR remapping cells, and TR cells had higher correlations on the original track axis than RR and non-RR cells.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 2p,q legend
claims.criterion: For each cell, the Pearson correlation of its trial-averaged maps before and after the switch, reward-aligned (circular coordinates rotated to the zone starts) and in track coordinates, pooled over 11 mice and 7 switch days. Reproduced when the four rank-sum tests are in the stated direction at p < 0.001.

claims.statement: A decoder trained before the switch decoded reward-relative position above shuffle from RR, TR and non-RR remapping cells when tested before the switch, but only RR cells decoded it above shuffle on trials after the switch.
claims.source: Results, Reward-relative remapping both near and far from reward, paragraph 3; Figure 3b
claims.quote: However, when we tested on trials after the reward switch, only the RR population decoded the animals’ RR position better than shuffle (Fig. 3b , bottom)
claims.criterion: As the Methods give it (Decoding of RR position). The circular-linear regression decoder of decode.py (CircularRegression, ridge 1e-4, tol 1e-5, 100 iterations, Fig3_Decoder.md:302) on deconvolved activity of the RR, TR or non-RR cells at speed above 2 cm/s, predicting position relative to the zone start; score cos(y - y_hat); tenfold cross-validation; data downsampled to equal occupancy per RR position bin (2pi/45) within trials before the switch or the last 30 trials after; 100 shuffles circularly shifting each cell's timeseries independently. Per session, the mean score against the mean of the shuffles; two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank over sessions per subpopulation, Bonferroni over the three subpopulations; effect size Hedges' g (pingouin pairwise_ttests, effsize hedges, Fig3_Decoder.md:982). Reproduced when all three exceed shuffle at corrected p < 0.05 tested before, RR exceeds shuffle tested after, and TR and non-RR do not (p of 0.05 or more, or real below shuffle); the effect sizes are compared with tolerance as well. Code variants shown, all post-switch trials in place of the last 30 (Fig3_Decoder.md:173, 423), 2pi/44 bins (Fig3_Decoder.md:177), contiguous test folds (decode.py:124).

claims.statement: Decoding of reward-relative position from RR cells, z-scored to the shuffle, exceeded 2 over most of the environment, from -104.5 +/- 20.1 cm to +152.7 +/- 22.9 cm relative to the reward zone start (mean +/- s.e.m. across switch days).
claims.source: Results, Reward-relative remapping both near and far from reward, paragraph 3; Figure 3c
claims.quote: Moreover, this above-shuffle decode of RR position using RR cells was significant across the majority of the environment (Fig. 3c ; range of z -scored decode >2... −104.5 ± 20.1 cm to +152.7 ± 22.9 cm relative to reward zone start; mean ± s.e.m. across switch days)
claims.criterion: The decoder of fig3b-decode-rr-position, trained before and tested after the switch, its score per RR-position bin z-scored to the session's shuffle (mean and s.d. over shuffles, Fig3_Decoder.md:644-646) and averaged over mice per switch day. Neither the Methods nor the code say how the range limits are found. Readings (a) per day, the most negative and most positive bin centres with mean z > 2; (b) per day, the limits of the contiguous run of bins with z > 2 that contains the zone start. Each then averaged over the seven switch days with its s.e.m. The values match under a reading when both limits are within tolerance.

claims.statement: RR cells formed sequences whose firing order was preserved across the reward switch, above a cell-identity shuffle in 75 of 77 sessions.
claims.source: Results, Preserved behavioral timescale sequences relative to reward, paragraph 1; Figure 4a-c
claims.quote: Sequence preservation (the circular–circular correlation coefficient between peak firing positions pre-switch versus post-switch) was higher than the shuffle of cell identities for nearly all animals and days (75 out of 77 sessions)
claims.criterion: As the Methods give it (Sequence detection and quantification). Unsmoothed binned dF/F in circular track coordinates; cells sorted by their peaks on odd trials before the switch; sequence positions the peaks of the even-before and the after trial averages (all post-switch trials, placeCellPlot.py:1428); circular-circular correlation (Kempter et al. 2012, corr_cc); 1,000 permutations of cell identities after the switch; P = (n of shuffled |rho| >= observed |rho| + 1)/1,001; significant at P < 0.05. Sessions with fewer than 5 cells count as not significant (placeCellPlot.py:1565). The value matches when the count is within tolerance.

claims.statement: TR cells likewise formed sequences preserved across the switch, above shuffle in 76 of 77 sessions.
claims.source: Results, Preserved behavioral timescale sequences relative to reward, paragraph 1; Figure 4d-f
claims.quote: The TR place cells likewise constructed robust behavioral timescale sequences (76 out of 77 sessions) relative to the ends of the track
claims.criterion: As fig4c-rr-sequences-preserved, for TR cells (RR cells excluded, placeCellPlot.py:1317).

claims.statement: Sequential firing was not preserved for most non-RR remapping cells; 61 of 77 sessions did not exceed the shuffle.
claims.source: Results, Preserved behavioral timescale sequences relative to reward, paragraph 1; Figure 4g-i
claims.quote: sequential firing was not preserved for most of the non-RR remapping cells (61 out of 77 sessions did not exceed shuffle
claims.criterion: As fig4c-rr-sequences-preserved, for non-RR remapping cells; the count is of sessions with P of 0.05 or more, sessions with fewer than 5 cells included as not significant.

claims.statement: The environment change reduced the proportion of TR cells, 8.4 +/- 3.1% of place cells on day 8 against 21.4 +/- 7.9% on switches within an environment.
claims.source: Results, Preserved behavioral timescale sequences relative to reward, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 5a
claims.quote: However, the environment change significantly reduced the proportion of cells identified as TR (Extended Data Fig. 5a ; 8.4 ± 3.1% of place cells across environments on day 8 versus 21.4 ± 7.9% within; mean ± s.d., n = 11 mice)
claims.criterion: TR fraction of place cells per mouse and switch day (RR cells excluded); pingouin Friedman test over the seven switch days, then pairwise two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Holm-corrected (Fig2_Ext2_identifyRewardRelative.md:465-485). Reproduced when the Friedman test gives p < 0.05, day 8 is lower than each other switch day at corrected p < 0.05, and the two values are within tolerance (the 21.4% over the 66 within-environment mouse-days pooled, as Fig2_Ext2_identifyRewardRelative.md:429-440 computes it).

claims.statement: The proportion of RR cells did not decrease upon the environment switch on day 8.
claims.source: Results, RR representation increased with learning, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 5f
claims.quote: there was no decrease in the proportion of RR cells upon the environment switch (Extended Data Fig. 5f )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The legend of panel f refers to panel a ("as in ( a )"), and the code runs the same tests on the RR fraction (Fig2_Ext2_identifyRewardRelative.md:493-511), a Friedman test over the seven switch days and pairwise two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, Holm-corrected. Reproduced when no post hoc comparison shows day 8 lower than another switch day at corrected p < 0.05; not reproduced when one does. The Friedman statistic, the day 8 and other-day medians are reported either way.

claims.statement: RR sequences spanned the whole track but over-represented a region from ~50 cm before to ~70 cm after the reward zone start, with the highest density following the start of the zone.
claims.source: Results, RR representation increased with learning, paragraph 1; Figure 4j
claims.quote: RR sequences spanned the entire track but over-represented a region from ~50 cm before to ~70 cm after the reward zone start, with the highest density of cells following the start of the reward zone
claims.criterion: As the Methods give it (Sequence detection and quantification) and the code (Fig4_Ext4_sequences.md:200-454). Each RR cell's post-switch peak relative to the zone start, per mouse and day the count per 2pi/45 bin divided by the mouse's place-cell count, averaged over mice; the expected uniform level is the mean fraction of place cells in the sequence divided by 45. The tolerance is one bin (~10 cm), the resolution of the measure, as 10% of the values is finer than a bin. Readings for the days (a) the mean over the seven switch days, (b) each day. Reproduced under a reading when the bins above the uniform level form a region whose limits are within tolerance and the densest bin lies at or after the zone start.

claims.statement: The density of RR cells within 50 cm of the reward zone start increased with task experience, while the fraction of place cells more than 50 cm from it stayed stable over days.
claims.source: Results, RR representation increased with learning, paragraph 1; Figure 4j,m
claims.quote: This density near reward increased with task experience, while the fraction of place cells >50 cm from the reward zone start remained stable over days
claims.criterion: The per-mouse fraction of place cells that are RR cells with post-switch peaks within 50 cm on either side of the zone start (near) or beyond (far), per switch day (Fig4_Ext4_sequences.md:702-731). Linear mixed-effects model, fraction ~ 1 + switch, switch 1-7 continuous, random intercept per mouse, REML, two-sided Wald test (plotUtils.py:209-219). The code fits the raw and the logit fraction (Fig4_Ext4_sequences.md:791-794), and the Methods say the raw fraction was usually used and the logit confirmed it; readings (a) raw, (b) logit. Reproduced under a reading when the near slope is positive at p < 0.05 and the far slope has p of 0.05 or more.

claims.statement: Over switch days mice increased their post-switch anticipatory lick rate and their running speed.
claims.source: Results, RR representation increased with learning, paragraph 1; Figure 4k,l,n,o
claims.quote: In parallel, mice increased their post-switch anticipatory lick rate (Fig. 4k,n ) and running speed over days (Fig. 4l,o )
claims.criterion: Per mouse and switch day, the trial-averaged post-switch lick rate (10 cm bins) and speed (2 cm bins), averaged over bins within 50 cm on either side of the zone start, or beyond (Fig4_Ext4_sequences.md:743-761); the mixed model of fig4m-rr-density-near-reward-grows on each. Lick rate is read in the near window ("anticipatory"). The paper does not say which window the speed result rests on; readings (a) within 50 cm, (b) beyond 50 cm. Reproduced when the near lick-rate slope is positive at p < 0.05 and, under a reading, the speed slope is positive at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: On a given day, the circular variance of the animal's licking positions correlated with the circular variance of the RR sequence, both before and after the switch.
claims.source: Results, RR representation increased with learning, paragraph 1; Figure 4p
claims.quote: Circular variance in licking positions significantly correlates with RR sequence variance before (left) and after the switch (right)
claims.criterion: Per session (77), the astropy circular variance of RR cells' relative peaks, against the circular variance of licking positions relative to the zone start, before and after the switch; linear regression pooled over sessions (scipy linregress, Fig4_Ext4_sequences.md:540-550). Readings for lick variance (a) the circular variance of the positions of all binned licks in the trial set (the legend's wording), (b) the code's circular mean over trials of each trial's circular variance (Fig4_Ext4_sequences.md:293-301). Reproduced under a reading when the slope is positive at p < 0.05 both before and after.

claims.statement: The variance of the RR sequence and of post-switch licking positions decreased across switch days, while the mean reward-relative position of the sequence did not change.
claims.source: Results, RR representation increased with learning, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 4h-j
claims.quote: The variance of both the RR distribution and the post-switch licking decreased across switch days (Extended Data Fig. 4h,i ) but the mean position of the sequence did not change (Extended Data Fig. 4j )
claims.criterion: Per mouse and switch day the circular variance and circular mean of RR relative peaks and the licking variance as in fig4p-lick-precision-sequence-precision; the mixed model of fig4m-rr-density-near-reward-grows on switch index (Fig4_Ext4_sequences.md:589-599). Reproduced when the RR variance and the post-switch lick variance have negative slopes at p < 0.05 and the mean position's slope has p of 0.05 or more (the paper's test for the absence). The code fills mouse-days without RR cells with 0 (Fig4_Ext4_sequences.md:229-270); main reading drops them, the code's zeros shown as a variant. The lick-variance readings of fig4p apply.

claims.statement: TR sequences tended to over-represent the ends of the track, and TR density far from the track ends decreased across days.
claims.source: Results, RR representation increased with learning, paragraph 1; Figure 4q,r
claims.quote: TR sequence density decreased at positions far from the track ends across days, consistent with selective stabilization of place fields near the landmarks
claims.criterion: TR cells' post-switch peaks in track coordinates, density per 2pi/45 bin per mouse and day as in fig4j-rr-overrepresent-reward. Reproduced when the mean density over mice and days in the bins within 50 cm of either track end exceeds the uniform level, and the mixed model of fig4m-rr-density-near-reward-grows on the fraction of place cells that are TR cells more than 50 cm from the track ends has a negative slope at p < 0.05. The raw and logit readings of fig4m apply.

claims.statement: Disappearing, appearing and non-RR remapping cells encoded a more uniform representation; the fraction of disappearing cells decreased with experience both near and far from reward, while non-RR remapping and appearing fractions did not change significantly.
claims.source: Results, RR representation increased with learning, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 4k,l
claims.quote: Both near ( ≤ 50 cm, top) and far from ( > 50 cm, bottom) the start of the reward zone, the fraction of place cells with disappearing fields decreases across experience. Non-RR remapping and appearing fractions did not show significant changes over experience
claims.criterion: Per mouse and switch day the fraction of place cells of each category with peaks within or beyond 50 cm of the zone start, the mixed model of fig4m-rr-density-near-reward-grows. Reproduced when the disappearing slope is negative at p < 0.05 in both windows and the non-RR remapping and appearing slopes have p of 0.05 or more in both (the paper's test for the absence). "More uniform" is not tested further.

claims.statement: In sessions imaged through the teleport, 32.7 +/- 10.8% of TR cells and 12.7 +/- 7.1% of RR cells peaked in the teleport period on days with a constant environment, against 41.9 +/- 5.4% and 27.2 +/- 5.7% on day 8, with no significant effect of day for either.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5d,i legends
claims.criterion: As the Methods give it (Analysis of teleport periods). In sessions imaged through the teleport (2P imaging, Methods), place cells re-identified with 10 cm bins from -50 cm (tunnel start) to the largest jitter bin with fewer than ten trials missing (up to 580 cm), and TR and RR re-categorized from them; the fraction peaking in the tunnel or jitter, mean +/- s.d. over the 7 mice with any teleport sampling, and a Friedman test of day over the 4 mice sampled on all days. The code holds no version of this analysis. The legends do not say whether the constant-environment value pools mouse-days or averages per mouse first; readings (a) mouse-day rows, as the code does elsewhere, (b) per-mouse means. Reproduced under a reading when the four values are within tolerance and both Friedman tests have p of 0.05 or more.

claims.statement: Across experience, RR cells were increasingly likely to remain RR on the next switch day.
claims.source: Results, Dynamic cell recruitment into the RR population, paragraph 1; Figure 5b
claims.quote: We found that across experience, RR cells were increasingly likely to remain RR on consecutive switches (Fig. 5a,b )
claims.criterion: Cells matched across days as the Methods give it (intersection over union of ROI pixels, with a threshold per dataset such that the best match's IoU always exceeds any second-best match), for the six consecutive switch-day pairs (3-5, 5-7, 7-8, 8-10, 10-12, 12-14). The fraction is the number of day-A RR cells that are RR on day B over the day-A RR cells matched to day B and a place cell there, set to missing below 5 such cells (Fig5_Ext6_TrackingCellsAcrossDays.md:123-141, 380-397). Mixed model, fraction ~ 1 + pair index 0-5, random intercept per mouse, REML, Wald test, no logit (Fig5_Ext6_TrackingCellsAcrossDays.md:608-625). Reproduced when the slope is positive at p < 0.05. Where the dataset holds no cross-day matching, the matching is done by the Methods' rule and said so.

claims.statement: An increasing fraction of non-TR place cells (appearing, disappearing and non-RR remapping) converted into RR cells on the next switch day over experience.
claims.source: Results, Dynamic cell recruitment into the RR population, paragraph 1; Figure 5d
claims.quote: Fraction of ‘non-TR’ place cells (combined appearing, disappearing and non-RR remapping) that convert into RR cells on subsequent switch days increases over task experience
claims.criterion: As fig5b-rr-remain-rr-increases, for day-A non-TR place cells (RR excluded) becoming RR. Reproduced when the slope is positive at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The fraction of non-place cells converting to RR cells on the next switch day showed a modest increase over experience.
claims.source: Results, Dynamic cell recruitment into the RR population, paragraph 1; Figure 5f
claims.quote: Fraction of non-place cells converting to RR cells on subsequent switch days shows a modest increase over task experience
claims.criterion: As fig5b-rr-remain-rr-increases, for day-A cells without significant SI in either trial set becoming RR. Reproduced when the slope is positive at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: TR cells were sometimes recruited into the RR population, at a rate that did not change over days.
claims.source: Results, Dynamic cell recruitment into the RR population, paragraph 1; Figure 5g,h
claims.quote: TR cells were sometimes also recruited, though this occurred at a constant rate over days
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, as fig5b-rr-remain-rr-increases for day-A TR cells becoming RR. Reproduced when the slope has p of 0.05 or more; not reproduced when p < 0.05. Slope and mean fraction reported either way.

claims.statement: The fraction of RR cells converting to TR cells decreased slightly over experience.
claims.source: Figure 5i legend
claims.quote: Fraction of RR cells converting to TR cells decreases slightly over task experience
claims.criterion: As fig5b-rr-remain-rr-increases for day-A RR cells becoming TR, without the 5-cell minimum (Fig5_Ext6_TrackingCellsAcrossDays.md:362-365). Reproduced when the slope is negative at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The TR population did not recruit more cells from non-TR place cells or non-place cells over days, and TR cells were not more likely to remain TR across experience.
claims.source: Results, Dynamic cell recruitment into the RR population, paragraph 1; Figure 5j-l
claims.quote: By contrast, the TR population did not recruit more cells from any other population (Fig. 5i–k ) and did not show an increased likelihood of remaining TR across experience (Fig. 5l )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, as fig5b-rr-remain-rr-increases for day-A non-TR place cells, non-place cells and TR cells becoming TR (Figure 5j, k, l). Reproduced when none of the three slopes is positive at p < 0.05; not reproduced when one is. Slopes and p reported either way. Figure 5i, which the Results cite here, is claim fig5i-rr-to-tr-decreases.

claims.statement: RR cells that first fired closer to reward were more likely to keep stable RR tuning across days, and TR cells closer to reward were more likely to remap relative to the track and become RR.
claims.source: Results, Dynamic cell recruitment into the RR population, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 6a
claims.quote: Furthermore, RR cells that originally fired closer to reward were more likely to have stable RR tuning over days, and TR cells closer to reward were more likely to remap with respect to the track and become RR
claims.criterion: As the Extended Data Fig. 6a legend and Fig5_Ext6_TrackingCellsAcrossDays.md:672-838 give it. For cells matched across consecutive switch-day pairs, categorized on day A, the absolute cross-day change in the pre-switch peak relative to reward (RR cells) and in track position (TR cells), binned by the day-A distance from the zone start in 10 cm bins (mean +/- s.e.m. over pooled cells, smoothed with a 10 cm s.d. Gaussian for display). The paper reports no test and no boundary between near and far, so how "closer to reward" is judged is open. Readings (a) the change within 50 cm of the zone start against beyond it (the near and far boundary of Figure 4m), two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum over pooled cells at p < 0.05; (b) a linear regression of the change on the day-A absolute distance from the zone start over pooled cells (the test Extended Data Fig. 6c uses for the neighbouring panel), at p < 0.05. Reproduced when under both readings the RR reward-relative change is smaller near reward (a) or grows with distance (b), and the TR track change is larger near reward (a) or falls with distance (b); not reproduced when both readings fail; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. The binned curves are reported.

claims.statement: RR cells that stayed RR across switch-day pairs shifted their peaks slightly toward the reward zone start over days, their initial position being weakly anticorrelated with the change.
claims.source: Results, Dynamic cell recruitment into the RR population, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 6b,c
claims.quote: RR cells near reward shifted their peak firing even closer to the reward zone start over days
claims.criterion: RR cells RR on both days of a pair, day-A relative peak within 80 cm of the zone start, the signed cross-day change against the day-A position, linear regression (legend; code at Fig5_Ext6_TrackingCellsAcrossDays.md:841-978). Reproduced when the slope is negative at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Across-day sequence correlations of RR and TR cells were generally lower than within-day sequence correlations, consistent with representational drift.
claims.source: Results, Dynamic cell recruitment into the RR population, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 6j-m; Figure 4c,f
claims.quote: Although sequence preservation across switch days was greater than chance in some sessions, correlation coefficients across days were generally lower (Extended Data Fig. 6j–m ) than within-day sequences (Fig. 4c,f )
claims.criterion: Across-day correlation as the Methods give it (Sequence detection and quantification), the sort from day-A trials before the switch, correlating day-A after-switch peaks with day-B before-switch peaks of matched cells, at least 5 cells. The Results cite panels j-m, which hold two cell sets; readings for the cells (a) cells followed agnostic of their day-B category (panels j for RR, l for TR), (b) cells keeping their category on day B (panels k, m). The paper names no test for "generally lower"; the comparison of medians is a reading, not the paper's. Reproduced under a cell reading when the median across-day rho over mouse-pairs is below the median within-day rho of fig4c-rr-sequences-preserved for RR cells and of fig4f-tr-sequences-preserved for TR cells.

claims.statement: RR and TR cells showed no reliable bias in their medio-lateral, antero-posterior or superficial-deep distribution within CA1.
claims.source: Results, Dynamic cell recruitment into the RR population, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 7
claims.quote: However, we found no reliable bias in the medio-lateral, antero-posterior or superficial-deep distributions of either subpopulation (Extended Data Fig. 7 )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's tests (Extended Data Fig. 7b,c,h legends). Per mouse (and per plane in m17 and m18), cells pooled over the seven switch days, a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test of RR against TR ROI centres of mass in ML and AP, at the legend's Bonferroni level p < 0.0038, and of estimated depth in single-plane mice at p < 0.0055. The code applies no correction (Ext7_Anatomical_Map.md:605-672). Counts tolerate one test, the smallest unit. Reproduced when in each axis the count of significant mice or planes is no more than the paper's count plus the tolerance (3 of 13 for ML, 2 of 13 for AP, 2 of 9 for depth); not reproduced otherwise. The direction of each significant test is reported.

claims.statement: RR cells with peaks after the reward zone start fired more after rewards than after omissions before the switch; the median reward versus omission index was above 0 in every mouse and significantly so in 9 of 11 mice.
claims.source: Results, Encoding of reward proximity versus movement covariates, paragraph 2; Figure 6e
claims.quote: At the population level, the RR cells fired significantly more following rewards compared to omissions, both before the reward switch (Fig. 6d,e ) and after
claims.criterion: As the Methods give it (Analysis of rewarded versus omission trials; Time warp modeling; Reward versus omission index). Trial sets before the switch with the zone at A or B and at least three omission trials; deconvolved activity in 10 cm bins at speed of 2 cm/s or more, each cell divided by its session mean; affinewarp PiecewiseWarping with three knots fit to the trial speed profiles (rewarded and omission together; warp_reg_scale 1e-6, smoothness_reg_scale 20, 50 iterations and 200 warp iterations, Fig6_Ext8_Rewarded_vs_Omission.md:333-337) and applied to the activity; RO index = sum(r - o)/sum(r + o) over bins of the trial-averaged warped activity; per mouse, cells pooled over days, two-sided one-sample Wilcoxon signed-rank test against 0 at p < 0.0045 (the legend's Bonferroni level; the code applies none). RR cells with peaks after the zone start; readings (a) the Methods, track peak between the zone start and the track end, (b) the code, positive circular offset from the zone start (Fig6_Ext8_Rewarded_vs_Omission.md:169). Reproduced under a reading when the count of mice with a positive median at that level is within tolerance; the count tolerates one mouse, the smallest unit.

claims.statement: After the switch too, RR cells fired more following rewards than omissions, with a positive median reward versus omission index significant in 9 of 11 mice.
claims.source: Results, Encoding of reward proximity versus movement covariates, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 8k
claims.quote: Reward vs. omission index across all switch days where the reward zone was at “A” or “B”, on the trials after the switch
claims.criterion: As fig6e-rr-prefer-reward on trial sets after the switch (zone at A or B after the switch). Reproduced under a reading of fig6e when the count is within tolerance.

claims.statement: Time warping reduced the mean squared error across trial-by-trial speed profiles, and the speed error was higher after the switch than before.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 8d,f legends
claims.quote: Time warp model fitting significantly reduces MSE across trial-by-trial speed profiles compared to the original speed data
claims.criterion: The warp of fig6e-rr-prefer-reward per trial set; MSE between each trial's speed profile and the mean over trials, raw and warped. Reproduced when warped MSE is below raw at p < 0.05 and raw MSE after exceeds before at p < 0.05 (two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank over sessions).

claims.statement: The GLM fit well (fraction deviance explained above 0.15 on held-out trials) 33% of place cells, 4,106 of 7,027 TR cells, 2,122 of 5,979 RR cells and 1,748 of 4,314 non-RR remapping cells; mean fraction deviance explained was 0.32 for TR cells and 0.29 for RR cells.
claims.source: Results, Encoding of reward proximity versus movement covariates, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 9b,c
claims.quote: Only well-fit neurons (fraction deviance explained > 0.15) 37 were included in further analysis (33% of place cells across 11 mice and seven switch days; TR cells, 4,106 out of 7,027; RR cells, 2,122 out of 5,979; non-RR remapping cells, 1,748 out of 4,314
claims.criterion: As the Methods give it (GLM). Poisson GLM at ~15.5 Hz, speed of 2 cm/s or more; 45 cosine bases of track position, 45 of RR position, 45 of rewarded x position, 7 B-spline bases (degree 3, 5 knots, on quantile-transformed values) for each of speed, acceleration (5-sample Gaussian) and licks (2-sample Gaussian), z-scored; trials split 85/15 by GroupShuffleSplit separately for rewarded-before, rewarded-after and omission trials, random_state 30 (Fig7_Ext9_GLM.md:284); fivefold cross-validation grouped by trial over the training trials; GLM_Tensorflow_2 GLM_CV with group lasso, lambda 10^linspace(-1, -6, 11), Adam, learning rate 0.01, exponential link, lambda chosen by best cross-validated deviance (Fig7_Ext9_GLM.md:292-302); FDE = 1 - dev_model / dev_null on the held-out trials. The response is the deconvolved activity (the code scales it by 10, which leaves FDE unchanged). The Methods give "0.32 +/- 0.13 for TR cells" and "0.29 +/- 0.11 for RR cells" next to 0.10 for all place cells and do not say over which cells; readings for the FDE means (a) the well-fit cells, (b) all cells of the subpopulation. The values match under a reading when all are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Track position was the top GLM predictor for 81.3% of TR cells; for RR cells, RR position gave the highest relative contribution and was the top predictor for 32.8%, followed by speed (21.3%), track position (17.6%) and reward (14.0%); ~56% of well-fit RR cells had RR position as first or second predictor.
claims.source: Results, Encoding of reward proximity versus movement covariates, paragraph 4; Figure 7d,e; Extended Data Fig. 9d,e
claims.quote: Track position was the top predictor for 81.3% of TR cells (Fig. 7e ) ... For RR cells, RR position provided the highest relative contribution at the population level (Fig. 7d ) and the top predictor for 32.8% of RR cells, followed by speed (21.3%), linear track position (17.6%) and the receipt of reward (14.0%) ... Overall, ~56% of RR neurons well-fit by the GLM had RR position as a first or second predictor
claims.criterion: The well-fit cells of glm-well-fit-cells, pooled over mice and switch days. Relative contribution by ablation as the Methods give it, (dev_ablated - dev_full)/(dev_null - dev_full) on the cross-validation data, each variable's coefficients zeroed, binned by track position and averaged over bins (Fig7_Ext9_GLM.md:426-512). Top predictor, the variable with the largest contribution; second, the largest of the rest (Fig7_Ext9_GLM.md:854-1052). Figure 7d, the variable with the highest median contribution in each subpopulation must be track position for TR and RR position for RR. Reproduced when both Figure 7d orderings hold and all six values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the orderings hold and the RR and TR top-predictor rankings match but some values fall outside tolerance.

claims.statement: The RR population's remap trial preceded the licking remap trial by about two trials for backward (2.1 +/- 0.6) and forward (1.7 +/- 0.7) reward moves, preceded the speed remap trial by 4.4 +/- 1.1 trials for backward moves, and was synchronous with speed for forward moves (0.5 +/- 0.5).
claims.source: Results, RR cell activity often updates before behavior, paragraph 2; Figure 8e
claims.quote: Neural remapping preceded changes in licking by approximately two trials regardless of whether the reward was moved backward or forward on the track (backward... 2.1 ± 0.6 trials (mean ± s.e.m.), neural before licking; forward... 1.7 ± 0.7 trials), but only preceded changes in speed when reward was moved backward (4.4 ± 1.1 trials, neural before speed) and was synchronous with speed when reward was moved forward (0.5 ± 0.5 trials before speed)
claims.criterion: As the Methods give it (K-means clustering and distance score analysis). Per session and RR population, deconvolved activity in 10 cm bins smoothed (10 cm Gaussian), min-max scaled per cell; lvl factorized k-means, k = 2, 100 restarts; sessions accepted when the k = 2 model beats rotation shuffles on speckled holdout (50 repeats) by a Wilcoxon test at P < 0.05 (the Methods say two-sided, the code one-sided greater, kMeansDistScore.py:211-217; both shown; the paper accepted 50 of 77); cluster labels set so cluster one comes first; distance score; sigmoid L/(1 + exp(-k(x - x0))) + b by curve_fit (dogbox, p0 [max y, median x, 1, min y]), its inflection the remap trial (regression.py:172-195); the same for max-normalized binned licks and speed; sessions kept when all three fits converge. Direction, forward when the new zone is further down the track. Mixed model remap_trial ~ C(datatype, reference PV) * C(direction) + switch, random intercept per mouse, coefficient p Benjamini-Hochberg corrected (Fig8_Ext10_DistanceScore.md:759-790). The four values equal the model's coefficients (backward lick 2.125; forward 2.125 - 0.398; backward speed 4.417; forward 4.417 - 3.871), but the paper does not say how the "mean +/- s.e.m." is taken. Readings (a) the model coefficients and their combinations; (b) mean over sessions of per-session differences; (c) mean over mice of per-mouse means. Reproduced under a reading when the four values are within tolerance and the lick - PV and speed - PV coefficients are positive and the interaction negative at corrected p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Remapping of appearing cells followed changes in behavior, and RR remap trials were the most consistent; mean remap trials were 31.91 +/- 2.37 for RR, 32.86 +/- 3.91 for non-RR remapping and 43.0 +/- 7.22 for appearing cells.
claims.source: Results, RR cell activity often updates before behavior, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 10e-g
claims.quote: By contrast, remapping of the appearing cells significantly followed changes in behavior (Extended Data Fig. 10c,d,f,g )
claims.criterion: The procedure of fig8e-rr-remap-precedes-behavior for appearing and non-RR remapping populations (appearing limited to sessions where two clusters could be identified). Reproduced when for appearing cells the lick - PV and speed - PV coefficients are negative at corrected p < 0.05, the appearing - RR coefficient of the pooled model (fixed effects subpopulation, direction, their interaction and switch day; random intercept per mouse) is positive at p < 0.05, the RR remap trials have the smallest s.d. of the three populations, and the means are within tolerance.

claims.statement: The fraction of cells keeping a single place field both before and after the switch increased across switch days for all subpopulations, most clearly for RR cells.
claims.source: Results, Independent remapping of individual place fields per cell, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 3d
claims.quote: However, the fraction of cells maintaining a single place field increased with task experience (Extended Data Fig. 3d )
claims.criterion: Place fields as the Methods give them (Place field definition and inclusion criteria), deconvolved activity smoothed 10 cm, regions of 20 cm or more above 20% of the trial-averaged maximum over the 30 trials before or the last 30 after, active (above mean + 1 s.d.) in at least 8 of the 30 trials; cells with significant SI or a significant field before and after. Per subpopulation (RR, TR, non-RR remapping), the pooled fraction with one field before and one after, linear regression on switch 1-7 (Ext3_FieldQuant.md). Reproduced when the slope is positive at p < 0.05 for all three subpopulations and the RR p is the smallest; partially reproduced when it is positive at p < 0.05 for RR only or for two of the three.

claims.statement: For RR cells with two fields before and after the switch, the offsets between the two fields were not correlated before against after, indicating independent remapping of the fields.
claims.source: Results, Independent remapping of individual place fields per cell, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 3f,g
claims.quote: We found no correlation in the offset between the two fields at the population level for RR cells, indicating largely independent remapping of fields
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. For RR cells with exactly two fields both before and after, the circular-circular correlation of the field offsets before against after, per switch day, cells pooled over mice, two-sided p without correction (legend). Reproduced when no switch day has a significant correlation of either sign at p < 0.05; not reproduced otherwise. The coefficients and p of every day are reported.

claims.statement: Appearing cells formed their fields on later laps and shifted backward more after the formation lap than RR, TR and non-RR remapping cells.
claims.source: Results, Independent remapping of individual place fields per cell, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 3m,o
claims.quote: At the population level, appearing cells showed more backwards shifting (Extended Data Fig. 3o ) and later formation laps than the other subpopulations
claims.criterion: Formation lap as the Methods give it (Formation lap identification and backwards shifting), within the trial-averaged field +/- 10 cm after the switch, trials whose binned activity exceeds mean + 1 s.d., the first five-trial window with at least three such trials, its first active trial; shift, the field's centre of mass on the formation lap subtracted from that of the mean of the last 30 trials (negative backward), from raw deconvolved activity. Primary fields (the field with peak activity), pooled over mice and switch days. Reproduced when appearing fields have later formation laps and more negative shifts than each other subpopulation by two-sided rank-sum tests at the legend's Bonferroni levels (0.0083 and 0.004).

claims.statement: Primary fields shifted more backward when the reward moved backward on the track than when it moved forward, in every subpopulation.
claims.source: Results, Independent remapping of individual place fields per cell, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 3p
claims.quote: Notably, the degree of backward and forward shifting depended on whether the reward moved backward or forward on the track, respectively (Extended Data Fig. 3p )
claims.criterion: Shifts of ed3mo-appearing-late-backward split by switch direction (backward when the new zone is earlier on the track). The legend's test is a two-sided permutation test on the rank-sum Z, permuting backward and forward session labels 100 times, at p < 0.01. Reproduced when for each subpopulation backward shifts are more negative and the permutation p is below 0.01; partially reproduced when that holds for some subpopulations.

claims.statement: A principal component analysis of the homecage behaviours of PACAPko and control mice gives three components, explaining 45.95%, 14.55% and 13.56% of the variance (80.05% together).
claims.source: Results 3.1, Jumping and repetitive jumping, paragraph 1; Figure 2A legend
claims.quote: PC1 accounts for 45.95% of the variance, PC2 for 14.55%, and PC3 for 13.56%, for a cumulative 80.05% of variability accounted for by these components.
claims.criterion: From the Figure 2 legend and Methods (Behavioral analysis). Inputs are the 16 behaviours of Table 3 (the legend says Table 2, which holds the TaqMan probes), as time spent (distance for travel) over the 12 dark hours, for 38 PACAPko and 18 control mice pooled; each behaviour standardized to mean 0 and SD 1; the number of components chosen by parallel analysis. Open, could change the outcome - whether the components were rotated. The loadings of Table 3 (all positive, each behaviour high on one component) suggest a rotation, but none is named. Readings are (a) unrotated components, (b) varimax-rotated components. Reproduced when, under one reading, parallel analysis keeps three components and the variance values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: PC1 loads most on locomotion (travel distance, 0.934) and hanging from the cage top (0.89), PC2 on jumping (0.845) and repetitive jumping (0.779), PC3 on remaining low (0.78) and grooming (0.72).
claims.source: Results 3.1, Jumping and repetitive jumping, paragraph 1; Table 3
claims.quote: PC1 is most heavily loaded towards locomotion (0.934) and climbing the cage top (0.89). PC2 is most heavily loaded towards jumping (0.845) and repetitive jumping (0.779). PC3 is most loaded towards remaining low in the cage (0.78) and grooming (0.72).
claims.criterion: Same PCA and the same two readings (unrotated, varimax) as fig2a-pca-components. Table 3 gives 0.88 for "Remain Hanging with all four paws from cage top" where the text gives 0.89 for climbing the cage top; the Table 3 behaviour is the one meant (the text and legend call it hanging from the cage top in Figure 2B). Table 3 also gives "Climbing on cage bottom" a PC1 loading of 0.9, above the 0.88 of cage-top hanging, so by the table cage-top hanging is not the second-highest PC1 loading; the rank is therefore not judged. Reproduced when, under one reading, each of the six behaviours loads highest on its stated component and each absolute loading is within tolerance.

claims.statement: Control mice cluster at low PC1 and PC2 scores, while PACAPko mice spread along two trajectories, high PC1 with lower PC2, or high PC2 with PC1 only slightly above control.
claims.source: Figure 2A
claims.quote: While control mice appear tightly clustered at low levels of PC1 and PC2 behaviors, PACAPko mice range widely, in two trajectories, towards high PC1 behaviors with lower PC2 behaviors, or high PC2 behaviors with PC1 behaviors only slightly above control levels
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test. Scores on PC1 and PC2 from the PCA of fig2a-pca-components, under each of its readings. Reproduced when the spread (SD) of PACAPko scores exceeds that of controls on both components, and among PACAPko mice above the control range on either component, some lie above it on PC1 only and some on PC2 only. This rule is the reader's, as the paper describes the pattern only in words; the scatter is shown.

claims.statement: PACAPko mice score higher than controls (time, or distance for travel) in the top two PC1 behaviours (travel distance, cage-top hanging) and PC2 behaviours (jumping, repetitive jumping), with no difference in the PC3 behaviours (remaining low, grooming).
claims.source: Results 3.1, Jumping and repetitive jumping, paragraph 1; Figure 2B
claims.quote: We found significantly higher levels of PC1 and PC2 index behaviors in PACAPko mice than controls, but no differences in PC3 index behaviors ( Figure 2b ).
claims.criterion: From the Figure 2B legend. For each of the six behaviours, a Mann-Whitney U test of PACAPko against control mice, the six p-values adjusted by Holm-Šídák. The reported U values are the smaller U (U = 28 of a possible 684). Reproduced when the four PC1 and PC2 behaviours are higher in PACAPko with adjusted p < 0.001 (the paper's bound), and the two PC3 behaviours have adjusted p >= 0.05 (a claim of absence, on the paper's test), with the U values within tolerance. Partially reproduced when the directions and significance hold but U values fall outside tolerance.

claims.statement: Travel distance of PACAPko mice does not differ from controls at weaning (p21) but is higher from p29 to the end of testing at p57.
claims.source: Results 3.1, Development of the constitutive PACAP knockout hyperlocomotor phenotype; Figure 3A
claims.quote: Šídák's multiple comparisons test showed that at postnatal day 21 (p21), travel distance did not differ across genotypes (p = 0.068), but by p29 PACAPko mice (blue) traveled significantly more than controls (orange), p = 0.001. The groups remained different through the end of testing at p57.
claims.criterion: From the Figure 3A legend. Travel distance per mouse and test day (p21 to p57), a mixed-effects model of day, genotype and their interaction (Geisser-Greenhouse corrected, as the fractional degrees of freedom show), with Šídák's comparisons of the genotypes at each day. Reproduced when the genotype effect and interaction have p < 0.05, the p21 comparison has p >= 0.05, and every comparison from p29 to p57 has p < 0.05 with PACAPko higher.

claims.statement: Jumping of PACAPko mice does not differ from controls at p21 and p28 but is higher at p36, p42, p50 and p57.
claims.source: Figure 3B
claims.quote: we found that on postnatal days 21 (t(4.98) = 0.473, adjusted p = 0.656) and 28 (t(10.45) = 2.347, adjusted p = 0.078) the genotypes did not differ, but on subsequent days the groups differed significantly
claims.criterion: From the Figure 3B legend. Jumping time per mouse and day; a Welch's t-test of the genotypes at each of the six days, adjusted by Holm-Šídák across the six. Reproduced when p21 and p28 have adjusted p >= 0.05 and p36 to p57 have adjusted p < 0.05 with PACAPko higher. The text says jumping "emerged early, at postnatal day 28"; the legend's test at p28 is not significant, and the legend is followed.

claims.statement: PACAPko mice raised with running wheels for 4 weeks after weaning show less repetitive jumping than littermates without wheels, with no change in single jumps, travel distance or cage-top hanging.
claims.source: Results 3.1, Development, paragraph 2; Figure 4
claims.quote: We found significant amelioration of repetitive jumping after wheel access, but no alterations in single jumps, travel distance, or cage top hanging ( Figure 4 ).
claims.criterion: From the Figure 4 legend. The four behaviours (jumping, repetitive jumping, travel distance, cage-top hanging) as values per mouse, a two-way ANOVA of wheel access by behaviour, and Šídák's comparisons of wheel against no wheel within each behaviour. Reproduced when the interaction has p < 0.05, repetitive jumping is lower with wheels at p < 0.05, and the other three behaviours have p >= 0.05 (absence, on the paper's test).

claims.statement: In whole-brain c-Fos counts after the early dark phase, PACAPko hemispheres have a higher density of c-Fos-positive cells than PACAP fl/fl in the dentate gyrus granule cell layer and polymorph layer, the only two regions significant after correction for multiple testing; PACAPko densities are 224% and 326% of control.
claims.source: Results 3.1, Association of the constitutive PACAP knockout hyperlocomotor phenotype with Fos induction, paragraph 1; Figure 5; Table 4
claims.quote: Cell counting and analysis revealed two regions where PACAPko mice had significantly higher c-Fos-positive cell density than controls after p-values were adjusted for multiple testing. These regions are the hippocampal dentate gyrus granule cell layer (DG-sg) and the dentate gyrus polymorph layer (DG-po).
claims.criterion: Method from the Supplemental Methods (Statistical analysis) and the Figure 5 legend. Unit is the hemisphere, PACAPko against PACAP fl/fl. CATNIP cell counts per region of the 561-region atlas; white matter tracts, nerves and ventricles, the cerebellum, SPVI and all layer 1 regions excluded, leaving 431 regions; counts of regions overlapping an artifact mask ignored; each count divided by the region's size (cells per cubic mm); outliers removed per region by the 1.5 IQR rule; scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu per region; statsmodels multipletests method "fdr_tsbky" over the 431 regions. The test is two-sided and exact, as Table 4 implies (raw p 2.65E-05 for U = 88 at 11 and 8 hemispheres is 2/C(19,8), the exact two-sided value for complete separation); U is that of the PACAPko sample (88 = 11 x 8 is its maximum). Open details, each named reading run - (1) the FRST threshold, chosen by an expert by eye and not given; readings are the threshold the dataset's derivatives mark as used, or, if none is marked, every threshold the derivatives hold. (2) Region size; readings are (a) the region's volume in that hemisphere's registered label image, (b) the atlas region volume. (3) The IQR rule; readings are (a) within each genotype, (b) both genotypes pooled. (4) Which hemispheres; the paper used 8 and 11 hemispheres from 6 and 6 mice without saying which were left out or why; readings are (a) the hemispheres the dataset marks as used, if it does, (b) every hemisphere of the two genotypes in the dataset. (5) The percentage; readings are the ratio of group means and the ratio of group medians, after outlier removal. (6) The alpha of the BKY procedure, not stated; the statsmodels default 0.05 is used and the result at 0.1 shown. Reproduced when, under the readings, DG-sg and DG-po both have PACAPko higher with BKY-adjusted p < 0.05; reported values within tolerance are reported and do not decide the outcome alone. Partially reproduced when one of the two holds. If the readings of (1) to (4) give different outcomes, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified with every result shown.

claims.statement: At an uncorrected cutoff of raw p <= 0.01, 13 further regions differ in c-Fos cell density between PACAPko and PACAP fl/fl, including substantia nigra reticular part, subthalamic nucleus and intergeniculate leaflet.
claims.source: Results 3.1, Association of the constitutive PACAP knockout hyperlocomotor phenotype with Fos induction, paragraph 1; Table 4; Figure 5
claims.quote: A less stringent cutoff of raw p-value <= 0.01 revealed 13 more regions ( Table 4 ; Figure 5 ) with differential cell counts. These included the Substantia Nigra reticulata (SNr), Subthalamic Nucleus (STN), and Intergeniculate Leaflet (IGL), among other regions.
claims.criterion: Same pipeline, tests and readings as fig5-dg-fos. Table 4 lists the 15 regions with raw p <= 0.01 (its title says p <= 0.05, but every row is <= 0.01) - DG-sg, DG-po, LGv, IGL, SNr, AUDp2/3, DTN, IO, AUDpo2/3, LGd, PST, LRN, STN, PGRNl and NB. Reproduced when SNr, STN and IGL, the three the text names, have raw p <= 0.01 with PACAPko higher, and the number of other regions with raw p <= 0.01 is within tolerance. Partially reproduced when one or two of SNr, STN and IGL meet the cutoff. The overlap of the regions found with the 15 of Table 4 is reported.

claims.statement: Table 4 gives, for each of the 15 regions with raw p <= 0.01, the Mann-Whitney U and PACAPko density as a percentage of PACAP fl/fl; every region but DTN (45%) is higher in PACAPko (167% to 326%).
claims.source: Table 4
claims.criterion: Same pipeline, tests and readings as fig5-dg-fos; U is that of the PACAPko sample. The Figure 5 legend gives the sample per region - 8 PACAP fl/fl and 11 PACAPko hemispheres, except LGv (one PACAP fl/fl outlier removed) and AUDp2/3 and STN (one PACAPko outlier removed). Reproduced when, under one reading, the direction (PACAPko above or below 100%) matches for all 13 regions and at least 10 of the 13 have both U and percentage within tolerance; partially reproduced when the direction matches for all and fewer are within tolerance; not reproduced when any direction differs. The threshold of 10 of 13 is this reader's, as the paper states no criterion for a table; every value is shown.

claims.statement: c-Fos IHC on sections confirms higher c-Fos-positive cell densities in PACAPko than wild-type mice in DG-sg, DG-po, STN and SNr, but not in IGL.
claims.source: Results 3.1, Association, paragraph 2; Figure 6A
claims.quote: We confirmed that PACAPko mice had significantly higher c-Fos positive cell counts during CleverSys testing in STN, SNr, DG-po, and DG-sg, but increased c-Fos in IGL was not confirmed ( Figure 6 ).
claims.criterion: From Methods 2.8 and the Figure 6 legend. Cells per square mm per region and animal from sum-projected 3-image z-stacks, counted with Find Maxima, at least 4 images per region and animal; unpaired t-tests (Student, as the integer degrees of freedom show) per region, Holm-Šídák across the five. How an animal's images are combined is not stated; readings are the mean density over images and total cells over total area. Reproduced when DG-sg, DG-po, STN and SNr are higher in PACAPko at adjusted p < 0.05 and IGL has adjusted p >= 0.05 (absence, on the paper's test).

claims.statement: Tamoxifen in adulthood depletes Adcyap1 transcript in hypothalamus, hippocampus and cerebellum of CAG-Cre/Esr1::PACAP fl/fl mice.
claims.source: Results 3.2, Adult and early postnatal KO, paragraph 2; Figure 7A
claims.quote: In both adult- and early postnatally-induced Cre-positive mice, Adcyap1 levels were significantly reduced in hypothalamus, hippocampus, and cerebellum
claims.criterion: From the Figure 7 legend and Methods 2.4. Relative Adcyap1 by 2^-ddCt against Gapdh, triplicate wells per sample; unpaired t-tests per region (Welch, as the fractional degrees of freedom show), Holm-Šídák across the three regions. The reference for ddCt (the Cre-negative group mean) is the standard choice and does not change the test. Reproduced when all three regions are lower in Cre-positive mice at adjusted p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Tamoxifen on postnatal days 1 to 3 depletes Adcyap1 transcript in hypothalamus, hippocampus and cerebellum of adult CAG-Cre/Esr1::PACAP fl/fl mice.
claims.source: Results 3.2, Adult and early postnatal KO, paragraph 2; Figure 7B
claims.quote: In postnatally-induced animals, multiple unpaired t-tests with Holm-Šídák correction for multiple tests show significant Adcyap1 depletion following tamoxifen
claims.criterion: As fig7a-adult-induction-adcyap1, for the postnatally induced mice. Reproduced when all three regions are lower in Cre-positive mice at adjusted p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Adult induction does not change the cPRG Xaf1 and slightly increases Pttg1 in cerebellum; postnatal induction changes neither Pttg1 nor Xaf1 in any region.
claims.source: Results 3.2, Adult and early postnatal KO, paragraph 2; Figure 7A, 7B
claims.quote: Adult-induced PACAP depletion did not alter expression of the cPRG Xaf1 , upregulated in constitutive PACAPko mice. Pttg1, downregulated in constitutive PACAPko mice ( 14 ), was slightly increased in cerebellum ( Figure 7a ). In mice induced on postnatal days 1, 2 and 3, no alterations in Pttg1 or Xaf1 transcription were seen in any region ( Figure 7b ).
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test for Xaf1 or Pttg1. The test of the Adcyap1 panels of the same figure is used - per gene and induction age, Welch unpaired t-tests per region with Holm-Šídák across the three regions, 2^-ddCt against Gapdh. Whether the cerebellar Pttg1 increase was significant is not said; readings are (a) higher in Cre-positive at adjusted p < 0.05, (b) higher at unadjusted p < 0.05. Reproduced when Xaf1 (adult) and Pttg1 and Xaf1 (postnatal) have adjusted p >= 0.05 in every region, and adult cerebellar Pttg1 is higher under one reading; partially reproduced when only the absences hold.

claims.statement: PACAP knockout induced in adulthood or on postnatal days 1 to 3 does not change jumping, repetitive jumping, locomotion or cage-top hanging.
claims.source: Results 3.2, Adult and early postnatal KO, paragraph 2; Figure 8
claims.quote: PACAP knockout induced either in adulthood or in early postnatal life did not induce hyperlocomotion.
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, on the paper's test (Figure 8 legend). For each induction age, the four behaviours per mouse, a two-way ANOVA of genotype by behaviour, with Šídák's comparisons of genotype within each behaviour. Reproduced when, at both ages, the genotype effect and the interaction have p >= 0.05; not reproduced when either has p < 0.05. Effect sizes and the Šídák p-values are shown.

claims.statement: After 3 h restraint, a postnatally induced CAG-Cre/Esr1::PACAP fl/fl mouse shows very little Adcyap1 or Fos mRNA in the PVN, where its Cre-negative littermate shows abundant signal of both.
claims.source: Results 3.2, Early postnatal KO of PACAP abrogates c-Fos induction; Figure 9
claims.quote: In Cre positive animals, there was very little of either Adcyap1 or Fos signal ( Figure 9 ).
claims.criterion: The paper shows one mouse per genotype and reports no quantification or test. Measure open; readings are (a) the number of Fos-positive and of Adcyap1-positive cells in the PVN, (b) mean RNAscope signal in the PVN. Reproduced when, under both readings, Fos and Adcyap1 in the PVN are lower in the Cre-positive mouse than in its Cre-negative littermate.

claims.statement: Baf53b-Cre::PACAP fl/fl mice do not differ from PACAP fl/fl mice in jumping, repetitive jumping, travel distance or cage-top hanging.
claims.source: Results 3.2, Abrogation of Adcyap1 transcription in new-born neurons; Figure 10A
claims.quote: Baf53b-Cre:: PACAP fl/fl mice did not differ from PACAP fl/fl animals in jumping, repetitive jumping, travel distance, or hanging from cage top ( Figure 10a ).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, on the paper's test (Figure 10A legend). A two-way ANOVA of genotype by behaviour over the four behaviours, with Šídák's comparisons. Reproduced when the genotype effect and the interaction have p >= 0.05; not reproduced when either has p < 0.05. Effect sizes are shown.

claims.statement: Baf53b-Cre::PACAP fl/fl mice lose a smaller percentage of body weight than Cre-negative controls 24 h after a 3-h restraint.
claims.source: Results 3.2, Baf53-Cre-driven KO of PACAP in post-mitotic neurons abrogates weight loss; Figure 10B
claims.quote: Like constitutive PACAPko mice, Baf53b-Cre::PACAP fl/fl mice lost a significantly smaller percentage of weight than controls 24 hours after a 3-hour restraint stress
claims.criterion: From Methods 2.5 and the Figure 10B legend. Percent weight loss from the weight on the day of restraint to the weight 24 h after its start; an unpaired Student t-test (11 degrees of freedom). Reproduced when Cre-positive mice lose less weight at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In Baf53b-Cre::PACAP fl/fl mice, Adcyap1 transcripts are greatly diminished in glutamatergic neurons of the dentate gyrus (Slc17a7) and subthalamic nucleus (Slc17a6).
claims.source: Results 3.2, Baf53-Cre-driven KO, paragraph 1; Figure 10C
claims.quote: In-situ hybridization confirms the knockdown, showing greatly diminished Adcyap1 in neurons, identified by the expression of Slc17a7 , encoding Vglut1 or Slc17a6 , encoding Vglut2 ( Figure 10c )
claims.criterion: The paper shows images and reports no quantification. Measure open; readings are (a) the fraction of Slc17a7- or Slc17a6-positive cells that are Adcyap1-positive, (b) mean Adcyap1 signal within those cells, in the DG polymorph layer and STN. Reproduced when, under both readings, Adcyap1 is lower in Cre-positive than Cre-negative mice in both regions.

claims.statement: PACAPko mice from heterozygous dams (exposed to maternal placental PACAP) do not differ from PACAPko mice from homozygous PACAPko dams in jumping, travel distance, repetitive jumping or cage-top hanging.
