Reproduced when, under every reading, overlap with the isolation pattern is greater with chi-square p < 0.05; methods_underspecified when readings disagree.

claims.statement: Per recording, PVH MC4R consumption responses in NCD mice are small early in the meal (Z 0.12 +- 0.11) and larger late (0.86 +- 0.09); in HFD mice they are already high early (0.72 +- 0.09) and do not increase late (0.79 +- 0.09).
claims.source: Results, Feeding-related responses ... elevated early in a meal in HFD-fed animals, paragraph on response magnitude; Figure 1k
claims.quote: On average, neural responses were minimal in NCD-fed animals in early trials (Z-score (NCD early) = 0.12 ± 0.11), but exhibited a robust increase in late trials ... (Z-score (NCD late) = 0.86 ± 0.09) ... (Z-score (HFD early) = 0.72 ± 0.09), with no further increase observed throughout the meal (Z-score (HFD late) = 0.79 ± 0.09)
claims.criterion: Cohort 1, 60-trial sessions with at least 30 triggered trials (39 NCD, 33 HFD). Early and late values per recording as in the opening comment, under each window W (0-10, 1-10, 1-9 s) and each Z reading (Z1, Z2). Reproduced when, under one combination, all four means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when no combination puts all four in tolerance but under one NCD late is above NCD early and HFD early is above NCD early. All combinations are shown.

claims.statement: In a linear mixed-effects model of recording-level responses with mouse as a random intercept, HFD early-meal responses exceed NCD early-meal responses and the diet by meal-phase interaction is significant.
claims.source: Figure 1k legend; Methods, Statistical analysis
claims.quote: Linear mixed-effects model (LME), p(NCD early vs. HFD early) < 0.001, p(Diet x Meal phase) < 0.001
claims.criterion: The Methods model, Value ~ Diet * Meal phase + (1 | Mouse), statsmodels mixedlm with its defaults (REML), on two rows per recording (early, late), Diet reference NCD. The Methods say this model was used for "Fig. 1 i"; the legend places it on Fig. 1k, the recording-level panel, which is followed. Early meal as the reference level is read from the legend's "p(NCD early vs. HFD early)". Reproduced when, under one W and Z combination of fig1k-early-late-recordings, the HFD coefficient is positive with p < 0.001 and the interaction is negative with p < 0.001; partially reproduced when both hold at p < 0.05 only. All combinations are shown.

claims.statement: Per mouse, every NCD mouse increases its response from early to late in the meal (Z 0.19 +- 0.24 to 0.91 +- 0.13), while HFD mice do not change (0.73 +- 0.19 to 0.80 +- 0.20).
claims.source: Results, Feeding-related responses ... elevated early in a meal in HFD-fed animals, paragraph on response magnitude; Figure 1l
claims.quote: all individual NCD-fed animals exhibited an overall increase in consumption-related neural responses in the late meal phase (Z-score (NCD early) = 0.19 ± 0.24, Z-score (NCD late) = 0.91 ± 0.13)) ... This pattern was consistent across all subjects (Z-score (HFD early) = 0.73 ± 0.19, Z-score (HFD late) = 0.80 ± 0.20)
claims.criterion: Mouse values are the mean of each mouse's recording values (Methods, heatmaps and legend "by combining the sessions for each mouse"), under each W and Z reading. The legend's test is a paired, two-tailed t-test between early and late per diet; the p-values are shown only in the figure, not read here. Reproduced when, under one combination, the four means are within tolerance, all 6 NCD mice have late above early, the NCD paired t-test has p < 0.05, and the HFD paired t-test has p >= 0.05; partially reproduced when the tests come out so but a mean is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: With a longer response window of 1 to 20 s after the cue, HFD mice still show no change in response from early to late in the meal.
claims.source: Results, Feeding-related responses ... elevated early in a meal in HFD-fed animals, paragraph on response magnitude; Supplementary Figure 1i
claims.quote: HFD-fed animals did not show a change in response from early to late in the meal when considering a longer window of 0–20 s post tone
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The Results say 0-20 s and the legend 1-20 s post-cue; both windows are run. Mouse values (6 NCD, 5 HFD mice) under each Z reading; the legend's test, a two-way ANOVA (diet x meal phase) with Tukey HSD across the four diet and phase groups. Reproduced when the Tukey comparison of HFD early against HFD late has p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The difference is reported either way, as is the NCD early-late comparison.

claims.statement: Expressed as dF/F, HFD mice have stronger consumption responses than NCD mice at the start of the meal, and these persist to the end of the feeding bout.
claims.source: Results, Feeding-related responses ... elevated early in a meal in HFD-fed animals, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 1h
claims.quote: at the start of the meal, HFD-fed animals exhibited stronger feeding-evoked neural responses than NCD-fed animals, and these acute responses persisted until the end of the feeding bout
claims.criterion: No test is reported. Per-recording mean dF/F0 in the response window (each W reading), early and late meal, cohort 1. Reproduced when, under one window, the HFD early-meal mean exceeds the NCD early-meal mean and the HFD late-meal mean is at least as high as the HFD early-meal mean minus its s.e.m. over recordings.

claims.statement: Despite calorie matching, HFD mice consume less Ensure than NCD mice, per recording session and per mouse.
claims.source: Results, Feeding-related responses ... elevated early in a meal in HFD-fed animals, paragraph 2; Figure 1g, h
claims.quote: Despite calorie matching to ensure comparable acute hunger states (Fig. 1 d), the HFD animals consumed less Ensure volume during the experimental recordings (Fig. 1 g, h)
claims.criterion: Cohort 1. Unpaired, two-tailed Student's t-test (equal variances, scipy default), as the legend states, on per-session totals (g) and per-mouse means (h). The volume is the recorded total Ensure consumed (Methods, "The total consumed Ensure throughout the experiment was noted"); where it is not available, the number of triggered trials times ~50 uL (Methods) is the reading used, and said. The paper does not say whether sessions with fewer than 30 triggered trials are in panel g; both sets are run. Reproduced when the HFD mean is lower with p < 0.05 in both g and h under one session set; partially reproduced when in one of them.

claims.statement: During food restriction, HFD mice are about 30% heavier than NCD mice.
claims.source: Results, Feeding-related responses ... elevated early in a meal in HFD-fed animals, paragraph 2; Figure 1c
claims.quote: HFD-fed mice were ~ 30% heavier than the NCD-fed mice
claims.criterion: Cohort 1 body weights during the recording period. The paper does not say which days or how they are averaged; readings are (a) the mean over recording days per mouse, then over mice; (b) the mean over all recording-day weights pooled. Reproduced when one reading is within tolerance; partially reproduced when HFD is heavier by 20% to 40%.

claims.statement: Both NCD and HFD mice reduce their licking from the early to the late phase of the session.
claims.source: Results, Feeding-related responses ... elevated early in a meal in HFD-fed animals, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 1c, d
claims.quote: Both NCD- and HFD-fed animals steadily reduced their licking rates from early to late phases of the session
claims.criterion: Supp. Fig. 1d measure, per mouse, the area under the post-cue lick-rate curve normalized to the pre-tone baseline lick rate, early against late meal. Open details, each run as a reading. Normalization is (a) subtraction of or (b) division by the mean lick rate of the 10 s before the tone; the AUC window is (i) 1-10 s post tone (the Methods' reward-window lick rate) or (ii) 0-50 s (the whole post-cue trace); the test is (x) unpaired two-tailed t-test (Supp. Fig. 1d legend) or (y) paired two-tailed t-test (Methods list Supp. Fig. 1d under paired tests). Reproduced when all readings give late below early with p < 0.05 in both diets; partially reproduced when that holds in one diet under all readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when readings disagree.

claims.statement: Food-seeking locomotion is negligible in HFD mice compared with NCD mice, and falls further near the end of the meal.
claims.source: Results, Feeding-related responses ... elevated early in a meal in HFD-fed animals, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 1e
claims.quote: Compared to NCD-fed animals, food-seeking-related locomotion was negligible in HFD-fed animals ... and it was further reduced to a minimum level late near the end of the meal
claims.criterion: No test is reported. Per mouse mean running speed over triggered trials, early and late meal, cohort 1. The window is not given in the Supp. Fig. 1e legend or the Methods; readings are (a) the whole trial, 10 s before to 50 s after the tone, and (b) the 10 s before the tone (the pre-cue period of Supp. Fig. 2g). Reproduced when, under every reading, the HFD mean over mice is below the NCD mean in both phases and the HFD late mean is below the HFD early mean; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. Per-mouse values are shown.

claims.statement: In 90-trial sessions NCD mice consume Ensure in 70.1 +- 2.1 trials and HFD mice in 52.9 +- 1.98 trials.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 1; Figure 2b
claims.quote: NCD-fed mice consumed Ensure during 70.1 ± 2.1 out of 90 possible trials, whereas HFD-fed animals only consumed Ensure during 52.9 ± 1.98 out of 90 trials
claims.criterion: Cohort 2, 90-trial sessions, mean over recordings. The legend names an unpaired, two-tailed Student's t-test; its p is shown only in the figure, not read here, and the text does not call the difference significant. Sessions included are open; readings are (a) all 90-trial sessions, (b) those with at least 30 triggered trials (the Methods default, and 59/54 is the count of Fig. 2a-e), (c) those with at least 15 (Fig. 2f-s). Reproduced when, under one reading, both means are within tolerance and the Student's t-test gives p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Per recording, the change in response from early to late in the meal is 0.52 +- 0.09 in NCD mice and only 0.12 +- 0.08 in HFD mice.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 1; Figure 2c
claims.quote: in NCD-fed animals, excitatory responses increased over the meal, with a positive mean change in Z-score (ΔZ-score) between early and late in the meal of 0.52 ± 0.09. However, in HFD-fed animals, the increase was minimal (ΔZ-score = 0.12 ± 0.08; Fig. 2 c)
claims.criterion: Cohort 2, recordings with at least 30 triggered trials (59 NCD, 54 HFD). Delta Z-score under D5 and D15, each W (1-9, 1-10 s) and Z reading. The legend's test is an unpaired two-tailed Student's t-test. Reproduced when, under one combination, both means are within tolerance and the t-test gives NCD above HFD with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when the t-test holds but a mean is out of tolerance. All combinations are shown.

claims.statement: Per mouse, the early-to-late change in response is 0.56 +- 0.10 in NCD mice and 0.28 +- 0.09 in HFD mice.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 1; Figure 2d
claims.quote: Similar results were observed across individual animals (ΔZ-score: NCD = 0.56 ± 0.10, HFD = 0.28 ± 0.09) (Fig. 2 d)
claims.criterion: As fig2c-delta-z-recordings, with each mouse's value the mean of its recordings' delta Z-scores (legend, "averaged across sessions"), 7 NCD and 7 HFD mice, unpaired two-tailed Student's t-test. Reproduced when, under one combination, both means are within tolerance and NCD is above HFD with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when the means hold and the test does not.

claims.statement: Throughout the 90-trial meal NCD mice lick at a higher rate during the cue than HFD mice; NCD licking begins to decline after about 50 trials and HFD licking after about 20.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 2; Figure 2e
claims.quote: Throughout the meal, NCD-fed animals exhibited higher licking vigor than HFD-fed animals (Fig. 2 e). In NCD-fed animals, licking vigor began to decline steadily after ~ 50 trials ... in HFD-fed animals, licking vigor began to decline much earlier, after only ~ 20 trials
claims.criterion: Cue lick rate is licks per second in the 0-1 s tone window (Methods), triggered trials only, per trial index 1 to 90, averaged across mice (legend) of recording means, cohort 2 recordings with at least 30 triggered trials. "Throughout" has two readings, NCD above HFD (a) at every trial index both groups have data or (b) in every 15-trial block. Onset of decline is not defined; readings are (i) the trial index of the maximum of the curve smoothed with a 15-trial moving mean, (ii) the first trial after which the 15-trial moving mean stays below the mean of the first 15 trials. Reproduced when NCD is higher under one reading and both onsets are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when NCD is higher and the NCD onset is later than the HFD onset but the onsets are out of tolerance.

claims.statement: Sessions with smaller meals have lower lick rates early in the meal; initial cue lick rates span 4 to 5.5 licks/s across NCD meal-size groups and 2 to 5.7 licks/s across HFD groups.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 3; Figure 2f-j, p
claims.quote: Sessions with smaller meal sizes (fewer total triggered trials and lower caloric intake) exhibited lower lick rates early in the meal (i.e., the initial lick rate during the cue was 4–5.5 licks/s for NCD mice versus 2–5.7 licks/s for HFD mice)
claims.criterion: Cohort 2 sessions with at least 15 triggered trials, grouped by triggered trials (15-29, 30-44, 45-59, 60-74, 75-90). "Initial lick rate" is open; readings are (a) the group mean cue lick rate of the first triggered trial, (b) of the first 15 triggered trials. Reproduced when, under one reading, the lowest and highest group means of each diet are within tolerance of the reported bounds and, in each diet, the smallest meal-size group has a lower mean than the largest.

claims.statement: The mid-meal cue lick rate correlates positively with meal size in both NCD and HFD sessions.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 6; Figure 2p
claims.quote: lick rate early in the meal positively correlated with the number of trials triggered in the session for both diet groups (Fig. 2 p)
claims.criterion: Pearson correlation (legend) per diet over recordings with at least 15 triggered trials, of meal size (triggered trials) with the cue lick rate averaged over the 15th to 29th triggered trial (legend); the Results' "early in the meal" (first 15 triggered trials) is a reading too. Reproduced when, under one reading, r > 0 with p < 0.05 in both diets; partially reproduced in one.

claims.statement: In sessions of 45 to 74 triggered trials, where early licking vigor is comparable between groups, HFD mice still have larger PVH MC4R responses early in the meal than NCD mice.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraphs 4 and 5; Figure 2g, h, l, m
claims.quote: Critically, despite both HFD- and NCD-fed mice having similar licking vigor early during a session (e.g., Fig. 2 h), HFD-fed mice still showed elevated PVH MC4R responses in the early trials (e.g., Fig. 2 m)
claims.criterion: No test is reported. Within the 45-59 and 60-74 meal-size groups, the mean over recordings of the early-meal response (first 15 triggered trials, each W and Z reading) and of the early-meal cue lick rate. Reproduced when, under one combination, in both groups the HFD early response mean exceeds the NCD mean by more than the sum of their s.e.m.s while the HFD and NCD early lick-rate means differ by less than the sum of their s.e.m.s; partially reproduced when that holds in one group.

claims.statement: In HFD sessions, mid-meal PVH MC4R responses correlate negatively with meal size (r = -0.46, p = 0.001).
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 6; Figure 2q
claims.quote: the PVH MC4R responses in HFD-fed animals negatively correlated with meal size (HFD: r = − 0.46, p = 0.001)
claims.criterion: Mid-meal response is the mean response over the 15th to 29th triggered trial (legend), each W and Z reading; recordings with at least 15 triggered trials (Results, "in sessions with at least 15 triggered trials"), and with at least 30 as a reading (Methods default). Reproduced when, under one combination, r is within tolerance and p < 0.05; partially reproduced when r < 0 with p < 0.05 but out of tolerance. The NCD correlation is reported.

claims.statement: In HFD mice, absolute body weight on the recording day correlates positively with mid-meal Z-scored responses.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 7; Figure 2r
claims.quote: We found that absolute body weight positively correlated with mid-meal Z-scored MC4R activity for HFD mice, indicating that heavier HFD mice exhibit stronger neuronal activation during the meal (Fig. 2 r)
claims.criterion: Pearson correlation (legend) over HFD recordings of the recording-day body weight with the mid-meal response, under the readings of fig2q-midmeal-response-meal-size. Reproduced when, under one reading, r > 0 with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when r > 0 and p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: In HFD mice, meal length (triggered trials) correlates negatively with absolute body weight.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 7; Figure 2s
claims.quote: meal length (i.e. the number of triggered trials) correlated negatively with absolute body weight in HFD-fed animals (Fig. 2 s)
claims.criterion: Pearson correlation (legend) over HFD recordings, with at least 15 and, as a reading, at least 30 triggered trials. Reproduced when, under one reading, r < 0 with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when r < 0 and p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Ensure volume consumed correlates robustly with the number of triggered trials in both diet groups, so meal size is defined as triggered trials.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 2a
claims.quote: there was a robust correlation between volume of Ensure consumed and number of triggered trials for both NCD- and HFD-fed animals
claims.criterion: No test is named; Pearson correlation, the paper's test for its other meal-size correlations (Fig. 2p-s), per diet over cohort 2 recordings with a recorded Ensure volume. Reproduced when r > 0 with p < 0.05 in both diets.

claims.statement: Across sessions, the within-meal change in response correlates with meal size with r = -0.34 (p = 0.012) in NCD mice and r = 0.26 (p = 0.048) in HFD mice. The sentence calls the NCD correlation positive and the HFD one negative, opposite to the printed signs.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 9; Supplementary Figure 2h
claims.quote: This analysis revealed a positive correlation in the NCD-fed group and a negative correlation in the HFD-fed group (NCD: r = − 0.34, p = 0.012, HFD: r = 0.26, p = 0.048)
claims.criterion: Per diet over cohort 2 recordings, Pearson correlation of triggered trials with the delta Z-score, read as the legend's late-meal minus early-meal mean (D15) and as the Methods' D5, each W and Z reading. Reproduced when, under one combination, both r are within tolerance with p < 0.05. If instead the signs come out as the sentence's words (NCD positive, HFD negative, both p < 0.05), partially reproduced, noting that the words and numbers disagree.

claims.statement: HFD mice show reduced locomotion, but locomotion does not correlate with meal size.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 8; Supplementary Figure 2f, g
claims.quote: Although HFD-fed animals exhibited reduced locomotion, this did not correlate with meal size (Supplementary Fig. 2f, g)
claims.criterion: The paper names no test for either part. Locomotion is the mean running speed in the pre-cue period (Supp. Fig. 2g legend) over triggered trials, per recording. Reduced locomotion holds when the HFD mean over recordings is below the NCD mean. The absence of a correlation is judged with Pearson correlation of triggered trials against locomotion per diet (the paper's test for its other meal-size correlations, a choice recorded as a deviation); reproduced when p >= 0.05 in both diets and HFD locomotion is lower; not reproduced when either correlation has p < 0.05. Locomotion after reward (1-10 s) is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Pre-Ensure spontaneous signal variability correlates weakly with absolute body weight in HFD mice.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 10; Supplementary Figure 2i, j
claims.quote: Our analysis revealed a weak correlation when assessing absolute body weight for HFD-fed animals (Supplementary Fig. 2 j)
claims.criterion: Variability is a rolling standard deviation of dF/F0 in the period before the first Ensure delivery, averaged per recording; the rolling window length and the F0 for this continuous trace are not given anywhere. Readings for the window are 1 s, 10 s and 60 s, and F0 is the mean of the pre-Ensure period. Pearson correlation over HFD recordings with recording-day body weight. Reproduced when all readings give p < 0.05 with |r| below 0.5 (the paper's "weak"); blocked as methods_underspecified when readings disagree.

claims.statement: NCD females show slightly larger early-meal responses than males, a difference more pronounced in HFD mice.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 11; Supplementary Figure 2k
claims.quote: NCD-fed females exhibited slightly larger neural responses than males early in the meal ... a trend that was even more pronounced in HFD-fed animals
claims.criterion: No test is reported. Mean over recordings of the early-meal response (first 15 triggered trials) for M-NCD, F-NCD, M-HFD, F-HFD (26, 33, 31, 23 recordings), each W and Z reading. Reproduced when, under one combination, F exceeds M in both diets and the F minus M difference is larger in HFD than in NCD.

claims.statement: An additional overnight fast does not significantly alter licking or PVH MC4R response dynamics in either diet group.
claims.source: Results, HFD alters neural and behavioral responses ..., paragraph 12; Supplementary Figure 2l-p
claims.quote: However, additional fasting did not significantly alter licking or PVH MC4R response dynamics for either group (Supplementary Fig. 2l–p)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence for which the paper names no test. Fasted against nonfasted recordings within each diet (NCD 28 and 31, HFD 23 and 31), on the mean cue lick rate over triggered trials, the early-meal response and the delta Z-score (D15), each W and Z reading. Readings for the test are (a) an unpaired two-tailed Student's t-test on recordings, the paper's test for recording comparisons in Fig. 2b-c, and (b) a linear mixed-effects model, measure ~ fasting + (1 | Mouse), the paper's model for repeated sessions. Reproduced when every reading gives p >= 0.05 for every measure in both diets; not reproduced when every reading finds some effect at p < 0.05; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. Effect sizes are reported.

claims.statement: HFD mice needed more training sessions than NCD mice to reach stable task performance.
claims.source: Methods, Behavioral training on wheels; Supplementary Figure 2q
claims.quote: Although HFD mice required more sessions to reach stable task performance (Supplementary Fig. 2q)
claims.criterion: Unpaired two-tailed Student's t-test (Methods, statistical analysis, item 3) on the number of training sessions per mouse. Reproduced when HFD is higher with p < 0.05. Testable only if training sessions are in the dataset.

claims.statement: After switching from HFD to NCD, early-meal PVH MC4R responses fall from their level on HFD toward NCD levels, while HFD->HFD mice keep high early-meal responses.
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraphs 2 and 5; Figure 3h
claims.quote: PVH MC4R neuron responses remained attenuated relative to prior responses while on HFD for most of the experiment (Fig. 3 f, h)
claims.criterion: Early-meal response per recording (first 15 triggered trials, W 1-9 and 1-10 s, each Z reading), recordings with at least 30 triggered trials, six groups (NCD->NCD, HFD->NCD, HFD->HFD, each before and after the switch). The legend's test, a two-way ANOVA (condition x phase) with Tukey HSD across the six groups. Reproduced when, under one combination, HFD->NCD after is below HFD->NCD before with Tukey p < 0.05 and HFD->HFD after is not below HFD->HFD before at p < 0.05; partially reproduced when HFD->NCD after is lower but not significantly. The before-switch HFD groups against NCD->NCD are reported.

claims.statement: After the diet switch, NCD->NCD mice show a significant increase in response from early to late in the meal, while HFD->NCD mice show only a slight, nonsignificant increase.
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraph 4; Figure 3i; Supplementary Figure 3i
claims.quote: The HFD → NCD group displayed an intermediate pattern between the HFD → HFD and NCD → NCD groups, with a slight but nonsignificant increase in PVH MC4R responses across the meal
claims.criterion: Second-diet recordings. Two tests the paper names, both run. (1) The Fig. 3i LME, Value ~ C(Condition, Treatment('NCD|NCD')) * Meal phase + (1 | Mouse) on two rows per recording; within-group early-late effects are the meal-phase coefficient with each group in turn as reference. (2) The Supp. Fig. 3i paired two-tailed t-test on mouse means. The NCD->NCD increase is reproduced when both give late above early with p < 0.05 under one W and Z combination. The HFD->NCD part is a claim of absence, judged on these two tests; reproduced when neither finds p < 0.05 and the late mean is above the early mean, not reproduced when both do, and blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. HFD->HFD is reported.

claims.statement: After the switch, the per-mouse early-to-late change in response is 0.37 +- 0.03 in NCD->NCD, 0.14 +- 0.05 in HFD->NCD and -0.05 +- 0.07 in HFD->HFD mice; it is significantly smaller in HFD->HFD.
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraph 4; Figure 3j
claims.quote: we observed a significantly smaller increase in neural responses across trials in the HFD → HFD group ... six weeks of NCD exposure in formerly HFD-fed animals failed to fully restore this effect to NCD levels (ΔZ-score: NCD → NCD = 0.37 ± 0.03, HFD → NCD = 0.14 ± 0.05, HFD → HFD = − 0.05 ± 0.07)
claims.criterion: Second-diet recordings with at least 30 triggered trials; mouse values are means of recording delta Z-scores, D5 (the Methods name Fig. 3j) and D15, each W and Z reading. One-way ANOVA with Tukey HSD (legend). Reproduced when, under one combination, the three means are within tolerance and HFD->HFD is below NCD->NCD with Tukey p < 0.05; partially reproduced when the order NCD->NCD > HFD->NCD > HFD->HFD holds and the Tukey test does, with means out of tolerance.

claims.statement: After the switch, HFD->NCD mice consume as much Ensure per session as NCD->NCD mice and significantly more than HFD->HFD mice.
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraph 4; Figure 3k
claims.quote: the HFD → NCD group consumed a volume of Ensure comparable to the NCD → NCD group and significantly higher than the HFD → HFD group during individual recording sessions (Fig. 3 k)
claims.criterion: Ensure volume per recording (recorded total; triggered trials times ~50 uL as a reading where the total is absent), six groups (three conditions before and after), two-way ANOVA (condition x phase) with Tukey HSD (legend). Whether recordings with fewer than 30 triggered trials are included is open; both sets are run. Reproduced when, under one set, HFD->NCD after exceeds HFD->HFD after with p < 0.05 and the Tukey test of HFD->NCD after against NCD->NCD after gives p >= 0.05; partially reproduced when only the first holds.

claims.statement: In the second diet phase, HFD->HFD mice stop consuming Ensure early, never exceeding 60 triggered trials.
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraph 2; Figure 3d, g
claims.quote: The HFD → HFD group maintained high early-meal PVH MC4R responses (Fig. 3 d, g, h) and ceased to engage in Ensure consumption even earlier in the session, never exceeding 60 triggered trials
claims.criterion: Over all second-phase HFD->HFD 90-trial recordings. Reproduced when no session has more than 60 triggered trials; partially reproduced when no more than one of the 23 sessions does.

claims.statement: After at least six weeks on NCD, formerly HFD mice lick with more vigor during the cue, a reinstated motivation to consume food.
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraph 2; Figure 3c; Supplementary Figure 3f
claims.quote: After at least six subsequent weeks on NCD, these same animals displayed an increase in licking vigor during cue presentation (Fig. 3 c (bottom right panel), Supplementary Fig. 3f)
claims.criterion: No test is reported. Cue lick rate (0-1 s) over triggered trials per trial index, averaged across HFD->NCD recordings with at least 30 triggered trials (Supp. Fig. 3f legend), before against after the switch. Reproduced when the after curve's mean over trials 1-90 (each trial index weighted equally, indices with data in both phases) is above the before curve's and the mean over recordings of each recording's mean cue lick rate is higher after as well.

claims.statement: NCD mice switched to HFD for 6 weeks keep their response dynamics, with a significant early-to-late increase in response after the switch, comparable to the change before it, and stable licking vigor.
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraphs 3 and 4; Supplementary Figure 3a-d, h
claims.quote: the NCD → HFD 6w group retained their response properties, exhibiting comparable changes in response magnitude before (NCD) and after the diet switch (HFD 6w ) between early and late meal stages, despite a significant weight gain after the diet switch
claims.criterion: Supp. Fig. 3c (1-9 s) and 3d (1-19 s) windows, each Z reading; mouse means of early and late meal responses, paired two-tailed t-test (legend), in the NCD phase and the HFD6w phase. The text calls only the second-phase increase significant; "comparable" before the switch is read as the same paired test also giving late above early with p < 0.05 in the NCD phase. Reproduced when late exceeds early with p < 0.05 in both phases under one Z reading in the 1-9 s window; partially reproduced when in the HFD6w phase only. Licking stability is reported as the mean cue lick rate per phase, not judged.

claims.statement: NCD->HFD6w mice gain significant body weight over the 6-week HFD phase, while HFD->NCD mice do not lose weight (a slight, nonsignificant gain).
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraphs 3, 4 and 7; Supplementary Figure 3j
claims.quote: these animals showed a significant increase in body weight during the 6-week HFD phase (Supplementary Fig. 3j)
claims.criterion: The Methods model, per condition, body weight ~ phase + (1 | Mouse) on recording-day weights, statsmodels mixedlm. Reproduced when the NCD->HFD6w phase effect is positive with p < 0.05 and the HFD->NCD phase effect has p >= 0.05 and is not negative with p < 0.05 (absence, judged on this model); partially reproduced when only the first holds.

claims.statement: In the second diet phase, mid-meal responses correlate positively with weight gain in NCD->HFD6w mice (r = 0.53, p = 0.001) and also in NCD->NCD mice (r = 0.46, p = 0.003).
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraph 6; Supplementary Figure 3m (text) or 3n (legend)
claims.quote: we observed a strong positive correlation (r = 0.53, p = 0.001) between mid-meal neural responses and the diet-induced weight gain in the NCD → HFD 6w group during the second diet phase ... we also observed a positive correlation in the NCD → NCD group (r = 0.46, p = 0.003)
claims.criterion: Per second-phase recording, mid-meal response (15th-29th triggered trial, each W and Z reading) against weight on the recording day (C) relative to weight at the start of ad libitum feeding (A), as the Supp. Fig. 3n legend defines it (the text cites panel m, whose legend is meal size). "Relative to" is read as C - A and as C / A. Reproduced when, under one combination, both r are within tolerance with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when both are positive with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In the second diet phase, absolute body weight does not predict meal length in NCD->NCD or NCD->HFD6w mice.
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraph 6; Supplementary Figure 3l
claims.quote: absolute body weight does not predict meal length in animals exposed to NCD or HFD 6w during the second meal phase (Supplementary Fig. 3l)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence; the test is Pearson correlation, read from the linear fits of the legend and the paper's correlations in this section. Per group, second-phase recordings, triggered trials against recording-day body weight. Reproduced when p >= 0.05 in both groups; not reproduced when either has p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In HFD->NCD mice, meal length correlates negatively with weight change, so mice that lost more weight before the session tended to eat larger meals; neural responses do not correlate with weight change.
claims.source: Results, Effects of diet switching ..., paragraph 7; Supplementary Figure 3p, q
claims.quote: In the HFD → NCD group, we observed no correlation with neural responses (Supplementary Fig. 3j, p), but a significant negative correlation between meal length and weight change, indicating that animals that lost more weight before the session tended to have larger meals
claims.criterion: Second-phase HFD->NCD recordings. Weight change is open; the text gives body weight relative to (a) the maximum ad libitum weight or (b) the weight before HFD exposure, and the legend relative to the start of ad libitum feeding (A); each as a difference and as a ratio. Pearson correlation of triggered trials with weight change. The "no correlation with neural responses" is cited to Supp. Fig. 3p, whose legend correlates mid-meal response with meal size, while the text pairs it with weight change; both are run, mid-meal response (15th-29th triggered trial, each W and Z reading) against (i) weight change and (ii) triggered trials. Reproduced when, under one weight-change reading, the first has r < 0 with p < 0.05 and the neural correlations have p >= 0.05 under both (i) and (ii); partially reproduced when the first holds and only one of (i) and (ii) has p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Below and near the electroporation threshold (43 to 570 V/cm, 1-us pulses), the membrane depolarizes at the cathode-facing pole and hyperpolarizes at the anode-facing pole, polarization decreases from the poles towards the equator, and it scales proportionally with field strength, as the Schwan equation describes.
claims.source: Figure 1, 43 to 570 V/cm; Results 3.1, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Electric pulses below and near the electroporation threshold produce a well-known spatial pattern of membrane polarization, such as in Fig. 1, 43–570 V/cm. The membrane depolarizes at the cathode-facing membrane pole and hyperpolarizes at the opposite, anode-facing pole. Polarization gradually decreases from the poles towards the cell equator, and scales up proportionally with the electric field strength
claims.criterion: Figure 1 shows one cell, which the paper does not identify; the test uses the Di-8-ANEPPS 1-us escalation cells (Fig. 4B, n = 5), collapsed profiles and pole values as in the common method, at each field strength from 43 to 570 V/cm. The paper gives no test for the pattern; the parts are read as follows. (1) Sign, the mean cathodic pole dF is above zero and the mean anodic pole dF below zero at every strength. (2) Decrease to the equator, the mean |dF| of each pole arc is larger than that of +-5 degree arcs at the two equator points (90 degrees from the poles; the paper defines no equator arc, and the +-5 degree width is taken from the pole arcs of Methods 2.3) at every strength from 150 V/cm (at 43 V/cm the paper reports bleaching of about 5% dF, Results 3.2, comparable to the signal). (3) Proportional scaling, a linear regression (Grapher, Methods 2.5) of the per-cell pole dF on field strength over 43 to 570 V/cm is significant at p < 0.05 at each pole. "Proportionally" also implies a line through zero, which the paper does not test; the regression intercept and the pole dF per 100 V/cm at each strength are reported. Background readings (a) and (b) of the header both run. Reproduced when (1) to (3) hold under both; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1-us pulses, polarization grows with field strength up to 570 V/cm; at 780 V/cm the cathodic pole stops increasing and dims, and at 1000 to 1400 V/cm the poles show reduced or absent polarization while regions nearer the equator stay polarized and may polarize more than the poles.
claims.source: Figure 1 and its legend; Results 3.1, paragraph 1
claims.quote: At a higher electric field strength of 780 V/cm, polarization at the cathodic pole does not further increase but dims out, indicating a less efficient charging of the partially permeabilized membrane. Still stronger electric fields produce a distinct pattern of reduced or absent polarization at the poles ... while regions closer to the equator remain relatively intact and may polarize more than the poles
claims.criterion: Figure 1 shows images of one cell, which the paper does not identify; the test uses the Di-8-ANEPPS 1-us escalation cells (Fig. 4B, n = 5), collapsed profiles and pole values as in the common method. Reproduced when (1) the mean cathodic pole dF at 780 V/cm is not above that at 570 V/cm, and (2) at 1400 V/cm the largest mean dF of the cathode-facing hemisphere lies outside the +-5 degree polar arc. The paper gives no test or threshold for this; the two conditions are read from the legend's wording. Background readings (a) and (b) both run.

claims.statement: With FluoVolt, pole dF rose with field strength until it saturated at 66% (255 mV) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole and -83% (-320 mV) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole; stronger fields did not increase the anodic response and decreased the cathodic one.
claims.source: Figure 2A; Results 3.2, paragraph 2
claims.quote: ΔF increased proportionally to the electric field strength until reaching apparent saturation at 66% ΔF (255 mV IMP) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole, and −83% ΔF (−320 mV IMP) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole. Further escalation of the electric field strength did not increase the dye response at the anodic pole and even decreased it at the cathodic pole.
claims.criterion: Per-image pole dF (common method, Fig. 2 measure) over the 60 pulse images of each set, averaged per cell and then across the 4 cells. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance, the cathodic means at 570 and 780 V/cm are not above that at 360 V/cm by more than the tolerance, the anodic means at 780 to 1400 V/cm are not more negative than at 570 V/cm by more than the tolerance, and the cathodic means at 1000 to 1400 V/cm are below that at 360 V/cm.

claims.statement: FluoVolt measurements were stable without pulses (no significant bleaching or photosensitization), and the response within each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses, even at 1000 V/cm and above.
claims.source: Figure 2A; Results 3.2, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Without PEF (first 40 datapoints, or ~ 7 s in each set), measurements were stable, indicating no significant photosensitization or dye bleaching ... but the dye response in each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses applied
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The paper reports no test for it; the test it names for Fig. 2 is a 2-tailed paired t-test at p < 0.05 over cells (n = 4). Per set and pole, compare the start and the end of the 60 pulse images, and of the 40 baseline images. The paper does not say how many images form the start and the end; readings (a) the first and the last image, (b) the first 10 and the last 10 images. Reproduced when under both readings no set at 1000 to 1400 V/cm, and no baseline, shows a significant change; not reproduced when under both readings any does; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The size of each change is reported.

claims.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS dF kept increasing with field strength up to 570 V/cm at both poles.
claims.source: Figure 2B; Results 3.2, paragraph 3
claims.quote: This dye has a lower sensitivity to membrane polarization (note the vertical scale different from Fig. 2A), but ΔF kept climbing up to the electric field strength of 570 V/cm at both cell poles.
claims.criterion: Per-image pole dF averaged over each set's 60 pulse images, per cell, then across the 5 cells. Reproduced when the mean |dF| at each pole increases at every step from 43 to 570 V/cm.

claims.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS responses were somewhat affected by bleaching, most visibly at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added about 5% to dF at the anodic pole and took about 5% from it at the cathodic pole.
claims.source: Figure 2B; Results 3.2, paragraph 3
claims.quote: The responses were somewhat affected by dye bleaching (particularly noticeable at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added ~5% to ΔF at the anodic pole and reduced it by the same ~5% at the cathodic pole.
claims.criterion: Per-image pole dF of the Fig. 2 measure (F0 the mean of the 40 baseline images), 43 V/cm set, mean across the 5 cells. The paper does not say how the shift was measured. As F0 is the baseline mean, a steady loss of F makes dF drift downward through the set at both poles, which matches the text's signs. Readings for the shift (a) per pole, the mean dF of the last 10 pulse images (91 to 100) minus that of the first 10 pulse images (41 to 50); (b) the offset common to both poles, the mean of the cathodic and the anodic set-mean dF over the 60 pulse images (the text says the shift is the same ~5% at both poles, and the field response is opposite in sign at the two poles). Reproduced when under one reading the shift (at each pole, for reading a) is within tolerance. The tolerance is the protocol's 10% of the reported value.

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS, responses to pulses of 780 V/cm and above decreased gradually within each set of 60 images.
claims.source: Figure 2B; Results 3.2, paragraph 3
claims.quote: In addition, responses to PEFs at and above 780 V/cm decreased gradually in each set of 60 images, consistent with expectations of adding membrane damage by additional electroporation pulses in each set
claims.criterion: The paper gives no test; it reads a direction. Per set, the mean |dF| at the start and at the end of the 60 pulse images, averaged across the 5 cells; start and end as in fig2a-fluovolt-stable, readings (a) first and last image, (b) first 10 and last 10. The Results do not name the pole; the Discussion, point (a), cites Fig. 2B for a progressive decrease at the cathodic pole, so the cathodic pole is tested and the anodic pole is shown as a variant. Reproduced when under both readings the cathodic end is below the start for every set from 780 to 1400 V/cm; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The 2-tailed paired t-test of Fig. 2 is reported for each set.

claims.statement: Repeated alternating sets at 150 and 230 V/cm (480 pulses and 800 flashes) gave dF responses constant within and between sets.
claims.source: Figure 2C and 2D; Results 3.2, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Repeated sets of PEFs at 150 and 230 V/cm, delivered in alternation, produced ΔF responses that stayed constant both within each set and between the sets (Fig. 2C and D).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the 2-tailed paired t-test at p < 0.05 of the Fig. 2 legend (n = 8). Per cell and set, the mean pole dF over the 60 pulse images (Fig. 2D); every set before the 1000 V/cm set is compared with the first set at the same field strength (the legend's dashed lines are the first-trial means), at each pole. Reproduced when none differs; not reproduced when any does. Within-set changes are shown as in fig2a-fluovolt-stable, as a variant.

claims.statement: At 1000 V/cm the cathodic pole dF fell from 40 +- 10% at the start of the set to 26.6 +- 8% at its end, a trend that was not statistically significant.
claims.source: Figure 2C; Results 3.2, paragraph 4
claims.quote: In contrast, at an electroporating field strength of 1000 V/cm, ΔF at the cathodic pole decreased from 40 ± 10% at the beginning of the set to 26.6 ± 8% at the end of it. Although not statistically significant (p > 0.05)
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e. Per-image cathodic pole dF; start and end are not defined, readings (a) the first and the last image of the 60, (b) the first 10 and the last 10 images. Reproduced when under one reading both values are within tolerance and the 2-tailed paired t-test gives p > 0.05.

claims.statement: Set-averaged dF stayed nearly constant before the 1000 V/cm exposure but was about 20% lower in the sets after it.
claims.source: Figure 2D and legend; Results 3.2, paragraph 4
claims.quote: ΔF values averaged across each set of 60 PEFs stayed nearly constant before the electroporation, but dropped by about 20% in the sets acquired after it (Fig. 2D, p < 0.05).
claims.criterion: Per cell and set, the mean pole dF over the 60 pulse images; each set after the 1000 V/cm set compared by a 2-tailed paired t-test (n = 8) with the sets before it at the same field strength. The legend's dashed lines mark the first-trial means, and the text compares with the sets before electroporation, which stayed nearly constant; readings for the reference (e) the first set, (f) the mean of all sets before 1000 V/cm, at the same field strength. The text does not say which pole or how the 20% is pooled; readings (a) cathodic pole, (b) anodic pole, (c) each post-1000 set separately, (d) the mean over the post-1000 sets. Reproduced when under one reading the reduction is within tolerance and at least one post-1000 set is significantly lower at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Fitted linearly through the origin over -150 to +150 mV IMPC, FluoVolt changes by 26% and Di-8-ANEPPS by 9.1% dF per 100 mV, with correlation coefficients 0.96 and 0.78.
claims.source: Figure 3 and legend; Results 3.3, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The correlation coefficients of the fits equaled 0.96 for FluoVolt and 0.78 for Di-8 ANEPPS (due to a lower signal-to-noise ratio), with respective slope coefficients of 26% and 9.1% ΔF per 100 mV of IMP.
claims.criterion: All 360 perimeter points of every cell in the 43 to 360 V/cm sets of 1-us pulses at 900 ns, dF against IMPC computed per cell and point (Eq. 1, tau from the fit of reference [20], an outside input). Points with IMPC from -150 to +150 mV fit by least squares through the origin (Grapher). Grapher's correlation coefficient for a fit through the origin is not defined in the paper; readings (a) Pearson r of dF with IMPC in that range, (b) the square root of the uncentred R2 of the fit through the origin. Radius readings (a) and (b) and background readings (a) and (b) of the header all run. Reproduced when the slopes are within tolerance and the correlation coefficients are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: FluoVolt departed from linearity from about +-200 mV IMPC, while Di-8-ANEPPS stayed nearly linear from -500 to +500 mV; so FluoVolt's early departure reflects its dynamic range, not electroporation.
claims.source: Figure 3 and legend; Results 3.3, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The actual measurements with FluoVolt gradually became non-linear already at ±200 mV, while those for Di-8-ANEPPS stayed essentially linear throughout the tested range from −500 to +500 mV.
claims.criterion: The paper judges this by eye from a LOESS smooth (Grapher, span not given) against the linear fit; it gives no threshold. Measure here, as the paper's figure compares them, the smoothed dF against the line through the origin of fig3-dye-sensitivity, over the same points. Readings for the smooth (a) LOESS with span 0.3, (b) 0.5, (c) 0.75, (d) means in 50-mV IMPC bins. The paper gives no span and no departure threshold; the spans and the band below are not from the paper. A departure is the smooth lying closer to zero than the line by more than 10% of the line's value. Reproduced when under every reading the FluoVolt smooth departs from the line at every |IMPC| from 220 mV (the paper's 200 mV plus 10%) to the end of the data on both sides, and the Di-8-ANEPPS smooth does not depart at any |IMPC| from 150 to 500 mV where the data have points (inside +-150 mV the line is fit to the same points, and near zero 10% of the line's value is smaller than the noise, so the test there would turn on noise alone).

claims.statement: FluoVolt measured and calculated IMP matched only at 43 and 150 V/cm; with stronger 1-us pulses the pole dF peaked at 71 +- 10% (cathodic) and -83.5 +- 5% (anodic), about +260 and -330 mV.
claims.source: Figure 4A; Results 3.4, paragraph 1
claims.quote: However, this assumption held only for the applied fields of 43 and 150 V/cm, where measured and calculated IMP matched. With stronger PEFs, maximum ΔF reached 71 ± 10% and −83.5 ± 5% at the cathodic and anodic poles, respectively.
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e. Collapsed pole dF per cell and field strength, mean across the 4 cells; the maximum is the largest mean |dF| over field strengths at each pole. Measured IMP (dF / 26%) compared with the cell's pole IMPC by Student's t-test at p < 0.05 (Methods 2.5, which does not say paired or unpaired; readings (a) 2-tailed paired, (b) 2-tailed unpaired). The paper judges the match from Fig. 4A and reports no test for it. Reproduced when both maxima are within tolerance, the test finds no difference at 43 and 150 V/cm at either pole, and finds measured below calculated at either pole at each of 230 V/cm and above. The test conditions are judged under both readings (a) and (b); the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: FluoVolt cathodic polarization fell from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45 to 50% at 1000 to 1400 V/cm.
claims.source: Figure 4A; Results 3.4, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Notably, polarization at the cathodic pole decreased from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45–50% at 1000–1400 V/cm, indicating that the more severe membrane damage prevented its polarization to the maximum.
claims.criterion: Collapsed cathodic pole dF, mean across the 4 cells, per field strength. The 360 V/cm tolerance is the paper's s.e. for the same 71% (Results 3.4, paragraph 1). Reproduced when the 360 V/cm value is within tolerance and each of the 1000, 1200 and 1400 V/cm values lies within 40.5 to 55%.

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1-us pulses, measured IMP fell below the calculated value at 570 V/cm, where dF peaked at 57 +- 14% (cathodic) and -55 +- 4% (anodic), over 600 mV.
claims.source: Figure 4B; Results 3.4, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The measured IMP decreased below the calculated value when the electric field reached 570 V/cm, concurrently with reaching the maximum ΔF of 57 ± 14% at the cathodic pole and − 55 ± 4% at the anodic pole. These values corresponded to membrane polarization by over 600 mV, which is twice the value measured with FluoVolt.
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e. Collapsed pole dF per cell and field strength, mean across the 5 cells. Reproduced when the largest mean |dF| at each pole occurs at 570 V/cm and is within tolerance, and measured IMP (dF / 9.1%) is below the pole IMPC at 570 V/cm by Student's t-test at p < 0.05 (at either pole) but not below it at 43 to 360 V/cm. Methods 2.5 does not say paired or unpaired; readings (a) 2-tailed paired, (b) 2-tailed unpaired. The test conditions are judged under both readings; the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. The paper reports no test for this comparison.

claims.statement: Averaged over only the first 10 of the 60 pulses, Di-8-ANEPPS cathodic polarization reached 66 +- 15% (710 +- 200 mV), so the 600-mV maximum is not the dye's limit.
claims.source: Figure 4B, dotted lines; Results 3.4, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Polarization measured this way reached 66 ± 15% (710 ± 200 mV) at the cathodic pole, suggesting that the 600-mV maximum, averaged from 60 PEFs, was not the dye limit but the actual IMP
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the paper's s.e. As the common method, with the polarization image collapsed from the first 10 of the 60 pulse images; mean across the 5 cells, largest over field strengths. Reproduced when within tolerance and above the 60-image maximum of fig4b-di8-limits.

claims.statement: Above 780 V/cm the pole IMP fell progressively with field strength, more at the cathodic pole; at 1400 V/cm the cathodic pole no longer charged and the anodic pole fell to about -30% dF (-330 mV).
claims.source: Figure 4B; Results 3.4, paragraph 4
claims.quote: As the electric field increased further, the IMP reached at the poles progressively decreased, and the reduction was more pronounced at the cathodic pole ... At 1400 V/cm, charging was no longer detectable at the cathodic pole (i.e., the membrane became fully permeable) and dropped to ~30% ΔF (~ −330 mV) at the anodic pole.
claims.criterion: Collapsed pole dF, mean across the 5 cells. Reproduced when (1) the mean |dF| at each pole decreases from 780 to 1000, 1200 and 1400 V/cm, (2) the fraction lost between 780 and 1400 V/cm is larger at the cathodic pole, (3) the cathodic pole dF at 1400 V/cm does not differ from zero by a one-sample t-test at p < 0.05 (the test of Methods 2.5), and (4) the anodic value is within tolerance.

claims.statement: At the apparent electroporation threshold of 570 V/cm and at 780 V/cm, permeabilization judged by the shortfall from the calculated IMP was about the same at the two poles.
claims.source: Figure 4B; Results 3.4, paragraph 4
claims.quote: At the apparent electroporation threshold of 570 V/cm, as well as with a more intense exposure at 780 V/cm, permeabilization at both poles (judged by the difference from the theoretical values) was approximately the same.
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The paper names no test for it; the test used is the Student's t-test of Methods 2.5 at p < 0.05, n = 5. Per cell, at 570 and at 780 V/cm, the measured pole IMP (collapsed pole dF / 9.1%) as a fraction of the cell's pole IMPC (Eq. 1), at each pole; cathodic against anodic fraction. Methods 2.5 does not say paired or unpaired; readings (a) 2-tailed paired, (b) 2-tailed unpaired. Reproduced when neither reading finds a difference at either strength; not reproduced when both find one at a strength; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. The two fractions are reported.

claims.statement: Membrane regions nearer the equator were unaffected by pole electroporation and followed the cosine dependence of the Schwan equation up to 1000 V/cm.
claims.source: Figure 4C and legend; Results 3.4, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Membrane areas closer to the equator ... appeared relatively unaffected and followed the cosine dependence predicted by Schwan formula up to 1000 V/cm (Fig. 4C).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence of a deviation. The paper names no test and no angular range for "closer to the equator". Measured IMP (dF / 9.1%) and IMPC per perimeter point, averaged per cell within arcs about the two equator points; readings (a) +-15 degrees, (b) +-30 degrees from the equator, on each side of each pole hemisphere. At 570, 780 and 1000 V/cm, measured against calculated by Student's t-test at p < 0.05 (Methods 2.5, n = 5), which the paper does not say is paired; readings (c) 2-tailed paired, (d) 2-tailed unpaired. Reproduced when no arc differs at any of these strengths under every combination of (a) or (b) with (c) or (d); not reproduced when some arc differs under every combination; blocked as methods_underspecified when the combinations disagree. The ratio of measured to calculated is reported.

claims.statement: With 0.3-us pulses at higher fields (357 to 3320 V/cm), imaged at 275 ns, the maximum dF was 53 +- 4% (about 600 mV) at both poles, as with 1-us pulses, and the response changed with field strength in the same way.
claims.source: Figure 4D; Results 3.4, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Contrary to the expectations, the results were similar to those with 1-μs pulses in Fig. 4B: the maximum ΔF reached was 53 ± 4% (~600 mV) at both cell poles. The pattern of how the response changed with increasing PEF strength was not different from that with 1-μs PEFs either.
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the paper's s.e. Collapsed pole dF per cell and field strength, mean across the 10 cells. Reproduced when the largest mean |dF| at each pole is within tolerance, and, as with 1-us pulses (fig4b-cathodic-asymmetry), the mean |dF| at both poles declines at the field strengths above the one giving the maximum, more at the cathodic pole. The paper gives no test for "not different"; none is applied.

claims.statement: With 1 mM Gd3+ the anodic pole charged to -864 +- 44 mV, against -542 +- 57 mV in parallel controls (p < 0.001).
claims.source: Figure 5A; Results 3.5, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Indeed, we found that 1 mM Gd3+ extended the range of membrane charging at the anodic pole down to −864 ± 44 mV (p < 0.001 compared to −542 ± 57 mV in parallel control experiments, Fig. 5A).
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e. Collapsed anodic pole dF converted to IMP (dF / 9.1%), per cell and field strength (150 to 1400 V/cm). Which datapoints are compared is not stated; readings (a) the most negative group mean over field strengths in each group, compared at those strengths, (b) the two groups at the same field strength, at the strength giving the Gd3+ minimum, (c) each cell's own most negative value. Two-tailed unpaired t-test. Reproduced when under one reading both values are within tolerance and p < 0.001.

claims.statement: With Gd3+, the measured IMP stayed nearly identical to IMPC down to -780 mV, so the Di-8-ANEPPS calibration holds at high IMPs.
claims.source: Figure 5A; Results 3.5, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Furthermore, measured IMP remained nearly identical to the theoretical IMPC down to −780 mV, indicating that the dye response remained linear and its calibration was valid even at high IMPs.
claims.criterion: A claim of absence of a deviation. Gd3+ group, anodic pole, every field strength whose mean IMPC is -780 mV or less negative; measured IMP against IMPC by Student's t-test at p < 0.05 (Methods 2.5, n = 7), which the paper does not say is paired; readings (a) 2-tailed paired, (b) 2-tailed unpaired. Reproduced when none differs under (a) and (b); not reproduced when any differs under both; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. The ratio of measured to calculated is reported. The Discussion, point (c), puts the linearity at about -700 mV; the test with -700 mV as the bound is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: At the cathodic pole Gd3+ cells reached 647 +- 44 mV, not significantly above controls, but Gd3+ prevented the decline of IMP with stronger fields.
claims.source: Figure 5A; Results 3.5, paragraph 2
claims.quote: At the cathodic pole, polarization in the presence of Gd3+ reached 647 ± 44 mV, a value not significantly higher than that in the control group without Gd3+. However, Gd3+ prevented the progressive decline in IMP as the electric field was increased.
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the paper's s.e. Collapsed cathodic pole IMP per cell and field strength. The comparison with controls is a claim of absence, judged on the 2-tailed t-test of the Fig. 5 legend at p < 0.05, Gd3+ (n = 7) against control (n = 5), with the readings for which datapoints of fig5a-gd-extends-anodic. "Prevented the progressive decline" has no test; read as the Gd3+ mean cathodic IMP at 1200 and 1400 V/cm being no lower than its maximum by more than the s.e., while the control mean declines from its maximum. Reproduced when the value is within tolerance, no reading finds Gd3+ significantly higher, and the decline condition holds.

claims.statement: Gd3+ and control data differ significantly for datapoints with IMPC below -700 mV and above 1200 mV.
claims.source: Figure 5A legend
claims.quote: Differences between Gd3+ and control group data are significant at p < 0.05 or better (2-tailed t-test) for datapoints below −700 mV and above 1200 mV.
claims.criterion: Datapoints are field strengths, placed by their mean IMPC (the x axis of Fig. 5A, which the "mV" bounds refer to). For each field strength and pole, measured IMP of the Gd3+ against the control cells by a 2-tailed unpaired t-test. The two groups' mean IMPC differ (Fig. 5A legend), and the legend does not say whose IMPC places a datapoint; readings (a) the Gd3+ group's, (b) the control group's, (c) the mean of the two. Reproduced when under every reading every datapoint with mean IMPC below -700 mV or above 1200 mV differs at p < 0.05; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: By Eq. (2), the effective membrane conductivity barely affects charging while it stays far below cytosol and medium conductivities; a 10-fold rise reduces IMP by about 2% and a 100-fold rise by 12%.
claims.source: Figure 5B; Results 3.5, paragraph 3
claims.quote: its 10-fold increase would go unnoticed, yielding just a ~2% IMP reduction, and a 100-fold increase would reduce IMP by just 12%.
claims.criterion: A computation from Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 (lambda_i 0.4 S/m, lambda_o 1.64 S/m, R 8 um, d 5 nm, intact lambda_m 3e-7 S/m); it uses no recordings. The reduction is relative to IMPC, readings (a) 1 - f/1.5, (b) 1 - f(lambda_m)/f(3e-7 S/m). Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation-induced effective membrane conductivity 2 to 3-fold.
claims.source: Figure 5C; Results 3.5, paragraph 4
claims.quote: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation- induced effective conductivity 2–3-fold.
claims.criterion: For each field strength and pole, the ratio of mean measured to mean calculated IMP in each group (Fig. 5C uses the datapoints of Fig. 5A, mean values), converted to effective conductivity through Eq. (2) as in fig5b-conductivity-calibration. Datapoints whose measured IMP is not below IMPC give no conductivity increase and are left out. Reproduced when more than half of the remaining datapoints have a control-to-Gd3+ ratio between 1.8 and 3.3.

claims.statement: A single 1-us pulse caused clear Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/cm, with the signal elevated through 5 min; the small rise at 780 V/cm was not significant.
claims.source: Figure 6A; Results 3.6, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Exposure to a single 1-μs pulse at escalating field strengths, from 0 to 1200 V/cm established a clear peak of Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/ cm, and Ca2+ signal remained elevated through the 5-min observation period (Fig. 6A). A subtle ΔF increase after exposure at 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not statistically significant.
claims.criterion: Fluo-4 dF (Methods 2.4), background-subtracted, F0 the mean before the pulse, 14 cells. The test is not named; the paper uses a one-sample t-test against zero for the pulse-train Ca2+ data (Results 3.6), applied here at p < 0.05. The window is not given; readings (a) the peak frame after the pulse, (b) the last 30 s of the recording. Reproduced when at 1000 and 1200 V/cm dF is significantly above zero under both windows, and at 780 V/cm it is not under either window (a claim of absence, judged on that test); blocked as methods_underspecified when the windows disagree.

claims.statement: After a train of sixty 1-us pulses at 6 Hz, 28% of cells responded strongly at 780 V/cm and nearly all at higher field strengths.
claims.source: Figure 6B; Results 3.6, paragraph 3
claims.quote: A strong Ca2+ response was recorded in 28% of cells exposed at 780 V/cm and in nearly all cells at higher intensities (Fig. 6B).
claims.criterion: Each cell exposed once; Fluo-4 dF as in Methods 2.4. The paper does not define a strong response. Readings (a) peak dF after the train above the mean plus 3 s.d. of the pre-train baseline of the same cell, (b) peak dF above 50%, (c) peak dF above 100%. Reproduced when, under one reading, the 780 V/cm fraction is within tolerance, at least 90% of cells respond at each higher strength, and the 650 V/cm fraction is 2 cells (5.9%).

claims.statement: At 650 V/cm only 2 cells (5.9%) responded strongly, yet the mean Ca2+ signal at the end of recording differed from zero (p < 0.001) and was marginally higher than at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05).
claims.source: Figure 6B; Results 3.6, paragraph 3
claims.quote: At 650 V/cm, only 2 cells (5.9%) showed a strong response, but the mean Ca2+ signal by the end of recording was significantly different from zero (p < 0.001, one sample t-test) and marginally higher than after exposure at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, single-tailed t-test).
claims.criterion: Fluo-4 dF per cell (Methods 2.4). "By the end of recording" is not defined; readings (a) the last frame, (b) the mean of the last 10 s, (c) the mean of the last 30 s. One-sample t-test against zero at 650 V/cm; one-tailed unpaired Student's t-test of 650 against 230 V/cm. Reproduced when under one reading both p-values are within their bounds.

claims.statement: The azimuthal profile of a 150 V/cm test pulse given 5 us after a conditioning pulse kept the cosine shape of an undamaged membrane after conditioning pulses up to 1000 V/cm, while after 1200 and 1400 V/cm charging at the poles was markedly reduced.
claims.source: Figure 7A and legend; Results 3.7, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Polarization still followed a cosine function after conditioning PEFs of up to 1000 V/cm. However, 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging by the test pulse at cell poles, indicating a persistent membrane permeabilization.
claims.criterion: Two-pulse sets with a 5-us interval only. Collapsed profiles of 360 points at 900 ns into the test pulse, Di-8-ANEPPS, n = 5 (Fig. 7A legend), as in the common method. The paper judges the shape by eye, fitting a cosine up to 1000 V/cm and LOESS for the last two graphs (legend), with the 150/150 cosine fit copied over the other graphs as the benchmark for an undamaged membrane. It gives no test for a departure from the cosine. The cosine form is taken from Eq. (1), dF = A cos(theta) with theta measured from the field direction, fit by least squares to the mean profile. What the profile is compared with has two readings the legend allows, (a) its own cosine fit, (b) the 150/150 benchmark cosine. A departure is a pole (+-5 degree arc) whose per-cell dF differs from the cosine's value there by a two-sided one-sample t-test at p < 0.05 (the t-test of the Fig. 7 legend). Reproduced when under both readings no pole departs at any conditioning strength up to 1000 V/cm and at least one pole is below the cosine at each of 1200 and 1400 V/cm; not reproduced when both readings fail; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The fraction of the cosine reached at each pole is reported.

claims.statement: Normalized to 150 V/cm, pole polarization during the conditioning pulse fell 1.5 times below linear scaling at 560 V/cm and 2-fold at 760 V/cm, and further at stronger fields (p < 0.01 for every point from 560 V/cm).
claims.source: Figure 7B, top panels; Results 3.7, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Actual measurements fell 1.5 times below this line for 560 V/cm PEFs, 2- fold for 760 V/cm PEFs, and diverged further for more intense PEFs (p < 0.01 for all datapoints ≥560 V/cm, one sample t-test).
claims.criterion: Data are those of Fig. 4B (Di-8-ANEPPS, 1-us pulses, no test pulse), as Results 3.7, paragraph 4 states; single-pulse sets inside the two-pulse recordings, if the dandiset holds them, are shown as a variant only. Pole dF as in fig4b-di8-limits, each strength as % of the 150 V/cm value, compared with the linear line (100% x E / 150 V/cm). Not stated whether normalization is per cell or of the means; readings (a) per cell, (b) of the means (the ratios), with the test per cell under both. Which pole is not stated; readings (c) each pole, (d) the mean of the poles. One-sample t-test of the per-cell values against the line. Reproduced when under one reading both ratios are within tolerance, the ratio at 1000 to 1400 V/cm exceeds 2, and every datapoint from 560 V/cm is below the line at p < 0.01.

claims.statement: A 150 V/cm test pulse 5 us after the conditioning pulse charged the poles as in undamaged cells after conditioning up to 760 V/cm, to about 80% (not significant) after 1000 V/cm, and to about 70% and 50% after 1200 and 1400 V/cm, a persistent permeabilization.
claims.source: Figure 7A and 7B, bottom panels; Results 3.7, paragraphs 3 and 5
claims.quote: However, 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging by the test pulse at cell poles, indicating a persistent membrane permeabilization ... In contrast, measurements 6 μs later (test pulse) did not differ from the control up to 760 V/cm strength of the conditioning PEF; they were at ~80% of the control reading after 1000 V/cm conditioning PEF but the difference was not statistically significant. Still more intense PEFs of 1200 and 1400 V/cm reduced charging by the test pulse to ~70% and ~ 50%, respectively (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, two-sided t-test).
claims.criterion: Two-pulse sets with a 5-us interval only (the paper's protocol). Collapsed pole dF at 900 ns into the test pulse, as % of the 150/150 V/cm value, n = 5. The test, from the Fig. 7 legend, is a two-sided t-test of the difference from the undamaged membrane; the legend does not say which form, readings (a) one-sample t-test of per-cell % values against 100%, (b) paired t-test of dF against the same cell's 150/150 value. Pole readings as in fig7b-charging-during-pulse. The points from 150 to 760 V/cm and at 1000 V/cm are claims of absence, judged on that test at p < 0.05; since the two forms are both the paper's test as written, the absence holds when neither finds a difference, fails when both do, and the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. Reproduced when the absence holds, and under one reading the three values are within tolerance and 1200 and 1400 V/cm meet their p bounds. The 1400 V/cm cathodic value that the paper drops as negative (Results 3.7, paragraph 6) is reported both ways.

claims.statement: Within 6 us of the electroporating pulse, effective membrane conductivity at the poles fell by a factor of about 10 (range 7 to 20) for most datapoints; the cathodic pole, more conductive during the pulse, no longer differed from the anodic pole at the test pulse.
claims.source: Figure 7C; Results 3.7, paragraph 7
claims.quote: Fig. 7C shows a profound reduction in the λm,eff within just 6 μs after the electroporating pulse. For most datapoints, it dropped by a factor of 10 (range: 7–20). While the cathodic pole became more conductive than the anodic pole during the electroporating pulse ... no difference between the poles was detected by the test pulse.
claims.criterion: As Methods 2.3 and Results 3.7 give it. From the mean values of fig7b-charging-during-pulse and fig7ab-test-pulse-recovery, each pole and field strength, the measured fraction (of the linear line, and of the 150/150 control) converted to effective conductivity through Eq. (2) as in fig5b-conductivity-calibration. The 1400 V/cm cathodic test value is left out if negative, and a test value above 100% is set to 100%, as the paper did. Datapoints with no conductivity increase during the conditioning pulse are left out. A test value of 100% maps to the intact 3e-7 S/m (full resealing, fig7c-full-reseal-mild), which gives a finite ratio far above 22; the paper's "most datapoints" leaves open whether these count, readings (a) left out, (b) counted as outside the range. Reproduced when more than half of the counted datapoints fall within 6.3 to 22 fold, the cathodic conductivity exceeds the anodic during the conditioning pulse at 1000 V/cm and above, and at the test pulse the cathodic and anodic dF do not differ at any conditioning strength by a two-sided paired t-test at p < 0.05 over the 5 cells (the t-test of the Fig. 7 legend, applied between the poles; a claim of absence). The paper gives no test for the pole comparison; the ratio of the two poles' test-pulse conductivities is reported.

claims.statement: After mildly electroporating 570 and 760 V/cm pulses the membrane resealed fully within 6 us; after stronger pulses a residual conductivity increase persisted.
claims.source: Figure 7C; Results 3.7, paragraph 7
claims.quote: For mildly electroporating PEFs of 570 and 760 V/cm, membrane resealed fully (within the accuracy of measurements) within just 6 μs. With more intense PEFs, the residual increased conductivity persisted for at least 6 μs, indicating the formation of more stable membrane lesions.
claims.criterion: Judged on the test of fig7ab-test-pulse-recovery. Reproduced when the test-pulse pole dF after 570 and 760 V/cm conditioning does not differ from the control (so the inferred effective conductivity is the intact value), after 1200 and 1400 V/cm it is significantly reduced at either pole, and after 1000 V/cm the mean is below 100% at both poles (the statement's "more intense PEFs" include 1000 V/cm, whose ~80% is not significant; Fig. 7C is computed from the mean values, Fig. 7 legend).

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1-us pulses, polarization grows with field strength up to 570 V/cm; at 780 V/cm the cathodic pole stops increasing and dims, and at 1000 to 1400 V/cm the poles show reduced or absent polarization while regions nearer the equator stay polarized and may polarize more than the poles.
claims.source: Figure 1 and its legend; Results 3.1, paragraph 1
claims.quote: At a higher electric field strength of 780 V/cm, polarization at the cathodic pole does not further increase but dims out, indicating a less efficient charging of the partially permeabilized membrane. Still stronger electric fields produce a distinct pattern of reduced or absent polarization at the poles ... while regions closer to the equator remain relatively intact and may polarize more than the poles
claims.criterion: Figure 1 shows images of one cell, which the paper does not identify; the test uses the Di-8-ANEPPS 1-us escalation cells (Fig. 4B, n = 5), collapsed profiles and pole values as in the common method. Reproduced when (1) the mean cathodic pole dF at 780 V/cm is not above that at 570 V/cm, and (2) at 1400 V/cm the largest mean dF of the cathode-facing hemisphere lies outside the +-5 degree polar arc. The paper gives no test or threshold for this; the two conditions are read from the legend's wording. Background readings (a) and (b) both run.

claims.statement: With FluoVolt, pole dF rose with field strength until it saturated at 66% (255 mV) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole and -83% (-320 mV) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole; stronger fields did not increase the anodic response and decreased the cathodic one.
claims.source: Figure 2A; Results 3.2, paragraph 2
claims.quote: ΔF increased proportionally to the electric field strength until reaching apparent saturation at 66% ΔF (255 mV IMP) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole, and −83% ΔF (−320 mV IMP) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole. Further escalation of the electric field strength did not increase the dye response at the anodic pole and even decreased it at the cathodic pole.
claims.criterion: Per-image pole dF (common method, Fig. 2 measure) over the 60 pulse images of each set, averaged per cell and then across the 4 cells. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance, the cathodic means at 570 and 780 V/cm are not above that at 360 V/cm by more than the tolerance, the anodic means at 780 to 1400 V/cm are not more negative than at 570 V/cm by more than the tolerance, and the cathodic means at 1000 to 1400 V/cm are below that at 360 V/cm.

claims.statement: FluoVolt measurements were stable without pulses (no significant bleaching or photosensitization), and the response within each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses, even at 1000 V/cm and above.
claims.source: Figure 2A; Results 3.2, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Without PEF (first 40 datapoints, or ~ 7 s in each set), measurements were stable, indicating no significant photosensitization or dye bleaching ... but the dye response in each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses applied
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The paper reports no test for it; the test it names for Fig. 2 is a 2-tailed paired t-test at p < 0.05 over cells (n = 4). Per set and pole, compare the start and the end of the 60 pulse images, and of the 40 baseline images. The paper does not say how many images form the start and the end; readings (a) the first and the last image, (b) the first 10 and the last 10 images. Reproduced when under both readings no set at 1000 to 1400 V/cm, and no baseline, shows a significant change; not reproduced when under both readings any does; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The size of each change is reported.

claims.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS dF kept increasing with field strength up to 570 V/cm at both poles.
claims.source: Figure 2B; Results 3.2, paragraph 3
claims.quote: This dye has a lower sensitivity to membrane polarization (note the vertical scale different from Fig. 2A), but ΔF kept climbing up to the electric field strength of 570 V/cm at both cell poles.
claims.criterion: Per-image pole dF averaged over each set's 60 pulse images, per cell, then across the 5 cells. Reproduced when the mean |dF| at each pole increases at every step from 43 to 570 V/cm.

claims.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS responses were somewhat affected by bleaching, most visibly at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added about 5% to dF at the anodic pole and took about 5% from it at the cathodic pole.
claims.source: Figure 2B; Results 3.2, paragraph 3
claims.quote: The responses were somewhat affected by dye bleaching (particularly noticeable at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added ~5% to ΔF at the anodic pole and reduced it by the same ~5% at the cathodic pole.
claims.criterion: Per-image pole dF of the Fig. 2 measure (F0 the mean of the 40 baseline images), 43 V/cm set, mean across the 5 cells. The paper does not say how the shift was measured. As F0 is the baseline mean, a steady loss of F makes dF drift downward through the set at both poles, which matches the text's signs.
