claims.statement: With 0.3-us pulses at higher fields (357 to 3320 V/cm), imaged at 275 ns, the maximum dF was 53 +- 4% (about 600 mV) at both poles, as with 1-us pulses, and the response changed with field strength in the same way.
claims.source: Figure 4D; Results 3.4, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Contrary to the expectations, the results were similar to those with 1-μs pulses in Fig. 4B: the maximum ΔF reached was 53 ± 4% (~600 mV) at both cell poles. The pattern of how the response changed with increasing PEF strength was not different from that with 1-μs PEFs either.
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the paper's s.e. Collapsed pole dF per cell and field strength, mean across the 10 cells. Reproduced when the largest mean |dF| at each pole is within tolerance, and, as with 1-us pulses (fig4b-cathodic-asymmetry), the mean |dF| at both poles declines at the field strengths above the one giving the maximum, more at the cathodic pole. The paper gives no test for "not different"; none is applied.

claims.statement: With 1 mM Gd3+ the anodic pole charged to -864 +- 44 mV, against -542 +- 57 mV in parallel controls (p < 0.001).
claims.source: Figure 5A; Results 3.5, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Indeed, we found that 1 mM Gd3+ extended the range of membrane charging at the anodic pole down to −864 ± 44 mV (p < 0.001 compared to −542 ± 57 mV in parallel control experiments, Fig. 5A).
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e. Collapsed anodic pole dF converted to IMP (dF / 9.1%), per cell and field strength (150 to 1400 V/cm). Which datapoints are compared is not stated; readings (a) the most negative group mean over field strengths in each group, compared at those strengths, (b) the two groups at the same field strength, at the strength giving the Gd3+ minimum, (c) each cell's own most negative value. Two-tailed unpaired t-test. Reproduced when under one reading both values are within tolerance and p < 0.001.

claims.statement: With Gd3+, the measured IMP stayed nearly identical to IMPC down to -780 mV, so the Di-8-ANEPPS calibration holds at high IMPs.
claims.source: Figure 5A; Results 3.5, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Furthermore, measured IMP remained nearly identical to the theoretical IMPC down to −780 mV, indicating that the dye response remained linear and its calibration was valid even at high IMPs.
claims.criterion: A claim of absence of a deviation. Gd3+ group, anodic pole, every field strength whose mean IMPC is -780 mV or less negative; measured IMP against IMPC by a 2-tailed paired t-test at p < 0.05 (n = 7; the Student's t-test of Methods 2.5). Reproduced when none differs; not reproduced when any does. The ratio of measured to calculated is reported.

claims.statement: At the cathodic pole Gd3+ cells reached 647 +- 44 mV, not significantly above controls, but Gd3+ prevented the decline of IMP with stronger fields.
claims.source: Figure 5A; Results 3.5, paragraph 2
claims.quote: At the cathodic pole, polarization in the presence of Gd3+ reached 647 ± 44 mV, a value not significantly higher than that in the control group without Gd3+. However, Gd3+ prevented the progressive decline in IMP as the electric field was increased.
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the paper's s.e. Collapsed cathodic pole IMP per cell and field strength. The comparison with controls is a claim of absence, judged on the 2-tailed t-test of the Fig. 5 legend at p < 0.05, Gd3+ (n = 7) against control (n = 5), with the readings for which datapoints of fig5a-gd-extends-anodic. "Prevented the progressive decline" has no test; read as the Gd3+ mean cathodic IMP at 1200 and 1400 V/cm being no lower than its maximum by more than the s.e., while the control mean declines from its maximum. Reproduced when the value is within tolerance, no reading finds Gd3+ significantly higher, and the decline condition holds.

claims.statement: Gd3+ and control data differ significantly for datapoints with IMPC below -700 mV and above 1200 mV.
claims.source: Figure 5A legend
claims.quote: Differences between Gd3+ and control group data are significant at p < 0.05 or better (2-tailed t-test) for datapoints below −700 mV and above 1200 mV.
claims.criterion: Datapoints are field strengths, placed by their mean IMPC (the x axis of Fig. 5A, which the "mV" bounds refer to). For each field strength and pole, measured IMP of the Gd3+ against the control cells by a 2-tailed unpaired t-test. Reproduced when every datapoint with mean IMPC below -700 mV or above 1200 mV differs at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: By Eq. (2), the effective membrane conductivity barely affects charging while it stays far below cytosol and medium conductivities; a 10-fold rise reduces IMP by about 2% and a 100-fold rise by 12%.
claims.source: Figure 5B; Results 3.5, paragraph 3
claims.quote: its 10-fold increase would go unnoticed, yielding just a ~2% IMP reduction, and a 100-fold increase would reduce IMP by just 12%.
claims.criterion: A computation from Eq. (2) with the constants of Methods 2.3 (lambda_i 0.4 S/m, lambda_o 1.64 S/m, R 8 um, d 5 nm, intact lambda_m 3e-7 S/m); it uses no recordings. The reduction is relative to IMPC, readings (a) 1 - f/1.5, (b) 1 - f(lambda_m)/f(3e-7 S/m). Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation-induced effective membrane conductivity 2 to 3-fold.
claims.source: Figure 5C; Results 3.5, paragraph 4
claims.quote: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation- induced effective conductivity 2–3-fold.
claims.criterion: For each field strength and pole, the ratio of mean measured to mean calculated IMP in each group (Fig. 5C uses the datapoints of Fig. 5A, mean values), converted to effective conductivity through Eq. (2) as in fig5b-conductivity-calibration. Datapoints whose measured IMP is not below IMPC give no conductivity increase and are left out. Reproduced when more than half of the remaining datapoints have a control-to-Gd3+ ratio between 1.8 and 3.3.

claims.statement: A single 1-us pulse caused clear Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/cm, with the signal elevated through 5 min; the small rise at 780 V/cm was not significant.
claims.source: Figure 6A; Results 3.6, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Exposure to a single 1-μs pulse at escalating field strengths, from 0 to 1200 V/cm established a clear peak of Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/ cm, and Ca2+ signal remained elevated through the 5-min observation period (Fig. 6A). A subtle ΔF increase after exposure at 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not statistically significant.
claims.criterion: Fluo-4 dF (Methods 2.4), background-subtracted, F0 the mean before the pulse, 14 cells. The test is not named; the paper uses a one-sample t-test against zero for the pulse-train Ca2+ data (Results 3.6), applied here at p < 0.05. The window is not given; readings (a) the peak frame after the pulse, (b) the last 30 s of the recording. Reproduced when at 1000 and 1200 V/cm dF is significantly above zero under both windows, and at 780 V/cm it is not under reading (a) (a claim of absence, judged on that test).

claims.statement: After a train of sixty 1-us pulses at 6 Hz, 28% of cells responded strongly at 780 V/cm and nearly all at higher field strengths.
claims.source: Figure 6B; Results 3.6, paragraph 3
claims.quote: A strong Ca2+ response was recorded in 28% of cells exposed at 780 V/cm and in nearly all cells at higher intensities (Fig. 6B).
claims.criterion: Each cell exposed once; Fluo-4 dF as in Methods 2.4. The paper does not define a strong response. Readings (a) peak dF after the train above the mean plus 3 s.d. of the pre-train baseline of the same cell, (b) peak dF above 50%, (c) peak dF above 100%. Reproduced when, under one reading, the 780 V/cm fraction is within tolerance, at least 90% of cells respond at each higher strength, and the 650 V/cm fraction is 2 cells (5.9%).

claims.statement: At 650 V/cm only 2 cells (5.9%) responded strongly, yet the mean Ca2+ signal at the end of recording differed from zero (p < 0.001) and was marginally higher than at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05).
claims.source: Figure 6B; Results 3.6, paragraph 3
claims.quote: At 650 V/cm, only 2 cells (5.9%) showed a strong response, but the mean Ca2+ signal by the end of recording was significantly different from zero (p < 0.001, one sample t-test) and marginally higher than after exposure at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, single-tailed t-test).
claims.criterion: Fluo-4 dF per cell (Methods 2.4). "By the end of recording" is not defined; readings (a) the last frame, (b) the mean of the last 10 s, (c) the mean of the last 30 s. One-sample t-test against zero at 650 V/cm; one-tailed unpaired Student's t-test of 650 against 230 V/cm. Reproduced when under one reading both p-values are within their bounds.

claims.statement: Normalized to 150 V/cm, pole polarization during the conditioning pulse fell 1.5 times below linear scaling at 560 V/cm and 2-fold at 760 V/cm, and further at stronger fields (p < 0.01 for every point from 560 V/cm).
claims.source: Figure 7B, top panels; Results 3.7, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Actual measurements fell 1.5 times below this line for 560 V/cm PEFs, 2- fold for 760 V/cm PEFs, and diverged further for more intense PEFs (p < 0.01 for all datapoints ≥560 V/cm, one sample t-test).
claims.criterion: Data are those of Fig. 4B (Di-8-ANEPPS, 1-us pulses, no test pulse), pole dF as in fig4b-di8-limits, each strength as % of the 150 V/cm value, compared with the linear line (100% x E / 150 V/cm). Not stated whether normalization is per cell or of the means; readings (a) per cell, (b) of the means (the ratios), with the test per cell under both. Which pole is not stated; readings (c) each pole, (d) the mean of the poles. One-sample t-test of the per-cell values against the line. Reproduced when under one reading both ratios are within tolerance, the ratio at 1000 to 1400 V/cm exceeds 2, and every datapoint from 560 V/cm is below the line at p < 0.01.

claims.statement: A 150 V/cm test pulse 5 us after the conditioning pulse charged the poles as in undamaged cells after conditioning up to 760 V/cm, to about 80% (not significant) after 1000 V/cm, and to about 70% and 50% after 1200 and 1400 V/cm, a persistent permeabilization.
claims.source: Figure 7A and 7B, bottom panels; Results 3.7, paragraphs 3 and 5
claims.quote: Polarization still followed a cosine function after conditioning PEFs of up to 1000 V/cm. However, 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging by the test pulse at cell poles, indicating a persistent membrane permeabilization ... In contrast, measurements 6 μs later (test pulse) did not differ from the control up to 760 V/cm strength of the conditioning PEF; they were at ~80% of the control reading after 1000 V/cm conditioning PEF but the difference was not statistically significant. Still more intense PEFs of 1200 and 1400 V/cm reduced charging by the test pulse to ~70% and ~ 50%, respectively (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, two-sided t-test).
claims.criterion: Collapsed pole dF at 900 ns into the test pulse, as % of the 150/150 V/cm value. The test, from the Fig. 7 legend, is a two-sided t-test of the difference from the undamaged membrane; readings (a) one-sample t-test of per-cell % values against 100%, (b) paired t-test of dF against the same cell's 150/150 value. Pole readings as in fig7b-charging-during-pulse. The 570/760 and 1000 V/cm points are claims of absence, judged on that test at p < 0.05. Reproduced when under one reading the three values are within tolerance, 1200 and 1400 V/cm meet their p bounds, and no point up to 1000 V/cm differs. The 1400 V/cm cathodic value that the paper drops as negative (Results 3.7, paragraph 6) is reported both ways.

claims.statement: Within 6 us of the electroporating pulse, effective membrane conductivity at the poles fell by a factor of about 10 (range 7 to 20) for most datapoints; the cathodic pole, more conductive during the pulse, no longer differed from the anodic pole at the test pulse.
claims.source: Figure 7C; Results 3.7, paragraph 7
claims.quote: Fig. 7C shows a profound reduction in the λm,eff within just 6 μs after the electroporating pulse. For most datapoints, it dropped by a factor of 10 (range: 7–20). While the cathodic pole became more conductive than the anodic pole during the electroporating pulse ... no difference between the poles was detected by the test pulse.
claims.criterion: As Methods 2.3 and Results 3.7 give it. From the mean values of fig7b-charging-during-pulse and fig7ab-test-pulse-recovery, each pole and field strength, the measured fraction (of the linear line, and of the 150/150 control) converted to effective conductivity through Eq. (2) as in fig5b-conductivity-calibration. The 1400 V/cm cathodic test value is left out if negative, and a test value above 100% is set to 100%, as the paper did. Datapoints with no conductivity increase during the conditioning pulse are left out. A test value of 100% maps to the intact 3e-7 S/m (full resealing, fig7c-full-reseal-mild), which gives a finite ratio far above 22; the paper's "most datapoints" leaves open whether these count, readings (a) left out, (b) counted as outside the range. Reproduced when more than half of the counted datapoints fall within 6.3 to 22 fold, the cathodic conductivity exceeds the anodic during the conditioning pulse at 1000 V/cm and above, and at the test pulse the cathodic and anodic dF do not differ at any conditioning strength by a two-sided paired t-test at p < 0.05 over the 5 cells (the t-test of the Fig. 7 legend, applied between the poles; a claim of absence). The paper gives no test for the pole comparison; the ratio of the two poles' test-pulse conductivities is reported.

claims.statement: After mildly electroporating 570 and 760 V/cm pulses the membrane resealed fully within 6 us; after stronger pulses a residual conductivity increase persisted.
claims.source: Figure 7C; Results 3.7, paragraph 7
claims.quote: For mildly electroporating PEFs of 570 and 760 V/cm, membrane resealed fully (within the accuracy of measurements) within just 6 μs. With more intense PEFs, the residual increased conductivity persisted for at least 6 μs, indicating the formation of more stable membrane lesions.
claims.criterion: Judged on the test of fig7ab-test-pulse-recovery. Reproduced when the test-pulse pole dF after 570 and 760 V/cm conditioning does not differ from the control (so the inferred effective conductivity is the intact value), and after 1200 and 1400 V/cm it is significantly reduced at either pole.

claims.statement: After a conditioning pulse of up to 1000 V/cm, polarization by the 150 V/cm test pulse 5 us later still follows a cosine of the angle to the field, while 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning pulses markedly reduce charging at the cell poles.
claims.source: Results, 3.7, paragraph 3; Figure 7A
claims.quote: Polarization still followed a cosine function after conditioning PEFs of up to 1000 V/cm. However, 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging by the test pulse at cell poles, indicating a persistent membrane permeabilization.
claims.criterion: Per conditioning strength, the test-pulse dF profile over the 360 perimeter points, averaged over the n = 5 cells (Methods 2.3; Fig. 7A legend), is fit by least squares with a cosine of the angle to the field (A cos(theta - phi)), as Fig. 7A fits it; the benchmark is the fit after the 150 V/cm conditioning pulse (Fig. 7A legend). "Follows a cosine" has no stated measure. It is not read as matching the benchmark amplitude, since the paper puts the 1000 V/cm test response at ~80% of control and still calls it a cosine. Readings - (a) the mean pole dF (+-5 degree arcs) at each pole lies within the s.e. outline of the profile (Fig. 7A legend, gray outline) around the strength's own cosine fit at that pole; (b) pole dF does not differ from the benchmark by the two-sided t-test of Fig. 7B at p < 0.05 (readings of that test as in fig7b-test-pulse-unchanged-to-760). "Markedly hindered" at 1200 and 1400 V/cm is pole dF below the benchmark at p < 0.05 by that test (as in fig7b-test-pulse-reduced-1200-1400). Reproduced when, under a reading, every conditioning strength up to 1000 V/cm follows a cosine and 1200 and 1400 V/cm are hindered at the poles. The cosine amplitude and R^2 of every strength are reported.

claims.statement: During the electroporating pulse, pole polarization falls below the linear scaling expected for an undamaged membrane, 1.5-fold below at 560 V/cm and 2-fold at 760 V/cm and further at stronger fields, significantly for every strength of 560 V/cm or more.
claims.source: Results, 3.7, paragraph 5; Figure 7B, top panel
claims.quote: Actual measurements fell 1.5 times below this line for 560 V/cm PEFs ... and diverged further for more intense PEFs (p < 0.01 for all datapoints ≥560 V/cm, one sample t-test)
claims.criterion: The paper takes these data from the Fig. 4B experiments (Di-8-ANEPPS, single 1-us pulses, imaged at 900 ns, n = 5), so they may be in another dandiset. Pole dF in +-5 degree arcs, from collapsed baseline and polarization images (Methods 2.3); dF at 150 V/cm taken as 100%, linear expectation E/150 x 100% (Fig. 7B legend). Open, with readings. Which pole the 1.5 and 2-fold refer to - (a) cathodic, (b) anodic, (c) the mean of both. How the 150 V/cm normalization is applied - (i) per cell, each cell's values divided by its own 150 V/cm value, and the one-sample t-test of the per-cell values against E/150 x 100%; (ii) on group means, with the one-sample t-test of per-cell dF x 150/E against the group mean at 150 V/cm. Two-sided (Fig. 7B legend, "two-way"). Reproduced when, under one pole reading and one normalization reading, both ratios are within tolerance and every strength of 560 V/cm or more differs from the line at p < 0.01.

claims.statement: Polarization by the test pulse 6 us after the conditioning pulse does not differ from the undamaged control for conditioning pulses up to 760 V/cm, and is at about 80% of control after 1000 V/cm, a difference that is not significant.
claims.source: Results, 3.7, paragraph 5; Figure 7B, bottom panel
claims.quote: measurements 6 μs later (test pulse) did not differ from the control up to 760 V/cm strength of the conditioning PEF; they were at ~80% of the control reading after 1000 V/cm conditioning PEF but the difference was not statistically significant
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a two-sided t-test at p < 0.05 for the difference from the undamaged membrane, n = 5 (Results 3.7; Fig. 7B legend). Pole dF in +-5 degree arcs at 900 ns into the test pulse; the test pulse after a 150 V/cm conditioning pulse is the control, taken as 100% (group mean; the legend draws the control as a gray band between dashed lines, so it keeps its spread). The legend does not say whether the two-sided t-test pairs cells, which each received every conditioning strength; readings (i) paired t-test of per-cell dF against the same cell's control dF; (ii) unpaired two-sample t-test. A one-sample t-test of per-cell normalized values against 100% does not fit the legend's control band and is shown as a variant only. Each pole is tested. Reproduced when no conditioning strength up to 760 V/cm differs from control, and 1000 V/cm does not differ either; not reproduced when any does. When readings (i) and (ii) give different outcomes the claim is methods_underspecified, with both shown. The 80% value is checked under the pole readings (a) cathodic, (b) anodic, (c) mean of both. Effect sizes are reported.

claims.statement: Conditioning pulses of 1200 and 1400 V/cm reduce charging by the test pulse 6 us later to about 70% and 50% of control (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01).
claims.source: Results, 3.7, paragraph 5; Figure 7B, bottom panel
claims.quote: Still more intense PEFs of 1200 and 1400 V/cm reduced charging by the test pulse to ~70% and ~ 50%, respectively (p < 0.05 and p < 0.01, two-sided t-test)
claims.criterion: Measures and test readings as in fig7b-test-pulse-unchanged-to-760 (test (i) paired or (ii) unpaired; pole (a) cathodic, (b) anodic, (c) mean of both). Reproduced when, under one combination, both values are within tolerance and the 1200 and 1400 V/cm differences reach p < 0.05 and p < 0.01; partially reproduced when both are reduced and significant but a value is outside tolerance.

claims.statement: Effective membrane conductivity at the poles falls by about 10-fold (range 7 to 20) within 6 us after the electroporating pulse, for most datapoints.
claims.source: Results, 3.7, paragraphs 6 and 7; Figure 7C
claims.quote: Fig. 7C shows a profound reduction in the λm,eff within just 6 μs after the electroporating pulse. For most datapoints, it dropped by a factor of 10 (range: 7–20).
claims.criterion: As the paper does it (Results 3.7, paragraph 6; Fig. 7C legend), lm,eff is interpolated from the group mean values of Fig. 7B, per pole and conditioning strength, with Eq. (2) and the stated parameters. During the conditioning pulse the ratio of measured to calculated IMP is the mean pole dF over the linear expectation E/150 x 100%; at the test pulse it is the mean pole dF over the control (100%). A negative dF is omitted and a value above 100% is set to 100%, as the paper did. The fold drop is conditioning lm,eff over test lm,eff, for strengths of 560 V/cm and above. "Most datapoints" is read as more than half of the pole and strength pairs for which the test lm,eff is above the intact value (a ratio below 100%; a pair with the test at 100% has no finite fold). Reproduced when the median of those folds is within 9 to 11 and more than half lie within 6.3 to 22 (the range widened by 10% of each bound); partially reproduced when the median is within 6.3 to 22 but not 9 to 11. Every fold is reported.

claims.statement: After mildly electroporating pulses (570 and 760 V/cm) the membrane reseals fully within 6 us, while after stronger pulses increased conductivity persists for at least 6 us; the cathodic pole is more conductive than the anodic during the pulse, but the test pulse finds no difference between the poles.
claims.source: Results, 3.7, paragraph 7; Figure 7C
claims.quote: While the cathodic pole became more conductive than the anodic pole during the electroporating pulse (Fig. 7B, see also Figs. 1 and 4B–D), no difference between the poles was detected by the test pulse. For mildly electroporating PEFs of 570 and 760 V/cm, membrane resealed fully (within the accuracy of measurements) within just 6 μs. With more intense PEFs, the residual increased conductivity persisted for at least 6 μs
claims.criterion: lm,eff as in fig7c-conductivity-drops-10-fold. Full reseal at 570 and 760 V/cm is judged as the paper judges it, by the test-pulse pole dF not differing from control in the two-sided t-test (fig7b-test-pulse-unchanged-to-760). Residual conductivity after the stronger pulses (1000, 1200 and 1400 V/cm; the abstract says residual conductivity persisted after PEFs above 780 V/cm) is judged as the paper judges it in Fig. 7C, by the test-pulse lm,eff lying above the intact value (test dF below 100% of control) at each of them; the significance of fig7b-test-pulse-reduced-1200-1400 is reported, and the paper calls the 1000 V/cm reduction not significant. Pole difference during the pulse - the cathodic lm,eff exceeds the anodic at most conditioning strengths of 1000 V/cm and above (Results 3.4, paragraph 4, gives both poles about equally permeabilized at 570 and 780 V/cm and the cathodic reduction larger above them; the cathodic 1400 V/cm point counts as higher if its dF is negative, which the paper reads as no charging). No pole difference at the test pulse - a two-sided paired t-test of cathodic against anodic normalized test dF, per strength, finds none at p < 0.05 (the paper names no test for this; the paired t-test is the Methods' Student's t-test applied to the two poles of the same cells; the unpaired t-test is shown as a variant). Reproduced when all four parts hold; partially reproduced when the reseal and residual parts hold.

claims.statement: With 1-us pulses, polarization grows with field strength up to 570 to 780 V/cm; at stronger fields the poles become leaky and show reduced or absent polarization, while regions closer to the equator remain polarized and may exceed the poles.
claims.source: Figure 1 legend; Results, 3.1, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Still stronger electric fields produce a distinct pattern of reduced or absent polarization at the poles (where the membrane becomes too leaky to accumulate the charge) while regions closer to the equator remain relatively intact and may polarize more than the poles
claims.criterion: Fig. 1 shows images of Di-8-ANEPPS cells at 900 ns into 1-us pulses of 43 to 1400 V/cm; the same protocol gives the data of Fig. 4B-C, on which this is judged. Pole dF in +-5 degree arcs from collapsed images, group means. Reproduced when cathodic pole dF is largest at 570 or 780 V/cm and lower at each of 1000 to 1400 V/cm, and at 1400 V/cm |dF| off the pole exceeds |dF| at the cathodic pole. "Closer to the equator" fixes no angle; readings, arcs of +-5 degrees centred (a) 30, (b) 45, (c) 60 degrees from the cathodic pole; the claim holds under any of them.

claims.statement: FluoVolt dF rises in proportion to field strength until apparent saturation at 66% (255 mV) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole and -83% (-320 mV) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole; stronger fields do not raise it further and lower it at the cathodic pole.
claims.source: Results, 3.2, paragraph 2; Figure 2A
claims.quote: ΔF increased proportionally to the electric field strength until reaching apparent saturation at 66% ΔF (255 mV IMP) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole, and −83% ΔF (−320 mV IMP) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole
claims.criterion: Fig. 2 method (Methods 2.3) - per image, mean F in +-5 degree pole arcs, F0 the mean of the 40 baseline images of the set, dF averaged over the 60 pulse images and over the n = 4 cells. Reproduced when the cathodic maximum over strengths is at 360 V/cm and the anodic minimum at 570 V/cm, both values within tolerance, and the cathodic dF at 1000 V/cm and above is below its 360 V/cm value. Saturation at a neighbouring strength with both values in tolerance is partially reproduced.

claims.statement: FluoVolt baseline fluorescence is stable without pulses (no significant bleaching), and the response stays stable through the 60 pulses of each set even at strongly electroporating fields of 1000 V/cm and above.
claims.source: Results, 3.2, paragraph 2; Figure 2A
claims.quote: Field strengths of 1000 V/cm and higher caused strong electroporation (see Section 3.5), but the dye response in each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses applied
claims.criterion: Per cell and set, pole dF per image as in fig2a-fluovolt-saturation. The paper gives no measure of stability. Readings, each tested on the group means at 1000, 1200 and 1400 V/cm - (a) the mean of the first 10 pulse images against the last 10 (10 is the window of Fig. 4B dotted lines), two-sided paired t-test over cells at p < 0.05; (b) the linear regression slope of dF on image index over the 60 images (Methods 2.5, Grapher regression), tested against zero at p < 0.05. Reproduced when neither finds a change at either pole in any of these sets (a claim of absence; both readings are shown and the effect sizes reported), and the baseline images likewise show no trend.

claims.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS dF keeps rising up to 570 V/cm at both poles, and responses at 780 V/cm and above decrease gradually within each set of 60 pulses.
claims.source: Results, 3.2, paragraph 3; Figure 2B
claims.quote: ΔF kept climbing up to the electric field strength of 570 V/cm at both cell poles ... responses to PEFs at and above 780 V/cm decreased gradually in each set of 60 images
claims.criterion: Fig. 2 method as in fig2a-fluovolt-saturation, Di-8-ANEPPS, n = 5. Part 1 - the group mean |dF| at each pole increases from each strength to the next up to 570 V/cm. Part 2 - "decreased gradually" is judged under the readings of fig2a-fluovolt-stable-within-set ((a) first 10 against last 10 pulse images, (b) regression slope), at 780 V/cm and each stronger strength, by the group mean |dF| being lower at the end of the set (a negative slope). The paper reports no test for this decline and calls the like decline of Fig. 2C at 1000 V/cm (n = 8) not significant, so significance is reported, not required. The text names no pole; readings (i) both poles, (ii) the cathodic pole (Discussion, point (a), cites Fig. 2B for the cathodic pole). Reproduced when part 1 holds and part 2 holds under one window and one pole reading at most of those strengths.

claims.statement: Repeated alternating sets of 150 and 230 V/cm pulses give dF responses that stay constant within and between sets, up to 800 flashes and 480 pulses before the 1000 V/cm exposure.
claims.source: Results, 3.2, paragraph 4; Figure 2C and 2D
claims.quote: Repeated sets of PEFs at 150 and 230 V/cm, delivered in alternation, produced ΔF responses that stayed constant both within each set and between the sets
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a two-tailed paired t-test at p < 0.05 (Fig. 2D legend) of each set's dF averaged over its 60 pulse images against the first set at the same field strength, n = 8 cells, per pole. Reproduced when no set before the 1000 V/cm exposure differs from the first; not reproduced when any does. Within-set stability is shown under the readings of fig2a-fluovolt-stable-within-set.

claims.statement: At 1000 V/cm, dF at the cathodic pole declines from 40 +- 10% at the start of the set to 26.6 +- 8% at its end, a trend that is not significant.
claims.source: Results, 3.2, paragraph 4; Figure 2C
claims.quote: at an electroporating field strength of 1000 V/cm, ΔF at the cathodic pole decreased from 40 ± 10% at the beginning of the set to 26.6 ± 8% at the end of it. Although not statistically significant (p > 0.05)
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the reported s.e. Fig. 2 method, n = 8. "Beginning" and "end" of the set are not defined; readings (a) the first and the last pulse image; (b) the means of the first 10 and last 10 pulse images. The test is not named; the paired two-tailed t-test of Fig. 2D is used. Reproduced when, under one reading, both values are within tolerance, the end value is lower, and the test gives p > 0.05.

claims.statement: dF averaged over each set stays nearly constant before electroporation but drops by about 20% in the sets acquired after the 1000 V/cm exposure (p < 0.05).
claims.source: Results, 3.2, paragraph 4; Figure 2D
claims.quote: ΔF values averaged across each set of 60 PEFs stayed nearly constant before the electroporation, but dropped by about 20% in the sets acquired after it (Fig. 2D, p < 0.05)
claims.criterion: Per cell and set, dF averaged over the 60 pulse images, per pole; each 150 and 230 V/cm set after the 1000 V/cm exposure compared with the first set at the same strength (dashed lines of Fig. 2D) by a two-tailed paired t-test, n = 8. Which pole the 20% refers to is not said; readings (a) cathodic, (b) anodic, (c) both. The size has two readings from the paper - the text's "about 20%" (20 +- 2) and the Fig. 2D legend's "small (<=20%)" (a drop above zero and at most 22%, the bound widened by 10%). Reproduced when, under one pole reading and one size reading, the mean relative drop over the post-exposure sets is within it and at least one post-exposure set differs at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Fit through the origin over -150 to +150 mV of calculated IMP, FluoVolt dF changes by 26% and Di-8-ANEPPS by 9.1% per 100 mV, with correlation coefficients 0.96 and 0.78.
claims.source: Results, 3.3; Figure 3
claims.quote: The correlation coefficients of the fits equaled 0.96 for FluoVolt and 0.78 for Di-8 ANEPPS (due to a lower signal-to-noise ratio), with respective slope coefficients of 26% and 9.1% ΔF per 100 mV of IMP
claims.criterion: As Results 3.3 and the Fig. 3 legend fix it - every individual dF at every perimeter point of every cell at 43 to 360 V/cm (1-us pulses, 900 ns), against IMPC for that point (Eq. 1, the cell's R and tau from the fit of [20]); points with IMPC within -150 to +150 mV fit by least squares with a line through the origin. The correlation coefficient is not defined for a fit through the origin; readings (a) Pearson r of dF and IMPC over those points; (b) the square root of the uncentred R^2 of the fit through the origin. Reproduced when both slopes are within tolerance and, under one reading, both correlation coefficients are. The outside input is the tau-radius fit of Semenov et al. 2025, Bioelectrochemistry 168, 109143 (ref. [20]); at 900 ns into the pulse its effect is small, and the result with tau set to 0 is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: FluoVolt departs from linearity already at +-200 mV of calculated IMP, while Di-8-ANEPPS stays essentially linear from -500 to +500 mV, so the early FluoVolt departure reflects the dye's range and not electroporation.
claims.source: Results, 3.3; Figure 3
claims.quote: The actual measurements with FluoVolt gradually became non-linear already at ±200 mV, while those for Di-8-ANEPPS stayed essentially linear throughout the tested range from −500 to +500 mV
claims.criterion: Data and fit as in fig3-dye-calibration-slopes; the paper smooths all points with LOESS and compares it with the line. The LOESS span is not given; readings, spans of (a) 0.3 and (b) 0.5 of the data. Linearity has no stated measure; the measure used is the LOESS value as a fraction of the linear-fit value. Reproduced when, under one span, the FluoVolt fraction falls below 0.9 at |IMPC| of 200 to 300 mV at both signs, and the Di-8-ANEPPS fraction stays within 0.9 to 1.1 from -500 to +500 mV (wherever data exist). The 0.9 to 1.1 band is the protocol's default 10% tolerance, not the paper's.

claims.statement: With FluoVolt, measured and calculated IMP match only at 43 and 150 V/cm; stronger pulses give a maximum dF of 71 +- 10% at the cathodic and -83.5 +- 5% at the anodic pole, and cathodic polarization falls from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45 to 50% at 1000 to 1400 V/cm.
claims.source: Results, 3.4, paragraph 1; Figure 4A
claims.quote: this assumption held only for the applied fields of 43 and 150 V/cm, where measured and calculated IMP matched. With stronger PEFs, maximum ΔF reached 71 ± 10% and −83.5 ± 5% at the cathodic and anodic poles, respectively ... polarization at the cathodic pole decreased from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45–50% at 1000–1400 V/cm
claims.criterion: FluoVolt, 1-us pulses, n = 4; pole dF in +-5 degree arcs from collapsed images, means over cells (Methods 2.3). Tolerances for the maxima are the reported s.e. The maxima are the extreme group means over strengths. The 45 to 50% range holds when each of the 1000, 1200 and 1400 V/cm cathodic means lies in 40.5 to 55. "Matched" at 43 and 150 V/cm is judged by the pole IMP (dF / 26 x 100 mV) within 10% of the mean IMPC (protocol default), and at 230 V/cm and above by it falling outside. Reproduced when all hold.

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS, measured IMP falls below the calculated value when the field reaches 570 V/cm, as dF reaches its maximum of 57 +- 14% at the cathodic and -55 +- 4% at the anodic pole, over 600 mV, twice the FluoVolt value.
claims.source: Results, 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
claims.quote: The measured IMP decreased below the calculated value when the electric field reached 570 V/cm, concurrently with reaching the maximum ΔF of 57 ± 14% at the cathodic pole and −55 ± 4% at the anodic pole. These values corresponded to membrane polarization by over 600 mV
claims.criterion: Di-8-ANEPPS, 1-us pulses, n = 5, averaged over all 60 pulse images; pole dF as in fig4a-fluovolt-limit; tolerances are the reported s.e. Measured pole IMP is dF / 9.1 x 100 mV. "Decreased below the calculated value" has no stated test; per cell the ratio of measured IMP to IMPC, and a one-sample t-test of the ratios against 1 (Methods 2.5), two- sided at p < 0.05. Reproduced when both maxima are within tolerance and occur at 570 V/cm, and 570 V/cm is the lowest strength at which the ratio is below 1 at p < 0.05 at one pole or more; partially reproduced when the maxima hold but the first significant strength is 780 V/cm (the Fig. 1 legend gives 570 to 780 V/cm).

claims.statement: Averaged over the first 10 of the 60 pulses, cathodic polarization reaches 66 +- 15% (710 +- 200 mV), so the 600-mV maximum over 60 pulses is not the dye limit.
claims.source: Results, 3.4, paragraph 3; Figure 4B, dotted lines
claims.quote: Polarization measured this way reached 66 ± 15% (710 ± 200 mV) at the cathodic pole
claims.criterion: As fig4b-di8-threshold-570, with the polarization image collapsed from the first 10 of the 60 pulse images (Fig. 4B legend; Results 3.4). Tolerances are the reported s.e. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance and the first-10 maximum exceeds the 60-image maximum.

claims.statement: Above the threshold, pole IMP falls progressively as the field rises, more at the cathodic pole; at 1400 V/cm charging is no longer detectable at the cathodic pole and is about 30% dF (about -330 mV) at the anodic pole.
claims.source: Results, 3.4, paragraph 4; Figure 4B
claims.quote: As the electric field increased further, the IMP reached at the poles progressively decreased, and the reduction was more pronounced at the cathodic pole ... At 1400 V/cm, charging was no longer detectable at the cathodic pole (i.e., the membrane became fully permeable) and dropped to ~30% ΔF (~ −330 mV) at the anodic pole
claims.criterion: Data as fig4b-di8-threshold-570. Reproduced when the mean |IMP| at each pole is lower at each strength above 780 V/cm than at the one below it, the drop from the pole's maximum to 1400 V/cm is larger at the cathodic pole, the cathodic dF at 1400 V/cm is not above zero by a one-sample t-test (two-sided, p < 0.05), and the anodic values are within tolerance. At 570 and 780 V/cm the paper says both poles are about equally permeabilized; the ratios to IMPC at the two poles are reported.

claims.statement: Membrane regions near the equator remain unaffected and follow the cosine dependence predicted by the Schwan equation up to 1000 V/cm, even when the poles are electroporated.
claims.source: Results, 3.4, paragraph 4; Figure 4C
claims.quote: appeared relatively unaffected and followed the cosine dependence predicted by Schwan formula up to 1000 V/cm
claims.criterion: Data as fig4b-di8-threshold-570, the 360-point profiles. "Closer to the equator" fixes no width; readings, points within (a) 20 and (b) 40 degrees of the equator (both sides). Per strength, the mean over cells of measured IMP (dF / 9.1 x 100 mV) against IMPC at those points. A mean over points on both sides of the equator would cancel to about zero, so agreement is measured point by point - the slope of a least-squares line through the origin of measured IMP on IMPC over the equatorial points (the fit of Results 3.3). Reproduced when, under one width reading, at every strength up to 1000 V/cm that slope is within 0.9 to 1.1 (protocol default 10%, not the paper's) or its 95% interval includes 1, and at 780 and 1000 V/cm the pole ratio of measured IMP to IMPC is lower than the equatorial slope.

claims.statement: With 0.3-us pulses of 357 to 3320 V/cm imaged at 275 ns, the maximum dF is 53 +- 4% (about 600 mV) at both poles, and the dependence on field strength is like that with 1-us pulses.
claims.source: Results, 3.4, paragraph 5; Figure 4D
claims.quote: the maximum ΔF reached was 53 ± 4% (~600 mV) at both cell poles. The pattern of how the response changed with increasing PEF strength was not different from that with 1-μs PEFs either
claims.criterion: Di-8-ANEPPS, 0.3-us pulses, n = 10, image at 275 ns, IMPC at t = 275 ns; pole dF as in fig4b-di8-threshold-570; tolerance the reported s.e. Reproduced when both pole maxima are within tolerance and, as with 1-us pulses, |dF| at each pole decreases at the strongest fields after its maximum. The ratio of the 0.3-us to the 1-us maximum per pole is reported.

claims.statement: 1 mM Gd3+ extends anodic charging to -864 +- 44 mV against -542 +- 57 mV in controls (p < 0.001), and measured IMP stays nearly equal to calculated IMP down to -780 mV, so the dye response is linear at high IMPs.
claims.source: Results, 3.5, paragraph 1; Figure 5A
claims.quote: 1 mM Gd3+ extended the range of membrane charging at the anodic pole down to −864 ± 44 mV (p < 0.001 compared to −542 ± 57 mV in parallel control experiments, Fig. 5A). Furthermore, measured IMP remained nearly identical to the theoretical IMPC down to −780 mV
claims.criterion: Di-8-ANEPPS, 1-us pulses of 150 to 1400 V/cm, pole dF converted to IMP (9.1% per 100 mV), n = 7 Gd3+ and 5 control (Fig. 5A legend); tolerances the reported s.e.; test the 2-tailed t-test of the legend, unpaired. The extreme value is not defined; readings (a) per cell the most negative anodic IMP over strengths, averaged over cells; (b) the group mean at the strength where the group mean is most negative. Reproduced when, under one reading, both values are within tolerance and the groups differ at p < 0.001; and the Gd3+ group's anodic IMP is within 10% (protocol default) of its IMPC at every strength with IMPC down to -780 mV.

claims.statement: At the cathodic pole Gd3+ cells reach 647 +- 44 mV, not significantly more than controls, but Gd3+ prevents the progressive decline of IMP with stronger fields.
claims.source: Results, 3.5, paragraph 2; Figure 5A
claims.quote: At the cathodic pole, polarization in the presence of Gd3+ reached 647 ± 44 mV, a value not significantly higher than that in the control group without Gd3+. However, Gd3+ prevented the progressive decline in IMP as the electric field was increased.
claims.criterion: Data and readings (a) and (b) of the extreme as in fig5a-gd-extends-anodic-charging. Part 1, a claim of absence on the paper's test - the Gd3+ cathodic maximum is not higher than the control's by the 2-tailed unpaired t-test at p < 0.05. Part 2 - the Fig. 5A legend's test; Gd3+ and control differ at p < 0.05 by 2-tailed t-test at the strongest strengths (those with IMPC above 1200 mV at the cathodic pole), with Gd3+ higher. Part 3 - the control's cathodic IMP falls from its maximum to 1400 V/cm and the Gd3+ group's falls less; the paper gives no measure for "prevented the decline", so the size of each fall and its s.e. are reported. Reproduced when the value is within tolerance and all three parts hold.

claims.statement: Under Eq. (2), effective membrane conductivity barely affects charging while it stays far below cytosol and medium conductivity; a 10-fold increase reduces IMP by about 2% and a 100-fold increase by 12%.
claims.source: Results, 3.5, paragraph 3; Figure 5B
claims.quote: its 10-fold increase would go unnoticed, yielding just a ~2% IMP reduction, and a 100-fold increase would reduce IMP by just 12%
claims.criterion: A computation from Eq. (2) with the Methods' parameters (li 0.4 S/m, lo 1.64 S/m, R 8 um, d 5 nm, intact lm 3e-7 S/m); it uses no recording. Reduction is 1 - f/1.5. The tolerance for "~2%" is half its last digit (0.5 percentage point), as the value is given to one significant figure; the 12% has the default 10%. Eq. (2) as read in the header gives 1.3% for 10-fold and 11.9% for 100-fold (1 - f/1.5), or 1.2% and 11.7% taken relative to the intact f; the "~2%" may be read from the Fig. 5B graph, and the equation itself is read from garbled text, so a mismatch at 10-fold is reported with both values.

claims.statement: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduces the electroporation-induced effective membrane conductivity 2- to 3-fold.
claims.source: Results, 3.5, paragraph 4; Figure 5C
claims.quote: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation ... induced effective conductivity 2–3-fold
claims.criterion: For each datapoint of Fig. 5A (pole and field strength, group means of measured IMP and IMPC), lm,eff interpolated with Eq. (2) from the ratio of measured to calculated IMP (Fig. 5C legend); the fold is control lm,eff over Gd3+ lm,eff at the same pole and strength. Pairs where either ratio is 1 or above (no finite increase) are reported and left out. Reproduced when more than half of the remaining folds lie within 1.8 to 3.3 (the range widened by 10% of each bound).

claims.statement: A single 1-us pulse causes clear Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/cm, with the signal elevated through the 5-min observation; the small rise after 780 V/cm is not significant.
claims.source: Results, 3.6, paragraph 2; Figure 6A
claims.quote: established a clear peak of Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 ... and Ca2+ signal remained elevated through the 5-min observation period (Fig. 6A). A subtle ΔF increase after exposure at 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not statistically significant.
claims.criterion: Fluo-4 dF in a circular region over the cell, background-subtracted, F0 the mean before the pulse (Methods 2.4); 14 cells per strength (Fig. 6A legend). The test and the time point are not given. Test readings, both used in Section 3.6 for Fig. 6B - (i) the one-sample t-test against zero, two-sided, p < 0.05; (ii) an unpaired t-test against the 0 V/cm group, two-sided, p < 0.05. Time point readings (a) the peak dF after the pulse; (b) dF at the end of the recording (the measure of Section 3.6 for Fig. 6B). Reproduced when, under one test and time reading, dF at 1000 and 1200 V/cm is above zero (or the 0 V/cm group) at p < 0.05, the end-of-recording dF at those strengths is above zero, and 780 V/cm is not significant under that same reading. The 780 V/cm part is a claim of absence on a test the paper does not name; every reading is shown, and when they give different outcomes for it the claim is methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: With trains of 60 1-us pulses at 6 Hz, a strong Ca2+ response occurs in 28% of cells at 780 V/cm and nearly all cells at higher strengths; at 650 V/cm only 2 cells (5.9%) respond strongly, but the mean signal at the end is above zero (p < 0.001) and above that at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, one-tailed).
claims.source: Results, 3.6, paragraph 3; Figure 6B
claims.quote: A strong Ca2+ response was recorded in 28% of cells exposed at 780 V/cm and in nearly all cells at higher intensities (Fig. 6B). At 650 V/cm, only 2 cells (5.9%) showed a strong response, but the mean Ca2+ signal by the end of recording was significantly different from zero (p < 0.001, one sample t-test) and marginally higher than after exposure at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, single-tailed t-test)
claims.criterion: Fluo-4 dF as in fig6a-ca-single-pulse, 28 to 54 cells per strength, 224 in all, each tested once. The mean-signal tests are fixed by the text - dF at the end of the recording (read as the last frame; the mean of the last five frames, 10 s, is shown as a variant), one-sample t-test against zero, and an unpaired one-tailed t-test against 230 V/cm. "Strong response" is not defined in the paper, its legends or Methods; no threshold can be taken from them, so the two percentages are judged only if the dataset marks responders, and otherwise are blocked as methods_underspecified with the distribution of end dF per strength shown. Reproduced when the two tests reach p < 0.001 and p < 0.05 (and the percentages match where they can be judged).

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS and 1 us PEFs, polarization depolarizes the cathode-facing pole and hyperpolarizes the anode-facing pole, falls off towards the equator and scales with field strength up to 570 V/cm; at 780 V/cm the cathodic pole stops increasing and dims; at 1000 to 1400 V/cm the poles show reduced or absent polarization while regions nearer the equator remain polarized and may exceed the poles.
claims.source: Results, section 3.1, paragraph 1; Figure 1 and legend
claims.quote: At a higher electric field strength of 780 V/cm, polarization at the cathodic pole does not further increase but dims out, indicating a less efficient charging of the partially permeabilized membrane. Still stronger electric fields produce a distinct pattern of reduced or absent polarization at the poles
claims.criterion: Figure 1 shows representative images; the paper does not identify the cells. Tested on the Di-8-ANEPPS 1 us escalation data (the Fig. 4B group, n = 5), with polarization images as in section 2.3 and perimeter dF resampled to 360 points. Reproduced when, in the mean over cells, (1) cathodic pole dF is positive and anodic pole dF negative at 43 to 570 V/cm and pole |dF| rises with field strength over that range; (2) cathodic pole dF at 780 V/cm is not above that at 570 V/cm; (3) at 1000 to 1400 V/cm pole |dF| is below its value at 570 V/cm at the cathodic pole, while the largest |dF| on the cathodic half of the profile lies away from the +-5 degree pole arc in at least one of those fields. Partially reproduced when (1) holds and one of (2) or (3) fails.

claims.statement: In FluoVolt-loaded cells, pole dF rose with field strength until apparent saturation at 66% (255 mV) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole and -83% (-320 mV) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole; stronger fields did not increase the anodic response and decreased the cathodic one.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 2; Figure 2A
claims.quote: ΔF increased proportionally to the electric field strength until reaching apparent saturation at 66% ΔF (255 mV IMP) at 360 V/cm at the cathodic pole, and −83% ΔF (−320 mV IMP) at 570 V/cm at the anodic pole. Further escalation of the electric field strength did not increase the dye response at the anodic pole and even decreased it at the cathodic pole.
claims.criterion: Fig. 2A, n = 4 cells, 9 sets escalating from 43 to 1400 V/cm. Pole dF per image against F0, the mean of the set's first 40 images (section 2.3), averaged over the 60 PEF images of the set and then over cells. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance, the cathodic maximum over fields is at 360 V/cm or within its tolerance of the 360 V/cm value, the anodic dF at fields above 570 V/cm is not more negative than at 570 V/cm by more than the tolerance, and the cathodic dF at the strongest field is below its 360 V/cm value.

claims.statement: Without PEF (the first 40 images of each set) FluoVolt measurements were stable, showing no significant photosensitization or dye bleaching.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 2; Figure 2A
claims.quote: Without PEF (first 40 datapoints, or ~ 7 s in each set), measurements were stable, indicating no significant photosensitization or dye bleaching.
claims.criterion: A claim of absence for which the paper names no test. Methods 2.5 names linear regression with fit significance (Grapher) and paired t-tests (Fig. 2 legend), so two readings are run, per pole and set, on the 40 baseline dF values averaged over the n = 4 cells. (a) linear regression of dF on image index, fit significance p < 0.05; (b) 2-tailed paired t-test across cells of the mean of baseline images 1 to 20 against 21 to 40, p < 0.05. Reproduced when neither finds a significant change in any set at either pole, not reproduced when both do in the same sets; when the readings disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified. The slope and the change in dF over the 40 images are reported.

claims.statement: At 1000 V/cm and above, which strongly electroporated the cells, the FluoVolt response stayed stable through the 60 pulses of each set.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 2; Figure 2A
claims.quote: Field strengths of 1000 V/cm and higher caused strong electroporation (see Section 3.5), but the dye response in each set stayed stable through the 60 pulses applied
claims.criterion: The paper names no test. Readings as in fig2a-fluovolt-baseline-stable, run on the 60 PEF images of the sets at 1000 V/cm and above, per pole; (b) compares PEF images 1 to 30 with 31 to 60. Reproduced when neither reading finds a significant change; not reproduced when both do; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS has a lower sensitivity than FluoVolt, but its dF kept rising with field strength up to 570 V/cm at both poles.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 3; Figure 2B
claims.quote: This dye has a lower sensitivity to membrane polarization (note the vertical scale different from Fig. 2A), but ΔF kept climbing up to the electric field strength of 570 V/cm at both cell poles.
claims.criterion: Fig. 2B, n = 5 cells; pole dF per set as in fig2a-fluovolt-saturation. Reproduced when the cathodic dF increases and the anodic dF becomes more negative at each step from 43 to 570 V/cm in the mean over cells, and the largest pole |dF| up to 570 V/cm is smaller than the FluoVolt value at the same field and pole (Fig. 2A group).

claims.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS responses were somewhat affected by bleaching, most noticeably at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added about 5% to dF at the anodic pole and reduced it by about 5% at the cathodic pole.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 3; Figure 2B
claims.quote: The responses were somewhat affected by dye bleaching (particularly noticeable at 43 V/cm, where bleaching added ~5% to ΔF at the anodic pole and reduced it by the same ~5% at the cathodic pole.
claims.criterion: The paper does not say how the bleaching contribution was measured. Readings allowed by the text (a) the drift of pole dF over the 100 images of the 43 V/cm set, from a linear regression of the 40 baseline values extrapolated over the 60 PEF images (the drift adds to the hyperpolarizing anodic response and subtracts from the depolarizing cathodic one); (b) the difference in dF between the first and the last 10 images of the 43 V/cm set. Reproduced when, under a reading, both poles show a downward drift of F whose size is within tolerance; partially reproduced when the direction holds at both poles but the size is outside the tolerance under every reading.

claims.statement: Di-8-ANEPPS responses to PEFs at and above 780 V/cm decreased gradually within each set of 60 images.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 3; Figure 2B
claims.quote: In addition, responses to PEFs at and above 780 V/cm decreased gradually in each set of 60 images, consistent with expectations of adding membrane damage by additional electroporation pulses in each set
claims.criterion: Fig. 2B, n = 5 cells. The paper names no test. Readings, per set at 780 V/cm and above, on pole |dF| averaged over cells (a) linear regression of |dF| on PEF image index, negative slope with fit significance p < 0.05; (b) 2-tailed paired t-test across cells of PEF images 1 to 10 against 51 to 60 (the first 10 of 60 are the window used in Fig. 4B), lower at the end with p < 0.05. The paper does not name the pole; readings (i) the cathodic pole, (ii) the anodic pole, (iii) both. Reproduced when, under a reading of each kind, the response declines significantly within every set at 780 V/cm and above; partially reproduced when it does in some of them. The slope for every set and pole is reported, and the slope at 43 to 570 V/cm is shown for comparison.

claims.statement: Repeated alternating sets of 150 and 230 V/cm PEFs produced dF responses that stayed constant within each set and between sets, so that 800 flashes and 480 pulses had no obvious impact before the 1000 V/cm exposure.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 4; Figure 2C and D
claims.quote: Repeated sets of PEFs at 150 and 230 V/cm, delivered in alternation, produced ΔF responses that stayed constant both within each set and between the sets (Fig. 2C and D).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Fig. 2C and D, n = 8 cells; set means of pole dF over the 60 PEF images. The paper's test, from the Fig. 2 legend, is a 2-tailed paired t-test of each set mean against the first set at the same field strength (the dashed lines mark the first trial's means), at p < 0.05. Reproduced when no 150 or 230 V/cm set before the 1000 V/cm exposure differs from the first set of its field strength at either pole; not reproduced when any does. The within-set change (first against last 10 PEF images) is reported as a variant, as are the differences in percent.

claims.statement: At 1000 V/cm, cathodic pole dF fell from 40 +- 10% at the start of the set to 26.6 +- 8% at its end, a trend that was not statistically significant.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 4; Figure 2C
claims.quote: In contrast, at an electroporating field strength of 1000 V/cm, ΔF at the cathodic pole decreased from 40 ± 10% at the beginning of the set to 26.6 ± 8% at the end of it. Although not statistically significant (p > 0.05)
claims.criterion: Tolerances are the paper's s.e. The paper does not say how many images form the beginning and the end. Readings (a) the first and the last PEF image; (b) the mean of PEF images 1 to 10 and 51 to 60; (c) the mean of images 1 to 5 and 56 to 60. Reproduced when, under a reading, both means are within tolerance, the end is lower, and a 2-tailed paired t-test across the 8 cells gives p > 0.05.

claims.statement: Set-averaged dF stayed nearly constant before electroporation but dropped by about 20% (a small but persistent reduction of at most 20%) in the 150 and 230 V/cm sets acquired after the 1000 V/cm exposure.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 4; Figure 2D and legend
claims.quote: ΔF values averaged across each set of 60 PEFs stayed nearly constant before the electroporation, but dropped by about 20% in the sets acquired after it (Fig. 2D, p < 0.05).
claims.criterion: Fig. 2D, n = 8 cells. Set means of pole dF over the 60 PEF images, each set compared with the first set of the same field strength (the legend's dashed lines) by a 2-tailed paired t-test across cells. The paper does not say which pole or how the 20% is summarized. Readings (a) each pole separately; (b) both poles' |dF| averaged; and, for the size, (i) the mean reduction over all post-1000 V/cm sets, (ii) the reduction of each set. Reproduced when, under a reading, the post-exposure sets show a reduction within tolerance with p < 0.05 for at least one set, and no pre-exposure set differs at p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when the reduction is significant but its size is outside the tolerance under every reading.

claims.statement: Fitting dF against IMPC from -150 to +150 mV with a line through the origin gave slopes of 26% (FluoVolt) and 9.1% (Di-8-ANEPPS) dF per 100 mV, with correlation coefficients of 0.96 and 0.78.
claims.source: Results, section 3.3, paragraph 1; Figure 3 legend
claims.quote: The correlation coefficients of the fits equaled 0.96 for FluoVolt and 0.78 for Di-8 ANEPPS (due to a lower signal-to-noise ratio), with respective slope coefficients of 26% and 9.1% ΔF per 100 mV of IMP.
claims.criterion: From section 3.3 and the Fig. 3 legend. Cells exposed to 1 us PEFs at 43 to 360 V/cm, imaged at 900 ns; every perimeter location's dF (polarization against baseline image, 360 points per cell) paired with IMPC from Eq. (1) for that location, the cell's radius and its tau from the fit of [20] (outside input). All points from -150 to +150 mV IMPC, pooled over cells and fields, fit by least squares with a line through the origin; the correlation coefficient of that fit. The paper does not say which cells form Fig. 3; readings (a) the Fig. 4A and 4B groups at 43 to 360 V/cm; (b) every cell of the dye at those fields in the dataset. It does not say whether the correlation coefficient is for the through-origin fit or an ordinary Pearson r; both are shown. Reproduced when, under a reading, both slopes are within tolerance; partially reproduced when one is. The coefficients are reported against their values.

claims.statement: FluoVolt measurements became non-linear already at +-200 mV, while Di-8-ANEPPS stayed essentially linear from -500 to +500 mV, so FluoVolt's early departure reflects the limit of the dye's range and not electroporation.
claims.source: Results, section 3.3, paragraph 1; Figure 3 legend
claims.quote: The actual measurements with FluoVolt gradually became non-linear already at ±200 mV, while those for Di-8-ANEPPS stayed essentially linear throughout the tested range from −500 to +500 mV.
claims.criterion: Data as in fig3-dye-slopes over the whole IMPC range. The paper judged linearity by eye against a LOESS curve and names no test, so the method is open. Readings, using the tests Methods 2.5 names (a) per 50 mV bin of IMPC (a bin width not given by the paper), the per-cell mean dF compared with the through-origin line by a one-sample t-test across cells at p < 0.05; (b) a regression of dF on IMPC with a cubic term added to the through-origin line, over the whole range, with the fit significance of that term at p < 0.05. Reproduced when, under both readings, FluoVolt departs from the line beyond +-200 mV (bins beyond 200 mV on at least one side significantly below the line in magnitude, or a significant cubic term shrinking the response) and Di-8-ANEPPS does not depart within -500 to +500 mV; not reproduced when both readings find the opposite for either dye; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The per-bin ratios of measured to line are reported.

claims.statement: FluoVolt-measured and calculated IMP matched only at 43 and 150 V/cm; with stronger PEFs pole dF reached at most 71 +- 10% (cathodic) and -83.5 +- 5% (anodic), about +260 and -330 mV, and the cathodic value fell from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45 to 50% at 1000 to 1400 V/cm.
claims.source: Results, section 3.4, paragraph 1; Figure 4A
claims.quote: However, this assumption held only for the applied fields of 43 and 150 V/cm, where measured and calculated IMP matched. With stronger PEFs, maximum ΔF reached 71 ± 10% and −83.5 ± 5% at the cathodic and anodic poles, respectively. ... Notably, polarization at the cathodic pole decreased from 71% at 360 V/cm to 45–50% at 1000–1400 V/cm
claims.criterion: Fig. 4A, n = 4 cells, 1 us, 43 to 1400 V/cm; pole dF from the polarization image, mean over cells; IMPC at the poles from Eq. (1) with tau from [20]. Tolerances for the maxima are the paper's s.e.; the 45 to 50% range is widened by 10% of each bound (40.5 to 55). Reproduced when both maxima are within tolerance, cathodic dF at each of 1000, 1200 and 1400 V/cm (those present) lies within 40.5 to 55%, and measured IMP (dF / 0.26 per mV) is within the s.e. of IMPC at 43 and 150 V/cm but below IMPC by more than its s.e. at 230 V/cm and above at both poles (the text says the match held only at 43 and 150 V/cm).

claims.statement: With Di-8-ANEPPS, measured IMP fell below the calculated value when the field reached 570 V/cm, together with the maximum dF of 57 +- 14% at the cathodic pole and -55 +- 4% at the anodic pole, a polarization of over 600 mV, twice that measured with FluoVolt.
claims.source: Results, section 3.4, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
claims.quote: The measured IMP decreased below the calculated value when the electric field reached 570 V/cm, concurrently with reaching the maximum ΔF of 57 ± 14% at the cathodic pole and − 55 ± 4% at the anodic pole. These values corresponded to membrane polarization by over 600 mV
claims.criterion: Fig. 4B, n = 5 cells; pole dF from the polarization image (60 PEF images), mean over cells; IMP = dF / 0.091 per mV; IMPC from Eq. (1) with tau from [20]. Tolerances are the paper's s.e. Reproduced when both maxima are within tolerance and occur at 570 V/cm, and measured IMP at the poles is within the s.e. of IMPC at the fields below 570 V/cm and below it at 570 V/cm.

claims.statement: Averaging dF over the first 10 of the 60 PEFs, cathodic pole polarization reached 66 +- 15% (710 +- 200 mV), above the 600 mV maximum averaged over 60 PEFs.
claims.source: Results, section 3.4, paragraph 3; Figure 4B (dotted lines)
claims.quote: Polarization measured this way reached 66 ± 15% (710 ± 200 mV) at the cathodic pole, suggesting that the 600-mV maximum, averaged from 60 PEFs, was not the dye limit but the actual IMP
claims.criterion: Fig. 4B, n = 5 cells; the polarization image formed from the first 10 of the 60 PEF images (Fig. 4B legend), baseline image from the 40 baseline images. Tolerance is the paper's s.e. Reproduced when the maximum over fields of the mean cathodic dF is within tolerance and above the maximum from all 60 PEF images.

claims.statement: Above 780 V/cm the IMP reached at the poles decreased progressively with field strength, more at the cathodic pole; at 1400 V/cm charging was no longer detectable at the cathodic pole and dropped to about 30% dF (about -330 mV) at the anodic pole.
claims.source: Results, section 3.4, paragraph 4; Figure 4B
claims.quote: As the electric field increased further, the IMP reached at the poles progressively decreased, and the reduction was more pronounced at the cathodic pole. ... At 1400 V/cm, charging was no longer detectable at the cathodic pole (i.e., the membrane became fully permeable) and dropped to ~30% ΔF (~ −330 mV) at the anodic pole.
claims.criterion: Fig. 4B, n = 5 cells, pole dF from the polarization image. "No longer detectable" is read as a mean cathodic dF at 1400 V/cm whose s.e. interval includes 0. Reproduced when pole |dF| decreases from 780 V/cm to 1400 V/cm at both poles, the fractional decrease from the pole's maximum is larger at the cathodic pole, the cathodic value at 1400 V/cm is not distinguishable from 0, and the anodic value is within tolerance. Note that -330 mV at 9.1% per 100 mV is -30% dF; the text prints the dF without its sign.

claims.statement: Membrane regions nearer the equator appeared unaffected and followed the cosine dependence predicted by the Schwan equation up to 1000 V/cm, even when the poles were electroporated.
claims.source: Results, section 3.4, paragraph 4; Figure 4C
claims.quote: Membrane areas closer to the equator (at polar angles closer to 0◦and 270◦) appeared relatively unaffected and followed the cosine dependence predicted by Schwan formula up to 1000 V/cm (Fig. 4C).
claims.criterion: Fig. 4B data (n = 5), perimeter dF resampled to 360 points, IMP = dF / 0.091 per mV, against IMPC from Eq. (1). The paper does not say how far from the poles "closer to the equator" reaches. Readings (a) the points within 30 degrees of the equator; (b) within 45 degrees. The paper compares by eye; the measure is, separately for the cathodic and anodic halves, the mean measured IMP over the points in that range divided by the mean IMPC over the same points (a ratio of means, since IMPC tends to 0 at the equator), against 1 with the protocol's default tolerance of 10% (0.9 to 1.1). Reproduced when, under a reading, that ratio is within 0.9 to 1.1 at 780 and 1000 V/cm while the ratio in the +-5 degree pole arcs is below 0.9 at the same fields.

claims.statement: With 0.3 us PEFs at 357 to 3320 V/cm (imaged at 275 ns), the maximum dF was 53 +- 4% (about 600 mV) at both poles, similar to 1 us pulses, and its pattern with increasing field strength did not differ from that with 1 us pulses.
claims.source: Results, section 3.4, paragraph 5; Figure 4D
claims.quote: Contrary to the expectations, the results were similar to those with 1-μs pulses ... the maximum ΔF reached was 53 ± 4% (~600 mV) at both cell poles. The pattern of how the response changed with increasing PEF strength was not different from that with 1-μs PEFs either.
claims.criterion: Fig. 4D, n = 10 cells; pole dF from the polarization image, mean over cells. Tolerance is the paper's s.e. Reproduced when the maximum |dF| over fields is within tolerance at both poles, and, as in fig4b-asymmetric-decline, pole |dF| declines at fields beyond the maximum with the larger fractional decline at the cathodic pole. Partially reproduced when one pole's maximum is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: 1 mM Gd3+ extended membrane charging at the anodic pole down to -864 +- 44 mV, against -542 +- 57 mV in parallel controls (p < 0.001).
claims.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 1; Figure 5A
claims.quote: Indeed, we found that 1 mM Gd3+ extended the range of membrane charging at the anodic pole down to −864 ± 44 mV (p < 0.001 compared to −542 ± 57 mV in parallel control experiments, Fig. 5A).
claims.criterion: Fig. 5A, Di-8-ANEPPS, 1 us, 150 to 1400 V/cm; anodic pole dF from the polarization image converted to IMP at 9.1% per 100 mV. Tolerances are the paper's s.e. The paper does not say how the extreme is taken. Readings (a) the most negative group mean over field strengths, with its s.e., the groups compared at that field by a 2-tailed two-sample t-test; (b) each cell's most negative IMP over field strengths, averaged per group and compared by a 2-tailed two-sample t-test. Reproduced when, under a reading, both values are within tolerance and p < 0.001; partially reproduced when the Gd3+ value is more negative with p < 0.05 but a value is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: With Gd3+, measured IMP stayed nearly identical to IMPC down to -780 mV, showing that the Di-8-ANEPPS response stayed linear and its calibration valid at high IMPs.
claims.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 1; Figure 5A
claims.quote: Furthermore, measured IMP remained nearly identical to the theoretical IMPC down to −780 mV, indicating that the dye response remained linear and its calibration was valid even at high IMPs.
claims.criterion: Fig. 5A Gd3+ group, n = 7; anodic pole IMP against IMPC per field strength, means and s.e. both ways, compared with the bisector of Fig. 5A. The paper names no test for "nearly identical". Readings (a) a one-sample t-test (Methods 2.5) of per-cell measured IMP minus IMPC against 0, not significant at p < 0.05; (b) the mean measured IMP within 10% of the mean IMPC (the protocol's default tolerance). Reproduced when, under both readings, every field strength whose mean IMPC is between 0 and -780 mV passes; not reproduced when both fail at any of them; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: At the cathodic pole, polarization with Gd3+ reached 647 +- 44 mV, not significantly higher than in controls, but Gd3+ prevented the progressive decline of IMP as field strength increased.
claims.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 2; Figure 5A
claims.quote: At the cathodic pole, polarization in the presence of Gd3+ reached 647 ± 44 mV, a value not significantly higher than that in the control group without Gd3+. However, Gd3+ prevented the progressive decline in IMP as the electric field was increased.
claims.criterion: Readings for the maximum and its comparison as in fig5a-gd-anodic-extension, at the cathodic pole. The absence of a difference is judged on the paper's test, a 2-tailed two-sample t-test at p < 0.05. Reproduced when, under a reading, the Gd3+ maximum is within tolerance and not significantly above the control's, and the Gd3+ cathodic IMP at the strongest field is not below its maximum by more than its s.e. while the control's is.

claims.statement: Differences between Gd3+ and control data are significant at p < 0.05 or better for the datapoints below -700 mV and above 1200 mV.
claims.source: Figure 5A legend
claims.quote: Differences between Gd3+ and control group data are significant at p < 0.05 or better (2-tailed t-test) for datapoints below −700 mV and above 1200 mV.
claims.criterion: Fig. 5A; per field strength and pole, measured IMP of the two groups compared by a 2-tailed two-sample t-test. The text does not say which axis the -700 and 1200 mV refer to. Readings (a) IMPC (horizontal axis) below -700 mV at the anodic pole and above 1200 mV at the cathodic pole; (b) measured IMP below -700 mV in the Gd3+ group for the anodic pole, with IMPC above 1200 mV for the cathodic pole. Reproduced when, under a reading, every datapoint in those ranges has p < 0.05.

claims.statement: By Eq. (2), effective membrane conductivity has little effect on charging while it stays much smaller than the cytosol and medium conductivities; a 10-fold increase gives about a 2% IMP reduction and a 100-fold increase about 12%.
claims.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 3; Figure 5B
claims.quote: As expected, effective conductivity had little impact on charging for as long as it remained much smaller than the cytosol and media conductivities ... its 10-fold increase would go unnoticed, yielding just a ~2% IMP reduction, and a 100-fold increase would reduce IMP by just 12%.
claims.criterion: A computation from Eq. (2) with the parameters in section 2.3 (cytoplasm 0.4 S/m, medium 1.64 S/m, intact membrane 3e-7 S/m, R = 8 um, d = 5 nm); it uses no recordings. Reduction is 1 - f/1.5 (the ratio of calculated to measured IMP is 1.5/f) at 10 and 100 times the intact membrane conductivity. Reproduced when both are within tolerance. If Eq. (2) as printed (the extracted text garbles it) gives a value of f far from 1.5 at the intact conductivity, both its literal form and the form normalized so that the intact membrane gives 1.5 are shown.

claims.statement: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation-induced effective membrane conductivity 2 to 3 fold.
claims.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 4; Figure 5C
claims.quote: For most datapoints, Gd3+ reduced the electroporation- induced effective conductivity 2–3-fold.
claims.criterion: As the Fig. 5C legend says, per field strength and pole, the effective conductivity from the ratio of the group-mean measured IMP to the group-mean IMPC, interpolated on the Eq. (2) curve of fig5b-eq2-sensitivity. The range 2 to 3 widened by 10% of each bound is 1.8 to 3.3. Reproduced when the control-to-Gd3+ ratio lies in 1.8 to 3.3 for more than half of the datapoints where both groups show a reduction of IMP below IMPC; the ratios are listed.

claims.statement: A single 1 us pulse at 0 to 1200 V/cm produced a clear Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/cm, with the signal elevated through the 5 min observation; the small increase after 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not significant.
claims.source: Results, section 3.6, paragraph 2; Figure 6A
claims.quote: Exposure to a single 1-μs pulse at escalating field strengths, from 0 to 1200 V/cm established a clear peak of Ca2+ entry at 1000 and 1200 V/ cm, and Ca2+ signal remained elevated through the 5-min observation period (Fig. 6A). A subtle ΔF increase after exposure at 780 V/cm was at the detection limit and not statistically significant.
claims.criterion: Fig. 6A; the legend says the means are across 14 cells, and does not say whether these are 14 cells per field strength or 14 cells in all; Fluo-4 dF against F0 the mean before the pulse, background-subtracted (section 2.4). The paper does not name the test or the time point. Readings for the test (a) one-sample t-test of dF against 0 (Methods 2.5); (b) two-sample t-test against the 0 V/cm group, both 2-tailed at p < 0.05; for the time, (i) the peak dF after the pulse, (ii) dF at the end of the 5 min recording. Reproduced when, under every reading, 1000 and 1200 V/cm give dF significantly above the comparison and 780 V/cm does not; not reproduced when every reading fails for 1000 or 1200 V/cm or finds 780 V/cm significant; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The size of the 780 V/cm effect is reported under each reading.

claims.statement: With trains of 60 1 us pulses at 6 Hz (224 cells, each tested once), a strong Ca2+ response occurred in 28% of cells at 780 V/cm and nearly all cells at higher fields; at 650 V/cm only 2 cells (5.9%) responded strongly, but the mean signal at the end of recording was significantly above zero (p < 0.001, one-sample t-test) and marginally higher than at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, single-tailed t-test).
claims.source: Results, section 3.6, paragraph 3; Figure 6B
claims.quote: A strong Ca2+ response was recorded in 28% of cells exposed at 780 V/cm and in nearly all cells at higher intensities (Fig. 6B). At 650 V/cm, only 2 cells (5.9%) showed a strong response, but the mean Ca2+ signal by the end of recording was significantly different from zero (p < 0.001, one sample t-test) and marginally higher than after exposure at 230 V/cm (p < 0.05, single-tailed t-test).
claims.criterion: Fig. 6B; Fluo-4 dF against F0 the mean before the train (first 30 s), background-subtracted. "By the end of recording" is read as (a) the last frame; (b) the mean of the last 10 s (5 frames at 2 s). The single-tailed test is a two-sample Student's t-test, 650 above 230 V/cm. The paper does not define a strong response, and no reading is given; the fractions (28%, 5.9%, nearly all at higher fields) are tested only if the dataset or a reader's answer gives the definition, and otherwise that part is blocked as methods_underspecified with the distribution of end-of-recording dF per field shown. Reproduced when the cell count is 224 with 28 to 54 cells per field, and under a reading of the end, both tests give p below their bounds; partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: Polarization by a 150 V/cm test pulse 5 us after a conditioning pulse still followed a cosine after conditioning PEFs up to 1000 V/cm, while 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging at the cell poles.
claims.source: Results, section 3.7, paragraph 3; Figure 7A
claims.quote: Polarization still followed a cosine function after conditioning PEFs of up to 1000 V/cm. However, 1200 and 1400 V/cm conditioning PEFs markedly hindered charging by the test pulse at cell poles, indicating a persistent membrane permeabilization.
claims.criterion: Fig. 7A, n = 5; perimeter dF (360 points) during the test pulse, mean over cells, fit with a cosine of the polar angle by least squares (Grapher, Methods 2.5). The 150/150 V/cm cosine is the benchmark (legend). The paper judges "followed a cosine" by eye. Read here as the absence of flattening at the poles, the mean dF in each +-5 degree pole arc not below the profile's own cosine fit by more than its s.e. Reproduced when this holds at both poles for every conditioning strength up to 1000 V/cm, and for 1200 and 1400 V/cm the mean pole dF is below the benchmark cosine's pole value by more than its s.e. at both poles. The fit significance, r and residuals of every cosine fit are reported.

claims.statement: During the conditioning pulse, pole polarization normalized to 150 V/cm fell 1.5 times below linear scaling at 560 V/cm, 2-fold at 760 V/cm and further for stronger PEFs (p < 0.01 for all points at 560 V/cm and above, one-sample t-test).
claims.source: Results, section 3.7, paragraph 5; Figure 7B, top panel
claims.quote: Actual measurements fell 1.5 times below this line for 560 V/cm PEFs, 2- fold for 760 V/cm PEFs, and diverged further for more intense PEFs (p < 0.01 for all datapoints ≥560 V/cm, one sample t-test).
claims.criterion: Section 3.7 says the top panel uses the Fig. 4B data (conditioning pulses without test pulses; n = 5), with pole dF at 150 V/cm taken as 100% and linear scaling as E/150 x 100%. The fields 560 and 760 V/cm are read as the 570 and 780 V/cm sets of Fig. 4B. The paper does not say whether normalization is per cell or of the group mean; readings (a) per cell, then averaged; (b) group mean over group mean. Per pole, the one-sample t-test of per-cell normalized values against the linear expectation. Reproduced when, under a reading, both ratios are within tolerance at both poles or in their mean, the ratio grows beyond 760 V/cm, and p < 0.01 at every field of 560 V/cm and above.
