claims.statement: Odor-period active cells were more likely to have spatial fields than inactive cells, in CA1 (71 of 108 against 273 of 477) and PFC (83 of 128 against 76 of 160).
claims.source: Results, Representations of choice and space are maintained independently during stem running, paragraph 2; Figure 7b
claims.quote: Cells that were odor period active were more likely to have spatial fields on the track (odor sampling periods were excluded in spatial responses, see Methods ), compared to cells that were not ( Figure 7b , binomial test
claims.criterion: Binomial test of the active cells with fields against n active, with null probability the fraction of inactive cells with fields, one-sided upper (code F7/SummaryObjPlaceInteractions.m lines 432 to 434; the code's P(X > k) is shown beside P(X >= k)). Reproduced when both regions give p < 0.05 with active cells more likely to have fields.

claims.statement: Odor-period active cells had higher mean firing rates during running than inactive cells, in CA1 and PFC.
claims.source: Results, Representations of choice and space are maintained independently during stem running, paragraph 2; Figure 7-figure supplement 1b
claims.quote: Additionally, for both CA1 and PFC neurons, we found odor period active cells had higher firing rates overall ( Figure 7—figure supplement 1b )
claims.criterion: Mean firing rate of each cell during running on the maze, excluding the odor sampling periods (legend), at speed over 3 cm/s; rank-sum of active against inactive cells (code lines 485 and 500). Reproduced when both regions give p < 0.05 with active cells higher.

claims.statement: Place field width, peak rate and sparsity did not differ between odor-period active and inactive cells in either region.
claims.source: Results, Representations of choice and space are maintained independently during stem running, paragraph 2; Figure 7c; Figure 7-figure supplement 1c-d
claims.quote: Surprisingly however, we found no difference in field width ( Figure 7c , rank-sum tests ... field peak rate ( Figure 7—figure supplement 1c ), or field sparsity
claims.criterion: Each outbound field counted separately (Methods and legend 7c). Width by flood fill from the peak to the bins where rate falls below 25% of peak; peak rate on the smoothed linearized map; sparsity as Skaggs et al. 1993 (Methods). Rank-sum of active against inactive fields. Absence claim - reproduced when all six tests give p >= 0.05, not reproduced when any gives p < 0.05; medians are reported.

claims.statement: Trajectory-selective cells were more likely than non-selective cells to be active in the odor period.
claims.source: Results, Representations of choice and space are maintained independently during stem running, paragraph 3; Figure 7-figure supplement 1e
claims.quote: although trajectory-selective cells were significantly more likely than trajectory-nonselective cells to respond in the decision-making period ( Figure 7—figure supplement 1e )
claims.criterion: Trajectory selective as in the Methods (Trajectory selectivity) - the correlation of the left and right outbound linearized tuning curves below the 5th percentile of a null from shuffling trajectory identity across runs; the code has no such shuffle (a plain correlation, code line 944) and uses splitter scores instead, so the Methods' rule is used with 500 shuffles (the code's count for its scores, F7/CalcLinTrajectories.m) and the code's SplitterScore at p < 0.05 is a variant. Binomial test as in fig7b-odor-active-more-fields, the share of trajectory-selective cells that are odor active tested against the share among non-selective cells. Reproduced when both regions give p < 0.05 in that direction.

claims.statement: Among choice-selective cells, the preferred run trajectory was unrelated to the preferred choice in the odor period.
claims.source: Results, Representations of choice and space are maintained independently during stem running, paragraph 3; Figure 7d
claims.quote: there was no relationship between the preferred trajectory during run periods and preferred choice during the odor-cued decision-making period ( Figure 7d , rank sum test
claims.criterion: Trajectory selectivity index from the Methods - the mean rate on each outbound run from 0.5 s after odor port exit once speed exceeds 3 cm/s to the run's end (goal reached or speed under 3 cm/s for more than 0.5 s), averaged per trajectory, (left - right)/(left + right). Rank-sum of the index between choice-selective cells preferring one choice and those preferring the other (code line 1065). Absence claim - reproduced when both regions give p >= 0.05; medians are reported.

claims.statement: A decoder trained on odor-period activity decoded the choice from run activity in the first fifth of the track, nearest the odor port, but at chance thereafter.
claims.source: Results, Representations of choice and space are maintained independently during stem running, paragraph 4; Figure 7e
claims.quote: We found that choice identity could be decoded at the first quintile of track, nearest to the odor port, but decoding accuracy diminished to chance level thereafter ( Figure 7e )
claims.criterion: Memoryless Poisson Bayesian decoder (Methods, Bayesian decoder) built per choice from spikes in the odor sampling period, applied to spikes of each run in each fifth of the linearized outbound trajectory (equal fifths of 123 cm, legend); runs from 0.5 s after odor port exit at speed over 3 cm/s; null from 200 shuffles of choice labels in the training set; rank-sum of real against shuffled accuracy (legend; the code's paired signed-rank over sessions, F7/Claire_Odor_Routedecoder.m line 629, a variant). Cells are task-responsive cells (legend, "task-responsive ensemble activity"); the code's units active on at least 10 trials (line 429) are a variant. The unit of the test is sessions, as in the code. Reproduced when quintile 1 is above chance with p < 0.05 and quintiles 2 to 5 are not; partially when quintile 1 is and one later quintile also is.

claims.statement: Decoders trained on the spatially active ensemble in each fifth of the track decoded the upcoming choice at every position along the trajectory.
claims.source: Results, Representations of choice and space are maintained independently during stem running, paragraph 4; Figure 7f
claims.quote: In contrast, the animal's upcoming behavioral choice could be accurately decoded at all periods along the trajectory if instead the spatially active ensembles in each respective spatial quintile was used as the training set ( Figure 7f )
claims.criterion: As fig7e-odor-decoder-first-quintile, but trained and tested on run activity in each quintile with five-fold cross-validation over runs (Methods) and 200 label shuffles. "Spatially active" is not defined; readings (a) cells with a place field on either outbound trajectory (fig7-spatial-field-counts), (b) cells firing in run, active on at least 10 runs (code lines 780 and 998 to 1000). Reproduced when all five quintiles are above chance with p < 0.05 in CA1 and in PFC; partially when four of five are in each region. The outcome is the one both readings give; when they differ the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: In CA1 the firing rate of choice-selective ensembles during outbound runs was highest within 20 cm of the odor port and fell thereafter.
claims.source: Results, Representations of choice and space are maintained independently during stem running, paragraph 4; Figure 7-figure supplement 1f
claims.quote: This is further supported by the fact that, at least for CA1, choice-selective ensemble firing rate is highest within 20 cm of the odor port, and decreases thereafter
claims.criterion: Mean over choice-selective cells of each cell's linearized outbound rate (code F7/SummaryObjPlaceInteractions.m lines 834 to 873 use odor-selective cells, though the legend says odor period active; both shown); null from circularly shifting each cell's curve by a random number of bins 1000 times (code lines 834 to 873), a position marked when the ensemble rate exceeds the null's 99th percentile (legend). The Results say choice-selective and the legend odor period active, so the cell set is a reading of which subset is meant, a match under either. Reproduced when the CA1 ensemble rate peaks within 20 cm of the odor port and is lower beyond 20 cm than within it; the marked positions are reported.

claims.statement: In a Y-maze preference test between saline and 2-phenylethanol, mice spend more time in the arm with the APP odor.
claims.source: Figure 1B and 1C; Results, APP and AV odors elicit innate behavioral responses, paragraph 1
claims.quote: In a preference test between saline (SAL) and the APP odor, mice spent significantly more time in the arm with the APP odor ( t (16) = −5.7, p < 0.001; Figures 1B and 1C ), indicating approach to the APP odor.
claims.criterion: Time in each arm from tracking over the 10 min session (Methods, Odor preference behavior tests), expressed as percent change of time in the odor arm against the saline arm (Figure 1C legend). What the t-test compares is open. Readings are (a) unpaired, SAL-vs-SAL mice against SAL-vs-APP mice on the percent change (the legends' groups; this gives df 15, not 16), (b) paired, time in the odor arm against the saline arm within the APP mice (df 8), and (c) unpaired, time in the odor arm against time in the saline arm across the 9 APP mice (Figure 1B shows time in each arm; df 16, as reported). Reproduced when p < 0.05 with more time near the APP odor under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: In a preference test between saline and mountain lion urine, mice spend more time in the saline arm.
claims.source: Figure 1B and 1C; Results, APP and AV odors elicit innate behavioral responses, paragraph 1
claims.quote: In contrast, in a preference test between SAL and the AV odor, mice spent significantly more time in the arm with SAL ( t (14) = −5.06, p < 0.001; Figures 1B and 1C ), indicating avoidance of the AV odor.
claims.criterion: As in fig1c-app-approach, with readings (a) unpaired SAL-vs-SAL against SAL-vs-AV mice (df 14, as reported), (b) paired within AV mice (df 7) and (c) unpaired, odor arm against saline arm time across the 8 AV mice (df 14, as reported). Reproduced when p < 0.05 with more time in the saline arm under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Neither odor changes total distance traveled or velocity in the preference test, and there are no sex differences in approach or avoidance.
claims.source: Results, APP and AV odors elicit innate behavioral responses, paragraph 1; Figure S1A to S1D (not in the text read)
claims.quote: Neither the APP nor the AV odor affected total distance traveled or velocity ( Figures S1A and S1B ). We did not find any sex differences in approach or avoidance behavior in response to odor exposure ( Figures S1C and S1D ).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The test in Figure S1 is not in the text read; the Methods give a one-way ANOVA for three groups (SAL, APP, AV) and a two-tailed t-test for two (male against female), alpha 0.05. Reproduced when none of these finds a difference at p < 0.05; give the effect sizes.

claims.statement: The total number of cFos+ cells in the VP increases after exposure to either odor, while the number of ChAT+ neurons does not differ between groups.
claims.source: Figure 1F; Results, Approach and avoidance behaviors engage VP cholinergic neurons
claims.quote: The total number of cFos + cells in the VP significantly increased following exposure to either odor ( F (2, 64) = 12.79, p < 0.001; pairwise comparisons: APP vs. SAL [ t = 4.29, p < 0.001], AV vs. SAL [ t = 4.64, p < 0.001]; Figure 1F , right). ... The number of cholinergic neurons identified was equivalent between groups (ChAT counts; Figure 1F , left).
claims.criterion: Imaris counts in the whole VP (Methods, Quantification). The unit of analysis is open. The Methods average 4 to 6 slices per mouse, which gives df (2, 22); the reported df (2, 64) implies 67 observations, which fits neither 25 mice nor 4 to 6 slices per mouse (100 to 150). Readings are (a) per-mouse means and (b) per-slice counts. Reproduced when the ANOVA and both pairwise comparisons give p < 0.05 with more cFos+ cells after each odor. The equal ChAT counts are a claim of absence, judged by the same one-way ANOVA at alpha 0.05.

claims.statement: Exposure to either odor increases the number of ChAT+ cFos+ VP neurons and the percentage of ChAT+ neurons that are cFos+ (about 20%).
claims.source: Figure 1G; Results, Approach and avoidance behaviors engage VP cholinergic neurons
claims.quote: Cholinergic neurons were activated following exposure to either odor (number of co-localized ChAT and cFos + neurons [ Figure 1G , left]: F (2, 64) = 4.19, p < 0.05; pairwise comparison: APP vs. SAL [ t = 2.77, p < 0.05], AV vs. SAL [ t = 2.26, p < 0.05]; percentage of ChAT neurons that were cFos + after odor exposure [ Figure 1G , right]: F (2, 64) = 4.35, p < 0.05; pairwise comparisons: APP vs. SAL [ t = 2.63, p < 0.05], AV vs. SAL [ t = 2.59, p < 0.05]).
claims.criterion: As in fig1f-cfos-total, with the same two readings of the unit. The 20% is stated in Results, Distinct and non-overlapping subpopulations, paragraph 1 ("equivalent numbers (~20%)"). Reproduced when all six tests give p < 0.05 with higher values after each odor and the percentage after each odor is within the tolerance.

claims.statement: The AUC of the z-scored calcium signal of VP cholinergic neurons rises during APP odor deliveries compared with the pre-odor and post-odor periods.
claims.source: Figure 1I and 1K; Results, VP cholinergic neurons display time-locked increases in calcium activity, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The area under the curve (AUC) was significantly increased during each APP odor delivery ( F (4, 34) = 14.28, p < 0.001, Figure 1K ; pairwise comparisons: APP 1 vs. pre-odor [ t = 6.35, p < 0.001], APP 1 vs. post-odor [ t = 5.66, p < 0.001], APP 2 vs. pre-odor [ t = 3.02, p < 0.05], APP 3 vs. pre-odor [ t = 4.74, p < 0.001], APP 3 vs. post-odor [ t = 4.04, p < 0.05]).
claims.criterion: Signal from the 470 nm channel normalized to the 415 nm isosbestic channel (Methods; the code's normalization of the signal to its own biexponential fit is a variant), initialization frames (5 s) removed, 5 Hz bins, dF/F z-scored (Methods and code, whole session). AUC of the z-score in each 10 s delivery. The length of the pre-odor and post-odor windows is open, as is the design behind df (4, 34), which matches neither an independent (4, 30) nor a repeated measures (4, 24) ANOVA over 7 mice; readings are (a) 10 s windows before the first and after the last delivery and (b) the whole pre-odor and post-odor periods of the session. Reproduced when the ANOVA gives p < 0.05, each APP delivery exceeds pre-odor at p < 0.05 (as reported for all three) and APP 1 exceeds post-odor at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The AUC of the z-scored calcium signal rises during AV odor deliveries compared with the pre-odor and post-odor periods.
claims.source: Figure 1J and 1L; Results, VP cholinergic neurons display time-locked increases in calcium activity, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Likewise, the integrated Ca 2+ signal (AUC), was significantly increased following each AV odor delivery ( F (4, 34) = 12.34, p < 0.001, Figure 1L ; pairwise comparisons: AV 1 vs. pre-odor [ t = 5.78, p < 0.001], AV 1 vs. post-odor [ t = 5.15, p < 0.001], AV 2 vs. pre-odor [ t = 4.16, p < 0.05], AV 2 vs. post-odor [ t = 3.53, p < 0.05], AV 3 vs. pre-odor [ t = 3.81, p < 0.05], AV 3 vs. post-odor [ t = 3.19, p < 0.05]).
claims.criterion: As in fig1k-app-calcium-auc. Reproduced when the ANOVA gives p < 0.05 and each AV delivery exceeds pre-odor at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The maximum z-scored dF/F is higher during the first APP and the first AV odor delivery.
claims.source: Figure 1M and 1N; Results, VP cholinergic neurons display time-locked increases in calcium activity, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The maximum Z -score × F/F was significantly increased during the first APP odor ( F (4, 34) = 4.4, p < 0.05; t = 3.69, p < 0.05; Figure 1M ) and first AV odor ( F (4, 34) = 5.19, p < 0.05; t = 3.90, p <0.05; Figure 1N ).
claims.criterion: Max z-score dF/F is the highest z-score in the 10 s delivery (Methods); processing and the open windows as in fig1k-app-calcium-auc. The comparison the pairwise t names is not stated; readings are first delivery against pre-odor and against post-odor. Reproduced when each ANOVA gives p < 0.05 and the first delivery exceeds the comparison epoch at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Chemogenetic inhibition of VP cholinergic neurons (hM4Di) abolishes approach to the APP odor, and mice spend more time in the saline arm than in the APP arm.
claims.source: Figure 2B and 2C; Results, Silencing VP cholinergic neurons not only abolishes but reverses approach behavior, paragraph 1
claims.quote: In contrast, hM4Di inhibition of VP cholinergic neurons abolished this effect, and mice spent significantly more time in the SAL arm than in the arm with the APP odor ( t (8) = 4.21, p < 0.05; Figures 2B [right] and 2C ).
claims.criterion: What the t-test compares is open. Readings are (a) percent change of time in odor against saline arm (Figure 2C), sham (eGFP plus clozapine) against hM4Di mice, unpaired two-tailed t-test (df 8 matches 5 and 5), and (b) time in the saline arm against time in the APP arm across the 5 hM4Di mice, unpaired (the sentence's comparison; also df 8). Reproduced when p < 0.05 with the hM4Di mice spending more time in the saline arm under both readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Chemogenetic inhibition of VP cholinergic neurons does not change avoidance of the AV odor, and does not change locomotion or time in each arm with saline in both arms.
claims.source: Figure 2D and 2E; Figure S3 (not in the text read); Results, Silencing VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Mice with hM4Di inhibition of VP cholinergic neurons also displayed avoidance of the AV odor ( Figures 2D [right] and 2E ). These results indicate that inhibition of cholinergic signaling in the VP was not sufficient to alter avoidance of the AV odor. These results were not due to any hM4Di-induced changes in behavior, as mice in both groups displayed comparable locomotor activity ( Figures S3A – S3D ). Furthermore, mice with hM4Di inhibition of VP cholinergic neurons displayed equal time spent in each arm during a preference test with SAL in both arms of the Y-maze ( Figures S3E and S3F ), ...
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged by an unpaired two-tailed t-test of sham against hM4Di mice (n = 7 and 7) at alpha 0.05 (Methods). Reproduced when it finds no difference and both groups avoid the AV odor (mean percent change below zero); give the effect size. The locomotion and SAL-SAL parts (Figure S3) have no test in the text read; they are judged by the same two-tailed t-test (sham against hM4Di for locomotion, saline arm against saline arm for the SAL-SAL test) and reported apart.

claims.statement: When the same odor is given on both days, virtually all VP cholinergic neurons labeled by ADCD on day 1 are also cFos+ on day 2; saline on both days labels very few.
claims.source: Figure 3B to 3D; Results, Distinct and non-overlapping subpopulations, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Notably, in each case, virtually all of the ADCD + VP cholinergic neurons (activated during the first exposure) were also cFos + (reactivated during the second exposure).
claims.criterion: Counts of ChAT+ ADCD+, ChAT+ cFos+ and ChAT+ ADCD+ cFos+ neurons per mouse, averaged over 4 to 6 VP slices (Methods). No threshold for "virtually all" is given; reproduced when the reactivated count is at least 90% of the ChAT+ ADCD+ count in the APP/APP and AV/AV groups (n = 4 mice each) and SAL/SAL counts are far below both (the 90% is this file's reading of "virtually all", named as such).

claims.statement: Neurons activated by one odor are not reactivated by the opposite-valence odor a day later; the number of reactivated VP cholinergic neurons is far greater with the same odor on both days.
claims.source: Figure 4B to 4D; Results, Distinct and non-overlapping subpopulations, paragraphs 2 and 3
claims.quote: If mice were exposed to the same odor on days 1 and 2, there was a significantly greater number of reactivated VP cholinergic neurons ( F (3, 17) = 68.8, p < 0.001; Figure 4D , APP/APP and AV/AV compared to APP/AV and AV/APP), whereas if mice were exposed to a different odor on day 2, there was no overlap between ChAT + /ADCD + and ChAT + /cFos + VP cholinergic neurons.
claims.criterion: Reactivated counts (ChAT+ ADCD+ cFos+) per mouse across the four groups, one-way ANOVA (Methods). Reproduced when p < 0.001 and the APP/AV and AV/APP groups have zero, or essentially zero, reactivated neurons; partially reproduced when p < 0.05 with the same pattern.

claims.statement: ChAT+ counts do not differ across the reactivation experiments, and both odors increase ADCD+ and cFos+ VP cholinergic neurons compared with saline, whichever day they are given.
claims.source: Figures S5A to S5C and S6 (not in the text read); Results, Distinct and non-overlapping subpopulations, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Importantly, the number of ChAT + neurons was not significantly different across experiments ( Figure S5A ), and both odors increased the number of ADCD + ( Figure S5B ) and cFos + ( Figure S5C ) neurons, regardless of which day the odor was presented.
claims.criterion: Tests in Figures S5 and S6 are not in the text read. Methods give one-way ANOVA across groups, alpha 0.05. Reproduced when ChAT+ counts show no difference and odor groups exceed SAL for ADCD+ and cFos+ at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The non-overlap of APP- and AV-activated VP cholinergic neurons is replicated with the RAM system in C57 mice.
claims.source: Figures S7 and S8 (not in the text read); Results, Distinct and non-overlapping subpopulations, paragraph 3
claims.quote: We replicated these findings using the robust activity marking (RAM) system in C57 mice ( Figures S7 and S8 ).
claims.criterion: No number or test for this replication is in the text read. Reproduced when the RAM data show reactivation with the same odor and essentially none with the opposite odor, as in fig4d-different-odor-no-reactivation.

claims.statement: A second odor of the same valence reactivates most day-1 neurons, about 80% for two APP odors (2-phenylethanol then peanut butter oil) and about 70% for two AV odors (mountain lion urine then peppermint oil).
claims.source: Figure S9 (not in the text read); Results, Distinct and non-overlapping subpopulations, paragraph 3
claims.quote: In these mice, ~80% of VP cholinergic neurons activated on day 1 were reactivated on day 2 ( Figures S9A and S9B ). ... In these mice, ~70% of day-1-activated VP cholinergic neurons were reactivated ( Figures S9C and S9D ).
claims.criterion: Percentage is ChAT+ ADCD+ cFos+ over ChAT+ ADCD+. Whether it is pooled over mice or the mean of per-mouse percentages is open; both readings are run.

claims.statement: Selective inhibition (ADCD-hM4Di) of VP cholinergic neurons activated by the APP odor abolishes approach to it and produces avoidance.
claims.source: Figure 5B and 5C; Results, Selective inhibition of VP cholinergic neurons previously activated by the APP odor, paragraph 1
claims.quote: However, selective silencing of VP cholinergic neurons that were previously activated by exposure to the APP odor abolished this behavior ( t (11) = 2.72, p < 0.05; Figures 5B [right] and 5C ). Particularly striking was that inhibition of previously activated APP odor VP cholinergic neurons not only blocked approach behavior but in fact elicited active avoidance of the APP odor.
claims.criterion: Percent change of time in odor against saline arm on day 2 with clozapine, sham against ADCD-hM4Di, unpaired two-tailed t-test (df 11 matches 6 and 7). Reproduced when p < 0.05 with the inhibited group below zero.

claims.statement: Selective inhibition of VP cholinergic neurons activated by the AV odor does not change avoidance of it, nor locomotion.
claims.source: Figure 5D and 5E; Figure S10 (not in the text read); Results, Selective inhibition, paragraph 2
claims.quote: In sharp contrast to the dramatic effects of silencing APP-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, mice with ADCD-hM4Di silencing of VP cholinergic neurons previously activated by exposure to the AV odor had no effect ( Figures 5D [right] and 5E ). These results underscore our findings using hM4Di for non-selective inhibition of VP cholinergic neurons ( Figure 2 ) and were devoid of any changes in locomotor activity ( Figure S10 ).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged by an unpaired two-tailed t-test of sham (n = 5) against ADCD-hM4Di (n = 6) at alpha 0.05 (Methods). Reproduced when it finds no difference; give the effect size.

claims.statement: APP- and AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons are spatially intermingled within the VP from bregma +0.62 to +0.14.
claims.source: Figure S11 (not in the text read); Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons are intermingled, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Across the targeted regions (bregma +0.62 to +0.14), we found that these differentially activated subgroups of VP cholinergic neurons are spatially intermingled within the VP ( Figure S11 ).
claims.criterion: Shown as a map with no test. Reproduced when cells of both groups occupy overlapping positions on each mapped section, with no section or VP subregion holding one group alone.

claims.statement: APP- and AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons both have a higher maximum firing rate than home-cage VP cholinergic neurons.
claims.source: Figure 6F; Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Both APP and AV VP cholinergic neurons displayed a greater rate of maximum firing ( F (2, 38) = 10.71, pairwise comparisons: ALL vs. APP t (31) = 5.36, p < 0.01; ALL vs. AV t (27) = 2.80, p < 0.05; Figure 6F ) and sag potential ( Figure S12A ).
claims.criterion: Max firing rate as defined in the opening comment (Methods item 16; spike detection from the code v1.0.0). Cells are those of Figure 6 (APP 12, AV 8, ALL 21, compared with the dataset's counts); the Methods' exclusion rules (series resistance over 25 MOhm, input resistance under 50 MOhm, resting potential above -50 mV, or a change of more than 20% in any of these) are applied, and any rule the data do not allow to be checked is named. The test is open between two readings, both run; when they disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified. (a) Cell-level one-way ANOVA over the three groups (df 2, 38) and uncorrected two-tailed unpaired t-tests for each pair (df 31 and 27, as reported). (b) The nested ANOVA the Methods name, cells nested in mice nested in group. Reproduced when both pairwise comparisons give p < 0.05 with APP and AV above ALL; the F is compared with 10.71 and the t values with 5.36 and 2.80, without deciding the outcome.

claims.statement: APP- and AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons both have a larger sag potential than home-cage VP cholinergic neurons.
claims.source: Figure S12A (not in the text read); Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Both APP and AV VP cholinergic neurons displayed a greater rate of maximum firing ... and sag potential ( Figure S12A ).
claims.criterion: Sag as defined in the opening comment (Methods item 2, with the code's smoothing and windows). The test in Figure S12A is not in the text read; the two readings of fig6f-max-firing-rate are used. Reproduced when APP and AV each exceed ALL at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Most other passive and active electrophysiological features do not differ between home-cage and odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons.
claims.source: Figure S12 (not in the text read); Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Most other passive and active features were shared by control and odor-sensitive VP cholinergic neurons ( Figure S12 ).
claims.criterion: A claim of absence over the eighteen features of the Methods, less the four the paper reports as different (max firing rate, sag, membrane potential, AHP amplitude). Each feature is tested by the one-way ANOVA over the three groups at alpha 0.05 (reading (a) of fig6f-max-firing-rate, the test whose df the paper reports). Which features Figure S12 shows is not known here. Reproduced when more than half of the fourteen remaining features show no difference (this file's reading of "most"); list every feature with its effect and p.

claims.statement: AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons have a more hyperpolarized membrane potential than APP-odor-activated ones.
claims.source: Figure 6C and 6G; Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Specifically, AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons were slightly more hyperpolarized than APP-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons ( F (2, 38) = 11.39, p < 0.001; pairwise comparisons: APP vs. AV t (18) = 2.72, p < 0.05; Figures 6C and 6G ).
claims.criterion: Membrane potential with the two readings in the opening comment ((a) the code's baselineVm, (b) a segment with no injected current), crossed with the two test readings of fig6f-max-firing-rate. Reproduced when the ANOVA gives p < 0.05 and the APP against AV comparison gives p < 0.05 with AV more negative under every reading run; partially reproduced when only the pairwise comparison holds. If the readings disagree the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified, with every result shown.

claims.statement: AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons have a smaller afterhyperpolarization amplitude than APP-odor-activated ones.
claims.source: Figure 6B (right), 6D and 6H; Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 3
claims.quote: AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons also had a smaller amplitude of the afterhyperpolarization potential ( F (2, 38) = 4.53, p < 0.05; pairwise comparisons: APP vs. AV, t = 2.74, p < 0.05; Figures 6D and 6H ).
claims.criterion: AHP amplitude per the Methods (item 12), with threshold at dV/dt 20 mV/ms, under the two readings in the opening comment ((a) the minimum within 100 ms after threshold, (b) the voltage at 100 ms); the code v1.0.0 definition is shown as a variant. Tests as the two readings of fig6f-max-firing-rate. Reproduced when the ANOVA and the APP against AV comparison give p < 0.05 with AV smaller under every Methods reading; blocked as methods_underspecified if they disagree.

claims.statement: APP-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons are less excitable than AV-odor-activated ones, with different action potential profiles.
claims.source: Figure 6B to 6E; Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 3
claims.quote: The net effect of the differences in these features underlies the phenotype that APP VP cholinergic neurons are less excitable than AV VP cholinergic neurons.
claims.criterion: An interpretation with no test of its own. Figure 6B (middle) shows "differences in latency to fire an action potential" at rheobase. The measure of excitability is open; readings are (a) spike latency at rheobase (Methods item 9) longer in APP and (b) rheobase (item 5) higher in APP, each by the two test readings of fig6f-max-firing-rate at p < 0.05. Reproduced when every reading gives a significant difference in that direction, not reproduced when none does, blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: The convex hull of APP-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons has a smaller surface area (and volume) than that of AV-odor-activated neurons.
claims.source: Figure 6I and 6J; Figure S13C (not in the text read); Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 4
claims.quote: The convex hull enveloping APP-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons was smaller in surface area ( F (1, 10) = 12.22, p < 0.05; Figure 6J ) and volume ( Figure S13C ) compared to AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons.
claims.criterion: Convex hull from the Imaris filament reconstruction of the soma-proximal arbor (Methods, Neuronal morphology). Tests as the two readings of fig6f-max-firing-rate with two groups (df 1, 10 matches 12 cells). Reproduced when surface area is smaller in APP at p < 0.05; the volume has no test in the text read and is reported by the same test.

claims.statement: APP-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons have a smaller dendrite area and dendrite volume than AV-odor-activated neurons.
claims.source: Figure 6K and 6L; Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 4
claims.quote: APP-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons also exhibited a significantly smaller dendrite area ( F (1, 10) = 26.77, p < 0.05; Figure 6K ) and dendrite volume ( F (1, 10) = 57.31, p <0.05; Figure 6L ).
claims.criterion: Imaris filament dendrite area and volume. Tests as the two readings of fig6f-max-firing-rate with two groups. Reproduced when both are smaller in APP at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: APP-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons have more Sholl intersections at 10 and 20 micrometres from the soma than AV-odor-activated neurons.
claims.source: Figure 6M; Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 4
claims.quote: In addition to these features, APP-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons had a significantly greater number of intersecting points in a Sholl analysis at distances close to the soma (at 10 μm F (1, 10) = −2.69, p <0.05; at 20 μm F (1, 10) = −3.16, p <0.05; Figure 6M ).
claims.criterion: Imaris Sholl intersections; the shell spacing is not given, and the two distances named (10 and 20 micrometres) imply a step of 10 micrometres at most. Tests as the two readings of fig6f-max-firing-rate with two groups at each distance. Reproduced when APP exceeds AV at both distances at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: About 80% of AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons have dendrites reaching at least 100 micrometres from the soma, against less than 20% of APP-odor-activated neurons.
claims.source: Figure 6N; Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 4
claims.quote: The dendritic arbor of ~80% of AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons extended at least 100 μm from the soma, whereas less than 20% of APP-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons reached this distance ( Figure 6N ).
claims.criterion: Percentage of reconstructed cells (AV n = 6, APP n = 10, Figure 6M legend) with a Sholl intersection at 100 micrometres or beyond. No test is reported. Reproduced when AV is within 80 +- 8% and APP is below 22%. With 6 AV cells, 80% is not an exact fraction (5 of 6 is 83%).

claims.statement: Other morphometric features do not differ between APP- and AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons.
claims.source: Figure S13 (not in the text read); Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Additional morphometric features that were not statistically different between APP- and AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons are shown in Figure S13 .
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Which features Figure S13 shows is not known here; the Methods' nested ANOVA at alpha 0.05 is the test. Testable only if the features are named, which needs the supplement.

claims.statement: Equal numbers of VP cholinergic neurons are activated by the APP and AV odors, but a larger percentage of BLA-projecting (Fast Blue+) VP cholinergic neurons is activated by the AV odor.
claims.source: Figure 7D; Results, APP- vs. AV-odor-activated VP cholinergic neurons, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Although we found an equal number of VP cholinergic neurons that were activated by the APP vs. AV odor ( Figure 7D , left), the relative proportion of BLA-projecting APP vs. AV VP cholinergic neurons was not equivalent. The percentage of BLA-projecting VP cholinergic neurons that were activated by the AV odor was significantly greater than the number of BLA-projecting VP cholinergic neurons activated by the APP odor ( t (6) = −2.98, p < 0.05; Figure 7D , right).
claims.criterion: Counts per mouse averaged over slices (Methods). The percentage is open between (a) ChAT+ Fast Blue+ cFos+ over ChAT+ Fast Blue+ neurons in the VP (the sentence and the Figure 7D legend) and (b) ChAT+ Fast Blue+ cFos+ over ChAT+ cFos+ neurons (the "relative proportion of BLA-projecting APP vs. AV" neurons). Unpaired two-tailed t-test of AV against APP mice. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with AV higher under both readings, blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree; the equal ChAT+ cFos+ counts (Figure 7D, left) are a claim of absence by the same test at alpha 0.05.

claims.statement: In WT mice SGC somata lie closer to the GCL-MOL boundary than GC somata (SGCs in the top cell body layers, under 20 micrometres from the surface).
claims.source: Figure 1F; Results, SGCs have unique morphological and electrical properties, paragraph 2
claims.quote: SGC cell body locations were significantly different from those of GCs (**** P < 0.0001, Welch’s t test [two-tailed]; t = 8.471, df = 19.16)
claims.criterion: Soma position is the vertical distance from the cell body centre to the GCL-MOL boundary (Methods, Imaging and image analysis). Two-tailed Welch's t test of WT SGC against WT GC positions, as in the legend. Reproduced when p < 0.0001 with SGCs nearer the boundary; partially reproduced when p < 0.05 with SGCs nearer the boundary.

claims.statement: WT SGCs have wider dendritic splay angles than WT GCs.
claims.source: Figure 1G
claims.quote: The splay angle (angle between the two farthest dendrites measured at the center of the cell body) was significantly larger in SGCs compared with GCs (* P = 0.0168, Welch’s t test [two-tailed]; t = 2.754, df = 12.59)
claims.criterion: Splay angle as the Methods define it (FIJI angle tool, from the most laterally displaced dendritic termination through the soma centre to the opposite one). Two-tailed Welch's t test. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with SGCs wider.

claims.statement: WT GCs have more dendritic branch points per primary dendrite than WT SGCs.
claims.source: Figure 1H
claims.quote: The number of branch points was significantly higher in GCs compared with SGCs (** P = 0.0023, Mann–Whitney test, U = 2)
claims.criterion: Branch points from the Imaris reconstruction divided by the number of primary dendrites (legend). Two-tailed Mann-Whitney test (the legend does not state tails, but U = 2 with 11 and 5 cells gives the reported P only two-tailed). Reproduced when p < 0.05 with GCs higher.

claims.statement: WT GCs have greater dendritic length per primary dendrite than WT SGCs.
claims.source: Figure 1I
claims.quote: The normalized dendritic length was significantly higher in GCs compared with SGCs (*** P = 0.0004, Welch’s t test [two-tailed]; t = 5.348, df = 9.366)
claims.criterion: Total dendritic length divided by the number of primary dendrites (legend). Two-tailed Welch's t test. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with GCs longer.

claims.statement: In WT mice SGCs have a more hyperpolarized resting membrane potential than GCs.
claims.source: Figure 1J; Results, SGCs have unique morphological and electrical properties, paragraph 2
claims.quote: SGCs have a significantly more hyperpolarized resting membrane potential compared with GCs (* P = 0.02, Mann–Whitney test, U = 26; N = 14 cells [GCs] and 9 cells [SGCs] from 5 mice)
claims.criterion: RMP per cell as defined in the opening comment (code, baseline before step onset). WT SGCs against WT GCs by two-tailed Mann-Whitney test (tails are not stated, but U = 26 with 14 and 9 cells gives P = 0.02 only two-tailed). Reproduced when p < 0.05 with SGCs more negative. The cell counts are compared with 14 and 9, and U with 26.

claims.statement: In WT mice SGCs have narrower action potentials than GCs.
claims.source: Figure 1K; Results, SGCs have unique morphological and electrical properties, paragraph 2
claims.quote: SGCs have a significantly narrower spike width compared with GCs (* P = 0.012, Mann–Whitney test, U = 24
claims.criterion: Spike width at half height between threshold and peak of the first spike at rheobase, threshold at dV/dt 20 mV/ms (Kim et al, the Methods' reference); the code's 10 mV/ms threshold is shown as a variant. Two-tailed Mann-Whitney test (U = 24 with 14 and 9 cells gives P = 0.012 only two-tailed). Reproduced when p < 0.05 with SGCs narrower.

claims.statement: In WT mice SGCs have a faster action potential downstroke than GCs.
claims.source: Figure 1L; Results, SGCs have unique morphological and electrical properties, paragraph 2
claims.quote: SGCs have a significantly faster downstroke compared with GCs (* P = 0.046, Mann–Whitney test, U = 31
claims.criterion: Downstroke as the minimum dV/dt on the repolarizing phase of the first spike at rheobase (Kim et al). The code's window, from 5 ms before the first peak to the end of the first 500 ms of the step, is a second reading, as the code disagrees with the Methods' reference only where the rheobase sweep holds more than one spike. Two-tailed Mann-Whitney test (U = 31 with 14 and 9 cells gives P = 0.046 only two-tailed). Reproduced when p < 0.05 with SGCs more negative under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree, with each shown.

claims.statement: Phase plots of the action potential at rheobase show differences in waveform kinetics between WT GCs and SGCs.
claims.source: Figure 1M; Results, SGCs have unique morphological and electrical properties, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The pronounced differences in the kinetics of the SGC action potentials can be seen in the phase plots for APs at rheobase
claims.criterion: For each cell, dV/dt against Vm minus threshold for the first spike at rheobase, dV/dt as the first difference over the time step (makephaseplot.m). Shown as a figure; the claim is judged as reproduced when fig1k-sgc-narrower-spike and fig1l-sgc-faster-downstroke are, since the paper reads the plot through those two measures.

claims.statement: In WT cells (GCs and SGCs together), RMP, spike width, downstroke, rheobase, sag and upstroke-downstroke ratio covary with soma position.
claims.source: Figure S1A to F; Results, SGCs have unique morphological and electrical properties, paragraph 3
claims.quote: We found that RMP ( Fig S1A , P = 0.0129), spike width ( Fig S1B , P = 0.0543), and downstroke ( Fig S1C , P = 0.0139) significantly covaried with soma position ... We also found that rheobase ( Fig S1D , P = 0.0475), sag ( Fig S1E , P = 0.0359), and upstroke–downstroke ratio ( Fig S1F , P = 0.0131) significantly covaried with soma positions in the GCL
claims.criterion: The legend reports P and R2 per property, so each is a simple linear regression of the property on soma position over the 23 WT cells (14 GC, 9 SGC), as fitted in Prism (Methods, Statistical analysis). The paper counts spike width (P = 0.0543) as significant, so a property matches when its slope p is at most 1.1 times the reported p or its R2 is within tolerance. Reproduced when all six match; partially reproduced when four or five match. Feature definitions as in the opening comment; the code's variants are shown.

claims.statement: The remaining electrophysiological properties differ neither between WT GCs and SGCs nor with soma position.
claims.source: Results, SGCs have unique morphological and electrical properties, paragraph 3
claims.quote: The remainder of the properties did not differ significantly between GCs and SGCs or by soma position
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's tests at p < 0.05. For each property other than the six of figs1a-f and the three of Fig 1J to L, WT GC against SGC by Welch's t test when both groups pass Shapiro-Wilk and Kolmogorov-Smirnov normality tests and by Mann-Whitney test otherwise (Methods, Statistical analysis), and a linear regression on soma position as in Fig S1. Which properties make up the remainder depends on the 20 features, which the paper does not list (opening comment); the readings are (a) the 18 features of Fig S2C less the five named (RMP, spike width, downstroke, rheobase, sag), and (b) the 21 outputs of the code less those five. Reproduced when no property in the reading finds an effect; not reproduced when any does. Every test's p and effect size is shown.

claims.statement: Among WT GCs alone, downstroke and sag still covary with soma position, while RMP, spike width, rheobase and upstroke-downstroke ratio do not, so the GC-SGC differences in RMP and spike width are cell-type features.
claims.source: Figure S1G to L; Results, SGCs have unique morphological and electrical properties, paragraph 3
claims.quote: we found that downstroke and sag were still significantly correlated with soma positions ( Fig S1I , downstroke, P = 0.006, and Fig S1K , sag, P = 0.03), whereas the rest of the properties did not correlate with soma positions ( Fig S1G , RMP, P = 0.22, Fig S1H , spike width, P = 0.1, Fig S1J , rheobase, P = 0.06, and Fig S1L , upstroke–downstroke ratio, P = 0.4)
claims.criterion: Simple linear regressions on soma position over the 14 WT GCs, as in Fig S1A to F. Reproduced when downstroke and sag have p < 0.05 and RMP, spike width, rheobase and the ratio have p >= 0.05 (the absence half judged on this test as written); partially reproduced when the two significant ones hold and one of the four absences fails. Every slope, p and R2 is shown.

claims.statement: Golgi staining labels the same total number of GCs in WT and V321L DG, but V321L DG has a higher percentage of GCs with multiple primary dendrites and a lower percentage with a single one.
claims.source: Figure 2A; Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 1
claims.quote: There was no difference in the total number of cells labeled by the Golgi stain between genotypes ( Fig 2A , left; P = 0.68). However, V 321 L mice had a significantly higher number of Golgi-stained GCs with multiple primary dendrites compared with WT mice and a significantly lower number of GCs with single primary dendrites compared with WT mice
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the percentage of Golgi-stained GCs with one and with several primary dendrites. Two-way ANOVA (genotype by dendrite class) with Bonferroni post hoc comparisons (the Methods' parametric correction). The design is not named; the reported F(1,7) fits dendrite class as a repeated measure within mouse (error df = mice minus 2, so 9 mice) and not an ordinary two-way ANOVA (16 error df with 5 mice per genotype), so the repeated-measures ANOVA is the test and the ordinary one is shown as a variant. Reproduced when the interaction has p < 0.05, both genotype comparisons have p < 0.05 in the stated directions, and the total count does not differ by two-tailed Welch's t test at p < 0.05. The Results print P = 0.68 and the legend P = 0.7 for the total; both are recorded as one test.

claims.statement: In V321L mice SGC and GC soma positions do not differ; SGCs are found throughout the GCL.
claims.source: Figure 2B, 2C and 2H; Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 2
claims.quote: SGC cell body locations are not significantly different to those of GCs ( P = 0.9012, Welch’s t test [two-tailed]; t = 0.1256, df = 21.78
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on two-tailed Welch's t test of V321L SGC against V321L GC soma positions at p < 0.05. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; the difference in means is shown.

claims.statement: In V321L mice the splay angle does not differ between GCs and SGCs.
claims.source: Figure 2D
claims.quote: The splay angle was not significantly different between GCs and SGCs
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on two-tailed Welch's t test at p < 0.05. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; the difference is shown.

claims.statement: In V321L mice GCs still have more branch points and greater dendritic length per primary dendrite than SGCs.
claims.source: Figure 2E and 2F
claims.quote: In contrast, the differences in dendritic complexity between GCs and SGCs were preserved in the V 321 L mutant DG
claims.criterion: Measures as in Fig 1H and 1I. Reproduced when both tests give p < 0.05 with GCs higher (Mann-Whitney two-tailed, as U = 13 with 9 and 13 cells gives P = 0.0013 only two-tailed); partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: Linear discriminant analysis of 15 morphological parameters separates GCs from SGCs along LD1, but not WT from V321L cells.
claims.source: Figure 2G and Figure S2A; Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 2
claims.quote: LDA resulted in successful capture of cell-type differences between GCs and SGCs (along the primary classifier ... LD1) but not between genotypes
claims.criterion: Features z-scored with scale(), then LDA (MASS lda), as the Methods (LDA) describe. Whether PCA precedes this LDA, as it does for the classifier, is not stated; readings are (a) LDA on the z-scored features and (b) LDA on their top 9 PCs, and the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. The groups are not stated; Fig 2G shows LD1 and LD2, which needs at least three classes, so the reading is four classes (genotype by cell type). The parameter set is the morphological variables of Fig S2A. Reproduced when the LD1 scores of GCs and SGCs separate (a two-tailed Mann-Whitney test of LD1 by cell type at p < 0.05 and at least 90% of cells on their type's side of the midpoint between the type medians) while LD1 does not differ by genotype within either cell type (Mann-Whitney p >= 0.05). The 90% bound is not from the paper; the overlap is reported either way.

claims.statement: k-means clustering (k = 3) of morphological data groups cells by cell type, with all WT GCs in one cluster and all WT SGCs in another; all but one V321L GC and all but two V321L SGCs fall in the corresponding clusters.
claims.source: Figure S2B
claims.quote: All WT GCs and SGCs segregate into k1 and k2, respectively. All but one V 321 L GCs occupy k1, whereas the one was in k3. All but 2 V 321 L SGCs occupy k2 with one in k1 and another in k3
claims.criterion: k-means with k = 3 on the morphological data, on the PCA scores shown in the panel. The paper gives neither the number of PCs, the scaling nor the seed; readings are k-means on (a) the z-scored features and (b) the first two PCs of the z-scored features, each with 100 random starts (a standard choice). Reproduced when, under every reading, the cluster that holds most WT GCs holds all WT GCs and no WT SGC and the counts of V321L cells outside their type's cluster are within one of the paper's (1 GC, 2 SGCs).

claims.statement: In V321L mice GCs and SGCs do not differ in RMP; both lie near the WT SGC median.
claims.source: Figure 2I; Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 3; Discussion, Composition of cell-type identity, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Unlike WT GCs and SGCs, we found no differences in electrical properties between V 321 L GCs and SGCs ( Fig 2I–K , RMP, P = 0.9
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on Welch's t test of V321L GC against SGC RMP at p < 0.05. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; the difference and both group medians, beside the WT GC and SGC medians, are shown.

claims.statement: In V321L mice GCs and SGCs do not differ in spike width.
claims.source: Figure 2J
claims.quote: Spike width ( P = 0.2776, Mann–Whitney test, U = 55)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on a two-tailed Mann-Whitney test at p < 0.05, with spike width as in fig1k-sgc-narrower-spike. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; the code's threshold is shown as a variant and the medians are shown.

claims.statement: In V321L mice GCs and SGCs do not differ in downstroke.
claims.source: Figure 2K
claims.quote: Downstroke ( P = 0.5392, Mann–Whitney test, U = 63.5)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on a two-tailed Mann-Whitney test at p < 0.05, with downstroke as in fig1l-sgc-faster-downstroke (Kim et al definition). Reproduced when p >= 0.05; the code's window is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: LDA of electrical properties separates WT GCs from all other groups (WT SGCs, V321L GCs, V321L SGCs) along LD1, driven mainly by spike width and downstroke.
claims.source: Figure 2M and Figure S2C; Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 3
claims.quote: LDA resulted in separation of WT GCs and all other groups (WT SGCs, V 321 L GCs, and V 321 L SGCs) along LD1 driven strongly by spike width
claims.criterion: The 18 features of Fig S2C, z-scored with scale() (Methods, LDA), LDA (MASS lda) with four classes (genotype by cell type; Fig 2M shows LD1 and LD2). Whether PCA precedes this LDA as it does for the classifier is not stated; readings are (a) LDA on the z-scored features and (b) LDA on their top 9 PCs. Cells with a missing feature are dropped. Reproduced when, under every reading, the WT GC mean LD1 lies on one side and the means of the other three groups on the other, and spike width or downstroke has the largest absolute LD1 coefficient; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: k-means clustering (k = 3) of electrophysiological data places V321L GCs and SGCs in clusters in nearly the same proportions as WT SGCs, while WT GCs spread across all three clusters.
claims.source: Figure S2D; Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 3
claims.quote: WT GCs are evenly distributed across all clusters, whereas SGCs largely occupy k3 with a minority in k1. All V 321 L GC and SGC cluster occupancy was virtually identical to WT SGCs
claims.criterion: k-means with k = 3 on the 18 features of Fig S2C. The scaling, number of PCs and seed are not given; readings are (a) z-scored features and (b) the first two PCs of the z-scored features, 100 random starts each. Reproduced when, under every reading, WT GCs occupy all three clusters with none holding more than half of them, and WT SGCs, V321L GCs and V321L SGCs each have most cells in one same cluster.

claims.statement: Controlling for soma position, spike amplitude and upstroke covary with cell type in WT mice, while no electrophysiological property shows a cell-type effect in V321L mice.
claims.source: Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 4
claims.quote: In WT mice, we found that two electrophysiological properties, spike amplitude ( P = 0.042, β1 = −46.2) and upstroke ( P = 0.038, β1 = −117.88), significantly covaried with cell type when controlling for soma position. However, this model did not detect significant cell-type effects for any electrophysiological properties in V 321 L mice
claims.criterion: Per property and genotype, lm(property ~ CellType + SomaPosition + CellType x SomaPosition) in R (Methods, Statistical analysis), soma position in micrometres from the GCL-MOL boundary. The coding of cell type is not stated; readings are SGC = 1 and GC = 1 (the sign of beta1 flips between them, so a beta1 matches when its magnitude is within tolerance and its sign fits one coding used for both properties). Reproduced when in WT the beta1 p-values for spike amplitude and upstroke are below 0.05 with beta1 within tolerance, and in V321L no property's beta1 has p < 0.05 (the absence half judged on this test). The property set for the V321L half is open (opening comment); readings are the 18 features of Fig S2C and the 21 outputs of the code. The WT properties other than these two are shown.

claims.statement: PCA of the electrophysiological features separates WT GCs from WT SGCs on the first two components, while V321L GCs and SGCs overlap.
claims.source: Figure S2E; Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Principal component analysis (PCA) revealed a clear separation between GCs and SGCs in WT mice along the first two principal components, whereas cells in V 321 L mice showed substantial overlap
claims.criterion: PCA (prcomp) of the 18 z-scored features of Fig S2C over all cells, with 95% ellipses per group as in the legend. The ellipse type is not stated; readings are (a) the 95% normal data ellipse (ggplot2 stat_ellipse default) and (b) the 95% confidence ellipse of the group mean. Reproduced when, under every reading, the WT GC and WT SGC centroids each lie outside the other group's ellipse and the V321L GC and SGC centroids each lie inside the other's; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. The centroid distances are shown.

claims.statement: In the WT-trained LDA, the distance between GC and SGC centroids along LD1 is much smaller in V321L than in WT, with both V321L centroids on the WT SGC side of the boundary.
claims.source: Figure S2F; Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Centroid analysis demonstrated a striking reduction in the separation between GC and SGC centroids in V 321 L mice along the first linear discriminant (LD1) axis
claims.criterion: The classifier of figs2g-lda-classifier-accuracy; LD1 scores of WT cells and of V321L cells (projected through the WT PCA and LDA). Reproduced when the V321L GC-SGC centroid distance on LD1 is less than half the WT distance and both V321L centroids lie on the WT SGC side of the LD1 decision boundary. The bound of one half is read from Fig S2F (about 1.3 against 3.3 units) and is not stated in the text.

claims.statement: An LDA classifier trained on WT electrophysiology classifies held-out WT cells with 78% accuracy (Cohen's kappa 0.57) but V321L cells with only 52% accuracy (kappa 0.08).
claims.source: Figure S2G; Results, V321L mutation in Nrg1 results in altered composition of the DG granule cell population, paragraph 5
claims.quote: The LDA classifier, trained on 80% of the WT data, achieved 78% accuracy in cell-type classification of the remainder 20% WT cells (Cohen’s κ = 0.57) ( Fig S2G , top). Using this classifier on the recordings obtained from V 321 L mice resulted in 52% classification accuracy (Cohen’s κ = 0.08)
claims.criterion: As the Methods (LDA) describe. The 18 features of Fig S2C, z-scored with scale(); PCA with prcomp on WT; the top 9 PCs; caret train with method lda and trainControl(method cv, number 5); the WT PCA and LDA applied to the V321L data. Kappa tolerances are 0.1, not 10%, because with about 21 to 23 cells one reclassified cell moves kappa by about 0.08. Open details, with readings run. (1) Whether V321L data are scaled with their own mean and SD or the WT ones ("applied to the scaled V321L data"). (2) Whether 78% is caret's mean accuracy over the five folds or the pooled out-of-fold accuracy; the WT confusion matrix in Fig S2G counts 21 cells (16 correct, 76%), so it pools all folds. (3) The fold seed, not given; each value is the median over 100 random fold assignments (a standard choice), with the range shown. Reproduced when under one reading all four values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the two accuracies are, or when WT accuracy exceeds V321L accuracy by at least 15 points. The V321L matrix in Fig S2G (8, 5, 7, 3; 11 of 23 correct, 48%, kappa near -0.09) does not match the text's 52% and 0.08; both are compared and the mismatch is recorded.

claims.statement: In WT mice most Penk+ GCs lie in the top two cell body layers of the suprapyramidal GCL; this bias toward the GCL-MOL boundary is lost in V321L mice.
claims.source: Figure 3B; Results, V321L mice have a higher number and altered positioning of Penk+ GCs compared with WT mice, paragraph 1
claims.quote: In WT mice, most of the Penk + GCs were in the top 2 cell body layers of the suprapyramidal GCL, whereas this bias toward the GCL-MOL boundary was lost in the V 321 L DG
claims.criterion: Distances of Penk+ somata from the GCL-MOL boundary in FISH images (cells with at least 5 puncta or large clusters; Methods), pooled per genotype. Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with V321L cells farther from the boundary.

claims.statement: V321L mice have a higher percentage of Penk-expressing GCs in snRNA-Seq.
claims.source: Figure 3D; Results, V321L mice have a higher number and altered positioning of Penk+ GCs compared with WT mice, paragraph 2
claims.quote: the total percentage of Penk + GCs was significantly higher in V 321 L mice
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the percentage of GCs (clusters 0, 1, 5 and 18) with a raw Penk count above 0 (snMultiome code). Two-tailed Mann-Whitney test. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with V321L higher (U = 0 gives the smallest p available with 4 and 4, 0.029).

claims.statement: The total number of Prox1+ GCs does not differ between WT and V321L mice.
claims.source: Figure S3B; Results, V321L mice have a higher number and altered positioning of Penk+ GCs compared with WT mice, paragraph 2
claims.quote: We found no differences in the total number of Prox1 + neurons (GCs) ( Fig S3B ; Mann–Whitney test, P = 0.69, U = 6)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The Results and the legend name different tests; both are the paper's, so both are run at p < 0.05 on per-mouse Prox1+ GC counts. Reproduced when neither finds a difference.

claims.statement: Among the four GC clusters (0, 1, 5, 18), cluster 18 has the highest percentage of Penk+ cells in both genotypes.
claims.source: Figure S3C; Results, V321L mice have a higher number and altered positioning of Penk+ GCs compared with WT mice, paragraph 2
claims.quote: cluster 18 contained the highest percentage of Penk + cells indicating enrichment for SGCs in cluster 18 in both genotypes
claims.criterion: Per mouse and cluster, percentage of Penk+ GCs. Two-way repeated-measures ANOVA (cluster by genotype, cluster within mouse) with Bonferroni comparisons of each cluster against 18. Reproduced when the cluster effect and all three comparisons have p < 0.05 with cluster 18 highest.

claims.statement: Sorcs3 is the distinguishing marker of GC cluster 18, and Sorcs3+ cells are biased toward the GCL-MOL boundary in FISH.
claims.source: Figure S3D; Results, V321L mice have a higher number and altered positioning of Penk+ GCs compared with WT mice, paragraph 2
claims.quote: However, cluster 18 was uniquely marked by the expression of Sortilin Related VPS10 Domain Containing Receptor 3 ( Sorcs3 )
claims.criterion: Seurat FindConservedMarkers across WT and V321L for each GC cluster (Methods). Reproduced when Sorcs3 is among the conserved markers of cluster 18 and not of clusters 0, 1 or 5. The FISH half is not tested here (no statistic is given).

claims.statement: V321L mice have more Penk+Sorcs3+ and Penk+Sorcs3- GCs than WT, while Sorcs3+Penk- GCs are unchanged.
claims.source: Figure S5A; Results, V321L mice have a higher number and altered positioning of Penk+ GCs compared with WT mice, paragraph 3
claims.quote: V 321 L mice also showed an increase in the percentage of Penk + Sorcs3 + GCs ( Fig S5A ; P = 0.009). We found that there were no significant differences in the proportion of Penk-Sorcs3+ cells between WT and V 321 L mice
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the percentage of GCs in each marker class (raw count above 0 for each gene). Two-way ANOVA (marker class by genotype) with Bonferroni comparisons of genotype within class. The design is not named; the reported F(2, 12) fits marker class as a repeated measure within mouse (error df (3 - 1) x (8 - 2) = 12) and not an ordinary two-way ANOVA (18 error df), so the repeated-measures ANOVA is the test and the ordinary one is shown as a variant. Reproduced when the two Penk+ classes differ at p < 0.05 with V321L higher and Sorcs3+Penk- does not (p >= 0.05).

claims.statement: In FISH, V321L mice have more Penk+Sorcs3+ cells in the suprapyramidal blade than WT mice.
claims.source: Figure 4A; Results, Discovery of novel marker genes for SGCs, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We found that V 321 L mice had significantly higher numbers of cells co-expressing Penk and Sorcs3
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the count of Penk+Sorcs3+ cells in the suprapyramidal blade (averaged over its sections, each dot one mouse). Two-tailed Welch's t test. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with V321L higher.

claims.statement: Penk+Sorcs3+ cells in V321L DG are not restricted to the layers at the GCL-MOL boundary.
claims.source: Figure 4a'
claims.quote: the V 321 L mice showing more Penk+Sorcs3+ cells present in the lower layers of the GCL, away from the GCL-MOL boundary
claims.criterion: Distances of Penk+Sorcs3+ cells from the GCL-MOL boundary pooled per genotype; two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with V321L cells farther from the boundary.

claims.statement: Differential expression finds 102 genes significantly enriched in Penk+ GCs over Penk- GCs (fold change of at least 2, adjusted P at most 0.05).
claims.source: Figure 4B; Results, Discovery of novel marker genes for SGCs, paragraph 2
claims.quote: We assessed differential gene expression in Penk + GCs compared with Penk -negative GCs yielding 102 genes whose expression was significantly enriched in Penk + GCs (fold change of ≥2 and adj. P ≤ 0.05)
claims.criterion: Seurat FindMarkers of Prox1+Penk+ against Prox1+Penk- GCs (snMultiome code, workbook 58), log2 fold change at least 1 and adjusted p at most 0.05. Reproduced when the count is within tolerance.

claims.statement: For each selected SGC marker gene except Grp, V321L mice have a higher proportion of GCs co-expressing Penk and that marker.
claims.source: Figure 4b''; Results, Discovery of novel marker genes for SGCs, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Except for gastrin-releasing peptide ( Grp ) ... all other marker gene Penk-co-expressing cells formed a significantly higher proportion of all GCs in the V 321 L mice
claims.criterion: Per mouse, cells co-expressing Penk and each marker divided by all cells in clusters 0, 1, 5 and 18 (legend). Mann-Whitney test per gene, FDR by the two-stage Benjamini-Krieger-Yekutieli method. The nine genes are those of Fig 4b' and 4b''. With 4 and 4 mice the smallest two-tailed p is 0.029, so the threshold is the paper's FDR adjusted p of 0.03 as printed. The Results and the legend disagree on what 0.03 is (the Results give P = 0.03 with q = 0.002, and for Grp P = 0.1 with q = 0.01; the legend gives FDR adjusted P = 0.03, and 0.14 for Grp), so the judgement rests on U and the q values are shown. Reproduced when every gene except Grp has U = 0 with V321L higher and Grp does not.

claims.statement: In WT FISH, 84% of Penk+ GCs express Nptx2, 67% express Sorcs3, and 64% express both.
claims.source: Figure 4D and 4d'; Results, Discovery of novel marker genes for SGCs, paragraph 2
claims.quote: We found that on average 84% of the Penk + GCs also expressed Nptx2 , and 67% of the Penk + GCs also expressed Sorcs3 . The co-expression of Nptx2 and Sorcs3 was detected in 64% of the Penk + GCs
claims.criterion: Per mouse, percentages over Penk+ cells in the suprapyramidal blade, then the mean over the three mice; tolerances are the SDs the legend gives. Reproduced when all three are within tolerance.

claims.statement: The increase in marker+Penk+ GCs in V321L mice is seen in Nrg1-expressing Penk+ GCs and not in Nrg1-non-expressing ones; about 94% of Penk+ GCs co-express Nrg1 in FISH.
claims.source: Figure S6A and S6B; Results, Discovery of novel marker genes for SGCs, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Intriguingly, this increase in numbers of marker + Penk + cells was only observed in Penk and Nrg1 co-expressing GCs ( Fig S6A ) and not in Nrg1 -non-expressing Penk + GCs ( Fig S6B ). In FISH experiments for Penk and Nrg1 , we found that most of the Penk + GCs co-expressed Nrg1 (∼94%)
claims.criterion: As fig4b2-marker-penk-cells-increased, split by Nrg1 raw count above 0. The paper's threshold here is FDR adjusted p < 0.1 (legend). Reproduced when in Penk+Nrg1+ GCs every marker except Grp reaches adjusted p < 0.1 with V321L higher, and in Penk+Nrg1- GCs fewer markers reach it. The FISH percentage is checked only if the FISH counts are available.

claims.statement: In WT GCs the top gene explaining pseudotime is Sorcs3, and late pseudotime falls at the end of cluster 1 and in cluster 18; in V321L GCs trajectories are altered and the latest pseudotime is in cluster 5.
claims.source: Figure 5B; Results, Non-SGCs harbor the potential to express an SGC-like transcriptomic state, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The top gene explaining pseudotime in WT DG was found to be Sorcs3 ... Trajectories in the V 321 L DG were highly altered, and cells with late pseudotime were present in cluster 5
claims.criterion: Monocle3 on the GC clusters per genotype, root in cluster 0 (highest Camk4), graph_test with neighbor_graph principal_graph (Methods; snMultiome code lines 2948 to 3228). Reproduced when Sorcs3 has the highest Moran's I among genes with q < 0.05 in WT, the WT cells in the top decile of pseudotime are mostly in clusters 1 and 18, and the V321L top decile is mostly in cluster 5. The decile is not from the paper.

claims.statement: WT (original and downsampled) and V321L GC trajectories have significantly lower spherical distances than randomized ones, so they have definite directionality; WT spherical distances exceed V321L ones.
claims.source: Results, Non-SGCs harbor the potential to express an SGC-like transcriptomic state, paragraph 1
claims.quote: WT original and downsampled trajectories resulted in significantly lower spherical distances compared with randomized ones indicating the presence of a definite directionality within the trajectories ... the spherical distances obtained for the WT trajectories were greater than those for the V 321 L trajectory
claims.criterion: TrajectoryGeometry analyseSingleCellTrajectory on the top 50 PCs rescaled to 0 to 100 with Monocle3 pseudotime, nSamples 1000, N 1000, randomization byPermutation and permuteWithinColumns, statistic mean (Methods). The downsampling seed is not given; the downsampled WT result is the median over 20 draws. Reproduced when all three tests give p < 0.05 with lower distances than random and the mean WT distance exceeds the V321L one.

claims.statement: In ATAC space, the Penk+ GC cluster 9 is populated evenly by WT and V321L nuclei, while cluster 4 (Camk4+ GCs) is about 75% WT.
claims.source: Figure 5d'; Results, Non-SGCs harbor the potential to express an SGC-like transcriptomic state, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Cluster 9 was comprised of the Penk + GCs, and it was uniformly populated by WT and V 321 L GCs; however, cluster 4 that was comprised of the Camk4 + GCs (cluster 0 in the “RNA space”) was disproportionately populated by WT GCs, which made up ∼75% of all cells in that cluster
claims.criterion: Clustering of GC nuclei in ATAC space at resolution 0.5 (Methods; ATAC code). Reproduced when the WT share of cluster 4 is within tolerance and that of cluster 9 is between 40 and 60% (a reading of "uniformly", not stated by the paper).

claims.statement: SGC-enriched genes are accessible in cluster 9 and in nearly all other ATAC clusters of GCs in both genotypes, though their expression is largely restricted to cluster 18 in WT.
claims.source: Figure 5E and 5F; Results, Non-SGCs harbor the potential to express an SGC-like transcriptomic state, paragraph 3
claims.quote: However, we also found SGC-enriched genes to be accessible in cells in nearly all other clusters for both genotypes
claims.criterion: Signac GeneActivity per gene (TSS and 1 kb), nine genes of Fig 5E and 5F. Reproduced when for each gene the fraction of nuclei with nonzero activity is above zero in at least 8 of the 10 ATAC clusters in each genotype (a reading of "nearly all"), while in WT RNA the expressing fraction is highest in cluster 18.

claims.statement: The percentage of GCs with an accessible Penk locus does not differ between WT and V321L mice.
claims.source: Figure S8b''; Results, Non-SGCs harbor the potential to express an SGC-like transcriptomic state, paragraph 3
claims.quote: the total number of GCs having the Penk locus accessible was not significantly different between the genotypes
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on a Mann-Whitney test at p < 0.05 of per-mouse percentages of GCs with nonzero Penk gene activity. Reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Genes enriched in Penk+ GCs and correlated with maximal pseudotime are strongly enriched for regulation by Suz12, a core PRC2 component.
claims.source: Results, Non-SGCs harbor the potential to express an SGC-like transcriptomic state, paragraph 4; Table S4
claims.quote: We found strong enrichment for regulation of these genes by Suz12, a core component of the polycomb repressive complex 2 (PRC2)
claims.criterion: The 60 genes (fig s10 intersection) submitted to ChEA and ENCODE. The paper names the databases, not the tool or library versions; the Methods use the enrichR package for GO terms, so the readings are the enrichR libraries ENCODE_and_ChEA_Consensus_TFs_from_ChIP-X, ChEA_2022 and ENCODE_TF_ChIP-seq_2015, and the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree. Within a reading that gives ChEA and ENCODE separately, reproduced when SUZ12 is the top term by adjusted p in at least one of them; within the consensus library, when it is the top term.

claims.statement: The number of Penk+ cells in the suprapyramidal GCL of WT mice increases with age, from between 2 and 3 months.
claims.source: Figure 6a'; Results, SGC numbers in the DG increase during the adolescence-adulthood transition in WT mice, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We confirmed that WT mice indeed show an increase in Penk expression starting between 2 and 3 mo of age
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the total count of Penk+ cells in the suprapyramidal GCL at 1, 2, 3 and 9 to 12 months. Brown-Forsythe ANOVA with Dunnett's T3 comparisons. The Results print P = 0.0032 and the legend P = 0.002. Reproduced when the age effect and the 2 against 3 month comparison have p < 0.05 with the count higher at 3 months.

claims.statement: The number of Penk+Nptx2+Sorcs3+ cells (SGCs) in the suprapyramidal GCL of WT mice increases with age.
claims.source: Figure 6b'; Results, SGC numbers in the DG increase during the adolescence-adulthood transition in WT mice, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We found that the numbers of Penk+Nptx2+Sorcs3+ GCs also increased with age
claims.criterion: Per mouse counts at 1, 2, 3 and 9 to 12 months; Kruskal-Wallis test with Dunn's comparisons. The Results print P = 0.0012 and the legend P = 0.001. Reproduced when both have p < 0.05 with 12 months higher than 1 month.

claims.statement: The age-dependent increase in SGC number seen in WT mice is lost in V321L mice.
claims.source: Figure S9A; Results, SGC numbers in the DG increase during the adolescence-adulthood transition in WT mice, paragraph 1
claims.quote: These dynamics of SGC abundance over adolescence were lost in the V 321 L DG
claims.criterion: Two-way ANOVA (genotype by age) of per-mouse Penk+Nptx2+Sorcs3+ counts with Bonferroni comparisons between ages within genotype (legend). Reproduced when the WT 1 against 12 month comparison has p < 0.05 and no V321L comparison does (the absence half judged on these comparisons).

claims.statement: The percentage of Penk+ cells that are Nptx2+Sorcs3+ does not change with age in either genotype.
claims.source: Figure S9B; Results, SGC numbers in the DG increase during the adolescence-adulthood transition in WT mice, paragraph 1
claims.quote: There were no significant differences in the overall percentage of Nptx2 - or Sorcs3 -expressing Penk + GCs at any of the ages
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on Brown-Forsythe ANOVA per genotype at p < 0.05. Reproduced when neither genotype shows an age effect.

claims.statement: At 3 months, Penk+ cells in the GCL of WT mice do not express the immature neuron marker Dcx.
claims.source: Figure S9D; Results, SGC numbers in the DG increase during the adolescence-adulthood transition in WT mice, paragraph 2
claims.quote: we did not find any Penk + cells that expressed the immature neuron marker doublecortin ( Dcx ) at 3 mo of age
claims.criterion: Count of Penk+Dcx+ cells in the GCL in FISH (cells with at least 5 puncta of each). Reproduced when the count is zero.

claims.statement: The 60 genes both enriched in Penk+ GCs and in the cluster 18 end-trajectory modules are enriched for gene ontology terms whose top term by odds ratio is regulation of resting membrane potential, driven by Kcnk1 and Kcnj2.
claims.source: Figure S10C and S10D; Results, SGC numbers in the DG increase during the adolescence-adulthood transition in WT mice, paragraph 2
claims.quote: we identified 60 genes that met this criterion ... the feature of highest odds ratio being regulation of RMP, in line with our results showing a more hyperpolarized RMP in morphologically identified SGCs ( Fig 1J ). This enrichment was driven by two potassium channel genes ... Kcnk1 and Kcnj2
claims.criterion: Monocle3 find_gene_modules on WT GCs, modules correlated with the cluster 18 end trajectories, intersected with the Penk+ enriched genes; enrichR GO_Biological_Process_2023, terms with adjusted p < 0.05 ranked by odds ratio (legend and Methods). Reproduced when the count is within tolerance and the top term is regulation of resting membrane potential with Kcnk1 and Kcnj2 as its genes.

claims.statement: Type III Nrg1 expression in the suprapyramidal DG of WT mice declines from 1 to 12 months of age; the decline from 1 to 3 months is not significant.
claims.source: Figure 7A; Results, Natural decline in capacity for Nrg1 nuclear back-signaling corresponds to the SGC fate, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We found that Type III Nrg1 expression declined from 1 to 12 mo of age in WT mice; however, the reduction between 1 and 3 mo of age was not significant
claims.criterion: Per mouse, Type III Nrg1 FISH fluorescence intensity density normalized to the area of the suprapyramidal blade (Methods). Kruskal-Wallis with Dunn's comparisons. Reproduced when the age effect and 1 against 12 months have p < 0.05 with lower values at 12 months, and 1 against 3 months has p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Bace1 expression peaks at intermediate pseudotime and drops at maximal pseudotime while Nrg1 rises along pseudotime; fewer than 10 WT cells co-express Penk, Nrg1 and Bace1, so most Penk+Nrg1+ GCs lack detectable Bace1.
claims.source: Figure 7B and 7C; Results, Natural decline in capacity for Nrg1 nuclear back-signaling corresponds to the SGC fate, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Bace1 expression was found to be higher in cells at intermediate pseudotime compared with the beginning or end of the trajectories ... examination of cells expressing Penk, Nrg1 , and Bace1 in WT DG resulted in <10 cells showing co-expression of all three markers
claims.criterion: WT GC pseudotime from fig5b-pseudotime-sorcs3-top, split into thirds. Reproduced when mean Bace1 expression is highest in the middle third and lower in the last third than the middle, mean Nrg1 is highest in the last third, and fewer than 10 WT GCs have raw counts above 0 for all of Penk, Nrg1 and Bace1. The thirds are not from the paper.
