claims.statement: Penk+Sorcs3- GCs are excluded from cluster 18 in both WT and V321L mice.
claims.source: Figure S5B and S5C; Results, V321L mice have a higher number and altered positioning of Penk+ GCs compared with WT mice, paragraph 3
claims.quote: we found that Penk + Sorcs3 - cells were excluded from cluster 18 in both WT and V 321 L mice
claims.criterion: GCs with a raw Penk count above 0 and a raw Sorcs3 count of 0 (as in figs5a-penk-sorcs3-subsets), counted per cluster and genotype. Reproduced when cluster 18 holds none of them in either genotype, as the legend of Fig S5C says ("Note the absence of cells in cluster 18 in both genotypes").

claims.statement: With WT GCs downsampled to the V321L number, the pseudotime ordering is preserved and Sorcs3 still marks the cells with maximal pseudotime.
claims.source: Figure S7A and S7B; Results, Non-SGCs harbor the potential to express an SGC-like transcriptomic state, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We found that the pseudotime ordering of GCs and associated gene expression states were robust to differences in sampling frequency, with Sorcs3 still representing cells with the maximal pseudotime
claims.criterion: WT GCs downsampled at random to the number of V321L GCs, then Monocle3 and graph_test as in fig5b-pseudotime-sorcs3-top. The seed is not given; 20 draws, as in trajectory-geometry-directionality. Reproduced when in most draws Sorcs3 is among the top ten genes by Moran's I with q < 0.05 (the legend says "some of the top pseudotime-associated genes") and the Spearman correlation of each downsampled cell's pseudotime with its pseudotime in the full WT analysis is positive. The top-ten bound and the correlation are readings, not the paper's.

claims.statement: In ATAC space the Penk+ GCs (cluster 9) have the maximal pseudotime; WT GC trajectories have three end points and V321L GC trajectories one, ending at cluster 9.
claims.source: Figure S8A; Results, Non-SGCs harbor the potential to express an SGC-like transcriptomic state, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Once again, we found that the Penk + GCs (now located in ATAC cluster 9) had the maximum pseudotime values based on chromatin accessibility ... However, in the V 321 L GCs, there was only one end point terminating at cluster 9
claims.criterion: Monocle3 on the ATAC GC subset, run separately on WT (LL) and V321L (VV) cells (Methods, Single-nucleus ATAC-Seq analysis), root chosen from Camk4 and the other markers the Methods list. Reproduced when cluster 9 has the highest median pseudotime in each genotype and the learned principal graph has three leaf end points (other than the root) in WT and one in V321L. Monocle3 graph learning depends on its settings, which the Methods do not give beyond the workflow; the snMultiome code's settings are used.

claims.statement: At E18.5, cells expressing SGC-enriched genes (Penk, Scg2, Nrg1, Cit) lie at the dorsal border of the developing GCL, so marker expression is unlikely to reflect cellular age alone.
claims.source: Figure S9C; Results, SGC numbers in the DG increase during the adolescence-adulthood transition in WT mice, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We found cells expressing SGC-enriched genes such as Penk , Scg2 , Nrg1 , and Cit in the dorsal border of the developing GCL at E18.5
claims.criterion: A qualitative reading of public ISH images, with no statistic. Reproduced when the Allen E18.5 ISH images for each of the four genes show labelled cells at the dorsal border of the developing GCL. The image series are not given; any E18.5 series for the gene is a reading.

claims.statement: The dandiset's sessions can be linked to the paper's published per-session behavioural tables, and the linked records agree on trial counts, outcomes, evidence and pulse timing.
claims.source: Data availability; the paper's data/Sessions_trials at GitHub commit 0ea8fdb
claims.quote: Rat behavioural and electrophysiological data are available at https://github.com/Brody-Lab/flexible_decision_making_rats.
claims.criterion: Records are matched by rat and session name (protocol, date and letter, taken from the source file names in the paper's tables). The link holds (reproduced) when at least 95% of the paper's sessions that have valid trials are found in the dandiset; in at least 95% of matched sessions the number of valid trials and the fraction correct are equal; and in a seeded sample of 20 sessions that pass the selection, the per-trial context, correct side, evidence strengths, choice and position in block agree on at least 99% of valid trials and the pulse counts in the code's 10 ms bins agree on at least 99% of trial bins. It is partially reproduced when the lowest of these fractions is between 80% and the threshold, and not reproduced below 80%. The per-rat numbers of trials passing the selection are compared with the paper's table numsessions_all_rats.mat, and the sessions in one source only are listed.

claims.statement: The study used 26 male Long-Evans rats, aged between 6 and 24 months.
claims.source: Methods, Subjects
claims.quote: All subjects were male Long-Evans rats between the ages of 6 and 24 months ... A total of 26 rats were used for the experiments presented in this study
claims.criterion: The tolerance on the count is 0 as it is a count of named animals. Reproduced when the dandiset holds 26 subjects, all male and Long Evans, and the age at every session that passes the selection lies within 5.4 to 26.4 months (the range widened by 10% of each bound). Partially reproduced when the count, sex and strain hold and at least 90% of those sessions are within the widened range.

claims.statement: Rats performed on average 542 trials per session.
claims.source: Methods, Behaviour
claims.quote: rats performed on average 542 trials per session
claims.criterion: The paper does not say which sessions or trials are counted. Readings, before the analysis are (a) all trials in sessions that pass the selection; (b) valid trials in those sessions; (c) all trials in every session of the three task protocols; (d) valid trials in those. Reproduced when the mean is within tolerance under any reading.

claims.statement: On average, rats switched across 14.6 context blocks per session.
claims.source: Methods, Behaviour
claims.quote: On average, rats switched across 14.6 context blocks per session
claims.criterion: A block is a run of trials with the same context, over all trials. Readings are the number of blocks or the number of switches (blocks minus one), each over (a) sessions that pass the selection or (b) every session of the three task protocols. Reproduced when the mean is within tolerance under any reading.

claims.statement: Behavioural sessions lasted 2 to 4 hours.
claims.source: Methods, Behaviour
claims.quote: Behavioural sessions lasted 2–4 h
claims.criterion: Duration is the stop time of the last trial minus the start time of the first. Reproduced when the median duration lies within 1.8 to 4.4 hours (the range widened by 10% of each bound) over (a) sessions that pass the selection or (b) every session of the three task protocols, under either reading. The fraction of sessions inside the range is reported.

claims.statement: Block switches occurred after a minimum of 30 trials per block, and when a local estimate of performance reached 80% correct.
claims.source: Methods, Behaviour
claims.quote: block switches occurred after a minimum of 30 trials per block, and when a local estimate of performance reached a threshold of 80% correct
claims.criterion: Over the blocks of sessions that pass the selection, leaving out the last block of each session (which the session end cuts short), the length of a block is counted (a) over all trials or (b) over valid trials. Reproduced when at least 95% of blocks have at least 30 trials under either reading; partially reproduced when at least 80% do. The local performance estimate is not defined in the paper, so the 80% part is described (fraction correct over the last 30 valid trials before each switch) and does not decide the outcome.

claims.statement: Twenty rats each contributed more than 120,000 trials after training.
claims.source: Figure 1c legend; Extended Data Figure 1c
claims.quote: Logistic fits of psychometric curves for 20 rats after training (more than 120,000 trials for each rat)
claims.criterion: Tolerance 0, as the count follows from a fixed rule on the trial counts. Valid trials are counted over sessions that pass the selection, as Figure1c.m does.

claims.statement: After training, choices are mostly driven by location in the location context and by frequency in the frequency context.
claims.source: Figure 1c; Extended Data Figure 3a,d
claims.quote: In the LOC context, choices are mostly affected by location; in the FRQ context, choices are mostly affected by frequency
claims.criterion: For each of the 20 rats, over its trials in sessions that pass the selection, one logistic regression per context of choice on the two generative strengths. Reproduced when the relative weight of location in the location context and of frequency in the frequency context both exceed 0.5 in all 20 rats; partially reproduced when they do in at least 15.

claims.statement: Rats switch the feature they attend to within about four trials of a new context block.
claims.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 1e (legend panel g)
claims.quote: were able to switch between selected stimulus features within four trials of a new context block
claims.criterion: As in compute_taskswitch.m, per rat, a logistic regression of choice on the two generative strengths for the valid trials at each position k (counting all trials since the switch) of the new block, k from 1 to 30, pooled over sessions that pass the selection (main) or the code's looser selection (fraction correct and index at least 0.65; variant); relative weights are averaged over rats with a fit. The plateau is the mean relative weight of the new block's relevant feature over positions 10 to 30. Readings are "within four trials" (position 4) and "within 4 to 5 trials" (position 5). Reproduced when, under either reading, the across-rat mean relative weight of the relevant feature at that position is at least 90% of its plateau for both switch directions; partially reproduced when for one. The weight at position 1 is reported.

claims.statement: Most rats learned the task in two to five months.
claims.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 2g
claims.quote: most rats learned the task in a timespan between two and five months
claims.criterion: Training starts at (i) the rat's first session in the dandiset or (ii) its first session of any TaskSwitch protocol. The rat has learned the task at (a) its first session with at least 100 valid trials and a feature selection index of at least 0.7 (the red line of Extended Data Figure 2g; the index is undefined until both features vary in both contexts), or (b) its first session that passes the full selection. Months are 30.44 days. Reproduced when, under any pairing of readings, more than half of the rats with a defined value took 1.8 to 5.5 months (two to five widened by 10% of each bound).

claims.statement: Differential behavioural kernels predominantly converge towards the end of the pulse train, that is the difference between contexts in the weight of a feature shrinks for later pulses.
claims.source: Methods, Behavioural logistic regression, paragraph 3; Figure 4; Extended Data Figure 3c,f
claims.quote: Empirically we found that differential behavioural kernels predominantly displayed convergence towards the end of the pulse stimulus presentation
claims.criterion: For the 18 rats of Figure 4 (more than 120,000 valid trials and not rats numbered below 15, as Figure4.m selects), slope indices over all 26 bins for location and frequency, 36 values. Reproduced when more than half are negative and their median is negative. The count of negative values and their range are reported; Figure4.m sets its axes to -0.8 to -0.15, which suggests all 36 lie in that range.

claims.statement: Across rats, the shape of the differential behavioural kernel for one feature does not predict the shape for the other feature.
claims.source: Results, Linking neural and behaviour variability, paragraph 1; Figure 4 top right
claims.quote: The shape of an individual’s differential behavioural kernel for one feature did not appear to predict the shape of the kernel for the other feature
claims.criterion: The paper gives no test; Pearson correlation across the 18 rats between the location and frequency slope indices, two-sided, is chosen here as the paper uses it for Figure 5d and Extended Data Figure 3g. Reproduced when p is 0.05 or more; not reproduced when below. The correlation and its 95% interval are reported.

claims.statement: The behavioural slope index computed from the first half of a rat's trials is correlated with the index from the second half (r = 0.58, p = 0.000013).
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 3g legend
claims.quote: The slope index computed from behavioral trials in the first half split is highly correlated with the slope index computed using the second half split (r = 0.58; p = 0.000013)
claims.criterion: As ExtDataFigure3g.m, rats with at least 100,000 valid trials in sessions that pass the selection; trials of each context split in their order into a first and second half; kernels fitted on each half with the penalty weight chosen for that rat and context on all its trials; slope indices over all 26 bins; one correlation over location and frequency values together. Reproduced when r is within tolerance and p < 0.05; partially reproduced when r is positive with p < 0.05 but outside tolerance; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Bilateral optogenetic silencing of the frontal orienting fields during the stimulus impairs performance of the task (three rats).
claims.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 4g
claims.quote: bilateral optogenetic silencing of rat FOF demonstrated that they are required for accurate performance of the task
claims.criterion: Opto sessions are those with an opto_epochs table and at least 100 valid trials. An epoch belongs to the trial whose start and stop contain its start. Per rat, the fraction correct on valid trials with a bilateral full-trial epoch is compared with valid trials with no epoch in the same sessions, two-sided Fisher exact test. Readings of which rats are meant, as the paper does not name them, are (a) the three with the most opto sessions and (b) all rats with opto sessions; the epoch type reading is (i) full trial, as the legend says, or (ii) any bilateral epoch. Reproduced when, under a reading, accuracy is lower with p < 0.05 in every rat of that reading; partially reproduced when it is in at least one.

claims.statement: The neurons in the paper's published neural data can be linked to the dandiset's rats and sessions; they come from 199 sessions of 7 rats.
claims.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 2 (n = 199 sessions, n = 7 rats); the paper's data/neural_data and data/rat_for_each_neuron.mat at GitHub commit 0ea8fdb
claims.quote: we recorded from n = 3,495 putative single neurons during n = 199 sessions from n = 7 rats
claims.criterion: The neural files name the rat but not the session. A cell is matched to a session of the same rat when its trials (context, location strength and choice) equal a contiguous run of that session's valid trials. The link holds (reproduced) when the 7 rats are in the dandiset, at least 95% of cells match exactly one session, and the number of distinct matched sessions is within tolerance; partially reproduced when 80% to 95% of cells match.

claims.statement: The recordings yielded 3,495 putative single units, 2,047, 832, 258, 94 and 54 from five rats in FOF and 112 and 98 from two rats in mPFC.
claims.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 2; Methods, Analysis of neural data, paragraph 1
claims.quote: In total, 3,495 putative single units were recorded from 5 rats in FOF (number of units in each rat: 2,047, 832, 258, 94, 54), while 210 units were recorded from 2 rats in mPFC (number of units in each rat: 112, 98)
claims.criterion: Tolerance 0, as these are counts of files. The Methods state both that 3,495 units were recorded in FOF and per-rat FOF counts that sum to 3,285; the per-rat counts are taken as the claim. Reproduced when the per-rat counts and the region named in each cell file match the seven stated counts.

claims.statement: Neural slope indices vary across rats and features, with no apparent correlation between the location and frequency indices across the seven recorded rats.
claims.source: Results, Pulse analyses distinguish solutions, paragraph 2; Figure 3h
claims.quote: Instead, there was high variability across rats in this measure, and even across features within a single rat; no apparent correlation between the LOC and FRQ slope indices was visible
claims.criterion: Neural slope indices per rat and feature from the paper's fitted per-neuron pulse kernels, by the procedure of get_neural_slope.m (choice axis from the first principal component of the choice kernels from 0 to 1.3 s; the projected differential pulse response, time-reversed, divided by its largest absolute value, slope against time). The paper gives no test; Pearson correlation across the 7 rats, two-sided, p of 0.05 or more reproduces the absence. The range across rats is reported.

claims.statement: The behavioural slope index and the neural slope index are anti-correlated across rats and features (r = -0.73, P < 0.01), and for location (r = -0.71) and frequency (r = -0.71) alone (P < 0.1).
claims.source: Results, Linking neural and behaviour variability, paragraph 1; Figure 5d
claims.quote: We found robust support in the data for the theoretical prediction that the two measures should be correlated ... with the correlation also holding for LOC evidence alone ... or for FRQ evidence alone
claims.criterion: Behavioural slope indices of the seven recorded rats from the dandiset, sessions passing the Methods selection (the code's 0.65 and 0.6 thresholds are a variant), over the second half of the stimulus (bins 14 to 26, as the Methods and compute_slope.m say); neural slope indices as in fig3h-neural-uncorrelated, matched by rat. Reproduced when the 14-point r is within tolerance with p < 0.01; partially reproduced when it is negative with p < 0.05 but outside tolerance; not reproduced otherwise. The two single-feature values are reported and do not decide the outcome.

claims.statement: Choice-related population activity in FOF evolves along an essentially one-dimensional line during the stimulus (73.3% of variance; 81.3% for the two-dimensional choice subspace).
claims.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 3; Figure 1e
claims.quote: the two-dimensional subspace that best accounts for the contribution of the animal’s choice to the neural activity (accounting for 81.3% of the variance) ... this choice-related information in firing rates evolved along an essentially one-dimensional straight line in neural space (accounting for 73.3% of the variance)

claims.statement: Choice axes estimated separately in the two contexts are essentially parallel (average angle 1.6 degrees, not different from 0 in 6 of 7 rats).
claims.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 5
claims.quote: we found that the choice axes, estimated separately for each of the two contexts, were essentially parallel (average angle between contexts = 1.6°; not significantly different from 0 (P > 0.1) for 6 out of 7 rats
claims.criterion: As ExtDataFigure5ag.m, per rat the first principal component of the choice kernels (from 0 s, 66 time points) of the paper's per-neuron fits in each context; the two are projected on the first 3 principal components of both contexts' choice kernels from 0 s (each divided by its matrix norm, stacked), and the angle between the projections is folded to at most 90 degrees, the value the code plots. The average over the 7 rats decides the outcome. The paper's test of each angle against 0, a permutation test over shuffled context labels described in the Methods, is not in its code and needs the per-neuron kernels refitted for every shuffle, so it is not run; the angle in the full space, which the code computes first and overwrites, is shown as a variant. (Corrected after the first verification round. The criterion first described only that first angle, unfolded, as the code's; both readings are outside the tolerance. After the second round the sentence on the test against 0 was corrected; it first said the Methods do not describe the test.)

claims.statement: In FOF, trajectories for different evidence strengths separate along each sensory axis whether the feature is relevant or irrelevant, so irrelevant information is not gated out before frontal cortex.
claims.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 2; Figure 1f
claims.quote: We found that trajectories for different evidence strengths were clearly separated along the axis of each sensory feature ... This was true regardless of whether the feature was relevant or irrelevant

claims.statement: RNNs trained by backpropagation through time favour selection vector modulation.
claims.source: Figure 3a
claims.quote: Distribution of 1,000 RNNs trained using backpropagation through time: networks favoured SVM

claims.statement: In RNNs engineered across the solution space, neural and behavioural slope indices are tightly anti-correlated.
claims.source: Figure 5c
claims.quote: RNN models follow the theoretical prediction, with anti-correlated slope indices for neural differential pulse kernels and differential behavioural kernels

claims.statement: Two-photon fluorescence shows robust eBRIC expression in neuronal somata and processes in the whisker barrel cortex, and the neurons look healthy and intact three months after surgery.
claims.source: Results, In Vivo BLI of Ca2+ Dynamics in Live Mice, paragraph 1; Figure 4B
claims.quote: Two-photon excited fluorescence revealed robust eBRIC expression in neuronal somata and processes. Neurons appeared healthy and morphologically intact even three months after surgery
claims.criterion: The paper judges this by eye from images and gives no measure, so it can only be checked qualitatively. Reproduced when the dandiset's two-photon fluorescence images show labelled cell bodies and processes in the transduced region. Whether an image is from three months after surgery is reported from the file metadata if it is given; health and morphology are not judged.

claims.statement: Laser speckle contrast imaging shows that the region of viral expression responds with blood flow changes to electrical stimulation of the whisker pad.
claims.source: Results, In Vivo BLI of Ca2+ Dynamics in Live Mice, paragraph 1; Figure 4C legend
claims.quote: Laser speckle contrast imaging was used to confirm that the viral expression was in a region that responded to electrical stimulation of the whisker pad
claims.criterion: The paper gives no measure or test for the speckle result. Reproduced when speckle data are present for a mouse and show a change in speckle contrast (blood flow) over the eBRIC-expressing region during whisker pad stimulation compared with before it, judged from the images or traces as the paper shows them. No threshold is fixed by the paper; the size of the change is reported. Blocked if the dandiset holds no speckle data.

claims.statement: Infusing DTZ at 25 uL/min through the tail vein gives a steady level of baseline bioluminescence during the recording.
claims.source: Results, In Vivo BLI of Ca2+ Dynamics in Live Mice, paragraph 1; Figure 4D
claims.quote: Infusion at 25 μL/min generated a steady level of baseline bioluminescence
claims.criterion: The paper gives no measure of steadiness. As a reading of "steady" that the analysis can apply, for each recording the pre-stimulus baseline of each trial (the mean of the signal in the 5 s before stimulus onset; 5 s matches the stimulus length, a standard choice) is computed, and the change of baseline over the recording is compared with the mean evoked response at 4 mA in the same recording (response as in fig4d-evoked-increase). Reproduced when, in the mouse or mice tested, the baseline changes from the first to the last trial by less than the mean 4 mA evoked response, so responses stand out from any drift. The baseline over time is shown for every recording. This threshold is not the paper's; the outcome is to be read with that in mind and the drift reported as numbers.

claims.statement: Whisker pad stimulation (5 Hz for 5 s) at 4 mA and at 2 mA, through each of the two electrodes, gives clear increases in cortical eBRIC bioluminescence.
claims.source: Results, In Vivo BLI of Ca2+ Dynamics in Live Mice, paragraph 1; Figure 4D
claims.quote: clear increases in bioluminescence were observed with stimulation (4 and 2 mA) at both electrodes on the whisker pad
claims.criterion: From the Figure 4D legend, traces smoothed with a 1-s moving average and averaged over trials per electrode and current. The response window, the baseline window and the test are not given. The baseline is the 5 s before stimulus onset (a standard choice). The response window has two readings the text allows, as the Results describe a delayed peak for one electrode, (a) the 5-s stimulation period, (b) the stimulation period and the 5 s after it. Response per trial is the mean signal in the response window minus the baseline mean. The paper reports no test, so the test has two readings, both one-sided against zero on the trial responses, (1) a Wilcoxon signed-rank test, (2) a one-sample t-test; an increase is counted when the mean response over trials is positive and the test gives p < 0.05. With fewer than 5 trials in a condition, (1) cannot reach p < 0.05 and only (2) is applied. The windows (a, b) and tests (1, 2) are method details the paper leaves open, so the outcome is the one they all give, and methods_underspecified when they differ. Figure 4D shows one representative mouse that the paper does not identify, so there are two readings of which mice must show it, (i) at least one mouse, as in the figure, (ii) every mouse recorded with both currents and both electrodes; the claim is reproduced if it holds under either. Reproduced when all four conditions (two electrodes by two currents) show an increase; the notebook shows every combination.

claims.statement: At 4 mA the response is strong enough to detect individual stimulation events, in single trials without averaging.
claims.source: Results, In Vivo BLI of Ca2+ Dynamics in Live Mice, paragraph 1; Figure 4D; Discussion, paragraph 4
claims.quote: with the 4 mA condition producing a sufficiently strong response to detect individual stimulation events
claims.criterion: The paper gives no detection rule. "Individual stimulation events" has two readings, (a) single 5-s stimulation trials, as the Discussion puts it ("clear neural responses to single whisker pad shocks in individual trials"), (b) single pulses of the 5 Hz train. Reading (b) cannot be resolved in traces smoothed with the 1-s moving average of the legend; it is tested on the unsmoothed signal by averaging it at each pulse time within a trial (event-triggered on the 0.2-s pulse period) and is shown as a variant. For reading (a), with windows as in fig4d-evoked-increase, a trial is detected when its response exceeds k times the standard deviation of its smoothed baseline, with k = 2 or k = 3 named as the two readings of a threshold the paper does not give. The windows and the threshold are method details the paper leaves open, so under reading (a) the outcome is the one all windows and both thresholds give, and methods_underspecified when they differ. Reproduced when most 4 mA trials (more than half) in the mouse or mice tested, as in the two readings of fig4d-evoked-increase, are detected. The paper does not say that 2 mA trials fail to be detected, so the 2 mA fraction is reported and does not decide the claim. Every fraction is reported.

claims.statement: The responses to the two electrode locations differ in timing; stimulation of region 1 gives a delayed peak, and region 2 an earlier rise after stimulation onset.
claims.source: Results, In Vivo BLI of Ca2+ Dynamics in Live Mice, paragraph 1; Figure 4D
claims.quote: Stimulation of region 1 resulted in a delayed peak response, while region 2 elicited an earlier rise in signal following stimulation onset
claims.criterion: Per electrode and current, the trial-averaged trace smoothed with a 1-s moving average (Figure 4D legend), baseline the 5 s before onset. Time to peak is the time of the maximum within the stimulation period and the 5 s after it; time of rise is the first time after onset at which the averaged trace exceeds half its peak above baseline (a standard choice, not the paper's). The paper does not say which electrode is region 1, and the colours of Figure 4D could not be read without the PDF; if the dataset labels the electrodes 1 and 2, those labels are used, otherwise both assignments are shown and the claim is tested as (a) one electrode has both the later peak and the later rise. The paper does not say at which current; the readings are 4 mA, 2 mA, or both. Reproduced when region 1 has the later time to peak and region 2 the earlier time of rise at either current, in the representative mouse reading (at least one mouse) of fig4d-evoked-increase; the values for every mouse are reported.

claims.statement: In awake head-fixed mice, footshock (0.8 mA, 1 s, every 40 s, 13 trials) gives a significant and consistent increase in BLA bioluminescence with eBRIC and sDTZ, larger than in mice expressing the Ca2+-insensitive control BREP.
claims.source: Results, In Vivo BLI of Ca2+ Dynamics in Live Mice, paragraph 2; Figure 5B and 5C
claims.quote: As expected, we observed a significant and consistent increase in bioluminescence in the eBRIC group in response to footshocks
claims.criterion: As in the Figure 5C legend, each mouse's response averaged over its 13 trials, and the eBRIC and BREP groups (4 and 3 mice) compared with an unpaired two-tailed t-test. The P value is printed only in the figure and was not read. The response measure follows "an established procedure" cited in the Methods and is not given in the text. Reproduced when eBRIC responses exceed BREP responses at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Mice expressing BREP show minimal to no change in bioluminescence under footshock.
claims.source: Results, In Vivo BLI of Ca2+ Dynamics in Live Mice, paragraph 2; Figure 5B and 5C
claims.quote: As a negative control, we generated mice expressing BREP, a Ca 2+ -insensitive bioluminescent protein, and observed minimal to no changes in bioluminescence under electric footshock stimulation
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test of the BREP change on its own and no threshold for "minimal"; its only test is the eBRIC against BREP comparison of fig5-bla-footshock-increase. The BREP group mean response over 13 trials and its s.d. (Figure 5C, 3 mice) are reported. Absent a test or threshold from the paper, the claim is judged against the paper's own comparison only, reproduced when the BREP response is smaller than the eBRIC response in that test, and its size relative to zero is reported.

claims.statement: eBRIC with sDTZ allowed BLI of the awake mouse brain at 10 Hz (100 ms exposures without intervals).
claims.source: Results, In Vivo BLI of Ca2+ Dynamics in Live Mice, paragraph 2; Methods, BLI of BLA Ca2+ Dynamics in Awake Mice
claims.quote: The combination of eBRIC and sDTZ allowed digitalization at a frequency of 10 Hz, which has not been achieved in previous studies

claims.statement: Under the same footshock condition, the eBRIC response in the BLA is nearly twice that of BRIC in the authors' earlier experiments.
claims.source: Results, In Vivo BLI of Ca2+ Dynamics in Live Mice, paragraph 2; Discussion, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Compared to prior experiments with BRIC under the same stimulation condition, the response magnitude of eBRIC has nearly doubled
claims.criterion: The BRIC values come from "prior experiments with BRIC under the same stimulation condition", which the text does not identify at this sentence. The candidates the paper names are the BRIC paper, Tian et al. 2022, Nat. Commun. 13 3967 (doi:10.1038/s41467-022-31673-x), and the bioRxiv preprint on water-soluble luciferins (doi:10.1101/2024.04.30.591933) listed in the paper's notes; which of them, if either, holds BRIC footshock BLA data is for the author to establish. The eBRIC value comes from Figure 5C. The ratio of the eBRIC group mean response to the BRIC group mean response, each as the mean over mice of the 13-trial average. "Nearly doubled" is read as the expected value 2 with 10% tolerance.

claims.statement: After three rounds of directed evolution, eBRIC shows an 18.2-fold Ca2+-induced increase in bioluminescence (39 uM Ca2+ against no Ca2+) in bacterial cell lysates.
claims.source: Results, Engineering and Characterization of eBRIC In Vitro, paragraph 2; Figure 1A
claims.quote: Through three rounds of directed evolution, we successfully generated a drastically enhanced BRIC (eBRIC) variant with an 18.2-fold Ca 2+ -included bioluminescence increase in cell lysates

claims.statement: eBRIC carries five mutations from BRIC, two in teLuc, one in mScarlet-I and two in the CaM-M13 region, and the two CaM-M13 mutations are mainly responsible for the larger response.
claims.source: Results, Engineering and Characterization of eBRIC In Vitro, paragraph 3; Figure 1A to 1C
claims.quote: During this process, five mutations were identified ... Notably, the two mutations in the CaM-M13 region are primarily responsible for the observed response enhancement

claims.statement: In purified protein, the response between 65 nM and 1.35 uM Ca2+ rises from 1.7-fold (BRIC) to 4.6-fold (eBRIC), and the change between 0 and 39 uM Ca2+ from 6.5-fold to about 17-fold.
claims.source: Results, Engineering and Characterization of eBRIC In Vitro, paragraph 4; Figure 1D
claims.quote: From BRIC to eBRIC, the response between 65 nM and 1.35 μM of Ca 2+ increased from 1.7-fold to 4.6-fold, while the overall Ca 2+ -induced change between 0 and 39 μM of free Ca 2+ increased from 6.5-fold to ∼17-fold

claims.statement: The apparent Kd of eBRIC for Ca2+ is 2.3 uM with a Hill coefficient of 1.3, from a four-parameter Hill fit to bioluminescence at 600 nm (3 technical replicates); BRIC's was 133 nM.
claims.source: Figure 1E legend; Results, Engineering and Characterization of eBRIC In Vitro, paragraph 4
claims.quote: A four-parameter Hill equation was used to fit the data to determine the dissociation constant ( K d = 2.3 μM and Hill coefficient = 1.3)

claims.statement: In bacterial lysates, eBRIC is dimmer than BRIC in the Ca2+-free state and brighter in the Ca2+-bound state.
claims.source: Results, Engineering and Characterization of eBRIC In Vitro, paragraph 2; Figure S2
claims.quote: Compared to BRIC, eBRIC displayed reduced brightness in the Ca 2+ -free state but enhanced brightness in the Ca 2+ -bound state
claims.criterion: Figure S2 is in the Supporting Information, which was not in the text read, so its values and any test are unknown. Judged on the direction of the two differences only.

claims.statement: In HeLa cells stimulated with 20 uM histamine, eBRIC reports Ca2+ oscillations, and its maximal change (dBL/BL0) is nearly 5-fold that of BRIC (33 eBRIC and 34 BRIC cells, unpaired two-tailed t-test).
claims.source: Results, Characterization of eBRIC in Cultured Mammalian Cells and Primary Neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 2A and 2B
claims.quote: Comparing this to BRIC at identical conditions, the magnitude of the change (ΔBL/BL 0 ) was nearly 5-fold higher
claims.criterion: As in the Figure 2B legend, the maximal dBL/BL0 of each cell after histamine, with baselines corrected for monoexponential decay, compared between 33 eBRIC and 34 BRIC cells by an unpaired two-tailed t-test. The P value is printed only in the figure and was not read, and the text claims only the fold difference, so the test is reported and does not decide the claim. Reproduced when the ratio of means is within tolerance.

claims.statement: In HEK 293T cells, 10 uM acetylcholine gives a 3.5-fold (dBL/BL0) eBRIC bioluminescence increase (20 cells).
claims.source: Results, Characterization of eBRIC in Cultured Mammalian Cells and Primary Neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 2C
claims.quote: We observed a robust 3.5-fold (ΔBL/BL 0 ) bioluminescence increase
claims.criterion: The Figure 2C legend shows traces of 20 cells as mean and s.d. and does not say how the 3.5-fold value is taken, so two readings, (a) the peak dBL/BL0 of the mean trace, (b) the mean over cells of each cell's maximal dBL/BL0, as in Figures 2B and 3B. The claim is reproduced if either is within tolerance.

claims.statement: In cultured primary mouse neurons, high K+ depolarization gives a 7.3-fold (dBL/BL0) increase in eBRIC bioluminescence, 5.6 times the response of BRIC (24 eBRIC and 17 BRIC cells, unpaired two-tailed t-test).
claims.source: Results, Characterization of eBRIC in Cultured Mammalian Cells and Primary Neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 3B
claims.quote: high K + depolarization induced a 7.3-fold increase (ΔBL/BL 0 ) in eBRIC bioluminescence, resulting in a 5.6-fold increase in responsiveness from BRIC
claims.criterion: As in the Figure 3B legend, the maximal dBL/BL0 of each cell, 24 eBRIC and 17 BRIC cells, compared by an unpaired two-tailed t-test (P value only in the figure, not read; the text claims only the fold values, so the test is reported and does not decide the claim). The 7.3-fold value is read as the mean over eBRIC cells of the maximal dBL/BL0. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: In HeLa cells eBRIC is dimmer than BRIC in the Ca2+-free state and about twice as bright after histamine stimulation, with a similar trend in primary neurons.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of eBRIC in Cultured Mammalian Cells and Primary Neurons, paragraph 2; Figure S2
claims.quote: eBRIC exhibited reduced brightness in the Ca 2+ -free state but demonstrated approximately twice the brightness of BRIC after stimulation. A similar trend was observed in primary neurons
claims.criterion: Figure S2 was not in the text read, so how brightness was measured is unknown. Judged on the ratio and the direction of the Ca2+-free difference.

claims.statement: The emission spectrum of eBRIC in HEK 293T cells closely resembles that in lysates and as purified protein, so expression in mammalian cells does not change BRET efficiency.
claims.source: Results, Characterization of eBRIC in Cultured Mammalian Cells and Primary Neurons, paragraph 2; Figure S3
claims.quote: The spectral profile closely resembled that of eBRIC in lysates and as a purified protein, suggesting that expression in mammalian cells does not alter the BRET efficiency
claims.criterion: Figure S3 was not in the text read; the paper's measure of resemblance is unknown.

claims.statement: In physiologically stimulated live cells, eBRIC is 4.5- to 5.6-fold more responsive than BRIC and 7.4- to 18-fold more responsive than Orange CaMBIs.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 1; Table S1
claims.quote: Compared to Orange CaMBIs, we gained 7.4- to 18-fold increase in Ca 2+ responsiveness using the new eBRIC Ca 2+ sensor in physiologically stimulated live cells ( Table S1 ). Compared to our previously reported BRIC sensor, eBRIC is 4.5- to 5.6-fold more responsive
claims.criterion: Table S1 is in the Supporting Information, which was not in the text read. The Orange CaMBI values come from the literature (Oh et al. 2019, Nat. Chem. Biol. 15 433, doi:10.1038/s41589-019-0256-z); which cells and stimuli enter each ratio is given only in Table S1. The range holds when each bound is within the range widened by 10% of each bound.

claims.statement: The analysed segment of each recording holds about 40 population bursts (38 ± 4, mean ± SE).
claims.source: Methods, Comparing data from different sources
claims.quote: The recording durations per data source were selected so that each recording contained around 40 bursts (38 ± 4 bursts, mean ± SE)
claims.criterion: Bursts detected as in the opening comment over HO1 to HO8, MO1 to MO9, MS and Pr1 to Pr8, under the code's recording lengths (reading a). Reproduced when the mean count is within tolerance. Reading (b) fixes the count by construction and is not a test of it.

claims.statement: In the example human organoid of Figs. 1 and 2, 46 bursts occur in a three-minute interval.
claims.source: Figure 1C legend; Figure 2C legend
claims.quote: The population firing rate (gray lines) is plotted relative to the burst peak for 46 burst events measured across a three-minute interval for the same organoid
claims.criterion: The example organoid is not named in the paper (the HMM code uses HO1 as its example). Bursts detected as in the opening comment on the first 180 s of each of HO1 to HO4, with a minimum peak distance of 700 ms (Methods) and 800 ms (code variant). Reproduced when one of the four recordings gives a count within tolerance; that recording is the example organoid for claims fig4d-burst-similarity and fig4f-pca-variance.

claims.statement: In each of the 8 human organoids the distribution of unit mean firing rates is well fit by a lognormal distribution (R² 0.97 ± 0.04, mean ± STD), while the rates of backbone units alone are not (R² 0.45 ± 0.30).
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 1A to C
claims.quote: we observed that the distribution of firing rates follows a heavy-tailed, right-skewed lognormal distribution ( n = 8, R 2 = 0.97 ± 0.04, Extended Data Fig. 1A – C ) ... Backbone neurons alone are not well described by a lognormal distribution. R 2 values are 0.45±0.30 across the 8 human brain organoids
claims.criterion: Mean rate per unit is its spike count over the recording length. The fit is open between the Methods and code and the Extended Data Fig. 1C legend. Readings (a) a lognormal density fitted by nonlinear least squares to the probability histogram of rates in 20 bins from 0 to 10 Hz, ordinary R² (Methods, and plot_multi_rec_figs_backbone.m, whose density divides by (2 sigma)^2 where the standard form has 2 sigma^2, shown as a variant); (b) a normal density fitted to the probability histogram of log rates in ceil(n^0.4) bins (legend). Units either all sorted units (code) or those with at least 30 spikes (Methods). Reproduced when, under one reading, both means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when only the all-unit mean is.

claims.statement: Burst durations in the human organoids are on the order of 10² ms.
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 1; Figure 1D; Supplementary Fig. 1C
claims.quote: Bursts exhibited consistent rate profiles within organoids ( Fig. 1C ), with durations spanning timescales on the order of ≈ 10 2 milliseconds ( Fig. 1D , Supplementary Fig. 1 C )
claims.criterion: Burst duration is end minus start as in the opening comment (10% of peak on the coarse population rate). "On the order of 10² ms" is read as the decade from 100 to 1000 ms, a standard reading. Reproduced when the median burst duration of each of HO1 to HO4 (Fig. 1D) lies in that decade; partially reproduced when three of the four do. The medians of all 31 recordings (Supplementary Fig. 1C) are reported.

claims.statement: Most units reach their peak firing rate close to the peak of the population burst.
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 1; Figure 1E
claims.quote: A majority of units firing rates peaked in close proximity to the population burst maxima ( Fig. 1E )
claims.criterion: Peak time per unit and burst, the time of its maximum rate between burst start and end relative to the burst peak, in bursts where it fires at least two spikes (Methods). HO1 to HO4. "Close proximity" is not fixed by the paper. Readings for the quantity, (i) each unit's median peak time, (ii) all unit-burst peak times pooled; for the bound, (a) within 50 ms and (b) within 100 ms of the burst peak (the Results speak of lags near 10 ms and sequences of about 10² ms). Reproduced when more than half of the values fall within the bound in each organoid, under every reading.

claims.statement: Backbone units, which fire at least twice in every burst, are 28% ± 14% (mean ± STD) of the units in the 8 human organoids.
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 3; Supplementary Fig. 1A
claims.quote: Backbone units, comprising 28% ± 14% (mean ± STD) of total neurons ( n = 8 organoids, Supplementary Fig. 1 )
claims.criterion: Backbone units as in the opening comment. The denominator can be read as (a) all sorted units in the recording or (b) units with at least 30 spikes. Reproduced when the mean and the standard deviation are both within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when only the mean is. The tolerance on the mean is the paper's stated spread.

claims.statement: Backbone units have higher burst-to-burst correlations of their firing rate than non-rigid units.
claims.source: Figure 2E legend; Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Backbone neurons consistently exhibited higher burst-to-burst correlation coefficients compared to non-rigid units ( P < 10 −16 , two-sided linear mixed-effects model, n = 4 organoids and 507 single-units)
claims.criterion: Burst-to-burst correlation per unit as in the Methods. Burst-only rates; for each pair of bursts, the rate from 250 ms before to 500 ms after each burst peak, MATLAB xcorr with maxlag 10 ms and 'coeff' normalization, maximum over lags; mean over all pairs of bursts in which the unit has at least 2 spikes in that window. Units kept when they have at least 2 spikes in at least 30% of bursts (Methods; the code keeps units with at least 2 spikes in at least 70% of bursts, a variant) and at least 30 spikes (code). HO1 to HO4 (code, Fig 2E comment). Test, correlation on unit type with a random intercept per organoid. Reproduced when backbone units are higher with p < 0.05; the unit count is reported against 507.

claims.statement: Among backbone units, the variance of firing-rate peak times across bursts grows with the unit's position in the sequence, so later-firing units are more variable.
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 3; Figure 2F and 2G
claims.quote: Finally, the variability of firing peak times increased with their average latency ( Fig. 2F ), a relationship consistently observed across organoids ( Fig. 2G , P < 10 −5 , linear mixed-effects model)
claims.criterion: Per backbone unit of HO1 to HO4, the median and the variance of its peak time over the bursts in which it fires at least two spikes (Methods). The "relative position of the peak (from 0 to 1)" of the Methods is read as (a) the unit's rank by median peak time scaled to 0 to 1, or (b) its median peak time rescaled over the backbone period to 0 to 1. Model, variance on relative position with a random intercept per organoid. Reproduced when the slope is positive with p < 0.05 under both readings.

claims.statement: When bursts are clustered by their pairwise unit correlation matrices, the firing rates of non-rigid units vary more between clusters than those of backbone units.
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 3F
claims.quote: Clustering bursts by their pairwise correlation matrix confirmed that backbone patterns were preserved across clusters, whereas non-rigid units varied substantially ( P < 10 −20 , linear mixed-effects model; Extended Data Fig. 3 )
claims.criterion: As in the Supplementary Methods, Burst clustering, and ExtractBurst_ElbowSeeds.py. Per burst, the burst-only rates from 250 ms before to 500 ms after the peak, the correlation matrix of all unit pairs (numpy corrcoef), its lower triangle as a vector; k-means++ on these vectors for k from 2 upward, the best of several seeds per k. The elbow is picked by eye in the paper; readings (a) the knee of the SSE curve by the kneedle rule, (b) the k with the largest silhouette coefficient (the code computes both). Per unit, the CV (STD over mean) of its mean rate across clusters. Recordings, HO1 to HO8; the paper shows HO5 (Or5) as its example and does not name the set, so HO1 to HO4 alone is a second reading. Test, CV on unit type with a random intercept per organoid. Reproduced when non-rigid CV is higher with p < 0.05 under every reading.

claims.statement: In murine organoids, blocking GABA-A receptors with gabazine increases the number of population bursts.
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 4B
claims.quote: Meanwhile, the number of bursts increase after gabazine treatment ( P < 0.05, two-sided linear mixed-effect model)
claims.criterion: Bursts detected as in the opening comment in the baseline and gabazine recordings of MO10 to MO14. Burst count (or rate, if the recordings differ in length) on condition with a random intercept per organoid. Reproduced when gabazine is higher with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Blocking AMPA and NMDA receptors with NBQX and R-CPP abolishes population bursts in murine organoids.
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 4B
claims.quote: Note that bursting disappears after NBQX and R-CPP treatment reflected as a significant decrease in bursting compared to baseline conditions ( P < 0.001, two-sided linear mixed-effect model)
claims.criterion: As in ed4b-gabazine-more-bursts, baseline against NBQX with R-CPP. Reproduced when the count falls with p < 0.05 and the treated recordings hold no burst or nearly none (at most one per recording, given that the paper says bursting disappears).

claims.statement: Gabazine increases the fraction of bursts in which units fire at least two spikes.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 4C
claims.quote: The fraction of bursts in which units are active increases significantly after gabazine treatment ( P < 10 −7 , two-sided linear mixed-effect model)
claims.criterion: Per unit and recording, the fraction of bursts with at least two spikes between burst start and end. Units are matched between conditions only if the dataset identifies them across recordings (the paper records "the same electrode configuration"); otherwise units are pooled per condition. Model, fraction on condition with a random intercept per organoid (and per unit when matched). Reproduced when gabazine is higher with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Gabazine makes the order of backbone sequences more consistent across bursts.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 4D
claims.quote: There is a significant increase in backbone sequence order similarity after treatment with gabazine ( P < 10 −20 , two-sided linear mixed-effect model)
claims.criterion: As in the Supplementary Methods, Firing rate peak rank order correlations. Per burst, the backbone units ranked by their peak rate time; Spearman correlation for every pair of bursts; each normalized to the mean over 100 shuffles. The legend says z-scored and the Supplementary Methods say (A - B)/(A + B); both are readings. Backbone units defined per recording with the 80% murine organoid threshold. Model, normalized correlation of burst pairs on condition with a random intercept per organoid. Reproduced when gabazine is higher with p < 0.05 under both readings.

claims.statement: The fraction of backbone units declines as human and murine organoids mature.
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 2; Supplementary Fig. 2A
claims.quote: Longitudinal recordings showed that the relative fraction of backbone units declined over development ( Supplementary Fig. 2 )
claims.criterion: No test is reported. Backbone fraction per organoid and age (human organoids at 6, 7 and 8 months per plot_develomental_analysis.m; murine organoids at their recorded weeks). Readings for "declined", (a) the mean fraction over organoids is lower at the oldest age than at the youngest, (b) it is lower at the oldest age in every organoid. Reproduced when this holds for both human and murine organoids under both readings; partially reproduced when it holds for one of them.

claims.statement: The burst-to-burst correlation of units increases over development in human and murine organoids, and backbone units are higher than non-rigid units at every age.
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 3; Supplementary Fig. 2C
claims.quote: Their firing patterns remained stable across hours ( Supplementary Fig. 8 ) and persisted over months, with correlations increasing during development in both human and murine organoids ( Supplementary Fig. 2C , P < 10 −5 , two-way ANOVA)
claims.criterion: Burst-to-burst correlation per unit as in fig2e-b2b-correlation, for each organoid and age. Two-way ANOVA of unit correlations on age and unit type (the second factor is not named; unit type is the reading the panel's layout implies, organoid is a second reading). Reproduced when the age effect has p < 0.05 with correlations higher at older ages in both groups, and backbone means exceed non-rigid means at every age.

claims.statement: Units classed as backbone in one recording are mostly classed as backbone again 4 h later, units classed as non-rigid are mostly classed as non-rigid again, and backbone units keep more consistent firing patterns across the two recordings than non-rigid units.
claims.source: Supplementary Fig. 8A and 8E
claims.quote: the majority of units that was detected as a backbone unit at time point 0-hour was also detected as backbone unit at time point 4-hour (top left) for both organoids. Meanwhile, the majority of units that were detected as non-rigid units at time point 0-hour were also detected as non-rigid units at time point 4-hour (bottom right) for both organoids
claims.criterion: HO2 and HO3, recordings at 0 h and 4 h. Units must be identified across the two recordings; the paper does not say how, so this is tested only if the dataset links them (for example by joint sorting). Reproduced when more than half of the 0 h backbone units are backbone at 4 h and more than half of the 0 h non-rigid units are non-rigid at 4 h in both organoids, and the mean 0-to-4 h burst-to-burst correlation (bursts paired across recordings, Methods) is higher for backbone than for non-rigid units in both.

claims.statement: Randomizing spike times while keeping unit and population rates reduces burst-to-burst correlations.
claims.source: Results, Temporal dynamics of neuronal firing sequences, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 5D; Supplementary Fig. 9A
claims.quote: Randomized spike trains that preserved mean and single-unit firing rates abolished sequences and significantly reduced burst-to-bust correlations ( Extended Data Fig. 5 , Supplementary Figs. 9 - 10 )
claims.criterion: Burst-to-burst correlation per unit as in fig2e-b2b-correlation on the real and on the 100 shuffled matrices, HO1 to HO8. No test is named. Readings (a) a linear mixed-effects model of correlation on data type (real or shuffled mean) with random intercepts for unit and organoid, (b) the normalized value (A - B)/(A + B) tested above 0 with a random intercept per organoid, one-sided as in Extended Data Fig. 2F. Reproduced when real exceeds shuffled with p < 0.05 for backbone units under both readings.

claims.statement: Pairwise cross-correlations of firing rates are higher between backbone units than between backbone and non-rigid units or between non-rigid units.
claims.source: Figure 3E legend; Results, Backbone units are a highly correlated ensemble
claims.quote: Correlations between backbone units (blue) are significantly higher ( P < 10 −20 , 2-sided linear mixed effects model, n = 4 organoids and 34,056 single unit pairs) than the cross-correlations between pairs of backbone and non-rigid units (gray) and pairs of non-rigid units (yellow)
claims.criterion: As in the Methods, Pairwise firing rate correlations. Burst-only rates over the whole recording, MATLAB xcorr with maxlag 350 ms and 'coeff', maximum over lags; units with at least 30 spikes (legend, code). HO1 to HO4 (code comment for Fig. 3E). Model, correlation on pair type with a random intercept per organoid, emmeans contrasts. Reproduced when backbone pairs exceed both other pair types with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The distribution of pairwise correlations is skewed and roughly lognormal, and backbone-backbone pairs lie in its upper tail in every organoid.
claims.source: Figure 3F legend; Results, Backbone units are a highly correlated ensemble
claims.quote: The histogram of all pairwise cross-correlations follows a skewed, lognormal distribution ( x -axis is log scale). The pairwise connections between pairs of backbone units populate the tail of this distribution for all organoids
claims.criterion: Pairwise correlations as in fig3e-pairwise-correlation, HO1 to HO4. The paper marks the mean of the backbone-backbone correlations on each histogram and fixes no bound for the tail. Readings, that mean lies above (a) the 75th or (b) the 90th percentile of all pairs. Reproduced when this holds in all four organoids under both readings. The skew of all pairs and the R² of a normal fit to their logarithm (Supplementary Fig. 12C) are reported, not judged.

claims.statement: The spread of burst similarity across pairs of bursts is high outside bursts, drops at burst onset and stays low until the bursts end.
claims.source: Results, Population firing rate timing across burst epochs, paragraph 1; Figure 4C
claims.quote: Variance in similarity showed the opposite trend: it was high during non-bursting periods, rapidly declining at burst onset, and remaining low until bursts ended ( Fig. 4C )
claims.criterion: Burst similarity over all units as in fig4d-burst-similarity, for every pair of bursts at each frame from the earliest burst start to the latest burst end relative to the peak (Methods, Burst similarity score); at each frame, the standard deviation over burst pairs (Fig. 4C legend). Example organoid from fig1c-example-burst-count. No test is reported, and the paper does not say which frames count as inside a burst; readings, inside is (a) from the median burst start to the median burst end relative to the peak, (b) the backbone window. Reproduced when the mean standard deviation over frames inside is lower than over the frames outside, under both readings. HO1 to HO8 are reported.

claims.statement: Across pairs of bursts, the population firing vectors of backbone units are more similar (cosine similarity) throughout the backbone window than those of non-rigid units or of shuffled data.
claims.source: Figure 4D legend; Results, Population firing rate timing across burst epochs, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Backbone units consistently display significantly higher similarity throughout the backbone window compared with non-rigid or shuffled controls ( P < 10 −20 , paired two-sided t-test)
claims.criterion: As in the Methods, Burst similarity score, and comp_burst_sim in the code. At each 1 ms frame relative to the burst peak, the cosine similarity of the unit rate vectors of every pair of bursts. The code z-scores each unit's rate over the recording first (the Methods are silent, the code is followed) and uses full rates for real data and burst-only rates for the shuffles. Backbone window, from the earliest to the latest median peak time of backbone units. At each frame of the window, a paired two-sided t-test over burst pairs (lower triangle) of backbone against non-rigid and backbone against shuffled, at Bonferroni alpha 0.05 over frames (code). Example organoid from fig1c-example-burst-count. Reproduced when backbone is higher and significant at every frame of the window for both comparisons; partially reproduced when that holds for at least 90% of frames. HO1 to HO8 are reported.

claims.statement: In every human organoid the burst similarity rises from the onset of the backbone period and stays high during it.
claims.source: Results, Population firing rate timing across burst epochs, paragraph 1; Figure 4E; Supplementary Fig. 13D
claims.quote: Across organoids, burst similarity increased at backbone onset and plateaued during their activation ( Fig. 4E , Supplementary Fig. 13D , n = 8 organoids)
claims.criterion: Burst similarity over all units as in fig4d-burst-similarity, for HO1 to HO8, within each backbone period. No test is reported. Reproduced when, in all 8 organoids, the mean similarity over the backbone period exceeds its value at the first frame of the period; partially reproduced when that holds in 6 or 7.

claims.statement: The 20% of units with the highest average pairwise correlation give a higher burst similarity than all units together, and the 20% with the lowest give a lower one.
claims.source: Results, Population firing rate timing across burst epochs, paragraph 1; Supplementary Fig. 13A to C
claims.quote: Notably, the top 20th percentile of highly correlated units (from Fig. 3C ) generated significantly higher burst similarity than the full population, with the effect diminishing as larger percentiles were included ( Supplementary Fig. 13A , C ). Conversely, the lowest 20th percentile reduced similarity
claims.criterion: Units ranked by their mean pairwise correlation (Fig. 3C matrix); burst similarity of the top 20% and of the bottom 20% against all units at every frame of the backbone window by a paired two-sided t-test over burst pairs (Methods), in the example organoid. Reproduced when the top 20% are higher and the bottom 20% lower, each significant at p < 0.05 Bonferroni-corrected over frames, at a majority of frames of the backbone window. The difference in summed similarity for top against bottom percentiles from 20 to 95 is reported.

claims.statement: In the example organoid, the first two principal components of backbone unit rates explain 73% of their variance against 25% for non-rigid units, and across organoids backbone units need fewer components than all units while non-rigid units need more.
claims.source: Results, Population firing rate timing across burst epochs, paragraph 2; Figure 4F and 4G; Supplementary Fig. 14
claims.quote: When populations were divided, backbone units captured far more variance (73%) in the first two PCs compared to non-rigid units (25%) ( Fig. 4F middle/right, Fig. 4G , Supplementary Figs. 14 - 15 )
claims.criterion: PCA as in compute_manifolds of the code, on burst-only rates, each unit mean-centred and scaled to unit standard deviation (the Methods' z-score), by SVD, for all, backbone and non-rigid units. The example organoid is the one of fig1c-example-burst-count; if none matches there, any of HO1 to HO8 that matches counts, as the number's subject is not named. Reproduced when both percentages are within tolerance and, in every organoid of HO1 to HO8, the cumulative variance of the first two PCs is higher for backbone than for all units and lower for non-rigid than for all units; partially reproduced when only the across-organoid pattern holds.

claims.statement: Hidden Markov models fitted to the organoid spike trains give a higher held-out log likelihood on real data than on randomized data with the same unit and population rates.
claims.source: Results, Revealing temporal structure with a hidden Markov model, paragraph 1; Supplementary Fig. 18
claims.quote: Log likelihood is always greater for real than for randomized data, with no overlap between the distributions for real and shuffled data
claims.criterion: Poisson-observation HMMs (SSM), 30 ms bins, K from 10 to 30, fitted by EM (code tolerance 1e-3, at most 5000 iterations), for HO1 to HO8 (Supplementary Methods). Validation by 5-fold cross-validation. The Supplementary Methods fit each fold on a random 80% of the data and score the other 20%; the code (cv_scores) holds out a random 10% of the time bin by unit entries instead, shown as a variant. Score, held-out log likelihood per entry on real data against the randomized (Okun) surrogate in the held-out region. Reproduced when real exceeds surrogate in every fold, K and organoid.

claims.statement: The diversity of HMM states is high before and after bursts and reaches a minimum near the burst peak, where states follow a stereotyped path.
claims.source: Results, Revealing temporal structure with a hidden Markov model, paragraph 2; Figure 5C; Supplementary Fig. 19B
claims.quote: Notably, entropy consistently approaches a local minimum near burst peaks, indicating a convergence toward specific states with higher transition probabilities during the initiation of sequential activation patterns
claims.criterion: HMMs as in supp18-hmm-likelihood-real-above-shuffled fitted to the full data; most likely state per bin (the code uses SSM most_likely_states); per bin from 500 ms before to 500 ms after each burst peak, the Shannon entropy of the state distribution across bursts (Supplementary Fig. 19B), per model, then averaged over K. "Near burst peaks" is not fixed; readings, the minimum lies (a) within 90 ms (three bins) of the peak, (b) within the backbone window. Reproduced when, in at least 6 of the 8 organoids, the minimum is near the peak and lower than the entropy at both ends of the window, under both readings.

claims.statement: Backbone units are active across a larger pool of HMM states than non-rigid units.
claims.source: Results, Revealing temporal structure with a hidden Markov model, paragraph 3; Figure 5D; Supplementary Fig. 21
claims.quote: Backbone ensembles spanned a larger pool of HMM states than non-rigid units ( Fig. 5D , Supplementary Fig. 21 )
claims.criterion: Consistency of a unit in a state, the fraction of the state's realizations (bins where it is most probable) in which the unit fires at least once (Supplementary Methods). The size of the "pool" is not defined; readings (a) the number of states with consistency above 0.5, (b) the mean consistency over states. HO1 to HO8, K from 10 to 30. No test is reported; a linear mixed-effects model on unit type with random intercepts for organoid and K. Reproduced when backbone is higher with p < 0.05 under both readings.

claims.statement: A linear classifier on HMM state consistency separates backbone from non-rigid units with 83.9% ± 12.0% accuracy, above the 63.2% ± 10.4% reached with firing rate alone.
claims.source: Results, Revealing temporal structure with a hidden Markov model, paragraph 3; Figure 5F
claims.quote: Linear support vector machine classifiers trained on hidden state features distinguished backbone from non-rigid units with 83.9% ± 12.0% accuracy, significantly exceeding the 63.2% ± 10.4% achieved when using firing rate alone ( Fig. 5F )
claims.criterion: Features per unit, its K consistencies; classifier, standardization then a linear SVM (the code uses sklearn SGDClassifier with its default hinge loss), leave-one-out accuracy over units; baseline, the same classifier on the unit's mean rate (Fig5.py). K from 10 to 30, so 21 models per organoid; means and SDs pooled over models (states) and over organoids (rate), as Fig5.py prints them. The tolerances are the paper's stated spreads. The test is open; readings (a) a paired two-sided t-test over the 8 organoids of mean state accuracy against rate accuracy (legend, n = 8), (b) per organoid a one-sample t-test of the 21 state accuracies against the rate accuracy (Fig5.py), required in all 8 ("in all cases"). Classifier seeds are a standard choice. Reproduced when both means are within tolerance and states beat rate with p < 0.05 under both readings.

claims.statement: In neonatal mouse cortical slices, backbone units have higher burst-to-burst correlations than non-rigid units.
claims.source: Figure 6F legend; Results, Endogenous sequences in early developing neonatal cortex, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Backbone units consistently exhibited higher correlations than non-rigid units (P < 10 −20 , two-sided linear mixed-effects model, n = 6 mice and 959 single units)
claims.criterion: As fig2e-b2b-correlation, on the six slices, with the backbone threshold at 90% (Methods) and at 70% (Fig. 6B legend), and a random intercept per slice or per animal. Reproduced when backbone units are higher with p < 0.05 under every reading.

claims.statement: In neonatal slices, backbone-backbone pairs are more strongly correlated than mixed or non-rigid pairs.
claims.source: Figure 6G legend
claims.quote: Backbone–backbone correlations were significantly stronger than mixed or non-rigid pairs (P < 10 −20 , two-sided linear mixed-effects model, n = 6 mice and 125607 single unit pairs)
claims.criterion: As fig3e-pairwise-correlation, on the six slices, with the slice readings of fig6f-slice-b2b-correlation. Reproduced when backbone pairs exceed both other types with p < 0.05 under every reading.

claims.statement: Backbone units fire at higher rates than non-rigid units in every model type (human and murine organoids, neonatal slices and primary cultures).
claims.source: Results, Comparing sequences across neurodevelopmental models, paragraph 1; Figure 7A
claims.quote: Backbone neurons had significantly higher firing rates than non-rigid counterparts ( Fig. 7A , P < 10 −6 , linear mixed-effects model, Supplementary Fig. 23 )
claims.criterion: Mean rate per unit (spike count over recording length), units with at least 30 spikes, log10-transformed (Fig7.ipynb plots log10 rate; Methods log-transform skewed data). Model, log rate on unit type, model type and their interaction with a random intercept per recording; emmeans contrasts of backbone against non-rigid within each model type. Thresholds per model type as in the opening comment, with both slice readings. Reproduced when backbone is higher with p < 0.05 in all four model types; partially reproduced in two or three. Unit counts are reported (the paper gives 1048 for both human organoids and primary cultures).

claims.statement: Primary cultures fire at higher rates than organoids and neonatal slices, in both unit groups.
claims.source: Results, Comparing sequences across neurodevelopmental models, paragraph 1; Figure 7A
claims.quote: However, primary cultures exhibited overall higher firing rates across both populations ( P < 10 −10 for organoids and neonatal slices)
claims.criterion: Model of fig7a-backbone-higher-rate; emmeans contrasts of primary cultures against each of the other three model types, within backbone and within non-rigid units. Reproduced when all six contrasts favour primary cultures with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when at least four do.

claims.statement: After normalization to shuffled data, backbone units remain more correlated from burst to burst than non-rigid units in organoids and neonatal slices, and backbone units of organoids and slices are more correlated than those of primary cultures.
claims.source: Results, Comparing sequences across neurodevelopmental models, paragraph 1; Figure 7B
claims.quote: backbone units in organoids and neonatal slices showed significantly stronger normalized burst-to-burst single-unit firing correlations compared to primary cultures ( Fig. 7B , Supplementary Fig. 9 ). After normalization relative to randomized data, backbone units remained significantly more correlated than non-rigid units in organoids and slices ( P < 10 −10 and P = 7×10 −4 , linear mixed-effects model)
claims.criterion: Burst-to-burst correlation per unit as in fig2e-b2b-correlation, normalized as (A - B)/(A + B) to the 100 shuffles (Methods; btb_corr_m in the code's single_unit table). Model as in fig7a-backbone-higher-rate on the normalized value (not log-transformed). Reproduced when backbone exceeds non-rigid with p < 0.05 in human organoids, murine organoids and slices, and backbone units of each of these three exceed those of primary cultures with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when only the within-type contrasts hold. The Results and the legend print different p-values for the same panel; both are recorded. Supplementary Fig. 9B describes the normalization as subtracting the shuffle mean (A - B); that is shown as a variant, as for fig7e-pca-backbone-variance.

claims.statement: In primary cultures, normalized burst-to-burst correlations do not differ between backbone and non-rigid units.
claims.source: Results, Comparing sequences across neurodevelopmental models, paragraph 1; Figure 7B
claims.quote: whereas no significant difference was observed in primary cultures ( P = 0.06)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the contrast of backbone against non-rigid in primary cultures in the model of fig7b-normalized-b2b at alpha 0.05. Reproduced when p >= 0.05, not reproduced when p < 0.05; the effect size is given either way.

claims.statement: After normalization to shuffled data, backbone-backbone pairs are more correlated than non-rigid pairs in human and murine organoids.
claims.source: Figure 7C legend
claims.quote: Backbone pairs showed significantly higher correlations in organoids (human: P = 9 × 10 −7 ; murine: P = 1 × 10 −8 ), but not in slices ( P = 0.10) or primaries ( P = 0.16)
claims.criterion: Pairwise correlations as in fig3e-pairwise-correlation, normalized as (A - B)/(A + B) to the 100 shuffles; per recording, the median over pairs of each type (med_corr in the code's unit_pair_avg table, which Fig7.ipynb plots). Model, the per-recording median on pair type (backbone-backbone, non-rigid-non-rigid), model type and their interaction with a random intercept per recording; emmeans contrast within each model type. Reproduced when backbone pairs are higher with p < 0.05 in both human and murine organoids. Pair-level values with a random intercept per recording are a variant. Supplementary Fig. 12B describes the normalization as subtracting the shuffle mean (A - B); that is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Normalized pairwise correlations of backbone pairs do not differ from those of non-rigid pairs in slices or in primary cultures.
claims.source: Figure 7C legend
claims.quote: but not in slices ( P = 0.10) or primaries ( P = 0.16)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the contrasts of the model of fig7c-normalized-pairwise at alpha 0.05, with both slice readings. Reproduced when both are non-significant; partially reproduced when one is; not reproduced when neither is. Effect sizes are given.

claims.statement: Backbone-backbone pairs in organoids and slices are more correlated than in randomized data, while in primary cultures they are not.
claims.source: Results, Comparing sequences across neurodevelopmental models, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Backbone-to-backbone pairs in organoids and slices exhibited significantly higher correlations compared to randomized controls ( P < 10 −10 , linear mixed-effects model), an effect not observed in primary cultures ( P > 0.99)
claims.criterion: Normalized backbone-backbone pair correlations, (A - B)/(A + B), tested above 0 per model type with a linear mixed-effects model and a random intercept per recording, one-sided as in Extended Data Fig. 2F (the Results do not name the sidedness; two-sided is a variant). Reproduced when the value is above 0 with p < 0.05 in organoids and in slices and not significant in primary cultures (the absence judged on the same test at alpha 0.05).

claims.statement: Lags of maximum cross-correlation between backbone units are longer in human and murine organoids than in primary cultures, and lags in human organoids differ from those in murine organoids and in slices.
claims.source: Results, Comparing sequences across neurodevelopmental models, paragraph 2; Figure 7D
claims.quote: Correlation Lag-times between backbone units were larger for organoids compared to primary cultures (human organoid vs primary: P = 1 × 10 −8 ; murine organoids vs primary: P = 0.011), with human organoid differing from murine organoids ( P = 0.0096) and slices ( P = 0.0002)
claims.criterion: Per backbone pair, the lag of the maximum pairwise correlation (fig3e-pairwise-correlation, maxlag 350 ms), absolute and log10-transformed (lag_vals_log in the code's lag_data table). Zero lags have no logarithm and the code's handling is not shown; readings (a) drop them, (b) set them to 1 ms. Model, log lag on model type with a random intercept per recording; emmeans contrasts. The text gives the direction only for the contrasts against primary cultures (larger in organoids); for human organoids against murine organoids and against slices it says only that they differ, so either direction counts and the direction found is reported. Reproduced when the two contrasts against primary cultures are larger in organoids and all four have p < 0.05, under both readings; partially reproduced when the two contrasts against primary cultures hold.

claims.statement: Backbone lag times do not differ between murine organoids and slices.
claims.source: Figure 7D legend
claims.quote: Murine organoids vs slices ( P = 0.47) and primary cultures were not significant ( P = 0.53)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the model of fig7d-lag-times at alpha 0.05. The legend's second contrast reads as murine organoids against primary cultures, which the same legend reports as P = 0.011, so it is read as slices against primary cultures. Reproduced when murine organoids against slices is non-significant; the slices against primary cultures contrast is reported and judged the same way.

claims.statement: In human and murine organoids, backbone units explain a larger normalized fraction of variance in the first three principal components than non-rigid units; slices and primary cultures show no such difference.
claims.source: Results, Comparing sequences across neurodevelopmental models, paragraph 3; Figure 7E; Supplementary Fig. 15
claims.quote: Differences were significant for organoids (human: P = 2 × 10 −7 ; murine: P = 0.036), but not slices ( P = 0.29) or primaries ( P = 0.21)
claims.criterion: PCA as in fig4f-pca-variance. Per recording and unit set, the variance of the first three PCs divided by that of the first X PCs, X the smallest number of PCs among all, backbone and non-rigid units; normalized as (A - B)/(A + B) to 100 shuffles (Methods; m_value in the code's pca table; Supplementary Fig. 15 says the shuffle mean was subtracted, a variant). Model, value on unit type, model type and their interaction with a random intercept per recording. The legend plots all units, backbone and non-rigid and says only "Differences were significant", and the Methods compare "the three selections", so which contrast is meant is open; readings (a) backbone against non-rigid (unit types backbone and non-rigid), (b) backbone against all units (all three selections in the model). Reproduced when backbone exceeds the comparison group with p < 0.05 in human and murine organoids and the contrasts in slices and primary cultures are non-significant at alpha 0.05 (absence on the same test), under both readings; partially reproduced when only the organoid contrasts hold. The Results also say organoid backbone units exceed those of other model types; that contrast is reported.
