Reproduced when both one-sided tests have p below 0.05, the two-sided group test is not significant at 0.05 (a claim of absence on the paper's test), and the means are within tolerance.

claims.statement: A decoder of head direction trained on the first and tested on the last session was accurate for both environments, with no difference between the weekly and single groups (weekly 35.9, single 43.9 degrees median error; P = 0.438).
claims.source: Results, Memory from a single visit is stable over weeks, paragraph 1; Fig. 4e
claims.quote: This was further supported by the high accuracy of a decoder of head direction for both environments (not significantly different from other animals)
claims.criterion: Decoder as in the opening comment, trained on the first and tested on the last session of each environment for mice 6 to 10. The group test is a claim of absence on the paper's test, two-sided Wilcoxon at 0.05. "High accuracy" is read as every mouse's error below its time-reversed chance. The comparison with "other animals" has no named test or data and is not tested. Reproduced when the means are within tolerance, the group test is not significant and every error is below chance.

claims.statement: The change in preferred direction from first to last visit did not differ between the two environments (circular mean 1.6 against 5.1 degrees; two-sided Wilcoxon, p = 1.0, n = 10).
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 10c legend
claims.quote: Change in preferred direction first versus last visit, classified by environment identity. Circular mean ± s.d. in degrees... 1.6 ± 14.1, 5.1 ± 8.0. Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 1.0, W statistic = 7.0, n = 10
claims.criterion: A claim of absence on the paper's test, a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank at 0.05, paired by mouse across the two environments of mice 6 to 10 (n = 10 read as 5 mice by 2 environments). The legend does not say which environment is which; the readings are both assignments of square and circular. Reproduced when the test is not significant and the means are within tolerance under one assignment.

claims.statement: Per animal of the single-visit protocol, the circular mean change in preferred direction relative to the first visit was 4.7, -0.4, -15.5, 5.4 and -6.2 degrees.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 10b legend
claims.quote: Circular mean ± s.d. per animal with pooled environments in degrees... 4.7 ± 3.4, −0.4 ± 5.8, −15.5 ± 34.7, 5.4 ± 10.8, −6.2 ± 10.9
claims.criterion: Per session of mice 6 to 10, the change in preferred direction relative to the first visit of its environment, pooled over both environments. The mapping of the legend's order to mice 6 to 10 is taken as ascending. Reproduced when at least four of five are within tolerance.

claims.statement: The electric fields estimated from the stimulation artifact in the 1-minute experiments had medians of 0.77, 1.42, 2.86 and 6.04 mV/mm for 50, 100, 200 and 400 uA.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 1; Figure 1C
claims.quote: The magnitude of electric fields was assessed from sACS artifacts in electrophysiological recordings, and had medians of 0.77 ± 0.29, 1.42 ± 0.60, 2.86 ± 1.20, and 6.04 ± 1.68 mV/mm for 50, 100, 200, 400 μA sACS amplitudes, respectively
claims.criterion: Method from Methods 2.8. For each rat and amplitude, every channel of every trial of that amplitude is band-pass filtered at the stimulation frequency (5, 10, 20 or 40 Hz); the peak voltage of each stimulation cycle is averaged over the stimulation period per channel; differences between neighbouring electrodes along each array axis are divided by the 0.5 mm spacing (Methods 2.3), the two orthogonal fields combined by vector addition, outliers removed by Grubbs' test (alpha 0.05), and the field averaged over the frequency trials of the amplitude. Tolerances are the paper's stated spread. Open, with readings run (a) the median over rats of each rat's average field, (b) the median over all channel-pair estimates of all rats (Fig. 1C left shows these); "maximal" field per axis read as (i) each neighbour pair or (ii) the largest pair per axis and rat. The band-pass filter is not named; a zero-phase Butterworth band of +/- 1 Hz around the stimulation frequency on the LFP stream is the standard choice and is stated as one. Reproduced when all four medians are within tolerance under one reading and rise with amplitude.

claims.statement: The median electric field in the 20-minute 100 uA experiments was 1.65 mV/mm.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 1; Figure 1D
claims.quote: The median electric field produced for these experiments was 1.65 ± 0.21 mV/mm
claims.criterion: As efield-1min-medians (Methods 2.8, 40 Hz band), over the 13 rats, with the same readings; tolerance the stated spread.

claims.statement: In the finite element model the electric field falls to about half of its value at the recording electrodes about 70 um deeper.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 2C legend
claims.quote: Within the model, the electric field dropped to ~50% of the intensity measured at the recording electrodes at a further ~70 µm in depth
claims.criterion: Sim4Life Electro Ohmic Quasi-Static solver on the ViZOO Big Male Rat model with resected tissue removed, 1.5 x 1.5 x 0.1 mm gold electrodes, grid 0.5 mm (0.1 mm between electrodes), scaled so that the RMS field in the 2 x 2 mm array space 300 um deep matches the measured fields (Methods 2.8). The dataset supplies only the measured fields.

claims.statement: Cerebral electric field RMS values in the model follow log-normal distributions with shape 1.28 at every amplitude and scale 0.217, 0.400, 0.807 and 1.70 for 50, 100, 200 and 400 uA.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 2D
claims.quote: The cerebral electric field root mean square (RMS) values were fitted with log-normal distributions, with shape, location, and scale parameters of 1.28, 8.54E-03, 2.17E-01 for 50 µA; 1.28, 1.57E-02, 4.00E-01 for 100 µA; 1.28, 3.17E-02, 8.07E-01 for 200 µA; and 1.28, 6.70E-02, 1.70 for 400 µA
claims.criterion: scipy.stats lognorm fitted to the cerebral RMS values of the model of fem-depth-falloff (Methods 2.8); units as the paper's (mV/mm, read from the 1 mV/mm threshold). The locations (8.54E-03 to 6.70E-02) are reported alongside.

claims.statement: Ellipsoids fitted to the hemispheric volumes with fields of at least 1 mV/mm have axes of 7.37, 2.46, 1.58 mm (50 uA), 7.37, 3.32, 2.22 mm (100 uA), 7.86, 4.73, 3.28 mm (200 uA) and 8.80, 6.57, 4.35 mm (400 uA).
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 2E
claims.quote: Ellipsoids were fit to thresholded hemispheric volumes experiencing electric field magnitude of at least 1 mV/mm, with primary, secondary, and tertiary axes lengths of 7.37, 2.46, and 1.58 mm for 50-µA ACS; 7.37, 3.32, and 2.22 for 100-µA ACS; 7.86, 4.73, and 3.28 mm for 200-µA ACS; and 8.80, 6.57, and 4.35 mm for 400-µA ACS
claims.criterion: RMS field of the model thresholded at 1 mV/mm; pyvista.principal_axes on the surface points, standard deviations along each axis times 1.96 as radii (Methods 2.8). Each of the twelve axis lengths within 10% of the paper's value; "lengths" read as (a) the radii, (b) twice the radii, both run.

claims.statement: In the 1-minute experiments a median of 5 neurons was detected per channel and 66 per rat, of which 71% (405 of 586 cumulatively) fired at 0.25 Hz or more in at least half of the 10-second windows and were analysed.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 3; Figure 3A, B
claims.quote: Across rats, a median of 5.00 ± 0.17 neurons were detected per recording electrode channel using SpyKING CIRCUS ... This amounted to 66.00 ± 19.60 neurons per rat, of which 71.43 ± 10.39% (or, cumulatively, 405/586) had FRs ≥0.25 Hz in at least half of 10-second windows (of baseline and stimulation periods) and were, therefore, included in subsequent analysis
claims.criterion: Sorting and inclusion as in the opening comment, under readings S1 and S2. The per-channel tolerance is 10% (the stated 0.17 is narrower than the integer steps of a count); the others are the stated spread, or 10% for the totals. A neuron counts as included when it passes in (a) at least one trial, (b) at least half of its trials; both run. Spike sorting has settings the paper does not give, so counts can differ for reasons other than the data; the result is reported for each reading.

claims.statement: In the 20-minute experiments a median of 44 neurons was detected per rat and 4 per channel; 52% (343 of 620) passed the 0.25 Hz criterion and were analysed.
claims.source: Results 3.4, paragraph 1
claims.quote: A median of 44.00 ± 10.36 neurons were detected per rat, with 4.00 ± 0.60 neurons per electrode channel. Of these neurons, 51.61 ± 10.62% (or, cumulatively, 343 of 620) had FRs ≥0.25 Hz in at least half of all 1-minute windows across baseline and stimulation periods
claims.criterion: As units-1min. The Results say 1-minute windows here while Methods 2.6 and phaseextract.py use 10-second windows; readings (a) 10-s windows over the 20 min baseline and the 20 min stimulation with more than 2 spikes in each (code), (b) 1-min windows, both run, each under S1 and S2.

claims.statement: Median baseline firing rates were 1.20 Hz in the 1-minute and 1.05 Hz in the 20-minute experiments.
claims.source: Supplementary Figure S1.1; Results 3.1, paragraph 4 and 3.4, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Neurons from 1-min experiments had a median firing rate of 1.20 ± 2.11 Hz, and those from 20-min experiments had a median firing rate of 1.05 ± 4.92 Hz
claims.criterion: Mean baseline FR of each included neuron (Figure S1.1, all neurons of all rats), median over neurons. 10% tolerance, as the stated spreads (2.11 and 4.92 Hz) are wider than the values and do not bound a median. For the 1-min experiments a neuron enters once per included trial (a) or once with its mean over trials (b); both run.

claims.statement: Median baseline entrainment (sqrt|PPC|) was 0.12, 0.12, 0.11 and 0.11 to the 5, 10, 20 and 40 Hz waveforms in the 1-minute experiments and 0.14 to 40 Hz in the 20-minute experiments.
claims.source: Supplementary Figure S1.2; Results 3.1, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Neurons from 1-min experiments had median √|PPC| of 0.12 ± 0.05, 0.12 ± 0.07, 0.11 ± 0.10, 0.11 ± 0.09 to 5, 10, 20, and 40 Hz endogenous oscillatory frequencies, respectively, and those from 20-min experiments had a median √|PPC| of 0.14 ± 0.06 to 40 Hz frequencies
claims.criterion: Baseline spike phases taken from the stimulating waveform at the same offset (phaseextract.py), sqrt|PPC| per included neuron and trial, median over neurons by stimulation frequency; tolerances the stated spread. For the 1-min experiments a neuron enters once per included trial (a) or once with its mean over the trials of a frequency (b); both run.

claims.statement: Across 1-minute trials about 75% of included neurons per rat were significantly affected (FR or entrainment change), and some neurons were affected under every frequency and amplitude combination.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 3; Table 1
claims.quote: Across trials, about 75% of neurons were affected (amplitude/frequency-specific percentages are listed in Table 1 )
claims.criterion: Table 1 gives, per combination, the median over rats and 95% CI of the percentage of included neurons with a significant change (legend); the overall value is its last cell. Its tolerance is the printed CI half-width. "Overall" read as (a) the median of all rat-by-combination percentages, (b) the median of the 16 combination medians; both run, each under W1/W2 and P1/P2. Reproduced when the overall value is within tolerance and the median is above zero in all 16 combinations.

claims.statement: In 1-minute trials a change in FR was far more common than a change in spike timing (about 70% against under 10% of neurons).
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 3; Table 1
claims.quote: A change in FR was more frequent than a change in spike timing (approximately 70% vs. <10%; Table 1 )
claims.criterion: Overall cells of Table 1, readings as table1-any-change. Reproduced when the four values are within tolerance (the CI half-widths) and the share with any FR change is larger than the share with any sqrt|PPC| change, the latter below 10%.

claims.statement: The FR change in 1-minute trials was mostly a decrease, about 60% of neurons inhibited against under 10% excited.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 1; Table 1; Figures 4C, D and 10
claims.quote: The majority of neurons responding to sACS decreased their FRs during stimulation (60% of neurons were inhibited by sACS while <10% were excited, Table 1 )
claims.criterion: The text gives 60% where Table 1's overall cell is 69.23% (95% CI half-width 12.64, so 56.59 to 81.87%). Reproduced when the overall median share with a significant FR decrease lies in 56.59 to 81.87% and the share with an FR increase is below 10%, under the readings of table1-any-change.

claims.statement: Of the neurons whose spike timing changed in 1-minute trials, nearly all increased their entrainment (about 4%), and very few decreased it (under 0.5%).
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 4; Table 1; Figures 6 and 7
claims.quote: whereas the vast majority of spike timing affected neurons showed increases in entrainment (4%, Table 1 ... and only a few neurons exhibited negative Δ√|PPC| values (<0.5%; Table 1
claims.criterion: Overall cells of Table 1 (4.17 +/- 2.61% increase, 0.00 +/- 0.44% decrease), readings as table1-any-change. Reproduced when the share with a sqrt|PPC| increase is within 4.17 +/- 2.61%, the share with a decrease is below 0.5%, and the increase is larger.

claims.statement: Among affected neurons in 1-minute trials the median changes were +0.32 and -0.13 in sqrt|PPC| and +0.85 and -0.91 Hz in FR.
claims.source: Table 2
claims.criterion: Per Table 2's legend, the median and 95% CI of the change from baseline to stimulation among neurons significant in that category; tolerance the CI half-width. Readings for the pooling (a) all affected neuron-trials pooled, (b) per-rat medians then the median; each under W, P and G readings (G applies as the values may be cleaned before tabulation).

claims.statement: In 1-minute trials FR changes stayed within about 2 Hz of baseline, while entrainment changes were pronounced, Delta sqrt|PPC| reaching 0.55.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 4; Table 2
claims.quote: FR remained within ~2 Hz of baseline level ( Table 2 ), 1.20 ± 2.11 Hz ( Supplementary Fig. S1.1 ), whereas entrainment levels achieved were pronounced (Δ√|PPC| of up to 0.55
claims.criterion: Table 2 medians as in table2-magnitudes, per combination. Reproduced when every combination's median FR change (excited and suppressed) has absolute value below 2 Hz and the largest median sqrt|PPC| increase is 0.55 +/- 0.07 (Table 2's CI) at 40 Hz, 400 uA.

claims.statement: With increasing amplitude and frequency, the distribution of neurons' changes broadens, shifting toward stronger entrainment and slight suppression of firing.
claims.source: Figure 4 legend
claims.quote: With increasing sACS amplitude (A) and frequency (B), neurons exhibit a broader distribution of responses, with a shift toward stronger entrainment from baseline and a slight suppression of their activity (C, D)
claims.criterion: All included neuron-trials (legend, "all neurons"), Delta sqrt|PPC| and Delta FR grouped by amplitude (A, C) and by frequency (B, D). The paper fits density functions and names no measure of breadth or shift; readings for breadth (a) standard deviation, (b) interquartile range. Reproduced when, under one reading, the breadth of Delta sqrt|PPC| is larger at 400 than at 50 uA and at 40 than at 5 Hz, the median Delta sqrt|PPC| is higher at 400 than 50 uA and at 40 than 5 Hz, and the median Delta FR is below zero at 400 uA and at 40 Hz.

claims.statement: Among neurons with increased entrainment, the interaction of amplitude and frequency positively affected the degree of entrainment (LMER), with no significant main effects.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 1; Table 3
claims.quote: An LMER revealed that the interaction between amplitude and frequency positively affected the degree of entrainment ( Table 3 , p = 0.02
claims.criterion: Methods 2.6. Delta sqrt|PPC| of neurons with significant increases, on amplitude (uA) and frequency (Hz) as numbers with their interaction (Table 3 gives one coefficient each), random intercepts for neuron within subject, lme4 with Satterthwaite df (Table 3 prints df), Grubbs-cleaned (G readings). Reproduced when the interaction is positive with p < 0.05 and the amplitude and frequency main effects have p >= 0.05 (Table 3, 0.683 and 0.410), under one reading of W, P and G; partially when the interaction is positive and significant but a main effect is too.

claims.statement: Among neurons with decreased entrainment, only amplitude significantly affected the decrease, larger amplitudes giving smaller decreases.
claims.source: Results 3.2, paragraph 1; Table 3
claims.quote: Only amplitude was found to significantly affect decreases in entrainment ( Table 3 , p = 0.01; Fig. 7 ; Supplementary Tables S1.2–S1.5 ), with increasing amplitude yielding smaller magnitudes of entrainment decrease
claims.criterion: Model as lmer-ppc-increase-interaction, on the Delta sqrt|PPC| (negative) of neurons with significant decreases. Reproduced when the amplitude effect is positive with p < 0.05 and frequency and interaction have p >= 0.05, under one reading.

claims.statement: The FR change of neurons that increased their FR did not depend on stimulation parameters.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 1; Table 3
claims.quote: Neurons that increased their FR during sACS did not show a dependence of their induced FR change on the sACS parameters ( Table 3 )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the LMER of Methods 2.6 (as lmer-ppc-increase-interaction) on Delta FR of neurons with significant FR increases, at p <= 0.05. Reproduced when amplitude, frequency and their interaction all have p > 0.05 (Table 3, 0.434, 0.408, 0.463); not reproduced when any is significant. Estimates are reported either way, under W1 and G1 (the readings that do not touch the test as written are shown as variants).

claims.statement: For suppressed neurons, amplitude and frequency had independent and interactive effects on the decrease in FR (larger amplitude and frequency, deeper suppression).
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 1; Table 3 and legend
claims.quote: an LMER revealed that amplitude and frequency had independent and interactive effects on the decrease in FR ( Table 3 , independent effect of amplitude
claims.criterion: Model as lmer-ppc-increase-interaction on Delta FR of neurons with significant FR decreases. The Results print p = 0.001 for the interaction where Table 3 gives 1.31E-02 and its legend p = 0.01; the table is used. Reproduced when amplitude and frequency are negative and the interaction positive, each with p < 0.05, under one reading.

claims.statement: At 400 uA the increase in entrainment grew with stimulation frequency, 5.10e-3 Delta sqrt|PPC| per Hz.
claims.source: Figure 6A; Results 3.2, paragraph 2; Table S1.2
claims.quote: The 400 µA linear regressions showed significant increases in Δ√|PPC| with increasing frequency at 5.10 × 10 −3 Δ√|PPC| per Hz, p = 0.002)
claims.criterion: Least-squares regression (scipy.stats.linregress) of Delta sqrt|PPC| of neurons with significant increases at 400 uA on frequency (5, 10, 20, 40 Hz), readings R1/R2, W, P and G. Reproduced when the slope is positive with p <= 0.05 and within tolerance under one reading; partially when positive and significant but outside tolerance. Of the other amplitudes Table S1.2 reports none significant. The Results cite Table S1.4 for this regression, but the slope and p are in Table S1.2.

claims.statement: At 5 and 40 Hz the increase in entrainment grew with amplitude, by 7.22e-4 and 7.63e-4 Delta sqrt|PPC| per uA.
claims.source: Figure 6B; Results 3.2, paragraph 2; Table S1.3
claims.quote: with increasing sACS amplitudes, the degree of entrainment increased across 5 and 40 Hz stimulation frequencies (p = 0.004 and 0.0002, respectively); growing at a rate of 7.22 × 10 −4 and 7.63 × 10 −4 Δ√|PPC| per μA
claims.criterion: As fig6a-ppc-frequency-400ua, regressing on amplitude (50 to 400 uA) at each frequency. Reproduced when both slopes are positive with p <= 0.05 and within tolerance under one reading; partially when one holds.

claims.statement: At 40 Hz the share of neurons entrained rose with amplitude, by 6.04e-2 % per uA.
claims.source: Figure 6D; Results 3.2, paragraph 2; Table S1.5
claims.quote: 40 Hz also showed an increase in the number of neurons entrained with increasing stimulation amplitude (6.04 × 10 −2 % per μA, p = 0.007)
claims.criterion: One point per rat and amplitude (the share of its included neurons in that trial, as Table 1), regressed on amplitude with scipy.stats.linregress; Table S1.5 gives 6.04E-04 in fractions, the same slope. Readings W and P. Reproduced when the slope is positive with p <= 0.05 and within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: For neurons with decreased entrainment, only the 400 uA regression across frequency (-1.74e-3 per Hz) and the 5 Hz regression across amplitude (2.67e-4 per uA) were significant.
claims.source: Figure 7A, B legend; Table S1.2, S1.3
claims.quote: Only the 400-µA regression (A) across frequencies and the 5-Hz regression across amplitudes (B) showed significance, with -1.74 × 10 −3 Δ√|PPC| per Hz and 2.67 × 10 −4 Δ√|PPC| per µA (p = 0.04 and 0.005, respectively)
claims.criterion: As fig6a-ppc-frequency-400ua, on the Delta sqrt|PPC| of neurons with significant decreases. Reproduced when both named slopes have the paper's sign, p <= 0.05 and are within tolerance under one reading, and no other of the eight regressions is significant; partially when the two named slopes hold but another regression is also significant.

claims.statement: At 100 uA the FR increase of excited neurons grew with frequency, 3.65e-2 Hz per Hz.
claims.source: Figure 8A; Results 3.3, paragraph 1; Table S1.2
claims.quote: Linear regressions of 100 μA sACS response data versus sACS frequency showed increases in the magnitude of FR increase in excited neurons with increasing frequency (3.65 × 10 −2 ΔHz per Hz, p = 0.0003)
claims.criterion: As fig6a-ppc-frequency-400ua, on Delta FR of neurons with significant FR increases at 100 uA.

claims.statement: At 5 Hz the FR increase of excited neurons grew with amplitude, 2.22e-3 Hz per uA.
claims.source: Figure 8B; Results 3.3, paragraph 1; Table S1.3
claims.quote: The 5 Hz response regression across amplitudes ( Fig. 8B ; Supplementary Table S1.3 ) showed an increase in the magnitude of FR increase of excited neurons with increasing amplitude (2.22 × 10 −3 ΔHz per μA, p = 0.002)
claims.criterion: As fig6b-ppc-amplitude-5-40hz, on Delta FR of neurons with significant FR increases at 5 Hz.

claims.statement: At 200 uA the share of excited neurons fell with frequency.
claims.source: Figure 8C; Results 3.3, paragraph 1; Table S1.4
claims.quote: The 200 µA response regression showed a significant decrease in the percentage of excited neurons with increasing frequency ( Fig. 8C ; Supplementary Table S1.4 ) (-2.30 × 10 −3 % per Hz, p = 0.01)
claims.criterion: One point per rat and frequency at 200 uA, regressed on frequency. Table S1.4 gives -2.30E-03 in fractions (intercept 0.105, about 10%), so the slope is -0.23 percentage points per Hz; the text's "% per Hz" is read as the table's fraction, and the other reading (-2.30e-3 percentage points per Hz) is reported alongside. Reproduced when the slope is negative with p <= 0.05 and within tolerance under one reading of W and P.

claims.statement: For suppressed neurons at 50 and 100 uA, FR decreased further with frequency, by -8.33e-3 and -1.19e-2 Hz per Hz.
claims.source: Figure 9A legend; Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Table S1.2
claims.quote: The 50 and 100 µA regressions across frequencies (A) showed greater degrees of suppression in FRs with increasing frequency (-8.33 × 10 −3 and -1.19 × 10 −2 ΔHz per Hz, p = 0.0004 and <0.0001, respectively)
claims.criterion: As fig6a-ppc-frequency-400ua on Delta FR of neurons with significant FR decreases. The Results print "50 and 10 μA"; the legend's 100 uA is used (10 uA was not tested). Reproduced when both slopes are negative, p <= 0.05 and within tolerance under one reading; partially when one holds.

claims.statement: Only at 5 Hz did suppressed neurons' FR decrease further with amplitude, -1.36e-3 Hz per uA.
claims.source: Figure 9B legend; Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Table S1.3
claims.quote: Only the 5-Hz regression (B) showed increased suppression with increasing amplitude (-1.36 × 10 −3 ΔHz per µA, p = 0.0008)
claims.criterion: As fig6b-ppc-amplitude-5-40hz. Reproduced when the 5 Hz slope is negative, p <= 0.05 and within tolerance, and the 10, 20 and 40 Hz regressions are not significant, under one reading; partially when the 5 Hz slope holds and another is also significant.

claims.statement: The share of suppressed neurons showed no linear dependence on frequency and was maintained across amplitudes.
claims.source: Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Figure 9C, D; Tables S1.4, S1.5
claims.quote: with no (linear) stimulation frequency dependence of the fraction of neurons affected ( Fig. 9C ; Supplementary Table S1.4 ) ... However, the fraction of neurons affected was maintained across sACS amplitudes
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, scipy.stats linear regressions of the per-rat share of included neurons with a significant FR decrease against frequency (one per amplitude) and against amplitude (one per frequency), at p <= 0.05, under W1 and P1. Reproduced when none of the eight is significant; not reproduced when any is. Slopes are reported either way.

claims.statement: Taking all FR-changed neurons together, suppression deepened with frequency at 50, 100 and 200 uA (-1.02e-2, -1.33e-2, -1.47e-2 Hz per Hz), while it was largely maintained across amplitudes.
claims.source: Figure 10 legend; Results 3.3, paragraph 2; Tables S1.2, S1.3
claims.quote: When considering grouped FR changes, most amplitudes of stimulation elicited further suppression with increasing stimulation frequency (at rates of -1.02 × 10 −2 , -1.33 × 10 −2 , and -1.47 × 10 −2 ΔHz per Hz for 50, 100, and 200 µA trials; p = 0.0003, <0.0001, and 0.0001, respectively
claims.criterion: As fig6a-ppc-frequency-400ua on Delta FR of all neurons with a significant FR change (increase or decrease). Reproduced when the three slopes are negative, p <= 0.05 and within tolerance under one reading; partially when two hold. The amplitude regressions (Fig. 10B) are reported; "largely maintained" sets no test.

claims.statement: One minute of sACS produced no significant change in LFP power or LF-HF PAC from before to after stimulation.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 4; Tables S1.6, S1.7
claims.quote: LFP analysis did not show significant changes in power or LF-HF PAC before and after 1-min sACS ( Supplementary Tables S1.6–S1.7 )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the ANOVA tables of LMERs (Tables S1.6, S1.7), one per response category (increase or decrease in FR or sqrt|PPC|), of log power (or order-normalized MI) on timepoint (baseline or post-sACS), band (or band pair), amplitude and frequency with all interactions, on channels proximal to affected neurons. The S1.7 legend names six band pairs (theta, alpha, beta to low and high gamma, no delta pairs), which fits its 5 df. The S1.6 legend names five bands (theta to high gamma) where its 5 df imply six; readings (a) the five named, (b) all six bands of Methods 2.7. Reproduced when the timepoint term and every interaction containing it have p >= 0.05 in all eight models; not reproduced when any is below. Methods 2.5 say LFP was analysed only around the 20-min trials, so the windows are open; read as the 1 min before onset and the 1 min after offset in 2-s (power) and 10-s (MI) windows, with the L and M readings. Effects reported either way.

claims.statement: Under sham stimulation no neuron changed its FR in any of the 16 paradigms, and one or two neurons were spuriously detected as changing entrainment in some, without the trends seen under true sACS.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 5; Table S3.1
claims.quote: Under sham sACS, no neurons showed significant changes in firing rate across any of the 1-minute baseline to sham stimulation paradigms ( Supplementary Table S3.1 ). One or two neurons were spuriously detected as having significantly changed entrainment levels
claims.criterion: Methods 2.7, the 80-min sham recording cut into sixteen 3-min blocks, each assigned one amplitude and frequency, its first minute as baseline and its second as sham stimulation, through the 1-min pipeline; phases taken from a sinusoid at the assigned frequency, as no stimulating waveform exists (the phase offset does not change PPC). The phase reference for sham is not given; readings (i) the sinusoid, (ii) the recorded stimulation monitor channels of the sham recording, if the dataset holds them, as phaseextract.py uses for true sACS. Block assignment is random in the paper; it changes only the phase-reference frequency, and the 16 blocks are run in order (a standard choice). The FR part is a claim of absence judged on the paper's test, the FR permutation test at p <= 0.05; reproduced when no neuron in any block is significant, not reproduced otherwise, with counts reported. The sqrt|PPC| part holds when each block has at most two significant neurons in each of the two sqrt|PPC| categories (Table S3.1 shows 0 to 2 per category, and 3 in one block, 200 uA 5 Hz, counting both).

claims.statement: Without stimulation, LFP band power and modulation indices stayed stable over 80 minutes under propofol, for example delta power 1.71e-6 and delta to low-gamma MI 1.17e-3.
claims.source: Results 3.7, paragraph 2 and 3.8, paragraph 2
claims.quote: In 80-minute LFP recordings under propofol anesthesia without sACS perturbation, power was maintained at 1.71E-06 ± 6.94E-07 mV/Hz, 9.70E-07 ± 3.89E-07 mV/Hz, 6.66E-07 ± 2.72E-07 mV/Hz, 3.03E-07 ± 9.35E-08, 8.40E-08 ± 1.74E-08 mV/Hz, and 3.61E-08 ± 3.50E-09 mV/Hz for δ, θ, α, β, low-γ, and high-γ band activity
claims.criterion: Methods 2.7, the average and standard deviation of band power and of the raw MI in 1-min windows every 10 min of the sham recording; tolerances the stated SD. Open details, run as readings, power windows (a) 3 s, as the sham paragraph says, (b) 2 s, as for the 20-min analysis it claims to copy; units (the text prints mV/Hz) read as power spectral density in (i) mV^2/Hz, (ii) V^2/Hz; channels, all 16 averaged (none are singled out). The MI readings M1/M2 apply. Reproduced when, under one reading, all six power values and all eight MI values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Over the 20 minutes of sACS, 4% of neurons were entrained and 2% decreased their entrainment, while 54% increased and 34% decreased their FRs; on the whole neurons were excited.
claims.source: Results 3.5, paragraph 1; Table 4; Supplementary Figures S2.1, S2.2
claims.quote: 4% of all neurons were entrained, while in 2% of all neurons √|PPC| decreased ( Table 4 ; Supplementary Fig. S2.1 ). When considering the FRs of neurons, 54% showed increased FRs, while 34% decreased their FRs
claims.criterion: The 20 min of stimulation against the 20 min of baseline (Methods 2.6), the pooled percentages of Table 4 over all included neurons of the 13 rats. Readings S, W (including the code's 55-s FR null) and P. Reproduced when, under one reading, all five are within tolerance (10%, as Table 4 gives no spread for pooled values) and more neurons increase than decrease FR. The per-rat medians of Table 4 (91.89, 0.00, 0.00, 63.41, 24.39%) are reported alongside.

claims.statement: In the 10 minutes after the 20-minute sACS, 2% of neurons kept increased entrainment and 4% had decreased entrainment; 51% had decreased and 39% increased FRs, so excitation during sACS turned to suppression after it.
claims.source: Results 3.6, paragraph 1; Table 4; Supplementary Figures S2.3, S2.4
claims.quote: 2% of all neurons maintained imposed spiking patterns (i.e., showed increases in entrainment from baseline after stimulus offset) ... Finally, half of all neurons (51%) had decreased firing post-stimulation ... while 39% showed increased FRs post-sACS ... excitation during sACS thus turned to suppression post-sACS
claims.criterion: The first 10 min after offset against the last 10 min before onset (Methods 2.6; nulldistribution.py), pooled over the 343 included neurons. Readings S and P. Reproduced when all five are within tolerance (10%) and more neurons decrease than increase FR after offset, while 20min-during-percentages shows the reverse during stimulation.

claims.statement: Affected neurons changed sqrt|PPC| by +0.04 and -0.07 during 20-minute sACS and by +0.07 and -0.04 after it, with FR changes of +0.91 and -0.30 Hz during and +1.53 and -0.43 Hz after.
claims.source: Table 4
claims.criterion: Medians over the affected neurons of each category, pooled across rats (Table 4, with its 95% CI as tolerance); the same readings as the two percentage claims. The per-rat medians of Table 4 are reported alongside.

claims.statement: On the 12 channels near entrained neurons, log power fell from before to after 20-minute sACS in the delta, theta, alpha, beta and low-gamma bands.
claims.source: Results 3.7, paragraph 1; Figure 11B legend; Table S2.1
claims.quote: For channels near entrained neurons, significant decreases in log power observed across δ, θ, α, β, and low-γ frequency bands (emmean = -0.12, -0.15, -0,13, -0.06, and -0.04
claims.criterion: Methods 2.7 with readings L1/L2, B1/B2, N1/N2, F1/F2. Channels chosen from the neurons significant over the full 20 min of stimulation; LFP decimated to 1.2 kHz; FFT of non-overlapping 2-s windows over the 2 min before onset and after offset, mean power per band, log-transformed. Reproduced when, under one reading, the five bands decrease with p < 0.05 after correction and high gamma does not, and the contrasts are within tolerance (the SE printed in the Figure 11B legend for each response; for excited channels, whose legend prints 0.00, the 4.78E-03 of Table S2.1; channel counts 10%); partially when the signs and significance hold but the contrasts fall outside.

claims.statement: On the 78 channels near neurons whose FR rose, log power increased in all bands.

claims.source: Results 3.7, paragraph 2; Figure 11B legend; Table S2.1
claims.quote: and near suppressed neurons, decreases across all bands (emmean = -0.14, -0.19, -0.18, -0.16, -0.13, and 0.09
claims.criterion: As power-entrained-channels. The legend prints +0.09 for high gamma in a list of decreases "across all bands"; Table S2.1 gives -9.25E-02, so -0.09 is used. claims.source: Results 3.8, paragraph 1; Figure 12B legend; Table S2.2

claims.source: Results 3.8, paragraph 2; Figure 12B legend; Table S2.2

For beta to high gamma the legend prints -0.06 and Table S2.2 -0.60E-02, while the table's effect size (-0.152) and p (0.0105) with SE 0.0375 imply about -0.096; the value -0.06 with the SE tolerance covers -0.02 to -0.10.

claims.statement: In the sham group, seizure durations from the ipsilateral and contralateral hemispheres do not differ significantly across time blocks or between hemispheres.
claims.source: Results A, paragraph 1; Figure 2C
claims.quote: The Seizure Durations collected from both ipsilateral and contralateral hemispheres relative to the drug injection site were not significantly different across time or between hemispheres
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Seizures from M1, durations as in M2, sham rats, blocks baseline, condition, post 1, post 2 and post 3. Two-way ANOVA (hemisphere by block) with Bonferroni post hoc tests at P < 0.05 (Fig. 2 legend). The legend says each data point is one seizure, so the test unit is open; readings (a) one value per seizure, (b) one mean per rat. Reproduced when neither main effect nor any post hoc comparison is significant under the reading(s); not reproduced when one is. Effect sizes are given either way; if the readings differ, blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Pooled over blocks, most seizures in the sham group last less than 2 minutes, and the two hemispheres have similar distributions.
claims.source: Results A, paragraph 1; Figure 2D
claims.quote: The majority of recorded seizures lasted less than 2 minutes, and hemispheric distributions appear relatively similar
claims.criterion: Seizures from M1 in the 6 sham rats, all blocks pooled, per hemisphere. Reproduced when more than half of the seizures last under 120 s in each hemisphere. The similarity of the distributions has no test in the paper; the medians and a two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test are reported as description and do not decide.

claims.statement: In the sham group, seizure count does not differ significantly between time blocks or hemispheres, with a slight decrease in the last two hours.
claims.source: Results A, paragraph 1; Figure 2E
claims.quote: There were no significant differences in Seizure Count between time blocks or hemispheres; however, there was a slight decrease in number of seizures in the last two hours of the experiment
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Seizure Count per rat, hemisphere and block (M1, M2), sham rats, five blocks; two-way ANOVA (hemisphere by block) with Bonferroni post hoc tests at P < 0.05. Reproduced when no block or hemisphere effect or post hoc comparison is significant. The mean counts of post 2 and post 3 against the earlier blocks are reported for the slight decrease, which does not decide.

claims.statement: In the sham group, percent time in seizure in the contralateral hemisphere differs significantly between the sham condition block and post 3, suggesting the model is no longer stable in the fifth hour.
claims.source: Results A, paragraph 2; Figure 2F
claims.quote: percent time in seizure between sham and post 3 for the contralateral hemisphere was significantly different, which could mean that the seizure model is no longer stable during the fifth hour of the experiment
claims.criterion: Percent Time in Seizure (M2), sham rats, five blocks, two-way ANOVA (hemisphere by block) with Bonferroni post hoc tests (Fig. 2 legend, M3 readings). "sham" in the sentence is read as (a) the condition block of the sham group, or (b) its baseline block. Reproduced when, under one reading, the contralateral comparison with post 3 is significant at P < 0.05. The paper does not give the direction; it is reported and does not decide.

claims.statement: In the tFUS group, seizure count fell from baseline by 9%, 36% and 42% in the ipsilateral S1 and by 10%, 41% and 42% in the contralateral S1 during stimulation, post 1 and post 2, with significant reductions from baseline to post 1 and to post 2 in both hemispheres.
claims.source: Results B, paragraph 1; Figure 3A
claims.quote: The Seizure Counts in the ipsilateral S1 decreased from baseline by 9%, 36%, and 42% for stimulation, post 1, and post 2, respectively. The decrease in Seizure Count recorded from the contralateral S1 showed slightly higher reduction rates of 10%, 41%, and 42% ... Both hemispheres displayed significant reductions in Seizure Count between baseline and post 1, as well as between baseline and post 2
claims.criterion: Seizure Count (M1, M2) of the 10 tFUS rats; decreases as in M4, under each reading; tests as in M3. Reproduced when, under one reading of M4, all six decreases are within tolerance and, under one reading of M3, baseline against post 1 and baseline against post 2 are significant in both hemispheres. Partially reproduced when the four significant reductions hold but some decreases fall outside tolerance, or the decreases hold and only some of the four comparisons are significant.

claims.statement: Seizure count in the sham group stays steady, and the sham and tFUS groups differ significantly during post 1 and post 2.
claims.source: Results B, paragraph 1; Figure 3A
claims.quote: Seizure Count within the sham group remained steady throughout, and there were significant differences between the sham and tFUS groups during post 1 and post 2
claims.criterion: Seizure Count (M1, M2), group by block two-way ANOVA per hemisphere (M3). The text does not say in which hemisphere; readings (a) both hemispheres, (b) either. Reproduced when sham against tFUS is significant at post 1 and at post 2 under one reading of M3 and of the hemisphere, and no sham block differs significantly from sham baseline; partially reproduced when only one of post 1 and post 2 is significant.

claims.statement: In the tFUS group, percent time in seizure decreased significantly from baseline by 33% (ipsilateral) and 35% (contralateral) during stimulation and by 55% in post 1 and post 2 in both hemispheres.
claims.source: Results B, paragraph 2; Figure 3B; Discussion, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The Percent Time in Seizure significantly decreased by 33% in the ipsilateral S1 and by 35% in the contralateral S1 for stimulation, 55% for post 1, and 55% for post 2 in both hemispheres, respectively
claims.criterion: Percent Time in Seizure (M1, M2) of the 10 tFUS rats; decreases as in M4, tests as in M3. Which comparisons "significantly" covers is not said; readings (a) each of stimulation, post 1 and post 2 against baseline in both hemispheres, (b) at least one of them per hemisphere. Reproduced when, under one reading of M4, all six decreases are within tolerance and the comparisons are significant under one reading; partially reproduced when the decreases hold and only reading (b) gives significance, or significance holds and some decreases fall outside tolerance.

claims.statement: In the sham group, percent time in seizure decreased slightly but did not differ significantly from baseline in any block.
claims.source: Results B, paragraph 2; Figure 3B
claims.quote: Although Percent Time in Seizure for the sham condition decreased slightly across the experiment, there were no significant differences from baseline
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Percent Time in Seizure of the 6 sham rats, group by block two-way ANOVA per hemisphere with Bonferroni post hoc tests (M3). Reproduced when no sham block (condition, post 1, post 2) differs from sham baseline at P < 0.05 in either hemisphere, under the M3 reading(s); not reproduced when one does. Effect sizes given either way.

claims.statement: Percent time in seizure differs significantly between sham and tFUS during post 1 in the contralateral S1, and during stimulation and post 1 in the ipsilateral S1.
claims.source: Results B, paragraph 2; Figure 3B
claims.quote: Comparing the sham and tFUS groups, there were significant differences during the post 1 session in the contralateral S1 and during the stimulation and post 1 sessions in the ipsilateral S1
claims.criterion: Percent Time in Seizure (M1, M2), group by block two-way ANOVA per hemisphere (M3). Reproduced when, under one reading of M3, sham against tFUS is significant with tFUS lower for all three named comparisons (contralateral post 1; ipsilateral stimulation and post 1); partially reproduced for one or two of them.

claims.statement: Relative to baseline, the inter-seizure interval of the tFUS group increased by 27%, 49% and 28% (ipsilateral) and 30%, 52% and 31% (contralateral) during stimulation, post 1 and post 2; only post 1 in the contralateral S1 differed significantly from baseline.
claims.source: Results B, paragraph 3; Figure 3C
claims.quote: Relative to baseline, the ipsilateral S1 Inter-Seizure Interval increased by 27%, 49%, and 28% during stimulation, post 1, and post 2 ... The contralateral S1 Inter-Seizure Interval increased by 30%, 52%, and 31% during stimulation, post 1, and post 2, respectively. Only the post 1 session in the contralateral S1 showed significant differences relative to baseline
claims.criterion: Inter-Seizure Interval (M1, M2) of the 8 tFUS rats left after the Methods' exclusion of the two rats with a block without seizures (which two is read from the labels); increases as in M4, tests as in M3. Reproduced when, under one reading of M4, all six increases are within tolerance and, under one reading of M3, contralateral post 1 is significant against baseline and none of the other five comparisons is. Partially reproduced when the increases hold and the pattern of significance differs, or the reverse.

claims.statement: The inter-seizure interval of the sham group stays steady, and sham and tFUS differ significantly during post 1 in both hemispheres.
claims.source: Results B, paragraph 3; Figure 3C
claims.quote: The Inter-Seizure Interval of the sham group remained steady across the length of the experiment, and there were significant differences between sham and tFUS during post 1 in both hemispheres
claims.criterion: Inter-Seizure Interval (M1, M2), group by block two-way ANOVA per hemisphere (M3). Reproduced when, under one reading of M3, sham against tFUS at post 1 is significant with tFUS higher in both hemispheres and no sham block differs from sham baseline; partially reproduced when it holds in one hemisphere.

claims.statement: Seizure duration declines across time in both groups, and the only significant reduction is from baseline to post 2 in both hemispheres of the tFUS group.
claims.source: Results B, paragraph 4; Figure 3D
claims.quote: The Seizure Duration showed a steady decline across time for both the sham group and the tFUS group ... however, the only significant reduction occurred from baseline to post 2 in both hemispheres of the tFUS group
claims.criterion: Seizure Duration (M1, M2), group by block two-way ANOVA per hemisphere (M3). Reproduced when, under one reading of M3, tFUS baseline against post 2 is significant (post 2 shorter) in both hemispheres and no other within-group comparison against baseline is significant, and the group means at post 2 are below baseline in both groups. Partially reproduced when the post 2 reduction is significant in one hemisphere only, or other comparisons are also significant.

claims.statement: There are no significant changes in theta, alpha or gamma power ratios in either hemisphere.
claims.source: Results C, paragraph 1; Figure 4A, 4B and 4D
claims.quote: There were no significant changes in the theta, alpha, or gamma power ratios in either hemisphere
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Band power ratios as in M5 (both readings of the segment and of the total are reported), sham and tFUS, blocks baseline, condition, post 1, post 2; group by block two-way ANOVA per hemisphere and band with Bonferroni post hoc tests (M3, Fig. 4 legend). The Fig. 4 legend marks "significant differences to baseline within a group" apart from differences between groups, and the sentence speaks of changes, so the claim covers the within-group comparisons against baseline. Reproduced when no within-group comparison against baseline (sham or tFUS) is significant for theta, alpha and gamma in either hemisphere; not reproduced when one is. Sham against tFUS comparisons are reported and do not decide. If the M5 readings disagree, blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: The beta power ratio of the tFUS group decreased significantly during stimulation and post 1 compared with baseline.
claims.source: Results C, paragraph 1; Figure 4C; Discussion, paragraph 3
claims.quote: However, the beta ratio significantly decreased during tFUS and post 1 compared to baseline
claims.criterion: Beta (12 to 30 Hz) power over total (M5), tFUS group, tests as in M3. The hemisphere is not named; readings (a) both hemispheres, (b) either. Reproduced when, under a combination of the M3, M5 and hemisphere readings, the condition block and post 1 are both significantly lower than baseline; partially reproduced when only one is.

claims.statement: In the sham group, band power ratios show no significant change among time blocks or between hemispheres.
claims.source: Results C, paragraph 1; Figure S4
claims.quote: Within the sham group, the power ratios showed no significant change among time blocks or between hemispheres
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Band power ratios (M5) of the 6 sham rats, five blocks, per band a two-way ANOVA (hemisphere by block, as Fig. S4 plots it) with Bonferroni post hoc tests at P < 0.05. Reproduced when no block or hemisphere effect or post hoc comparison is significant in any band; not reproduced when one is. If the M5 readings disagree, blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: The normalized asymmetry index of the tFUS group increases significantly relative to baseline in the theta and alpha bands, and differs significantly from the sham group in every band.
claims.source: Results C, paragraph 1; Figure 4E-H
claims.quote: Normalized AI of the tFUS group increased significantly within the theta and alpha bands relative to baseline, and each frequency band displayed a significant difference between the normalized AI of the tFUS group and sham group
claims.criterion: AI per rat, band and block (M5), normalized to the group's baseline AI under readings (a) and (b) of M5; group by block two-way ANOVA per band (M3). Which blocks show the effects is not said in the text. Reproduced when, under one combination of readings, at least one tFUS block is significantly above baseline in theta and in alpha, and sham against tFUS is significant at one block or more in each of the four bands. Partially reproduced when either part holds alone. Since an increase means opposite things under the two normalizations when the baseline AI is negative, the sign of the mean baseline AI is reported.

claims.statement: During seizures (baseline block, after 4-AP) the asymmetry index is negative and differs from zero in every band, more than in the pre-4-AP baseline state; seizures disrupt the normal interhemispheric balance.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 4; Figure S5; Results C, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Our results indicated that seizures decreased AI, reflecting a disruption of normal interhemispheric balance
claims.criterion: AI (M5, not normalized) per rat and band, for seizure periods of the baseline block and for the pre-4-AP baseline state. The rats are not stated; readings (a) all 16 rats of the epilepsy study, (b) the 10 tFUS rats. The pre-4-AP state is read as (a) the resting baseline recording of target confirmation, (b) the first recording before the first injection, where the dataset holds one. One-sample t-tests against 0 per band (Fig. S5 legend). Reproduced when, under one combination, seizure AI is negative and significantly below 0 in all four bands and seizure AI is significantly lower than the pre-4-AP AI in at least alpha and beta; the test of that comparison is not named, so a paired t-test and a two-way ANOVA (state by band) with Bonferroni post hoc tests are both reported, as readings. Partially reproduced when only the tests against 0 hold.

claims.statement: tFUS of the CC in wild-type rats evokes potentials in the left S1 LFP that differ significantly from the sham (resting) recording at some time points.
claims.source: Figure 5B; Methods D, paragraph 1; Results D, paragraph 1
claims.criterion: For each of the 23 rats, the intracranial LFP of left S1 around the 200 tFUS trials of the target confirmation recording at the chosen coordinates (supplement), and around pseudo onsets in the resting baseline recording, normalized to the 20 ms before onset (Fig. 5B legend). Which channel or average of the 64 is not stated; readings for the channel (a) the mean over all 64 channels, (b) each channel. The normalization is read as subtracting the mean of the 20 ms before onset (a standard baseline correction; the legend says only "normalized"). The onsets of the sham are not stated; readings (a) every 2 s from the start of the resting recording, matching the inter-burst interval, (b) 200 onsets drawn at random with a fixed seed. The test is that of Methods F, which covers all comparisons "between groups and time points", a two-way ANOVA (group by time point) with Bonferroni-corrected post hoc tests of tFUS against sham at each time point, P < 0.05, under the M3 readings (a) ordinary, (b) repeated measures, the same 23 rats giving both groups. Reproduced when at least one time point after onset is significant under every combination of readings; not reproduced when none is; blocked as methods_underspecified if they disagree.

claims.statement: In wild-type rats, gamma band PLI decreases during and after tFUS relative to the pre-tFUS window in most brain regions, on average in both S1 and non-S1 regions, while it increases slightly in the sham.
claims.source: Results D, paragraph 1; Figure 5C-F and 5J
claims.quote: the PLI of the gamma band decreased during and after tFUS in most brain regions ... whereas the gamma PLI increased slightly in the sham group ... On average, the gamma PLI of the tFUS group decreased in both the S1 and non-S1 regions relative to the pre-tFUS window
claims.criterion: The 23 rats; EEG epochs around the 200 tFUS trials of the target confirmation recording at the chosen coordinates and around the sham onsets of fig5b-tfus-evoked-potentials (readings (a), (b) there). Gamma (30 to 80 Hz) PLI per channel pair (M6) in the windows -20 to 0, 0 to 20 and 20 to 200 ms; change from pre-tFUS under the M6 readings. Reproduced when, under one combination of readings, the mean change over S1 pairs and over non-S1 pairs is below zero in both the tFUS and post-tFUS windows for the tFUS epochs, more than half of all pairs decrease, and the sham mean change is above zero. The text claims no significance for these changes and the marks of Fig. 5J could not be read (no main PDF), so a two-way ANOVA (group by region) with Bonferroni post hoc tests (Fig. 5 legend) is reported and does not decide.

claims.statement: In wild-type rats, theta, alpha and beta PLI decrease only within the S1 regions during tFUS.
claims.source: Results D, paragraph 1; Figure 5G-I; Figure S6
claims.quote: The PLI in theta, alpha, and beta bands only decreased within the S1 regions during the tFUS conditions
claims.criterion: As fig5cdj-wild-type-gamma-pli-decrease, for theta (5 to 8 Hz), alpha (8 to 12 Hz) and beta (12 to 30 Hz). "During the tFUS conditions" is read as (a) the 0 to 20 ms window, (b) both the 0 to 20 and 20 to 200 ms windows. Reproduced when, under one combination of readings, the mean normalized PLI of the S1 pairs of the tFUS epochs is below the pre-tFUS reference in all three bands and the non-S1 mean is not below it in any of them. Partially reproduced when that holds for one or two bands. Significance marks of Fig. 5G-I could not be read (no main PDF); the two-way ANOVA (group by region) with Bonferroni post hoc tests is reported, not deciding.

claims.statement: In epileptic rats, the S1 PLI of the tFUS group decreases in theta, alpha, beta and gamma bands during stimulation, post 1 and post 2 relative to baseline seizures, while non-S1 PLI does not decrease; the decrease of S1 connectivity is significant.
claims.source: Results D, paragraph 2; Figure 6A-D
claims.quote: The S1 region of the tFUS group showed decreases in PLI within theta, alpha, beta, and gamma bands during stimulation, post 1, and post 2 compared to baseline. Comparatively, the non-S1 regions did not exhibit a reduction in PLI values due to stimulation
claims.criterion: PLI (M6) over the seizure periods (M1) of each block, per band, for S1 pairs and non-S1 pairs, normalized to the baseline block's seizures within each group (difference or ratio, M6). Reproduced when, under one combination of readings, the tFUS S1 mean is below its baseline in all four bands for the condition block, post 1 and post 2, the tFUS non-S1 mean is not below baseline in most of those 12 band and block cells, and a group by block two-way ANOVA per band and region with Bonferroni post hoc tests finds sham against tFUS significant for S1 in at least one band and block. Partially reproduced when the S1 decreases hold in some bands only, or without a significant group difference.

claims.statement: Comparing seizures (baseline block) with the pre-4-AP baseline state, the PLI change of S1 pairs differs significantly from that of non-S1 pairs in every band; the paper says PLI differences between wild-type and seizure rats may reflect distinct baseline network states.
claims.source: Figure S7B; Results D, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The PLI differences between wild-type and seizure rats may reflect distinct baseline network states
claims.criterion: PLI (M6) per band for S1 and non-S1 pairs, in the seizure periods (M1) of the baseline block and in the pre-4-AP baseline state (readings as in figs5-seizures-lower-ai), with the change as a difference or ratio (M6). Fig. S7B plots seizure S1 slightly above zero and seizure non-S1 below zero. Reproduced when, under one combination, a two-way ANOVA (region by band, or region by state) with Bonferroni post hoc tests finds seizure S1 against seizure non-S1 significant at P < 0.05 in all four bands with S1 higher; partially reproduced for one to three bands. The rats are not stated (readings as in figs5-seizures-lower-ai). The difference reading follows the Fig. S7A title, "Normalized Gamma PLI (seizure-baseline)". Fig. S7B also plots Baseline S1 and Baseline non-S1 bars, also near or below zero, whose quantity no text defines; they are not tested.

claims.statement: Wall-induced change in whisker midpoint angle does not differ significantly between awake and anesthetized mice for the C1, C2 and Greek whiskers (paired t-tests across 4 mice, Bonferroni alpha 0.017); the mean awake minus anesthetized difference is 2.28 degrees.
claims.source: Results, A wall-passing paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure S1F legend
claims.quote: Awake mice showed similar bending angle (mean difference: 2.28°) and curvature (mean difference: 1.66 × 10 −5 mm −1 ) changes, with no significant differences from the anesthetized condition across whiskers
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test (Methods, Data Analysis: Wall-Induced Whisker Retraction; FigS1_Stats.m). Per pass, the midpoint angle (Savitzky-Golay 21 frames, order 3, mean of the upper and lower envelopes) is averaged over 3 to 11 s minus its mean over -4.5 to 0 s; per mouse, whisker and condition, averaged over distances and passes; for each whisker a two-tailed paired t-test across the 4 mice, significant at 0.05/3. Reproduced when no whisker reaches p < 0.0167; not reproduced when any does. The mean difference is reported for each whisker; the paper does not say whether 2.28 degrees is pooled over whiskers or for one, so the readings are the mean over the three whiskers and each whisker alone. The code (FigS1_Code.m) takes the midpoint as a 101-frame Savitzky-Golay smoothing of the twice 21-frame-smoothed angle, with the envelope method commented out; this is the variant, shown, and the Methods' envelope midpoint is the main.

claims.statement: Wall-induced change in whisker curvature does not differ significantly between awake and anesthetized mice for any of the three whiskers.
claims.source: Results, A wall-passing paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure S1H-J legend
claims.quote: (H-J) Same as D-F, but for curvature. Significance reflects mouse-level paired comparisons (awake vs. anesthe- tized) with Bonferroni correction (α = 0.017): C1, p = 0.56 (n.s.); C2, p = 0.053 (n.s.), Greek: p = 0.43 (n.s.)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, as figs1f-angle-awake-vs-anesthetized, for curvature (signed planar curvature from a local second-order fit to a 4-mm arclength segment, minus its baseline mean over -4.5 to 0 s, averaged over 3 to 11 s; Methods). Reproduced when no whisker reaches p < 0.0167. The Methods do not say where along the whisker the 4-mm segment lies; this is open, and the author reports the segment used.

claims.statement: Under anesthesia the passing wall bends whiskers in the retraction direction, with larger angle changes and larger curvature changes at closer wall distances, so wall-induced bending grows roughly monotonically as the wall approaches.
claims.source: Results, A wall-passing paradigm, paragraph 2; Figure S1D, H
claims.quote: Under anesthesia, the moving wall pushed whiskers in the retraction direction, producing larger absolute bending angles ( Supplemental Figure S1D , right) and greater change in whisker curvature ( Supplemental Figure S1H , right) at closer wall distances
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test. Per distance, the across-mouse mean of the absolute change in midpoint angle and of the absolute change in curvature in the anesthetized condition (measures as in figs1f-angle-awake-vs-anesthetized). Reproduced when, for each of the two measures and each of the three whiskers, the value at 7 mm exceeds the value at 23 mm and the Spearman correlation between distance and value over the nine distances is negative. These two summaries are the readings of "larger ... at closer wall distances"; the outcome is the one both give. The cited panels (S1D and S1H, right) show one example C1 whisker in one mouse; the across-mouse curves per whisker are in S1F and S1J, which this criterion uses.

claims.statement: Of 46 tungsten-recorded PrV units from 14 mice, 41 (89.1%) were wall-activated, 3 (6.5%) wall-suppressed, and 43 (93.5%) wall-responsive in all, one unit being both.
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraphs 1-2
claims.quote: Of the 46 units, 41/46 (89.1%) were wall-activated and 3/46 (6.5%) were wall-suppressed; one unit showed both activation and suppression at different distances, yielding a total of 43/46 (93.5%) wall-responsive
claims.criterion: Classification as in the opening comment, applied to the tungsten sessions with their own distances (4 to 20 mm in 1-mm steps, so the binning into nine 2-mm bins does not apply; the code leaves the number of distances to each session). Responsiveness is judged with the Methods' uncorrected p < 0.05 per distance; the code's BH-FDR across distances is the variant, shown. Reproduced when all four counts are within tolerance under the Methods' test.

claims.statement: Of the 43 wall-responsive tungsten units, 39 (90.7%) were distance-tuned; 24 (55.8%) were broadly monotonic, firing more at closer distances, and 6 (14.0%) peaked at intermediate or far distances.
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 2; Figure S2D-F
claims.quote: Wall-responsive units with significant differences in mean firing rates for at least one distance pair were classified as "distance-tuned" (i.e., distance-selective; 90.7%, 39/43) ... The majority of wall-responsive units (55.8%, 24/43) showed a broadly monotonic, inversely proportional relationship with wall distance ... a distinct subset (14.0%, 6/43) showed peak responses at intermediate or far wall distances
claims.criterion: Distance tuning as in the opening comment (36 pairs become all pairs of the session's distances). The paper does not say how the 24 monotonic and 6 peaked units were defined for the tungsten data. Readings: (a) the silicon-probe rule, proximity (preferred at the closest distance) and map (preferred farther, with a significant BH-FDR one-tailed test against the closest distance), with activated or suppressed units both eligible as in the code's tungsten branch; (b) preferred distance at the closest distance against elsewhere, without the map test. Reproduced when all three counts are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Silicon probe recordings in wild-type mice yielded 1,141 single units from 36 mice passing isolation and firing criteria, out of 1,358 sorted units.
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 3; Methods, Isolation of Single Unit Activity
claims.quote: For silicon probe data, in wild-type mice, 1141 of 1358 units (36 mice), in TeLC experiments, 587 of 665 units (11 mice)
claims.criterion: Units with SNR of at least 5 and ISI false-alarm rate at most 2% (0.8 ms), not low-firing as defined in the opening comment, in wild-type full-array sessions (including the pre-cut part of whisker-cutting sessions). The number of mice is a count and must match exactly. If the deposit carries only curated units, the count of deposited units is compared and the difference reported.

claims.statement: Of the 1,141 units, 768 (67.3%) were wall-responsive; of these 532 (69.3%) were activated at one or more distances, 333 (43.4%) suppressed, and 97 both.
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Of the 1,141 units, 67.3% (768/1141) were significantly modulated by the passing-wall stimulus and classified as "wall-responsive". Among these wall-responsive units, 532/768 (69.3%) showed significant activation at one or more distances, 333/768 (43.4%) showed significant suppression, and 97 units met both criteria
claims.criterion: Classification as in the opening comment (Methods, uncorrected p < 0.05 per distance; variant, the code's BH-FDR across the nine distances, shown). Reproduced when all four counts are within tolerance under the Methods' test.

claims.statement: Over the full wall-contact period, 656 of 768 wall-responsive units (85.4%) were distance tuned; of these, 472 (72.0%) were activated at one or more distances (the activated population), 213 (32.5%) suppressed (the suppressed population), and 29 both.
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Across the full wall-contact period (8 s), we identified 656 out of the 768 (85.4%) wall-responsive units that were significantly tuned to wall distance. Within this distance-tuned population, 472/656 (72.0%) showed significant activation relative to baseline at one or more distances ... whereas 213/656 (32.5%) showed significant suppression at one or more distances ... A small subset of units (29/656; 4.4%) exhibited both
claims.criterion: Distance tuning as in the opening comment. Reproduced when all four counts are within tolerance under the Methods' responsiveness test (the code's BH-FDR variant shown). The 472 activated units are the population of Figures 2D-E, 5D, 6G-I and S4.

claims.statement: Among the 768 wall-responsive units, 266 (34.6%) were proximity units, 118 (15.4%) map units, 88 (11.5%) ambiguous, and 119 (15.5%) suppressed-only; the remainder (177, 23.0%) were untuned, giving a proximity to map ratio of 2.3 to 1.
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 7; Figure 2F; Figure 5E legend
claims.quote: We identified 266 proximity units (34.6%) and 118 map units (15.4%) out of the 768 wall-responsive units ( Figure 2F ) ... An additional 88 units (11.5%) were distance-selective but did not meet criteria for either map or proximity and were labeled "ambiguous" ... Suppressed-only units ... accounted for 119 out of 768 wall-responsive units (15.5%; Figure 2F )
claims.criterion: Categories as in the opening comment. The paper's counts are not consistent with each other (472 + 213 - 29 = 656 tuned implies 184 suppressed-only and 112 untuned; the five Figure 2F counts sum to 768 with 119 and 177). Readings for the last two: (a) the Figure 2F counts as printed; (b) the counts implied by fig2-distance-tuned-counts (184 and 112, same 10% tolerance; the Methods also count 112 silicon-probe units as wall-responsive but not distance-tuned, Characterizing Wall Distance Tuning). Reproduced when the proximity, map and ambiguous counts are within tolerance and the suppressed-only and untuned counts are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when only the proximity, map and ambiguous counts are.

claims.statement: Before wall movement, units of the activated population fire less than untuned units (5.46 against 6.93 sp/s).
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 4; Figure S4A
claims.quote: At baseline prior to wall movement onset, units in the activated population showed lower firing rates than untuned units (5.46 ± 0.670 vs. 6.93 ± 0.947 sp/s; two-tailed Kolmogorov-Smirnov (K-S) test: p = 2.47 × 10 − 7 )
claims.criterion: Per unit, the mean baseline rate (-4.5 to 0 s) over all passes; two-sample K-S test (two-tailed, kstest2) between the activated population and untuned units (Methods). The tolerances are the paper's printed spread (bootstrap CI half-width in the Methods, SEM in the legend). Reproduced when p < 0.05 with the activated mean lower and both means within tolerance; partially reproduced when the test holds but a mean is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: Units of the suppressed population have baseline firing comparable to untuned units (7.31 against 6.93 sp/s, not significant).
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 4; Figure S4A
claims.quote: whereas units in the suppressed population had baseline firing rates comparable to untuned units (7.31 ± 1.124 vs. 6.93 ± 0.947 sp/s; two-tailed K-S test: p = 0.63
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a two-tailed two-sample K-S test of per-unit mean baseline rates, suppressed population (213) against untuned units, at p < 0.05. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The difference of means is reported either way.

claims.statement: During wall passes the activated population fires more than at baseline (16.44 against 6.36 sp/s at the preferred distance) and the suppressed population fires less (4.47 against 6.19 sp/s).
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 5; Figure S4B
claims.quote: During wall-passing period, the activated population increased firing relative to baseline (16.44 ± 1.640 vs. 6.36 ± 0.704 sp/s; one-tailed K-S test: p = 9.26 × 10 −28 ; Supplemental Figure S4B , left), while the suppressed population exhibited a significant decrease in firing (4.47 ± 1.000 vs. 6.19 ± 1.076 sp/s; one-tailed K-S test: p = 3.06 × 10 −4
claims.criterion: Per unit, the mean wall rate (3 to 11 s) at the preferred distance (activated) or at the distance of minimum rate (suppressed; Figure S4B legend), against the unit's baseline rate; one-tailed two-sample K-S tests in the stated direction (Methods). The baseline paired with it is not specified, and the paper's 6.36 sp/s differs from the 5.46 sp/s of the same population's all-pass baseline (figs4a-baseline-activated-lower). Readings: (a) baseline of the passes at that same distance; (b) baseline over all passes. Reproduced when both tests give p < 0.05 in the stated direction and the four means are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when both tests hold but no reading puts the means within tolerance.

claims.statement: Untuned units do not change their firing between baseline and wall passes (6.93 against 6.32 sp/s).
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 5; Figure S4C
claims.quote: Untuned units showed no significant change between baseline and wall-passing periods (6.93 ± 0.947 vs. 6.32 ± 0.953 sp/s; two-tailed K-S test: p = 0.53
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a two-tailed two-sample K-S test between per-unit mean baseline rates and per-unit wall rates averaged across distances (Figure S4C legend) for untuned units, at p < 0.05. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The difference of means is reported either way.

claims.statement: In both the activated and the suppressed populations a large proportion of units prefer the closest wall position (7 mm), while others are best tuned to intermediate or far distances.
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 6; Figure 2D-E; Figure S4D, G
claims.quote: In both populations, while a large proportion of units preferred the closest wall position (7 mm), others were best tuned to intermediate or far distances ( Figure 2E , Supplemental Figure S4G ), revealing coexistence of proximity and map-like coding schemes in PrV
claims.criterion: Preferred distance is the maximum of the mean tuning curve (activated population, 472) and the minimum (trough, suppressed population, 213; Figure S4G legend and the code's pref_dist_sup). Reproduced when, in each population, 7 mm is the most frequent preferred distance and at least one unit prefers each of the eight distances from 9 to 23 mm. The paper reports no test; the most frequent bin and coverage of the range are the reading of "a large proportion ... others".

claims.statement: Preferred distances of the activated population are stable across two random halves of the wall passes, whereas the suppressed population is only partly reproducible, with only proximity-preferring responses stable.
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 6; Figure S4E-F
claims.quote: The resulting distance-tuning heatmaps of the activated population revealed little changes in the preferred distance between cross-validated partitions ( Supplemental Figure S4E ). In contrast, the suppressed population showed partial reproducibility, where only proximity-preferring responses were stable, while map-like profiles lacked consistent structure
claims.criterion: Per unit, passes at each distance are split at random into two halves (the code draws floor(reps/2) repetition indices without replacement, the same split for all distances of a unit); preferred distance (maximum for activated, minimum for suppressed units) is taken in each half. The paper gives no measure of stability. Readings: (a) the fraction of units whose preferred distance is the same in both halves; (b) the Spearman correlation of preferred distance across halves. Reproduced when, under both readings, the activated population is more stable than the suppressed population, and, within the suppressed population, units whose first-half trough is at 7 mm keep it more often than units with a trough at 9 mm or more. A fixed seed is a standard choice; the split is repeated 100 times and the median reported.

claims.statement: Wall-responsive units, and proximity and map units among them, lie preferentially in ventral PrV, toward the probe tip.
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraphs 3 and 7; Figure S4I-J
claims.quote: We identified 266 proximity units (34.6%) and 118 map units (15.4%) out of the 768 wall-responsive units ( Figure 2F ), which were preferentially located in ventral PrV ( Supplemental Figure S4J )
claims.criterion: Depth is the shank coordinate of the unit's peak channel (largest peak-to-trough amplitude of the mean waveform) from the probe tip, Poly2 probes only, in 100-um bins (Methods, Unit Depth Along Silicon Probe; FigS4I_probemap.m), n = 1050 well-isolated and 703 wall-responsive units (Figure S4I-J legends). The paper reports no test. Readings: (a) the median depth of wall-responsive units is smaller than that of unresponsive units, and the median depth of proximity and of map units is smaller than that of unresponsive units; (b) the fraction of units that are responsive is higher in the 0 to 400 um half of the shank than in the 400 to 800 um half, and so is the fraction that are proximity or map units. Reproduced when both readings agree.

claims.statement: Applied to temporal windows, the classification finds map units most often in the sustained period (122 of 768, 15.9%), less in the onset period (83, 10.8%) and fewest in the offset period (34, 4.4%).
claims.source: Results, PrV contains both proximity and map codes, paragraph 8; Figure S4L
claims.quote: Map units were most prevalent during the sustained period among wall-responsive units (15.9%, 122/768), but were also present during the onset epoch (10.8%, 83/768). In contrast, offset responses yielded fewer map units (4.4%, 34/768)
claims.criterion: The classification of the opening comment with the wall rate taken in the onset (2.5 to 4.5 s), sustained (4.5 to 9.5 s) or offset (9.5 to 11.5 s) window. The paper does not say whether the 768 wall-responsive units are reclassified for responsiveness in each window or kept from the full-period classification. Readings: (a) responsiveness kept from the full period, tuning and map tests rerun in each window; (b) all tests rerun in each window. Reproduced when the three counts are within tolerance, and ordered sustained > onset > offset, under one reading; partially reproduced when the order holds but a count is out of tolerance.

claims.statement: Population decoders trained on map, proximity, suppressed-only and combined map plus proximity units decode wall distance during the contact period better than shuffled and untuned controls.
claims.source: Results, The map code in PrV allows more accurate readout, paragraph 1; Figure 3A
claims.quote: As expected, decoding accuracy during the wall-contact period was higher in the map, proximity, suppressed-only, and combined "map + proximity" groups compared to shuffled and untuned controls ( Figure 3A )
claims.criterion: Decoding as in the opening comment. Reproduced when the overall accuracy (mean over the nine distances, 3 to 11 s) of each of the four groups exceeds that of both the shuffled and the untuned groups, and a two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test (MATLAB ranksum default, as in the code; the Table S2 value 1.83e-4 is the two-sided normal-approximation p for complete separation of 10 against 10) on the 10 subsample values has p < 0.05 for each such pair, under the Methods' 10-fold cross-validation and under the code's 15 splits.

claims.statement: Averaged across the nine distances, the map group decodes best (71.5%), ahead of the combined map plus proximity group (58.6%) and the proximity group (48.9%); the suppressed-only group reaches 32.6% and untuned units 15.7%, against a chance level of 11.1%.
claims.source: Results, The map code in PrV allows more accurate readout, paragraph 1; Table S2
claims.quote: the map group achieved the highest overall decoding accuracy averaged across all nine distances (71.5%), outperforming the proximity (48.9%) and combined "map + proximity" (58.6%) groups. The suppressed-only group had an average overall decoding accuracy of 32.6%. Untuned units performed slightly above chance (15.7%)
claims.criterion: Decoding as in the opening comment; values from the Table S2 "Average" row. The text says "During the sustained wall-passing period" while the Methods, the code (summary_period 3000 to 11000 ms) and the Table give the 3 to 11 s contact period. Readings: window (i) 3 to 11 s (main), (ii) 4.5 to 9.5 s; cross-validation (x) 10-fold (Methods), (y) 15 splits (code). Reproduced when the order map > combined > proximity > suppressed-only > untuned > shuffled holds and all six values are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when the order holds with the map group first but values are out of tolerance.

claims.statement: At the two closest distances (7 and 9 mm) the combined map plus proximity and proximity groups decode most accurately, whereas the map group is most accurate at 11 to 23 mm.
claims.source: Results, The map code in PrV allows more accurate readout, paragraph 2; Figure 3B-C; Table S2
claims.quote: At the closest distances (7 and 9 mm), the combined "map + proximity" and proximity populations achieved the highest accuracy. In contrast, the map population was most accurate at decoding more distal wall positions (11–23 mm)
