claims.criterion: Per-distance accuracy as in the opening comment, with the readings of fig3-overall-decoding-accuracy. Tolerances are 10% of the Table S2 values; the Table's 95% CIs over 10 subsamples (0.1 to 3 points) are left aside because a rerun draws new subsamples. Reproduced when, under one reading, (a) at 7 and at 9 mm the combined and proximity groups both exceed the map group, (b) at each of 11 to 23 mm the map group exceeds every other group, with the per-distance rank-sum tests (BH-FDR over nine distances) of map against proximity and map against combined giving q < 0.05 at 11 to 23 mm, and (c) the five values are within tolerance. Partially reproduced when (a) and (b) hold at all but one distance.

claims.statement: Decoding error grows with distance; proximity, map and combined groups reach submillimetre error at 7 and 9 mm, and only the map group is submillimetre at 13 and 15 mm.
claims.source: Results, The map code in PrV allows more accurate readout, paragraph 2; Figure 3C right; Table S3
claims.quote: While classification error generally increased with distance, proximity, map, and the combined "map + proximity" groups showed submillimeter precision when decoding the two closest distances (7 and 9 mm; Figure 3C , right; Table S3 ). Only the map population achieved submillimeter error at the intermediate distances of 13 and 15 mm
claims.criterion: Error per true distance is the confusion-matrix-weighted mean of the absolute difference between predicted and true distance, averaged over time bins in the contact period (Methods; code err_by_distance). Readings as in fig3-overall-decoding-accuracy. Reproduced when, under one reading, proximity, map and combined errors are below 1 mm at 7 and 9 mm, the map error is below 1 mm at 13 and 15 mm while proximity and combined errors are not, and the four values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Single-neuron decoders show the same pattern with lower accuracy than population decoders, proximity units being more accurate than map units at 7 mm and map units more accurate at 11 to 17 mm.
claims.source: Results, The map code in PrV allows more accurate readout, paragraph 2; Figure S5B-C; Table S4
claims.quote: These results are consistent with the performance of single-neuron decoders, although their overall decoding accuracy is lower than that of population decoders
claims.criterion: Per unit, spike counts in 200-ms bins over 3 to 11 s; a template (mean over training passes) per distance; nearest template in Euclidean distance; leave-two-out cross-validation (two passes per distance held out, exhaustively); accuracy the fraction of correct test passes (Methods). Tolerances are the Table S4 95% CIs across units. Per-distance proximity against map with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests, BH-FDR over nine distances. Reproduced when proximity exceeds map at 7 mm and map exceeds proximity at 11, 13, 15 and 17 mm, each with q < 0.05, every single-neuron group's mean accuracy is below the corresponding population value of fig3-overall-decoding-accuracy, and the four values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the directions hold but some tests or values do not.

claims.statement: The ranking of subpopulations is robust to the decoder; with a linear SVM the map group still has the highest average accuracy (72.1%) and proximity and combined groups are best at the closest distance.
claims.source: Results, The map code in PrV allows more accurate readout, paragraph 2; Figure S5D-E; Tables S2-S3
claims.quote: Importantly, these findings were robust to the choice of decoder (see STAR Methods , Supplemental Figure S5D , E , and Tables S2 , S3 for SVM classifier)
claims.criterion: As fig3-overall-decoding-accuracy and fig3c-decoding-by-distance with the Neural Decoding Toolbox libsvm_CL, linear kernel, C = 1, one-versus-one (Methods). Reproduced when, under one reading, the map group has the highest overall accuracy, the proximity and combined groups both exceed the map group at 7 mm, the map group is highest at 13 to 23 mm, and the four values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Cutting all whiskers but one does not change baseline firing across the recorded population (7.09 against 7.10 sp/s; 195 units from 18 mice).
claims.source: Results, PrV map tuning can persist, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Across the recorded population (n = 195 units from 18 mice), acute whisker cutting did not significantly alter baseline firing rates, measured before wall-movement onset for each wall pass (full array: 7.09 ± 1.034 vs. single whisker: 7.10 ± 1.038 sp/s; Wilcoxon signed-rank test: p = 0.70)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of per-unit mean baseline rates (-4.5 to 0 s; the code averages the per-distance means) between full-array and single-whisker conditions, at p < 0.05 (Methods; Fig4BC_WhiskerCutting_pairwise_FR_PrefDist.m, signrank on fr_base). Units are those passing the unit criteria with stable waveforms in both conditions (Methods). Reproduced when p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The difference of means is reported either way.

claims.statement: In the 86 wall-activated, distance-tuned units, firing during wall passes falls after cutting to a single whisker (11.58 against 8.18 sp/s), in many cases to below 1 sp/s.
claims.source: Results, PrV map tuning can persist, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
claims.quote: firing rates of wall-activated, distance-tuned units (activated population; n = 86) during wall-passing periods were significantly reduced following cutting down to a single whisker (full array: 11.58 ± 1.338 vs. single whisker: 8.18 ± 2.602 sp/s, p = 4.43 × 10 −8 ; Figure 4B )
claims.criterion: Units activated and distance-tuned in the full-array condition (classification of the opening comment). The per-unit wall rate in the code is the median over distances of the per-distance mean rate (fr_wall = median of fr_mean); the Methods say mean firing rate during wall passes. Readings: (a) median over distances (code); (b) mean over all passes (Methods). Two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test. The full-array spread is printed as 1.338 in the text and 2.986 in the Figure 4B legend; the larger is used as the tolerance. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with lower single-whisker rates and the three values within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when the test holds but a value does not.

claims.statement: Of the 86 activated units, 66 change firing significantly after cutting, 52 decreasing and 14 increasing.
claims.source: Results, PrV map tuning can persist, paragraph 2; Figure 4B
claims.quote: Among the 86 activated units, 66 showed significant changes in firing rates during wall-passing periods between cutting conditions (two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.05). Of these 66 units, 52 exhibited a significant decrease in firing rates ... whereas 14 units displayed increased firing rates
claims.criterion: Per unit, two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test of per-pass wall rates (3 to 11 s) between conditions, passes paired in order and truncated to the shorter condition (code), direction from the sign of the median difference (code). The paper gives three corrections. Readings: (a) uncorrected p < 0.05 (Results); (b) BH-FDR across the 86 units (Methods, Data Analysis: Acute Whisker-Cutting Manipulation; code mafdr); (c) Bonferroni across units (Methods, Characterizing Wall Distance Tuning; code alpha / (2n)). The code also differs on the pass set: (i) all passes pooled over distances; (ii) the code's exact-test block over repetitions. Reproduced when the three counts are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Of 21 map units in the full-array condition, 10 remain distance-tuned after cutting to a single whisker; of these, 2 shift their preferred distance to the closest distance (becoming proximity units), 6 shift their preferred distance while keeping map tuning, and 2 keep their preferred distance with a change in gain.
claims.source: Results, PrV map tuning can persist, paragraph 3; Figure 4C-I
claims.quote: Of the 21 units categorized as map cells in the full-array condition, 10 remained significantly tuned to wall distance after cutting down to a single whisker ... Two units shifted their preferred distance to the closest distance ( Figure 4D , E ), effectively converting from map cells to proximity cells. In contrast, six units shifted their preferred distance while retaining map tuning (e.g., Figure 4F , G ), and two additional units preserved their preferred distance but changed in response gain
claims.criterion: Classification of the opening comment run separately on full-array and single-whisker passes. "Remained tuned" is read as in the code, activated and distance-tuned in the single-whisker condition and not silenced (activated_tuned_mask); the variant drops the activation requirement. Map after cutting means the map category in the single-whisker condition (with the map test); a variant counts any preferred distance above 7 mm. Reproduced when all six counts are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when the first two are and the split of the 10 is off by at most one unit per class. Gain change is reported, not judged, as the paper gives no measure.

claims.statement: Of 45 proximity units in the full-array condition only 15 remain distance-selective after cutting; 9 stay proximity units with lower gain, 4 stay proximity units with higher gain, and 2 become map units.
claims.source: Results, PrV map tuning can persist, paragraph 4; Figure 4J-K
claims.quote: Of the 45 units categorized as proximity cells before whisker cutting, only 15 remained distance-selective after cutting down to a single whisker. Of these 15 units, nine remained proximity cells with reduced response gain ... four remained proximity cells with increased response gain ... and two shifted to exhibit map tuning
claims.criterion: As fig4c-map-units-after-cut. Gain is not defined in the paper. Readings for lower or higher gain: (a) the unit's peak mean wall rate in the single-whisker condition below or above that in the full-array condition; (b) its mean wall rate over distances below or above. Reproduced when all five counts are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Whisker cutting lowers population decoding accuracy in both map (31.0 to 21.5%) and proximity (24.1 to 20.2%) populations of 21 units, with the largest decreases at intermediate and far distances in the map population and less effect at the closest distances.
claims.source: Results, PrV map tuning can persist, paragraph 5; Figure S5F-G
claims.quote: Whisker cutting reduced overall decoding accuracy in both populations (map: 31.0 ± 0.10% vs. 21.5 ± 0.08%; proximity: 24.1 ± 0.82% vs. 20.2 ± 1.22%; mean ± 95% CI for full-array vs. single-whisker conditions), with the largest decreases occurring at intermediate and far distances in the map population
claims.criterion: MCC decoders as in the opening comment, trained and tested within each condition on units recorded in both, grouped by full-array category; map n = 21, proximity 21 of 45 drawn 10 times (Methods). Tolerances are 10%: the printed CIs (0.08 to 1.2 points) describe the spread over subsamples, not a rerun's error. Readings for cross-validation as in fig3-overall-decoding-accuracy. Reproduced when, under one reading, accuracy falls in both populations, the map population's largest per-distance drop is at 11 mm or farther and its mean drop per distance over 11 to 23 mm exceeds its mean drop over 7 and 9 mm, and the four values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the falls and the distance pattern hold but values do not.

claims.statement: Optogenetic silencing of local PrV inhibitory neurons (GtACR in vGat-Cre mice) strongly inhibits 18 of 112 units (putative inhibitory neurons); among 71 distance-tuned units, 17 are inhibited and 16 disinhibited by light, and disinhibited units keep their preferred distance, so local inhibition affects gain without changing distance preference.
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraph 2; Figure S6B-G
claims.quote: Among the 112 well-isolated units, 18 were putative inhibitory neurons expressing GtACR, as they were strongly inhibited during the "Laser ON" period (modulation index ≤ −0.5 ... Of distance-tuned units (71/112), 17 were opto-inhibited ... Sixteen units showed a reduction in inhibition under the "Laser ON" condition (modulation index > 0 ... Nonetheless, these opto-disinhibited neurons, regardless of whether they were proximity or map cells, retained their preferred distance
claims.criterion: MI = (FR on - FR off) / (FR on + FR off) of mean wall-period rates; a unit is modulated when its bootstrap CI on MI excludes zero; strongly inhibited MI <= -0.5, inhibited -0.5 < MI < 0, disinhibited MI > 0 (Methods). The paper does not give the CI level or what is resampled; readings, 95% percentile CI from 10,000 resamples (the paper's bootstrap elsewhere) of (a) passes within each laser condition, (b) passes within each condition and distance. Tuning is classified at the five distances (7 to 23 mm in 4-mm steps); the paper does not say on which passes, so the readings are (i) laser-off passes and (ii) all passes. Reproduced when the five counts are within tolerance under one reading and the disinhibited tuned units keep their preferred distance with laser on as off; the paper says they retained it but gives no number, so the readings are all of them and more than half of them, and the share is reported. The 17 inhibited units are counted among tuned units with MI below 0 (strongly or not); whether the 18 strongly inhibited are inside the 17 is not said, so both counts are compared as printed.

claims.statement: Chronic TeLC expression in SpVi does not change whisker kinematics during wall passes (whisker-array midpoint angle; mean difference 0.84 degrees, Wald t = 1.02, p = 0.31).
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraph 4; Figure S6I
claims.quote: Chronic TeLC expression in SpVi did not significantly alter whisker kinematics during wall passes, as measured by whisker array midpoint angle (mean difference across distance = 0.84°; two-tailed Wald's t -test: t = 1.02, p = 0.31
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test (Methods, Whisker Kinematics, Wild-Type vs SpVi-TeLC). Per pass, the change in midpoint angle averaged across tracked whiskers per frame; fitlme by maximum likelihood, theta_mid ~ TeLC + distance + (1|subject) + (1|session), two-sided Wald test of TeLC at p < 0.05. Reproduced when p >= 0.05, and no per-distance model theta_mid ~ TeLC + (1|subject) + (1|session) gives p < 0.05 (Figure S6I legend); not reproduced otherwise. The effect size is reported either way. The legend's group means carry its printed spread as tolerance.

claims.statement: In SpVi-TeLC mice, 587 of 665 sorted PrV units from 11 mice passed the unit criteria, of which 395 were wall-responsive and 252 wall-activated and distance-tuned.
claims.source: Methods, Isolation of Single Unit Activity; Figure 5C, E legends
claims.quote: in TeLC experiments, 587 of 665 units (11 mice)
claims.criterion: Unit criteria and classification as in the opening comment (the same code, Fig5CE_TeLC_heatmap_stacked_bar.m). Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance under the Methods' responsiveness test (the code's BH-FDR variant shown).

claims.statement: Wall-activated, distance-tuned units in SpVi-TeLC mice prefer closer distances than those in wild-type mice.
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraph 4; Figure 5C-D
claims.quote: Comparison of normalized tuning curves of all wall-activated, distance-tuned units revealed a reduction in the proportion of map units in SpVi-TeLC mice ( Figure 5C ) relative to wild-type mice ( Figure 2D ), shifting the population to prefer closer distances ( Figure 5D )
claims.criterion: Preferred distance (maximum of the mean tuning curve, binned to the nine centres) of activated, distance-tuned units; one-tailed two-sample K-S test that TeLC preferred distances are smaller (Fig5D_TeLC_Pref_Dist_CDF.m, kstest2 with Tail smaller, wild type first). Population readings: (a) activated and distance-tuned (Figure 5D legend, "same units in C"); (b) activated without the tuning requirement (the code's mask1 and mask2). Reproduced when p < 0.05 under reading (a); the result under (b) is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Among wall-responsive units, SpVi-TeLC mice have nearly threefold fewer map units than wild-type mice (5.8 against 15.4%), more proximity units (47.9 against 34.6%) and modestly fewer suppressed-only units (10.9 against 15.5%).
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraph 4; Figure 5E
claims.quote: In particular, the proportion of map units was nearly threefold lower in SpVi-TeLC mice than in wild-type mice (5.8% vs 15.4%; Z -statistic: 4.721, p = 1.2×10 −6 ), whereas the proportion of proximity units increased (47.9% vs 34.6%; Z -statistic: −4.33, p = 7.5×10 −6 ) ... The proportion of suppressed units decreased modestly (10.9% vs 15.5%; Z -statistic: 2.15, p = 0.02)
claims.criterion: Shares of the five categories among wall-responsive units in each group; pooled two-proportion Z = (p_WT - p_TeLC) / SE, one-tailed in the paper's direction (map and suppressed-only lower, proximity higher in TeLC; Methods; Fig5CE code). The Methods' denominator is "the total number of recorded units" while the legend and the code use wall-responsive units; readings (a) wall-responsive units (768 and 395, main), (b) all units passing criteria (1141 and 587). Reproduced when the three tests give p < 0.05 in the stated directions and the three TeLC shares are within tolerance under reading (a); partially reproduced when the map and proximity tests hold but the suppressed-only test or a share does not.

claims.statement: The shares of untuned (25.3 against 23.0%) and ambiguous (10.1 against 11.5%) units do not differ between SpVi-TeLC and wild-type mice.
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraph 4; Figure 5E legend
claims.quote: whereas the proportions of untuned (25.3% vs 23.0%; Z -statistic: −0.86, p = 0.39) and ambiguous units (10.1% vs 11.5%; Z -statistic: 0.62, p = 0.53) remained unchanged
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, two-tailed pooled two-proportion Z-tests (Figure 5E legend; code) on shares of wall-responsive units, at p < 0.05. Reproduced when neither test gives p < 0.05; not reproduced when either does. The difference in share is reported for each.

claims.statement: Untuned units in SpVi-TeLC mice fire more than in wild-type mice at baseline (10.01 against 6.93 sp/s) and during wall passes (9.64 against 6.32 sp/s).
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraph 5; Figure S6J
claims.quote: During both baseline and wall-passing periods, untuned units in SpVi-TeLC mice exhibited significantly higher firing rates than those in the wild-type population, consistent with loss of long-range inhibitory inputs from SpVi (baseline: 10.01 ± 2.431 vs 6.93 ± 0.947 sp/s, p = 3.98 × 10 −5 ; wall passes: 9.64 ± 2.772 vs. 6.32 ± 0.953 sp/s, p =9.64 × 10 −4 ; one-tailed K-S tests
claims.criterion: Per-unit mean baseline rate and wall rate averaged across distances; one-tailed two-sample K-S tests (TeLC higher), significant at 0.0125 (Figure S6K legend, four comparisons). The baseline p-value is printed as 3.98 x 10^-5 in the text and 3.98 x 10^-3 in the legend; both are below 0.0125. Untuned population readings: (a) wall-responsive but not distance-tuned (177 wild type, the population whose 6.93 and 6.32 sp/s match Figure S4); (b) the Table S5 "untuned" sets (550 wild type, 294 TeLC), every unit outside the activated-tuned and suppressed-only groups. Reproduced when both tests give p < 0.0125 and both TeLC means are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Wall-activated, distance-tuned units in SpVi-TeLC mice have baseline firing comparable to wild type (5.60 against 5.46 sp/s).
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraph 5; Figure S6K left
claims.quote: In contrast, distance-tuned units in SpVi-TeLC mice showed baseline activity comparable to that of wild-type mice in the absence of wall contact (5.60 ± 0.845 vs. 5.46 ± 0.670 sp/s; one-tailed K-S test: p = 0.14)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a one-tailed two-sample K-S test (TeLC higher) of per-unit mean baseline rates of activated, distance-tuned units, at the legend's Bonferroni level 0.0125. Reproduced when p >= 0.0125; not reproduced when p < 0.0125. The result at 0.05 and the difference of means are reported as well.

claims.statement: During wall contact, wall-activated, distance-tuned units in SpVi-TeLC mice fire more than in wild type (9.96 against 9.02 sp/s, averaged across distances).
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraph 5; Figure S6K right
claims.quote: but exhibited significantly greater wall-evoked firing (9.96 ± 1.209 vs. 9.02 ± 1.005 sp/s; one-tailed K-S test: p = 9.34 × 10 −3
claims.criterion: Per-unit wall rate (3 to 11 s) averaged across the nine distances; one-tailed two-sample K-S test (TeLC higher). Reproduced when p < 0.0125 and both means are within tolerance; partially reproduced when 0.0125 <= p < 0.05 or the test holds with a mean out of tolerance.

claims.statement: The TeLC increase in firing of activated, distance-tuned units is distance dependent, largest at 7 mm (4.74 sp/s) and significant only at 7 and 9 mm, whereas untuned units show a roughly uniform increase of about 2 sp/s, significant at every distance.
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraph 5; Figure S6L; Table S5
claims.quote: This enhancement was distance dependent, with the largest increase at the closest wall distance ( Supplemental Figure S6L , bottom; Table S5 ). Thus, SpVi inhibition appears to be strongest at close distances for distance-tuned units
claims.criterion: Per distance, per-unit mean wall rate; TeLC minus wild-type difference of means with a bootstrap 95% CI, and a two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum test at the Bonferroni level 0.00556 (Table S5; Figure S6L legend). Tolerances are the larger half of each Table S5 CI around its mean. Populations as Table S5 (tuned 472 and 252; untuned 550 and 294). Reproduced when, for tuned units, the largest difference is at 7 mm, the tests are significant at 7 and 9 mm and at no distance from 11 to 23 mm, and, for untuned units, every distance is significant, with the four values within tolerance; partially reproduced when the tuned-unit difference is largest at 7 mm and significant there but the pattern elsewhere differs.

claims.statement: A feedforward model in which PrV neurons sum sparse sigmoidal TG excitation and SpVi-relayed inhibition yields both proximity-like and map-like tuning across 1,225 model neurons; halving long-range inhibition loses map units and expands proximity units.
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraphs 6-7; Figure 6C-F
claims.quote: When long-range inhibitory input to each PrV neuron was reduced by 50% to simulate TeLC-mediated silencing of SpVi inhibition, the model showed a loss of map units and a corresponding expansion of proximity units ( Figure 6D – F , right)
claims.criterion: A simulation, not a test on recorded data. Run PrV_simulation/simulate_prv.py at the commit with its defaults (M1 = 20, seed 42, p_untuned 0.4, long_inh_gain 10, local_inh_gain 1.7), without and with --telc (telc_inh_scale 0.5); classification as in the Methods (untuned when max - min < 0.1 over nine bins, suppressed when max below zero, proximity when the peak is at bin 0, map when it is later). Reproduced when the map share of distance-tuned model neurons falls and the proximity share rises with --telc, and the two tuned counts are within tolerance. The Methods' equations and the code's defaults are both recorded; where they differ (the code adds local excitation and inhibition terms the Methods do not write), the code is run, as only it gives the figure's numbers.

claims.statement: Compared with wild type, activated, distance-tuned units in SpVi-TeLC mice show little change in tuning width, a modest increase in tuning amplitude and a pronounced shift of monotonicity toward proximity-like (near-preferring) tuning, a pattern the model with reduced inhibition reproduces.
claims.source: Results, Inhibition contributes to the PrV map code, paragraph 7; Figure 6G-I
claims.quote: This simulated manipulation also recapitulated the experimental population-level changes in tuning curve shape ( Figure 6G – I ; see STAR Methods ): tuning width changed relatively little, tuning amplitude showed a modest rightward shift, and monotonicity exhibited a pronounced leftward shift toward more proximity-like responses
claims.criterion: Experimental part, on 472 wild-type and 252 SpVi-TeLC activated, distance-tuned units (Methods, Distance Tuning Curve Shape; Fig6GHI_left_TC_shape_analysis.m). Width is the full width at half maximum above the 4.5-s baseline, in mm, by linear interpolation, truncated at the sampled edges, undefined units dropped; amplitude is peak minus baseline in sp/s; monotonicity is (far-edge minus near-edge response) / peak after subtracting the curve's minimum. The paper reports no test. Readings for "shift": (a) difference of medians; (b) difference of means. Reproduced when, under both readings, TeLC monotonicity is lower than wild type and TeLC amplitude is higher, and the width shift, expressed as a fraction of the pooled interquartile range, is smaller than the monotonicity shift so expressed. The model part (Fig6GHI_right_model_TC_shape_analysis.m, simulation outputs) is reported, not judged.

claims.statement: Across 174 sites in 5 mice, the dominant DA-ACh cross-correlation (the largest magnitude Pearson r within 1 s lags) during spontaneous behavior is negative at 132 sites, 127 of them with DA leading, and positive at 42 sites, 31 of them with ACh leading.
claims.source: Results, Spatially organized coupling of transient DA-ACh dynamics during behavior, paragraph 1; Figure 1e
claims.quote: The polarity of the strongest correlation varied significantly across striatal sites, with some exhibiting dominant positive correlations (42/174 sites, 31 with ACh leading) and others dominant negative (132/174 sites, 127 with DA leading)
claims.criterion: Spontaneous sessions of UG27 to UG31 (those without reward events). Per session and site, Pearson r of DA at t with ACh at t plus k samples for k from -18 to 18, NaN samples dropped; r averaged over sessions per site, as the code does; the dominant r is the extreme with the larger magnitude. DA leads when k > 0 and ACh when k < 0. Reproduced when all four counts are within tolerance; partially reproduced when negative sites outnumber positive ones, most negative sites have DA leading and most positive ones ACh leading, but a count is outside tolerance; not reproduced otherwise. Correlation over concatenated sessions is a variant.

claims.statement: The dominant correlations form a significant hotspot, identified by local Moran's I, in the anterior dorsolateral striatum (aDLS), where the strongest correlations are negative.
claims.source: Results, Spatially organized coupling of transient DA-ACh dynamics during behavior, paragraph 1; Figure 1f
claims.quote: This analysis identified a significant 'hotspot' in the aDLS where the dominant correlations were highest, and the polarity of the strongest correlations were negative
claims.criterion: The hotspot procedure of the opening comment on the 174 dominant r values. Reproduced when a hotspot is found, its mean smoothed value is negative, and its centroid is anterior dorsolateral as defined above; partially reproduced when a negative hotspot is found elsewhere; not reproduced when no hotspot is found or its mean is positive.

claims.statement: Sites inside the aDLS hotspot have more negative dominant correlations than sites outside (Wilcoxon rank-sum p = 1.67e-16).
claims.source: Figure 1h
claims.quote: Sites inside the hotspot show significantly stronger negative correlations
claims.criterion: Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test of the dominant r of sites inside against outside the hotspot of fig1f-adls-hotspot. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with the median inside lower; not reproduced otherwise. The p value is reported against the paper's; the test is partly circular, as the hotspot is drawn from the same values.

claims.statement: Dominant positive correlations lie in the posterior striatum.
claims.source: Results, Spatially organized coupling of transient DA-ACh dynamics during behavior, paragraph 1; Figure 1f
claims.quote: These maps revealed a clear topography, with dominant negative correlations concentrated in the anterior dorsolateral striatum (aDLS) and dominant positive correlations in the posterior striatum
claims.criterion: One-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test that the AP coordinate of sites with a positive dominant r is lower (more posterior) than that of sites with a negative dominant r. Reproduced when p < 0.05; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: The hotspot is consistent across mice; in each mouse, sites inside the group hotspot have more negative dominant correlations than sites outside.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 2d; Results, Spatially organized coupling of transient DA-ACh dynamics during behavior, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The presence and anatomical localization of this hotspot was remarkably consistent across mice (Extended Data Fig. 2).
claims.criterion: Per mouse, two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test of dominant r inside against outside the group hotspot, for mice with at least two sites on each side. Reproduced when at least 4 of 5 mice have the median inside lower with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when at least 4 have the median inside lower but fewer than 4 reach p < 0.05; not reproduced otherwise. The per-mouse hotspots of Extended Data Figure 2b and 2c are not computed.

claims.statement: Mice expressing non-functional sensors (a mutant ACh sensor and tdTomato, n = 3) show only sparse, weak positive red-green correlations with no anatomical organization; no hotspot is found.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 1i-k; Results, Spatially organized coupling of transient DA-ACh dynamics during behavior, paragraph 1
claims.quote: showing sparse weak positive correlations with no anatomical organisation. ... No significant hotspot was identified for these mice.
claims.criterion: AD4 to AD6, identified by their indicators in the files. Their 15 sessions with rewards and no cues, with the 6 s after each reward delivery and first lick left out, as the paper uses ITI data only; DfOverFexpHp series; dominant r as in fig1e-dominant-polarity. A claim of absence, judged by the paper's test, the hotspot procedure. Reproduced when no hotspot is found; not reproduced when one is. The median dominant r, the fraction positive and the median magnitude against the sensor mice are reported either way.

claims.statement: For coincident transients of opposite polarity (ACh trough with DA peak, ACh peak with DA trough) the DA transient leads; for same-polarity pairs (peak with peak, trough with trough) the ACh transient leads.
claims.source: Figure 2a; Results, Spatially organized coupling of transient DA-ACh dynamics during behavior, paragraph 2
claims.quote: opposite signed pairs (cases 1 and 2) had timings indicating DA leading, while timings of same sign pairs (cases 3 and 4) indicated ACh leading (Fig. 2a).
claims.criterion: Transients per the Methods (at least 3 consecutive samples above the 97.5th or below the 2.5th percentile of a null of the mean of 3 randomly drawn samples, 10000 draws per site and session), on all sessions of UG27 to UG31, leaving out transients that start within 6 s after a reward delivery or first lick, as the code does. A pair is a transient whose onset and peak both fall within 1 s (18 samples) after those of a transient of the other signal in the same session, matched as in the code. Directionality index (A - B)/(A + B), A the ACh-first pairs. Reproduced when the median index over sites is negative for both opposite-polarity types and positive for both same-polarity types, each with a one-sample Wilcoxon p < 0.05; partially reproduced for three of the four; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Magnitudes of paired transients are negatively correlated at many sites for opposite-sign pairs (121 of 174 for ACh troughs with DA peaks, 81 of 174 for ACh peaks with DA troughs) and positively for same-sign pairs (97 of 174 peak-peak, 78 of 174 trough-trough), with no site significant in the other direction.
claims.source: Results, Spatially organized coupling of transient DA-ACh dynamics during behavior, paragraph 3; Figure 2d
claims.quote: For opposite sign event pairs, a majority of sites had significant negative magnitude correlations ... 121/174 sites significant for ACh troughs vs DA peaks; 81/174 sites for ACh peaks vs DA troughs ... for same sign pairs, a majority had positive correlations (97/174 significant for peak-peak correlations, 78/174 for trough-trough
claims.criterion: As the Methods describe, per site and pair type, Pearson r of the signed magnitudes of 100 randomly drawn pairs (pairs in either order), repeated 1000 times (the paper 10000); the site's value is the mean r, and it is significant when 0 lies outside the 2.5th to 97.5th percentiles; sites with fewer than 100 pairs count as not significant. Reproduced when the four counts are within tolerance and no site is significant in the opposite direction; partially reproduced when for each type significant sites of the stated sign outnumber those of the other sign but a count is outside tolerance; not reproduced otherwise. The code's computation (Pearson r over all pairs, p < 0.05) is a variant.

claims.statement: Magnitude correlations of opposite-sign pairs, but not same-sign pairs, are stronger inside the aDLS hotspot than outside (rank-sum p < 0.05 for opposite-sign pairs, p > 0.05 for same-sign pairs).
claims.source: Figure 2d; Results, Spatially organized coupling of transient DA-ACh dynamics during behavior, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Magnitude correlations for opposite sign transient pairs, but not same sign pairs, were significantly stronger for sites inside the aDLS global correlation hotspot region (Fig. 1f) than outside
claims.criterion: Two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test of the per-site mean r of fig2-magnitude-correlations (sites with at least 100 pairs), inside against outside the hotspot. Reproduced when both opposite-sign types are more negative inside with p < 0.05 and neither same-sign type differs with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when one opposite-sign type holds, or both hold and a same-sign type differs; not reproduced when no opposite-sign type holds.

claims.statement: The frequency of paired transients is highest in aDLS, in a region overlapping the correlation hotspot, for all four pair types (volume overlap test, p < 0.01 for each).
claims.source: Figure 2b-c; Results, Spatially organized coupling of transient DA-ACh dynamics during behavior, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The frequencies of all paired events were highest in the aDLS within a region significantly overlapping with the hotspot identified by correlation analysis
claims.criterion: Pairing occurrence per site as in the code, the fraction of a site's ACh and DA transients that belong to pairs of the type. The hotspot procedure with the highest-mean component, then the overlap test against the hotspot of fig1f-adls-hotspot. Reproduced when all four pair types have a hotspot overlapping with p < 0.05; partially reproduced for two or three; not reproduced otherwise. Occurrence inside against outside the correlation hotspot is reported as well.

claims.statement: DA and ACh transient rates are higher at sites inside the global correlation hotspot than outside.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 3d-e
claims.quote: Sites inside the hotspot showed significantly higher transient rates
claims.criterion: Transients per second per site over the sessions of fig2a-directionality, for DA peaks, DA troughs, ACh peaks and ACh troughs; two-sided rank-sum inside against outside. Reproduced when all four are higher inside with p < 0.05; partially reproduced for one to three; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: After unpredicted rewards, trial-by-trial DA peak magnitude correlates with ACh; dominant correlations are negative at 114 of 174 sites with DA leading (mean latency 177.9 +/- 96.7 ms) and positive at 58 of 174 with ACh leading (-41.2 +/- 218.9 ms).
claims.source: Results, Conserved spatial structure of distinct anti-correlated dynamics to unpredicted rewards and Pavlovian cues following conditioning and extinction, paragraph 1; Figure 3b
claims.quote: sites with dominant negative correlations (114/174 sites) indicated the DA peak leading ACh at a latency aligning with the ACh dip (177.9 + 96.7ms mean latency), and sites with dominant positive correlations indicated the DA peak lagging ACh (58/174 sites)
claims.criterion: As the code does. Reward sessions of UG27 to UG31; trigger at the first lick after each reward delivery and before the next; window -0.5 to 1.5 s; trials pooled per mouse; on each trial the DA peak is the local maximum within 9 samples of the trial-averaged peak in 0 to 1 s that is nearest to it; ACh is taken at -9 to +9 samples from each trial's DA peak; Pearson r across trials (at least 11); dominant r and its latency (lag times 1000/18 ms). The latency tolerances are the standard errors implied by the stated spreads (96.7/sqrt(114) and 218.9/sqrt(58)), because the spreads are across sites. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the counts are within tolerance and the mean latency is positive for negative sites and negative for positive sites, or when two or three values are within tolerance; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Reward-evoked DA-ACh correlations are significantly more negative inside the global hotspot than outside.
claims.source: Figure 3d; Results, Conserved spatial structure of distinct anti-correlated dynamics to unpredicted rewards and Pavlovian cues following conditioning and extinction, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Correlations were significantly more negative inside than outside the hotspot (Fig. 3d).
claims.criterion: Two-sided rank-sum test of the dominant reward r inside against outside the hotspot of fig1f-adls-hotspot. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with the median inside lower; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Reward anti-correlations form an aDLS hotspot that significantly overlaps the hotspot of spontaneous correlations (volume overlap test, p = 0.008).
claims.source: Figure 3c, 3e; Results, Conserved spatial structure of distinct anti-correlated dynamics to unpredicted rewards and Pavlovian cues following conditioning and extinction, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The anatomical organization of these correlations indicated a 'hotspot' of dominant negative correlations in the aDLS which significantly overlapped with the hotspot identified from spontaneous events (Fig. 3c,e).
claims.criterion: The hotspot procedure on the dominant reward r, then the overlap test against the hotspot of fig1f-adls-hotspot. Reproduced when the reward hotspot has a negative mean and overlaps with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when it is negative but the overlap has p >= 0.05; not reproduced when there is no negative hotspot.

claims.statement: After Pavlovian conditioning, the conditioned light cue evokes an ACh peak, then a DA peak, then an ACh dip at a majority of sites (49 of 75).
claims.source: Results, Conserved spatial structure of distinct anti-correlated dynamics to unpredicted rewards and Pavlovian cues following conditioning and extinction, paragraph 2; Figure 4a
claims.quote: conditioned cues evoked a temporal sequence of ACh peak→ DA peak→ ACh dip at a majority of sites (49/75 sites).
claims.criterion: AD1 to AD3. Learning sessions are those in which every light cue is followed by a reward (from the files' events); the last 3 per mouse are used, as the code does; light cue onsets; DfOverFexpHp; window -0.5 to 3 s; trials pooled per mouse; the null is drawn from times more than 9 s after a cue onset and more than 5 s after a reward. A site has the sequence when its cue-triggered average has a significant ACh peak, a significant DA peak and a significant ACh dip, and the times of the ACh maximum, the DA maximum and the ACh minimum of the mean trace are in that order. Readings for the window of significance and of the extremes are (a) 0 to 1 s for all three, as the code tests cue responses, and (b) 0 to 1.5 s. Reproduced when the count is within tolerance under either reading; partially reproduced when the sequence is found at between a third and the lower bound of the tolerance; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: For conditioned light cues, ACh correlates with the trial-by-trial DA peak negatively at lagging times at 39 of 75 sites (ACh lagging, 202.28 +/- 128.4 ms) and positively at leading times at 26 of 75 (ACh leading, -79.1 +/- 224.0 ms).
claims.source: Results, Conserved spatial structure of distinct anti-correlated dynamics to unpredicted rewards and Pavlovian cues following conditioning and extinction, paragraph 2; Figure 4c
claims.quote: Correlations of the ACh ΔF/F with the peak DA ΔF/F were negative at lagging timepoints (39/75 sites; ACh lagging DA; 202.28 + 128.4ms) and positive at leads (26/75 sites; ACh leading DA; - 79.1 + 224.0ms)
claims.criterion: The correlation of fig3b-reward-correlation on the light-cue trials of fig4-cue-sequence, DA peak in 0 to 1 s. The denominator can be read as (a) the sites with a significant cue DA peak, which the code uses for this panel and which fits 39 + 26 = 65 of 75, or (b) all 75 sites. Latency tolerances are standard errors from the stated spreads. Reproduced when under one reading all four values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when under one reading the counts are within tolerance and the latency signs are as stated, or two or three values are within tolerance; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: After cue-specific extinction (light cue rewarded on 20% of trials), cue-evoked DA dips correlate negatively with lagging ACh (DA dip then ACh late peak) at 41 of 74 sites, mean lag 117.9 +/- 176.2 ms.
claims.source: Results, Conserved spatial structure of distinct anti-correlated dynamics to unpredicted rewards and Pavlovian cues following conditioning and extinction, paragraph 3; Figure 4g-h
claims.quote: the timing relationships for correlations with DA dip magnitudes closely resembled those for the DA peak sites with dominant negative correlations indicating ACh lagging (DA dip→Ach late peak) (Fig. 4h; 41/74 sites; mean lag 117.9 + 176.2ms).
claims.criterion: Light-extinction sessions are those in which 20% of light cues are rewarded; the last 3 per mouse; all light-cue trials; on each trial the DA trough nearest the trial-averaged trough in 0 to 1.5 s, as the legend and Methods describe; ACh correlated as in fig4c-cue-correlation. The denominator can be read as (a) sites with a significant DA dip in 0 to 1.5 s, as the code selects, or (b) all 75 sites. Reproduced when under one reading both values are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the count is within tolerance and the mean lag positive, or the lag within tolerance and most selected sites negative; not reproduced otherwise. The code correlates the DA peak (polarity 1) in this step; that is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Conditioned-cue DA-ACh correlations are more negative at sites inside the global aDLS hotspot than outside.
claims.source: Figure 4d-e; Results, Conserved spatial structure of distinct anti-correlated dynamics to unpredicted rewards and Pavlovian cues following conditioning and extinction, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The spatial structure of DA-ACh correlations was also similar, with a significant aDLS hotspot of dominant anti-correlations overlapping with the hotspot for paired spontaneous events (Fig. 4b-e).
claims.criterion: AD1 to AD3 sites with a significant cue DA peak, placed in the grid of fig1f-adls-hotspot by their coordinates; two-sided rank-sum test of the dominant cue r inside against outside. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with the median inside lower; not reproduced otherwise. The overlap test of the cue hotspot is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: After extinction, DA dip to ACh correlations are more negative at sites inside the global aDLS hotspot than outside.
claims.source: Figure 4i-j; Results, Conserved spatial structure of distinct anti-correlated dynamics to unpredicted rewards and Pavlovian cues following conditioning and extinction, paragraph 3
claims.quote: The spatial organization of dominant negative correlations was also aligned, significantly overlapping with the aDLS correlation hotspot (Fig. 4g,i,j; Extended Data Fig. 5e,f).
claims.criterion: As fig4d-cue-in-out for the extinction correlations of fig4h-extinction-correlation, among sites with a significant DA dip. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with the median inside lower; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: At locomotion initiations, ACh rises and then falls at 131 of 174 sites; DA dips at 119 of 174 sites, rises at 73, and both rises and dips at 32.
claims.source: Results, Spatially organized anti-correlations corresponding to phase specific locomotion signals, paragraph 1; Figure 5d
claims.quote: initiations from rest were associated with rapid ACh increases at many sites, followed by decreases (131/174 sites, Fig. 5a-c). In contrast, DA release at some sites (119/174 sites) rapidly decreased, and at others in the same mouse, rapidly increased (73/174 sites) ... only a minority of sites had both DA increases and decreases (32/174 sites).
claims.criterion: Spontaneous sessions of UG27 to UG31, concatenated per mouse with NaN padding. Velocity is the wheel velocity low-pass filtered at 1.3 Hz (zero-phase 4th-order Butterworth, standing in for MATLAB lowpass) and smoothed over 5 samples (0.3 s). Initiations are a crossing of 0.0208 m/s (the code's value of the median velocity during reward consumption) after at least 1 s below it, with the bout lasting at least 2.27 s (the Methods; the code's 2.2 s is a variant). Triggered averages from -1 to 2 s, significance in -0.5 to 1 s. The ACh count can be read as (a) sites with both a significant ACh peak and a significant ACh dip, the peak first, or (b) sites with a significant ACh peak. Reproduced when all four counts are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when two or three are; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Initiation-related signals occur in sequence; DA dips first (median latency 111.11 ms), then ACh peaks (222.22 ms) and DA peaks (227.78 ms), then ACh dips (611.11 ms).
claims.source: Results, Spatially organized anti-correlations corresponding to phase specific locomotion signals, paragraph 1
claims.quote: DA dips were earliest (median latency 111.11, IQR 55.56-708.33 ms), followed by ACh peaks and DA peaks (median latencies 222.22, IQR 222.22-277.78 ms; and 227.78, IQR -388.89-444.44 ms, respectively), then ACh dips (median latency 611.11, IQR 500.00-722.22 ms).
claims.criterion: Latency is the time of the minimum (dips) or maximum (peaks) of the site's initiation-triggered average within -0.5 to 1 s, over sites with that significant feature in fig5d-initiation-responses. The tolerance is one sample (55.6 ms), because the latencies are multiples of the sample interval and 10% of them is smaller than it. Reproduced when the medians are in the order DA dip, then ACh peak and DA peak, then ACh dip, and all four are within tolerance; partially reproduced when the order holds but a value is outside tolerance; not reproduced when the order does not hold.

claims.statement: Initiation-related DA dips are concentrated in the aDLS and DA peaks in dorsomedial and posterior striatum; ACh dips are localized to the aDLS.
claims.source: Results, Spatially organized anti-correlations corresponding to phase specific locomotion signals, paragraph 1; Figure 5e-g
claims.quote: early DA dips were concentrated in the aDLS, followed by DA peaks in the dorsomedial and posterior striatum (Fig. 5e,f; Extended Data Fig. 6a). ... later ACh dips were localized to the aDLS (Fig. 5e,g).
claims.criterion: Dominant DA response per site, the extreme of the initiation-triggered average in -0.5 to 1 s with the larger magnitude. (i) Sites with a negative dominant DA response are more anterior and more lateral than sites with a positive one (one-sided rank-sum p < 0.05 for both AP and ML). (ii) Sites with a significant ACh dip are more anterior and more lateral than sites without (same test). Reproduced when (i) and (ii) hold; partially reproduced when one holds; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: At sites with initiation-related DA dips (119 sites), trial-by-trial DA dip magnitudes correlate negatively with ACh with DA leading (mean latency 193.80 +/- 177.68 ms).
claims.source: Results, Spatially organized anti-correlations corresponding to phase specific locomotion signals, paragraph 3; Figure 6a
claims.quote: dominant negative correlations were present between DA and ACh with timings indicating DA leading (Fig. 6a; mean latency 193.80 +/- 177.68ms).
claims.criterion: As the code does; on each initiation the DA trough within 9 samples of the averaged trough in -0.5 to 1 s nearest to it; ACh at -9 to +9 samples; Pearson r across initiations; sites with a significant DA dip. The mean latency can be read over (a) sites with a dominant negative r, or (b) all selected sites. The tolerance is the standard error from the stated spread (177.68/sqrt(119)). Reproduced when most selected sites have a dominant negative r and the mean latency is within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when most are negative with a positive mean latency outside tolerance; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Initiation DA dip to ACh correlations are concentrated in the aDLS and more negative inside the global hotspot than outside.
claims.source: Figure 6b-d; Results, Spatially organized anti-correlations corresponding to phase specific locomotion signals, paragraph 3
claims.quote: these correlations were concentrated in the aDLS, the area expressing the largest initiation evoked DA dips, and this region significantly overlapped with the previously identified hotspot (Fig. 6b-d).
claims.criterion: Two-sided rank-sum test of the dominant initiation r inside against outside the hotspot of fig1f-adls-hotspot, among sites with a significant DA dip. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with the median inside lower; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: At locomotion invigorations, GLM-estimated DA peak magnitudes correlate negatively with ACh at lagging times, and these correlations are concentrated in the aDLS, more negative inside the global hotspot (131 sites with invigoration DA peaks).
claims.source: Results, Spatially organized anti-correlations corresponding to phase specific locomotion signals, paragraph 3; Figure 6e-h; Methods, generalized linear model
claims.quote: Again, dominant negative correlations were observed at lags relative to the DA peak and were selectively concentrated in the aDLS, significantly overlapping with the previously identified anatomical hotspot (Fig. 6e-h;).
claims.criterion: As the code does. Per site, a linear model of DA or ACh, over samples within -1 to 2 s of initiations, on velocity, acceleration, and FIR terms at -0.5 to 1 s for initiations and for all positive local maxima of acceleration; residuals with the invigoration terms set to zero; invigoration events are the first local maximum of acceleration after each initiation. Sites with an invigoration DA peak are those with at least 3 consecutive FIR coefficients positive with p < 0.05. The correlation of fig6a-initiation-correlation on the residuals with the DA peak. Reproduced when most selected sites have a dominant negative r and the rank-sum test inside against outside the hotspot gives p < 0.05 with the median inside lower; partially reproduced when one of the two holds; not reproduced otherwise. The number of selected sites is reported against 131.

claims.statement: Optogenetic stimulation of midbrain DA neurons evokes significant DA release at 179 of 180 sites.
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic dopamine stimulation drives spatially selective ACh suppression in the hotspot, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 10b
claims.quote: Significant stimulation evoked release was measured at all sites but one (99%, 179 of 180 fibers; Extended Data Fig. 10b).
claims.criterion: The six ADS mice; DfOverFexp (not high-pass filtered, as the Methods state); stimulation trains during the ITI (no reward within 1 s), as the code selects; triggered averages -0.5 to 2.5 s, significance in -0.11 to 2 s (the code's -2 to 36 samples); null times exclude 5 s after reward deliveries and first licks and 1 s after stimulation onsets. Reproduced when the count of sites with a significant DA peak is within tolerance; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: DA stimulation evokes significant ACh suppression at a subset of sites (116 of 180, 64%).
claims.source: Results, Optogenetic dopamine stimulation drives spatially selective ACh suppression in the hotspot, paragraph 1; Figure 7e
claims.quote: significant ACh suppression following DA stimulation was observed only in a subset of fibers (64%, 116 of 180 sites), and these responses were spatially concentrated in the aDLS (Fig. 7b-e).
claims.criterion: As fig7-da-release, counting sites with a significant ACh dip. Reproduced when the count is within tolerance; partially reproduced when the count is outside tolerance but a minority of sites show no dip as stated (between 40% and 90% of sites); not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: The stimulation cohort replicates the aDLS anti-correlation hotspot in spontaneous release outside stimulation periods; its dominant correlations are more negative inside the original hotspot, and its own hotspot overlaps the original.
claims.source: Extended Data Figure 9a-d; Results, Optogenetic dopamine stimulation drives spatially selective ACh suppression in the hotspot, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We confirmed that an aDLS DA-ACh anti-correlation hotspot was present in this separate cohort of mice which significantly overlapped with that reported in previous cohorts (Extended Data Fig. 9a-d).
claims.criterion: As the code does. Sessions of the six ADS mice concatenated per mouse, DfOverFexp, samples left out when within 6 s after a reward delivery and within 6 s after a first lick and within 3 s after a stimulation onset (the code combines the three with AND; OR is a variant); dominant r over lags of -18 to 18 samples. (i) Two-sided rank-sum test of dominant r for sites inside against outside the original hotspot (sites placed by coordinates). (ii) The hotspot procedure on the cohort and the overlap test against the original. Reproduced when (i) gives p < 0.05 with the median inside lower and (ii) gives a negative hotspot overlapping with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when one holds; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Stimulation-evoked ACh dips are larger inside the cohort's correlation hotspot than outside, and their own hotspot overlaps it.
claims.source: Figure 7d, 7f-g; Results, Optogenetic dopamine stimulation drives spatially selective ACh suppression in the hotspot, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The spatial concentration of ACh stimulation-evoked dips significantly overlapped with the anti-correlation hotspot for spontaneous release events ... ACh ΔF/F dip magnitudes were significantly higher, on average, inside than out (Fig. 7f,g).
claims.criterion: ACh dip magnitude per site is the mean over trials of each trial's minimum in -0.11 to 2 s, as the code computes. Two-sided rank-sum test inside against outside the cohort hotspot of ed9-cohort-hotspot. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with the minima inside lower; not reproduced otherwise. The overlap test of the ACh-minimum hotspot and the test against the original hotspot are variants.

claims.statement: The D2 agonist quinpirole suppresses evoked ACh release in DLS and NAcC, more strongly in DLS; two-way ANOVA region effect F(1,40) = 105.9, region by stimulus interaction F(4,40) = 3.014, stimulus effect F(4,40) = 17.80.
claims.source: Figure 8b; Results, Differential D2R-mediated inhibition across striatal regions inside and outside the aDLS hotspot, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Quinpirole suppressed evoked ACh release in both DLS and NAcC (Fig. 8a,b), but the magnitude of suppression was significantly greater in DLS across all stimulation pulses (Fig. 8b).
claims.criterion: Ordinary two-way ANOVA of Peak_ACh in sheet Figure_8b on region, stimulus number and their interaction, each stimulus a row as the degrees of freedom imply. Reproduced when the three F values are within tolerance and the DLS mean is lower than the NAcC mean; partially reproduced when the region effect is within tolerance and DLS lower but another F is not; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Cocaine reduces evoked ACh release more in DLS than in NAcC; two-way ANOVA stimulus by region interaction F(4,55) = 10.75, stimulus effect F(4,55) = 36.37, region effect F(1,55) = 199.9.
claims.source: Figure 8e; Results, Differential D2R-mediated inhibition across striatal regions inside and outside the aDLS hotspot, paragraph 2
claims.quote: cocaine robustly reduced ACh release at the second through fourth pulses in DLS, while producing only modest suppression in NAcC (Fig. 8d,e).
claims.criterion: As fig8b-quinpirole-region, on sheet Figure_8e.

claims.statement: The D2 antagonist L-741,626 attenuates the cocaine-induced suppression in both regions; D2R block effect F(1,55) = 231.9 in DLS and F(1,40) = 32.57 in NAcC.
claims.source: Figure 8f-g; Results, Differential D2R-mediated inhibition across striatal regions inside and outside the aDLS hotspot, paragraph 2
claims.quote: This effect was significantly attenuated by the D2R antagonist L-741,626 in both regions (Fig. 8f,g)
claims.criterion: Ordinary two-way ANOVA of Peak_ACh on condition, stimulus number and their interaction, sheets Figure_8f (DLS) and Figure_8g (NAcC). Reproduced when both condition F values are within tolerance and the block raises ACh in both; partially reproduced when one is; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: Cocaine elevates evoked DA release to a similar degree in DLS and NAcC (two-way ANOVA, cocaine by region interaction F(8,36) = 0.20, p = 0.98).
claims.source: Figure 8c; Results, Differential D2R-mediated inhibition across striatal regions inside and outside the aDLS hotspot, paragraph 2
claims.quote: we enhanced DA availability with the reuptake inhibitor cocaine, which elevates DA release by similar degree in both regions (Fig. 8c).
claims.criterion: Blocked unless the ANOVA's factors can be identified. The sheets hold mean DA time courses per mouse and condition, and the stated degrees of freedom (8 for cocaine) do not match a two-level cocaine factor.

claims.statement: 406 units were recorded from 7 juvenile WT rats and 372 from 5 juvenile Fmr1-/y rats; 543 units from 6 adult WT rats and 507 from 6 adult Fmr1-/y rats.
claims.source: Results, paragraphs 2 and 7
claims.quote: We recorded 406 units from 7 WT rats and 372 units from 5 Fmr1-/y rats ... we recorded PoSub activity in adult Fmr1-/y rats (n = 507 units from 6 rats) and WT littermates (n = 543 units from 6 rats)
claims.criterion: Units are the rows of every file's units table, each recording counted once, in the main grouping. Readings are (a) all units, (b) putative excitatory units. Reproduced when, under one reading, the units and the rats of all four groups are within tolerance; partially reproduced when three groups are. The archive's grouping, and counting H4825's file as a recording of its own, are shown as variants.

claims.statement: Juvenile recordings held 8 to 83 putative excitatory units each, adult recordings 30 to 114.
claims.source: Results, paragraphs 2 and 7
claims.quote: (range: 8-83 putative excitatory units per recording; Figure S1e) ... (range: 30-114 putative excitatory units per recording; Figure 3a, Figure S2a-d)
claims.criterion: Per recording day (H4825 left out), under readings (a) all units, (b) putative excitatory units by trough-to-peak duration, (c) cells as defined above for session 1. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when the juvenile or the adult pair is.

claims.statement: Juvenile Fmr1-/y and WT rats do not differ in the time spent inactive, the time spent in the centre of the arena, or the speed while active.
claims.source: Figure S1c (t-tests on animal averages, t(10) = 1.53, 1.07 and 1.53, P > 0.05)
claims.quote: Juvenile Fmr1-/y rats showed no differences in exploratory behaviour in comparison with their WT littermates (Figure S1b-c).
claims.criterion: Claim of absence, judged by two-sided Student's t-tests on animal averages at 0.05. Over the tracked frames of both exploration sessions, inactive is speed below 1 cm/s (the paper's movement threshold for tuning curves); the centre is the disc of half the arena radius around the middle of the tracked extent; active speed is the mean speed of frames at or above 1 cm/s. Reproduced when none of the three tests is significant; not reproduced when any is.

claims.statement: Adult Fmr1-/y and WT rats do not differ in the time spent inactive, the time spent in the centre of the arena, or the speed while active.
claims.source: Figure S2c (t-tests on animal averages, t(10) = 1.21, 0.29 and 0.51, P > 0.05)
claims.quote: percentage of time spent inactive (left; t-test on animal averages: t(10) = 1.21, P > 0.05) and in the centre of the arena (middle; t-test on animal averages: t(10) = 0.29, P > 0.05), and the average speed within the active period
claims.criterion: As for figs1c-juvenile-behaviour-similar, on the adult rats.

claims.statement: In juveniles, cluster contamination, mean and peak firing rates, and the resultant vector length of PoSub cells do not differ between genotypes.
claims.source: Figure S1f-i (LME, no genotype effect, P > 0.05)
claims.quote: This difference in tuning was not associated with differences in cluster quality (Figure S1f), firing rates (Figure S1g-h) or electrode positions (Figure S1d) ... resultant vector length across the genotypes (LME: no genotype effect, P > 0.05)
claims.criterion: Claim of absence, by the LME test at 0.05 on the cells of session 1. Mean rate is spikes over the duration of session 1; peak rate is the maximum of the tuning curve; resultant vector length is from the tuning curve. Reproduced when none of the four is significant; partially reproduced when one to three are; not reproduced when all four are.

claims.statement: In adults, cluster contamination, mean and peak firing rates, and the resultant vector length of PoSub cells do not differ between genotypes.
claims.source: Figure S2f-i (LME, no genotype effect, P > 0.05)
claims.quote: cluster contamination scores across the two groups (LME: no genotype effect, P > 0.05) ... mean firing rates (g; LME: no genotype effect, P > 0.05) and peak firing rates (h; LME: no genotype effect, P > 0.05) of PoSub cells ... resultant vector length across the genotypes
claims.criterion: As for figs1-juvenile-cell-metrics-similar, on the adult rats.

claims.statement: PoSub cells of juvenile Fmr1-/y rats are more sharply tuned to head direction than those of WT littermates, with higher HD information and narrower tuning curves.
claims.source: Figure 1e-f; Results, paragraph 3 (LME, genotype effect, P < 0.05 for both)
claims.quote: Quantification of HD tuning using either HD information (HD info) or the width of the tuning curves (Figure 1e-f) confirmed that overall PoSub cells in juvenile Fmr1-/y rats were more sharply tuned to HD than PoSub cells in their WT littermates.
claims.criterion: LME test on the cells of session 1. Reproduced when HD information is higher and the half-width lower in Fmr1-/y rats, each with p < 0.05; partially reproduced when one of the two holds; not reproduced when neither does.

claims.statement: In juveniles the HD information of a cell is stable between the two halves of an exploration session (WT r = 0.90, Fmr1-/y r = 0.95).
claims.source: Figure 1g
claims.quote: Relationship between HD tuning of PoSub cells across two halves of the exploration epoch (WT, r = 0.90 ... Fmr1-/y, r = 0.95
claims.criterion: Pearson correlation over cells of the HD information of the tuning curves from the first and second halves of session 1 (cells with at least 100 spikes in session 1).

claims.statement: Within a session, the tuning curves of juvenile Fmr1-/y cells drift less relative to the room than those of WT cells; the angular offset between the two halves is smaller.
claims.source: Figure 1h (LME, genotype effect, P < 0.05)
claims.quote: HD receptive fields in juvenile Fmr1-/y rats drifted less than those of WT rats with respect to the allocentric reference frame of the open field within individual sessions (Figure 1h)
claims.criterion: The absolute offset in degrees maximising the cross-correlation of the two halves' tuning curves, per cell of session 1, by the LME test. Reproduced when the offset is smaller in Fmr1-/y rats with p < 0.05. The same test on cells with half-width below 120 degrees is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Bayesian decoding shows less drift of the HD signal relative to the room in juvenile Fmr1-/y rats than in WT rats.
claims.source: Figure 1i-j (t-test on animal averages, t(10) = 2.44, P < 0.05)
claims.quote: This improved anchoring of the HD signal to the external world in juvenile Fmr1-/y rats was further confirmed on the population level via Bayesian decoding (Figure 1i-j).
claims.criterion: Decoder drift as in the version 2 Methods (version 1 gives none), with the version 1 speed threshold of 2 cm/s; the mean absolute drift of the second half of session 1, averaged per rat over its recordings with at least 6 cells. Reproduced when a two-sided t-test on the animal averages gives p < 0.05 with Fmr1-/y lower. The SD of drift and the 1.5 cm/s threshold of version 2 are variants.

claims.statement: In juveniles HD information is preserved between the two exploration sessions (WT r = 0.85, Fmr1-/y r = 0.85).
claims.source: Figure S1j
claims.quote: HD tuning is preserved across the two exploration epochs in both genotypes (WT, r = 0.85 ... Fmr1-/y, r = 0.85
claims.criterion: Pearson correlation over cells of the HD information in sessions 1 and 2, for cells with at least 100 spikes in each.

claims.statement: In juveniles the drift of tuning curves between the two exploration sessions does not differ between genotypes.
claims.source: Figure S1k (LME, no genotype effect, P > 0.05)
claims.quote: HD receptive fields in juvenile Fmr1-/y rats drifted less than those of WT rats ... despite no difference in overall drift between recording sessions (Figure S1k).
claims.criterion: Claim of absence. The absolute offset between the tuning curves of sessions 1 and 2, per cell with at least 100 spikes in each, by the LME test at 0.05. Reproduced when not significant; not reproduced when significant.

claims.statement: In juveniles the HD information of tuning curves computed against the Isomap angle of the waking population activity matches that of real HD tuning curves (WT r = 0.84, Fmr1-/y r = 0.92).
claims.source: Figure 2c
claims.quote: Magnitude of HD tuning in PoSub cells is preserved in the tuning curves reconstructed only from population activity during WAKE (WT, r = 0.84 ... Fmr1-/y, r = 0.92
claims.criterion: Isomap of session 1 as in the version 1 Methods (all 200 ms bins of the session; tuning curves in 6 degree bins with 12 degree SD smoothing from bins with speed above 2 cm/s, against the Isomap angle and against real HD); Pearson correlation over cells of the two HD informations. Recordings with fewer than 6 cells are left out.

claims.statement: Juvenile Fmr1-/y cells are better tuned than WT cells to the internal HD signal of the waking manifold, independently of any reference frame.
claims.source: Figure 2d (LME, genotype effect, P < 0.05)
claims.quote: these intrinsic Isomap tuning curves were better HD-tuned in juvenile Fmr1-/y rats than in their WT littermates (Figure 2d).
claims.criterion: LME test on the Isomap HD information of fig2c. Reproduced when higher in Fmr1-/y rats with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In juveniles the HD information of tuning curves computed against the Isomap angle of REM sleep activity matches that of real HD tuning curves (WT r = 0.73, Fmr1-/y r = 0.90).
claims.source: Figure 2e-g
claims.quote: Magnitude of HD tuning in PoSub cells is preserved in the Isomap REM tuning curves in both genotypes (WT, r = 0.73 ... Fmr1-/y, r = 0.90
claims.criterion: Isomap as for fig2c on the 200 ms bins of all REM intervals of the recording (bins within each interval), for recordings with at least 60 s of REM and 6 cells with at least 100 spikes in REM; tuning curves against the REM Isomap angle from all REM bins; correlation over cells with the HD information of the real HD tuning curves of fig2c.

claims.statement: Juvenile Fmr1-/y cells are better tuned than WT cells to the internally generated HD signal during REM sleep.
claims.source: Figure 2h (LME, genotype effect, P < 0.05)
claims.quote: PoSub cells in juvenile Fmr1-/y rats still showed enhanced HD tuning relative to that of WT rats even when the tuning was computed from internally generated activity during REM sleep (Figure 2h).
claims.criterion: LME test on the REM Isomap HD information of fig2g. Reproduced when higher in Fmr1-/y rats with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In adults HD tuning does not differ between Fmr1-/y and WT rats, in HD information or tuning curve width.
claims.source: Figure 3e-f (LME, no genotype effect, P > 0.05)
claims.quote: overall there were no significant differences in the tuning to HD between the groups (Figure 3e-f; Figure S2e-j).
claims.criterion: Claim of absence, by the LME test at 0.05 on HD information and on half-width. Reproduced when neither is significant; not reproduced when either is.

claims.statement: In adults HD information is stable between the two halves of an exploration session (WT r = 0.94, Fmr1-/y r = 0.94).
claims.source: Figure 3g
claims.quote: Degree of HD tuning in PoSub cell tuning curves is preserved between two halves of an exploration epoch, indicating stable tuning fidelity (WT, r = 0.94 ... Fmr1-/y, r = 0.94
claims.criterion: As for fig1g-juvenile-halves-correlation, on the adult rats.

claims.statement: Within a session the tuning curves of adult Fmr1-/y cells drift more relative to the room than those of WT cells.
claims.source: Figure 3h (LME, genotype effect, P < 0.05)
claims.quote: adult Fmr1-/y rats showed the opposite effect, with stronger drift of the HD signal both within individual sessions (Figure 3g-j)

claims.statement: At 3 M, CA2 PNN area coverage does not differ between 5XFAD and control mice.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 1C and 1G
claims.quote: At 3 M, CA2 PNNs were indistinguishable between 5XFAD and controls
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test. PNN-AREA per slice (unit is the slice, as the legend's n), 5XFAD and control at 3, 6, 9 and 12 M, in a two-way ANOVA on genotype and age with Tukey's multiple comparisons (Figure 1 legend). Reproduced when the Tukey comparison of 5XFAD against control at 3 M has p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The mean difference and its p are reported, under each threshold reading.

claims.statement: CA2 PNN area coverage is significantly lower in 5XFAD than in age-matched control mice at 6 M, and stays lower at 9 and 12 M.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 1D to 1G
claims.quote: at 6 M, we observed a significant reduction in CA2 PNN area in the 5XFAD mice ... This decrease in the PNN coverage persisted in the 9 and 12 M old 5XFAD
claims.criterion: PNN-AREA per slice, two-way ANOVA on genotype and age with Tukey's multiple comparisons (Figure 1 legend). Reproduced when, at each of 6, 9 and 12 M, 5XFAD is below control with Tukey p < 0.05 under every threshold reading; partially reproduced when this holds at one or two of the three ages. The legend lists levels from p < 0.05 to p < 0.0001 without the figure, so p < 0.05 is the bound recorded.

claims.statement: WFA intensity in CA2 is significantly lower in 5XFAD than in control mice at 6 to 12 M.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 1H
claims.quote: we computed WFA intensity in the CA2 area which was similarly reduced significantly at 6-12 M in 5XFAD mice
claims.criterion: PNN-INTENSITY per slice, two-way ANOVA on genotype and age with Tukey's multiple comparisons (Figure 1 legend), under each intensity and threshold reading. Reproduced when, under every reading, 5XFAD is below control with Tukey p < 0.05 at each of 6, 9 and 12 M; partially reproduced when at one or two of these ages. If the readings give different outcomes the claim is methods_underspecified, with every result shown. The 3 M comparison is reported as well.

claims.statement: Normal aging also reduces CA2 PNN coverage in control mice, but the loss is significantly more pronounced in 5XFAD mice.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 2; Figure 1G and 1H
claims.quote: Note that normal aging also presented with a reduction in PNN coverage, yet the loss of PNNs was significantly more pronounced in 5XFAD mice
claims.criterion: PNN-AREA per slice, two-way ANOVA on genotype and age with Tukey's multiple comparisons over all eight cells (Figure 1 legend). The paper does not say which comparisons show the aging effect, so the reading of the reported finding is any older control group (6, 9 or 12 M) below control at 3 M with Tukey p < 0.05. Nor does it say which result makes the 5XFAD loss "significantly more pronounced"; the two-way ANOVA named in the legend tests this as the genotype by age interaction, which is used. Reproduced when the aging decline holds, the interaction has p < 0.05, and at each of 6, 9 and 12 M the 5XFAD loss relative to 5XFAD at 3 M is larger than the control's loss relative to control at 3 M. Partially reproduced when the aging decline holds and the 5XFAD loss is larger but the interaction is not significant. The same is reported for PNN-INTENSITY.

claims.statement: In 6 M 5XFAD mice, the PNNs around PV neurons in CA2 remain relatively intense, while those around CA2 pyramidal neurons are lost.
claims.source: Results 3.1, paragraph 1; Figure 1A to 1D
claims.quote: however we observed relatively intense PV neuron-associated PNNs in 5XFAD mice
claims.criterion: The paper reports no measure or test for this observation, and says the PNNs of pyramidal and PV neurons in CA2 could not be analysed separately (Results 3.1, paragraph 1). No source fixes how a PV neuron's PNN would be measured, and that choice could change the outcome, so the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified unless the dataset itself holds a per-PV-neuron WFA measure, which is then compared between 6 M 5XFAD and control by the Methods 2.10 default for two groups (two-tailed unpaired t-test); reproduced when the 5XFAD mean is not below the control mean at p < 0.05 while claim fig1g-pnn-area-reduced-6-to-12m holds at 6 M. As variants only, the mean WFA intensity in (a) a 2 um ring outside the PV cell outline and (b) the WFA mask overlapping the PV cell outline may be shown; they are not the basis of the outcome.

claims.statement: Along the periphery of a single CA2 pyramidal neuron, the WFA line profile shows many high-intensity peaks in control and loses this peak and valley pattern in 5XFAD.
claims.source: Figure 1B
claims.quote: showing many high-intensity WFA peaks in control (dark magenta line) compared to the 5XFAD (light magenta line) group
claims.criterion: The paper shows one example neuron per group and defines no peak measure, no peak threshold and no test. Testable only if the dataset holds the high magnification images or line profiles of Figure 1B, identified as such. Reproduced when the control profile has a higher maximum intensity than the 5XFAD profile and more peaks under peak prominence thresholds of both 10% and 25% of the control profile's intensity range; these two thresholds are not from the paper and stand for "many high-intensity peaks" only when they agree. Otherwise blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: PV neuron density in CA2 does not differ between 5XFAD and control mice at 3 or 6 M.

Reproduced when p >= 0.05 at both 3 and 6 M; not reproduced when either has p < 0.05.

Reproduced when no 5XFAD against control comparison has p < 0.05 under either reading; not reproduced when one does under both; if the readings disagree, methods_underspecified with both shown.

claims.statement: The evoked protocol recorded 104 cells in 53 animals (35 OFF, 45 ON, 24 NEUTRAL) and the ongoing protocol 62 cells in 30 animals (25 OFF, 25 ON, 12 NEUTRAL).

claims.criterion: Cells are units labelled ON, OFF or NEUTRAL; animals are subjects. The paper gives two groupings. Reading (a), the Methods: evoked is the "evoked" and "evoked/ongoing" files together (45 ON, 35 OFF, 4 + 20 NEUTRAL), ongoing is the "ongoing" files. Reading (b), Table S11: three sets, Evoked (45, 35, 4 in 35 animals), Evoked/Ongoing (0, 0, 20 in 18 animals), Ongoing (25, 25, 12 in 50 animals). claims.statement: The population PSTHs of Figure 1c pool 70 ON and 60 OFF cells, with 185 ON and 155 OFF trials aligned to withdrawal and 182 ON and 151 OFF trials aligned to heat onset, for windows that run to 150 s.

claims.criterion: All ON and OFF units of all files. The window ends 150 s after the event (Results, this paragraph); its start is open: (a) -30 s, as in Panel_1.ipynb (plot_spikes_around_event_fancy_figure, 0.1 s PSTH bins), (b) -10 s, the Methods' pre-event window (Data processing). Reproduced when the counts match under one reading. Trials kept by the rule of Spike2Tools.get_all_event_spike_trains, which applies the Methods' exclusion (Data processing, "if the recording ended within the window or if the next event ... truncated the usable interval"): for withdrawal alignment, the trial is dropped when the next heat onset, pinch or recording end is less than 150 s after the withdrawal, or the previous withdrawal or pinch (or the recording start) is less than 30 s before it; for heat alignment, the same with the next heat, pinch or end and any previous event (with 30 s or 10 s before the event, by reading). Reproduced when all six counts are within tolerance under one reading. The exact counts are reported for both.

claims.statement: Population ON and OFF activity is sharply time-locked to paw withdrawal; aligned to heat onset the PSTHs show a clear lag and shallower slopes.
