claims.criterion: The paper quantifies the slopes with the piecewise models (Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity, paragraph 9; Tables S3, S5, S6, S7). It does not quantify the lag; the reading used is the switch times of the same fits, which the tables give: ON t_switch -0.184 s withdrawal-aligned (Table S3) against 8.694 s heat-aligned (Table S5); OFF 1.346 s (Table S7) against 11.718 s (Table S6). Using the four fits of fig2-trial-counts and tables3-s7-withdrawal-steeper: reproduced when, for both cell types, the heat-aligned t_switch 97% HDI lies wholly after the withdrawal-aligned one (the paper judges differences of these fits by their HDIs, as in tables3-s7-withdrawal-steeper), and tables3-s7-withdrawal-steeper is reproduced. Partially reproduced when only one of the two parts holds.

claims.statement: For the models, windows from 10 s before to 100 s after the event gave 195 ON and 170 OFF trials aligned to withdrawal and 197 ON and 172 OFF trials aligned to heat onset; cells were not selected by pre-trial firing and every trial with a withdrawal was included.

claims.quote: This resulted in 195 ON-cell and ... 170 OFF-cell trials aligned to withdrawal, and 197 ON-cell ... and 172 OFF-cell trials aligned to heat onset

claims.statement: A null model with a constant mean spike count fits significantly worse than every piecewise model, for ON and for OFF cells, so both an evoked departure and a recovery are needed.
claims.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure S8
claims.quote: Both null models clearly performed worse than either of the parametric fits.
claims.criterion: The null model is build_mean_model of bayesian_cell_models.py (notebooks 20 and 27), fitted to the same summed counts. Each model is sampled as the Methods give it (NUTS in PyMC, 4 chains, 1000 tuning steps, 1000 draws; target_accept 0.8 from sample_model) and compared by the expected log predictive density. The paper names ELPD without fixing the estimator: the model comparison plots use PSIS-LOO (plot_loo_comparison; notebook 23 prints LOO and WAIC, notebook 17 WAIC), so both are readings. Its word "significantly" is not defined; the readings are that the null model's ELPD is below each piecewise model's by more than (a) one or (b) two standard errors of the difference (dse of arviz.compare). Reproduced when, for each cell type, the null model is below every piecewise model of that type under one reading of each. The paper's notebooks print ELPD-LOO -11683 for the ON null against -7215 and -7454, and -9237 for the OFF null against about -6265 (difference 2972, dse 124).

claims.statement: The switch from response to recovery comes 0.18 s before withdrawal for ON cells (97% HDI 0.27 to 0.095 s before) and 1.35 s after it for OFF cells (97% HDI 0.85 to 1.9 s after), so ON cells peak slightly before withdrawal while OFF cells keep falling after it.
claims.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraph 3; Figure 2g and 2i
claims.quote: differed for ON- and OFF-cells (Figure 2g) ... 0.18 s before withdrawal (97% HDI: 0.27–0.095 s before), and ... switch = 1.35 s after withdrawal (97% HDI: 0.85–1.9 s af ... Thus ON-cells peak slightly before withdrawal, while ... OFF-cells enter a brief post-withdrawal depression
claims.criterion: The ON double-exponential model (build_double_exponential_on_model) and the OFF linear plus exponential model (build_linear_slope_recovery_off_model) fitted to the withdrawal-aligned counts of fig2-trial-counts, with the Methods' priors (Piecewise Bayesian modeling; the notebooks set the same values: ON log r ~ N(3, 0.5), log k_pre ~ N(4, 0.1), log k_post ~ N(2.5, 1), rates LogNormal(log 0.1, 0.5) and LogNormal(log 1/50, 0.5), t_s ~ U[-4, 4]; OFF b ~ HalfNormal(4), a and c = b + HalfNormal(4), k3 ~ HalfNormal(1), u0 ~ U[b, a], t_s ~ U[-4, 4]). The Methods give k, k2 ~ N(0, 1); the code places these priors on log k and log k2, which is run as a variant. Sampling as in figs8-null-model-worse. The tolerance is the larger distance from the reported value to its HDI bound; reproduced when both posterior means lie inside the paper's 97% HDIs and the ON mean is below 0 and the OFF mean above 0. The text's ON HDI (-0.27 to -0.095) differs from Table S3 (-0.257 to -0.108) and the OFF one (0.85 to 1.9) from Table S7 (0.904 to 1.832); the wider interval of each pair is used, and the disagreement is recorded. The Discussion (paragraph 3) puts the OFF nadir more than 2 s after withdrawal, which disagrees with the Results' 1.35 s; the Results' value is tested.

claims.statement: ON-cell recovery is better described by a double exponential, two decay timescales, than by a single exponential, which misses the sharp peak and the prolonged decay.

The paper says "best captured" and states no margin, so, as in fig2h-off-linear-exponential, reproduced when the double exponential has the higher ELPD under either estimator. The difference and its standard error are reported. The paper's notebook 17 prints ELPD-WAIC -7215.5 against -7453.6, difference 238, dse 23.

claims.statement: ON-cell firing rises before withdrawal with time constant 0.653 s and recovers with a fast component of 4.157 s and a slow component of 164.223 s.

claims.quote: constant τpre = 0.653 s (97% HDI: 0.570–0.739 s). After paw ... τfast = 4.157 s (97% HDI: 3.582–4.722 s) and a slow compo ... nent τslow = 164.223 s (97% HDI: 129.571–199.809 s)
claims.criterion: The ON double-exponential fit of fig2g-switch-times; the time constants are the inverses of the rate parameters (tau = 1/beta), as in the Methods and notebook 18. claims.statement: OFF-cell firing falls before withdrawal with sigmoid slope k = 2.852 s-1, then recovers with an exponential component of 4.760 s and a linear drift of 0.186 counts per second.

claims.criterion: The OFF linear plus exponential fit of fig2g-switch-times; tau = 1/k2 (Table S7 caption). Reproduced when the three posterior means lie inside the paper's 97% HDIs; partially reproduced when two do. The paper gives k in s-1 here and in "total spikes per bin" in paragraph 6, and k3 in counts per second while the model's counts are per 50 ms bin summed over trials; the values are compared as the model's parameters, whatever their unit.

claims.statement: A Gaussian CDF (erf) response for OFF cells fits significantly worse than the sigmoid, with either recovery model.
claims.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraph 3; Supplementary Tables S9 and S10, Gaussian CDF Fits, Figure S9
claims.quote: this fitted significantly worse than the sigmoid ... across all recovery models (see Supplemental Gaussian CDF
claims.criterion: The erf models of bayesian_cell_models.py (build_erf_off_model with double-exponential recovery, notebook 28; build_linear_erf_off_model with linear plus exponential recovery, notebook 29), with the Methods' priors (k_offset, k_scale ~ HalfNormal(10), k_slope ~ HalfNormal(4)), fitted to the withdrawal-aligned OFF counts; each compared by ELPD with the sigmoid model of the same recovery (notebooks 24 and 21). Readings of "significantly" as in figs8-null-model-worse. Reproduced when, for both recoveries, the sigmoid's ELPD is higher by more than one standard error of the difference (reading a) or two (reading b); partially reproduced when it is higher for both but by less. The paper's own notebook 29 prints ELPD-LOO -6263.78 for the linear erf model, above the -6264.95 of the linear sigmoid model, which disagrees with the text; this is recorded either way.

claims.statement: Both populations leave baseline well before withdrawal; OFF firing has fallen 10% at 1.5 s before it and ON firing has risen 10% at 1.7 s before it, and both cross 50% of their change within a narrow window before withdrawal (OFF 726 ms, ON 630 ms before).
claims.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraph 6; Supplementary Table S2 and Figure S1
claims.quote: ready decreased by 10% from baseline at 1.5 s before the paw ... withdrawal (97% HDI: 1.746–1.306 s), and ON-cell firing in ... creased by 10% on a similar timescale, at 1.7 s before with ... a narrow pre-withdrawal window (OFF: 726 ms before; 97% ... HDI: 810–645 ms; ON: 630 ms before; 97% HDI: 690–570 ms)
claims.criterion: From the ON double-exponential and OFF linear plus exponential withdrawal-aligned fits, as calculate_rate_percentages_of_peak and calculate_rate_percentages_of_peak_OFF do (notebooks 18 and 21): for each posterior draw, the rate is predicted on a grid (ON 20000 points from -10 to 400 s; OFF 2000 points from -10 to 100 s); the baseline is the rate at the first grid point; the extremum is the grid maximum (ON) or minimum (OFF); the time of x% is the first grid time before the extremum at which the rate has moved x% of the way from baseline to extremum. Summary is the mean over draws and the 97% HDI. Reproduced when all four means lie inside the paper's HDIs; partially reproduced when two or three do.

claims.statement: ON firing reaches 90% of its peak 240 ms before withdrawal, while OFF suppression reaches 90% only 41 ms after it, so ON activation peaks before OFF suppression is complete.
claims.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraphs 6 and 7; Supplementary Table S2
claims.quote: (240 ms before, 97% HDI: 320–180 ms), while OFF-cell sup ... response (41 ms post, 97% HDI: 95 ms pre –180 ms post)
claims.criterion: As figs1-departure-timing, at 90%. The paper compares the two intervals and states no test (its HDIs, -0.32 to -0.18 s and -0.095 to 0.18 s, are disjoint). Reproduced when both means lie inside the paper's HDIs and the ON 97% HDI lies wholly before the OFF one; the fraction of paired draws, taken independently from the two fits, in which the ON time is earlier is reported.

claims.statement: After withdrawal ON cells return to 50% of their post-withdrawal baseline by 15.39 s but need 222 s to reach 90%; OFF cells return to 50% by 18 s and 90% by 83 s.
claims.source: Results, Evoked ON/OFF activity unfolds over multiple timescales, paragraph 8; Supplementary Table S2
claims.quote: to 50% of their post-withdrawal baseline by 15.39 s after ... the withdrawal (97% HDI: 9.373-22.43 s), but required more ... reaching 90% of their baseline by 222 s (97% HDI: 183.6-248.8 ... s). OFF-cells increased back to 50% of their baseline by 18 s ... post-withdrawal (97% HDI: 15-21 s) but to 90% of their base ... line by 83 s (97% HDI: 82-84 s)

claims.statement: The ongoing-activity analyses use 25 ON, 25 OFF and 32 NEUTRAL cells recorded without external stimulation.
claims.source: Results, RVM ON- and OFF-cells exhibit slow quasi-periodic structure during ongoing activity, paragraph 1

Each ON and OFF cell (and each NEUTRAL cell of the ongoing files) contributes the 1500 s ending at the heat onset that closes its longest gap between heat onsets (Spike2Tools.get_event_windows, size 25 min; Methods, Data processing, "a 1500 s segment ... relative to the start of the first post–ongoing activity trial"); NEUTRAL cells of the evoked/ongoing files contribute their whole 960 s. claims.statement: ON and OFF cells show clear low-frequency spectral peaks, often with harmonics, at a period of about five minutes (ON 286.86 s, FWHM 16.92 s; OFF 298.33 s, FWHM 16.12 s).
claims.source: Results, RVM ON- and OFF-cells exhibit slow quasi-periodic structure during ongoing activity, paragraph 2; Figure 3b and 3c
claims.quote: Both ON- and OFF-cells exhibited clear ... low-frequency spectral peaks, often accompanied by har ... istic period of approximately five minutes (TON ... peak = 286.86 ... s, full width at half maximum (FWHM) = 16.92 s; TOFF ... 298.33 s, FWHM = 16.12 s)
claims.criterion: As Panel_3.ipynb and the supplement ("Spike train power spectra"): each cell's 1500 s segment (ongoing-cell-counts) binned at 5 ms, its periodogram with a Hann window over one segment, zero-padded (the code's FFT length is 50 times the spike count of the first ON cell, a resolution of 1.65e-4 Hz), DC removed, normalized to unit area (get_auto_correlation_freqs_with_rate); the class PSD is the mean over cells; the peak is the highest local maximum of the mean PSD between 0.0001 and 0.1 Hz (get_summary_psd_stats), and the period its inverse. The FWHM is computed per cell with scipy peak_widths at half height on the highest peak between 0.5 and 1.95 times the class peak frequency, and averaged over cells, in Hz. The paper reports the FWHM in seconds without saying how it was converted; the readings are (a) FWHM_Hz / f_peak squared, (b) 1/(f_peak - FWHM_Hz/2) - 1/(f_peak + FWHM_Hz/2), (c) the same as (b) from the half-height width of the mean PSD. The code's stored results (fwhm_results_ON.pkl, fwhm_results_OFF.pkl) give peaks at 288.9 s and 303.3 s and FWHMs of 2.13e-4 and 1.23e-4 Hz (about 17.8 and 11.4 s under reading b), which do not all match the text. The supplement ("Spike train power spectra", paragraph 3) describes a further estimate, which is also a reading: hierarchical bootstrapping at the rat level, N rats (the number in the class) resampled with replacement with all their cells, the mean PSD per iteration, its highest peak and that peak's FWHM taken per iteration, 1000 iterations; the period and FWHM are then the mean over iterations, with the FWHM in seconds under readings (a) and (b). Reproduced when both periods are within tolerance and the FWHMs match, under one reading; partially reproduced when only the periods do. Whether peaks near 600 s and 150 s (harmonics) are present is reported.

claims.statement: NEUTRAL cells lack consistent low-frequency spectral peaks and instead show broad low-frequency components and prominent power above 10 Hz, reflecting regular tonic firing.
claims.source: Results, RVM ON- and OFF-cells exhibit slow quasi-periodic structure during ongoing activity, paragraph 2; Figure 3d
claims.quote: lacked consistent spectral peaks, instead showing broad low ... frequency components and prominent high-frequency power ... (> 10 Hz), reflecting regular, tonic firing
claims.criterion: As fig3bc-psd-peaks, for the 32 NEUTRAL cells over their whole recordings (Panel_3.ipynb uses all NEUTRAL spike trains uncut; the supplement gives their lengths as 960 s and about 3000 s, zero-padded for a common grid). The paper does not define "consistent"; the reading used is the code's: the peak search of fig3bc-psd-peaks on the NEUTRAL mean PSD, and the per-cell peak frequencies between 0.5 and 1.95 times the ON peak frequency. Reproduced when the NEUTRAL mean PSD has no local maximum between 0.0025 and 0.0045 Hz (periods 220 to 400 s) that exceeds the median of the mean PSD over 0.001 to 0.01 Hz by more than its ON-cell counterpart's ratio divided by 2, and the NEUTRAL mean PSD has local maxima above 10 Hz that the ON and OFF mean PSDs lack. The bounds 220 to 400 s and the factor 2 are not in the paper and are named as open; the NEUTRAL peak the code finds (stored at 3.05e-4 Hz, beyond the window) and the spectra above 10 Hz are reported.

claims.statement: NEUTRAL cells fire regularly and fast (CV 0.35 ± 0.26, mean ISI 0.17 ± 0.25 s), while ON and OFF cells fire irregularly, with CVs well above 1 (ON 4.91 ± 4.32, OFF 3.70 ± 3.09) and broad ISI distributions (ON 1.25 ± 4.80 s, OFF 0.84 ± 1.36 s).
claims.source: Results, RVM ON- and OFF-cells exhibit slow quasi-periodic structure during ongoing activity, paragraph 3; Figure 3e; Supplementary Table S1

In contrast, ON- and ... with coefficients of variation well above 1 ( CVON = 4.91 ± ... 4.32, CVOFF = 3.70 ± 3.09) and broad interspike interval (ISI) ... distributions (ISION = 1.25 ± 4.80 s, ISIOFF = 0.84 ± 1.36
claims.criterion: As ongoing_CV_isi_table.ipynb: for each of the 82 cells of the ongoing and evoked/ongoing files, over its whole recording, the CV of its ISIs (elephant.statistics.cv, standard deviation over mean) and its mean ISI; then the mean and sample standard deviation over the cells of each class (Table S1). The tolerance is the paper's stated spread (protocol default), which is wide; reproduced when all six means are within it, the NEUTRAL mean CV is below 1 and both ON and OFF mean CVs above 1. Whether the six values also lie within 10% of the paper's is reported.

claims.statement: Scans of a periodic Gaussian process over the period show clear minima of the negative log marginal likelihood near 300 s for ON and OFF cells, with further minima at 600 and 900 s, while NEUTRAL cells, with one exception, have flat profiles without consistent minima.
claims.source: Results, A periodic Gaussian process reveals dominant slow oscillations in ON- and OFF-cell activity, paragraph 1; Figure 4
claims.quote: ON- and OFF-cells showed clear minima in the ... negative log marginal likelihood (NLML) near 300 s, with ... additional subharmonic peaks at 600 and 900 s ... contrast, NEUTRAL-cells (with one exception) displayed flat
claims.criterion: As GP_period_scoping.ipynb and the Methods (Gaussian process modeling, paragraph 1): each cell's rate from its spikes with a Gaussian kernel of 2 s sampled every 2 s (elephant.instantaneous_rate), edges removed, and a GPy GPRegression with a StdPeriodic kernel of fixed lengthscale 1.0 and variance 5.0 (GPy's default noise variance 1.0), its NLML evaluated at 200 periods evenly spaced. The Methods give 0.1 to 500 s; the Results and the code give 0.1 to 1500 s, which is used, since minima at 600 and 900 s cannot appear in a scan to 500 s (the 500 s scan is run as a variant for the 300 s minimum). The Methods remove the first and last 2 s; the code removes two samples (4 s), a variant. ON and OFF segments as in ongoing-cell-counts; NEUTRAL recordings whole. The paper does not define a "clear minimum"; the reading used is the code's display, each cell's NLML divided by its maximum: a cell has a minimum near p when its profile has a local minimum within 10% of p. Reproduced when a majority of ON and of OFF cells have a minimum near 300 s and the class means of the normalized profiles have local minima near 300, 600 and 900 s, and at most 4 of the 32 NEUTRAL cells (one, with 10% of 32 as tolerance) have a minimum near 300 s; partially reproduced when the ON and OFF part holds and more NEUTRAL cells have one. Counts per class are reported, and the stored scan PERIOD_SCOPE_RESULTS_200.npz is compared.

claims.statement: A Poisson-type periodic Gaussian process fits the training data of all three cell classes with significant accuracy (pseudo-R2 different from 0; ON p = 0.0047, OFF p = 0.0004, NEUTRAL p < 0.0001).
claims.source: Results, A Poisson Gaussian process predicts slow quasi-periodic fluctuations in ongoing RVM firing, paragraph 2; Figure 5b; Supplementary Figure S4
claims.quote: All three cell classes achieved significant training accuracy ... (pON = 0.0047, pOFF = 0.0004, pNEUTRAL < 0.0001)
claims.criterion: The GP fit, from the Methods (Gaussian process modeling, paragraph 2) and Poisson_GP_main_fit_notebook.ipynb with non_poisson_gpytorch_model.py: spikes in 5 s bins; each cell trained on all but its last 300 s (ON and OFF 1500 s segments split at 1200 s; evoked/ongoing NEUTRAL cells, 960 s, at 660 s as the notebook has it, with params.json's 700 s as a variant; ongoing NEUTRAL cells over their whole recording, the Methods' "full recording period" (Data processing, paragraph 2), less its last 300 s, with the code's split at 1200 s of a 1500 s segment as a variant); a sparse variational GP (GPyTorch ApproximateGP, fixed inducing points evenly spaced over the training span; the Methods give 200 inducing points, the code 100, a variant), constant mean, scaled periodic kernel, lengthscale prior N(0.1, 0.1) on the raw lengthscale, period initialized at 300 s and lengthscale at 0.1, mean and outputscale initialized by set_mean_and_scale; rate 10 softplus(x); generalized Poisson likelihood with theta = mu(1 - alpha), alpha < 1, prior N(0, 0.5); uniform contamination on 0 to 200 counts with p_noise 0.001 (Methods; the code fixes 0.01, a variant); Adam, learning rate 0.05, for 10000 iterations (params.json; the notebook's last call uses 100, a variant); seeds 0 (torch and pyro). Pseudo-R2, which the paper does not define, is the code's (compare_log_liks): 1 minus the summed expected log likelihood of the periodic GP over that of a constant-mean GP with a diagonal kernel and the same likelihood, on the training and the test bins. The test, as bootstrap_R2_across_animals.ipynb: the observed median pseudo-R2 of a class against the medians of 10000 permutations that flip the sign of all cells of one animal together (the Results, paragraph 2, "all cells per animal"; animals are dandiset subjects); the code groups by recording file, run as a variant, which is the same when each file is one animal. p is the fraction with absolute null median at least the absolute observed median. Reproduced when all three classes have p < 0.05 with positive medians; the median per class is reported, and the paper's stored values (combined_data.csv) are compared.

claims.statement: Training pseudo-R2 does not differ between the three classes (permuted, Bonferroni-corrected Mann-Whitney U tests; Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.117).

claims.quote: paring R2 values using a similarly permuted and Bonferroni ... corrected Mann Whitney U test revealed no significant differ ... ences between training R2 for the three groups
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's tests as bootstrap_R2_across_animals.ipynb runs them on the training pseudo-R2 of fig5b-train-r2: for each pair of classes, the Mann-Whitney U statistic against 1000 permutations that relabel the cell classes of each recording file as a block (mannwhitney_blockwise, seed 42; Figures S6 and S7 say the permutation is within animals, so blocks by subject are run as a variant), two-sided by distance from the null median, Bonferroni-corrected over the three pairs; and the Kruskal-Wallis H against 1000 such permutations over the three labels (kruskal_blockwise, seed 42). Reproduced when no corrected pair p and not the Kruskal-Wallis p is below 0.05; not reproduced when any is. The statistics and p-values are reported either way.

claims.statement: Test pseudo-R2 of NEUTRAL cells differs from that of ON cells (p < 0.001) and OFF cells (p = 0.006), ON and OFF cells do not differ (p = 0.939), and the Kruskal-Wallis test across the three is significant at test time (p < 0.001).

Reproduced when both NEUTRAL pairs and the Kruskal-Wallis test have p < 0.05 and the ON-OFF pair has p >= 0.05 (a claim of absence, judged on this test); partially reproduced when the Kruskal-Wallis test and one NEUTRAL pair hold. claims.statement: Single-cycle phase-normalized reconstructions of the GP fits show cell-specific oscillatory signatures in ON and OFF cells, while NEUTRAL cells have near-constant phase profiles.
claims.source: Results, A Poisson Gaussian process predicts slow quasi-periodic fluctuations in ongoing RVM firing, paragraph 6; Figure 5d

Reading, named as open: for each cell, the predicted rate of its GP fit of fig5b-train-r2 over one fitted period, on a phase grid from 0 to 1 with zero phase at the fit's maximum (as get_phase of figs2-phase-latency); the modulation depth is (maximum minus minimum) over the mean of that cycle. claims.statement: A subset of cells of every class shows significant low-frequency coherence with heart rate (5 of 32 NEUTRAL, 4 of 25 OFF, 8 of 25 ON).
claims.source: Results, Low-frequency coherence between RVM activity and heart rate, paragraph 3; Figure 6b and 6c
claims.quote: A subset of cells (5/32 NEUTRAL, 4/25 OFF, 8/25 ON) ... showed significant low-frequency coherence with heart rate
claims.criterion: As the Methods (Coherence estimation) and 07_mt_sig_test_phase_shifts.ipynb: for each cell, its spikes and the EKG beats of its recording over the cell's ongoing segment (ON, OFF and ongoing NEUTRAL 1500 s segments of ongoing-cell-counts; evoked/ongoing NEUTRAL whole 960 s; the Methods say only "the recording", so each cell's whole recording is a second reading), each binned at 2 s; 500 s segments with 50% overlap, each demeaned; multitaper spectra with DPSS tapers, NW 3.5, K 6, and the magnitude-squared coherence averaged over segments; 1000 surrogates with the heart-rate segments phase-randomized (seed 1); the threshold is the 99.9th percentile of the surrogates' maximum coherence over all frequencies (max-statistic, alpha 0.001). A cell is coherent when its coherence exceeds the threshold at any frequency, as the code counts (the code does not restrict the frequency; the Results say "low-frequency"; the count restricted to below 0.01 Hz is shown as a variant). Tolerance 10% of each count, so the counts must match exactly; reproduced when all three do under one reading, partially reproduced when each is within 2 of the paper's. Because the surrogates are random, the counts at three other seeds are reported.

claims.statement: Peak coherence frequencies do not match the ~300 s period exactly, but the heart-rate power spectrum has peaks at multiples of this period.

claims.criterion: The heart-rate spectrum is described in the supplement ("Spike train power spectra", last paragraph: computed by bootstrapping "in the same manner as for the cells", one heart rate per animal) and the Figure 6 legend ("Combined averaged heart rate power spectrum over all animals"); no code for it was found in the repository, and the paper does not say whether the EKG beats are treated as a point process or converted to a rate, which segments are used, or what "multiples" means (periods of 600 and 900 s, or frequencies of 2 and 3 times 1/300 Hz). Readings: the EKG beat train of each ongoing and evoked/ongoing recording (one per animal), (a) as a spike train over the same 1500 s segment and (b) over the whole recording, with the PSD method of fig3bc-psd-peaks; the mean over animals; a "peak at a multiple" is a local maximum within 10% of 600 or 900 s (subharmonics) or of 150 or 100 s (harmonics). Reproduced when, under one reading, at least one such peak is the highest peak below 0.01 Hz; the lowest-frequency peak (marked in Figure 6d) is reported. The rule "highest peak below 0.01 Hz" is not in the paper and is named as open. The first part of the statement is reported, not judged: the frequency of peak coherence of each coherent cell of fig6c-coherence-counts, against 1/300 Hz.

claims.quote: CA1 deletion of Stx3 does not affect locomotion in the elevated plus maze as demonstrated by the summary plot of distance traveled
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Total distance in the 5 min session, unpaired t-test as in Fig 1C. Reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: The example sessions of Fig 2A-B hold 1208 cells and 120 familiar trials (Ctrl-3, day 5), 1568 cells and 20 novel trials (Ctrl-3, day 1), 1087 cells and 17 familiar trials (Cre-3, day 5) and 936 cells and 17 novel trials (Cre-3, day 1).
claims.source: Figure 2A and 2B legends
claims.quote: (Ctrl-3, N=1208 cells, 120 trials). Right - Same as (Left) for novel trials on day 1 (N=1568 cells, 20 trials)
claims.criterion: Counts of mCherry+ cells (all analysed cells of the session) and of completed trials of the given type in the named sessions. Each count is matched within its tolerance. The Cre-3 numbers are in the Fig 2B legend ("Day 5 familiar trial decoding - N=1087 cells, 17 trials, Day 1 novel trial decoding - N=936 cells, 17 trials").

claims.statement: On familiar arm trials, control mice licked at a higher rate than Cre mice as they approached the reward zone, across the six days.
claims.source: Figure 1F; Results, Stx3-dependent postsynaptic membrane fusion in CA1 is critical for novel environment preference and reward anticipation, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Control mice licked at a higher rate as they approached the reward zone for both familiar and novel arms (Fig. 1F-G)
claims.criterion: Anticipatory lick rate is the lick rate (licks/s) in the 30 cm preceding the reward zone of the arm (Methods, VR behavioral analyses), on familiar arm trials, averaged over the trials of each day (Fig 1F legend, "across trial average for each mouse"), days 1 to 6. Mixed effects ANOVA (virus between, day within). Open and run as readings, the Cre mice (a) Cre-1 to Cre-7 or (b) Cre-1 to Cre-8 (legend N=8, df 15); and the rate (i) licks over time spent in the 30 cm per trial or (ii) the mean of the three 10 cm bins' rates. All familiar trials of the day are used, rewarded or not, as no exclusion is stated. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with control higher. The printed F and p disagree (F(1,15)=10.66 gives p near 0.005); either p is below 0.05.

claims.statement: On novel arm trials, control mice licked at a higher rate than Cre mice as they approached the reward zone.
claims.source: Figure 1G; Results, Stx3-dependent postsynaptic membrane fusion in CA1 is critical for novel environment preference and reward anticipation, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Control mice licked at a higher rate as they approached the reward zone for both familiar and novel arms (Fig. 1F-G)
claims.criterion: As fig1f-anticipatory-licking-familiar, on novel arm trials (block 6 of days 1 to 5, all novel trials of day 6), with the same readings of the Cre mice and of the rate. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with control higher.

claims.statement: Both control and Cre mice learned the context-dependent reward locations, licking more and running slower only in the bins just before the reward zones, and anticipatory licking on familiar trials changed over days.
claims.source: Results, Stx3-dependent postsynaptic membrane fusion in CA1 is critical for novel environment preference and reward anticipation, paragraph 4; Figures 1F and S2B-E
claims.quote: Both Cre and control mice rapidly learned the context-dependent reward locations, evidenced by increased licking and decreased running speed only in the spatial bins immediately preceding the reward zones
claims.criterion: The paper gives no test of the spatial pattern; the comparison its sentence makes is between the bins preceding the reward zone and the rest of the track. On day 6, for each group and each arm (left, right), from the across-animal mean of position-binned normalized lick rate and normalized running speed (each mouse's binned value over its overall mean, Methods, VR behavioral analyses; Fig S2C and S2E), the pattern holds when the mean normalized lick rate in the 30 cm before the reward zone exceeds that of every bin outside the reward zone and those 30 cm, and the normalized speed in those 30 cm is below 1. The day effect holds when the day main effect of the fig1f ANOVA has p < 0.05 with the day 6 mean above the day 1 mean. Reproduced when both hold, partially when one does. Readings of the Cre mice as in fig1f.

claims.statement: When the novel arm block began, control mice slowed down more than Cre mice on familiar arm trials, most clearly on day 1.
claims.source: Figure S2F; Results, Stx3-dependent postsynaptic membrane fusion in CA1 is critical for novel environment preference and reward anticipation, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Control animals slow down more than Cre animals in familiar arm trials after the novel arm block is removed
claims.criterion: Normalized speed is log10 of the mean running speed on the block 6 trials divided by the mean running speed in the 10 trials preceding block 6 (Methods, VR behavioral analyses). The Methods use the whole block; the legend plots "the first two familiar arm trials of block 6". Readings, run both, (a) the first two familiar trials (legend), (b) all familiar trials of block 6 (Methods). The Methods do not say how "average running speed" is taken; readings, run both, (i) the mean of the position binned speeds, (ii) distance over time (time-averaged speed). Days 1 to 5; mixed effects ANOVA; posthoc t-test per day with Holm correction over the five days. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with control lower (more slowing) and the day 1 posthoc has p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Control and Cre mice slowed similarly on novel arm trajectories.
claims.source: Figure S2G
claims.quote: Control and Cre animals slow similarly to novel arm trajectories
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. As figs2f-novelty-slowing-familiar ("Same as (F)") on novel arm trials, with the first two novel trials of block 6 as the measure and all novel trials of block 6 as a variant. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Cre mice have more variable running speed during reward approach (higher coefficient of variation) than control mice, on familiar and novel trials.
claims.source: Figures S2H-I; Results, Stx3-dependent postsynaptic membrane fusion in CA1 is critical for novel environment preference and reward anticipation, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Cre animals have more variable running speed during reward approach indicated by a higher coefficient of variation
claims.criterion: CV per 10 cm bin is the standard deviation over trials of running speed divided by its mean over trials, for the trials of a type on a day; the value per mouse and day is the mean CV over the bins in the 30 cm preceding the reward zone (Methods, VR behavioral analyses). Days 1 to 6, mixed effects ANOVA per trial type. Readings of the Cre mice as in fig1f. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with Cre higher for both trial types; partially when for one.

claims.statement: Controlling for the number of cells, position decoding error did not differ between control and Cre mice on familiar or novel trials.
claims.source: Figures 2C-D; Results, CA1 Stx3 deletion does not affect gross measures of place code quality and stability, paragraph 1
claims.quote: When controlling for the number of cells used in the decoders, we did not find significant differences in decoder error between models trained on data from control or Cre animals (Fig. 2C-D)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Naive Bayes decoder with uniform prior (maximum likelihood), rate maps from the trial-averaged activity rate of each cell in each bin on the training trials, Poisson log likelihood with continuous rates (the quasi-Poisson form of the Methods, whose equation the text omits), leave-one-trial-out cross-validation; error is the mean absolute distance between the most likely bin and the true bin, in cm; per mouse, 50 models each with 128 cells drawn with replacement, averaged (Methods, Naive Bayes decoding; Fig 2C legend). Per trial type, days 1 to 6, mixed effects ANOVA. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p >= 0.05 for both trial types.

claims.statement: Decoding error fell as the mice gained experience over days, on familiar and novel trials, with day 1 worse than every later day.
claims.source: Figures 2C-D; Results, CA1 Stx3 deletion does not affect gross measures of place code quality and stability, paragraph 1
claims.quote: the decoders’ performance improved as the animals gained experience in the environments over days
claims.criterion: Decoding error as in fig2cd-decoding-no-group-difference. Day main effect of the same ANOVA; posthoc paired t-tests over all 15 pairs of days, both groups pooled, Holm corrected (Fig 2C-D legends). Reproduced when for both trial types the day effect has p < 0.05 and day 1 error is significantly higher than each of days 2 to 6 (as the paper reports for both); partially when the day effect holds but not all five day 1 contrasts.

claims.statement: The fraction of cells with significant spatial information did not differ between control and Cre mice, on familiar or novel trials.
claims.source: Figure S3A; Results, CA1 Stx3 deletion does not affect gross measures of place code quality and stability, paragraph 1
claims.quote: There was also no difference between groups in the fraction of cells with significant spatial information or the stability of spatial representations within a day
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Fraction of the session's mCherry+ cells that are place cells (header, Place cells), per trial type and day, days 1 to 6; mixed effects ANOVA. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p >= 0.05 for both trial types.

claims.statement: Within-day stability of spatial representations, the mean trial by trial population vector correlation, was similar between control and Cre mice.
claims.source: Figure S3B
claims.quote: Average trial x trial population vector correlation for familiar (Left) and novel (Right) trials on each day shows similar within-day stability between conditions
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. For each pair of trials of a type on a day, the correlation of their population vectors; the mean over pairs per mouse and day; days 1 to 6; mixed effects ANOVA. The paper does not define the population vector correlation. Readings, (a) Pearson correlation of the flattened cells by bins matrices, (b) the mean over bins of the Pearson correlation of the cell vectors at each bin; cells, (i) all cells, (ii) the place cells of that trial type and day. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p >= 0.05 for both trial types under every reading; when readings disagree the claim is methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Place codes were largely uncorrelated between the familiar and novel arms (global remapping) in both groups, and the familiar to novel population vector correlation did not differ between control and Cre mice.
claims.source: Figure S3C; Results, CA1 Stx3 deletion does not affect gross measures of place code quality and stability, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Place cell codes were largely uncorrelated between the novel and familiar arms of the Y-maze in both groups (i.e. “global remapping”), indicating that contextual discrimination is intact after Stx3 deletion
claims.criterion: A claim of absence for the group comparison. Population vector correlation between the average familiar trial activity and the average novel trial activity on each day (Fig S3C legend), days 1 to 6, mixed effects ANOVA, with the readings of the correlation and cells of figs3b. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p >= 0.05. The "largely uncorrelated" part has no test or number in the paper; the notes give each group's mean familiar to novel correlation beside its within-type correlation from figs3b. The text cites Fig 3E-F for remapping, which is the place field analysis; Fig 2E-F and S3C show it.

claims.statement: The across-day population vector correlation of place cells tracked over all six days did not differ between control and Cre mice, for familiar or novel trials.
claims.source: Figures 2G-H; Results, paragraph after Figure 3 legend ("In order to compare the long-term stability")
claims.quote: the population vector correlation of average place cell responses across days did not significantly differ between groups (Fig. 2G-H)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Cells tracked across all six days; each cell's trial-averaged rate map per day; the day by day PV correlation matrix per mouse and its mean over the off-diagonal entries (the "average across day PV correlation"); unpaired t-test control against Cre. Readings, cells (a) all tracked cells (Fig 2G legend, "each cell"), (b) tracked place cells (Fig 2E-F, Results "place cell responses"), with the PV correlation readings of figs3b. Reproduced when p >= 0.05 for both trial types under every reading.

claims.statement: Position decoders trained on one day and tested on other days did not differ in accuracy between control and Cre mice.
claims.source: Figures S3D-G; Results, paragraph after Figure 3 legend ("In order to compare the long-term stability")
claims.quote: Spatial decoders trained across days also did not significantly differ in their accuracy between control and Cre animals (Fig. S3D-G)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Decoder as in fig2cd, using all cells tracked over the six days (Methods, Naive Bayes decoding), fit on the trials of one day and tested on the trials of each other day; the per mouse value is the average of the day by day error matrix (Fig S3E legend). Readings, (a) off-diagonal entries only, (b) with the diagonal filled by leave-one-trial-out within-day error. Unpaired t-test; reproduced when p >= 0.05 for both trial types under both readings.

claims.statement: In a separate morph VR task, Cre mice showed normal experience-dependent contextual remapping, with trial by trial similarity matrices like those of control mice.
claims.source: Figure S4D-E; Results, CA1 Stx3 deletion does not affect gross measures of place code quality and stability, paragraph 1
claims.quote: As a stronger test of intact contextual coding, Cre mice showed normal experience dependent contextual remapping patterns in a separate VR task71 (Fig. S4)
claims.criterion: The paper shows example similarity matrices only, for session 8 of example mice, and gives no measure, test or count of mice; the task's methods are cited to Plitt & Giocomo 2021 (ref 71) and not given here. Not specified by the paper; recorded so the finding is covered.

claims.statement: Place fields were present in CA2/3 and dentate gyrus imaged in Cre mice, on familiar and novel trials.
claims.source: Figure S5; Results, Spatial coding in Cre animals may be passively inherited from upstream activity, paragraph 1
claims.quote: place fields were intact in the CA3 region and the dentate gyrus in a small cohort of Cre mice in which we additionally injected the same GCaMP virus in these regions
claims.criterion: The paper shows example cells only (Cre-8 CA2/3 on day 1; Cre-7 DG in a session repeating day 6) and gives no count or test. The test the Methods allow is the place cell criterion of the header on those sessions; its 95% shuffle threshold admits about 5% of cells by chance. Reproduced when, on familiar and on novel trials of each session, the fraction of significant cells exceeds 5% with a binomial test p < 0.05. The 5% chance level follows from the paper's threshold; the paper states no count to match.

claims.statement: In the CA3-CA1 K-Winners-Take-All model, both the Plasticity and the No-Plasticity versions produce place-selective CA1 units with a spatially stable code from the first trial.
claims.source: Figures 3B-C; Results, Spatial coding in Cre animals may be passively inherited from upstream activity, paragraph 1
claims.quote: In both models, individual units were clearly place-selective, and the population maintained spatially stable place coding from the first trial (Fig. 3B-C)
claims.criterion: A simulation, not a test on recorded data. The Methods give M=N=1000, input variance 0.5 on x in [0,10], K=50, output noise 0.5N(0,1), stimulus noise 0.05N(0,1), eta 1e-4 and alpha 9e-4 (Plasticity) or 0 and 0 (No-Plasticity), weight noise 0.001N(0,1), wmax 10, lognormal initial weights (mean 0, sd 0.5). The text read omits the weight update equation and the input tuning function, and gives no number of trials, no position sampling and no measure of stability or place selectivity. Not specified by the paper; recorded so the finding is covered.

claims.statement: Place fields are wider in the Plasticity model than in the No-Plasticity model.
claims.source: Figure 3D; Results, Spatial coding in Cre animals may be passively inherited from upstream activity, paragraph 2
claims.quote: place fields were wider in the Plasticity model than the No-Plasticity model (Fig. 3D)
claims.criterion: A simulation, as fig3bc-model-stable-place-cells. The paper does not say how a model place field or its width is defined, nor the trial on which it is measured. Not specified by the paper; recorded so the finding is covered.

claims.statement: Units in the No-Plasticity model have more place fields per cell than units in the Plasticity model.
claims.source: Figure 3E; Results, Spatial coding in Cre animals may be passively inherited from upstream activity, paragraph 2
claims.quote: place cells from the No-Plasticity model were more likely to have multiple place fields per cell (Fig. 3E)
claims.criterion: A simulation, as fig3bc-model-stable-place-cells; the definition of a model place field is not given. Not specified by the paper; recorded so the finding is covered.

claims.statement: On familiar trials, place fields of Cre mice are narrower than those of control mice.
claims.source: Figure 3F; Results, Spatial coding in Cre animals may be passively inherited from upstream activity, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Place fields from Cre mice were narrower than those from control mice (Fig. 3F-G)
claims.criterion: Fields from the single place field method of the header on familiar trials of the day; width is the number of contiguous significant bins times 10 cm; per mouse and day, the mean over fields ("across cell average", Fig 3F legend; readings, mean over fields, or mean over cells of each cell's mean width). Which fields enter is open; readings, (a) all candidate fields of at least 20 cm, (b) only fields with a formation lap, as for the other single-field analyses. Days 1 to 5 mixed effects ANOVA; day 6 unpaired t-test. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with Cre narrower and the day 6 test has p < 0.05; partially when only one holds.

claims.statement: On novel trials, place fields of Cre mice are narrower than those of control mice.
claims.source: Figure 3G; Results, Spatial coding in Cre animals may be passively inherited from upstream activity, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Place fields from Cre mice were narrower than those from control mice (Fig. 3F-G)
claims.criterion: As fig3f-narrower-fields-cre-familiar, on novel trials.

claims.statement: On familiar trials, place cells of Cre mice have more place fields per cell than those of control mice.
claims.source: Figure 3H; Results, Spatial coding in Cre animals may be passively inherited from upstream activity, paragraph 2
claims.quote: place cells from Cre mice had more place fields on average than place cells from control mice (Fig. 3H-I)
claims.criterion: Number of fields per cell from the single place field method, with the field readings of fig3f; cells counted are, readings, (a) cells with at least one field, (b) place cells (SI significant) for that trial type and day. Per mouse and day the mean over cells; days 1 to 5 mixed effects ANOVA; day 6 unpaired t-test. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with Cre higher and the day 6 test has p < 0.05; partially when only one holds.

claims.statement: On novel trials, place cells of Cre mice have more place fields per cell than those of control mice.
claims.source: Figure 3I; Results, Spatial coding in Cre animals may be passively inherited from upstream activity, paragraph 2
claims.quote: place cells from Cre mice had more place fields on average than place cells from control mice (Fig. 3H-I)
claims.criterion: As fig3h-more-fields-per-cell-cre-familiar, on novel trials.

claims.statement: During block 6, population activity on familiar trials, relative to the preceding baseline, is lower in Cre mice than in control mice.
claims.source: Figures 4C and 4E; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for increased neural activity in novel environments, paragraph 1
claims.quote: control animals showed an overall larger increase in population activity rate than Cre animals in both trial types
claims.criterion: Each cell's position-binned activity rate on each block 6 trial is divided by that cell's mean activity rate over the 10 trials preceding block 6; the population value is log10 of the mean over all cells (Methods, Novel arm population activity rate); the per mouse and day value is its mean over bins and over the block 6 familiar trials. The Fig 4A legend instead takes the log per cell before averaging; that is undefined for bins with zero activity, which the paper does not treat, so it is shown as a variant where defined and does not decide. Days 1 to 5, mixed effects ANOVA; posthoc unpaired t-tests per day, Holm corrected. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with Cre lower.

claims.statement: During block 6, population activity on novel trials, relative to the preceding baseline, is lower in Cre mice than in control mice.
claims.source: Figures 4C and 4E; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for increased neural activity in novel environments, paragraph 1
claims.quote: control animals showed an overall larger increase in population activity rate than Cre animals in both trial types
claims.criterion: As fig4e-block6-familiar-activity-lower-cre, on the block 6 novel trials. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with Cre lower.

claims.statement: The difference between novel and familiar trial population activity in block 6 is larger in control mice than in Cre mice.
claims.source: Figure 4E; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for increased neural activity in novel environments, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The difference in the population activity rate between novel arm and familiar arm trials was also greater in control animals compared to Cre animals
claims.criterion: Per mouse and day, the novel trial value minus the familiar trial value of fig4e-block6-novel-activity-lower-cre and fig4e-block6-familiar-activity-lower-cre; days 1 to 5, mixed effects ANOVA. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with control larger.

claims.statement: In block 6 population activity increased above baseline on familiar and novel trials in both groups, more on the arms than on the stem, and more on novel than on familiar trials in both groups.
claims.source: Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for increased neural activity in novel environments, paragraph 1; Figure 4C
claims.quote: During this block of trials, we observed an increase in population activity for both familiar and novel arm trials. This increase in activity rate was larger on the arms of the Y-Maze than the stem and greater for novel compared to familiar arm trials in both control and Cre animals
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test. Measure of fig4e-block6-familiar-activity-lower-cre, averaged per mouse over days 1 to 5; group values are across-animal means. Holds when, in each group, (i) the familiar and the novel values are above 0, (ii) the value over arm bins exceeds the value over stem bins for each trial type, (iii) novel exceeds familiar. Where the stem ends is open; readings, (a) the first 150 cm (stem and arms are of equal length, Methods), (b) the first 100 cm (trajectories diverge two thirds of the way down the stem). Reproduced when all three hold in both groups; partially when some do.

claims.statement: The increase in activity on novel trials did not dissipate over days and grew stronger over the five days.
claims.source: Figures 4C and 4E; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for increased neural activity in novel environments, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The increase in activity rate for novel trials did not dissipate over days, and in fact grew stronger over the five days of the experiments (Fig. 4C & E)
claims.criterion: Novel trial values of fig4e-block6-novel-activity-lower-cre. Reproduced when the day main effect has p < 0.05 and the across-animal mean on day 5 exceeds that on day 1 (both groups pooled, as the day effect is).

claims.statement: On day 5 the larger activity increase of control mice is spread over a large part of the population, roughly half of the cells on novel trials, and is not due to a small population of highly active cells.
claims.source: Figure 4D; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for increased neural activity in novel environments, paragraph 2
claims.quote: we observed that roughly half of the cells displayed increased activity rates in control animals as compared to Cre animals. Thus, the effect is driven by a large proportion of the population and is not due to a small population of the highly active neurons (Fig 4D)
claims.criterion: The paper gives no test or measure for this panel (the legend refers to the tests of Fig 4C). Per cell, the block 6 novel trial activity of day 5, each position-binned rate divided by the cell's mean over the 10 trials preceding block 6 and averaged over bins and trials (Methods, Novel arm population activity rate; Fig 4D legend, "trial averaged activity rates across cells"); per mouse, the cumulative distribution over cells (a log transform does not change it). "Roughly half of the cells" is not defined by the paper; the reading used is that the across-animal mean control quantile exceeds the Cre quantile at every decile from the median (0.5) to 0.9, so that the shift is not confined to the top tail. Familiar trials are shown as a variant. Not a test; the notes give both groups' quantiles.

claims.statement: In the fourth (familiar) block, normalized population activity did not differ between control and Cre mice.
claims.source: Figure S6B; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for increased neural activity in novel environments, paragraph 1
claims.quote: These results were not driven by a general increase in activity rate over the course of imaging or increases in running speed during the last block of trials (Fig. S6 & S2F-G)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Measure of fig4e-block6-familiar-activity-lower-cre applied to block 4, each cell normalized by its mean over the 10 trials preceding block 4 (Methods, "the 10 trials preceding the block of trials to be analyzed"). Days 1 to 5, mixed effects ANOVA. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Familiar trial activity in block 6 depends on the number of trials since the last novel trial, in control and in Cre mice.
claims.source: Figure S6E; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for increased neural activity in novel environments, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The magnitude of the increase in activity rate during familiar trials also depended on the time since encountering a novel trial (Fig. S6)
claims.criterion: Per familiar trial of block 6, the population value of fig4e-block6-familiar-activity-lower-cre, grouped by the number of trials since the last novel trial; per mouse, day and group, the mean; a two-way repeated measures ANOVA (day and trials since novel, within) per virus group. The legend names 4 conditions and 5 days but prints F(2,.) and F(5,.), which fit 3 levels and 6 days; the Cre df fit 4 mice with complete data. Readings, levels (a) 1, 2, 3 trials since, (b) 1, 2, 3 or more; days (i) 1 to 5, (ii) 1 to 6. Reproduced when in each group the trials since novel effect has p < 0.05 under a reading. The paper states no direction for the effect; the notes give it.

claims.statement: Control mice allocate a greater proportion of place cells to the locations just before the reward zone than Cre mice, on familiar and novel trials.
claims.source: Figures S7A-B; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for place cell reward representations and memory, paragraph 1
claims.quote: we find that control animals allocate a greater proportion of place cells to rewarded locations than Cre animals (Fig. 5A-D & S7)
claims.criterion: Among the place cells of a trial type and day, the proportion whose peak of the trial-averaged rate map lies in the 50 cm preceding the front of that arm's reward zone (Methods, Reward overrepresentation analysis); logit transform; days 1 to 6, mixed effects ANOVA per trial type. The peak is taken from all trials of the type (the Methods' split halves are for the sequence plots). Proportions of 0 or 1, which logit cannot take, are clipped to half a cell (a standard choice, said if used). Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with control higher for both trial types; partially for one.

claims.statement: Control mice have a larger proportion of reward cells, active before the reward zone on both arms, than Cre mice, and the proportion changes over days.
claims.source: Figure 5D; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for place cell reward representations and memory, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Proportion of the population defined as “reward cells” shown for each mouse on each day. Statistical tests performed on logit transformed proportions
claims.criterion: A reward cell has significant spatial information on both familiar and novel trials and its peak lies near the front of the reward zone on both (Methods, Reward overrepresentation analysis). Readings, peak window (a) the 50 cm preceding the front of the zone (as in the same section's place cell rule), (b) within 50 cm of the front on either side ("within 50 cm of the front"); denominator, (i) all cells of the session ("proportion of the population"), (ii) cells significant on both trial types. Logit transform; days 1 to 6, mixed effects ANOVA. Reproduced when the virus main effect has p < 0.05 with control higher.

claims.statement: The proportion of reward cells increased over days in control mice.
claims.source: Figure 5D; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for place cell reward representations and memory, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The proportion of reward cells also increased over days for the control animals indicating accumulating plasticity in the place code (Fig. 5D)
claims.criterion: Proportions of fig5d-reward-cells-fewer-in-cre. The paper's test is the day main effect of that ANOVA, over both groups. Reproduced when it has p < 0.05 and the control across-animal mean on day 6 exceeds that on day 1 under a reading.

claims.statement: Averaged across days, the fraction of reward cells exceeds the level expected from random remapping in control mice but not in Cre mice.
claims.source: Figure 5D legend; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for place cell reward representations and memory, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Across-day average fraction of reward cells is greater than chance in control but not Cre animals
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the mean over days 1 to 6 of the reward cell fraction of fig5d-reward-cells-fewer-in-cre, against chance by a one sample t-test. Chance is "the proportion of reward coding neurons expected by random remapping between novel and familiar arms with constant coding for the stem of the maze" (Fig 5D legend), computed in a way the paper does not give. Readings, (a) per mouse and day, the reward cell fraction after randomly permuting across cells the novel trial peak locations of cells whose peaks lie on the arms, stem peaks kept (1,000 permutations, mean); (b) analytically, with arm peaks uniform over arm bins and independent between trial types, stem peaks equal. Reproduced when the control test has p < 0.05 above chance and the Cre test p >= 0.05 under a reading; partially when control holds and Cre is also above chance. The Discussion says Cre mice have more reward coding neurons than chance, which the legend's p=.080 does not support.

claims.statement: After the reward locations were switched, control mice kept licking at the old reward zone longer than Cre mice; a binomial mixed model of licking fits better than with shuffled group labels.
claims.source: Figures 5E-I; Results, CA1 Stx3 is necessary for place cell reward representations and memory, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The true model fit exceeded those from a shuffled distribution in which animal identities were scrambled, indicating that the Cre and control animals displayed significantly different licking behavior (Fig. 5H-I)
claims.criterion: Left arm trials after the reversal (day 7 from block 3, and day 8). Outcome per trial is whether the mouse licked more than once in the previous reward anticipatory zone. The paper names that zone two ways, "the previous reward anticipatory zone" (Fig 5H-I legends) and "the old reward zone" (Results). Readings, zone (A) the 30 cm preceding the old left reward zone (the anticipatory window of Methods, VR behavioral analyses), (B) the old 25 cm left reward zone itself. Binomial generalized linear mixed model in statsmodels (BinomialBayesMixedGLM, statsmodels' binomial mixed model) with trial number, virus and their interaction as fixed effects (the paper compares intercepts and slopes between groups) and a random intercept per mouse. Model fit is the mean log loss of the fitted probabilities; the null refits with virus labels permuted across mice (1,000 permutations, a standard choice); p is the fraction of shuffles with log loss at or below the true one. Open and run as readings, trial number (a) counted on from day 7 into day 8, (b) day 7 only; random effects (i) intercept, (ii) intercept and slope. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with control predicted to lick more.

claims.statement: Mice of both genotypes show sigmoidal psychometric curves, with the proportion of rightward choices increasing as the stimulus contrast increases on the right.

claims.statement: Psychometric bias, slope and lapse rates do not differ between WT and KO mice (bias p = 0.94, slope p = 0.95, left lapse p = 0.16, right lapse p = 0.22).

claims.criterion: Over the switches between biased blocks, the proportion of choices toward the new block side, by trial number after the switch (0 to 39), all contrasts. Lateralized when the peak pixel of the right-minus-left stimulus map and the peak pixel of the left-minus-right map lie on opposite sides of the midline, and at each peak the trials of the stimulus that defines it respond more than those of the other side (one-sided Mann-Whitney p < 0.05). claims.source: Figure 4C and 4D; Results, An encoding model reveals unique contributions of movement variables to cortical activity in Nrxn1α KO mice, paragraph 2
