claims.quote: L2/3 IT HPCAL1 neurons stood out with a small membrane time constant (tau) and narrow action potential (AP) width (Fig. 2d–f )
claims.criterion: Groups as in the code (opening comment); the legend counts 30 L2/3 IT HPCAL1, 17 IT RORB, 119 L5 IT FEZF2, 22 VEN, 16 L5 ET and 13 L6 PC neurons. Tau as in the Methods, an exponential f(t) = a exp(-t/tau) + C fitted from step onset to the sag minimum, averaged over all hyperpolarizing traces; the code's first-sweep tau is a variant. Test, two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the features of the comparison, as calFDR_ephsio.m does (the legend names the test; the paper's FDR values are in Supplementary Table 2, not read). The Methods do not list every feature ("The adaptation indices ... For instance"), so the code settles the FDR family, the 39 features of Ins_patchseq_ephs.xlsx that calFDR_ephsio.m takes, those the Methods define computed as defined there and the others as createFeatures.m computes them. The family of the 20 features the Methods name (rheobase, threshold, amplitude, rise and decay time, half-width, latency, AHP, maximal firing rate, sag value, sag ratio, sag time, sag area, RMP, input resistance, tau, rebound, ISI and amplitude adaptation indices and the latency slope) is a variant. "Stood out" allows two readings, as the code computes both, (a) L2/3 IT HPCAL1 against the other five pooled, and (b) against each other group. Reproduced when its median tau is the lowest of the six groups and the comparison has FDR < 0.05 (conventional) under (a) or every comparison does under (b); partially reproduced when the median is lowest but neither reading is significant. The code's plot exclusion (tau of 1 ms or less) is a variant.

claims.statement: L2/3 IT HPCAL1 neurons have a narrow AP width compared with the other projection neuron groups.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq revealed extensive cellular heterogeneity in the primate AIC, paragraph 3; Figure 2f
claims.quote: L2/3 IT HPCAL1 neurons stood out with a small membrane time constant (tau) and narrow action potential (AP) width (Fig. 2d–f )
claims.criterion: AP width is the half-width of the first AP of the rheobase sweep, at half the threshold-to-peak amplitude, threshold at the maximum third derivative in the 20 ms before the peak (Methods; the code plots Half_Width_ms as "AP width"). Tests and readings (a) and (b) as in fig2d-l23it-small-tau. Reproduced when its median half-width is the lowest of the six groups and the comparison is significant at FDR < 0.05 (conventional) under (a), or every comparison is under (b); partially reproduced when the median is lowest but neither reading is significant. The code table gives a lower median for IT RORB than for L2/3 IT HPCAL1, so "lowest" may fail with the claim still holding against the pooled groups; the rank and both readings are reported. The code's plot exclusion (widths outside 1 to 5 ms) is a variant.

claims.statement: IT RORB and L6 PC neurons have a distinctive input resistance among projection neuron groups.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq revealed extensive cellular heterogeneity in the primate AIC, paragraph 3; Figure 2e; Supplementary Figure 11
claims.quote: Other types exhibit specific characteristics including distinctive membrane resistance in IT RORB and L6 PC neurons
claims.criterion: Input resistance as in the Methods, the slope of steady-state voltage (last 100 ms of the step) minus RMP against injected current over the steps without APs; the code takes HEKA sweeps 1 to 6 (-200 to -100 pA) and the last two thirds of the step, a variant. The text does not give the direction; "distinctive" is read as differing from the other groups, and the direction is reported. Test and readings (a), each against the other five pooled, and (b), against each other group, as in fig2d-l23it-small-tau (Supplementary Fig. 11 and Table 2 not read). Reproduced when both IT RORB and L6 PC differ at FDR < 0.05 (conventional) under one reading; partially reproduced when one of them does.

claims.statement: L5 IT FEZF2 neurons have a higher AP threshold and a longer spike latency than the other projection neuron groups.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq revealed extensive cellular heterogeneity in the primate AIC, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 11
claims.quote: Other types exhibit specific characteristics including ... a higher AP threshold and longer spike latency in L5 IT FEZF2 neurons
claims.criterion: Threshold as in fig2f-l23it-narrow-ap; latency from step onset to the AP threshold of the first AP (Methods), in the rheobase sweep as the code takes it. Test and readings (a) and (b) as in fig2d-l23it-small-tau (Supplementary Fig. 11 not read). Reproduced when, under one reading, L5 IT FEZF2 has the higher median and FDR < 0.05 (conventional) for both features; partially reproduced when for one.

claims.statement: VENs have a broader AP than the other Patch-seq projection neuron groups.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq revealed extensive cellular heterogeneity in the primate AIC, paragraph 3; Figure 2f; Supplementary Figure 11
claims.quote: Other types exhibit specific characteristics including ... a broader AP width in VENs
claims.criterion: Half-width as in fig2f-l23it-narrow-ap. Test and readings (a) and (b) as in fig2d-l23it-small-tau. Reproduced when, under one reading, VENs have the highest median and FDR < 0.05 (conventional); partially reproduced when the median is highest without significance.

claims.statement: L5 ET neurons have a deeper sag than the other projection neuron groups.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq revealed extensive cellular heterogeneity in the primate AIC, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 11
claims.quote: Other types exhibit specific characteristics including ... and a deeper sag in L5 ET neurons
claims.criterion: The Methods define sag value (RMP minus steady state at the largest hyperpolarizing step), sag ratio, sag time and sag area; "deeper" names none, and the code table holds Sag_Ratio. Readings of the measure, (i) sag ratio and (ii) sag value. Test and readings (a) and (b) of the comparison as in fig2d-l23it-small-tau. Reproduced when, under every measure reading and one comparison reading, L5 ET has the deepest sag with FDR < 0.05 (conventional); blocked as methods_underspecified when the measure readings disagree.

claims.statement: VENs have lower firing rates and greater variability in spike timing than PCs.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq revealed extensive cellular heterogeneity in the primate AIC, paragraph 3; Supplementary Tables 1 and 2
claims.quote: Notably, VENs exhibit lower firing rate and greater variability in spike timing than PCs
claims.criterion: Firing rate is the maximal firing rate, the largest AP count over the 600 ms step (Methods). The text names no measure of spike-timing variability; readings from the code's feature table, (i) ISI CV (std/mean of the ISIs of the maximal-rate sweep, createFeatures.m) and (ii) ISI Fano factor of that sweep. "PCs" is read as (a) the five PC groups pooled, as calFDR_ephsio.m compares VEN against the others, (b) each PC group, and (c) the layer 5 PC groups pooled (L5 IT FEZF2 and L5 ET), as the Discussion says "Compared with neighbouring PCs". Test, two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR as in fig2d-l23it-small-tau (Supplementary Tables 1 and 2 not read). Reproduced when, under one comparison reading, VENs have a lower median firing rate and a higher median variability under both measure readings, each at FDR < 0.05 (conventional); partially reproduced when only the firing rate holds; blocked as methods_underspecified when the measure readings disagree.

claims.statement: L5 ET neurons have a deeper sag, a lower input resistance and a higher firing rate than L5 IT neurons.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Specifically, L5 ET neurons in macaque AIC consistently exhibit deeper sag, lower input resistance and higher firing rates than L5 IT neurons.
claims.criterion: L5 ET against L5 IT FEZF2, groups as in the code; sag readings as in supp11-l5et-deep-sag, input resistance as in supp11-rm-itrorb-l6pc, maximal firing rate as in ven-firing-rate-variability. Test, two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the features of the pairwise comparison (calFDR_ephsio.m, FDR_L5IT_vs_L5ET). Reproduced when all three differ in the stated direction at FDR < 0.05 (conventional); partially reproduced when two do.

claims.statement: The AP phase-plane plots of VENs show a more prominent biphasic shape than those of PCs, with the AIS phase decaying before the SD phase in a saddle-like shape.
claims.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 3; Figure 3d
claims.quote: VENs showed a more prominent biphasic phase than PCs. Different from PCs, the AIS phase of VENs exhibited a clear decay before the SD phase
claims.criterion: The paper shows six example cells and says it quantifies the 'saddle-like' shape by the phase peak index ("We used an index ... to quantify the 'saddle-like' shape"). The claim is therefore judged by fig3e-phase-peak-index and takes its outcome. The fraction of cells whose phase plot has a local minimum of dV/dt between the AIS and SD peaks (maximal-rate sweep, dV/dt smoothed over 5 samples as in calPhaseHeightIdx.m), VENs against the PC groups pooled, is not a measure the paper uses; it is shown as a description that does not decide.

claims.statement: VENs have lower phase peak indices than any PC group.
claims.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 3; Figure 3e
claims.quote: The VENs had lower phase peak indices than any type of PCs (Fig. 3e )
claims.criterion: Index (Psd - Pais)/(Psd + Pais), Psd and Pais the peaks of the SD and AIS phases of dV/dt against Vm; where a phase has no clear peak, "the point with the lowest derivative value" (Methods, Calculation of the phase peak index). The paper read the peaks by hand (calPhaseHeightIdx.m), so an automatic reading is fixed here and its open parts named. Sweep, the maximal-rate sweep (the code's). Peaks, Pais the first local maximum of smoothed dV/dt (5 samples) on the rising phase and Psd the largest maximum after it; with one maximum only, the point of the rising phase where d2V/dt2 is lowest (the shoulder) before the global maximum stands for the missing peak, which is how "lowest derivative" is read. Open, which APs, readings (a) the first AP of the sweep and (b) the median index over its APs. Test, Kruskal-Wallis over the six groups followed by Dunn's test (legend), with the correction not stated; readings Bonferroni and Sidak, at 0.05 (conventional). Reproduced when, under every AP reading and both corrections, the VEN median is the lowest and Dunn's test separates VENs from every PC group; partially reproduced when the median is lowest and some groups are separated; blocked as methods_underspecified when the AP or correction readings disagree. The automatic peak reading is not the paper's (the peaks were clicked by hand); when its outcome differs from the one the code's per-cell indices give, that is reported as a deviation. The code's per-cell values (PeakIdx_Fig5e.xlsx) are compared with the automatic ones as a check that does not decide.

claims.statement: APs of VENs (n = 281) are broader and lower in amplitude than those of L5 PCs (n = 306), throughout the spike train evoked by supra-threshold current.
claims.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 4; Figure 4a-c
claims.quote: APs in VENs were broader and had a lower amplitude compared with L5 PCs (Fig. 4a-c ). These differences were consistently observed throughout the spike train evoked by supra-threshold current injections.
claims.criterion: The 281 VENs and 306 L5 PCs are "additional" whole-cell recordings; the paper does not say where they are deposited, and the dandiset may hold only the Patch-seq cells. If the dataset holds them, the first near-threshold AP (rheobase sweep) is measured, amplitude and half-width as in the Methods; two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum, VEN against PC (Fig. 4a legend). Reproduced when VEN half-width is larger and amplitude smaller, each with p < 0.001, and the counts are within tolerance. "Throughout the spike train" is shown in Fig. 4c by the first and the penultimate AP of the supra-threshold train, with no test; the same comparison is run on the penultimate AP of the maximal-rate sweep and reported, and does not decide. If the dataset holds only the Patch-seq cells, the claim is blocked as data_missing, and the same comparison on the Patch-seq VENs and L5 PCs (the PC_L5 and L5 ET labels of the cell table) is shown as a variant that does not decide.

claims.statement: In real neurons the phase peak index decreases linearly with the distance of the AIS from the soma (n = 62).
claims.source: Figure 4i legend; Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Bottom: real neurons ( n = 62, each data point was averaged of 2–30 neurons except for the rightmost one with n = 1). Data are shown as mean ± s.e.m. Two-tailed Student’s t -test, P < 0.0001 for slope.
claims.criterion: AIS distance per neuron is a morphological measure the dataset does not hold; it comes from the reconstructions (NeuroMorpho.org doi:10.13021/y4be-0p18) or the code's NeuronPeakIdx_summary.mat (axonDist, 62 neurons), matched to the recordings by cell ID. Which 62 neurons is not said; they are taken as the Patch-seq cells with a reconstructed axon origin. Peak index as in fig3e-phase-peak-index, under its readings. As in Fig4itop_plot_PhasePeakIdx_vs_AISd.m, indices are averaged in 10 um bins of AIS distance and a line fitted to the bin means against the bins' left edges; the slope is tested by a two-tailed t-test (legend). Reproduced when the slope is negative with p < 0.05 under every peak-index reading. A regression on the 62 neurons is a variant. The ANCOVA against the model belongs to model-ais-distance-ap-shape and needs the simulations (data elsewhere, see the claims file of DANDI:001750).

claims.statement: AP width and amplitude do not differ between VEN-L (n = 85) and VEN-S (n = 41).
claims.source: Results, Multimodal profiling of two VEN subtypes, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 9c,d
claims.quote: Despite their distinct morphological and transcriptomic profiles, both VEN subtypes exhibited similar physiological properties (Extended Data Fig. 9 and Supplementary Table 8 )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the two features (Extended Data Fig. 9c,d legend), at 0.05 (conventional), on the first AP's half-width and amplitude. Reproduced when neither has FDR < 0.05, with the median differences reported; not reproduced when either does. The 85 and 41 cells are more VENs than the Patch-seq table holds (68) and the code identifies them by number only; the paper does not say where they are deposited. If the dataset does not hold them, the claim is blocked as data_missing and the test on the Patch-seq VEN-L and VEN-S is shown as a variant that does not decide.

claims.statement: Across electrophysiological features, VEN-L and VEN-S recorded without RNA extraction do not differ.
claims.source: Results, Multimodal profiling of two VEN subtypes, paragraph 2; Supplementary Table 8; github.com/RFLiu2021/AIC_proj at commit 44cd8a6, ephysio/calFDR_VENsubtype_ephysio.m
claims.quote: Despite their distinct morphological and transcriptomic profiles, both VEN subtypes exhibited similar physiological properties (Extended Data Fig. 9 and Supplementary Table 8 )
claims.criterion: Supplementary Table 8 (not read) gives "Quantified features and FDR-adjusted P values for comparisons of electrophysiological features between VEN-L and VEN-S", and the Extended Data Fig. 9 legend says these comparisons were "obtained without RNA extraction", so the paper's cells are the additional whole-cell recordings (as for ext9cd-ven-subtypes-ap), not the Patch-seq cells; the Patch-seq VEN-L against VEN-S comparison belongs to Supplementary Table 9 ("among Patch-seq recorded VEN-L, VEN-S and L5/6 CT"). Where the paper and the code disagree the paper comes first. A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test as in the Extended Data Fig. 9 legend and the code (calFDR_VENsubtype_ephysio.m), two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum per feature with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the feature family of fig2d-l23it-small-tau, at 0.05 (conventional). If the dataset holds the VEN-L and VEN-S recorded without RNA, with their subtype, reproduced when no feature has FDR < 0.05 and not reproduced when one does. If it does not, the claim is blocked as data_missing, and the same test on the Patch-seq VENs, grouped as calFDR_VENsubtype_ephysio.m does (VEN in cluster 16 against VEN in cluster 8) and by the expert labels VEN_Long and VEN_Short, is shown as a variant that does not decide, with the features of lowest FDR.

claims.statement: VEN-L differs more from L5/6 CT neurons in physiology than VEN-S does.
claims.source: Results, Multimodal profiling of two VEN subtypes, paragraph 2; Supplementary Table 9
claims.quote: Mirroring the transcriptomic similarity between VEN-S and L5/6 CT, VEN-L shows greater physiological disparity from L5/6 CT than does VEN-S (Supplementary Table 9 )
claims.criterion: As in calFDR_ephysCmp_VEN_vs_L56CT.m, VEN-L (cluster 16 VEN), VEN-S (cluster 8 VEN) and L5/6 CT (cluster 8 PC; n = 10 in the Extended Data Fig. 9i legend); two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum per feature with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR over the features of fig2d-l23it-small-tau. "Greater disparity" is not quantified in the text; it is read as more features with FDR < 0.05 (conventional) for VEN-L against L5/6 CT than for VEN-S against L5/6 CT. Reproduced when the count is larger for VEN-L; not reproduced when it is equal or smaller. The median FDR over features is reported as a second measure that does not decide.

claims.statement: Morphological differences between projection neuron groups are more pronounced than their physiological differences, with more features differing.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq revealed extensive cellular heterogeneity in the primate AIC, paragraph 3; Supplementary Tables 3 and 4, as cited (Supplementary Table 2 holds the electrophysiological FDR values)
claims.quote: Overall, morphological differences between projection neuron types were more pronounced than their physiological differences ( P < 0.05 for more features; Supplementary Table 3 and 4 )
claims.criterion: Morphological features (40, Methods, Extraction of morphological features) need the reconstructions (NeuroMorpho.org doi:10.13021/y4be-0p18), matched by cell ID. The comparisons are those of calFDR_ephsio.m and its morphological counterpart, each group against the rest and each pair, with BH FDR within each comparison. "More features" can be read as (a) the count or (b) the fraction of features with FDR < 0.05, summed over comparisons; the feature counts differ (40 morphological, the Methods' electrophysiological features). Reproduced when morphology exceeds physiology under both readings; blocked as methods_underspecified when they disagree.

claims.statement: Across pairs of projection neuron types, distances in membrane time constant correlate with transcriptomic distances (r = 0.53), and other morphoelectric properties show similar correlations.
claims.source: Results, Transcriptomic distinctions underlie phenotypic variation, paragraph 1; Figure 7a-i
claims.quote: Pooling the pairs across all clusters revealed a high correlation ( r = 0.53) between the membrane time constant (tau) distances and RNA distances (Fig. 7a–c ). Similar correlations extended to other morphoelectric properties
claims.criterion: Tau per cell from the dataset (fig2d-l23it-small-tau, both of its tau readings); the RNA side needs the scRNA-seq counts (GEO GSE319557). Per transcriptomic type, the tau distance is the Euclidean distance between type means; the transcriptomic distance is the correlation distance (1 - Pearson r) of mean log2(x + 1) 10x counts over the 500 most variable genes (Methods, Variability analysis; Results, "correlation distance"). Types, the 12 clusters with more than five mapped Patch-seq neurons, as the code's notebook (Fig7cf_supplFig16a_ephyFeatures_2_10X_Ext.ipynb) lists them (0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18); the Methods give no minimum. Pearson r over all pairs. The code instead takes the log of the mean Patch-seq counts over its own variable genes; that is shown as a variant. Reproduced when r is within tolerance with the Methods' tau; partially reproduced when r is positive with p < 0.05 but outside tolerance. The code's first-sweep tau is a variant that does not decide. The maximal firing rate (Fig. 7d-f) is shown the same way, with no stated r, and does not decide.

claims.statement: The whole-cell scRNA-seq atlas of the macaque AIC holds 122,663 transcriptomes in four classes, excitatory neurons (21,733, 17.8%), inhibitory neurons (17,007, 13.9%), glial cells (83,283, 67.8%) and vascular cells (640, 0.5%), divided into 78 transcriptomic types.
claims.source: Results, Transcriptomic landscape of the macaque AIC, paragraph 2; Figure 1b,c; Extended Data Figure 1e,f
claims.quote: we categorized these cells into four main classes: excitatory neurons (21,733 cells, 17.8%), inhibitory neurons (17,007 cells, 13.9%), glial cells (83,283 cells, 67.8%) and vascular cells (640 cells, 0.5%)
claims.criterion: Counted from the deposited cluster labels; tested in full under the claims file of DANDI:001750 (scrna-classes, scrna-78-types).

claims.statement: VENs are found only in layer 5b of the AIC and ACC; Extended Data Fig. 1d compares soma size and neuron density between AIC and V1 in layers 2/3 and 5, with no result stated in the text read.
claims.source: Results, Transcriptomic landscape of the macaque AIC, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 1a-d
claims.quote: The VENs, characterized by spindle-shaped perikarya and bipolar thick dendrites, were exclusively identified in layer 5b of the macaque AIC and anterior cingulate cortex (ACC)
claims.criterion: Not testable on this dataset. The text does not state the direction of the soma size and density differences; judged from the Source Data, two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum per layer, AIC against V1, with the correction under both readings the legend names (Bonferroni and Benjamini-Hochberg), at 0.05 (conventional), and the direction reported. Soma size from 105 AIC L2/3, 85 V1 L2/3, 90 AIC L5 and 90 V1 L5 cells; density from 15, 20, 15 and 20 ROIs, three animals per region (legend).

claims.statement: In Pan-Nav stained sections the AIS of VENs lies farther from the soma than that of PCs, and VENs have a shorter AIS.
claims.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 2; Figure 3c
claims.quote: showed that the AIS in VENs was, on average, located significantly farther from the soma than in PCs (Fig. 3c ). Additionally, VENs had a shorter AIS than PCs.
claims.criterion: Tested in full under the claims file of DANDI:001750 (fig3c-ais-distance-length), with the readings of the ANOVA's factors named there.

claims.statement: Somatic Na+ currents in outside-out patches are lower in VENs (n = 14) than in L5 PCs (n = 21).
claims.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 4; Figure 4d
claims.quote: outside-out patch-clamp recording showed that the somatic Na + currents evoked in VENs ( n = 14) were significantly lower than those of L5 PCs ( n = 21) (Fig. 4d )
claims.criterion: Tested in full under the claims file of DANDI:001750.

claims.statement: In the VEN model, moving the AIS farther from the soma makes APs wider and smaller and the phase-plane plot more saddle-like, while the PC model does not show this; the models reproduce the measured differences in AP amplitude and width, and the VEN model's linear decrease of the phase peak index with AIS distance matches that of the real neurons.
claims.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 5; Figure 4e-i; Extended Data Figure 7b
claims.quote: Crucially, simulating an increase in the distance of the AIS from the soma in the VEN model led to APs being wider and smaller in amplitude, and the phase–plane plot becoming more ‘saddle-like’, (Fig. 4g and Extended Data Fig. 7b ). This effect was not replicated in the PC model (Fig. 4h ). Furthermore, the linear decrease in the phase peak index with increasing AIS distance observed in the VEN model closely matched the experimental data
claims.criterion: Tested under the claims file of DANDI:001750 (fig4g-model-ais-distance-ap-shape and fig4i-peak-index-ais-distance), with the criteria named there.

claims.statement: Paired VENs and PCs respond to deep-layer stimulation with similar latencies (5.13 and 5.02 ms), and VEN eEPSPs are larger, for VEN-L and VEN-S alike.
claims.source: Results, VENs respond robustly to deep-layer synaptic input, paragraph 1; Figure 4j; Extended Data Figure 9e,f
claims.quote: The postsynaptic response latencies were similar between VENs and PCs (5.13 ± 0.29 ms for VENs and 5.02 ± 0.30 ms for PCs, two-tailed paired t -test ... whereas the response amplitudes in VENs were significantly higher than those in adjacent PCs
claims.criterion: Tested under the claims file of DANDI:001750 (fig4j-eepsp-latency and fig4j-eepsp-amplitude), with the readings named there.

claims.statement: VENs receive fewer spontaneous and miniature excitatory and inhibitory events than PCs at similar amplitudes, and form almost no local monosynaptic connections (PC-to-PC 24 of 503 pairs; VEN-to-VEN 0 of 110, VEN-to-PC 0 of 200, PC-to-VEN 1 of 200).
claims.source: Results, Altered connectivity profile of deep-layer AIC neurons, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 5b-i

PCs formed monosynaptic connections with other PCs in 24 out of 503 tested pairs
claims.criterion: Tested in full under the claims files of DANDI:001752 and DANDI:001751.

claims.statement: VEN-L has a long prominent basal dendrite and a larger basal arborization than PCs, VEN-S a short one similar to PCs; both have the axon origin farther from the soma than PCs. VEN-L expresses DSG2, HAPLN4, TOX2, TRPC4, CAMK1G and TAGLN2, VEN-S ATP8A2, POC5 and SEMA3E.
claims.source: Results, Multimodal profiling of two VEN subtypes, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 6a-j

claims.criterion: Tested under the claims file of DANDI:001750 (fig6-ven-subtype-morphology and fig6h-subtype-markers), with the readings named there.

claims.statement: Of 581 metabolites, 228 differ between AIC and V1 and 108 between AIC and parietal cortex, and AIC shows a glycolytic bias with elevated citrate, reduced 2-ketobutyrate and increased glutamate.
claims.source: Results, Cortical metabolomics reveals a glycolytic bias of the AIC, paragraphs 1 to 4; Figure 8
claims.quote: we identified 228 differentially abundant metabolites between the AIC and V1 (Welch’s ANOVA test followed by Games–Howell test, P < 0.05) compared with only 108 between the AIC and PrC
claims.criterion: Tested under the claims file of DANDI:001750 (fig8a-metabolite-gradient and fig8de-glycolytic-bias).

claims.statement: In the unimplanted cohort, relative dominants collected more rewards than relative subordinates when competing in dyads.
claims.source: Figure 1b; Results, first paragraph
claims.quote: Mice with higher relative ranks (dominant; Dom ) collected more rewards than relative subordinates ( Sub ) when competing in dyads
claims.criterion: Per dyad, total rewards won by the relative dominant and the subordinate over the session, as in the legend; Wilcoxon signed-rank test across the 12 dyads. Reproduced when p < 0.05 with dominants higher. Percent competitions won by absolute rank (6 per rank, Figure 1b right) is reported and not judged, as the text states no result for it.

claims.statement: In the unimplanted cohort, relative dominants had higher port occupation, higher pushing success, and higher time displaced from the port (as the legend words it) than relative subordinates.
claims.source: Figure 1c
claims.quote: Port occupation, pushing success (pushing that resulted in displacement of competitor), and time displaced from port was higher for relative dominants
claims.criterion: Per dyad, dominant against subordinate, Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on port occupation time, pushing success (percent of pushes that displaced the competitor, Methods 6, Reward competition behavioral analysis) and time displaced. The legend leaves open which way the displacement measure runs; readings (a) time spent displacing the competitor, as the main text says dominants "were more successful at displacing competitors", (b) time being displaced, as printed. Reproduced when all three tests give p < 0.05 with dominants higher under one reading.

claims.statement: In the unimplanted cohort, relative dominants have higher pushing success during the tone.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 1d
claims.quote: Relative dominant mice have higher pushing success during the tone (n=12 per group, paired t-test p=0.025)
claims.criterion: Pushing success (percent of pushes that displaced the competitor, Methods 6) during the 10 s tone, per mouse, paired across the 12 dyads. Reproduced when the paired t-test gives p < 0.05 with dominants higher.

claims.statement: In the unimplanted cohort, the distance to the reward port around the tone differs by trial outcome (win against lose) but not by relative rank.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 1g
claims.quote: Distance to reward port across time by trial type and relative rank
claims.criterion: Per trial, the mean AlphaTracker distance to the human-marked port location over the windows the legend gives (-5 s to tone onset; -5 s to +10 s); 2-way ANOVA of trial type by relative rank on trials. Reproduced when trial type has p < 0.05 and rank has p >= 0.05 in both windows; the legend gives no direction for trial type, which is reported. The rank result is a claim of absence judged on this test.

claims.statement: AlphaTracker tracks two unmarked mice with higher precision than human annotators.
claims.source: Figure 1e; Extended Data Fig. 2
claims.quote: AlphaTracker performance surpasses human accuracy when tracking 2 or 4 mice
claims.criterion: Needs the annotated evaluation frames of Methods 15 (800 frames from 4 videos, 200 double-annotated), which the paper does not deposit. Reproduced when AlphaTracker's average precision over body parts exceeds the between-human precision on those frames.

claims.statement: A 6-state HMM-GLM decodes the 9 behaviour labels from mPFC multi-unit activity above chance and better than a GLM or an ensemble of 9 GLMs, while the GLM and the 9 GLMs do not differ.
claims.source: Figure 1i; Extended Data Fig. 5j; Methods 17
claims.quote: An HMM-GLM model with 6 hidden states decoded behavioral labels from neural activity with superior cross-validated performance to static models
claims.criterion: Input, from Methods 17 (Dataset), multi-unit rates on the 32 channels after common average reference, spikes at 4 SD from the mean, in 70 bins of 200 ms per trial (aligned at -2 to +12 s from tone onset, from the dandiset description; the paper gives no alignment), and one of the 9 labels per bin. HMM-GLM as fixed by run_model.m and model_HMMGLM.m (see the opening comment). FT, GLM (multinomial logit, 9-output softmax), SVM (Gaussian kernel, one against all) and 9 GLMs (one logit GLM per label) as Methods 17 describe. Per behaviour, the AUC is the mean over the 10 folds. Tests as the legend gives them; the printed p-values match a two-sided sign test of 9 of 9 AUCs above 0.5 (0.0039) and an exact rank-sum with no overlap between 9 and 9 (4.1e-5). Reproduced when HMM-GLM AUCs exceed 0.5 by the sign test (p < 0.05), exceed the GLM and 9-GLM AUCs by rank-sum (p < 0.05), and the GLM against 9 GLMs rank-sum gives p >= 0.05 (a claim of absence, judged on that test). Open, with readings; spike threshold (a) negative crossings below mean minus 4 SD, (b) crossings in either direction; rates (a) counts per bin, (b) z-scored per channel; AUC (a) with the one-bin backward shift the Methods describe (auc_ROC_delay), (b) without (auc_ROC); folds (a) contiguous in session order, as the code forms them, (b) random. The processed input in the code repository is a variant input, not the basis of the outcome.

claims.statement: Held-out log-likelihood of the HMM-GLM increases with the number of hidden states and plateaus at 6 states.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5j, left; Methods 17, Cross-validation and Model Selection
claims.quote: We found that as you increase the number of hidden states, the log likelihood increases, reaching a plateau at the 6-state model
claims.criterion: Per number of states, the trial-averaged held-out log-likelihood over 10 folds, with SEM across folds (Methods 17), other settings as in fig1i-hmmglm-decodes-behaviour. The number of states tried is not given; read as 1 to 10. "Plateau" is not defined; readings (a) 6 is the smallest number whose mean lies within one SEM of the best mean, (b) 6 has the highest mean. Reproduced when one reading selects 6, partially reproduced when it selects 5 or 7.

claims.statement: The 6-state HMM-GLM predicts behaviour above chance whichever relative rank group is used for training and for testing.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5k; Results, mPFC neurons encode competition behavior
claims.quote: The model performed equally well when training for one relative rank and testing on the other
claims.criterion: The model of fig1i-hmmglm-decodes-behaviour trained on dom trials and tested on sub trials, and the reverse, plus within-group 10-fold runs. Per behaviour the AUC on the test trials. Reproduced when every train and test combination gives a sign test of the 9 AUCs against 0.5 at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In the recording cohort, rank 1 mice won the highest percentage of competitions.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5b
claims.quote: Percent competitions won by absolute rank is highest for rank 1 mice in dataset used for mPFC recordings
claims.criterion: A competition is won by the mouse that won more of its trials (the meaning ED Fig. 8d gives to a winner). Ties are not covered by the paper; readings (a) a tie counts as not won, (b) ties are left out. Reproduced when rank 1 has the highest percentage under one reading.

claims.statement: Among mice wearing loggers, relative dominants and subordinates obtained similar numbers of rewards, while the body weight difference between competitors correlated with rewards won.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5c
claims.quote: number of rewards obtained by relative dominants ( dom ) and subordinates ( sub ) during the reward competitions between animals wearing loggers
claims.criterion: The rewards part is a claim of absence judged on the paired t-test across the 22 pairs (reproduced when p >= 0.05). The correlation holds when Pearson p < 0.05, using only mice with a same-day weight.

claims.statement: In win trials, relative subordinates had longer latencies to pick up the reward than relative dominants.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5d
claims.quote: Subordinates had longer latencies to pick up the reward during win trials
claims.criterion: Latency of the winner's port entry to pick up the reward in win trials. No section of the Methods defines this latency; Methods 5 and ED Fig. 1a measure reward latency from tone onset. Readings (a) from tone onset, (b) from delivery at 2 s, which differ by a constant and give the same tests. Reproduced when the rank-sum gives p < 0.05 with subordinates slower. The RM-ANOVA is recorded as printed; its F and p do not agree (F(1,24) = 2.06 gives p near 0.16) and its factors are not given, so it is not judged.

claims.statement: Percent port occupancy during the tone did not differ by relative rank in the recording cohort.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5e
claims.quote: Percent port occupancy during tone across relative rank (n=31 sessions, paired t-test p=.90)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on a paired t-test of percent of the 10 s tone spent at the port, dom against sub per session. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; the difference is reported.

claims.statement: Relative dominants were more successful at displacing subordinates from the port, over the whole competition and during the tone.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5f
claims.quote: Relative dominants were more successful displacing subordinates from the reward port throughout the competition
claims.criterion: Displacement success as Methods 6 define pushing success (percent of pushes that displaced the competitor), from the hand-scored labels, dom against sub per session, paired t-test. Reproduced when both give p < 0.05 with dominants higher.

claims.statement: Total time being displaced from the port did not differ by relative rank in the recording cohort.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5g
claims.quote: Total time being displaced from reward port by relative rank in dataset used for mPFC recordings (n=31 sessions; paired t-test p=0.15)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on a paired t-test of total time labelled displaced, dom against sub per session. Reproduced when p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: mPFC trajectories for win and lose trials, and for self and other port entries, occupy segregated subspaces, already before cue onset.
claims.source: Figure 2a; Results, mPFC reflects rank and winning
claims.quote: Neural trajectories during the cue and port entries of the self or other (competitor) for win or lose trials occupied segregated neural activity subspaces even before the cue onset
claims.criterion: The paper gives no test and no measure of segregation. With the shared trajectory method, the bin-by-bin distance between the win and lose trajectories over -5 to 0 s is compared with the distance between trajectories of two random halves of the data over 50 iterations, the only reference distance the paper reports (ED Fig. 7g-h, right). The paper gives no threshold for this comparison; readings (a) the win against lose distance exceeds the mean random-half distance, (b) it exceeds the 95th percentile of the random-half distances. Reproduced when, for dom and for sub, both readings agree that it exceeds; when they disagree the claim is methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: The alignment of win and lose trajectories is lower for relative dominants than for relative subordinates.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 6d
claims.quote: alignment of win and lose trajectories was significantly lower for dominant mice
claims.criterion: Alignment index of Methods 14 (after Miri et al.), Tr(P1' Cov(D2) P1) / Tr(P2' Cov(D2) P2), with D1 and D2 the neurons by time-bin mean rates for win and lose trials (-5 to 5 s, 100 ms) and P1, P2 their principal components, per leave-one-animal-out iteration (13 per group). The number of PCs is not given; readings (a) as many as reach 90% of each condition's variance, (b) the first 8, as in the SVM, (c) the first 3, as plotted. Reproduced when the rank-sum gives p < 0.05 with dominants lower.

claims.statement: Relative subordinates have longer neural trajectories than relative dominants for win and for lose trials.
claims.source: Figure 2b; Results, mPFC reflects rank and winning
claims.quote: Relative subordinates had longer neural trajectories compared to relative dominants
claims.criterion: Shared trajectory method, tone-aligned win and lose trials, groups by relative rank in the session. Per leave-one-animal-out iteration (14 dom, 13 sub, giving 25 error df), length over baseline (-5 to 0 s) and over event (0 to 5 s); 2-way RM-ANOVA, rank between and event within. Reproduced when, for win and for lose, the rank effect has p < 0.05 with sub longer, under the shared readings.

claims.statement: Firing rate variance is higher for relative subordinates, and firing rates do not change faster for them.
claims.source: Figure 2b, right; Results, mPFC reflects rank and winning
claims.quote: our analyses revealed larger firing rate variance, but not faster firing rate changes, for relative subordinate mice
claims.criterion: Per neuron, dom against sub, KS test and Wilcoxon rank-sum as in the legend. Variance is not defined; readings (a) variance over 100 ms bins of the trial-averaged rate from -5 to 5 s, (b) the same over 0 to 5 s, (c) variance across trials of the 0 to 5 s rate. Reproduced when, under one reading, lose trials give p < 0.05 in both tests and win trials give KS p < 0.05, with sub higher.

claims.statement: Firing rate rate of change is higher for relative dominants in win trials only.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 6c
claims.quote: Firing rate rate of change is higher for relative dominants only in win trials
claims.criterion: Per neuron, dom against sub. Rate of change is not defined; readings (a) mean absolute difference between adjacent 100 ms bins of the trial-averaged rate over -5 to 5 s, (b) the same over 0 to 5 s. Reproduced when, under one reading, win trials give p < 0.05 in both tests with dom higher and lose trials give p >= 0.05 in both (absence judged on those tests).

claims.statement: Within intermediate-rank mice (ranks 2 and 3), trajectories for win and lose trials are longest when the mouse is the relative subordinate.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 6b
claims.quote: Neural trajectory lengths (using principal components that captured 90% of variance) for win and lose trials are highest for relative subordinates in intermediate (ranks 2 or 3) mice
claims.criterion: Shared trajectory method restricted to sessions of rank 2 and 3 mice, grouped by relative rank. Reproduced when both rank effects have p < 0.05 with sub longer.

claims.statement: Trajectory lengths for self and other port entries, during the tone and during the ITI, are higher for relative subordinates.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 6e-f
claims.quote: trajectory lengths (using PCs that captured 90% of variance) for self entry (top) and other entry (bottom) during the tone are higher for relative subordinates
claims.criterion: Shared trajectory method on port entries of the subject (self) and of the competitor (other), during the tone or outside it (ITI). Reproduced when all four rank effects have p < 0.05 with sub longer; partially reproduced for two or three.

claims.statement: In the recording cohort, distance to the reward port differed by trial type but not by rank.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 7b
claims.quote: Distance to reward port differed by trial-type but not by rank
claims.criterion: Per trial, mean AlphaTracker distance to port; the window is not given, readings (a) -5 to 0 s, (b) 0 to 5 s, (c) -5 to 5 s from tone onset, from ED Fig. 7a. Reproduced when, under one reading, trial type has p < 0.05 and rank has p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: The correlation of single-unit firing rate with distance to port does not differ by rank.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 7c
claims.quote: Distribution of the correlation coefficients for firing rate and distance to port for the population of mPFC single units did not differ by rank
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Per unit, the correlation of binned firing rate with distance to port over the session; bin width not given, 100 ms (the PCA bin) is used as a standard choice, and Pearson as the default correlation. Reproduced when the KS test gives p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Trajectories are longer for relative subordinates in win and lose trials whether the mice were close to or far from the port at tone onset.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 7d-e
claims.quote: Neural trajectory lengths were higher for relative subordinates during win trials in which mice were close or far to the reward port during tone onset
claims.criterion: Shared trajectory method on sessions with matched video conditions (dom 19, sub 18 sessions, leaving out one session per iteration). The split between close and far is not given; readings (a) median split of distance at tone onset, (b) within or outside the port contact range. Reproduced when all four rank effects have p < 0.05 with sub longer under one reading.

claims.statement: Trajectories remain longer for relative subordinates after removing cells correlated with distance to port.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 7f
claims.quote: neural trajectories for self entry during the tone are highest for relative subordinates without the distance correlated cells
claims.criterion: Shared trajectory method on 18 dom and 18 sub sessions after removing cells whose correlation with distance (ed7c) is significant; the level is not given, readings (a) p < 0.05, (b) p < 0.01. The second panel's event is not named; it is read as win trials. Reproduced when both rank effects have p < 0.05 with sub longer.

claims.statement: Trajectory lengths from two random halves of the data show no group effect, so the rank effect is not due to chance.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 7g-j
claims.quote: trajectory lengths for win and lose trials when data is divided randomly show no effect of group indicating that the effect of rank is not due to chance
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. 50 random splits of the data from 49 sessions of 20 mice into two halves; per split, trajectory lengths of each half for baseline and event; 2-way ANOVA of event by group on the 50 iterations (F(1,196) fits 50 x 2 x 2 values). What is split is not given; readings (a) sessions, (b) neurons. The legend says "bootstrapping"; halves are drawn without replacement, as "halves" implies. Reproduced when all six group effects have p >= 0.05 under the paper's test.

claims.statement: An SVM decodes competitive success and relative rank from single-trial mPFC population activity above chance, and rank more accurately than outcome.
claims.source: Figure 2c; Results, mPFC predicts future wins
claims.quote: An SVM was able to decode both competitive success and relative rank
claims.criterion: Shared SVM method, labels win against lose, or dom against sub. Which window forms the features of Figure 2c is not fixed; readings (a) -5 to 5 s, (b) -30 to 30 s. Reproduced when, under one reading, both AUC sets exceed shuffled by rank-sum at p < 0.05 and rank AUCs exceed outcome AUCs at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: mPFC activity predicts whether the next trial will be won or lost about 30 s before the trial begins, with decoding above chance across the trial.
claims.source: Results, mPFC predicts future wins; Figure 2c
claims.quote: PFC neural activity could predict whether the next trial would be a win or a loss ~30 seconds before the competition trial began
claims.criterion: Shared SVM method on win against lose with features from -30 to 0 s before the cue only. The time resolution of Figure 2c is not given; readings (a) one model on all of -30 to 0 s, (b) separate models on 5 s windows from -30 s, as the -5 to 5 s feature window suggests. Reproduced when AUCs exceed shuffled by rank-sum at p < 0.05 for reading (a), or for the -30 to -25 s window and every later window under reading (b).

claims.statement: Win and lose decoding trained on relative dominants generalizes to subordinates, but decoding trained on subordinates does not generalize to dominants.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 8b-c
claims.quote: mPFC population encoding of win/lose in relative dominants generalizes to relative subordinates
claims.criterion: Shared SVM method on win against lose, trained on one group's trials and tested on the other's (10 models from the folds of the training group). Reproduced when dom/dom, dom/sub and sub/sub exceed shuffled at p < 0.05 and sub/dom gives p >= 0.05 (absence judged on that test).

claims.statement: Competition outcome decoders trained on winner mice and tested on loser mice, and the reverse, perform above chance during the cue, and better during the cue than at baseline.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 8d
claims.quote: Decoder performance for classifying competition outcome using training data from winner data
claims.criterion: Winner and loser mice are those that won or lost the majority of trials. Baseline is read as -5 to 0 s and cue as 0 to 5 s (the -5 to 5 s window of the Methods). The legend does not say which panel is which; the order of the sentence is used (left winner to loser). Reproduced when both cue decoders beat shuffle at p < 0.05 and both sign-rank tests on the 10 folds give p < 0.05 with cue higher.

claims.statement: Relative rank can be decoded in intermediate-rank mice (ranks 2 and 3).
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 8e; Results, mPFC predicts future wins
claims.quote: SVM performance for decoding relative rank specifically for intermediate (ranks 2 or 3) mice
claims.criterion: Shared SVM method on trials of rank 2 and 3 mice, labelled by relative rank. Reproduced when AUCs exceed shuffled at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Absolute rank can be decoded from mPFC population activity during competition (one model per rank, and rank 1 against rank 4) and while mice perform the task alone.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 8f-h; Results, mPFC predicts future wins
claims.quote: Notably, we can decode the absolute social rank of individuals from mPFC activity, even when alone
claims.criterion: Shared SVM method, one against all for each absolute rank (Methods 14). "Mean performance across ranks" is read as the per-fold AUC averaged over the four models, against the same for shuffled labels. Reproduced when all three comparisons give p < 0.05.

claims.statement: mPFC activity decodes alone tone trials from win trials of the same session, but does not decode early from late trials within a task.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 8i-j
claims.quote: mPFC population activity can decode between alone tone presentations and win trials during the competition trials
claims.criterion: Shared SVM method on the sessions with alone trials followed by competition trials. Early and late are not defined; read as the first and second half of the trials of each task. Reproduced when alone against win exceeds shuffled at p < 0.05 and both early against late tests give p >= 0.05 (absence judged on them).

claims.statement: Tone trajectories are longer for subordinates during competition, and the distance between alone and competition tone trajectories increases from rank 1 to rank 4.
claims.source: Figure 2d-e; Results, mPFC predicts future wins
claims.quote: Subordinate mice (rank 4) had larger changes induced by competition with longer tone trajectory lengths during competition
claims.criterion: Shared trajectory method, groups by absolute rank (1, 2 and 3, 4) and task (alone, competition), tone-aligned; for competition all trials are read as used. How the common subspace is built is not given; readings (a) one PCA on alone and competition tone rates together, (b) the competition global PCA with alone rates projected. The distance is over all pairs of alone and competition leave-one-out trajectories. Reproduced when rank 4 has the longest competition trajectory with the interaction p < 0.05, and the distance rises from rank 1 to rank 4 with the 1-way ANOVA p < 0.05, under one reading.

claims.statement: mPFC single units have diverse responses to tone and port-entry events, form functional clusters, and the distribution across clusters differs between relative dominants and subordinates.
claims.source: Figure 3a; Extended Data Fig. 9a; Methods 14
claims.quote: mPFC single units showed diverse responses to the tone for win or lose trials and to port entries performed by self or the other
claims.criterion: As Methods 14 describe, the concatenated mean rates of the six events, cells with baseline rate at or above 0.05 Hz, agglomerative clustering on Euclidean distance cut at 0.4. The linkage is not given; readings (a) MATLAB linkage default (single), (b) Ward. Strong responders have a mean z-score of at least 2 or at most -1 for at least one event (Methods 14, ED Fig. 9a). The paper reports no test of the rank difference in cluster distribution, only the percent enrichment per cluster (Figure 3a right); that part is shown, under each linkage, and not judged. The outcome rests on the counts against the expected values.

claims.statement: In win trials, excitation magnitude differs by relative rank (larger in subordinates) with no difference in the number of responsive cells; lose trials differ in neither.
claims.source: Figure 3b; Results, Rank-dependent mPFC representations
claims.quote: subordinates had larger responses to win trials and port entries of the other
claims.criterion: Shared responsive-cell method, tone-aligned win and lose trials, groups by relative rank, 20 mice. Reproduced when win excited magnitude gives p < 0.05 with sub higher, and the four lose tests and the win Fisher test give p >= 0.05 (absence judged on them).

claims.statement: Relative dominants have more cells responsive to their own port entries during the tone; for the competitor's port entries the number does not differ but excitation magnitude is larger in subordinates.
claims.source: Figure 3c
claims.quote: number of mPFC self tone port entry responsive cells was higher for relative dominants
claims.criterion: Shared responsive-cell method on port entries during the tone, by self or by the competitor. Reproduced when self Fisher gives p < 0.05 with dom more and other excitation gives p < 0.05 with sub larger, and other Fisher gives p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: During the ITI, relative dominants have more cells responsive to self and to other port entries, while subordinates have larger excitation magnitudes.
claims.source: Figure 3d
claims.quote: relative dominants had more mPFC responsive cells to self port entries during the ITI while relative subordinates had larger excitation magnitude
claims.criterion: Shared responsive-cell method on port entries outside the tone. Reproduced when both Fisher tests give p < 0.05 with dom more and both excitation tests give p < 0.05 with sub larger.

claims.statement: While mice perform the task alone, rank 1 and rank 4 mice do not differ in the number of responsive cells or response magnitude to the tone, tone port entries or ITI port entries.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 9b; Results, Rank-dependent mPFC representations
claims.quote: During competition, but not while alone, relative dominants had more cells that were responsive to self port entries
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Shared responsive-cell method on alone sessions of rank 1 and rank 4 mice. Reproduced when the three Fisher tests and the rank-sum tests on magnitudes all give p >= 0.05; counts are reported against the legend's.

claims.statement: During competition, dominants have more cells responsive to self port entries than subordinates by absolute rank (1 against 4, during the tone and the ITI), and within intermediate mice by relative rank during the tone (not significant during the ITI, p = 0.06).
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 9c-d
claims.quote: Total responsive cells and response magnitude to task-relevant event during social competition for absolute rank 1 vs rank 4
claims.criterion: Shared responsive-cell method. Reproduced when the rank 1 against 4 self entry tests (tone and ITI) and the intermediate tone test give p < 0.05 with dominants having more. The intermediate ITI test is reported and not judged.

claims.statement: Ex vivo, ChrimsonR-expressing mPFC-BLA and mPFC-LH cells respond to red light with shorter latencies than neighbouring cells, which sets the phototagging latency threshold.
claims.source: Figure 4a
claims.quote: average photo-latency of action potentials (AP) or excitatory postsynaptic potentials (EPSPs) for mPFC-BLA (left plot) and mPFC-LH (right plot) ChrimsonR+ cells compared to neighboring cells
claims.criterion: Latency from light onset to the peak AP or EPSP, averaged over 10 pulses (Methods 16). Reproduced when both t-tests give p < 0.05 with ChrimsonR+ shorter.

claims.statement: Phototagging identified mPFC-LH and mPFC-BLA neurons in 3 of 12 and 3 of 8 mice.
claims.source: Methods 12; Figure 4b; Extended Data Fig. 10c
claims.quote: 3 out of 8 mice had mPFC-BLA phototagged cells and 3 out of 12 mice had mPFC-LH phototagged cells
claims.criterion: Phototagging as the shared method gives. ED Fig. 10c gives 43 mPFC-LH neurons and Figure 4b 42; both readings are accepted. Mouse counts are compared exactly.

claims.statement: mPFC-LH neurons fire more than mPFC-BLA neurons during reward delivery in win trials of the competition, but not when the task is performed alone; mPFC-LH tone responses differ between alone and competition.
claims.source: Figure 4b; Results, mPFC-LH neurons modulate dominance
claims.quote: We found that mPFC-LH neurons had stronger excitation to reward delivery than mPFC-BLA neurons during reward competition, but not when performing the task alone
claims.criterion: Per tagged neuron, the mean response over win trials (competition) or tone trials (alone). The legend's "reward delivery (0-2 s)" is read (a) as 0 to 2 s after delivery (2 to 4 s after tone onset), (b) as 0 to 2 s after tone onset; the measure is (a) z-scored rate, as the legend's alone comparison uses, (b) raw rate. The alone against competition test is not named; it is read as a rank-sum (different neuron counts), over the tone read as (a) 0 to 10 s, (b) 0 to 5 s. Reproduced when, under one reading, LH exceeds BLA at p < 0.05 in competition, the alone comparison gives p >= 0.05, and mPFC-LH alone against competition gives p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Proportions of cells responsive to tones and port entries differ between mPFC-LH and non-phototagged cells.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 10c
claims.quote: Responsive cells to tones and port entries while performing the reward task alone vs in social competition
claims.criterion: Shared responsive-cell method. The legend does not say which event the Fisher test is for; a Fisher test on the printed counts gives 0.006 for alone entries during tone and 0.06 for competition self entries during ITI, neither 0.011. Readings are each event of the legend. Reproduced when, under one reading, the responsive fraction of mPFC-LH cells exceeds that of non-phototagged cells at p < 0.05, and the counts are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Stimulating mPFC-LH neurons in subordinate mice increased trials won and reward port occupation and decreased time being displaced.
claims.source: Figure 4c-d; Results, mPFC-LH neurons modulate dominance
claims.quote: ChR2-expressing mice won more rewards during the entire competition, had greater reward port occupation, and spent less time being displaced when they received optical stimulation
claims.criterion: Light OFF session against light ON session, per mouse, whole session (Methods 5). Reproduced when the two interactions give p < 0.05, the ChR2 post hoc tests give p < 0.05 with ON higher, and the ChR2 displacement test gives p < 0.05 with ON lower.

claims.statement: mPFC-LH stimulation did not change reward latency alone, home-cage feeding, social preference, open-field anxiety, place preference or effort-based choice.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 10e-k; Results, mPFC-LH neurons modulate dominance
claims.quote: stimulating mPFC-LH neurons did not affect reward-seeking behavior while performing the reward competition assay alone, feeding in the home cage, anxiety, sociability, place preference or general effort
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's tests; paired t-tests for e and g, and 2-way RM ANOVA (light, virus, interaction) for f, h, i and k. Reproduced when none finds an effect at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The dandiset's recordings are the 35 outside-out patches of the paper's code table (14 VEN and 21 PC), and the maximal Na+ current computed from each recording agrees with the value the table gives for it.
claims.source: Data availability; github.com/RFLiu2021/AIC_proj at commit 44cd8a6, ephysio/data_ephy/rawdata_ephysio/metadata_outSideOutSodiumCurrentRec.csv
claims.quote: https://dandiarchive.org/dandiset/001750 (sodium channel currents)
claims.criterion: Recordings are matched to table rows by NWB file name (fileName_nwb), and the cell type is compared with the dataset's own label where it has one. For each cell, the maximal peak inward current is computed under each reading of fig4d-sodium-current-lower. The link holds (reproduced) when all 35 files are found, every cell type the dataset gives agrees with the table, and, under at least one reading, the absolute computed maximum is within 10% of the absolute max_Na_current for at least 28 of the 35 cells. Partially reproduced when the files and types match but fewer than 28 values agree under every reading; not reproduced when files are missing or types disagree. Which reading agrees best is reported; it does not choose the reading for the finding, which is judged under all of them.

claims.statement: Somatic Na+ currents recorded in outside-out patches are significantly lower in VENs (n = 14) than in L5 PCs (n = 21).
claims.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 3; Figure 4d
claims.quote: outside-out patch-clamp recording showed that the somatic Na + currents evoked in VENs ( n = 14) were significantly lower than those of L5 PCs ( n = 21) (Fig. 4d )
claims.criterion: Selection, every outside-out patch of a VEN or an L5 PC, typed as the dataset labels it or, when it does not, as metadata_outSideOutSodiumCurrentRec.csv does (through na-cell-table-link). Protocol, steps from -80 to 0 mV in 5 mV increments, 25 ms, leak subtracted online (Methods). Measure, per patch, the largest peak inward current over the steps, as an absolute value in pA; the code compares abs(maxNaCurrent) in pA (Fig4d_plotNaCurrent.m), and the Methods' model section speaks of "peak sodium current", so current, not current density, is compared. Repeated sweeps of a step are averaged before the peak is taken, as the code does for its example traces. Open and run as readings, (a) baseline, (a1) the trace as recorded, already leak subtracted (Methods), or (a2) a pre-step baseline subtracted as in the code's example traces, the mean of the first 100 samples of a cut starting 2 ms before the step onset (2 ms at 50 kHz, 1 ms at 100 kHz); (b) steps, (b1) the 17 steps from -80 to 0 mV (Methods, and the code's nTraces = 17) or (b2) every step recorded (the code's example array holds 28); (c) window, (c1) 0 to 20 ms after the step onset (the code's plotted window) or (c2) the whole 25 ms step (Methods). The sampling rate and step onset are read from each file, as the code's examples differ (50 kHz and 40 ms against 100 kHz and 20 ms). Test, two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum, VEN against PC (Fig. 4d legend; ranksum in the code), at p < 0.05 (conventional; the panel's P value was not readable). Reproduced when, under every reading, the VEN median is lower with p < 0.05 and the counts are within tolerance; not reproduced when the VEN median is not lower or p >= 0.05 under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when readings disagree. The two-sample t-test the code also runs, and the current density (current over the area from each patch's capacitance at 1 uF/cm2, Methods), are shown as variants that do not decide.

claims.statement: The VEN model's somatodendritic Na+ conductance (55 pS/um2, against 80 pS/um2 in the PC model) was set from the recorded ratio of peak Na+ current in VENs to PCs, which puts that ratio near 55/80, about 0.69.
claims.source: Methods, Computational model, paragraph 3
claims.quote: The VEN model's somatodendritic conductance (55 pS µm −2 ) was set based on the experimentally recorded ratio of peak sodium current in VENs relative to PCs. (Fig. 4d )
claims.criterion: The ratio is not printed; 0.6875 is 55/80, both values from the Methods, and "set based on" may allow rounding, so the 10% tolerance stands. The Extended Data Fig. 7c legend says the range of somatic Na+ conductance "was defined by experimental data and previous publications", so 55 pS/um2 may not be the recorded ratio alone; this is reported with the result. The per-patch maxima of fig4d-sodium-current-lower, under each of its readings. Which group summary forms the ratio is not said; readings of the reported number, (i) mean VEN over mean PC and (ii) median VEN over median PC. Reproduced when the ratio is within tolerance under one summary reading for every reading of the measure; partially reproduced when it is within tolerance for some readings of the measure only; not reproduced otherwise.

claims.statement: The outside-out patches have a capacitance of about 50 fF, a membrane area of about 5 um2 at 1 uF/cm2, and similar membrane areas were sampled from both cell types.
claims.source: Methods, Electrophysiological recording, paragraph 2
claims.quote: No differences in the degree or time of suction applied to the back of pipettes were required to form high resistance (3–10 GΩ) seals at somatic sites, suggesting that similar membrane areas were sampled ... the membrane surface area (~5 µm 2 ) of outside-out patches was calculated from the capacitance (~50 fF) assuming a specific membrane capacitance of 1 µF cm −2
claims.criterion: Per patch, the capacitance recorded with the patch (as the dataset stores it, for example the PatchMaster slow or fast capacitance compensation value), and the area as capacitance over 1 uF/cm2 (Methods). The "~" values are not said to be a mean or a median; readings of the reported number, the mean and the median over all 35 patches. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading. The paper reports no test of VEN against PC patch size (its "similar" rests on the suction applied); VEN and PC medians and a two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum test are shown as a description that does not decide. Blocked as data_missing when the dataset holds no patch capacitance.

claims.statement: In the PC model, lowering the somatodendritic Na+ conductance over the tested range (80 to 55 pS/um2, defined by experimental data and previous publications) only modestly changes the AP (slightly lower and broader) and does not produce the saddle-like phase-plane shape.
claims.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 5; Extended Data Figure 7c
claims.quote: A reduction in somatodendritic Na + channel density in the PC model only produced modest changes in AP shape (slightly lower amplitude, broader width) but did not induce the saddle-like phase–plane pattern.
claims.criterion: Simulations of the PC model as in the Methods (Computational model) with somatodendritic Na+ conductance from 55 to 80 pS/um2. Reproduced when AP amplitude rises and half-width falls with the conductance, each slope with two-tailed t-test p < 0.05 (Extended Data Fig. 7c legend), and the phase-plane plot shows no decay of the AIS phase before the SD phase at any value.

claims.statement: Simultaneous recordings of up to eight layer 5b neurons tested 1,292 potential connections among 377 neurons and found 31 monosynaptic connections.

claims.statement: VENs form no connections with VENs (0 of 110), PCs (0 of 200) or interneurons (0 of 55), receive none from interneurons (0 of 55) and one in 200 PC-to-VEN pairs, while PCs connect to PCs in 24 of 503 pairs.

claims.statement: The frequencies of spontaneous and miniature EPSCs and IPSCs are lower in VENs than in neighbouring PCs.

Reproduced when the VEN median is lower with p < 0.05 for each type. Tested in full under the claims file of DANDI:001752.

claims.statement: The amplitudes of spontaneous and miniature EPSCs and IPSCs do not differ significantly between VENs and PCs.
claims.source: Results, Altered connectivity profile of deep-layer AIC neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 5c
claims.quote: whereas the amplitudes were not significantly different between VENs and PCs (Fig. 5c )

The paper does not say how a cell's amplitude summarizes its events (Clampfit, Methods); readings, (a) the mean and (b) the median of the cell's event amplitudes. Reproduced when p >= 0.05 for each type, with the effect size reported.

claims.statement: The whole-cell scRNA-seq atlas of the macaque AIC holds 122,663 transcriptomes in four classes, excitatory neurons (21,733, 17.8%), inhibitory neurons (17,007, 13.9%), glial cells (83,283, 67.8%) and vascular cells (640, 0.5%).

claims.quote: 273 excitatory neurons mapped to 18 of the 20 excitatory types, while 34 inhibitory neurons mapped to 17 of the 33 inhibitory types

claims.statement: The axons of VENs emanate from their basal dendrite, while those of PCs originate at the base of the soma.

Measured on the reconstructed VENs and PCs whose axon was recovered (Fig. 6e counts 36 VEN-L, 20 VEN-S and 74 PCs with axonal information). claims.statement: In Pan-Nav stained sections the AIS of VENs lies farther from the soma than that of PCs, and VENs have a shorter AIS.

claims.statement: VENs have lower AP phase-plane peak indices than every PC type.

claims.statement: In 281 VENs and 306 L5 PCs, APs of VENs are broader and lower in amplitude.

What the ANCOVA slope P tests is not said (common slope against zero, or difference of slopes); it is reported under both readings and does not decide. The printed F(1, 93) = 1.07 is placed before both P values and gives p of about 0.30, matching neither 0.5729 nor 0.0031, so which term it belongs to is open; it is recorded under the intercept as the text's order suggests and does not decide.

claims.statement: Latencies of eEPSPs evoked by deep-layer stimulation do not differ between paired VENs and PCs (5.13 and 5.02 ms).

claims.statement: eEPSP amplitudes are higher in VENs than in adjacent PCs, with effects of cell type and stimulation level in an ANOVA.

Whether it treats the 26 VEN-PC pairs and the stimulation levels as repeated measures is not said; readings, (a) ordinary two-way ANOVA and (b) repeated-measures ANOVA with the pair as subject. claims.statement: In simulations, the VEN model fires more than the PC model to the same synaptic input trains, and a distal axon origin raises the somatic response to distal basal inputs.

The Methods define the distance as "the Pearson correlation"; the Results call it the "correlation distance between average log counts", so it is taken as 1 - r, the reading the Results give and the one under which a positive r between distances is possible. The pairs are those of all projection neuron types with mapped Patch-seq neurons ("Pooling the pairs across all clusters"); no minimum number of cells per type is given.

claims.statement: Of 581 metabolites, 228 differ between AIC and V1 and only 108 between AIC and parietal cortex.

claims.statement: In the models, varying AIS length (10 to 70 um) has no significant effect on AP shape; the legends give, for the VEN model, p = 0.3887 for amplitude and p = 0.0515 for width, and for the PC model p = 0.087 for amplitude and p = 0.0038 for width (wider with longer AIS).
claims.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 5; Extended Data Figure 7d,e
claims.quote: Varying AIS length had no significant effect on AP shape in either model.
claims.criterion: Simulations as in the Methods (Computational model), AIS length from 10 to 70 um in each model. A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the two-tailed t-test of the slope of AP amplitude and of AP width against AIS length (Extended Data Fig. 7d,e legends), at 0.05 (conventional). Reproduced when the VEN amplitude, VEN width and PC amplitude slopes give p >= 0.05. The PC width slope is significant in the paper's own legend (p = 0.0038), which conflicts with the Results sentence; it is reported with its slope and does not decide.

claims.statement: VENs have thicker basal dendrites than PCs (n = 72 VENs, 86 PCs), compared along the distance from the soma.
claims.source: Results, VENs respond robustly to deep-layer synaptic input, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 7i
claims.quote: These findings indicated that VENs responded more robustly to deep-layer inputs than PCs, likely due to their thicker basal dendrites (Extended Data Fig. 7i ).
claims.criterion: Basal dendritic diameter as a function of distance from the soma, in 50 um bins with a 10 um sliding step, VEN against PC by two-tailed Student's t-test per bin (Extended Data Fig. 7i legend), at p < 0.05 (conventional). Open, with readings, (a) which dendrite, the prominent (thickest) basal dendrite of each cell, as in Fig. 6b and the AB_thickRatio of the Methods, or all basal dendrites; (b) which bins must differ, every bin holding data from both groups, or at least one bin with none significant in the other direction. Reproduced when VEN means are larger with p < 0.05 under every reading, not reproduced when under none, and blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree; the per-bin results are shown.

claims.statement: Among projection neuron subclasses, L2/3 IT HPCAL1 neurons stand out with a small membrane time constant and a narrow AP width.
claims.source: Results, Patch-seq revealed extensive cellular heterogeneity in the primate AIC, paragraph 3; Figure 2d,f
claims.quote: L2/3 IT HPCAL1 neurons stood out with a small membrane time constant (tau) and narrow action potential (AP) width (Fig. 2d–f )
claims.criterion: Tau and AP half-width as defined in the Methods (Extraction of electrophysiological features), per subclass, n = 30 L2/3 IT HPCAL1, 17 IT RORB, 119 L5 IT FEZF2, 22 VEN, 16 L5 ET and 13 L6 PC (Fig. 2 legend); two-tailed Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (legend), at FDR < 0.05 (conventional). The paper's values are in Supplementary Tables 1 and 2, not in the text read. "Stood out" is read as the lowest median of the six subclasses with FDR < 0.05 against each other subclass, for tau and for AP width. Partially reproduced when the medians are lowest but not every comparison is significant.

claims.statement: Among Patch-seq projection neuron subclasses, the AIS of VENs lies farther from the soma than in the other subclasses.
claims.source: Results, The AIC evolved a neural signal-processing strategy, paragraph 3; Figure 3f
claims.quote: The VENs had lower phase peak indices than any type of PCs (Fig. 3e ), reflecting the unique AIS geometry in VENs (Fig. 3f )
claims.criterion: The quote cites Fig. 3f without stating its result; the direction is read from the Fig. 3f legend (AIS distance from the soma compared among cell types) and from Fig. 3c, which places the VEN AIS farther from the soma. AIS distance from the soma per Patch-seq neuron, n = 25 L2/3 IT HPCAL1, 16 IT RORB, 54 L5 IT FEZF2, 18 VEN, 11 L5 ET and 13 L6 PC (Fig. 3f legend, as Fig. 2h); two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (legend), at FDR < 0.05 (conventional). Reproduced when the VEN median is the highest and VENs differ from each other subclass at FDR < 0.05; partially reproduced when the median is highest but not every comparison is significant. The paper's values are in Supplementary Tables 3 and 4, not in the text read.

claims.statement: Simultaneous recordings of up to eight layer 5b neurons tested 1,292 potential connections among 377 neurons and found 31 monosynaptic connections.
claims.source: Results, Altered connectivity profile of deep-layer AIC neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 5d
claims.quote: In total, we tested 1,292 potential connections from an additional set of 377 neurons in layer 5b and confirmed 31 monosynaptic connections.
claims.criterion: A neuron is one recorded cell (one channel of one slice recording, counted once across the files of that slice). A potential connection is an ordered pair, a presynaptic cell stimulated while another cell of the same slice is recorded; the paper counts direction apart (VEN-to-PC and PC-to-VEN each 0 or 1 of 200, Results), so ordered pairs are the reading its text gives. A connection is a uEPSP or uIPSP evoked by single presynaptic spikes in the response averaged over more than 20 sweeps (Fig. 5f legend), uEPSPs at -70 mV and uIPSPs at -60 mV (Methods). The paper and its code give no amplitude, latency or noise rule for calling a connection, so the connections counted are those annotated, with two readings of the annotation, (a) the dataset's own connection labels and (b) the ConnType annotations of the code's metadata_multiPatch.xlsx, matched through file name and channels; each is run where it exists, and when neither exists the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified. Whether the code's "OK" quality connections count is not said; counted, with the count without them shown. A detection from the traces themselves would be the author's rule and is shown only as a variant that does not decide. Reproduced when all three counts are within tolerance under every reading run; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree.

claims.statement: PCs form monosynaptic connections with other PCs in 24 of 503 tested pairs (4.77%).
claims.source: Results, Altered connectivity profile of deep-layer AIC neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 5i; Supplementary Table 5
claims.quote: A breakdown of these connections by cell type revealed that PCs formed monosynaptic connections with other PCs in 24 out of 503 tested pairs (Supplementary Table 5 )

claims.statement: PC-PC connections span a wide range of soma distances, 111.8 ± 61.2 um (mean ± s.d.); the distances given for the other classes are 135.7 ± 60.0 um for VEN-VEN, 119.3 ± 63.1 um for VEN-PC, 107.0 ± 60.1 um for PC-IN and 97.4 ± 36.8 um for VEN-IN.

claims.criterion: The s.d. describes the spread of pairs, not an uncertainty of the mean, so each mean and each s.d. gets 10% of its value, not the s.d. as tolerance. It does not say which pairs enter each value; for VEN-VEN, VEN-PC and VEN-IN, with no or one connection, only the tested pairs can, so reading (i) is all tested pairs of the class (each unordered pair once, as VEN-to-PC and PC-to-VEN share one value), and for PC-PC the Results say "these connections", so reading (ii), the connected PC-PC pairs only, is also run. Reproduced when the values are within tolerance under every reading run; blocked as methods_underspecified when readings disagree; blocked as data_missing when the dataset holds no soma positions.
