The sign of each network block and pair of networks is reported. Without that assignment the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: In the nonsurgical control animals, scans 6 to 7 weeks apart showed no systematic pattern of functional connectivity change.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 1; Fig. 4a,b bottom, Fig. 4c right
claims.quote: In these control animals, a comparison conducted between scans acquired 6–7 weeks apart did not reveal a systematic pattern of functional changes
claims.criterion: A claim of absence for which the paper reports no test; it compares Fig. 4a and 4b by eye. Judged on the measure of fig4a-cortical-down-subcortical-up applied to monkeys B, W and H. Reproduced when, under both readings, the DBS pattern (cortical block negative and subcortical block positive) is not present; not reproduced when it is. The block values of both groups are given side by side, and the count of significant ROIs from fig4b-roi-changes-counts is noted (the paper's own tables list 44 in the controls).

claims.statement: Before stimulation, the SCC was positively connected with vmFC, dACC, PCC, STG, hippocampus, amygdala and DLPFC, and negatively with the insula and somatosensory cortex.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 2; Fig. 5a top row; Extended Data Fig. 7 top row
claims.quote: Before stimulation, the SCC showed positive connectivity to the ventromedial frontal cortex (vmFC), dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC), posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), superior temporal gyrus (STG), hippocampus (HIP), amygdala (AMY) and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), as well as negative connectivity to the insula and somatosensory cortex
claims.criterion: No test is reported; Fig. 5a shows maps thresholded at P < 0.01. Pre-DBS normalized seed connectivity (opening comment), mean over the target ROI's voxels pooled over N and T, for vmFC, dACC, PCC, STG, HIP, AMY, DLPFC, anterior-dorsal insula and somatosensory cortex. Readings (a) ROIs in the stimulated hemisphere; (b) both hemispheres pooled; each with per-run and concatenated runs. Reproduced when, under every reading, all seven are positive and both insula and somatosensory cortex negative; partially reproduced when at least seven of the nine signs match under every reading.

claims.statement: After SCC-DBS, functional connectivity of the stimulated SCC decreased with vmFC, PCC, STG, hippocampus, amygdala, DLPFC and dACC in the stimulated hemisphere, with a significant PrePost x side interaction.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 3; Fig. 5b and legend; Extended Data Fig. 9; Supplementary Table 9
claims.quote: Following 6 weeks of SCC-DBS, there was a marked reduction in functional connectivity between the SCC and the PCC as well as the vmFC. Reductions were also apparent between the SCC and HIP, AMY and DLPFC
claims.criterion: From Methods (EPI data analysis), Supplementary Methods 4 and the Fig. 5b and Extended Data Fig. 9 legends. Normalized seed connectivity voxels of the 17 target ROIs of Supplementary Table 8, both hemispheres, pre and post, N and T. ANOVA DBS x side x ROI full factorial plus monkey (df 1,20279), Tukey-Kramer over the 68 cells. Run with per-run and concatenated seed maps. Reproduced when, under both, the interaction has P < 0.05 and each of the seven stimulated-side ROIs has a pre against post P < 0.05 with post lower; partially reproduced when the interaction holds and at least four of the seven do.

claims.statement: After SCC-DBS, functional connectivity of the stimulated SCC increased with the anterior-dorsal insula and the somatosensory cortex.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 3; Fig. 5a,b; Extended Data Fig. 9; Supplementary Table 9
claims.quote: The insula and somatosensory cortex exhibited increases in functional connectivity with the SCC following DBS
claims.criterion: With the model of fig5b-scc-decreases. Reproduced when the stimulated-side anterior-dorsal insula and somatosensory cortex each have a pre against post P < 0.05 with post higher, under both seed-map readings.

claims.statement: Although stimulation was unilateral, SCC functional connectivity also changed in the unstimulated control hemisphere, including vmFC, PCC, anterior-dorsal insula and dACC.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 3; Fig. 5b legend; Extended Data Figs. 8 and 9; Supplementary Table 9
claims.quote: Despite DBS being delivered unilaterally and white matter remodeling being confined to the stimulated hemisphere ... functional connectivity changes were also apparent in the unstimulated control hemisphere
claims.criterion: With the model of fig5b-scc-decreases. Reproduced when, under both seed-map readings, the control-side vmFC, PCC, anterior-dorsal insula and dACC each have a pre against post P < 0.05, and the number of control-side ROIs with P < 0.05 is within tolerance of 11 (PCC, vmFC, STG, insula, dACC, DLPFC, area 25, area 32, HIP, somatosensory cortex, MT in Supplementary Table 9).

claims.statement: Connectivity between the stimulated SCC and motor-related regions (primary motor cortex, SMA) and the MCC did not change.
claims.source: Discussion, Effect of SCC-DBS on functional networks, paragraph 3, and Interaction between functional and structural effects of DBS, paragraph 2; Supplementary Table 9
claims.quote: Notably, we found that there were no apparent changes in connectivity between the stimulated SCC and motor-related regions, including the primary motor cortex or supplementary motor area
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the Tukey-Kramer post hoc of fig5b-scc-decreases at P < 0.05. Reproduced when the stimulated-side motor cortex, SMA and MCC pre against post comparisons all have P >= 0.05; not reproduced when any has P < 0.05. The change and P of each are given either way.

claims.statement: The reductions in SCC functional connectivity after DBS were consistent across both monkeys.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figs. 7 and 8
claims.quote: These reductions in functional connectivity from SCC were consistent across both monkeys
claims.criterion: No test per monkey is reported (Fig. 5b shows each monkey's mean as a symbol). For each monkey, the mean post minus pre normalized connectivity in the stimulated hemisphere for vmFC, PCC, STG, HIP, AMY, DLPFC and dACC. Reproduced when all seven are negative in both monkeys under both seed-map readings; partially reproduced when at least five of the seven are negative in each monkey.

claims.statement: The reductions in SCC connectivity, and bilateral changes, seen after SCC-DBS were absent in the nonsurgical control group over 6 weeks.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 3; Fig. 5a bottom row; Extended Data Fig. 7 right column; Extended Data Fig. 8 bottom row
claims.quote: Notably, such reductions in connectivity were absent in the nonsurgical control group, indicating that these changes are specific to SCC-DBS
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the voxelwise post minus pre map of connectivity with the right SCC in monkeys B, W and H, thresholded at P < 0.01 with clusters larger than 20 voxels (cluster-level corrected P < 0.01, two-sided; the Fig. 5a legend). The paper does not name the voxelwise test or the cluster neighbourhood; the readings are (a) a two-sample t-test per voxel between the pre and post run maps pooled over the three monkeys; (b) a one-sample t-test of the three monkeys' post minus pre maps; each with faces-only and faces, edges and corners neighbourhoods, and with per-run and concatenated seed maps. The paper thresholds the same control maps at P < 0.01 (Fig. 5a, Extended Data Fig. 7) and at P < 0.05 (Extended Data Fig. 8 bottom row, clusters > 20 voxels); both thresholds are run. Reproduced when, under the readings, no significant cluster of decrease lies in the vmFC, PCC, STG, HIP, AMY, DLPFC or dACC ROIs of either hemisphere; not reproduced when one does. If the readings disagree, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified with every result shown. The ROI-level change of the controls (the measure of fig5b-scc-decreases, without the monkey term) is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: After SCC-DBS, functional connectivity of the stimulated SCC with the hubs of the default mode, limbic and central executive networks decreased, with a significant PrePost x side interaction.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 4; Fig. 5c and legend
claims.quote: After chronic stimulation, the DMN, LIM and CEN showed significantly decreased functional connectivity with SCC
claims.criterion: From Methods (EPI data analysis) and the Fig. 5c legend. Each network's voxels are the union, with repeats, of its hub ROIs' voxels (opening comment), LIM under readings (a) with area 25 and (b) without. ANOVA DBS x side x network full factorial plus monkey, Tukey-Kramer over the 24 cells. Reproduced when, under all readings, the interaction has P < 0.05 and the stimulated-side DMN, LIM and CEN each have a pre against post P < 0.05 with post lower.

claims.statement: SCC connectivity with the sensorimotor network increased after SCC-DBS, although that network has few direct CB connections.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 4; Discussion, Effect of SCC-DBS on functional networks, paragraph 3; Fig. 5c
claims.quote: As noted above, there was an increase in connectivity between the SCC and the SMN
claims.criterion: With the model of fig5c-dmn-lim-cen-decrease. Reproduced when the stimulated-side SMN pre against post comparison has P < 0.05 with post higher, under all readings.

claims.statement: SCC connectivity with the visual network, and with the areas within it, did not change after SCC-DBS.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 4; Fig. 5c; Extended Data Fig. 9
claims.quote: In comparison, there was no change in relation to the VIS or areas within the VIS
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's tests, the Tukey-Kramer post hoc of fig5c-dmn-lim-cen-decrease (VIS) and of fig5b-scc-decreases (visual cortex and MT), at P < 0.05. The sentence names no hemisphere. The Fig. 5c legend lists no VIS difference on either side, so the VIS network is judged on both sides; for the areas the stimulated side is judged, because the paper's own Supplementary Table 9 gives control-side MT P = 7.85e-7 against its sentence. Reproduced when the VIS comparisons of both sides and the stimulated-side visual cortex and MT comparisons all have P >= 0.05; not reproduced when any has P < 0.05. The control-side visual cortex and MT are reported.

claims.statement: In the stimulated hemisphere, the salience network as a whole showed no change in connectivity with the stimulated SCC, because its anterior-dorsal insula node increased and its dACC node decreased.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 4; Fig. 5b,c; Extended Data Fig. 9
claims.quote: did not as a whole exhibit consistent changes after SCC-DBS ... Specifically, the anterior-dorsal insula exhibited increased connectivity with the SCC, whereas the dACC showed decreased connectivity following 6 weeks of DBS
claims.criterion: With the models of fig5c-dmn-lim-cen-decrease and fig5b-scc-decreases. Reproduced when the stimulated-side SAN comparison has P >= 0.05 (the paper's test for the absence), and the stimulated-side anterior-dorsal insula increases and dACC decreases, each at P < 0.05.

claims.statement: In the unstimulated lead-implanted monkey D, FA decreased in the CB of the implanted hemisphere and did not change in the other tracts.
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 2; Fig. 6a and legend; Extended Data Fig. 10a
claims.quote: Second, in direct contrast to the SCC-DBS animals, we saw a significant decrease in FA in the CB of the implanted hemisphere and no changes in any of our other target tracts
claims.criterion: As fig2a-cb-fa-increase, for monkey D alone, without the monkey term (df 1238). Reproduced when the PrePost x side x tract interaction has P < 0.05, the sham-side CB pre against post comparison has P < 0.05 with post lower, and none of the other five tract and side comparisons has P < 0.05.

claims.statement: In monkey D the CB FA decrease was significant in the dACC portion of the implanted hemisphere, more anterior than and opposite in direction to the MCC-CB increase after stimulation, although reductions were diffuse across the CB.
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 2; Fig. 6b and legend
claims.quote: This decrease in FA is more anterior and the opposite direction of that observed in the stimulation group
claims.criterion: As fig2b-mcc-cb-fa-increase, for monkey D alone, without the monkey term (df 492). Reproduced when the interaction has P < 0.05, the sham-side dACC-CB pre against post comparison has P < 0.05 with post lower, and the sham-side MCC-CB shows no significant increase.

claims.statement: In monkey D, the CC1/DAPI ratio in the MCC-CB did not differ between the implanted and control hemispheres.
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 2; Fig. 6c and legend
claims.quote: the ratio of myelinated oligodendrocytes (CC1/DAPI) in the MCC-CB did not differ between the implanted and control hemispheres
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, a two-sided paired t-test of the 28 field ratios between hemispheres at P < 0.05 (Methods). How fields are paired across hemispheres is not stated; readings (a) by section and field number as recorded in the dataset; (b) by order within section when no field number is recorded. Reproduced when the test has P >= 0.05; not reproduced when P < 0.05. The mean difference and dz are given either way, and an unpaired test is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: In monkey D, whole-brain connectivity changes after implantation were less coherent than after SCC-DBS, cortico-cortical changes were mixed, and subcortico-subcortical connectivity decreased, the opposite of the SCC-DBS group.
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 10c
claims.quote: Cortical-to-cortical connections showed more random connectivity changes, and subcortical-to-subcortical connections showed a consistent negative change, which is the opposite direction of what we saw after SCC-DBS
claims.criterion: No test of the blocks is reported. With the readings of fig4a-cortical-down-subcortical-up applied to monkey D's difference connectome. Reproduced when, under both readings, the subcortical value is negative. The cortical value and the fraction of negative cortical entries are reported; "more random" is not otherwise tested.

claims.statement: In monkey D, SCC functional connectivity changed little after implantation, apart from a localized increase at the implantation site.
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 3; Fig. 6d; Extended Data Fig. 10d
claims.quote: Additionally, there was very little alteration in the functional connectivity associated with the SCC, except for a localized increase in connectivity at the site of implantation
claims.criterion: Judged on the voxelwise thresholded map of the Fig. 6d legend (P < 0.01, clusters larger than 20 voxels), with the voxelwise test readings of fig5a-nonsurgical-no-reduction that apply to one animal (reading (a), pre against post runs). Reproduced when a significant cluster of increase lies at the lead track and no significant cluster of decrease lies in the vmFC, PCC, STG, HIP, AMY, DLPFC or dACC ROIs. The paper gives the lead location only as images; if the dataset does not give it, the claim is blocked as metadata_insufficient.

claims.statement: In monkey D the reductions in SCC connectivity with the DMN, LIM and CEN seen after SCC-DBS were not observed.
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 3; Fig. 6e and legend
claims.quote: Notably, the widespread reductions in connectivity that we saw in the DMN, LIM and CEN after SCC-DBS were not observed
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the model of fig5c-dmn-lim-cen-decrease for monkey D alone without the monkey term (df 10972), Tukey-Kramer at P < 0.05, with the LIM readings. What "not observed" covers is open, (a) the sham side, (b) both sides; the paper's own legend lists significant control-side DMN and CEN differences without their direction. Reproduced when no DMN, LIM or CEN comparison of the sides the reading covers is a significant decrease; not reproduced when one is. If the readings disagree, blocked as methods_underspecified with both shown.

claims.statement: Among vmFC, PCC, anterior-dorsal insula and dACC, monkey D showed a significant pre against post difference in SCC connectivity only for the sham-side vmFC and the control-side anterior-dorsal insula.
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 10d legend
claims.quote: A significant pre–post difference was observed in the sham side vmFC ( P = 7.83e-04) and control side anterior-dorsal insula
claims.criterion: The model of fig5b-scc-decreases for monkey D alone, without the monkey term (17 ROIs, df 10106). Reproduced when the interaction has P < 0.05 and, of the eight comparisons (four ROIs, two sides), exactly the sham-side vmFC and the control-side anterior-dorsal insula have P < 0.05. Directions are reported; the paper does not give them.

claims.statement: In monkeys N and T, time spent moving and foraging in the home cage increased after 6 weeks of SCC-DBS (one-way ANOVA, movement F(1,236) = 34.61, foraging F(1,236) = 17.35).
claims.source: Results, SCC-DBS induces selective macroscale remodeling in the CB, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 1
claims.quote: Time spent moving and foraging both increased after SCC-DBS, with concordant effects observed across subjects
claims.criterion: Bins of 10 s, 60 per 10-min video, 1 when movement (or foraging) occurs (Methods, Behavior analysis). anovan with the full model monkey x stim on the bins of N and T, as in FigE1_dbs_behavior_analysisscript_a.m (error df 236). Reproduced when the stim effect has p < 0.05 with the post proportion higher, for both movement and foraging, and each animal's post proportion exceeds its pre proportion; partially reproduced when this holds for one of the two behaviors.

claims.statement: The nonstimulation control animal (monkey D) showed no change in movement or foraging.
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 1
claims.quote: First, there was no change in the amount of movement or foraging in naturalistic behavior
claims.criterion: A claim of absence for which the paper reports no test; the test it used for N and T (one-way ANOVA of the binarized bins, pre against post, p < 0.05) is applied to the 60 pre and 60 post bins of D. Reproduced when neither movement nor foraging differs at p < 0.05; not reproduced when either does. The pre and post proportions are reported.

claims.statement: After 6 weeks of SCC-DBS, FA increased in the cingulum bundle of the stimulated hemisphere (PrePost x side interaction F(1,3187) = 4.64, p = 0.0312; Tukey-Kramer pre against post in the stimulated CB, p = 0.022).
claims.source: Results, SCC-DBS induces selective macroscale remodeling in the CB, paragraph 3; Fig. 2a
claims.quote: We found there was a selective increase in FA in the CB in the stimulated hemisphere, particularly the mid-cingulate portion, after 6 weeks of SCC-DBS
claims.criterion: FA as in [FA] of the header, model and post hoc as in [FA-ANOVA] (Fig2A_dbs_FA_wholetract_analysisscript_a.m). Reproduced when the PrePost x side interaction has p < 0.05 and the Tukey-Kramer pre-post comparison in the stimulated CB has p < 0.05 with post FA higher, under every reading of the lead-track exclusion (header). The voxel counts are checked against the expected values as a check on the masks.

claims.statement: FA did not change consistently in the stimulated UF or FM, nor in any of the three tracts in the control hemisphere.
claims.source: Results, SCC-DBS induces selective macroscale remodeling in the CB, paragraph 3; Fig. 2a bottom; Extended Data Figs. 2 to 4
claims.quote: No consistent changes were apparent in either the stimulated UF or the FM ... or in the same tracts within the control hemisphere
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the Tukey-Kramer post hoc of [FA-ANOVA] at p < 0.05. Reproduced when none of the five pre-post comparisons (stimulated UF, stimulated FM, control CB, control UF, control FM) has p < 0.05; not reproduced when any does. The mean change and p of each are reported.

claims.statement: Both stimulated monkeys showed an FA change in the same direction in the stimulated CB.
claims.source: Results, SCC-DBS induces selective macroscale remodeling in the CB, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 2
claims.quote: Importantly, both monkeys exhibited changes in the same direction
claims.criterion: The paper shows this with per-monkey maps and symbols, without a test. Per monkey, the mean over the stimulated CB voxels of post FA minus the mean of pre FA ([FA]). Reproduced when it is positive in both N and T.

claims.statement: Of four CB subregions, only the mid-cingulate part on the stimulated side showed an FA increase, in both animals (PrePost x side interaction F(1,1357) = 5.42, p = 0.020; Tukey-Kramer for the stimulated MCC-CB, p = 0.0017).
claims.source: Results, SCC-DBS induces selective macroscale remodeling in the CB, paragraph 4; Fig. 2b
claims.quote: Comparing the FA values before and after 6 weeks of DBS in four CB subregions revealed that only the mid-cingulate region on the stimulated side showed an increase in FA in both animals
claims.criterion: FA as in [FA], subregions as in [CB-PARTS], model and post hoc as in [FA-ANOVA] (Fig2B_dbs_FA_CB_part_analysisscript_a.m). Reproduced, under every reading of [CB-PARTS] and of the lead-track exclusion (header), when the PrePost x side interaction has p < 0.05, the stimulated MCC-CB pre-post comparison has Tukey-Kramer p < 0.05 with post higher, none of the other seven pre-post comparisons shows a significant increase, and each monkey's mean MCC-CB FA rises on the stimulated side. Partially reproduced when the stimulated MCC-CB increase holds but another subregion also increases significantly or one monkey does not rise.

claims.statement: The proportion of CC1-positive cells among DAPI-stained cells was higher in the MCC-CB of the stimulated hemisphere than in the control hemisphere, in both animals (F(1,108) = 9, p = 0.0034).
claims.source: Results, SCC-DBS induces increased myelinating oligodendrocytes and the degree of myelination, paragraph 1; Fig. 3b,c
claims.quote: The proportion of CC1 positive cells in the whole DAPI stained population was higher in the mid-cingulate portion of the CB on the stimulated side compared to the control side in both animals
claims.criterion: Counts and test as in [IF], on the MCC-CB fields of N and T (Fig3CandE5_dbs_IF_CC1_MCC_CB_analysisscript_a.m). The tolerance on the field count is 0 as it is the design (7 fields x 4 sections x 2 animals). Reproduced when the side effect has p < 0.05 with the stimulated side higher and each animal's mean ratio is higher on the stimulated side.

claims.statement: In the MCC-CB the number of CC1-positive cells was higher on the stimulated side (F(1,108) = 6.22, p = 0.0142), while the number of DAPI-positive cells did not differ (F(1,108) = 0.55, p = 0.4617).
claims.source: Extended Data Fig. 5 legend
claims.quote: The main effect of side for the number of CC1 positive cells was significant ... while no significant difference was observed for the number of DAPI positive cells
claims.criterion: As in [IF]. Reproduced when the side effect on CC1 counts has p < 0.05 with the stimulated side higher and the side effect on DAPI counts has p >= 0.05 (the paper's test for the absence); partially reproduced when only one of the two holds.

claims.statement: In the dACC portion of the CB, neither the CC1/DAPI ratio nor the CC1 or DAPI counts differed between hemispheres (ratio F(1,108) = 2.93, p = 0.0899).
claims.source: Results, SCC-DBS induces increased myelinating oligodendrocytes and the degree of myelination, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 6a
claims.quote: No changes were observed in the anterior portion of CB, consistent with the lack of FA alterations there
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, [IF] on the dACC-CB fields of N and T (FigE6A_dbs_IF_CC1_dACC_CB_analysisscript_a.m) at p < 0.05. Reproduced when the side effect is not significant for the ratio, the CC1 count or the DAPI count; not reproduced when any is. Effect sizes are reported.

claims.statement: In the region where the UF and FM overlap, oligodendrocyte measures did not differ between hemispheres (CC1/DAPI ratio F(1,76) = 1.45, p = 0.2319).
claims.source: Results, SCC-DBS induces increased myelinating oligodendrocytes and the degree of myelination, paragraph 1; Extended Data Fig. 6b
claims.quote: Similarly, the region where the FM and UF overlap showed no oligodendrocyte changes
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, [IF] on the UF-FM overlap fields of N and T (FigE6B_dbs_IF_CC1_UF_FMoverlap_analysisscript_a.m) at p < 0.05. Reproduced when the side effect is not significant for the ratio, the CC1 count or the DAPI count; not reproduced when any is.

claims.statement: The g-ratio of myelinated axons in the MCC-CB was lower in the stimulated than in the control hemisphere in both animals, meaning a greater degree of myelination (F(1,696) = 58.98, p = 5.42e-14).
claims.source: Results, SCC-DBS induces increased myelinating oligodendrocytes and the degree of myelination, paragraph 2; Fig. 3d-f
claims.quote: the MCC-CB g -ratio was decreased compared to the control hemisphere in both animals
claims.criterion: Measures, exclusions and test as in [EM] (Fig3F_dbs_EMgratio_analysisscript_a.m). Reproduced when the side effect has p < 0.05 with the stimulated side lower and each animal's mean g-ratio is lower on the stimulated side.

claims.statement: After SCC-DBS, cortico-cortical functional connectivity was broadly reduced and subcortico-subcortical connectivity increased.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 1; Fig. 4a,b
claims.quote: Broadly, we observed a reduction in cortico–cortical functional connectivity and a concurrent increase in subcortico–subcortical functional connectivity
claims.criterion: Matrices as in [EPI] and [MATRIX], mean post minus pre over N and T. The paper shows this in the difference matrix without a test. Readings for the summary, (a) the mean and (b) the median of the change over all cortico-cortical pairs and over all subcortico-subcortical pairs. Matrices per run then averaged (Methods); the code's one matrix per session is a variant. Reproduced when, under both summary readings, the cortico-cortical value is below 0 and the subcortico-subcortical value above 0; blocked as methods_underspecified when the two readings differ.

claims.statement: SCC-DBS induced widespread changes in functional connectivity, with many CHARM and SARM ROIs showing a significant change from zero in their connectivity to the rest of the brain (Supplementary Table 1 lists 69 ROIs).
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 1; Fig. 4b; Supplementary Table 1
claims.quote: In contrast to the localized structural alterations observed in white matter, SCC-DBS induced widespread functional changes
claims.criterion: Per-ROI test as in [MATRIX] for the DBS group, the rank-sum of each ROI's 121 changes against zeros (legend and code; pre against post values is a variant). Readings, the threshold (0.01/122 from the Methods and legend, or 0.05/122 from the code and the table), each paired with its own expected count. Reproduced when the count is within tolerance under one reading and the significant ROIs overlap those of Supplementary Table 1 by at least 80%; partially reproduced when the count is within tolerance but the overlap is lower. The signs of the significant ROIs (cortical against subcortical) are reported.

claims.statement: Sorted by cortical network membership, connectivity within and across cortical networks was reduced after SCC-DBS.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 1; Fig. 4c left
claims.quote: When the functional connectivity was sorted based on cortical networks membership, it was clear that connectivity within and across networks was reduced
claims.criterion: Circular plot of Fig. 4c, pairs of the 54 cortical ROIs with a group-mean change beyond 0.1 in absolute value (legend; the code's 0.15 is a variant). The network assignment of the ROIs is not given, so the claim is judged over all cortical pairs. Reproduced when pairs with a change below -0.1 outnumber pairs with a change above 0.1.

claims.statement: In the nonsurgical control group, scans 6 to 7 weeks apart showed no systematic pattern of functional connectivity change like that after SCC-DBS.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 2; Fig. 4a-c bottom and right; Supplementary Table 2
claims.quote: In these control animals, a comparison conducted between scans acquired 6–7 weeks apart did not reveal a systematic pattern of functional changes
claims.criterion: The paper judges this by eye; its own Supplementary Table 2 lists 44 ROIs significant by the per-ROI test, so a systematic pattern is read as the DBS group's pattern. Matrices as in [MATRIX], mean over B, W and H. Reproduced when the control group does not show both a cortico-cortical decrease and a subcortico-subcortical increase (as in fig4a-cortical-decrease-subcortical-increase, same readings); not reproduced when it shows both. The number of circular-plot pairs beyond 0.1 in each group and the count of significant ROIs, against the expected value, are reported, not judged.

claims.statement: Before stimulation, the SCC had positive connectivity with vmFC, dACC, PCC, STG, hippocampus, amygdala and DLPFC, and negative connectivity with the insula and somatosensory cortex.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 3; Fig. 5a top row; Extended Data Fig. 7 top row
claims.quote: Before stimulation, the SCC showed positive connectivity to the ventromedial frontal cortex (vmFC), dorsal anterior cingulate cortex (dACC), posterior cingulate cortex (PCC), superior temporal gyrus (STG), hippocampus (HIP), amygdala (AMY) and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), as well as negative connectivity to the insula and somatosensory cortex
claims.criterion: Seed maps as in [EPI] and [SEED], pre-DBS sessions of N and T. The paper shows maps without an ROI test. Per target ROI, the mean normalized z over its voxels pooled across the two animals. Readings, ROIs (a) in the stimulated hemisphere, (b) in both hemispheres pooled. Reproduced when, under one reading, the seven ROIs named are above 0 and the anterior-dorsal insula and sensory cortex below 0; partially reproduced when at least seven of the nine signs hold.

claims.statement: After SCC-DBS, connectivity of the stimulated SCC fell with PCC, vmFC, STG, hippocampus, amygdala, DLPFC and dACC (PrePost x side interaction F(1,20279) = 186.48, p = 2.87e-42; Tukey-Kramer p < 0.001 in the stimulated hemisphere).
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 4; Fig. 5b; Extended Data Fig. 9; Supplementary Table 9
claims.quote: Following 6 weeks of SCC-DBS, there was a marked reduction in functional connectivity between the SCC and the PCC as well as the vmFC. Reductions were also apparent between the SCC and HIP, AMY and DLPFC
claims.criterion: Seed maps as in [EPI] and [SEED], model and post hoc as in [SEED-ANOVA] (Fig5BCandE9_dbs_FC_25norm_mkNT_analysisscript_a.m). Reproduced when, under every reading of [SEED] (header), the PrePost x side interaction has p < 0.05 and each of the seven ROIs in the stimulated hemisphere has Tukey-Kramer p < 0.05 with post below pre; partially reproduced when PCC and vmFC hold but fewer than all seven do. The voxel counts of all 17 ROIs are compared with Supplementary Table 8.

claims.statement: Connectivity of the stimulated SCC with the anterior-dorsal insula and somatosensory cortex increased after SCC-DBS (Tukey-Kramer p < 0.001).
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 5; Fig. 5a,b; Extended Data Fig. 9; Supplementary Table 9
claims.quote: The insula and somatosensory cortex exhibited increases in functional connectivity with the SCC following DBS
claims.criterion: As in fig5b-scc-decreases. Reproduced when both ROIs in the stimulated hemisphere have Tukey-Kramer p < 0.05 with post above pre; partially reproduced when one does.

claims.statement: The reductions in connectivity from the SCC were consistent across both stimulated monkeys.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 4; Extended Data Figs. 7 and 8
claims.quote: These reductions in functional connectivity from SCC were consistent across both monkeys
claims.criterion: Shown in per-monkey maps without a test. Per monkey, the mean over the ROI's voxels of post minus pre normalized z ([SEED]), stimulated hemisphere, for the seven ROIs of fig5b-scc-decreases. Reproduced when all seven are below 0 in both N and T; partially reproduced when PCC and vmFC are below 0 in both but not all seven.

claims.statement: Although stimulation was unilateral, connectivity changes with the stimulated SCC were also present in the unstimulated control hemisphere.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 5; Fig. 5b,c; Extended Data Figs. 8 and 9; Supplementary Table 9
claims.quote: Despite DBS being delivered unilaterally and white matter remodeling being confined to the stimulated hemisphere ... functional connectivity changes were also apparent in the unstimulated control hemisphere
claims.criterion: As in fig5b-scc-decreases, the control-hemisphere pre-post comparisons. Supplementary Table 9 has 11 of 17 control-side ROIs at p < 0.05 (PCC, vmFC, STG, anterior-dorsal insula, dACC, DLPFC, area 25, area 32, HIP, sensory cortex, MT). Reproduced when the four hubs of Fig. 5b (vmFC, PCC, anterior-dorsal insula, dACC), all reported significant on the control side in its legend, each have Tukey-Kramer p < 0.05 on the control side; partially reproduced when two or three do. The number of significant control-side ROIs is reported against the table.

claims.statement: The reductions in SCC connectivity, and bilateral changes, were absent in the nonsurgical control group over a comparable interval.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraphs 4 and 5; Fig. 5a bottom row; Extended Data Fig. 7 right column; Extended Data Fig. 8 bottom row
claims.quote: Notably, such reductions in connectivity were absent in the nonsurgical control group
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the thresholded seed map (voxel P < 0.01, cluster above 20 voxels, cluster-level corrected P < 0.01, two-sided; Fig. 5a legend) of the change with the right area 25 in B, W and H ([SEED]). The paper does not say what voxel test gives P; readings (a) a two-sample t-test per voxel of post against pre normalized z across runs pooled over animals, (b) a one-sample t-test of the per-animal change; cluster correction (a) AFNI 3dClustSim at the stated thresholds. Reproduced when no significant negative cluster covers PCC or vmFC under the readings; not reproduced when one does. If the readings disagree, the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified with both shown.

claims.statement: After SCC-DBS, connectivity between the stimulated SCC and the DMN, LIM and CEN hubs decreased significantly (PrePost x side interaction F(1,21967) = 51.09, p = 9.10e-13; Tukey-Kramer p < 0.001).
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 6; Fig. 5c
claims.quote: After chronic stimulation, the DMN, LIM and CEN showed significantly decreased functional connectivity with SCC
claims.criterion: Networks and model as in [SEED-ANOVA]. Reproduced when the interaction has p < 0.05 and the stimulated-side DMN, LIM and CEN each have Tukey-Kramer p < 0.05 with post below pre; partially reproduced when one or two do. The Methods' LIM without area 25 is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Connectivity between the SCC and the sensorimotor network also changed after SCC-DBS, as an increase, though the SMN has limited direct CB connections.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 6; Fig. 5c; Discussion, Effect of SCC-DBS on functional networks, paragraph 2
claims.quote: There were, however, also changes in networks with limited direct CB connections, such as the SMN
claims.criterion: As in fig5c-network-decreases. The direction comes from the Discussion ("an increase in connectivity between the SCC and the SMN"). Reproduced when the stimulated-side SMN has Tukey-Kramer p < 0.05 with post above pre.

claims.statement: Connectivity between the stimulated SCC and the primary motor cortex or the supplementary motor area did not change after SCC-DBS.
claims.source: Discussion, Effect of SCC-DBS on functional networks, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 9; Supplementary Table 9
claims.quote: Notably, we found that there were no apparent changes in connectivity between the stimulated SCC and motor-related regions, including the primary motor cortex or supplementary motor area
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the Tukey-Kramer post hoc of [SEED-ANOVA] (ROI model) at p < 0.05, stimulated hemisphere. Reproduced when motor cortex and SMA both have p >= 0.05; not reproduced when either is significant. The mean changes and the control-side results are reported.

claims.statement: Connectivity between the SCC and the visual network, or areas within it, did not change.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 6; Fig. 5c; Extended Data Fig. 9; Supplementary Table 9
claims.quote: In comparison, there was no change in relation to the VIS or areas within the VIS
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the Tukey-Kramer post hoc of [SEED-ANOVA] at p < 0.05, stimulated hemisphere. Reproduced when VIS (network model) and V1 and MT (ROI model) all have p >= 0.05; not reproduced when any is significant. The control side is reported (Supplementary Table 9 has control-side MT significant, p = 7.85e-07).

claims.statement: The salience network as a whole did not change its connectivity with the SCC, because its nodes changed in opposite directions, the anterior-dorsal insula increasing and the dACC decreasing.
claims.source: Results, Whole-brain functional connectivity changes following SCC-DBS, paragraph 6; Fig. 5b,c; Extended Data Fig. 9
claims.quote: Specifically, the anterior-dorsal insula exhibited increased connectivity with the SCC, whereas the dACC showed decreased connectivity following 6 weeks of DBS
claims.criterion: Model as in [SEED-ANOVA]. Reproduced when the stimulated-side SAN pre-post comparison has Tukey-Kramer p >= 0.05 (the paper's test for the absence), the stimulated-side anterior-dorsal insula rises and the dACC falls, each at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In the nonstimulation control animal (lead implanted, no stimulation), FA decreased in the CB of the implanted hemisphere (Tukey-Kramer p = 5.07e-09), with no change in the other tracts.
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 2; Fig. 6a; Extended Data Fig. 10a
claims.quote: Second, in direct contrast to the SCC-DBS animals, we saw a significant decrease in FA in the CB of the implanted hemisphere and no changes in any of our other target tracts
claims.criterion: FA as in [FA], model as in [FA-ANOVA] for monkey D (Fig6A_dbs_FA_wholetract_mkD_analysisscript_a.m). Reproduced when the sham-side CB pre-post comparison has Tukey-Kramer p < 0.05 with post below pre, and none of the other five pre-post comparisons has p < 0.05 (the paper's test for the absence); partially reproduced when the CB decrease holds and another tract also changes.

claims.statement: In the nonstimulation control animal, the FA decrease lay in the dACC portion of the CB, more anterior than and opposite to the increase after stimulation, although diffuse reductions were seen across the CB (PrePost x side F(1,492) = 24.55, p = 9.97e-07; dACC-CB Tukey-Kramer p = 1.30e-08).
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 2; Fig. 6b
claims.quote: This decrease in FA is more anterior and the opposite direction of that observed in the stimulation group, although diffuse reductions were seen across the CB
claims.criterion: FA as in [FA], subregions as in [CB-PARTS], model as in [FA-ANOVA] for monkey D (Fig6B_dbs_FA_CB_part_mkD_analysisscript_a.m). Reproduced when the interaction has p < 0.05 and the sham-side dACC-CB has Tukey-Kramer p < 0.05 with post below pre, and the sham-side MCC-CB shows no significant increase.

claims.statement: In the nonstimulation control animal, the CC1/DAPI ratio in the MCC-CB did not differ between the implanted and control hemispheres (paired t-test, t(27) = -0.99, p = 0.33).
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 2; Fig. 6c; Extended Data Fig. 10b
claims.quote: the ratio of myelinated oligodendrocytes (CC1/DAPI) in the MCC-CB did not differ between the implanted and control hemispheres
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the paired t-test of [IF] (Fig6C_dbs_IF_CC1_mkD_MCC_CB_analysisscript_a.m) at p < 0.05. Reproduced when p >= 0.05; not reproduced when p < 0.05. The mean difference and dz are reported.

claims.statement: After lead implantation alone, whole-brain connectivity changes were less coherent; cortico-cortical changes looked random and subcortico-subcortical connectivity decreased, the opposite of SCC-DBS.
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 3; Extended Data Fig. 10c; Supplementary Table 10
claims.quote: Cortical-to-cortical connections showed more random connectivity changes, and subcortical-to-subcortical connections showed a consistent negative change, which is the opposite direction of what we saw after SCC-DBS
claims.criterion: Matrices as in [MATRIX] for monkey D alone. Readings for the summary, (a) the mean and (b) the median change over pairs, as in fig4a-cortical-decrease-subcortical-increase. Reproduced when, under both summary readings, the subcortico-subcortical value is below 0 and the fraction of cortico-cortical pairs with a negative change is closer to one half than in the DBS group; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings differ. The count of significant ROIs is compared with the expected value and reported.

claims.statement: After lead implantation without stimulation, connectivity of the SCC changed little, apart from a local increase at the implantation site; among the DMN and SAN hubs only the sham-side vmFC and control-side anterior-dorsal insula changed (PrePost x side F(1,10106) = 4.58, p = 0.0323).
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 3; Fig. 6d; Extended Data Fig. 10d
claims.quote: Additionally, there was very little alteration in the functional connectivity associated with the SCC, except for a localized increase in connectivity at the site of implantation
claims.criterion: Seed maps as in [SEED] for monkey D (seed in the implanted hemisphere), model as in [SEED-ANOVA] for D (Fig6DandE10D_dbs_FC_25norm_mkD_analysisscript_a.m), on the four hubs of Extended Data Fig. 10d (vmFC, PCC, anterior-dorsal insula, dACC). Reproduced when PCC and dACC on the sham side show no significant decrease (Tukey-Kramer p < 0.05) and at most two of the eight pre-post comparisons are significant. The local increase at the lead site is read from the map thresholded as in fig5a-control-group-no-reduction and reported, not judged.

claims.statement: After lead implantation without stimulation, the reductions in connectivity between the SCC and the DMN, LIM and CEN seen after SCC-DBS did not appear (PrePost x side F(1,10972) = 7.36, p = 0.0067).
claims.source: Results, The impact of SCC-DBS lead insertion on functional and structural brain networks, paragraph 3; Fig. 6e
claims.quote: Notably, the widespread reductions in connectivity that we saw in the DMN, LIM and CEN after SCC-DBS were not observed
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the paper's test, the Tukey-Kramer post hoc of [SEED-ANOVA] for D at p < 0.05. The paper lists significant changes in control-side DMN and CEN (direction not stated), so the claim is read on the implanted (sham) side, where the seed and the lead are. Reproduced when none of sham-side DMN, LIM and CEN has a significant decrease; not reproduced when any does. The control-side results and their directions are reported.

claims.statement: In vivo, 0.5 s pulses of blue light of increasing intensity evoke somatic spiking at increasing rates, with corresponding bAPs in the dendrites.
claims.source: Figure 1d legend; Results, Dendritic voltage mapping, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Optogenetic stimulation with pulses of increasing blue light intensity evoked action potentials with increasing spike rates and corresponding bAPs in the dendrites.
claims.criterion: Shown for one neuron (Fig. 1c-d). Somatic spikes are counted in each blue light pulse of the intensity series; the paper gives no spike detection method, so spikes are detected under two readings, (a) peaks above 5 and (b) above 4 robust standard deviations (median absolute deviation) of the high-pass filtered soma trace, a standard choice that the paper does not fix. Reproduced when, under both readings, the spike rate rises with pulse order (Spearman rho > 0 and higher in the last pulse than in the first), and the dendritic traces show events within 5 ms after most somatic spikes.

claims.statement: Spike-triggered averages of dendritic fluorescence, triggered off somatic spike times, peak after the somatic spike, as expected for back-propagation.
claims.source: Figure 1f-g legend; Results, Dendritic voltage mapping, paragraph 1
claims.quote: The dendritic events peaked after the somatic spike (dashed line), as expected for back-propagation.
claims.criterion: For the Fig. 1 neuron, the spike-triggered average of each dendritic trace, triggered off the somatic spike peaks. Reproduced when the dendritic STA peak follows the somatic peak (delay > 0) at all four dendrites; partially reproduced for two or three.

claims.statement: For optogenetically evoked single spikes in anesthetized mice, bAP amplitude did not vary from trial to trial beyond baseline noise at any recording site, so bAP failures were infrequent.
claims.source: Results, Mapping bAP propagation, paragraph 1; Figure 2c
claims.quote: For these optogenetically evoked single spikes, we did not observe trial-to-trial variation in the bAP amplitude beyond baseline noise fluctuations at any of the recording sites (see e.g., Fig 2c ), indicating that bAP failures were infrequent under these conditions.
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test. For each Fig. 2 recording site (40 pulses, 8 ms, 5 Hz), the single-spike dendritic bAP amplitudes are compared with the baseline noise. The paper does not define either quantity, so two readings are run, (a) the s.d. of single-trial bAP amplitudes against the s.d. of the same measure taken in pre-stimulus windows of the same length, and (b) the fraction of single bAPs smaller than 2 s.d. of baseline noise (a failure count). Reproduced when, under both readings, at least 90% of sites show amplitude variation no larger than 1.5 times the baseline variation and failures in under 10% of spikes; these bounds are not in the paper and the result is reported with the values.

claims.statement: In anesthetized mice, the bAP peak amplitude decays to 50% at a contour distance from the soma of 242 ± 30 μm (95% C.I., 30 sites, 5 neurons, 5 mice), with R2 = 0.49 for amplitude against distance.
claims.source: Results, Mapping bAP propagation, paragraph 2; Figure 2e legend
claims.quote: The bAP peak amplitude decayed to 50% at a contour distance from the soma of 242 ± 30 μm (95% C.I., n = 30 recording sites, 5 neurons, 5 mice, Fig. 2e ).
claims.criterion: The distance tolerance is the paper's 95% C.I. (± 30 μm, 30 sites); the R2 tolerance is 10%. Amplitude is the peak of each site's mean bAP waveform (-dF/F), triggered off the soma spike peaks, using the background-robust dF/F of the Methods (Robust estimate of dF/F). The paper does not say what curve is fit or what the 50% is relative to. Readings, (a) a linear regression of amplitude on contour distance, distance where the fit falls to half its value at distance 0; (b) an exponential fit, distance ln(2) times the length constant; (c) amplitude normalized to the somatic spike amplitude of the same recording, distance where the linear fit reaches 0.5. Reproduced when, under one reading, the distance is within 212 to 272 μm and R2 within tolerance; the readings are all reported.

claims.statement: Back-propagation delays range from 1.5 to 4 ms over contour distances from the soma of 50 to 280 μm.
claims.source: Results, Mapping bAP propagation, paragraph 2; Figure 2f
claims.quote: Back-propagation delays ranged from 1.5 to 4 ms, over contour distances from the soma of 50-280 μm ( Fig. 2f ).
claims.criterion: Delay is the time of the peak of each site's mean bAP waveform minus the time of the somatic spike peak (Fig. 2f legend, "Peak delay"). At 500 or 1,000 Hz the paper does not say how the peak is timed below one frame; readings, (a) the sample of the maximum and (b) a parabolic fit through the maximum and its two neighbours, in both soma and dendrite. Reproduced when, under one reading, the delays of sites between 50 and 280 μm lie within 1.35 to 4.4 ms.

claims.statement: At distances over 50 μm from the soma, the bAP conduction speed is 0.09 ± 0.02 m/s (95% C.I., 30 sites, 5 neurons, 5 mice), with R2 = 0.43 for delay against distance.
claims.source: Results, Mapping bAP propagation, paragraph 2; Figure 2f legend
claims.quote: Conduction speeds were 0.09 ± 0.02 m/s (95% C.I., n = 30 recording sites, 5 neurons, 5 mice), consistent with prior theoretical predictions
claims.criterion: The speed tolerance is the paper's 95% C.I. (± 0.02 m/s, 30 sites); the R2 tolerance is 10%. From the Fig. 2f legend, a linear regression of peak delay on contour distance for sites more than 50 μm from the soma; speed is the inverse of the slope. The peak timing readings are those of fig2f-delay-range. The paper does not say whether the fit pools all sites or is made per neuron; readings, (a) one pooled fit over the sites, (b) the mean of per-neuron fits. Reproduced when, under one reading, the speed is within 0.07 to 0.11 m/s and the pooled R2 within tolerance.

claims.statement: Spontaneous voltage in pairs of dendritic branches of the same neuron is highly cross-correlated, 91 ± 3% (mean ± s.d.) in the anesthetized state and 73 ± 4% in the awake state (23 branch pairs, 3 neurons, 3 mice).
claims.source: Results, Dendrite-Dendrite coupling, paragraph 2; Figure 3d legend
claims.quote: Remarkably, dendrites displayed a 91 ± 3% cross-correlation (mean ± s.d.) in the anesthetized state and 73 ± 4% in the awake state ( Fig. 3d ).
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the reported s.d. of the pairs. Per pair of simultaneously recorded branches, the cross-correlation of spontaneous traces; the mean over the 23 pairs per state. Fig. S9 legend takes the zero-lag value as the measure for the shot-noise bound, but the paper does not say whether the branch-pair value is taken at zero lag or at the peak over lags, nor whether spikes are kept in the traces. Readings, (a) zero-lag Pearson correlation of the full traces; (b) peak of the normalized cross-correlation within ±10 ms; (c) as (a) with spikes removed by excluding 10 ms around each somatic spike where a soma recording exists. Reproduced when, under one reading, both means are within tolerance and the anesthetized mean exceeds the awake mean.

claims.statement: Accounting for photon shot noise, the upper bounds on dendrite-to-dendrite cross-correlation are 94 ± 2% (anesthetized) and 85 ± 4% (awake), so the electrical dynamics are largely shared throughout the L2/3 apical dendritic tree.
claims.source: Results, Dendrite-Dendrite coupling, paragraph 2; Figure S9; Methods, Contribution of shot noise
claims.quote: Accounting for the influence of shot noise ( Fig. S9 , Methods), the upper bounds on the dendrite-to-dendrite cross-correlations were estimated to be 94 ± 2% (anesthetized) and 85 ± 4% (awake).
claims.criterion: Tolerance is the reported spread. The Methods split each branch's region of interest into two interleaved checkerboard pixel sets and take the zero-lag cross-correlation of the two signals. This needs pixel-level movies; if the dataset holds only per-branch traces the claim cannot be tested and is reported so. Reproduced when both bounds are within tolerance and each exceeds the matching fig3d mean.

claims.statement: Normalized dendrite-dendrite coupling amplitude decreases by 50% beyond about 200 μm of interbranch distance and stays near 50% out to 300 μm (92 pairs, 5 neurons, 5 mice), so most apical dendrites of L2/3 neurons are electrically coupled in vivo.
claims.source: Results, Dendrite-Dendrite coupling, paragraph 4; Figure 3i legend
claims.quote: Figure 3i shows dendrite-dendrite coupling amplitude vs. interbranch distance, displaying a 50% decrease after ∼200 μm, and similar ∼50% coupling out to 300 μm.
claims.criterion: From the Results and Methods (Dendrite-dendrite coupling matrix), the stimulus-triggered average of each branch for each stimulated branch (50 repeats, 10 ms pulses, 5 Hz), its amplitude as background-robust dF/F, each row divided by the amplitude at the stimulated branch; interbranch contour distance from the reconstruction. The figure's distance bins and the bins its Wilcoxon rank-sum p-values compare are not in the text (no PDF was available). Readings, (a) bins of 0 to 100, 100 to 200, 200 to 300 μm and beyond; (b) bins of 50 μm. Reproduced when, under both readings, the mean coupling of the bins beyond 200 μm is within 0.45 to 0.55, is lower than that of the bin nearest 0 by a Wilcoxon rank-sum test at p < 0.05 (the conventional threshold; the paper prints none in the text), and pairs beyond 300 μm, if any, keep a mean coupling above 0.4.

claims.statement: Strong dendrite-targeted stimuli usually evoke spikes that correspond to bAPs; in 2 of 40 trials they evoke dendritic and not somatic spikes.
claims.source: Results, Dendrite-Dendrite coupling, paragraph 5; Figure S11
claims.quote: Simultaneous recordings at soma and dendrites in anesthetized mice showed that these spikes usually corresponded to bAPs, although occasionally (2 of 40 trials) dendrite-targeted stimuli evoked dendritic and not somatic spikes ( Fig. S11 ).
claims.criterion: Tolerance 0, since the 10% default (0.2 trials) admits no count but 2. A trial is one strong dendrite-targeted stimulus with soma and dendrite recorded (anesthetized). The paper does not say what the 40 trials are; readings, (i) all strong dendrite-targeted stimuli, including those that evoked only subthreshold events (Fig. S11e), and (ii) only the trials in which a spike was detected at the soma or the dendrite. The paper gives no detection rule for spikes or dendritic spikes; readings for an event, (a) a peak above 5 and (b) above 4 robust s.d. of the trace, the standard choices used in fig1d-light-intensity-spike-rate. A dendritic spike with no somatic spike is one with no somatic spike in the 10 ms before it (a window not in the paper). Reproduced when, under one reading, 40 trials are found, exactly 2 of them have a dendritic spike with no somatic spike, and in most trials with a dendritic spike a somatic spike precedes it ("usually"); the counts of every reading are reported.

claims.statement: In awake mice some cells fire spontaneous spike doublets with a narrow distribution of inter-spike intervals, 18 ± 7 ms (mean ± s.d., 216 events, 3 neurons, 3 mice).
claims.source: Results, Accelerating spike rate favors spontaneous bAP propagation, paragraph 1; Figure 4a
claims.quote: In some cells, we observed spike doublets with a narrow distribution of inter-spike intervals (ISIs, 18 ± 7 ms, mean ± s.d., n = 216 events, 3 neurons, 3 mice, Fig. 4a ).
claims.criterion: The paper does not define a doublet. Readings, (a) a pair of somatic spikes with ISI below 75 ms (the threshold the paper uses for triplets), preceded and followed by ISIs above 75 ms; (b) any consecutive pair with ISI below 75 ms. Spike detection as in fig1d-light-intensity-spike-rate. Reproduced when, under one reading, mean, s.d. and count are within tolerance.

claims.statement: In spontaneous spike doublets, the first spike typically fails to propagate to distal dendrites while the second succeeds (doublet ISIs 18 ± 7 ms, 10 branches, 3 neurons, 3 mice).
claims.source: Results, Accelerating spike rate favors spontaneous bAP propagation, paragraph 1; Figure 4b-c legend
claims.quote: Examination of individual spike doublets ( Fig. 4b , S12 ) as well as the average doublet waveforms ( Fig. 4c ) revealed that the first spike typically failed to propagate to distal dendrites, while the second spike succeeded.
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test. Doublets as in fig4a-doublet-isi, the average dendritic waveform triggered off the first somatic spike peak, per branch. bAP amplitude is the peak of the dendritic trace within 0 to 5 ms after each somatic spike peak (covering the 1.5 to 4 ms delays of Fig. 2f) minus the mean of the 5 ms before the first spike; this window is not in the paper, so a second reading of 0 to 8 ms is run. Distal is read as (a) all 10 branches and (b) branches with conduction delay > 3 ms (the Methods' split for optogenetic data). Reproduced when, under every reading, the second bAP exceeds the first in at least 70% of branches, with the median ratio of second to first over branches above 1.

claims.statement: In spontaneous spike trios, the third bAP is amplified relative to the second when the spike rate accelerates (ISI n-1 > 75 ms, ISI n < 75 ms) and suppressed when it decelerates (186 spike triplets, 10 branches, 3 neurons, 3 mice), so spontaneous bAP propagation is favored by an accelerating spike rate.
claims.source: Results, Accelerating spike rate favors spontaneous bAP propagation, paragraph 2; Figure 4d legend; Methods, Analysis of bAP failures during spontaneous activity
claims.quote: The third bAP in accelerating trios experienced amplification relative to the second bAP, while the third bAP in decelerating trios experienced suppression relative to the second (10 branches, 3 neurons, 3 mice).
claims.criterion: From the Methods, somatic spikes and their dendritic events; for each dendritic compartment bAPs normalized by their mean amplitude; trios classified by the somatic ISIs at the 75 ms threshold of the Fig. 4d legend. The figure tests with a Wilcoxon signed-rank test, but its p-value is printed only in the figure and the paired quantity is not stated. Readings, (a) per trio and branch, third against second normalized amplitude, paired, within each class; (b) per branch, mean third-to-second ratio, accelerating against decelerating, paired over the 10 branches; (c) as the Methods word it ("The amplitude of the third spike in each triplet was determined and was classified"), the normalized third-spike amplitude in each class against the per-compartment mean of 1, by signed-rank test. The bAP amplitude window is that of fig4bc-doublet-first-fails, both readings. Reproduced when, under every reading, accelerating trios show third > second and decelerating trios third < second (in (b), accelerating ratio above decelerating; in (c), accelerating third above 1 and decelerating third below 1), at p < 0.05 by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test (the conventional threshold). The number of trios found is reported against the paper's 186.

claims.statement: With sustained (400 ms) blue light on the soma, the first bAP in each evoked spike train is highly attenuated in the dendrites relative to the soma, and subsequent bAPs propagate.
claims.source: Results, Accelerating spike rate favors optogenetically triggered bAP propagation, paragraph 2; Figure 4f-g legend
claims.quote: As in the spontaneous activity, the first bAP in each spike train was highly attenuated in the dendrites relative to the soma ( Fig. 4f-g ).
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test. Fig. 4g shows one neuron (n = 10 trials); the claim is tested over all sustained-pulse recordings (16 trials, 7 neurons, Fig. 4h legend), and for the Fig. 4g neuron alone where it can be identified. The statement compares the dendrite with the soma, which the Methods' normalization does not; readings, (a) bAP amplitudes normalized per dendrite by the mean bAP amplitude 200 to 400 ms after stimulus onset (Methods, Analysis of bAP failures during optogenetic stimulation); (b) per spike, the dendritic bAP amplitude divided by the somatic spike amplitude of the same spike, normalized by the same ratio's 200 to 400 ms mean. Reproduced when, under both readings, in electrotonically distal dendrites (delay > 3 ms, Methods), the median normalized value of the first bAP of each train is below that of the second and later bAPs in the first 150 ms (a window not in the paper, the end of the Results' 50 to 150 ms window), and below 1, with the windows of fig4bc-doublet-first-fails.

claims.statement: In distal dendrites, bAP amplitude during sustained optogenetic stimulation is biphasic in time after stimulus onset, suppressed for the first bAPs, enhanced in a window from 50 to 150 ms, then decreasing (16 trials, 7 neurons, 7 mice).
claims.source: Results, Accelerating spike rate favors optogenetically triggered bAP propagation, paragraph 2; Figure 4h legend
claims.quote: There was a window from 50 –150 ms after stimulus onset where bAP amplitude increased; then bAP amplitude decreased again ( Fig. 4h ).
claims.criterion: From the Methods, spikes sorted into time bins after stimulus onset; in each bin the STA at soma and dendrite triggered off the soma spike times and its mean bAP amplitude, normalized by the 200 to 400 ms mean; distal dendrites have conduction delay > 3 ms. The bin widths and the bins the legend's Wilcoxon signed-rank tests compare are not in the text, nor are the p-values. Readings, (a) bins of 0 to 50, 50 to 150, 150 to 200 and 200 to 400 ms (the window the Results name); (b) bins of 25 ms; (c) bins of 50 ms. In each reading the first bin, and the peak bin within 50 to 150 ms, are compared over the 16 trials with the 200 to 400 ms value of 1 by a Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Reproduced when, under every reading, the first bin is below 1 and a 50 to 150 ms bin above 1, each at p < 0.05 (the conventional threshold), and the amplitude after 150 ms is below that peak.

claims.statement: The biphasic modulation of bAP amplitude is larger in dendrites further from the soma, by mean propagation delay, than in more proximal dendrites (25 branches, 7 cells, 7 mice).
claims.source: Results, Accelerating spike rate favors optogenetically triggered bAP propagation, paragraph 2; Figure S13
claims.quote: This biphasic modulation of bAP amplitude was larger in dendrites further from the soma (as measured by mean propagation delay) than in more proximal dendrites ( Fig. S13 , 25 branches, 7 cells, 7 mice).
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test. Branches split at a conduction delay of 3 ms (Methods and Fig. S13 legend), the time-binned normalized amplitudes of fig4h under each of its bin readings. Modulation is not defined; readings, (a) the peak bin within 50 to 150 ms minus the first bin; (b) the range of bin values. Reproduced when, under every reading, the mean modulation of distal branches exceeds that of proximal branches.

claims.statement: Contralateral whisker air puffs in awake mice evoke bursts of spikes in which all detected dendritic spikes start as bAPs from the soma, and the first spike in the burst typically fails to propagate to distal dendrites while subsequent spikes succeed (13 trials).
claims.source: Results, Accelerating spike rate favors sensory evoked bAP propagation; Figure 4i-k legend
claims.quote: Examination of the single-trial responses ( Fig. 4j ) as well as the average evoked waveforms ( Fig. 4k ) revealed that the first spike in the burst typically failed to propagate to distal dendrites, while subsequent spikes succeeded (n = 13 trials).
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test. Air-puff trials with a somatic burst; the average dendritic waveform triggered off the first somatic spike peak (Fig. 4k legend). bAP amplitude windows as in fig4bc-doublet-first-fails; distal read as delay > 3 ms and as all recorded dendrites. Reproduced when, under every reading, the first bAP is smaller than the mean of the subsequent bAPs of the burst in the average and in at least 9 of the 13 trials (a bound not in the paper, for "typically"), and every dendritic spike detected in the air-puff trials (spike detection as in fig1d, both readings) follows a somatic spike within the bAP windows of fig4bc-doublet-first-fails ("all detected dendritic spikes initiating as bAPs from the soma").

claims.statement: The average sensory-evoked dendritic response is a fast upstroke followed by a sustained plateau depolarization lasting about 400 ms, much longer than the 100 ms stimulus.
claims.source: Results, Accelerating spike rate favors sensory evoked bAP propagation; Figure 4l legend
claims.quote: The average dendritic waveform showed a fast sensory-evoked upstroke, followed by a sustained plateau depolarization which lasted ∼400 ms, substantially longer than the stimulus.
claims.criterion: The stimulus-triggered average dendritic trace, triggered off air-puff onset (Fig. 4l). The paper does not define the plateau's duration; readings, (a) time from puff onset until the average falls back within 1 s.d. of the 500 ms pre-stimulus baseline; (b) full width at half of the plateau amplitude, the plateau taken as the mean from 50 to 150 ms after onset. Reproduced when, under one reading, the duration is within 360 to 440 ms and the depolarization outlasts 100 ms in both.

claims.statement: During spontaneous activity, bAP failures occur in both anesthetized and awake recordings.
claims.source: Figure S12 legend
claims.quote: We observe bAP failures in both anesthetized and awake recordings.
claims.criterion: The paper reports no test and shows example traces only. Spontaneous recordings with soma and dendrite, split by state (anesthetized, awake). A failure is a somatic spike whose dendritic bAP amplitude, in the windows of fig4bc-doublet-first-fails, is below 2 s.d. of the dendrite's baseline noise (the failure reading (b) of fig2c-no-trial-variation; the paper gives no rule). Spike detection as in fig1d-light-intensity-spike-rate, both readings. Reproduced when, under every reading, failures are found in at least one recording of each state; their fraction per state is reported.

claims.statement: In bulk RNA-seq of sorted midbrain DANs, both early-stage mitochondrial PD models (cMfn2KO-early and MP-early) show significant downregulation of the Anxa1 transcript among DAN subtype markers.
claims.source: Results, Anxa1 is a marker of an early PD vulnerable SNc DAN subpopulation, paragraph 1; Figure 1A and 1B
claims.quote: Differential expression analysis of genes enriched in midbrain DAN subtypes revealed that both PD models showed a shared profile of significant early-stage downregulation of the Annexin A1 (Anxa1) transcript
claims.criterion: Figure 1B marks markers downregulated at FDR < 0.05. The pipeline (aligner, counting, differential expression package) is not given in the text and is open (the Acknowledgements credit NBIS staff with the RNA-seq analysis; reference 41, Filograna et al. 2021, is the group's earlier cMfn2KO data). Reproduced when Anxa1 is downregulated against its controls at FDR < 0.05 in both models in the paper's own differential expression results, if GEO holds them. Otherwise the readings are DESeq2 and edgeR with default settings on the deposited counts, and the claim is judged only where both give the same outcome. The paper names one deposit for its RNA-seq data, GSE282753 (Code and data availability), and no other place for the cMfn2KO counts; reference 41 is cited for the mouse model only. Where the deposit lacks the cMfn2KO-early data, that half cannot be tested and the claim stays blocked; the MitoPark half is run and reported. The paper does not say how technical libraries of a mouse are combined. The legend counts mice (MP-early n = 5), so the mouse is the unit, and libraries are summed per mouse before the test (reading a); treating each library as a sample does not fit the legend's n and is shown only as a variant. GEO holds more mice than the legend's 5 per model; which were used is not given, and all are used.

claims.statement: About 99% of Anxa1+ DANs co-express Aldh1a1, while about 40% of Aldh1a1+ DANs express Anxa1.
claims.source: Results, Anxa1 is a marker of an early PD vulnerable SNc DAN subpopulation, paragraph 2; Figure 1C; Figure S1
claims.quote: We found that ∼99% of Anxa1+ DANs co-expressed Aldh1a1, while ∼40% of the Aldh1a1+ DANs expressed Anxa1
claims.criterion: Counts of Th+ cells by Anxa1 and Aldh1a1 status, pooled over the sections and mice of Figure 1C and Figure S1 (control mice). Whether the fractions pool cells or average mice is open; reproduced when both values fall within tolerance under either reading.

claims.statement: Anxa1+ DANs lie in the ventral SNc, with a small fraction in the VTA; they are lateral in anterior SNc and progressively more medial in posterior planes.
claims.source: Results, Anxa1 is a marker of an early PD vulnerable SNc DAN subpopulation, paragraph 2; Figure 1C to 1E
claims.quote: we found that the Anxa1+ DANs were localized in the ventral part of the SNc, and a small fraction was found in the VTA region ... Anxa1+ DANs were localized laterally in the anterior portions of the SNc, with their distribution becoming progressively more medial towards more posterior coronal planes
claims.criterion: From cell coordinates (X-Y per section, Methods, Anatomical tracing) with the medial lemniscus as the SNc-VTA border. Reproduced when the median dorsoventral position of Anxa1+ DANs is ventral to that of Aldh1a1+/Anxa1- and Th-only DANs, most Anxa1+ DANs lie in SNc, and their median mediolateral distance from the midline decreases from the most anterior to the most posterior section. The paper gives no measure or test; this rule is set here.

claims.statement: In MP-early mice the number of Anxa1+ DANs in the ventral tier of the SNc and the fraction of Anxa1+ DANs among Th+ SNc cells are significantly reduced, while the VTA Anxa1+ DANs are not reduced.
claims.source: Results, Anxa1 is a marker of an early PD vulnerable SNc DAN subpopulation, paragraph 3; Figure 1F to 1H; Figure S1
claims.quote: These experiments revealed a significant reduction in the number of Anxa1+ DANs in the ventral tier of the SNc in MP-early mice ... we observed a significant decrease in the fraction of Anxa1+ DANs relative to the total Th+ cells in the SNc, whereas no reduction was found in the Anxa1+ DANs of the VTA
claims.criterion: Per mouse, the proportions of the three SNc subpopulations (Anxa1+ Aldh1a1+ Th+, Aldh1a1+ Anxa1- Th+, Th+ only) among Th+ cells; two-way ANOVA genotype by subtype with Sidak's post hoc, as in the legend of Figure 1H. Reproduced when the interaction has p < 0.05 and the Anxa1+ proportion is lower in MP-early mice at Sidak p < 0.05. The legend does not say which subtype carries p = 0.0452 and which p < 0.0001; both are reported. The reduced count of Anxa1+ DANs in the ventral tier (Figure 1G, a dorsoventral line graph) has no test in the text; it is reported per mouse and not judged. The VTA part (Figure S1) is a claim of absence whose test is in the supplement, which was not read; it is judged with the same two-way ANOVA and Sidak test on VTA cells, reproduced when the Anxa1+ fraction does not differ at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In iPSC-derived DANs from PD patients with SNCA triplication, ANXA1 mRNA is significantly reduced against healthy donors, while ALDH1A1 is not significantly altered.
claims.source: Results, Anxa1 is a marker of an early PD vulnerable SNc DAN subpopulation, paragraph 4; Figure 1I and 1J
claims.quote: While ALDH1A1 expression was not significantly altered, we observed a significant reduction in ANXA1 expression in iPSC-DANs carrying the SNCA-trp mutation
claims.criterion: RT-qPCR normalized to B2M (Methods). The legend names no test and no n. The Methods' two-group tests are (a) the two-sided unpaired t-test per gene and (b) multiple two-sided unpaired t-tests with Holm-Sidak adjustment over the genes compared (Methods); both are applied to the normalized expression per line or culture. Reproduced when, under a reading, ANXA1 is lower in SNCA-trp at p < 0.05 and ALDH1A1 does not differ at p < 0.05. Whether the unit is a donor line or a differentiation is open; both are run where the data allow.

claims.statement: After a mild unilateral 6-OHDA lesion, the Anxa1+ fraction of SNc DANs is significantly lower on the lesioned side than on the intact side.
claims.source: Results, Anxa1 is a marker of an early PD vulnerable SNc DAN subpopulation, paragraph 5; Figure 1K to 1M
claims.quote: In this model, we observed a significant decrease in the Anxa1+ fraction in the SNc compared to the intact side
claims.criterion: Per mouse and side, the proportions of the three SNc subpopulations among Th+ cells; RM two-way ANOVA side by subtype with Sidak's post hoc, as in the legend. The residual df of 9 with 4 mice fits side as the repeated factor and subtype as a between factor (12 mouse-subtype rows, 12 - 3 = 9); that layout is used, and the fully repeated layout is a variant. Reproduced when the interaction has p < 0.05 and the Anxa1+ proportion is lower on the lesioned side at Sidak p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The low-dose 6-OHDA model gives a partial loss of about 50% of Th+ DANs.
claims.source: Results, Anxa1 is a marker of an early PD vulnerable SNc DAN subpopulation, paragraph 5; Figure S1
claims.quote: This approach established a mild degeneration model, resulting in partial loss (∼50%) of Th+ DANs
claims.criterion: Loss is one minus the ratio of Th+ SNc cells on the lesioned side to the intact side. The text does not say how mice are combined; readings are (a) per mouse, then the mean over mice, and (b) counts pooled over mice. Whether SNc alone or SNc and VTA are counted is shown in Figure S1, which was not read; both readings are run, with (a) and (b) for each.

claims.statement: In 24-week-old cAtg7KO mice with Lewy body-like inclusions the SNc shows a specific, significant reduction of Anxa1+ DANs.
claims.source: Results, Anxa1 is a marker of an early PD vulnerable SNc DAN subpopulation, paragraph 5; Figure 1N to 1P
claims.quote: In the SNc of cAtg7KO mice, we observed a specific and significant reduction in Anxa1+ DANs
claims.criterion: As in fig1h-mp-early-anxa1-loss, two-way ANOVA genotype by subtype with Sidak's post hoc. Reproduced when the interaction has p < 0.05, the Anxa1+ proportion is lower in cAtg7KO at Sidak p < 0.05, and no other subtype is lower at p < 0.05 (the legend reports one post hoc difference only).

claims.statement: In the 6-OHDA and cAtg7KO models the Anxa1+ fraction in the VTA is not significantly changed.
claims.source: Results, Anxa1 is a marker of an early PD vulnerable SNc DAN subpopulation, paragraph 5; Figure S1
claims.quote: Notably, analyses of the VTA in both models revealed no significant effects on the Anxa1+ fraction
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The test is in Figure S1, which was not read; the paper's tests for the matching SNc panels are an RM two-way ANOVA (6-OHDA) and a two-way ANOVA (cAtg7KO) with Sidak's post hoc, and these are applied to VTA proportions. Reproduced when, in each model, the Anxa1+ fraction does not differ at Sidak p < 0.05; the size of the difference is reported.

claims.statement: Anxa1+ DANs extend long dendrites deep into the anterior and medial SNr, with a dendron-like structure in anterior SNr.
claims.source: Results, Specialized organization of Anxa1+ DANs, paragraphs 1 and 3; Figure 2C to 2E and 2I
claims.quote: We observed that Anxa1+ DANs extend long dendrites deep into the anterior and medial portions of the SNr
claims.criterion: Anatomical images; the paper gives no measure or test. Reproduced when eYFP+ dendrites are present in SNr and their density is higher in anterior than posterior and in medial than lateral SNr sections of the images. This rule is set here, as the paper gives none.

claims.statement: Anxa1+ DANs project densely to the most dorsal domain of the CP, with a density gradient enriched anteromedially, and sparsely to the core and medial shell of the ACB.
claims.source: Results, Specialized organization of Anxa1+ DANs, paragraph 1; Figure 2F to 2H
claims.quote: we found that Anxa1+ DANs formed a dense projection to the most dorsal domain of the CP (dCP) and some axonal labeling in the core and medial shell of the ACB ... Anxa1+ axonal labeling revealed a pronounced density gradient enriched in the anteromedial regions of the dCP
claims.criterion: eYFP optical density in coronal striatal sections (OD, Figure 2 abbreviations). The paper gives no test. Reproduced when the dorsal band of CP has higher eYFP density than central CP and ACB in each section, and the dCP density is higher in anterior and medial than posterior and lateral portions. Region boundaries are drawn from the atlas; the band depth is open. This rule is set here, as the paper gives none.
