Reproduced when all four hold; partially reproduced when two or three hold; not reproduced otherwise. Whether GS with MLi-2 differs from WT is reported. The uncropped blots are not re-quantified.

claims.statement: RIM1 and RIM2 bind unphosphorylated RAB3A in preference to RAB3A phosphorylated at T86, while RILPL1 and RILPL2 prefer the phosphorylated form.
claims.source: Figure 3D to 3F; Results, Phosphorylation of RAB3A decreases its binding to the effector proteins RIM1 and RIM2 from mouse brain, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The RAB3A effector proteins RIM1 and RIM2 showed a marked preference for binding to unphosphorylated RAB3A (Fig. 3D, E) ... Conversely, we found that p-RAB3A preferentially associated with RILPL1 and RILPL2 (Fig. 3D, F)
claims.criterion: The DIA-NN protein intensities of the six RAB3A and six p-RAB3A pulldowns deposited in PXD065125 (FilteredDataset.pg_matrix.Brain_Rab3A.csv), log2, compared per protein by the paired two-sided Student t-test of Figure 3E and 3F, replicates paired in the order of the runs, over the pairs with both values. For each gene the protein group whose genes field is that gene alone is used; where there are several, the one with the most values, the others reported. Four comparisons decide the outcome, RIM1 and RIM2 higher with RAB3A, RILPL1 and RILPL2 higher with p-RAB3A, each at p < 0.05. Reproduced when all four hold; partially reproduced when two or three hold; not reproduced otherwise. The p values are reported next to the paper's (RIM2 0.011, RILPL1 0.002). The Methods' imputation with an unpaired test, and the deposited limma table, are variants.

claims.statement: Fewer TH+/VAMP2+ striatal synaptosomes from G2019S mice contain bassoon, and the remaining bassoon clusters are larger.
claims.source: Figure 4D and 4E; Results, LRRK2 alters the composition and organization of active zone release sites in dopaminergic striatal synaptosomes, paragraph 2
claims.quote: we found a significant decrease in the percentage of TH + /VAMP2+ synaptosomes that contained the active zone marker bassoon (Fig. 4D). In addition, the remaining active zone clusters in LRRK2G2019S TH + /VAMP2+ synaptosomes had an increased average area of bassoon staining when compared to wildtype (Fig. 4E)
claims.criterion: Two parts. (A) The per-area values of the source data, two-tailed unpaired Student t-tests over areas as in the legend; the percentage of TH+/VAMP2+ synaptosomes with bassoon lower in GS with p < 0.05, and the bassoon area higher in GS with p < 0.05. (B) The Methods' FIJI procedure re-run on the images (folder BSN for the percentage, BSN-area for the area; genotype and mouse from the file name, wt or ki; channels as the archive annotates them, 488 bassoon, 568 TH, 647 VAMP2). Rolling-ball background subtraction, radius 33 pixels; ImageJ's Default threshold; particles 0.04 to 0.40 um2 (TH 0.06 to 0.60) with circularity 0.30 to 1.00; a particle is positive for a protein when its mean intensity is more than twice the image mean. Per image, the percentage of TH+ VAMP2+ particles of the VAMP2 segmentation that are bassoon+, and the mean area of the bassoon and TH overlaps that are VAMP2+, read as (i) the area of the overlap or (ii) the area of the bassoon particle; then the same t-tests over images. Reproduced when (A) gives both effects and (B) gives both, in the same direction at p < 0.05, under one reading; partially reproduced when (A) gives both and (B) does not, or (A) gives one; not reproduced when (A) gives neither. Counts of areas and images are reported against the legend's.

claims.statement: RIM1 is reduced in striatal synaptosomes of G2019S mice (p = 0.0245) but not in other striatal fractions or the SNc.
claims.source: Figure 4H to 4L; Results, LRRK2 alters the composition and organization of active zone release sites in dopaminergic striatal synaptosomes, paragraph 3
claims.quote: However, we observed a decrease in RIM1 levels in the LRRK2G2019S synaptosome fraction compared to controls (Fig. 4I and Supplementary Fig. 4F). In contrast, RIM1 levels in other striatal fractions or SNc lysates did not change (Fig. 4J–L)
claims.criterion: The RIM1 values of the source data for synaptosomes (Figure 4I), the S1 fraction (4J) and the SNc (4L), each compared by a two-tailed unpaired Student t-test. Reproduced when GS is lower in synaptosomes with p < 0.05 and neither the S1 nor the SNc comparison has p < 0.05; partially reproduced when the synaptosome result holds and one of the others has p < 0.05; not reproduced when the synaptosome result does not hold. The p value is reported next to the paper's 0.0245. The uncropped blots are not re-quantified.

claims.statement: Bassoon cluster density is reduced and cluster volume increased in Aldh1a1+ but not Aldh1a1- dopamine axons of G2019S mice, and the same holds in Anxa1+ axons.
claims.source: Figure 5D, 5E, 5G and 5H; Results, LRRK2 disrupts the number and composition of active zone release sites in vulnerable dopamine axons, paragraph 1
claims.quote: We observed a decrease in the density of bassoon+ clusters in vulnerable Aldh1a1+ but not resilient Aldh1a1- axons of LRRK2G2019S, compared to LRRK2WT mice (Fig. 5D) ... an increase in the volume of the remaining bassoon clusters in Aldh1a1+ but not Aldh1a1- dopamine axons ... We confirmed these findings using an independent mouse line, Anxa1Cre (Fig. 5F–H).
claims.criterion: The per-section values of the source data. A section entered twice (identical values in both cell types and both measures) is counted once; the values as deposited are a variant. Aldh1a1 mice, for density (5D) and volume (5E) each, a two-way ANOVA of cell type and genotype with interaction over sections, as the legend's degrees of freedom imply, and Sidak-adjusted comparisons of GS with WT within each cell type on the pooled variance. Anxa1 mice (5G, 5H), two-tailed unpaired Student t-tests. Six parts. (1) Aldh1a1+ density lower in GS, p < 0.05. (2) Aldh1a1- density, p >= 0.05. (3) Aldh1a1+ volume higher in GS, p < 0.05. (4) Aldh1a1- volume, p >= 0.05. (5) Anxa1 density lower in GS, p < 0.05. (6) Anxa1 volume higher in GS, p < 0.05. Reproduced when all six hold; partially reproduced when three to five hold; not reproduced otherwise. Section counts are reported against the legend's. The 542 GB of SIM images are matched to the source data by file name only; the Imaris analysis is not re-run.

claims.statement: The volume occupied by TH+ fibres in the dorsal striatum does not differ between G2019S and WT mice.
claims.source: Figure 5I and 5J; Results, LRRK2 disrupts the number and composition of active zone release sites in vulnerable dopamine axons, paragraph 2
claims.quote: We found no differences in the volume (Fig. 5I, J, Supplementary Fig. 5C), area, and intensity of TH signal in immunopositive ALDH1A1 fibers (Supplementary Fig. 5D, E) in the dorsal striatum.
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, judged on the legend's two-tailed unpaired Student t-test over the per-section TH volumes of the source data at p < 0.05. Reproduced when the test does not find a difference and not reproduced when it does; the difference of means and Cohen's d are reported either way. The images are matched to the source data by file name and counted; the Imaris analysis is not re-run.

claims.statement: In vivo, JF608-HTL is 3.6 times brighter than JF585-HTL with similar voltage sensitivity, giving a 50% increase in spike signal-to-noise ratio.
claims.source: Results, Molecular and optical tools for wide-area all-optical electrophysiology, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 1A to E
claims.quote: we found the redder JF608-HTL to be 3.6 times brighter, with similar voltage sensitivity, leading to a 50% increase in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) in vivo
claims.criterion: Same cells imaged with JF585-HTL, then with JF608-HTL ten days later, under the same 590 nm illumination (Supplementary Figure 1A to E). The paper does not say how the ratios are formed; readings (a) ratio of the mean over cells, (b) median of per-cell ratios. Reproduced when the ratio of photon counts and the SNR increase are within tolerance under one reading and both one-sided rank-sum tests give p <= 0.001.

claims.statement: Soma-targeted red illumination raised the signal-to-background ratio about 7.5-fold, from 0.15 +/- 0.05 to 1.12 +/- 0.32 (mean +/- s.d., 320 cells).
claims.source: Results, Molecular and optical tools, paragraph 4; Figure 1B, 1C; Supplementary Figure 5
claims.quote: This targeting increased the signal-to-background ratio ∼7.5-fold, from 0.15 ± 0.05 to 1.12 ± 0.32 (mean ± s.d., n = 320 cells
claims.criterion: Needs wide-field and targeted images of the same field. The paper does not define signal-to-background; readings (a) (cell fluorescence minus background) divided by background, (b) cell fluorescence divided by background, with background taken from the pixels around each soma outside any cell. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Single-spike SNR (spike height over baseline shot noise) was 4.5 +/- 0.7; the estimated false-discovery proportion of spike detection was 17 +/- 13% and the false-negative rate 28 +/- 19%.
claims.source: Results, Molecular and optical tools, paragraph 5; Supplementary Figure 7
claims.quote: The single-spike SNR (spike-height:baseline shot noise) was 4.5 ± 0.7 (mean ± s.d.). Using a fitted mixture model, we estimated the spike-detection false-discovery proportion to be 17 ± 13% across all neurons, and false-negative rate to be 28 ± 19%
claims.criterion: As in Methods, Detecting spikes; SNR is spike height (mean of the spike Gaussian of the two truncated Gaussian mixture) over shot noise (1.4826 times the median absolute deviation of the one-frame difference); error rates from the fitted mixture. Over the 520 cells of Supplementary Figure 7 (two mice). Which session and which 520 cells are not given; readings (a) the behavior sessions, (b) every session, with QC cells or all cells with a fit. Reproduced when the three means are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: After 1 h of continuous imaging at 16 mW/mm2, spike SNR fell to 76 +/- 13% of its initial value.
claims.source: Results, Molecular and optical tools, paragraph 5; Supplementary Figure 8
claims.quote: After 1 h of continuous voltage imaging at 16 mW/mm 2 , the spike SNR decreased to 76 ± 13% of its initial value
claims.criterion: SNR per cell in 3 min chunks (Supplementary Figure 8A), n = 520 cells, two mice; the ratio of the chunk ending at 60 min to the first chunk, mean over cells. Whether the mean of ratios or ratio of means is meant is open; both are shown, and the claim holds when either is within tolerance.

claims.statement: Targeted stimulation of 76 randomly chosen cells raised their mean firing rate 16-fold, while the unstimulated cells rose only 1.4-fold.
claims.source: Figure 1D legend; Results, Molecular and optical tools, paragraph 6
claims.quote: Stimulation increased the average firing rate of the stimulated cells (blue) 16-fold, and of the un-stimulated cells (red) 1.4-fold
claims.criterion: From the 3 s stimulation epochs repeated every 40 s (Figure 1D); rate during stimulation epochs over rate outside them. Readings (a) ratio of population mean rates, (b) mean of per-cell ratios. The dandiset description does not list this session; if it is absent the claim cannot be tested.

claims.statement: Displacing the stimulation spot from the soma showed that off-target excitation decays with length constants of 47 um for subthreshold voltage and 25 um for firing rate.
claims.source: Results, Molecular and optical tools, paragraph 6; Supplementary Figure 9
claims.quote: we laterally displaced the stimulation spots from the somas and found the excitatory response decayed with length constants of 47 and 25 μm for subthreshold voltage and firing rate, respectively
claims.criterion: Lattice experiment of Methods, Characterization of blue light off-target effects (1000 trials, 20 distance bins of 15 um; voltage increase 60 to 190 ms after onset minus -130 to 0 ms; rate increase 0 to 130 ms minus -130 to 0 ms). The fit is not given; readings (a) exponential with no offset fitted to the population-average increase by bin, (b) the same on log values. The dandiset description does not list this session.

claims.statement: The recordings sampled about 20% of neurons in the focal plane and about 12% (320 of 2,702) of NDNF-positive L1 interneurons in the cylinder under the field of view; their density was 2,860 per mm3.
claims.source: Results, Molecular and optical tools, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 6
claims.quote: we recorded from ∼20% of the neurons in a focal plane of depth 50 μm and thickness ∼40 μm, and ∼12% (320/2,702) of all the NDNF-positive L1 interneurons
claims.criterion: Needs the spinning-disk z-stack (Supplementary Figure 6), segmented with a fine-tuned Cellpose 3.0 model; the dandiset description does not list it. If absent, the claim cannot be tested.

claims.statement: Spike-rate adaptation is weakly positively correlated with spike after-depolarization (R = 0.23, p = 1.9E-8, 564 neurons, 2 mice).
claims.source: Results, Intrinsic excitability, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 10E
claims.quote: firing rate adaptation was positively correlated with spike after-depolarization (V adp; Supplementary Fig. 10E, R = 0.23, p = 1.9E-8, Pearson correlation, n = 564 neurons, 2 mice
claims.criterion: Per-cell adaptation (third step) and V_adp as defined in Methods, Calculating neural intrinsic excitability properties, from the sparseOpto sessions of both mice, pooled. The cells giving n = 564 are not stated; readings (a) QC cells with finite values of both properties, (b) all cells with finite values. Reproduced when R is within tolerance with p < 0.05 under one reading.

claims.statement: Ward hierarchical clustering of the five z-scored intrinsic properties of the 320 cells of one mouse gives three bins of 94, 116 and 110 cells.
claims.source: Figure 2C legend
claims.quote: We divided these cells into 3 bins via hierarchical clustering (left panel), n = 94, 116, and 110 for clusters 1, 2, and 3 respectively
claims.criterion: As in code, reproduce_figure2_from_nwb.m (linkage of the column-wise z-scored five properties of all 320 cells of M-YQ0201-29, Ward's method, cluster with maxclust 3), which the code README says should give these counts exactly; hence tolerance 0. The three counts are compared as a set, as cluster labels are arbitrary.

claims.statement: Bin 1 has the highest firing rate and the highest optical rheobase; bin 2 the lowest firing rate, the lowest adaptation and the highest membrane time constant; bin 3 the highest after-depolarization and adaptation and the lowest optical rheobase.
claims.source: Results, Intrinsic excitability, paragraph 4; Figure 2G to K
claims.quote: Bin 1 had both the highest firing rate and the highest optical rheobase (i.e. it required the greatest depolarization to begin spiking); bin 2 had the lowest firing rate and lowest spike-rate adaptation, and the highest membrane time constant; bin 3 showed the highest after-depolarization and spike-rate adaptation and the lowest optical rheobase
claims.criterion: The paper calls these comparisons descriptive. Bins identified by their sizes (94, 116, 110). For each property the bin medians (the boxes of Figure 2G to K), after removing values more than 6 s.d. from the mean as the code does (rmoutliers, 'mean', ThresholdFactor 6). "Firing rate" is not named; readings (a) maximum firing rate (Figure 2I, one of the five properties), (b) the cluster-average firing rate of Figure 2F. Reproduced when all eight orderings hold; partially reproduced when six or seven hold. The code's two-sided rank-sum p values between bins are reported.

claims.statement: The two mice show similar broad distributions of intrinsic properties; by two-sided rank-sum tests they differ in optical rheobase (p <= 0.001) and membrane time constant (0.01 < p <= 0.05), not in V_adp, maximum rate or adaptation.
claims.source: Results, Intrinsic excitability, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 10H (marks read from the rendered PDF page 16)
claims.quote: We repeated this protocol on two mice and saw similar broad distributions of intrinsic properties in both animals
claims.criterion: Per property, two-sided rank-sum test between the sparseOpto sessions of the two mice. The legend gives n = 320 per mouse; readings (a) all cells with a finite value, (b) QC cells. Reproduced when rheobase and membrane time constant differ at p <= 0.05 and the other three do not; partially reproduced when four of the five calls match.

claims.statement: Optogenetic mapping found 802 inhibitory connections among 7,280 tested pairs in one mouse and 667 among 7,032 in the other, about 3 +/- 3 outgoing and 3 +/- 3 incoming per cell of 25 +/- 9 tested, a pairwise probability of 11 +/- 9% within 400 um.
claims.source: Results, Synaptic inhibition, paragraph 6
claims.quote: We identified 802 statistically significant synaptic connections out of 7,280 pairs tested in one mouse, and 667 of 7,032 pairs tested in a second mouse. This corresponds to 3 ± 3 outgoing connections per cell and 3 ± 3 incoming connections per cell out of 25 ± 9 possible connections tested in each direction (mean ± s.d., n = 576 cells, 2 mice
claims.criterion: Count of stored synaptic_connection flags among ordered pairs of QC cells at most 400 um apart, per mouse; the 60 to 400 um band is a second reading (code, loadFigure5SessionFromNWB.m lines 15 to 23, 800 connections for M-YQ0201-27 in the band, 814 without it, 667 for M-YQ0201-29). The paper's "pairs tested" may be (a) ordered pairs of QC cells within 400 um, or (b) pairs with a stored IPSP measurement; both shown. Per-cell probability is connections over pairs tested for that cell (outgoing), mean +/- s.d. over 576 cells.

claims.statement: The median unitary IPSP among connected pairs was -2.8% of a spike height per presynaptic spike, while correlated spontaneous fluctuations were about 20% of a spike height.
claims.source: Results, Synaptic inhibition, paragraphs 4 and 5
claims.quote: Median unitary IPSP amplitude among connected cells was -2.8% of a spike height ... In contrast, correlated fluctuations were ∼20% of a spike height
claims.criterion: IPSP amplitude is the stored ipsp_amplitude_norm_per_presynaptic_spike (positive values, sign flipped), median over pairs with synaptic_connection set, both mice pooled; the per-mouse medians are shown. For the fluctuations the paper gives no method and no code computes the 20%; the reading chosen here is the code's cross-STA depolarization (code, reproduce_figure4_from_nwb.m, range of the quiet-state spike-triggered voltage over lags -100 to -2 frames, mean over pairs 60 to 400 um apart), per mouse and averaged. Reproduced when both are within tolerance (for the pooled or a per-mouse median).

claims.statement: The mapping detected IPSPs with 50% probability at an amplitude of -2 +/- 1.1% of a spike, and spikelets at 0.8 +/- 0.48% of a spike.
claims.source: Results, Synaptic inhibition, paragraph 5; Results, Gap junction coupling, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 15
claims.quote: This procedure established a 50% detection probability for IPSP amplitude of -2 ± 1.1% of a spike (mean ± s.d., n = 100 neuron-pairs from each mouse, near detection cutoff) ... This procedure established a 50% detection probability for spikelet amplitudes of 0.8 ± 0.48% of a spike
claims.criterion: The paper and code do not say how the 50% point was estimated beyond "n = 100 neuron-pairs from each mouse, near detection cutoff". Readings (a) for the 100 pairs per mouse whose statistic lies nearest the Benjamini-Hochberg cutoff, the amplitude of each, mean +/- s.d.; (b) for those pairs, the amplitude of a scaled template added to null waveforms that is detected in half of the null draws. Reproduced when the mean is within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Spikelet mapping found 3,553 directed electrical connections among 7,280 tested pairs in one mouse and 2,199 among 7,032 in the other, 10 +/- 6 outgoing and 10 +/- 5 incoming per cell, a pairwise probability of 41 +/- 15%; the median spikelet was 1.2% of a spike.
claims.source: Results, Gap junction coupling, paragraphs 2 and 3
claims.quote: We identified 3,553 statistically significant directed functional electrical connections out of 7,280 pairs tested in one mouse, and 2,199 of 7,032 in a second mouse. This corresponds to 10 ± 6 outgoing connections per cell and 10 ± 5 incoming connections per cell ... the pair-wise probability of unidirectional gap junction connections above our detection threshold was 41 ± 15%
claims.criterion: As for synaptic-connection-counts, with the stored gap_junction_connection flag and spikelet_amplitude (frames 0 and 1 against frames -4, -3, -2, 4, 5, 6 of the cross-STA, Methods). The connection counts are taken in the 60 to 400 um band, as the code settles (loadFigure5SessionFromNWB.m lines 15 to 23 give 3553 for M-YQ0201-27 and 2199 for M-YQ0201-29 in that band); all pairs within 400 um is a variant. For "pairs tested" the readings of synaptic-connection-counts apply, with or without pairs under 60 um.

claims.statement: During Hadamard-coded stimulation, stimulated cells fired at 25.4 +/- 16.6 Hz and non-stimulated cells at 3.9 +/- 4.5 Hz; each cell received about 640 stimuli and fired about 12,380 evoked spikes in total.
claims.source: Results, Gap junction coupling, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Stimulated cells spiked rapidly (25.4 ± 16.6 Hz, mean ± s.d.) compared to non-stimulated cells (3.9 ± 4.5 Hz), and evoked spikes were largely uncorrelated between cells. Each cell received on average 640 stimuli, which elicited on average a cumulative 12,380 spikes per cell
claims.criterion: In the Hadamard chunks of the sparsePulseHad sessions, each QC cell's spike rate during its 750 ms on blocks and during its off blocks; mean +/- s.d. over cells, both mice pooled. Whether "non-stimulated cells" means cells in their off blocks or cells never stimulated in a block is open; the first is the reading, as every cell is stimulated with a 50% duty cycle.

claims.statement: Fluorescence scattered from a spiking cell decays over a much shorter distance than the spikelet amplitude (spikelet to scatter ratio above 2.5 at 60 um), so pairs under 60 um were excluded.
claims.source: Results, Gap junction coupling, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 17
claims.quote: This scattered fluorescence signal decayed over a substantially shorter distance than the spikelet amplitude (at 60 μm separation, spikelet:scattered fluorescence > 2.5
claims.criterion: Needs interstitial pixels within 400 um of each triggering cell (Methods), which only a movie holds; the dandiset has the raw movie for four blocks of one spontaneous session. Scatter STA normalized by the trigger cell's spike fluorescence (frame 0 minus frame -2), scatter spikelet extracted as a spikelet; 40 um distance bins (Supplementary Figure 17B). Reproduced when the ratio of mean spikelet to mean scatter in the bin at 60 um exceeds 2.25 and the scatter falls with distance faster than the spikelet.

claims.statement: Under high-magnification imaging, spikelet amplitude was strongly correlated with the weight of the post-junctional cell's own spike footprint in the cross-STA image (R = 0.94, 720 pairs from 48 cells), supporting a somatic post-junctional origin.
claims.source: Results, Gap junction coupling, paragraph 5; Supplementary Figure 18D
claims.quote: Spikelet amplitude was strongly correlated with the coefficient of the self-STA footprint fitted to the cross-STA image (R = 0.94, p < 1E-15, n = 720 pairs from 48 cells
claims.criterion: Needs the 7.5x high-magnification recordings (16 cells per field, Voltron2), which the dandiset description does not list. If present, the method of Methods, High magnification spikelet footprint analysis.

claims.statement: Correcting the IPSP matrix for spikes evoked in non-targeted cells by lasso regression changes little; the corrected and raw matrices correlate with R = 0.82 and fewer than 20% of significant IPSPs differ by more than 20%.
claims.source: Methods, Analysis for mapping synaptic connections, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 16C
claims.quote: The two matrices are highly correlated, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.82, p < 2E-308, n = 1755 pairs from 2 mice, and less than 20% of statistically significant IPSPs differ from the connectivity matrix by more than 20%
claims.criterion: Model IPSP matrix R = S W with S the evoked spikes per stimulus in targeted and non-targeted cells; W by lasso. The penalty and the choice of the 1755 pairs are not given; readings for the penalty (a) the value minimizing 10-fold cross-validated error, (b) the largest within one standard error of it. Reproduced when R is within tolerance and the fraction is below 22% under one reading.

claims.statement: Synaptic connectivity had an exponential degree distribution, a connection probability of 24% for cells under 150 um apart and a length constant of about 105 um; gap junction probability was 83% under 150 um with a 159 um length constant.
claims.source: Results, The structure of connectivity in L1, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 19C to F
claims.quote: The synaptic connectivity matrix had a single-scale network structure 47 , with an exponential degree distribution. The probability of connection was 24% for closely separated cells (< 150 μm) and fell with a ∼105 μm length constant (Supplementary Fig. 19C,D). The gap junction matrix showed greater connectivity (connection probability 83% for cells separated by < 150 μm) and fell with a 159 μm length constant
claims.criterion: No code computes these. Probability is connected over tested ordered pairs of QC cells by distance, both mice pooled (per-mouse values shown). The fit is not given; readings (a) p(r) = A exp(-r/lambda) by least squares on binned probability, (b) a line fitted to log probability, with bins of 30 um (as Figure 3F, 3H) or 60 um (as Figure 3E, 3G), from 60 um (gap) or 0 um (synaptic) to 400 um. Degree distribution exponential when an exponential fits the in- and out-degree histograms better than a power law (lower residual on log counts), a reading chosen here. Reproduced when the four numbers are within tolerance under one reading and the degree distributions are exponential.

claims.statement: IPSP and spikelet amplitudes both decay with the distance between the cells.
claims.source: Figure 3E, 3G; Results, The structure of connectivity in L1, paragraph 2
claims.quote: IPSP and spikelet amplitudes both decayed with cell-cell distance
claims.criterion: As in code, reproduce_figure3_from_nwb.m panels E and G. IPSP pairs with stored amplitude above 1e-3 (no significance gate), spikelet pairs all, 60 to 400 um, six equal bins (linspace(60,400,7)), per mouse. The caption's 60 um bins give the same range. The connected-only selection is shown as a variant. Reproduced when, in both mice, the median in the nearest bin exceeds the median in the farthest bin for both measures and the Spearman correlation of amplitude with distance is negative at p < 0.05 (the test is a reading chosen here).

claims.statement: Spikelet peak times increase with distance, giving a conduction speed of 0.28 m/s, consistent across two mice.
claims.source: Figure 3H; Results, The structure of connectivity in L1, paragraph 2
claims.quote: The spikelet peak times, determined by sub-frame interpolation, showed a distance-dependent time delay corresponding to a conduction speed of 0.28 m/s, consistent across n = 2 mice
claims.criterion: As in code, reproduce_figure3_from_nwb.m panel H. Mean Hadamard cross-spike STA of all pairs in twelve 30 um bins from 60 to 420 um (the caption's ten 30 um bins are the variant), each bin's time mean subtracted; coarse peak within 16 frames of lag 0; cubic fit over frames -2 to +4 around it and its maximum; delay in seconds at 1.27 ms per frame; distance regressed on delay with intercept, pooling 12 bins times 2 mice. Reproduced when the pooled speed is within tolerance; per-mouse speeds are shown.

claims.statement: IPSP and spikelet amplitudes both follow approximately log-normal distributions.
claims.source: Results, The structure of connectivity in L1, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 19A, B
claims.quote: IPSP and spikelet amplitudes both followed approximately log-normal distributions
claims.criterion: Amplitudes of connected pairs, both mice pooled. The paper shows a Gaussian fit to the log histogram and no test. Reading chosen here, reproduced when, for both measures, the skewness of log amplitudes lies within -0.5 to 0.5 and the skewness of raw amplitudes exceeds 1.

claims.statement: The population-average effect of one L1 spike is a brief excitatory pulse of about 2 ms spreading at 0.28 m/s with a decay length of about 160 um, followed by inhibition that peaks around 30 ms and decays with a time constant of about 35 ms.
claims.source: Results, The structure of connectivity in L1, paragraph 3; Supplementary Movie 3
claims.quote: a single L1 action potential evoked a brief excitatory pulse with a duration of ∼2 ms that rapidly propagated outward (0.28 m/s) with a ∼160 μm decay length constant, followed by a slower field of inhibition that peaked around 30 ms and decayed with a time constant of ∼35 ms
claims.criterion: The paper gives no method for Movie 3. The inhibitory part is read from the population-average IPSP waveform per presynaptic spike (blue_pulse_ipsp minus crosstalk, unconnected pairs counted as zero, as code panel 3F), the excitatory part from the population-average spikelet waveform (code panel 3H). Peak time measured from the stimulus or spike; decay from an exponential fitted after the peak; duration as full width at half maximum; length constant as in connection-distance-structure for the product of connection probability and mean amplitude. Readings for the time zero of the IPSP (a) pulse onset, (b) pulse end. Reproduced when the four values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: IPSP amplitude of a pair is strongly correlated with the presynaptic cell's mean output to other cells (R = 0.61) and only weakly with the postsynaptic cell's mean input from other cells (R = 0.26).
claims.source: Figure 3J, 3K; Results, The structure of connectivity in L1, paragraph 4
claims.quote: The per-cell mean outgoing connection strength was a better predictor of single-synapse strength than was mean incoming connection strength (outgoing: R = 0.61, p = 1.1E-51, n = 497 pairs, vs. incoming: R = 0.26, p = 4.3E-9, n = 482 pairs
claims.criterion: As in code, reproduce_figure3_from_nwb.m (M-YQ0201-29). Pairs with synaptic_connection set, 60 to 400 um, IPSP tau SE/tau below its 90th percentile over all pairs with a defined SE, tau inside the range of positive tau values shrunk by 1e-3 at each end (code, tauLimits); leave-one-out arithmetic mean of the other pairs' amplitudes of the same presynaptic (J) or postsynaptic (K) cell; Pearson R on natural logs of pairs with both values positive. The code README expects R = 0.61 and 0.26 with a mask count of 561; the paper's n (497, 482) is read as the plotted pairs with a finite leave-one-out mean, shown with the counts. Reproduced when both R are within tolerance and the outgoing R exceeds the incoming R.

claims.statement: IPSP decay time constant is correlated with the mean time constant of other inputs to the postsynaptic cell (R = 0.33) and not with that of the presynaptic cell's other outputs (R = 0.07, p = 0.06).
claims.source: Figure 3M, 3N; Results, The structure of connectivity in L1, paragraph 5
claims.quote: The per-cell mean inbound synaptic time constant, 〈 τ kj 〉 k ≠ i , was a better predictor of single-synapse time constant τ ij than was mean outgoing time constant, 〈 τ ik 〉 k ≠ i (incoming: R = 0.33, p = 4.7E-18, n = 651 pairs, vs. outgoing: R = 0.07, p = 0.06 , n = 653 pairs
claims.criterion: As fig3jk-presynaptic-sets-amplitude, on ipsp_decay of M-YQ0201-27 (code; README expects R = 0.07 and 0.33, mask count 706). Reproduced when the incoming R is within tolerance with p < 0.05 and the outgoing correlation is not significant (p >= 0.05, the paper's test for its absence); the outgoing R and p are reported either way.

claims.statement: A linear mixed-effects model attributes more variance of IPSP amplitude to presynaptic than to postsynaptic identity, and more variance of IPSP decay time constant to postsynaptic than to presynaptic identity, each ordering holding in all but under 0.1% of bootstrap simulations.
claims.source: Figure 3L, 3O legends; Methods, Linear mixed effects model
claims.quote: More variance of IPSP amplitude is explained by presynaptic identity than by postsynaptic identity ... ***: < 0.001 of the simulations produced higher postsynaptic variance ... More variance of IPSP decay time constant is explained by postsynaptic identity than by presynaptic identity
claims.criterion: As in code, tutorials/tutorial5_pre_post_variance. Connected QC pairs of both mice at 60 um or more, positive amplitude; log response ~ 1 + animal + distance term + (1|pre) + (1|post), distance term linear or log distance chosen by AIC of ML fits; decay weighted by 1/(SE^2 + s0^2); REML; 2000 parametric bootstrap refits (seeds 12012, 12014). Reproduced when presynaptic variance exceeds postsynaptic for amplitude and postsynaptic exceeds presynaptic for decay, each in more than 99.9% of the bootstrap replicates.

claims.statement: Gap-junction strength shows little association with pre- or post-junctional identity.
claims.source: Results, The structure of connectivity in L1, paragraph 5
claims.quote: The gap junction connection strength showed little association with pre- or post-junctional identity in this analysis
claims.criterion: The analysis of fig3jk-presynaptic-sets-amplitude applied to spikelet_amplitude of pairs with gap_junction_connection set, 60 to 400 um, each mouse. No number is given; reading chosen here, reproduced when both the outgoing and the incoming log-scale Pearson R are below 0.26, the value the paper calls a weak correlation, in both mice.

claims.statement: In the quiet state subthreshold voltages of nearby cells (60 to 120 um) correlate at 0.6 and the correlation decays with a 2.4 mm length constant; in the whisking state the values are 0.5 and 4.0 mm.
claims.source: Results, Spontaneous spikes and subthreshold voltages have distinct spatiotemporal dynamics, paragraph 3; Figure 4B; Supplementary Figure 20A, D
claims.quote: In the quiet state, the voltage dynamics were strongly correlated between nearby cells (correlation = 0.6, 60 μm < r < 120 μm) and decayed with an exponential length constant of 2.4 mm ( Fig. 4B ; Supplementary Fig. 20D); in the whisking state, the short-range correlation was 0.5 and the decay length constant was 4.0 mm
claims.criterion: As in code, reproduce_figure4_from_nwb.m STATS. Stored state-dependent voltage cross-correlations; 60 um distance bins from 60 to 1800 um; zero-lag value of the 60 to 120 um bin; length constant 1/slope of a line fitted to log zero-lag correlation against distance over all non-empty bins; per mouse, then averaged over the two mice. Recomputing the cross-correlation from the voltage (normalized by the lag-1 s.d.) is a variant. Reproduced when the four values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Subthreshold dynamics are low dimensional; the first 10 principal components explain 72% of the variance in the quiet state and 62% in the whisking state.
claims.source: Results, Spontaneous spikes and subthreshold voltages, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 21B
claims.quote: principal components analysis (PCA) showed that the first 10 components accounted for 72% of the variance in the quiet state and 62% of the variance in the whisking state
claims.criterion: As in Methods, Dimensionality of subthreshold fluctuations; covariance of the subthreshold voltage of the behavior session per state, diagonal replaced by the lag-1 variance where the voltage is not smoothed, eigenvalues over total variance. No code. Open, with readings (a) the stored subthreshold voltage (smoothed, diagonal kept), (b) the normalized voltage with the lag-1 diagonal; and per mouse or averaged over the two mice. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading, with the quiet value above the whisking value.

claims.statement: In the quiet state, but not the whisking state, subthreshold dynamics often show global oscillations between 1 and 10 Hz.
claims.source: Results, Spontaneous spikes and subthreshold voltages, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 21A, C
claims.quote: In the quiet state - but not the whisking state - the subthreshold dynamics often showed global oscillations between 1 and 10 Hz
claims.criterion: Population-average Welch power spectrum of the subthreshold voltage per state (Methods, Frequency spectrum; Welch segment length a standard choice, 2 s). Reading chosen here, reproduced when in both mice the power integrated over 1 to 10 Hz is higher in the quiet than in the whisking state.

claims.statement: Quiet-state oscillations are traveling waves with various directions, a slight bias toward medial-posterior, and a mean speed of 18.2 +/- 8.3 mm/s (3,858 events, 2 mice); a 5 Hz oscillation has a wavelength of about 4 mm.
claims.source: Results, Spontaneous spikes and subthreshold voltages, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 21D to H
claims.quote: with a slight bias toward the medial-posterior direction and an average speed of 18.2 ± 8.3 mm/s (mean ± s.d., n = 3858 events, 2 mice). For a typical 5 Hz oscillation, the wavelength was ∼4 mm
claims.criterion: As in Methods, Wave propagation analysis. Events are peaks of the derivative of the population-average voltage above 3.5 times its s.d. during whisking, in quiet epochs; each event spans the voltage minimum to maximum flanking the peak; speed is the slope of pairwise distance against lag of peak cross-correlation. No code. The slope can be read (a) as distance regressed on lag, (b) lag regressed on distance and inverted; both shown. Direction from the phase gradient (Hilbert phase, 325 um Gaussian smoothing, 160 um grid). Reproduced when the mean speed and the event count are within tolerance under one reading and the circular mean direction lies in the medial-posterior quadrant.

claims.statement: Spike-rate cross-correlograms peak sharply in space (length constants of 277 um quiet and 270 um whisking) and time (50% decay by 2.5 ms lag), unlike subthreshold correlations (2.4 mm, full width at half maximum 80 ms).
claims.source: Results, Spontaneous spikes and subthreshold voltages, paragraph 5; Figure 4C, 4D; Supplementary Figure 20F, G
claims.quote: While the subthreshold cross-correlations decayed slowly over space (quiet-state length constant 2.4 mm) and time (quiet-state full-width at half-maximum 80 ms), the spike-rate cross-correlogram had a peak that was sharply localized in space (length constants of 277 and 270 μm for quiet and whisking state respectively) and time (decayed by 50% at lags of just 2.5 ms
claims.criterion: As in code, reproduce_figure4_from_nwb.m STATS. Synchrony is the correlogram maximum over lags -1 to 1 frame minus the larger of the means over frames -5 to -3 and 3 to 5 (Supplementary Figure 20G); length constants by log-linear fit per mouse, averaged. Readings for the 277 and 270 um (a) the synchrony fit restricted to r < 800 um, (b) the fit of the 2.5 ms-lag correlogram over all bins. FWHM is the code's quiet-state median over bins. The 2.5 ms is read as the half-width of the correlogram peak in the 60 to 120 um bin (code spikeHalfWidth, whisking state as in the code; quiet as a variant). Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Each cell's spontaneous voltage-to-spike relationship (conditional spike rate as a function of subthreshold voltage) is sigmoidal, with substantial cell-to-cell variation in threshold and maximum rate.
claims.source: Results, Threshold nonlinearities and private excursions, paragraph 2; Figure 4E, 4F
claims.quote: These curves all had a characteristic sigmoidal shape, with substantial cell-to-cell variations in threshold and maximum firing rate
claims.criterion: Quiet-state frames without running; P(spk|V) as the histogram of V at spike times over the histogram of all V, divided by 1.27 ms; voltage bins of 0.04 SH from -2 to 2 (code, reproduce_figure4_from_nwb.m). The Methods/caption say V in the 10 ms before spikes, the code uses the sample at the spike frame (the code notes the author kept the wording); both shown. Reading chosen here, reproduced when for more than half of cells a four-parameter logistic fitted over bins holding at least 100 frames explains at least 90% of the variance, and the fitted midpoints and maxima have coefficients of variation above 0.2 across cells.

claims.statement: Voltages of neighbouring cells (under 200 um) are most correlated near rest and during hyperpolarizing fluctuations, and much less as voltage approaches spike threshold.
claims.source: Results, Threshold nonlinearities and private excursions, paragraph 3; Figure 4G
claims.quote: The correlation between V i and V j was strongest near resting potential and for hyperpolarizing fluctuations, but was markedly reduced as the subthreshold voltage approached spike threshold
claims.criterion: As in code, reproduce_figure4_from_nwb.m panel G. Pairs 60 to 200 um apart, both orderings, quiet frames without running, 100 voltage bins from -2 to 2 SH, counts pooled over both mice, P(V_j|V_i). Reading chosen here, reproduced when the slope of the conditional mean of V_j on V_i over V_i from -0.5 to 0.2 SH is at least twice the slope over V_i from 0.5 to 1 SH.

claims.statement: For cells under 200 um apart, self- and cross-STAs of membrane voltage track each other at lags beyond 30 ms, but the spiking cell has a higher baseline and an upward divergence in the 30 ms before its spike.
claims.source: Results, Threshold nonlinearities and private excursions, paragraph 4; Figure 4H, 4I
claims.quote: For cells separated by < 200 μm, the subthreshold components of these two waveforms closely followed each other at lags > 30 ms ( Fig. 4H ). However, the spiking cell saw both a higher baseline and an upward divergence in the self-STA in the 30 ms preceding the spike
claims.criterion: Stored quiet-state spike-triggered voltage, pairs 60 to 200 um (Results, "< 200 um", with the 60 um scatter cut of Figure 4B; code panel H draws its examples from this band, panel I uses all distance bins), per mouse. Reading chosen here, reproduced when in both mice the mean self-STA minus the mean cross-STA is larger at -5 ms than at -30 ms by more than the s.d. of that difference over lags -140 to -30 ms, and the self-STA is above the cross-STA at -30 ms.

claims.statement: Cells with higher optical rheobase fire less at a given subthreshold voltage, both under ramp stimulation and during quiet spontaneous activity.
claims.source: Figure 5A; Results, Intrinsic properties shape subthreshold-to-spiking transfer functions, paragraph 1
claims.quote: in both datasets, cells with higher optical rheobase showed lower firing rate for a given subthreshold depolarization
claims.criterion: As in code, reproduce_figure5_from_nwb.m panel A (M-YQ0201-27, n = 280 cells). Bins by rheobase, five equal-width bins between its 1st and 99th percentiles (code; the caption's quintiles as a variant); P(spk|V) pooled counts per bin, V bins of 0.05 SH; spontaneous from quiet non-running chunks with no blue within 80 um; evoked from the first half of the ramp. Reproduced when, at V = 0.5 SH, rate falls across the five bins with Spearman rho below -0.8 in both conditions (a reading chosen here).

claims.statement: Optical rheobase is negatively correlated with the conditional spike rate at V = 0.5 SH, both evoked (R = -0.59) and spontaneous (R = -0.32).
claims.source: Supplementary Figure 22A, B
claims.quote: Correlation between optogenetically evoked conditional spike rate at VV= 0.5 and optical rheobase. R = -0.59 (Pearson correlation), p = 7.8e-52, n = 543 ... Correlation between spontaneous activity conditional spike rate at VV= 0.5 and optogenetically measured rheobase. R = -0.32 (Pearson correlation), p = 4.1e-14, n = 543
claims.criterion: Per cell, P(spk|V) as in fig5a in the bin containing V = 0.5 SH, both mice pooled. No code. Which 543 cells is open (QC cells give 576); readings (a) QC cells with a finite rate at 0.5 SH in both conditions, (b) cells passing the 1st to 99th percentile rheobase range in each mouse. Reproduced when both R are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Cells with more spike-rate adaptation spike preferentially in response to rapidly rising subthreshold voltage during spontaneous activity (R = 0.26 between adaptation and the conditional rate at dV/dt = 0.35).
claims.source: Figure 5B; Results, Intrinsic properties shape subthreshold-to-spiking transfer functions, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 22C
claims.quote: Cells with higher spike-rate adaptation preferentially spiked in response to rapidly rising inputs
claims.criterion: P(spk|dV/dt) in quiet spontaneous activity with V restricted to 0.2 to 0.8 SH (Methods). The Methods shift dV/dt by 6 ms; the code (panel B) uses an 8-frame centred difference shifted by 4 frames, a median-threshold quiet rule, and a V window applied to 0.25 SH bin centres, in effect 0.25 to 0.75 SH; both shown, Methods first. Per cell, the rate at dV/dt = 0.35, against adaptation, both mice, cells as in supp22-rheobase-correlations. Reproduced when R is within tolerance with p < 0.05 and, in the panel B quintile curves, the highest-adaptation bin has the highest rate at dV/dt = 0.35.

claims.statement: Cells with greater after-depolarization fire more bursts during spontaneous activity (R = 0.52 between V_adp and the 2.5 to 15 ms autocorrelogram).
claims.source: Figure 5C; Results, Intrinsic properties shape subthreshold-to-spiking transfer functions, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 22D
claims.quote: Cells with greater after-depolarization were more likely to fire spikes in bursts
claims.criterion: Burst rate is the mean spike autocorrelogram from lag 2.5 to 15 ms (Methods, Average firing rate and average burst rate), from spontaneous activity in quiet and whisking (Results), both mice, cells as in supp22-rheobase-correlations. The code (panel C) triggers on quiet-state spikes only; shown as a variant. Reproduced when R is within tolerance with p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Relative to distance-matched unconnected controls, a presynaptic spike is followed 15 to 30 ms later by a postsynaptic hyperpolarization of -2.1% of a spike height for the strongest quintile of connections and -1% at median strength; unconnected control pairs instead rise by 1% of a spike height from -20 to -5 ms to 15 to 30 ms.
claims.source: Results, Local connectivity shapes network dynamics, paragraph 2; Figure 5D, 5E; Supplementary Figure 23F
claims.quote: For cell-pairs in the top quintile of synaptic strength, a presynaptic spike induced a median postsynaptic voltage decrease of -2.1% of a spike height in the 15 - 30 ms after a spike, relative to the distance-matched unconnected controls (p = 1.9E-33, n = 293 cell pairs, 2 mice). For the median synaptic strength (among connected pairs), this hyperpolarization was -1% of a spike height (p = 5.7E-39, n = 1,467 cell pairs, 2 mice, Wilcoxon rank sum test ... The STA waveform showed an increase by 1% of a spike height in the interval 15 – 30 ms after the triggering spike vs. the -20 to - 5 ms before the spike
claims.criterion: Voltage suppression per pair is frames 12 to 25 minus frames -17 to -4 of the spontaneous cross-STA (Methods, Effect of connections). Connected pairs with synaptic_connection set, 60 to 400 um, quintiles of IPSP amplitude, both mice; controls per Methods (cell k within 400 um of i and j, not connected to i). No code for the numbers. Open, with readings (a) median over connected pairs of suppression minus the median over their controls; (b) median over connected pairs of (pair suppression minus mean over its own controls); (c) suppression of the quintile average after regressing out the control average (Methods, Estimating cross STAs). "Median strength" read as all connected pairs (n = 1,467) or as the third quintile; both shown. Test, rank-sum of pair suppressions, connected against controls, one-sided (Supplementary Figure 23F) and two-sided. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading and both tests give p < 0.05.

claims.statement: For the strongest quintile of synaptic connections, a presynaptic spike lowers the postsynaptic rate by 0.18 Hz 5 to 13 ms later, a loss of 7e-3 spikes over the IPSP; near median strength, by 0.083 Hz, a loss of 2.7e-3 spikes.
claims.source: Results, Local connectivity shapes network dynamics, paragraph 3; Figure 5E; Supplementary Figure 23D, H
claims.quote: For cell-pairs in the top quintile of synaptic strength, a presynaptic spike induced a median postsynaptic decrease in spike rate of 0.18 Hz in the 5-13 ms after the triggering spike, measured relative to nearby non-connected controls. Integrating the decrease in spike rate over the entire IPSP duration gave a median loss of 7×10 -3 spikes in the post-synaptic cell. For cell-pairs near median synaptic strength (among connected pairs), this decrease was 0.083 Hz, corresponding to a loss of 2.7×10 -3 spikes
claims.criterion: Rate suppression is frames 4 to 10 minus frames -10 to -4 of the spontaneous cross-correlogram (Methods), in Hz; readings for the comparison with controls and for "median strength" as in fig5e-inhibition-in-spontaneous-voltage. The integration window for spikes lost ("the entire IPSP duration") is open; readings (a) 0 to 100 ms, (b) from 0 ms to where the control-subtracted rate returns to zero. Reproduced when the four values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Gap-junction coupling raises spontaneous spike synchrony; for the strongest quintile, synchronous firing (lag <= 2.5 ms) exceeds near-synchronous firing by 0.86 Hz more than in unconnected neighbours, and by 0.32 Hz at median coupling.
claims.source: Results, Local connectivity shapes network dynamics, paragraph 4; Figure 5F, 5G; Supplementary Figure 23I
claims.quote: for cell-pairs in the top quintile of gap junction coupling, the rate of synchronous firing (time lag ≤ 2.5 ms) was 0.86 Hz greater than near-synchronous firing (time lag 5 ms, p = 8.6E-53, n = 1151 pairs, 2 mice, Wilcoxon rank sum test against unconnected neighbors; Supplementary Fig. 23I). Integrating the change in spike rate across the entire spikelet duration gave a gain of 1.7×10 -3 spikes. For the median gap-junctional coupling, the synchrony enhancement was 0.32 Hz (p = 1.9E-61, n = 5752 pairs, 2 mice, Wilcoxon rank sum test against unconnected neighbors), corresponding to a gain of 7×10 -4 spikes
claims.criterion: Synchrony per pair is the maximum of the cross-correlogram over frames -1 to 1 minus the mean of the 3 frames before frame -1 or after frame 1, whichever is larger (Methods). Pairs with gap_junction_connection set, 60 to 400 um; n = 5752 is 3553 + 2199, the counts the code gives in that band (loadFigure5SessionFromNWB.m lines 15 to 23), and Results, Gap junction coupling, paragraph 4, excludes pairs under 60 um from further analysis. Readings for the comparison with controls and for "median coupling" (all pairs or third quintile) as in fig5e-inhibition-in-spontaneous-voltage; spikes gained integrated over the spikelet duration, readings (a) frames -1 to 1, (b) lags with control-subtracted rate above zero around lag 0. Reproduced when the four values are within tolerance under one reading and both rank-sum tests give p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Scaled by connection probability, spikes lost to inhibition per connected pair (2.7e-3, about four times the 7e-4 gained by gap junctions) and spikes gained from gap junctions are approximately balanced.
claims.source: Results, Local connectivity shapes network dynamics, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Hence, oppositely acting synaptic and gap-junctional influences are approximately balanced
claims.criterion: Product of median spikes lost per synaptic pair and synaptic connection probability, against product of median spikes gained per gap-junction pair and gap junction probability, from the values of the claims it depends on (the paper's own numbers give 3.0e-4 and 2.9e-4). Reading chosen here, reproduced when the ratio of the two products lies between 0.5 and 2.

claims.statement: About 49% of recorded neurons are NPY-positive (166 of 320 and 145 of 320); the two subtypes are intermixed and have similar spike SNR and mean spike rate.
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates functional and genetic L1 interneuron subtypes, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 24A to D
claims.quote: Approximately 49% of recorded neurons were NPY (+) (166/320 in mouse 1, 145/320 in mouse 2). The two subtypes were intermixed throughout the field of view, and had similar spike SNR and similar average spike-rate
claims.criterion: Stored gfp_positive over all 320 cells per mouse; which mouse is "mouse 1" is not stated, so the two counts are compared as a set. Similar SNR and rate (Supplementary Figure 24B, D, 257 NPY- and 248 NPY+ behavior-session cells), reading chosen here, two-sided rank-sum p >= 0.05 or a difference of medians under 10%. Intermixed, reading chosen here, a two-sided Kolmogorov-Smirnov test of x and y coordinates between subtypes with p >= 0.05 in each mouse. Reproduced when the counts are within tolerance and both similarity tests hold.

claims.statement: NPY-negative neurons have greater after-depolarization, lower optical rheobase, more spike-rate adaptation, slightly lower maximum firing rate and a shorter membrane time constant than NPY-positive neurons, each difference at p <= 0.001.
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates functional and genetic L1 interneuron subtypes, paragraph 2; Figure 6B, 6C; Supplementary Figure 24E (marks read from the rendered PDF page 39)
claims.quote: The NPY (-) neurons had greater after-depolarization, lower optical rheobase, more spike-rate adaptation, slightly lower maximum firing rate, and a shorter membrane time constant
claims.criterion: Per-cell properties from the sparseOpto sessions of both mice, QC cells, grouped by gfp_positive; two-sided rank-sum test per property. The legend's n (257, 248) matches the behavior-session cells; readings (a) QC cells of the sparseOpto sessions, (b) cells on the behavior-session correlation index. Reproduced when all five differ in the stated direction at p <= 0.001 under one reading; partially reproduced when four do.

claims.statement: A logistic-regression classifier on the five intrinsic properties identifies NPY status with 78% cross-validated balanced accuracy (95% CI 74 to 81%) against 50% (46 to 55%) for shuffled labels; after-depolarization is the most informative feature.
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates functional and genetic L1 interneuron subtypes, paragraph 2; Methods, Cell type classification
claims.quote: Using these five electrophysiological parameters, a logistic-regression classifier identified cell type with 78% (95% CI [74%, 81%]) cross-validated balanced accuracy, compared with a 50% (95% CI [46%, 55%]) chance level. The most impactful feature for cell-type classification was spike afterdepolarization
claims.criterion: Tolerances from the confidence intervals (the wider side). Logistic regression on the five properties, trained on 80% and tested on 20% of cells, 10,000 resampled folds, 2.5 and 97.5 percentiles; control by 5-fold cross-validation with shuffled labels (Methods). No code. Open, with readings for the cells (a) QC cells of both sparseOpto sessions pooled, (b) each mouse; for scaling, (a) z-scored features, (b) raw; and for the most impactful feature, (a) largest absolute coefficient on z-scored features, (b) largest drop in balanced accuracy when the feature is left out. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance and V_adp is the top feature under one reading of each.

claims.statement: NPY-positive cells are more likely to synapse onto other L1 interneurons (outgoing probability within 400 um 14 +/- 15%) than NPY-negative cells (7 +/- 11%).
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates, paragraph 3; Figure 6D; Supplementary Figure 25A
claims.quote: NPY (+) cells were significantly more likely to synapse onto other L1 interneurons of either class (outgoing connection probability within 400 μm: 14 ± 15%, n = 307 NPY (+) cells, 2 mice) compared to NPY (-) cells (connection probability: 7 ± 11%, n = 269 NPY (-) cells, 2 mice, P < 0.001, Wilcoxon rank sum test
claims.criterion: Per QC cell of the sparsePulseHad sessions (576 = 307 + 269), outgoing synaptic connections over tested partners within 400 um, grouped by gfp_positive; two-sided rank-sum. Reproduced when NPY+ exceeds NPY- with p < 0.001 and the means are within tolerance.

claims.statement: IPSPs from NPY-positive presynaptic cells are larger (-3.7 +/- 2.7% of a spike height, 977 pairs) than from NPY-negative cells (-3.1 +/- 2.3%, 490 pairs).
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 25B
claims.quote: The IPSP amplitudes averaged across all detected synaptic connections were significantly larger for NPY (+) presynaptic cells (−3.7 ± 2.7% of a spike height, n = 977 pairs, 2 mice) than for NPY (-) presynaptic cells (−3.1 ± 2.3% of a spike height, n = 490 pairs, P < 0.001, Wilcoxon rank sum test
claims.criterion: Stored IPSP amplitudes of pairs with synaptic_connection set, 60 to 400 um, both mice (1,467 pairs as in fig5e, 800 + 667 in that band by the code), grouped by presynaptic gfp_positive; two-sided rank-sum. Reproduced when NPY+ amplitudes are larger with p < 0.001 and the means are within tolerance.

claims.statement: IPSPs last longer in NPY-positive postsynaptic cells (58 +/- 63 ms, 699 pairs) than in NPY-negative cells (43 +/- 54 ms, 646 pairs).
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 25C
claims.quote: For synaptic inputs, IPSP durations were significantly longer in NPY (+) postsynaptic cells (58 ± 63 ms, n = 699 pairs, 2 mice) than in NPY (-) cells (43 ± 54 ms, n = 646 pairs, 2 mice, P < 0.001
claims.criterion: Duration is the IPSP decay time constant (Supplementary Figure 25C, whose group counts sum to 699 and 646), stored ipsp_decay of connected pairs with a finite fit, both mice, grouped by postsynaptic gfp_positive; two-sided rank-sum. Reproduced when NPY+ is longer with p < 0.001 and the means are within tolerance.

claims.statement: Outgoing and incoming gap-junction connectivity does not differ systematically between NPY-positive and NPY-negative cells.
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 25D, E (marks read from the rendered PDF page 41)
claims.quote: The gap junction out-going and incoming connectivity did not differ systematically between NPY (+) and NPY (-) sub-types
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, on the paper's test, two-sided rank-sum tests among the four pre/post subtype groups of per-cell gap-junction connection probability (Supplementary Figure 25D) and pair spikelet amplitude (25E). The published panels mark several pairwise differences as significant, so "systematically" is read as a consistent direction. Reproduced when there is no subtype effect significant at p <= 0.05 in the same direction in both matched comparisons, for outgoing ((-) to (-) against (+) to (-), and (-) to (+) against (+) to (+)) and for incoming ((-) to (-) against (-) to (+), and (+) to (-) against (+) to (+)); not reproduced otherwise. Effect sizes are given either way.

claims.statement: Population-average subthreshold voltages of NPY-positive and NPY-negative cells are almost indistinguishable (R = 0.97, slope 0.96).
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates, paragraph 4; Figure 6E, 6H
claims.quote: The population-average subthreshold voltages were almost indistinguishable between NPY (+) and NPY (-) subpopulations ( R = 0.97, slope = 0.96
claims.criterion: Tolerance on R set to 0.03, as R cannot exceed 1. Mean subthreshold voltage over NPY+ cells and over NPY- cells of the behavior session of M-YQ0201-29 (Figure 6H; 117 and 141 cells), frame by frame. No code. Open, with readings for the frames (a) all frames of the first 2000 s, (b) non-running frames; and for the slope (a) NPY+ regressed on NPY-, (b) the reverse. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Clustering spontaneous firing patterns alone gives two groups that co-assort with NPY status; 157 of 203 group 1 cells are NPY-negative and 202 of 302 group 2 cells are NPY-positive.
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates, paragraph 4; Figure 6E to G
claims.quote: The sorted spike raster clearly showed two subpopulations (Group 1 and 2, Fig. 6E,F ), which co-assorted with the NPY (-) and NPY (+) subtypes respectively (157/203 Group 1 cells were NPY (-) and 202/302 Group 2 cells were NPY (+) , n = 2 mice
claims.criterion: As in code, reproduce_figure6_from_nwb.m (E to G). Spike trains with frames where more than 15 cells spike zeroed, rates in 500 ms box bins over the first 2000 s, z-scored per cell, projected by svds (u*s) as the UMAP input, UMAP (n_neighbors 20, 2 components), k-means k = 2, each behavior session separately, groups labelled by matching group-mean to subtype-mean rates; the Methods' 500 ms moving average is a variant. UMAP and k-means are unseeded; run with 10 seeds and report the spread. Reproduced when the median counts over seeds are within tolerance and the association of group with NPY status has p < 0.05 by Fisher's exact test (a test chosen here).

claims.statement: At whisking onset NPY-positive cells raise their spike rate from 1.4 +/- 1.7 Hz to 2.8 +/- 4.3 Hz, while NPY-negative cells show no significant change (1.8 +/- 2.1 Hz to 2.0 +/- 2.6 Hz).
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates, paragraph 4; Figure 6H, 6J; Supplementary Figure 26B
claims.quote: In NPY (+) cells, spike rate increased from 1.4 ± 1.7 Hz to 2.8 ± 4.3 Hz (n = 248 cells, N = 2 mice, P < 0.001, Wilcoxon rank sum test). In NPY (-) cells, spike rate did not show a significant change (from 1.8 ± 2.1 Hz to 2.0 ± 2.6 Hz, n = 257 cells, N = 2 mice
claims.criterion: Whisking onsets by the lasso deconvolution of Methods (lambda 1 to 15 chosen to minimize whisking variance in the 2 s before onset; the code uses the stored reconstructions and keeps onsets more than 1.5 s apart). Per cell, mean rate in the 640 ms before and after each onset, averaged over onsets (Supplementary Figure 26B), both behavior sessions (505 cells). Two-sided rank-sum test, before against after, per subtype, as the paper names it; the signed-rank test is a variant. Reproduced when NPY+ rises with p < 0.001 and NPY- shows no change at p > 0.05 (the absence judged on the rank-sum test).

claims.statement: At the peaks of quiet-state subthreshold oscillations, NPY-negative cells spike at a higher rate than NPY-positive cells, while their mean subthreshold voltages do not differ.
claims.source: Supplementary Figure 26A; Figure 6I
claims.quote: NPY(-) cells spiked at a higher rate during quiet-state subthreshold oscillations
claims.criterion: Peaks of the population-average subthreshold voltage band-passed 1.5 to 10 Hz above zero in quiet epochs (Methods, Oscillation peak detection; code, reproduce_figure6_from_nwb.m, butter(4, [1.5 10]*2/fs) with filtfilt). Per cell, the peak-triggered average voltage and rate (Supplementary Figure 26A). How a cell's value is taken from it is not stated; readings (a) the mean over the code's Figure 6I window of +/- 300 frames (+/- 381 ms), (b) the value at the peak frame. Both behavior sessions. Reproduced when the rate differs at p <= 0.001 with NPY- higher and the voltage does not differ at p <= 0.05.

claims.statement: Whisking decreases the excitability of NPY-negative cells and increases that of NPY-positive cells; in the quiet state NPY-negative cells spike faster at a given voltage, in the whisking state NPY-positive cells do.
claims.source: Results, Brain state differentially modulates, paragraph 5; Figure 6K; Supplementary Figure 26C (marks read from the rendered PDF page 43)
claims.quote: Whisking induced a significant decrease in NPY (-) excitability and a significant increase in NPY (+) excitability ... In the quiet state the NPY(-) cells spiked faster and in the whisking state the NPY(+) cells spiked faster
claims.criterion: Per cell, P(spk|V) for V between 0.4 and 0.6 SH (Supplementary Figure 26C), in quiet epochs and in the 640 ms after whisking onsets without running (code uses frames 0 to 500 after onset, 635 ms), both behavior sessions. Two-sided rank-sum tests. Reproduced when the four comparisons (NPY- quiet above whisking, NPY+ whisking above quiet, NPY- above NPY+ in quiet, NPY+ above NPY- in whisking) each hold with p <= 0.05; partially reproduced when the two within-subtype comparisons hold.

claims.statement: In LEC layer 2/3 of young mice, 479 neurons were recorded from 5 WT mice and 846 from 5 APP-KI mice.
claims.source: Results, Disrupted associative memory encoding in lateral entorhinal cortex layer 2/3 neurons, paragraph 1
claims.quote: recorded 479 and 846 neurons from n = 5 young WT and n = 5 young APP-KI mice, respectively
claims.criterion: Counts of sorted units from young WT and young APP-KI tetrode sessions. The putative principal cells (peak-trough width above 230 us and more than 100 spikes in the session, Methods) are counted as well and compared with 423 and 636 (Fig. 2d legend) and with the per mouse counts of Supplementary Fig. 2. Reproduced when both totals are within tolerance.

claims.statement: The proportions of narrow, regular and wide spiking LEC L2/3 cells differ between young WT and young APP-KI mice.

claims.criterion: Peak-trough width as in ed4a-spike-type-distribution; principal cells are RS plus WS, interneurons NS (Supplementary Fig. 2b). Wilcoxon rank sum test on cells. Supplementary Table 1 gives p = 1.7e-30 for the principal cells where the legend gives 3.9e-15; either is significant. Reproduced when the principal cells are narrower in APP-KI at p < 0.05 and the interneurons do not differ at p < 0.05 (the paper's test, a claim of absence for that part). The per mouse t-test is shown as well.

claims.statement: Mean firing rates of putative principal neurons and interneurons in LEC L2/3 are higher in young APP-KI mice than in young WT mice.

The rate's definition is not given; readings (a) spike count over the whole recording of the session, (b) over the AB12 session's trial periods only. Reproduced when both cell classes have higher rates in APP-KI at p < 0.05; partially when one class does. The peak rate (not defined; read as the maximum of the 50 ms, sigma 100 ms smoothed rate) and the per mouse t-tests of Supplementary Fig. 2c, 2d are shown.

claims.statement: At the end of the session (T5), 16% of LEC L2/3 principal neurons respond to at least one odor cue in young WT mice and 34% in young APP-KI mice; the distribution of response classes differs at T1, T3 and T5.

claims.quote: While 16% of LEC L2/3 neurons fired to at least one odor cue at T5 in WT mice, an excessive 34% of neurons exhibited cue responses in APP-KI mice
claims.criterion: Principal cells of all young sessions (correct and error). Each cell is classed at T1, T3 and T5 by the number of odor types (0 to 4) it responds to, as in Shared method, Spike response (odor period, p < 0.05), under readings D+ and D+-; T1, T3, T5 do not depend on the T-a, T-b readings. Chi-squared test of the class by strain table at each timepoint, Benjamini-Hochberg post hoc per class. Reproduced when, under one reading, both T5 percentages are within tolerance and the T5 chi-squared test has p < 0.05 with more responsive cells in APP-KI. The any-period variant of Shared method is shown. The printed chi2 of 2.29 cannot give p = 3.6e-9 on these counts and is not used as a target.

claims.statement: Among LEC L2/3 cells, young APP-KI mice have a higher percentage of Odor-A responsive cells than young WT mice through T1 to T5.
claims.source: Results, Disrupted associative memory encoding in lateral entorhinal cortex layer 2/3 neurons, paragraph 2; Extended Data Fig. 5; Supplementary Table 1
claims.quote: Among these cue-responsive neurons in APP-KI mice, the percentage of Odor-A responsive cells was higher in APP-KI mice compared to those in WT mice
claims.criterion: Response classes by odor combination (A, B, 1, 2, A-1, and so on, and none) from the responses of fig2d-more-cue-responsive, under the same readings, as a percentage of all principal cells. Supplementary Table 1 gives the post hoc tests per combination class (A, 1, A-1, B-1, null), so the Odor-A class is the cells responding to A only; cells responding to A among others are shown as a variant. Reproduced when, under one of the D readings, the Odor-A class is larger in APP-KI at T1, T3 and T5 with a post hoc p < 0.05 at each; partially when that holds at one or two timepoints.

claims.statement: Analysed per mouse, the response type distribution of LEC L2/3 cells differs between young WT and young APP-KI mice at T5, with fewer non-responsive cells and more 1-odor cells in APP-KI mice.
claims.source: Fig. 2j; Extended Data Fig. 3c
claims.quote: Similar results were obtained when data were separated and analyzed per animal
claims.criterion: Per mouse percentages of principal cells responding to 1, 2, 3 or 4 odors or none at T5, under the readings of fig2d-more-cue-responsive; two-way ANOVA type by strain on the 50 mouse-by-type values, Tukey post hoc. Reproduced when, under one reading, the interaction has p < 0.05 and the non-responsive percentage is lower in APP-KI with a Tukey p < 0.05.

claims.statement: In young WT mice, the PCA distance between Odor-A and Odor-1 population trajectories is slightly above the shuffle at T1 and below it from T2 to T5, so the two rewarded cues become similarly represented.

claims.criterion: PCA, shuffle and SI as in Shared method on the 423 young WT principal cells, correct and error sessions pooled, under the readings N1, N2, F1, F2, S1, S2, M1, M2 (method, all run) and T-a, T-b (alternatives). "Smaller than the shuffle" is a reading of the paper's words, with alternatives (a) below the mean shuffle distance (SI above 0), (b) below the 95th percentile threshold (the red line of Fig. 2g). Reproduced when, under the readings, the A-1 distance is above the shuffle at T1 and below it at each of T2 to T5; partially when below at three of the four. The shuffle thresholds (from Supplementary Table 1) are a check of the pipeline and are reported, not judged alone.

claims.statement: In young APP-KI mice, the Odor-A and Odor-1 trajectories stay far apart throughout the session, the A-1 distance remaining above the shuffle from T1 to T5.
claims.source: Results, Disrupted associative memory encoding in lateral entorhinal cortex layer 2/3 neurons, paragraph 3; Fig. 2f, 2g, 2h; Supplementary Fig. 4b
claims.quote: However, A-1 distance in APP-KI mice remained above shuffle, indicating that Odors-A and -1 representations were not generalized together in APP-KI mice
claims.criterion: As fig2g-wt-a1-generalized on the 636 young APP-KI principal cells. "Above shuffle" is read as (a) above the mean shuffle distance (SI below 0), (b) above the 95th percentile threshold. Reproduced when, under the readings, the A-1 distance is above the shuffle at each of T1 to T5; partially when at four of the five.

claims.statement: Bootstrapped similarity between Odor-A and Odor-1 representations is higher in young WT than in young APP-KI mice across the session, significantly at T1a and T1c to T5.
claims.source: Results, Disrupted associative memory encoding in lateral entorhinal cortex layer 2/3 neurons, paragraph 3; Fig. 2i; Extended Data Fig. 8e
claims.quote: A bootstrapping analysis confirmed the decreased A-1 similarity in APP-KI mice compared to WT mice throughout the session
claims.criterion: Bootstrap as in Shared method (readings BS1 and BS2) on the SI of fig2g and fig2f, with the same PCA readings. Reproduced when, under the readings, WT minus APP-KI SI is positive with p < 0.05 at each of T1a, T1c, T2, T3, T4 and T5, the timepoints the paper reports as significant; partially when it is at three to five of them. Bootstrap p values below 0.001 cannot be matched exactly under BS2 and are compared as bounds.

claims.statement: Analysed per mouse, the A-1 PCA distance at T5 is larger in young APP-KI mice than in young WT mice.

The family of the correction is a method detail left open, with readings (a) T1, T3 and T5, (b) the six odor pairs at each timepoint, (c) both together, all run under the rule for readings. Reproduced when, under the readings, the T5 A-1 distance is larger in APP-KI with corrected p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Analysed per mouse, the A-1 similarity index is lower in young APP-KI mice than in young WT mice across learning.

claims.criterion: Per mouse SI from fig2k-per-mouse-distance at T1a, T1b, T1c, T2, T3, T4, T5; two-way ANOVA strain by timepoint on the 70 values. Reproduced when the strain effect has p < 0.05 with WT higher.

claims.criterion: PCA as in fig2g-wt-a1-generalized on trials 1 to 3, 4 to 6 and 7 to 9 of each odor type. Reproduced when, under the readings, the old WT A-1 distance is below the shuffle at each of T2 to T5, the old APP-KI distance is above it at each of T1 to T5, and the bootstrap difference is positive with p < 0.05 at T1b, T1c, T2, T4 and T5; partially when one or two of these timepoints fail.

claims.statement: In both young WT and young APP-KI mice, a decoder trained on Odor-A against Odor-B activity discriminates Odor-1 from Odor-2 in correct sessions but not in error sessions.

claims.criterion: Methods, Decoding analysis. Mean firing rates in 50 ms bins, 1 to 4 s after odor onset, normalized; binary support vector machine trained on Odor-A against Odor-B, tested on Odor-1 (as A) and Odor-2 (as B); 10 bootstraps of resampled data (Extended Data Fig. 7b); correct and error sessions apart (young WT 352 and 71 cells, APP-KI 411 and 225); timepoints T1a to T5 (Supplementary Table 1). The kernel is not given; the linear kernel, MATLAB's default for a binary SVM, is a standard choice and is recorded as a deviation. Method details left open, all run under the rule for readings. The test window, given as 2 to 5 s in the same paragraph, with readings (a) 1 to 4 s, (b) 2 to 5 s; what a sample is, with readings (c) each 50 ms bin's population vector, (d) each odor type's mean over the window; the normalization, with readings N1, N2 and a z-score per neuron. Reproduced when the session by time interaction has p < 0.05 in both strains and correct exceeds error sessions with Tukey p < 0.05 at each of T2 to T5 in both strains. The paper gives no test that error sessions are at chance; error-session performance is reported, not judged.

claims.statement: In young APP-KI mice, Abeta plaque density is higher in the SNc than in the VTA.
claims.source: Results, Dysfunction of lateral entorhinal cortex dopamine activity, paragraph 1; Fig. 3b
claims.quote: The density of Aβ plaques was higher in the SNc than that in the VTA

claims.statement: The density of TH-positive dopamine neurons in the VTA and SNc does not differ between APP-KI and WT mice.

claims.statement: In APP-KI mice, Abeta accumulates with age, starting in the LEC at 2 months and in the VTA and SNc from 4 months.

Reproduced when the ANOVA has p < 0.05 in each region and 12 month APP-KI exceeds 12 month WT with Tukey p < 0.05 in each. The paper gives no test for the onset ages (2 months in the LEC, 4 months in the VTA and SNc); the group means are reported against them, not judged.

claims.statement: In correct sessions of control mice, LEC dopamine fibers respond at T1 to prelearned Odor-A, to novel Odor-1 and to novel Odor-2; with learning the Odor-2 signal disappears while the Odor-A and Odor-1 signals remain to T5.

claims.statement: In APP-KI mice, Odor-1 dopamine signals emerge late, from T3, in correct sessions and are absent in error sessions (39% of sessions), while Odor-A signals stay intact.

claims.quote: dopamine activity was significantly decreased in APP-KI mice during Odor-1 trials at T1
claims.criterion: Per hemisphere mean z-scored GCaMP signal for Odor-1 at T1 to T5, correct and error sessions together, window G1 (1 to 4 s, Fig. 4d legend); two-way ANOVA strain by timepoint on the 90 values, Tukey post hoc. claims.criterion: As fig4d-app-odor1-dopamine-decreased on correct sessions only. Reproduced when, under G1, the Odor-1 interaction and the T1 Tukey comparison have p < 0.05 with WT higher.

claims.statement: In error sessions, dopamine activity does not differ between young WT and young APP-KI mice.

claims.statement: The WT minus APP-KI dopamine difference at T1 is larger for Odor-1 than for Odor-A or Odor-B.

claims.criterion: How a WT minus APP-KI difference is formed per unit is not given; F(3,28) implies 8 values per odor and Supplementary Table 1 says 8 WT and 8 APP-KI units. Method details left open, all run under the rule for readings. What the 3 SD is taken from, with readings (a) the SD of the precue baseline, (b) the SD of the session's signal; the window, with readings G1 and G2 (Shared method, Photometry). Reproduced when, under the readings, r is within tolerance and p < 0.05.

claims.statement: Young APP-KI mice perform worse than young WT mice on novel odor associations at T5 (78.6% against 90.6% correct).

claims.quote: Young WT mice performed at 90.6 ± 0.9% in T5, whereas young APP-KI performed at 78.6 ± 2.1%
claims.criterion: Behavioral performance as in Shared method (readings B1, B2), per mouse means over all sessions; two-way ANOVA odor pair (A/B, 1/2) by strain on the 54 values, Tukey post hoc. Reproduced when, under one reading, both means are within tolerance (the s.e.m.), the interaction has p < 0.05 and the 1/2 Tukey comparison has p < 0.05; partially when the tests hold and the means do not.

claims.statement: Young and old APP-KI mice retrieve the prelearned Odor-A/B association as well as WT mice.

claims.statement: Young WT mice learn the new association in 77.5% of sessions, young APP-KI mice in 59.1%.

claims.statement: Old APP-KI mice are further impaired on novel associations compared with old WT mice (67.9% against 84.9% correct at T5).
claims.source: Results, Impaired associative memory formation in amyloid precursor protein knock-in mice, paragraph 3; Fig. 1f, 1g
claims.quote: 84.9 ± 1.8% correct trials for old WT mice versus 67.9 ± 2.0% for old APP-KI mice
claims.criterion: As fig1d-young-new-association-impaired, for old mice.

claims.statement: Old WT mice learn the new association in 81.3% of sessions, old APP-KI mice in 47.3%.
claims.source: Results, Impaired associative memory formation in amyloid precursor protein knock-in mice, paragraph 3; Fig. 1h
claims.quote: Old WT mice correctly learned 81.3 ± 6.4% of all sessions, whereas APP-KI correctly learned 47.3 ± 6.5%
claims.criterion: As fig1e-young-correct-sessions, for old mice.

claims.statement: Old WT mice show a slight decline of novel association performance compared with young WT mice.
