claims.source: Results, Impaired associative memory formation in amyloid precursor protein knock-in mice, paragraph 3; Supplementary Fig. 1c
claims.quote: Notably, old WT mice showed a slight decline of associative memory compared to young WT mice
claims.criterion: As fig1d-young-new-association-impaired with age in place of strain, WT mice only. Reproduced when the 1/2 performance is lower in old WT with Tukey p < 0.05.

claims.statement: APP-KI and WT mice need comparable numbers of days to reach criterion in the prelearning (Odor-A/B) sessions.
claims.source: Results, Impaired associative memory formation in amyloid precursor protein knock-in mice, paragraph 3; Supplementary Fig. 1f
claims.quote: APP-KI and WT mice showed comparable duration for the training with prelearning sessions using Odor-A and Odor-B
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, on the paper's test. Days of prelearning to reach 80% per mouse; two-way ANOVA strain by age, Tukey post hoc. Reproduced when neither Tukey comparison within age has p < 0.05 and the interaction has p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Optogenetic stimulation of LEC dopamine fibers during Odor-1 trials improves young APP-KI mice's novel association performance at T5 (95.2% against 77.9% in control sessions).
claims.source: Results, Rescued memory by dopamine reactivation, paragraph 1; Fig. 5b, 5c
claims.quote: stimulation: 95.2 ± 1.6% versus control: 77.9 ± 4.9% at T5
claims.criterion: As fig1d-young-new-association-impaired with session type (control, stimulation) in place of strain, per mouse means over sessions of each type. The interaction p is 0.045 in the text and 0.047 in the legend and Supplementary Table 1. Reproduced when, under one reading, both means are within tolerance and the 1/2 Tukey comparison has p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The percentage of correct sessions rises with stimulation (86.9% against 50.1%).
claims.source: Results, Rescued memory by dopamine reactivation, paragraph 1; Fig. 5d
claims.quote: The percentage of total correct sessions significantly increased with stimulation
claims.criterion: As fig1e-young-correct-sessions, stimulation against control sessions per mouse, with the paper's unpaired t-test (a paired test is shown as a variant).

claims.statement: Stimulating LEC dopamine fibers during all four odor types does not rescue associative learning in young APP-KI mice.
claims.source: Results, Rescued memory by dopamine reactivation, paragraph 1; Supplementary Fig. 9a
claims.quote: No rescuing effect was observed when dopamine axons were stimulated during all four odor types
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, on the paper's test. As fig5c-optogenetic-rescue for the all-odor stimulation mice. Reproduced when the interaction has p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: L-DOPA restores young APP-KI mice's novel association performance at T5 (82.6% against 67.1% with saline).
claims.source: Results, Rescued memory by dopamine reactivation, paragraph 2; Fig. 6a, 6b
claims.quote: L- DOPA groups 82.6 ± 1.7% versus saline group 67.1 ± 4.2% at T5
claims.criterion: As fig1d-young-new-association-impaired with drug in place of strain, over the 5 injection days. Reproduced when, under one reading, both means are within tolerance and the 1/2 Tukey comparison has p < 0.05.

claims.statement: L-DOPA raises the percentage of correct sessions in young APP-KI mice (78.5% against 33.1%).
claims.source: Results, Rescued memory by dopamine reactivation, paragraph 2; Fig. 6c
claims.quote: The percentage of total correct sessions significantly increased with L- DOPA treatment
claims.criterion: As fig1e-young-correct-sessions, L-DOPA against saline mice.

claims.statement: In L-DOPA treated APP-KI mice, Odor-A and Odor-1 trajectories become close and the SI is above 0 from T1c to T5, while saline-treated APP-KI mice keep them separated with negative SI.
claims.source: Results, Rescued memory by dopamine reactivation, paragraph 3; Fig. 6e to 6h
claims.quote: Saline-injected APP-KI mice showed separated trajectories for prelearned rewarded Odor-A and novel rewarded Odor-1 (Fig. 6e,g ), resulting in negative SI values ... As a result, SI values were above 0 from trials 7–9 (T1c) to T5
claims.criterion: PCA, shuffle and SI as in fig2g-wt-a1-generalized on the L-DOPA and saline principal cells. Reproduced when, under the readings, the L-DOPA A-1 SI is above 0 at each of T1c, T2, T3, T4 and T5 and the saline SI is below 0 at each of the same timepoints (the paper gives no timepoints for "negative SI values"; the L-DOPA range is used); partially when one or two timepoints fail.

claims.statement: Bootstrapped A-1 similarity is higher with L-DOPA than with saline from T1c to T4.
claims.source: Fig. 6i; Supplementary Table 1
claims.quote: The subtraction confirms higher similarity in the representations between Odor-A and Odor-1 in L -dopa treatment compared to that in saline control
claims.criterion: As fig2i-si-wt-above-app, L-DOPA minus saline. Reproduced when, under the readings, the difference is positive with p < 0.05 at each of T1c, T2, T3 and T4; partially when at two or three of them. T5 (p = 0.12) is not required.

claims.statement: L-DOPA also rescues novel association performance in young PS19 tau model mice (84.8% against 64.8% with saline).
claims.source: Results, Rescued memory by dopamine reactivation, paragraph 3; Fig. 6j to 6l; Supplementary Fig. 10
claims.quote: L -DOPA groups 84.8 ± 3.8% versus saline group 64.8 ± 4.6% at T5
claims.criterion: As fig6b-ldopa-rescue for PS19 mice.

claims.statement: L-DOPA has no effect on the associative learning of control WT mice.
claims.source: Results, Rescued memory by dopamine reactivation, paragraph 3; Supplementary Fig. 11
claims.quote: No effect was observed in L -DOPA-treated control WT mice
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, on the paper's test. As fig6b-ldopa-rescue for WT mice. Reproduced when the interaction has p >= 0.05.

claims.statement: Optogenetic stimulation of LEC dopamine fibers during Odor-2 trials impairs novel association learning in young WT mice.
claims.source: Supplementary Fig. 9b; Supplementary Table 1
claims.quote: The stimulation during Odor-2 impaired associative memory in WT mice
claims.criterion: As fig5c-optogenetic-rescue for the WT mice stimulated on Odor-2 trials, control against stimulation sessions in the same mice. Reproduced when the 1/2 performance at T5 is lower with stimulation with Tukey p < 0.05. The binomial test of correct sessions (p < 0.001) is shown. F(1,16) does not fit 4 mice in a 2 by 2 design (12 error degrees of freedom); the result is reported against the paper's numbers all the same.

claims.statement: Insertion yields were low, 21.4% (3 of 14 sensors) in monkey T and 33% (3 of 9) in monkey P, counted as recording sites that stayed functional after insertion until the end of the study.
claims.source: Results and Discussion, paragraph 3
claims.quote: insertion yields remained low ranging from 21.4% (3/14 individual sensors) in monkey T to 33% (3/9) in monkey P. These values indicate the number of recording sites that retained functionality after insertion, until the end of this study.
claims.criterion: Needs the list of implanted sensors per monkey and whether each kept recording. Reproduced when both yields are within tolerance.

claims.statement: The s-µIPs kept recording for more than a year after implantation; the example sites were recorded 483 days (c8dg), 496 days (c3bs-c3a) and 390 days (monkey P) after implantation.
claims.source: Figure 3A, 3B and Figure 5 legends; Results and Discussion, paragraph 6
claims.quote: sites c8dg and c8ds: 483 days postimplant ... site c3bs-c3a: 496 days postimplant ... site c33:390 days postimplant ... Measurements were made from chronically implanted s-μIPs that maintained functionality >1 year postimplant.
claims.criterion: Needs the implantation date of each site. The tolerance is one day, since a count of days can only be off by the convention for the first day. Reproduced when all three are within tolerance.

claims.statement: FSCV applied a triangular waveform from -0.4 to 1.3 V at 400 V/s, every 100 ms (10 Hz).
claims.source: Methods, FSCV and EPhys Recordings, paragraph 2
claims.quote: FSCV operates by applying a triangle waveform from −0.4 to 1.3 V at a rate of 400 V/s ... The triangular waveform is applied every 100 ms for an effective sampling frequency of 10 Hz.
claims.criterion: Measured from the applied voltage series of session 09/13/2024. The sweep rate is the median absolute step between samples of the rising ramp times the sampling rate, and the scan frequency is one over the median interval between scan starts. Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance, partially reproduced when three are.

claims.statement: EPhys was sampled at 30 kHz in monkey P and 32 kHz in monkey T, and band-pass filtered from 0.1 to 7500 Hz.
claims.source: Methods, FSCV and EPhys Recordings, paragraph 3
claims.quote: EPhys recordings were made using a unity-gain analog amplifier headstage ... at a sampling frequency of 30 (monkey P) or 32 kHz (monkey T), and bandpass filtered from 0.1 to 7500 Hz.
claims.criterion: Sampling rates from the timestamps or rate of the raw series; the filter from the Neuralynx settings stored in the electrodes table (monkey P's file has none). Reproduced when all four values are within tolerance.

claims.statement: In the shape task, forced trials made up 25% of all trials, and the cue-reward association was reversed after blocks of 50 to 300 trials.
claims.source: Methods, Behavioral Tasks, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Forced choice trials were also interleaved (25% of all trials) where only one value cue was displayed ... The cue-reward association was reversed after a block of 50–300 trials depending on the session.
claims.criterion: Forced trials are those with code 119, of all trials in the trials table. A block is a run of trials in which the same cue image (code 81 or 88) signals the large reward in the successful forced trials; a reversal is placed at the first trial after the last forced trial of the earlier association. Block lengths count all trials, and the first and last blocks, cut by the start and end of the file, are reported but not judged. Reproduced when the forced share is within tolerance and every complete block is 45 to 330 trials long (the reported range widened by 10% of each bound); partially reproduced when only one of the two holds.

claims.statement: The dandiset reproduces the processed data the paper deposited on Zenodo; the trial selections and the beta power of the paper's example trial computed from the dandiset agree with the paper's own files.
claims.source: Data Availability Statement (doi:10.5281/zenodo.14826579)
claims.quote: Data used in this study are available at zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14826579).
claims.criterion: Trials are matched by their number (1 to 1501 in the trials table of session 09/26/2024). The four Zenodo lists of successful trials (large reward, small reward, left, right) are compared with the selections decoded here from the event codes, and the beta power computed here for the 35th trial of the large-reward list is compared with the Zenodo example trace (-3 to 12 s from the value cue). Reproduced when each list agrees for at least 99% of the trials in either and the beta traces correlate at r >= 0.9 at a lag of at most 10 ms; partially reproduced when only one of the two holds.

claims.statement: Dopamine was measured from two neighbouring channels of one dual-channel s-µIP (sites c8dg and c8ds, 0.1 to 0.2 mm apart), and both showed dopamine increases after the value cue in a single forced large-reward trial.
claims.source: Figure 3A; Results and Discussion, paragraph 4
claims.quote: These measurements also demonstrate the ability to measure dopamine from two neighboring channels on a single s-μIP with 0.1–0.2 mm separation between the recording tips. ... (e.g., increases in both channels after the value cue, V).
claims.criterion: Needs the trial-aligned dopamine of both c8dg and c8ds. Reproduced when, in forced large-reward trials, the mean change in dopamine from the value cue over 0 to 3 s after it is above zero at both sites in more than half of the trials.

claims.statement: The single-trial FSCV colour plot shows dopamine redox current, with changes near 0.6 V (oxidation) and -0.2 V (reduction) after the value cue.
claims.source: Figure 3A
claims.quote: Color plot shows clear dopamine redox current (i.e., color changes ∼0.6 and −0.2 V).
claims.criterion: Needs the raw FSCV current on the trial clock. The background-subtracted voltammogram (mean of 0.5 to 2 s after the value cue minus the scan at the value cue), averaged over forced large-reward trials, should have its largest positive value on the rising sweep within 0.45 to 0.75 V and its most negative value on the falling sweep within -0.35 to -0.05 V. Reproduced when both hold.

claims.statement: Single-trial bipolar LFP from site c3bs-c3a shows beta bursts (one to a few cycles of high beta power) whose frequency changes around the cue and other task events.
claims.source: Figure 3B; Results and Discussion, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Single-trial LFPs measured from another s-μIP are shown to display fluctuations in the frequency of β-band “bursts” (i.e., 1–few cycles of high β-band power) around the cue and other task events
claims.criterion: Successful large-reward trials of session 09/26/2024. A burst is a run of beta power above the 75th percentile of the beta power over all trial windows of the session that lasts at least 50 ms (one cycle at 20 Hz). For each trial the burst rate (burst onsets per second) is counted in -1 to 0 s and 0 to 1 s from the value cue. Reproduced when the burst rates in the two windows differ by a two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test at p < 0.05. Thresholds at the 50th and 90th percentiles are shown as variants. The paper does not define a burst; the threshold and minimum length here are common choices.

claims.statement: Trial-averaged dopamine at site c8dg is higher after large-reward than after small-reward value cues, in successful forced trials of the shape task.
claims.source: Figure 4A
claims.quote: Higher dopamine levels are observed following the display of large reward associated value cues as compared to small reward cues in monkey T
claims.criterion: Successful forced trials of session 09/13/2024 that have a row in the trial-aligned FSCV table. Per trial, the mean of the re-referenced dopamine over 0 to 3 s after the value cue (inside the value cue fixation, which ends at feedback). Reproduced when the large-reward median exceeds the small-reward median and the Mann-Whitney test gives p < 0.05. Variants (not deciding) are the stored `da` without re-referencing, the oxidation current `iox` re-referenced the same way, and windows of 0 to 1.5 s and 1.5 to 3 s.

claims.statement: Beta-band LFP power at c3bs-c3a in the direction task is more suppressed (stronger event-related desynchronization) after large-reward than after small-reward value cues, in a brief window after the cue.
claims.source: Figure 4B
claims.quote: Trial-averaged β-band LFP power for large and small reward conditions in the direction task, showing increased suppression (i.e., ERD, highlighted in yellow) for large as compared to small reward cues during the brief time window following the value cue at 0 s
claims.criterion: Successful trials of session 09/26/2024, large against small reward. Per trial, the mean beta power over 0 to 0.5 s after the value cue. Reproduced when the large-reward median is below the small-reward median and the Mann-Whitney test gives p < 0.05. Variants (not deciding) are windows of 0 to 1 s and 0.25 to 0.75 s, and power divided by each trial's mean over -0.5 to 0 s.

claims.statement: With the reward fixed at large, beta-band LFP power is more suppressed when the cue is on the left (contralateral) than on the right (ipsilateral).
claims.source: Figure 4C
claims.quote: Increased suppression for contralateral is observed as compared to ipsilateral movement conditions.
claims.criterion: Successful large-reward trials of session 09/26/2024, left against right condition. Per trial, the mean beta power over 0 to 0.5 s after the value cue. Reproduced when the left median is below the right median and the Mann-Whitney test gives p < 0.05. Variants as for fig4b-beta-reward.

claims.statement: Spikes recorded from an s-µIP in the caudate of monkey P (site c33, 390 days post implant) fire at a different rate for large and small reward during the value cue fixation of the direction task.
claims.source: Figure 5A; Results and Discussion, paragraph 5
claims.quote: Spike measurements from an s-μIP in the CN of monkey P also displayed reward-modulated differences in firing rate during the value cue fixation window
claims.criterion: Needs the value cue time and reward size of each trial of monkey P's session. Reproduced when the firing rate of the sorted unit over 0 to 1 s after the value cue differs between large and small reward trials by a Mann-Whitney test at p < 0.05.

claims.statement: The s-µIP recorded a spike-sorted unit in monkey P, shown by its average waveform and its interspike interval histogram.
claims.source: Figure 5B and 5C
claims.quote: Average spike waveform ± standard deviation. ... Interspike interval (ISI) histogram showing the distribution of the timing between spikes detected.
claims.criterion: The sorted unit is Plexon unit 1, as in the paper's spikes_PCA.m (Plexon unit 0 is the unsorted cluster). Reproduced when fewer than 1% of its interspike intervals are under 1 ms and the trough of its mean stored waveform is deeper than 3 times the noise level of the raw signal, taken as the median absolute deviation divided by 0.6745 of 300 to 6000 Hz band-passed signal over 600 s. Partially reproduced when only one holds.

claims.statement: In a single trial (trial 133 of the session), dopamine concentration changes at site c8ds fluctuate, especially after the value cue display.
claims.source: Figure 8A and its legend
claims.quote: Single trial measurements of dopamine concentration changes (Δ[DA]) as a function of time relative to value cue display (V) at 0 s (trial 133 in the session). ... Δ[DA] fluctuations are especially visible after the value cue display.
claims.criterion: The trial's dopamine trace (the `da` column) is referenced to its value at V. The standard deviation over 0 to 5 s after V is compared with that over 5 s to 0 s before V. Reproduced when the ratio after to before exceeds 1. The trial can be read as trial id 133 (1-based, as in the paper's Zenodo lists; index 132) or as index 133; reproduced when either reading gives a ratio above 1. The ratio over all successful trials is reported as a reference.

claims.statement: Trial-averaged dopamine at site c8ds, aligned to the value cue, increases more for large than for small reward trials, especially between the value cue display and reward.
claims.source: Figure 8B and its legend
claims.quote: Trial averaged Δ[DA] aligned to V at 0 s for large and small reward trials, showing increased dopamine release for large in comparison to small reward trials, especially between the value cue display and reward (RW) event.
claims.criterion: For each successful trial, the `da` trace is referenced to its value at V (the paper subtracts the background at V; the PCA estimate is linear in the current, so this is the same up to the model) and averaged from V to the trial's RW. Reproduced when the large trials' values exceed the small trials' (difference of means above 0) with a two-sided Mann-Whitney test p < 0.05. Not reproduced otherwise. Trials whose window holds only NaN are dropped and counted. Other windows (0 to 2 s, RW to RW + 3 s) and the two halves of the session are shown as variants.

claims.statement: Spikes recorded at site c5d on a chamber-implanted CFE can be shown as a raster and a peristimulus time histogram aligned to the value cue display, for large and small reward trials.
claims.source: Figure 9A and its legend; Results, section 3.5, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Raster plot of spikes detected on each trial (y-axis) as a function of time relative to value cue display (V) at 0 s (site c5d). ... Peristimulus time histogram (PSTH) showing average spike firing rate (y-axis) for the large (red) and small (blue) reward conditions
claims.criterion: The thresholded spikes of the paper's file (the `thresholded_units` table, the unit with nearly all spikes) are used; the Plexon unit is a variant. Reproduced when (i) at least 90% of successful trials have a spike within 1 s before to 3 s after V, and (ii) the trial-averaged firing rate is modulated around V, by the variance across 100 ms bins from -1 to 3 s of the PSTH exceeding the 95th percentile of the same statistic over 200 random alignments (V replaced by a uniform time within the same trial's span). The large and small PSTHs are shown and their difference reported without deciding the outcome, as the paper states none.

claims.statement: The spikes at site c5d have a consistent waveform (mean and standard deviation) and an interspike interval distribution (1 ms bins) consistent with a single unit.
claims.source: Figure 9B and 9C and their legends
claims.quote: Average spike waveform + /− standard deviation. C. Interspike interval (ISI) histogram showing the distribution of the timing between spikes detected. Bin widths are 1 ms.
claims.criterion: Same unit as fig9a-spikes-task-aligned. Reproduced when fewer than 1% of interspike intervals are shorter than 1 ms (a common refractory criterion; the paper gives none) and the largest absolute value of the mean waveform is more than twice the standard deviation across spikes at that sample. Partially reproduced when only one holds.

claims.statement: Trial-averaged beta-band LFP power at c7b referenced to c5c is suppressed more in the brief window after the value cue for large than for small reward cues.
claims.source: Figure 9D and its legend
claims.quote: Trial averaged beta-band LFP power showing increased suppression during the brief time window immediately following the cue (V) for large as compared to small reward cues (site c7b-c5c).
claims.criterion: The stored bipolar LFP is band-passed to 13 to 30 Hz (a common beta band; the paper gives none) with a 4th order zero-phase Butterworth filter over V - 3 s to V + 3 s, and power is the squared Hilbert envelope. Per successful trial, the measure is log10 of mean power over 0 to 0.5 s after V divided by mean power over 0.5 s before V. Reproduced when large trials are lower than small (difference of medians below 0) with a two-sided Mann-Whitney test p < 0.05. Partially reproduced when both conditions have a median below 0 and large is lower but p >= 0.05. Not reproduced otherwise. Trials with NaN in the window are dropped and counted. Windows of 0 to 0.3 s and 0 to 1 s, a 1 s baseline, and bands of 15 to 30 and 12 to 25 Hz are variants.

claims.statement: The chamber system provided recordings of dopamine and electrical neural activity in two monkeys (T and J).
claims.source: Abstract, Results; Results, section 3.5, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Our chamber system was shown to provide successful recordings of dopamine and electrical neural activity in two monkeys

claims.statement: 53% (21/40) and 25% (13/51) of implanted sCFEs retained functionality (background current above 500 nA and noise below 0.05 nA) in monkeys T and J.
claims.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 1
claims.quote: 53 % (21/40) and 25 % (13/51) of the implanted sCFE’s retained functionality (background current > 500 nA and noise < 0.05 nA) in monkeys T and J, respectively.

claims.statement: 73% (29/40) and 39% (20/51) of implanted sCFEs retained background current above 500 nA in monkeys T and J, of which 28% and 35% had noise above 0.05 nA.
claims.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 1
claims.quote: 73 % (29/40) and 39 % (20/51) of the implanted sCFE’s retained viable background current > 500 nA, and of these several (28 % and 35 % in monkeys T and J, respectively) fell short of full functionality with noise levels > 0.05 nA.

claims.statement: 21.4% (3/14) and 14.2% (2/14) of mCFEs retained functionality in monkeys T and J.
claims.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 2
claims.quote: On the other hand, the mCFE’s retained a lower functional yield of 21.4 % (3/14) and 14.2 % (2/14) in T and J, respectively.

claims.statement: Of the functional CFEs, 63% (15/24) and 53% (8/15) in monkeys T and J displayed visible dopamine signals and were used during task performance.
claims.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 4
claims.quote: Of the functional CFEs, 63 % (15/24) and 53 % (8/15) in monkeys T and J, respectively, displayed visible dopamine signals (i.e., current changes along dopamine redox potentials), and were successfully applied in measurements during task performance.

claims.statement: Monkey T kept negative bacterial cultures for all samples; in monkey J, staphylococcus cultured at 29 days post-implant was cleared by 39 to 44 days and the chamber stayed aseptic for 286 days after treatment.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 3; Abstract
claims.quote: Bacteria (staphylococcus) was cultured about a month post-implant (29 days) in monkey J ... Monkey T maintained negative cultures for all collected samples. ... 39 – 44 days post-implant the samples began to show negative results ... maintained aseptic condition for the next 286 days

claims.statement: Fluid aspirated from the chamber per session ranged from 0.3 to 4.8 mL in monkey T and 0.2 to 9.8 mL in monkey J, and was sanguinous for the first 18 (T) and 217 (J) days.
claims.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 1; Figure 6
claims.quote: Fluid collected from the chamber aspiration tube for a given day varied between 0.3 – 4.8 mL for monkey T and between 0.2 – 9.8 mL for monkey J (Fig. 6). ... sanguinous (i.e., bloody) in the first few weeks or months (18 days post-implant in monkey T and 217 days in J)

claims.statement: Bone growth was observed within and around the chamber in both monkeys, and the chamber margins stayed relatively healthy.
claims.source: Results, section 3.3, paragraph 1, and section 3.4, paragraph 1; Figure 7
claims.quote: Prominent bone growth was observed in both monkeys within and around the chamber interfaces (Fig. 7). ... The margins of the chamber in both monkeys remained relatively healthy and intact (Fig. 7D and E).

claims.statement: Seven dishes met the paper's inclusion rule (spontaneous activity observed continuously for more than 10 days) and were summarized.
claims.source: Results, Self-organization of power law in PCA, paragraph 3; Methods, Data processing and principal component analysis, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Averaging data across seven dishes revealed that power law in PCA was consistently established around 15 DIV
claims.criterion: Count the dishes in which recordings with activity above 0.03 Hz (reading S1 or S2) run continuously, without a day missing activity, over more than 10 days (Methods, Data processing, paragraph 1, "continuously observed for more than 10 days"). A count of dishes is exact; tolerance 0 for that reason.

claims.statement: Spontaneous activity became detectable at about 2 to 3 DIV.
claims.source: Results, Self-organization of power law in PCA, paragraph 1
claims.quote: Spontaneous activity became detectable approximately 2 – 3 days in vitro (DIV)
claims.criterion: For each dish, the earliest DIV with a recording whose activity exceeds 0.03 Hz (readings S1, at least one electrode above 0.03 Hz, or S2). Reproduced when the median over dishes lies within the reported range 2 to 3 widened by 10% of each bound (1.8 to 3.3, the expected value and tolerance above). The paper gives no detection rule beyond the 0.03 Hz selection, which is used for that reason. If the dataset starts each dish later than this, the claim cannot be tested.

claims.statement: As the cultures matured, spiking changed from asynchronous firing to synchronous bursting.
claims.source: Figure 1B; Results, Self-organization of power law in PCA, paragraphs 1 and 4
claims.quote: During this transition from exponential to power-law decay, spiking activity evolved from asynchronous firing to synchronous bursting
claims.criterion: The paper shows this in raster plots only and defines no burst or synchrony measure. Readings, each over all recordings of all dishes against DIV, (a) the mean pairwise Pearson correlation of the 100 ms spike counts (the bins of the Methods), (b) the largest fraction of electrodes active within one 100 ms bin, as a share of electrodes. Reproduced when under each reading the Spearman correlation with DIV is positive with p < 0.05, and the dish median at 15 DIV and later exceeds that at 3 to 5 DIV. The test and threshold are a reading of "evolved" chosen here, as the paper gives none.

claims.statement: In early cultures the variance spectrum decays faster than a power function; as the culture matures it follows a power function, linear on log-log axes.
claims.source: Figure 1D; Results, Self-organization of power law in PCA, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Initially, the variance spectrum decayed more rapidly than a power function. However, as the culture matured, the spectrum began to follow a power function, appearing linear on a bilogarithmic scale
claims.criterion: Fit b per recording (fit readings F1 and F2). Reproduced when in a majority of the seven dishes the recordings of the first three recorded DIV have b at or above 0.1 and the recordings from 15 DIV on have b below 0.1. The 0.1 boundary is the paper's own threshold between its Exponential and Power-law groups (Results, Co-occurrence, paragraph 3). The first three DIVs, the 15 DIV boundary (from Results paragraph 3) and the majority of dishes are readings chosen here, as the paper gives no rule for Figure 1D.

claims.statement: In the example dish the variance spectrum shifted from exponential to power-law decay around 10 DIV and stayed so to at least 19 DIV, with a power-law fit of exponent 1.30.
claims.source: Figure 1E and legend; Results, Self-organization of power law in PCA, paragraph 2
claims.quote: in this dish, the variance spectrum shifted from exponential decay to power-law decay around 10 DIV and remained stable at least until 19 DIV
claims.criterion: The example dish is not identified, and the paper does not say which spectra the red line of Figure 1E fits. The shift is the first DIV from which b stays below 0.1 (the paper's group threshold). The exponent is read as (a) the median of c over that dish's recordings from the shift to 19 DIV, (b) c fitted to the 19 DIV spectrum, (c) a pure power law fitted to all the dish's spectra from the shift on, pooled. Reproduced when at least one of the seven dishes has a shift within tolerance, b below 0.1 at every recording from the shift to 19 DIV, and an exponent within tolerance under one reading, with fit reading F1 or F2.

claims.statement: Across seven dishes the exponential decay rate of the variance spectrum is large early in development and falls as the culture matures, so that the power law in PCA is established around 15 DIV.
claims.source: Figure 1F (left); Results, Self-organization of power law in PCA, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Averaging data across seven dishes revealed that power law in PCA was consistently established around 15 DIV ... The exponential decay rate, which quantifies the degree of exponential decay, was large in the early stages of development, indicating a dominance of exponential decay. As the culture matured, the decay rate decreased, reflecting a shift toward power-law decay
claims.criterion: Fit b per recording (F1 and F2). The decrease holds when the Spearman correlation of b with DIV over all recordings is negative. "Established" is read as the first DIV from which b stays below 0.1 (the paper's group threshold), taken as (a) on the 3-day moving average over DIV of b pooled over dishes (the thick line of Figure 1F), (b) per dish, the median over dishes. Reproduced when b decreases with DIV and the DIV is within tolerance under one reading.

claims.statement: Once established, the power-law exponent of the variance spectrum stabilized at about 1.2.
claims.source: Figure 1F (right); Results, Self-organization of power law in PCA, paragraph 3
claims.quote: The powerlaw exponent stabilized at approximately 1.2
claims.criterion: The exponent c of the fit, over recordings after the transition DIV found in fig1f-transition-15div. Readings (a) the median of c over those recordings, (b) the 3-day moving average of c at the last DIV. Reproduced when the value is within tolerance under one reading, with fit reading F1 or F2.

claims.statement: Temporal shuffling leaves the variance spectrum unchanged early in development but, once the power law has emerged, disrupts it and returns it to exponential decay.
claims.source: Figure 1D, dashed lines and legend; Results, Self-organization of power law in PCA, paragraph 4
claims.quote: During the initial development period, shuffling did not alter the variance spectra. However, after the emergence of the power law in PCA, shuffling significantly disrupted the power law, reverting them to exponential decay
claims.criterion: Shuffle each recording as in the Figure 1D legend and fit b to the original and the shuffled spectra (F1 and F2). The paper reports no test. Early recordings are those in the Exponential group (b at or above 0.1); late ones those in the Power-law group. Reproduced when (i) in early recordings the median ratio of shuffled to original b lies within 0.9 to 1.1 (the registry's default 10%), and (ii) in late recordings the shuffled b is at or above 0.1 in a majority and exceeds the original b, with a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test over recordings at p < 0.05. The test and the 10% band are readings of "did not alter" and "significantly" chosen here, as the paper gives none; the effect sizes are reported.

claims.statement: Early in development (3 DIV) all PCs correspond to a few scattered electrodes; in mature cultures (15 DIV) dominant PCs correspond to localized clusters of electrodes, while minor PCs remain on globally distributed, sporadic electrodes.
claims.source: Figure 2B; Results, Self-organization of spatial structure of PCs, paragraph 2
claims.quote: In the early stages of development(3 DIV), all PCs corresponded to a small number of scattered electrodes. However, as the culture matured (15 DIV), dominant PCs began to correspond to localized clusters of electrodes, while minor PCs remained associated with globally distributed, sporadic electrodes
claims.criterion: Shown as maps of PC weights; judged with the paper's own measure. Reproduced when fig2c-locality-spectrum is reproduced and, in a majority of dishes at 15 DIV (or the nearest recorded DIV), the mean locality of the first 10 PCs exceeds that of the last 10, while at 3 DIV it does not exceed it by more than 10%. The 10-PC groups follow the window of the Figure 2C moving average; the groups, the majority and the 10% band are readings chosen here, as the paper judges Figure 2B by eye.

claims.statement: The locality spectrum (the number of electrodes with local Moran's I above threshold, against PC index) is flat early in development and becomes steeper as the culture matures.
claims.source: Figure 2C; Results, Self-organization of spatial structure of PCs, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Initially, the locality spectrum was flat, but as culture matured, it became steeper
claims.criterion: Locality spectra and slopes as in the opening comment (readings M1 and M2, L1 and L2). Steeper means a more negative slope (dominant PCs more local). The sign is read from the definition of locality, as the text gives no slope values and Figure 2D was not read. Reproduced when the Spearman correlation of the locality slope with DIV, over all recordings, is negative with p < 0.05, and the median slope at 3 to 5 DIV is closer to zero than that at 15 DIV and later. The test is a reading of "became steeper", which the paper does not test.

claims.statement: The slope of the locality spectrum confirms that spatial structure emerges progressively and is absent in the initial stages of development.
claims.source: Figure 2D; Results, Self-organization of spatial structure of PCs, paragraph 3
claims.quote: analysis of the slope of the locality spectrum confirmed the progressive emergence of spatial structure, which was absent during the initial stages of development
claims.criterion: As fig2c-locality-spectrum, on the 3-day moving average of the slope over DIV (Figure 2D, blue line). Reproduced when the moving average is near zero at the first recorded DIVs (its magnitude below 10% of its most negative value) and falls over DIV, without returning to zero once below half of its most negative value. The 10% and half bounds are readings chosen here of "absent" and "progressive", as the paper gives no number or test.

claims.statement: Temporal shuffling, which removes inter-electrode correlations, disrupts the spatial structure of PCs; the locality spectrum becomes nearly independent of PC index.
claims.source: Figure 2D, dashed line; Results, Self-organization of spatial structure of PCs, paragraph 4
claims.quote: applying a circular shift to data with an established spatial structure, which removed inter-electrode correlations, disrupted the structure ... the locality spectrum became nearly independent of the PC indices
claims.criterion: Shuffle as in the Figure 1D legend. Data with established structure are read as (a) recordings from 15 DIV on, (b) recordings in the PCA Power-law group. Reproduced when, under each of M1 and M2 and L1 and L2, the median shuffled slope has a magnitude below 10% of the median original slope and the shuffled slopes are less negative than the original ones by a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test at p < 0.05. "Nearly independent" and the test are readings chosen here, as the paper gives no number or test.

claims.statement: Across seven dishes the cascade size distribution shifted from exponential to power-law decay at about 15 DIV, with a power exponent of about 1.5.
claims.source: Figure 3C; Results, Co-occurrence of power law in PCA and neuronal avalanches, paragraph 2
claims.quote: Data summarized from seven dishes show that the distribution shifted from an exponential decay to a power-law decay at approximately 15 DIV, with an exponent around 1.5
claims.criterion: Cascades and sizes as in the opening comment (readings A1 and A2), fit over sizes 1 to 128 (F1 and F2), per recording. The shift DIV is read as in fig1f-transition-15div, on the avalanche b with the same 0.1 boundary, (a) on the pooled 3-day moving average, (b) per dish, the median. The exponent is the median c over recordings after the shift. Reproduced when both values are within tolerance under one reading. The 0.1 boundary for avalanches is carried over from the PCA groups; the paper gives none for avalanches.

claims.statement: The exponential decay rates of the variance spectrum and of the cascade size distribution are positively correlated across recordings, so the two power laws are established concurrently.
claims.source: Figure 3D; Results, Co-occurrence of power law in PCA and neuronal avalanches, paragraph 3
claims.quote: A clear positive correlation between the two exponential decay rates indicates that two power laws are established concurrently in the dissociated culture
claims.criterion: One point per recording (all dishes and DIVs), PCA b against avalanche b, under the fit and size readings F1, F2, A1, A2. The paper reports no correlation coefficient or test. "Clear" is read as a Spearman correlation and a Pearson correlation both positive with two-sided p < 0.05, a reading chosen here; the coefficients and their per-dish values are reported.

claims.statement: Recordings classified by the PCA decay rate alone (Power-law group, b below 0.1) show both power laws, while the Exponential group shows neither.
claims.source: Figure 3E and 3F; Results, Co-occurrence of power law in PCA and neuronal avalanches, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Interestingly, although these groups were categorized based solely on the power law in PCA, regardless of the power law in the neuronal avalanches, it was clearly observed that both phenomena appeared in the Power-law group ( Fig. 3E ). In contrast, neither power law was observed in the Exponential group
claims.criterion: Groups by PCA b with the paper's threshold 0.1, a method value used as given. The panels show representative recordings. Readings, (a) per recording, the avalanche b is lower in the Power-law group than in the Exponential group (one-sided Mann-Whitney U, p < 0.05, a test chosen here) and the median avalanche b is below 0.1 in the Power-law group and at or above 0.1 in the Exponential group; (b) the cascade size distribution pooled over all recordings of each group, fitted, has b below 0.1 for the Power-law group and at or above 0.1 for the Exponential group. Reproduced when one reading holds under the fit and size readings.

claims.statement: A similar co-occurrence is seen when recordings are classified by their neuronal avalanches.
claims.source: Figure S1, cited in Results, Co-occurrence of power law in PCA and neuronal avalanches, paragraph 3
claims.quote: A similar co-occurrence was also observed when data were classified based on the neuronal avalanches (Fig. S1)
claims.criterion: Figure S1 and its legend are not in the text read, so the threshold on the avalanche b is not known. The reading is the same threshold as the PCA groups, 0.1, on the avalanche b, with readings (a) and (b) of fig3ef-groups-cooccur applied with the roles of the two decay rates swapped. A different threshold in the supplement could change the outcome; the claim is open on that point until the supplement is read.

claims.statement: The co-occurrence of the two power laws is easily disrupted by temporal shuffling, reflecting that the two phenomena are not inherently associated.
claims.source: Figure S2, cited in Results, Co-occurrence of power law in PCA and neuronal avalanches, paragraph 3; Discussion, paragraph 2
claims.quote: This co-occurrence is notable because it is easily disrupted by temporal shuffling, reflecting that these phenomena are inherently unassociated (Fig. S2)
claims.criterion: Figure S2 and its legend are not in the text read, so neither the shuffle applied to the avalanche analysis nor the measure of disruption is known. Readings, on recordings of the Power-law group shuffled as in the Figure 1D legend, (a) the shuffled data keep avalanche b below 0.1 while their PCA b is at or above 0.1 (the Discussion says sequences with avalanches but no power law in PCA are easy to construct), in a majority of recordings; (b) over all recordings, the correlation of fig3d-decay-rates-correlated computed on shuffled data is not positive with p < 0.05. The claim is open on this point until the supplement is read; where the readings disagree it is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: The cultures did not show the in vivo temporal structure of PCs, in which dominant PCs have longer time scales than minor PCs.
claims.source: Discussion, paragraph 4
claims.quote: This temporal structure is characterized by dominant PCs exhibiting longer time scales, while minor PCs exhibit shorter time scales. However, our study using the dissociated neuronal culture was unable to replicate such a temporal structure
claims.criterion: A claim of absence, but the paper names no measure or test. Readings, on recordings from 15 DIV on, (a) the time scale of each PC's projection as the lag at which its autocorrelation (100 ms bins) first falls below 1/e, (b) the integral of the positive part of that autocorrelation; the claim holds when the Spearman correlation of time scale with PC rank is not negative with p < 0.05 in a majority of recordings. As the paper names no test, the outcome is reported under both readings, and the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified where they disagree.

claims.statement: In the binary threshold network with heavy-tailed (Cauchy) connections, the variance spectrum decays exponentially for weak connections and becomes a power law at the critical point, with exponent 1.56, where neuronal avalanches also occur.
claims.source: Figure 4C and 4D; Results, Heavy-tailed connectivity is important for the co-occurrence, paragraph 4
claims.quote: The variance spectrum exhibited an exponential decay when the typical connection strength was sufficiently smaller than the critical point. However, as the connection strength increased, the spectrum transitioned to a power-law decay at the critical point. ... The power-law exponent at the critical state was 1.56
claims.criterion: A simulation, not a test on the recorded data. The Methods give the threshold theta 1, connection probability 0.01, the critical point at g 1, and Gaussian or Cauchy weights of strength g, but the network size N, the scaling of the distributions with g (the formulas are lost from the text), the run length, the initial state and inputs, and how model activity is binned for PCA are not given. Cannot be specified from the text read; recorded so the finding is covered.

claims.statement: Networks with Gaussian connections, which lack neuronal avalanches, show no power law in PCA at any connection strength.
claims.source: Figure 4C and 4D; Results, Heavy-tailed connectivity is important for the co-occurrence, paragraph 4
claims.quote: In contrast, Gaussian networks, which fails to reproduce neuronal avalanches, were also unable to reproduce a power law in PCA at any connection strength
claims.criterion: A simulation, not a test on the recorded data; unspecified as for fig4d-cauchy-model-power-law. Recorded so the finding is covered.

claims.statement: The analysis used 42 LC single units from 32 sessions in monkey Oz and 63 units from 51 sessions in monkey Ci, recorded with pupil diameter during passive fixation with occasional startling beeps.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 1
claims.quote: N = 42 single units from 32 sessions in monkey Oz and 63 units from 51 sessions in monkey Ci
claims.criterion: Counts of units and sessions in the code's include lists that hold beep trials with LC spikes and pupil. Tolerance zero, as these are counts of recorded units and sessions, not estimates.

claims.statement: Trial-by-trial baseline LC firing rate is positively correlated with baseline pupil diameter within sessions, after correcting both for linear drift, in both monkeys.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 2; Figure 2, row 1
claims.quote: trial-by-trial measurements of baseline LC activity were positively correlated with simultaneously recorded measurements of baseline pupil diameter over the course of a session
claims.criterion: Per unit, the partial Spearman correlation of row 1 (opening comment). Reproduced when, in each monkey, the median coefficient is above zero and the population test gives p < 0.05 under T1; partially reproduced when this holds in one monkey only. The p-values are reported beside the paper's.

claims.statement: Baseline-subtracted evoked LC responses are positively correlated with baseline-subtracted evoked pupil responses within units, in both monkeys.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 2; Figure 2, row 2
claims.quote: Likewise, baseline-subtracted evoked LC responses were positively correlated with baseline-subtracted evoked pupil responses (p = 0.0135 for monkey Oz, p = 0.0018 for monkey Ci)
claims.criterion: Per unit, the Spearman correlation over beep trials of evoked firing rate with evoked pupil, under E1 and under E2. Reproduced when, in each monkey, the median coefficient is above zero and the population test (T1) gives p < 0.05, under E1 and under E2; partially reproduced when this holds in one monkey only. When E1 and E2 give different outcomes the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Baseline-subtracted evoked pupil responses are negatively correlated with baseline pupil diameter (drift residuals) within sessions, in both monkeys.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 3; Figure 2, row 3
claims.quote: baseline-subtracted evoked pupil responses were negatively correlated with baseline pupil diameter (using residuals; p = 1.16×10-6 for monkey Oz, p = 5.02×10-9 for monkey Ci; Figure 2, row 3)
claims.criterion: Per session, the Spearman correlation over beep trials (each trial once) of evoked pupil with the baseline pupil residual, under E1 and under E2. Reproduced when, in each monkey, the median coefficient is below zero and the population test (T1) gives p < 0.05, under E1 and under E2; partially reproduced when this holds in one monkey only. When E1 and E2 give different outcomes the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified. Sessions are the paper's 51 for Ci; the code's 50 (legacy removal, opening comment) is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Baseline-subtracted evoked LC responses are negatively correlated with baseline LC activity (drift residuals) within units, in both monkeys.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 3; Figure 2, row 4
claims.quote: Similarly, baseline-subtracted evoked LC responses were negatively correlated with baseline LC activity (using residuals; p = 5.88×10-7 for monkey Oz, p = 1.04×10-11 for monkey Ci; Figure 2, row 4)
claims.criterion: Per unit, the Spearman correlation over beep trials of evoked firing rate with the baseline firing-rate residual. Reproduced when, in each monkey, the median coefficient is below zero and the population test gives p < 0.05 under T1; partially reproduced when this holds in one monkey only.

claims.statement: Evoked pupil responses are not reliably related to baseline LC activity; the median per-unit correlation does not differ from zero in either monkey.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 4; Figure 2, row 5
claims.quote: evoked pupil responses were rarely positively or negatively related to baseline LC activity in a reliable manner (Wilcoxon rank-sum test for H0... p = 0.894 for monkey Oz, p = 0.904 for monkey Ci)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Per unit, the Spearman correlation over beep trials of evoked pupil with the baseline firing-rate residual. The paper's test is the population test at 0.05 per monkey, T1 (opening comment). The evoked pupil has two readings (E1, E2), both run. Reproduced when the test gives p >= 0.05 in both monkeys; not reproduced when it gives p < 0.05 in either. When E1 and E2 give different outcomes the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified. The median coefficient per monkey is reported either way, and T2 and the code's evoked pupil are shown as variants.

claims.statement: Baseline pupil diameter is not reliably related to evoked LC responses across monkeys; the median per-unit correlation does not differ from zero in Oz (p = 0.915) and does in Ci (p = 0.008).
claims.source: Results, paragraph 4; Figure 2, row 6
claims.quote: Likewise, baseline pupil diameter was rarely positively or negatively related to evoked LC responses reliably across monkeys (Figure 2, bottom row) (p = 0.915 for monkey Oz, p = 0.008 for monkey Ci)
claims.criterion: Per unit, the Spearman correlation over beep trials of evoked firing rate with the baseline pupil residual. Population test per monkey at 0.05, T1 as main, T2 as variant (as in fig2-row5-baseline-lc-vs-evoked-pupil). The claim is that the relationship is not reliable across monkeys. Reproduced when Oz gives p >= 0.05 and Ci gives p < 0.05, the paper's pattern; partially reproduced when neither monkey reaches p < 0.05 (still no relationship across monkeys, but Ci's is not found); not reproduced when both monkeys give p < 0.05 with medians of the same sign; partially reproduced in the other cases (Oz p < 0.05 with Ci p >= 0.05, or both p < 0.05 with medians of opposite sign), where no relationship holds across monkeys but the paper's pattern is not found. Medians and p-values are reported.

claims.statement: Despite consistent within-epoch relationships between LC activity and pupil size, there are no reliable relationships between the two across epochs (baseline of one against evoked of the other).
claims.source: Results, paragraph 4, last sentence; Discussion, paragraph 3
claims.quote: Thus, despite consistent relationships between LC activity and pupil size within each epoch, there were no reliable relationships between the two when comparing across epochs
claims.criterion: Reproduced when rows 1 and 2 are reproduced (within-epoch relations in both monkeys) and neither cross-epoch row (rows 5 and 6) shows p < 0.05 with medians of the same sign in both monkeys. Not reproduced when either cross-epoch row does; partially reproduced when the cross-epoch rows hold but a within-epoch row holds in one monkey only.

claims.statement: The correlation between baseline pupil and evoked LC responses does not depend on the range of evoked LC responses in either monkey.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 5 (first additional analysis)
claims.quote: We found that the relationship between baseline pupil diameter and evoked LC responses was not systematically impacted by the range of evoked LC responses for either monkey (Spearman’s rho = 0.02, p = 0.89 for monkey Oz; rho = 0.07, p = 0.589 for monkey Ci)
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Across units, per monkey, the Spearman correlation between each unit's row 6 coefficient and the range (maximum minus minimum) of its evoked firing rates over beep trials, as in compute_manuscript_stats.m (build_evoked_range_by_unit). The paper says the range is per session; the code takes it per unit, which is followed. Reproduced when p >= 0.05 in both monkeys; not reproduced when p < 0.05 in either. Rho is reported.

claims.statement: The correlation between baseline LC activity and evoked pupil responses does not depend on the range of evoked pupil responses in Ci (rho = 0.18, p = 0.16), but in Oz it becomes more negative as that range grows (rho = -0.33, p = 0.03).
claims.source: Results, paragraph 5 (first additional analysis)
claims.quote: the relationship between baseline LC activity and evoked pupil responses was not systematically impacted by the range of evoked pupil responses for monkey Ci (rho = 0.18, p = 0.16). However, we did observe a modest impact for monkey Oz (rho = -0.33, p = 0.03)
claims.criterion: Across units, per monkey, the Spearman correlation between each unit's row 5 coefficient and the range (maximum minus minimum) of its evoked pupil responses over beep trials, as in compute_manuscript_stats.m, under E1 and E2. Reproduced when, under both, Ci gives p >= 0.05 and Oz gives p < 0.05 with rho within tolerance of -0.33; partially reproduced when Ci gives p >= 0.05 and Oz gives p < 0.05 with a negative rho outside the tolerance; not reproduced otherwise. When E1 and E2 give different outcomes the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: Using raw baseline measures in place of drift residuals gives results similar to those of Figure 2.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 6 (second additional analysis); Supplemental Figure 1
claims.quote: we obtained similar results when using raw baseline measurements as opposed to residuals (see Supplemental Figure 1)
claims.criterion: The six Figure 2 coefficients recomputed with raw baseline pupil and raw baseline firing rate in place of their residuals, as the code's "baseline" mode does (PaperFigures/plot_S1_summary.m; row 1 stays the partial Spearman controlling for trial time), and the population test per monkey. "Similar" is judged on the paper's own Figure 2 pattern, the sign of the median and whether p < 0.05, for 12 row and monkey cells. Reproduced when all 12 match the pattern the paper reports with residuals (rows 1 to 4 significant in the reported direction in both monkeys, row 5 not significant in either, row 6 not significant in Oz and significant in Ci); partially reproduced when 10 or 11 match; not reproduced below 10. The population test is T1 (T2 shown as a variant). Run under E1 and under E2; when they give different outcomes the claim is blocked as methods_underspecified.

claims.statement: The relationship between baseline and evoked pupil responses is better described by a quadratic than a linear fit in only a minority of sessions (7 of 32 for Oz, 6 of 51 for Ci).
claims.source: Results, paragraph 7 (third additional analysis); Supplemental Figure 2, first panel
claims.quote: The relationship between baseline and evoked pupil responses was better described by a non-linear fit for a minority of sessions (LLR > critical value of 3.841... 7/32 sessions for monkey Oz, 6/51 sessions for monkey Ci)
claims.criterion: Per session, beep trials each once, evoked pupil regressed on the baseline pupil residual with a linear and a quadratic model fit by maximum likelihood (the code's fitlme with formulas y ~ x and y ~ x*x, compute_manuscript_stats.m); LLR = 2 times the difference in log-likelihood, counted above 3.841. Sessions with fewer than 4 valid trials or 3 distinct predictor values are left out, as in the code. Run under E1 and E2, and with all sessions (the paper's 51 for Ci) or the code's 50 Ci sessions (legacy removal, opening comment; compute_manuscript_stats.m prints 6/50). Tolerance of one session, as 10% of these counts is under one session and would demand an exact count. Reproduced when both counts are within tolerance and below half the sessions under one reading; partially reproduced when the counts are outside tolerance but below half the sessions.

claims.statement: LC evoked responses are rarely better described by a quadratic than a linear function of baseline LC activity (2 of 42 units for Oz, 3 of 63 for Ci).
claims.source: Results, paragraph 7; Supplemental Figure 2, second panel
claims.quote: LC neuronal responses were rarely better characterized using a non-linear fit (2/42 neurons for monkey Oz, 3/63 for monkey Ci)
claims.criterion: Per unit, beep trials, evoked firing rate regressed on the baseline firing-rate residual, linear against quadratic as in figs2-llr-pupil-baseline-evoked (prepare_figure_analysis_tables.m, compute_llr). The code drops rows 43 and 65 of its unit table before counting (a "legacy" removal, leaving 61 Ci units); the paper's denominator is 63. Readings, all units (the paper's denominator) and the code's removal. Tolerance of one unit, for the reason in figs2-llr-pupil-baseline-evoked. Reproduced when both counts are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when they are outside tolerance but below a tenth of the units.

claims.statement: Across-epoch relationships are rarely better described by a quadratic than a linear fit (baseline LC against evoked pupil, 4 of 42 units for Oz and 4 of 63 for Ci; baseline pupil against evoked LC, 2 of 42 and 5 of 63), so the null cross-epoch findings are not due to a non-linear relationship.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 7; Supplemental Figure 2, third and fourth panels
claims.quote: across-epoch comparisons showed similar trends that favored a linear relationship (baseline LC versus evoked pupil... 4/42 for monkey Oz, 4/63 for monkey Ci; baseline pupil versus evoked LC... 2/42 for monkey Oz, 5/63 for monkey Ci)
claims.criterion: Per unit, beep trials, evoked pupil regressed on the baseline firing-rate residual, and evoked firing rate on the baseline pupil residual, linear against quadratic as in figs2-llr-pupil-baseline-evoked, under E1 and E2, and with all units or the code's removal of two (figs2-llr-lc-baseline-evoked). Tolerance of one unit, for the reason given there. Reproduced when all four counts are within tolerance under one reading; partially reproduced when they are outside tolerance but each below a tenth of the units.

claims.statement: With data z-scored per session or unit and pooled across trials, sessions and units for each monkey, the within-epoch relationships of Figure 2 hold (baseline LC with baseline pupil and evoked LC with evoked pupil positive; evoked against baseline negative for pupil and for LC).
claims.source: Results, paragraph 8 (fourth additional analysis); Figure 3, columns 1 to 4
claims.quote: we applied our single-unit analyses (Figure 2) to data pooled across all trials, sessions, and units (Figure 3). The results are qualitatively similar for the pooled and single-unit analyses
claims.criterion: As in compute_manuscript_stats.m (Figure 3 block). Firing rates z-scored per unit over its baseline, raw evoked and fixation-only rates (zscore_tables.m), evoked rate as z-scored raw evoked minus z-scored baseline; pupil as stored, which the code uses. The Methods and the Figure 3 legend z-score pupil per session; when the stored trace is not so z-scored, the pupil samples are z-scored per session as the Methods say (main reading) and the stored values are shown as the code's variant. Drift residuals recomputed. Per monkey, a Spearman correlation over pooled trials for each column, beep and fixation-only trials pooled for column 1, beep trials each once per session for column 3. The Figure 3 legend draws linear regression lines; the code's test, Spearman, is followed. Reproduced when all four columns give p < 0.05 in the sign of the corresponding Figure 2 row in both monkeys, under E1 and E2; partially reproduced when six or seven of the eight column and monkey cells do. The code's raw-baseline version (PaperFigures/plot_S1_combined.m) is shown as a variant.

claims.statement: In the pooled data, neither baseline pupil against evoked LC nor baseline LC against evoked pupil shows a reliable relationship across monkeys, also when units are split by the sign of their significant baseline LC-pupil relationship.
claims.source: Results, paragraph 8; Figure 3, columns 5 and 6
claims.quote: in neither case showing a reliable relationship between baseline pupil and evoked LC responses or baseline LC activity and evoked pupil responses across monkeys. This result also held when LC units were separated based on the direction of their baseline relationship with pupil size
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. Pooled data as in fig3-pooled-within-epoch; Spearman correlation per monkey of evoked firing rate with the baseline pupil residual (column 6) and of the baseline firing-rate residual with evoked pupil (column 5), at 0.05, in all units and in the two groups of units whose row 1 partial Spearman correlation has p < 0.05 with positive or with negative sign (Figure 3 legend). The code's per-group pooled Spearman is in PaperFigures/plot_S1_combined.m (rows 3 and 4, raw baselines; groups from the z-scored stats table after the legacy removal of two units); the Figure 3 script itself is not in the repository (commented out in make_all_figures.m), so the residual version follows that code with residuals in place of raw baselines, as the Figure 3 block of compute_manuscript_stats.m uses them. "Across monkeys" is read, as in fig2-row6-baseline-pupil-vs-evoked-lc, as significant with the same sign in both monkeys. Reproduced when no column in no group is so; not reproduced when any is. Rho and p for every cell are reported, under E1 and E2.

claims.statement: Pcdh-gamma proteins (Pcdh-gamma-GFP in fusg mice) are present in all five retinal layers and in all six retinal cell types (photoreceptors, horizontal, bipolar, amacrine, RGCs and Mueller glia).
claims.source: Results, Broad expression of gamma protocadherins in retina, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 1
claims.quote: As judged by localization of GFP in Pcdh-γ fusg mice, Pcdh-γs are present in all five retinal layers ... All six cell types were Pcdh-γ-positive ... Thus, Pcdh-γs are expressed in all cell types of the neural retina.
claims.criterion: Qualitative, from immunostained sections and dissociated cells. Reproduced when GFP is seen in all five layers and in cells carrying each of the markers the paper lists. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: Pcdh-gamma is present in the IPL, neuroblast layer and RGC axons at P0, appears in the developing OPL by P7, and reaches the adult pattern by P14.
claims.source: Results, Broad expression of gamma protocadherins in retina, paragraph 4; Figure 2
claims.quote: At this time, Pcdh-γ is present on cells in the neuroblast layer, in the IPL, and on RGC axons ( Figure 2A ) ... By P7, Pcdh-γ appears in the OPL, as it divides the neuroblast layer into INL and ONL ( Figure 2C ). By P14, the adult pattern described above is established
claims.criterion: Qualitative, from sections at P0, P3, P7 and P14. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: Pcdh-gammas are present in pre- and postsynaptic compartments of rod and cone synapses in the OPL, though little is in horizontal cell varicosities, and at many but not only synaptic sites in the IPL.
claims.source: Results, Synaptic localization of Pcdh-γ proteins in the retina, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 3
claims.quote: Thus, Pcdh-γs were present in pre- and post-synaptic compartments of rod and cone synapses. In contrast, although horizontal cell processes labeled with anti-calbindin ... were Pcdh-γ-positive, little Pcdh-γ was present in their synaptic varicosities
claims.criterion: Qualitative, from double-labelled confocal sections. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: Chx10-Cre recombination is extensive (above 90%) in the INL and ONL, while about half of the cells in the GCL are not recombined.
claims.source: Results, Inactivation of Pcdh-γs in the retina leads to neuronal and synaptic loss, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 1A and 1B (not read)
claims.quote: Recombination was extensive (>90%) in the INL and ONL but occasional columns of cells were spared ... In contrast, approximately half of the cells in the GCL were GFP-negative and LacZ-positive
claims.criterion: Reproduced when the recombined fraction exceeds 90% in the INL and ONL and the GCL value is within tolerance. From Z/EG reporter sections, which the data set does not hold.

claims.statement: At P18, retinas lacking Pcdh-gammas in Chx10-Cre mutants are properly laminated but about 25% thinner than controls, from a selective reduction of about 40% in INL and IPL thickness.
claims.source: Results, Inactivation of Pcdh-γs in the retina leads to neuronal and synaptic loss, paragraph 5; Figure 4B to 4H
claims.quote: However, mutant retinas were ∼25% thinner than those of wild-type mice or heterozygote littermates. The difference resulted from a selective reduction of ∼40% in the thickness of the INL and the IPL ( Figure 4H ).
claims.criterion: Thickness from single optical sections adjacent to the optic nerve head, two to four areas per retina and two sets of perpendicular measurements per area (Methods, Histology). Reproduced when both reductions are within tolerance and the INL and IPL differences have p < 0.01 by ANOVA with Tukey post hoc. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: The INL and IPL are thinned to the same extent in Chx10-Cre;Pcdh-gamma fcon3/fcon3 and fdel/fdel retinas, so fcon3 is functionally a null.
claims.source: Results, Inactivation of Pcdh-γs in the retina leads to neuronal and synaptic loss, paragraph 5; Figure 4D to 4H
claims.quote: The INL and IPL were thinned to the same extent in Chx10-Cre;Pcdh-γ fcon3/fcon3 and Chx10-Cre;Pcdh-γ fdel/fdel mice
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The paper names no test for the difference between the two alleles; Figure 4H uses ANOVA with Tukey post hoc at p < 0.01 over the three genotypes. Reproduced when the Tukey comparison of fcon3 against fdel is not significant for INL and IPL. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: In peripheral Pax6alpha-Cre;Pcdh-gamma fcon3/fcon3 retina at P18, bipolar, amacrine and retinal ganglion cells are reduced by 45 to 65%, Mueller glia by about 20%, while horizontal cells and photoreceptors differ little from controls.
claims.source: Results, Inactivation of Pcdh-γs in the retina leads to neuronal and synaptic loss, paragraph 6; Figure 4I
claims.quote: Numbers of bipolar, amacrine, and retinal ganglion cells were reduced by 45-65% ( Figure 4I ). Müller glia were also decreased, but only by ∼20%. In contrast, numbers of horizontal cells and photoreceptors differed little between mutants and controls
claims.criterion: Counts of marker-positive cells per area (0.13 mm2 for calbindin, Brn3a and Pax6alpha-GFP; 0.05 mm2 for Chx10; 0.02 mm2 for Sox9; 1280 um2 for photoreceptors; Methods, Histology). Reproduced when the bipolar, amacrine and RGC reductions each lie within 40.5 to 71.5% (the stated range widened by 10% of each bound), the Mueller glia reduction is within tolerance, and horizontal cells and photoreceptors are not significantly reduced by Mann-Whitney test. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: Mutant and control retinas do not differ perinatally (E17.5 to P3); INL and IPL are thinner in mutants by P7, about 40% thinner by P14, and change little over the following months.
claims.source: Results, Increased postnatal apoptosis in the absence of Pcdh-γs, paragraph 1; Figure 5A to 5I
claims.quote: We detected no differences in laminar arrangement or thickness between mutant and control retinas perinatally ... Both layers were ∼40% thinner in mutants than in controls by P14, then changed little over the following several months
claims.criterion: Reproduced when no stage up to P3 differs by Student's t-test, the reductions from P14 on are within tolerance with p < 0.001, and they do not grow over later stages. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: Apoptosis (cleaved caspase-3) follows the normal time course but is significantly higher in mutant than control retinas during the first postnatal weeks.
claims.source: Results, Increased postnatal apoptosis in the absence of Pcdh-γs, paragraph 2; Figure 5J to 5N
claims.quote: Apoptosis followed a similar time course in Pcdh-γ deficient retinas, but levels were significantly higher in mutants than in controls ... Although increased apoptosis was seen in both neuroblast and ganglion cell layers at P0, it was confined to the INL at P7
claims.criterion: The Results and the legend disagree on the layers. The Results say the increase is in both neuroblast and ganglion cell layers at P0 and only in the INL at P7; the legend says the differences are significant in the "NBL/IPL" (as printed, likely NBL/INL) at P0 and P7 and in the ganglion cell layer only at P7. The text also cites panels K, L and M where the legend labels J, K, M and N. Both readings are named. Reproduced when mutant counts exceed control counts by Student's t-test or Mann-Whitney test at p < 0.05 at P0 and P7, with the layer pattern of either reading. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: In central retina of Pax6alpha-Cre;Pcdh-gamma fcon3/fcon3 mice, where only the Pax6alpha amacrines lack Pcdh-gammas, these amacrines are 58% fewer than in controls, a loss equivalent to that in peripheral retina.
claims.source: Results, Cell autonomy of Pcdh- γ -dependent cell survival in retina, paragraph 2; Figure 6B, 6C and 6F
claims.quote: The number of Pax6α-amacrines in central retina was 58% lower in mutants than in controls ... loss of Pax6α-positive amacrines is equivalent in peripheral and central retina
claims.criterion: Reproduced when the reduction is within tolerance and significant at p < 0.05 by Student's t-test (equal variances by F-test) or Mann-Whitney test (Figure 6F legend, Methods), and the central and peripheral (Figure 4I, AC) reductions do not differ significantly. The paper names no test for the central against peripheral comparison; the same tests at p < 0.05 are used, and this is open. The figure's significance marks run from p < 0.05 to p < 0.0001 and the legend does not say which applies to which bar. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: Loss of Pcdh-gammas from Pax6alpha amacrines in central retina does not affect the survival of bipolar cells, horizontal cells, Mueller glia or starburst amacrines, but causes a small (about 15%) significant loss of Brn3a-positive RGCs.
claims.source: Results, Cell autonomy of Pcdh- γ -dependent cell survival in retina, paragraph 3; Figure 6F
claims.quote: Loss of Pcdh-γs from the Pax6α-positive amacrines had no detectable effect on the survival of bipolar cells, horizontal cells or Müller glia ... In contrast, we detected a small (∼15%) but significant loss of Brn3a-positive RGCs from central retina
claims.criterion: For the spared types a claim of absence, judged on the paper's tests (Student's t-test, with equal variances checked by F-test, or Mann-Whitney test, at p < 0.05; Methods, Histology). Reproduced when none of bipolar, horizontal, Mueller glia and starburst counts differ and the RGC reduction is within tolerance and significant. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: In Pcdh-gamma mutant retina at P18, processes of all ten examined amacrine and bipolar subtypes are arrayed in their appropriate IPL sublaminae, though with occasional gaps.
claims.source: Results, Pcdh- γ s are dispensable for laminar targeting of retinal neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 7
claims.quote: In all ten cases, processes were arrayed in appropriate sublaminae in mutant retinas at P18, although disruptions or gaps were sometimes present
claims.criterion: Qualitative, from immunostained sections with the ten markers listed in the Results. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: Deleting Bax rescues the neurons that die in Pcdh-gamma mutant retina; INL and GCL thickness and Chx10+ bipolar number do not differ between Pcdh-gamma-positive and -negative Bax-/- retinas, and the IPL expands to the Bax-/- thickness.
claims.source: Results, Synapses and arbors of Pcdh-γ-deficient neurons destined to die, paragraph 1; Figure 8A to 8D
claims.quote: Likewise, Bax deletion rescued neurons destined to die in Pcdh-γ mutant retina: the thickness of the INL and GCL and the number of Chx10-positive bipolar cells were indistinguishable
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The paper names no test for this comparison; the Methods list ANOVA, Student's t-test (equal variances by F-test) and Mann-Whitney test. Reproduced when none of these finds a difference at p < 0.05 between the two Bax-/- genotypes for INL, GCL, IPL thickness and Chx10+ count. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: Synapse density in the IPL and OPL (PNA or Bassoon staining) does not differ significantly between Pcdh-gamma-positive and Pcdh-gamma-negative Bax-/- retinas.
claims.source: Results, Synapses and arbors of Pcdh-γ-deficient neurons destined to die, paragraph 2; Figure 8E to 8L; Supplementary Figure 2 (not read)
claims.quote: The density of synapses in the IPL and OPL, as judged by staining for PNA or Bassoon, did not differ significantly between Pcdh-γ-positive and Pcdh-γ-negative Bax −/− retinas
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The test is not named in the text read; it may be in the Supplementary Figure 2 legend, which was not available. The Methods list ANOVA, Student's t-test and Mann-Whitney test. Reproduced when the test used finds no difference at p < 0.05. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: Neurons rescued from death by Bax deletion target their processes to the appropriate IPL sublaminae as specifically as in Pcdh-gamma single mutants, and the gaps of the single mutants are absent.
claims.source: Results, Synapses and arbors of Pcdh-γ-deficient neurons destined to die, paragraph 3; Figure 8M and 8N
claims.quote: In all cases, targeting of processes to appropriate laminae was as specific in double mutants as in Pcdh-γ single mutants
claims.criterion: Qualitative, from immunostained sections. Not testable on a spike-recording data set.

claims.statement: Figure 9C to 9H report 115 RGCs from mutant retinas and 143 RGCs from control retinas.
claims.source: Figure 9 legend, panels C to H
claims.quote: plots a cumulative histogram of that quantity for RGCs in mutant retinas (red curve, 115 cells ... and control retinas (black curve, 143 cells
claims.criterion: Counted as the sorted units in the data set's mutant and control recordings, as the data set labels them. Mutant pools Chx10-Cre mutant retinas with the peripheral region of Pax6alpha-Cre mutant retinas (Results, Functional visual circuits, paragraph 2); control is Pax6-Cre;Pcdh-gamma +/f-del or Pcdh-gamma f-del/f-del (Figure 9 legend). The paper does not say whether every unit was kept, so the counts both of all units and of units with a flicker response are reported. Reproduced when the counts are within tolerance.

claims.statement: RGCs in mutant and control retinas show a similar variety of responses to small flashing spots, including sustained and transient ON, OFF and ON-OFF responses.
claims.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 3; Figure 9A
claims.quote: RGCs in Pcdh-γ mutant and control retinas showed a similar variety of responses to small flashing spots, including sustained and transient ON, OFF and ON-OFF responses
claims.criterion: The paper shows example rasters only and defines no classes. ON, OFF and ON-OFF are read from the On-Off index of Figure 9C (spikes in the on-phase over all spikes); the paper gives no cut-offs and none for transient against sustained. Readings for the ON/OFF cut-offs are (a) index below 1/3 OFF, above 2/3 ON, otherwise ON-OFF; (b) below 0.2 OFF, above 0.8 ON. Transient against sustained is read as the ratio of the spike rate in the second half of a phase to that in the first, with readings (a) below 0.5 transient, (b) below 0.3 transient. Reproduced when, under every reading, the mutant group and the control group each hold cells of each of the three polarities and of both time courses; the class counts per group are reported.

claims.statement: The proportions of ON- and OFF-dominated responses are the same in mutant and control retinas.
claims.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 3; Figure 9C
claims.quote: Proportions of ON- and OFF-dominated responses were identical in mutants and controls ( Figure 9C )
claims.criterion: A claim of absence. The measure is from the Figure 9C legend, per cell, (number of spikes fired during the on-phase of the spot)/(total number of spikes fired), from the flashing-spot experiment of panel A. The paper's comparison is the overlap of the 95% confidence bands of the two cumulative histograms (header, readings a to c). Reproduced when the bands overlap under every reading; not reproduced when they separate under every reading; blocked as methods_underspecified when the readings disagree. A two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test and the difference of medians are shown as a variant.

claims.statement: Mutant RGCs respond to very dim flashes, which excite only rods, and to bright flashes, which mainly excite cones, so both rod and cone pathways function.
claims.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 3 (data not shown)
claims.quote: Mutant RGCs responded to very dim flashes, which excite only rods, and also to bright flashes, which predominantly excite cones (data not shown)
claims.criterion: The paper shows no data and gives no flash intensities. Reproduced when the data set holds mutant recordings at two flash intensities the data set marks as dim (scotopic) and bright (photopic), and some mutant cells fire more during either phase of the flash than in the matched part of the other phase at each intensity.
