attempts.label: DANDI:000009
attempts.paper_title: Maintenance of persistent activity in a frontal thalamocortical loop
attempts.entry_title: Persistent activity in a frontal thalamocortical loop (Guo et al. 2017)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Guo, Inagaki, Daie, Druckmann, Gerfen and Svoboda (2017) on dandiset 000009, which holds silicon-probe recordings from ALM, thalamus and SNr during a delayed licking task with optogenetic photoinhibition, and whole-cell recordings of ALM neurons during thalamus, M1 or contralateral ALM photoinhibition. It tests behaviour under ALM photoinhibition, unit classes, trial-type selectivity, the collapse of ALM and thalamic activity under photoinhibition of the other area, onset latencies, SNr responses and membrane potential measures. Behaviour-only, muscimol, weak photoinhibition, non-behaving whole-cell and anatomical data are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Guo et al. (2017) from dandiset 000009

outcomes.statement: Mice performed the delayed-response task at 77.6% correct on average, with 10.3% lick-early trials and 1.1% no-response trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: mean percent correct 77.6%; lick-early before ‘go’ cue 10.3%, no response 1.1%
outcomes.notes: Over all 173 behavioural recordings percent correct is 70.66% (reading a, pooled) to 75.46% (reading c, mean over sessions), within 77.6 +/- 7.76%. Lick-early trials are 14.66 to 18.18% against 10.3 +/- 1.03%, and no-response trials 0.73 to 0.98% against 1.1 +/- 0.11%. No reading puts all three within tolerance. The 36 whole-cell recordings alone give 77.42 to 83.47% correct, 7.93 to 9.65% lick early and 0.96 to 1.55% no response, at most two values within tolerance. Per mouse, lick-early rates range from 3.6 to 37.2%. Partially reproduced before the first verification; changed to not reproduced because the criterion asks all three values under one reading and two of the three are out under every reading of the full set of recordings.
deviations: The dandiset holds recording sessions only; the paper's averages may come from behaviour sessions that are not deposited.
Rows with no outcome and no pole times (5369 extracellular rows, type 'non-performing') are not counted as trials.

outcomes.statement: Unilateral photoinhibition of ALM during the delay epoch biased responses to the ipsilateral side, lowering performance on contra trials and raising it on ipsi trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 1; Figure 1c
outcomes.quote: Unilateral photoinhibition of ALM during the delay epoch produced an ipsilateral response bias ... reducing performance for contralateral trials and increasing performance for ipsilateral trials ( P < 0.001; paired t -test, Fig. 1c )
outcomes.notes: In 66 recording sessions of 11 PV-Cre x Ai32 mice, ALM photoinhibition at 1.5 mW in the delay epoch lowers contra performance from 0.774 to 0.368 (paired t = -16.67, p = 3.6e-25; no session increases) and raises ipsi performance from 0.673 to 0.744 (t = 3.99, p = 0.00017; 46 of 66 sessions increase). With all photoinhibition powers pooled, p = 4.7e-25 and 0.00054. Contra performance falls in every mouse. The answer of 2026-10-20 (convention P) puts the 0.75 and 0.79 mW trials outside the condition, as the main test already did; the outcome is unchanged.
deviations: Tested on the behavioural trials of the 66 recording sessions (ALM, thalamic and SNr recordings), not on the paper's 84 behaviour sessions, which are not in the dandiset.
Photoinhibition trials at 1.5 mW (the Methods' power, convention P); trials at 0.75 or 0.79 mW are pooled in a variant only.

outcomes.statement: Unilateral photoinhibition of thalALM during the delay epoch lowered performance on contra trials and caused a small, non-significant improvement on ipsi trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 3; Figure 1d
outcomes.quote: Similar to ALM, unilateral photoinhibition of thal ALM during the delay epoch reduced performance for contralateral trials and caused a small improvement in performance for ipsilateral trials ( P < 0.001 for contralateral trials, not significant for ipsilateral trials, paired t -test
outcomes.notes: The only Gad2 sessions (genotype 'Ai35D x GAD2_Cre', 9 thalamic recordings of 2 mice) carry no photostimulus trial, and there are no behaviour-only sessions with thalamus photoinhibition in Gad2-IRES-Cre mice.

outcomes.statement: Photostimulating TRN axons in thalamus of Gad2-IRES-Cre mice reduced thalALM spike rates, recorded near VM/VAL, to 67.8% of control during the delay epoch.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 2c
outcomes.quote: Photostimulating axonal terminals of TRN GABAergic neurons in thalamus reduced spike rates in thal ALM (recorded near VM/VAL, to 67.8% during the delay epoch
outcomes.notes: The 9 Gad2 thalamic sessions hold 84 units, the 26 + 41 + 17 optrode units of Extended Data Fig. 2c, but every trial has photostimulus period 'N/A' and power 0, so photoinhibition trials cannot be told from control trials. The genotype is given as 'Ai35D x GAD2_Cre', where the paper used Gad2-IRES-Cre with ChR2 injected in TRN.

outcomes.statement: In VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice, thalamus photoinhibition reduced activity 0.5 to 1.1 mm from the fibre tip to 15.9% of control.
outcomes.source: Methods, Photoinhibition, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 2d
outcomes.quote: Photoinhibition reduced activity (0.5-1.1 mm from the tip of the optical fiber) to 15.9 ± 9.3%
outcomes.notes: Over the whole photostimulus (reading W1), putative thalamic units 0.5 to 1.1 mm from the fibre site fall to 17.0 to 20.3% of control (Q1) or 16.5 to 19.3% (Q3), within 15.9 +/- 9.3%; Q2 gives 37.5 to 51.2%. In the 20 to 120 ms window (W2) they fall to 1.2 to 1.5% (Q1). 63 to 79 units qualify (paper 114), grouped 23 to 24, 21 to 24 and 31 to 42 near 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0 mm (paper 34, 42, 38). Every trial of the VGAT thalamic sessions has a 1.3 s delay, so W1 ends with the delay epoch and holds no time after the photostimulus (W1 on 1.3 s delays only gives the same values). In 100 ms bins the ratio is 21.6% in the bin from 1.4 s after pole onset, falls to 9 to 11% by the end of the delay and returns to 100% in the response epoch.
deviations: Distance is measured from the files' photostimulus site (AP -1.5, ML 0.9, DV -4.1 mm), the same nominal coordinate in every session, not from the fibre tip as placed in each mouse.
The files give the photostimulus power as 2.23 mW; the paper gives 10 mW.
Unit classes under readings P1 (computed width) and P2 (file label) of convention C.

outcomes.statement: Small doses of muscimol infused near VM/VAL produced an ipsilateral bias in licking responses, while infusions outside thalALM, anterior or dorsal (1.1 to 1.6 mm anterior or 1.6 to 1.9 mm dorsal to VM/VAL in the Results; about 0.3 to 0.8 mm anterior to VM/VAL and 0.2 to 0.5 mm dorsal to MD in the legends), did not, even at ten-fold higher doses.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus is required for motor preparation, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 3
outcomes.quote: Inhibition near VM/VAL produced ipsilateral bias in the licking response ( Extended Data Fig. 3a, b ). Inhibition outside of thal ALM (1.1 - 1.6 mm anterior or 1.6-1.9 dorsal to VM/VAL) did not cause ipsilateral bias, even at 10-fold higher doses

statistics.about: performance change near VM/VAL against control

outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds no muscimol sessions or infusion metadata.

outcomes.statement: Of 1214 ALM units, 1006 were putative pyramidal neurons (spike width > 0.6 ms), 166 putative fast-spiking (< 0.4 ms) and 42 unclassified; the spike-width distribution was bimodal.
outcomes.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 4b
outcomes.quote: In ALM, 1214 single units were recorded across 57 behavioral sessions. ... units with width < 0.4 ms were defined as putative fast-spiking (FS) neurons (166/1214) and units with width > 0.6 ms as putative pyramidal neurons (1006/1214)
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 966 ALM units in 47 sessions (paper 1214 in 57). By computed width (P1) 577 units exceed 0.6 ms and 127 are below 0.4 ms; by file label (P2) 810 are 'Wide width spiking' and 121 'Narrow width spiking'. The fractions under P2, 0.839 and 0.125, are close to the paper's 0.829 and 0.137; no count is within tolerance under either reading. 514 of the 577 units above 0.6 ms have their waveform peak at the last sample, so their widths are lower bounds. The width histogram has two modes (0.28 ms and 0.68 to 0.72 ms) with a trough at 0.36 ms (4 units). The answer of 2026-10-20 makes P1 the Methods' rule and keeps P2 as a reading; no count is within tolerance under either, so the outcome is unchanged, the fractions under P2 matching.
deviations: The deposited mean waveforms are too short to measure the widths the Methods use; both the computed widths (P1) and the files' labels (P2) are shown, as convention C says.

outcomes.statement: Most ALM putative pyramidal neurons (70%, 704/1006) distinguished trial types; 145 had preparatory activity only, 272 peri-movement selectivity only and 287 both.
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity in thalamus, paragraph 1; Figure 2e
outcomes.quote: For a majority of neurons, activity differed across trial types (70%, 704/1006; P < 0.05, t -test; Methods). ... subsets of neurons showed selective preparatory activity ( Fig. 2b , left column; Fig. 2e , 145/1006), selective peri-movement activity during the response epoch ( Fig. 2b , right column; Fig. 2e , 272/1006), or both ( Fig. 2b , middle column; Fig. 2e , 287/1006)
outcomes.notes: Under P1 and the first selectivity reading, 398 of 577 units are selective (95, 154, 149 by type). Under P2, 571 of 810 (70.5%) are selective against 70% in the paper, with 132 preparatory only, 222 peri-movement only and 217 both; scaled to 1006 units, 164, 276 and 270 against 145, 272 and 287. Over all 32 readings the selective fraction is 0.62 to 0.73. No reading puts the four counts within tolerance because the dandiset holds 577 or 810 pyramidal units against 1006; the fractions agree with the paper.
deviations: Each unit's trials are those from the trial holding its first spike to the trial holding its last, as the files give no observation interval per unit; this applies to every unit analysis.

A window that ends after the last stored spike of a trial (spikes are stored to about 4.8 s after pole onset) is counted as missing for that trial; this applies to every unit analysis and touches 221 of 8991 kept ALM trials, 173 of 14997 thalamic and 19 of 3573 SNr for R1.
Unit classes under readings P1 and P2 of convention C (answer of 2026-10-20; P3 does not apply to ALM). Outcome unchanged.

outcomes.statement: Approximately equal numbers of selective ALM neurons preferred contra and ipsi movements.
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity in thalamus, paragraph 1; Figure 2e
outcomes.quote: Approximately equal numbers of neurons preferred contra- or ipsi-lateral movements ( Fig. 2e )
outcomes.notes: Under all 32 readings the contra-preferring fraction of selective ALM neurons is 0.495 to 0.543, the binomial test does not reject one half, and the fraction lies within 0.45 to 0.55; both readings of the criterion hold everywhere.
deviations: Unit classes under readings P1 and P2 of convention C (answer of 2026-10-20). Outcome unchanged.

outcomes.statement: Of 790 thalamic units, 672 were putative thalamic neurons (spike width > 0.5 ms) and 313 lay within 0.4 mm of the VM/VAL centre; 295 VM/VAL units were analysed.
outcomes.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analysis, paragraph 3; Results, Preparatory activity in thalamus, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 4e
outcomes.quote: In thalamus, 790 single units were recorded across 73 behavioral sessions. ... Units with spike width > 0.5 ms were selected as putative thalamic neurons (672/790) ... units within 0.4 mm from the VM/VAL center ... were scored as VM/VAL neurons (313/790)
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds 789 thalamic units in 72 sessions (paper 790 in 73). By file label (P2) 682 are putative thalamic units, within 672 +/- 67; by computed width (P1) only 148. 259 units lie within 0.4 mm of the L2 centre (313 +/- 31) and 222 (P2) or 20 (P1) putative units among them (295 +/- 30). The total and the P2 class count are within tolerance, the location counts are not.
deviations: The files have no VM/VAL label (reading L1 cannot be applied); reading L2 uses the claims file's proxy centre.
Unit classes under readings P1 and P2 of convention C; the criterion excludes P3 for these counts (answer of 2026-10-20). Outcome unchanged.

outcomes.statement: A majority of VM/VAL neurons (69%, 204/295) distinguished trial types, a fraction indistinguishable from ALM; 43 had preparatory activity only, 82 peri-movement selectivity only and 79 both, a distribution similar to ALM.
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity in thalamus, paragraph 2; Figure 2f
outcomes.quote: A majority of VM/VAL neurons discriminated trial types (69%, 204/295; indistinguishable from ALM, chi-squared test, P = 0.79). ... VM/VAL neurons exhibited similar selectivity and time-course to ALM (chi-squared test, P > 0.5)
outcomes.notes: Under P1 only 20 VM/VAL units qualify (13 selective under the first reading), and their types do not differ from ALM. Under P2, 149 of 222 (67%) are selective against 204/295 (69%), and the fraction does not differ from ALM's 70.5% (chi-squared p = 0.37). The types differ from ALM in all 16 P2 readings (2 x 4 and 2 x 3 tests p < 0.05; first reading 38, 75 and 36, p = 0.011 and 0.0053), where the paper finds p > 0.5. The answer of 2026-10-20 adds reading P3 (all 259 VM/VAL units regardless of width). Under P3, 174 are selective under the first reading (156 to 177 over the readings, below 204 +/- 20), the fraction does not differ from ALM in any reading, and the types differ from ALM in all 32 readings (first reading 40, 89 and 45; p = 0.024 and 0.0098 against ALM P1). Counts are below tolerance in every reading. The selective fraction holds; the type distribution holds only on the 20 P1 units. Outcome unchanged.
deviations: VM/VAL by reading L2 only; unit classes under P1, P2 and P3 of convention C.

outcomes.statement: Strong photoinhibition of thalALM (VGAT-ChR2-EYFP) decreased ALM activity to 6% of control, inhibiting 309 of 314 neurons (155 significantly) and significantly activating none.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 3c
outcomes.quote: Thal ALM photoinhibition decreased ALM activity to 6% of control, reducing activity in nearly all neurons ( Fig. 3c , 309/314 inhibited, 3/314 activated, 155/314 significantly inhibited, 0/314 significantly activated, t -test, P < 0.05)
outcomes.notes: In 234 (P1) or 261 (P2) VGAT ALM putative pyramidal units from 3 mice, thalamus photoinhibition at 10 mW lowers activity to 2.1 to 2.5% (Q1) or 5.1 to 5.2% (Q2) of control, the median ratio being 0. Under P2 and T1, 256 of 261 units are inhibited, 2 activated, 127 (Student) or 208 (Welch) significantly inhibited and none significantly activated. The unit counts (230 to 261) are below 314 +/- 31 and no reading puts every value within tolerance; the criterion's partial condition holds in every reading. With the PV-Cre x Ai32 ALM sessions at 10 mW (a variant), activity falls to 21.7% (P2, T1) and 7 units are significantly activated. The answer of 2026-10-20 confirms VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice at 10 mW and keeps the PV-Cre x Ai32 sessions as a variant, as the attempt already ran; P1 and P2 stay the unit readings. Outcome unchanged.
deviations: Only the VGAT-ChR2-EYFP sessions at 10 mW, as the criterion says; the PV-Cre x Ai32 ALM sessions with thalamic photostimulation are shown as a variant, not judged.
Unit classes under P1 and P2 of convention C.

outcomes.statement: Thalamus photoinhibition reduced ALM activity across all cortical layers.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 3d
outcomes.quote: across all cortical layers ( Fig. 3d )
outcomes.notes: By the sign of the change (m1), inhibited neurons outnumber activated ones in every depth bin under every reading (12 of 12 bins of 100 um, 7 of 7 of 200 um), and the population rate under photoinhibition is at most 0.205 of control in any bin. Counting significant changes (m2), 1 to 3 bins fail with Student's test and 1 with Welch's, each holding 1 to 4 neurons with no significant change in either direction (0 against 0). The criterion blocks a claim whose readings disagree. The reduction is seen at every depth sampled (0.1 to 1.3 mm). The answers of 2026-10-20 leave its units (VGAT at 10 mW, P1 and P2) as they were; outcome unchanged.
deviations: Depth is the files' `unit_y`, described only as "y-coordinate of this unit (mm)"; whether it is depth below the pia is not stated.

outcomes.statement: ALM neurons with preparatory activity, peri-movement selectivity or both were equally inhibited by thalamus photoinhibition.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 3b
outcomes.quote: neurons showing preparatory activity, peri-movement selectivity or both were equally inhibited; Fig. 3b , P > 0.2, t -test
outcomes.notes: Under the first selectivity reading both measures find a difference between groups, the rate difference (p < 0.0001, peri-movement only against both) and the ratio (p = 0.016 with P1, 0.010 with P2, T1); the claim would not be reproduced there. Over all 64 combinations of selectivity, trial and unit readings, the difference measure finds a pair at p < 0.05 in all and the ratio measure in 13, so the measures disagree in most readings, which the criterion calls methods underspecified. Mean ratios are about 0.13 (preparatory only), 0.04 to 0.05 (peri-movement only) and 0.02 (both). The answers of 2026-10-20 leave its units as they were; outcome unchanged.
deviations: Groups and populations under the selectivity readings of convention S and P1, P2.

outcomes.statement: Strong photoinhibition in VGAT-ChR2-EYFP mice abolished thalALM activity nearly completely, to 2% of control.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 1; Figure 3f
outcomes.quote: Photoinhibition abolished thal ALM activity nearly completely (to 2 % of control without photoinhibition) ( Fig. 3f )
outcomes.notes: Putative thalamic units of the VGAT thalamic sessions fall to 1.1% (T1) or 0.9% (T2) of control (Q1; Q2 0.9 to 1.4%) on 93 (P1) or 113 (P2) units against 148 +/- 15; none is activated and 101 of 113 are significantly inhibited (P2, T1, Student). With all 134 units the count is within tolerance but narrow units raise Q1 to 18%. The silencing is nearly complete as the paper states; the 2% and the unit count are not both within tolerance under any reading. No VGAT thalamic unit lies within 0.4 mm of the L2 centre, so reading (b) has no units. One mouse gives Q1 1.8% and the other 35.2% with all units.
deviations: The files give the photostimulus power as 2.23 mW; one session was photostimulated in the sample epoch and drops out.
Unit classes under P1 and P2 of convention C (Fig. 3, so P3 does not apply; all units are shown as a variant). Outcome unchanged.

outcomes.statement: Photoinhibition reduced thalALM activity 2.5 ms after photostimulus onset, and ALM spike rates were reduced 8.2 ms after onset, a latency difference consistent with direct thalamocortical drive.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 3; Figure 3e, f
outcomes.quote: Photoinhibition reduced thal ALM activity 2.5 ± 0.8 ms after photostimulus onset (mean ± SEM, activity reduction onset detected by 3 × std, Fig. 3f ). Hyperpolarization of ALM neurons and reduction of ALM spike rates were detected 7.9 ± 1.7 ms and 8.2 ± 1.5ms after photostimulus onset
outcomes.notes: Under reading O2 with correct and incorrect trials (T1), the thalamic onset is 2.0 ms (SEM 1.08 with P1, 0.96 with P2) and the ALM onset 9.0 ms (P1, SEM 3.68) or 7.0 ms (P2, SEM 3.16), within 2.5 +/- 0.8 and 8.2 +/- 1.5 ms, ALM later. Under O1 the ALM onset is 0 ms in three of four cases (the first 1 ms bin already lies 3 SD below control) and under T2 with O2 it is 6 ms; those readings fail. The pass rests on one reading of four, and the onset rule is fragile. On photostimulus PSTHs simulated from each unit's control PSTH with no effect it reports an onset below 10 ms in 30 to 48% of runs, and with a step at 8 ms it reports one before 8 ms in 18 to 43% and within 6.5 to 9.5 ms in 60 to 84%. The ALM onset of 0 ms under O1 is such a false onset.
deviations: The photostimulus onset is the delay onset of the trial table (1.3 s after pole onset), as the extracellular files hold no laser trace; the data check shows thalamic units fall within 5 ms of it.
Populations are those of fig3f-thalamus-silenced (reading a) and fig3-alm-collapse, which the answers of 2026-10-20 leave unchanged; outcome unchanged.

outcomes.statement: During the delay epoch the mean membrane potential of ALM neurons was close to spike threshold, 12.7 mV below it on average.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraph 2

With the deposited kink, 6.88 and 6.15 mV. Leaving out cell_21_1, whose trial start times are shifted by one row, changes these by at most 0.14 mV. The kink is the first sample searched (1.5 ms before the peak) in 1.7% of spikes (0.4 to 6.8% per cell); leaving those spikes out gives 7.23 mV with baseline (a).

Spike peaks are located from the deposited spike-removed trace; the kink and clipping are computed by the claims file's rule and match the deposited trace.

outcomes.statement: Thalamus photoinhibition hyperpolarized ALM neurons by 18.7 mV, preventing spiking, with an onset 7.9 ms after photostimulus onset.
outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus drives ALM preparatory activity, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 3g, 4b, c

outcomes.notes: The criterion's onset readings are E (1.3 s after pole_in_time) and M (0.1 s after pole_out_time); the files also hold the laser trace, an OptogeneticSeries the first attempt did not read, whose onset (reading L, asked about in question 7) lies 1.4725 s after pole_in_time in these cells, 28 ms before M. Under E the 20 to 120 ms window precedes the change and Vm changes by +0.31 mV. Under L thalamus photoinhibition changes Vm by -13.68 +/- 1.14 mV (all 16 cells hyperpolarize, -4.7 to -21.7 mV) and the spike rate falls from 3.24 to 0.14 spikes/s; the onset is 9.60 +/- 1.98 ms by V2, within 7.9 +/- 1.7, and 0.40 ms by V1, which is not. The hyperpolarization and the loss of spiking are present at 73% (L) or 90% (M) of the paper's -18.7 +/- 1.1 mV; no reading puts both values within tolerance. Measured is reading M, a reading the criterion lists.

The criterion has no partial clause; the hyperpolarization and the silencing are present under M and L at 73 to 90% of the paper's value, but no listed reading meets the criterion.

outcomes.statement: The hyperpolarization of ALM neurons during thalamus photoinhibition was caused mainly by a loss of excitation, not by an increase in inhibition; it was larger with negative current injection.

statistics.about: slope of the regression of the Vm change on baseline Vm

outcomes.statement: Photoinhibition of M1 during the delay epoch caused only a slight hyperpolarization (3.3 mV) and a small drop in spike rate (1.4 spikes per s) in ALM neurons.

outcomes.notes: Under M the 11 cells change by -2.75 +/- 1.30 mV, within -3.3 +/- 1.0, and by +0.76 +/- 1.29 spikes/s, outside -1.4 +/- 0.6. outcomes.statement: thalALM drives ALM more strongly than M1 or contralateral ALM, the other reciprocally connected structures tested.

outcomes.statement: The latency of ALM hyperpolarization is too short for the thalamus to M1 to ALM pathway; thalamus photoinhibition hyperpolarized M1 neurons after 11.0 ms and M1 photoinhibition hyperpolarized ALM neurons after 13.9 ms, so that pathway would give a latency difference above 14.3 ms against the 5.4 ms observed.

The other onset, ALM after M1 photoinhibition, can be measured from the laser trace the whole-cell files hold (reading L, question 7) and is 8.7 +/- 4.6 ms (V1) or 27.3 +/- 6.6 ms (V2), against 13.9 +/- 3.2; the claim needs both.

outcomes.statement: Photoactivating thalamus in Olig3-cre x Ai32 mice depolarized ALM neurons after 3.6 ms, an estimate of the thalamocortical conduction delay.

outcomes.source: Results, Thalamus contributes to selectivity in ALM, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 7c-e; Supplementary information

Over the stored part of each trial (a variant) the same units fire 36.0 (P1) or 38.1 (P2) spikes/s and the other units 13.1 (10 units, P1) or 20.3 (35 units, P2) against 23.4. outcomes.statement: ALM is reciprocally connected with ipsilateral thalamic nuclei, most consistently the VM/VAL complex; a retrograde injection into ALM labelled 17375 thalamic neurons, against 38062 in contralateral ALM and 26599 in M1.

outcomes.statement: In ALM and in VM/VAL, population selectivity emerged in the sample epoch and increased throughout the delay epoch; it peaked at the beginning of the response epoch in ALM and during the response epoch in VM/VAL.
outcomes.source: Results, Preparatory activity in thalamus, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 2e, f; Extended Data Figure 4c, f

Selectivity emerged in the sample epoch, increased throughout the delay epoch, and reached a maximum during the response epoch
outcomes.notes: With VM/VAL P3 (258 units, t2) and ALM P2 (810 units, t2), both areas meet the criterion. Selectivity emerges in the sample epoch (first window above twice its SEM centred at 0.1 s in ALM and 0.3 s in VM/VAL), is higher at the end of the delay than at its start (ALM 0.85 to 1.10, VM/VAL -0.05 to 0.38 spikes/s), and peaks in the response epoch (3.0 and 3.3 s). Six combinations of readings meet the criterion in both areas, all with VM/VAL P3 (all neurons with t2, selective neurons with t1 and t2) and ALM P1 or P2. With VM/VAL P1 or P2, selectivity is lower at the end of the delay than at its start in every reading (P2, all neurons, t1, 0.83 against 0.17), and with P3, all neurons and t1 as well (0.57 against 0.53), so the VM/VAL increase holds in 3 of 12 VM/VAL readings. The ALM peak lies 0.4 to 0.6 s after the go cue, not within its first 200 ms. The answers of 2026-10-20 keep both trial readings (t1, t2) and add P3.

outcomes.statement: GABAergic neurons in ALM do not project to thalALM, so ALM photoinhibition does not inhibit thalamus directly.
outcomes.source: Results, ALM drives thalamic preparatory activity, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 8h, i
outcomes.quote: Second, GABAergic neurons in ALM do not project to thal ALM ( Extended Data Fig. 8h, i ), excluding direct photoinhibition of thal ALM
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds no histology.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds 966 of the paper's 1214 ALM units (47 of 57 sessions), 789 of 790 thalamic units (72 of 73 sessions) and 181 of 227 SNr units (18 of 23 sessions; apparently only the putative GABAergic units). Behaviour-only sessions, the muscimol experiments, the weak (0.5 mW) thalamus photoinhibition of Fig. 5, non-behaving whole-cell recordings with current injection, M1 whole-cell recordings, Olig3-cre recordings and the histology are not deposited.

Spikes are stored only from each trial's start to about 4.8 s after pole onset, although trials last about 9 s, and not between trials. The end is fixed to pole onset, not to the go cue, so in trials with delays above about 2 s the response epoch is not stored; spike rates over whole trials or sessions cannot be computed.

Most units hold spikes over only part of their session (median 70% of its trials; 1358 of 1936 units below 90%), and the Units table gives no observation interval, so the trials in which a unit was recorded must be inferred from its first and last spikes.

The mean waveforms are cut short (29 to 38 samples at 25 kHz, trough at sample 15 to 19), so trough-to-peak widths above about 0.5 ms cannot be measured; in 78% of ALM units labelled 'Wide width spiking' the peak is the last sample.

The Units `cell_type` labels ('Wide width spiking', 'Narrow width spiking', 'Cannot be determined') have no stated rule; they cannot be derived from the deposited waveforms but give class sizes close to the paper's.

The whole-cell trial tables leave every photostimulus column empty, and `stim_present` marks the photostimulus trials without description. The laser time is held only in an OptogeneticSeries (stimulus/presentation/photostim_on_*) whose description is 'no description'. It starts between the two delay onsets the trial times allow, 0.10 to 0.17 s after 1.3 s past pole_in_time and 0.03 to 0.10 s before 0.1 s past pole_out_time (1.40 s after pole onset in mouse anm300476, 1.47 s in the others), and it is on in one trial not marked by stim_present (cell_21_1).
In the whole-cell file of cell_21_1 (anm300476) the trial start and stop times are shifted by one row against the pole and cue times (85 rows), and the table is not in time order.
The whole-cell Vm series state unit 'mV' with conversion 0.001, but the values are already in mV; applying the conversion gives values a thousand times too small.

Every electrode group, in thalamus and SNr as well as ALM, carries the ALM coordinates (AP 2.5, ML -1.5, DV 0); the SNr units of anm00261336 are placed at AP -1.56 mm, outside SNr; photostimulus sites give ML negative for the left hemisphere while units give it positive.

The Units column unit_y is described only as "y-coordinate of this unit (mm)", with no reference, so whether it is depth below the pia is not stated; session_start_time is the date of conversion (all sessions on 2017-06-27), not of recording, and no sorter is named, so the ALM sessions missing from the dandiset cannot be identified.
Thalamic units have no nucleus label (brain_subregion 'N/A'), so VM/VAL units can be selected only by distance from a centre the paper does not give in coordinates.

The 9 Gad2 thalamic sessions give the genotype 'Ai35D x GAD2_Cre' (an Arch line), where the paper used Gad2-IRES-Cre with ChR2 injected in TRN, and mark no photostimulus trial, though their 84 units match the optrode units of Extended Data Fig. 2c.
The VGAT-ChR2-EYFP thalamic sessions give the photostimulus power as 2.23 mW where the paper gives 10 mW (Extended Data Fig. 2d); the thalamic fibre site is one nominal coordinate in every session.

Photostimulation at galvo position (0.5, 0.5) mm in mouse anm00264943, interleaved with ALM photoinhibition, is not named; trials labelled 'delay' with power 0 are not explained; the trial columns photo_stim_period, photo_stim_type and is_good have no description.

The dandiset holds data the paper does not describe, 21 ALM sessions of PV-Cre x Ai32 mice with thalamic photostimulation at 10, 22.5 and 45 mW and 12 thalamic sessions of C57BL6 mice without photostimulation.

attempts.label: DANDI:000010
attempts.paper_title: A motor cortex circuit for motor planning and movement
attempts.entry_title: A motor cortex circuit for motor planning and movement (Li et al. 2015)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Li, Chen, Guo, Gerfen and Svoboda (2015) on dandiset 000010, which holds 99 extracellular sessions (19 mice) and 59 two-photon imaging planes (4 mice) from left ALM during the object location discrimination task. It tests behaviour, unit classes, trial-type selectivity and its time course, error trials, contralateral bias, PT and IT neurons and their antidromic latencies, and the imaging counts. The reaction time is run but blocked, as the paper does not fix how it is read from the signal. The photostimulation and anatomy findings are blocked, as the dandiset holds none of those data.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Li et al. (2015) from dandiset 000010

outcomes.statement: Mice in the object location discrimination task performed at 78.4% correct on average, and fewer than 13% of responses came before the go cue.
outcomes.source: Results, ALM is required for movement planning, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: (mean per cent correct, 78.4%; responses before the go cue, ,13%)
outcomes.notes: Without the trials with tagging light, in the 99 extracellular sessions, per cent correct is 76.5% pooled, 75.8% over sessions and 75.2% over mice with no-lick trials counted as not correct (reading x), and 77.2%, 76.5% and 75.9% with them left out (reading y), all within 78.4 +/- 7.84%. Early licks are 11.6% of trials over sessions, below 14.3%, but 14.5% pooled and 14.7% over mice, so the claim holds under reading (b) only, with either no-lick reading. Keeping the light trials gives 75.3%, 75.0% and 74.4% correct under (x) (76.6%, 76.3% and 75.7% under y) and 13.0%, 11.7% and 14.7% early licks. The imaging sessions, which flag no early licks, give 82.3% (x) and 83.5% (y) correct pooled. The answer on no-lick trials made (x) and (y) readings of the criterion, either of which may decide; both were already run, so the outcome is unchanged, and the measured value is now that of (x), the first reading listed (75.8%, earlier 76.5% under y). Dropping also the 103 trials without an early lick whose go cue is missing or not 2.6 s after the sample event, as the other claims' trial masks do, gives 75.8% (x) and 76.5% (y) over sessions and 11.7% early licks over sessions (14.5% pooled, 14.8% over mice), the same outcome.
deviations: The dandiset holds 23 of the paper's 42 task mice (the recording and imaging mice).
Trials with tagging light are found from the laser traces, as the trial tables do not flag them.
1,540 extracellular trials with a lick instruction but no events (1,447 of them marked right, hit, no early) are left out; counted as given they would raise performance.
Only the extracellular sessions are used, as the imaging files flag no early licks.

outcomes.statement: Unilateral photoinhibition of ALM during the delay epoch biases licking to the ipsilateral side, raising performance on ipsilateral (lick left for left ALM) trials and lowering it on contralateral trials, with the reverse pattern for right ALM.
outcomes.source: Results, ALM is required for movement planning, paragraph 2; Figure 1d
outcomes.quote: Inhibiting left ALM caused a tendency to lick the left port, resulting in increased performance in 'lick left' trials and decreased performance in 'lick right' trials (Fig. 1d). The reversed pattern of bias was observed when inhibiting right ALM
outcomes.notes: The VGAT-ChR2-EYFP and PV-ires-Cre x ReaChR photoinhibition mice of Figure 1 are not among the dandiset's 23 subjects, and no file holds a photoinhibition record. The paper names no other public deposit of these data.

outcomes.statement: The ipsilateral bias is smaller when ALM is photoinhibited during the sample epoch than during the delay epoch.
outcomes.source: Results, ALM is required for movement planning, paragraph 2; Figure 1d
outcomes.quote: This ipsilateral bias was smaller when photoinhibiting during the sample epoch
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig1d-delay-inhibition-ipsi-bias; the photoinhibition data are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: 1,408 single units were recorded from left ALM in 19 mice over 99 sessions; by spike width 124 were fast-spiking, 1,245 putative pyramidal and 39 intermediate.
outcomes.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 1a
outcomes.quote: A total of 1,408 single units were recorded across 99 recording sessions ... Units with spike width ,0.35 ms were defined as fast-spiking neurons (124/1,408) and units with spike width .0.45 ms as putative pyramidal neurons (1,245/1,408)
outcomes.notes: The files hold 1,441 units: 1,245 labelled Pyr, 124 FS, 45 PT and 27 IT. Every PT and IT unit has a spike train identical to a Pyr unit in the same file, so there are 1,369 distinct units (within 1,408 +/- 140.8; 1,441 is also within). Sessions 99 and mice 19 match. By trough-to-peak width of the mean waveform, 124 units are fast-spiking (below 0.35 ms) and 1,245 putative pyramidal (above 0.45 ms), as in the paper, and none is intermediate, against 39. Five of six counts match; the intermediate units are not in the dandiset. The waveforms are 29 samples with the trough at sample 15, so widths cap at 0.666 ms (746 units), which does not affect the thresholds.
deviations: Duplicated PT/IT units are counted once.

outcomes.statement: 73% (912 of 1,245) of putative pyramidal neurons distinguished the trial types in at least one trial epoch.
outcomes.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 1; Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: A large fraction(73%,912/1,245)ofneuronsdistinguishedtrialtypes(P , 0.05, two-tailed t-test, not corrected for multiple comparisons) (Fig. 2b)
outcomes.notes: Correct trials, a 1.3 s response epoch and all trials (t1) give 912 of 1,245 putative pyramidal neurons selective (0.733). The other readings give 910, 846 and 851; without the trials with tagging light (t2), 870 (0.699), 868, 795 and 792. All are within tolerance. The answer on light trials wrote (t1) and (t2) into this criterion for every electrophysiology claim of Figs 2 and 3, either of which may decide; both were already run and agree here, so the outcome is unchanged.
deviations: Trials with tagging light are found from the laser traces, as the trial tables do not flag them.
66 extracellular trials without an early lick whose go cue is not 2.6 s after the sample event, those with no go cue (75 extracellular, 2 imaging) and trials without events are dropped.

outcomes.statement: Among selective neurons, 219 of 912 had selective preparatory activity only, 389 peri-movement activity only, and 304 both.
outcomes.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 1; Figure 2d
outcomes.quote: subsets of neurons showed selective preparatory activity (Fig. 2b, left column; Fig. 2d, 219/912 neurons), peri-movement activity during the response epoch (Fig. 2b, right column; 389/912), or both
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading, 231 selective neurons are preparatory only (paper 219, within), 284 peri-movement only (paper 389) and 397 both (paper 304). Over the eight readings (trials, response epoch, light trials kept or left out), preparatory only is 228 to 233 (always within), peri-movement only 272 to 294 (never within) and both 289 to 397 (within in three readings). No reading puts all three counts within tolerance. The answer on light trials named two readings, (t1) all trials and (t2) trials without the light, either of which may decide; the outcome is the same under both, so it is unchanged. Counted by class, 628 neurons are preparatory (sample or delay) against the paper's 523 (219 + 304) and 681 peri-movement (response) against 693 (389 + 304), so the mismatch lies in the preparatory class.
deviations: Trials with tagging light are found from the laser traces; readings (t1) and (t2) are both run and give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Selectivity emerges in the sample epoch, increases through the delay epoch and peaks at the beginning of the response epoch.
outcomes.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 1; Figure 2c; Extended Data Figure 1d, f
outcomes.quote: Selectivityemergedinthesampleepoch,increasedthroughoutthedelay epoch, and reached a maximum at the beginning of the response epoch
outcomes.notes: With 200 ms and 50 ms steps, pre-sample windows hold 52 to 65 selective neurons (binomial limit 71 to 74), sample-epoch windows reach 272 and 280, the count grows through the delay (326 to 408, 321 to 408), and the maximum (574, 582) falls 0.2 s and 0.35 s after the go cue. The first window after the go cue holds 500, so reading (3a) fails and (3b) holds under both steps. Without the trials with light the same holds (maximum 525 and 538 at 0.2 s and 0.25 s). The answer on light trials named two readings, (t1) all trials and (t2) trials without the light, either of which may decide; the outcome is the same under both, so it is unchanged.
deviations: Spikes are stored only from 0.57 s before the sample event, so there are two (200 ms step) or eight (50 ms step) pre-sample windows.
Trials with tagging light are found from the laser traces; readings (t1) and (t2) are both run and give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Individual neuron responses are dynamic although selectivity is stable at the level of the population (Fig. 2c, bottom, population selectivity and the correlation of the population response with that at the go cue).
outcomes.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 1; Figure 2c, bottom; Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Individualneuronresponseswere dynamic, despite stable selectivity at the level of the population (Fig. 2c, bottompanelandExtended Data Fig.2a)
outcomes.notes: With the light trials kept (t1), all 24 correlation readings hold (neurons a or b, normalization v or s, concatenated or difference vector, go-cue bin gs, gc or ge). The mean correlation with the go-cue vector is lower over the sample epoch (-0.12 to 0.24) than over the delay epoch (0.04 to 0.78), below 1, and the population selectivity is above 0 in every delay bin under the four selectivity readings, n10 and n20 (minimum 0.62 spikes/s). Without the light trials (t2), 22 of 24 correlation readings hold; two fail (all neurons, variance, difference vector, bin starting at or centred on the go cue, sample 0.078 and 0.126 against delay 0.054 and 0.103). The answers on the three details named readings (v)/(s), (n10)/(n20) and (gs)/(gc)/(ge); the centred bin (gc) is new and holds under t1 (sample -0.04 to 0.24, delay 0.11 to 0.67). The answer on light trials lets either of (t1) and (t2) decide, so the claim, earlier blocked because one t2 reading failed, is reproduced under t1. Under (ge) the go-cue bin lies inside the delay epoch, so its correlation of 1 enters the delay mean; (gs) avoids this and holds in all 8 t1 rows (sample -0.123 to 0.148, delay 0.036 to 0.478).
deviations: The bin centred on the go cue comes from a second grid of 200 ms bins shifted by 0.1 s, normalized over that grid.
Trials with tagging light are found from the laser traces; under (t2) two readings fail.

outcomes.statement: On error trials ALM activity predicts the direction the mouse licked, so most selective neurons switch their trial-type preference relative to correct trials.
outcomes.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 2c
outcomes.quote: On error trials, when mice licked in the opposite direction to the instruction provided by object location (Fig. 1a), a majority of ALM neurons switched their trial type preference to predict the licking direction, as indicated by the negative correlations
outcomes.notes: Correlation across selective neurons between correct-trial and error-trial selectivity: delay r = -0.30 (897 neurons, at least one error trial of each type) and -0.25 (833, at least five); response -0.38 and -0.34; all P < 1e-12. Without the light trials: delay -0.29 and -0.32, response -0.33 and -0.30. Sample epoch near 0 (-0.025 to 0.045). Per mouse the delay r ranges from -0.76 to 0.49. The answer on light trials named two readings, (t1) all trials and (t2) trials without the light, either of which may decide; the outcome is the same under both, so it is unchanged.
deviations: Trials with tagging light are found from the laser traces; readings (t1) and (t2) are both run and give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Contra-preferring and ipsi-preferring neurons are present in equal proportions in left ALM, and the overall spike count shows no significant contralateral bias (P = 0.13; 8% spike rate modulation across all task-selective neurons).
outcomes.source: Results, ALM contains neurons with bilateral selectivity, paragraph 2; Figure 2e; Results, A movement command emerges in the pyramidal tract neurons, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Significant contralateral bias also did not appear in the overall spike count across the recorded population of neurons (Extended Data Fig. 1; P 5 0.13, two-tailed t-test against 0) ... The contra-preferring and ipsi-preferring neurons were present in equal proportions

statistics.about: overall spike count difference, lick right minus lick left

outcomes.notes: On the paper's test as written (overall spike count over the three epochs, all putative pyramidal neurons), the lick right minus lick left difference is not different from 0 (P = 0.82; 0.52 without light trials). The bootstrap finds no contralateral excess (419 of 912 selective neurons contra-preferring, 0.459; 408 of 870 without light trials). The statement's equal proportions do not hold strictly: ipsi-preferring neurons are the majority (two-sided binomial P = 0.016, or 0.072 without light trials). In the 570 ms before the go cue the difference reaches P = 0.022 to 0.050 across neuron and light readings, and the delay epoch gives P = 0.051 to 0.12. The 8% modulation is matched in some readings (all neurons, 570 ms, over the mean rate, 8.5%; selective neurons, delay, light trials left out, 8.0% and 8.3%) and not in others (5.8% to 10.7%). Only one reading meets both the absence test and the 8% modulation, selective neurons, delay epoch, light trials left out (P = 0.060, 7.97%), and its value is the measured one (earlier 8.5%, from all neurons in the 570 ms window, where the test gives P = 0.036 with a contralateral excess). The answer on light trials named two readings, (t1) all trials and (t2) trials without the light, either of which may decide; the outcome is the same under both, so it is unchanged. The outcome rests on reading (a)(i) because the protocol judges a claim of absence on the paper's test as written ("the overall spike count across the recorded population"). It is fragile: in the 570 ms window, where the Results report the same P = 0.13 for all task-selective neurons, all four tests give P = 0.022 to 0.050 with a contralateral excess. The criterion sets no rule for deciding a claim of absence across its readings, so the outcome depends on the reading taken: on the paper's second P = 0.13 test, for all task-selective neurons, the 570 ms window gives P = 0.050 and 0.038 with a contralateral excess and the delay epoch P = 0.12 and 0.060.
deviations: The claim of absence is judged on the paper's test as written ('overall spike count across the recorded population'), reading (a)(i); the other window and neuron readings of the criterion are shown, and the 570 ms window finds a contralateral excess.
Trials with tagging light are found from the laser traces; readings (t1) and (t2) are both run and give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Fast-spiking neurons have higher baseline firing rates and are less selective than putative pyramidal neurons.
outcomes.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 1b to e
outcomes.quote: Fast-spiking neurons had higher baseline firing rates and were less selective than putative pyramidal neurons (Extended Data Fig. 1)
outcomes.notes: Fast-spiking neurons have higher baseline rates under both readings (0.5 s before the sample: median 4.51 against 1.50 spikes/s, mean 6.90 against 2.92; Mann-Whitney P = 1.3e-17). They are not less selective: 0.750 of them are selective against 0.733 of putative pyramidal neurons (Fisher P = 0.75; 0.710 and 0.699 without light trials), and their mean absolute rate difference is larger (median 1.46 against 0.62 spikes/s). The baseline part holds and the selectivity part goes the other way. The criterion requires both parts under every reading, so the outcome, earlier partially_reproduced, is not_reproduced (first verification). The answer on light trials named two readings, (t1) all trials and (t2) trials without the light, either of which may decide; the outcome is the same under both.
deviations: Baseline reading (b) covers the 0.57 s of recorded time before the sample event, as spikes are stored almost only in trial windows (at least 99% of them in 97 of 99 sessions), so it is close to reading (a).
Trials with tagging light are found from the laser traces; readings (t1) and (t2) are both run and give the same outcome.

outcomes.statement: Of 73 neurons antidromically activated from pyramidal tract axons, 45 passed the collision test (PT neurons), 22 failed and 6 could not be tested; of 134 activated from IT axons, 27 passed (IT neurons), 106 failed and 1 could not be tested.
outcomes.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, paragraph 4; Extended Data Figure 5f
outcomes.quote: Neurons that passed the collision test were classified as pyramidal tract neurons (45/73) or intratelencephalic neurons (27/134). Neurons that failed the test were classified as pyramidal-tract-activated (22/73) or intratelencephalic-activated (106/134)
outcomes.notes: The files label 45 units PT and 27 IT, the paper's counts. The 22 PT-activated and 106 IT-activated neurons that failed the collision test, and the 7 that could not be tested, carry no label, so two of the four counts cannot be checked. The 8 IT units of the two Tlx x Ai32 mice have no light record in their files.
deviations: Only the labelled classes can be counted.

outcomes.statement: PT neurons had shorter antidromic latencies (mean 2.7 ms) than IT neurons (4.6 ms), and both had smaller jitter (0.1 and 0.2 ms) than activated neurons that failed collision (latency 8.3 and 9.8 ms, jitter 2.8 and 2.4 ms).
outcomes.source: Methods, Electrophysiology data analyses, paragraph 4; Results, A movement command emerges in the pyramidal tract neurons, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 5e
outcomes.quote: Pyramidal tract neurons and intratelencephalic neurons had shorter mean antidromic spike latencies (pyramidal tract neurons, 2.7ms; intratelencephalic neurons, 4.6 ms) and smaller temporal jitter (mean s.d. of the antidromic spike latency, pyramidal tract neurons, 0.1 ms; intratelencephalic neurons, 0.2 ms) than the pyramidal-tract-activated (mean latency, 8.3ms; jitter, 2.8ms) and intratelencephalic-activated neurons
outcomes.notes: PT latency is below IT latency in all 18 combinations of reading and parameter (windows of 5, 8 and 10 ms; collision intervals of 5, 10 and 20 ms for (c); 0.5 and 1 ms around the evoked peak for (r)). PT latency is within tolerance in all (2.65 to 2.78 ms, paper 2.7); IT latency in 10 (4.63 to 5.00 ms with the 8 and 10 ms windows under (w) and (c), 4.90 to 4.91 ms under (r) with 8 ms; 3.61 to 3.66 ms with 5 ms and 5.09 ms under (r) with 10 ms are outside). The jitter matches the printed precision only under (r), 0.115 to 0.129 ms for PT and 0.188 to 0.211 ms for IT with 0.5 ms around the peak (0.31 to 0.33 ms with 1 ms); under (w) and (c) it is 0.30 to 0.64 ms and 0.75 to 0.96 ms, which include spontaneous spikes. All four measurable values are within tolerance in one combination ((r), 8 ms window, 0.5 ms; PT 2.674 and 0.115 ms, IT 4.905 and 0.197 ms); keeping spikes within 0.5 ms of the peak bounds the s.d., so that agreement is partly set by the reading, and the window and peak width are open parameters chosen here (1 of 18 combinations). The 22 PT-activated and 106 IT-activated neurons that failed collision carry no label, so their four values, and the comparison of jitter with them, cannot be tested. 45 PT and 19 of 27 IT units have a light record. The answer named readings (w), (c) and (r) with the window and intervals open; the claim, earlier blocked as methods_underspecified, is tested under all three and is partially reproduced under each, as the order holds and values fall outside or cannot be measured.
deviations: The open parameters are run at several values (window 5, 8 and 10 ms; collision interval 5, 10 and 20 ms; peak width 0.5 and 1 ms around the 0.1 ms histogram bin with most spikes).
Only the neurons that passed collision are labelled, so the activated neurons cannot be measured.
The 8 IT units of the two Tlx x Ai32 mice have no light record and are not included.

outcomes.statement: Both PT and IT neurons show preparatory and movement-related activity.
outcomes.source: Results, A movement command emerges in the pyramidal tract neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 3e, i
outcomes.quote: Both intratelencephalic and pyramidal tract neurons displayed preparatory and movement-related activity (Fig. 3e, i)

findings.statement: The dandiset holds none of the photoinhibition (Figure 1) or photoactivation (Figure 5, Extended Data Figures 3, 6 and 7) data, and no histology. Nine of the paper's findings cannot be tested for this reason. The Ai32 mice that are in it have no record of light.

Every unit labelled PT (45) or IT (27) is a second copy of a unit labelled Pyr in the same file, with an identical spike train, so the 1,441 units are 1,369 distinct units. Counting units by label double-counts the tagged neurons.
The 39 units of intermediate spike width (0.35 to 0.45 ms) that the paper recorded and excluded are not in the dandiset, which does not say so; no deposited unit has an intermediate width.

The activated neurons that failed the collision test (22 from the pons, 106 from ALM) and the 7 that could not be tested carry no label, so the tagging outcome can be read only for the 72 neurons that passed.

In 75 sessions the antidromic tagging light was delivered during behavioural trials (4,332 of 14,388 correct trials in those sessions). The trial tables do not flag these trials; they can be found only from the laser traces under stimulus/presentation, whose series have the description 'no description'.
The laser power series are labelled 'watts' but hold values of 47.1 and 82 at the pulses, the milliwatts of the Methods (47 to 82 mW); the AOM input traces, also labelled 'watts', run from 0 to 4.

The extracellular trial tables hold 1,540 trials with a lick instruction that have no behavioural events; 1,447 of them are marked 'right', 'hit' and 'no early', last exactly 5.5 s, and 1,345 hold no spike from any unit. They look like placeholders for removed trials filled with default values. Taken as given they raise performance and bias trial counts towards lick right. 1,502 of them are in the 75 sessions with tagging light, 754 (49%) in the first or last tenth of a session, and 7 in the Ai32 mouse 218693, so they are not the photoactivation trials.

The imaging files flag no trial as an early lick (all False, stored as booleans, where the extracellular files use 'early'/'no early'), so early-lick trials cannot be excluded from the imaging analyses.
No imaging plane gives its depth, so the layer 5 PT and IT populations of Figure 4g, h cannot be selected; the files label 843 included cells IT against the paper's 542 in layer 5.

The imaging mice are given the genotype 'Rosa-lsl-tdtomato' (one) or none (three); the Methods use C57Bl/6Crl mice. The ROI labels include 'Pyr' (23) and 'interneuron' (9), which the paper does not describe, and the `included` flag is described only as 'whether to include this roi into later analyses', without its rule; 424 included ROIs are not 5% brighter than their neuropil by the median ratio.

The `lick_trace` series (10 kHz) is described only as the tongue movement when licking; nothing says it is the photodiode signal used for reaction times or how a reaction time is read from it. Its level and direction differ between sessions (median baselines 0.069 to 4.83 a.u.; it falls after the go cue in 15 of 99 sessions), and nothing describes the gain or polarity.

66 extracellular trials without an early lick have a go cue that is not 2.6 s after the sample event (65 sooner, down to 0.03 s, and one later, 2.68 s), against 2.6 s in all others, and 75 have no go cue; they are dropped here.

Spikes are stored almost only within 5.5 s trial windows (from 0.57 s before the sample event); in 97 of 99 sessions at least 99% of the spikes fall in a window. In two sessions (mice 214429 and 219031) 24% and 30% fall between trials, in gaps between the windows. So baselines before the trial and inter-trial activity cannot be measured in most sessions, and in early-lick trials, where the go cue comes later, part of the response epoch is not stored.

attempts.entry_title: Robust preparatory activity in mouse premotor cortex (Li, Daie et al. 2016)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Li, Daie, Svoboda and Druckmann (2016) on dandiset 000011, which holds extracellular recordings from left ALM of 12 control mice during unilateral and bilateral photoinhibition (58 sessions) and 33 sessions of 7 further mice with no photostimulus record. It reads the photostimulus conditions from the laser traces, and tests unit classification, selectivity, recovery of spike rates and selectivity after photoinhibition, the coding direction analyses and the network models of the paper. The behavioural photoinhibition sessions, the photoactivation and untrained mice, and the callosotomy conditions are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: 1012 single units were recorded in left ALM during behaviour in 58 sessions (20 unilateral, 38 bilateral experiment sessions); by spike width 72 were fast-spiking, 890 putative pyramidal, and 50 intermediate and excluded.

Units with spike width < 0.35 ms were defined as fast-spiking (FS) neurons (72/1012) and units with spike widths > 0.45 ms as putative pyramidal neurons (890/1012). Four of five values are within tolerance; the intermediate count is 15 against 50. The dandiset holds 33 units fewer than the paper's 1012, about the 35 intermediate units missing, so these were probably not deposited. With widths from waveforms interpolated to ten times the stored rate (a variant) 11 units are intermediate, so the 19.5 kHz sampling does not explain the shortfall. The criterion defines no partial outcome; four of five values hold, so the outcome is partial by the rule stated in the notebook's summary (at least half of the parts hold under every reading that must agree).

outcomes.notes: On the 846 putative pyramidal units with identifiable control trials, no combination of readings (R1 or R2, O1 or O2, Student or Welch) puts all four counts within tolerance, with lick-early trials dropped (K1) or kept (K2). With K1 only the response-epoch count reaches its band (445 or 446 under three readings with correct trials); any epoch (at most 565, band 571 to 697), sample (at most 156, band 158 to 194) and delay (at most 294, band 303 to 371) fall short. With K2 three of four reach their bands with correct trials (any 575 to 588, delay 315 to 320, response 453 to 464) and the sample count does not (at most 149). outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 6b
outcomes.quote: The biases in movement were predicted based ALM activity trajectories
outcomes.notes: The side of the boundary where bilateral trials end agrees in sign with the behavioural bias in 13 to 15 of 24 sessions with the rule as written (T1; one-sided binomial p 0.15 to 0.42), and in 11 to 13 of 19 to 23 with T2, not above chance under any reading. The legend's five example sessions are not identified. What the answers changed (questions 1 and 5) is that the outcome must hold under K1 and K2 with T1; it is not reproduced under both, so the outcome is unchanged.

outcomes.statement: Reaction times were faster on trials whose cd trajectory was far from the decision boundary at the go cue.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 9f
outcomes.quote: Reaction times are faster on trials in which the trajectory is far from the decision boundary at the time of the ‘go’ cue
outcomes.notes: The analysis ran. The answer (question 9) found no lick rule in the paper and asked for the outcome over a range of thresholds, so the first lick was read from lick_trace under ten rules (raw level 0.10, 0.12, 0.14; baseline plus 0.01, 0.02, 0.05; baseline plus 3, 5, 10, 20 s.d.). In the 24 experiment-2 sessions of convention A the trace holds no licks; on correct trials its maximum after the go cue is a median 0.0019 above the pre-go baseline, and pooled over 3660 correct and 61 no-response trials no rule detects a lick on correct trials more often than on no-response trials (3 s.d. 0.59 against 0.38; level 0.14 0.05 against 0.03, in one session, 28 ms after the go cue; all others 0.02 or less). In reference sessions of experiment 3 and of the mice without a photostimulus record the same rules detect licks on 73% to 100% of correct trials. The Spearman test holds under 3 of 20 combinations of threshold and lick-early reading, on 3 to 10 trials, so by the criterion's rule the outcome would also be methods_underspecified. What the answer changed is that the claim was run; the block moved from methods_underspecified to data_missing, as the lick times are not in the dandiset for these sessions. After the first verification round raw levels 0.16, 0.20 and 0.25 were added (the levels 0.10 to 0.14 lie below the 0.166 to 0.193 baseline of these sessions); the test then holds under 5 of 26 combinations, on 3 to 10 trials. Per session the median rise after the go cue on correct trials is 0.0013 to 0.0022, as on no-response trials (0.0013 to 0.0021), and example traces are shown. In experiment 3, whose trace carries licks (median rise 0.0385 to 0.0717 on correct trials), the same test on its 6 sessions, a variant on another experiment, holds under 18 of 26 combinations, failing for the levels near or above the trace and a rise of 0.05; it does not decide the outcome.

outcomes.statement: The recovery along cd after unilateral perturbation does not depend on the window used to compute cd (first or last 400 ms of the delay epoch).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 9c
outcomes.quote: The recovery of ALM dynamics along the coding direction ( cd ) is robust to the choice of time window for the calculation of cd
outcomes.notes: With cd from the first or the last 400 ms of the delay, the ipsilateral ROC is within 0.05 of control and the bilateral ROC is lowest under H1 and H2 with lick-early trials dropped (K1), and under H2 with them kept (K2; under H1 the first-window ipsilateral ROC is 0.059 to 0.072 below control). What the answers changed (questions 1 and 5) is that the outcome must hold under K1 and K2 with the rule as written (T1); it does, under H1 or H2 for each, so the outcome is unchanged.

outcomes.statement: Bisecting the ALM corpus callosum did not affect performance on control trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Contralateral input is required for recovery, paragraph 1; Figure 5b; Extended Data Figure 10b
outcomes.quote: Remarkably, behavioral performance was unaffected ( Fig. 5b , control trials, before vs. after callosotomy, p>0.05, two-tailed t-test)
outcomes.notes: There are no sessions before the callosotomy, and no file marks any mouse as callosotomised; the 7 mice are identified as the callosotomy group only by their genotypes, delay and the absence of a photostimulus record. Control trials of their sessions cannot be identified either.

outcomes.statement: After callosotomy, performance became highly sensitive to unilateral (one spot) photoinhibition, with a significant interaction between callosotomy and photoinhibition, and dropped to the level of bilateral photoinhibition in control mice.
outcomes.source: Results, Contralateral input is required for recovery, paragraph 1; Figure 5b
outcomes.quote: However, behavioral performance was now highly sensitive to transient unilateral photoinhibition ( Fig 2b , 1 laser spot: p=0.0019, two-tailed t-test against control). There was a significant interaction between callosotomy and unilateral photoinhibition (p=0.0035, repeated measure two-way ANOVA)

statistics.about: unilateral one spot against control, after callosotomy
interaction of callosotomy and unilateral photoinhibition

outcomes.notes: The 33 sessions of the 7 mice contain silenced trials (in 23 of 35 unlabelled sessions the fraction of trials with population rate below 30% of median in the light window exceeds the one 1.5 s later by 0.1 or more) but no photostimulus record, so photoinhibition and control trials cannot be told apart.

outcomes.statement: Preparatory activity after callosotomy was similar to control; 254 of 496 putative pyramidal neurons were selective.
outcomes.source: Results, Contralateral input is required for recovery, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 10e-g
outcomes.quote: Preparatory activity in callosotomized mice (n=7 mice) was similar to control mice ( Fig. 5c ; Extended Data Fig. 10 ), providing additional evidence that the two ALM hemispheres can maintain preparatory activity independently
outcomes.notes: Control trials cannot be identified (as fig5b-callosotomy-unilateral-sensitivity). The sessions hold 519 putative pyramidal units by width (paper 496, within tolerance, if these are the callosotomy mice, which no file says), 15 fast-spiking and 30 intermediate. Counted on all trials, photoinhibition trials included, 331 to 340 are selective with correct trials (paper 254 on control trials) and 81 to 84 in the sample epoch; this is not the claim's measure.

outcomes.statement: After callosotomy, ipsilateral photoinhibition left spike rates recovered on average but selectivity failed to recover; contralateral photoinhibition selectivity recovered in 217 ms; bilateral did not recover.
outcomes.source: Results, Contralateral input is required for recovery, paragraph 2; Figure 5d, e legend
outcomes.quote: After ipsilateral photoinhibition, ALM neurons recovered their average spike rate ( Fig. 5c, d ), but selectivity failed to recover ( Fig. 5e )
outcomes.notes: The photoinhibition conditions (ipsilateral, contralateral, bilateral) of the callosotomy sessions are not recorded in any file.

outcomes.statement: After callosotomy, selectivity along cd was reduced following ipsilateral photoinhibition.
outcomes.source: Results, Contralateral input is required for recovery, paragraph 2; Figure 5f
outcomes.quote: Selectivity in the cd direction was reduced ( Fig. 5f , 16 sessions)
outcomes.notes: As fig5-callosotomy-no-recovery; the ipsilateral trials of the callosotomy sessions cannot be identified.

outcomes.statement: Monolithic network models (integrator, integrator with corrective feedback, trained random recurrent networks) do not recover the unperturbed trajectory after transient silencing of half their neurons.
outcomes.source: Results, Robust model networks, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 1f-i
outcomes.quote: Overall, all “monolithic” models consisting of one network were unable to explain robustness
outcomes.notes: Each of 10 simple integrators (persistent input) ends 20% to 22% of its selectivity away from its unperturbed output at 2 s after half of its units are silenced, and each of 10 FORCE networks trained to ramp after a transient input ends 13% to 76% away (median 41%); all exceed the 10% bound. Transient-input and cascaded integrators end about 50% away. The corrective-feedback and tamed-chaos models lack parameters in the text and were not built.
deviations: FORCE target (a ramp to plus or minus 1 at 2 s), feedback weights, learning rate and update every 2 ms are standard choices the paper does not give.

outcomes.statement: Modular networks of two coupled modules (attractor, integrator, trained recurrent network) recover after silencing of one module; the modular attractor drifts to a random fixed point when both modules are silenced.
outcomes.source: Results, Robust model networks, paragraph 2; Figure 6b-d
outcomes.quote: Selective commissural connections restored activity on the other side after unilateral transient silencing ( Fig. 6b ). When the two sides are silenced, the network drifts to one of the fixed points randomly
outcomes.notes: With noise drawn once per step (n2) the modular attractor ends at the instructed fixed point in 100% of trials after unilateral silencing and in 48% (1 ms step, h1) or 50% (0.1 ms, h2) after bilateral silencing; with Euler-Maruyama noise of intensity 0.01 (n1) it does so in 41.5% to 51% of trials whatever the silencing (51% and 48.5% unperturbed), so the unilateral part fails. The modular integrator built from the printed matrix restores lick right trials (0.2% from unperturbed at 2 s with h1, 5.4% with h2) but not lick left ones (50% away), as its recovery unit passes only right-preferring activity. What the answer changed (question 10) is that n1, n2, h1 and h2 are named and the outcome must hold under all four; h2 was added, and all four give partial, so the outcome is unchanged. The criterion defines no partial outcome; two (n1) or three (n2) of four parts hold, so it is partial by the rule stated in the notebook's summary.
deviations: The trained modular FORCE network is not specified enough to rebuild and was not built.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the recording sessions. The behavioural photoinhibition sessions (Figs 1d, 2b, 5b and Extended Data Fig. 3), the photoactivation mice (Extended Data Fig. 5), the untrained mice used to map photoinhibition (Extended Data Fig. 2d) and any session before callosotomy are not in it. Nine of the paper's findings cannot be tested for this reason.

33 sessions of 7 mice (the callosotomy group by genotype and delay) and 3 experiment-1 sessions of mouse 255200 have no photostimulus record (no laser traces, no photostimulus events, no trial column), though most of them contain trials whose activity is silenced in the light window of the other sessions. Their photoinhibition trials cannot be identified.
No file says which mice were callosotomised, on which side, or when; the subject description holds only the JAX strain numbers.

The trial table has no photostimulus column. The condition of a trial (site, number of laser spots, timing) can be recovered only from the per-site laser power traces (one 5 s chunk per photostimulus trial, matched to trials by time) and the photostim_start_time events, whose value is the peak power. The number of spots is not stated anywhere and is inferred from the waveform and power.

In lick-early trials the photostim_start_time and photostim_stop_time events are logged at the restarted delay, after the light seen in the laser trace (20 of 41 lick-early photostimulus trials in two sessions read in full); in other trials they agree within 5 ms. Over all labelled sessions, 339 lick-early photostimulus trials have the event more than 0.1 s after the light, with the light up to 10 s before the logged go cue.

Session 258250_20141202 holds two interleaved sequences of trial ids (1 to 24 and 105 to 160) whose times overlap (98 overlapping pairs), so its events cannot be assigned to trials. In 28 units of 3 sessions the spike times are not in time order, and two sessions have trials out of time order.
The control mice hold 979 units against the paper's 1012; 15 have intermediate spike widths against 50, so about 33 intermediate units were not deposited.
The units' cell_type labels intermediate-width units (0.35 to 0.45 ms trough to peak) as FS, where the Methods exclude them (45 units in all).
The asset sub-255200_ses-20140910_behavior.nwb holds only metadata (no trials, events or time series).

The paper's neuron and session counts for its selectivity and population analyses (55, 143 and 40 selective neurons; 16 sessions with 6 to 20 neurons) cannot be reached with the criteria the paper states; the dataset gives 138 to 173, 221 to 293, 58 to 62 and 24 sessions with 6 to 37 neurons. Experiment 1 holds 4 mice where the paper reports 6.

No file holds lick times; licks exist only as the analogue lick_trace (5 s chunks at 10 kHz, unit a.u.). In the 24 experiment-2 sessions used for the activity space the trace stays within about 0.002 of its baseline after the go cue on correct trials, and lick-detection rules fire no more often on correct than on no-response trials, so it holds no licks; an experiment-1 session read for reference is flat as well, while an experiment-3 session and a session of the mice without a photostimulus record carry licks. Reaction times cannot be computed for these sessions.

disagreements.reason: None of the 16 reading combinations has all four counts within tolerance, with lick-early trials dropped (K1) or kept (K2); the sample-epoch count is 132 to 156 against a floor of 158.4, which is borderline. The 44 putative pyramidal units of the three unlabelled experiment-1 sessions are dropped, so 846 units are tested, not 890; the variant that includes them reproduces under K1 (sample 162 to 165) and misses under K2 by about 1.5 units (157), which would make the outcome methods_underspecified.

The VGAT ipsilateral normalised rate is 0.177 to 0.356 (needs < 0.1) under every reading. PV (0.035 to 0.052), bilateral and contralateral pass under K1. The 299 neurons match the legend's 300. Under K2 the photostimulus event is logged after the light in early-lick trials, which dilutes the effects (0.14 to 0.36). The "at least 2 trials" rule is an author choice; the outcome holds across it.
The control ROC is 0.680 to 0.689, below the floor of 0.72.
Control is 0.649 to 0.685 against 0.72 +/- 0.02 in every reading.
