attempts.label: DANDI:000019
attempts.paper_title: Functional organization of human sensorimotor cortex for speech articulation
attempts.entry_title: Speech articulation in human sensorimotor cortex (Bouchard et al. 2013)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Bouchard, Mesgarani, Johnson and Chang (2013) on dandiset 000019, which holds raw ECoG and syllable annotations of subjects reading consonant-vowel syllables. High gamma is computed from the raw voltage. It tests the active electrodes, the articulator timing, the mixed tuning of electrodes and the cortical state-space analyses. The spatial maps cannot be tested, as the dandiset gives no electrode positions relative to the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Bouchard et al. (2013) from dandiset 000019

outcomes.statement: Three subjects with high-density ECoG (two left, one right hemisphere) read aloud CV syllables made of 18 or 19 consonants followed by /a/, /i/ or /u/, each CV produced 15 to 100 times, with the microphone recorded with the ECoG at 3052 Hz.
outcomes.source: Methods, Subjects and Experimental Task, and Data acquisition and Signal Processing; Supplementary Table 1
outcomes.quote: Three native English speaking human subjects underwent chronic implantation of a high-density, subdural electrocortigraphic (ECoG) array over the left hemisphere (two subjects) or right hemisphere (one subject) ... composed of 18–19 consonants (19 consonants for two subjects, 18 consonants for one subject), followed by one of three vowels. Each CV was produced between 15 and 100 times
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds four subjects (EC2, EC9, GP31, GP33); EC2, GP31 and GP33 are taken to be the paper's EC2, EC31 and EC33, and EC9 is not in the paper. The rate is 3051.76 Hz. The three subjects have 57, 55 and 57 CVs (169, paper 168), each with 19 consonants, and 2 to 107 renditions per CV (EC2 /thi/ 10, GP31 /thi/ 2, 33 GP31 CVs above 100); leaving out CVs below 15 renditions gives 56 + 54 + 57 = 167. The audio was removed. EC2 and GP31 have negative x coordinates (left hemisphere if x is the usual axis); GP33 has no coordinates, so the right hemisphere of EC33 cannot be checked. The answer of 2026-10-22 on CVs with fewer than 15 renditions leaves this claim as it was; the paper's 168 CVs fit neither reading, and the outcome is unchanged. No field in the files links GP31 and GP33 to EC31 and EC33; the subject fields hold only species and id, and the session descriptions name only the block. The electrode group of EC2 and GP31 is named `L256Grid electrodes` in every file, which fits a left hemisphere; that of GP33 is `auto_group`, with location `location`. In EC2 and GP31, 18 consonants have all three vowels with 15 or more renditions each, and in GP33 19, so GP31 fits the paper's subject with 18 consonants and 54 CVs.
deviations: The correspondence of GP31 and GP33 to the paper's EC31 and EC33 is an assumption; no metadata links them.

outcomes.statement: About 30 active vSMC electrodes were found per subject during syllable articulation, an electrode being active when its high-gamma z-score changed by more than 2 for any syllable.
outcomes.source: Results, vSMC Physiology During Syllable Production, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: During syllable articulation, approximately 30 active vSMC electrode sites were identified per subject (~1200 mm 2 , change in z-score > 2 for any syllable)
outcomes.notes: Mean active vSMC electrodes per subject. With every CV, 24.3 with the pre-utterance baseline (EC2 15, GP31 49, GP33 9), 21.3 with the whole block and 34.0 with the rest period; none is within 27 to 33, so this CV reading gives not reproduced. With only CVs of 15 or more renditions, 10.7, 7.0 and 27.0 (rest; EC2 29, GP31 31, GP33 21), so one baseline is within tolerance, at its lower edge, and this reading gives partially reproduced. Both readings of the change give the same counts. The count depends strongly on the threshold (41.7 at 1.5, 11.7 at 2.5, pre baseline, every CV). What the answers changed. The rest period, a variant in the first run, is now baseline reading (c) of the claims file, and the CV set is now a reading of the claims file whose two readings give different outcomes. The first run recorded not reproduced; the outcome is now blocked as methods_underspecified. Measured is the first reading (pre, every CV). The CV split comes from one syllable. Every GP31 electrode active with every CV but not with the 15+ CVs is above 2 for /thi/, which GP31 has 2 renditions of (40 electrodes under pre, 43 under whole, 20 under rest); in EC2 one electrode is active through /thi/ (10 renditions). A variant that leaves out the 162 trials overlapping intervals marked as ECoG artifacts, not a reading of the claims file, gives means of 22.7, 21.0 and 26.0 with every CV and 8.0, 6.7 and 15.0 with the 15+ CVs, none within 27 to 33; GP31's count under rest with the 15+ CVs falls from 31 to 2, so the one reading within tolerance rests on trials the files mark as artifacts.
deviations: High gamma computed from the raw ECoG with a filter bank whose widths the paper does not give (standard choice); bad channels from the dataset's flags.
vSMC taken as the electrodes labelled precentral or postcentral, good in every block (268 over the three subjects, paper 266); no label marks the guenon.

outcomes.statement: In one subject, dorsal electrodes (e124, e108) were active for /b/ (lips), mid vSMC electrodes (e129, e133, e105) for /d/ (front tongue), and a more ventral electrode (e104) was most active for /g/ (back tongue).
outcomes.source: Results, vSMC Physiology During Syllable Production, paragraph 1; Figure 1c-e
outcomes.quote: Dorsally located electrodes (e.g. e124, e108; black) were active during production of /b/, which requires transient closure of the lips. In contrast, mid-positioned electrodes (e.g. e129, e133, e105; grey) were active during production of /d/ ... Amore ventral electrode (e.g. e104; red) was most active during production of /g/
outcomes.notes: No subject, numbering from 1 or from 0, puts all six named electrodes on vSMC. The most is 5 of 6, in EC2 counted from 0, where e129 is labelled middle temporal; GP31 has at most 4 and GP33 at most 3. The criterion blocks the claim in that case. The dataset does not say how the paper numbered electrodes, and gives no distance from the Sylvian fissure for the order part. For information, in EC2 counted from 1 (3 of 6 on vSMC), five of the six named electrodes prefer their syllable under both measures and all three baselines; counted from 0, two or three do. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

outcomes.statement: Fricatives with different tongue-tip constriction locations (/th/, /s/, /sh/) engaged different electrodes; front-tongue consonants of different manner (/l/, /n/, /d/) engaged overlapping electrodes with different magnitudes; for /ja/, /ji/, /ju/ the activity was similar before the C-V transition, while a dorsal electrode was active during /u/ only.
outcomes.source: Results, vSMC Physiology During Syllable Production, paragraph 2; Figure 1f-h
outcomes.quote: Syllables with the same consonant followed by different vowels ( Fig. 1h, /ja/, /ji/, /ju/ ) revealed similar activity patterns preceding the CV transition. During vowel phonation, a dorsal electrode is clearly active during /u/ (black arrow), but not /i/ or /a/
outcomes.notes: Under all 96 readings (3 baselines, 2 CV sets, 8 timing readings for T_A, 2 p-value readings) no GLM electrode with a positive lips weight has z above 2 for /ju/ at +250 ms and below 2 for /ja/ and /ji/ in any subject. With the rest baseline some lips-positive electrodes exceed 2 for /ju/ (13 of 96 readings, largest 3.54), but at each of them /ja/ or /ji/ is above 2 as well; under the pre and whole baselines the largest /ju/ value is below 2. The fricative and manner contrasts are not judged, as the claims file says. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and the CV set are now readings of the claims file; the 32 rest readings added give the same outcome, not reproduced, as in the first run. Without the GLM selection, among all vSMC electrodes, one EC2 electrode under rest (both CV sets) has /ju/ above 2 and /ja/ and /ji/ below 2; under pre and whole no vSMC electrode in any subject reaches 2 for /ju/ (largest 1.19), so there the result does not come from the selection.
deviations: The lips weights come from the GLM of fig2a-lips-dorsal, which is blocked for its spatial judgement only; the weights and electrode selection need no positions and are computed, so this claim is tested.

outcomes.statement: Each articulator is represented across vSMC; the lip representation lies in dorsal vSMC and the tongue representation is spread over its ventral part.
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial Representation of Articulators, paragraph 1; Figure 2a
outcomes.quote: We found representations for each articulator distributed across vSMC ( Fig. 2a ). For example, the lip representation was localized to the dorsal aspect of vSMC, whereas the tongue representation was more distributed across the ventral aspect
outcomes.notes: The claim judges where the lips and tongue weights lie as dorsal-ventral distance from the Sylvian fissure. The dandiset gives no electrode position relative to the Sylvian fissure or the central sulcus. EC2 and GP31 have x, y, z coordinates with no unit or frame; GP33 has none. The GLM electrodes and weights are computed (they need no positions) and used by fig1f-h, suppfig6 and suppfig9. For information only, under the first reading the median z coordinate of the top 10% of lips weights is above that of the tongue weights in EC2 (36.6 against 15.6); GP31 has no tongue window in that reading, so it gives no comparison. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

outcomes.statement: Across subjects the articulator representations are laid out from dorsal to ventral as larynx, lips, jaw, tongue and larynx, with a laryngeal representation at the dorsal end of vSMC as well as a ventral one.
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial Representation of Articulators, paragraph 2; Figure 2b; Discussion, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: We found an overall somatotopic dorsal-ventral arrangement of articulator representations laid out in the following sequence: larynx (X), lips (L), jaw (J), tongue (T), and larynx (X)
outcomes.notes: Needs positions relative to the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure in all three subjects (see fig2a-lips-dorsal). The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

outcomes.statement: Electrodes with similar articulator representations lie closer together than chance; the mean spatial autocorrelation within 3 mm is 0.45 against 0.26 for permuted electrode positions.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 3a, b legend
outcomes.quote: The correlation values for the data (0.45 ± 0.03, mean ± s.e., 3 subjects x 4 articulators, n = 12) were significantly greater than for the randomized data (0.26 ± 0.02, mean ± s.d., 1000 randomizations for each subject; P < 10-3)

statistics.test: permutation test, electrode locations shuffled within subject, 1000 randomizations

outcomes.notes: Needs the smoothed maps in the plane of distances from the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure (see fig2a-lips-dorsal). The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

outcomes.statement: Each articulator's representation lies in a more consistent place across subjects than chance (mean cross-subject correlation within 3 mm 0.195 against 0.031).
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 3c, d legend
outcomes.quote: The correlation values for the data (0.195 ± 0.064, mean ± s.e., 3 subjects x 4 articulators, n = 12) were significantly greater than for the randomized data (0.031 ± 0.021, mean ± s.d., P < 10-3, 1000 iteration permutation test)
outcomes.notes: Needs maps in a common frame across subjects, from distances to the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure (see fig2a-lips-dorsal); GP33 has no coordinates at all. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

outcomes.statement: Within each subject, adjacent articulator representations (larynx-tongue, tongue-jaw, jaw-lips) are spatially sequenced along the dorsal-ventral axis, with positive cross-correlation on one side of the diagonal (0.099) and negative on the other (-0.102), both beyond chance.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 3e, f legend
outcomes.quote: The correlation values for the above diagonal data were positive (0.099 ± 0.052, mean ± s.e., 3 subjects x 3 cross-articulator comparisons, n = 9) and significantly greater than for the randomized data ... the correlation values for the below diagonal data were negative (-0.102 ± 0.052, mean ± s.e., n = 9)

statistics.test: permutation test, 1000 permutations for each subject
permutation test, 1000 permutations for each subject

outcomes.notes: Needs the maps of suppfig3b-spatial-clustering (see fig2a-lips-dorsal). The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

outcomes.statement: The observed map is neither a perfect linear somatotopy nor random; the mean distance between electrodes preferring the same articulator (11.06 mm) and between those preferring different ones (15.11 mm) lie between the two null models.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 5b legend
outcomes.quote: The observed intra-articulator distances (11.06 ± 1.01 mm. mean ± s.e., n = 3188 pair-wise distances) and across articulator distances (15.11 ± 1.01mm, mean ± s.e., n = 4587 pair-wise distances) are both intermediate to these bounding values

statistics.about: observed against both null models; printed as "P >10-3", which with the figure's *** marks reads as P < 10-3
statistics.test: comparison with 1000 simulated maps per null model

outcomes.notes: Needs Euclidean distances in mm between electrodes in the paper's plane (see fig2a-lips-dorsal). The EC2 and GP31 coordinates have no stated unit or frame, and GP33 has none. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

outcomes.statement: Single electrodes show a clear preferred articulator and also carry weights for other articulators.
outcomes.source: Results, Spatial Representation of Articulators, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 6
outcomes.quote: This analysis revealed clear preferred tuning for individual articulators at single electrodes (Fig. 2c, electrodes categorized according to the strongest articulator representation), and also demonstrated that single electrodes had functional representations of multiple articulators
outcomes.notes: Under all 96 readings, each group of GLM electrodes (grouped by largest weight) has its preferred articulator with the largest mean share of positive weight (lips 63 to 79%, tongue 48 to 96%, larynx 49 to 84%, jaw 69 to 84%) and non-zero shares of the others; in one reading no electrode prefers the tongue. The GLM electrodes number 49 to 117 over the three subjects. In the readings where a subject has no window T_A for an articulator, its weights there are missing. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and the CV set are now readings of the claims file; the 32 rest readings added hold as well, and the outcome is reproduced, as in the first run. The criterion barely discriminates. On weights permuted across each subject's electrodes, which removes any tuning of single electrodes, the same test holds in 94 of 96 readings, because grouping by the largest weight puts the preferred articulator first almost by construction. The outcome follows the criterion; a clear preferred articulator beyond what the grouping gives is not shown by it.
deviations: Uses the GLM weights of fig2a-lips-dorsal, which is blocked for its spatial judgement only.

outcomes.statement: Articulator correlations follow a staggered sequence consistent across subjects; lip and tongue correlations begin well before sound onset, jaw and larynx align to the C-V transition, and the high and back tongue vowel features peak near the vowel midpoint (~250 ms).
outcomes.source: Results, Timing of Articulator Representations, paragraph 1; Figure 3a-d
outcomes.quote: lip and tongue correlations began well before sound onset ( Fig. 3a, c, d ); jaw and larynx correlations were aligned to the CV transition ( Fig. 3a, c, d ); high tongue and back tongue features showed high temporal specificity for the vowel phase, peaking near the acoustic mid-point of the vowels (~250 ms, Fig. 3b–d ). This sequence of articulator correlations was consistent across subjects
outcomes.notes: Under all 96 readings (3 baselines, 2 CV sets, threshold per subject or pooled and over all articulators or per articulator, onset at threshold or half peak, ANOVA on onset or peak) none of the three order conditions holds. Mean lips onsets are -270 to -54 ms, but tongue onsets are -26 to +290 ms, so lips and tongue both precede the substitute acoustic onset (-110 ms, CV range -257 to -11 ms) in no reading; jaw onsets are -270 to -116 ms, as early as the lips; high-tongue peaks are 276 to 325 ms. Against t = 0, shown beside it as the criterion now asks, lips and tongue both begin before 0 ms in 2 of 96 readings and the outcome is the same. The ANOVA has F = 9.4 to 39.2 with p below 1e-10 in 76 of 96 readings. Electrodes 162 to 226 (paper 211). Measured values are from the first reading (175 electrodes; mean of back and high tongue peaks, 235 and 305 ms). What the answers changed. The criterion now allows the hand-marked syllable start as the acoustic onset, as a deviation, which the first run had used while asking; the rest baseline and the CV set are now readings. The outcome is not reproduced, as in the first run. Tongue electrodes number 2 to 7 under the readings with one threshold for all six articulators (2 to 45 over all readings), so those tongue onsets rest on few electrodes. A variant that leaves out the trials overlapping intervals marked as ECoG artifacts gives the same outcome (one condition holds in 4 of 96 readings, none in the others; lips onsets -338 to -125 ms, tongue -6 to 289 ms).
deviations: The acoustic onset is the hand-marked syllable start of the trial table, averaged per CV, as the audio is not in the dandiset; the criterion allows this substitute since the answer of 2026-10-22. The outcome against t = 0 is the same.

outcomes.statement: Onset latencies of the articulator model fit do not differ between electrodes just anterior and just posterior to the central sulcus (within 10 mm), nor across the guenon.
outcomes.source: Results, Timing of Articulator Representations, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 7
outcomes.quote: we found no significant latency differences in those areas immediately anterior and posterior to the central sulcus (±10 mm), or across the geunon (a-b, P > 0.4, Rank-Sum test; n = 71 and n = 67 electrodes

statistics.n: 71 electrodes (pre against post central) and 67 electrodes (across the guenon), three subjects

outcomes.notes: Needs electrodes within 10 mm anterior and posterior of the central sulcus and the guenon's boundary; the dandiset gives no distances to the central sulcus and no guenon label. The answer of 2026-10-22 to the question on positions says the paper measures them on each subject's MRI reconstruction and gives no way to derive them from grid geometry, unlabelled coordinates or atlas labels, so the block stands.

outcomes.statement: The cortical state-space has nine spatial PCs in every subject, the eigenvalues falling fast up to the ninth and slowly after, together explaining about 60% of the variance.
outcomes.source: Results, Phonetic Organization of Spatial Patterns, paragraph 1; Methods, PCA and Cortical-State Space; Supplementary Figure 8
outcomes.quote: we used principal components analysis to transform the observed cortical activity patterns into a ‘cortical state-space’ (9 spatial PCs for all subjects, ~60% of variance explained
outcomes.notes: With row z-scoring, nine PCs explain a mean of 0.60 to 0.66 over subjects, within 0.54 to 0.66 in 11 of 12 baseline, CV set and window readings (rest, every CV, -375 to 620 ms gives 0.661). With time z-scoring, 0.49 to 0.56, within under the rest baseline (4 readings) and once under the whole block, outside in the other 7. The readings give different outcomes (16 within, 8 not). The variance explained does not depend on the input projected. No sharp change at the ninth eigenvalue is seen; not judged. Measured is the first reading (pre, row, every CV, epoch). What the answers changed. The paper fixes neither z-scoring nor the CV set, which the claims file now names as readings, and the rest period is now a baseline reading; the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run. The z-scoring decides most of the split (row 11 of 12 within, time 5 of 12); the CV set and the window do not change the count (8 of 12 within each).

outcomes.statement: At the consonant time (-25 ms) k-means clustering of the cortical state-space groups syllables by major oral articulator (labial, coronal, dorsal), and three clusters are more parsimonious than two or four (mean silhouette 0.47 against 0.45 and 0.43).
outcomes.source: Results, Phonetic Organization of Spatial Patterns, paragraph 1; Figure 4a; Methods, Clustering Analysis, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: On average across subjects, this analysis validated the claim that three clusters (Average Silhouette = 0.47) was a more parsimonious clustering scheme than either two (Average Silhouette = 0.45) or four clusters (Average Silhouette = 0.43)
outcomes.notes: Under 23 of the 24 readings (3 baselines, 2 z-scorings, 2 projections, 2 CV sets) k = 3 does not have the highest mean silhouette (not reproduced). Under one, rest baseline, time z-scoring, projection (i) and every CV, k = 3 is highest by a small margin (0.333 against 0.329 for k = 2 and 0.241 for k = 4), with values outside tolerance (partially reproduced). k = 3 gives 0.19 to 0.36 against the paper's 0.47. GP31's k = 2 silhouette is 0.35 to 0.80 with every CV and 0.24 to 0.68 with CVs of 15 or more renditions. Measured values are the first reading (pre, row, projection i, every CV) for k = 3, 2 and 4. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and projection (ii) are now readings, and one of the readings added gives partially reproduced, so the readings differ. The first run recorded not reproduced; the outcome is now blocked as methods_underspecified. Over the 24 readings k = 2 has the highest mean silhouette in 20, k = 4 in 3 and k = 3 in 1.

outcomes.statement: Clusters of the cortical state-space match the major articulators at the consonant time (median co-clustering 0.50 against 0.32 by chance) and the vowels at the vowel time (0.65 against 0.37), across subjects.
outcomes.source: Results, Phonetic Organization of Spatial Patterns, paragraph 1; Supplementary Figure 11a, b
outcomes.quote: clustering of CV’s in the cortical state-space co-clustered with the major articulators significantly more than expected by chance (Red: observed distribution, median = 0.50, Black: null distribution from 1000 random permutations of articulator assignments of CVs, median = 0.32
outcomes.notes: Clusters match the major articulators beyond chance in every reading (consonant p from 9e-23 to 3e-13). Observed consonant medians 0.633 to 0.909 with labels (a) and 0.595 to 0.800 with labels (b) (paper 0.50 +- 0.05), vowel medians 0.41 to 0.70 (paper 0.65 +- 0.065), nulls 0.336 to 0.412 for consonants and 0.343 to 0.430 for vowels (paper 0.32 and 0.37). Of the 48 readings (24 by two label readings) 38 give partially reproduced. In five readings, all with projection (i) (row with 15+ CVs under each baseline, rest with row and every CV, rest with time and 15+ CVs), the vowel test gives p from 3e-10 to 5e-07, above 1e-10, and not reproduced under both label readings. Projection (ii) gives partially reproduced in all 24 of its readings. Each label reading is judged with its own consonant test and the vowel test. Measured is the first reading (pre, row, projection i, every CV, labels a). What the answers changed. The answers left z-scoring and the CV set open and added the rest baseline and projection (ii) as readings; projection (ii) gives partially reproduced in every reading, and the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run.

outcomes.statement: Hierarchical clustering of the state-space puts the major oral articulator (dorsal, labial, coronal) at the top tier for consonants, superordinate to constriction location, with constriction degree only at the lowest level; for vowels the first split is lip rounding (/u/ against /a/ and /i/).
outcomes.source: Results, Phonetic Organization of Spatial Patterns, paragraph 2; Figure 4c, d
outcomes.quote: For consonants, this analysis confirmed that the primary tier of organization was defined by the major oral articulator features: dorsal, labial, or coronal ( Fig. 4c ) ... during the vowel period, a primary distinction was based upon the presence/absence of lip-rounding (/u/ vs. /a/ & /i/)
outcomes.notes: Both splits hold together in at most one subject, EC2 (14 of 24 readings), so no reading gives reproduced; 28 of the 48 readings (with the two label readings) give partially reproduced and 20 not reproduced. Under time z-scoring with projection (i) no subject meets both. The vowel split never holds in GP31. The purity rule of two thirds is the claims file's own. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and projection (ii) are now readings, and z-scoring and the CV set stay open; the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run. Projection (ii) gives partially reproduced in 20 of 24 readings and projection (i) in 8 of 24; the CV set and the label reading do not change the counts (14 of 24 each).

outcomes.statement: Over early times (-375 to 120 ms) constriction location correlates with the state-space structure more than constriction degree, which correlates more than the upcoming vowel; over later times (125 to 620 ms) vowel configuration correlates most.
outcomes.source: Results, Phonetic Organization of Spatial Patterns, paragraph 3; Figure 4e, f
outcomes.quote: Across early time points (−375:120 ms), we found that consonant features describing constriction location yielded a significantly greater correlation with the cortical state-space than constriction degree, which in turn was significantly more correlated than the upcoming vowel ... across later time points (125:620 ms), we found that vowel features provided the greatest correlation

statistics.about: early window, location against degree against vowel
late window, vowel configuration against the others

outcomes.notes: Early window, location over degree over vowel with p < 1e-10 under every Euclidean reading (n = 297) except two (rest, projection i, 15+ CVs, location over degree p = 3e-05 and 3e-04). Late window, the vowel features correlate more than both other sets with p < 1e-10 in 10 of 24 readings (reproduced), every 15+ reading with projection (ii) among them; the other 14 give partially reproduced, mostly with every CV, where location correlates as much as or more than the vowel features. Hamming distances are a variant and are not judged. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and projection (ii) are now readings, and z-scoring and the CV set stay open; the readings still give reproduced and partially reproduced, and the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run. Projection (ii) gives 8 of the 10 reproduced readings, and the 15+ CVs 8 of 10.

outcomes.statement: Cluster separability, averaged over subjects, rises from about -300 ms and peaks about 200 ms before the C-V transition for consonants, and rises from about 50 ms and peaks at +250 ms for vowels.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of Phonetic Representations, paragraph 2; Figure 5c
outcomes.quote: separability peaked ~200 ms before the CV transition for consonants (onset, ~−300 ms), and at +250 ms for vowels (onset, ~50 ms)
outcomes.notes: Under all 120 readings (24 baseline, z-scoring, projection and CV readings by five cluster readings) the peaks are not both within tolerance. With phonetic groups the consonant peak is at -155 to +15 ms (paper -200) and the vowel peak at 155 to 235 ms; with k-means at each time one curve serves both, peaking between -170 and 375 ms. Consonant onsets (reading a) are -375 to -180 ms, vowel onsets 55 to 105 ms. Measured is the first reading (pre, row, projection i, every CV, groups a; onset reading a). What the answers changed. The rest baseline and projection (ii) are now readings; the readings added give the same outcome, not reproduced, as in the first run. After the first verification the bootstrap no longer pairs a token with its own copies, which changes only the s.e. of onset reading (a) (first reading's vowel onset 100 to 105 ms); every reading factor still gives not reproduced in all its readings.
deviations: The onset reading (a) takes the curve's value at -500 ms as its pre-epoch level, the earliest time of the epoch. The claims file says "pre-epoch level" without a time; this is the attempt's choice, and it decides only the onset, not the peaks on which the outcome rests.

outcomes.statement: Cluster separability and the correlation of the state-space with phonetic features are tightly linked over time for consonants and vowels in each subject (R2 0.42 to 0.98, all P < 1e-10).
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of Phonetic Representations, paragraph 2; Figure 5c, d
outcomes.quote: Across subjects, we found that cluster separability and the correlation between cortical state-space organization and phonetic features were tightly linked for both consonants and vowels in a time-dependent fashion (R 2 range = [0.42–0.98], P < 10 −10 for all)

statistics.test: linear regression R2 between time courses
statistics.n: 3 subjects x consonants and vowels, time points as samples

outcomes.notes: With phonetic-group clusters and the matching feature set (location for consonants, vowel for vowels), the six R2 lie within 0.38 to 1 with p < 1e-10 in 80 of 96 readings, are positive and significant with some below 0.38 in 15, and fail in 1 (R2 0.14 to 0.99). With the mean of the three feature sets, or with k-means clusters, the coupling fails in every reading. The claims file's own readings give different outcomes. What the answers changed. The rest baseline and projection (ii) are now readings; the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run. Two readings of the claims file decide the split, that of R and that of the clusters. With the mean of three feature sets all 120 readings fail, and with k-means clusters all 48 fail, the 24 with the matching feature set among them. Every level of the baseline, z-scoring, projection and CV set has both reproduced and not reproduced readings, so the split does not come from these details.

outcomes.statement: Consonant and vowel representations occupy distinct regions of the state-space; consonant-vowel distances are larger than consonant-consonant and vowel-vowel distances, and consonant-consonant distances are larger than vowel-vowel ones.
outcomes.source: Results, Dynamics of Phonetic Representations, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 13
outcomes.quote: We found that the distribution of distances comparing consonants and vowels was significantly greater than the consonant-consonant comparison or vowel-vowel comparison, and the consonant-consonant comparison was greater than the vowel-vowel comparison
outcomes.notes: With row z-scoring, and with time z-scoring and projection (ii), consonant-vowel distances exceed consonant-consonant ones, which exceed vowel-vowel ones, with corrected p < 1e-10; with time z-scoring and projection (i) the consonant-vowel distances are shorter than the consonant-consonant ones in every baseline and CV set. The pairs number 4677 (every CV) or 4567 (15+ CVs), not 4623, so no reading meets the criterion as written. The criterion defines only reproduced; a reading where all orderings hold and only the pair count differs is counted as partially reproduced (36 of 48), by the protocol's general definition of an effect that holds in part, and one where an ordering fails as not reproduced (12, all with time z-scoring and projection (i)). Read strictly, every reading is not reproduced; the outcome is kept blocked because the pair count is fixed by the dataset's syllables (data-composition), while whether the orderings hold depends on readings the paper does not fix. What the answers changed. The paper fixes neither z-scoring nor the CV set, and projection (ii), added as a reading, gives the orderings under both z-scorings; the outcome stays blocked as methods_underspecified, as in the first run.

outcomes.statement: The first three PCs are weighted toward tongue over lips, and toward lips over jaw and larynx, while jaw and larynx do not differ.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Figure 9a legend
outcomes.quote: the magnitude of the articulator weightings (log10(|(PCNi*Wij)|)) was significantly biased towards tongue over lips (P < 0.05) over jaw and larynx (P < 0.001 for each), while the difference between jaw and larynx was not significant (P > 0.2)

statistics.n: 266 electrodes across subjects for each PC

statistics.about: lips (in one reading, tongue and lips) against jaw and larynx
statistics.n: 266 electrodes across subjects for each PC
266 electrodes across subjects for each PC

outcomes.notes: Under all 288 readings the condition fails in all three PCs; tongue weights are not larger than lips weights. In the reading printed in full (268 vSMC electrodes, pre, every CV) lips minus tongue has a median paired difference of +0.03 in log10 (corrected p = 1), and jaw and larynx differ (corrected p = 5e-11). By Methods Eq. 6 the PC term cancels in paired comparisons of one electrode's articulators, so the three PCs give the same tests. What the answers changed. The rest baseline is now a reading (96 readings added); the input projected does not enter this test. The outcome is not reproduced, as in the first run. Electrodes without a window T_A for an articulator are dropped, none in 168 readings, up to 83 in the others (GP31 lacks a tongue window in some timing readings), leaving 32 to 268 electrodes; every reading fails either way.
deviations: Uses the GLM weights of fig2a-lips-dorsal, which is blocked for its spatial judgement only.

findings.statement: No electrode has a position relative to the central sulcus or the Sylvian fissure, the frame of the paper's spatial analyses. EC2 and GP31 have x, y, z coordinates with no unit or coordinate frame described; GP33 and EC9 have none. No electrode is labelled as on the guenon. Seven spatial findings of the paper cannot be tested.

The microphone recordings were removed (dandiset description), so the acoustic onset, peak and offset of each syllable used by the paper cannot be computed; only hand-marked start, C-V transition and stop times are given.

Subjects GP31 and GP33 do not carry the paper's names (EC31, EC33), and nothing links them. GP31's coordinates fit a left hemisphere, as the paper's EC31; GP33 has no coordinates, so the right hemisphere of EC33 cannot be checked. The subject fields hold only species and id. The electrode group of EC2 and GP31 is `L256Grid electrodes`; that of GP33 is `auto_group`, with location `location`, so no field gives GP33's hemisphere.
The dandiset holds a fourth subject, EC9 (7 blocks, 1653 trials), that is not in the paper. It has extra syllables (/ch/, /dh/, /j/, /sk/), labels on 79 of 256 electrodes and no coordinates.

Renditions per syllable range from 2 to 107 (GP31 /thi/ 2, EC2 /thi/ 10, GP31 up to 107) against the paper's 15 to 100, and GP31 lacks /tha/ and /thu/. The three subjects have 169 distinct syllables against the paper's 168 (57 + 57 + 54). The dandiset does not say which trials or syllables the paper used.

The raw ElectricalSeries gives unit volt with a conversion factor of 0.001, but the stored values have an SD of a few 1e-5, which is a usual ECoG amplitude if read as volts and tens of nanovolts with the factor; the data are consistent with values already in volts.
Two syllable labels are misspelt (`she` for `shee` in EC2 and EC9, `ha` for `haa` in GP33 and EC9). Electrode ids start at 0 in EC2 and GP31 and at 1 in GP33 and EC9.

The archive summary counts four subjects and 31 files; bad-channel flags differ between blocks of one subject (EC2 has none in two blocks and up to 10 in others), and 162 of 9370 analysed trials overlap intervals marked as ECoG artifacts (38 in GP31 block 63, whose rest period has a high-gamma SD of 0.3 times the block's). One file (EC2 block 1) holds a power spectrum of the 256 channels in a processing module; no other file has one.

attempts.label: DANDI:000023
attempts.entry_title: Human supragranular glutamatergic neurons by Patch-seq (Berg et al. 2020)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Berg, Sorensen, Ting, Miller et al. (2020) on dandiset 000023, which holds the whole-cell recordings of 318 human L2/3 neurons from 56 neurosurgical donors. The 18 electrophysiological features are computed from the recordings with IPFX and linked to the paper's per-cell table of t-types and depths from its code, to test the cohort counts, the depth of each t-type, the differences between the homologous and deep L3 t-types, the depth dependence within FREM3, the classifier, the cross-species comparison and the pathology comparison. Claims on the code's morphology, pathology and NeuN section data are tested apart.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Berg et al. (2020) from dandiset 000023

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's recordings can be matched to the paper's per-cell table (t-type and depth) by specimen ID, and the 18 features computed from them agree with the paper's feature table.
outcomes.source: Methods, Electrophysiology feature analysis; code data/human_IVSCC_excitatory_L23_consolidated_0131.csv and data/human_mouse_ephys_all_0127.csv at commit 3daf9f0
outcomes.notes: No file carries a SpecimenID. The answer to the question (questions/000023.yaml) found that the paper names no identifier and allows both readings, and the criterion names them and asks for both to be run and reported; the outcome is under M2, and under M1 it would be not reproduced. M1, a SpecimenID stored in the files, matches 0 files. M2, the SpecimenID recovered from the file as the next SpecimenID of the same donor above the file's session id (offsets 13 to 685, the next candidate at least 28 further), gives 318 distinct cells of the 385-cell table, including all 283 cells with features in the code. With the Methods' sweep QC, 261 of these have features on both sides; the median relative difference from the code's table is 0 for all 18 features, 128 cells agree on every shared feature and 248 on at least 80% of them, and a match on the features alone, within donor, picks the M2 cell for 261 of 261 files. With IPFX's sweep QC alone the agreement is closer (145 cells identical on every shared feature; 1 of the code's cells with no features here, against 22), and the match on features alone picks the M2 cell for 282 of 282 files, 21 of 21 among those with no features under the Methods' sweep QC; the remaining cell of the 283 (H18.03.322.11.11.01.02) gives features under neither QC, and its sample date matches. The 35 cells with no features in the code cannot be checked by features; for all 35 the date in the cell's sample_id equals the file's local recording date (279 of the 283 checked cells too, the other 4 started after midnight, the day after the sample's date), and in each of 71 rig-days with two or more files (253 files, 27 of the 35) tube numbers rise with recording time without exception. These checks support the 35 links without proving them, as the date separates only cells recorded on different days. The donor table agrees on sex for 55 of 56 donors and on age within a year for 55 of 56. The files hold no t-type or depth, so every label comes from the code's table. Every claim that needs a label uses M2 and says so.
deviations: The SpecimenID of each file was recovered from its session id and donor, not read from the file; the code's per-cell features confirm the match for 261 of the 283 cells that have them under the Methods' sweep QC and for 282 under IPFX's sweep QC alone, and the sample dates and tube order support it for the 35 cells without features in the code.
Features computed with IPFX 2.1.2 (the paper gives no version), read from its output as the code's feature names imply (patchseq_l23.FEATURE_SOURCES); the code does not hold that step.

The sweep QC is the Methods'. IPFX 2.1.2 applies only the noise limits to sweeps, so the Methods' bias current (0 +/- 100 pA) and bridge balance (below 20 MOhm and 15% of input resistance) limits were added, with the input resistance of IPFX's cell QC for the 15% limit, which the Methods do not fix (asked in questions/000023.yaml). Long squares without a bias current value were kept.

outcomes.statement: 385 Patch-seq neurons passing transcriptomic QC mapped to the five supragranular glutamatergic t-types, and 283 of them had recordings complete enough to compute electrophysiological features.
outcomes.source: Results, Patch-seq pipeline for human neurosurgical tissue analysis, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: A total of 385 neurons that passed transcriptomic data QC mapped with higher confidence to the five supragranular human glutamatergic t-types than to any other neuron type. ... Most neurons (283) also had sufficiently complete recordings to calculate electrophysiological features.
outcomes.notes: 318 cells of the code's 385-cell table have a recording in the dandiset. Cells giving features are 280 under reading (a), 241 under (b) and 280 under (c), none 283; with IPFX's sweep QC alone they are 307, 256 and 307. The code's own table has features for exactly 283 human cells, all with a file here; 22 of them give no features here under the Methods' sweep QC, against 1 under IPFX's sweep QC alone (IPFX raises a ValueError, `ydata` must not be empty), and 19 cells give features here but have none in the code (2 of them fail IPFX cell QC). M2 gives every file a cell of the table, so no other cell can be found among the files. Uses reading M2 of features-and-labels-link; under M1 no cell is linked and the claim could not be tested.
deviations: The cells with features are those for which IPFX 2.1.2 gives features after the Methods' sweep QC; the paper's rule for which recordings were complete enough is not given.

outcomes.statement: The neurons came from neurosurgical specimens of 90 tissue donors.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: across human neurosurgical specimens from 90 different tissue donors
outcomes.notes: Both readings give 56 donors. The code's cell table has 82 donors (54 among its 283 cells with features) and its pathology table 89 distinct donors in 90 rows, 52 of which have a file here. Reading (b) uses reading M2 of features-and-labels-link; under M1 no cell is linked and only reading (a) could be tested.

outcomes.statement: The electrophysiology figures show 66 LTK, 25 GLP2R and 136 FREM3 neurons, and 21 deep FREM3, 17 CARM1P1 and 37 COL22A1 neurons.
outcomes.source: Figure 4a legend; Figure 6b legend
outcomes.quote: Bottom panels compare the intrinsic electrophysiological responses for 66 LTK, 25 GLP2R and 136 FREM3 neurons. ... Electrophysiological description of the intrinsic electrophysiology responses of 21 deep FREM3, 17 CARM1P1 and 37 COL22A1 neurons.
outcomes.notes: Measured values are reading (a). At most one of six counts matches under any reading; readings (a) and (c) give 71 LTK, 24 GLP2R, 136 FREM3, 24 deep FREM3, 16 CARM1P1 and 33 COL22A1 (FREM3 matches), reading (b) 62, 23, 112, 16, 12 and 32 (none). The code's 283 cells give 67, 25, 143, 25, 17 and 31 (two), and IPFX's sweep QC alone, reading (a), 75, 25, 156, 28, 18 and 33 (one). 13 FREM3 cells have no depth. Uses reading M2 of features-and-labels-link; under M1 no cell is linked and the claim could not be tested.

outcomes.statement: LTK neurons lie mainly in L2 and at the L2/L3 border, GLP2R mainly in upper L3, FREM3 span L2 and L3 and continue into L4, and CARM1P1 and COL22A1 lie almost entirely in deep L3 and along the L3/L4 border.
outcomes.source: Results, High-confidence Patch-seq neuron t-type mapping, paragraph 4; Figure 3d
outcomes.quote: Human LTK neurons were found primarily in L2 and in the border region of L2 and L3. GLP2R neurons were found primarily in upper L3, with some neurons found in L2. FREM3 neurons spanned L2 and L3, continuing into L4, consistent with their heterogeneous gene expression profile. CARM1P1 and COL22A1 were found almost entirely in deep L3 and along the L3/L4 border.
outcomes.notes: Over every cell of the code's table with a depth, as the criterion says, the LTK median (0.086) is below the GLP2R median (0.425), which is below 0.575; FREM3 has cells shallower than the LTK median; all 18 CARM1P1 and 96.7% of 30 COL22A1 cells are deeper than 0.575, so both readings of "almost entirely" hold. No FREM3 cell is deeper than 1 (deepest 0.992), so FREM3 does not continue into L4. The 288 cells with a recording here and a depth give the same (LTK median 0.082, all 29 COL22A1 deeper than 0.575). The judged cell set does not use the link; the variant uses reading M2.

outcomes.statement: Among the three human homologous t-types (LTK, GLP2R, FREM3), 3 of 18 electrophysiological features explain more than 10% of variance by t-type (input resistance, f-I slope and rheobase), at FDR below 1e-5, with a maximum R2 of 0.16.

findings.statement: The files carry no SpecimenID, the identifier by which the paper's code and tables name cells. Each file can be linked only by its donor and its ephys session id, which lies 13 to 685 below the cell's SpecimenID. The code's per-cell features confirm the link for 261 of the 283 cells that have them under the Methods' sweep QC and for 282 under IPFX's sweep QC alone (one gives no features under either); for the 35 cells without features in the code, the sample dates and tube order in the code's sample_id are consistent with it.

The files carry no t-type, soma depth, brain region or medical condition, on which every finding of the paper rests; they must be taken from the paper's code. session_description and the filtering field read PLACEHOLDER, and the archive summary gives the variable measured as ProcessingModule and the technique as "analytical technique".

The dandiset holds 318 of the 385 cells of the paper's table, including all 283 cells with electrophysiological features in the paper's code; the other 67 are absent. Of the 35 cells without features in the code, 19 give features here under the Methods' sweep QC (2 of them fail cell QC) and 25 under IPFX's sweep QC alone, and which recordings were judged too incomplete, or why, is not said.
Donor H18.03.318 is female in the files and male in the paper's donor table and cell table; donor H18.06.005 is 56 years old in the files (P20440.0D) and 57 in both tables.

The code's feature table measures adaptation as the mean over all spiking long squares, initial firing rate on the hero sweep (about 50 pA above rheobase) and tau from long squares, where the Methods describe adaptation at about 50 pA above rheobase, initial rate at rheobase and tau from short pulses. The features recomputed here match the code's table, not the Methods.

The code's feature table is consistent with sweep QC on noise alone, as IPFX applies it, not with the Methods' sweep QC. With the Methods' bias current and bridge balance limits (input resistance from IPFX's cell QC for the 15% limit), 22 of its 283 cells have no features here, against 1 with IPFX's sweep QC alone, and fewer features equal the table's. 29 of its 283 cells fail the cell QC as IPFX computes it (seal, access resistance, electrode offset).

Code7_cortical_depth_code_mouse.r as committed does not give the values its comments print. It names the four mouse boundary lines L2, L4, L5 and L6 and sets 100 um = 330 pixels for all three mouse sections, which gives mouse L2/3 thicknesses of 32, 133 and 90 um (printed 281, 223 and 257), a density of 350 thousand per mm3 (printed 165) and puts every mouse soma below the lower L2/3 line. Reading the lines as L1 to L4, as Code6 reads the human ones, with case_set_1 at 100 um = 165 pixels, the scale its own comment gives, reproduces its printed thicknesses, L2 fractions, densities (165 +/- 24.9 and 27.7 +/- 4.46), pooled area quantiles and six largest areas, and its two ratios of mean soma area; its two ratios of SD need the repeated rows of the next finding.

Code6_cortical_depth_code_human.r never sets q9 to NULL (Code7 does, for each section), and run on its own stops at q9. When q9 is present, it grows from section to section, and cbind repeats each human section's 20 bins once per 20 values of q9, so the human bin table Code7 averages counts the five sections unequally. Counting each section once gives SD ratios of 2.33 (L2) and 3.94 (deep L3), against the 2.4 and 4.0 Code7 prints; with the repeated rows and one or two sections' worth of q9 at the start, the port gives all four printed ratios.

The code's gene-depth table (frem_genes_depth.csv) is from the revision (4417 genes at FDR below 0.05), not the preprint (790), and the Patch-seq transcriptomes behind either are not in the repository.

Spike times computed here with IPFX equal the spike times stored in each file's processing/spikes for the rheobase sweep of all 280 cells with features, and no spike occurs in the second before any long-square step, so the stored spikes, responses and stimuli share one clock.

attempts.entry_title: SpikeInterface spike sorter comparison (Buccino et al. 2020)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Buccino, Hurwitz, Garcia, Magland, Siegle, Hurwitz and Hennig (2020) on dandiset 000034, which holds the mouse, simulated, rat and retina recordings the paper sorts and two manual curations of its Kilosort2 output. It checks that the recordings are as described, that the curated and ground-truth spike times share the recordings' clocks, and compares the two curations. The findings about sorter outputs are blocked, as three of the six sorters need MATLAB and a GPU, which the runner lacks.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds no output of the six spike sorters the paper compares, including the Kilosort2 run that the two experts curated. Every comparison of sorters in the paper, and the comparison of the curations with Kilosort2, can be repeated only by running the sorters again, three of them in MATLAB, and a new Kilosort2 run will not give the units the curators worked on.

The two curated files hold a Units table of ids and spike times only (description 'Autogenerated by NWBFile'), with no sampling rate, no unit labels, no curator name and no link to the Kilosort2 clusters they were curated from; which file is curator 1 and which curator 2 is not stated (the files differ only by session time, 15:55:42 and 15:55:43). Their spike times fall on whole frames at 30 kHz and match the mouse recording's clock.

The retina recording is stored as unsigned 16-bit values centred near 2048 and reaching 4096, consistent with raw counts of a 12-bit converter, while the file states a conversion of 1e-6 V per unit and no offset, which would put every channel near +2 mV. The converter's gain and offset are not in the file.

The mouse 412804 recording stores int16 values with a conversion of 1e-6 V and no gain or channel_conversion per channel. Read that way its band-passed noise SD is about 50 uV and the median curated trough about 455 uV, several times usual Neuropixels levels; at the Neuropixels 1.0 gain of about 0.195 uV per bit the noise would be about 10 uV. The values are consistent with raw counts given a conversion that treats them as microvolts; the file holds nothing to show which.

The electrode tables give location 'unknown' and filtering 'none' for every channel and placeholder group descriptions; the mouse recording has 248 channels where the paper says 246 are active, without marking which; the simulated file does not say which ground-truth cells are excitatory or inhibitory or what noise was added; the archive's species summary lists only house mouse though one recording is from a rat (its file gives 'rattus rattus').

Every raw series is stored in chunks of one channel by 7911 to 26368 frames, so reading a stretch of all channels through h5py fetches one chunk per channel. Streamed from the archive at 0.087 to 0.155 s per chunk in this run, reading a whole recording that way would take 6.2 to 16.9 h; one bulk ranged read of a file ran at 72 MB/s, 1.4 to 6.5 min per recording. These times vary between runs.
The paper gives 226 of 351 curated units as 64.2%; 226/351 is 64.39%.

attempts.label: DANDI:000035
attempts.paper_title: Phenotypic variation of transcriptomic cell types in mouse motor cortex
attempts.entry_title: Patch-seq neurons of mouse motor cortex at physiological temperature (Scala, Kobak et al. 2021)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Scala, Kobak et al. (2021) that can be tested on dandiset 000035, which holds the paper's follow-up recordings at 34 degrees C (185 neurons, mostly layer 5 Sst and excitatory cells). It extracts the paper's 17 electrophysiological features from the traces, checks the cohort and the stimulus against the Methods, tests whether IT and ET neurons overlap electrophysiologically, and compares Sst t-types between temperatures using the paper's published room-temperature features. The findings on the main room-temperature data set are in dandiset 000008 and are not tested here.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Scala, Kobak et al. (2021) from dandiset 000035

outcomes.statement: After quality control, 1,227 Patch-seq neurons from mouse primary motor cortex were assigned to transcriptomic types, covering 77 of the 90 neuronal t-types of the reference taxonomy.
outcomes.source: Results, "Patch-seq of mouse primary motor cortex", paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 1a
outcomes.quote: leaving 1,227 neurons for further analysis ... The resulting data set covered 77 out of the 90 neuronal t-types (Fig. 1a)
outcomes.notes: The finding rests on the 1,329 cells of the main data set and their sequencing. The dandiset holds only the 185 cells of the follow-up at 34 degrees, with their t-type labels but no gene counts. The main data set's recordings are in dandiset 000008, its sequencing data at NeMO (dat-kq04hua) and GEO (GSE163764), and its processed tables in the paper's repository.

outcomes.statement: A sparse reduced-rank regression of 17 electrophysiological features on gene expression, using 25 genes and a rank-5 latent space, reached a cross-validated R2 of 0.38, with cross-validated correlations of 0.90, 0.74 and 0.67 between the first three pairs of projections.
outcomes.source: Results, "Distinct phenotypes of major families", paragraph 1; Figure 2
outcomes.quote: The selected model used 25 genes with a 5-dimensional latent space and achieved a cross-validated R2 of 0.38 ... The cross-validated correlations between the first three pairs of projections were 0.90, 0.74, and 0.67, respectively.
outcomes.notes: Needs gene expression and features of the main data set. The dandiset holds no gene counts and none of the main data set's cells; they are in dandiset 000008 and at NeMO and GEO.

outcomes.statement: A reduced-rank regression restricted to ion channel genes did not perform much worse than the full model, with a cross-validated R2 of 0.33 and correlations of 0.86, 0.71 and 0.56.
outcomes.source: Results, "Distinct phenotypes of major families", paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 5e-f
outcomes.quote: A reduced-rank regression model restricted to using only ion channel genes (Extended Data Fig. 5) did not perform much worse than the full model (cross-validated R2 = 0.33 and correlations 0.86, 0.71, and 0.56, respectively
outcomes.notes: As fig2-rrr-prediction.

outcomes.statement: In a k-nearest-neighbour classification of cells into seven transcriptomic families from electrophysiological features, the confusion matrix was mostly diagonal, with only the ET and IT subclasses strongly overlapping.
outcomes.source: Results, "Distinct phenotypes of major families", paragraph 3; Figure 3a, d
outcomes.quote: We quantified this separation using a confusion matrix for k-nearest neighbours (kNN) classification of cells into families: it was mostly diagonal, with only the ET and IT subclasses strongly overlapping (Fig. 3d).
outcomes.notes: Needs the main data set's cells, which are in dandiset 000008. The same classifier was run on the 34 degree cells for ed6-it-et-overlap, where Lamp5, Vip and CT cells are absent.

outcomes.statement: Families were less separable by morphology than by electrophysiology among inhibitory neurons, and most separable when electrophysiological and morphological features were combined.
outcomes.source: Results, "Distinct phenotypes of major families", paragraph 4; Figure 3b-d
outcomes.quote: The separability between inhibitory families was weaker than with electrophysiological features (Fig. 3d). The between-family separability was strongest when we had combined electrophysiological and morphological features into a joint representation (Fig. 3c, d)
outcomes.notes: Needs morphological reconstructions, which are not in the dandiset (none were recovered in the 34 degree experiments). They are in the Brain Image Library, with features in the paper's repository.

outcomes.statement: Across 200 pairs of t-types from the same family, the transcriptomic distance and the electrophysiological distance between t-types were correlated with r = 0.60.
outcomes.source: Results, "Continuous phenotypic variation", paragraph 2; Figure 4c
outcomes.quote: Pooling the pairs across all families, we found that these two distance measures were correlated, with r = 0.60 (Fig. 4c, n = 200 pairs
outcomes.notes: Needs the main data set's cells (dandiset 000008) and the reference 10x expression data.

outcomes.statement: Among IT t-types, transcriptomic distances were strongly correlated with differences in average soma depth, r = 0.70.
outcomes.source: Results, "Continuous phenotypic variation", paragraph 3; Figure 4d
outcomes.quote: Transcriptomic distances between t-types were strongly correlated with the average soma depth differences (r = 0.70; Fig. 4d).
outcomes.notes: Needs the main data set's IT cells (their soma depths are in the paper's repository and dandiset 000008) and the reference 10x expression data.

outcomes.statement: Most t-types were classified into their own family from electrophysiology, but some, such as Sst Pvalb Calb2, Lamp5 Egln3_1 and Vip Mybpc1, were often classified into another family.
outcomes.source: Results, "Variability in individual t-types", paragraph 1; Figure 5a
outcomes.quote: Most t-types could be unambiguously placed into the correct family (Fig. 5a), but some t-types were in between two families ... Vip Mybpc1 neurons often had Sst-like firing.
outcomes.notes: Needs the main data set's cells, in dandiset 000008. The t-types named in the claim are not among the 34 degree cells except Sst Pvalb Calb2.

outcomes.statement: Many t-types had a normalized total variance of electrophysiological features well above that of k-means clusters, while some, such as Pvalb Vipr2_2, appeared homogeneous.
outcomes.source: Results, "Variability in individual t-types", paragraph 3; Figure 5b
outcomes.quote: We found that many t-types had total variance substantially above the variances of the k-means clusters (Fig. 5b) ... some of them, such as Pvalb Vipr2_2 (chandelier cells), appeared morpho-electrically homogeneous.
outcomes.notes: Needs the main data set's cells, in dandiset 000008.

outcomes.statement: At physiological temperature, 185 neurons were sequenced from 8 adult mice (7 Sst-Cre/Ai9 and 1 Pvalb-Cre/Ai9); 177 got a t-type (110 Sst, 43 IT, 12 ET, 10 Pvalb, 2 NP); 175 were in layer 5; electrophysiological features were extracted for 184.
outcomes.source: Methods, "Experiments at physiological temperature", paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: We sequenced in total 185 neurons, obtained from 8 adult mice (7 Sst-Cre/Ai9 and 1 Pvalb-Cre/Ai9), of which 177 neurons passed the transcriptomic quality control and got a t-type assignment ... One hundred and ten cells mapped to the Sst subclass, 43 to IT, 12 to ET, 10 to Pvalb, and 2 to NP.
outcomes.notes: Every count matches the Methods. All 17 features are defined for 185 cells against 184 in the paper, within the 10% tolerance. Families are read from the t-type names in the files; the 12 ET cells are named L5 PT_1 to L5 PT_4 there.
deviations: The number of cells with features comes from the re-implemented extraction here; the paper's table has no row for 20200406_sample_4.

outcomes.statement: Cells at physiological temperature were stimulated with the same paradigm as the main data set, 600 ms current pulses from -200 pA upwards in 20 pA steps up to 1,380 pA, sometimes stopped earlier.
outcomes.source: Methods, "Patch-seq recording procedures", paragraph 4, and "Experiments at physiological temperature", paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Each neuron was injected with 600-ms-long current pulses starting from −200 pA and up to 1,380 pA with 20-pA increment steps (in some cases stimulation was stopped before reaching 1,380 pA) ... Intrinsic electrophysiological recordings were obtained using the same stimulation paradigm as described above.
outcomes.notes: In all 185 cells every step lasts 600 ms and consecutive steps differ by 20 pA; all 14,054 sweeps with a nonzero step start at 0.1 s and end at 0.7 s, and 139 cells end at 1,380 pA. 174 of 185 (94.1%) conform to the whole ladder. Nine cells of mouse_UEQOU end at 1,400 to 1,580 pA, and two cells of other mice start at -180 pA and -100 pA and end above 1,380 pA. The intervals of 1.3 or 1.4 s between pulses cannot be checked because every series has an undefined starting time.

outcomes.statement: Follow-up experiments at 34 degrees C confirmed the electrophysiological overlap between IT and ET neurons seen at room temperature.
outcomes.source: Results, "Distinct phenotypes of major families", paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 6a-g
outcomes.quote: We confirmed the electrophysiological overlap between IT and ET neurons in follow-up experiments at 34 °C (Extended Data Fig. 6).
outcomes.notes: With the paper's kNN classifier (k = 10, leave-one-out, 17-feature representation, all 185 cells), 58.3% of ET cells (7 of 12) are classified as IT and no IT cell as ET; Sst cells are classified as Sst 100% of the time and Pvalb cells 60%. ET cells go to IT in both mice with ET cells (1 of 3 and 6 of 9). The overlap is one-sided and partly reflects that IT cells are 78% of IT and ET cells. With IT subsampled to 12 cells and an odd k (no ties), 10.5% (k = 9) and 12.4% (k = 11) of ET cells go to IT and 33.4% and 36.5% of IT cells to ET; a class-balanced logistic regression separates layer 5 IT from ET with a balanced accuracy of 0.83 against a shuffled-label null of 0.50 (p = 0.005). The result on layer 5 cells alone, and without 20200406_sample_4 (the paper's 184 cells), is the same as on all cells (58.3% and 0%). All ET cells come from two mice. Within mouse_UEQOU alone (10 IT, 9 ET), the kNN classifies 33.3% of ET cells as IT and 20.0% of IT cells as ET, and the logistic regression reaches 0.78 (p = 0.025). The criterion does not require a test within mouse.
deviations: The paper shows the 34 degree comparison as feature distributions and two-feature scatter plots (Extended Data Fig. 6a-g); it reports no classifier at 34 degrees. The test applies the room-temperature classifier of Fig. 3d to the 34 degree cells, with four families present instead of seven.
Features are computed by the re-implementation here; link-features shows they agree with the paper's.
The main test uses all 185 cells, including 20200406_sample_4 (layer 5 IT), which the paper leaves out; the 184-cell result is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: At 34 degrees C, the AP threshold showed a prominent difference between layer 5 IT and ET neurons.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 6e and its legend
outcomes.quote: The last panel additionally shows one feature that showed prominent difference at 34 °C.
outcomes.notes: Layer 5 IT median -27.0 mV (43 cells) against ET -33.1 mV (12 cells), Mann-Whitney p = 0.00035, area under the curve 0.84; second of 17 features after input resistance (p = 0.0001). Without 20200406_sample_4, p = 0.00026 (42 IT cells). Same sign in both mice with both subclasses, but within mouse_UEQOU alone the gap is smaller and not significant (-29.3 against -31.8 mV, area under the curve 0.73, p = 0.094, 10 IT and 9 ET cells). All ET cells come from two mice, so a difference between mice may contribute; the criterion does not require a test within mouse. The ranking of the first two features is the one the paper's code prints for 34 degrees.
deviations: The ranking covers the 17 features used here, not all 29 the paper's code ranks.
The main test uses all 185 cells, including 20200406_sample_4, which the paper leaves out; the 184-cell result is shown as a variant.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's recordings are the cells of the paper's published table of the 34 degree cohort, with the same t-type, layer and soma depth.
outcomes.source: Data availability; mini-atlas data/m1_patchseq_phys_temp_meta_data.csv
outcomes.quote: All preprocessed data (gene counts, electrophysiological and morphological features) and meta data are available at https://github.com/berenslab/mini-atlas ... https://dandiarchive.org/dandiset/000035 (physiological temperature) in NWB format.
outcomes.notes: All 185 files match a row of the paper's table by cell id and no row lacks a file. Family, layer, soma depth and mouse agree for every cell; the files' inferred layer equals the layer the paper's code computes from soma depth and cortical thickness. The t-type name agrees for 93.5% of cells, below the criterion's 95%, only because the 12 ET cells are named L5 PT_1 to L5 PT_4 in the files and L5 ET_1 to L5 ET_4 in the table, one to one; with that renaming the agreement is 100%. The partial outcome reflects the names, not a mismatch of cells. The verifier of round 1 would call this reproduced; the outcome is kept because the criterion, written before the analysis, compares t-type names.
deviations: The criterion did not anticipate renamed t-types and was applied as written, to the names.

outcomes.statement: The electrophysiological features computed here from the dandiset's traces agree with the paper's published features for the same cells.
outcomes.source: Methods, "Extraction of electrophysiological features", paragraphs 1 and 12; mini-atlas data/m1_patchseq_phys_temp_ephys_features.csv
outcomes.quote: Twenty-nine electrophysiological properties of the neurons were automatically extracted based on the raw membrane voltage traces ... For all statistical analysis we used 17 features out of the extracted 29
outcomes.notes: 184 of the 185 cells are in the paper's feature table. The Spearman correlation between the features computed here and the published ones is at least 0.9 for 16 of 17 features and 0.877 for the lowest, the AP coefficient of variation. The median absolute difference is zero to three decimals for all features but the AHP (0.011 mV). By mouse, 0.895 (mouse_UEQOU) to 0.995 of values are within 10% of the paper's. The maximum number of APs differs between the Methods' and the code's definitions for 3 cells.
deviations: The extraction is a re-implementation of the paper's methods and code (scala34.py), not the paper's code, which is under the Allen Institute's license.
The maximum number of APs follows the Methods (sweeps with spikes in the 100 ms before or the 200 ms after the step are excluded before taking the maximum); the code's version is shown.

outcomes.statement: For layer 5 Sst t-types, AP amplitude and AP width changed the most between room temperature and 34 degrees C, but the relative differences between t-types stayed roughly the same; AHP, input resistance, rebound and sag ratio changed little, and the relative differences between t-types stayed the same.
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 6h and its legend
outcomes.quote: AP amplitude and AP width changed the most between conditions, but the relative differences between t-types stayed roughly the same. The other four shown features did not change much, and the relative differences between t-types stayed the same.
outcomes.notes: 147 layer 5 Sst cells at 25 degrees (published features) and 101 at 34 degrees (computed here); seven t-types have at least 5 cells in both. Shifts in units of the 25 degree SD are AP width -1.78, AP amplitude -1.66, input resistance -0.61, rebound -0.33, AHP -0.25 and sag ratio -0.02, so AP width and amplitude change most. Spearman correlations of t-type medians between temperatures are 0.75 (AP amplitude), 0.88 (AP width), 0.93 (AHP, input resistance, rebound) and 0.96 (sag ratio), median 0.93. The same holds with the paper's published 34 degree features and with t-type means. In each of the 7 mice with such cells, the 34 degree medians of AP amplitude and width lie below the room-temperature medians.
deviations: The room-temperature side uses the paper's published features of dandiset 000008's cells, not features recomputed from that dandiset.
The legend says the relative differences "stayed roughly the same"; the criterion turns this into Spearman correlations of t-type medians and a shift measured in standard deviations.

outcomes.statement: At physiological temperature, as at room temperature, morpho-electric properties of layer 5 Sst neurons varied continuously across the transcriptomic landscape, and the electrophysiological distance between Sst t-types correlated with their transcriptomic distance.
outcomes.source: Results, "Continuous phenotypic variation", paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 6i
outcomes.quote: Here we also found that morpho-electric properties varied continuously across the transcriptomic landscape ... We confirmed this effect in follow-up experiments at physiological temperature (Extended Data Fig. 6).
outcomes.notes: The transcriptomic distance between Sst t-types needs the average expression of each t-type in the single-cell 10x v2 reference data (Yao et al. 2021). The paper's code reads it from reduced-allen-data.zip on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.5118962), member 10X_cells_v2_AIBS.pickle. The notebook reads the archive's directory (87.9 MB compressed, 517.0 MB uncompressed) and times a 1 MB range request. In the delivered run the rate was 62 kB/s, about 24 minutes for the member. The rate varies between runs; in the earlier runs of this attempt (not in the delivered notebook) it was 27, 114, 44, 149 and 58 kB/s, about 55, 13, 33, 10 and 25 minutes. A run that fetched the member would have exceeded the 30 minute limit in two of these six runs and fitted in the others, so the claim was not tested. The reference is public, and the verifier of round 2 holds that the claim is testable; the block reflects this attempt's choice not to make the run depend on Zenodo's rate. Proposed change for another round, fetch the member in the run, write a criterion for the claim (it has none), and test it. The original reference data at NeMO are much larger. The electrophysiological half is computed from the dandiset as in the paper's code (cell 19 of physiological-temperature.ipynb), for 9 layer 5 Sst t-types with at least 5 cells (Sst Chodl left out), as the paper's code prints, with distances between their mean standardized features of 1.54 to 5.24. It tests nothing without the transcriptomic half. A proxy transcriptomic distance from the paper's own 34 degree Patch-seq counts was not computed, as it differs from the paper's method. The paper reports the correlation and its p-value only inside the figure.

findings.statement: Every voltage series states the unit volts and every stimulus series amperes, with a conversion of 1, but the values are in millivolts (-150 to 67) and picoamperes (-200 to 1,580).

Every series has an undefined (NaN) starting time, so the timing of sweeps relative to each other is not recorded. Within a sweep the response and the stimulus share a clock (onset at 0.1 s, offset at 0.7 s).

The t-type of the 12 ET cells is stored under the older names L5 PT_1 to L5 PT_4, which differ from the paper's and its tables' L5 ET_1 to L5 ET_4; no mapping is given. All other t-type names match the paper's table.
The dandiset's description repeats the main data set's "over 1300 neurons"; the dandiset holds 185 neurons of the follow-up at 34 degrees.

In the published version the contributor list has a placeholder "Last, First" with Zizhen Yao's ORCID, the brain region is typed as a disorder, and the assets summary gives no approach or measurement technique. The unpublished draft corrects these.
Eleven cells were stimulated beyond the 1,380 pA the Methods give (up to 1,580 pA), and two of them started at -180 pA and -100 pA, not -200 pA. Nine of the eleven are from one mouse (mouse_UEQOU).

The paper's code takes the maximum number of APs before excluding sweeps with spikes outside the step, and looks for those spikes over the whole trace before and after the step; the Methods exclude such sweeps first and look 100 ms before and 200 ms after. The two definitions differ for 3 of the 185 cells.

The Methods build the electrophysiological representation from 17 principal components of 17 features and later call it "the 16-dimensional electrophysiological representation"; the paper's code uses all 17.

The legend of Extended Data Fig. 6j describes it as "the same analysis as in (c)", but in the paper's code panel j is the 34 degree version of panel i (the Sst overlay and the transcriptomic-distance correlation), not of panel c.
