attempts.paper_title: Parkinson’s Disease-vulnerable and -resilient dopamine neurons display opposite responses to excitatory input
attempts.entry_title: Responses of SNr GABA and SNc dopamine neuron subtypes to STN and PPN input (Hadjas et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the mouse fiber photometry findings of Hadjas et al. (2025) on dandiset 001528, which holds recordings from 120 mice during optogenetic stimulation of STN or PPN inputs to the substantia nigra. It compares responses of SNr GABA neurons, SNc pan-DA neurons, striatal dopamine release in TS and DLS, DA terminals, and Vglut2+ and Anxa1+ DA neurons across train durations and frequencies, using the lab's dF/F stored in the files. The human tissue counts of Figure 1 are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Hadjas et al. (2025) from dandiset 001528

outcomes.statement: The number of mice per experimental group is as given in the figure legends; SNr GABA neurons STN 7 and PPN 8 (Figure 2); SNc pan-DA neurons STN 11 and PPN 9 (Figure 3); GRAB-DA in TS and DLS, STN 6 and 7, PPN 9 and 9 (Figure 4); DA terminals in TS and DLS with STN stimulation, 9 and 9 (Figure S3); Vglut2+ DA neurons STN 10 and PPN 10, Anxa1+ terminals in DLS STN 8 and PPN 10 (Figure 5); Anxa1+ cell bodies in SNc STN 5 and PPN 4 (Figure S4).
outcomes.source: Legends of Figures 2 to 5, S3 and S4
outcomes.inferred: Counts gathered from the legends of Figures 2 to 5, S3 and S4; no single sentence states them.
outcomes.notes: 10 of 16 counts match. SNr GABA, pan-DA and GRAB-DA groups match exactly, as do DA terminals in TS and Vglut2 with PPN. DA terminals in DLS have 8 mice (paper 9) and Vglut2 with STN 9 (paper 10). The Anxa1 groups have DLS recordings for 5 (STN) and 4 (PPN) mice against the paper's 8 and 10, and SNc recordings for 8 and 10 against 5 and 4. All four Anxa1 counts would match if the nine recordings without a site suffix were DLS recordings; their signals resemble the SNc recordings, and the paper's cell-body statistics are matched by the dual mice's SNc recordings alone, so the DLS recordings of those nine mice appear to be missing. For Vglut2 STN the paper's own Wilcoxon statistics fit 9 mice (W = 41, 43, -5 give exact p = 0.0117, 0.0078, 0.82 with n = 9, the paper's values, and 0.037, 0.027, 0.85 with n = 10), so the legend's 10 is likely an error; counted that way 11 of 16 match, still below 12.
deviations: Counted from the durations protocol; the frequencies protocol gives the same counts.

outcomes.statement: Optogenetic stimulation of STN or PPN inputs increases SNr GABA neuron activity (paired t-test on the 1 s train, STN t = 3.8, p = 0.008; PPN t = 9.2, p < 0.0001).
outcomes.source: Results, STN and PPN activation increase SNr GABA neuron activity in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 2B and 2E with insets
outcomes.quote: Optogenetic stimulation of either STN or PPN led to a significant increase in SNr GABA neuron activity (paired t-test, STN: t=3.8, p=0.008; PPN: t=9.2, p<0.0001)
outcomes.notes: 1 s 40 Hz trains, mean during the train against the 1 s before onset. STN mean 18.89 % dF/F, paired t = 3.86, p = 0.0083, n = 7 (paper t = 3.8, p = 0.008); PPN 6.45 %, t = 9.19, p = 3.7e-05, n = 8 (paper t = 9.2). The 0.25 and 4 s trains also give significant increases (p 1.4e-05 to 0.0066).
deviations: The response window (mean during the train) and pre-stimulus window (same length, before onset) are choices; the paper does not state them.
All seven STN mice have 10 trials per condition, where the Methods state 5.

outcomes.statement: The SNr GABA response scales with stimulation frequency from 5 to 40 Hz (Friedman test on 1 s trains, STN F = 21.0, p = 0.0001; PPN F = 18.2, p = 0.0004).
outcomes.source: Results, STN and PPN activation increase SNr GABA neuron activity in vivo, paragraph 3; Figure 2C and 2F
outcomes.quote: the amplitude of the response scaled with the frequency, increasing from 5 to 40 Hz (Friedman’s test, STN: F=21.0, p=0.0001; PPN: F=18.2, p=0.0004)
outcomes.notes: 1 s trains of the frequencies protocol. STN means rise from 4.07 to 32.66 % between 5 and 40 Hz, Friedman 21.00, p = 0.00011, 7 of 7 mice higher at 40 than 5 Hz; PPN 1.57 to 6.10 %, Friedman 18.15, p = 0.00041, 8 of 8 (paper 21.0 and 18.2). A repeated-measures ANOVA variant gives p = 0.014 and 0.0001.
deviations: The conversion code names the STN 1 s block of these mice as 10 mW, while the files and the Methods give 5 mW; the analysis takes the files as they are.

outcomes.statement: A 250 ms 40 Hz train of STN inputs elicits a net increase in SNc pan-DA neuron activity that peaks after stimulus offset (latency to peak 0.50 +/- 0.03 s, mean +/- SEM).
outcomes.source: Results, STN and PPN activation drive multiphasic responses in DA neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 3B
outcomes.quote: a brief (250 ms) 40 Hz train of STN inputs elicited a net increase in DA neuron activity that peaked after stimulus offset (Figure 3B; latency to peak, 0.50 +/− 0.03 s).
outcomes.notes: With the window fixed in the criterion (peak from onset to 2.25 s) the mean latency is 0.786 s, SEM 0.204, n = 11, outside 0.50 +/- 0.03 s, because two mice peak at 2.03 and 2.24 s. Ten of 11 mice peak after offset and the net response over 0 to 1.25 s is positive (2.89 %, t = 3.28, p = 0.0083). With a window ending at 1.25 s, a variant, the mean latency is 0.492 s, SEM 0.033, the paper's value. The two late-peaking mice (C4217, B8612) have small responses, an early local maximum at 0.41 and 0.62 s, and a slow rise that continues past the window (maximum over 0 to 5 s at 2.97 and 2.78 s), which looks like a late rebound or drift.
deviations: The paper does not give the window in which the peak is sought; the criterion fixed 0 to 2.25 s, and the variant 0 to 1.25 s matches the paper.

outcomes.statement: For SNc pan-DA neurons the STN-evoked response varies with train duration; with 1 and 4 s trains an initial increase is followed by inhibition (Friedman test, F = 13.0, p = 0.005).
outcomes.source: Results, STN and PPN activation drive multiphasic responses in DA neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 3B and 3C
outcomes.quote: When the train was extended to 1 or 4 s, we observed an initial increase in activity followed by inhibition (Friedman’s test, F=13.0, p=0.005)
outcomes.notes: Means during 0.25, 1 and 4 s trains are 0.52, 0.97 and -3.13 %, n = 11. Reading (a), Friedman over three durations, 13.64, p = 0.0011; reading (b), with the pre-stimulus window as a fourth group, 12.93, p = 0.0048, matching the paper's F = 13.0, p = 0.005; reading (c), area under the curve, p = 0.06. In 4 s trains the first 0.5 s (0.71 %) is above the last 1 s (-5.05 %) in all 11 mice, paired t = 4.81, p = 0.00071.
deviations: The paper's F and p fit four groups while three durations were tested; readings (a) and (b) match, and (b) gives the paper's value.

outcomes.statement: The amplitude of the SNc pan-DA response during STN stimulation does not scale with frequency (Friedman test, F = 4.2, p = 0.24).
outcomes.source: Results, STN and PPN activation drive multiphasic responses in DA neurons, paragraph 2; Figure 3D
outcomes.quote: the amplitude of the responses evoked during stimulation did not scale neatly with frequency (Friedman’s test, F=4.2, p=0.24) (Figure 3D).
outcomes.notes: 1 s trains, Friedman 4.20, p = 0.24, n = 11 (paper F = 4.2, p = 0.24); 40 minus 5 Hz 0.21 % dF/F. Variants with 0.25 s (p = 0.31) and 4 s trains (p = 0.18, 5 mice with all four frequencies) also find no effect.
deviations: The paper does not say which train duration Figure 3D shows; the 1 s train was fixed in the criterion.

outcomes.statement: PPN stimulation also evokes SNc pan-DA responses that vary with train duration (Friedman test, F = 11.5, p = 0.009).
outcomes.source: Results, STN and PPN activation drive multiphasic responses in DA neurons, paragraph 3; Figure 3F and 3G
outcomes.quote: Stimulation of PPN inputs led to similarly variable and dynamic DA responses... (Varying durations: Friedman’s test, F=11.5, p=0.009
outcomes.notes: Means during 0.25, 1 and 4 s PPN trains are -0.60, 1.03 and 0.70 %, n = 9. Friedman p = 0.26, 0.25 and 0.46 under readings (a) to (c), where the paper reports F = 11.5, p = 0.009. Without the three PPN recordings whose clock could not be shown from the response (C3164, C5007, C5008), n = 6, readings (a) and (b) give p = 0.11 and 0.14.
deviations: The paper's measure for this comparison is not stated; the mean during the train (and the area under the curve) were used, as for the STN comparison, which matches the paper there.

outcomes.statement: The SNc pan-DA response to PPN stimulation does not vary with frequency (repeated-measures one-way ANOVA, F2,15 = 1.35, p = 0.28).
outcomes.source: Results, STN and PPN activation drive multiphasic responses in DA neurons, paragraph 3; Figure 3H
outcomes.quote: Stimulation of PPN inputs led to similarly variable and dynamic DA responses... Varying frequencies: RM one-way ANOVA, F2,15=1.35, p=0.28)
outcomes.notes: 1 s trains, repeated-measures ANOVA F = 1.35 on Greenhouse-Geisser corrected df 1.85 and 14.8, p = 0.29, n = 9 (paper F2,15 = 1.35, p = 0.28); 40 minus 5 Hz 1.30 %. Variants with 0.25 and 4 s trains give p = 0.83 and 0.32.

outcomes.source: Results, STN and PPN inputs evoke opposite patterns of DA release in striatal subregions, paragraph 3; Figure 4E and 4H; Figure S3F and S3L
outcomes.quote: Notably, low-frequency (i.e. 5 Hz) optogenetic stimulation of either the STN or PPN increased DLS dopamine levels
outcomes.notes: 1 s trains at 5 Hz (Figure 4E and 4H), mean GRAB-DA in DLS during the train, STN 1.51 % (4 of 7 above 0, p = 0.22), PPN 1.40 % (6 of 9, p = 0.13). The sentence also cites Figure S3F and S3L, the 4 s DLS panels; for 4 s trains, a variant, STN 5.41 % (7 of 7, p = 0.00062) and PPN 2.01 % (6 of 9, p = 0.07), one input of two, which would be partially reproduced under that reading. The 1 s after offset is positive in all six conditions (0.96 to 6.76 %).
deviations: The paper does not state the window or test for this observation; the mean during 1 s trains (Figure 4E and 4H) against 0 was fixed in the criterion. The sentence cites both the 1 s panels and the 4 s panels (Figure S3F and S3L), and its account of summation over pulses fits longer trains; under the 4 s reading the effect holds for STN only.

outcomes.statement: In DLS the DA inhibition is followed by a post-stimulus rebound above baseline.
outcomes.source: Results, STN and PPN inputs evoke opposite patterns of DA release in striatal subregions, paragraph 3; Figure 4C and 4F
outcomes.quote: The DA inhibition was sustained for the duration of the stimulus and was followed by a post-stimulus rebound increase in evoked DA above baseline (Figure 4C, F).
outcomes.notes: After 1 s 40 Hz trains, PPN 4.53 % (8 of 9 above 0, p = 0.017), STN 0.87 % (5 of 7, p = 0.29). After 0.25 and 4 s trains the rebound is significant for both inputs (p 0.0039 to 0.015).
deviations: The rebound window (1 s after offset) and test are choices; the paper gives no statistic.

outcomes.statement: Calcium in DA terminals in TS and DLS shows opposite responses to STN stimulation, as the GRAB-DA recordings do.
outcomes.source: Results, STN and PPN inputs evoke opposite patterns of DA release in striatal subregions, paragraph 4; Figure S3N and S3O
outcomes.quote: Consistent with the GRABDA recordings, calcium responses in DA terminals in TS and DLS showed opposite patterns of activity in response to STN stimulation (Figure S3N-O).
outcomes.notes: DA terminal GCaMP, 1 s trains, TS 8.96 % (9 of 9 above 0), DLS -4.41 % (7 of 8 below 0), site by time interaction F(1, 15) = 26.2, p = 0.00013. The DLS terminals rebound after offset (6.73 %, 8 of 8 above 0).
deviations: 8 DLS mice, where the paper has 9.

outcomes.statement: Stimulation of STN or PPN inputs increases the activity of Vglut2+ DA neurons in SNc (STN, Wilcoxon, 0.25 s W = 41, p = 0.012, 1 s W = 43, p = 0.008, 4 s W = -5, p = 0.82; PPN, paired t-test, 0.25 s t = 2.9, p = 0.02, 1 s t = 3.4, p = 0.008, 4 s t = 3.0, p = 0.01).
outcomes.source: Results, Excitatory input from STN and PPN evoke opposite responses in PD-vulnerable and PD-resilient DA subtypes, paragraph 2; Figure 5B, 5C, 5G and 5H; Figure S4A and S4D
outcomes.quote: Stimulation of either STN or PPN inputs evoked an increase in the activity of Vglut2+ DA neurons in SNc
outcomes.notes: STN Wilcoxon W = 43 and 43 for 0.25 and 1 s (p = 0.0078 each, n = 9; paper 41 and 43); PPN paired t = 2.89 and 3.42 (p = 0.018 and 0.0076, n = 10; paper 2.9 and 3.4). For 4 s trains STN W = -5, p = 0.82 as in the paper, and PPN t = 2.56, p = 0.031 (paper 3.0, p = 0.01).
deviations: 9 STN mice, where the legend gives 10; the paper's W and p values are the exact values for 9 mice.

outcomes.statement: The Vglut2+ DA neuron increase scales with frequency for short STN trains and for all PPN durations (Friedman, STN 0.25 s F = 15.5, p = 0.001, 1 s F = 5.9, p = 0.11, 4 s F = 7.0, p = 0.07; PPN F = 18.8, 24.8, 20.2, p <= 0.0003).
outcomes.source: Results, Excitatory input from STN and PPN evoke opposite responses in PD-vulnerable and PD-resilient DA subtypes, paragraph 2; Figure 5D, 5E, 5I and 5J
outcomes.quote: increases in activity scaled with frequency for short-duration STN stimulations and all durations tested for PPN
outcomes.notes: STN 0.25 s Friedman 13.53, p = 0.0036; PPN 0.25, 1 and 4 s 11.23, 17.91, 16.20 (p = 0.011, 0.0005, 0.0010), all with the 40 Hz mean above the 5 Hz mean. STN 1 and 4 s are not significant (p = 0.43 and 0.16), as in the paper (0.11 and 0.07).
deviations: The PPN tests use the 7 of 10 mice that have all four frequencies; C3412, C3798 and C4707 have no 5 Hz trains in the dandiset. The paper's PPN 1 s Friedman statistic of 24.8 needs at least 9 mice (the maximum is 3n), so the paper had 5 Hz trains that are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: In DLS terminals of SNc Anxa1+ neurons, STN and PPN stimulation produce inhibition (STN, 0.25 s t = 6.4, p = 0.0004, 1 s W = -36, p = 0.005, 4 s W = -36, p = 0.008; PPN, 0.25 s t = 3.9, p = 0.004, 1 s W = -55, p = 0.002, 4 s t = 3.8, p = 0.004).
outcomes.source: Results, Excitatory input from STN and PPN evoke opposite responses in PD-vulnerable and PD-resilient DA subtypes, paragraph 3; Figure 5L, 5M, 5Q and 5R; Figure S4B and S4E
outcomes.quote: In DLS terminals from SNc Anxa1+ neurons, stimulation of both STN and PPN inputs produced inhibition followed by apparent rebound at stimulus offset
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds Anxa1 DLS recordings for 5 (STN) and 4 (PPN) mice where the paper has 8 and 10. At these numbers the Wilcoxon tests the paper uses for three of the six conditions cannot reach p < 0.05 (smallest p 0.0625 and 0.125), so reproduced (6 of 6) cannot be reached with the deposited mice. The three t-tests can reach it, so partially reproduced (3 to 5 of 6) was reachable and was not reached; 2 of 6 tests are significant (STN 0.25 s t = -6.14, p = 0.0036; PPN 0.25 s t = -3.46, p = 0.041; PPN 4 s p = 0.13). No STN mouse goes up in any condition, and one PPN mouse in 4 s trains. With the nine recordings without a site suffix added to DLS, a variant, all 6 tests are significant. Its STN 4 s W = -36 (p = 0.0078) is the paper's, but the other two W (-34 and -51 against -36 and -55) and the t values (2.65, 2.47, 2.98 against 6.4, 3.9, 3.8) differ, while the cell-body statistics match closely with the dual mice (p to two digits, t within 0.08). The paper's statistics fix its n; W = -36 and -55 equal -n(n+1)/2 for n = 8 and 10, and t = 6.4 with p = 0.0004 needs 7 df (4 df give p = 0.0031). The DLS recordings of nine of the paper's mice are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: The Anxa1+ terminal inhibition scales with frequency (STN, 0.25 s F = 18.0, 1 s F = 15.5, 4 s F = 15.3; PPN, 0.25 s F = 11.5, 1 s F2,15 = 11.0, 4 s F2,18 = 7.2).
outcomes.source: Results, Excitatory input from STN and PPN evoke opposite responses in PD-vulnerable and PD-resilient DA subtypes, paragraph 3; Figure 5N, 5O, 5S and 5T
outcomes.quote: The inhibition again scaled with frequency for shorter-duration STN stimulation and all durations tested for PPN
outcomes.notes: With the dandiset's DLS recordings (5 STN, 4 PPN mice) 5 of 6 tests hold (p 0.0043 to 0.026, 40 Hz below 5 Hz); PPN 4 s does not (F = 1.95, p = 0.24). With the unsuffixed recordings added, 3 of 6 hold. The paper's F2,15 and F2,18 for PPN 1 and 4 s imply about 8.5 and 10 mice (6.8 to 13.3 with the dfs rounded), against 4 here, so the samples are smaller than the paper's for the reason given under fig5-anxa1-dls-inhibited.
deviations: 5 and 4 mice, where the paper has 8 and 10 (see fig5-anxa1-dls-inhibited).

outcomes.statement: Anxa1+ terminals in DLS show a transient increase in activity at stimulus offset, for both inputs.
outcomes.source: Results, Excitatory input from STN and PPN evoke opposite responses in PD-vulnerable and PD-resilient DA subtypes, paragraph 3; Figure 5L and 5Q
outcomes.quote: In DLS terminals from SNc Anxa1+ neurons, stimulation of both STN and PPN inputs produced inhibition followed by apparent rebound at stimulus offset
outcomes.notes: After 1 s trains, STN 1.02 % (5 of 5 above 0, p = 0.0044), PPN 0.57 % (3 of 4, p = 0.14). The 0.25 and 4 s trains give the same picture (STN p = 0.036 and 0.026, PPN p = 0.20 and 0.11).
deviations: 5 and 4 mice, where the paper has 8 and 10.
The rebound window (1 s after offset) and test are choices; the paper gives no statistic.

outcomes.statement: Anxa1+ SNc cell bodies show stimulation-induced inhibition (paired t-test, STN 0.25 s t = 3.1, 1 s t = 4.0, 4 s t = 7.2, n = 5; PPN t = 4.8, 8.4, 3.3, n = 4) followed by post-stimulus rebound activation.
outcomes.source: Results, Excitatory input from STN and PPN evoke opposite responses in PD-vulnerable and PD-resilient DA subtypes, paragraph 3; Figure S4C and S4F
outcomes.quote: analysis of that subset revealed the same pattern of responses including stimulation-induced inhibition of activity... followed by post-stimulus rebound activation (Figure S4C, F).
outcomes.notes: With all SNc-labelled recordings (8 STN, 10 PPN mice) 5 of 6 tests show a significant decrease (p 0.0003 to 0.014); STN 0.25 s does not (t = -1.56, p = 0.16). Restricted to the mice with both a DLS and an SNc file (5 and 4, the paper's n), a variant, all 6 are significant with the paper's statistics (t = 3.13, 3.98, 7.26, 4.72, 8.35, 3.33 against 3.1, 4.0, 7.2, 4.8, 8.4, 3.3). The statement's post-stimulus rebound is not seen in the cell bodies after 1 s trains (STN -0.08 %, PPN 0.03 %, p = 0.65 and 0.80; dual mice p = 0.53 and 0.16).
deviations: The dandiset labels 8 and 10 mice as SNc where the paper analysed 5 and 4; the outcome uses the dandiset's labels as fixed in the criterion.

outcomes.statement: Excitatory inputs from STN and PPN activate PD-resilient Vglut2+ DA neurons but inhibit PD-vulnerable Anxa1+ DA neurons.
outcomes.source: Title; Abstract; Results, Excitatory input from STN and PPN evoke opposite responses in PD-vulnerable and PD-resilient DA subtypes, paragraph 3; Figure 5
outcomes.quote: excitatory inputs from STN and PPN led to activation of PD-resilient Vglut2+ DA neurons but inhibition of PD-vulnerable Anxa1+ DA neurons.
outcomes.notes: 1 s 40 Hz trains. STN, Vglut2 6.54 % against Anxa1 DLS -1.73 % (Welch t = 3.56, p = 0.0066); PPN 9.35 % against -1.48 % (t = 3.90, p = 0.0032). It holds with the unsuffixed Anxa1 recordings added to DLS (p = 0.0097 and 0.005) and against the Anxa1 SNc recordings (p = 0.017 and 0.0065).
deviations: Anxa1 DLS recordings of 5 and 4 mice, where the paper has 8 and 10.

outcomes.statement: In human SNc, TH+ neurons (Mann-Whitney U = 2.0, p = 0.002) and TH+/ANXA1+ neurons (U = 1.0, p < 0.0001) are fewer in PD cases (n = 7) than in controls (n = 12).
outcomes.source: Results, ANXA1 is expressed in human SNc and marks a PD-vulnerable DA subtype, paragraph 2; Figure 1D and 1E
outcomes.quote: the total number of TH-expressing neurons was significantly decreased in PD cases compared to controls (Mann-Whitney’s test, U=2.0, p=0.002) (Figure 1D). The number of ANXA1+ DA neurons was also significantly reduced in PD cases (U=1.0, p<0.0001)
outcomes.notes: The human RNAscope counts are not in the dandiset, which holds mouse photometry only. The preprint has no data availability statement, and the dandiset metadata and the conversion repository link no other deposit.

outcomes.statement: Among remaining DA neurons in PD, ANXA1+ neurons are de-enriched to 10 +/- 7% of control, ALDH1A1+ to 41 +/- 12%, while CALB1+ neurons trend toward enrichment (301 +/- 103%).
outcomes.source: Results, ANXA1 is expressed in human SNc and marks a PD-vulnerable DA subtype, paragraph 2; Figure 1F
outcomes.quote: a trend toward enrichment of CALB1+ DA neurons (301 +/− 103 %control, unpaired t-test, t=1.9, p=0.10) compared to the significant de-enrichment observed for ALDHA1A1+ DA neurons (41 +/− 12 %control, t=4.9, p=0.002), and especially ANXA1+ DA neurons
outcomes.notes: Human tissue counts are not in the dandiset nor in any deposit the paper or the dandiset names (see fig1de-th-anxa1-reduced).

outcomes.statement: TH+/CALB1+ neuron counts are not significantly changed in PD (U = 19.5, p = 0.08) while TH+/ALDH1A1+ counts are reduced (U = 1.0, p < 0.0001).
outcomes.source: Results, ANXA1 is expressed in human SNc and marks a PD-vulnerable DA subtype, paragraph 2; Figure S1B to S1F
outcomes.quote: the number of CALB1+ DA neurons was not significantly affected, though a trend was observed (U=19.5, p=0.08) (Figure S1B-C), while ALDH1A1+ DA neurons were significantly reduced in PD (U=1.0, p<0.0001)
outcomes.notes: Human tissue counts are not in the dandiset nor in any deposit the paper or the dandiset names (see fig1de-th-anxa1-reduced).

outcomes.statement: Immunofluorescence confirms fewer TH+ and TH+/ALDH1A1+ neurons and a lower fraction of TH+ neurons expressing ALDH1A1 in PD (n = 11) than in controls (n = 15), and counts agree with RNAscope in four cases processed both ways.
outcomes.source: Results, ANXA1 is expressed in human SNc and marks a PD-vulnerable DA subtype, paragraph 1; Figure S1G to S1J
outcomes.quote: Quantification of IF showing significant decrease in TH+, TH+/ALDH1A1+, and % TH+/ALDH1A1+ showing de-enrichment in PD (n=11) relative to control (n=15).
outcomes.notes: Human immunofluorescence counts are not in the dandiset nor in any deposit the paper or the dandiset names (see fig1de-th-anxa1-reduced).

findings.statement: For the Anxa1 mice the dandiset holds DLS terminal recordings for 5 (STN) and 4 (PPN) mice where the paper analyses 8 and 10. Nine mice (C5903, C5906, C5992, C6900, C6902, C7244, C7245, C7248, C7249) have only recordings labelled SNc, without a site suffix in the file name. Their signals resemble SNc recordings, and the paper's cell-body statistics are reproduced closely by the other nine mice's SNc recordings (p to two digits, t within 0.08), so the DLS recordings of these nine mice appear not to be deposited, and the nine SNc recordings were not used in the paper.
The dandiset includes Anxa1 SNc recordings from nine mice that the paper's cell-body analysis (n = 5 and 4) leaves out, and it does not say which recordings the paper used.
The human RNAscope and immunofluorescence counts of Figure 1 and Figure S1 and the histology of Figure S2 are not in the dandiset, and the preprint has no data availability statement.
DA terminals in DLS have 8 mice where Figure S3 gives 9.

The Figure 5 legend gives 10 mice for Vglut2+ neurons with STN stimulation, while the paper's Wilcoxon statistics (W = 41, 43, -5 with p = 0.012, 0.008, 0.82) are the exact values for 9 mice; the dandiset holds 9.
Three Vglut2 PPN mice (C3412, C3798, C4707) have no 5 Hz trains in their frequencies sessions, while the paper's Friedman statistic for PPN 1 s (24.8) needs at least 9 mice with all four frequencies.
Subject C4608 (SNr GABA, PPN) has no 4 s trains in its frequencies session; the conversion notes say they were recorded in a separate session, which is not in the dandiset.

The dF/F series are stated in a.u. but hold percent (100 times (Gc - fit) / fit); a recomputation from the stored signals agrees with a median correlation of 0.9999 (durations) and 0.9988 (frequencies).
Every session start time carries the offset -00:01, the local mean time of London that pytz gives when a time zone is attached with replace; the true offset is lost.
The session description of the frequencies protocol gives an interval of 10 s between trains; the epochs and the Methods give 20 s.
Thirteen mice (SNr GABA and pan-DA, ids starting with B) have 10 trials per condition where the Methods state 5, and 30 mice have 16 s trains that the paper does not mention.
The conversion code names the 1 s block of the STN to SNr GABA frequencies sessions s1s10mW, suggesting 10 mW, while the epoch tables and the Methods give 5 mW.

The conversion repository's Python re-implementation of the dF/F forces the robust fit through the origin, saying the MATLAB version does so, while its own description of the MATLAB scripts includes an intercept.

The files describe the modulation inconsistently. The excitation source descriptions give 465 nm modulated at 210 Hz and 405 nm at 330 Hz, as the Methods do, while the processed series descriptions give the calcium signal as demodulated at 330 Hz and the isosbestic signal at 210 Hz, as the conversion repository's description of the MATLAB scripts does. This attempt did not check which is right against the raw signal.

The file names and session ids of nine Anxa1 mice carry no recording site, and every Anxa1 file lists both an SNc and a DLS fiber in its fiber photometry table, so the site rests on the name of the dF/F series alone.
Eight subject ids are written in lower case (c3015, c3016, c4379, c4708, c4709, c4977, c4978, c5113) while the others are upper case.

The Results give F1,11 = 12.8 for the DLS frequency effect with 1 s trains for both STN (p = 0.0005) and PPN (p = 0.002); F(1, 11) = 12.8 gives p = 0.0043, and the data give F = 26.2 for STN. Two Friedman entries for Anxa1 terminals also do not fit their p-values (F = 11.5 with p = 0.0002, F = 15.5 with p = 0.015; with 3 df these give 0.0093 and 0.0014). F1,11 is also not possible for a one-way repeated-measures ANOVA in 7 or 9 mice. The Figure 5 legend says the Anxa1 STN frequency panels (N, O) show no significant effect of frequency, while the Results report significant effects for all three STN durations.
The lab's MATLAB analysis scripts are not public; the preprint names custom MATLAB code and has no code availability statement. The conversion repository describes them.
The dandiset has no published version; this attempt used the draft as modified on 2026-09-01T15:27:47Z.

attempts.label: DANDI:001538
attempts.paper_title: State-dependent modulation of spiny projection neurons controls levodopa-induced dyskinesia in a mouse model of Parkinson’s disease
attempts.entry_title: State-dependent modulation of spiny projection neurons in levodopa-induced dyskinesia (Zhai et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Zhai, Cui, Wokosin, Sun, Tkatch, Crittenden, Graybiel and Surmeier (2025) on dandiset 001538. It measures somatic excitability (rheobase and spike counts) and the dendritic excitability index of dSPNs and iSPNs in the LID off- and on-states and under D1R, D2R and M1R antagonists, CDGI deletion and M1R deletion, and evoked ACh release with GRAB-ACh3.0. It links the recordings to the paper's per-cell tables on Zenodo. The Sr2+-oEPSC, ACh and AIM data hold too few cells or mice for most of the paper's tests, and the spine data are raw stacks only.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zhai et al. (2025) from dandiset 001538

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's somatic current-step recordings are those behind the paper's somatic excitability figures, and the spike counts computed from them agree with the paper's per-cell tables.
outcomes.source: Figures 1E, 3C, 6C, 7C and 9D; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: Groups are matched by name and every group the dandiset holds has the paper's n (12 of 12 groups, 123 cells). 90 of 123 cells (73.2%) match a row of the paper's table exactly over 20 to 300 pA and 105 (85.4%) within 3 spikes, below the 80% and 95% of the criterion; 108 have the same rheobase as their best match. dSPN on has the fewest exact matches (6 of 15). The best matches are not one-to-one (9 paper rows are the best match of two or three cells); with each row used once, 89 cells (72.4%) match exactly and 103 (83.7%) within 3 spikes. The best-match rows follow the dandiset's order by date and cell number, every cell at its own rank in 8 of 12 groups and 10 of 15, 11 of 15, 11 of 12 and 10 of 11 cells in the others. Of the 14 cells with a repeated step, keeping the last sweep in place of the first gives the same best-match difference in 13 and a closer one in 1.
deviations: The paper's spike counts come from its script run on Prairie View exports; the differences of 1 to 24 spikes may come from the export or from cells whose steps are missing or repeated in the files (18 cells miss a step, 14 repeat one).

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's dendritic line scans are those behind the paper's dendritic excitability index figures, and the index computed from them agrees with the paper's per-cell values.
outcomes.source: Figures 1I, 3F, 6D and 7F; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: Three site series hold six trials, two sites under one name; split, they give their cells 0.293, 0.146 and 0.327 against the paper's 0.299, 0.146 and 0.309. With the split, 91 of 92 cells have an index (iSPN on+sul 20190508 cell 3 has only a distal site). Counts of cells with an index equal the paper's n in 9 of 10 groups, and counts of cells with dendritic sites in 10 of 10, so every group is matched, by order or (Figure 6D) by date and letter. Over 91 matched cells the index differs from the paper's by a median of 2.9% (78 within 10%, Spearman 0.938). Two cells differ by more than the paper's value, dSPN on+SCH 20190411 cell 1 (0.584 against 0.228; only its second pair of sites is in the dandiset) and iSPN off 20160524 cell 2 (1.062 against 0.527; its first proximal site has one trial, and without it the cell gives 0.553). The best-match rows of the somatic link follow the dandiset's order (link-somatic-cells), which supports matching by order. With the sites as labelled, 89 of 92 cells have an index.
deviations: Outside Figure 6D the paper's table has no cell identifiers, so cells are matched by order, an assumption supported by the somatic link.
The background constants of the paper's script (55 red, 161 green) are used for every session, as the files carry no per-session background.
Three six-trial series are split into their first and last three trials, the half with the smaller area taken as distal, a choice made here from the data; the sites as labelled are a variant.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's Sr2+-oEPSC recordings are cells of the paper's Figures 2 and 4, and their events agree with the paper's per-cell values.
outcomes.source: Figures 2G to 2I and 4F to 4H; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: All 14 dandiset cells match a paper identifier (date and session letter); the paper has 33 cells (17 off, 16 on), so the dandiset holds one cell per mouse. In every cell the detector here finds fewer events (2 to 85, against 29 to 127 in the paper's tables) and a higher mean amplitude than the paper's events; 2 of 14 cells are within 25% on both, and also 2 of 14 when the paper's amplitude is read as its per-cell value (0.70 to 0.96 times the mean of its histogram events). In 20230405b (2 events against 73) the detection window opens on the slow decay of a large synchronous current, and the small events on it stay below the threshold (figure in the notebook). The paper's frequency equals its event count over 3.6 s. With the paper's per-cell amplitudes, on-state dSPNs are all above off-state ones and on-state iSPNs all below (Mann-Whitney P = 0.057 each).
deviations: Events are found with a threshold detector written here (low-pass 1 kHz, five robust SD, local baseline); the paper used TaroTools with visual verification, which cannot be repeated.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's GRAB-ACh recordings are regions of the paper's Figure 5F, and the normalised areas computed from them agree with the paper's per-region values.
outcomes.source: Figure 5F; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds one region per mouse, 11 of the paper's 34 (3 of 13 unlesioned, 3 of 10 6-OHDA, 5 of 11 off-state). The paper's regions have no identifier linking them to mice; by the nearest vector of single-pulse areas only 5 of 11 mice have a paper region within 0.05 on every treatment (the 20240402 mouse within 0.007), so the regions cannot be identified. One paper region is the best match of two off-state mice; with each region used once, 5 of 11 are still within 0.05.
deviations: The stimulus time is taken from the trial table (3 s after the trial start in six files), where the paper's script fixes 10 s.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's AIM score tables are mice of the paper's Figures 8 and 10, with genotypes and scores that agree with the paper's tables.
outcomes.source: Figures 8B, 8C and 10B; the paper's tables at Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059
outcomes.notes: 7 of 9 dandiset mice are in the paper's tables (4124 and 5871 are not). The two Figure 10 mice (5844 control, 5846 M1R deletion) have totals equal to the paper's in all 10 sessions; the five Figure 8 mice (1945, 2519, 2828 and 6572 KO, 2587 wild type) agree in 5 of 25 sessions (for 1945, session 1, 33.5 against 27.0). The dandiset's own genotype labels for the CDGI mice contradict each other, so the paper's labels were used. The paper's tables give session totals only; for the Figure 8 mice they equal neither the dandiset's sums over 20 to 80 min nor, outside those 5 sessions, the sums over all time points (1945 session 1 has four time points summing to 33.5), so the scores differ, not only the time points summed.
deviations: The paper's session total is taken to be the sum over the session's time points; the Figure 8 mice have 4 time points in some dandiset sessions and 6 in others.

outcomes.statement: In dSPNs the rheobase is lower in the LID on-state than in the off-state.
outcomes.source: Figure 1F; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 2 (P < 0.0001, Mann-Whitney)
outcomes.quote: in on-state dSPNs, the current needed to evoke a spike (rheobase) was significantly smaller than that in the off-state
outcomes.notes: Rheobase on-state 140 pA against off-state 220 pA (15 cells each from 10 and 8 mice), Mann-Whitney P = 8.86e-06, effect r = -0.95. With one value per mouse P = 0.000425 and complete separation.

outcomes.statement: In on-state dSPNs suprathreshold current steps evoke more spikes than in off-state dSPNs across a range of intensities.
outcomes.source: Figure 1E; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 2

deviations: The paper shows F-I curves without a test; the summed count and its test were chosen here.

outcomes.statement: Bath application of the D1R antagonist SCH 23390 does not reverse the lower rheobase of on-state dSPNs.
outcomes.source: Figure 1F; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 2 (P = 0.589, Mann-Whitney)
outcomes.quote: bath application of the D1R antagonist SCH 23390 (3 μM) did not reverse the leftward shift in the F-I relationship curve (Fig. 1E) or the reduction in rheobase
outcomes.notes: Rheobase on-state 140 pA (15 cells) against on-state with SCH 140 pA (10 cells), P = 1.0, effect r = 0.007. In the 5 cells recorded in both conditions the median paired difference is 0 pA (Wilcoxon P = 1.0). Five cells are in both groups, so the unpaired test's samples are not independent; the criterion follows the paper's test.

outcomes.statement: The dendritic excitability index of dSPNs is higher in the on-state than in the off-state.
outcomes.source: Figure 1I; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 3 (P = 0.0115, Mann-Whitney)

outcomes.notes: Index on-state 0.476 against off-state 0.330 (10 cells each), P = 0.0058 (exact 0.0039), effect r = 0.74; without background P = 0.0046; with a basal-ratio rule of 0.8 to 1.25 (8 cells each) P = 0.0070; with the sites as labelled P = 0.0091.
deviations: Background constants from the paper's script; basal-ratio rule (0.5 to 2) chosen here, dropping no pair; one six-trial series split into two sites.

outcomes.statement: SCH 23390 reverses the higher dendritic excitability of on-state dSPNs.
outcomes.source: Figure 1I; Results, Intrinsic excitability and synaptic connectivity of dSPNs increased in the on-state of LID, paragraph 3 (P = 0.0133, Mann-Whitney)
outcomes.quote: the elevation in on-state dSPN dendritic excitability was readily reversed by bath application of the D1R antagonist SCH 23390

statistics.n: 10 on-state and 9 on-state with SCH cells

outcomes.notes: The criterion (P < 0.05 with the SCH median lower) is not met, though the difference has the stated direction. On-state with SCH 0.419 (9 cells) against on-state 0.476 (10 cells), P = 0.0662 (exact 0.0653), effect r = -0.51; with the stricter basal-ratio rule P = 0.524. The difference from the paper comes from one cell, SCH 20190411 cell 1, whose index is 0.584 here and 0.228 in the paper's table; the dandiset holds only its second pair of sites. Without that cell P = 0.0266; with the paper's value for it P = 0.016 (exact 0.0133, the paper's P). The other eight SCH cells differ from the paper's values by 2.4% to 10.9%. That the missing sites explain the difference is an inference from the recovered P, as the paper does not list each cell's sites.
deviations: Matching the SCH cells to the paper's rows by order is an assumption (link-dendritic-cells).

statistics.n: 10 on-state and 8 on-state with sulpiride cells

outcomes.notes: The paper's test finds the difference the claim says is absent. On-state with sulpiride 0.506 (7 cells) against on-state 0.339 (10 cells), P = 0.0097, effect r = 0.74; the paper reports P = 0.0545 with 8 and 10 cells, and its own medians go the same way (0.499 and 0.345). The sulpiride cell without an index (20190508 cell 3, only a distal site in the dandiset) has 0.217 in the paper's table; with that value P = 0.0545, the paper's P. Under the main basal-ratio rule the outcome turns on that one cell; under the stricter rule P = 0.0663 without it, which would also meet the criterion, so the outcome depends on the basal-ratio rule as well. That the missing site explains the difference is an inference from the recovered P, as the paper does not list each cell's sites.

outcomes.notes: On the paper's tables, MCI-Park against control distance 4.678 against 10.35 m (P = 1.05e-05), time mobile P = 6.97e-06; M1R deletion alone P = 0.628 and 0.467; levodopa with deletion against levodopa alone 28.09 against 6.52 m (P = 0.000332) and 276.4 against 127.45 s (P = 0.000567).
deviations: Tested on the paper's tables; the open-field data are not in the dandiset.
outcomes.where: Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17307059 (Figure 10E and 10F sheets); raw ANY-maze data in Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.17260198

findings.statement: The dandiset holds no patch-clamp recordings from unlesioned control or 6-OHDA-lesioned mice, which make up the control and 6-OHDA groups of Figures 1E, 1F, 1I, 3C, 3D and 3F (10, 12, 11 and 9 dSPNs; 21, 11, 14 and 9 iSPNs), nor the oxo-M line scans of Figure 7E or the open-field data of Figure 10. The paper's raw data on Zenodo (doi:10.5281/zenodo.17260198) list folders for all of these.

The Sr2+-oEPSC files hold one cell per mouse (14 of the paper's 33 cells), the GRAB-ACh files one region per mouse (11 of 34 regions) and the AIM tables 7 of the paper's 44 mice plus two mice (4124, 5871) not in the paper. The dandiset does not say that it holds a subset or how the cells, regions and mice were chosen, and with these numbers the paper's tests cannot reach P < 0.05 for most comparisons.

Session names state a drug (D1RaSch, D2RaSul) for files that also hold baseline on-state sweeps. 11 cells in such files have a baseline condition; 7 of them were also recorded with the drug and 4 are baseline only (dSPN 20190507 cell 1, iSPN 20190408 cell 1, 20190409 cell 1 and 20190508 cell 2). The condition of each sweep is only in the RecordingsIndexTable column condition_subfolder; grouping by session name puts baseline cells in the drug groups.

The genotypes of the CDGI behaviour mice contradict each other. Subject genotype is Wild-type CDGI and every session name says WT for all of them; the AIM table's genotype column says CDGI Knockout, Wild Type or unknown, changing between sessions of one animal; the video files of mice 1945, 2519, 2587, 2828 and 6572 say CDGI KO. The paper lists 2587 as wild type and the others as KO.

The AIM session totals of the five Figure 8 mice in the dandiset differ from the paper's table in 20 of 25 sessions (mouse 1945 session 1, 33.5 against 27.0), while the two Figure 10 mice agree in all sessions. Some dandiset sessions have 4 time points and others 6.

Three dendritic site series hold six trials, two sites under one name, while the cell has no series of the other compartment with that number (iSPN 20160526 cell 3 Distal1, iSPN 20160608 cell 1 Proximal1, dSPN 20170204 cell 1 Proximal1); their first and last three trials differ in baseline and area. Split, they give the paper's values for these cells. One series holds a single trial (iSPN 20160524 cell 2 Proximal1), one two and one four.

Two dendritic cells lack the sites the paper's values need. dSPN on+SCH 20190411 cell 1 has only its second pair of sites, which gives 0.584 against the paper's 0.228; with the paper's value the SCH test gives the paper's P (0.0133), without it P = 0.066. iSPN on+sul 20190508 cell 3 has only a distal site; with the paper's 0.217 the sulpiride test gives the paper's P (0.0545), without it P = 0.0097. Under the main basal-ratio rule these two cells decide fig1i-dspn-dendritic-sch-lower and fig3f-ispn-dendritic-sul-no-change; under the stricter rule (0.8 to 1.25) the sulpiride test gives P = 0.0663 without the cell. Reading the gap as data missing is an inference from the recovered P values, as the paper does not list each cell's sites.

The dandiset holds the raw spine image stacks and the rotation videos but no spine counts or rotation counts (none of the 86 spine files has a processing module or analysis entry), the measurements behind Figures 2B, 2C, 4B, 4C, 4K, 6F, 7H, 8A, 9F and 10A. They are only in the paper's Zenodo tables.

The stimulus series of every dendritic sweep (CurrentClampSeries_CellN_Dendritic_Stimulus) is all zero, though the three spikes per sweep show the 2 nA injections were delivered; and the index table gives no kymograph slice for 53 of 997 dendritic sweeps.

In the Sr2+-oEPSC files the light-pulse OptogeneticSeries is all zero in 69 of 140 sweeps, and the intracellular recordings table references no stimulus (its stimulus rows are empty). The pulse time (0.02 s) is only in the optogenetic epochs table.

The GRAB-ACh background reference images are described as taken at zero laser power, but their mean (381 to 525) is above the signal (F0 179 to 355), so they cannot be the PMT background the Methods subtract.

The files cite the bioRxiv preprint (related_publications) and describe the behaviour data with the preprint's figure numbers ("Figure 7J" for the CDGI AIM scores, "Figure 8" for the M1R study), which are Figures 8 and 10 in the published paper the dandiset names.

Patch-clamp subjects are named by recording date (for example Subject20160523LIDOFFeGFP and SubjectRecordedAt20160523000000 for the same day), with no animal identifier, so recordings and spine stacks of one mouse cannot be linked, and the archive has 185 subject folders.

Recomputed on the paper's own per-cell tables, some reported P values differ; the oxo-M test in CDGI KO gives P = 0.47 where the paper reports 0.910, and the rotation test of Figure 8A gives 0.012 where the text reports 0.0092. Others agree closely (0.009766 against 0.0098 for oxo-M in wild type).
18 somatic cells miss one or more current steps between 20 and 300 pA and 14 repeat a step; spike counts for these cells cannot be complete.

attempts.label: DANDI:001550
attempts.paper_title: Individual variability of neural computations underlying flexible decisions
attempts.entry_title: Context-dependent evidence accumulation in rats (Pagan et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Pagan, Tang, Aoi, Pillow, Mante, Sussillo and Brody (2025) on dandiset 001550, which holds the behaviour of 26 rats trained on a task that switches between accumulating location and frequency evidence. It links the dandiset to the paper's published behavioural tables, checks the session statistics and selection, fits the behavioural pulse kernels and their slope indices, tests the optogenetic inactivation, and, with the paper's neural data from GitHub, the link between behavioural and neural slope indices.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Pagan et al. (2025) from dandiset 001550

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's sessions can be linked to the paper's published per-session behavioural tables, and the linked records agree on trial counts, outcomes, evidence and pulse timing.
outcomes.source: Data availability; the paper's data/Sessions_trials at GitHub commit 0ea8fdb
outcomes.quote: Rat behavioural and electrophysiological data are available at https://github.com/Brody-Lab/flexible_decision_making_rats.
outcomes.notes: Sessions are matched by rat and session name taken from the source file names in the paper's tables. Of 15,278 paper sessions with valid trials, 15,277 (0.9999) are in the dandiset; the missing one, P189 TaskSwitch6-210516a, has 27 valid trials. In all 15,277 the number of valid trials and the fraction correct are equal, and both relative weights agree to 1e-6 in 0.898; of the 1,553 that differ, 861 agree once this attempt's values are capped at 1 as the paper's table does. Of the 692 left, 627 have a missing value on both sides, 5 in the paper's table only, and 60 differ with both values present (median difference 0.87 after capping, not explained); 3 of the 692 are in the paper's selection. In 20 seeded sessions every valid trial agrees on context, correct side, strengths, choice, outcome and position in block, and 0.99996 of 10 ms pulse bins agree. Over every matched session, 627 have an empty per-trial record in the paper's tables; in the other 14,650 the 7,447,692 valid trials agree on every per-trial field and position in block, and 0.99996 of 50 ms pulse bins agree over the 6,532,005 trials whose pulses were binned. The dandiset's Methods selection keeps all 8,843 sessions of the paper's selection plus 6 (5 P187 and P189 sessions not in the paper's tables, and P059 TaskSwitch4-170331a, whose relative weight of 1.112 the paper's table caps at 1.0). Per-rat selected trial counts equal the paper's numhits for 23 of 26 rats and exceed them by 213 (P059), 1,442 (P187) and 609 (P189).
deviations: The paper's `good` flag is not in the dandiset and is not applied; it removes no session that passes the other criteria.

outcomes.statement: The study used 26 male Long-Evans rats, aged between 6 and 24 months.
outcomes.source: Methods, Subjects
outcomes.quote: All subjects were male Long-Evans rats between the ages of 6 and 24 months ... A total of 26 rats were used for the experiments presented in this study
outcomes.notes: 26 subjects, all male Long Evans, one date of birth each. Ages at the 8,849 selected sessions are 3.0 to 39.1 months (median 15.4); 0.913 lie within 5.4 to 26.4 months and 0.844 within 6 to 24. Eighteen rats have selected sessions before 5.4 months and eight after 26.4. The dates of birth put 25 rats at 1.6 to 2.7 months at their first session in the dandiset; P189 is at 14.1 months, on the day P187 (born 2019-02-21) starts, and its date of birth (2018-02-21) may be a year early.

outcomes.statement: Rats performed on average 542 trials per session.
outcomes.source: Methods, Behaviour
outcomes.quote: rats performed on average 542 trials per session
outcomes.notes: Mean valid trials per session 551.8 over the 8,849 selected sessions (reading b) and 494.2 over all 15,400 task sessions (reading d), both within 487.8 to 596.2. All trials average 817.9 and 749.7 (readings a and c), outside. The 13 unreadable sessions (1 to 3 trials) are left out of readings c and d; added, they give 749.1 and 493.8.
deviations: The Methods do not say which sessions or trials are counted; four readings are shown and two match.

outcomes.statement: On average, rats switched across 14.6 context blocks per session.
outcomes.source: Methods, Behaviour
outcomes.quote: On average, rats switched across 14.6 context blocks per session
outcomes.notes: Blocks per session average 16.98 over selected sessions and 13.90 over all task sessions; switches average 15.98 and 12.90. Blocks over all sessions (13.90) and switches over selected sessions (15.98) are within 13.14 to 16.06; the first is recorded as measured.
deviations: Whether blocks or switches are counted, and over which sessions, is not stated; two of four readings match.

outcomes.statement: Behavioural sessions lasted 2 to 4 hours.
outcomes.source: Methods, Behaviour
outcomes.quote: Behavioural sessions lasted 2–4 h
outcomes.notes: Median duration 2.50 h over selected sessions and 2.57 h over all task sessions. Only 0.559 and 0.556 of sessions last 2 to 4 h (0.65 within 1.8 to 4.4); 5% to 95% of selected sessions span 1.26 to 4.41 h, and the range is 0.26 to 7.74 h.
deviations: Duration is taken from the first trial start to the last trial stop; the files hold no session end time.

outcomes.statement: Block switches occurred after a minimum of 30 trials per block, and when a local estimate of performance reached 80% correct.
outcomes.source: Methods, Behaviour
outcomes.quote: block switches occurred after a minimum of 30 trials per block, and when a local estimate of performance reached a threshold of 80% correct
outcomes.notes: All 141,359 non-final blocks of selected sessions have at least 30 trials counted over all trials (1st percentile 30, median 44); counted over valid trials 0.817 do. Over the last 30 valid trials before a switch the median fraction correct is 0.828 and 0.601 of blocks reach 0.8, so the 80% part is not shown on that window; the task's local estimate is not described.

outcomes.statement: Twenty rats each contributed more than 120,000 trials after training.
outcomes.source: Figure 1c legend; Extended Data Figure 1c
outcomes.quote: Logistic fits of psychometric curves for 20 rats after training (more than 120,000 trials for each rat)
outcomes.notes: Twenty rats have more than 120,000 valid trials in selected sessions (the twentieth, P189, has 128,309; the next, P124, 115,123). The same 20 pass at 120,000 or more.

outcomes.statement: After training, choices are mostly driven by location in the location context and by frequency in the frequency context.
outcomes.source: Figure 1c; Extended Data Figure 3a,d
outcomes.quote: In the LOC context, choices are mostly affected by location; in the FRQ context, choices are mostly affected by frequency
outcomes.notes: In all 20 rats both relative weights exceed 0.5; location in the location context 0.770 to 0.860, frequency in the frequency context 0.724 to 0.870.
deviations: Tested by the Methods' logistic regression on generative strengths, not by the four-parameter psychometric fits that the figure shows.

outcomes.statement: Rats switch the feature they attend to within about four trials of a new context block.
outcomes.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 1e (legend panel g)
outcomes.quote: were able to switch between selected stimulus features within four trials of a new context block
outcomes.notes: Across 26 rats, at position 4 of a new block the relevant relative weight is 0.91 of its plateau when switching to location and 0.963 when switching to frequency (Methods selection), and 0.914 and 0.961 with the code's 0.65 selection. At position 1 it is 0.502 and 0.560, against plateaus of 0.854 and 0.789. All 26 rats have a fit at positions 1 to 5 (103 to 6,096 trials), so the 30-trial minimum drops nothing. Bootstrapping rats, the position 4 value for the switch to location has a 95% interval of 0.874 to 0.946 and reaches 0.9 in 0.678 of resamples; at position 5, which the criterion also allows, the values are 0.956 and 0.977 and reach 0.9 in 0.998 and 1.000 of resamples.
deviations: The paper's code uses a 0.65 selection for this analysis; the Methods selection is the main result and the code's is a variant.

outcomes.statement: Most rats learned the task in two to five months.
outcomes.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 1; Extended Data Figure 2g
outcomes.quote: most rats learned the task in a timespan between two and five months
outcomes.notes: From each rat's first session to its first session with an index of at least 0.7, 17 of 26 rats took 1.8 to 5.5 months (times 0.85 to 8.18 months). With the full selection 19 of 26; counted from the first TaskSwitch session 13 (exactly half) and 17. Within the unwidened 2 to 5 months the counts are 12, 16, 10 and 13. 24 rats start with ProAnti3Marino sessions.
deviations: The paper does not define the start of training or when a rat counts as trained; four pairings of readings are shown, three match.

outcomes.statement: Differential behavioural kernels predominantly converge towards the end of the pulse train, that is the difference between contexts in the weight of a feature shrinks for later pulses.
outcomes.source: Methods, Behavioural logistic regression, paragraph 3; Figure 4; Extended Data Figure 3c,f
outcomes.quote: Empirically we found that differential behavioural kernels predominantly displayed convergence towards the end of the pulse stimulus presentation
outcomes.notes: All 36 slope indices of the 18 Figure 4 rats are negative (median -0.432, range -0.774 to -0.097). With the code's fixed penalty of 200 all 36 are negative (median -0.491), and they agree with the indices from the paper's saved weights to at most 0.0177 (r = 0.99973).
deviations: The Methods' ridge penalty is read as the code's penalty on neighbouring weight differences, with its weight chosen by 3-fold cross-validation over 20, 200 and 2000 (chosen weights 20 to 2000); the code fixes it at 200.
The differential kernel is divided by its largest absolute value before the line fit, as the code does; the Methods do not say.

outcomes.statement: Across rats, the shape of the differential behavioural kernel for one feature does not predict the shape for the other feature.
outcomes.source: Results, Linking neural and behaviour variability, paragraph 1; Figure 4 top right
outcomes.quote: The shape of an individual’s differential behavioural kernel for one feature did not appear to predict the shape of the kernel for the other feature
outcomes.notes: Across 18 rats r = 0.180 (95% CI -0.313 to 0.597), p = 0.475; with the fixed penalty r = 0.092, p = 0.717; from the paper's saved weights r = 0.094, p = 0.71.
deviations: The paper gives no test; a two-sided Pearson correlation was chosen before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: The behavioural slope index computed from the first half of a rat's trials is correlated with the index from the second half (r = 0.58, p = 0.000013).
outcomes.source: Extended Data Figure 3g legend
outcomes.quote: The slope index computed from behavioral trials in the first half split is highly correlated with the slope index computed using the second half split (r = 0.58; p = 0.000013)

statistics.test: correlation, significance from the Student’s t distribution

outcomes.notes: Over 24 rats and 48 values r = 0.552 (95% CI 0.318 to 0.723), p = 4.7e-05, within 0.522 to 0.638. With the fixed penalty r = 0.577, p = 1.8e-05. Location alone r = 0.470, frequency alone r = 0.736.
deviations: The halves use the penalty weight chosen on all of that rat's trials in that context.

outcomes.statement: Bilateral optogenetic silencing of the frontal orienting fields during the stimulus impairs performance of the task (three rats).
outcomes.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 2; Extended Data Figure 4g
outcomes.quote: bilateral optogenetic silencing of rat FOF demonstrated that they are required for accurate performance of the task
outcomes.notes: Four rats have opto sessions (P116 47, P124 74, P127 4 and P131 88 with at least 100 valid trials). With bilateral full-trial epochs accuracy is lower than on control trials in the same sessions with p < 0.05 in 2 of the 3 rats with most sessions, P116 (0.639 against 0.733, 873 trials, p below 1e-4) and P131 (0.686 against 0.727, 1,988 trials, p = 0.0001). P124 is higher (0.712 against 0.687, p = 0.17) and P127 lower but not significantly (0.603 against 0.634, p = 0.55). Any bilateral epoch gives 2 of 3 and 2 of 4 as well. Every trial with an epoch has the laser connected; with laser-connected trials only the accuracies and p values are the same.
deviations: The paper does not say which three rats were analysed, which sessions, or its test; the readings and the Fisher test were chosen before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: The neurons in the paper's published neural data can be linked to the dandiset's rats and sessions; they come from 199 sessions of 7 rats.
outcomes.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 2 (n = 199 sessions, n = 7 rats); the paper's data/neural_data and data/rat_for_each_neuron.mat at GitHub commit 0ea8fdb
outcomes.quote: we recorded from n = 3,495 putative single neurons during n = 199 sessions from n = 7 rats
outcomes.notes: All 7 rats are in the dandiset and every cell file names one of them. Under the criterion's rule (the cell's trials equal a contiguous run of one session's valid trials) 2,371 of 3,495 cells (0.678) match one session and none matches more than one; they come from 110 sessions against 199. With gaps allowed (a variant) 3,269 cells (0.935) match exactly one session, from 112 sessions; 226 cells match none, 189 of them P100's. The neural files leave out some trials of a session, so the contiguous rule is stricter than needed, but neither rule finds 199 sessions. Searching every TaskSwitch protocol (adding P100's 13 TaskSwitch4repeat sessions) gives 2,425 contiguous matches (0.694) from 113 sessions and 3,349 with gaps (0.958) from 115; the 146 cells left share a median 0.43 of their 8-trial windows with their best session, and 61 of those 64 best sessions are already matched.
deviations: The neural files carry no session identifier; cells are matched by their trial sequence.

outcomes.statement: The recordings yielded 3,495 putative single units, 2,047, 832, 258, 94 and 54 from five rats in FOF and 112 and 98 from two rats in mPFC.
outcomes.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 2; Methods, Analysis of neural data, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: In total, 3,495 putative single units were recorded from 5 rats in FOF (number of units in each rat: 2,047, 832, 258, 94, 54), while 210 units were recorded from 2 rats in mPFC (number of units in each rat: 112, 98)
outcomes.notes: The cell files hold 3,495 units, FOF 2,047 (P100), 832 (P059), 258 (P055), 94 (P095) and 54 (P049), mPFC 112 (P101) and 98 (P102), and rat_for_each_neuron.mat agrees with every file. The Methods sentence that puts all 3,495 in FOF counts the 210 mPFC units as well.

outcomes.statement: Neural slope indices vary across rats and features, with no apparent correlation between the location and frequency indices across the seven recorded rats.
outcomes.source: Results, Pulse analyses distinguish solutions, paragraph 2; Figure 3h
outcomes.quote: Instead, there was high variability across rats in this measure, and even across features within a single rat; no apparent correlation between the LOC and FRQ slope indices was visible
outcomes.notes: Neural slope indices range from -0.221 to 1.728 (location) and 0.465 to 1.500 (frequency); across the 7 rats r = -0.177 (95% CI -0.821 to 0.665), p = 0.704. The Methods say differential pulse responses only showed positive (or zero) slope indices; three location indices here are negative (P049 -0.221, P101 -0.045, P095 -0.007). The criterion does not test this.
deviations: The per-neuron kernels are the paper's fitted ones from its repository; the GLM was not refitted from spikes.
The paper gives no test; a two-sided Pearson correlation was chosen before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: Choice axes estimated separately in the two contexts are essentially parallel (average angle 1.6 degrees, not different from 0 in 6 of 7 rats).
outcomes.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 3; Extended Data Figure 5
outcomes.quote: we found that the choice axes, estimated separately for each of the two contexts, were essentially parallel (average angle between contexts = 1.6°; not significantly different from 0 (P > 0.1) for 6 out of 7 rats
outcomes.notes: By ExtDataFigure5ag.m on the paper's per-context kernels, the angle the code plots (the two context choice axes projected on the first 3 principal components of both contexts' choice kernels, folded to at most 90 degrees) is 5.53, 7.91, 4.49, 1.82, 1.12, 4.25 and 8.00 degrees (P049, P055, P059, P095, P100, P101, P102), mean 4.73, against the reported 1.6 (tolerance 1.44 to 1.76); no rat is in the tolerance. The 3 components explain 0.85 to 0.94 of the variance. The full-space angle, which the code computes first and overwrites, averages 40.34 (29.43 folded). All units of each rat have fits in both contexts. The reported test against 0 (not different from 0 in 6 of 7 rats) is a permutation test the Methods describe, shuffling the trials' context labels and recomputing both axes; it is not in the repository's code and needs the per-neuron kernels refitted for every shuffle, so it was not run.
deviations: The criterion was corrected after the first verification round to follow the angle the code plots; it first described only the full-space angle, now a variant. Both are outside the tolerance.

outcomes.statement: The behavioural slope index and the neural slope index are anti-correlated across rats and features (r = -0.73, P < 0.01), and for location (r = -0.71) and frequency (r = -0.71) alone (P < 0.1).
outcomes.source: Results, Linking neural and behaviour variability, paragraph 1; Figure 5d
outcomes.quote: We found robust support in the data for the theoretical prediction that the two measures should be correlated ... with the correlation also holding for LOC evidence alone ... or for FRQ evidence alone
outcomes.notes: Behavioural slope indices from the dandiset (Methods selection, bins 14 to 26) against neural indices from the paper's kernels give r = -0.697 over 14 values (95% CI -0.896 to -0.264), p = 0.0056, within -0.803 to -0.657. Location alone r = -0.675 (p = 0.096), frequency alone r = -0.772 (p = 0.042); the paper reports -0.71 for each with P < 0.1, and both hold at that level. With the code's 0.65 and 0.6 selection and penalty 200, r = -0.765 (p = 0.0014), and the paper's saved behavioural indices give -0.768. The match of neurons to rats, which this claim needs, holds for every cell; the session-level link that fails in neural-link is not used here.
deviations: The Methods selection keeps 23,014 and 25,847 trials of P049 and P059 against 135,001 and 162,317 under the code's selection, and their location indices change sign (0.131 against -0.432, 1.292 against -0.613).
Neural kernels are the paper's fitted ones, not refitted from spikes.

The result is close to the tolerance and depends on P049 and P059. With those two rats from the code's selection r = -0.834, and with the code's selection and cross-validated penalty r = -0.830, both beyond the tolerance on the negative side; leaving out one rat at a time gives -0.655 to -0.895, inside the tolerance for 4 of 7. All five 14-point correlations shown are negative with p < 0.01.

outcomes.statement: Choice-related population activity in FOF evolves along an essentially one-dimensional line during the stimulus (73.3% of variance; 81.3% for the two-dimensional choice subspace).
outcomes.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 3; Figure 1e
outcomes.quote: the two-dimensional subspace that best accounts for the contribution of the animal’s choice to the neural activity (accounting for 81.3% of the variance) ... this choice-related information in firing rates evolved along an essentially one-dimensional straight line in neural space (accounting for 73.3% of the variance)
outcomes.notes: Figure1e.m projects the per-context choice kernels on principal components but computes neither 81.3% nor 73.3%, and the text does not say which kernels, time window or normalisation the percentages refer to. The data (combined_kernels_per_context.mat, and the mTDR fits in data/Arrays_Pagan) are public in the paper's repository.

outcomes.statement: In FOF, trajectories for different evidence strengths separate along each sensory axis whether the feature is relevant or irrelevant, so irrelevant information is not gated out before frontal cortex.
outcomes.source: Results, Flexible evidence accumulation in rats, paragraph 2; Figure 1f
outcomes.quote: We found that trajectories for different evidence strengths were clearly separated along the axis of each sensory feature ... This was true regardless of whether the feature was relevant or irrelevant
outcomes.notes: Needs the mTDR fits of the MATLAB toolbox in the repository's mbtdr folder (with minFunc) on data/Arrays_Pagan. MATLAB cannot be installed in the entry's locked Python environment and the toolbox was not ported.

outcomes.statement: RNNs trained by backpropagation through time favour selection vector modulation.
outcomes.source: Figure 3a
outcomes.quote: Distribution of 1,000 RNNs trained using backpropagation through time: networks favoured SVM
outcomes.notes: Needs 1,000 RNNs trained by backpropagation through time (train_model.py in flexible_decision_making_rnn at commit 13cd245) and their linearisation; the repository holds three trained models. Training them is far beyond the 30-minute limit.

outcomes.statement: In RNNs engineered across the solution space, neural and behavioural slope indices are tightly anti-correlated.
outcomes.source: Figure 5c
outcomes.quote: RNN models follow the theoretical prediction, with anti-correlated slope indices for neural differential pulse kernels and differential behavioural kernels
outcomes.notes: The engineered RNNs and their pulse and behavioural kernels are built by MATLAB scripts (handcraft_model.m and others in flexible_decision_making_rnn at commit 13cd245), which cannot run in the entry's environment and were not ported.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds only the behaviour. The electrophysiology behind Figures 1d to 1f, 3h and 5d (3,495 units from 7 rats) is not in it; it is public only in the paper's GitHub repository, as one MATLAB file per unit with binned spike counts, without raw data or spike sorting output.

Nothing links the paper's units to dandiset sessions. Matched by trial sequence, 3,269 of 3,495 units fall in exactly one dandiset session when gaps are allowed (2,371 without gaps), from 112 sessions, where the paper reports 199; 226 units match no session. Searching every TaskSwitch protocol gives 3,349 units from 115 sessions, and 146 unmatched.
Every optogenetic epoch gives a wavelength of 473 nm; Extended Data Figure 4 says 450 nm, and the conversion's documentation says the value was corrected to 450.
Optogenetic epochs are present for four rats (P116, P124, P127, P131), where the paper reports three; nothing in the dandiset or the paper says which three were analysed.

The dates of birth give ages of 3.0 to 39.1 months at the sessions the paper's selection keeps (18 rats younger than 5.4 months at some), where the Methods state 6 to 24 months. Either the dates of birth or the stated ages are wrong. The dates of birth put 25 rats at 1.6 to 2.7 months at their first session; P189's (2018-02-21) puts it at 14.1 months on the day P187, born 2019-02-21, starts, and may be a year early.

Thirteen task sessions (1 to 3 trials each) lack HistorySection_result_history or a pulse column, and 95 of the other 15,400 lack HistorySection_hit_history. Where both outcome columns exist they agree on every trial.
One session of the paper's tables with 27 valid trials, P189 TaskSwitch6-210516a, is not in the dandiset; the conversion's notes list it among aborted sessions left out.
Six task sessions of P187 and P189 (TaskSwitch6, 2021) are in the dandiset but not in the paper's tables; five of them pass the Methods selection, adding 1,442 and 609 trials to those rats.
HistorySection_gammafreq_history, a signed strength, is stored as uint8 or int16 in 570 files; in all of them its values equal the float gamma_freq, so nothing was lost.

The paper's code also requires a per-session `good` flag that the Methods do not describe and the dandiset does not hold, and caps relative weights at 1; neither changes the selection except for one P059 session.

The Methods describe ridge regression with the regulariser chosen by cross-validation; the code adds a fixed penalty of 200 on squared differences of neighbouring weights. The code also uses looser selections (0.65 correct and 0.6 index) for the recorded rats in Figure 5d and for Extended Data Figure 1e than the Methods' 0.7.

The paper's own code (ExtDataFigure5ag.m), applied to its own fitted per-context kernels, gives angles of 1.1 to 8.0 degrees between the context choice axes (mean 4.7), not the reported average of 1.6 degrees. The permutation test of each angle against 0 that the Methods describe is not in the code.

The Methods say 3,495 units were recorded from 5 rats in FOF and list FOF counts that sum to 3,285; the 3,495 include the 210 mPFC units. The main text calls a converging differential behavioural kernel a slope index above 0, while the Methods and the code give converging kernels negative indices, as the data have.

attempts.label: DANDI:001616
attempts.paper_title: Decoding movie content from neuronal population activity in the human medial temporal lobe
attempts.entry_title: Single units of the human medial temporal lobe during a full-length movie (Gerken, Darcher et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Gerken, Darcher et al. (eLife reviewed preprint 106758, 2025) on dandiset 001616 (SUMMER), which holds 2286 units from 29 patients watching "500 Days of Summer" with 53 frame-wise annotations. It counts units responsive to the onsets of movie features, runs the cluster permutation test by region, and decodes characters, location and cuts with the paper's logistic regression, pooled, per patient, per region and on subsets of units. The paper's LSTM is not run.

outcomes.statement: The data are 2286 single and multi-units from 29 patients (17 female), 30 to 137 units per patient, in the amygdala (580), hippocampus (794), entorhinal cortex (440), parahippocampal cortex (373) and piriform cortex (99).
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 1; Figure 1d; Results, Patient-wise decoding performance, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: We recorded from 29 patients (17 female ... a total of 2286 single- and multi-neurons across the amygdala (A; 580 neurons, 25.37%), hippocampus (H; 794, 34.73%), entorhinal cortex (EC; 440, 19.25%), parahippocampal cortex (PHC; 373, 16.32%), and piriform cortex (PIC; 99, 4.33%) ... units per patient range from 30 to 137
outcomes.notes: 29 patients, 2286 units and 17 female patients, as stated, with 30 to 137 units per patient. With AH, MH and PH grouped as hippocampus (the dataset's code), the regions hold A 559 (paper 580), H 846 (794), EC 493 (440), PHC 293 (373) and PIC 68 (99), and 27 units lie in FF, LG and PRC. A and H are within 10%; EC, PHC and PIC are not. Every unit's region matches that of its electrode.
deviations: Regions are read from the dandiset's `brain_region` and grouped as in the dataset's code; the paper gives no mapping.

outcomes.statement: Over half of the parahippocampal neurons responded to camera cuts (193 of 373, 51.74%).
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulus-aligned responsive neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 2b; Table S1
outcomes.quote: Over half of the parahippocampal neurons responded to Camera Cuts during the movie (193/373, 51.74%
outcomes.notes: The Methods' test counts 222 of 293 PHC units (75.77%) responsive at alpha 0.001 and 228 (77.82%) at 0.01 (paper 193 of 373, 51.74%). The same test counts 72.35% of PHC units and 68.4% of all units responsive at random event times (69.2% in the per-label check with 884 random times), and all synthetic Poisson units at 2 Hz with 884 random events, so its false-positive rate is far from its alpha and the procedure differs from the paper's. The test compares integer counts in 100 ms bins with the baseline mean per 100 ms across hundreds of trials, which a signed-rank test finds different even without a response. The dataset code's ZETA test (responsive_zeta_cuts.ipynb, all units) is not anticonservative (none of 400 units at random times at alpha 0.001, 1.0% at 0.01) and finds 35 of 293 PHC units (11.95%) at 0.001 and 67 (22.87%) at 0.01, below the paper's fraction; neither test as run here gives the paper's count.
deviations: The responsive-unit test follows the Methods as fixed in the claims file (baseline count over -1000 to 0 ms divided by 10, 19 overlapping 100 ms bins, two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank, Simes); the Methods do not say more.
The ZETA variant uses 100 resamplings in place of the code's 1000, for time; for PHC units and scene cuts, 1000 resamplings change the counts by 1 and 2 units.
The fraction is compared, as the dandiset's PHC holds 293 units against the paper's 373.

outcomes.statement: Camera cuts evoked responses in a large share of neurons in every region (amygdala 46.90%, entorhinal cortex 45.68%, hippocampus 38.92%).
outcomes.source: Table S1; Results, Stimulus-aligned responsive neurons, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: We found individual neurons with significant stimulus-evoked responses in all regions for visual transitions
outcomes.notes: Depends on fig2b-phc-camera-cuts. The miscalibrated test counts A 73.70%, EC 73.63%, H 64.54% and PHC 75.77% at alpha 0.001 (paper 46.90, 45.68, 38.92, 51.74%), and 62 to 73% of each region at random times. The ZETA test of the dataset's code counts A 3.22%, EC 0.61%, H 1.30% and PHC 11.95% (responsive_zeta_cuts.ipynb).
deviations: The responsive-unit test follows the Methods as fixed in the claims file (baseline count over -1000 to 0 ms divided by 10, 19 overlapping 100 ms bins, two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank, Simes); the Methods do not say more.

outcomes.statement: Few parahippocampal neurons responded to scene cuts (25 of 373, 6.70%), but the modulation was consistent across the responsive neurons (cluster permutation test, p = 0.018).
outcomes.source: Results, Stimulus-aligned responsive neurons, paragraph 1; Figure 2b; Table S1
outcomes.quote: Comparatively few parahippocampal neurons responded to Scene Cuts (25/373, 6.70%), although there was nonetheless a consistent pattern of modulation across responsive neurons (p = 0.018, cluster permutation test)

With this split the largest cluster has p = 0.055 with the Methods' z-scoring and p = 0.020 with the code's per-trial z-scoring at alpha 0.001, and there is no cluster at 0.01. The ZETA test finds 12 of 293 (4.10%) at 0.001 and 29 (9.90%) at 0.01, either side of the tolerance of 4.16 to 9.24%; with 1000 resamplings 11 and 31 (responsive_zeta_cuts.ipynb).

The code's onset rule (no minimum duration) changes them little (1019 and 1191). The ZETA test of the dataset's code, conservative at random times, counts 11 for Summer and 13 for Tom (responsive_zeta_labels.ipynb), and 79 for camera cuts (paper 1025).

Training 700 epochs per label and fold on a CPU would also exceed the time limit; this was not tried. findings.statement: The units' `brain_region` gives A 559, hippocampus 846 (AH 418, MH 16, PH 412), EC 493, PHC 293 and PIC 68 units, and 27 in FF, LG and PRC, where the paper reports A 580, H 794, EC 440, PHC 373 and PIC 99 for the same 2286 units. Neither the dandiset nor the paper maps one assignment to the other, so the paper's region analyses cannot be repeated on the paper's regions.
Spike times in the units table are in milliseconds (its description says so), where NWB requires seconds; the watchlogs' recording times are also in milliseconds.
The start and stop columns of `annotations_patient_aligned` are described as seconds but hold milliseconds of the recording clock, as the table's own description says.

The face labels (summer-faces, tom-faces and others) hold only 0 and 1. The Methods define face labels with frames excluded when a face is neither shown nor clearly absent; those frames cannot be identified.

Published version 0.260519.1133 holds 57 files, the 29 of the later version and 28 older copies (`ses-1_behavior+ecephys`) with the same units and spike times, one per patient except patient 3. Version 0.260702.0824 holds each recording once.

The dataset's code identifies responsive units with the ZETA test (zetapy; alpha 0.01 in its notebook), where the Methods describe a bin-wise Wilcoxon signed-rank test with Simes correction. With ZETA, 79 units respond to camera cuts at alpha 0.001 (Table S1 1025), 11 to Summer (46) and 13 to Tom (216), and 11.95% of PHC units to camera cuts (51.74%).

The responsive-unit test as the Methods describe it (spike counts in 19 bins of 100 ms against the baseline count per 100 ms, signed-rank across pseudo-trials, Simes) counts 68% of units responsive at random event times on this data with 884 events, and 10 to 55% with as many as each label's onsets, so the procedure behind Figure 2 and Table S1 cannot be recovered from the text. The ZETA test of the dataset's code does not give the paper's counts either. The paper's LSTM code and its per-label hyperparameters are not published.
The threshold for responsive units is alpha 0.01 in the Methods and 0.001 in the Results, the Figure 2 legend and Table S1; the cluster test section splits units at p 0.01.
The Results give the 29 patients' ages as 22 to 63; the Methods give 19 to 62 for all 46 patients recorded. The dandiset's 29 patients are 19 to 62.
The dandiset has 958 camera cuts in the 83-minute film, one every 5.25 s; the supplement says one every 3 s.

The training code of the dataset's repository (ML_framework/nwb_loading/nwb_loading.py, get_unit_ids_for_patient_nwb) compares `brain_region` with the region group name in place of its subregions; no unit is labelled `H`, so asking for the hippocampus selects no unit.

Neither the dandiset nor the paper states that subject ids are the paper's patient numbers. Taking them as such, the patients the paper names in Figure 4 are among the best here (7 of 8 above kappa 0.2).
