attempts.label: DANDI:001888
attempts.paper_title: Absence seizures and sleep-wake abnormalities in a rat model of GRIN2B neurodevelopmental disorder
attempts.entry_title: Absence seizures and sleep in Grin2b+/- rats (Hristova, Fasol et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the EEG findings of Hristova, Fasol et al. (2025) on dandiset 001888, which holds the 24-h wireless EEG and EMG recordings, sleep scores and SWD events of 14 Grin2b+/- rats, 2 wild type rats and one rat without genotype. It compares SWD number, duration and timing, sleep-wake amounts and bouts, state spectra computed from the raw EEG, the state in which SWDs start, and the correlation of SWD time with sleep measures. The western blots, development measures, visual scoring and pharmacology recordings of the paper are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Hristova, Fasol et al. (2025) from dandiset 001888

outcomes.statement: Grin2b+/- rats have more SWDs than WT across the 24-h day; hour of day has no effect and does not interact with genotype (linear mixed model, genotype F = 55.36, p < .00001; hour p = .16; interaction p = .49).
outcomes.source: Figure 2B
outcomes.quote: Hour of the day had no effect on the number of seizures between the two genotypes, and Grin2b+/− rats had significantly more seizures overall when compared to wild‐type littermates
outcomes.notes: Split-plot ANOVA on SWDs per ZT hour, genotype F = 11.45, p = 0.0045 (Het higher), hour p = 0.069, interaction p = 0.9998. Het hourly means 19.2 to 37.8, WT 0 to 8.2. With GRIN2B-132 as WT or Het the genotype effect holds (p = 0.0011, 0.013) and hour reaches p = 0.041. Without GRIN2B-228, GRIN2B-238 or both, genotype p = 0.0001, 0.048 and 0.0036, hour p 0.070 to 0.074. A fitted random-intercept model (MixedLM) gives the same genotype and interaction statistics. The paper's genotype F is 55.36 with 9 WT; here there are 2.
deviations: Two WT rats, where the paper has nine.
The random-intercept mixed model is tested as a split-plot ANOVA.

outcomes.statement: Grin2b+/- rats have more SWDs over 24 h than WT (Wilcoxon rank-sum, W = 4.5, p = .0002).
outcomes.source: Figure 2C, left
outcomes.quote: The above reflected a statistically significant increase in the total number of SWDs over the full 24 h in Grin2b+/− rats when compared to wild‐type
outcomes.notes: Het 690.6 SWDs per day, WT 56.3 (GRIN2B-238 none, GRIN2B-240 112.5); W = 1, p = 0.047. GRIN2B-240 ranks above one Het, GRIN2B-228, which has 1 SWD per day. With GRIN2B-132 as WT p = 0.020, as Het p = 0.062. Without GRIN2B-228 p = 0.034 (W = 0); with GRIN2B-238 left out one WT remains and p = 0.20.
deviations: Two WT rats, where the paper has nine.

outcomes.statement: SWDs are longer on average in Grin2b+/- rats than in WT (two-sample t test, df = 22, T = -5.26, p = .00003).
outcomes.source: Figure 2C, middle
outcomes.quote: Furthermore, Grin2b+/− rats had a longer average SWD duration and total SWD duration than
outcomes.notes: Het mean SWD duration 4.54 s against 1.47 s in GRIN2B-240, the only WT rat with SWDs; t test p = 0.16 (df 13). With GRIN2B-132 (1.70 s) as WT p = 0.062; without GRIN2B-228 p = 0.090. A t test against a single WT value says little either way.
deviations: One WT rat has SWDs, so the WT group has one value.

outcomes.statement: The total time in SWDs over 24 h is higher in Grin2b+/- rats than in WT (Wilcoxon rank-sum, W = 5.5, p = .0002).
outcomes.source: Figure 2C, right
outcomes.quote: Furthermore, Grin2b+/− rats had a longer average SWD duration and total SWD duration than
outcomes.notes: Het 57.77 min per day, WT 1.37 min; W = 1, p = 0.033. With GRIN2B-132 as WT p = 0.012, as Het p = 0.029. Without GRIN2B-228 p = 0.019; with GRIN2B-238 left out one WT remains and p = 0.27.
deviations: Two WT rats, where the paper has nine.

outcomes.statement: Over 24 h, Grin2b+/- rats spend on average 59.97 min in SWDs, while WT littermates average less than a minute.
outcomes.source: Discussion, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Over 24 h, Grin2b+/− mutants had on average of 59.97 min of SWDs, almost an entire hour of the day in an absence seizure. In contrast, wild‐type littermates had average totals of less than a minute.
outcomes.notes: The Het mean of 57.77 min per day (SEM 9.04, 14 rats) is within 59.97 +- 6.0. The WT mean is 1.37 min (0 and 2.75), not below 1 min. Without GRIN2B-228 the Het mean is 62.21, also within tolerance; without GRIN2B-238 the WT mean is 2.75. Counting the epochs SWD events overlap as 5 s each gives 110.57 min, and counting the epochs the scorer flags gives 60.2 min, so the paper's number fits both the event durations and the flags.
deviations: Two WT rats, where the paper has nine; the WT part rests on GRIN2B-240 alone.

outcomes.statement: The number of SWDs does not differ between the light and dark phases, and Grin2b+/- rats have more SWDs than WT in both (linear mixed model, genotype p < .00001, phase p = .28, interaction p = .53).
outcomes.source: Figure S5A; Results, Absence seizures in Grin2b+/- rats, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Number of SWD events during the light and dark phases did not differ significantly but were increased significantly in Grin2b+/− rats
outcomes.notes: Phase F = 1.19, p = 0.29; genotype F = 11.45, p = 0.0045; interaction p = 0.86. Het 316.7 SWDs in the light and 373.9 in the dark, WT 12.5 and 43.8. Within Het, light minus dark median -79.8 (signed-rank p = 0.19). Without GRIN2B-228, GRIN2B-238 or both, phase p = 0.30 and genotype p = 0.0001, 0.048 and 0.0036.
deviations: Two WT rats; the mixed model is tested as a split-plot ANOVA.

outcomes.statement: Sex does not affect the number, mean duration or total duration of SWDs (two-way ANOVA sex x genotype, sex p = .74, .99 and .99).
outcomes.source: Figure S8B
outcomes.quote: Grin2b+/− rats had a statistically greater number of SWDs, with longer average and total durations than Grin2b+/+ rats, and these differences were not influenced by the animals’ sex

statistics.about: effect of sex on SWD number
statistics.n: 3 male and 6 female wild-type, 8 male and 7 female Grin2b+/- rats

statistics.about: effect of sex on SWD average duration
statistics.n: 3 male and 6 female wild-type, 8 male and 7 female Grin2b+/- rats

statistics.about: effect of sex on total SWD duration
statistics.n: 3 male and 6 female wild-type, 8 male and 7 female Grin2b+/- rats

outcomes.notes: Sex term p = 0.29, 0.94 and 0.78 for number, mean duration and total duration. Within Het, females 763.3 SWDs per day against 617.9 in males (t test p = 0.31), 4.59 against 4.50 s, 60.3 against 55.2 min. Without GRIN2B-228, GRIN2B-238 or both the sex terms have p from 0.31 to 0.94.
deviations: The ANOVA has no sex by genotype interaction, as both WT are female; the paper's model has one.

outcomes.statement: The EEG spectrum during SWDs has a clear peak in the theta range with a harmonic, in both genotypes.
outcomes.source: Figure 2D; Results, Absence seizures in Grin2b+/- rats, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: In SWD epoch averages we found a clear peak in the theta frequency range with a secondary harmonic in both genotypes
outcomes.notes: All 15 rats with at least 5 usable SWD epochs in the raw windows (13 Het, the WT GRIN2B-240 and GRIN2B-132) have a peak at 7.0 to 8.0 Hz and another at 14.0 to 16.0 Hz. The stored spectra show peaks near the same frequencies (7.4 to 8.2 and 14.4 to 16.2 Hz). GRIN2B-240 has 18 usable SWD epochs.
deviations: Spectra from about 4.8 h of raw EEG per rat (one 24-min chunk at six ZT hours of each day), on the SWD-detection channel, with a 2-s Welch segment chosen here.
The peak rule (local maximum with prominence 0.1 in log10 power, harmonic within 1 Hz of twice the peak) was chosen here; the paper describes the peak by eye.

outcomes.statement: Delta power during SWDs is higher in Grin2b+/- rats than in WT (two-way ANOVA genotype x band, interaction p = .015; Tukey delta p = .039).
outcomes.source: Figure 2E
outcomes.quote: Quantification of average power in commonly used frequency bands during SWDs, showing an increased delta power in Grin2b+/− rats
outcomes.notes: Only one WT rat (GRIN2B-240) has SWDs; GRIN2B-238 has none in either day, and the paper's other seven WT rats are not in the dandiset. The claim's rule needs at least two animals per genotype (also other, too few animals). A search of the archive for GRIN2B, Gonzalez-Sulser and the paper's DOI finds only this dandiset. As an illustration only, with GRIN2B-132 (no genotype) counted as WT, Het SWD delta power is lower than WT (-0.34, Tukey p = 1.0), against the paper's direction.

outcomes.statement: Grin2b+/- rats have less REM sleep per hour than WT across the day, and the reduction is not specific to certain hours (linear mixed model, genotype F = 9.98, p = .0045; hour x genotype p = .53).
outcomes.source: Figure 3D
outcomes.quote: Grin2b+/− rats had overall significantly less REM sleep compared to wild‐type littermates, and this reduction was not specific to certain hours of the day
outcomes.notes: Genotype F = 4.69, p = 0.048 (Het lower); interaction p = 0.096. At the threshold; with GRIN2B-132 as WT p = 0.19, as Het p = 0.038 (interaction p = 0.071); with the scorer's flags or the stored scores p = 0.049 and 0.050. Without GRIN2B-228 genotype p = 0.060; without GRIN2B-238 or both genotype p = 0.019 and 0.025 but the interaction has p = 0.0001 and 0.00005. The outcome holds with all 16 rats and with GRIN2B-132 counted as Het, and not without GRIN2B-228 or GRIN2B-238. A fitted mixed model (MixedLM) gives genotype Wald p = 0.030 and interaction p = 0.086.
deviations: Two WT rats; the mixed model is tested as a split-plot ANOVA.
SWD epochs are the epochs SWD events overlap; the lab's scorer uses its per-epoch flags.

outcomes.statement: Grin2b+/- rats spend less total time in REM sleep over 24 h than WT (two-sample t test, df = 22, T = 3.16, p = .0045).
outcomes.source: Figure 3G, left
outcomes.quote: Similarly, Grin2b+/− rats spent less total time in REM sleep than wild‐type littermate controls when total minutes per animal were analyzed
outcomes.notes: Het 44.8 min of REM per day, WT 69.7 (54.3 and 85.2); t = 2.16, df 14, p = 0.048. With GRIN2B-132 as WT p = 0.19, as Het p = 0.038; SWD-epoch variants p = 0.049 and 0.050, and 0.049 with only the SWD time removed. Without GRIN2B-228 p = 0.060; without GRIN2B-238 p = 0.019.
deviations: Two WT rats, where the paper has nine.

outcomes.statement: Grin2b+/- rats have fewer REM bouts than WT (two-sample t test, df = 22, T = 3.94, p = .00069).
outcomes.source: Figure 3G, middle
outcomes.quote: It is likely that this reduction was due to fewer REM sleep bouts in Grin2b+/− animals
outcomes.notes: Het 37.9 REM bouts per day, WT 74.0; t = 4.12, df 14, p = 0.0010. Both WT have more bouts than every Het. With GRIN2B-132 as WT p = 0.068. Without GRIN2B-228, GRIN2B-238 or both p <= 0.0017; with bouts not split by SWD epochs p = 0.0007.
deviations: Two WT rats; the bout definition (runs of one state, ended by SWD epochs) was chosen here.

outcomes.statement: REM bouts are longer on average in Grin2b+/- rats than in WT (Wilcoxon rank-sum, W = 33, p = .043).
outcomes.source: Figure 3G, right; Results, Sleep–wake abnormalities in Grin2b+/- rats, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Of interest, the average duration of REM sleep bouts was longer for Grin2b+/− animals
outcomes.notes: Het REM bouts 71.9 s, WT 56.8 s; W = 2, p = 0.067. With GRIN2B-132 (95.5 s) as WT the difference is 2.2 s (p = 0.59). Without GRIN2B-228 p = 0.076; with bouts not split by SWD epochs p = 0.067.
deviations: Two WT rats; bout definition chosen here.

outcomes.statement: Total NREM sleep over 24 h does not differ between genotypes (two-sample t test, df = 22, T = -.09, p = .93).
outcomes.source: Figure 3H, left
outcomes.quote: Similarly, there was no difference between Grin2b+/− and ... rats in the total amount of time spent in NREM sleep over the full 24 h
outcomes.notes: Het 450.5 min, WT 419.3 min, difference 31.2 min; t = -1.29, p = 0.22. With GRIN2B-132 as WT the difference is 48.4 min, p = 0.035. Without GRIN2B-238 the Het have 17.6 min less (p = 0.54); with only the SWD time removed p = 0.19. With two WT the test has little power to find a difference.
deviations: Two WT rats, where the paper has nine.

outcomes.statement: Grin2b+/- rats have fewer NREM bouts, which are longer, than WT (Wilcoxon rank-sum, bouts W = 29.5, p = .025; mean bout duration W = 26, p = .015).
outcomes.source: Figure 3H, middle and right
outcomes.quote: Nonetheless, Grin2b+/− rats demonstrated abnormal NREM distributions when compared to ... littermates, as they had statistically fewer NREM bouts, which where longer in average duration
outcomes.notes: Mean NREM bout duration Het 127.1 s, WT 92.3 s, W = 0, p = 0.017. Number of NREM bouts Het 218.5, WT 273.0 per day, W = 25, p = 0.10. With the scorer's flags, the stored scores or bouts not split by SWD epochs both parts have p < 0.05 (bouts p = 0.032). Without GRIN2B-228 bouts p = 0.11, duration p = 0.019.
deviations: Two WT rats; bout definition chosen here.

outcomes.statement: Grin2b+/- rats spend less total time awake over 24 h than WT (Welch t test, df = 10.25, T = 2.26, p = .047).
outcomes.source: Figure 3I, left; Results, Sleep–wake abnormalities in Grin2b+/- rats, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: When compared to wild‐type littermates, the total minutes awake was significantly reduced in Grin2b+/− rats
outcomes.notes: Het 834.1 min awake per day, WT 944.9, difference -110.8 min; Welch p = 0.35. With the scorer's flags -68.1 min (p = 0.49), with only the SWD time removed -65.5 min (p = 0.50), with the stored scores -10.8 min (p = 0.89), so most of the difference is SWD time removed from wake. Without GRIN2B-228 -121.2 min (p = 0.33).
deviations: Two WT rats; SWD epochs are the epochs SWD events overlap.

outcomes.statement: Grin2b+/- rats have more wake bouts of shorter duration than WT (Wilcoxon rank-sum, W = 18, p = .0035; Welch t test on mean bout duration, df = 8.91, T = 2.97, p = .016).
outcomes.source: Figure 3I, middle and right
outcomes.quote: When compared to wild‐type littermates, the total minutes awake was significantly reduced in Grin2b+/− rats, with mutants having more wake bouts of shorter duration
outcomes.notes: Het 559.4 wake bouts per day against WT 294.5 (W = 2, p = 0.067); mean wake bout 100.6 s against 206.2 s (Welch p = 0.31). With the stored scores, where SWD epochs count as wake, both reverse (190.8 against 241.0 bouts, p = 0.017; 304.2 against 239.2 s), and they reverse with bouts not split by SWD epochs too (186.3 against 241.0 bouts, p = 0.017; 275.4 against 237.7 s). The outcome rests on SWD epochs ending wake bouts, which follows the Methods' exclusion of SWD times but builds part of the difference in. Without GRIN2B-228 the bout count has p = 0.019.
deviations: Two WT rats; bout definition chosen here; SWD epochs end wake bouts.

outcomes.statement: EEG spectral power during REM sleep does not differ between genotypes (two-way ANOVA genotype x band, genotype p = .14, interaction p = .69).
outcomes.source: Figure 4A
outcomes.quote: No statistically significant differences were found between Grin2b+/− and ... rats during REM sleep
outcomes.notes: Normalized REM band power, genotype F = 3.30, p = 0.073; interaction p = 0.998; Het lower by 0.19 on average. Contiguous bands give genotype p = 0.034, SWD epochs from flags p < 0.0001, the stored spectra p = 0.17, the cleaner S1 channel p = 0.067; the slope rejection removes no epoch. Without GRIN2B-228 p = 0.094, without GRIN2B-238 p = 0.19. The windows cover a median of 5 to 10% of each state's epochs (1.1% of GRIN2B-129's REM). With two WT the test has little power, and the band ANOVA treats an animal's five bands as separate observations, as the paper's does.
deviations: Spectra from about 4.8 h of raw EEG per rat on the SWD-detection channel; the paper used one representative channel and all epochs.

Band limits (delta 1-4, theta 4-8, sigma 10-15, beta 15-30, gamma 30-48 Hz) and the Welch segment are not given in the paper. The spectral-slope rejection, read here as a slope below -5 of log10 power against log10 frequency or power at 1 Hz above 500 mV^2/Hz, removes no epoch.
The paper chose the S1 channel with fewer artefacts by eye; that choice is not in the dandiset. The main channel is S1_Tr_R, and the per-animal channel with fewer artefact epochs is a variant.

outcomes.statement: During NREM sleep Grin2b+/- rats have higher beta power than WT (two-way ANOVA genotype x band, interaction p = .038; Tukey beta p = .0008, other bands p >= .82).
outcomes.source: Figure 4B
outcomes.quote: In NREM sleep, Grin2b+/− animals had statistically higher beta power in comparison to wild‐type rats
outcomes.notes: NREM beta is lower in Het (difference -0.078 normalized, Tukey p = 1.0); interaction p = 0.90. Every variant with both WT (GRIN2B-132 either way, contiguous bands, SWD epochs from flags, slope rejection, cleaner S1 channel, stored spectra) has Het beta lower, by 0.0035 to 0.30. With GRIN2B-238 left out Het beta is higher in 7 of 12 variants, by 0.0032 to 0.147, with Tukey p >= 0.99 and interaction p >= 0.92.
deviations: As for fig4a-rem-spectrum; two WT rats.

outcomes.statement: During wake, spectral power is reduced in Grin2b+/- rats overall, without a difference in single bands (two-way ANOVA genotype x band, genotype p = .01, interaction p = .86).
outcomes.source: Figure 4C
outcomes.quote: In the wake state, spectral power was significantly reduced in Grin2b+/− rats relative to ... littermates, although this reduction was not restricted to individual frequency bands
outcomes.notes: Normalized wake power is higher in Het on average (+0.081; genotype F = 0.58, p = 0.45), and higher on average in every variant on the raw EEG with both WT (+0.0065 to +0.168). The stored spectra have Het lower on average (-0.027, p = 0.59; p = 0.0072 only with GRIN2B-132 counted as WT), as does the cleaner S1 channel without GRIN2B-238 (-0.0072, p = 0.93).
deviations: As for fig4a-rem-spectrum; two WT rats.

outcomes.statement: Over both genotypes, SWDs occur mostly in wake (94.8%), then NREM (4.4%), and rarely in REM sleep (0.5%).
outcomes.source: Figure 5A; Results, Brain state abnormalities in Grin2b+/- rats are not correlated with absence seizure activity, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Collectively for both genotypes, we observed that SWDs predominantly occurred during wake (94.8%), followed by NREM (4.4%) and scarcely during REM sleep (.5%)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a) gives wake 94.18%, NREM 5.55%, REM 0.27% over 16 rats with SWDs; wake is within tolerance and the order holds, NREM and REM are not. Reading (b) 92.87, 6.81, 0.32; (c) 91.17, 8.64, 0.19; (d) 89.27, 10.50, 0.23. Readings (c) and (d) follow the Supplementary Methods' rule. No reading puts all three within tolerance. Without GRIN2B-228 the values move by at most 0.6 percentage points.
deviations: The paper's text allows four readings of how the percentages are formed; all are shown.
Two of the paper's nine WT rats; GRIN2B-132 is included.

outcomes.statement: Compared with WT, Grin2b+/- rats have a higher share of SWDs in NREM and a lower share in wake (two-way ANOVA genotype x state, interaction p = .00008; Tukey NREM p = .0011, wake p = .0022).
outcomes.source: Figure 5A
outcomes.quote: Compared to wild‐type littermates, Grin2b+/− rats have fewer SWDs in wake and more SWDs in NREM
outcomes.notes: Only one WT rat has SWDs (GRIN2B-240, 0% of its SWDs after NREM), and the paper's other seven WT rats are not in the dandiset, so the per-state comparison between genotypes cannot be tested under the claim's rule of two animals per group (also other, too few animals). As an illustration only, with GRIN2B-132 (no genotype) counted as WT, 6.30% of Het SWDs follow NREM against 0.23% in the two WT (interaction p = 0.013, Tukey NREM p = 0.29).

outcomes.statement: All Grin2b+/- rats have SWDs that start at wake-NREM transitions, against 3 of 9 WT rats (Fisher's exact test, p = .00062).
outcomes.source: Figure 5C; Results, Brain state abnormalities in Grin2b+/- rats are not correlated with absence seizure activity, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: all Grin2b+/− rats had SWDs initiating at wake‐NREM transitions, whereas this was the case for only a small fraction of ... littermates (33.33%, 3/9 rats)
outcomes.notes: 13 of 14 Het rats have at least one SWD at a wake-NREM transition, 0 of 2 WT; Fisher p = 0.025. GRIN2B-228 (2 SWDs in two days, none after NREM) has none. The claim's statement that all Het have such SWDs does not hold for GRIN2B-228; it may not be one of the paper's rats. Without GRIN2B-228 13 of 13 Het count (Fisher p = 0.0095), which would meet the criterion; the outcome is judged on all 16 rats.
deviations: The definition of a wake-NREM transition (a wake epoch followed by an NREM epoch within the six epochs before the SWD) was chosen here.

outcomes.statement: In Grin2b+/- rats 24.2% of SWDs occur during the wake-NREM transition, similar to the 22.39% of the WT rats that have such SWDs (two-sample t test, p = .74).
outcomes.source: Results, Brain state abnormalities in Grin2b+/- rats are not correlated with absence seizure activity, paragraph 1; Figure S5B
outcomes.quote: 24.2% of SWDS in Grin2b+/− rats occurred during the wake‐NREM transitional period, which was similar to the 22.39% observed in
outcomes.notes: Reading (i), the share of NREM-initiated SWDs that are transitional, with an SWD initiated in NREM when any of the six epochs before it is NREM (the Supplementary Methods), gives 22.93% (SEM 1.97, 13 Het), within 24.2 +- 2.42. Reading (ii), the share of all SWDs, gives 2.23%. With NREM taken from the epoch before the SWD, the rule of the first criterion, reading (i) gives 36.31%. Leaving out GRIN2B-228 does not change reading (i). The claim's WT part is not tested, as no WT rat has transitional SWDs, so the WT value and the t test were not computed.
deviations: The denominator is not stated; two readings are shown.
The criterion's NREM rule was corrected after verification round 1, once the analysis had been seen, to the six-epoch rule the Supplementary Methods state; the first rule gave 36.31%.
The transition definition (a wake epoch followed by an NREM epoch within the six epochs before the SWD) was chosen here.

outcomes.statement: In Grin2b+/- rats, total SWD duration is negatively correlated with total time awake (Pearson, R = -.51, p = .048).
outcomes.source: Figure 5F, left
outcomes.quote: Quantification revealed total SWD duration is negatively correlated with total time awake
outcomes.notes: R = -0.81, p = 0.0005 over 14 Het (-0.82 with GRIN2B-132, -0.73 without GRIN2B-228). With the scorer's flags R = -0.75; with the stored scores R = -0.06 (p = 0.83); with only the SWD time removed from wake R = -0.74 (p = 0.0024). The correlation arises from SWD time being taken out of wake. In Het the SWD epochs removed total 110.6 min per day against 57.8 min of SWD time.
deviations: 14 Het, where the paper has 15.

outcomes.statement: In Grin2b+/- rats, total SWD duration is not correlated with total REM or NREM time, the number of REM, NREM or wake bouts, or the mean REM, NREM or wake bout duration (Pearson, all p >= .066).
outcomes.source: Figure 5D-F
outcomes.quote: Quantification revealed total SWD duration is negatively correlated with total time awake ... and is uncorrelated to all other sleep measurements
outcomes.notes: Two of the eight measures correlate with total SWD time, the number of wake bouts (R = 0.54, p = 0.046) and mean wake bout duration (R = -0.58, p = 0.028); the other six have p from 0.16 to 0.96. With the scorer's flags the same two correlate (R = 0.82, -0.72); with the stored scores, with bouts not split by SWD epochs or without GRIN2B-228 none does. The paper gives R = 0.17 and -0.25 for these two.
deviations: 14 Het; the criterion grades eight tests (none significant reproduced, one or two partial).

outcomes.statement: GluN2B protein is reduced by about 50% in somatosensory cortex and hippocampus of Grin2b+/- rats (homogenate t test p = .000104; synaptosome Wilcoxon p = .00094).
outcomes.source: Figure 1C; Figure S2C
outcomes.quote: Glun2B protein levels in homogenates and synaptosome fractions were reduced by ~50% in adult heterozygous knockout ... rats compared to wild‐types
outcomes.notes: The western blot quantification is not in the dandiset, which holds only EEG/EMG files, and the paper's data statement says raw data are available on request.

outcomes.statement: GluN2A, GluR1 and PSD95 expression are unchanged in Grin2b+/- rats.
outcomes.source: Figure 1D-F; Figure S2D-F
outcomes.quote: The expression of GluN2A, GluR1, and PSD95 synaptic proteins in Grin2b+/− rats was unaffected in the somatosensory cortex (Figure 1D–F) and the hippocampus (Figure S2D–F).
outcomes.notes: Western blot data not in the dandiset (see fig1c-glun2b-reduced).

outcomes.statement: Grin2b+/- rats survive, grow and develop motor reflexes like WT littermates (survival 48% and 52%; body weight, righting reflex and negative geotaxis do not differ).
outcomes.source: Results, Normal physical and motor development in Grin2b+/- rats, paragraph 1; Figure S4
outcomes.quote: Following weaning, survival rates were determined to be 48% for Grin2b+/− rats and 52% for ... Taken together, these findings indicate that Grin2b haploinsufficiency does not impair physical development or gross motor function

statistics.about: pup body weight, effect of genotype (Figure S4A)

findings.statement: The dandiset holds 2 of the paper's 9 analysed wild type rats (14 or 15 of its 15 Grin2b+/-), so genotype comparisons rest on two WT, one of which has no SWDs. The pharmacology and intrathalamic infusion recordings (Figures 6, 7, S11, S12), western blots (Figures 1, S2, S3), development measures (Figure S4) and the visual scoring used to validate the scorer (Table S1) are not in it. The paper says raw data are available on request.
GRIN2B-132 has no genotype and sex U, so it cannot be placed in either group. The conversion repository marks both as still to be confirmed by the lab.

The paper analysed 15 Grin2b+/- and 9 WT rats and excluded 4 and 9 descendants of one founder. The dandiset does not say which of its rats the paper analysed, and holds a Grin2b+/- rat (GRIN2B-228) with 1 SWD per day, unlike the paper's statement that all Grin2b+/- rats had SWDs at wake-NREM transitions.
The sleep_states description gives code 4 for SWD epochs, but no file holds code 4; the stored scores are the scorer's output before SWD epochs are set, so SWD epochs are scored as wake, NREM or REM.

swd_epoch_counts is described as the number of SWD events per 5-s epoch but holds the scorer's flags (6 for an SWD epoch, 4 otherwise). The flagged epochs cover a median of 51% (0 to 73%) of the epochs SWD events overlap, mostly the last epoch of each SWD, and only about a tenth of SWD onsets fall in a flagged epoch.

In seizure_totals_by_zt the per-hour SWD counts are in spike_wave_discharge, while number_of_seizure_events and Day hold the day's total in the first row and 0 elsewhere; the description itself marks the columns as unconfirmed.

sleep_state_power_spectra is described as a baseline-corrected PSD normalized to the average over states, with units to be confirmed. The lab's scorer writes the mean log10 multitaper amplitude referenced to each frequency's 5th percentile over the day, which is what the values (0 to about 1.6) fit; the paper's Welch spectra are not in the dandiset.

The raw EEG and EMG are stored as unsigned 12-bit codes with offset 0, so every channel reads about +8 mV of DC in volts. Signal loss is written as 32767 on all channels at once, and some files hold other values outside 0 to 4095; neither is described. In the windows read, 21 to 73% of 5-s epochs per rat contain such samples (73% for GRIN2B-238).
The dandiset's assets summary counts 16 files and 16 subjects, while the draft holds 17 NWB files of 17 rats.

The Methods exclude SWD times from the sleep states, while the lab's scorer replaces only the flagged epochs, which cover about half of the epochs SWD events overlap. The paper's wake results depend on this; with the stored scores (SWD epochs as wake) the wake bout differences reverse and the correlation of SWD time with wake time disappears.

In the Figure 5 legend, NREM time gives T = -1.47 with R = -0.13 and df = 13, which implies T = -0.47; REM bouts give T = 0.704 with R = -0.19, of opposite sign; and REM bout duration and wake bouts have identical statistics (T = 0.61, R = 0.17, p = 0.55). The Figure 5A ANOVA gives genotype F = 1 with p = 0.98, which do not match for df = 1.

The Figure 3 legend says no net differences between genotypes were observed for wake, while reporting a genotype effect on hourly wake time of F = 7.14, p = 0.014, and the Results say Grin2b+/- rats spent less time awake.

The Supplementary Methods chose, by eye and per animal, the S1 EEG channel (left or right) and the EMG channel with fewer artefacts for sleep scoring; the dandiset does not record which channels were used.
The paper does not give its frequency band limits, Welch segment length, bout definition or the rule for wake-NREM transitions, and neither linked repository holds the statistics or figure code.

attempts.entry_title: LRRK2-G2019S and dopamine release from Anxa1+ and Calb1+ neurons (Chen, He et al. 2026)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Chen, He et al. (2026). On dandiset 001933, which holds GRAB-DA3m fiber photometry in the dorsal striatum during optogenetic stimulation of Anxa1+ (15 mice) or Calb1+ (12 mice) SNc dopamine neurons in LRRK2-WT and LRRK2-G2019S mice, it compares evoked and spontaneous dopamine release between genotypes, per power and per mouse, and links the dandiset to the paper's published source data. The imaging, proteomics and western blots of Figures 1 to 5 are not in the dandiset; their claims are tested on the data the paper deposited on Zenodo, in PRIDE and in the BioImage Archive, and counted apart.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Chen, He et al. (2026) from dandiset 001933

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's recordings are those behind the paper's Figure 6 and Supplementary Figures 7 and 8, and the paper's published per-stimulation traces, evoked integrals and spontaneous transient integrals can be recomputed from them.
outcomes.source: Figure 6C to 6F, Supplementary Figures 7B, 7C, 8C to 8E; Source Data (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19930567); Data availability
outcomes.quote: Raw tubular Data generated in this study from all experiments, and uncropped western blot images with metadata files in this study are available in source data file via the open-access option on the Zenodo repository (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19930567).
outcomes.notes: All 27 mice of the source data are in the dandiset with the same genotype and line. The Anxa1 half links. 120 of 120 traces of Figure 6C and 479 of 480 of Supplementary Figure 7B equal the dandiset's dF/F from 1 s before onset (largest difference among matched traces 5.7e-13 in each), the evoked integrals equal the code's measure times 0.0001 for all Anxa1 records but one, and the transient counts match for 15 of 15 mice. The one miss in each is the last 4 mW stimulation of mouse 4398, whose processed series ends 0.8 s after onset. The Calb1 half does not link; 0 of 384 traces, 0 of 384 integrals and the transient counts of 1 of 12 mice match. dF/F recomputed from the raw signal with the code's processing reproduces the stored Calb1 series (largest difference 1.47 % dF/F) but not the published traces (median differences 66 to 519 % dF/F; 22 to 88 at the best background fraction per mouse). The published spontaneous values are 0.005 times the mean dF/F over each transient (ratio 0.004994 to 0.004999), so part (4) as fixed, with integrals, matches for no mouse; with the transient mean it matches for 13 of 27 mice within 1% (Anxa1 13 of 15; 4398 and 4007 each fail by one sorted value, 1.03% and 1.67%), and for none within the 1e-4 of part (3); integrals match for none at either tolerance. The four parts match for 1.0, 0.609, 0.609 and 0 of their records (0.481 with the transient mean), so the outcome is not reproduced under either measure. The Calb1 mismatch is not one of epoch or power labels; searched over all 64 epochs and 8 powers of each mouse, no epoch is within 1e-6 of any of the 384 S8D traces (closest 15.7 to 150.8 % dF/F), and against the matched epochs the per-mouse median slopes are 0.21 to 0.75 and offsets -13.8 to 16.2 % dF/F. The Figure 6E integrals match the 0.5 mW epochs (120 of 120) and none of the 4 mW ones. The published values reproduce the paper's statistics (Figure 6E p = 1.1e-20, Cohen's d 2.06 and 0.765), so the Calb1 differences come from the data, not from the paper's computation on them.
deviations: The criterion fixed the integral of each spontaneous transient; the published values turned out to be the mean dF/F over the transient. The mean is shown as a variant and does not change the outcome.

findings.statement: The Calb1 dF/F in the dandiset is not the trace behind Supplementary Figure 8. None of the 384 published Calb1 triggered traces or evoked integrals match it, no epoch of any power matches a published trace, the transient counts match for 1 of 12 mice, and dF/F recomputed from the deposited raw signal with the published code reproduces the dandiset's series, not the paper's, at any single background fraction. The processing the paper used for Calb1 is neither deposited nor described, so the Calb1 results of the paper cannot be recomputed from the dandiset.

The dandiset holds only the fiber photometry of Figure 6 and Supplementary Figures 7 and 8. The imaging, proteomics and western blots of Figures 1 to 5 are elsewhere (BioImage Archive, PRIDE, Zenodo), so eight of the paper's main findings cannot be tested on it.

The processed series of mouse 4398 ends 0.8 s after its last onset, a 4 mW stimulation, while the paper's trace for that stimulation is complete and differs from the dandiset's in the samples both hold.

The OptogeneticEpochsTable description gives 8 ms on and 8 ms off for 500 ms, four powers and trains at least 20 s apart. The tables hold eight powers, two kinds of train in Anxa1 files (9 ms pulses every 10 ms for 0.33 s, and 8 ms every 16 ms for 0.51 s), and pairs of trains 15.3 s apart (51% of gaps under 20 s). One train each in mice 4652 and 740 has a pulse length of 0, no period and one pulse.

Two Anxa1 G2019S mice (3742 and 4885) received the paper's four powers as 0.33 s trains of 9 ms pulses, while every other mouse received them as 0.51 s trains of 8 ms pulses. Neither the paper nor the dandiset says so. In these two mice the response does not follow the labelled power (in 3742 the 0.5 mW trains give the smallest response, median 5.7 against 33.5 % dF/F x s at 0.1 mW), so the data cannot confirm their power labels. Leaving the two mice out does not change the Anxa1 result.
The dF/F series (FiberPhotometryResponseSeriesDfOverF) is stated in a.u.; its description and its values are percent dF/F.
The archive's summary of the dandiset lists only a behavioral approach and BehavioralTimeSeries; the files hold fiber photometry and optogenetics.
The dandiset holds the 27 mice the paper kept after excluding four on histology (one Anxa1 G2019S, one Calb1 G2019S, two Calb1 WT). It does not say that mice were left out or why.

chunking_index.m computes the start of each window as trigger - fs*ti, so with ti = -1 the window used for the evoked integral and for the spontaneous exclusion starts 1 s after onset. The source data show that the figures used the intended window starting 1 s before onset; the code as published gives the reverse sign.
plot_results.m selects power code 'h' for Figure 6E, which the lab's stimulation key, as used by the conversion, maps to 4 mW; the figure, its legend and the source data are at 0.5 mW.

The Methods and transient_by_threshold.m give the integral of dF/F over each spontaneous transient; the published values of Figure 6F and Supplementary Figure 8C are 0.005 times the mean dF/F over each transient, a duration-normalized integral. The code that computes them is not in the repository.

For the per-mouse comparisons the Methods and the asterisks name Welch's test, the legends give one-tailed two-sample t-test p-values, and the code runs a two-tailed Student test. The Figure 6F count of 6 of 8 follows the one-tailed Student test; Welch's test gives 7.
The paper does not cite the dandiset; its data statement names Zenodo, PRIDE and the BioImage Archive.

attempts.description: Tests the findings of Chen, He et al. (2026). On dandiset 001933, which holds GRAB-DA3m fiber photometry in the dorsal striatum during optogenetic stimulation of Anxa1+ (15 mice) or Calb1+ (12 mice) SNc dopamine neurons in LRRK2-WT and LRRK2-G2019S mice, it compares evoked and spontaneous dopamine release between genotypes, per power and per mouse, and links the dandiset to the paper's published source data. The imaging, proteomics and western blots of Figures 1 to 5 are not in the dandiset; their claims are tested on the data the paper deposited on Zenodo, in PRIDE and in the BioImage Archive, and counted apart.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's recordings are those behind the paper's Figure 6 and Supplementary Figures 7 and 8, and the paper's published per-stimulation traces, evoked integrals and spontaneous transient integrals can be recomputed from them.
outcomes.source: Figure 6C to 6F, Supplementary Figures 7B, 7C, 8C to 8E; Source Data (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19930567); Data availability
outcomes.quote: Raw tubular Data generated in this study from all experiments, and uncropped western blot images with metadata files in this study are available in source data file via the open-access option on the Zenodo repository (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19930567).
outcomes.notes: All 27 mice of the source data are in the dandiset with the same genotype and line. The Anxa1 half links. 120 of 120 traces of Figure 6C and 479 of 480 of Supplementary Figure 7B equal the dandiset's dF/F from 1 s before onset (largest difference among matched traces 5.7e-13 in each), the evoked integrals equal the code's measure times 0.0001 for all Anxa1 records but one, and the transient counts match for 15 of 15 mice. The one miss in each is the last 4 mW stimulation of mouse 4398, whose processed series ends 0.8 s after onset. The Calb1 half does not link; 0 of 384 traces, 0 of 384 integrals and the transient counts of 1 of 12 mice match. dF/F recomputed from the raw signal with the code's processing reproduces the stored Calb1 series (largest difference 1.47 % dF/F) but not the published traces (median differences 66 to 519 % dF/F; 22 to 88 at the best background fraction per mouse). The published spontaneous values are 0.005 times the trapezoid integral of each transient divided by its number of samples (within-mouse spread of the ratio at most 2.2e-15; 15 of 15 Anxa1 mice and 0 of 12 Calb1 mice match at 1e-4), so part (4) as fixed, with integrals, matches for no mouse at either tolerance. The four parts match for 1.0, 0.609, 0.609 and 0 of their records, so the outcome is not reproduced. With the published measure in part (4) they match for 1.0, 0.609, 0.609 and 0.556, which would be partially reproduced; the criterion fixed integrals, so this is a variant. The mean dF/F over each transient comes close (13 of 15 Anxa1 mice within 1%, none within 1e-4). The Calb1 mismatch is not one of epoch or power labels; searched over all 64 epochs and 8 powers of each mouse, no epoch is within 1e-6 of any of the 384 S8D traces (closest 15.7 to 150.8 % dF/F), and against the matched epochs the per-mouse median slopes are 0.21 to 0.75 and offsets -13.8 to 16.2 % dF/F. The Figure 6E integrals match the 0.5 mW epochs (120 of 120) and none of the 4 mW ones. The published values reproduce the paper's statistics (Figure 6E p = 1.1e-20, Figure 6F p = 2.75e-177, Cohen's d 2.06 and 0.765), so the Calb1 differences come from the data, not from the paper's computation on them.
deviations: The criterion fixed the integral of each spontaneous transient; the published values turned out to be 0.005 times the integral divided by the number of samples in the transient. That measure, and the mean dF/F, are shown as variants and do not change the outcome.

outcomes.statement: LRRK2 kinase inhibition with MLi-2 changes 289 phosphopeptides in striatal synaptosomes of G2019S mice, including RAB3 T86.
outcomes.source: Figure 2A to 2C; Results, LRRK2 phosphorylates RAB3 isoforms in vivo, paragraphs 1 and 2
outcomes.quote: we identified 289 significantly altered phosphopeptides (Fig. 2B, supplementary data 1) ... the decreased phosphorylation at the T86 site of the RAB3 GTPase in LRRK2G2019S mice treated with MLi-2, compared to the vehicle group (Fig. 2B).
outcomes.notes: On the log2 abundances as deposited, 1694 (reading a, all six values) or 1810 (reading b, two per group) phosphopeptides pass p <= 0.05 and |difference| > 0.58, against 289, and nearly all are lower with vehicle (1673 and 1785), as the samples labelled MLi-2 have higher abundances overall (median log2 17.84 to 18.12 against 17.25 to 17.47). The RAB3 T86 peptide passes (p = 0.00892) but is lower with vehicle (difference -1.31), so neither part of the criterion holds. Centring each sample on its median, a step the criterion did not fix, gives 243 and 282 peptides (282 within tolerance) and RAB3 T86 still higher with MLi-2 (difference -0.693, p = 0.0238). The paper's volcano table holds MLi-2 minus vehicle as the samples are labelled; on the 4340 peptides with all six values its difference equals that difference plus a constant to within 1.6e-06, and against vehicle minus MLi-2 the residual reaches 13. Its p-values are near those of a t-test on median-centred values but not equal (median gap in -log10 p 0.0088 Welch, 0.0161 Student). It gives 254 peptides at the legend's thresholds, and RAB3 T86 +0.688, which the legend reads as higher with vehicle. As the samples are labelled, the RAB3 T86 phosphopeptide rises after MLi-2. RAB10 T73 does not change (0.15, p = 0.775), so the data cannot tell whether the labels or the figure's direction are swapped. If the labels are swapped, the median-centred reading b gives 282 peptides and RAB3 T86 higher with vehicle (+0.693), which would reproduce the claim, so the outcome rests on a labelling question the data cannot answer. Attempt -01 blocked this claim with data_missing under pilot-6; under pilot-7 it is tested on the PRIDE data.
deviations: The criterion fixed log2 abundances without normalisation; the paper's volcano table follows median-centred values. The median-centred result is shown as a variant and does not change the outcome.
The legend does not say which peptides were tested; two readings (all six values, two per group) are shown.
The search (Proteome Discoverer with Byonic and Sequest, commercial) is not re-run; the test starts from the deposited abundances.

outcomes.source: Figure 3D to 3F; Results, Phosphorylation of RAB3A decreases its binding to the effector proteins RIM1 and RIM2 from mouse brain, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The RAB3A effector proteins RIM1 and RIM2 showed a marked preference for binding to unphosphorylated RAB3A (Fig. 3D, E) ... Conversely, we found that p-RAB3A preferentially associated with RILPL1 and RILPL2 (Fig. 3D, F)
outcomes.notes: RIM1 (Q99NE5-7) and RIM2 are higher with RAB3A (log2 differences 2.42 and 2.17, paired p = 0.00361 and 0.0124) and RILPL1 higher with p-RAB3A (-6.02, p = 9.8e-05). RILPL2 is detected in all six p-RAB3A and in none of the RAB3A pulldowns, so the criterion's paired test has no pair and does not find it higher with p-RAB3A; three of four comparisons hold. With the Methods' imputation (seeded), a variant, it is higher with p-RAB3A (-7.92, p = 1.21e-08), and the limma table gives logFC -7.58, so the data point the way of the claim for RILPL2. The paper's p-values for RIM2 and RILPL1 (0.011, 0.002) are those of the paired test on intensities without the log (0.0109, 0.0022). The deposited limma table agrees in direction for every group. Its counts at the text's p-value < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1 are 121 and 32; the paper's 69 and 16 are the counts at adjusted p < 0.05. Attempt -01 blocked this claim with data_missing under pilot-6; under pilot-7 it is tested on the PRIDE data.
deviations: RILPL2 has no pair for the criterion's paired test and is counted as not holding; the Methods' imputation followed by an unpaired t-test, which gives four of four, is shown as a variant.
The tests use log2 intensities; the paper's p-values follow intensities without the log. Both are shown.
Replicates are paired in run order, as the paper does not give the pairing.

outcomes.statement: Fewer TH+/VAMP2+ striatal synaptosomes from G2019S mice contain bassoon, and the remaining bassoon clusters are larger.
outcomes.source: Figure 4D and 4E; Results, LRRK2 alters the composition and organization of active zone release sites in dopaminergic striatal synaptosomes, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: we found a significant decrease in the percentage of TH + /VAMP2+ synaptosomes that contained the active zone marker bassoon (Fig. 4D). In addition, the remaining active zone clusters in LRRK2G2019S TH + /VAMP2+ synaptosomes had an increased average area of bassoon staining when compared to wildtype (Fig. 4E)

statistics.about: percentage of TH+/VAMP2+ synaptosomes with bassoon
statistics.n: 39 WT areas from 3 mice and 35 G2019S areas from 3 mice
43 WT areas from 4 mice and 57 G2019S areas from 4 mice

outcomes.notes: Part A holds. In the source data fewer TH+/VAMP2+ synaptosomes contain bassoon in GS (12.0 against 21.4 %, p = 6.38e-05; 0.000118 without the GS value under 1 %) and the bassoon area is larger (0.0862 against 0.0750 um2, p = 0.0301, the paper's value); with one value per mouse p = 0.263 and 0.474. Part B does not. The Methods' FIJI procedure as re-implemented here gives, GS against WT, 48.8 against 52.4 % with bassoon (p = 0.459) and a bassoon area of 0.0682 against 0.0696 um2 (overlap, p = 0.805) or 0.132 against 0.141 um2 (bassoon particle, p = 0.206). The re-implementation keeps a median of 183 VAMP2 particles per image against the legend's about 1000; the Default threshold alone gives a median of 1186 objects, of which the size limit keeps 193 and the circularity limit 183. Its percentages are more than twice the paper's, so part B may fail because of this attempt's segmentation, and its null result is weak evidence against the claim. The OME metadata of 165 of 168 images confirm the channel order. Attempt -01 blocked this claim with data_missing under pilot-6; under pilot-7 it is tested on the Zenodo values and the BioImage Archive images.
deviations: The FIJI procedure is re-implemented in Python (rolling ball as ImageJ shrinks it, ImageJ's Default threshold, scikit-image perimeters); it is not FIJI, and its particle counts are far below the paper's.

The images cannot be matched to the published areas one by one; part B compares genotypes over the deposited images (35 GS and 39 WT for the percentage, 49 and 43 for the area, one image in each folder with nothing to measure).
outcomes.where: BioImage Archive S-BIAD2074 (images); Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.19930567 (per-area values)

outcomes.statement: RIM1 is reduced in striatal synaptosomes of G2019S mice (p = 0.0245) but not in other striatal fractions or the SNc.
outcomes.source: Figure 4H to 4L; Results, LRRK2 alters the composition and organization of active zone release sites in dopaminergic striatal synaptosomes, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: However, we observed a decrease in RIM1 levels in the LRRK2G2019S synaptosome fraction compared to controls (Fig. 4I and Supplementary Fig. 4F). In contrast, RIM1 levels in other striatal fractions or SNc lysates did not change (Fig. 4J–L)
outcomes.notes: RIM1 in synaptosomes is lower in GS, 0.206 against 0.319, two-tailed p = 0.0245 (the paper's value), Cohen's d -1.53. RIM1 in the S1 fraction (p = 0.896) and in the SNc (p = 0.936) does not differ, nor do synaptophysin (4G, p = 0.445) and the protein of 4H (p = 0.634). Attempt -01 blocked this claim with data_missing under pilot-6; under pilot-7 it is tested on the Zenodo data.
deviations: The test starts from the deposited band values; the uncropped blots are not quantified again, as the Methods do not say how bands were measured.

outcomes.statement: Bassoon cluster density is reduced and cluster volume increased in Aldh1a1+ but not Aldh1a1- dopamine axons of G2019S mice, and the same holds in Anxa1+ axons.
outcomes.source: Figure 5D, 5E, 5G and 5H; Results, LRRK2 disrupts the number and composition of active zone release sites in vulnerable dopamine axons, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: We observed a decrease in the density of bassoon+ clusters in vulnerable Aldh1a1+ but not resilient Aldh1a1- axons of LRRK2G2019S, compared to LRRK2WT mice (Fig. 5D) ... an increase in the volume of the remaining bassoon clusters in Aldh1a1+ but not Aldh1a1- dopamine axons ... We confirmed these findings using an independent mouse line, Anxa1Cre (Fig. 5F–H).

statistics.about: Aldh1a1+ bassoon cluster density, GS against WT
statistics.test: Šídák’s multiple comparisons test following a two-way ANOVA

statistics.about: Aldh1a1+ bassoon cluster volume, GS against WT
statistics.test: Šídák’s multiple comparisons test following a two-way ANOVA

statistics.n: 16 WT sections from 3 mice and 18 G2019S sections from 4 mice
16 WT sections from 3 mice and 18 G2019S sections from 4 mice

outcomes.notes: Five of six parts hold. With section 5 of WT mouse 1723 counted once (its four values equal those of section 4), Aldh1a1+ density is lower in GS (0.164 against 0.217) at Sidak p = 0.058, so part 1 fails; Aldh1a1- density does not differ (p = 0.713); bassoon volume is larger in GS Aldh1a1+ axons (p = 0.0425) and not in Aldh1a1- axons (p = 0.699); in Anxa1+ axons density is lower (p = 0.0374) and volume larger (p = 0.0148). As deposited, with the section twice, all six hold and the ANOVA gives the legend's numbers (5D Sidak p 0.0344, 5E 0.0385). Attempt -01 blocked this claim with data_missing under pilot-6; under pilot-7 it is tested on the Zenodo values.
deviations: The analysis starts from the per-section values; the 542 GB of SIM images (S-BIAD2071) are matched by file name and not analysed again, as the Methods' analysis runs in Imaris 10.1.
One section that appears twice in the source data is counted once, as the claims file fixes; the paper counts it twice.
outcomes.where: BioImage Archive S-BIAD2071 (images); Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.19930567 (per-section values)

outcomes.statement: The volume occupied by TH+ fibres in the dorsal striatum does not differ between G2019S and WT mice.
outcomes.source: Figure 5I and 5J; Results, LRRK2 disrupts the number and composition of active zone release sites in vulnerable dopamine axons, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: We found no differences in the volume (Fig. 5I, J, Supplementary Fig. 5C), area, and intensity of TH signal in immunopositive ALDH1A1 fibers (Supplementary Fig. 5D, E) in the dorsal striatum.
outcomes.notes: The paper's test does not find a difference in TH volume, two-tailed p = 0.117 over 12 sections per genotype; GS is 7.1 % lower (0.929 against 1.000), Cohen's d -0.67. Attempt -01 blocked this claim with data_missing under pilot-6; under pilot-7 it is tested on the Zenodo values.
deviations: The test starts from the per-section values; the images (S-BIAD2072) are matched by file name and not analysed again, as the Methods' analysis runs in Imaris 10.1.
outcomes.where: BioImage Archive S-BIAD2072 (images); Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.19930567 (per-section values)

findings.statement: Still present from attempt -01. The Calb1 dF/F in the dandiset is not the trace behind Supplementary Figure 8. None of the 384 published Calb1 triggered traces is within 1e-6 of any epoch of its mouse (closest 15.7 % dF/F), none of the evoked integrals match, the transient counts match for 1 of 12 mice, and dF/F recomputed from the deposited raw signal with the published code reproduces the dandiset's series, not the paper's. The processing the paper used for Calb1 is neither deposited nor described.

Still present from attempt -01, where it was recorded as data_missing. The dandiset holds only the fiber photometry of Figure 6 and Supplementary Figures 7 and 8. The imaging, proteomics and western blots of Figures 1 to 5 are public on Zenodo, in PRIDE and in the BioImage Archive, but neither the dandiset's description nor its related resources name those deposits.
Still present from attempt -01. The processed series of mouse 4398 ends 0.81 s after its last onset, a 4 mW stimulation, while the paper's trace for that stimulation is complete.

Still present from attempt -01. The OptogeneticEpochsTable description gives 8 ms on and 8 ms off for 500 ms, four powers and trains at least 20 s apart. The tables hold eight powers, two kinds of train in Anxa1 files (0.33 s and 0.51 s), and pairs of trains 15.3 s apart. Two trains have a pulse length of 0.

Still present from attempt -01. Two Anxa1 G2019S mice (3742 and 4885) received the paper's four powers as 0.33 s trains of 9 ms pulses, while every other mouse received them as 0.51 s trains of 8 ms pulses. Neither the paper nor the dandiset says so, and in these two mice the response does not follow the labelled power.
Still present from attempt -01. The dF/F series (FiberPhotometryResponseSeriesDfOverF) is stated in a.u.; its description and its values are percent dF/F.
Still present from attempt -01. The archive's summary of the dandiset lists only a behavioral approach and BehavioralTimeSeries; the files hold fiber photometry and optogenetics.
Still present from attempt -01. The dandiset holds the 27 mice the paper kept after excluding four on histology, and does not say that mice were left out or why.

Still present from attempt -01 (the repository is at the same commit). chunking_index.m computes the start of each window as trigger - fs*ti, so with ti = -1 the window starts 1 s after onset; the figures used the intended window starting 1 s before onset.
Still present from attempt -01. plot_results.m selects power code 'h' (4 mW) for Figure 6E; the figure, its legend and the source data are at 0.5 mW.

Still present from attempt -01, and made more exact. The Methods and transient_by_threshold.m give the integral of dF/F over each spontaneous transient; the published values of Figure 6F and Supplementary Figure 8C are 0.005 times the trapezoid integral divided by the number of samples in the transient (exact to 2.2e-15 in every Anxa1 mouse; attempt -01 described them as about 0.005 times the mean dF/F), and the code that computes them is not in the repository.

Still present from attempt -01. For the per-mouse comparisons of Figure 6 the Methods and the asterisks name Welch's test, the legends give one-tailed two-sample t-test p-values, and the code runs a two-tailed Student test.
Still present from attempt -01. The paper does not cite the dandiset (none of its 99 references names DANDI); its data statement names Zenodo, PRIDE and the BioImage Archive.

New. In the synaptosome phosphoproteomics (PRIDE PXD065006, equal to Supplementary data 1) the RAB3 T86 phosphopeptide is higher in the samples labelled MLi-2 than in those labelled vehicle (median-centred log2 difference vehicle minus MLi-2 of -0.693, p = 0.0238), and the paper's volcano table holds MLi-2 minus vehicle (equal to it up to a constant within 1.6e-06 on 4340 peptides), while the Figure 2B legend reads a positive difference as higher with vehicle and the text reports less RAB3 phosphorylation with MLi-2. Either the sample labels of the deposit or the direction of Figure 2B is swapped.
New. The paper's volcano table (Supplementary data 1) gives 254 phosphopeptides at the legend's thresholds (p <= 0.05, |difference| > 0.58), where the text gives 289.

New. The text gives 69 and 16 proteins preferring RAB3A and p-RAB3A at p-value < 0.05 and |log2FC| = 1; the deposited limma table (PRIDE PXD065125) gives 121 and 32 at that p-value, and 69 and 16 at adjusted p < 0.05. The Figure 3E and 3F p-values are of paired tests on intensities without the log, which the legend does not say.

New. The Figure 1D legend gives a two-tailed unpaired t-test over 16 sections with p = 0.0008; on the source data that test gives p = 4.65e-06, and 0.0008 matches a paired test over sections or an unpaired test of the three mouse means.

New. In the source data of Figure 5D and 5E, sections 4 and 5 of WT mouse 1723 carry the same four values to six digits, so one section appears to have been entered twice. Counted once, the Aldh1a1+ density comparison has Sidak p = 0.058 in place of 0.0344.

New. The source data and the legends differ in counts. Figure 4E has 51 G2019S areas against the legend's 57 (the source data give the legend's p = 0.0301); Figure 5E has 21 G2019S Aldh1a1+ sections against 20; and the 5E legend gives a genotype F of 1.277, the 5D value, where the data give 5.234 with the legend's p = 0.0252. One Figure 4D value (0.0766 %) is of the size of the Figure 4E areas and may have been pasted from there.

New. The source data of Figure 5G, 5H and 5J give one animal column holding WT IDs for both genotypes, so the G2019S animals are not identified. The BioImage Archive names them (S-BIAD2071 1019, 1020, 1022, 1052; S-BIAD2072 3243, 3246, 4120, 4369). S-BIAD2071 names a WT mouse 1923 where the source data name 1723, and two of its files carry no mouse ID. S-BIAD2074 names mice only by a number from 1 to 5 per genotype.

S-BIAD2070 has 7 images per mouse for Figure 1D, which has 5 or 6 sections per mouse; S-BIAD2071 has a fourth Anxa1 WT mouse (1018) not in Figure 5G and 5H; S-BIAD2072 has 64 volume images per genotype where the legend gives 96; and the synaptosome images of S-BIAD2074 differ in number per mouse from the published areas (G2019S 14, 10 and 12 images against 14, 11 and 10 areas in Figure 4D; 50 images against 51 areas in Figure 4E).

attempts.label: DANDI:002013
attempts.paper_title: Microinvasive Probes for Monitoring Electrical and Chemical Neural Activity in Nonhuman Primates
attempts.entry_title: Microinvasive probes for dopamine, LFP and spikes in monkeys (Amjad et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Amjad, Mahajan, Choi, Shrivastav, Murray, Somich, Coyne and Schwerdt (2025) on dandiset 002013, which holds the three example sessions of the paper. It checks the recording parameters and task structure, the dopamine response to large and small reward cues at site c8dg, beta-band LFP suppression by reward and cue side at c3bs-c3a, beta bursts around the cue, and the isolation of the sorted unit of monkey P, and compares the dandiset with the paper's Zenodo deposit.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Amjad et al. (2025) from dandiset 002013

outcomes.statement: Insertion yields were low, 21.4% (3 of 14 sensors) in monkey T and 33% (3 of 9) in monkey P, counted as recording sites that stayed functional after insertion until the end of the study.
outcomes.source: Results and Discussion, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: insertion yields remained low ranging from 21.4% (3/14 individual sensors) in monkey T to 33% (3/9) in monkey P. These values indicate the number of recording sites that retained functionality after insertion, until the end of this study.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds one or two sites per session and no list of the implanted sensors or of which kept working, in its files or its metadata. None of the ten file names of the paper's Zenodo deposit, printed in the data check, points to such a list.

outcomes.statement: The s-µIPs kept recording for more than a year after implantation; the example sites were recorded 483 days (c8dg), 496 days (c3bs-c3a) and 390 days (monkey P) after implantation.
outcomes.source: Figure 3A, 3B and Figure 5 legends; Results and Discussion, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: sites c8dg and c8ds: 483 days postimplant ... site c3bs-c3a: 496 days postimplant ... site c33:390 days postimplant ... Measurements were made from chronically implanted s-μIPs that maintained functionality >1 year postimplant.
outcomes.notes: The subject, device and electrode fields of the files hold no implantation date, and none of the mentions of implantation in the files' general section or the dandiset metadata (all printed in the data check) comes with a date, so days post-implant cannot be computed. The two Monkey T sessions are 13 days apart, which matches the difference between the 483 and 496 days of the legends.

outcomes.statement: FSCV applied a triangular waveform from -0.4 to 1.3 V at 400 V/s, every 100 ms (10 Hz).
outcomes.source: Methods, FSCV and EPhys Recordings, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: FSCV operates by applying a triangle waveform from −0.4 to 1.3 V at a rate of 400 V/s ... The triangular waveform is applied every 100 ms for an effective sampling frequency of 10 Hz.
outcomes.notes: The applied voltage runs from -0.347 to 1.340 V at 400.5 V/s, one scan every 0.1 s. Three of four values are within tolerance; the lowest potential is outside -0.4 +- 0.04 V. The dandiset's own description (-0.35 to 1.34 V) agrees with the data, so the Methods state the nominal waveform. The data of the applied voltage have conversion 1 and offset 0, so the values are read as stored.
deviations: Measured on session 09/13/2024 only, the only FSCV session in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: EPhys was sampled at 30 kHz in monkey P and 32 kHz in monkey T, and band-pass filtered from 0.1 to 7500 Hz.
outcomes.source: Methods, FSCV and EPhys Recordings, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: EPhys recordings were made using a unity-gain analog amplifier headstage ... at a sampling frequency of 30 (monkey P) or 32 kHz (monkey T), and bandpass filtered from 0.1 to 7500 Hz.
outcomes.notes: Monkey P's raw timestamps have a median interval of 33.333 µs (30 kHz) and Monkey T's series a rate of 32000 Hz. The Neuralynx settings of both Monkey T channels give a low cut of 0.1 Hz and a high cut of 8000 Hz, inside the tolerance of 7500 Hz but not equal to it; the dandiset's description also says 0.1 to 7500 Hz (printed). Monkey P's file stores no filter settings; its notes, printed in full, and its electrode columns name no filter or cut-off.

outcomes.statement: In the shape task, forced trials made up 25% of all trials, and the cue-reward association was reversed after blocks of 50 to 300 trials.
outcomes.source: Methods, Behavioral Tasks, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: Forced choice trials were also interleaved (25% of all trials) where only one value cue was displayed ... The cue-reward association was reversed after a block of 50–300 trials depending on the session.
outcomes.notes: Forced trials are 358 of 1468 (24.4%). The eight complete blocks of the cue-reward association are 71 to 273 trials long; the first and last blocks, cut by the file, are 61 and 194 trials.
deviations: Blocks are found from the image codes of successful forced trials, as choice trials carry no feedback code; a reversal is placed after the last forced trial of the earlier association, so block edges are uncertain by the gap between forced trials.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset reproduces the processed data the paper deposited on Zenodo; the trial selections and the beta power of the paper's example trial computed from the dandiset agree with the paper's own files.
outcomes.source: Data Availability Statement (doi:10.5281/zenodo.14826579)
outcomes.quote: Data used in this study are available at zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14826579).
outcomes.notes: Trials are matched by number. The decoded selections agree with the four Zenodo lists for 569 of 570, 602 of 602, 594 of 594 and 577 of 578 trials; the only difference is trial 1501, the last of the session, absent from the Zenodo large-reward and right lists. The Zenodo example "trial35" is the 35th trial of the large-reward list (trial 84). Beta power computed here correlates with its trace at r = 0.943 at a lag of 6 ms, with a median amplitude ratio of 0.943, so the dandiset's LFP, its trial times and the beta pipeline used here agree with the paper's files. The Zenodo example's raw LFP variable is a copy of its time variable, so the LFP trace itself could not be compared. The criterion tests only r and was written after r = 0.94 was known. The amplitudes differ (maximum 2184 µV² here against 1560 µV² in the Zenodo trace), so the paper's filter or envelope probably differs from the one used here.
deviations: The beta filter (4th-order Butterworth, forwards and backwards, squared Hilbert envelope) is a common choice; the paper's code is not public, and r = 0.943 suggests its filter differs somewhat.

outcomes.statement: Dopamine was measured from two neighbouring channels of one dual-channel s-µIP (sites c8dg and c8ds, 0.1 to 0.2 mm apart), and both showed dopamine increases after the value cue in a single forced large-reward trial.
outcomes.source: Figure 3A; Results and Discussion, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: These measurements also demonstrate the ability to measure dopamine from two neighboring channels on a single s-μIP with 0.1–0.2 mm separation between the recording tips. ... (e.g., increases in both channels after the value cue, V).
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds FSCV from site c8dg only. Site c8ds is not in it, and the Zenodo deposit holds processed FSCV of c8dg only; its one FSCV file is FSCV_trlists_c8dg_09132024_firsthalf.mat (file list printed in the data check). The c8dg half can be tested and holds; the mean of the re-referenced dopamine over 0 to 3 s is above zero in 56 of 85 large-reward forced trials (65.9%), and in 58 of 85 with a baseline of the mean over -1 to 0 s.

outcomes.statement: The single-trial FSCV colour plot shows dopamine redox current, with changes near 0.6 V (oxidation) and -0.2 V (reduction) after the value cue.
outcomes.source: Figure 3A
outcomes.quote: Color plot shows clear dopamine redox current (i.e., color changes ∼0.6 and −0.2 V).
outcomes.notes: The raw FSCV current is in the dandiset, but its timing could not be linked to the trials. Its scan times are an exact 0.1 s grid starting at the first trial start and running 24120 s, past the last trial; at 0.6 V it does not match the stored oxidation current of any of six rows tested at the stored times (|r| below 0.06) or anywhere in the record (best r 0.16 to 0.20 at offsets that differ from row to row); and it shows no large-against-small contrast at the stored value cue times (p = 0.46). The same search at 0.50 V, 0.70 V and -0.19 V gives best r 0.17 to 0.22 at offsets that differ from row to row. Computed at the stored times (not deciding), the background-subtracted voltammogram of 164 large-reward forced trials has its largest rising-sweep value at -0.24 V (at 0.6 V it is -0.033) and its most negative value at the switching potential, 1.34 V, with an SD of 0.042 over the scan; it does not meet the criterion. A colour plot of a forced large-reward trial therefore cannot be placed in the trial.

outcomes.statement: Single-trial bipolar LFP from site c3bs-c3a shows beta bursts (one to a few cycles of high beta power) whose frequency changes around the cue and other task events.
outcomes.source: Figure 3B; Results and Discussion, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Single-trial LFPs measured from another s-μIP are shown to display fluctuations in the frequency of β-band “bursts” (i.e., 1–few cycles of high β-band power) around the cue and other task events
outcomes.notes: With the threshold at the 75th percentile (356 µV²) and bursts of at least 50 ms, the burst rate of 570 large-reward trials is 1.51 per s in the second before the value cue and 1.21 in the second after it (Wilcoxon p = 9.5e-10). The rate changes around the cue at the 50th and 90th percentiles too (p below 1e-40), rising at the 50th and falling at the 90th, so its direction depends on the threshold while the change does not. The rate dips just after the cue (0.51 per s in 0 to 0.25 s) and falls again from 6 s after it, after the feedback. On the smoothed power 95.1% of runs above the 75th percentile last at least 50 ms (median 206 ms), so the minimum length does little; on the unsmoothed envelope the rate also falls after the cue (3.07 to 2.11 per s, p = 6.8e-34). At the deciding threshold the fall in bursts coincides with the drop in beta power after the cue, so it is not separate evidence from the suppression of fig4b-beta-reward.
deviations: The paper shows a single trial and does not define a burst; the threshold, minimum length and test were chosen here before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: Trial-averaged dopamine at site c8dg is higher after large-reward than after small-reward value cues, in successful forced trials of the shape task.
outcomes.source: Figure 4A
outcomes.quote: Higher dopamine levels are observed following the display of large reward associated value cues as compared to small reward cues in monkey T
outcomes.notes: Over 0 to 3 s after the value cue, the re-referenced dopamine has a median of 1.28 in 85 large-reward trials and 0.19 in 80 small-reward trials (Mann-Whitney p = 0.023; 3 trials of 168 have no valid samples in the window). The difference lies in 1.5 to 3 s (p = 0.0072), not 0 to 1.5 s (p = 0.41). The effect is weak. Before the cue the groups differ the other way (p = 0.064). Without re-referencing (the stored da) there is no difference (p = 0.3), nor in the re-referenced oxidation current (p = 0.41). It holds in trials 1 to 367 (p = 0.013) and not in trials 368 to 734 (p = 0.51). With a baseline of the mean over -1 to 0 s in place of the sample at the cue the result is the same (1.38 against 0.10, p = 0.022).
deviations: Only the first 734 of 1468 trials of the session have trial-aligned FSCV in the dandiset, so 168 successful forced trials are used.

The stored da is not referenced at the value cue; it is re-referenced here by subtracting its value at the cue, which equals background subtraction there only if the PCA projection was linear and the nulling (NaN) masks are ignored.
Small reward is inferred from the absence of the big-reward code, confirmed by the cue condition codes 35 and 36 in all 303 successful forced trials.
The paper gives no window or test; 0 to 3 s and the Mann-Whitney test were chosen before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: Beta-band LFP power at c3bs-c3a in the direction task is more suppressed (stronger event-related desynchronization) after large-reward than after small-reward value cues, in a brief window after the cue.
outcomes.source: Figure 4B
outcomes.quote: Trial-averaged β-band LFP power for large and small reward conditions in the direction task, showing increased suppression (i.e., ERD, highlighted in yellow) for large as compared to small reward cues during the brief time window following the value cue at 0 s
outcomes.notes: Over 0 to 0.5 s after the value cue, median beta power is 275 µV² in 570 large-reward trials and 327 µV² in 602 small-reward trials (ratio 0.84, Mann-Whitney p = 1e-08), with no difference before the cue (ratio 1.006, p = 0.82). It holds relative to pre-cue power (ratio 0.82, p = 1.1e-06) and on each side (left p = 0.0016, right p = 1e-07). It is confined to a brief window, as the legend says; over 0 to 1 s large is slightly higher (ratio 1.04, p = 0.09) and over 0.25 to 0.75 s there is no difference (p = 0.66). The 0.25 s smoothing does not carry the difference from before the cue; on the unsmoothed envelope it holds over 0 to 0.5 s (ratio 0.834, p = 1.9e-08) and 0.125 to 0.5 s (ratio 0.671, p = 4.8e-19); in 0.1 s bins large and small do not differ before the cue (ratios 0.95 to 1.05), large is lower from 0.1 to 0.4 s (0.85, 0.59, 0.60) and higher from 0.5 s on (1.32 to 1.49). The criterion, lower power over 0 to 0.5 s, is met; the bins fit a deeper suppression after large-reward cues and equally an earlier suppression with an earlier rebound, so the part of the claim saying the suppression is greater is not shown. The LFP's 1497 joins do not step (largest change at a join 20.3 µV, below the 99.9th percentile of 26.0 µV over all samples), and 118 of 1172 successful trials have one within -0.5 to 1 s of the cue, 23 to 36 in each reward and side condition. Trial 1501, absent from the Zenodo lists, is included; one trial of 570 cannot change the result.
deviations: The paper does not give the window highlighted in Figure 4B or a test; 0 to 0.5 s and the Mann-Whitney test were chosen before the analysis.

outcomes.statement: With the reward fixed at large, beta-band LFP power is more suppressed when the cue is on the left (contralateral) than on the right (ipsilateral).
outcomes.source: Figure 4C
outcomes.quote: Increased suppression for contralateral is observed as compared to ipsilateral movement conditions.
outcomes.notes: Among large-reward trials, median beta power over 0 to 0.5 s is 245 µV² for left cues and 301 µV² for right cues (282 and 288 trials, ratio 0.81, Mann-Whitney p = 1.6e-06). Before the cue left is slightly higher (ratio 1.095, p = 0.013), so relative to pre-cue power the difference is larger (ratio 0.71, p = 2.1e-09). It holds over 0 to 1 s (p = 0.019), not over 0.25 to 0.75 s (p = 0.75), and also in small-reward trials (p = 1.5e-10). On the unsmoothed envelope left is lower over 0 to 0.5 s (ratio 0.807, p = 1.7e-06) and 0.125 to 0.5 s (ratio 0.688, p = 3.2e-17), most from 0.1 to 0.3 s (ratios 0.54 and 0.55).
deviations: Left is taken as contralateral, as the Methods state; the files do not say which hemisphere was implanted.
Window and test chosen before the analysis, as for fig4b-beta-reward.

outcomes.statement: Spikes recorded from an s-µIP in the caudate of monkey P (site c33, 390 days post implant) fire at a different rate for large and small reward during the value cue fixation of the direction task.
outcomes.source: Figure 5A; Results and Discussion, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: Spike measurements from an s-μIP in the CN of monkey P also displayed reward-modulated differences in firing rate during the value cue fixation window
outcomes.notes: Monkey P's file has no trials table and no events, so value cue times and reward sizes are not in the dandiset. The paper's Zenodo deposit has the session's raw Neuralynx events (session126_events.mat) as TTL values without names; their codes differ from those of the Monkey T sessions, so they could not be decoded (metadata insufficient). The notebook now reads that file, with 20812 events with 36 distinct TTL values and no names; the trial-start code 128 does not occur and the value cue code 23 occurs 20 times.

outcomes.statement: The s-µIP recorded a spike-sorted unit in monkey P, shown by its average waveform and its interspike interval histogram.
outcomes.source: Figure 5B and 5C
outcomes.quote: Average spike waveform ± standard deviation. ... Interspike interval (ISI) histogram showing the distribution of the timing between spikes detected.
outcomes.notes: Plexon unit 1 has 31247 spikes at 2.61 Hz. One of 31246 interspike intervals is under 1 ms (0.003%), and its mean waveform trough (-30.6 µV) is 5.66 times the raw noise level (5.41 µV, 300 to 6000 Hz, 600 s). The units table's unit 0 (unsorted and poor-quality spikes merged) has 11.65% of intervals under 1 ms and is not a unit.
deviations: The noise level and the two thresholds are common choices; the paper shows the waveform and histogram without numbers.
The paper names the site c33; the file names it cl3. The session is taken as the paper's.

findings.statement: Each event is stored about five times in the events tables of both Monkey T sessions (85665 stored times, 17686 distinct, in 09/13/2024; 59702 and 12434 in 09/26/2024), once for every overlapping 60 s trial window that contains it.

The trials tables hold only times, no trial conditions. Conditions must be decoded from the event codes. Session 09/13/2024 has no small-reward code, and the labels of codes 35 and 36 ("right cue reward condition 1/2") do not say that they code large and small reward, which the data show in all 303 successful forced trials.

The trial-aligned FSCV table of session 09/13/2024 has rows for only the first 734 of its 1468 trials (from a source file named "firsthalf"), and the dandiset has FSCV from c8dg only; the second site of Figure 3A (c8ds) is missing.
The trial-aligned FSCV columns (da, ph, m, iox) carry no units, and da is not referenced at the value cue as the Methods describe; the reference point is not stated.
The raw FSCV current is labelled amperes, but its values range from -1527 to 1557; the unit is likely nA or the data are not current.

The raw FSCV scan times are an exact 0.1 s grid starting at the first trial start and running 24120 s, past the last trial, and the raw current cannot be matched to the trial-aligned oxidation current at any offset or to the task at the stored times. The conversion notes say the times were interpolated between trial-start codes; the data do not support that they are on the trial clock.
The bipolar LFP of session 09/26/2024 stores values already in volts (around 1e-4) with a conversion factor of 3.05e-8, so that read as NWB prescribes it is in picovolts.

The raw ephys of session 09/26/2024 has starting_time 0 and no timestamps, but it matches the stored LFP (r 0.92 to 0.98) only when read 9831.35 s later on the trial clock, consistently from the first trial to the last.

In Monkey P's file the spike times (6800 to 18785 s) are 6800.666 s later than the raw signal's timestamps (0 to 11985 s); the spike-triggered average of the raw signal shows the spike only with that shift. The file does not say the two use different clocks.

In Monkey P's units table, unit 0 merges the unsorted (0) and poor-quality (-1) thresholded spikes, including 7 spike times below 1 s and 3 repeated times; the poor-quality spikes of the thresholded table are not in time order.
Monkey P's file has no trials or events, so the reward-related firing of Figure 5A cannot be tested. The paper's Zenodo events for this session are raw TTL values without a code map.
No implantation dates are given, so the days post-implant of each session cannot be checked.

Monkey P's site is named cl3 in the file and dandiset description, c33 in the Figure 5 legend; the files' related_publications cite the bioRxiv preprint, not the article; the acquisition high cut is 8000 Hz in the Neuralynx settings, not the 7500 Hz the description states.
The applied FSCV waveform runs from -0.347 to 1.340 V, as the dandiset description says; the paper's Methods give -0.4 to 1.3 V.
