attempts.label: DANDI:002014
attempts.paper_title: Aseptic, semi-sealed cranial chamber implants for chronic multi-channel neurochemical and electrophysiological neural recording in nonhuman primates
attempts.entry_title: Dopamine, spikes and LFP through an aseptic cranial chamber in a rhesus monkey (Choi et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the recording findings of Choi et al. (2025) on dandiset 002014, which holds one session of monkey T recorded through the paper's semi-sealed chamber. It compares dopamine and beta-band LFP power between large and small reward trials, aligns spikes to the value cue, and checks the unit's waveform and interspike intervals. The surgical, culture, drainage and yield results, and monkey J, are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Choi et al. (2025) from dandiset 002014

outcomes.statement: In a single trial (trial 133 of the session), dopamine concentration changes at site c8ds fluctuate, especially after the value cue display.
outcomes.source: Figure 8A and its legend
outcomes.quote: Single trial measurements of dopamine concentration changes (Δ[DA]) as a function of time relative to value cue display (V) at 0 s (trial 133 in the session). ... Δ[DA] fluctuations are especially visible after the value cue display.
outcomes.notes: In trial 133 (1-based, a successful large reward trial) the SD of dopamine referenced at V over the 5 s after V is 2.02 times that over the 5 s before. Under the other reading (index 133, trial 134) the ratio is 2.04, with 36% and 46% of samples NaN. The test is weak. Of the 889 successful trials with a reference at V, the median ratio is 1.27, 64% exceed 1, and trial 133's ratio is above 76.9% of them. The criterion was written after trial 133's values had been printed.
deviations: The paper shows the trial as a figure with no measure; the SD ratio and its windows were chosen here.
The paper's trial numbering is not stated; both 1-based and 0-based readings are shown, and both match.

outcomes.statement: Trial-averaged dopamine at site c8ds, aligned to the value cue, increases more for large than for small reward trials, especially between the value cue display and reward.
outcomes.source: Figure 8B and its legend
outcomes.quote: Trial averaged Δ[DA] aligned to V at 0 s for large and small reward trials, showing increased dopamine release for large in comparison to small reward trials, especially between the value cue display and reward (RW) event.
outcomes.notes: From V to reward, dopamine referenced at V averages 1.88 in large and 1.10 in small reward trials (difference 0.78 in the file's unstated unit, Cohen's d 0.19, Mann-Whitney p = 0.0035, 429 and 460 trials, 23 and 39 dropped for lack of a reference at V). Shuffling the labels within blocks of 50 consecutive trials, which keeps the drift across the session in the null, gives p = 0.0045. The difference is small in the first 2 s after V (p = 0.44) and largest from reward to 3 s after (difference 1.59, p = 0.0001, within blocks p = 0.0010); before V there is none (p = 0.50). It holds in the second half of the session (p = 0.0125) and not significantly in the first (p = 0.075). Without trial 1411, p = 0.0031.
deviations: The PCA dopamine estimate at V is subtracted, in place of subtracting the background voltammogram at V before the PCA; the two agree if the PCA model is linear, which the dandiset does not let us check.
The window (V to each trial's reward) and the test were chosen here; the paper states none.
Trial 1411, which the paper's large reward list leaves out, is included (one trial of 452); without it p = 0.0031.
Where dopamine is NaN at V, the reference is interpolated between the nearest valid samples if both lie within 0.2 s; none of the 62 such trials has them, so all are dropped.

outcomes.statement: Spikes recorded at site c5d on a chamber-implanted CFE can be shown as a raster and a peristimulus time histogram aligned to the value cue display, for large and small reward trials.
outcomes.source: Figure 9A and its legend; Results, section 3.5, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Raster plot of spikes detected on each trial (y-axis) as a function of time relative to value cue display (V) at 0 s (site c5d). ... Peristimulus time histogram (PSTH) showing average spike firing rate (y-axis) for the large (red) and small (blue) reward conditions
outcomes.notes: With the spike times moved to the trial clock by the offset measured in the data check (11812.11 s), all successful trials have a spike within V - 1 s to V + 3 s, and the variance across 100 ms bins of the PSTH is 0.49 against a 95th percentile of 0.06 over random alignments (p = 0.005 with 200); 0.48 with the 7 ms lag also corrected. The rate falls from 5.63 spikes/s before V to 4.58 in the first 0.2 s and rises to 7.70 at 0.3 to 0.5 s. Large and small trials do not differ over 0 to 1 s (5.69 against 5.66 spikes/s, p = 0.90); the paper states no difference. The Plexon unit gives 0.17 against 0.06. With the spike times as stored, 42% of trials have a spike in the window and the variance is 0.01 against 0.03, so the claim fails on the file as published.
deviations: The spike times are moved by an offset measured from the data (the raw ephys located in the stored LFP); the file places them 11812.11 s early.
The spikes are those of the thresholded table (the paper's Zenodo file); the Plexon unit is a variant.
The paper states no effect for this panel; the criterion (spikes in most trials, and a rate locked to V beyond chance) was chosen here.

outcomes.statement: The spikes at site c5d have a consistent waveform (mean and standard deviation) and an interspike interval distribution (1 ms bins) consistent with a single unit.
outcomes.source: Figure 9B and 9C and their legends
outcomes.quote: Average spike waveform + /− standard deviation. C. Interspike interval (ISI) histogram showing the distribution of the timing between spikes detected. Bin widths are 1 ms.
outcomes.notes: The criterion holds, but the evidence for a single unit is weak. No ISI is under 1 ms (9 of 101732 under 2 ms), and the mean waveform's trough of -56.4 µV is 4.79 times the SD across spikes at that sample. Neither part could easily fail. The shortest ISI, 1.562 ms, just exceeds the 48-sample (1.50 ms) waveform, so the detector's dead time excludes ISIs under 1 ms, and every one of the 101733 spikes exceeds the 40 µV threshold (smallest peak 40.3 µV), which nearly forces the trough above twice the SD. Above the dead time, ISIs per ms at 1.56 to 3 ms are 0.106 times those at 10 to 30 ms (Plexon unit 0.204), which fits a refractory period in most spikes but does not rule out other units. Only 54411 of the Plexon unit's 90912 spikes lie within 0.2 ms of a spike of thresholded unit 1 (101733 spikes). The Plexon unit has 1 ISI under 1 ms, 14 (0.015%) under 1.56 ms and 39 (0.04%) under 2 ms.
deviations: The paper states no measure for these panels; the 1% ISI rule and the trough-to-SD ratio are common choices made here.
The waveforms are read as microvolts, although the file states volts.

outcomes.statement: Trial-averaged beta-band LFP power at c7b referenced to c5c is suppressed more in the brief window after the value cue for large than for small reward cues.
outcomes.source: Figure 9D and its legend
outcomes.quote: Trial averaged beta-band LFP power showing increased suppression during the brief time window immediately following the cue (V) for large as compared to small reward cues (site c7b-c5c).
outcomes.notes: Beta power (13 to 30 Hz) falls after V in both conditions (median log10 ratio of 0 to 0.5 s after V to 0.5 s before, -0.158 for large and -0.125 for small, each p < 0.001 against 0). The fall is larger for large cues, but not significantly (difference of medians -0.033, Mann-Whitney p = 0.108; 452 and 499 trials, none dropped; shuffling within blocks of 50 trials, p = 0.19). Averaged over trials, as in the paper's figure, power over 0 to 0.5 s is 0.839 of the baseline for large (95% CI 0.782 to 0.903) and 0.885 for small (0.831 to 0.940), a difference of -0.046 (-0.125 to 0.036). No variant reaches p < 0.05 (15 to 30 Hz, p = 0.063; 1 s baseline, p = 0.108; 12 to 25 Hz, p = 0.19; windows of 0 to 0.3 s and 0 to 1 s, p = 0.59 and 0.84; without baseline, p = 0.17). The paper states no test for this panel.
deviations: The band, the filter, the power measure, the baseline, the window and the test were chosen here; the paper gives none.
The stored series, described as beta-band LFP, is broadband and was band-passed here.

outcomes.statement: The chamber system provided recordings of dopamine and electrical neural activity in two monkeys (T and J).
outcomes.source: Abstract, Results; Results, section 3.5, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Our chamber system was shown to provide successful recordings of dopamine and electrical neural activity in two monkeys
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds one session of monkey T only (one NWB file). No recording of monkey J is in it or in the paper's Zenodo record, which also holds monkey T only. The monkey T part is tested by the Figure 8 and 9 claims.

outcomes.statement: 53% (21/40) and 25% (13/51) of implanted sCFEs retained functionality (background current above 500 nA and noise below 0.05 nA) in monkeys T and J.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: 53 % (21/40) and 25 % (13/51) of the implanted sCFE’s retained functionality (background current > 500 nA and noise < 0.05 nA) in monkeys T and J, respectively.
outcomes.notes: The per-electrode background current and noise measured at implantation and during recovery, for 40 and 51 sCFEs, are not in the dandiset, which holds one FSCV electrode (c8ds) on one day. Not found in the Zenodo record either.

outcomes.statement: 73% (29/40) and 39% (20/51) of implanted sCFEs retained background current above 500 nA in monkeys T and J, of which 28% and 35% had noise above 0.05 nA.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: 73 % (29/40) and 39 % (20/51) of the implanted sCFE’s retained viable background current > 500 nA, and of these several (28 % and 35 % in monkeys T and J, respectively) fell short of full functionality with noise levels > 0.05 nA.
outcomes.notes: As for scfe-functional-yield; the electrode-level background and noise measurements are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: 21.4% (3/14) and 14.2% (2/14) of mCFEs retained functionality in monkeys T and J.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: On the other hand, the mCFE’s retained a lower functional yield of 21.4 % (3/14) and 14.2 % (2/14) in T and J, respectively.
outcomes.notes: No mCFE measurements are in the dandiset or the Zenodo record.

outcomes.statement: Of the functional CFEs, 63% (15/24) and 53% (8/15) in monkeys T and J displayed visible dopamine signals and were used during task performance.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.5, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Of the functional CFEs, 63 % (15/24) and 53 % (8/15) in monkeys T and J, respectively, displayed visible dopamine signals (i.e., current changes along dopamine redox potentials), and were successfully applied in measurements during task performance.
outcomes.notes: The dandiset holds the FSCV of one electrode; the 24 and 15 functional CFEs and which of them showed dopamine signals are not deposited.

outcomes.statement: Monkey T kept negative bacterial cultures for all samples; in monkey J, staphylococcus cultured at 29 days post-implant was cleared by 39 to 44 days and the chamber stayed aseptic for 286 days after treatment.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 3; Abstract
outcomes.quote: Bacteria (staphylococcus) was cultured about a month post-implant (29 days) in monkey J ... Monkey T maintained negative cultures for all collected samples. ... 39 – 44 days post-implant the samples began to show negative results ... maintained aseptic condition for the next 286 days
outcomes.notes: The culture results (IDEXX BioAnalytics) are not in the dandiset, the Zenodo record or the protocols.io protocols the paper cites.

outcomes.statement: Fluid aspirated from the chamber per session ranged from 0.3 to 4.8 mL in monkey T and 0.2 to 9.8 mL in monkey J, and was sanguinous for the first 18 (T) and 217 (J) days.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.2, paragraph 1; Figure 6
outcomes.quote: Fluid collected from the chamber aspiration tube for a given day varied between 0.3 – 4.8 mL for monkey T and between 0.2 – 9.8 mL for monkey J (Fig. 6). ... sanguinous (i.e., bloody) in the first few weeks or months (18 days post-implant in monkey T and 217 days in J)
outcomes.notes: The aspirated volumes per session are not in the dandiset or the Zenodo record.

outcomes.statement: Bone growth was observed within and around the chamber in both monkeys, and the chamber margins stayed relatively healthy.
outcomes.source: Results, section 3.3, paragraph 1, and section 3.4, paragraph 1; Figure 7
outcomes.quote: Prominent bone growth was observed in both monkeys within and around the chamber interfaces (Fig. 7). ... The margins of the chamber in both monkeys remained relatively healthy and intact (Fig. 7D and E).
outcomes.notes: The observations are photographs and surgical notes, which are not deposited.

findings.statement: The raw ephys and the spike times are not on the clock of the trials, events, LFP and FSCV table. The raw ephys is stored with a starting time of 0 s and a rate, and the spike times count from its first sample. Locating the raw c7b minus c5c signal in the stored LFP puts raw time 0 at 11812.11 s on the trial clock (correlation 0.98 to 1.00 at eight points, drift about 4 ms per hour). Without this correction spikes cannot be aligned to the task. The dandiset description says all data are expressed relative to the start of the Neuralynx recording, which the data contradict.

The absolute times disagree. On the trial clock the raw samples run from 12:06:44 to 17:12:20, while the Neuralynx header gives the recording as opened at 08:49:52 (the session start) and closed at 15:12:24, two hours before the raw samples end. The header span (22952 s) is also longer than the raw samples (18336 s).

The stored spike times of the thresholded units are about 7.1 ms after the spike troughs in raw c5d (in one 300 s segment of 1633 spikes, per-spike trough lags of -7.4 to -6.9 ms from the 10th to the 90th percentile, 98.8% within 0.5 ms of -7.1 ms).

The series "bipolar_lfp_series" is described as beta-band LFP but is broadband with line noise removed. Its values are already in volts, while it carries the raw int16 conversion factor (3.05e-8), which would scale them about 3e7 times too small.
The thresholded spike waveforms are stated in volts but hold microvolts (mean trough about -56), and the raw FSCV current is stated in amperes but holds nanoamperes (values around 1000).
The columns of the trial-aligned FSCV table (da, ph, m, iox) state no units, and the `good` column is true for every trial.

The subject description ("Two adult female rhesus monkeys were used for in vivo validation of the s-µIP device"), the session and experiment descriptions and the keyword "micro-invasive neural implant" describe the lab's micro-invasive probe study, not this paper's chamber.

The event table stores each event once per overlapping 60 s trial window, about five copies of each (7221 stored trial-start events for 1412 distinct ones), and its event times are not sorted. The Plexon units table's spike times are not sorted either.

The trial tags are all "initial cue display" and carry no trial type. Reward size and outcome can be rebuilt from the events, and they then match the paper's Zenodo trial lists except trial 1411, which the events mark as a successful large reward trial and the list leaves out.

The paper says the reward size depends on whether the target is at the top or bottom of the screen. The events code left and right conditions, and both reward sizes occur on both sides, so the target position that sets the reward is not in the dandiset.

The raw FSCV minute files are joined without their gaps (328 min of scans against 302 min of trials, placed from a single starting time), and the trial-aligned oxidation current cannot be located in them, so the raw FSCV's clock could not be established.

Only one session of monkey T is deposited. The data behind the electrode yields, cultures, drainage volumes and bone growth, and all of monkey J, are not, so eight of the thirteen claims cannot be tested.

attempts.label: CRCNS:ret-1
attempts.entry_title: Retinal ganglion cell responses in Pcdh-gamma mutant retina (Lefebvre et al. 2008)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Lefebvre, Zhang, Meister, Wang and Sanes (2008) on CRCNS data set ret-1, which holds multielectrode recordings of 325 units from 16 mutant and control mouse retinas stimulated with flickering bars and checkerboards. It compares receptive field size, response time course, firing rate and Linear-Nonlinear model threshold and gain between Pcdh-gamma mutant and control retinas (Figure 9D to 9H). The histology of Figures 1 to 8 and the flash, spot and grating experiments of Figure 9A to 9C are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Lefebvre et al. (2008), Figure 9, from CRCNS ret-1

outcomes.statement: Pcdh-gamma proteins (Pcdh-gamma-GFP in fusg mice) are present in all five retinal layers and in all six retinal cell types (photoreceptors, horizontal, bipolar, amacrine, RGCs and Mueller glia).
outcomes.source: Results, Broad expression of gamma protocadherins in retina, paragraphs 2 and 3; Figure 1
outcomes.quote: As judged by localization of GFP in Pcdh-γ fusg mice, Pcdh-γs are present in all five retinal layers ... All six cell types were Pcdh-γ-positive ... Thus, Pcdh-γs are expressed in all cell types of the neural retina.
outcomes.notes: The claim rests on histology (sections, dissociated cells or counts of stained cells). The data set holds only spike times and white-noise stimuli from the multielectrode recordings, and the paper names no other deposit of its images or counts.

outcomes.statement: Pcdh-gamma is present in the IPL, neuroblast layer and RGC axons at P0, appears in the developing OPL by P7, and reaches the adult pattern by P14.
outcomes.source: Results, Broad expression of gamma protocadherins in retina, paragraph 4; Figure 2
outcomes.quote: At this time, Pcdh-γ is present on cells in the neuroblast layer, in the IPL, and on RGC axons ( Figure 2A ) ... By P7, Pcdh-γ appears in the OPL, as it divides the neuroblast layer into INL and ONL ( Figure 2C ). By P14, the adult pattern described above is established
outcomes.notes: The claim rests on histology (sections, dissociated cells or counts of stained cells). The data set holds only spike times and white-noise stimuli from the multielectrode recordings, and the paper names no other deposit of its images or counts.

outcomes.statement: Pcdh-gammas are present in pre- and postsynaptic compartments of rod and cone synapses in the OPL, though little is in horizontal cell varicosities, and at many but not only synaptic sites in the IPL.
outcomes.source: Results, Synaptic localization of Pcdh-γ proteins in the retina, paragraphs 1 and 2; Figure 3
outcomes.quote: Thus, Pcdh-γs were present in pre- and post-synaptic compartments of rod and cone synapses. In contrast, although horizontal cell processes labeled with anti-calbindin ... were Pcdh-γ-positive, little Pcdh-γ was present in their synaptic varicosities

outcomes.statement: Figure 9C to 9H report 115 RGCs from mutant retinas and 143 RGCs from control retinas.
outcomes.source: Figure 9 legend, panels C to H
outcomes.quote: plots a cumulative histogram of that quantity for RGCs in mutant retinas (red curve, 115 cells ... and control retinas (black curve, 143 cells
outcomes.notes: The data set's labels give 200 mutant units (87 Chx10-Cre in 6 retinas, 113 Pax6-Cre in 4) and 122 control units (95 labelled "WT (chx10 het)" in 3 retinas, 27 "WT (pax6 het)" in 2), against 115 (103.5 to 126.5) and 143 (128.7 to 157.3). Every unit fired during the bar stimulus. Units whose STA peak exceeds 1.5 times the null's number 138 mutant and 113 control; above 2 times, 103 and 107. Neither mutant count shown is inside its tolerance (103 is just below 103.5), but the mutant count falls from 138 to 103 between the two thresholds, so a threshold between them could put it inside, and with the 20080702 frames as deposited the count above 1.5 is 126, inside it. No count of control units can exceed 122, so the counts miss under any reading of a flicker response because of the control count. Without the second unit of each duplicate pair, 189 and 118. The Bax -/- retina (3 units) is in neither group. The notebook tabulates the units per retina and label; the files do not give the region recorded in the Pax6-Cre retinas, so the paper's peripheral subset cannot be formed.
deviations: The claims file asks also for the count of units with a flicker response without defining one; the counts above two thresholds of the STA peak over a null STA are shown as a standard choice, and none can change the outcome.
The control retinas are as the data set labels them; 95 of the 122 control units carry a label ("WT (chx10 het)") that the paper's description of its controls does not include.

outcomes.statement: RGCs in mutant and control retinas show a similar variety of responses to small flashing spots, including sustained and transient ON, OFF and ON-OFF responses.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 3; Figure 9A
outcomes.quote: RGCs in Pcdh-γ mutant and control retinas showed a similar variety of responses to small flashing spots, including sustained and transient ON, OFF and ON-OFF responses
outcomes.notes: The data set holds no flashing-spot recordings; every recording is binary white noise (flickering bars or checkerboards). The claim also depends on fig9c-on-off-index, blocked for the same reason. The paper names no other deposit.

outcomes.statement: The proportions of ON- and OFF-dominated responses are the same in mutant and control retinas.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 3; Figure 9C
outcomes.quote: Proportions of ON- and OFF-dominated responses were identical in mutants and controls ( Figure 9C )
outcomes.notes: The On-Off index needs the flashing-spot experiment of Figure 9A, which is not in the data set; every recording is binary white noise.

outcomes.statement: Mutant RGCs respond to very dim flashes, which excite only rods, and to bright flashes, which mainly excite cones, so both rod and cone pathways function.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 3 (data not shown)
outcomes.quote: Mutant RGCs responded to very dim flashes, which excite only rods, and also to bright flashes, which predominantly excite cones (data not shown)
outcomes.notes: The data set holds no flashes, dim or bright; every recording is binary white noise at one luminance range, so the criterion's pair of intensities is absent.

outcomes.statement: Both ON and ON-OFF direction-selective RGCs are found in mutant retinas.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 3; Figure 9B
outcomes.quote: Both ON and ON-OFF direction-selective cells were encountered in mutant retinas ( Figure 9B and data not shown)

outcomes.statement: Receptive field centre size varies greatly among RGCs, but its distribution is similar in control and mutant retinas.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 4; Figure 9D
outcomes.quote: The size of the receptive field center varied greatly among RGCs, but the distribution was similar in control and mutant retinas ( Figure 9D )
outcomes.notes: The outcome rests on one borderline combination and on the frame correction of the 20080702 bar recordings. The readings disagree. In 17 of 18 combinations (3 recording readings, 2 separations, 3 bands) the 95% bands separate with mutant centres smaller; under reading B with the svd separation the DKW bands overlap (median 134 against 156 um, KS p = 0.004). Reading A, svd, median 122 against 156 um (KS p below 1e-4). This follows the correction of the frame of the 20080702 bar recordings; with the frames as deposited the reading B DKW bands separate too and all 18 separate, which was the outcome (not_reproduced) of the first run. Much of the difference comes from mutant units with weak STAs (97 of 200 mutant and 15 of 122 control units have an STA peak less than twice the null's). Among units above that, the medians are 145 and 158 um (reading A, KS p = 0.19), the binomial and bootstrap bands separate only between 82 and 101 um, and the DKW bands overlap; over the three readings 13 of 18 combinations separate in that subset, and 1 of the 6 DKW ones, so the outcome there is blocked too. With the 16.6 um bars alone 16 of 18 separate (the svd DKW bands overlap under readings A and B), and with Pax6-Cre mutants alone the svd DKW bands overlap under reading A. Under shuffled group labels the binomial and bootstrap bands of this measure separate in 38 and 45% of shuffles and the DKW band in none. The answer to the question in questions/crcns-ret-1.yaml (which bar recording) found that the paper does not say, and the criterion requires the outcome under the three recording readings A, B and C, which are run here.
deviations: All 5 retinas recorded with 8.3 um bars are mutant; every control retina was recorded with 16.6 um bars.
The mutant group cannot be restricted to the peripheral region of the Pax6-Cre retinas, as the data set does not say where they were recorded.
The vertical bars of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 are rebuilt with a frame of 16.6718 ms, the frame of the other bar recordings, not the stated 16.6691 and 16.6653 ms (see findings).

outcomes.statement: Some control and mutant RGCs have receptive field surrounds of opposite sign to the centre, so lateral inhibition functions in mutant circuits.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 3 (not read)
outcomes.quote: Some control and mutant RGCs had receptive field surrounds, where light has the opposite effect of the center
outcomes.notes: Under all 12 readings (3 recording readings, 2 separations, depths of 10% and 20%) at least one mutant and one control unit have a lobe of opposite sign on both flanks of b(x); reading A, svd, 20%, 90 of 200 mutant and 16 of 122 control units. The same rule applied to null STAs (spike counts shifted by half the recording) is met by 194 to 198 of 200 mutant and 119 to 121 of 122 control units, so the rule is met by noise. Among units with an STA peak above twice the null's, at least 7 mutant and 4 control units meet it at 20% in every reading. The outcome follows the criterion, but the result is no evidence for or against surrounds.
deviations: The vertical bars of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 are rebuilt with a frame of 16.6718 ms, as for fig9d-rf-size-similar.

outcomes.statement: The time course of the light response is significantly slower in mutant retina, measured as the time to peak of the temporal integration function a(t).

The DKW band, which never separated under shuffled labels, separates in every combination. The result holds in every variant, including units with clear STAs (103 mutant, 107 control), each Cre line alone and the Pax6-Cre heterozygous controls alone under reading A, and among units with clear STAs, with 16.6 um bars alone and with the 20080702 frames as deposited under all three readings (36 of 36 separate in each). With the frames as deposited, 8 binomial and bootstrap combinations (peak separation, readings A and C) also hold 1 or 2 values where the bands separate the other way; with the frames corrected none do. outcomes.statement: Mutant RGCs fire at much lower rates than control RGCs in response to flickering gratings.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 4; Figure 9F
outcomes.quote: Moreover, mutant RGCs fired at much lower rates in reponse to flicker stimuli ( Figure 9F )
outcomes.notes: In all 9 combinations (3 recording readings, 3 bands) the bands separate with the mutant curve at lower rates, DKW included; reading A, median 3.82 against 9.02 Hz (ratio 0.42; 0.38 to 0.45 over readings). By retina, mutant medians 1.9 to 15.9 Hz, control 3.8 to 23.6 Hz. Every variant gives a lower mutant median; with Pax6-Cre mutants alone (ratio 0.68) and among units with clear STAs (0.66), the DKW bands overlap while the binomial and bootstrap bands separate (those two separate in 38 and 39% of label shuffles for this measure). With the Pax6-Cre heterozygous controls alone (ratio 0.41) the DKW bands separate. The outcome depends on using all units, as the claims file's header reads the groups (all units of each group, the paper naming no exclusion). Among units with clear STAs, over the three readings, 6 of 9 combinations separate and no DKW one, which the criterion would call blocked. With the frames as deposited and with 16.6 um bars alone all 9 separate. outcomes.statement: In a Linear-Nonlinear model fitted to the flicker responses, the response threshold of mutant RGCs is unaltered.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 4; Figure 9G
outcomes.quote: Based on fitting with a Linear-Nonlinear model ... we found that the threshold is unaltered, but the gain is reduced in mutants ( Figures 9G-H )
outcomes.notes: In all 36 combinations (3 recording readings, 2 fits, 2 forms, 3 bands) the bands separate, with mutant thresholds higher, DKW included; reading A, frame fit, median 1.12 against 0.44 SD of the generator (continuous form) and 1.69 against 0.01 (printed form). Part of this comes from mutant units with weak STAs, whose generator predicts little of the rate; among units with clear STAs the medians are 0.86 against 0.41 (reading A, frame fit, continuous form), and over the three readings 24 of 36 combinations separate and no DKW one, which the criterion would call blocked. The outcome depends on using all units, as the claims file's header reads the groups. With the frames as deposited and with 16.6 um bars alone all 36 separate. The binned fit in the printed form stops at a grid edge in 107 of 200 mutant fits, all at the top, and 39 of 122 control fits, 33 at the top and 6 at the bottom (reading A); why they reach the top is not shown. Without the edge fits its medians are -0.03 and -0.03 (KS p = 0.21) and its DKW and bootstrap bands overlap, but that comparison drops most high mutant fits by construction and is no evidence that the threshold is unaltered. The frame fit in the continuous form has 1 fit per group at a grid edge, at the top, and separates under every band. With the Pax6-Cre heterozygous controls alone the DKW bands still separate.

The vertical bars of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 are rebuilt with a frame of 16.6718 ms, as for fig9d-rf-size-similar.

outcomes.statement: In the same Linear-Nonlinear model, the gain of mutant RGCs is reduced.
outcomes.source: Results, Functional visual circuits form in the absence of Pcdh- γ s, paragraph 4; Figure 9H
outcomes.quote: we found that the threshold is unaltered, but the gain is reduced in mutants ( Figures 9G-H )

With the printed form (B + G y above theta), mutant gains are lower and the bands separate in all 18 combinations (reading A, frame fit, median 18.4 against 23.1 Hz per SD, ratio 0.80). With the continuous form (B + G (y - theta)), the bands overlap in 9 of 18, separate with mutant gains lower in 4 (reading B, binomial and bootstrap) and the other way in 5 (readings A and C); the DKW bands overlap in all 6 continuous-form combinations (reading A, frame fit, median 30.4 against 30.8, KS p = 0.76). Under reading B the continuous-form separations rest mostly on the 4 to 13 mutant gains below the lowest control gain, and under reading A, frame fit, bootstrap, on 1 mutant against 6 control cells; the others lie inside the distributions (reading A, binned fit, 165 of 200 mutant and 113 of 122 control cells at or below 41.46; reading C, frame fit, 16 to 19 mutant against 23 to 25 control cells near 21.2). Among units with clear STAs neither form gives lower mutant gains under reading A (printed 23.1 against 23.4, continuous 33.1 against 31.0); over the three readings in that subset the printed form separates with mutant gains lower in 6 of 18 combinations and the continuous form in 4, with 6 the other way and no DKW separation, so the outcome there is blocked too. With the frames as deposited the continuous form separates in 4 of 18, all with mutant gains lower, and the outcome is the same. On synthetic cells that follow the continuous form (theta 0.5, G 20), the printed-form frame fit returns theta 0.75 and G 13.4, so part of the printed-form gain reduction may mirror the higher mutant thresholds.

findings.statement: The data set holds only the white-noise recordings behind Figure 9D to 9H. The histology of Figures 1 to 8 and Supplementary Figure 1, and the flashing-spot, flash, moving-bar and grating recordings of Figure 9A to 9C, are not in it, and the paper names no other deposit. Of the 26 claims, 19 cannot be tested.

The data set holds 200 mutant and 122 control units (and 3 from a Bax -/- mutant), where the paper's Figure 9 has 115 mutant and 143 control cells. The data set does not say how its units relate to the paper's, which were kept, or why the counts differ.

The data set labels 95 of its 122 control units "WT (chx10 het)", while the paper's Figure 9 legend gives the controls as Pax6-Cre;Pcdh-gamma +/f-del or Pcdh-gamma f-del/f-del without Cre. The labels and the paper disagree on what the controls were.

In the 8 recordings of 20080628_R4, 20080628_R6, 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4, 82 of 86 spike trains are not in time order. Each runs to 1440 s and then holds a second segment between 720 and 780 s, though the stimulus runs to 1500 s. The 4 trains in order have spikes between 1440 and 1500 s, about as many as between 720 and 780 s, and moving the segments by 720 s raises their STA peaks over the null in most units. This is consistent with the last minute stored with a 720 s offset in place of 1440 s. One checkerboard recording (20080628_R5) has 1 or 2 spikes near 2 s out of order in 15 units.

The frame lengths stated for the vertical-bar recordings of 20080702_R1 and 20080702_R4 (16.6691 and 16.6653 ms) are not those of the stimulus. Rebuilt with the stated frame, the bars of 20080702_R4 give no STA above the null in any of its 12 units (median ratio 0.96), though all 12 respond to the checkerboard of the same retina. A scan of the frame peaks at 16.671 to 16.672 ms in both recordings; with 16.6718 ms, the frame of every other bar recording and half the checkerboard frame of the same two retinas, the median ratio is 2.57 and 10 of the 12 units have peaks above twice the null's.

16 pairs of units share 70 to 100% of their spikes within 0.5 ms in every recording of their retina (12 pairs in mutant retinas, 4 in a control retina), most likely single neurons sorted twice. The data set does not mark them.

The files do not give the age of the mice, the Pcdh-gamma allele (the paper's Results say fcon3 and its Figure 9 legend f-del), the region recorded in the Pax6-Cre retinas (the paper used their periphery only), or the cell type of the units.

attempts.label: DRYAD:4j0zpc8hz
attempts.entry_title: Chronic warming and dry soils in beech and oak (Didion-Gency et al. 2024)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Didion-Gency, Vitasse, Buchmann, Gessler, Gisler, Schaub and Grossiord (2024) on Dryad dataset 4j0zpc8hz, one table of 96 beech and oak trees grown in open-top chambers under warming and soil moisture reduction, in monocultures and mixtures, from 2019 to 2021. It tests the phenology regressions on air temperature, the treatment effects on leaf water potential, carbon relations and growth, and the effects of species mixture. The soil moisture and chamber climate records are not in the dataset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Didion-Gency et al. (2024) from Dryad dataset 4j0zpc8hz

outcomes.statement: Warmer spring air advanced bud swelling in both species, by 1.1 days per degree in beech and 2.3 days per degree in oak, across 2020 and 2021 and the four treatments.
outcomes.source: Results, Phenology, paragraph 1; Figure 1A and 1B
outcomes.quote: Higher daily air temperatures in spring were linked to an earlier bud swelling in both species, where beech was advanced by −1.1 d °C−1 and oak by −2.3 d °C−1 across the 2 yr and treatments

statistics.n: monoculture trees, 6 per treatment, species and year, 2020 and 2021

outcomes.notes: Slopes of bud swelling on Tspring, monoculture trees 2020 and 2021, -1.078 days per degree in beech and -2.296 in oak, both within tolerance; P1 p = 0.00011 and 1.2e-08, P2 (8 treatment-year means) p = 0.033 and 0.010. The slopes are equal under P1 and P2 because every treatment-year has six trees. With a random intercept per treatment and year added to P1 (a variant, not a reading of the claims file), p = 0.0060 and 0.0002.
deviations: Reading P1 uses each tree-year against its treatment's temperature, as the dataset gives one temperature per treatment and year and no chamber value.
The sensor height (H1, 50 cm, or H2, 2 m) of the deposited temperatures is not stated, so H1 and H2 could not be run separately.

outcomes.statement: Warmer spring air shortened leaf development duration by 0.7 days per degree in both species.
outcomes.source: Results, Phenology, paragraph 1; Figure 1C and 1D
outcomes.quote: A shorter leaf development duration was also found, with a reduction of −0.7 d °C−1 in both species
outcomes.notes: Slopes of development duration on Tspring, -0.651 (beech) and -0.659 (oak) days per degree, within 0.7 +- 0.07. Under P1 p = 0.0010 and 0.0039; under P2 the oak regression has p = 0.16, so only P1 meets the criterion, which needs one reading. P1 treats the 48 tree-years as independent although the temperature is one value per treatment and year; with a random intercept per treatment and year (a variant, not a reading of the claims file), oak has p = 0.11 and beech 0.012, so the oak result rests on P1 as the claims file gives it.
deviations: Reading P1 uses each tree-year against its treatment's temperature, as the dataset gives one temperature per treatment and year and no chamber value.
The sensor height (H1, 50 cm, or H2, 2 m) of the deposited temperatures is not stated, so H1 and H2 could not be run separately.

outcomes.statement: Warmer fall air extended leaf senescence duration by 3.4 days per degree in beech and 3.1 days per degree in oak.
outcomes.source: Results, Phenology, paragraph 1; Figure 1G and 1H
outcomes.quote: Similarly, senescence duration was extended by +3.4 d °C−1 in beech and +3.1 d °C−1 in oak
outcomes.notes: Slopes of senescence duration on Tfall, 3.396 (beech) and 3.084 (oak) days per degree, within tolerance; p <= 0.0056 under P1 and P2, and p < 0.0001 with a random intercept per treatment and year (a variant).
deviations: Reading P1 uses each tree-year against its treatment's temperature, as the dataset gives one temperature per treatment and year and no chamber value.
The sensor height (H1, 50 cm, or H2, 2 m) of the deposited temperatures is not stated, so H1 and H2 could not be run separately.

outcomes.statement: Warmer annual air lengthened the growing season by 4.5 days per degree in beech and 5.7 days per degree in oak.
outcomes.source: Results, Phenology, paragraph 1; Figure 1I and 1J
outcomes.quote: The growing seasons were extended by +4.5 d °C−1 and +5.7 d °C−1 for beech and oak, respectively, with an increase in daily mean annual air temperature
outcomes.notes: Slopes of the deposited growing season length on Tannual, 4.460 (beech) and 5.652 (oak) days per degree, within tolerance; p <= 0.035 under P1 and P2. The deposited Growth_length never equals onset of senescence minus bud swelling, the Methods' definition (median difference 55 days); with that definition, which the criterion repeats (bud swelling to onset of senescence), the slopes are 1.09 (beech, P1 p = 0.085) and 2.16 (oak, P1 p = 0.0014), and the claim would not be reproduced. Neither the workbook nor Metadata.csv defines Growth_length. The outcome uses the deposited column, which gives the paper's slopes within 0.04; a question asks which is to be tested. With a random intercept per treatment and year (a variant), p = 0.0067 and < 0.0001.
deviations: Reading P1 uses each tree-year against its treatment's temperature, as the dataset gives one temperature per treatment and year and no chamber value.
The sensor height (H1, 50 cm, or H2, 2 m) of the deposited temperatures is not stated, so H1 and H2 could not be run separately.
The deposited Growth_length is used; it does not follow the Methods' definition (see findings).

outcomes.statement: The temperature-driven advance was larger in oak than in beech (P = 0.004, least squares analysis).
outcomes.source: Results, Phenology, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: However chronic warming was more advantageous to oak than to beech as the advancement of bud swelling extension was higher in oak (P = 0.004 using Least-squares analysis)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), bud swelling on Tspring by species, each tree-year (P1): oak slope -2.30 against beech -1.08, species by temperature interaction p = 0.0046 (paper 0.004). With a random intercept per species, treatment and year added to P1 (a variant, not a reading of the claims file), reading (a) gives p = 0.097, so the result rests on P1 as the claims file gives it.
deviations: Reading P1 uses each tree-year against its treatment's temperature, as the dataset gives one temperature per treatment and year and no chamber value.

findings.statement: Metadata.csv and the README sheet give the treatment codes as C, W, MR and WMR; the Treatment column holds C, D, H and HD. The Warming and Soil moisture reduction columns map them one to one (H is W, D is MR, HD is WMR).

The 'Total Data' sheet has 35 rows that repeat another row exactly (trees 17, 35, 45 and 144; tree 35 has 24 rows in place of 9), and tree 144 has two rows for campaign 5 of 2020 with different sugar (7.71 and 6.69 %) and starch (4.99 and 9.99 %) values.

Starch (77 tree-campaign rows, down to -6.28 %), sugar (3, down to -4.06 %) and Asat (5, down to -0.29) have negative values, which a concentration or a light-saturated assimilation rate cannot have; the paper takes their square root.

Growth_length ('growing season length') never equals onset of senescence minus bud swelling (Senes_10 - Flush_S1), the Methods' definition: it is a median 55 days longer, and 2 to 33 days longer than the end of senescence (Senes_10 + Senes_time) minus bud swelling. Its definition is not given.
Diameter_growth is labelled cm, but its values (median 0.42, up to 4.46 a year) on stems of 5.2 to 6.1 mm at planting (Table S4) are consistent with mm.

The soil moisture (Mspring, Mfall, Mannual), the chamber climate records (air temperature, relative humidity, VPD, soil temperature and water content at 10 min) and the initial heights and diameters (Table S4) are not deposited; five claims rest on them.

Tspring, Tfall and Tannual are one value per treatment and year (the same in the four chambers of a treatment), and the sensor height (50 cm or 2 m) they come from is not stated; GDD and Chill_days are given per tree without the records they were computed from, and the GDD description does not say whether the excess over 5 C or the daily mean is summed.
Four compartments (6 in chambers A3, A4, B3 and B4) hold a beech monoculture tree and an oak mixture tree, which the design (a compartment holds a monoculture or a mixture) does not allow.
AGB_growth (estimated AGWB increment) is exactly 0 in 57 of 191 tree-years of 2020 and 2021, whose median height increment is 5 cm, and is never negative; how it was bounded is not described.

Refitting the paper's treatment model on the dataset with marginal F tests gives Supplemental Table S1's F values for oak AGWB increment exactly and for beech Asat within 0.25, which links the deposited table to the paper's analysis; other traits match less closely.

The Methods say the treatments started in June 2019, after the first leaf flushing and measurement campaign, and that 2019 is not included in the study, yet the treatment model has year 2019 to 2021 as a fixed effect (Table S1's F and p pairs for terms with year fit two numerator df, as the claims file notes). Under reading T1, which follows that model, the 2019 yearly means (L1) and the 2019 campaign values (L2) include the first campaign, measured before the treatments began.

attempts.entry_title: Phage selection and resistance-virulence trade-offs in Ralstonia solanacearum (Wang et al. 2024)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Wang, Wang, Yang, Lu, Fields, Xu, Shen, Wei and Friman (2024) on Dryad dataset tdz08kq5d, one workbook with the data behind each figure of the paper. It covers the selection experiment (bacterial and phage densities, colony types), the phage resistance, growth, twitching, biofilm and virulence of evolved clones, the variant calls of 28 sequenced clones, the phage adsorption assay and the transcriptome tables. The growth curves, per-clone variant calls, genome reads and the pilB and pilM data of Table S6 are not in the dataset.

outcomes.notes: Days 2 to 12, as the criterion now names them, temperature x phage x time F(5, 180) = 3.870, p = 0.0024, as in Table S1a; the -P minus +P difference at day 12 (0.3219 at 25 C, -0.0080 at 35 C) is below its largest earlier value (0.4362, 0.5046, day 2). The reader's answer put days 2 to 12 in the criterion and ruled out days 0 to 10, so the outcome stands on the criterion's own time points and the other two sets are variants that decide nothing. The criterion compares only the last day with the largest earlier value; at 25 C the difference is not a steady decline, falling to 0.049 on day 8 and rising to 0.322 on day 12.

statistics.about: phage effect on area under the density curve at 25 degrees C
phage effect on area under the density curve at 35 degrees C

outcomes.notes: Reading (a), trapezoid over days 2 to 12, 64.55% and 33.73% (F = 63.16 and 11.26 at df (1, 18)). findings.statement: The twitching sheet (Figure 2D) does not identify its clones. It has no morphotype column; its four 35_1 rows carry the names of four 35_0 SCV clones (6b6s1, 6b6s2, 6b8s1, 6b8s2) with different values, where the biofilm and disease sheets name the 35_1 clones 6b1s1, 6b1s2, 6b2s3 and 6b2s4; and in 25_0 the four mucoid names 6d5a2 to 6d8a2 appear twice with different values, where the other sheets have four SCVs.

The deposited twitching values do not reproduce Table S3d: with the colony types of the design, the residual sum of squares is 28.32 against 35.78 and the temperature sum of squares 2.48 against 3.857; only colony type x phage (27.04) and temperature x colony type (0.081) agree. The total sum of squares of the data is 72.28 against 82.08 summed from Table S3d, so no assignment of colony types reproduces it if its sums of squares are sequential, which the table does not state. Every other ANOVA the paper prints (Tables S1a, S1b, S2, S3a to S3c, S3e, S3f) is reproduced from the deposited data.

The variant table (snp_indel) gives, per variant and group of four sequenced clones, the number of clones that carry it, not which clones. Per-clone mutation counts and co-occurrence (for example whether the gspE and gspF mutations of 35 C +P SCVs are in different clones) cannot be read, and the genome reads are not public.

BioProject PRJNA1028400, named in the paper for the genomes of the evolved clones, has 28 BioSamples and 14 assemblies and no sequencing runs, so the reads the variant calls come from are not public. The RNA-seq reads are public in PRJNA1032726 (ten runs), though the Methods say they are shared on request.

The growth curves the maximum growth rates and carrying capacities were fitted to are not deposited, only one fitted value per clone, so the fits cannot be repeated and the model behind them (logistic, as the Methods say, or the code's best of four by AIC) cannot be checked. The pilB and pilM data of Table S6 are not deposited either.

The data disagree with statements of the text: SCVs form more biofilm than the ancestor in every clone (0.58 to 0.95 against 0.49 OD570), where the text says they retained ancestral-level biofilm; gspG is upregulated (log2FC 2.04) in the deposited DESeq2 table and Figure 4C list, where the text lists it as downregulated; phcS has log2FC 0.41, below the threshold under which the text calls it significantly upregulated; mucoid colonies are 15.3% at 25 C without phage, where the text says around 20%; and the 0.24% the text gives as an SCV frequency is the mucoid frequency of the 25 C +P treatment.

Small misprints in the paper's statistics, against the data: the area-under-curve ANOVAs are printed with df (1, 19) for 20 populations (the data give the printed F at df (1, 18)); the phage density time effect is printed in the text as F1,18 = 84.88, which is its sum of squares (F(2, 36) = 86.963 in Table S1b); Table S3e prints the temperature sum of squares as 0.346 for 0.3646; Table 1 places the RSc3091 deletion at C-432461, the variant table at 431461.

The OD600 values of Figure 1B include day 0 and negative values (eight, down to -0.029, at 25 C with phage), so they are blank-corrected and include the inoculation, neither of which the README or Methods says; the paper's ANOVA uses days 2 to 12. The README does not give units for the growth rate (headed maxgrowthrate(OD600)) or say that adsorption is a proportion.

In the carrying capacity sheet the ancestor's value (1.4355) is headed maxgrowthrate(OD600). The variant table's GENE column holds PROKKA names that differ from the paper's (phcS is sasA_8, pilD outO, gspE hxcR, gspF epsF_1); the gene_blast sheet gives the paper's names by locus tag. The Figure 4B list holds 11 genes where the paper speaks of 13.

attempts.label: EBRAINS:Q0FG-1X8
attempts.entry_title: Object-centered population coding in CA1 (Nagelhus et al. 2023)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Nagelhus, Andersson, Gonzalo Cogno, Moser and Moser (2023) on EBRAINS dataset 10.25493/Q0FG-1X8 (v1), which holds spike times and tracking of CA1 and CA3 cells in rats foraging in an open field with and without an object, from tetrodes and Neuropixels probes. It covers the template matching of object-tuned cells, changes of firing between trials, object traces, the Bayesian decoding of the object's presence as a function of distance, single-cell distance tuning, subsets of cells, and words and counts of population activity.

notebooks.title: Data check; object tuning, firing fields and whole-trial changes of single cells
Within- and between-trial changes of single cells, and object traces
Decoding the object from population activity, with its controls
Distance tuning of single cells and the cell properties that predict it
Decoding with random subsets of cells
Words and counts of population activity

outcomes.notes: Kruskal-Wallis H = 15.5 and 18.0 (p = 0.0038 and 0.0012), bin 1 above bin 5 by signed-rank test (p = 0.0021 and 0.0017; medians 0.169 against 0.050 bits), and no effect of distance on shuffled labels (p = 0.41 and 0.98).
deviations: The divergence sums over words seen in both trials, as the claims file says.

outcomes.statement: The entropy of words was higher than that of counts (1.65 against 0.84 bits).
outcomes.source: Results, Objects are encoded by distinct patterns of joint activity, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: the entropy was higher for words than counts (entropy of words: 1.65 bits ± 0.06; entropy of counts: 0.84 bits ± 0.02; mean ± SEM)
outcomes.notes: Word entropy is 5.5 to 5.9 bits without the all-zero word (readings a, c) and 1.90 to 1.97 bits with it (b), against 1.65 +/- 0.165; count entropy is 1.07 to 1.08 bits (a, c) and 0.92 to 0.93 (b), against 0.84 +/- 0.084. No reading puts both within tolerance. Words have the higher entropy in every reading.

outcomes.statement: The number of distinct words did not differ between trial types or across distance bins.
outcomes.source: Results, Objects are encoded by distinct patterns of joint activity, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 7C and 7D
outcomes.quote: In contrast to the identity of words, the number of words was independent of trial type and distance from the object (Figures S7C and S7D)
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 (the paper does not say) names the two readings run before, now w-a (distinct words of each session's whole trial, 16 against 16) and w-b (the 80 session and distance bin values). The outcome is unchanged. The number of distinct words does not differ across distance bins (NO p = 0.91 and 0.90, O p = 0.78) or between NO and O (w-a p = 0.94, w-b p = 0.85).

outcomes.statement: After downsampling words to as many states as counts, words still carried more information than counts.
outcomes.source: Results, Objects are encoded by distinct patterns of joint activity, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 7E
outcomes.quote: after downsampling the number of states to be equal for words and counts, words were still much more informative (Figure S7E)
outcomes.notes: Corrected after round 1. The words are now downsampled as the criterion says, per session and distance bin, keeping the c most frequent words of both trials together (c the number of distinct counts there, 5 to 16 under subset reading a and 5 to 18 under b). Downsampled words are more informative than counts in all 80 session-bin pairs, signed-rank W = 0, p = 7.9e-15, with or without bias subtraction and under both subset readings; medians 0.053 to 0.064 bits against 0.0007 to 0.0013 for counts, below all words (0.096 to 0.148). Before, each trial kept its own most frequent words, so a word kept in one trial only carried the label (median 0.30 bits, above all words); that selection is shown as a variant. The Methods say "In a given trial"; the question is asked.
deviations: The selection is the criterion's, per session and distance bin over both trials; the per-trial selection of the Methods' wording is shown as a variant (asked).

outcomes.statement: Single cells decoded with almost flat accuracy across distance; their distance tuning (bin 1 minus bin 5 accuracy) averaged 0.02, 98.7% lay between -0.2 and 0.2, 12.2% (145) had significant positive and 3.8% (45) significant negative tuning.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance-specific reorganization of the hippocampal map is widely distributed, paragraph 2; Figure 6A and 6B
outcomes.quote: CA1 cells had a slight positive bias in distance tuning (mean: 0.02; for reference, the same mean calculated from populations is 0.19; Figure 4C) and nearly all cells were contained between the bounds ... and 0.2 (98.7% of cells) ... some cells had significant positive distance tuning (12.2%, n = 145/1,189 cells) ... and some cells had significant negative distance tuning (3.8%, n = 45/1,189 cells)
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. The outcome is unchanged. Under every speed and cell reading, the mean tuning (0.016 to 0.017), the fraction within -0.2 to 0.2 (0.977 to 0.985) and the fraction with significant positive tuning (0.124 to 0.129) are within tolerance, while the fraction with significant negative tuning (0.047 to 0.056) is above 0.038 +/- 0.0038, which is the criterion's partial case. The measured values are those of speed a, cell reading a.
deviations: The 897 decoding-session cells that are also in the CA1 file take their values from it (same recording and tracking).

outcomes.statement: After removing the cells with significant positive distance tuning, decoding accuracy still fell gradually with distance.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance-specific reorganization of the hippocampal map is widely distributed, paragraph 2; Supplementary Figure 5L
outcomes.quote: after removing cells with significant positive distance tuning (12.2%), we still observed a gradual drop in decoding accuracy ... obtained with population data as a function of object distance (Figure S5L)
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. Before, bin 2 was highest under one of the four readings (speed b, rm a), so the outcome was blocked. Now, without the 149 or 151 positively tuned cells, the Kruskal-Wallis test gives H = 25.4 and 23.9, p at most 8.3e-5, with bin 1 highest under both speed readings (median 0.705 against 0.673 and 0.684 in bin 2).

outcomes.statement: After removing all object-tuned cells, decoding accuracy still fell gradually with distance.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance-specific reorganization of the hippocampal map is widely distributed, paragraph 5; Supplementary Figure 5M
outcomes.quote: After removing all object-tuned cells (19.9%) from the data and re-running the decoder, we observed the same gradual fall in decoding accuracy as a function of distance (Figure S5M)
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. fig1c-object-tuned-fraction is now tested, so this claim is no longer blocked by it. Removing the object-tuned cells among the 897 linked cells (277 under w a, 186 under w b) leaves Kruskal-Wallis H = 42.3 to 44.1, p at most 1.5e-8, bin 1 highest, under both width and both speed readings. The 283 tetrode cells of unknown status stay in. Removing them too leaves bin 1 highest with p = 0.032 to 0.044 under three readings and 0.065 under w a, speed a.
deviations: Object-tuning status exists only for the 897 decoding-session cells linked to the CA1 file.

outcomes.statement: In the 620-cell session, random subsets of every size except a single cell showed decoding accuracy falling with distance.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance-specific reorganization of the hippocampal map is widely distributed, paragraph 3; Figure 6C
outcomes.quote: All curves showed reduced decoding accuracy as a function of distance, except the curve constructed using only a single cell (Figure 6C)

statistics.about: all other curves (printed as W >= 11.89, p <= 0.0182)

outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. The speed and size-list readings still give different outcomes. The single-cell curve shows no decline in any reading (signed-rank p = 0.29 and 0.33, Kruskal-Wallis p at least 0.70). Every size from 100 cells up declines (both tests p at most 0.0012). Without the speed filter, with the legend's sizes and the signed-rank test, every other size gives p < 0.05, so the criterion is met there; with the filter, 5 cells give signed-rank p = 0.14 and it is met under no size list. Round 1 variant with 100 subsets per size: of 5 disjoint groups of 20 subsets, sizes 5 and 10 give p < 0.05 with bin 1 higher in 3 and 3 groups with the speed filter and in 0 and 2 without it, and the single cell in 1 of 5 under both; over all 100 subsets every size, the single cell included (p = 0.041 and 0.013), gives p < 0.05. The small sizes are not reliably significant with 20 subsets.

outcomes.statement: The difference between bins 1 and 5 grew, and the slope of accuracy over distance became more negative, as more cells were used, both reaching their extremes at 500 cells.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance-specific reorganization of the hippocampal map is widely distributed, paragraph 3; Figure 6D
outcomes.quote: The difference between bins #1 and #5 grew systematically with the number of cells (Figure 6D; left y axis, blue)
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. The speed readings still give different outcomes. Without the speed filter both Kruskal-Wallis tests give p < 0.05 and the largest mean difference and most negative mean slope are at 500 cells under every size list, so the criterion is met; with the filter both extremes are at 400 cells and the slope test gives p = 0.040 to 0.078. It also depends on fig6c-subsets-decline, which is blocked. In the round 1 variant with 100 subsets per size the largest mean difference is at 500 cells under both speed readings (0.067 and 0.077), 0.001 above 400 cells with the filter.

outcomes.statement: The growth of distance reorganization with the number of cells held in the tetrode sessions and in the 135-cell Neuropixels session.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance-specific reorganization of the hippocampal map is widely distributed, paragraph 3; Supplementary Figure 8A to 8D
outcomes.quote: The finding was upheld in data from animals with smaller numbers of cells (135 cells in a Neuropixels recording; 25–39 cells in tetrode recordings)
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. The outcome is unchanged. In the 14 tetrode sessions pooled and in the 135-cell session both Kruskal-Wallis tests across sizes give p at most 6.4e-18 under both speed readings (H = 528 to 587 tetrode, 84 to 93 for the 135-cell session). Over the sizes the mean difference rises and the mean slope falls (rank correlation with size, and the largest size beyond the smallest), but not at every step. In the tetrode sessions the full count gives a difference of 0.176 and 0.184 against 0.200 and 0.205 at 30 cells, and a slope of -0.0426 and -0.0442 against -0.0466 and -0.0480. In the 135-cell session with the speed filter the slope is -0.0508 at 30 cells and -0.0495 at 50.

outcomes.statement: Even the 20% of cells with the lowest distance tuning showed distance reorganization, with a bin 1 minus bin 5 difference of 0.121 and a slope of -0.0267.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance-specific reorganization of the hippocampal map is widely distributed, paragraph 4; Figure 6E and 6F
outcomes.quote: even the 20% of cells with lowest tuning was sufficient to demonstrate the distance modulation, in the form of positive distance tuning as well as a negative slope (Figures 6E and 6F; rightmost point on blue curve: 0.121; on orange curve
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. The outcome is unchanged. The 124 cells (20%) of the 620-cell session with the lowest distance tuning give a bin 1 minus bin 5 difference of -0.346 and -0.344 and a slope of +0.081 and +0.077 under the two speed readings, against 0.121 and -0.0267, so accuracy rises with distance. All 620 cells give 0.064 and 0.082 and slopes of -0.014 and -0.016, and keeping the lowest 80% already reverses the sign. The cells kept by the rule (lowest values first) are those with negative tuning.

outcomes.statement: Single-cell properties barely predicted distance tuning; correlations with object-tuning score (r = 0.12), spatial information (r = -0.13), spatial correlation (r = -0.08) and rate overlap (r = -0.18) were significant but weak.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance-specific reorganization of the hippocampal map is widely distributed, paragraph 5; Figure 7A to 7D
outcomes.quote: The object-tuning score had a significant positive correlation with distance tuning, but very weakly so (r = 0.12 ... Spatial information had a significant negative correlation, but also this was very weak ... spatial correlation and rate overlap were also negatively but weakly correlated with distance tuning
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. The answer on lambda (the paper does not say) names two readings, si-a (speed-filtered spikes over time) and si-b (the occupancy-weighted mean of the smoothed map); before, only si-a was run. fig1c-object-tuned-fraction is now tested, so the claim is no longer blocked by it. No reading meets the whole criterion, because spatial information is not correlated with distance tuning under either lambda reading (r = -0.038 to -0.002, p at least 0.23, against -0.13); the lambda readings change spatial information (median 0.90 and 1.72 bits per spike) but not this. Over the 1189 cells the other three correlations are within 0.05 of the printed values with p < 0.05 under every reading (object-tuning score r = 0.11 to 0.15, spatial correlation -0.081 and -0.089, rate overlap -0.154 to -0.160). Over the 897 linked cells the object-tuning score under w a (0.067, 0.069) and the rate overlap (-0.117 to -0.124) fall outside. Every |r| is below 0.3. The measured values are those of speed a, w a, rate overlap a, si-a, cell reading a.
deviations: Spatial information is run under both lambda readings of the criterion.

outcomes.statement: Using the slope of accuracy against distance in place of distance tuning gave similar weak correlations with the same four properties.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance-specific reorganization of the hippocampal map is widely distributed, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: We obtained similar results when, instead of distance tuning, we used the slope of the regression line fitted to decoding accuracy vs. distance as a measure of reorganization
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. fig7-single-cell-properties is now tested, so this claim is no longer blocked by it; the lambda readings are run as there. With the slope, the object-tuning score (r = -0.071 to -0.150, every reading) and rate overlap (r = 0.148 to 0.156 over the 1189 cells) are within 0.05 of the printed values; spatial information (r = -0.011 to 0.023, printed 0.10) is not under either lambda reading, and spatial correlation has the opposite sign (r = +0.065 to +0.088, printed -0.08). Changed after round 1 from partially_reproduced, as the verifier gave. The claim is that the four correlations are similar; two match, spatial information is near zero and spatial correlation has the opposite sign.

outcomes.statement: The arena walls did not act as a pivot as the object did; position decoding error and population vector correlations were comparable near (under 15 cm) and far from the walls.
outcomes.source: Results, Decoding the presence of an object from neural-population activity, paragraph 5; Supplementary Figure 5J and 5K
outcomes.quote: The internal walls of the recording environment did not play a similar role as the free-standing object, since position decoding accuracy and population vector correlations were comparable near and far away from the walls (Figures S5J and S5K)
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. The outcome is unchanged. All 6 signed-rank tests (2 speed readings x 3 measures) find a difference between near and far from the walls (p = 6.1e-5 to 0.0010). Position errors are 8.2 to 9.7 cm larger near the walls (medians 36 to 38 against 27 to 29 cm), and population vector correlations between the halves of NO are 0.08 lower.
deviations: The position decoder and the paired test are the claims file's readings; the paper reports no test.

outcomes.statement: In the tetrode sessions and the 135-cell Neuropixels session too, keeping only the cells with the lowest distance tuning weakened but did not at first remove the distance reorganization; the slope reached zero when 60% (tetrode) or 50% (135-cell session) of the least-tuned cells were kept.
outcomes.source: Results, Distance-specific reorganization of the hippocampal map is widely distributed, paragraph 4; Supplementary Figure 8E to 8H
outcomes.quote: As before, the finding also held in smaller-sized tetrode and Neuropixels data (Figures S8E–S8H)
outcomes.notes: The answer of 2026-10-21 on rate maps (the rate per bin, unvisited bins 0, then smoothed, as calculateRateMap.m does) leaves one map reading in place of two. The outcome is unchanged. With all cells the bin 1 minus bin 5 difference is positive and the slope negative in both datasets (tetrode mean 0.176 and 0.184, slopes -0.043 and -0.044; 135-cell session 0.291 and 0.273, slopes -0.068 and -0.066), both shrink as fewer of the least-tuned cells are kept, and the largest kept fraction with a mean slope of zero or above is 0.4 in both under both speed readings, within 0.6 +/- 0.2 and 0.5 +/- 0.2. The 20% values are negative differences (tetrode -0.075 and -0.088, 135-cell -0.15 and -0.10).

findings.statement: In the two Neuropixels population files (populationanalyses_27012.mat and populationanalyses_27207.mat) the tracking y equals x in every sample. The same recordings in singlecellanalyses_CA1.mat (sessions 58 and 59) have the same timestamps, x and spike trains and a y of their own, so the y column of the population files is a copy of x.
No cell identities across days and no day of exposure to the object are deposited, so the cross-day analyses (Figures 1G and 1H) cannot be run.

Of the 425 tetrode units of the population files, 283 have no match in the CA1 single-cell file and carry no identifier; they are presumably repeat recordings of cells the file gives from another day, so they have no Object Moved or No Object' trial and no object-tuning status.
The implant sites (Supplementary Figure 1) and head direction are not deposited; the data descriptor says histology is not shared, and tracking holds one position per sample.
The CA3 file holds 341 cells from 4 rats (including two Neuropixels sessions, 221 cells), while the paper's Supplementary Figure 3 counts 313 CA3 cells; which cells the paper used is not documented.

In CA3 session 3 (rat 25987) the Object trial's object is near a corner (61.4 cm from the centre) and the Object Moved trial's near the centre (9.0 cm), the reverse of the protocol; the trials or the positions may be swapped.
Three units of singlecellanalyses_CA1.mat have spike times out of order within the Object Moved trial.

A few deposited units break the paper's inclusion rules as computed from the trials (4 of 1189 CA1 units more than 1% ISIs under 2 ms, 7 outside 0.05 to 10 Hz), perhaps because the rates were computed over a recording not deposited.
26 of 273 gaps between trials in the single-cell files exceed 10 min (up to 4.1 h), while the Methods describe 1 to 3 min between trials.
The Methods use 15 tetrode decoding sessions, the legends 14; the dataset holds 14, with the two Neuropixels sessions 16 in all.

The population files hold the No Object and Object trials only; the Object Moved and No Object' trials of the decoding sessions exist only for the cells the single-cell file gives there (3 to 15 per tetrode session). The control file gives each cell once, and only one control session has 25 or more cells.
The tracking unit is stored as a MATLAB string object, which scipy and other non-MATLAB readers return as an opaque object; its value (centimeters) can be recovered only from the raw bytes.

The paper's code holds no single-cell rate maps, field detection, object-vector score, population vector correlation or sampling analysis. The object-vector method cites references 11 and 12 for its vector maps and does not say which cells its exclusion before the criteria removes (28.8% of CA1 cells).

verifications.by: Independent agent run by CatalystNeuro (same harness, separate context, did not write the notebooks)
verifications.reviewed: Round 1. The handover of the author-answers run (commit 5a839c2c), the six executed notebooks with the conclusions and summaries removed, objcode.py and the claims file, with the paper under paper/. The verifier read the code, tested helper functions on synthetic inputs and checked the archive metadata; it did not re-run the notebooks.

disagreements.reason: Under width reading b the CA1 fraction is 0.187 (inside tolerance), but the control "chance" is 0.041 (9/219) or 0.073, both outside 0.0503 +/- 0.005. Width reading a gives 0.278 and 0.119 to 0.169. Binomial p < 0.05 in all four.

0 of 12 readings pass. The largest distance is 104 to 125 cm against a limit of 88.8 cm, and some minima are 3.3 cm. The mean is inside tolerance in 8 of 12. Fields are taken as connected regions above 3 x MAD, not the Methods' iterative contour from the peak, which can split or merge fields; the counts and ranges are sensitive to it. It asked how many cells have their nearest field beyond 88.8 cm.
0 of 12 readings pass; at most 2 of the 3 values are inside tolerance in any reading.

Speed-filtered rates give p = 0.013; whole-trial rates give p = 0.24. Both readings are allowed and they disagree. The notebook's per-reading tables do not flag that the outcome depends on a reading the criterion allows.

Spatial tests 4 of 4 significant. Rate overlap 0 of 4 significant with whole-trial rates, 1 of 4 with speed-filtered rates (OM-NO' p = 0.008). Run on 341 cells, not 313; using only the 120 tetrode cells, 2 of the 4 spatial tests become non-significant, and the choice is not justified.
Trace fraction 0.061 to 0.098 against 0.183 +/- 0.018. The NO-NO' changed count (908 to 916) is inside tolerance.

Width reading b gives p = 0.47 to 1.0 in all 16 readings. Width a fails (p < 1e-12), but only because its starting fraction (0.278) already misses 0.199. It rests on about half the paper's trace cells, so the absence result is weaker evidence than it looks.

Reproduced (fragile). 27 of 96 readings fall in 40 +/- 4, all under the author's own "x-b" exclusion; none under "x-a". Counts range from 9 to 53. The exclusion readings, the spatial-information lambda, the field rule and the distance reading are all the author's own, and the pass rests entirely on x-b. Neither exclusion reading matches the paper's 28.8% excluded (x-a 59 to 70%, x-b 19 to 21%).
Speed reading a with sectors from 0 degrees gives H = 10.26, p = 0.036; the other three readings give p = 0.065 to 0.21.

Speed reading a: means 0.499 to 0.502, smallest t-test p = 0.063. Speed reading b: bin 1 t-test p = 0.009. Labels are permuted against fixed decisions, so accuracy is about 0.5 by construction; the deviations the t-tests pick up come from unequal NO/O sample counts. This is consistent with the paper's description, but the test says little.

Speed- and occupancy-matched decoders hold in all 8 readings (p < 1e-5, bin 1 highest). Head direction is blocked (data_missing, confirmed). The head-direction block is confirmed from metadata; the notebook never printed the fields of the tracking struct.

Blocked (other). The output does not test the claim: the top-c words are chosen separately in each trial and then pooled, so a word in one trial's top set but not the other's is kept only for that trial's samples and becomes perfectly informative about the label (on synthetic data, swapping the ranks of two words raised the mutual information from about 0.001 to 0.08 bits). The 0.30 bits and the 80 of 80 pairs are therefore not evidence. This follows the paper's "In a given trial" wording; the claims file says "per session and distance bin". A rerun is needed with the top-c words chosen once over both trials per session and distance bin.

Sizes >= 20 decline in every reading. The full criterion passes in only 1 of 12 combinations (speed b, size list b, signed-rank). Sizes 5 and 10 fail elsewhere, and in every combination under the Methods' speed filter. It uses only 20 random subsets; it could not tell whether sizes 5 and 10 are reliably significant and asked for 100 subsets per size.
Passes under speed reading b for all three size lists. Under speed a the extremes fall at 400 cells (0.071 against 0.070). It uses only 20 random subsets per size.

Spatial information r is -0.002 to -0.038 against -0.13, in every reading. Under lambda reading si-a, lambda is not the map's occupancy-weighted mean, so the values can be negative (minimum -0.34 bits/spike); both lambda readings fail anyway.
Spatial information r is about 0 against 0.10; spatial correlation r is +0.07 to +0.09 against -0.08.

verifications.reviewed: Round 2. The author-revise-1 run (commit 7c4cb363), with the attempt record and the six executed notebooks with their conclusions and summaries, objcode.py, the claims file and the paper under paper/. The verifier did not download the data or re-run anything.

disagreements.reason: I disagree and would record not_reproduced. The claim's main quantity is the trace fraction. It is 0.061 to 0.098 against 0.183 +/- 0.018 under every field, ROI and rate-overlap reading, less than half the paper's value (nb02 c12). Being above the 1% chance level, and the NO-NO' count falling within tolerance, do not make up for that. This is not like fig1c, where the miss is within sampling error.
