attempts.label: FIGSHARE:24639285
attempts.entry_title: Replicate Apollo sample magnetizations (Tarduno, Cottrell and Zhou 2024)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Tarduno, Cottrell and Zhou (2024) on Figshare item 24639285, which holds the thermal paleointensity measurements of 22 Apollo 64455 glass subsamples that failed the selection criteria and the replicate measurements of twelve single silicate crystals. It recomputes the fit statistics of Table 2, the magnetization thresholds of Table 1, the consistency of replicate directions and the alteration checks.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Tarduno, Cottrell and Zhou (2024) from Figshare 24639285

outcomes.statement: The deposit holds the measurements of the 22 Apollo 64455 glass subsamples that failed the paleointensity selection criteria, named as in Table 2, and replicate measurements for the twelve single crystals of Table 1.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, Glass, paragraph 2; Methods, paragraph 2; Table 2; Data Records
outcomes.quote: Plots for all the data not meeting paleointensity criteria1 (n=22) are provided26 with photomicrographs of specimens that were measured
outcomes.notes: All 22 glass specimens of Table 2 are sheets of 64455lunar_cryodata.xlsx (Table 2's s11 is sheet ss11; sheet g2 labels its rows 64455g2), and all 12 crystals of Table 1 have a workbook, each with steps, moments, declinations and inclinations. No other specimen is in the deposit. The 10 glass specimens with AF steps (ss19, ss22, ss27, ss34, ss38, ss41, ss43, ss45, ss46, ss48) are exactly those with the second mark in Table 2, and the other 12 have none, as the claims file's reading of the marks has it. 71055g1 and 71055g3 have one NRM measurement each, the other crystals two or three. Four glass sheets (g2, ss8, ss39, ss48) hold scaled copies of one measurement in place of replicates (see findings).

outcomes.statement: Of the Apollo 64455 glass subsamples given thermal paleointensity experiments, 12% passed the selection criteria (3 of 25, 13 run without and 12 with AF pre-treatment).
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, paragraph 3; Methods, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: In the thermal studies1 of Apollo 64455 (Methods), the success rate was 12%
outcomes.notes: 22 failed specimens in the deposit give 3 / 25 = 12.0%. 12 have no AF steps and 10 do; with the Methods' one and two successful specimens this gives 13 and 12.

outcomes.statement: For the nine failed glass specimens with a line fit (ss19, ss43, ss22, ss41, ss6, ss9, ss10, ss30, ss34), the number of points, temperature range, MAD, R2 and pTRM check differences are as in Table 2, which lists the criteria each failed.
outcomes.source: Methods, Paleointensity Selection criteria, paragraph 2; Table 2
outcomes.quote: Reasons for de-selection are provided in Table 2
outcomes.notes: With the mean vector of each step's repeated measurements, n matches Table 2 for all nine specimens, and 23 of 29 values match under one of the named readings (79%, the criterion asks 80% for reproduced and 50 to 80% for partially reproduced), MAD 8 of 9, R2 6 of 9, pTRM checks 9 of 11. Measured values are MAD under reading (a), a free line, and R2, in the claims file's order; the last value is the fraction of the 29 values that match. MAD reading (a) alone gives all 8 matching MADs (median difference 0.2 deg, six within 0.3 deg); readings (b) and (c) give 2 and 0. Outside tolerance under every reading are ss10's MAD (33.3 against 42.9 deg) and R2 (0.23 against 0.15), ss9's R2 (0.89 against 0.74), ss34's R2 (0.03 against 0.06, tolerance 0.006), and the pTRM checks of ss19 at 250 C (23.7 to 105.9% against 30%) and ss30 at 450 C (8.2 to 43.8% against 10%). The matching pTRM checks need different readings for different specimens; no single reading matches more than 5 of 11. With the first measurement of each step, 11 of 29 values match (38%), which would not reproduce the claim. Against the stated thresholds, reported and not judged, ss30 and ss34 have R2 below 0.9 and n of 4 or more, as their single failure "R2" says; ss6 has R2 0.89 here, so its listed R2 failure follows here. Counting ss6's R2 as a miss, since its 250.1 step averages two groups of directions, gives 22 of 29 (76%). With one pTRM reading held fixed the score is 17, 16, 19 and 14 of 29 (readings a_i, a_ii, b_i, b_ii; 48 to 66%), partial or lower under every fixed reading. None of the nine is a synthetic sheet. Within a step, ss10's field-off steps and its 100, 175 and 250 C field-on steps scatter by 20 to 113 deg (resultant over n 0.79 to 0.98), and ss9's 360 and 550 C steps by 57 and 30 deg, so how these steps are combined moves the MAD and R2 that miss. The deposit's Supplementary Figure 1, read from its vector drawing, plots TRM gained from the mean vectors and NRM as the mean of the rows' moments for 12 of its 14 non-synthetic specimens (median difference 0.1% or less; ss27 and ss34 fit no reading), including ss6's averaged 250 C step, and 11 of its 12 pTRM checks at the check's TRM referred to the field-off step before it (reference i). With NRM read that way, R2 matches for 7 of 9 (ss10 0.152 against 0.15; ss9 0.916 and ss34 0.032 still miss) and 24 of 29 values match under any reading (83%); holding pTRM reference (i), as the figure plots the checks, gives 8 of 11 pTRM checks and 23 of 29 (79%). The outcome is kept, as the figure's NRM reading crosses the 80% bar only together with a pTRM reference the same figure does not use.
deviations: The paper does not say how the repeated measurements of a step (2 to 19 per step) enter Table 2. Assumed here that they are averaged as vectors, the usual treatment of repeated measurements and the reading under which the MADs of six specimens come within 0.3 deg of Table 2. The first measurement of each step is shown as the other reading and gives a different outcome. The deposit's Supplementary Figure 1 supports averaging; it takes NRM as the mean of the rows' moments, not the moment of the mean vector, which changes R2 by at most 0.08 here and is shown as a second reading.

MAD is Kirschvink's principal component measure under the claims file's three readings, and the pTRM check difference is taken on the TRM-gained axis, where Figures 1 and 2 plot the checks (legends, "red triangles represent partial thermal remanent magnetization checks"). The paper gives no formula for either; it names PmagPy and "standard paleointensity definitions" (Technical Validation).

ss6's 250.1 step holds 19 rows in two groups of directions (inclination near 71 and near -13 deg); all are averaged, as for every step. Ten other steps of six glass sheets also hold two groups of directions more than 45 deg apart (s11 360.1, 550 and 550.1, ss10 250 and 360, ss18 100, ss24 NRM and 550, ss29 175.1, ss36 450.1) and are averaged the same way.

outcomes.statement: The other thirteen failed glass specimens (g2, ss8, s11, ss18, ss24, ss27, ss29, ss36, ss38, ss39, ss45, ss46, ss48) gave no fit, most because they did not acquire TRM in a regular fashion and some because their directions trend out of the origin.
outcomes.source: Methods, Paleointensity Selection criteria, paragraph 2; Table 2
outcomes.quote: We note that some specimens did not acquire TRM in a regular fashion, or showed directions that trended out of ... the origin of their respective orthogonal vector plots
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a), TRM gained not increasing at every step, all 11 specimens marked "no regular TRM acquisition" are irregular (9 of 11 under reading b, a fall of more than 15%); the same with first measurements. Without the four synthetic sheets (g2, ss8, ss48 among the 11), 8 of 8 under (a) and 6 of 8 under (b). ss36 and ss39 have field-off vectors that move away from the origin over the last step of their ranges (ss36 1.77 to 6.00, ss39 2.31 to 9.67, in 1e-9 emu). Reading (a) counts any fall; the median standard error of the mean TRM gained is 1 to 6% of the TRM gained for the non-synthetic specimens. ss29's only fall, 0.6%, is below its median standard error of 2.5%; counting it as regular leaves 10 of 11 under (a). The trend out of the origin rests on ss36 and on ss39, a synthetic sheet. The pTRM checks of these specimens, reported only, match Table 2 under some reading for 6 of 10; ss36 has no pTRM check at 450 C in its sheet although Table 2 prints 25%, and ss27 has 5 paired steps from 100 to 550 C where Table 2 gives 6.
deviations: Repeated measurements averaged as in table2-fit-statistics; first measurements give the same counts.

outcomes.statement: Glass subsamples ss43 and ss19, which failed the reliability criteria, show hints of linear directional components on orthogonal vector plots, from which nominal paleointensities can be calculated with the 18 uT laboratory field.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, Glass, paragraph 2; Figure 1
outcomes.quote: some of these data reveal linear directional components, and nominal paleointensities can be calculated (Fig. 1)
outcomes.notes: With averaged replicates and MAD reading (a), ss43 has MAD 10.3 deg and R2 0.90 (Table 2 10.0 and 0.90) and ss19 MAD 30.1 deg and R2 0.96 (30.1 and 0.94). Nominal paleointensities, |slope| x 18 uT, are 9.6 uT for ss43 and 23.0 uT for ss19 (8.5 and 23.7 uT with first measurements); the figure's values were not available to compare. With first measurements ss43's R2 is 0.99, outside 0.90 plus or minus 0.09. With NRM as the mean of the rows' moments, as the deposit's Supplementary Figure 1 plots it for other specimens, R2 is 0.909 and 0.956 and the nominal paleointensity of ss43 9.2 uT.
deviations: Rests on the averaging of repeated measurements assumed in table2-fit-statistics.

outcomes.statement: Glass subsamples ss41 and ss22 show field-off directions that change over a temperature interval, consistent with a changing ambient field during magnetization, and curved NRM lost against TRM gained plots.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, Glass, paragraph 2; Figure 2; Table 2
outcomes.quote: Other specimens show a changing vector, consistent with a changing ambient field (Fig. 2)
outcomes.notes: With averaged replicates, ss41 (500 to 580 C) turns 33.3 deg between its first and last field-off directions against a line MAD of 24.1 deg, and a great circle fits with MAD 15.1 deg; ss22 (250 to 500 C) turns 107.8 deg against a line MAD of 35.4 deg, great-circle MAD 32.0 deg. Both readings hold for both specimens, also with first measurements. R2 is 0.384 and 0.378 (0.38 plus or minus 0.038); with first measurements it is 0.16 and 0.44, outside tolerance. Both readings are weak tests. With no changing field and 3 vectors, as in ss41's range, reading (a) holds for 98% of random directions and 78% of points along one line with noise, and reading (b) for 56% and 51% (median line MAD 21.1 and 16.7 deg, against ss41's 24.1); with 4 vectors, as in ss22's range, (a) holds for 95% and 66% and (b) for 56% and 51% (median line MAD 28.1 and 23.6 deg, against ss22's 35.4). With NRM as the mean of the rows' moments R2 is 0.382 and 0.370. The curved Arai plot in the statement is not in the criterion and is not judged. A circle fit to the normalized points gives curvature -0.41 for ss41 and -1.12 for ss22, against -2.59 for ss19 and 0.67 for ss43, which the paper shows as linear, so with 3 or 4 points it does not separate them; ss22's NRM does not fall monotonically over its range (1.00, 0.65, 0.82, 0.28 of the first).
deviations: Rests on the averaging of repeated measurements assumed in table2-fit-statistics.
The great circle is fit through the origin (Kirschvink's plane MAD), a standard choice; the paper gives no fitting method.

outcomes.statement: The field-off directions of the failed glass specimens, as seen on orthogonal vector plots, are not random, implying the presence of an ambient field.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, Glass, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: The directions, as viewed on orthogonal vector plots, are not random and imply the presence of an ambient field
outcomes.notes: Watson's test rejects randomness of the thermal field-off directions (one per step, 2 to 9 steps) in 8 of 22 specimens with averaged replicates and 9 of 22 with first measurements, between a quarter and a half. Within the Table 2 ranges, 8 of 22 (7 with first measurements). Without the four synthetic sheets, 7 of 18. ss38 (k 27.9, p 0.0001), ss45, ss9, ss8, ss19, ss41, s11 and ss6 reject; ss39 and ss48 have two thermal steps each.
deviations: The p-value of Watson's test is computed exactly by simulation (200000 sets of uniform directions, fixed seeds), a standard form of the test the claims file names.

outcomes.statement: For nearly all glass samples given AF pre-treatment, AF cleaning did not significantly change the NRM direction or magnitude.
outcomes.source: Methods, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: For nearly all samples, AF cleaning did not significantly change the NRM direction or magnitude
outcomes.notes: Under both readings 8 of the 10 AF-treated specimens show no significant change; the direction after the last AF step is within 2.8 deg of the NRM and the moment within 1.1%. ss38 keeps its direction (2.4 deg) but its moment falls to 0.49 of the NRM at 20 mT, and ss48, a synthetic sheet, turns 17.5 deg and falls to 0.67. The same counts with first measurements.

outcomes.statement: For each of the twelve single crystals, the maximum field that cannot be excluded, given the magnetometer threshold of 8e-11 emu and the moment acquired at 590 C in a 20 uT field, is as in Table 1, between 0.20 and 0.51 uT.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, Single crystal measurements, paragraph 4; Table 1; Technical Validation, Example of threshhold detection limit
outcomes.quote: Considering a magnetometer threshold value (see Methods) the maximum field that cannot be excluded by the data can be calculated from the data for each crystal. These values are presented in Table 1
outcomes.notes: Under reading (b), M590 the moment of the single 590.1 measurement, all 24 values are within tolerance and the 12 M590 values equal Table 1 to its four digits; the max intensities run from 0.200 to 0.500 uT. Reading (a) with averaged 590.0 replicates also gives 24 of 24, and with the first replicate 23 of 24. Table 1's max intensities equal the formula on its own M590 column rounded to two places for 4 of 12 crystals, and rounded up for 10 of 12; the exceptions are 14053g1 (0.4995, printed 0.51) and 12053g2 (0.2005, printed 0.20). The equal M590 of 12021g3 and 12040g3 (6.292e-09 emu) is in the data, two 590.1 measurements with different directions.

outcomes.statement: The maximum fields that the single crystal data cannot exclude define a baseline of about 0.2 to 0.5 uT below which fields cannot be evaluated with these data.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, paragraph 7
outcomes.quote: they nevertheless define a baseline of ~0.2 to ~0.5 μT below which fields cannot be evaluated with the present data
outcomes.notes: The twelve values of table1-max-intensity under reading (b) run from 0.200 uT (12040g1) to 0.500 uT (14053g1); under reading (a) from 0.203 or 0.204 to 0.501 or 0.503 uT.

outcomes.statement: For crystal 14053g1, the threshold field detection limit computed from the magnetometer sensitivity (8e-14 A m2) and a TRM at 590 C of 8e-12 A m2 in a 20 uT field is 0.2 uT.
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, Example of threshhold detection limit
outcomes.quote: Threshold field detection = Magnetometer sensitivity (8 × 10−14 A m2) / TRM590o (8 × 10−12 A m2) × Lab Field (20 μT) = 0.2 μT
outcomes.notes: Matches under reading (b) only, the misprint reading the criterion names. For 14053g1 the data give a TRM at 590 C of 3.203e-12 A m2 and 0.500 uT, not the example's 8e-12 and 0.2; for 12040g1 they give 8.002e-12 A m2 and 0.200 uT, the example's numbers. The values recorded are 12040g1's. The criterion calls the claim reproduced as written only when reading (a) matches, so a match under (b) alone is recorded as partially reproduced (changed from reproduced after verifier round 1).
deviations: The example's crystal name is read as a misprint for 12040g1, as the criterion's reading (b) allows; as written, for 14053g1, the example does not match the data.

outcomes.statement: For most crystals the replicate NRM measurements have a consistent direction, as shown on stereonets for 12040g1 and 14053g2.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, Single crystal measurements, paragraph 2; Figure 3a and 3d
outcomes.quote: These show that for most of the crystals there is consistency of the NRM direction (Fig. 3a,d)
outcomes.notes: Under reading (a) the NRM replicates have a higher Fisher k than the 590.0 replicates in 10 of 12 crystals, including 12040g1 (k 981) and 14053g2 (k 206); under reading (b) Watson's test rejects randomness of the NRM replicates in 8 of 12. 71055g1 and 71055g3 have one NRM measurement and count as not consistent. With two or three replicates per crystal, k and the test rest on few directions (12040g3 NRM k 1.3, 12053g1 k 9.8).

outcomes.statement: After demagnetization at 590 C in zero field, the replicate directions of the crystals are inconsistent, consistent with a null magnetization state.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, Single crystal measurements, paragraph 2; Figure 3b and 3e; Methods, Thermal measurements, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: but this consistency is not seen after demagnetization at 590 °C (Fig. 3b,e)
outcomes.notes: Under reading (b) Watson's test does not reject randomness of the 590.0 replicates in any of the 12 crystals (p 0.34 to 0.99, k 0.8 to 1.8); under reading (a) their k is below the NRM's in the 10 crystals with more than one NRM measurement. The 590.0 moments average 1.16e-10 to 5.68e-10 emu per crystal, and all 37 single 590.0 measurements are above the 8e-11 emu threshold.

outcomes.statement: The replicate directions after the zero-field alteration check at 590 C are also inconsistent.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, Single crystal measurements, paragraph 2; Figure 3c and 3f
outcomes.quote: The directions are also inconsistent after the alteration check at 590 °C (Fig. 3c,f)
outcomes.notes: Watson's test does not reject randomness of the 590.3 replicates in any of the 12 crystals (reading b); their k is below the NRM's in 10 of 12 (reading a). Mean 590.3 moments are 2.14e-10 to 5.12e-10 emu.

outcomes.statement: Crystal 14053g1, measured after heating to 400 C during initial tests, held a stable remanence, which was removed by treatment at 590 C.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, Single crystal measurements, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: One crystal (14053g1) was measured after heating to an intermediate temperature (400 °C) during initial tests, and found to be stable
outcomes.notes: The deposit holds three 400 C zero-field measurements of 14053g1, with one 400.1 and two 400.3 rows. The 400 C replicates are grouped (k 78, alpha95 14 deg, Watson p 0.0003) and the 590.0 replicates are not (k 1.0, p 0.79), so reading (a) holds. Under reading (b) the 400 C mean is 9.3 deg from the NRM mean, outside the NRM's alpha95 of 4.0 deg (two NRM measurements). The moment falls from 1.24e-09 emu (NRM) to 8.2e-10 (400 C) and 1.2e-10 (590 C).

outcomes.statement: Alteration during the laser heating of the single crystals was not significant; apparent recording efficiencies far above 100% were not observed and the alteration checks did not fail.
outcomes.source: Background & Summary, paragraph 5
outcomes.quote: If alteration had resulted in the formation of new magnetic minerals, apparent recording efficiencies ≫ 100% should have be observed (but these were not), and alteration checks should fail
outcomes.notes: Under reading (b) every crystal passes; the 40 uT TRM is 0.77 to 1.17 times twice the 20 uT TRM (0.79 to 1.14 with averaged 590.0 and 590.3 replicates), against the cutoff of 2. Under reading (a) 11 of 12 pass with first replicates and 10 of 12 with means; 14053g1's 590.3 moment exceeds its 590.0 moment by 9.8e-11 to 1.21e-10 emu, and 14053g3's by 9.9e-11 with means. The paper's words are recording efficiencies far above 100%; the largest here is 117% of linear recording. The 590.0 replicate moments of one crystal scatter by 0.6e-11 to 6.3e-11 emu (sd), below reading (a)'s allowance of 8e-11 emu; 14053g1's 590.3 excess is about 6 to 8 times its 590.0 sd of 1.6e-11 emu, so its failure under reading (a) is not replicate noise. The 590.0 moments themselves, 1.0e-10 to 6.0e-10 emu with random directions, are 1.3 to 7.5 times the threshold.
deviations: The cutoff of 2 on the ratio is the claims file's, not the paper's; the largest ratio, 1.17, is far from it. The cutoff fails a crystal only when the 40 uT TRM exceeds four times the 20 uT TRM, although the criterion's text says "about twice". Without the factor of two, TRM40/TRM20 is 1.54 to 2.35 and three crystals are above 2 (12053g1 2.35, 14053g3 2.08, 12053g2 2.06), so a cutoff of 2 on that ratio would fail reading (b) for them and no reading would pass every crystal. This is asked of a reader in questions/figshare-24639285.yaml; the claim is tested as the file has it.

outcomes.statement: Together with ref. 1, the data are consistent with impact plasma magnetization of the 64455 glass and with the absence of a long-lived lunar core dynamo recorded in the 3.9 to 3.2 Ga crystals.
outcomes.source: Abstract; Background & Summary, paragraphs 2 and 7
outcomes.quote: These 64455 field strengths1 match those predicted by the charge separation mechanism
outcomes.notes: The claims file says this interpretation is not tested, as it rests on ref. 1 and on models of impact plasmas, and is judged from four other claims. Their outcomes here are fig2-changing-field reproduced, glass-directions-not-random partially reproduced, fig3-590-inconsistent reproduced and table1-max-intensity reproduced.

findings.statement: In four glass sheets of 64455lunar_cryodata.xlsx (g2, ss8, ss39, ss48) the rows given as repeated measurements of each step are one row multiplied by factors between 0.95 and 1.03. In g2, ss8 and ss39 the same factor multiplies the moment, the declination and the inclination of a row; in ss48 each column has its own factors. Every step of these sheets is built this way and no step of the other 18 sheets or the 12 crystal files is. These rows are not measurements, and the scaling of a declination has no physical meaning (one ss8 declination becomes 361.7 deg). The deposit does not say how they were made.

Values outside their ranges or format in 64455lunar_cryodata.xlsx; sheet ss19, 10 mT step, an inclination of -136 deg (likely -13.6); sheet ss8, NRM, a declination of 361.692 deg; sheet ss18, row 41, a 250 C row with no moment, declination or inclination; sheet ss48 has an extra column CSD before the moment, so its columns differ from the Data Records' description.

The glass sheets hold 2 to 19 repeated measurements per step, and neither the deposit nor the paper says in words how they were combined for Table 2 and Figures 1 and 2. The mean vector reproduces most of Table 2; the first measurement does not. The deposit's Supplementary Figure 1 plots means (see the finding on it). Eleven steps of seven glass sheets hold two groups of directions more than 45 deg apart, nine of them inside the specimen's Table 2 range; sheet ss6's 250.1 step holds 19 rows in two groups (inclination near 71 deg and near -13 deg). NRM is labelled both 0 and 0.0 in ss27 and ss38.

Questions for the paper's authors. (1) Were the repeated measurements of each step averaged as vectors for Table 2 and Figures 1 and 2, or was one measurement used? (2) Is MAD a free (unanchored) line fit to the field-off vectors, without the three-point smoothing? A free fit to averaged replicates gives 8 of the 9 printed MADs. (3) How is the pTRM check percentage defined (denominator, and which field-off step the check is referred to)? No single definition tried here gives more than 5 of the 11 printed values. (4) Which measure supports "consistent" and "inconsistent" for the crystal replicates? (5) Were Table 1's max intensities rounded up? Ten of twelve equal the formula rounded up, not rounded. (6) Is Table 1's M590 the moment of the 590.1 measurement alone, or the vector difference of the 590.1 and 590.0 steps that the Methods define as the TRM? Supplementary Figure 1 answers part of (1) to (3) for the specimens it plots (mean vectors for TRM gained, mean of the moments for NRM, checks referred to the field-off step before them); Table 2's numbers for ss19, ss43, ss22 and ss41 are in the paper's Figures 1 and 2.

Table 1's M590 equals the moment of the single 590.1 (field-on) measurement to its four digits for all 12 crystals, while the Methods define the TRM as the vector subtraction of the field-on and field-off steps (Methods, Thermal measurements, paragraph 3). The vector difference with the 590.0 replicates differs from Table 1 by 0.2 to 4.2% with their mean and by up to 11% with the first replicate.

The deposit's "SupplFig1 - other Thelliers March 2024.pdf" plots, for 12 of its 14 specimens that are not synthetic sheets, TRM gained from the mean vectors of the repeated rows and NRM as the mean of their moments, to 0.1% or better. For the four sheets whose rows are scaled copies (g2, ss8, ss39, ss48) its points differ from every combination of the deposited rows by 0.5% or more (median), so these sheets' deposited rows are not the values plotted. One ss27 point is labelled 210 C, a step with no field-on measurement in the sheet.

The Technical Validation example of the threshold for 14053g1 uses a TRM of 8e-12 A m2 and gives 0.2 uT; the data and Table 1 give 3.2e-12 A m2 and 0.50 to 0.51 uT for 14053g1, and the example's numbers are those of 12040g1. The text before Figure 3 names 12041g1, which is not a specimen of the deposit; the Figure 3 legend has 12040g1.
Table 2 gives ss36 a pTRM check at 450 C (25%), but its sheet has no pTRM check step, and gives ss27 6 points from 100 to 550 C where its sheet has 5 paired steps (100, 305, 400, 500, 550 C).
The laboratory field of the glass experiments differs between sheets, 18 uT (10 sheets), 15 uT (11) and 14.4 uT (g2), given in a footnote of each sheet. The paper states only the 18 uT of Figure 1.

The crystals' moments after zero-field heating to 590 C (37 measurements, 1.0e-10 to 6.0e-10 emu per measurement) are all above the 8e-11 emu magnetometer threshold the paper uses for its bound on paleointensity. The directions of these measurements are random by Watson's test in every crystal.

The item's description lists files named "SI Figure 1 - Other Thelliers n=18.pdf" and "SI Figure 2 - All Stereonets copy.pdf", while the files are "SupplFig1 - other Thelliers March 2024.pdf" and "SuppFig2 - All Stereonet.pdf". The item's title differs from the paper's.

attempts.label: FIGSHARE:26877211
attempts.entry_title: The JECFA portal index (Ocagli et al. 2024)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Ocagli et al. (2024) on Figshare item 26877211, version 1, which holds the table scraped from the JECFA portal in May 2024 as an RDS file and a CSV file. It checks the row count and fields, the cleaning to unique pages, the availability of each field (Table 1), the counts by evaluation year and functional class (Table 2), the content of the unknowns, the most frequent FAS codes, and the count of pages with a JECFA name. The manual validation of 700 pages is not deposited.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Ocagli et al. (2024) from Figshare item 26877211

outcomes.statement: The deposited dataframe is the JECFA index of May 2024, with 6552 rows and the fields of Table 1.
outcomes.source: Data Records, paragraphs 1 and 2
outcomes.quote: As of May 2024, the final dataframe consists of 6552 rows. The RDS file contains a structured data frame to reflect the fields described in Table 1 of the manuscript
outcomes.notes: jecfa.rds has 6552 rows and 17 columns, one for each field of Table 1, named as in R/process_df.R in lower case with "." replaced by "_". JECFA.csv holds the same 6552 rows and 17 columns, with no differing cell. The MD5 of both files read matches the archive's computed_md5. The columns R/add_metadata.R adds are absent, so the deposit is the output of process_df.R. The "May 2024" date cannot be checked from the files, which carry no scrape date.

outcomes.statement: The 6552 scraped entries, cleaned of the duplicates of page 6316 and of test pages, give 6549 unique pages.
outcomes.source: Methods, Web-scraping, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: We validated the effectiveness of this method by identifying 6552 entries, which were then cleaned to remove duplicates of (E)-N-[2-(1,3-BENZODIOXOL-5-YL)ETHYL]-3- (3,4-DIMETHOXYPHENYL)PROP-2-ENAMIDE ... and test pages, resulting in 6549
outcomes.notes: D1 (distinct URLs) gives 6552, 3 from 6549 and outside the tolerance of 2, as no URL is repeated. D2 (distinct JECFA names less page 5883) and D3 (rows less page 5883 and less the second row of page 6316's chemical) give 6550, within tolerance. Page 6316's chemical appears twice, at pages 6316 (name only) and 6319 (full record); page 5883 is named TEST and carries nothing else. The paper's 6549 is reached, for example, by removing both rows of that chemical with the test page (the one variant tested).
deviations: The criterion's readings D1 to D3 are all run; measured is the first that matches (D2). D1 does not match.

outcomes.statement: The share of pages carrying each Table 1 field is 100% for URL and JECFA name, 82% chemical names, 79% synonyms, 35% CAS number, 71% JECFA number, 65% FEMA number, 46% COE number, 98% functional class, 98% evaluation year, 97% report and its link, 93% Tox monograph and its link, 92% specification and its link, and 93% FAS.
outcomes.source: Methods, Web-scraping, paragraph 3; Table 1, column Availability (%)
outcomes.inferred: Numbers from Table 1, column Availability (%), titled "Common content of most JECFA pages"; no sentence of the text states them.
outcomes.notes: Over all 6552 rows (U1 and U2 are the same, as no URL repeats), 16 of 17 shares are within tolerance with the deposited fas column (reading A), FAS being 81.38% against 93% (lower bound 83.7%), and 17 of 17 with fas after the step of R/add_metadata.R (reading B, 86.74%). Over the 6550 rows left after cleaning, no share moves by more than 0.05 points. Rounded to whole numbers 12 of 17 equal Table 1 (Chemical names 83, Synonyms 78, Report and its link 98 differ by one point, FAS by 12 under A). Counting the 752 empty fas strings as present gives 92.86%, which suggests Table 1 counted every non-NA value; the claims file's reading E counts them as absent. The outcome rests on 16 of 17 under A, or 17 under B, and does not depend on how the empty strings are counted.
deviations: The criterion names the FAS column of both process_df.R and add_metadata.R; the deposit holds the first. Both are run (A and B), and both give reproduced.

outcomes.statement: By evaluation year, 2357 evaluations fall in 1958 to 2000 (37%), 3099 in 2000 to 2010 (48%), 778 in 2010 to 2020 (12%) and 200 in 2020 to 2023 (3.1%), with 118 unknown.
outcomes.source: Data Records, paragraph 3; Table 2, Evaluation year
outcomes.quote: For the evaluation year, from 1958 to 2000 there were 2,356 evaluations, representing 37% of the total. Between 2000 and 2010, the number of evaluations increased significantly to 3,099 (48% of the total)
outcomes.notes: The four bins and the unknowns equal Table 2 exactly; shares are over the 6434 rows with a year. Counts are compared with the claims file's tolerances (236, 310, 78, 20 and 12). All years lie between 1958 and 2023. The text's 2,356 for the first bin differs by one from Table 2 and from the data.

outcomes.statement: Most substances are flavouring agents, 4635 (72%), followed by food additives 1453 (23%), veterinary drugs 277 (4.3%) and food contaminants 77 (1.2%), with 110 unknown.
outcomes.source: Data Records, paragraph 3; Table 2, Functional Class
outcomes.quote: In terms of functional class, the majority of the evaluated substances were flavoring agents, with 4,635 substances comprising 72% of the total
outcomes.notes: The counts equal Table 2 exactly; shares are over the 6442 rows with a class. Every functional_class string starts with one of the four class names (the data spell "Flavouring Agent"), so none is left unmatched. Flavouring agents are the largest class.

outcomes.statement: The records with unknown class or year have only the JECFA name, without chemical names or other information.
outcomes.source: Data Records, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: The unknowns have only the JECFA name without associated compound names or additional information.
outcomes.notes: 95 rows carry only a URL and a JECFA name, and each of them has both class and year unknown. They are 95 of 110 rows with an unknown class (86.4%) and 95 of 118 with an unknown year (80.5%), both below the criterion's 90%. The criterion states only when the claim is reproduced, so the outcome is not reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after verification round 1). The other 15 rows with an unknown class carry a year, a report and identifiers; 13 of them lie between pages 6385 and 6450 and 13 were evaluated in 2008. The other 23 with an unknown year all carry a functional class (13 food additives, 9 food contaminants, 1 flavouring agent), 15 of them chemical names and 14 synonyms; 11 of them are pages 6476 to 6533. The statement holds exactly for the 95 rows unknown on both class and year. Whether "the unknowns" means those rows is asked of a reader in questions/figshare-26877211.yaml; the claim is tested as the claims file has it.

outcomes.statement: Almost all 85 FAS codes are referenced, and FAS 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50 and 52 together account for 50% of the records.
outcomes.source: Data Records, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Although almost all 85 FAS codes are referenced, the ones collectively accounting for 50% of the records are 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50, and 52
outcomes.notes: The seven named codes hold 3036 rows, 46.34% of all 6552 rows (F1, within 5 points of 50%) under both FAS readings; over the rows with a FAS code (F2) 56.94% with the deposited column (A, outside tolerance) and 53.42% after add_metadata.R (B, within). They are not the seven most frequent; FAS 59 (351 rows) and FAS 54 (287) are more frequent than FAS 52 (286) under both readings, and FAS 60 (353) too under B; the named codes rank 1 to 6 and 9 (A) or 10 (B). The deposited column has 81 distinct non-empty values, which meets the 77 the criterion takes for "almost all 85", and 73 after add_metadata.R, which does not. The 81 include malformed values (eight such as "77 JECFA 86", five decimals such as "67.29", and "617") and "86", above 85. Counting only whole numbers from 1 to 85 gives 66 codes (A) and 71 (B), both below 77, so "almost all 85" does not hold under a cleaned reading; codes 2, 3, 4, 7, 9, 11, 61, 63, 66, 76, 79, 81, 84 and 85 are absent under both. The criterion sets the outcome by the share and the ranking, so this does not change it.
deviations: The criterion names the FAS column of both process_df.R and add_metadata.R; the deposit holds the first. Both are run (A and B), and both give partially reproduced.

outcomes.statement: In a manual check of 700 random pages, scraped and manually read values disagreed only for Report (0.6%), Report sourcelink (0.9%), Tox monograph sourcelink (5.3%) and Specification sourcelink (0.2%).
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: we observed minimal discrepancies, notably in only four contents across web pages that display the following percentages. Report (0.6%), Report sourcelink (0.9%), Tox Monograph sourcelink (5.3%), Specification sourcelink (0.2%)
outcomes.notes: The test needs the manual extraction of the 700 sampled pages, entered in REDCap at the University of Padova. It is not among the item's two files (the scraped table as RDS and CSV), not in the paper's GitHub repository at commit 2d8a5340, and the paper names no other place for it. The portal has changed since May 2024, so the check cannot be repeated on the pages as scraped.

outcomes.statement: A search of the JECFA portal by first character returned 6547 items, in line with the pages carrying a JECFA name (6551 less a duplicate and a test page).
outcomes.source: Technical Validation, paragraphs 2 and 3
outcomes.quote: The search functionality of the portal for chemicals by the first character yielded 6,547 items. This number aligns with the number of websites containing at least a JECFA name (n = 6,551 minus a duplicate and a test page)
outcomes.notes: The portal's 6547 is outside data, not public in its May 2024 state, and is not tested. In the dataset all 6552 rows carry a JECFA name, within the tolerance of the paper's 6551 but one more. After the cleaning of unique-pages, D2 and D3 give 6550, 3 more than 6547 and outside the margin of 2 the criterion takes for "aligns"; D1 gives 6552. The paper's own numbers (6551 less 2 is 6549) are within 2 of 6547; the one extra row in the deposit is what puts the count outside. The data do not explain the gap between 6552 and 6551; leaving out the test page, named "TEST", gives 6551, but the paper then removes the test page again. Removing both rows of page 6316's chemical with the test page gives 6549, within 2 of 6547, but that is none of the readings D1 to D3 and is not used. The criterion states only when the dataset's part is reproduced and gives no partial level; one of its two conditions fails, so the dataset's part is not reproduced, read as for unknowns-name-only. The portal part stays untested. The outcome was partially reproduced until verification round 3, which agreed with the change. The margin of 2 is the claims file's choice and puts the paper's own 6549 against 6547 at its edge, so this outcome rests on one row. No measured value is given, as the first expected value (the portal count) cannot be measured.

findings.statement: The manual extraction of 700 portal pages used for the Technical Validation (REDCap, University of Padova) is not deposited, so the discrepancy rates of the validation cannot be checked.

The Methods say the 6552 scraped entries were cleaned of a duplicate and a test page to 6549 unique pages, and Data Records says each entry corresponds to a unique chemical, but the deposited table holds all 6552 rows, including the test page 5883 (named TEST, with no other field) and page 6316, a name-only stub of the chemical whose full record is page 6319.

The item's description calls FAS a "FAO/WHO Food Additive Specification identifier". The column is the number of the Food Additives Series toxicological monograph, derived from the Tox monograph by R/process_df.R in every row, as the paper's Table 1 describes it.

The deposited fas column, from R/process_df.R, is empty for 355 rows whose Tox monograph is a FAS monograph (339 FAS 60, 10 FAS 74, 2 FAS 27, 4 written "FAS79"), which its "^FAS " pattern misses; 349 of the 752 empty values have a Tox monograph starting with the stray characters '">'. It holds 752 empty strings beside 468 NA, and some values keep a session or page ("77 JECFA 86", "67.29", "617"). R/add_metadata.R repairs part of this but its output is not deposited. With empty strings counted as absent the FAS share is 81.4%, against 93% in Table 1.

Table 1 describes the COE number as assigned by the Codex Alimentarius Commission; the item's description calls it the Council of Europe number. COE numbers are present for 3022 flavouring agents and 9 food additives and for no other class, which is consistent with the Council of Europe numbering of flavourings, not with Codex.

Scraped values carry formatting residue. 602 report, 349 Tox monograph and 398 specification values start with '">' (the Usage Notes mention this for Report); 33 FEMA numbers are plain integers padded with spaces; 31 JECFA numbers are not plain integers ("506a,b", "632.1"); 46 of 2127 plain CAS numbers fail the CAS check digit, and 190 CAS values hold several numbers or notes.

entries.name: 000003-senzai-2017
entries.title: Granule cells and mossy cells of the dentate gyrus (Senzai and Buzsaki 2017)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Senzai and Buzsaki (2017) on dandiset 000003, which holds silicon probe recordings of the dentate gyrus and CA3 in 16 mice, in 101 files from 94 recording days, with labelled granule cells, mossy cells, CA3 pyramidal cells and interneurons, sleep states, dentate spikes, light pulses, and positions on a circular T-maze and in open fields. It covers firing by brain state, theta and gamma phase locking, recruitment by dentate spikes, optogenetic tagging, monosynaptic transmission, place fields and remapping, and, on the 17 files that give each unit's shank, depth and the classification of granule and mossy cells.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Senzai and Buzsaki (2017) from dandiset 000003

entries.name: 000004-chandravadia-2020
entries.title: Human single neurons during a recognition memory task (Chandravadia et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the data descriptor of Chandravadia et al. (2020) on dandiset 000004, which holds 87 sessions of 59 epilepsy patients with single units from the amygdala and hippocampus during a new/old recognition task. It checks the files against the paper's description of the data records and subjects, and repeats the behavioural results (AUC, ROC asymmetry, accuracy by confidence) and the proportions of visually and memory selective cells of Figure 5.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Chandravadia et al. (2020) from dandiset 000004

entries.name: 000005-yu-2016
entries.title: VPM and layer 4 responses to touch and whisking, and their control by thalamus and FS interneurons (Yu et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the claims written from the full text of Yu, Gutnisky, Hires and Svoboda (2016) on dandiset 000005, which holds silicon probe recordings in VPM and single-cell recordings in layer 4 of barrel cortex of mice locating a pole with their whiskers. It measures touch responses, whisking rates and phase coupling of VPM units, FS interneurons and excitatory cells, their membrane potential, and the effects of thalamic photoinhibition and of PV interneuron suppression, by the paper's methods as the claims file gives them.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Yu et al. (2016) from dandiset 000005

entries.name: 000006-economo-2018
entries.title: Two types of pyramidal tract neuron in mouse motor cortex (Economo et al. 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Economo et al. (2018) that the claims file, written from the full text, lists. The dandiset holds silicon probe recordings from the anterior lateral motor cortex of 12 mice in a delayed response task, with tagged PTupper and PTlower units. The notebook rebuilds the paper's smoothed rates from the files, applies the paper's unit selection, single-unit measures and coding directions with the hierarchical bootstrap under every reading the claims file names, and compares the two types. The claims on sequencing and axon reconstructions are tested on the paper's Figshare record.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Economo et al. (2018) from dandiset 000006

entries.name: 000008-scala-2021
entries.title: Phenotypic variation of transcriptomic cell types in mouse motor cortex (Scala, Kobak et al. 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Scala, Kobak et al. (2021) on dandiset 000008, which holds the current-clamp recordings of 1,328 Patch-seq neurons of mouse primary motor cortex with each cell's t-type, family, layer and read counts. The paper's own feature extraction is run on every file; the cohort, the stimulus protocol, the features, the kNN family classification, the IT and ET differences, the t-type coverage and depths, and the variability of t-types are tested on the dandiset, and the claims that also need the paper's gene counts, morphology or transcriptomic reference data are tested with those inputs in separate notebooks.

notebooks.title: Recordings and metadata of dandiset 000008 (cohort, features, families, t-types)
Dandiset 000008 with the paper's gene counts and 10x reference (RRR, within-family distances)
Sequencing claims on the paper's count tables and reference data

entries.name: 000009-guo-2017
entries.title: Persistent activity in a frontal thalamocortical loop (Guo et al. 2017)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Guo, Inagaki, Daie, Druckmann, Gerfen and Svoboda (2017) on dandiset 000009, which holds silicon-probe recordings from ALM, thalamus and SNr during a delayed licking task with optogenetic photoinhibition, and whole-cell recordings of ALM neurons during thalamus, M1 or contralateral ALM photoinhibition. It tests behaviour under ALM photoinhibition, unit classes, trial-type selectivity, the collapse of ALM and thalamic activity under photoinhibition of the other area, onset latencies, SNr responses and membrane potential measures. Behaviour-only, muscimol, weak photoinhibition, non-behaving whole-cell and anatomical data are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Guo et al. (2017) from dandiset 000009

entries.name: 000010-li-2015
entries.title: A motor cortex circuit for motor planning and movement (Li et al. 2015)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Li, Chen, Guo, Gerfen and Svoboda (2015) on dandiset 000010, which holds 99 extracellular sessions (19 mice) and 59 two-photon imaging planes (4 mice) from left ALM during the object location discrimination task. It tests behaviour, unit classes, trial-type selectivity and its time course, error trials, contralateral bias, PT and IT neurons and their antidromic latencies, and the imaging counts. The reaction time is run but blocked, as the paper does not fix how it is read from the signal. The photostimulation and anatomy findings are blocked, as the dandiset holds none of those data.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Li et al. (2015) from dandiset 000010

entries.name: 000011-li-2016
entries.title: Robust preparatory activity in mouse premotor cortex (Li, Daie et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Li, Daie, Svoboda and Druckmann (2016) on dandiset 000011, which holds extracellular recordings from left ALM of 12 control mice during unilateral and bilateral photoinhibition (58 sessions) and 33 sessions of 7 further mice with no photostimulus record. It reads the photostimulus conditions from the laser traces, and tests unit classification, selectivity, recovery of spike rates and selectivity after photoinhibition, the coding direction analyses and the network models of the paper. The behavioural photoinhibition sessions, the photoactivation and untrained mice, and the callosotomy conditions are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Li, Daie et al. (2016) from dandiset 000011

entries.name: 000013-hires-2015
entries.title: Low-noise encoding of active touch by layer 4 (Hires et al. 2015)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Hires, Gutnisky, Yu, O'Connor and Svoboda (2015) on dandiset 000013, which holds the 52 loose-seal recordings of the paper (31 L4 cells in C2, 10 L4 cells outside C2, 11 L5 cells) with millisecond whisker tracking during pole localization. It covers the behaviour, the example cell, Table 1, the touch and phase coupled spikes of Figure 3, the population decoders of Figure 4, the modulation indices of Figure 5 and the Fano factors of Figure 6.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Hires et al. (2015) from dandiset 000013

entries.name: 000015-chen-2017
entries.title: Anticipatory activity in mouse motor cortex (Chen et al. 2017)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Chen, Li, Daie and Svoboda (2017) on dandiset 000015, which holds two-photon imaging of 105 image planes in left ALM and MM of six mice during a tactile delayed response task, with PT and IT labels in three of them. It tests the trial and neuron counts, the selectivity of single neurons for object location, lick direction and outcome, its map over ALM and MM, and the coding of PT and IT neurons. The plane depth, wide-field imaging, whisker tracking, photoinhibition and silicon probe data are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Chen et al. (2017) from dandiset 000015

entries.name: 000019-bouchard-2013
entries.title: Speech articulation in human sensorimotor cortex (Bouchard et al. 2013)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Bouchard, Mesgarani, Johnson and Chang (2013) on dandiset 000019, which holds raw ECoG and syllable annotations of subjects reading consonant-vowel syllables. High gamma is computed from the raw voltage. It tests the active electrodes, the articulator timing, the mixed tuning of electrodes and the cortical state-space analyses. The spatial maps cannot be tested, as the dandiset gives no electrode positions relative to the central sulcus and Sylvian fissure.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Bouchard et al. (2013) from dandiset 000019

entries.name: 000023-berg-2020
entries.title: Human supragranular glutamatergic neurons by Patch-seq (Berg et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Berg, Sorensen, Ting, Miller et al. (2020) on dandiset 000023, which holds the whole-cell recordings of 318 human L2/3 neurons from 56 neurosurgical donors. The 18 electrophysiological features are computed from the recordings with IPFX and linked to the paper's per-cell table of t-types and depths from its code, to test the cohort counts, the depth of each t-type, the differences between the homologous and deep L3 t-types, the depth dependence within FREM3, the classifier, the cross-species comparison and the pathology comparison. Claims on the code's morphology, pathology and NeuN section data are tested apart.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Berg et al. (2020) from dandiset 000023

entries.name: 000034-buccino-2020
entries.title: SpikeInterface spike sorter comparison (Buccino et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Buccino, Hurwitz, Garcia, Magland, Siegle, Hurwitz and Hennig (2020) on dandiset 000034, which holds the mouse, simulated, rat and retina recordings the paper sorts and two manual curations of its Kilosort2 output. It checks that the recordings are as described, that the curated and ground-truth spike times share the recordings' clocks, and compares the two curations. The findings about sorter outputs are blocked, as three of the six sorters need MATLAB and a GPU, which the runner lacks.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Buccino et al. (2020) from dandiset 000034

entries.name: 000035-scala-2021
entries.title: Patch-seq neurons of mouse motor cortex at physiological temperature (Scala, Kobak et al. 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Scala, Kobak et al. (2021) that can be tested on dandiset 000035, which holds the paper's follow-up recordings at 34 degrees C (185 neurons, mostly layer 5 Sst and excitatory cells). entries.name: 000041-watson-2016
entries.title: Firing rates across sleep states in rat frontal cortex (Watson et al. 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Watson, Levenstein, Greene, Gelinas and Buzsaki (2016) on dandiset 000041, which holds silicon probe recordings of units, LFP and sleep states from the frontal cortex of 10 rats in their home cage. It compares firing rates and bursting across WAKE, nonREM and REM, how rates of fast and slow firing cells change over sleep and within nonREM packets, how they relate to LFP band power, and the rate changes across state triplets. UP and DOWN state and spindle analyses are blocked, as their methods are in the unavailable supplement.

entries.name: 000044-grosmark-2016
entries.title: Rigid and plastic hippocampal sequences (Grosmark and Buzsaki 2016)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Grosmark and Buzsaki (2016) on dandiset 000044, which holds eight sessions of CA1 units, LFP, sleep states and track positions from four rats, each with sleep before and after exploring a novel track. It decodes candidate ripple events with a Bayesian decoder, compares sequence scores across PRE, MAZE and POST, estimates each place cell's contribution to sequences, and relates firing rate and ripple gain to coactivation and replay.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Grosmark and Buzsaki (2016) from dandiset 000044

entries.title: Standardized and reproducible decision-making in mice (The International Brain Laboratory 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of The International Brain Laboratory (2021) on dandiset 000045, which holds the trial tables of 178 mice trained in seven laboratories from June 2019 to March 2020. The dandiset holds no sessions before June 2019 and no training status.

notebooks.title: Reproducing The International Brain Laboratory (2021) from dandiset 000045

notebooks.title: Reproducing Peyrache et al. (2015) from dandiset 000056

notebooks.title: Reproducing Petersen & Buzsaki (2020) from dandiset 000059

entries.title: Structure and variability of delay activity in premotor cortex (Even-Chen et al. 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Even-Chen, Sheffer, Vyas, Ryu and Shenoy (2019) on dandiset 000121, which holds 12 sessions of delayed center-out reaching with Utah arrays in two monkeys (all 7 of R, 5 of the 16 of J). It checks the sessions and trial counts, the behaviour, the low-dimensional structure of PMd delay activity (PCA, the spatial plane, its time course, the speed axis), the variability of single-trial neural states on and off the reach axis, and SVM decoding of reach direction and distance.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Even-Chen et al. (2019) from dandiset 000121

entries.name: 000127-chowdhury-2020
entries.title: Active and passive arm movements in somatosensory area 2 (Chowdhury et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the active/passive findings of Chowdhury, Glaser and Miller (2020) on dandiset 000127, which holds one of the paper's twelve sessions. It compares hand and arm kinematics between active reaches and passive bumps, measures how well single neurons tell the two apart, and fits hand-only and whole-arm models of each neuron's firing. The paper's two-workspace experiment cannot be tested because those sessions are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Chowdhury, Glaser & Miller (2020) from dandiset 000127

entries.name: 000128-churchland-2010
entries.title: Preparatory and peri-movement tuning in motor and premotor cortex (Churchland et al. 2010)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Churchland, Cunningham, Kaufman, Ryu and Shenoy (2010) on dandiset 000128 (MC_Maze), which holds the J-array session of monkey Jenkins on the maze task, recorded with two Utah arrays. It tests the correlation between preparatory and peri-movement tuning, its time course, the dimensionality of preparatory activity, the performance and stability of preferred directions in the peri-movement, kinematic and task spaces, and the paper's oscillator model. The speed task, the single-electrode recordings and EMG are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Churchland et al. (2010) from dandiset 000128

entries.name: 000130-sohn-2019
entries.title: Bayesian computation through cortical latent dynamics (Sohn et al. 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Sohn, Narain, Meirhaeghe and Jazayeri (2019) on dandiset 000130, the Neural Latents Benchmark's DMFC_RSG set, which holds one session of monkey H performing the Ready-Set-Go task with 54 units from dorsomedial frontal cortex. It tests the behaviour and the Bayesian observer model, single-unit sensitivity to the prior and elapsed time, the geometry and speed of population trajectories, the alternative mechanisms, and single-trial GPFA trajectories. Monkey G and the recurrent network models are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Sohn et al. (2019) from dandiset 000130

entries.name: 000147-guan-2022
entries.title: Finger representations in human posterior parietal cortex after paralysis (Guan et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Guan, Aflalo et al. (2022) that dandiset 000147 can support. It checks online and offline finger decoding, single-unit tuning and whether the cue location can be decoded, builds the cross-validated finger RDMs of the ten sessions, compares them with the able-bodied fMRI models from the authors' repository, and tests whether the representation changed across sessions and runs. The calibration and control tasks, the component model RDMs and sorting quality metrics are not in the dandiset, so the claims that need them are blocked.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Guan, Aflalo et al. (2022) from dandiset 000147

entries.name: 000207-zheng-2022
entries.title: Cognitive boundaries and human medial temporal lobe neurons (Zheng et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Zheng et al. (2022) that can be tested on dandiset 000207, which holds spike times of medial temporal lobe neurons and the behaviour of 19 patients in a task with video clips that contain no boundary, a soft boundary or a hard boundary. It compares memory for temporal order and for scenes across the three kinds of clip, looks for boundary cells and event cells with the paper's definitions, counts neurons that respond to clip onsets, and measures how far the population state moves after a boundary. Eleven of the paper's twenty findings cannot be tested, because the dandiset has no local field potentials, no neurons outside the medial temporal lobe, no labels for the paper's cell classes, and no way to link test trials with soft or hard boundaries to the clips they came from.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zheng et al. (2022) from dandiset 000207

entries.name: 000213-tingley-2018
entries.title: Spatial phase coding in the lateral septum (Tingley and Buzsaki 2018)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Tingley and Buzsaki (2018) on dandiset 000213, which holds 67 sessions of simultaneous hippocampal and lateral septum recordings from five rats running on alternation mazes and a linear track. It decodes position from the spike rate and the spike theta phase of each LS and hippocampal unit, finds place fields, measures spatial information, relates phase coding to recording depth, and measures hippocampal-LS theta coherence and theta-gamma coupling, and detects hippocampal-LS cell assemblies on a random sample of pairs.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Tingley and Buzsaki (2018) from dandiset 000213

entries.name: 000218-tingley-2019
entries.title: Lateral septum HFOs and hippocampal ripples (Tingley and Buzsaki 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Tingley and Buzsaki (2019) on dandiset 000218, which holds LFP, sorted units, sleep states and trials from simultaneous recordings of the lateral septum and hippocampus in 6 rats. LS high-frequency oscillations and CA1 ripples are detected from the LFP, as the files hold no detected events, and the notebook tests their properties, their coupling and state dependence, the phase locking and co-activation of LS neurons, and which ripple features predict LS firing. The optogenetic experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Tingley and Buzsaki (2019) from dandiset 000218

entries.name: 000226-severson-2017
entries.title: Merkel and other whisker afferents during active touch and whisking (Severson et al. 2017)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Severson, Xu, Van de Loo, Bai, Ginty and O'Connor (2017) on dandiset 000226, which holds 56 trigeminal afferent recordings with high-speed whisker video and 4 EMG sessions. It checks the recordings against the paper's Table S1, the spike rates during non-whisking, whisking in air and touch, the classes of afferents, direction selectivity, the statistical and viscoelastic models of touch responses, phase tuning during whisking in air, the nasolabialis motor units and the curvature noise. The cutting conditions of the progressive cutting experiment, the intrinsic protractor EMG and the optogenetic tagging data are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Severson et al. (2017) from dandiset 000226

entries.name: 000232-chang-2023
entries.title: Rule-based modulation of a sensorimotor transformation across cortical areas (Chang et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Chang, Finkel, Xu and O'Connor (bioRxiv 2023, version 2) on dandiset 000232, which holds silicon-probe recordings from S1, S2, MM, ALM and AMM of mice performing a cross-modal sensory selection task, and the behaviour of optogenetic inhibition sessions in that task and in a tactile detection task. It covers behavioural performance, single-neuron rule and stimulus discrimination, population decoding of the rule, neural trajectories and subspaces, coding dimensions, rule transitions and the effects of optogenetic inhibition.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Chang et al. (2023) from dandiset 000232

entries.name: 000239-xu-2022
entries.title: Cortical processing of flexible sensorimotor sequences (Xu et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Xu, Dong, Chen, Delgado, Hughes, Zhang and O'Connor (2022) on dandiset 000239, which holds the trial tables, tongue tracking and sorted spikes of mice performing a sequence licking task. It decodes tongue kinematics, sequence identity and sequence time from S1TJ, M1TJ, ALM and S1BF populations, classifies backtracking and zigzag sequence context, and checks the behavioural measures and unit counts. The optogenetic and control experiments cannot be tested, as the files do not say which region was inhibited or which condition each session was.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Xu et al. (2022) from dandiset 000239

entries.name: 000350-mu-2019
entries.title: Futility-induced passivity and whole-brain neuronal and glial activity in zebrafish (Mu et al. 2019)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Mu, Bennett, Rubinov et al. (2019) that dandiset 000350 can test. The dandiset holds 12 light-sheet sessions of paralysed larval zebrafish swimming fictively in virtual reality, with swim bouts, stimulus signals and, in 8 of them, segmented neuronal or neuronal and glial traces. The entry measures passive and active epochs, swim intervals and vigor in closed and open loop, and whole-brain neuronal and glial activity around passivity onset. The perturbation and noradrenergic imaging experiments of Figures 4 to 6 are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Mu et al. (2019) from dandiset 000350

entries.name: 000409-ibl-2025
entries.title: The IBL brain-wide map of neural activity (International Brain Laboratory et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of the IBL brain-wide map paper (Nature 2025) on dandiset 000409, which holds 459 sessions of Neuropixels recordings from 139 mice performing the IBL decision-making task. It checks the dataset's composition and inclusion counts, the behavioural results of Figure 1, and, on a fixed set of regions, the decoding of stimulus, choice and feedback, single-cell selectivity, the latencies of stimulus trajectories and the feedback oscillations related to licking, and over all canonical regions the number with significant stimulus trajectories.

notebooks.title: Reproducing the IBL brain-wide map (2025) from dandiset 000409

entries.name: 000552-huszar-2022
entries.title: Birthdated CA1 pyramidal neurons in freely moving mice (Huszar et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Huszar, Zhang, Blockus and Buzsaki (2022) that can be tested on dandiset 000552, which holds sleep states, sharp-wave ripples, spike-sorted units and position from 17 mice electroporated at E13.5 to E16.5. It checks the description of the dataset and tests the findings on all pyramidal neurons on familiar and novel mazes (population-vector decorrelation, firing rates, spatial information and ratemap correlations). The units carry no light-responsiveness label and no optogenetic pulse times are stored, so the comparisons of same- and different-birthdate neurons are blocked.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Huszar et al. (2022) from dandiset 000552

entries.name: 000559-markowitz-2023
entries.title: Dopamine and spontaneous behaviour in mice (Markowitz, Gillis, Jay et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Markowitz, Gillis, Jay et al. (2023) on dandiset 000559, which holds the dLight photometry, MoSeq syllables and closed-loop optogenetic sessions of the paper. It relates DLS dopamine to velocity, syllable identity, syllable use and sequence entropy, compares DMS with DLS, and tests the reinforcement of target syllables by closed-loop dopamine release. The modelling of Figures 4 and 5 is not attempted.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Markowitz, Gillis, Jay et al. (2023) from dandiset 000559

entries.name: 000568-valero-2022
entries.title: Pulsed optogenetics in hippocampal CA1 (Valero et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Valero, Zutshi, Yoon and Buzsaki (2022) on dandiset 000568, which holds 28 sessions of CA1 units recorded with uLED probes in four CaMKIIa-Cre::Ai32 mice. Pulse times and laps are in two sessions only, so the light responses during ripples, theta and place fields are tested on those two; the ripple modulation of firing is tested on all sessions. The intracellular recordings and the light intensity levels are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Valero et al. (2022) from dandiset 000568

entries.name: 000582-sargolini-2006
entries.title: Grid, head-direction and conjunctive cells by entorhinal layer (Sargolini et al. 2006)
entries.description: Tests the 21 claims of Sargolini et al. (2006) on dandiset 000582, which holds spike times and tracked positions for 620 cell-sessions from the medial entorhinal cortex of 15 rats. For every cell it computes gridness, head-direction tuning and speed regressions by the paper's Supporting Online Material, under every reading the claims file names, and compares the cell classes found in each cortical layer.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Sargolini et al. (2006) from dandiset 000582

entries.name: 000625-geiller-2020
entries.title: Molecularly identified CA1 interneurons during random foraging (Geiller, Vancura et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Geiller, Vancura et al. (2020) that can be tested on dandiset 000625, which holds three random-foraging sessions of one mouse with 231 interneurons, 74 of them assigned one of the paper's six subtypes. It checks the imaging clock against the behaviour, then measures each interneuron's correlation with running speed, run-stop responses, spatial selectivity, position decoding and the stability of tuning curves within and across sessions. The sharp-wave ripple, novel-context, goal-oriented learning and VIP experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Geiller, Vancura et al. (2020) from dandiset 000625

entries.name: 000691-scherrer-2023
entries.title: Imaging thousands of neurons in a freely moving mouse with a large-FOV head-mounted microscope (Scherrer et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Scherrer, Lynch, Zhang and Fee (2023) on dandiset 000691, which holds one session of one mouse imaged with the large-FOV head-mounted microscope while it explores a looped maze, with 2948 EXTRACT footprints, the imaging video and a behaviour video. It counts the footprints, computes the field of view, registers the whole movie for its motion, tracks the mouse from the video, decodes its position and direction against shuffled activity, looks at the spread of coactive footprints and at place maps, and tests the bead resolution, field curvature and illumination profiles on measurements in the paper's code repository. The other mice, the birds and the other optical tests are not in the dandiset.

entries.name: 000718-zaki-2024
entries.title: Offline ensemble co-reactivation in the EEG/EMG experiment (Zaki et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Zaki et al. (2024) that can be tested on dandiset 000718, which holds two of the nine mice of the paper's calcium imaging and EEG/EMG experiment (one high-shock, one low-shock) with their encoding and recall sessions, the first offline recording after encoding, and cell registration for the high-shock mouse. It checks the deposited freezing against the paper's per-mouse values, compares freezing between the two mice, tests offline population bursts and their skew against shuffled activity and against movement, and compares overlap-neutral with overlap-aversive co-bursting in wake. The one-hour offline, behaviour-only, inhibitory tagging and no-shock experiments are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Zaki et al. (2024) from dandiset 000718

entries.name: 000727-brezovec-2022
entries.title: Brain-wide neural correlates of walking in Drosophila (Brezovec et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Brezovec, Berger, Druckmann and Clandinin (2022) on dandiset 000727, which holds whole-brain two-photon imaging and ball tracking of nine walking flies. It streams 12 planes of the authors' processed volumes in the Functional Drosophila Atlas for all flies, and tests the voxel correlations with forward and turning velocity, their symmetry, the principal components and the models that predict velocity from them, the demixing of velocity components, and the timing of neural activity relative to behaviour. Region-level results cannot be tested, as the dandiset has no neuropil labels.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Brezovec et al. (2022) from dandiset 000727

entries.name: 000947-schwab-2020
entries.title: GPi and VLa activity during reaching in macaques (Schwab et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Schwab, Kase, Zimnik, Rosenbaum, Codianni, Rubin and Turner (2020) on the pre-MPTP recordings of dandiset 000947, single units from the internal globus pallidus and the ventrolateral anterior thalamus of two monkeys performing a reaching task. It compares rates, spike widths, peri-movement responses and their latencies, spike and rate correlations of simultaneously recorded pairs, and the effect of GPi bursts and pauses on VLa activity, and links the dandiset's units to the paper's own unit list.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Schwab et al. (2020) from dandiset 000947

entries.name: 000971-seiler-2022
entries.title: Dorsomedial striatal dopamine and compulsive reward seeking (Seiler et al. 2022)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Seiler, Cosme, Sherathiya, Schaid, Bianco, Bridgemohan and Lerner (2022) on dandiset 000971, which holds the operant behavior of a fiber photometry cohort and three optogenetic cohorts, dual-site photometry from DMS and DLS dopamine axons during RI60 and RR20 training, and western blot images. It tests the shock probe phenotypes and their behavior, the DMS and DLS rewarded-unrewarded peak scores, and the effects of DMS and DLS terminal manipulations. RI30 and shock probe photometry, fear conditioning, open field and histology are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Seiler et al. (2022) from dandiset 000971

entries.name: 001038-azcorra-2023
entries.title: Functional responses of genetic subtypes of dopamine neurons (Azcorra, Gaertner et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the fiber photometry findings of Azcorra, Gaertner et al. (2023) on dandiset 001038, which holds the recordings from striatal axons and SNc somas of Vglut2, Calb1, Anxa1, Aldh1a1 and DAT mice running on a treadmill and receiving rewards and air puffs. It covers locomotion signaling (Figures 2, 3 and 5), reward and air puff responses (Figure 4), clustering (Figure 6), soma and axon correlation (Figure 7) and Extended Data Figures 1 and 6 to 9. Two snRNA-seq claims of Figure 1 are tested on the paper's GEO matrices.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Azcorra, Gaertner et al. (2023) from dandiset 001038

entries.name: 001075-randi-2023
entries.title: Neural signal propagation atlas of C. elegans (Randi et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Randi, Sharma, Dvali and Leifer (2023) on dandiset 001075, which holds the 113 wild-type-background recordings of whole-brain calcium imaging during single-neuron optogenetic stimulation, 110 of them with extracted traces. It checks the recordings, the number of measured neuron pairs, three example connections of Figure 1, the spatial specificity of the stimulation, the responses to RID stimulation in WT and, from the paper's OSF export, in unc-31 animals, and how the per-pair measurements and recordings link to the paper's Source Data and OSF export. The q values, the spontaneous recordings and the kernel analyses are not testable.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Randi et al. (2023) from dandiset 001075

entries.name: 001084-vu-2024
entries.title: Striatal dopamine release patterns and targeted stimulation through micro-fiber arrays (Vu et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Vu, Brown, Wen et al. (2024) on dandiset 001084, which holds multi-fiber photometry from mice with arrays of 30 to 103 fibers across the striatum. It re-runs the paper's GLM of dopamine release to light and tone in 280 fibers of 7 mice (amplitude maps, latencies and their spatial gradients), the isosbestic controls, the D1 calcium correlations, the chronic reward responses, and the spread of release evoked by single-fiber stimulation with its controls. The freely moving, histology and jaw movement data of Figures 3, 7 and S1 are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Vu et al. (2024) from dandiset 001084

entries.title: A hypothalamic line attractor for female mating (Liu, Nair et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Liu, Nair et al. (2024) on dandiset 001097, which holds miniscope imaging of VMHvl alpha-cells in female mice during mating, with annotations of male and female behaviour. It tests the behavioural dynamics of mating, single-cell tuning, GLM fits and persistence, and, with the authors' deposited rSLDS weights for two mice, how the receptive-day integration dimension and its cells behave across the oestrus cycle. Claims that need new rSLDS fits are blocked, as the model cannot be built or fit within the registry's environment and time limit.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Liu, Nair et al. (2024) from dandiset 001097

entries.name: 001170-ling-2023
entries.title: ON and OFF odor responses in the mouse olfactory bulb and locust antennal lobe (Ling et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Ling, Moss, Smith, Deng, Kroeger, Reimer, Raman and Arenkiel (bioRxiv 2023, v2 2024) on dandiset 001170, which holds two-photon imaging of olfactory bulb glomeruli in awake mice, seven sessions from four mice under the paper's block protocol and five random-order sessions. (2022) on dandiset 001172, which holds dual-colour mesoscopic imaging of ACh3.0 and jRCaMP1b with face video, pupil and wheel data from 4 of the paper's 6 mice. notebooks.title: Reproducing Lohani, Moberly et al. (2022) from dandiset 001172

entries.title: Optomotor swimming of zebrafish and Danionella cerebrum (Fouke et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the freely swimming findings of Fouke, He, Loring and Naumann (2025) on dandiset 001453, which holds the tracking data of 25 zebrafish and 12 Danionella cerebrum larvae during the optomotor protocol. notebooks.title: Reproducing Fouke et al. (2025) from dandiset 001453

entries.title: Responses of SNr GABA and SNc dopamine neuron subtypes to STN and PPN input (Hadjas et al. 2025)

(2025) on dandiset 001528, which holds recordings from 120 mice during optogenetic stimulation of STN or PPN inputs to the substantia nigra. It compares responses of SNr GABA neurons, SNc pan-DA neurons, striatal dopamine release in TS and DLS, DA terminals, and Vglut2+ and Anxa1+ DA neurons across train durations and frequencies, using the lab's dF/F stored in the files.
